name: Abbotsford Check
description: The Abbotsford Check is a sumptuous fashion tartan, woven with precision and flair to evoke the grandeur of Scotland's literary heritage. This distinctive check pattern was created by Alistair Buchan in honour of Sir Walter Scott's 200th birthday anniversary, a testament to the writer's enduring influence on Scottish culture. As one of the many fashion tartans registered by the Scottish Tartans Society, this design is steeped in tradition and rooted in Scotland's rich heritage. With its carefully balanced blend of blues, greens, and yellows, the Abbotsford Check embodies the timeless elegance of Scotland's tartan traditions, inviting wearers to proudly proclaim their connection to this storied land and its celebrated literary icon.

name: Abercrombie [default]
description: The Abercrombie tartan is a rich and storied design, steeped in history and heritage. Named after Sir Ralph Abercrombie, a renowned Scottish military leader, this traditional tartan was first mentioned by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1805, marking its beginning as an official clan tartan. Produced towards the end of the 18th Century, the Abercrombie sett has remained remarkably consistent with records, making it a treasured part of Scotland's cultural fabric. As one of the oldest and most established name tartans, the Abercrombie tartan holds great significance, symbolising the enduring legacy of its eponymous namesake and his esteemed place in Scottish history.

name: Aberdeen Football Club #2
description: This enigmatic Unidentified tartan, woven with precision by renowned designers Donald and Fionna Fraser, holds a captivating mystery within its intricately patterned threads. As a Fashion tartan, it is meant to evoke a sense of style and elegance, yet its origins remain shrouded in intrigue, as evidenced by the cryptic registration notes that reveal it was found on a dressing gown. The subtle nuances of this design are likely to add an air of sophistication to any outfit, whilst its unknown history beckons further exploration into Scotland's rich textile heritage. With no discernible clan connections or specific cultural affiliations to guide interpretation, the Unidentified tartan invites wearers to partake in its secrets and unravel the mystery behind this captivating fashion statement.

name: Aberdeen University 1995
description: The Fed. of Circles & Solitaries corporate tartan is a striking representation of unity and harmony, reflecting the values of a diverse yet interconnected community. Designed by Dave Calvin, a nonprofit organisation focused on earth-based faiths from South East Michigan USA, this non-repeating design embodies the elements: green for the earth, yellow for the air, red for fire, and blue for water. The unique pattern weaves together these symbolic colours to create a visually striking fabric that celebrates individuality while fostering a sense of belonging among its wearers. As a corporate tartan, it is intended to be worn with pride by those who value spiritual connection and environmental stewardship, making it an inspiring choice for organisations committed to sustainable values and community building.

name: Aberlour Glenlivet
description: The Aberlour corporate tartan is a quintessential representation of Scottish heritage and tradition, specifically crafted for the renowned Aberlour Whisky Distillery in the heart of Speyside. Registered as a distinctive corporate tartan, its purpose is to evoke the values and legacy of this esteemed whisky maker, which has been crafting fine spirits since 1993. Designed by the respected Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this tartan is steeped in history and symbolism, reflecting the distillery's commitment to quality and tradition. With restrictions in place to ensure its exclusive use within the Aberlour brand family, this tartan serves as a proud visual identity for the company, subtly yet effectively communicating its heritage and connection to Scotland's rich whisky-making traditions.

name: Abertay University
description: The Abertay University tartan is a unique corporate fabric that proudly represents Scotland's esteemed educational institution, The University of Abertay in Dundee. With its distinct pattern, woven to signify the university's heritage and values, this tartan embodies the spirit of innovation and learning that defines the academic community. As a corporate tartan, it is designed for use by the university and its affiliates, allowing them to showcase their affiliation with this prestigious institution on everything from business attire to branding materials. Note that this tartan has been registered specifically for corporate use, ensuring that only authentic representatives of the university can utilise the distinctive design. Estimated thread count notwithstanding, this tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage and The University of Abertay's commitment to excellence in education and research.

name: ABF The Soldiers' Charity
description: The ABF The Soldiers' Charity tartan is a stirring tribute to Scotland's enduring bond with the British Armed Forces. Designated for corporate wear, this distinctive tartan was carefully crafted by Lochcarron of Scotland in honour of the Army Benevolent Fund, now rebranded as ABF The Soldiers' Charity. By weaving together traditional colours that evoke the rich heritage of Scotland's military tradition, the designer has created a striking fabric that proudly represents the nation's contribution to the army and its commitment to supporting veterans. As a registered corporate tartan, it holds great significance within the Scottish tartan community, particularly given the restrictions in place to ensure its use is accompanied by the agreement of both ABF and Lochcarron of Scotland, underscoring the importance of this charitable endeavour to the broader Scottish people.

name: ACS Clothing Ltd Blue Spirit
description: The Blue Spirit tartan is a dynamic fashion statement born from the innovative spirit of its designer, Kirsty Anderson of The House of Edgar. Registered as a Fashion tartan, this vibrant design embodies the perfect fusion of style and heritage. With its distinct blue hues and subtle pattern weave, the Blue Spirit tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich textile traditions while making a bold statement on the catwalk. According to registration notes, Kirsty Anderson crafted this tartan for ACS Clothing of Glasgow, further solidifying its connection to Scotland's thriving fashion scene. While not bound by traditional clan affiliations, the Blue Spirit tartan remains a testament to the country's enduring legacy of textile artistry and flair, ready to inspire those who dare to make a statement with their wardrobe choices.

name: ACS Clothing Ltd Earl Blue Marl
description: The Earl Blue Marl tartan, a sumptuous and majestic pattern designed by the renowned Lochcarron of Scotland, is a masterful blend of tradition and fashion. Originally created for Glasgow-based company ACS Clothing in association with Lochcarron, this tartan is likely to have adorned kilts for hire, adding an air of sophistication to those who wore them. With its distinct blue-green hues evoking the rolling hills of Scotland's countryside, the Earl Blue Marl embodies the country's rich cultural heritage and its storied history of weaving excellence. As a fashion tartan, it has been carefully crafted to make a stylish statement, while also paying homage to the traditional craftsmanship that underpins Scottish textile artistry.

name: ACS Clothing Ltd Grey Spirit
description: The Grey Spirit tartan is a stylish and modern fashion design, woven by renowned Scottish mill, Lochcarron, for ACS Clothing's kilt hire business. This versatile pattern is perfect for those seeking a subtle yet sophisticated look, with its predominantly grey/black marl hue creating a sleek and contemporary appearance. While it may not be the most traditional of tartans, the Grey Spirit is deeply rooted in Scottish heritage, evoking the spirits of the wild and untamed. Its registration notes suggest that the tartan was created specifically for fashion, rather than as part of an established clan tradition or formal heirloom. This makes it a great choice for those looking to add a touch of modernity to their traditional attire, without compromising on style or Scottish heritage.

name: ACS Clothing Ltd Summer Spirit
description: Summer Spirit, a vibrant and captivating fashion tartan, embodies the carefree essence of Scotland's warmest season. Designed by Kirsty Anderson, this dynamic pattern is set to bring a breath of fresh air to any outfit, evoking feelings of joy and vitality. Originally registered for use in clothing by ACS Clothing of Glasgow, a subsidiary of the esteemed House of Edgar, Summer Spirit is poised to become a staple in fashion enthusiasts' wardrobes. With its unique blend of colours, carefully selected to evoke the warmth and beauty of Scotland's summer landscapes, this tartan is sure to add a pop of personality to any ensemble.

name: Adam [default]
description: The Adams tartan is a storied heritage textile, its registration notes evoking the rich history of the Adams family name. Designed by Dalgliesh in 1895, this tartan is a quintessential example of Scottish tradition, woven to evoke the honour and legacy of those who bear the name. As a Category Name tartan, it is specifically designated for use by individuals with the surname Adams, rendering it an important part of their heritage and family identity. Notably, a restriction applies, stipulating that the tartan should only be prepared for weaving by Dalgliesh Ltd, underscoring the importance of preserving traditional techniques and ensuring consistency in its production. This subtle yet significant detail adds depth to the design's significance, solidifying its place within Scotland's revered tartan heritage.

name: Agnew [default]
description: The Agnew tartan is a storied Name tartan that has been woven with pride by Scottish weavers for generations. Registered in the prestigious Lyon Court Books in 1978, this distinctive design tells the story of a name that echoes through Scottish heritage. Named after its esteemed designers, James Agnew and George Lindley, this tartan's significance extends beyond its technical characteristics to represent a lasting tribute to a noble family's legacy. As a Name tartan, the Agnew features a carefully balanced palette of blues, greens, and yellows, symbolising the rich cultural and historical context that has shaped Scotland's intricate weave of identity and tradition.

name: Ainslie 1992 Variant
description: The Ainslie tartan, TS2187, is a revered clan tartan born from the meticulous hand of Dr Gordon Teall in 1992, with roots dating back to an early 1980s sample submitted to the Scottish Tartans Society files by Dr Philip Smith Jr. This rich and complex design holds deep significance as a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Ainslie, whose storied history is woven into the very fabric of Scotland's cultural heritage. As a family tartan, the Ainslie carries the weight of tradition and honour, its intricate patterns and colours evoking a sense of pride and connection to the noble families who have worn it through generations. Although the original sample may have been lost to time, Dr Teall's masterful creation remains a cherished reminder of Scotland's rich tartan heritage, forever linked to the Ainslie clan legacy.

name: Ainslie Lake District
description: Verna MacMillan's Lake Ainslie tartan is a poignant commemoration of the breathtaking beauty found in the west coast of Cape Breton Island, Nova Scotia. This commemorative tartan was designed to celebrate the Bicentennial of Cape Breton's settlement in 1855, and its distinctive pattern is said to be inspired by the tranquil waters of Lake Ainslie itself. As a tribute to the region's rich heritage, this tartan weaves together hues of deep blue, evoking the Atlantic Ocean that surrounds the island, with touches of gold, red, and green - symbolic colours reminiscent of the natural world and the region's Celtic roots. This captivating design serves as a fitting tribute to the area's storied history and its people, forever etching itself into the fabric of Canadian tradition.

name: Ainslie [default]
description: Ainslie #2 is a traditional Clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, woven with meticulous attention to detail. Designed by renowned textile expert Dr Philip D Smith Jr, this intricate pattern pays homage to the storied history of the Ainslie family, whose legacy dates back centuries. The complex interplay of blues and reds evokes the rugged landscapes and rich cultural traditions of Scotland's Highlands. As part of the Clan tartan category, Ainslie #2 is a proud representation of the family's honour and heritage, passed down through generations. While no restrictions are currently in place for this tartan, its status as an officially registered design ensures that it remains true to its roots, continuing to be cherished by those with Scottish ancestry and connection to the Ainslie clan.

name: Aitken [default]
description: The Aitken tartan is a fascinating example of a non-registered clan tartan, its origins shrouded in mystery despite being worn with pride by its owner, Peter Aitken. Discovered on a vintage blanket purchased in New Zealand, this intriguing design tells the story of a family's unique heritage. The registration notes reveal that the blanket was originally part of a modern textile, suggesting that the Aitken tartan may have been adopted as a way to connect with Scottish roots. While not officially recognized by the Tartans Authority or other governing bodies, the Aitken tartan remains an important part of its owner's personal history and cultural favour, serving as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich textile heritage and the enduring power of tradition.

name: Aiton [default]
description: The Aiton/Ayton tartan is a storied Scottish heritage fabric, steeped in tradition and history. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds significant cultural importance, passed down through generations of the Ayton family. Woven with precision and care, this intricate pattern tells the story of a noble lineage and the lands they once called home. Designed by Ayrton S ?, this tartan has been officially registered, ensuring its authenticity and integrity for future generations to cherish. Originally woven in the occupational therapy department of Bellsdyke Hospital, it highlights the tartan's versatility and adaptability beyond traditional clan associations. The Ayton/Aiton tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich tapestry of heritage and tradition, weaving together history, culture, and identity in its every thread.

name: Akins [default]
description: The Akins Red Dress is a rich and vibrant Name tartan, steeped in family heritage and tradition. Its distinctive hues, carefully chosen by Steven L Akins, are inspired by the colours of his coat of arms, imbuing the fabric with a deep sense of identity and history. This tartan's significance lies not only in its beauty, but also in its connection to one's clan ancestry, making it a treasured possession for those who wear it as a badge of honour. As a Name tartan, it is reserved exclusively for members of the Akins family, adding an extra layer of exclusivity and intimacy to this already meaningful design.

name: Alexander (TL) personal
description: The Alexander tartan, registered under Peter MacDonald's skilled hands, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's clans and families. As a Name tartan, it was specifically designed for Mr TL Alexander's personal use, imbuing the pattern with an intimate connection to his heritage. This distinctive design weaves together the rich threads of Scottish tradition, evoking the warmth and camaraderie of the highlands. Though reserved for private use due to restrictions, the Alexander tartan remains a cherished symbol of Scottish identity, waiting to be worn with pride by those who hold it dear. Its preservation in the Dalgety Collection serves as a poignant reminder of the importance of preserving Scotland's cultural heritage, and its subtle beauty will forever be tied to the life and legacy of Mr TL Alexander.

name: Alexander Hunting
description: The Alexander Hunting tartan is a storied clan tartan, woven with precision by Peter MacDonald to pay tribute to its esteemed namesake, Mr TL Alexander. This family tartan holds deep significance within the Clan MacDonald heritage, denoting loyalty and kinship among those who bear it. Originally designed for personal use, this tartan now resides in the annals of Scottish tradition, a testament to the enduring legacy of the MacDonald clan. Though restricted to its original owner, this tartan remains an important part of Scotland's rich cultural fabric, reflecting the values of family, honour, and loyalty that have defined the Clan MacDonald for centuries.

name:
Alexander of Menstry [default]
[AKA] Alexander of Menstry
description: The Alexander of Menstry tartan is a deeply personal and meaningful design, crafted by Raydon Eiland Alexander with the intention of honouring his ancestors from Menstrie, a village at the foot of the Ochil Hills in Clackmannanshire. The distinctive purple and green block colours evoke the heather and grass of Scotland's rolling hills, while the white lines on blue are reminiscent of the Scottish Saltire flag when rotated through 45 degrees, paying homage to the country's rich heritage. This Clan tartan is a tribute to the ten Alexanders who emigrated from Menstrie in 1669, settling in Virginia and leaving behind a lasting legacy in the American South. By wearing this tartan, its wearers are connected to their ancestral roots and to the proud tradition of Alexander families around the world.

name:
Alexander of Menstry Dress
[AKA] Alexander of Menstry; Dress
description: The Alexander of Menstrie Dress is a poignant tribute to the heritage of Scotland's clans, particularly those with the storied name of Menstrie. Designed by Raydon Eiland in 2002, this family tartan pays homage to the ancestors who left their mark on history - specifically, the nine siblings and their father who emigrated from Menstrie (at the foot of the Ochil Hills) to Virginia in 1669. The subtle nod to Nova Scotia's flag and arms is a testament to the enduring legacy of Alexander, Earl of Stirling, whose pioneering spirit continues to inspire this tartan. With its unique blend of purple and green hues evoking the heather and grass of the Ochils, this fabric weaves together generations of tradition, history, and familial pride. By wearing this tartan, one not only bears the name of a distinguished clan but also connects with the rich tapestry of Scotland's cultural heritage.

name:
Alexander of Menstry Hunting
[AKA] Alexander of Menstry; Hunting
description: The Alexander of Menstrie Hunting tartan is a rich and evocative tribute to the storied heritage of Scotland's noble clans. Registered in 2002 by its talented designer, Raydon Eiland Alexander of San Antonio, Texas, this hunting tartan draws inspiration from the Ochil Hills in Clackmannanshire, where the Menstrie family originated. The design cleverly incorporates traditional elements, with purple and green blocks representing the heather and grass of the local landscape, while white lines on blue form a subtle yet striking echo of the Scottish Saltire flag. This tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Alexander descendants from this prominent clan, who emigrated to Virginia in 1669 and left an indelible mark on American history. As a symbol of family pride and cultural connection, the Alexander of Menstrie Hunting tartan is a treasured heirloom for those bearing the name, and a celebration of Scotland's timeless traditions.

name: Algarve [default]
description: The Algarve tartan is a unique and captivating pattern steeped in rich cultural heritage, originating from Portugal's picturesque southern coast. This intriguing design, categorised as 'Other', bears testament to the country's distinctive textile traditions, albeit influenced by the meticulous research of Johnston/Smith in their seminal work 'Tartans'. Specifically, the threadcount was inspired by traditional Portugese woman's head coverings, a nod to the region's rich folkloric legacy. The Algarve tartan is not associated with any specific clan or family heritage, but rather stands as a celebration of its unique cultural roots, evoking the warmth and beauty of Portugal's sun-kissed landscapes. Its registration notes serve as a poignant reminder of the importance of preserving traditional textiles and respecting their origins, while its design invites wearers to embody the essence of Portuguese tradition with elegance and pride.

name: All Ireland Red
description: All Ireland Red is a stunning District tartan, carefully crafted by renowned weavers at Lochcarron of Scotland in 1997. This richly coloured tartan pays tribute to the historic connections between Scotland and Ireland, reflecting the shared heritage that has woven these nations together for centuries. With its deep reds and subtle earth tones, All Ireland Red evokes the warmth and vitality of a bygone era, when both Scots and Irish people forged strong bonds through trade, culture, and community. This beautifully balanced design is a testament to the enduring spirit of Celtic unity, inviting wearers to claim their place in a proud tradition that spans the Emerald Isle and the Highlands.

name: Allan [default]
description: The Allen tartan, registered in 1996, is a stunning representation of Scottish heritage and tradition, specifically tied to the esteemed surname of Harry Cecil Allen, born in Edinburgh on July 17, 1912. This Name tartan was meticulously designed by Deborah DeWolf Allen, daughter-in-law to the original Harry Cecil, who generously bestowed her creation upon those wishing to bear the family name. With its rich, muted colours and precise threading, the Allen tartan embodies a sense of Scottish pride and heritage, evoking the storied past of this iconic clan name. While specific restrictions apply, this tartan remains an honourable choice for those seeking to connect with their Scottish roots, making it a cherished addition to any family's tartan legacy.

name: Allanton Dress
description: The Allanton Dress Tartan is a timeless fashion favourite, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's textile tradition. This stunning tartan was carefully crafted by D MacArthur of Darvel, Ayrshire, to evoke the elegance and sophistication of the 18th-century Highland dress. As a Fashion tartan, it has been specifically designed for wearability and style, making it an ideal choice for anyone seeking to add a touch of Scottish flair to their wardrobe. With its unique colour palette and intricate sett pattern, this tartan is a testament to the skill and craftsmanship of Scotland's textile artists, who have been weaving beautiful patterns like Allanton Dress for centuries.

name: Allanton
description: The Allanton tartan is a captivating fashion design that embodies the elegance and sophistication of Scottish heritage. Registered as a fashion tartan, it showcases the artistry of D MacArthur, who brought this unique pattern to life at Darvel. According to the registration notes, Allanton was carefully crafted with precision and attention to detail, reflecting the rich cultural traditions of Scotland's textiles. This beautiful tartan is now available for designers and enthusiasts alike to incorporate into their creations, allowing the wearer to embody a touch of Scottish flair and style. As a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's tartans, the Allanton design is poised to make a lasting impression on the fashion world, its beauty and craftsmanship inspiring a new generation of fans.

name: Allan 1998 (Personal)
description: The Allen tartan, designed by Keith Lumsden in 1998, is a storied Name tartan born from a desire to represent those bearing the surname Allen, as well as their variants. This richly woven fabric reflects the heritage of Christopher Allen Holler, an individual from Winter Park, Florida, whose name inspired the creation of this distinctive tartan. With its complex interplay of blues and greens, evoking the rolling hills and glacial waters of Scotland's Highlands, the Allen tartan embodies a connection to Scottish tradition that transcends geographical boundaries. As a Name tartan, it is reserved for those who bear the surname Allen or its variations, serving as a tangible thread between past and present, culture and identity.

name: Allan Hunting (Personal)
description: The enigmatic Allen Hunting tartan, shrouded in mystery and Scottish heritage, weaves a tale of ancestral roots and cultural exchange. Discovered through a threadcount taken from a plaid belonging to Bonita L Allan's Currie grandmother, this Ayrshire-inspired variation is believed to be an authentic local rendition of the Thomson tartan. Passed down through generations, it was later adopted by Christopher Allen Holler from Florida as his own distinctive Allen Hunting design. This intricate pattern holds within it the whispers of Scottish tradition and family legacy, its significance tied to the curative ties that bind heritage to identity.

name: Allan Joy's Fancy (Personal)
description: Joy's Fancy is a vibrant and intricate name tartan, steeped in Scottish tradition and heritage. Registered to Dr Philip D Smith Jnr, this unique design was woven with great care by Rob Robb, and worn with honour by Allen Joy in 1996. As a personal tartan, it holds a special place within the family's history, evoking memories of joyous occasions and cherished moments. A testament to the artisanal skills of its creator, Joy's Fancy is a beautiful example of the traditional weaving techniques that have been passed down through generations of Scottish weavers. This distinctive tartan is now a treasured part of Allen Joy's legacy, proudly carrying his family name with distinction and a sense of proud tradition.

name: Allen of Northumbria
description: The Allen - Northumbrian tartan is a quintessential representation of Scottish heritage, born from the hands of renowned designer Jeremy M P Allen. This highly personal and exclusive tartan was created to commemorate the family ties of its original owner, Jerry M P Allen, who carefully crafted it for his immediate family and relations. Originally registered as a Name tartan, this distinctive pattern is steeped in tradition and history, drawing inspiration from the rich cultural landscape of Northumbria. While its beauty and significance are undeniable, this tartan comes with a rare and honour-bound stipulation: permission must be sought from Jeremy M P Allen himself for others to wear it, underscoring the importance of family legacy and heritage.

name: Allison [default]
description: The Allison (MacGregor-Hastie) tartan is a timeless example of Scotland's rich textile heritage, woven from a deep connection to the country's clans and family histories. This traditional Name tartan is named after the MacGregor-Hastie clan, whose roots stretch back through generations of proud Highlanders. The subtle yet distinct sett, recorded in 'Clans Originaux' (1880), was carefully extracted from an original cloth sample held by the Scottish Tartans Society, providing a tangible link to the past. With its unique colour palette and intricate thread pattern, this tartan is not only a testament to the ingenuity of Scotland's weavers but also a celebration of the enduring legacy of the MacGregor-Hastie family, whose history has been forever intertwined with that of the Scottish Highlands.

name: Allt Dubh
description: Allt Dubh (Black Burn), a majestic fashion tartan inspired by the mysterious depths of Scotland's Highland streams, embodies the rugged beauty of the country's wild heartland. Designed by D Tulloch, a renowned textile expert from Thomas Gordon & Sons, this distinctive pattern is meant to evoke the dramatic atmosphere of a dark burn, veiled in heather and shrouded in mist. The restrictions on its use are a testament to the importance of preserving traditional Scottish heritage, as this tartan holds a special place within the cultural fabric of Scotland's clans and communities. As an iconic fashion design, Allt Dubh is poised to captivate those drawn to the timeless allure of the Highlands, while also respecting the intricate web of history and tradition that underpins it.

name: American Society of Travel Agents
description: The American Society of Travel Agents, The tartan is a unique corporate design that weaves together threads of heritage and tradition to reflect the esteemed history of its namesake organisation. Created by renowned Scottish textile experts at Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the Davidson sett, a traditional Scottish pattern dating back centuries. The design's roots lie in the 1930s, when the American Society of Travel Agents (ASTA) first came into being, with its inaugural Chairman, Mr E Irvine Davis, setting the tone for the organisation's values and principles. As a registered corporate tartan, it is now reserved exclusively for use by ASTA members and affiliated entities, serving as a symbol of pride and connection to this important chapter in American travel history.

name: AMEX American Express
description: The American Express tartan is an iconic corporate design that pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage, bearing the mark of the storied MacWilliam Clan. Originally based on their traditional tartan, this distinctive pattern has been adapted by Kinloch Anderson Ltd for incorporation into the prestigious American Express brand identity. Established in 1903 and acquired by WA Williamson Ltd in 1920, the company's Glasgow roots are woven seamlessly into this corporate tartan, symbolising a legacy of tradition and heritage that continues to influence modern business and design. As a testament to Scotland's enduring cultural significance, the American Express tartan serves as a powerful emblem of innovation, excellence, and global reach.

name: Amnesty International
description: The Amnesty tartan, designed by esteemed Scottish textile artist Scarlett MBE, Jamie, is a poignant tribute to the iconic human rights organisation's 40th anniversary celebration. As a commemorative tartan, it serves as a testament to Amnesty International's unwavering commitment to protecting and promoting human dignity across cultures and borders. The carefully selected colours reflect the organisation's dedication to bridging the divides of nationality, creed, and colour, evoking the rich tapestry of diversity that defines our global community. By wearing this tartan, individuals honour the courageous work of Amnesty International, paying tribute to its unshakeable principles of justice and compassion. As a badge of solidarity with this noble cause, the Amnesty tartan is a powerful symbol of unity in the pursuit of human rights and freedoms.

name: Ancient Atlantic
description: The Ancient Atlantic tartan, with its rich and earthy tones, embodies the timeless spirit of Scotland's rugged coastlines. Designed by Sol Gillis in 1964, this Fashion tartan has become a staple in the world of textiles, evoking the mystery and grandeur of the Atlantic Ocean that borders Scotland's shores. With its subtle colour palette, this tartan is said to have been inspired by Miss K Sinclair's original design from February 1968, although Gillis himself claimed creation in 1964. An intriguing variation with only four colours threads can be seen, raising questions about its origins. Regardless, the Ancient Atlantic tartan remains a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and tradition of textile craftsmanship, perfectly capturing the essence of the country's majestic coastline.

name: Anderson Arisaid #2
description: The Anderson Dress tartan is a storied and esteemed clan tartan, steeped in tradition and heritage. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Society, this tartan holds profound significance for the members of Clan MacKenzie, who are entitled to wear it as their family tartan. The distinctive pattern, characterized by its bold and vibrant colours, was originally designated for formal dress and is still worn today at clan gatherings and Highland events, serving as a symbol of honour and identity. Its legacy not only reflects the rich history and culture of Clan MacKenzie but also continues to celebrate the enduring traditions of Scottish heritage.

name: Anderson Blue
description: Anderson Blue, a fashion-inspired tartan designed by renowned mill West Coast Woolen Mill in Vancouver, pays homage to the storied heritage of Clan Anderson. This muted blue variation on the classic tartan takes its cue from traditional Scottish weaving, evoking the rugged beauty of the North Atlantic coast where the clan was originally hailing. As a fashion tartan, Anderson Blue offers a sophisticated and understated alternative for those seeking a subtle nod to Scotland's rich cultural legacy. With its restrained colour palette, this tartan is suited to a range of formal and informal occasions, from high-end dressing gowns to tailored kilts and accessories.

name: Anderson Blue Westwood
description: The Anderson Blue, a fashion tartan reimagined by the iconic Vivienne Westwood in 1993, embodies the intersection of tradition and innovation. Originally part of the Anderson family's heritage, this blue and white tartan was traditionally worn by members of Clan Campbell and later adopted as a distinctive colour scheme for the House of Campbell. Westwood's bold design modification injects new life into this storied pattern, infusing it with her signature eclectic flair. This Fashion category tartan is not tied to any specific clan or heritage group, instead becoming a statement piece in its own right, celebrating individuality and self-expression through the timeless language of tartan.

name: Anderson Green
description: The Anderson Green tartan is a vibrant and stylish fashion tartan, designed by renowned Scottish textile experts at the West Coast Woolen Mill in Vancouver, Canada. This particular variation of the iconic Anderson tartan has been adapted to incorporate a fresh, modern twist, resulting in a stunning green version that embodies the spirit of the traditional clan tartan while evoking a sense of contemporary flair. Registration notes confirm its status as an official fashion tartan, available for use by designers and enthusiasts alike. With its unique blend of heritage and innovation, the Anderson Green tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage and the enduring appeal of traditional tartan design in modern times, perfect for adding a touch of subtle Scottish sophistication to any fashion ensemble.

name:
Anderson of Ardbrake [default]
[AKA] Anderson of Ardbrake
description: The Anderson of Ardbrake tartan is a vibrant representation of Scottish heritage, born from the desire to create a distinctive family identity for those bearing the name Anderson. Designed by David A R Waterton-Anderson in response to member requests, this tartan proudly showcases a bold red background, reminiscent of the rich soil and rugged landscape of Scotland's north-east. The classic motif of broad white and two yellow (tramline) stripes on black provides a strong visual anchor, paying homage to the traditional associations of the Anderson name with the powerful Clan Gordon and other prominent families of the region. With its evocative colour palette and carefully considered design, the Anderson of Ardbrake tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish clans and their rich history, proudly worn by those who bear this noble surname.

name:
Anderson of Kinneddar Hunting
[AKA] Anderson of Kinneddar; Hunting
description: The Anderson of Kinneddar Hunting tartan is a revered clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, born from the skilled hands of David Waterton-Anderson in 1978. This majestic design, chosen by the renowned family, tells the story of their storied history and tradition of hunting prowess. With its intricate, closely-woven threads, this tartan embodies the proud heritage of Anderson, a name synonymous with bravery and nobility. As one of the many clan tartans registered with the Scottish Tartans Society, it is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish clansmen who wore these distinctive patterns on their kilts, sashes, and other traditional garments. Through its rich colours and technical precision, this tartan design proudly represents the Anderson family's honourable tradition, forever woven into the fabric of Scotland's storied past.

name:
Anderson of Kinneddar Red
[AKA] Anderson of Kinneddar; Red
description: The Anderson of Kinnedear Red tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Clan Anderson, one of Scotland's most storied clans. Designed by renowned tartan expert Peter MacDonald in 1993 at the behest of the Anderson Commander, Hope-Vere Anderson, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the clan's proud history and legacy. With its bold, crimson-red hues and intricate weave, this tartan embodies the spirit of Scotland's greatest families, evoking images of rugged Highlands landscapes, ancestral castles, and centuries-old traditions. As a registered Clan tartan, the Anderson of Kinnedear Red is an honour to wear, symbolising the wearer's connection to their Scottish roots and their place within the proud lineage of Clan Anderson.

name: Anderson Old
description: The Anderson Old (Makinlay) tartan is a storied and storied clan tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of the Makinlay family. Its origins date back to the early 20th century, when James Makinlay painstakingly compiled a collection of hand-coloured tartan strips between 1930 and 1950. This labour of love is now preserved in the Scottish Tartans Society archive, serving as a poignant reminder of the craftsmanship and tradition that defines Scotland's iconic woven textiles. As a family tartan, the Anderson Old (Makinlay) holds great significance for those who claim descent from this illustrious clan, and its intricate pattern is a testament to the enduring legacy of James Makinlay's meticulous work.

name: Anderson Red
description: The Anderson Red (Westwood) tartan is a vibrant, fashion-forward interpretation of Scotland's iconic heritage fabric, crafted by the renowned Vivienne Westwood. As a registered fashion tartan, its purpose is to evoke the spirit of Scottish culture and tradition, while also pushing the boundaries of modern style. Originally modified from the traditional Anderson tartan, this bold red variation has been meticulously recreated with precision, showcasing the meticulous attention to detail that defines the art of tartan design. Recognised by the Scottish Tartans Authority, its threadcount represents a tangible connection to Scotland's rich textile history. By embracing the iconic colours and motifs of the Anderson family's heritage fabric, Westwood's Anderson Red tartan pays homage to Scotland's storied past while forging a bold new path for fashion enthusiasts and tartan enthusiasts alike.

name: Anderson Ross
description: The Ross Anderson tartan, registered for fashion purposes by renowned Scottish mill Botany Woolen Mills, tells the story of a complex heritage that has been shrouded in controversy. Named after two influential families - the esteemed Clan Ross and the distinguished Anderson clan - this tartan was originally conceived as a variation of the more well-known Anderson Grey, with Pendleton Woolens mistakenly dubbing it 'Ross-Anderson'. In reality, Botany Woolen Mills seems to have been inspired by the iconic Ross necktie they sold in California from 1935 to 1950. This tartan's intricate history is a testament to the fluidity of Scottish textile traditions and the sometimes blurry lines between cultural identity and commercial influence.

name: Anderson [default]
description: The Anderson tartan is an intricate and distinctive pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, its origins shrouded in mystery despite being recognised by several Highland Clans, including Clan Ross and Clan Donald. Dating back to the early 20th century, this complex weave showcases a fusion of traditional techniques with the influence of 'fancy' designs that emerged in the pre-1822 era, reflecting the burgeoning popularity of tartan wear among Scottish clansmen. According to historian James D Scarlett, its evolution was likely driven by the increasing demand for stylish and symbolic patterns, which ultimately led to the Anderson tartan being adopted as a clan tartan, its variations passed down through generations as a badge of family honour.

name: Anglicare
description: Anglicare tartan embodies the unwavering spirit of compassion and community service embodied by Australia's largest charity. Designed by Betty Johnston, this distinctive corporate tartan is a testament to the Anglican Church in Australia's rich heritage, dating back to the early days of European settlement when congregations provided care to widows and orphans. With its bold red cross at its centre, subtly woven into a blue background, evoking the traditional colours of the Anglican Church of Australia, this tartan pays tribute to the organisation's enduring commitment to serving those in need. Marton Mills and Ingles Buchan have been approved as permitted weavers, ensuring that only authentic reproductions can be purchased through the Anglicare organisation. As a symbol of hope and unity, Anglicare tartan serves as a powerful reminder of the enduring impact of Christian values on Australian society, its significance woven into every thread of this iconic design.

name: Arbuthnot [default]
description: The Arbuthnott tartan, named after its titular family, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's ancient clans. This distinctive tartan is closely tied to the storied Black Watch regiment, drawing inspiration from the iconic woven patterns of the 42nd Royal Highland Regiment. The unique threadcount recorded here mirrors that found in the Lyon Court Books (LCB15) on a fateful day in October 1962, lending authenticity to its historical significance. As part of the Clan/Family category, the Arbuthnott tartan is an integral part of Scotland's cultural fabric, woven with pride and tradition by generations past, present, and future. Its enduring presence serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of those who have worn it, carrying the honour of their forebears on every thread.

name: Argyle Dress
description: The Argyle Dress tartan, a family heirloom passed down through generations, whispers tales of tradition and heritage. Registration notes reveal its origins as a threadcount sent to Jack Dalgety in 1985 by Stuart Davidson, hinting at an asymmetric pattern, characteristic of the intricate designs often associated with Scottish textiles. This Clan tartan is deeply rooted in the history of Patons of Tillicoultry, one of Scotland's most esteemed weaving houses. Despite its unclear provenance, the Argyle Dress tartan remains a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland, evoking images of Highland clansmen and women who wore these intricate patterns with pride. As a family tartan, it is likely been woven for generations, its threads infused with stories of love, loyalty, and community, awaiting the next family member to proudly wear its colours.

name: Armstrong (Alec) personal; Victoria City
description: The Victoria, City of tartan is a vibrant and evocative tribute to the stunning heritage of British Columbia's capital city. Designed by esteemed brothers Alec and Edith Armstrong, this District tartan weaves together a rich tapestry of colours inspired by the iconic landmarks and architectural treasures of Victoria. The registration notes describe a bold palette that juxtaposes old red bricks with the radiant turquoise glow of oxidised copper domes, punctuated by the deep, rich tones of ox blood red and hunter green. As if woven from the very fabric of the city's storied past, this tartan echoes the warmth and romance of Victorian-era tradition, conjuring images of bustling streets, majestic granite buildings, and a sense of civic pride that is quintessentially British Columbia.

name: Armstrong [default]
description: The Armstrong tartan is a testament to the storied heritage of Scotland's most renowned clan, whose ancestors were said to have earned their land through a heroic feat of strength in battle. Described by Sobieski Stewarts in 1842, this majestic tartan was first documented as part of the Vestiarium Scotorum, and its significance extends far beyond its technical characteristics. As a Clan tartan, it holds dear honour among Armstrong families worldwide, who proudly weave their heritage into every thread. With restrictions in place to ensure only legitimate descendants may wear the design, this tartan remains an integral part of Scottish tradition, its very existence a nod to the bravery and loyalty of Fairbairn, the armour bearers to Scotland's kings.

name: Asselin (Madeleine) personal; Contrecoeur
description: The Contrecoeur tartan, designed by Madeleine Asselin, is a rich tapestry of colours woven from the very fabric of Quebec's history and heritage. As a District tartan, it proudly represents Contrecoeur township in southern Quebec, with each hue carefully chosen to reflect its unique story. Red stands for the bravery of the town's founders, while yellow nods to its esteemed past, as well as its thriving 'holiday centres'. The Saint-Laurent river's gentle blue provides a soothing counterpoint, evoking Antoine-Pecaudt's native land and the township's strategic linkages. White represents the unwavering pride and determination of the people, alongside the majestic pine green that echoes the towering trees and fertile soil that nourish the region. Steel grey adds a modern touch, signifying industrial development, while brown pays homage to the traditional footwear industry born in 1883. This vibrant tartan is not just a colourful tribute to Contrecoeur's rich past, but also a testament to its people's indomitable spirit and connection to the land they call home.

name: Asselin (Madeleine) personal; Contrecoeur Dress
description: The Contrecoeur Dress tartan, designed by Madeleine Asselin, is a poignant tribute to the rich heritage of southern Quebec's smallest township. Asymmetric in its composition, this intricate pattern tells the story of Contrecoeur's history and symbolism. Red evokes the courage of its founders, while yellow nods to the town's esteemed past and its role as a hub for 'holiday centres'. The blue hue represents the Saint-Laurent river, which connects the town to its indigenous roots in France, as well as the proud spirit of its people. Pine green signifies the region's fertile soil, giant pines, and idyllic islands, while steel grey acknowledges the industrial development that has shaped the town's identity. The inclusion of brown tones also pays homage to the traditional footwear industry established in 1883, underscoring the township's enduring connection to its past. This thoughtful design serves as a lasting testament to the community's history and cultural traditions, weaving together a narrative that is both deeply personal and proudly Canadian.

name: Atlanta National Gold Course Club
description: The Bailey Atlanta National tartan is a striking example of modern Scottish heritage, crafted with precision by Marjorie Warren. Registered as a Corporate tartan, this bold design embodies the spirit of the Atlanta National Gold Course Club, whose members are drawn to its strength and sophistication. Characterised by a distinctive grid pattern, the tartan's colours - navy blue, yellow-green, blue-black, and blue-tinged with red - evoke the rolling hills and verdant landscapes of Scotland, while also showcasing a modern twist. With its restricted usage tied to the club, this corporate tartan serves as a symbol of unity and camaraderie among members, their individual ties woven together in a shared identity that proudly wears its Scottish roots.

name: Auburn  University of Alabama
description: The Auburn University tartan, designed by esteemed academic Dr Phil Smith Jnr, embodies the spirit of American Southern hospitality with its rich, autumnal hues. As a corporate tartan, it is meant to evoke the pride and tradition of one of the United States' most prestigious universities, Auburn University in Alabama. The carefully crafted design features a unique threadcount correction, implemented by Dr Smith's note, ensuring an authentic representation of his original intent. Registered as a symbol of university affinity, this tartan now bears the sole agency of Scotpress, reflecting its strong connection to the institution and the region it represents. A testament to the enduring legacy of Auburn University, this tartan design weaves together tradition, academia, and Southern charm, making it an invaluable tribute to the university's storied history.

name: Auchairne Estate Estate
description: The Auchairne tartan, designed by Ian J McDonnell, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's corporate identity, reflecting the timeless spirit of its namesake estate nestled in south Ayrshire. Registered as a corporate tartan, it pays tribute to the area's natural beauty and storied history, evoking the windswept coastlines and rolling hills that have shaped this iconic part of Scotland for centuries. With its distinct pattern of blues, greens, and yellows, Auchairne embodies the warmth and hospitality often associated with Scottish hospitality, while its unique characteristics set it apart as a distinguished addition to the world of corporate tartan design.

name: Auchairne Estate Grey
description: The Auchairne Grey corporate tartan, designed by Ian J. McDonnell, pays homage to the rich heritage of Scotland's west coast, specifically the esteemed estate of Auchairne near Ballantrae in south Ayrshire. This distinctive tartan is a colour modification of its eponymous counterpart, adapted for corporate wear and bearing the 'Corporate' category in recognition of its utilitarian purpose. Registration notes highlight the estate's significance, underscoring the tartan's connection to Scotland's storied past. As a nod to this ancestral home, the Auchairne Grey tartan embodies the timeless essence of Scottish tradition, infused with the subtle nuances of its coastal heritage.

name:
Austin (Wilsons' No.137)
[AKA] Wilson's Collection; No.137
description: The Austin tartan is a storied family heirloom from Scotland's rich heritage, dating back to Wilsons' No.137, a respected weaving firm founded circa 1770 near Stirling. This Clan/Family tartan holds significant cultural importance, passed down through generations of the Austin family, who proudly wore it as a symbol of their Scottish roots. The design is rooted in traditional tartan-making techniques, woven by skilled artisans at Wilsons' Bannockburn workshop. With its unique pattern and colours, the Austin tartan has been carefully preserved, with original Pattern books and correspondence held in the National Museum Scotland, Edinburgh, and a copy deposited in the Scottish Tartans Society archive. As such, this tartan not only represents a family's honour but also serves as a tangible link to Scotland's history, tradition, and craftsmanship.

name:
Keith with Yellow
[AKA] No.173
description: Austin, also known as Wilsons' No.173, is a timeless Clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, its intricate weave reflecting the skill and tradition of Bannockburn's esteemed weaving firm, Wilsons, which was established circa 1770. This richly patterned tartan holds significant historical value, with its original pattern books preserved in the National Museum Scotland, Edinburgh, and a copy of the archive held by the Scottish Tartans Society. As a Clan tartan, Austin is woven to honour the connections between families bearing this name, with the design's subtle nuances telling a story of ancestral roots and loyalty. While specific details about its designer are unknown, the very existence of this tartan speaks to the enduring legacy of Scotland's weaving traditions, where craftsmanship and heritage blend seamlessly together.

name: Keith [default]
description: The Austin tartan, a storied family heirloom woven with precision and passion, is steeped in history and tradition. Recorded by David W Stewart in his seminal work 'Old and Rare Scottish Tartans' (1893), this set was previously documented in the 18th-century letters of Wilsons of Bannockburn. As part of a collection of forty-five unique tartans woven in silk, Austin is a testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage. With its distinctive design, carefully crafted to represent a family or clan, it embodies the values of unity and belonging that have defined Scottish identity for centuries. This iconic tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's complex and fascinating history, inviting wearers to connect with their ancestral roots and celebrate the enduring spirit of the nation.

name: Ayrshire Tourist Board
description: The Ayrshire Tourist Board tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate tartan that embodies the warmth and hospitality of Scotland's west coast. Registered in 1999 by renowned designer David McGill, International Tartans, this distinctive pattern celebrates the region's rich heritage and natural beauty. With its striking combination of blues, greens, and yellows, reminiscent of the rolling hills, sparkling lochs, and rugged coastline of Ayrshire, this tartan is the perfect representation of the region's proud identity. As a corporate registration, this tartan is now available for use by businesses and organisations looking to connect with the people and place of Scotland, making it an ideal choice for companies looking to add a touch of regional flair to their branding and marketing efforts.

name: Bagpipe Shop (Switzerland)
description: This distinctive Corporate tartan, designed by Nicole Irman, has been woven with precision to represent the esteemed Bagpipe Shop in Switzerland. Officially registered for use exclusively by House of Edgar, a trusted division of Macnaughton Holdings in Perth, this tartan is destined to adorn the online presence and corporate materials of Das Fachgeschaft fur Dudelsacke. By virtue of its unique design and careful restriction, this tartan serves as an emblem of the Bagpipe Shop's Swiss heritage and artisanal traditions, paying homage to the rich cultural legacy of Scotland's beloved instrument, the bagpipe. With its specific weaving requirements in place, this Corporate tartan is poised to become an integral part of the shop's brand identity, effortlessly conveying a sense of authenticity and connection to the country that first gave birth to the timeless sound of the piped bagpipes.

name: Baillie (Highland Society of London)
description: The Baillie tartan, borne by families in the Highlands, holds a rich history within its intricate sett. Dating back to the late 18th century, when the Highland Society of London began collecting tartans, this design was likely worn by several clans and families before clan and family names became associated with specific patterns. Notably, William Wilson of Bannockburn, a renowned weaver, produced a distinct set for Baillie, differing from his own signature Logan's Forbes tartan. The inclusion of purple threads in this sample suggests that the design was woven by Wilson around 1770, at his firm near Stirling. As one of the earliest recorded tartans, the Baillie represents a fascinating intersection of tradition and cultural heritage, embodying the evolving identity of Scottish families over time.

name:
Baillie Dress
[AKA] Baillie Turnberry
[AKA] Baillie Snaefell
description: The Baillie Dress tartan is a rich and storied textile heritage, born from the ancestral threads of the Baillie family and their Isle of Man roots. Originally designed by Robert Wood as Snaefell in 1979, this subtle sett was later reimagined by D MacArthur & Co as the Turnberry fashion check before being rediscovered and reinterpreted by D C Dalgliesh of Selkirk. With its nuanced blend of blues and greens evoking the rolling hills and rugged mountains of Scotland's west coast, this tartan whispers stories of a storied past. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds deep significance for those who wear it, signifying a connection to their family's history and heritage. Though its origins may be complex, the Baillie Dress tartan is a testament to the enduring power of tradition and the art of Scottish weaving.

name:
Baillie of Polkemmet [default]
[AKA] Baillie of Polkemmet
description: The Baillie of Polkemmet tartan is a storied and storied family heirloom, woven with deep roots in Scottish heritage. Registered by Geddes, A W, in 1937, this Clan tartan was specifically designed for the esteemed Baillies of Polkemmet, who proudly owned the historic Barony of Polkemmet. By adapting the classic MacKenzie tartan, Geddes subtly distinguished this family's legacy with an elegant twist: three slender white lines woven into the green, adding a touch of refinement and distinction to the traditional design. A testament to the rich history and tradition of Scottish clan life, this tartan embodies the intricate web of relationships and affiliations that bind families together across generations, its subtle variations a poignant reminder of the ever-changing yet enduring nature of identity and heritage.

name:
Baillie of Polkemmet Red
[AKA] Baillie of Polkemmet; Red
description: The Baillie of Polkemmet Red tartan is a timeless testament to Scotland's rich heritage, bearing witness to the traditions of the esteemed Baillie family. Registered in 1937 by renowned Scottish designer A W Geddes, this distinctive tartan was gifted to Margaret O MacDougall of Inverness Museum by her relative J MacKinlay. Characterised by its striking red hues, the Baillie of Polkemmet Red tartan evokes the warmth and hospitality that has long been synonymous with Scotland's clan culture. As a Clan tartan, it is an honour to wear and display this design, symbolising loyalty, family pride, and a deep connection to the land and its storied history, while Geddes' skilled weaving ensures a lasting tribute to Scotland's rich textiles heritage.

name:
Baillie [default]
[AKA] Baillie Fencibles
description: The Baillie (Fencibles) tartan is a storied military heritage, steeped in the proud traditions of Scotland's finest fighting men. Registered to Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1819, this distinctive design was specifically crafted for the Baillie Fencibles, a regiment raised by Colonel John Baillie of Dunain in 1794 as part of the Inverness-shire Regiment. A testament to its historical significance, the tartan draws inspiration from the revered Black Watch, one of Scotland's oldest and most revered military regiments. Its unique characteristics pay homage to the bravery and camaraderie of the Baillie Fencibles, who played a pivotal role in shaping Scotland's military history. This tartan is not only a celebration of Scottish heritage but also a poignant reminder of the country's rich military traditions, passed down through generations of proud Scotsmen.

name: Bain (Robert) personal
description: The Bains of Caithness tartan is a richly woven tribute to the heritage of Robert Bain, a stalwart figure from Lybster in the far north of Scotland's rugged Caithness peninsula. Designed by local weaver Trudi Mann, this clan tartan was specifically created for the Bain family to reflect their ancestral roots and connection to this distinctive region. With its distinctive colour palette and intricate pattern, the Bains of Caithness tartan serves as a poignant emblem of community and kinship, binding together generations of Bains across the ages. Originally designated as a family tartan to encompass all variations of the Bain surname, this beautiful design stands as a testament to the enduring spirit of the Cairngorms' most northerly clan, its threads woven from the very fabric of Scotland's storied past.

name: Baird Dress
description: The Baird Dress, a timeless and storied tartan, holds a revered place within Scottish heritage. Originally an uncertain variant of either a dance or dress tartan for the Baird clan, its legitimacy was later confirmed as a legitimate dress tartan, ensuring its continued use by descendants of this esteemed family. This intricate weave, characteristic of traditional Scottish design, features a rich palette of blues and reds, evoking the rugged beauty of the Highland landscape. Woven with precision and care, the Baird Dress tartan has been passed down through generations, serving as a symbol of ancestral honour and identity. Its very existence is a testament to the enduring legacy of this noble clan, whose name has become synonymous with courage and distinction in Scottish history.

name:
Baird [default]
[AKA] Baird Hunting
description: The Baird Modern tartan is a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich clan heritage, with its intricate triple stripes evoking the storied history of the Baird family. First recorded in 1906 by notable Scottish authority, John Johnston, this tartan was originally woven in bold red hues, a testament to the family's Aberdeenshire estates and their later acquisition by the prominent Gordon clan. Today, the classic design is typically rendered in rich purple, a subtle nod to the passage of time. This Clan tartan, now available for those honouring their Baird heritage or simply drawn to its timeless beauty, holds within it the very fabric of Scotland's traditions - a testament to the enduring legacy of the ancient Highlands and the family ties that bind them together.

name: Baker [default]
description: The Baker tartan is a stylish and modern fashion design born from the renowned West Coast Woolen Mill, which brought this distinctive sett to life in collaboration with Fraser & Kirkbright. Originally created for Aljean, this tartan was rediscovered by the mill in 2002 and subsequently re-released under their esteemed brand. Characterised by its bright blue and red stripes on a predominantly white background, the Baker tartan embodies the quintessential essence of Scottish fashion, marrying traditional techniques with contemporary flair. Its inclusion within the Fashion category speaks to its suitability for cutting-edge attire, while the absence of any restrictions ensures its widespread adoption across various styles and occasions. As a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish textiles, the Baker tartan is a vibrant celebration of tradition and style, ready to add a touch of rugged sophistication to any ensemble.

name: Balfour Hunting
description: Balfour Hunting is a storied Name tartan, crafted by renowned designer Peter MacDonald. Hailing from a proud Scottish heritage, this timeless design weaves together a rich tapestry of tradition and history, paying homage to the esteemed House of Balfour. Characterised by its distinctive blend of earthy tones, including the vibrant green that replaces traditional grey, this tartan evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's rural landscapes and the skillful pursuit of hunting. As a registered Name tartan, it is reserved for wear by those who bear the Balfour surname, or by those who have been granted permission to wear it in honour of their connection to the family. With its unique threadcount taken from a D C Dalgliesh swatch, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textiles and the tradition of excellence that defines the world of tartans.

name: Balfour [default]
description: The Balfour #2 tartan, crafted with precision by Peter MacDonald, is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and enduring traditions. This Name tartan, born from the suggestion of esteemed patron Balfour Rombach, pays homage to the storied Gordon clan through its carefully woven design. Based on the Abergeldie tartan, this variant boasts a striking fusion of blue and brown hues that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's rolling hills and ancient castles. As recorded by the Scottish Tartans World Register, 'Balfour Blue & Brown' is an official recognition of this tartan's significance, solidifying its place in the fabric of Scottish identity and tradition. This carefully crafted design serves as a lasting tribute to the storied history and cultural legacy of the Gordon clan, forever etched in the tartan landscape of Scotland.

name: Ball Hunting
description: The Ball Hunting tartan is a distinctive Name tartan, woven with precision to reflect its origins in Scottish heritage. Designed by Bruce L Ball, this Hunting variation showcases the unique characteristics of the Ball family, with proportions derived from the ancient Fibannaci mathematical sequence. This intricate pattern weaves together a rich history of clan identity and tradition, echoing the timeless values of Scottish hunting culture. As specified in the registration notes, this tartan is open to anyone bearing the surname Ball, making it a cherished symbol of family heritage and unity.

name: Balmoral Estate; Green Lines; Royal
description: The Balmoral Green, a Royal tartan of unparalleled majesty, is steeped in tradition and heritage. Originating from the esteemed James Cantâs manuscript book, this iconic design has been woven with precision since 1951 by renowned mill James Ives & Co Ltd of Yeadon (Leeds). Initially crafted for car rugs for King George VI, its association with royalty has led to a storied history within the British monarchy. Due to its prestigious connections, the Balmoral Green is subject to strict restrictions, limiting it to use only by members of the Royal Family. This tartan's enduring allure lies in its subtle yet striking nuances, reflecting the essence of Scotland's rich cultural heritage and the timeless elegance of the British monarchy. As a testament to tradition and exclusivity, the Balmoral Green stands as an iconic representation of Scottish heritage, forever woven into the fabric of history.

name: Balmoral Estate; Lavender
description: The Balmoral (Lavender) tartan is a subtle yet majestic creation, woven with a sense of reverence for Scotland's rich heritage. Designed by D W Stewart, an esteemed figure in the world of traditional Scottish weaving, this tartan holds a special place in the annals of history - albeit not entirely accurate to its original form, as it was inadvertently included in Stewart's 1893 publication, Old & Rare Scottish Tartans. Despite its questionable provenance, the Balmoral (Lavender) tartan is steeped in tradition and represents the enduring spirit of the British monarchy, which has long associated itself with this picturesque Scottish estate. By convention, however, this tartan is not woven for commercial purposes, setting it apart as a rare and precious find, reserved for those who appreciate its historical significance and cultural importance.

name: Balmoral Hotel
description: The Balmoral Hotel tartan is an iconic corporate tartan born from a momentous occasion: the grand reopening of the esteemed hotel in Edinburgh, designed by renowned textile experts at Kinloch Anderson Ltd. In 1902, this stately tartan was specifically created for the Balmoral Hotel's inaugural event, where it has since become synonymous with luxury and sophistication. As an official corporate tartan, its distinctive design holds a special place within Scottish heritage, bearing testament to the rich tradition of tartan weaving that dates back centuries. Notably, this tartan is subject to restrictions, reserved exclusively for the hotel's corporate use, underscoring its significance as a bespoke emblem of prestige and refinement.

name: Barbour Countrywear
description: The Barbour tartan is an enduring symbol of Scottish heritage and tradition, steeped in history dating back to 13th century Ayrshire. Designed for corporate use by J Barbour Ltd, this stalwart tartan has been carefully crafted to reflect the iconic brand's rich legacy. Drawing inspiration from the traditional Ayrshire District sett, Kinloch Anderson Ltd have masterfully woven together a classic colour palette of brown and navy, complemented by crisp white, gold, and red overchecks that evoke the timeless elegance of Barbour's renowned wax jackets. As an important part of Scotland's cultural fabric, this tartan pays tribute to generations of Barbour patrons, while also proudly representing the J Barbour Ltd brand, its values, and its enduring commitment to quality craftsmanship.

name: Barclay Dress
description: The Barclay Dress tartan, a quintessential Clan tartan, holds profound significance within Scottish heritage, particularly in relation to the noble Barclay family. Dating back to the mid-19th century, this traditional sett is rooted in earlier hunting patterns showcased in the Vestiarium Scoticum of 1842, and has since become synonymous with the esteemed name. Crafted from threads counted meticulously by W & A K Johnston in 'The Tartans of the Clans and Septs of Scotland', this tartan embodies the timeless spirit of Scottish tradition, evoking images of rugged Highlands landscapes and generations of family history. Its status as a Clan tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Barclay name, whose roots stretch back through centuries of Scottish nobility, weaving an unbroken thread between past and present.

name: Barclay Hunting
description: The Barclay tartan is a storied and storied Scottish heritage, woven into existence by the esteemed Sobieski Stewarts in 1842. This Clan tartan has been an honourable part of the family's tradition for generations, originating from their own 'Vestiarium Scoticum' records. The intricate design features a rich colour palette that reflects its origins as a family legacy, with deep blues and greens evoking the rugged yet resilient spirit of the Scottish landscape. Featured in J Claude's seminal pattern book, 'Clans Originaux', this tartan holds significance not only for the Barclay clan but also as an important thread in Scotland's cultural tapestry, symbolising unity, pride, and family heritage.

name: Barkwell (Oilmen) personal
description: The Barkwell tartan is a unique and storied Scottish heritage textile, born from the passion of its creator, Don Barkwell. Originally designed as "Oilmens" for the 33rd Oilmens' Golf Tournament, this tartan took on new significance when the designer requested a rebranding to reflect his personal identity. The resulting tartan is a testament to the power of tradition and individuality, its distinctive patterns and colours woven from the threads of Scottish history and culture. As a Name tartan, the Barkwell design is reserved for those who bear the name in an honourable and traditional manner, making it a cherished symbol of family heritage and identity. With its rich history and exclusive registration, the Barkwell tartan remains a highly sought-after addition to any collection of Scottish textiles, connecting its wearers to the enduring traditions of Scotland's weavers and their timeless legacy.

name: Bartlett [default]
description: The Bartlett from Winnetka tartan is a distinctive Name tartan that tells the story of an American family with Scottish roots. Designed by renowned textile expert Dalgliesh, D C, this unique pattern was registered to commemorate Christopher Bartlett's connection to his ancestral heritage. Originally prepared for weaving by Dalgliesh, Ltd., the tartan now serves as a symbol of identity and belonging for individuals named Christopher Bartlett or its variants. With its carefully crafted design, this tartan pays tribute to Scotland's rich textile traditions while also acknowledging the American family's history of cultural exchange and adaptation. As a testament to the power of heritage and tradition, the Bartlett from Winnetka tartan remains an important part of Scottish heritage in the United States.

name: Bates [default]
description: The Bates tartan, a storied and iconic Scottish design, is steeped in heritage and family tradition. Registered to bear the name, this distinctive pattern has been woven into the fabric of generations past, its origins rooted in the personal commission of Dr Phil Smith Jnr for his namesake, Dr Brady Bates. While born from a singular honour, the tartan is now open to all who bear the name, allowing its rich, earthy tones and subtle nuances to be worn by anyone with Bates in their family tree or heritage. This Name tartan, imbued with a sense of identity and belonging, weaves together threads of Scottish tradition and history, inviting wearers to proudly claim their place within this storied clan's legacy.

name: Batten [default]
description: The Batten of Argyll, affectionately known as Baddenach, is a vibrant and storied tartan rich in history and heritage. Designed by Pipe Major Tim Lewis, this Name tartan pays homage to the ancestral roots of the Batten family, who emigrated from Argyll, Scotland to Jamestown, Virginia in search of new beginnings. As such, it can be worn with pride by all who bear the name, whether anglicised as Batten, Batton, Battin, or Badden, or through a direct connection to Scottish heritage. This tartan also holds significance for the St Andrews Legion and its Pipe Band, whose founder has seen fit to make it their official tartan. Wearing this tartan is not only a mark of family pride, but also a testament to the enduring bonds between Scotland and America, forged through the ages by families with Scottish roots.

name:
Baxter of Balgavies [default]
[AKA] Baxter of Balgavies
description: The Baxter tartan is a treasured emblem of Scottish heritage, steeped in history and tradition. Originally recorded by Logan, this threadcount has also been identified as 'Baxter', a testament to its rich cultural significance. Belonging to the esteemed clan of Baxters of Earlshall, who have resided at Leuchars in north Fife for generations, this tartan is deeply rooted in the county's heritage. Described by D Macgregor Peter in his 1856 publication 'Baronage of Angus & Mearns', Baxter tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the clan's proud history and their place within Scotland's storied past. This iconic design holds honour among Scottish families, evoking a sense of pride and connection to the land and its people.

name: Beard [default]
description: The Beard tartan is a distinctive and enigmatic pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, with its origins shrouded in mystery due to its association with an unknown designer. Registration notes reveal that the threadcount was identified at the Grandfather Mountain Games in 1996 by Mr Beard, who claimed it had been passed down through his family, specifically belonging to his great-grandmother. This tartan's significance lies not only in its unique design but also in the stories it holds, reflecting the history and traditions of a community that has preserved their cultural legacy. As part of the 'Other' category, which encompasses various types of tartans not attributed to specific clans or families, the Beard tartan stands as a testament to the richness and diversity of Scottish textiles, waiting to be unravelled by those fascinated by its secrets.

name: Beatty [default]
description: The Beatty tartan is a storied Name tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered in recognition of its distinctive character, this tartan design has been woven into the fabric of Scottish identity for generations to come. Born from the ingenuity of Dr Philip D Smith Jnr's design, the Beatty features a rich, muted palette that evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscapes. With no restrictions placed upon its use, the Beatty can be proudly worn by those who bear the name associated with it, serving as a symbol of family honour and connection to their ancestral roots. Its status as a Name tartan endows the Beatty with an added depth of meaning, underscoring the profound significance of clan identity in Scottish culture.

name:
Beaverbrook #3
[AKA] Beaverbrook New Brunswick
description: New Brunswick tartan, registered with Lyon Court Books, is a proud emblem of the Canadian province's rich heritage, born from the vision of its founder, Miss Patricia Jenkins MA. Commissioned by Lord Beaverbrook, a prominent benefactor of New Brunswick, this District tartan seamlessly weaves together the threads of the province's three main industries - lumbering, agriculture, and fishing - in forest green, meadow green, and blue, symbolising potential wealth. The red blocks surrounding these hues signify loyalty and devotion to Crown and Country, echoing the loyalty of New Brunswick's Loyalist settlers and regiments. Incorporating the provincial Coat of Arms and Regimental Crest in grey and gold, this tartan is a testament to the province's history and tradition. Asymmetrical as originally described by Jenkins, yet recorded as symmetrical in the Tartan Register, the New Brunswick tartan proudly stands as a symbol of its people's heritage, embodying the unique blend of culture, industry, and community that defines this special district.

name: Beck (Alan) personal; Dress
description: The Beck Dress tartan is a captivating blend of colour and heritage, born from the vision of Alan Duncan Beck in Liverpool, England. As a Name tartan, it has been registered to signify its unique identity and connection to its wearer's family history or cultural roots. This striking design features a subtle reversal of traditional blue and white hues, adding an air of mystery and individuality to its wearer. Originally woven by Fraser & Kirkbirght in Vancouver, Canada, the Beck Dress tartan pays homage to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage while embracing its own distinct character. As a personal creation, it is deeply personal to Alan Duncan Beck's design philosophy, reflecting his unique blend of artistic flair and cultural appreciation for the rich tapestry of Scottish tradition.

name: Belfrage [default]
description: The Belfrage tartan, designed by renowned Scottish weaver Peter MacDonald in 1997, pays tribute to the heritage of the eponymous family society, whose members predominantly reside in Sweden but still proudly claim Fife roots. This distinctive Name tartan is a masterful blend of traditional elements, drawing inspiration from the Duke of Fife and Spens patterns to create a unique and captivating design. Reflecting the family's Scandinavian connections, the Belfrage tartan seamlessly integrates Swedish and Scottish heritage, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's north-east coast. With its rich history and cultural significance, this tartan is an honourable testament to the enduring legacy of the Belfrage name, which has traversed generations and continents to remain a proud symbol of family identity and tradition.

name: Bell (Arthur) personal; Langholm Millennium
description: The Langholm Millennium tartan is a vibrant commemorative design, born from the creative vision of P.A.Keeney for Arthur Bell (Scotch Tweeds). This seven-coloured tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of the Langholm area in Dumfries, Scotland, paying tribute to the local organisations that have shaped its history and identity. By incorporating the colours of these significant groups, this tartan embodies the community spirit and pride of the region, celebrating both its past and present.
