As a commemorative tartan, it serves as a lasting tribute to Langholm's enduring legacy, while also being suitable for fashion wear, making it a versatile addition to any wardrobe that wishes to showcase its connection to this storied Scottish town.

name:
Bell Border
[AKA] Bell South
[AKA] Bell Southern Bell
[AKA] Bell of the Borders; #2
[AKA] Bell of the Borders #2
description: The Border Bell tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's clans and their revered traditions. Originally known as Blackethouse Bell, this distinctive tartan was initiated by May Roberts in 1986 as a tribute to Irving Bell, the Executive Director of Clan Bell Descendants. Designed by James Scarlett, MBE, it holds a special significance as a name tartan, signifying affiliation with the Bell family lineage. The tartan's history is deeply intertwined with Scottish folklore, its origins rooted in Blackethouse, the ancestral home of the Bells, and later renamed to reflect the changing fortunes of the clan. Today, the Border Bell tartan proudly represents Clan Bell Descendants' connection to their heritage, a symbol of honour and tradition that continues to be cherished by members of this storied clan.

name:
Bell of the Borders [default]
[AKA] Bell of the Borders
description: The Bell of the Borders tartan is a distinguished Corporate tartan, designed in 1984 by Bob Martin, who reworked the original design created by Col. William Bell, then President of Clan Bell Descendants. This striking tartan was unanimously approved at the 1984 Bell gathering in Staunton, Virginia, and subsequently registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority as an "Original Design", earning its nickname "Dress Blue". Named after Col. Bell's ancestral heritage, this tartan embodies the rich tradition of the Borders region, with its bold colours evoking a sense of heritage and pride. Available for public manufacture and sale, the Bell of the Borders tartan can be seen on everything from kilts to table coverings, paying homage to the legacy of Clan Bell Descendants and their esteemed leader, Col. William Bell.

name: Bell's Whisky #2
description: The Bell's Corporate Tartan is an emblematic representation of Scottish heritage, conceived by Claire Donaldson of House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. for Bell's Whisky company as a promotional motif. Originally designed to promote the iconic whisky brand, this striking tartan has since become synonymous with corporate identity and professional flair. Characterised by its distinctive dark blues and deep reds interwoven with light tones, the Bell's Tartan is a masterful blend of traditional craftsmanship and modern design sensibilities. Recognised as a Corporate registration, this tartan enjoys widespread acceptance within the world of business and industry, evoking a sense of professionalism, excellence, and Scottish heritage in equal measure.

name: Bell's Whisky
description: The Bell's Whisky tartan, expertly crafted by renowned designer Dalgliesh, D C, is a quintessential representation of Scottish heritage in corporate fashion. This distinctive tartan was specifically designed for use with whisky producers, paying homage to the storied history and tradition of Scotland's national spirit. By incorporating bold, rich colours reminiscent of aged oak barrels, this tartan exudes a sense of warmth and sophistication, evoking the rustic charm of the Highlands. As an official corporate design, it is both fitting and nostalgic, recalling the proud heritage of Scottish distilleries. Notably, the registration notes suggest that its origins lie in the 1980s, marking a significant moment in the tartan's evolution as a celebrated brand identifier.

name: Benson [default]
description: The Benson (New England) tartan is a timeless choice rooted in American heritage, born from the storied traditions of New England's esteemed Bensons family. Registered as a Name tartan, it is reserved exclusively for those sharing the surname Benson, making it a treasured symbol of identity and connection to this distinguished lineage. Weaving its rich history together are the expert hands of Molly Manaugh, who has brought this design to life with meticulous attention to detail. With its unique blend of subtle warmth and understated sophistication, this tartan is an enduring tribute to the enduring spirit of the Benson family, their legacy woven into the very fabric of American tradition.

name: Eynon of Wales
description: The Benyon of Wales tartan is a unique and modern name tartan that has captured the hearts of many with its distinctive characteristics. Weaved by Sheila Daniel at Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys (now closed), in collaboration with Wales Tartan Centres, this tartan pays homage to the country's rich heritage while also reflecting its growing commercial appeal. With its unusual thread count and colour palette, which deviates from traditional Celtic tartans, Benyon of Wales stands out as a testament to Welsh textile tradition's evolution. As a name tartan, it is not associated with any specific clan or territorial connection, but rather serves as an identifier for the design's origin. Notably, its inclusion in this index does not guarantee historical or genealogical credibility, and its use is purely to establish the design's provenance. Nonetheless, Benyon of Wales has become a beloved and iconic representation of Welsh culture, with its popularity growing steadily since its introduction by Wales Tartan Centres circa 1998.

name: Berkshire Highlanders Pipe Band Greylock Massachusetts
description: The Greylock tartan is a striking corporate design inspired by the majestic Mount Greylock, the highest peak in the Berkshire mountains just north of Pittsfield, Massachusetts. Designed for the Berkshire Highlanders Pipe Band by renowned designer William C Powers, this tartan pays homage to the region's rich Scottish heritage and its picturesque countryside. The palette, comprising shades of blue-green, yellow ochre, and deep grey, evokes the rolling hills and verdant valleys surrounding Mount Greylock. This corporate tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish culture in America, while also celebrating the unique beauty of the Berkshire region. Its distinctive pattern makes it an ideal choice for those seeking a bold and meaningful symbol of their association with the American Highland tradition.

name: Bethune [default]
description: The Bethune tartan is a distinctive and storied Name pattern, carefully crafted by Dr Philip D Smith Jr to evoke the rich heritage of Scotland's clans. This unique design is often likened to its more famous cousin, the Macbeth sett, yet it boasts an added layer of complexity with the incorporation of a light blue stripe amidst the darker blue ground. As a Name tartan, the Bethune is inherently tied to a specific Scottish family or sept, making each wearer part of a larger, intertwined narrative of clan history and tradition. With its subtle nuances and intricate details, this tartan design pays homage to Scotland's proud past while also asserting an individual's connection to their personal heritage.

name: Bijral [default]
description: The Bijral tartan is a poignant tribute to the rich heritage of 4th generation Scots, its intricate patterns woven from threads of tradition and identity. Registration notes reveal that this tartan was created specifically for those who bear the name Bijral, making it a deeply personal and meaningful connection to one's ancestral roots. As a Name tartan, it holds significance beyond mere aesthetic appeal, serving as a symbol of cultural continuity and family ties. With its unique characteristics and restricted availability to the Bijral name alone, this tartan stands as a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage and the importance of preserving traditional patterns for future generations.

name: Birch [default]
description: The Birch family tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage, woven with love and precision by renowned kiltmaker Mr Robin Birch of Connell Reid Kiltmakers. This Name tartan holds significant personal importance for its bearers, signifying their connection to the esteemed Birch clan. With its unique sett recorded by the Scottish Tartans Society, this tartan has been meticulously crafted to represent a family's history and tradition. As a symbol of honour and pride, the Birch family tartan is worn with dignity, evoking memories of ancestral lands, cultural roots, and generations of loyal service. Its registration status ensures that this special fabric remains faithful to its origins, a tangible link between past and present.

name: Birral [default]
description: The Birral/Burrell tartan, crafted with precision by Wilsons of Bannockburn, holds a rich history within Scotland's storied clan heritage. This ancestral threadcount was carefully extracted from a manuscript account book in the National Museums Scotland, Edinburgh, and is also mentioned in Telford Dunbar's seminal 1962 work 'History of Highland Dress', which cites its appearance on William Wilson's stock list of 1800. Dating back to an era when tartans were woven with meticulous attention to detail, this particular design has been passed down through generations, serving as a symbol of family pride and tradition. As one of the earliest recorded examples from Wilsons of Bannockburn, the Birral/Burrell tartan embodies the very essence of Scottish heritage, evoking images of Highland landscapes, ancestral homes, and generations of proud owners who have worn it with honour since its origins in the early 19th century.

name: Birse [default]
description: The Birse tartan is a storied Name tartan that carries the weight of tradition and heritage. Woven in November 1957 by T G Gordon of Glasgow, this distinctive design has been passed down through the ages, its origins rooted in the Scottish town of Arbroath, where it was previously recorded as 'Birse'. Although the designer remains anonymous, the tartan's significance is undeniable, having been carefully documented and preserved within the prestigious MacGregor-Hastie collection. As part of the cloth archive of the Scottish Tartans Society, this sample serves as a tangible link to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, evoking memories of ancient weavers and their skilled hands that brought these timeless patterns to life.

name: Bishop
description: The Bishop tartan is a timeless and distinctive Name tartan, crafted with meticulous attention to detail by master weavers D.C. Dalgliesh and Geoffrey. Registered in 1899, this iconic design embodies the heritage and tradition of the Bishop name, which proudly claims a place within Scotland's storied tapestry of clans and families. Characterised by its classic, symmetrical pattern, the tartan's precise colourwork reflects the craftsmanship and expertise of its creator, Michael Bishop. As with all Name tartans, use of this design requires permission from the registered owner, Mr William Bishop, who ensures that royalties are paid to maintain the integrity and tradition of this cherished Scottish textile heritage. With its enduring beauty and rich history, the Bishop tartan remains a beloved symbol of Scottish identity and family pride.

name: Bisset #2
description: The Bisset tartan, registered by the Scottish Tartans Society in 1977, is a rich and symbolic expression of family heritage. Inspired by the historic shield colours of Mrs E Bisset's clan, this intricate pattern combines blue, white, yellow, black, red, and green hues on a verdant background, evoking the essence of Scotland's ancient traditions. The deliberate choice of colours - from the blue and white of the shield to the yellow representing wood chips from an axe, symbolising resilience, and the fresh growth on the green background - pay homage to the motto 'Abscissa virescit', meaning "Cut me down and I shall grow again". As a Clan tartan, the Bisset design serves as a proud testament to family legacy, weaving together the threads of history, nature, and tradition in a vibrant tapestry of Scottish heritage.

name: Black (DCD)
description: The Black symmetrical tartan, registered to Dalgleish Ltd in 2003, embodies the sombre yet dignified spirit of Scotland's rich heritage. This iconic pattern, woven with precision by D C Dalgleish of Selkirk, is a testament to the country's proud tradition of textile craftsmanship. Originally intended as an asymmetrical design, it was later noted that its threadcount should be correctly readered (rather than reinterpreted) for its true character. Despite this nuance, the Black tartan remains a striking representation of Scottish identity, evoking feelings of gravitas and reverence. Its symmetrical layout ensures a sense of balance and harmony, while its dark hues recall the country's dramatic landscapes under twilight skies. As a registered Name tartan, it proudly bears the name of Dalgleish Ltd, symbolising the enduring legacy of Scotland's finest weavers.

name: Black and White Whisky #2
description: The Black and White colourway, categorised as a Corporate tartan, is a striking example of modern branding heritage, bearing testament to its origins in 19th-century Scotland. This versatile design was used by James Buchanan & Co for various promotional materials, including the iconic "Black & White" brand identity, underscoring its significance in shaping corporate visual identity. The restrictions surrounding this tartan are telling, as it is linked to a specific company, evoking memories of traditional Scottish trade and commerce. As a Corporate tartan, it has been carefully crafted to convey professionalism, sophistication, and unity - essential qualities for any business seeking to establish itself with authority and prestige in the modern world.

name: Black and White Whisky
description: The Black and White corporate tartan is a striking, modern design that embodies the sleek sophistication of the Scottish whisky industry. Registration notes reveal that this distinctive threadcount was taken from United Distillers for promotional material, aptly named "Black & White", highlighting its association with the iconic brand. As a Corporate tartan, it is designed to be versatile and professional, suitable for companies seeking a unique visual identity. Its simple yet bold colour palette of black and white creates a clean and modern aesthetic, evoking the crisp lines and precision of Scottish engineering. By embracing this tartan, organisations can tap into Scotland's rich heritage and convey a sense of respectability and tradition, making it an ideal choice for businesses looking to establish their roots in the country.

name: Black-MacDonald
description: The Black-MacDonald tartan is a deeply personal and storied design, woven with the rich heritage of Scotland's most iconic clans. Registered in the 19th century, it was originally created for Jane Black-MacDonald and her immediate family, symbolising their ancestral ties to the MacDonalds. However, its beauty and significance extend far beyond individual families, as it embodies the broader traditions of this storied clan. Inspired by the historic tartan of the MacDonalds, yet infused with the verdant hues of Scotland's glens and the rugged tones of the munroes, this design is a testament to the country's enduring cultural identity. Weaving together threads of history, family, and land, the Black-MacDonald tartan stands as a tribute to the enduring legacy of this beloved Scottish clan.

name: Blackcraig (Personal)
description: The Blackcraig personal tartan, registered by the renowned Scottish textile brand Lochcarron of Scotland, is a distinctive and captivating pattern steeped in heritage and tradition. This unique Name tartan is a testament to the individual's identity and connection to their surname or family lineage. Characterised by its dramatic black and navy blue hues, interwoven with subtle hints of gold and green, Blackcraig evokes the rugged, windswept landscapes of Scotland's Highland regions. As a personal tartan, it holds great sentimental value, allowing the wearer to proudly showcase their heritage and cultural roots. With its rich colour palette and distinctive weave, this tartan is sure to make a statement, honouring the wearer's name and connecting them to a timeless tradition that stretches back generations of Scottish clan history.

name: Blackstock Dress
description: The Blackstock Red (Dress) tartan is a poignant testament to the enduring legacy of the Scottish-Irish Blackstock family, whose heritage spans centuries and continents. Commissioned by Herbert Earl Blackstock in 1983, this distinctive tartan was carefully designed by kiltmaker and historian Bob Martin to reflect the clan's complex history and cultural roots. As part of their Clan tartan category, Blackstock Red pays homage to the Blackstocks' Ulster origins, where they would have worn these very colours with pride. The restrictions attached to its registration serve as a reminder of the family's commitment to preserving their heritage, and the tartan now bears testament to the intricate weave of Scottish-Irish identity that continues to captivate hearts around the world.

name: Blackstock Hunting
description: The Blackstock Hunting tartan is a storied fabric with deep roots in Scottish heritage, commissioned in 1983 by Herbert Earl Blackstock, President of the Clan Blackstock Society in the USA, to represent his esteemed family's history and legacy. As a Clan tartan, this distinctive pattern holds significant importance within the Blackstock family, tracing back to their 'Scotch-Irish' roots in what is now Ulster. Designed by skilled kiltmaker and historian Bob Martin of Greenville, South Carolina, the tartan expertly weaves together shades of blue, green, and brown hues to evoke a sense of ruggedness and tradition, perfectly capturing the spirit of hunting and exploration that has defined the Blackstock family for generations.

name: Blair Dress
description: The Blair Dress tartan is a storied heritage pattern, intricately woven with the rich traditions of the Scottish clans. Designed by renowned weaver Phil Smith in 1989 and brought to life by esteemed manufacturer John Buchan Mill in 1991 at Lochcarron of Scotland, this particular design holds significant cultural weight as a representation of the Blair family's legacy. As a Clan/Family tartan, it is an honour to wear or display this pattern with pride, evoking the history and identity of the Blairs throughout generations. While restrictions do apply in terms of its use, particularly regarding its adoption by other families or corporations without formal permission, for those who are fortunate enough to bear the name or affiliation, the Blair Dress tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring spirit and heritage of Scotland's esteemed clans.

name: Blair [default]
description: The Blair tartan, a timeless and iconic clan sett, weaves a rich narrative of Scottish heritage into its very fabric. Registered by the Scottish Tartan Society, this traditional tartan is steeped in history, reflecting the cultural traditions of a modern family. Described as a 'modern family sett', it evokes the warmth and camaraderie of kinship, while its subtle nuances speak to the ingenuity of 19th-century weavers. While its exact origins are shrouded in mystery, one thing is certain: the Blair tartan has been worn with pride by generations of Scots, symbolising a sense of belonging to something greater than oneself. This treasured tartan remains an integral part of Scottish identity, a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's clan system and the artistry of its weavers.

name: Blairmore School
description: The Blairmore House tartan is a sophisticated corporate design born from the collaboration between renowned designers John B Gillespie and Monique Baumann, in partnership with the esteemed Blairmore School in Glass, Aberdeenshire. This discerning tartan was created to reflect the school's heritage and prestige, whilst also serving as a professional and stylish identifier for its patrons. With its distinctive colour palette and precise sett, this corporate tartan is ideally suited for formal wear, business attire, and branding initiatives, evoking the rich history and tradition of Scotland's esteemed glassmaking community. As a testament to the skill of Gillespie/Baumann's design expertise, Blairmore House tartan has become a sought-after choice for those seeking to convey professionalism, elegance, and a deep connection to Scottish heritage.

name: Blalack [default]
description: Blalack is a striking fashion tartan that embodies the timeless elegance of Scotland's rich heritage. With its distinctive sett and subtle colour palette, this tartan exudes a sense of understated sophistication, making it perfect for those who appreciate traditional Scottish style with a modern twist. Registered in 1999 at Convergence - Atlanta, one of the most prestigious bi-annual handweavers' conventions, Blalack is part of a select group of fashion tartans that have been carefully crafted to showcase the art of Scottish weaving. While its designer remains unknown, this tartan's association with the esteemed Convergence convention lends it an air of authenticity and prestige, ensuring it will always hold a special place in the hearts of those who cherish Scotland's cultural traditions.

name: Blanton Dress
description: The Blanton tartan is a rich and storied design, proudly worn by those bearing the surname Blanton as their own distinct Scottish heritage. Though it may have originated from the Campbell clan tradition, this tartan was specifically created to give the Blantons worldwide a sense of identity and belonging. As such, its subtle use of the Campbell colours in the overcheck is a testament to Thomas William Blanton III's thoughtful consideration of his family's history. This dress tartan weaves together traditional Scottish craftsmanship with a deep sense of pride and connection to one's roots, making it an honourable tradition for those who bear this name.

name: Blanton [default]
description: The Blanton tartan, created by esteemed Thomas William Blanton III, holds a profound significance within Scottish heritage, particularly for those bearing the surname Blanton. Though often referred to as a sept of Clan Campbell, this distinctive tartan serves as a proud symbol of identity and distinction for the Blanton family worldwide, providing a sense of honour and connection to their ancestral roots. With its unique blend of colours, the Blanton tartan weaves together the rich history of Thomas William's heritage, incorporating his family colours into the over-check. Interestingly, noted textile expert Phil Smith notes that this design bears striking similarities to the Lamont tartan, with a subtle variation in hue - in this case, purple is used instead of white. As such, the Blanton tartan stands as a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish tradition and family pride.

name: Blaylock [default]
description: The Blaylock tartan, a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage, was first designed by esteemed Scotsman Dr Philip D Smith for Beverley Blaylock of Edmonton, Canada in a tradition steeped in clan history and identity. As a Name tartan, it is intended to be worn by all who bear the name Blaylock, as well as its various spellings, allowing it to transcend geographical boundaries while remaining true to its Scottish roots. With its unique threads woven together, the Blaylock tartan embodies the values of loyalty and community that define the name's bearer, evoking a sense of pride and belonging among those who wear it with honour.

name: Blue Knights Motorcycle Club
description: The Blue Knights, The tartan is a prestigious corporate design born out of the iconic Blue Knights International Law Enforcement Motorcycle Club. Crafted by renowned designer Helen Marshall at Marton Mills, this distinctive pattern was specifically created for the organisation's members, reflecting their unwavering dedication and brotherhood. As an exclusive tartan, its primary purpose is to serve as a badge of honour among the Blue Knights community, with all profits generated from sales supporting the chosen charities of the club. The fact that Marton Mills holds exclusive weaving rights underscores the significance of this tartan in perpetuating the club's identity and heritage, solidifying its place in Scottish textile history.

name: Bodog
description: The Bodog corporate tartan is a striking example of modern Scottish heritage, born from the visionary design of Calvin Ayre. Originally created to reflect the rebranded intellectual property of the bodogbrand.com empire, this tartan represents a bold new chapter in the company's history. As a corporate entity, its purpose lies at the heart of branding and identity, with the subtle yet distinctive red stripe expertly woven into the design to create a sense of depth and nuance. Despite restrictions on use, reserved for exclusive corporate licensing only, this tartan embodies the entrepreneurial spirit of Scotland's great brands. Its registration notes speak to a new era in brand management, while the House of Tartan's right to weave ensures that traditional Scottish weaving expertise is still at the heart of its creation.

name: bodog.com
description: The Bodog.com tartan, a pioneering corporate design, pays homage to the eponymous online brand that has left its mark on the digital world. Named after the pioneering web site, this unique tartan holds a special place in history as the first to bear the name of an internet domain. Originally registered by BodogBrand.com, a company based in St Johns, Antigua and Barbuda, this tartan now takes on new significance as it is slated to give way to a revised design under the same brand's rebranding efforts. As a testament to the rapidly evolving landscape of global commerce, the Bodog.com tartan serves as a striking representation of the digital age's influence on Scottish heritage and tradition. Its inclusion in the world of corporate tartans underscores the enduring power of traditional textile artistry to adapt and thrive in an ever-changing world.

name: Bonnar [default]
description: The Bonner or Bonnar tartan is an enigmatic and storied piece of Scotland's rich heritage, its origins shrouded in mystery but steeped in intrigue. Named after the French phrase "bonne chose" - a felicitous expression uttered by King Francis I in praise of Guilhen de Bonares, who earned this moniker for his bold defiance against Napoleon's forces - this tartan is imbued with a sense of history and cultural significance. Hand-coloured strips from James Mackinlay's Collection, now preserved in the Scottish Tartans Society archive, offer a glimpse into the design's possible Black Watch connection, while its abstract, muted hues evoke a sense of understated strength and resilience, characteristic of Scotland's finest tartan traditions.

name: Borthwick Dress
description: The Borthwick Dress tartan, designed by Alistair Buchan, is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Stuart clan's heritage. Originally commissioned in 1984 as a dress version of the historic Borthwick tartan, this family-specific pattern holds significant cultural importance within Scotland's Clan system. With subtle variations from its ancestral counterpart - specifically, the substitution of white for grey threads - the Borthwick Dress tartan embodies the evolution of Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered in 1984, this design has been carefully preserved to reflect both its technical accuracy, as documented in Lord Lyon Court Books (LCB47), and its distinctive thread count, identical to that recorded in Lochcarron's swatch archives. This tartan's presence within the Lochcarron collection is a tangible connection to Scotland's rich past, weaving together the threads of family history, cultural significance, and time-honoured tradition.

name:
Borthwick [default]
[AKA] Borthwick Hunting
description: The Borthwick Hunting tartan is a rich and storied Scottish fabric, steeped in history and heritage. Created for Major John Henry Stuart Borthwick of Crookston, Midlothian, one of Scotland's most senior families, this tartan reflects the proud tradition of the Borthwicks, who date back to the 14th century. The intricate design, featuring a subtle interplay of greys, blacks, and dark reds, is reminiscent of the family's noble heritage and their connection to the land and its history. With its origins in the 1950s, this tartan was formally recorded in the Lord Lyon Book in 1984, recognising its place within Scottish clan tartanry. As a symbol of family pride and tradition, the Borthwick Hunting tartan continues to be worn by members of the Borthwick family and other clans who favour its striking design.

name: Boswell Dress
description: The Boswell Dress, a personal tartan of great historical and familial significance, was designed by Col William P Boswell of Toberchurn, Col. A testament to his dedication to Scottish heritage and tradition, this unique tartan is rooted in the Colonel's own coat of arms, meticulously recorded in the Lyon Register V.74, P 61. Woven by Elliots of Selkirk with precision and care, the Boswell Dress reflects the intricate nuances of traditional tartan weaving, showcasing a rich interplay of colours that evoke the strong and storied roots of the Boswell family. Originally reserved for personal use, this tartan is now held in trust by the Boswells of Balmuto, a Maryland family lineage, ensuring its enduring connection to Scotland's proud clan heritage.

name: Bowie Black
description: The Bowie, Black tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans, its dark hues evoking the sombre tones of ancient battles fought on mist-shrouded lochs and heather-covered moors. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds significant cultural importance, bearing witness to the enduring legacy of a storied lineage. Designed by the esteemed House of Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan has been woven with precision, its distinctive pattern telling the story of a proud family's history and traditions. Interestingly, an earlier version of the design was mistakenly produced in black thread, but it has since become a distinct variation in its own right, known as Black Bowie. This unique blend of heritage and tradition makes the Bowie, Black tartan a truly special piece, steeped in the complex tapestry of Scottish history and identity.

name: Boyd [default]
description: The Boyd tartan, designed by Jamie Scarlett MBE for Lord Kilmarnock in 1956, is a rich and storied fabric of Scottish heritage. This Clan tartan tells the story of two noble families - the Hays, Earls of Errol, and the Stewarts - whose ancestral roots intertwine through its intricate design. The red section echoes the Hay-Leith tartan, while the green stripe nods to the Hunting Stewart, symbolising a deep connection to Scotland's storied past. With its carefully crafted minor alterations, this tartan pays homage to the town of Kilmarnock in the South West Lowlands, where the Boyd family has long been closely associated with the local community. name: Boyle (Damien) personal
description: The Boyle Personal Tartan is a richly woven tribute to the storied heritage of the Boyle family from County Donegal and the Grampian District. Characterised by its subtle blend of greens, blues, and earth tones, the Boyle Tartan reflects the dual influences of Donegal's rugged coastlines and the rolling hills of the Grampian District. With its restrictions grounded in the registration notes, this tartan serves as an enduring honour to the family's ancestral homeland, inviting wearers to proudly connect with their heritage and celebrate the rich tapestry of Scottish tradition.

name: Boys Brigade
description: The Boys Brigade tartan is a vibrant and enduring symbol of Scottish corporate identity, bearing witness to the values of community service and youth development embodied by this iconic organisation. Originally designated as 'B B Special Tartan' by Patons of Tillicoultry, this tartan has been meticulously woven by the Macnaughtons Group of Pitlochry at a request from a local Boys Brigade unit, reflecting the tartan's newfound connection to this esteemed charity. Rooted in Scottish heritage and tradition, the Boys Brigade tartan embodies the spirit of camaraderie, discipline, and social responsibility that defines this prestigious group, making it an honourable choice for corporate identity and a testament to the enduring legacy of this esteemed organisation.

name: Braid [default]

name: Brand Ambassador

Though only permitted for those in favour with the Brand Ambassador company, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage and tradition, expertly crafted for the 21st-century business world. Its restrictions may be stringent, but its significance to those who wear it is undeniable – a badge of honour worn by those privileged to represent this esteemed brand.

name: Braveheart (movie)
description: The Braveheart Corporate Tartan, designed by Knode/Cavell for Mel Gibson's 1995 epic, embodies the unyielding spirit of Scotland's legendary warrior, William Wallace. While not strictly adhering to traditional tartan principles, the Braveheart design captures the essence of its inspiration, with marled yarns adding depth and nuance to the overall graphic. As a corporate tartan, it has been designed for business wear, yet its rugged charm and associations with Scotland's proud history make it an excellent choice for individuals who aspire to embody courage and determination in their professional pursuits.

name: Brecheen [default]
description: Brecheen is a rich and storied tartan, born from a deliberate colour modification of the traditional Angus pattern, carefully crafted by Glen D Brecheen. name: Brice [default]
description: The Brice tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage in North America. The tartan's origins in Dekalb County, New York, where Brice settled, underscores its connection to this specific region of North America, while also highlighting the transatlantic exchange of cultural traditions that defined the Scottish-American experience.

name: Brides [default]
description: Brides Plaid, with its timeless charm, is a quintessential testament to Scotland's rich tapestry of heritage and tradition. With its rich history and subtle nuances, this tartan embodies the enduring spirit of Scottish culture, inviting wearers to weave their own tale of love and tradition.

name: Bright of Garth [default]
description: The Bright of Garth personal tartan, designed by the renowned Peter MacDonald, is a vibrant and distinctive choice that embodies the proud heritage of its creator's Scottish clan legacy. name: Brisbane [default]

The restrictions placed on its use are a testament to the importance of preserving Scotland's textile traditions, underscoring the Brisbane tartan as a treasured artefact in the country's tapestry of tartans.

name: Bristow Helicopters
description: The Bristow Helicopters tartan is a unique blend of tradition and innovation, reflecting the heritage of Aberdeen's aviation industry. With its bold yet subtle colour palette, this tartan embodies the perfect balance of tradition and contemporary flair, making it an ideal choice for those who embody the spirit of Bristow Helicopters.

name: British Airways
description: The British Airways tartan is a striking Corporate tartan, carefully crafted by renowned designer Peter MacDonald in association with the iconic airline. This distinctive pattern was originally created exclusively for British Airways, who retain ownership of the rights to the design. A testament to the airline's rich history and global reach, this tartan has been proudly displayed on the tailfins of various BA aircraft over the years, evoking a sense of national pride and aviation heritage. With its unique blend of colours and technical precision, this tartan is a quintessential representation of British Airways' brand identity, reflecting the values of innovation, tradition, and excellence that have come to define the airline's reputation.

name: British Caledonian Airways #1
description: The British Caledonian Airways #1 tartan is a fitting tribute to Scotland's rich heritage, born from the iconic flight attendant uniforms worn by staff at one of the country's most beloved airlines. As part of a series designed by Colin Hutcheson for British Caledonian, this particular tartan variation was woven with precision by Peter MacArthur in 2002 and adopted by the airline in 1985. A Stewart tartan, steeped in history and tradition, it boasts four distinctive colours, including Princess Mary blue, which is remarkably close to the original 'correct' shade. The association with this esteemed airline serves as a poignant reminder of British Caledonian's contribution to Scottish cultural exchange, highlighting the enduring bond between Scotland and its global connections.

name: British Caledonian Airways #2
description: The British Caledonian Airways #2 tartan, a corporate staple in the world of aviation heritage, pays homage to the rich Scottish tradition that has long been woven into the fabric of British Airways. As one of four colour variations of the prestigious Stewart tartan, this specific design is steeped in history and prestige, with its roots firmly planted in the royal family's own tartan legacy. Designed by the renowned firm, British Airways, this tartan has become synonymous with elegance and sophistication, worn proudly by flight attendants as part of the airline's uniform. Notably designated as 'Princess Mary', although a slight variation from the original, this tartan is a testament to the enduring influence of Scottish heritage on British culture. Woven by skilled artisans at Hamilton (now Biggar), this beautiful tartan is a true celebration of tradition and craftsmanship, evoking the warm hospitality and timeless charm that has come to define British Airways.

name: British Caledonian Airways #3
description: This distinctive corporate tartan, designated British Airways #3, holds a special place in the annals of Scottish heritage and aviation history. Inspired by traditional Stewart tartans, this variation boasts four carefully chosen colours, expertly woven to create a vibrant visual identity for British Airways' flight attendants. Originally registered as 'Princess Mary', although inaccurately named, it showcases the subtle nuances of tartan design, reflecting the intricate balance between form and function. Crafted by Peter Macarthur of Hamilton in 2002, now re-established in Biggar, this tartan embodies the enduring spirit of Scottish tradition, seamlessly blending cultural significance with modern corporate flair, its story woven into the fabric of British Airways' iconic identity.

name: British Caledonian Airways #4
description: The British Caledonian Airways #4 tartan is a poignant representation of corporate heritage, hailing from the prestigious aviation brand that once dominated the skies above Scotland. As one of four colour variations of the Stewart tartan, it holds a special place in the annals of Scottish tradition, paying homage to the noble Stewarts who have long been synonymous with Scottish nobility and excellence. The 'Princess Mary' designation, albeit somewhat colloquially applied, is a testament to the tartan's enduring appeal and historical significance. Woven by skilled artisan Peter MacArthur in 2002, this tartan has since become an iconic symbol of British Airways' rich legacy, its subtle nuances reflecting the brand's storied history as a Scottish icon of air travel excellence.

name: British Energy
description: The British Energy tartan is a modern, dynamic design that embodies the vibrant spirit of Britain's leading energy sector. Registered by Kennedy Millar Ltd specifically for use by British Energy, this striking pattern showcases the company's corporate colours in bold and harmonious balance. Category Corporate speaks to its utilitarian purpose, intended for business attire and corporate wear, reflecting the professionalism and authority of a major industry player. With its restrictions noting its exclusive association with British Energy, this tartan is an unmistakable symbol of company identity and pride, conveying the values of innovation, reliability, and expertise that define the energy sector.

name: Brittany Bro Dreger
description: The Bro-Dreger corporate tartan is a unique and intriguing design, born from the rich cultural heritage of Brittany in northwest France. Commissioned by Richard Duclos, owner of Fordiam, with input from Kirsty Anderson, this tartan celebrates the region's nine ancient areas, each represented by a distinct colour palette inspired by their respective flag designs. The result is a striking corporate tartan that pays homage to the Celtic roots and Highland heritage, while embodying the sophistication and elegance required for a French company specialising in fine Scottish dress. With its carefully chosen colours and distinctive patterns, Bro-Dreger embodies the spirit of French-British cultural exchange and mutual appreciation, making it an ideal choice for a business looking to forge strong connections with Scotland's rich traditions.

name: Brittany Bro Kerne
description: The Bro-Kerne tartan is a vibrant and distinctive corporate design commissioned by French company Fordiam, Paris, to showcase their connection to Brittany's rich Highland heritage. Inspired by the region's nine ancient areas, or 'Bro', each with its own unique flag colours, Kirsty Anderson has woven a striking pattern that pays homage to the cultural significance of these Breton regions. By taking inspiration from the local flags and incorporating them into a corporate tartan, Bro-Kerne seamlessly blends traditional Scottish craftsmanship with modern French flair. This unique design is a testament to the enduring appeal of Highland dress and its ability to transcend borders and cultures, as exemplified by Fordiam's owner Richard Duclos' initiative.

name: Brittany Bro Leon
description: The Bro-Leon tartan is a striking corporate design born from the rich cultural heritage of Brittany's Breton region. Named after the French word "bro," meaning area, this unique tartan draws inspiration from the nine ancient regions of Brittany, each with its own distinct flag colours. Weaving together these hues, Anderson, Kirsty, has created a distinctive and sophisticated pattern that pays homage to France's Highland-inspired traditions. As a corporate tartan for Fordiam, Paris, Bro-Leon is designed to evoke a sense of elegance and refinement, perfectly capturing the essence of French elegance with its understated yet striking colour palette. By combining historical significance with modern design sensibilities, this tartan offers a compelling fusion of tradition and innovation that is sure to make a lasting impression on any wearer or observer of corporate Highland dress.

name: Brittany Bro Naoned
description: The Bro-Naoned tartan is a striking corporate design born from the rich cultural heritage of Brittany, France's northwest region. Inspired by the ancient Breton 'Bro' words for areas, which evoke nine historic regions with distinct flag colours, this tartan brings together nine core hues to create a vibrant and unique pattern. Woven by The House of Edgar, in collaboration with Fordiam, a Paris-based company specialising in Highland dress, Bro-Naoned pays homage to the region's strong identity and history. As a corporate tartan, it is designated for use by Fordiam and its French affiliate, allowing them to proudly showcase their connection to Brittany's unique cultural landscape. With Kirsty Anderson at the helm of its design, this tartan represents a fascinating blend of French and Scottish heritage, poised to make a lasting impression in corporate circles.

name: Brittany Bro Roazhon
description: The Bro-Roazhon corporate tartan, designed with flair by Kirsty Anderson, is a unique and stylish addition to any Highland-inspired uniform or corporate attire. This distinctive design originates from Brittany, specifically the nine ancient areas known as 'Bro's, which were woven together to create a rich tapestry of colour. The result is a captivating palette that echoes the region's history and heritage. As a corporate tartan, Bro-Roazhon has been carefully crafted for Fordiam, a French company with a passion for Highland dress, and its owner Richard Duclos played a significant role in bringing this design to life. With its bold, Breton-inspired colours, the Bro-Roazhon tartan is sure to make a statement, evoking the rugged beauty and cultural richness of Brittany while adding a touch of modern sophistication to any outfit.

name: Brittany Bro Sant-Brieg
description: The Bro-sant-Brieg tartan is a distinctive corporate pattern woven with flair and attention to tradition, its creation a testament to the enduring spirit of Highland heritage in France. Named after nine ancient areas in Brittany, known as 'bro's, each of these regions boasts its own unique flag colours, which have been carefully combined by designer Kirsty Anderson into a singular tartan fabric. This innovative fusion reflects the cultural exchange between Scotland and Brittany, while still paying homage to the rich textile traditions of both nations. Registered specifically for Fordiam, a French company specialising in Highland dress, the Bro-sant-Brieg tartan is a striking example of how Scottish heritage can be reimagined with a contemporary twist, its unique colours and design making it an instantly recognised brand identity.

name: Brittany Bro Sant-Malou
description: The Bro-sant-Malou corporate tartan, carefully crafted by Kirsty Anderson, celebrates the rich heritage of Brittany's Breton culture while embracing its international flair. Inspired by the region's nine ancient areas, each represented by a distinct tartan, Bro-sant-Malou seamlessly blends traditional colour schemes with modern design. The 'mean' colours, derived from the average hues of these area flags, create a striking visual identity perfect for the French company Fordiam, which specialises in Highland dress. With its unique blend of historical and contemporary elements, this tartan is as much about cultural fusion as it is about corporate style, paying homage to Brittany's rich history while embracing the cosmopolitan spirit of France.

name: Brittany Bro Wened
description: The Bro-Wened tartan is a unique corporate design created to represent French company Fordiam, with a deep connection to Highland heritage. Named after the ancient Breton word for "area", this distinctive tartan takes its inspiration from the nine historic regions of Brittany, where the colours blend to form the "mean" hues of their respective flags. A true celebration of cultural fusion, the Bro-Wened tartan reflects Fordiam's commitment to Highland dress and its blend of French and Scottish influences. Woven with expertise by The House of Edgar, this stylish tartan is now a proud symbol of company identity, embodying the rich traditions and distinctive spirit of Scotland within France.

name: Brittany Bro Zol
description: The Bro-Zol tartan is a unique fusion of Scottish heritage and French flair, perfectly capturing the essence of its corporate origins as a bespoke design for Fordiam, Paris. Created by Kirsty Anderson, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the nine ancient areas in Brittany, where the colours are inspired by the mean hues of their respective flags - a nod to the region's rich cultural heritage. With its carefully considered colour palette and nuanced design, this tartan is sure to evoke a sense of elegance and refinement, while still honouring the traditions of Scotland's rich textile heritage.

name: Brodie Black & White
description: The Brodie (WCWM) fashion tartan, woven to perfection by renowned designers at West Coast Woolen Mill, is an iconic representation of timeless Scottish style. Originally registered with the prestigious registration office for Scottish tartans, the National Register of Tartans, this distinctive pattern bears testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland. Characterised by its striking black and white hues, the Brodie tartan evokes a sense of sophistication and elegance, perfect for adding a touch of Highland flair to any outfit. This fashion-forward design has become synonymous with glamour and refinement, and is sure to make a statement on anyone fortunate enough to wear it.

name: Brodie Dress
description: The Brodie Dress tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's clans, woven with tradition and history. Registered as a Clan tartan, this distinctive pattern is steeped in the Brodie family's legacy, its origins shrouded in mystery despite being dated back to 2001 when Dr Phil Smith recorded its threadcount from a D C Dalgliesh swatch. As such, it holds significant cultural importance for those tracing their ancestry through this storied clan. Although the identity of the designer remains unknown, the Brodie Dress tartan's intricate design and deep-rooted heritage evoke a sense of national pride and connection to Scotland's storied past, its unique characteristics a tangible link to the country's rich tapestry of tradition and family history.

name: Brodie Hunting
description: The Brodie Hunting tartan is a rich and storied design, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registration notes indicate its origins date back to the late 19th century, when it was featured in early publications on Scotland's clans and tartans. This particular tartan has been linked to the Brodie clan, who, according to historical records, adopted a variant of the Hunting Brodie as their own family tartan, likely due to its association with districts traditionally inhabited by the Gordons and Forbes families. With a provenance that predates the more modern 'invented' white-based tartans, this design evokes a sense of history and authenticity, reflecting the traditional dress sett of an era when bold colours were proudly worn as family identifiers. The inclusion of the Hunting Brodie within the Brodie clan's tartan heritage serves as a testament to the enduring significance of Scottish clans and their distinctive textiles.

Brodie Silver

Its intricate nuances and characteristic colouration are both a testament to the skill of Dr Smith Junior and a fitting tribute to the enduring legacy of the Bronte family, woven into the very fabric of Scottish tartan tradition.

name: Brooks Brothers Tattersall Blue
description: The Brooks Brothers Tattersall Blue tartan embodies the quintessential British heritage of elegance and sophistication, born from the iconic horse blanket checks that originated at London's prestigious Tattersalls market. With its timeless appeal and subtle nuances, the Brooks Brothers Tattersall Blue tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich textile heritage while exuding modern style and sophistication, making it an ideal choice for discerning fashion enthusiasts seeking a quintessentially British twist on classic designs.

name: Brooks Brothers Tattersall Camel
description: The Brooks Brothers Tattersall Camel is an iconic fashion tartan born from the legendary American heritage brand's penchant for timeless elegance. Inspired by the traditional checks of a horse blanket, this distinctive pattern has been adopted as a signature element in Brooks Brothers' luxurious luggage range. Originally designed to evoke the sophisticated aesthetic of London's Tattersalls horse market, where fine fabrics were once traded, the Tattersall Camel tartan embodies the perfect blend of classic charm and understated sophistication. With its clean lines, uniform squares, and subtle colour palette, this tartan is perfectly at home in high-end fashion, effortlessly exuding refinement and style that transcends traditional tartan associations, underscoring Brooks Brothers' enduring commitment to craftsmanship and excellence.

name: Brooks Brothers Tattersall Red
description: The Brooks Brothers Tattersall Red is a quintessential fashion tartan, steeped in heritage and tradition. Originally inspired by the classic checks used on horse blankets at London's iconic Tattersalls market, this design has been adopted by the esteemed American tailors as part of their signature luggage range. Characterised by its square pattern of alternating colours forming a solid foundation, the Tattersall Red is a masterful example of traditional British textile craftsmanship. By embracing this timeless check pattern, Brooks Brothers pay homage to the storied history of their brand and the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's tartan traditions, elevating it into a sophisticated fashion statement that exudes classic elegance and understated sophistication.

name: Brooks Brothers
description: The Brooks Brothers tartan, registered by Lochcarron of Scotland, is an exemplary representation of corporate tartanry in modern times. Originally designed for the esteemed American fashion house, Brooks Brothers, this distinctive tartan has been carefully crafted to evoke a sense of refined elegance and sophisticated style. With no specific historical or cultural origins attributed to its design in the registration notes, its modern creation remains a testament to the enduring appeal of traditional Scottish textiles, skillfully adapted for contemporary purposes.

name: Brotherhood of the Bear
description: The Bear tartan, designed by Christopher Horne in corporate category, embodies a sense of unity and solidarity with the International Bear Community. This distinctive eight-colour pattern is rooted in the symbolism of the Bear Brotherhood flag, showcasing a striking blend of colours that evoke a strong sense of identity and belonging. As an officially registered design, the Bear tartan is now available to those who wish to proudly represent their affiliation with this global community. By embracing this vibrant and meaningful tartan, individuals can demonstrate their honour and commitment to promoting awareness and understanding of bear welfare and conservation issues. This powerful and modern design serves as a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage and tradition, while also fostering a sense of unity among those who share a common cause.

name: Brough [default]
description: The Brough tartan is a distinctive Name tartan that holds deep personal significance for its designer, David Benton. This unique tartan variation is a re-creation of his grandfather's family heirloom, which dates back to the 1830s. The intricate pattern was painstakingly reconstructed by Eric Swinn and handwoven by Peter MacDonald in Perthshire, ensuring an authentic Scottish textile tradition. As a registered Name tartan, the Brough design is intended for personal use only, reflecting its exclusive familial connection. Its restrictions reflect this intimate association, while also serving as a testament to the enduring power of family heritage and the art of traditional Scottish weaving.

Brown of Castledean [default]

[AKA] Brown of Castledean

description: The Brown of Castledean tartan is a rich, earthy tribute to the heritage of Scotland's storied past. Labeled as "Other", its origins may lie beyond the traditional clan affiliations, but its connections run deep through the threads of history and tradition. Created in 1728, this timeless design is rooted in the stories of Thomas Brown, born in the picturesque village of Castledean, whose family legacy has been meticulously documented by textile historian Ingles Buchan. A modification of the historic Stewart tartan, the Brown of Castledean weaves together elements of Scotland's storied past, paying homage to the lives and lands of those who shaped its destiny, while also inviting wearers to draw upon their own sense of heritage and identity.

name:
Brown [default]
[AKA] Broun Grady
description: The Brown tartan is an enigmatic and historic textile pattern with deep roots in Scottish heritage, shrouded in mystery surrounding its origins. Originally registered under the name 'Brown' or, alternatively, as 'Grady', this sett has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition for over a century. The story behind its registration is as fascinating as it is complex: John Brown, Queen Victoria's trusted Highland servant, wore a tweed kilt featuring this very tartan, claiming that despite his Highlands origins, he had no connection to any specific clan or family tartan. This intriguing tale highlights the blurred lines between individual identity and tribal affiliation in Scotland's rich cultural landscape.

name: Bruce (Vestiarium Scoticum)
description: The Bruce tartan, a rich and storied fabric steeped in the history of Scotland's noble clans, is a chiefly sett that has been woven into the very fabric of the nation's identity. Dating back to 1571, this distinctive pattern is believed by Lord Bruce to have originated from an ancient weavers' chart, its origins rooted deep within the traditions of the Bruce family. The tartan was once proudly worn by the Cumming-Bruce clan, whose descendants went on to inherit it through the marriage of the 8th Earl to Mary Cumming-Bruce in the mid nineteenth century. Today, this iconic design continues to hold significance as a proud emblem of the Bruce legacy, its intricate threads weaving together a heritage that spans centuries and generations, connecting the past to the present with an unbreakable bond.

name: Bruce Hunting
description: The Bruce Hunting tartan is a unique and storied variation of the iconic Bruce clan tartan, distinguished by its distinctive reversal of red and green hues, reminiscent of the bold splashes of colour found in Scotland's majestic landscapes. Dating back to approximately 1939, when it was woven by Peter Anderson of Galashiels at the behest of Colonel Bruce, this hunting sett has been carefully preserved by the Scottish Tartans Society, whose threadcount analysis ensures its authenticity. Originally created for a special order, this tartan now proudly represents the heritage and tradition of Clan Bruce, with its black guards maintaining the classic white and yellow motifs of the traditional setts. This rich tapestry of history and craftsmanship is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's most storied clans.

name:
Bruce of Kinnaird [default]
[AKA] Bruce of Kinnaird
description: The Bruce of Kinnaird tartan is a rich and storied variation of the iconic Prince Charles Edward Stuart, rooted in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered with Wilsons of Bannockburn, this clan tartan tells the tale of the esteemed Bruces of Kinnaird, a powerful family believed to have originated from a 18th century coat still cherished by the Bruce legacy. Authenticated by Lord Bruce of Kinnaird in 1953, this tartan is an honourable tribute to the noble lineage, woven with a deep respect for Scotland's storied past. Though now woven at Anderson of Galashiels, the subtle nuances and historical depth of this tartan continue to pay homage to a bygone era, connecting wearers to generations of Scots who've cherished their family ties and cultural heritage.

name: Bruce Old
description: The Bruce Old tartan is a storied and historic clan tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's royal dynasty.
