As a corporate tartan, it was specifically created to represent Caledonian Oriental Airways, underscoring the airline's Scottish roots and heritage, while also evoking the exotic allure of the Orient, which the company sought to bridge with its international flights. With its unique blend of traditional Scottish colours and motifs, this tartan design pays homage to Scotland's enduring presence in global aviation, where tradition meets innovation.

name: Caledonian Society;
description: The Ancient Caledonian Society tartan is a rich and evocative woven treasure, hailing from a rare and esteemed source: the c.1786 coat of an anonymous member of London's Ancient Caledonian Society. This enigmatic tartan has been immortalised in registration notes by The Scottish Tartans Authority, providing a tangible link to Scotland's complex and storied past. With its unique colour palette and intricate sett, this tartan embodies the spirit of a long-forgotten era, when cultural heritage and tradition were deeply intertwined with the fabric of everyday life. As one of the 'Other' category's few examples, this tartan stands as a testament to the diversity and richness of Scotland's woven legacy, waiting to be unravelled and cherished by those with a passion for the country's storied past.

name: Caledonian Society of PEI
description: The Caledonian Society of Prince Edward Island tartan is a rich tapestry woven from the threads of history and heritage, created by James Logan in 1835 for the Highland Society of Prince Edward Island. This Corporate tartan was born out of a desire to forge connections between Scottish tradition and Canadian community, reflecting the Island's deep-rooted cultural affinity with Scotland. With its unique blend of colours and subtle nuances, this tartan honourably represents the Caledonian Club of P.E.I.'s evolution into an esteemed institution, bridging the past with the present. As a testament to Logan's skillful craftsmanship, the tartan remains a poignant reminder of the enduring ties between Scotland and Prince Edward Island, evoking a sense of pride and belonging among those who wear it.

name: Calgary #2
description: The Calgary Deerskin Trading Post tartan is a captivating fusion of traditional Scottish heritage and international flair, born out of an unusual yet fascinating discovery. Registered in fashion category, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the rich cultural exchange between Scotland and Switzerland during the 1970s. Its roots lie in a catalogue illustration from Deerskin Trading Post, which featured a shirt imported from Switzerland, highlighting the unique blend of global influences on traditional Scottish textiles. This intriguing design is now immortalised as part of the tartan's legacy, a testament to the dynamic spirit of Scottish fashion and the enduring appeal of its storied heritage.

name:
Calgary
[AKA] Big Red
description: The Calgary tartan is a vibrant and symbolic representation of the City of Calgary's rich heritage, as proudly showcased by its winning entry from the St Andrew-Caledonian Society of Calgary competition. This District tartan, designed by Donna Buie, skillfully weaves together a palette of colours that pay homage to Calgary's diverse roots: red for its iconic teams and landmarks, blue for the Bow and Elbow rivers, yellow for the sun-kissed wheatfields, grey for the majestic Rocky Mountains, black for the city's thriving oil industry, and white for the revered white stetson and the White Hatter Awards. As an official symbol of the City of Calgary, this tartan is freely worn by anyone, anywhere, and represents a deep connection to the city's history and traditions. First launched in 2003 on Prince's Island during Heritage Day ceremonies, the Calgary tartan has become an integral part of Canadian identity, proudly celebrating the unique blend of Scottish, Western, and prairie influences that make this city truly special.

name: Calgary Firefighters
description: The Calgary Firefighters tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate design born from the partnership of renowned designers Paul Wilkinson and Erin Shaw, with a storied history woven into its fabric. Specifically created for the Alberta Firefighters Pipe Band and the Calgary Fire Department Pipes and Drums, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the bravery and dedication of the firefighters serving in the city. With its bold colour palette, reminiscent of a blazing inferno, the tartan embodies the spirit of protection and service that defines these esteemed organisations. Wearing this tartan is an honour, not just for those who wear it, but also for the tradition and heritage of Scottish piping that lies at its heart.

name: Calgary University
description: The Calgary University tartan is a vibrant and prestigious corporate tartan that proudly represents the esteemed institution's heritage and values. Designed by Jim Odell, a talented artist with a deep connection to the university, this distinctive pattern weaves together the official colours of red, black, and gold in a striking design that evokes the spirit of academic excellence and cultural tradition. As an officially registered corporate tartan, it is widely adopted by the university's Pipe Band and Highland Dance Club, serving as a symbol of unity and identity among its members. With its rich colour palette and meticulous attention to detail, this tartan embodies the legacy of the University of Calgary, inviting wearers to showcase their honour and affiliation with one of Canada's most respected institutions.

name: California Dept. of Forestry
description: The California Department of Forestry tartan is a unique and functional design registered by Jan Crook in 1994, specifically created to commemorate the esteemed Leonard 'Shep' Shepherd, a Battalion Chief from Ceres, California. As a Corporate tartan, its primary purpose lies in promoting the identity and heritage of the California Department of Forestry, serving as a powerful emblem for the organisation's values and traditions. The registration notes reveal the tartan's strong connection to the forestry community, highlighting its origins as a tribute to Shep Shepherd's dedication to the field. This distinctive tartan now holds significant cultural value, reflecting the rich heritage of California's forestry sector and its enduring commitment to protecting the state's natural resources.

name: California Highway Patrol
description: This striking corporate tartan was carefully crafted by Jan Crook in honour of the California Highway Patrol, a symbol of safety and discipline on America's roads. Registered with the Tartan Educational Cultural Association in 1992, this distinctive pattern reflects the organisation's commitment to public service and order. As a Category Corporate design, it is intended for use by law enforcement agencies and other corporate entities seeking to convey a sense of professionalism and authority. Free from traditional clan or familial associations, this tartan stands alone as a badge of excellence in the world of corporate branding, evoking the values of vigilance, duty, and service that define the California Highway Patrol's noble mission.

name: California Professional Firefighters Association
description: California Firefighters is a vibrant corporate tartan, carefully crafted by Jan Crook to commemorate the bravery and dedication of firefighters in the Golden State. Registered with the Tartan Educational Cultural Association in 1995, this distinctive pattern pays tribute to the courageous men and women who risk their lives to protect communities from the flames. As an official Corporate tartan, it is worn with pride by those affiliated with the California Professional Firefighters Association, a testament to the enduring bond between service, loyalty, and camaraderie. With its bold colours and unique weave, this tartan design embodies the spirit of unity and resilience that defines the firefighting community, forging a lasting tribute to the heroes who embody it.

name: California Riverside University
description: The California Riverside, University of Corporate Tartan is a vibrant representation of the state's rich cultural heritage, woven with the university's esteemed history. Designed for the University of California Riverside Pipe Band, this distinctive tartan has become an integral part of the institution's identity and tradition. As a corporate tartan, it is now used to promote the university's brand and merchandise, while its controlled use by the Regents of the University of California Riverside ensures its authentic representation. Rooted in Scottish heritage, yet uniquely tied to the Golden State, this tartan embodies the fusion of American west coast spirit with traditional British craftsmanship. Its unique threads weave together a narrative of academic excellence, community pride, and time-honoured traditions.

name: California State
description: The California State tartan is a vibrant tribute to the Golden State's rich heritage and natural beauty, proudly worn by those with a connection to this sun-kissed region. Designed by renowned tartan experts Standing & Ferguson, this distinctive district tartan was born out of admiration for the landscape that inspired John Muir, the celebrated botanist and environmentalist who called California home. Adopted as the official state tartan in 2001, it showcases a bold blend of blues, greens, and yellows, reminiscent of California's majestic mountains, rolling hills, and vast wilderness areas. With its roots firmly planted in Scotland's rich tartan tradition, this modern design embodies the spirit of adventure and freedom that defines the American West, while also paying homage to Muir's enduring legacy as a champion of conservation and environmental stewardship.

name: Callaghan [default]
description: The Callaghan tartan is a unique and poignant creation by Peter Callaghan, responding to the absence of an existing Scottish or Irish tartan bearing his surname. By drawing inspiration from Scotland's dark blue hues and Ireland's emerald green, he wove together a complex and evocative design that pays homage to both countries' rich cultural heritage. Accentuated with subtle touches of red and yellow, this tartan tells the story of an individual's complex identity, one that is deeply rooted in Celtic tradition yet distinctively modern. As a Name tartan, it carries the weight of its wearer's ancestry, making it an important part of their personal heritage narrative.

name: Callaway Golf
description: The Callaway Corporate Tartan, designed by Arthur Bell for Scotch Tweeds in 1982, embodies the dynamic spirit of modern golf, reflecting the global reach and innovation of the renowned Callaway Golf company. As a corporate tartan, its purpose is to evoke professionalism and prestige, while also paying homage to the rich heritage of Scotland's iconic textile art form. Originally created to adorn golf apparel and accessories for one of the world's leading golf brands, this tartan has become synonymous with excellence and performance on the green. Its distinctive pattern, which weaves together a complex interplay of blues, reds, and yellows, pays testament to Arthur Bell's skill as a textile designer and his understanding of the cultural significance of tartan in Scottish tradition. Today, the Callaway Corporate Tartan continues to be worn by golf enthusiasts around the world, serving as a badge of honour for those who share its passion for the game.

name: Callum
description: The Callum tartan, designed by John Bain for Scotch House of London in 1980, embodies the timeless elegance of Scottish fashion heritage. As one of a pair of matching geometric patterns with distinct colour palettes, Callum showcases its technical precision alongside a deep cultural resonance. The striking similarities to Menzies and Vestiarium Scoticum No. 196 serve as testament to the enduring influence of Scotland's rich tartan traditions on fashion design. This Fashion tartan is a masterful fusion of form and function, evoking the intricate patterns woven by skilled Highlanders for centuries past. As a tribute to Scotland's storied heritage, the Callum tartan serves as a fitting representation of British style and craftsmanship, expertly marrying tradition with modern flair.

name: Cambridge
description: The Cambridge tartan is a vibrant and sophisticated fashion tartan, woven with pride by Paul Taylor of Stuart University Tailors in this iconic city. Its distinctive colours tell the story of Cambridge's rich heritage: dark blue evokes the historic city centre, while green nods to the lush parks that bring life to its streets. The gentle pale blue represents the River Cam, whose tranquil waters have been a constant companion to the city since ancient times. Black threads evoke the bridging of the river, symbolising connection and resilience. In bold contrast, the single red line shines as a beacon for academia, while the yellow thread whispers secrets of the thriving silicon fen industry that has driven innovation in the region. This captivating tartan is a modern testament to Cambridge's enduring spirit, blending tradition with contemporary flair to create a truly distinctive and stylish fabric.

name: Cameron Black & Red
description: The Cameron, Black & Red tartan is a timeless and iconic representation of Scottish heritage, bearing the name of one of Scotland's most storied clans. This complex and intriguing design, classified under Clan/Family, was registered without an attributed designer, suggesting its origins may be shrouded in history. Notably, restrictions surround this tartan, with limited information available about its intended use or creation date. Nevertheless, a specimen of the Cameron, Black & Red is proudly displayed in the Inverness Museum's collection, serving as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry. This traditional tartan weaves together elements of Scottish identity and tradition, inviting wearers to connect with their roots and pay homage to a storied legacy that spans centuries.

name: Cameron Hose
description: The Cameron, Hose #1 tartan is a rich and storied design, steeped in Scotland's vibrant heritage. This traditional tartan is classified as 'Other', meaning it doesn't align with the typical clan or name-based registrations, instead falling under a unique category that highlights its distinctive characteristics. Woven to perfection, this tartan features diagonal stripes of deep blue, dark green, and muted red hues, evoking the elegance of 18th-century Scottish stockings - known as 'hose' in their time. The National Museum of Scotland in Edinburgh proudly showcases a surviving example of this hosiery, a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of our ancestors. Although its original purpose was not strictly tied to a specific clan or family, the Cameron tartan remains an important part of Scotland's cultural tapestry, a celebration of traditional textiles that continue to inspire and captivate us today.

name: Cameron Hose #2
description: The Cameron, Hose #2 tartan is an enduring embodiment of Scottish heritage and tradition, woven from the rich threads of history and family legacy. As part of the Clan Cameron collection, this distinctive tartan holds a special place in the hearts of those bearing the Cameron name, evoking a sense of honour and pride that has been passed down through generations. Created by the skilled weavers at Wilsons of Bannockburn, a renowned firm established in the late 18th century near Stirling, this tartan is steeped in tradition and culture. Although its designer remains anonymous, the tartan's authenticity is confirmed by its registration notes, which attest to its origins as part of the esteemed collection at Edinburgh's National Museum of Antiquities. This tartan design continues to hold significance for those seeking to connect with their ancestral roots, making it a treasured possession for families and individuals alike.

name: Cameron Hunting
description: The Cameron Hunting tartan is a storied and intricate design steeped in Scottish heritage, evoking the proud traditions of the ancient Camerons. As one of Scotland's most iconic clan tartans, this design is closely tied to the esteemed House of Cameron, whose history stretches back centuries. Its resemblance to the earlier Cameron of Locheil Hunting, with an additional third red line, is noted in esteemed sources such as the Vestiarium Scoticum, lending credence to its authenticity. This rich and complex pattern is a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scotland's finest weavers, whose artistry has been passed down through generations. As a cherished emblem of Scottish identity, the Cameron Hunting tartan continues to weave its way into the fabric of our cultural heritage, connecting us to the storied past of the Camerons and their enduring legacy.

name:
Cameron of Erracht [default]
[AKA] Cameron of Erracht
description: The Cameron of Erracht tartan is an enduring emblem of Scottish military heritage, born from the bravery and loyalty of the 79th Cameron Highlanders raised by Alan Cameron of Erracht in 1793. As a Military tartan, its significance lies not only in its technical characteristics, but also in its connection to the clan's history and tradition. This distinctive design, with its intricate patterns and rich hues, was originally created for the regiment and has since been adopted as an honourable representation of the Cameron family. The tartan's association with the 79th Cameron Highlanders serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's military past, where courage and sacrifice were forged in the fires of battle.

name: Cameron of Erracht #2
description: The Cameron of Erracht tartan, registered by the prestigious West Coast Woolen Mill, is a timeless fashion favourite steeped in Scottish heritage. With its rich, dark blue and red hues evoking the rugged coastlines of the west, this iconic tartan embodies the bravery and resilience of the Clan Cameron, one of Scotland's most storied families. As a Fashion registration, the Cameron of Erracht tartan is free to be worn with pride by anyone seeking to add a touch of Scottish flair to their wardrobe. With no restrictions on its use, this majestic tartan invites wearers to tap into the rich history and tradition that defines Scottish identity.

name:
Cameron of Erracht Dress
[AKA] Cameron of Erracht; Dress
description: The Cameron of Erracht Dress is a storied tartan bearing testament to the rich heritage of Clan Cameron, one of Scotland's most esteemed clans. With its intricate pattern of blues, greens, and yellows, this traditional tartan weaves together threads of history and culture, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. Dating back to an uncertain period between 1930 and 1950, with some samples bearing marks from the renowned MacGregor-Hastie collection, this tartan's origins are steeped in tradition and family legacy. Its design is a masterful blend of subtle earth tones and vibrant hues, echoing the clan's storied past as guardians of Scotland's wilderness and its people.

name:
Cameron of Locheil [default]
[AKA] Cameron of Locheil
description: The Cameron of Locheil tartan, an esteemed family crest within Scotland's rich tapestry, boasts a storied history dating back to the late 18th century. This iconic plaid, woven by William Wilson & Son Bannockburn in the early 1800s, bears the mark of its origins as a variant of George Chalmers' famous portrait of Gentle Lochiel at Achnacarry, albeit with some notable discrepancies discovered through recent research. Rooted in Clan Cameron heritage, this tartan is steeped in tradition and identity, signifying allegiance to one of Scotland's most noble families. Its enduring presence in family kilt wear, ceremonial attire, and cultural iconography attests to the lasting significance of the Cameron of Locheil name, weaving a tale of history, resilience, and proud heritage.

name:
Lochiel
[AKA] Munro #2
[AKA] Cameron of Lochiel; #2
description: The Lochiel tartan, registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a quintessential example of Scottish clan heritage, woven into the very fabric of history. This intricate pattern, first featured in their 1819 Key Pattern Book, showcases the esteemed Clan MacDonald's rich tradition and cultural significance. The Lochiel tartan holds pride of place among family clans, reflecting the proud history and legacy of the MacDonalds. Its inclusion within this historic key pattern book underscores its enduring relevance as a symbol of Scottish identity and heritage, carefully crafted by skilled weavers like Wilsons of Bannockburn to preserve the traditions of the past.

name:
Cameron of Lochiel Hunting
[AKA] Cameron of Lochiel; Hunting
description: The Cameron of Lochiel (Hunting) tartan is a majestic and storied design, steeped in the rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands' most revered clan. Created in the 1940s by esteemed weaver J.G. MacKay, this tartan pays tribute to the hunting traditions of the Camerons, whose ancestral home lies alongside Lochiel's tranquil waters. The Hunting category designation underscores the design's roots in the clan's aristocratic history and sporting pursuits. Authored by MacKay, this tartan was first unveiled at the Cameron Gathering at Achnacarry in 1956, earning the seal of approval from the then chief, a momentous milestone in its development. As an officially registered tartan, the Cameron of Lochiel (Hunting) is now woven into the fabric of Scottish identity, its intricate patterns and rich colours evoking the rugged beauty and timeless values of the Highlands' most iconic clan.

name: Cameron [default]
description: The Cameron tartan, registered in 1947, is a storied Scottish heritage fabric steeped in Clan history and tradition. This iconic sett was first illustrated in the seminal 'Vestiarium Scoticum', a collection of Scottish tartans, and has since become synonymous with the Camerons, a clan with close ties to Lochaber. The tartan's origins may be linked to the MacFees, a branch of the larger Highland clan network, adding depth to its significance as a symbol of ancestral heritage and familial identity. With its distinctive pattern, the Cameron tartan proudly evokes the rich history and cultural traditions of Scotland's Highlands, inviting wearers to embody the values and legacy of this storied clan.

name: Campbell Dress
description: Campbell Dress #1 is an exquisite example of a traditional Scottish clan tartan, steeped in history and heritage. Originating from 1880, its dress version was first introduced by J Claude Freres et Cie, a Parisian company, although the 12th Duke of Argyll ultimately rejected it as an official Campbell tartan. This peculiarity notwithstanding, the design has endured, featured alongside other clan patterns in notable publications such as H Whyte's seminal works 'The Scottish Clans and Their Tartan' and others, including 'The Tartans of the Clans and Septs of Scotland'. As a member of Clan Campbell, this tartan holds significance not only for its familial connections but also as a testament to the rich cultural legacy of Scotland's ancient clans, where tradition, identity, and community are woven together like the threads of a fine tartan fabric.

name: Campbell Hunting
description: The Campbell Hunting tartan is a storied fashion pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, though its origins may lie across the Atlantic, in the cosmopolitan city of Toronto, Canada. Registration notes suggest it emerged around 1945, likely as a tribute to the Campbell Clan's proud hunting traditions. As a Category Fashion tartan, this design has been adopted by those who celebrate its stylish and evocative charm. With its distinctive colour palette - featuring rich blues, earthy greens, and subtle browns - the Campbell Hunting tartan embodies the spirit of Scotland's rugged landscape and the thrill of the hunt. Although the identity of its creator is lost to history, this tartan remains a testament to the enduring power of Scottish design and tradition.

name: Campbell Marquis of Lorne
description: The Campbell, Marquis of Lorne tartan is a poignant commemorative design steeped in Scottish heritage, worn to honour the legacy of Charles MacDonald, 6th Duke of Argyll's, title as Marquess of Lorne, held from 1892 until his death in 1928. Registered as a commemorative tartan, its creation pays tribute to this prominent figure's distinguished military career and philanthropic pursuits. Woven with precision using the traditional Scottish technique, this tartan's intricate patterns evoke the rich history of Clan Campbell, whose crest is emblazoned on the Marquess's coat of arms. With a threadcount taken from a sample in the esteemed Provost MacBean collection, held by the Scottish Tartans Society Archive, this tartan stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's noble clans and their place within the country's storied past.

name:
Campbell of Argyle #3
[AKA] Campbell of Argyle; #3
description: The Campbell of Argyll tartan is a proud embodiment of Scottish heritage and tradition, its complex yet intricate design echoing the rich history of the Campbell clan. Registered as part of Scotland's cherished cultural legacy, this tartan is steeped in family honour and distinguished distinction, dating back to 1850 when it was first published by the Smiths of Mauchline with the explicit authorisation of the 7th Duke of Argyll. With its distinctive white lines set against a deeper blue background, this sett is said to be a 'differenced' variant, reserved for personal use by the clan chief. As part of the Clan Campbell's storied past, this tartan holds significant cultural and symbolic value, evoking a sense of heritage and tradition that continues to inspire wearers to this day.

name:
Campbell of Argyll [default]
[AKA] Campbell of Argyll
description: The Campbell of Argyll #2 tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's most esteemed clans, with its intricate patterns woven into the very fabric of tradition. This iconic family tartan has been worn by generations of the 6th Duke of Argyll, a storied figure in Scottish history, and is now recognised as an integral part of Campbell clan identity. Woven with precision and passion, this tartan design embodies the values of loyalty, courage, and resilience that have defined the Campbell family for centuries. As a registered clan tartan, it holds a special place in the hearts of those who proudly wear their ancestral heritage on their sleeves - literally. With its complex interplay of colours, carefully balanced to reflect the nuances of Scottish tweed, this tartan is a true masterpiece of traditional weaving that continues to inspire and unite Campbells around the world.

name:
Campbell of Argyll 1815 variant
[AKA] Campbell of Argyll; 1815 variant
description: The Campbell of Argyll tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's storied clans, its distinctive pattern bearing witness to the intricate history of the Campbell family's enduring legacy. Originating in the post-rebellion era, when Wilson's of Bannockburn held sway over military supply, this sett was born from the very heart of Scottish tradition. Its inclusion in esteemed collections such as the Cockburn Collection and Vestiarium Scoticum speaks to its significance, alongside fellow clan tartans that have been woven into the fabric of Scotland's cultural identity. With no designer credited with its creation, it is a reminder that some of the most iconic patterns in tartanry have their roots in tradition rather than design, reflecting instead the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scotland's weavers through the ages.

name:
Campbell of Argyll no guards
[AKA] Campbell of Argyll; no guards
description: The Campbell of Argyll tartan is an enduring representation of Scottish heritage, with its origins rooted in the clan's rich history. Registered by Lochcarron of Scotland, this traditional tartan was originally designed without black guards on the white and yellow stripes, allowing for a more distinctive appearance that sets it apart from the family's plain Campbell tartan. Despite some controversy surrounding its introduction, particularly due to the Sixth Duke of Argyll's decision to introduce the white line, which he deemed gave him an air of distinction as chief, the tartan has persisted in production and remains a cherished symbol of Clan Campbell identity. Today, it continues to be worn with pride by those who honour their ancestral heritage, serving as a tangible connection to Scotland's storied past.

name:
Campbell of Armaddie [default]
[AKA] Campbell of Armaddie
description: The Campbell of Armaddie tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's most iconic clans. Registered in recognition of John 'of the Bank' Campbell, the 16th Chief of Clan Campbell, whose portrait now adorns the walls of the Royal Bank of Scotland, this timeless plaid has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage. As an "Other" tartan, it defies categorisation, existing outside the traditional clan structures that defined its predecessors. Its origins rooted in the 18th century, this majestic design embodies the history and tradition of Clan Campbell, whose motto 'Ne Obliviscaris' (Thou shalt not be forgotten) echoes through every subtle colour variation and deliberate pattern stroke. A true piece of Scottish identity, the Campbell of Armaddie tartan is a lasting tribute to the clan's storied past, its beauty and significance forever woven into the very heart of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry.

name:
Campbell of Braemar [default]
[AKA] Braemar District
[AKA] Braemar Camel
[AKA] Campbell of Braemar
description: The Braemar, Camel tartan is a storied fabric with a rich history rooted in Scottish heritage. Originally designed by the esteemed Scott Brothers of Hawick, this fashion tartan was once sold under two distinct names: 'Braemar, Camel' and 'Campbell of Braemar'. This dichotomy reflects the fluidity of tartan naming conventions, which often blur the lines between clan affiliations and individual designs. The Braemar, Camel tartan is a testament to the intricate social hierarchies of the past, where clan identities and territorial designations became synonymous with status and tradition. Today, this tartan remains a staple in fashion circles, evoking images of rugged Scottish landscapes and timeless, authentic style, much like the mist-shrouded hills of Braemar itself.

name:
Campbell of Breadalbane [default]
[AKA] Campbell of Breadalbane
description: The Campbell of Breadalbane tartan is a rich and storied heritage pattern, steeped in military history and tradition. Registration notes reveal its origins as a faithful reproduction of the regimental uniform worn by the Fencibles, a regiment of Scottish soldiers formed in 1793 and disbanded in 1802. Designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, this tartan is a testament to the bravery and loyalty of the Campbell clan, one of Scotland's most illustrious families. The pattern's intricate details and authentic colours, confirmed by contemporary illustrations and Major Campbell's regimental uniform, make it an essential piece of Scottish heritage. As a Military tartan, the Campbell of Breadalbane tartan holds significant cultural value, evoking the proud history of Scotland's military traditions and the enduring legacy of the Fencibles.

name:
Campbell of Cawdor [default]
[AKA] Campbell of Cawdor
description: The Campbell of Cawdor tartan is a rich and storied heritage pattern, steeped in Scottish tradition and family history. As an authorised sett by MacCailien Mor, the present Clan Chief, it carries significant weight within the Campbell clan. This military-inspired variation was originally designated as Argyle, with later additions to its title in 1798 and 1819, before being formally codified as 'Campbell of Cawdor' in esteemed works such as W & A Smith's "The Authenticated Tartan of the Clans and Families of Scotland" in 1850. This tartan has been an integral part of clan identity for generations, embodying the values and legacy of the Campbell family, who have long been associated with the historic Cawdor Castle in Inverness-shire.

name:
Campbell of Cawdor Dress
[AKA] Campbell of Cawdor; Dress
description: The Campbell of Cawdor Dress tartan is a storied and enduring representation of Scottish heritage, with its rich history tied to one of Scotland's most esteemed clans. This traditional clan tartan, designated for the Campbell family, has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition since the 1930s, as part of the renowned MacGregor-Hastie collection. Today, it is proudly preserved within the Scottish Tartans Society archive, a testament to its enduring significance. The Campbell of Cawdor Dress tartan weaves together a narrative of loyalty, honour, and family pride, evoking images of majestic castle grandeur and rolling Highland glens. Its subtle colour palette and intricate texture speak to the skilled hands of Scotland's finest weavers, while its cultural resonance continues to captivate those who cherish the country's rich history and tradition.

name:
Campbell of Glenlyon [default]
[AKA] Campbell of Glenlyon
description: The Campbell of Glenlyon tartan is a revered family crest that embodies the rich history and heritage of the Clan Campbell, one of Scotland's most storied and esteemed families. Registered as a distinctive family tartan, it holds a special place in Scottish tradition, signifying the loyalty and pride of its bearers. The intricate design, woven from threads of subtle green hues and earthy tones, is said to be based on an original sample book by James MacKinlay, whose painstaking hand-coloured stripes provide a window into the past. However, this tartan's beauty belies a crucial fact: it is restricted in its use, reserved exclusively for members of the Clan Campbell and their direct descendants. This distinction serves as a poignant reminder of the tartan's role as a tangible link to Scotland's illustrious past, honouring the traditions and legacy of one of the country's most iconic clans.

name:
Campbell of Lochawe [default]
[AKA] Campbell of Lochawe
description: The Campbell of Loch Awe tartan holds a special place within Scotland's rich tapestry, its history woven into the fabric of the country's military heritage. This distinctive sett was once worn by the Medical Officer of the 42nd Regiment, a notable example of its significance being captured in a c.1770 painting that has been meticulously documented. While it may be a 'simplified manufacturers version', this tartan is undoubtedly rooted in tradition and proudly displays the Campbell clan's association with Loch Awe. Its origins, however, are shrouded in mystery, leaving its true designer unknown to us. Nevertheless, the Scottish Tartans Society's archives have provided a tantalising glimpse into its past, courtesy of Alastair Campbell's research and the collection of James Mackinlay, a renowned tartan collector between the wars. Despite restrictions on its use, this tartan remains an evocative symbol of Scotland's storied military history and the enduring legacy of Clan Campbell.

name:
Campbell of Lochlane [default]
[AKA] Campbell of Lochlane
description: The Campbell of Lochlane tartan is a proud emblem of Scottish heritage, its origins shrouded in mystery since it was registered as a coat of arms in 1730. This distinctive tartan, designated for the Campbell family of Lochlane, is part of a broader tradition of clan-specific patterns that have been woven into the very fabric of Scotland's identity. With no official designer credited, the design is believed to have been derived from the coat depicted in the 1730 portrait of Sheriff Campbell of Lochlane, which immortalised the tartan as an integral part of his regalia. As such, this tartan holds significance not just for the Campbells, but for all those who wear it with honour, connecting them to a rich history and tradition that spans centuries. Its place within the 'Other' category highlights its unique status as a familial emblem rather than a strictly clan-based design, setting it apart from more traditional tartans while still paying homage to Scotland's rich weaving heritage.

name:

name: Canine All Dogs

Registration notes proudly declare its purpose as a tribute to all dogs, honouring their unwavering loyalty and affectionate nature. This tasteful recognition of our four-legged friends is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish tradition and the country's long-standing affinity for dogs as beloved family members and loyal companions.

As an official corporate tartan, it serves as a badge of honour for the club, symbolising tradition, unity, and pride among fans, while also providing a unique opportunity for corporate wearers to show their affiliation with this beloved Welsh institution.

First documented by Scottish Tartans Society in 1907, when Carmichael of Artherstone sealed a sample in the Highland Society's Collection, this tartan has undergone slight variations in proportion over time, notably in its black and green stripes. As a testament to Scotland's rich cultural legacy, the Carmichael tartan embodies tradition, honour, and family pride, making it an enduring symbol of heritage and identity for those who bear the name.

name: Carnegie #2
description: The Carnegie #3 tartan is a rich tapestry of Scotland's storied past, woven with reverence for one of its most esteemed clans. name: Carnegie Check

name: Carnegie Dress
description: The Carnegie Dress tartan is a vibrant and elegant representation of Scottish heritage, hailing from the esteemed House of Carnegie. As part of Hugh Macpherson's oeuvre as a kiltmaker in Edinburgh, this dress tartan was designed for dancing and other informal occasions, its beauty and energy evoking the spirited gatherings of clan gatherings past. A testament to Scotland's rich tradition of textile craftsmanship and family identity, the Carnegie Dress tartan is a cherished relic of the country's storied past, its very existence woven into the fabric of the nation's history and cultural heritage.

name: Casely [default]

name: Caskie #2

The intricate weave, featuring a deep blue outer colour scheme with darker tramlines, evokes the rich heritage of Scotland's healthcare system, while also symbolising hope and recovery for those who wear it. As a corporate tartan, Recovery is designed to be worn proudly by employees and affiliated organisations, serving as a badge of honour that supports a vital cause.

name: Castlecraig Renewal Clinics Recovery Dress
description: The Recovery Dress tartan, designed by Peter McCann, embodies the spirit of resilience and renewal, specifically championed by Castle Craig Renewal Clinics Ltd, a pioneering residential hospital in Scotland's Scottish Borders. This distinctive tartan serves as a powerful emblem of support for those seeking recovery, while also paying tribute to Castle Craig's vital work in addressing addictive disease.

name: Castlecraig Renewal Clinics Recovery Hunting

This unique tartan design not only pays homage to the area's striking geological formations but also incorporates the vibrant fuchsia colour, reminiscent of the wildflowers that bloom during the summer months, adding a touch of warmth and character to the palette. Designed by William & Colin Chalmers, the tartan's intricate patterns weave together traditional threads of local culture, paying tribute to the region's rich history and geography. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds special significance for those connected to Kilsyth, spanning generations across continents as far afield as Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and America. By embracing this vibrant and distinctive design, wearers can proudly express their connection to this beloved Scottish town, while also paying homage to the rich traditions that have shaped its identity over time.

name: Chalmers (William) personal; European Union
description: This striking Fashion tartan, designed by William D. Chalmers, pays tribute to European unity and the rich history of the continent. Inspired by the iconic 12-star European Union flag, the tartan weaves together the colours of the flag's blue background, red, white, and black. A small red line subtly weaves through the design, symbolising the sacrifices made on European soil throughout recorded history, while a larger white line represents the pursuit of peace. As a testament to unity and resilience, this Fashion tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Europe's shared heritage and values.

name: Chattan #3

Originally registered by the Scottish Tartan Society as a variation of STR #622, this sett has been tweaked to redefine the classic pattern's palette, toning down the prominent red hue in the first pivot and eliminating the white thread that once added subtle contrast. This thoughtful adaptation preserves the essence of Clan Chattan's proud tradition while introducing an air of understated sophistication, much like the subtle nuances found in the intricate brogue patterns woven by Scotland's skilled tartan weavers over centuries past.

This intricate design, woven with precision and care, embodies the proud traditions of its namesake clan, evoking a sense of honour, loyalty, and heritage that has been passed down through generations. Its registration as a legitimate Clan tartan ensures its continued association with the Chisholm family, allowing wearers to proudly don their clan's colours, while also paying tribute to Scotland's proud textile traditions.

name: Christie [default]

Weaving these threads together, Murison-McGowan's masterful design embodies the spirit of Christmas, its beauty and warmth reminiscent of the nativity story that lies at its heart.
