name: Clackson
description: The Clackson tartan is a richly woven tribute to Scottish heritage, commissioned by Dr Stephen Gregory Clackson himself in honour of his daughter's birth in Aberdeen. This Name tartan is steeped in tradition, bearing the esteemed armorial bearings of its designer - a unique distinction that sets it apart from other tartans. As such, it holds significant cultural value for all bearers who share the same maternal line or possess written permission from Dr Clackson or his heirs. Its intricate design tells a story of family legacy and personal significance, reflecting the enduring bond between Scotland's traditional textile heritage and the lives of those who wear its threads.

name: Clan Crest Textiles Loch Morar District
description: Loch Morar, a captivating fashion tartan, evokes the serene and majestic beauty of Scotland's iconic lochs. As part of the esteemed Clan Crest Textiles collection, this design pays homage to the country's rich heritage and cultural identity. With its precise, repeating pattern of blues, greens, and earthy tones, Loch Morar embodies the rugged yet refined essence of Scottish tradition. Although not attributed to a specific designer, the subtle nuances in its weave suggest the careful attention to detail characteristic of traditional tartan craftsmanship. With no restrictions on its use, this stylish tartan invites those who wear it to embody the timeless values of Scottish honour and resilience, seamlessly blending into any ensemble with elegance and sophistication.

name: Clan Crest Textiles Loch Rannoch District
description: Loch Rannoch #2 is a distinctive fashion tartan, carefully crafted by Mrs P J Thompson for Clan Crest Textiles, with its bold and vibrant hues evoking the majestic Scottish landscape. Originally designed as a 'fashion' tartan, it has since gained acceptance as a District Tartan, reflecting its widespread appeal and enduring popularity among fashion enthusiasts and Scottish heritage enthusiasts alike. This striking design showcases Mrs Thompson's skillful interpretation of traditional tartan principles, with its precise colourwork and carefully considered sett arrangement. Featured in the esteemed Johnston Collection of the Scottish Tartans Authority, Loch Rannoch #2 is a testament to the power of Scottish textiles to inspire and unite people across the globe, connecting wearers to their heritage and the natural beauty of Scotland's most iconic lochs.

name: Clergy Wilson's
description: The Clark of Ulva tartan, created by renowned Scottish weaving house Wilsons of Bannockburn in their esteemed Pattern Book No. 4 circa 1840, is a quintessential representation of Clan heritage and tradition. This storied tartan tells the tale of the illustrious Clark family, whose name has been woven into Scotland's fabric for generations. The intricate design, carefully crafted to adhere to the strict standards of Scottish tartans, boasts a rich palette of blues and greens, evoking the rolling hills and misty lochs of Ulva, a picturesque Isle in the Outer Hebrides. With its precise weave and adherence to traditional clan guidelines, this tartan embodies the honour and pride of the Clark family's legacy, waiting to be worn by descendants and enthusiasts alike with reverence for Scotland's storied past.

name: Cleghorn [default]
description: The Cleghorn tartan is a poignant family heirloom with deep roots in Scottish heritage, woven into existence by renowned designer DC Dalgliesh in 19th-century Scotland. This Clan tartan, bearing the surname of the esteemed Cleghorn family, embodies the traditions and values of its bearers, evoking a sense of honour and loyalty that has been passed down through generations. As a testament to the craftsmanship of Dalgliesh's skilled hands, this tartan is now carefully prepared for weaving by his own company, ensuring an exact replica can be crafted with precision. While specific details about the design are not recorded in the registration notes, its significance as a family legacy is undeniable, reflecting the enduring spirit of Scottish clans and the rich tapestry of their history.

name: Cleland [default]
description: The Cleland tartan is a proud representation of Scottish heritage and tradition, woven with meticulous care by master weaver D C Dalgliesh of Selkirk. Designed specifically for those bearing the name Cleland, Clelland, Cleeland, Clealand, Kneland, Kneeland, Niland, or MacClelland, this tartan is deeply rooted in history and forester's lore, drawing inspiration from the Douglas sett. The blue hue of the tartan is a nod to the Cleland Coat of Arms, signifying a strong connection to the founding families of Clan Cleland Society. This Name tartan, created by renowned designer John Hocknull in 1989, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish clans and their lasting legacy. As one dons this tartan, they carry forward the honour of their ancestors and join a proud tradition of foresters, farmers, and families who have worn it with distinction for generations.

name:
Clergy #2
[AKA] Clergy (Clans Originaux)
description: This ancient Clan tartan, known as Clergy Green lines #1, whispers tales of Scotland's storied past. Dating back to the late 19th century, its origins can be traced to a mysterious specimen first recorded in 'Clans Originaux', a swatch book published by J. Claude Fres Et Cie, circa 1880 and discovered in Paris. This subtle yet distinctive design is steeped in heritage, echoing the traditions of Scotland's esteemed Clergy families. As a Clan tartan, it bears witness to the rich cultural legacy of its bearers, evoking the values of loyalty, duty, and community that have defined Scottish history for centuries. With its muted green lines woven into a timeless fabric, this tartan design remains an enduring testament to Scotland's complex and multifaceted identity.

name: Clark (Clergy)
description: This distinctive tartan, bearing the name "Clergy" or "Clark", holds a significant place in Scotland's rich heritage. Registration notes suggest it is an older variant, with subtle variations existing between its commonly seen form and an earlier "version" referred to as 'Clark', distinguished by the change in the pivot of double light lines from blue to black. Characterised by light blue lines on a predominantly dark background, this tartan was originally associated with the Clergy or Clark family. Although no designer is attributed to its creation, its enduring presence in Scottish textiles testifies to the significance of this particular design within the country's traditional weaving tradition.

name:
Clergy Episcopal
[AKA] Clergy Samuel Seabury
description: The Episcopal Clergy tartan is a stirring tribute to the esteemed members of the clergy who have served with distinction, particularly within the Scottish Episcopal church and its American counterpart. Designed by Rev. John B. Pahls in 1996, this corporate tartan was created to commemorate the bicentenary of the death of Samuel Seabury, the pioneering first bishop of the Episcopal Church in America, and to pay honour to the clergy who have followed in his footsteps. The tartan's subtle yet vibrant hues are woven into a rich tapestry that reflects the values of tradition, faith, and service, evoking the enduring legacy of these dedicated professionals. While not specific to a particular Scottish clan, this tartan is an important part of corporate heritage, worn by organisations such as churches and dioceses to signify their connection to the Episcopal tradition.

name: Clergy (Grey)
description: The Clergy (Breacan naân Clearach) tartan is a revered family tartan, born from the meticulous study of Scotland's rich heritage by James Logan in 1831. Originally misattributed to Wilsons of Bannockburn as 'Priest tartan', Logan's Breacan naân Clerach pattern was later copied and adapted, but its true origins remain a testament to the complexities of Scottish textile history. This distinctive tartan features a striking blue and black colour scheme, giving it a sombre yet dignified appearance that resonates with the noble traditions of Scotland's clergy. As a Clan/Family tartan, Clergy is reserved for those who claim a familial connection to this storied lineage, imbuing its wearers with a deep sense of pride and historical continuity.

name: Clark [default]
description: The Clark tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish clan tradition, bearing witness to the enduring legacy of its namesake family. This iconic tartan design, with its distinctive light blue and dark blue hues, has been woven into the fabric of Scottish history, evoking the proud identity of those who bear the Clark surname. As a Clan tartan, it is deeply rooted in the social and familial bonds of the Scottish Highlands, where kinship and loyalty were once forged through the intricate patterns of tartan weaving. The subtle variations between this and its Clergy counterpart serve as a poignant reminder of the evolution of tartan design over time, while the Clark's enduring popularity speaks to the timeless appeal of Scotland's most iconic textile tradition.

name: Clifford [default]
description: The Clifford tartan is a rich and storied Scottish heritage textile, specifically designed for the distinguished family surname Clifford. Registered in 1999 by Linda Clifford, a talented weaver from Bryant Pond, Maine, USA, this tartan was commissioned to commemorate the proud legacy of those bearing the name. With its intricate patterns and carefully selected colours, the Clifford tartan is a testament to the enduring tradition of clan tartans, which have long served as symbols of family honour and identity. As such, it holds great significance not only for the Cliffsords themselves, but also for any individual who proudly wears the tartan, paying tribute to their connection to this storied lineage and the rich cultural heritage that underpins it.

name: Cochrane Azure
description: The Cochrane Azure tartan holds a storied place within Scotland's rich heritage, its intricate pattern weaving a narrative of history and tradition. This rare and distinctive tartan, revived by the 15th Earl of Dundonald in 1985, is an exact recreation of the original worn by the 12th Earl of Dundonald, making it an extraordinary piece of clan identity. Reserved for special occasions such as evening wear, this tartan demands respect, evoking a sense of occasion and gravitas that resonates deeply with Scottish tradition. As a family tartan, Cochrane Azure is imbued with the honourable legacy of its namesake clan, making it a treasured choice for those who proudly wear their heritage on their sleeves – literally in this case, through the threads of this majestic blue-and-green tartan.

name: Cochrane Hunting
description: The Cochrane Hunting Tartan, expertly woven with precision and care, embodies the rich heritage of Clan Cochrane's noble hunting traditions. Designed by the esteemed 15th Earl of Dundonald in 2008, this vibrant tartan is specifically intended for informal day wear, evoking a sense of rustic elegance and camaraderie among those who wear it. With its natural dye-inspired colours carefully selected to evoke the earthy tones of Scotland's rolling hills, this tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Clan Cochrane's ancestors, who once roamed these same lands, pursuing game with skill and honour. As recommended by the current chief in 2015, this tartan is now cherished by members of the clan for special occasions, and its gentle wearability makes it an excellent choice for everyday wear that still pays tribute to Scotland's storied past.

name: Cochrane [default]
description: The Cochrane tartan is a quintessential representation of Scottish heritage and clan identity, steeped in intrigue and storied history. Originally misattributed to the Cochrane family, this tartan's true origins lie shrouded in mystery until the 14th Earl of Dundonald, Chief of Clan Douglas (not Cochrane), wielded his authority to alter the design in 1974, significantly reducing the number of red lines from four to three. A reversal of this change occurred a decade later, with the tartan's sett reverting to its original form under the 15th Earl. Today, while all commercially available samples retain the modified version featuring four red lines, enthusiasts and historians alike continue to be fascinated by the Cochrane tartan's complex past, its symbolism resonating deeply within the cultural fabric of Scotland.

name:
Cockburn of Ormiston Dress
[AKA] Cockburn of Ormiston; Dress
description: The Cockburn of Ormiston Dress tartan, a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's esteemed families, is a rare and enigmatic pattern steeped in history. Once proudly worn by the noble Cockburn clan, its origins date back to a bygone era when tartans were woven with precision and passion. This family-specific tartan, held within the McGregor Hastie Collection, was reportedly being sold in Edinburgh's markets during the 1930s, before mysteriously disappearing from public view. Now preserved within the Scottish Tartans Society archive, the Cockburn of Ormiston Dress tartan remains a poignant reminder of Scotland's proud clan heritage, its intricate threads weaving together a complex tapestry of tradition and identity that continues to captivate those drawn to the mystique of Scotland's ancient textiles.

name: Cockburn old pattern
description: The Cockburn (Old Pattern) tartan is a quintessential example of Scotland's rich clan heritage, bearing testament to the storied history of the Border Clan family. This traditional tartan, originating from the esteemed Wilsons weavers of Bannockburn, was once woven for the noble families who owned lands in Langton, Ormiston, and Clerkington, a region steeped in the region's ancient lineage. The unique pattern is said to have derived its name from a place near Duns in Berwickshire, highlighting the close affinity between the local landscape and the clan's ancestral roots. With a storied past documented since 1952, this tartan has been carefully preserved and halved thread counts to showcase its full sett, allowing future generations to appreciate the intricate craftsmanship and cultural significance of this cherished family heritage.

name: Cockburn [default]
description: The Cockburn tartan, a storied family heirloom steeped in Scottish heritage, tells the tale of a noble clan's rich history through its intricate patterns and subtle colour variations. This distinctive tartan, categorised as Clan/Family, is rooted in the traditions of the 18th century, evoking images of rugged Highland landscapes and proud Scottish families. With its characteristic 16-shaft weave, the Cockburn features a striking blend of blue, green, yellow, black, red, and white hues, carefully interwoven to represent the clan's ancient coat of arms. As one of the most iconic tartans in Scotland, the Cockburn has been woven with precision by skilled weavers for generations, its beauty and significance cherished by families proud to bear its name.

name: Colgan [default]
description: This traditional Clan tartan, known as Colgan, holds deep historical significance for the descendants of John Colgan's family, originally from County Antrim in Northern Ireland. The intricate, carefully crafted pattern weaves together threads of Irish heritage with those of fostered kinship, a poignant reminder of the complex bonds of family and community that defined life in 18th-century Scotland. Registered as a Clan tartan, this distinctive design has been passed down through generations, its unique characteristics reflecting the rich tapestry of Scottish and Irish traditions. The subtle nuances of red, blue, green, yellow, black, brown, and purple hues evoke a sense of warmth, resilience, and unity, a testament to the enduring legacy of John Colgan's family and their storied connections with this timeless tartan.

name: College of Radiographers
description: This distinctive corporate tartan, registered by James Scarlett MBE in 1987, holds a special place in the hearts of those within the radiography community. Commissioned to commemorate an International Conference of Radiographers held in Glasgow in 1988, the College of Radiographers' tartan proudly showcases its vibrant colours - a rich blue, warm gold, crisp white, and bold black - evoking the professionalism, expertise, and unity that define this esteemed profession. By registering with the Tartan Register, Jamie Scarlett has ensured the continuation of this tartan's significance, connecting the past to the present and honouring the heritage of radiography. This enduring design not only represents a proud tradition but also serves as a symbol of affiliation for those who wear it, signifying their connection to an organisation that strives to improve patient care through education and innovation.

name: Colquhoun Dress
description: The Colquhoun Dress is a rich and storied tartan, steeped in heritage and tradition. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Society in 1984, it is a Clan tartan, evoking the proud history and honour of the Colquhoun family. This asymmetric thread count design, created circa 1960 by the esteemed Johnstons of Elgin, showcases a unique blend of blues, greens, and golds that seem to shimmer like the Scottish Highlands themselves. As one of Scotland's most iconic tartans, it is a fitting tribute to the land and people that have inspired countless generations of Colquhouns and Scots more broadly. The intricate patterns and subtle nuances of this tartan are not only a testament to traditional weaving techniques but also to the enduring legacy of Scottish clan culture.

name: Colquhoun [default]
description: The venerable Colquhoun #2 tartan is a quintessential Scottish heritage fabric, steeped in tradition and history. Registration notes confirm its authenticity, with records dating back to the earliest collections and certified by the Chief of the Clan, signifying its prestigious status as a Cowan tartan - a name synonymous with the noble House of Colquhoun. Woven at the beginning of the 19th century by Wilsons of Bannockburn, this tartan has been documented in pattern books since 1819 and is featured in esteemed publications like 'The Clan and Family Tartans of Scotland' (1850), which verifies its long-standing use and acceptance among Scottish authorities. With threadcounts varying across woven samples, this tartan remains an evocative representation of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, perfect for those seeking to honour the traditions of their ancestral clan or simply to pay tribute to the country's storied past.

name: Colvin [default]
description: The Colvin tartan is a timeless and storied design, expertly woven by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr in February 1998 for the esteemed Paul Colvin family. This Category Name tartan has been meticulously crafted to reflect the rich heritage of those who bear the surname, offering a sense of unity and belonging amongst its wearers. The distinctive pattern, featuring a captivating interplay of blues and greens, is said to be worn with favour by members of the Colvine clan in Scotland, and is now available for anyone who wishes to honour their connection to this storied family. With its inclusion in the Johnston Collection, a testament to its significance within Scottish Tartans Authority, the Colvin tartan stands as a proud representation of Scottish tradition and identity.

name:
Commonwealth Games 1998
[AKA] Maitland Chiefs
description: The Derry County, Crest Range tartan is a deeply rooted tribute to the rich heritage of Northern Ireland's largest city, Derry (also known as Londonderry). Registered by Viking Technology Limited in 2005 as part of their Irish County series, this distinctive tartan was born from the country's complex and storied history. As a District tartan, it holds special significance for those who call Derry home, its carefully woven threads evoking the city's proud traditions and resilience. Notably, due to ownership transfer to USA Kilts Inc in 2012, users must obtain prior written consent before reproducing this tartan - a testament to the intricate web of cultural rights and permissions that underpin Scotland's revered textile heritage.

name: Commonwealth Games 1986 Athletes
description: The Commonwealth Games 1986 #2 tartan is a vibrant commemorative design, woven with pride to commemorate one of Scotland's most iconic sporting events. Created by esteemed designer Ramsay Johnstone of Edinburgh Woollen Mill, this tartan celebrates the country's rich sporting heritage and its international connections through its bold colours: Royal Blue, reminiscent of the Scottish flag, white evoking the running lanes at the Edinburgh track, and Red, paying homage to the finishing tape that marked the end of each thrilling race. A testament to Scotland's enduring spirit, this tartan has remained a popular choice in fashion circles since 1994, its significance extending beyond the sporting world to symbolise national pride and unity. As a registered commemorative tartan, it is a cherished link to the past, woven from threads that reflect the country's history, culture and values.

name: Commonwealth Games 1986 Staff
description: The Commonwealth Games 1986 tartan is a vibrant and iconic corporate design that embodies the spirit of international unity and celebration. Created by Mrs L P G Dow, a talented weaver from Edinburgh, this distinctive tartan was specifically commissioned for the 1986 Commonwealth Games, an event that brings together nations from across the Commonwealth to showcase their rich cultural heritage. Woven by Lochcarron for BBC and worn by VIP hostesses and Games Headquarters staff, the tartan's design tells a story of British hospitality and warmth. Its inclusion in the Scottish Tartans Authority Johnston Collection is a testament to its enduring significance as a symbol of national pride and international friendship, making it a treasured part of Scotland's rich textile heritage.

name: Commonwealth Games 1986 Variation
description: The Commonwealth tartan, a stylish interpretation of Scotland's rich heritage by renowned textile artisans at Lochcarron of Scotland, was born out of the fervour of the 1986 Commonwealth Games held in Edinburgh. This fashion tartan proudly wears its sporting roots on its sleeve, evoking the vibrant energy and international spirit of the event that brought together nations from across the globe to compete and celebrate. With a palette of blues, reds, and greens reminiscent of Scotland's rolling hills and majestic lochs, this tartan embodies the values of unity, diversity, and excellence that define the Commonwealth movement. Whether worn with pride as a statement piece or subtly woven into everyday attire, the Commonwealth tartan serves as a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy as a hub of international sporting achievement.

name: Connacht Green (DCD trash)
description: Connaught Green, a storied District tartan, embodies the rich heritage of the north-eastern counties of Scotland. Originally registered with the Scottish Tartans Society, its threadcount was carefully documented in 1994, showcasing the intricate patterns that define this distinct textile. Notably, discrepancies have arisen regarding its origins, with the Uni-Quest Orn website attributing it to Connaught Green - a testament to the complexity and evolution of tartan design over time. Despite these variations, Connaught Green remains an important part of Scottish cultural heritage, evoking the history and traditions of this unique region. Its classification as a District tartan underscores its regional significance, underscoring the importance of preserving Scotland's rich tapestry of textiles and their associated stories.

name: Connell [default]
description: The Connel tartan, a timeless and storied design steeped in Scottish heritage, has been shrouded in mystery for centuries. With its origins uncertain, yet tantalisingly close to the 19th-century Wallace tartan, speculation surrounds the possible familial connections between these two revered patterns. The Connels and MacConnels, both claimed as septs of Clan Donald, lends credence to this theory, their histories intertwined with that of Scotland's most noble families. Dating back to at least 1842, this tartan has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition, its red sett, described in 1888, bearing testament to a legacy born from the annals of Clan Donald's storied past.

name: Cooper Dress #2
description: The Cooper/Couper Dress tartan, registered as Dalgleish #2, holds a place of intrigue within Scottish heritage. Designated as a Clan/Family tartan, this distinctive pattern is steeped in tradition and history, yet its status remains somewhat ambiguous. Originating from the talented hands of D C Dalgliesh, one of Scotland's most renowned tartan designers, this tartan is now prepared for weaving by his esteemed company. While it appears in Dalgliesh's swatch book of Dance Tartans, the authenticity of its use as a legitimate Dress version of the Clan Tartan versus its status as a mere dance sett remains unclear. Nonetheless, the Cooper/Couper Dress tartan retains an air of mystery and authenticity, drawing inspiration from Scotland's rich clan history and the proud traditions of the country's ancient weavers.

name: Cooper Dress #3
description: The Cooper Dress tartan, registered as Dalgliesh #1, is a richly woven tribute to the esteemed Couper family of Scotland's rich history. Weaving back to 1886, when Peter MacArthur and Company in Hamilton first brought it into being for the Gogar branch of this noble clan, this tartan has been passed down through generations as an honourable emblem of family heritage. With its distinctive white and dark blue hues replacing the original green, this dress version maintains the essence of the Couper of Gogar's storied past, while the Coupers' additional title as Baronets of Nova Scotia in 1638 adds a layer of distinction to their already revered legacy. As a designated clan tartan, its significance is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition and culture, inviting wearers to proudly claim their connection to this distinguished family.

name: Cooper [default]
description: This majestic Cooper/Couper tartan, registered for the esteemed clan/family association, is steeped in tradition and heritage. Woven with meticulous care by renowned mills Lochcarron and House of Edgar, its rich colours evoke a sense of history and authenticity. As part of the collection of James Cant, a respected scholar who passed away in 1960, this tartan holds a deep significance for those seeking to connect with their family roots. While no historical details were documented by Mr Cant, the tartan's very existence serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of his clan and the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's tartans. As such, it remains an honourable representation of Cooper/Couper identity, deserving to be worn with pride by those who bear this noble name.

name: Copar a'Beannichte Dress
description: The Copar a'Beannichte Dress, a rare and poignant family tartan, weaves together the rich heritage of its Van Koperen and Benoist bearers through the threads of its intricate pattern. Registered as a Name tartan, this unique fabric tells the story of two families bound by ancestry, loyalty, and love, their names merged in Gaelic to form "copar a'beannichte", meaning "The Blessed Copper". Designed exclusively for the use of Marc van Koperen's own families, this tartan stands as a heartfelt tribute to his mother, Mrs Yvonne Christina van Koperen-Benoist. With its complex history spanning centuries and continents, from 16th century Flanders to 19th century France, this tartan is a testament to the power of family legacy and cultural roots. Woven by the skilled hands of Lochcarron of Scotland, it remains a treasured family heirloom, reserved for the Van Koperen and Benoist families alone, as permission from its creator, Marc van Koperen, is strictly required.

name: Copar a'Beannichte
description: This exquisite, personal tartan, known as Copar a'Beannichte, is a heartfelt tribute to the van Koperen and Benoist families, whose connection has been woven into its fabric for generations. Registered by Marc Rudolf van Koperen, a Highland Dancer and Scotsman of Dutch-French heritage, this restricted family tartan tells the story of two ancestral lines that intersected in 16th-century Flanders and later in France and The Hague. Weaved as a token of gratitude from Mr Van Koperen to his 'being there' during times of need, the name 'Copar a'Beannichte', meaning 'The Blessed Copper', is a beautiful fusion of Gaelic and familial roots. This unique tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Dutch-French heritage and the enduring legacy of Scottish culture, which has captivated Marc van Koperen since his youth in Edinburgh's vibrant Highland dance scene.

name: Corcoran [default]
description: The Corcoran of Sherbrooke tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of the Corcoran family, whose ancestors hailed from the historic Sherbrooke region in Quebec, Canada. This distinctive Clan tartan was lovingly designed by Annie Corcoran in 1994, drawing inspiration from her own Canadian roots and the traditional weavings of Scotland. With its subtle nuances and carefully chosen colours, this tartan pays homage to the family's Scottish ancestry while also reflecting their unique identity as a French-Canadian clan. A swatch of this tartan is part of the esteemed Johnston Collection in the Scottish Tartans Authority's archives, ensuring its place within Scotland's revered tartan heritage. As such, the Corcoran of Sherbrooke tartan serves not only as a personal family heirloom but also as a vibrant representation of intercultural exchange and the enduring spirit of clan identity.

name: Cornish National Day
description: The Cornish National Day tartan is a vibrant and distinctive District tartan, proudly representing the people of Cornwall in the UK. Designed by Donald Rawe, a native of Probus, Cornwall, this tartan was created to commemorate a national day, symbolising the unique heritage and identity of the region. With its unique colour palette and technical characteristics, this tartan holds significant cultural value, marking an important part of Cornish history and tradition. As a District tartan, it is worn with honour by those who claim connection to Cornwall, and its registration with the Scottish Tartans Authority serves as a formal recognition of its authenticity and significance.

name: Cossar [default]
description: The Cossar tartan is a treasured family heirloom, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. This personal tartan, registered under John Struthers Cossar's name, holds deep significance for those who bear it, serving as a symbol of pride and connection to one's roots. Crafted by the renowned tweed mill Henry Ballantyne & Sons in Walkerburn during the early 1950s, the Cossar tartan reflects the innovative spirit of its designer, John Struthers Cossar. With restrictions limited to personal use only, this tartan is reserved for those closest to the family, allowing them to wear a tangible link to their ancestry with honour and distinction. As a testament to Scotland's rich weaving heritage, the Cossar tartan embodies the time-honoured art of tartan-making, its intricate patterns and subtle colour palette evoking a sense of warmth and tradition that transcends generations.

name: Cotswolds Distillery
description: The Cotswolds Distillery tartan is a masterful blend of earthy tones and natural hues, perfectly capturing the essence of England's picturesque countryside. Designed by renowned weaver DC Dalgiesh, this Corporate tartan was created to commemorate the first-ever single-malt whisky distillery in the Cotswolds, an Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB). The colours - a soothing blend of greens, blues, and yellows - evoke the rolling hills, wildflowers, and misty valleys that define this idyllic region. With its subtle nuances and restrained palette, this tartan is as much about understated elegance as it is about heritage and tradition, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to connect with the natural beauty of the Cotswolds.

name: Coulter Dress
description: This Coulter Dress tartan, registered as a personal clan tartan, embodies the rich heritage and tradition of the Scottish Highlands. Designed in the early 20th century by D C Dalgliesh Ltd., this distinctive pattern is believed to have been woven for a 'Coulter' family, whose surname holds significant cultural importance in Scotland. With its unique colour palette and intricate design, this tartan proudly represents the Coulter family's honour and ancestry, steeped in centuries of Scottish history and identity. Although restrictions apply, with the approval of the registration holder - D C Dalgliesh Ltd. - this tartan is an exceptional example of traditional weaving craftsmanship, its significance now woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage for future generations to treasure.

name: Coulter [default]
description: The Coulter tartan, registered to the personal name of its creator, is a distinct and intriguing example of Scottish textile heritage. Designed by the esteemed D C Dalgliesh of Selkirk, this Name tartan is likely one of a pair woven for the Coulter family, imbuing it with a deep sense of family legacy and history. While the registration notes remain somewhat enigmatic, it is clear that the Coulter tartan holds significance beyond its technical characteristics. As part of the rich tapestry of Scottish clan heritage, this tartan design may have been worn by Coulter family members as a symbol of pride and identity, connecting them to their ancestral roots. Its restricted preparation for weaving ensures that only authentic reproductions can be made, preserving the integrity of this historic textile art form.

name: Couper [default]
description: The Couper of Gogar tartan, a testament to Scotland's rich heritage, tells the story of a noble family with roots dating back to the 17th century. Weaved in the late 19th century by Peter MacArthur Ltd of Biggar, this Clan tartan is rooted in tradition, its intricate pattern echoing an ancient shawl or 'maud' from which it was copied, estimated to be at least a century old. The design's striking beauty belies its historical significance, for the Coupers of Gogar were not only esteemed members of their clan but also ennobled Baronets of Nova Scotia in 1638, their legacy woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition. With its subtle nuances and muted tones, this tartan design invites wearers to connect with a storied past, their honour bound by the threads of history and family ties.

name: Cowper [default]
description: The Cowper tartan, a humble yet storied name in the annals of Scottish heritage, whispers tales of tradition and individuality. As a Name tartan, it is a personal choice, worn by its wearer with pride and distinction. Its origins remain shrouded in mystery, but Clark/Clergy, a storied surname rooted in Scotland's clergy, provides a tantalising hint at the fabric's history. The subtle shift from one colour to another in the design suggests a quiet evolution over time, mirroring the intricate relationships between family, community, and land. With no clear provenance forthcoming, the Cowper tartan remains an enigma, waiting to be woven into its own narrative – a testament to the enduring power of Scottish tradition and the indelible mark left by those who wear it.

name: Craig Paisley
description: The Craig (Paisley) tartan is a storied and historic design born from the threads of Scotland's rich textile heritage. This distinctive pattern, inspired by an original plaid once owned by Mr A F Craig, has strong similarities to the well-documented Craig at #1574, suggesting it may be a personal variation on this classic Scottish motif. First created in 1866 by A F Craig & Co Ltd, Engineers, Paisley, this tartan was worn with pride by those who honoured their heritage and connection to the city of Paisley, a major hub for Scotland's textile industry. Although Phil Smith's threadcount analysis revealed similarities to an existing registered tartan, his work also uncovered the rich history behind this unique design, now recorded in the Scottish Register of Tartans, a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's iconic tartans.

name: Craig [default]
description: The Craig tartan, designed by esteemed weaver MacGregor Hastie, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's rich heritage. Born from a long-held desire to create a family tartan, Hastie skillfully wove together a vibrant palette inspired by the rugged beauty of the Highlands. Originally featuring a distinctive grey fleckwork reminiscent of granite, this clan-specific tartan has become an integral part of Scottish tradition. Its origins are shrouded in mystery, with some tracing its design to a request from a customer at the Scotch House in Knightsbridge, while others claim it was influenced by the Earl of Mar's permission for the Craigs to add colour to their ancestral tartan. Regardless of its provenance, the Craig tartan now bears witness to Hastie's masterful craftsmanship and has found a place in general production, allowing families to proudly don this distinctive heritage-inspired fabric on special occasions.

name: Crane (Stuart) personal; of Cluny
description: The Crane of Cluny tartan is a majestic and symbolic weaving, born from the creative vision of Stuart G Crane, Feudal Baron of Cluny in Fife. As one of three tartans specifically designed for the esteemed Baron, this Name tartan embodies the proud heritage and storied lineage of the Clan of Cluny. With its intricate design and carefully considered colour palette, the Crane of Cluny tartan is a testament to the rich tapestry of Scottish tradition, where history, family, and identity are deeply intertwined. Regulated by Stuart G Crane himself, this tartan is a unique and distinctive expression of his personal honour, making it all the more special for those fortunate enough to wear or display it with permission from the Baron.

name: Crane (Stuart) personal; of Cluny Dress
description: This exquisite tartan, known as the Crane of Cluny Dress, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish clan identity. Registered by Keith Lumsden, the design pays homage to Stuart G Crane of Cluny, a Feudal Baron with strong connections to Fife. This unique tartan is part of a trio of designs created specifically for its owner, reflecting the intricate web of relationships within Scottish clans and families. With restricted use governed by the noble clan patriarch himself, this tartan is steeped in tradition and family honour, its subtle nuances and complexities a reminder of the enduring power of kinship and legacy. As a Name tartan, it serves as a tangible link to Stuart G Crane's illustrious lineage, a symbol of his status and heritage that transcends the ordinary fabric of everyday life.

name: Crane (Stuart) personal; of Cluny Hunting
description: The Crane of Cluny Hunting tartan is a storied and exclusive design, steeped in Scottish heritage and woven with precision by renowned designer Keith Lumsden. As one of three bespoke tartans created for Stuart G Crane, Feudal Baron of Cluny in Fife, this intricate pattern holds great significance as a symbol of clan affiliation and family honour. Restricted to the personal use of its owner, the Crane of Cluny Hunting tartan is a testament to the rich traditions of Scottish tartanry, where complex designs and symbolic motifs convey respect, loyalty, and identity. As such, it is a rare and precious find for those fortunate enough to lay eyes on this unique and storied tartan, its technical nuances and cultural resonance woven together with centuries-old history and tradition.

name: Cranston Dress
description: The Cranston Dress, a traditional Clan tartan, holds a place of honour in the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage. Weaved with precision and care, its intricate pattern weaves together a complex interplay of reds, greens, blues, and yellows, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's natural landscapes. Dating back to the 18th century, this tartan was registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, highlighting its significance as a family crest and symbol of clan identity. While not designed by a specific individual, the Cranston Dress is remarkably similar to Unidentified Lindley #2, leaving some historians intrigued about its origins. Regardless, this timeless design has been adopted by families across Scotland, serving as a tangible connection to their ancestral roots and cultural traditions.

name: Cranston [default]
description: The Cranston tartan is a storied clan pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, carefully crafted by Sobieski Stewarts, The, with roots tracing back to Clans Originaux. This majestic fabric features two distinct greens, reminiscent of the tender leaves of an ash tree and the soft hue of freshly cut grass, weaving together to form a rich tapestry that echoes the natural beauty of Scotland's landscapes. The striking resemblance to the historic Lochcarron colours pays testament to the tartan's enduring connection to Scotland's tartan legacy, while its registration in the Scottish Tartans Authority Dalgety Collection ensures its authenticity and legitimacy as a proud symbol of clan identity.

name: Craparo [default]
description: The Craparo tartan is a distinctive and deeply personal design, born from the vision of Donald Suttie Smith in 2002 for John S Craparo, a proud bearer of the name. As a registered Name tartan, it carries the honour of its namesake, available to anyone with the surname Craparo, Crapara, Capraro, or Craprara. This unique tartan is not just a piece of fabric, but a symbol of heritage and identity, woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition. Its intricate design tells a story of family ties and cultural roots, evoking the rich history and legacy of the Craparo name. The Craparo tartan stands as a testament to the enduring power of Scotland's tartans, carrying the hopes and aspirations of its wearers forward through generations.

name: Crawford Arisaid; Dance
description: Crawford Arisaid, a captivating fashion tartan, tells the story of a family's love for dance through its intricate patterns and rich colours. This beautiful design is a testament to Scottish heritage, dating back to approximately 1985 when it was registered for Mrs. Joan Crawford Carlson's dancer daughter. The name 'Arisaid' holds a special meaning in Gaelic, translating to 'dance', highlighting the tartan's connection to the world of movement and performance. As a fashion tartan, Crawford Arisaid is perfect for those who want to make a statement with their clothing or accessories while still paying tribute to Scotland's rich cultural heritage. Its registration notes reveal a personal touch, demonstrating that even the most formal tartans can hold a special story behind them.

name: Crawford Red
description: The Crawford tartan is a rich and evocative woven fabric steeped in Scottish heritage, its origins shrouded in mystery until recently unravelled through historical records. Designed by the Sobieski Stuart brothers, this Clan tartan tells the story of a family's proud history, with its bright crimson red standing out against a backdrop of 'tender ash' green and 'grass-green'. The intricate design, first recorded in the Vestiarium Scoticum of 1842, is believed to have been crafted between that date and the publication of the Clans Originaux in 1880. As a testament to Scotland's storied past, the Crawford tartan embodies the traditions and values of those who bear its name, inviting wearers to embody the honour and pride associated with their clan heritage.

name: Crihfield [default]
description: The Crihfield Family tartan is a personal and exclusive design created by Brook Crihfield in 1996, adding to the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage. This name tartan holds great significance for its creator, marking a deep connection to their ancestral roots. The intricate patterns woven into this tartan tell a story of tradition and family legacy, with each thread carefully crafted to pay homage to the Crihfield clan's history and identity. As a personal design, it is likely to be treasured by those who bear the name, serving as a poignant reminder of their heritage and cultural ties. With its unique and distinctive characteristics, this tartan stands as a testament to the power of family and tradition, weaving together generations past, present, and future.

name: Crombie House Check
description: The Crombie House Check is a quintessential Corporate tartan, born from the legacy of Langholm, Dumfriesshire's esteemed textile heritage. Designed by William Johnston Ewart, this tartan pays homage to the J & J Crombie Ltd Overcoating Range, whose colours have been carefully adapted to create a distinctive and modern visual identity. Characterised by its striking dark green and royal blue hues, though subtly reinterpreted with lighter tones for maximum visibility, the Crombie House Check exudes a sense of professionalism and sophistication. As a Corporate tartan, it is perfectly suited for use on merchandise, conveying a strong yet approachable brand image that echoes the rich tradition of Scotland's iconic weavers.

name: Crookdake-Cheng
description: The Crookdake-Cheng tartan, a personal name tartan designed by Dr Philip D Smith in 1994, is a unique and meaningful creation that tells the story of its namesake's heritage. This intricately woven design features a predominantly blue-and-green colour scheme with subtle yellow accents, evoking the image of rice stalks that hold great significance for Michael Crookdake Cheng, whose name this tartan was created to represent. As a Name Tartan, it is reserved for individual use and holds personal importance, setting it apart from the more formal Clan or Corporate tarts. Interestingly, restrictions apply to the wearing of this tartan, likely due to its personal significance, adding to its exclusivity and value as a family heirloom. This tartan stands as a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's name system, where the careful design of these patterns reflects the story and identity of their bearers.

name: Crozier [default]
description: The Crozier/Crosser tartan is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's ancient clans, its complex patterns woven from threads of tradition and history. This distinctive design, registered in 1983, is believed to originate from mounted samples held by Messrs R.W. Forsyth of Glasgow, offering a glimpse into the craftsmanship of Scotland's tartan makers. The registration notes reveal that the count was taken from a pattern book belonging to Jardines Outfitters, a Glasgow-based outfitter renowned for its expertise in traditional Scottish textiles. As a Clan/Family tartan, the Crozier/Crosser is deeply rooted in the heritage of a specific family or clan, its unique character and story waiting to be told through the threads of its intricate pattern.

name: MacPherson Crubin
description: The Crubin Plaid, also known as MacPherson, is a rich and storied tartan that originates from Clan Chattan, one of Scotland's most ancient and noble clans. This iconic plaid was first registered in 1984 by James Scarlett, an esteemed Scottish heraldic authority who paid tribute to the long-standing heritage of the MacPherson family, whose name is synonymous with this distinctive design. The Crubin Plaid boasts a characteristic palette of blues, greens, and reds, woven together with precision to evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. As a Clan tartan, it holds deep significance for those bearing the MacPherson surname or its associated clans, serving as a proud symbol of family heritage and cultural identity.

name: Cruikshank [default]
description: The Cruikshank tartan is a poignant representation of family heritage, its distinctive pattern woven from threads of tradition and history. Registered as a Clan tartan, this tartan holds significant cultural importance, tracing its roots back to the Scottish Highlands. Although the designer's identity remains unknown, Phil Smith's meticulous documentation provides a glimpse into the intricate storytelling behind this unique design. Characterised by its muted colour palette, the Cruikshank tartan evokes the rugged yet resilient spirit of the Scottish clans that once roamed these shores. Its presence is a tribute to the enduring legacy of Scotland's rich history and the families who have worn their Tartans with pride through generations.

name:
Cumming Hunting
[AKA] Cumming District
[AKA] Cumming Glenorchy
description: The Buchan tartan is a richly woven tribute to the storied heritage of Scotland's Buchan district and its proud Clan Buchan family. Registered as both a District and Clan/Family tartan, this unique sett holds significant historical value, tracing its origins back to 1210 with the marriage of Margaret, daughter of King Edgar, to William Coymen, sheriff of Forfar. The name "Buchan" itself, though borne by a family, is rooted in territorial significance, evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of Aberdeenshire's Buchan region. With its asymmetrical sett, this tartan design embodies the complexities and nuances of Scottish clan history, while also paying homage to the long-standing relationships between the Buchans and their esteemed ancestors.

name:
Cumming [default]
[AKA] MacAulay #2
description: The Cumming tartan, registered in 1850 by W & A K Smith, is a rich and storied fabric woven from the threads of Scottish heritage. As certified by Sir William George Gordon Cumming, the clan's chief at the time of registration, this tartan represents the family's honour and tradition. The Cummin Tartan, as it was originally known, has been passed down through generations, its intricate patterns a testament to the craftsmanship and skill of Scotland's weavers. With its distinctive colour palette, including shades of blue, green, and yellow, this tartan is a proud symbol of the Cumming family's legacy, connecting past and present in a meaningful way that continues to evoke a sense of Scottish identity and pride.

name: Cunningham Dress Dance Blue
description: This captivating Dress Blue tartan, designated as Dance for fashion purposes, holds a rich heritage in Scotland's textile tradition. Inspired by the storied history of the Cunningham clan, whose name translates to "son of the crown", this vibrant design weaves together shades of indigo, blue, and gold to evoke a sense of nobility and grandeur. Although it may not be officially recognised by the Clan Cunningham Association in the USA, its origins remain tied to the ancestral traditions of this esteemed Scottish clan. As a fashion tartan, it offers an opportunity for wearers to connect with the country's rich cultural heritage while making a statement with their unique choice of colour and design.

name:
Cunningham Hunting
[AKA] MacNicol Hunting #2
[AKA] Nicolson Hunting #2
description: The Cunningham Hunting tartan is a deeply rooted family heirloom, steeped in the proud heritage of Clan Cunningham, whose history dates back to the 15th century. Woven with meticulous attention to detail, this distinctive tartan features a rich blend of blues and greens that evoke the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of Scotland's Borders region. Its origins remain shrouded in mystery, with some sources suggesting it was first seen at the Santa Rosa Games in 1990, while others whisper that it is, in fact, the McNicol Hunting tartan, with the Cunninghams' connection to this design remaining a subject of ongoing research. As a genuine clan tartan, the Cunningham Hunting bears the honour of being worn by members of Clan Cunningham and their families, a privilege reserved for those who bear the family name and can trace their ancestry back to the ancient Scottish clans.

name: Cunningham [default]
description: Cunningham #2 is a Lowland tartan with a rich history, born from the ingenuity of the Sobieski Stewarts, who "invented" it for the Cunningham family in their 1842 Vestiarium Scoticum publication. This striking design features alternating black and red stripes, which, while published as "blew", are typically produced by weavers as black to reflect the clan's heritage. Notably, this tartan draws inspiration from the MacGregor sett, with subtle variations that set it apart, including slightly wider red lines and guard lines that appear as black in the digital samples received by the Scottish Tartans Authority. As a Clan tartan, Cunningham #2 is steeped in tradition and represents the enduring spirit of the Lowland Cunninghams, whose history has been intertwined with that of the MacGregors, who adopted this pattern after their clan was broken and scattered.

name:
Currie of Arran [default]
[AKA] Currie of Arran
description: The Currie of Arran tartan is a poignant tribute to the Scottish heritage of Canada's Clan Currie Association. Commissioned by the association, this distinctive tartan weaves together rich colours to tell the story of its namesake family's history. The green hues evoke the rugged islands that dot the Canadian landscape, while the gold and white lines shimmer like the shoreline, evoking a sense of tranquility and stability. In the distance, the blue tone recalls the boundless skies and sea that have long shaped the lives of the Currie clan. And at its heart, the six red lines pay homage to the ancestral heritage of Mael Iosa Ua Dalaidh, chief man of learning who gave his descendants their name - a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's storied past in this distant but still deeply connected corner of the world.

name: Curry [default]
description: The Curry tartan, designed with love and legacy by Dr Philip D Smith in 1955, tells a poignant tale of cultural heritage and inter-service camaraderie. Originating from Petty Officer Bruce Curry, a devoted Mineman serving in the US Navy at Yokosuka, Japan, this unique Name tartan was woven into existence as a symbol of affection between two hearts - a silk sash gifted to his sweetheart by the proud sailor. Today, the Curry tartan proudly wears its heritage badge, inviting all who bear the surname 'Curry' to wear their family's rich history on their sleeve. A testament to the enduring power of Scottish textiles in bridging international ties and celebrating the intricate connections between nations, this tartan design whispers stories of devotion, duty, and the human spirit that weaves them together.

name: Cusack [default]
description: The Cusack tartan is a deeply personal and meaningful weaving, born out of a connection between designer Peter MacDonald and Jeremy Cusack, a Guernsey resident with strong roots in the island's history. Registered as a "Name" tartan, this unique pattern reflects the Cusack heritage and is reserved exclusively for those bearing the name, affording them a sense of ancestral pride and belonging. As an original design created by Peter MacDonald, the Cusack tartan embodies the tradition of intergenerational storytelling through textiles, where the threads of family history are woven into the fabric of everyday life. With its distinctive colour palette and expertly crafted weave, this tartan is more than just a pattern - it's a symbol of identity, community, and the enduring legacy of Jeremy Cusack and his descendants.

name: Daks Fashion 600150
description: The Daks (0600150) fashion tartan is a dynamic and modern Scottish pattern, born out of the esteemed Daks Simpson Group's London headquarters at 34 Jermyn Street. This striking design is believed to have been created with the fast-paced, urban lifestyle of the City in mind, reflecting the sleek and sophisticated aesthetic of the era. With its intricate colour scheme, subtly nuanced gradations, and computer-illustrated thread count, this tartan exudes a sense of cosmopolitan flair, evoking the glamour of 21st-century London. As a fashion tartan, it is designed to make a statement on the catwalk or in everyday attire, capturing the essence of modern British style and heritage.

name: Daks Fashion Black
description: The Daks (Black) tartan, created by Patrick A. Keeney, embodies the spirit of Scottish fashion with its bold, sleek design. As a Fashion tartan, it is intended to add a touch of sophisticated elegance to any outfit, whether for formal events or everyday wear. This variation of the traditional House Colours reference #2506 is notable for its subtle yet distinct difference in warp and weft colouration, with 14 black counts in the weft compared to 12 in the warp, ensuring an almost imperceptible shift from one side of the fabric to the other. With its characteristic 'lemon-white' hue and striking black tones, this tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage while exuding a modern, fashion-forward flair that is sure to make a statement on the catwalk or at any high-society gathering.

name: Daks Fashion Blue
description: The Daks Blue tartan is a quintessential corporate design, born from the innovative spirit of Arthur Bell's collaboration with Daks-Simpson Ltd in 1984. This striking blue-and-white pattern has become synonymous with professionalism and sophistication, making it a popular choice for businesses seeking to establish a strong visual identity. The category of Corporate tartan denotes its intended use for formal, business-related purposes, such as uniforms, stationery, or branding materials. While there are no inherent restrictions on the use of this tartan, its design does owe a debt of inspiration to traditional Scottish heritage, evoking the country's rich textile history and cultural traditions. Today, the Daks Blue tartan continues to serve as a powerful symbol of modernity and elegance, perfectly suited for organisations seeking to project a sense of refinement and authority.

name: Daks Fashion Blue Loden
description: The Daks (Blue Loden) tartan is a corporate stalwart, designed by the renowned Arthur Bell for Daks-Simpson Ltd in 1988. Originally conceived as a modern update to a classic Scottish pattern, this distinctive blue loden sett has since become an integral part of business attire and formal wear. With its subtle, nuanced colour changes, the Daks tartan embodies the sophistication and elegance that is synonymous with Scotland's rich heritage of textile traditions. As a Category Corporate design, it has been carefully crafted to evoke a sense of professionalism and authority, making it an ideal choice for businesses and institutions seeking to establish a strong, distinctive identity.

name: Daks Fashion Brown
description: The Daks (Brown) tartan is a timeless fashion choice that embodies the rugged yet refined spirit of Scotland's storied heritage. Registered in 1980 by renowned designer Daks-Simpson Ltd, this distinctive pattern is now synonymous with high-end style and sophistication. Originally created for the fashion world, the Daks tartan has transcended its commercial origins to become a beloved classic, evoking images of traditional Scottish tweed and woolen fabrics worn with pride by Scotland's finest Highland clansmen. With its rich, earthy tones and carefully balanced sett, this iconic pattern exudes a sense of enduring quality and timeless elegance, perfectly capturing the essence of Scotland's esteemed fashion tradition.

name: Daks Fashion Chino Check
description: The Daks Chino Check is a modern fashion tartan, expertly crafted by Sarah Jones to evoke the laid-back spirit of British heritage. This striking design falls under the Fashion category, where creativity knows no bounds, and tradition meets contemporary style. With its unique warp and weft construction, the Daks Chino Check features a harmonious blend of rich colours, including Lemon44, Tan6, Black13, Yellow4, Black4, Royal Blue 20, Olive Green6, and the subtle pops of Lemon4. Although designed for fashion purposes, this tartan's roots in traditional Scottish textile heritage remain evident, reflecting the timeless allure of the Chino check pattern.

name: Daks Fashion House
description: The Daks tartan, a Fashion category design, holds a distinctive place in the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage. Registered by Arthur Bell Ltd on behalf of Daks-Simpson Ltd in 1988, this tartan is deeply rooted in the tradition of textile artistry that has long been synonymous with British culture. Characterised by its bold colour palette, where the warm tones of red replace the traditional yellow, this design reflects the evolution of tartan aesthetics over time. With its unique blend of warp and weft differing subtly to create a distinctive visual effect, the Daks tartan embodies the timeless appeal of Scottish knitting traditions. Its classification as a Fashion category design underscores its use in modern clothing, where it continues to be celebrated for its bold, eye-catching presence on the runway and in fashion collections.

name: Daks Fashion House Check
description: The Daks (House Check) tartan is a quintessential fashion staple, expertly woven by the renowned designer Daks-Simpson for this esteemed retailer in 1998. This bold, graphic pattern was crafted specifically for major clothing brands, showcasing its versatility and style. As part of the Fashion category, it's a testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage and tradition, where vibrant colours and intricate designs have captivated audiences for centuries. With its distinctive chevron motif, this tartan pays homage to the House Check pattern popularised by Scottish tailors in the 19th century, symbolising both practicality and flair. While available for commercial use, it's a valuable addition to Scotland's cultural legacy, celebrating the country's rich textile heritage and showcasing its enduring influence on fashion worldwide.

name: Daks Fashion Invertere
description: The Invertere tartan, registered with distinction as Corporate, is a striking design born from the skilled hands of Arthur Bell for Daks-Simpson, later championed by Invertere Coat Co Ltd. This bold pattern eschews traditional precedents, introducing innovative colour combinations that have become synonymous with its identity. Characterised by its distinctive over-stripe in yellow on the warp, the Invertere tartan embodies a modernising spirit that blends with Scotland's rich heritage to forge a unique visual language. As an corporate design, it is aptly suited for business attire and professional wear, conveying a sense of dynamism and forward-thinking without sacrificing the timeless allure of traditional tartan craftsmanship.

name: Daks Fashion Loden
description: The Daks Loden tartan, designed by renowned fashion house Daks-Simpson, is an iconic fabric woven with rich cultural heritage and modern flair. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority in 1981, this fashion tartan pays homage to Scotland's storied tradition of weaving while reflecting the sleek, sophisticated aesthetic of its designer. Characterised by a subtle blend of earthy tones and deep blues, Daks Loden is both timeless and contemporary, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. Note that this tartan design is subject to certain restrictions due to trade regulations, underscoring the importance of respecting the integrity of Scotland's unique cultural fabric.

name: Daks Fashion Muted Loden
description: The Muted Loden Daks tartan is a quintessential example of corporate tartanry, woven with function and practicality in mind for the esteemed Daks-Simpson Ltd. This muted, earthy-toned design, first registered in 1985, embodies the values of understated sophistication and heritage. Inspired by the traditional Scottish Loden fabric, this tartan features a carefully calibrated palette of blues, greens, and browns that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's rural landscapes. As a trade design, it is intended for use on corporate merchandise, symbolising the company's commitment to quality and tradition while also catering to a wider audience seeking distinctive yet subdued branding options. The Daks-Simpson Ltd tartan serves as a testament to the enduring allure of Scottish heritage in modern business, offering a subtle and stylish means of establishing an organisation's identity.

name: Daks Fashion Navy
description: The Daks (Navy) tartan is a masterful creation by renowned designer, Daks-Simpson, crafted for the fashion category. This sophisticated design embodies the quintessential spirit of Scottish heritage, with its bold, navy blues evoking the mysterious and rugged landscapes of Scotland's Highlands. As one of many 'Daks' tarts, this particular pattern shares an intriguing characteristic: its thread count begins and ends with an odd number, reflecting a unique threading sequence that sets it apart from other tarts in the Daks family. Though its registration notes remain shrouded in mystery, it is clear that this tartan has been woven with a deep understanding of traditional Scottish textile expertise, marrying timeless elegance with modern flair to create a truly distinctive and alluring design.

name: Daks Fashion Simpson Muted Skye
description: Daks-Simpson, or Muted Skye, is a thought-provoking fashion tartan that embodies the subtleties of Scotland's ever-changing landscapes. This design, created by renowned designer Daks-Simpson, was registered as a Fashion tartan, signifying its intended use in high-end clothing and textiles. Characterised by a muted palette, reminiscent of Scotland's atmospheric skies on a grey day, this tartan features an intriguing variation in warp and weft threads, adding depth to its unique aesthetic. While the registration notes are somewhat cryptic, it is hinted at that Daks-Simpson was inspired by Arthur Bell's earlier design, 'Daks Muted Blue', further underscoring the significance of Scotland's rich tartan heritage. With no specific restrictions, this tartan invites designers and enthusiasts alike to weave its subtle charm into their creations, a testament to Scotland's timeless beauty and cultural identity.

name: Dalbraith, Eastern Western Motor Group
description: The Eastern Western Motor Group, Dalbraith tartan is a dynamic blend of colours that embodies the modern spirit of Scotland's automotive heritage. Registered as a corporate tartan, this distinctive pattern pays tribute to the Eastern Western Motor Group, a respected name in Scottish motoring. Designed by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, the tartan's composition features a striking combination of blues and greens, evoking the country's rolling hills and serene lochs. This bold and vibrant design serves as a symbol of unity and identity for the company, reflecting its proud history and dedication to excellence in the industry. Though restricted to use by the Eastern Western Motor Group, this corporate tartan remains an intriguing example of Scotland's rich textile heritage, offering a unique insight into the country's industrial past and its enduring legacy in modern times.

name: Dalgliesh Dress
description: The Dalgliesh Dress tartan is a quintessential example of Scottish heritage, its rich hues evoking the warmth and tradition of Scotland's esteemed clans. Registered as a family tartan, this distinctive pattern was designed by D C Dalgliesh, a renowned weaver who brought it to life for his clients seeking bespoke tartans. The subtle interplay of blues, greens, and reds in this carefully crafted design is said to be a personal favourite, tailored specifically for short runs of special orders, a testament to the artisan's skill and attention to detail. With its unique characteristics and restrictions on preparation by D C Dalgliesh Ltd., this tartan remains an important piece of Scottish textile history, cherished by those with connections to the Dalgliesh family and their heritage.

name: Dallas [default]
description: The Dallas tartan, registered in 1964, is a proud representation of Scottish clan heritage, tracing its origins to the esteemed Dalgliesh family. Designed by DC Dalgliesh Ltd, this distinctive tartan has been carefully prepared for weaving by the company's skilled experts. The vibrant, muted tones evoke the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of Scotland's Highland regions. Traditionally associated with a specific clan or district, the Dallas tartan holds significant cultural and historical value, its design reflecting the rich traditions and ancestry of those who bear the name Dalgliesh. While some may have sought to alter the original colours, as noted in 'Tartans' by Johnston/Smith (1999), the authentic Dallas tartan remains a testament to Scotland's storied past and the enduring spirit of its people.

name: Dalziel [default]
description: Dalziel #2, also known as Dalzell tartan, holds a rich history within Scottish heritage, tracing its roots to the 19th century when it was designed in honour of King George IV's visit to Scotland. Originally produced for a 'George IV' tartan, this family tartan shares similarities with the Munro pattern, reflecting its connections to the prominent Highland Clan system. The name Dalziel originates from the Barony of Dalzell in Lanarkshire, which translates to 'I dare' in Old Scots and bears significance on the family coat of arms as their motto. As a clan tartan, it is steeped in tradition and identity for those with ties to the Dalzell family or its cadet branches, such as the owners of House of the Binns in West Lothian, now preserved by the National Trust for Scotland.

name: Danish
description: The Danish tartan is a vibrant and distinctive district tartan, carefully crafted by David McGill to pay tribute to the heritage of Denmark and its people. Originally designed to celebrate the birth of Prince Christian of Denmark, this striking tartan has become an important symbol of connection for individuals with Danish roots or associations worldwide. Approved by the Danish Honorary Consul, Norman Irons in 2006, this tartan embodies the country's rich history and tradition. As a result of its registration under International Tartans, anyone holding the designer's consent is permitted to wear this tartan, allowing enthusiasts to proudly showcase their affinity for Denmark. This unique and meaningful design serves as a testament to the enduring spirit of Danish culture, inviting those who feel a connection to Denmark to don its colours with honour and pride.

name: Davidson (Paul) personal; Italian
description: The Italian tartan, registered in 2002, is a vibrant celebration of the strong cultural bonds between Scotland and Italy, as recognised by its creators Paul Davidson and Antonio Cirignaco. This District tartan is specifically designated for the Italian Scots community, honouring their heritage and shared traditions. With its unique colour palette, inspired by the Mediterranean coast, this tartan is a fitting tribute to the warm relations between these two nations. As an authentic Scottish tartan, it adheres to traditional weaving techniques, yet its distinctive characteristics set it apart as a symbol of Italian-Scottish unity and pride. This exclusive design can only be purchased from Tony Cirignaco, ensuring that its authenticity and cultural significance are preserved for the community it serves.

name: Davidson [default]
description: The Davidson tartan, borne by Sir David Davidson of Alltdinnie since its recording in 1961, is a storied and distinctive clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage. This traditional sett, now an integral part of the family's honour, is believed to be the basis for the more modern Henderson tartan, as noted by DC Stewart, a leading authority on Scottish tartans. With its rich, muted tones, this tartan weaves a narrative of tradition and continuity, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. Notably, the Davidson tartan diverges from earlier setts, omitting the white stripe that was once characteristic of the sett, instead showcasing a unique and timeless design that has been cherished by generations of the Davidson clan. Its inclusion in esteemed publications, such as 'Old and Rare Scottish Tartans' by D.W. Stewart (1893), serves as a testament to its enduring significance, and its variations - including the Half Davidson and Double Davidson tartans - add to the richness and diversity of this beloved clan tartan.

name: Davidson Double
description: The Davidson, Double tartan, crafted by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1847, is a testament to the rich heritage and tradition of Scotland's clans. This iconic threadcount, taken from the esteemed Telfer Dunbar Collection at Huntly House, showcases the intricate storytelling inherent in tartan design. The name "Half" refers to the sett being reduced by half, an adaptation likely made to make the design more accessible or appealing for modern wear. Davidson of Tulloch [default]

Now designated 'of Tulloch', this tartan serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Chattan and the Davidson family's storied past, with its complex history woven into every subtle variation in colour and pattern.

name:
Davidson of Tulloch Dress

The cadet bandsmen who wear this tartan are ambassadors of Scottish heritage, representing not only their family clan but also the values of music, discipline, and intellectual curiosity that define Valley Forge's esteemed academy. name: Davidson of Tulloch #2

Stewart and Smibert, who have documented this variation alongside its more familiar counterparts, including the 'Double Davidson' and 'Half Davidson'. With a distinctive set of restrictions in place, ensuring its authentic use is safeguarded for future generations, this tartan remains an important part of Scotland's cultural heritage, a testament to the enduring legacy of the clans that once roamed the Highlands.

name: Davies of Wales
description: The Davies of Wales tartan is a distinctive and modern creation that pays homage to the rich heritage of Wales. Designed by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill in Powys, its unique characteristics set it apart from other traditional Celtic tartans, featuring an unusual combination of thread numbers and colours that deviate from the norm. While not traditionally associated with historical or genealogical significance, the 'of Wales' designation serves as a testament to its creation by Welsh textile expert Sheila Daniel. As a relatively recent innovation, dating back to around 1998, this tartan's popularity has grown significantly since its introduction, with consent required from Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea, prior to weaving, ensuring its continued authenticity and cultural significance are respected.

name: Davis [default]
description: The Davis tartan, named in honour of its proud bearers, the sept of Clan Davidson, is a rich and storied textile that embodies the heritage and tradition of Scotland's northern Highlands. Designed by Leslie Davis of Spade Texas as a tribute to his roots, this Name tartan has been woven with love and care by Molly Manaugh, ensuring its intricate patterns and subtle nuances remain true to Scottish weaving traditions. While it shares similarities with the Artmark USA's Scott Red fashion tartan, the Davis is distinct in its own right, boasting a unique character that sets it apart as a proud representation of Clan Davidson's history and identity. As an example of the Name category, this tartan is available for all members of the sept to wear with pride, connecting them to their ancestral heritage and the storied traditions of Scotland's clan system.

name: De Maynard
description: The De Maynard tartan is a deeply personal and meaningful design, crafted with love and care by renowned Scottish weaver Tony Murray for his esteemed client, V. de Maynard. As a Name tartan, it was created to reflect the individuality and heritage of its wearer, rather than representing a specific clan or family lineage. With its unique and intricate pattern, this tartan pays tribute to the richness of Scottish tradition, evoking the warmth and hospitality that has long been synonymous with Scotland's cultural identity. The De Maynard tartan serves as a testament to the enduring power of personal connection and creativity in shaping our relationship with heritage, and its creator's dedication to preserving and celebrating these traditions is truly commendable.

name: Deas [default]

Its origins rooted in the historic records, the Deas tartan embodies the symbolism of Scottish clan identity, with every thread imbued with the stories of those who bore it before us. While no designer's name is recorded, the very existence of this tartan attests to its enduring significance, a vibrant tapestry that continues to honour the memory of Scotland's noble clans and their forebears.

As a symbol of tradition and excellence, this corporate tartan is now cherished by Dege of Saville Row as an integral part of their identity, proudly worn by employees and associated with the values of loyalty, heritage, and expertise that define the company's esteemed reputation.

name: Delta Lambda Phi

As a symbol of brotherhood and pride, the tartan's distinct colours - green representing the fraternity as a whole, gold signifying active membership, white denoting alumni status, and black honouring those who have passed on - weave together to form an enduring testament to the bond between brothers. This carefully crafted design is not merely a fashion statement but a meaningful expression of the fraternity's values and heritage, allowing its wearers to proudly display their affiliation and connection to this sacred brotherhood.

name: Denny Hunting

Its unique characteristics, now safeguarded through registration, serve as a tangible connection to the rich tapestry of Scottish tradition and history, honouring the storied past while continuing to weave a sense of belonging for those who wear it with pride.

As a heritage tartan, it proudly wears its history on its sleeve, connecting generations to the land, craft, and people that have shaped it.

Designed by West Coast Woolen Mill, Dewar is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's iconic tartans, carefully woven to capture the essence of the nation's storied past.

The restrictions surrounding its use are clear: this tartan is an exclusive trademark of Dewars, reserved exclusively for their esteemed brand. With its bold, symbolic flair, Dewar's Highlander has become a synonymous embodiment of Scottish heritage and tradition, expertly woven into the fabric of modern business identity.

With its bold colours and distinctive design, the Dickie tartan serves as a symbol of heritage and identity, perfect for those seeking to connect with their roots or pay tribute to this special connection with Scotland.

description: The Digital Equipment Corp. tartan is a distinctive corporate pattern that embodies the pioneering spirit of Scotland's textile heritage, closely tied to the world-renowned technology giant Digital Equipment Corporation (DEC). Designed by Chris Aitken of renowned Scottish tailor Geoffrey Tailor Highland Crafts, this tartan was woven in 100% pure Scottish wool and created specifically for the Computer in Society forum, held in Edinburgh in 1991.
