This enigmatic tartan has been identified as the ancestral fabric of the Black Douglas, an historical figure unconnected to this specific design, but still imbued with symbolism and significance. As part of Scotland's Clan family category, it is a testament to the intricate web of loyalty, duty, and kinship that bound families together in days gone by. Its designation as "Black" underscores the darkened history of this particular tartan, one whose roots stretch back through the ages to forge an enduring legacy of Scottish tradition and identity.

This tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile traditions, woven into the fabric of history and still proudly worn by descendants of the clans that once bore it.

Douglas of Roxburgh [default]

description: The Drambuie Dress tartan is a captivating blend of tradition and modernity, born from the marriage of two iconic Scottish heritage threads: the MacKinnon Hunting tartan and the corporate colours of the esteemed Drambuie Liqueur Co Ltd. Registered as a Corporate tartan, this distinctive design holds a special significance for those affiliated with the renowned liqueur company, and indeed, anyone drawn to its bold, honey-gold hues reminiscent of Scotland's sun-kissed hillsides. Only permitted for official use by the Drambuie Liqueur Co Ltd, this corporate tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, woven from threads of tradition, heritage, and modern elegance.

With restrictions in place to ensure authenticity, this tartan is a true representation of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, expertly woven to evoke the spirit of adventure, tradition, and luxury that defines the Drambuie brand.

name: Paisley Drennan
description: The Drennan tartan, named after its esteemed clan heritage, boasts an intricate weave of blues and greens reminiscent of Scotland's rolling hills and glacial lochs. Its rich colours evoke the rugged beauty of the Scottish Borders, where the tartan originated with D.C. Dalgliesh's adaptation of the original design. Although the green hue has been subtly altered to a vibrant lime tone, the essence of the tartan remains unchanged, connecting its wearers to the storied history and cultural identity of Clan Drennan. As a testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage, this tartan continues to be woven with pride by those who honour their ancestral roots.

name: Drummond (Clans Originaux) Grey
description: The Drummond, Grey is a classic Clan tartan steeped in Scotland's rich heritage, its subtle nuances evoking the storied history of the Drummond family. Registered with the Clans Originaux category, this timeless design is rooted in tradition, its intricate pattern weaving together the threads of loyalty and kinship that have defined Scottish clans for centuries. Although the original count was taken from a photograph in 1880, and has since been confirmed as inaccurate, the Drummond, Grey remains an iconic representation of the family's esteemed heritage, its distinctive shades of grey, blue, green, and yellow evoking the mist-shrouded glens and rugged heather-covered moors of Scotland's Highlands. This tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Clan Drummond, its beauty and significance forever etched in the fabric of Scottish tradition.

name: Drummond Grant variant
description: The Drummond tartan is a rich and storied fabric, its intricate sett woven with the precision of tradition. Dating back to 1822, when the esteemed clan wore it in formal attire for an audience with George IV in Edinburgh, this tartan holds a deep historical significance. The design closely resembles the pattern created by McIan, but controversy surrounds its origins, with some sources claiming it is actually a variation of the Grant tartan. Despite the uncertainty surrounding its provenance, one thing remains clear: the Drummond tartan has been an integral part of Scottish heritage for centuries, woven into the fabric of family legacy and clan identity. Its inclusion in the Smith brothers' 1850 publication, 'The Clan and Family Tartans of Scotland', solidified its place as a revered symbol of the Drummond name, and it continues to be cherished by families to this day.

name:
Drummond of Fingask [default]

The original 'Drummond of Perth' sett, with its distinctive red and blue hues, has been modified to create a variant that omits the white stripe border, evoking a sense of elegance and sophistication. As featured in Stewart's influential publication, 'Old and Rare Scottish Tartans', this tartan design is steeped in tradition and history, making it an invaluable addition to any collection, offering a poignant glimpse into Scotland's storied past and the revered legacy of Clan Drummond.

name:

The subtle nuances and subtle variations in tone evoke the rolling hills and storied history of Strathallan Castle, a true treasure trove of Scotland's cultural heritage.

The unassuming design may belie its complex history, with subtle variations and nuances that speak to the clan's storied tradition. Unfortunately, the designer's identity remains shrouded in mystery, adding to the tartan's enigmatic allure. Nevertheless, this historic fabric holds a deep honour within Scotland's cultural heritage, its threads woven from a long-forgotten era of grandeur and bravery, forever bound to the proud legacy of Clan Drummond.

name: Dryburgh [default]
description: The storied Dryburgh tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans, its bold, dark blues and reds evoking the very essence of tradition and honour. As a matriculated Name tartan, it has been woven with great care and attention to detail, drawing inspiration from the coat of arms of Sir William Dryburgh, whose name this tartan proudly bears. The three martlet birds, a symbol of courage and loyalty, are skillfully incorporated into the design, serving as a poignant reminder of the family's proud history. Woven by the talented hands of William J. Dryburgh himself, this tartan is not merely a fashion statement but a badge of pride for all who bear the name, their ancestry proudly displayed through every intricate thread and subtle nuance.

name: Dryfe [default]
description: The Dryfe tartan, named after the historic county of Dumfriesshire in Scotland's rich Lowlands, is a testament to the country's storied heritage. Registered by Jedburgh Woollen Mill, this distinctive Name tartan weaves together threads of traditional craftsmanship and family legacy. Originally classified as a Fashion tartan, its origins were later rediscovered as a family crest from a local clan, reflecting the intricate web of history and identity that underpins Scottish tartanry. Today, the Dryfe tartan stands proud in the Johnston Collection, a poignant reminder of Dumfriesshire's proud past, and invites wearers to pay homage to the county's storied traditions, while also embracing the timeless beauty and craftsmanship that defines this most authentic of Scottish textiles.

name: Dublin Irish County
description: The Dublin County tartan, created by Polly Wittering for House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., is a vibrant and iconic representation of Irish heritage, distinctly situated within the realm of fashion rather than traditional District designs. Originally intended to fall under the District category, its registration has been clarified by the Scottish Tartans Authority, who have specified that documentary proof is required to authenticate its status as an officially sanctioned tartan for the county. This striking design embodies the rich history and culture of Dublin, with its bold colours and intricate patterns paying homage to the city's storied past. As a fashion tartan, it lends itself perfectly to adding a touch of Irish flair to clothing and textiles, making it a popular choice among those seeking to celebrate their affinity for this magnificent Emerald Isle city.

name: Duclos (Richard) personal #2
description: The Brittany National tartan is a vibrant and historic district tartan born from the vision of Richard Duclos, a French weaver who sought to pay tribute to his Breton heritage. Originally designated as 'Tartan of Brittany', this stunning design has strong connections to the cultural traditions of the region. As a district tartan, its acceptance was not formally documented by local authorities, but it remains an integral part of inter-Celtic celebrations, particularly at the annual Tartan Day festival in Paris, organised by the Breizhlander Association, which brings together kilt wearers from Cornwall, Wales, Ireland, Manx, and Scotland. This tartan's significance extends beyond its technical characteristics, speaking to a rich cultural exchange and shared heritage among Celtic nations, with Duclos' creation serving as a symbol of cross-cultural appreciation and celebration.

name: Duclos (Richard) personal #3
description: The Brittany National Walking tartan is a vibrant and dynamic fashion design that proudly celebrates the rich cultural heritage of Brittany, France's westernmost region. Registration notes reveal its origins as an adaptation of STR #364, a tartan inspired by the Breton people's affinity for tradition and identity. As a Fashion category design, this tartan embodies the perfect blend of modernity and nostalgia, evoking the spirit of a nation that values community and cultural pride. Inspired by the annual Tartan Day festival in Paris, which brings together Celtic nations to celebrate their shared heritage, the Brittany National Walking tartan is a testament to the enduring power of tradition and inter-Celtic solidarity. Designed by Richard Duclos, this tartan is not only a stylish statement but also a tribute to the unique cultural identity of Brittany, where history, language, and community come together in perfect harmony.

name: Duke of Perth [default]
description: This exquisite Unnamed C18th #4 (Duke of Perth) tartan is a captivating representation of Scotland's rich heritage, woven from threads of history and tradition. Designed by renowned artist Dominique Dupra, this unique pattern is inspired by an 18th-century painting housed in the National Portrait Gallery in Edinburgh, and has been immortalised for posterity within the Register of Tartans. As a 'Other' category tartan, it defies traditional clan affiliations, instead embodying the essence of Scotland's broader cultural identity. With its intricate colour palette and masterful design, this tartan is an honour to its namesake, the Duke of Perth, and a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy as a land of timeless beauty and tradition.

name: Duke of Rothesay Hunting
description: The Rothesay Hunting, Duke of tartan is a historic District tartan woven with rich tradition and significance. Worn by Prince Charles as part of his private attire, yet retaining its original name, this tartan pays homage to Scotland's storied past. Designed in the 1940s by skilled weavers, it evolved from a colour change of the Wilsons' Rothesay sett, a classic kilt pattern. This tartan was once showcased in the West Highland and is now housed in the National Museum, testament to its enduring appeal. With its intricate count and subtle colour variations, the Rothesay Hunting, Duke of tartan embodies the elegance and heritage of Scottish tradition, evoking images of grand estates, hunting expeditions, and noble pursuits, all tied to a legacy that continues to inspire pride among Scots and tartan enthusiasts alike.

name: Duke of York Hunting
description: The Duke of York Hunting tartan is a majestic Royal design, steeped in tradition and heritage, gifted to His Grace by esteemed textile firm Kinloch Anderson Ltd. Bearing witness to the enduring legacy of Scottish tartantry, this regal pattern takes its place within the prestigious 'Royal Collection' of the Scottish Tartans Society. A masterful fusion of rich hues and intricate weaves, the Duke of York Hunting tartan evokes the storied traditions of Scotland's noble hunting heritage, conjuring images of bracing Highlands air and spirited chases across rolling glens. As a testament to the enduring bond between Scotland's aristocracy and its ancient textile traditions, this tartan design continues to delight and inspire those who wear it with honour and pride, forging an unbreakable link to Scotland's storied past.

name:
Duke of York [default]
[AKA] Duke of York Earl of Inverness
[AKA] Inverness Hunting #2
description: The Duke of York tartan is a storied District tartan steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition, worn by royalty with distinction. Originally associated with the Earl of Inverness, King George V was first seen wearing it while holding both titles, and later, his son King George VI continued to don the tartan. The design, featuring deep blues reminiscent of MacLaine of Lochbuie's colours, is woven with striking red and yellow lines that pay homage to its noble past. As a District tartan, its unique pattern tells a story of Scottish history and territorial identity, evoking images of Highland hunting grounds and the rugged beauty of Lochaber. Though its exact history remains shrouded in mystery, this tartan's association with royalty and nobility lends it an air of honour and tradition, making it a compelling choice for those seeking to weave their own connection to Scotland's storied past.

name: Dunbar Hunting
description: The Dunbar Hunting tartan is a richly woven tribute to the esteemed Clan Dunbar, with its distinctive black and blue hues evoking the wild beauty of Scotland's rugged landscapes. First designed by Tom Dunbar in 1986, the tartan was carefully vetted by the Chief of the Clan himself, Col. Dr. Sir James Dunbar of Mochrum, Bt., ensuring that it met the highest standards of quality and authenticity. With its unique combination of darker blues and muted greens, this tartan design pays homage to the clan's proud heritage as hunters and warriors, while also reflecting their deep connection to the land and traditions of Scotland. Though initially recorded in 2000, the Dunbar Hunting tartan remains an integral part of Clan Dunbar's identity, proudly worn by members of the family and their descendants around the world.

name: Dunbar Plaid
description: The Dunbar Plaid, a timeless and evocative tartan pattern, tells the story of a storied Scottish heritage. This distinctive design, with its rich blues and greys, is believed to have originated from a 19th century plaid once owned by Dunbars of Invereen, a prominent Highland clan. As an 'Other' category tartan, it does not bear the name of a specific Clan or community, yet its roots in Scottish tradition remain undeniable. Despite the unknown designer, the tartan's provenance is evident in its intricate weave and subtle nuances, which evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. With no restrictions on its use, this tartan invites those with a passion for Scotland's rich tapestry to incorporate it into their own heritage or as a nod to the country's storied past.

name: Dunbar [default]
description: The Dunbar tartan is a proud embodiment of Scotland's storied clan heritage, its rich history woven into the very fabric of its intricate pattern. Registered as part of The Sobieski Stewarts' family tartans, this esteemed Lowland clan has left an indelible mark on Scottish tradition. Dating back to the Vestiarium Scoticum, a seminal 17th-century collection of tartan patterns, the Dunbar sett is a testament to the enduring legacy of this once-mighty family. With its carefully balanced colours and subtle nuances, this tartan design reflects the complexities and intricacies of Scottish clan culture, evoking a sense of tradition, honour, and heritage that continues to captivate those who wear it today.

name: Dunbarton Quebeck
description: The Dunbarton (Quebec) tartan, a fashion favourite amongst enthusiasts of Scottish heritage, boasts a unique and captivating colour palette that reflects the province's rich cultural identity. Designed by PikMills Ltd, with an unknown creative mind behind it, this tartan is inspired by the storied history of Scotland, yet uniquely Canadian in its interpretation. Its restrictions reflect the distinction from the traditional Dunbarton tartan of Scotland, ensuring a distinctiveness that sets it apart as a distinctly Quebecois design. Weaving together elements of tradition and innovation, the Dunbarton (Quebec) tartan embodies the spirit of Canada's French-Scottish roots, inviting wearers to proudly showcase their connection to this storied heritage.

name: Dunbog Primary School
description: This vibrant Corporate tartan, registered by Colin Armstrong, pays homage to Dunbog Primary School in Newburgh, Fife, where the winning design was first showcased in a pupil competition. The distinctive pattern showcases a rich blend of colours, carefully selected to represent the school's spirit and community. As a corporate tartan, it is designed for business and organisational wear, yet its origins are deeply rooted in Scottish heritage and tradition. With its bold weave and thoughtful colour palette, this tartan is sure to be a striking addition to any company's attire or branding, proudly evoking the values of creativity, innovation, and community that define Dunbog Primary School.

name:
Duncan [default]
[AKA] Leslie of Wards
description: The Duncan tartan is a storied and enigmatic pattern, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's clans and families. Originally registered in 1880 as 'Duncan or Leslie of Wardis', this distinctive tartan was first recorded in Clans Originaux, a seminal work on Scottish tartanry. Although its origins are shrouded in mystery, with no early examples to illustrate its history, the Duncan tartan has remained a fascinating and unique contribution to Scotland's textile legacy. Notably, it diverges from the Leslie Hunting tartan (#1113), yet retains certain characteristics that evoke a sense of clan identity and tradition. Its association with the name 'Duncan' or 'Leslie', though unclear, underscores the complex and sometimes nuanced nature of Scottish clan affiliations, adding to the tartan's enduring allure as a symbol of Scottish heritage and cultural significance.

name: Dundas [default]
description: Dundas #2 is a stirring example of Scottish heritage, born from the heart of Clan Dundas and their enduring legacy. Designed by Sobieski Stewarts, The, this tartan weaves together a rich tapestry of traditional Highland colours - emerald green, navy blue, and jet black - with twin flashes of bold red, evoking the fiery passion of Scotland's turbulent past. For generations, the Dundas clan played a pivotal role in restoring the Highlands to its former glory, their bravery and resilience inspiring the creation of this iconic tartan. Registration notes confirm its connection to the Vestiarium Scoticum (1842), while Henry Dundas's pivotal bill to parliament in 1784 ensured the return of estates forfeited during the '45 rebellion, cementing the tartan's place in Scottish tradition.

name: Dundee Football Club
description: The Dundee Football Club tartan is a vibrant, corporate motif born from Scotland's proud sporting heritage. Designed by Tartan Sportswear in 1990, this distinctive tartan was woven to great acclaim by House of Edgar in 1997, with a sample now held in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Collection. Named after the legendary Jags of Dundee FC, this tartan embodies the passion and pride of Scotland's second city, reflecting the values of loyalty, dedication, and community that define the club and its supporters. As a corporate motif, it has become synonymous with the team's identity, worn by fans and patrons alike to show allegiance to the team's rich history and tradition.

name: Dundee United Football Club
description: The Dundee United Football Club tartan is a vibrant and iconic corporate tartan, born from the passion and pride of Scotland's largest football club. Registered by Lochcarron of Scotland, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the city of Dundee and its beloved team, showcasing a striking interplay of blues, yellows, and greens. As part of the Corporate category, this tartan is specifically designed for business and commercial applications, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to showcase their connection to the football club's rich history and Scottish heritage. With no restrictions on use or colour variation, this tartan invites businesses to don its colours with pride, symbolising unity, community, and a commitment to the values that have come to define Dundee United Football Club.

name: Dunlop Dress
description: The Dunlop Dress tartan, officially registered by the Scottish Tartans Authority in 1984, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans. This distinctive pattern, featuring bold blues, greens, and golds, was carefully crafted by Richard Dunlop, the second President of the Dunlop Family Clan Society, as part of an ongoing effort to establish a clan tartan for his esteemed family. The result is a vibrant and striking design that not only reflects the proud history of the Dunlops but also serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring bonds between Scottish families and their ancestral lands. Woven with meticulous care, this tartan now holds a special place in the hearts of those who wear it, symbolising honour, tradition, and a deep connection to Scotland's storied past.

name: Dunlop Hunting
description: The Dunlop Hunting tartan, officially registered in 1984 (#1197), is a rich tribute to the esteemed Dunlop clan. As the result of meticulous efforts by Richard Dunlop, second President of the Dunlop Family Clan Society, this distinctive tartan was unveiled at Grandfather Mountain Games in 1982, marking an important milestone in the clan's history. The intricate design weaves together the past and present, with its light brown hues sourced from a 19th-century woven sample now held within the Jack Dalgety Collection, adding a touch of authenticity to this family tartan. With its completion of both hunting and dress variants two years later, the Dunlop Hunting tartan has become an integral part of clan heritage, proudly worn by Dunlop kin and enthusiasts alike, symbolising tradition, unity, and the enduring spirit of Scotland's noble clans.

name: Dunlop [default]
description: The Dunlop tartan is a proud emblem of Scottish heritage, born from the dedication of Richard Dunlop, the second President of the Dunlop Family Clan Society, in 1974. This storied clan tartan was formally established in 1982, with Charles Thompson's expertise playing a significant role in its creation, alongside Richard's vision. The resulting design is a masterful blend of colours and threads, woven by esteemed houses such as House of Edgar & Lochcarron, which has since become an integral part of Scottish tradition. Originally registered under the number 1197 with the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan was showcased at the Grandfather Mountain Games in 1982, marking a significant milestone for the Dunlop clan family. Notably, the design underwent a count change in 2005 to align with the Scottish Tartans Society's documentation of 1983, solidifying its place in the annals of Scottish tartan history. Today, the Dunlop tartan proudly represents the heritage and legacy of this esteemed clan family, evoking a sense of connection to Scotland's rich cultural tapestry.

name: Dunmore [default]
description: The Hose (Dunmore) tartan is an intriguing and historic design, imbued with significance from its origins as a 18th-century family heidgear, worn by the Dunmore clan. Discovered in a portrait of Jonny Dunmore circa 1760, this particular tartan is believed to have been a favourite among his kin, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of the Scottish Highlands during this period. Classified under 'Other', the Hose (Dunmore) tartan defies traditional categorisation by clan or geographical association, yet its presence in historical records solidifies its connection to Scottish tradition and heritage. Designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, a renowned weavers' dynasty at the time, this tartan's subtle nuances and earthy tones evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's natural landscape, while its intriguing provenance reminds us of the intricate stories woven into the fabric of our history.

name: Dunn (John) personal
description: Dunn #2 is a storied Name tartan that proudly embodies the heritage and identity of the Dunn clan. Designed by esteemed weaver John Dunn, this distinctive pattern has been carefully crafted to represent his family's history and traditions. Originating from 'A Wee Bit of Scotland' in Ontario, Canada, this tartan holds great significance for those tracing their ancestry back to the Dunn lineages. Due to its strong connections to a specific clan, it is essential that permission is sought from John Dunn before weaving, ensuring its authentic representation. Woven with precision by Fraser and Kirkbright of Vancouver, Dunn #2 remains an essential part of Scottish textile heritage, rich in tradition and steeped in cultural significance.

name: Dunn
description: The Dunn tartan, woven by David McGill of International Tartans, holds a rich heritage within its carefully crafted threads. Commissioned by Stuart Nichol of Edinburgh on behalf of Miss Rona Dunn and her family, this tartan represents a distinctive name tartan, one that pays tribute to the esteemed individual whose legacy it embodies. As a Name tartan, Dunn's significance lies in its association with a single family or surname, imbuing the fabric with personal connection and cultural tradition. The subtle nuances of its colour palette, including a deep blue sett that evokes the Scottish skies, serve as a poignant reminder of the enduring bonds between this family and their Scottish heritage. By virtue of its restrictions requiring the designer's consent for use, the Dunn tartan remains a treasured family heirloom, preserved for posterity through careful stewardship.

name: Dyce [default]
description: The Dyce tartan, with its distinct blue and green hues, tells the story of a family's heritage in Scotland's ancient clans. Registration notes reveal that this traditional pattern was first documented by J Claude in his 1880 'Clans Originaux' pattern book, which predates the modern woven version by nearly three decades. The Dyce tartan's evolution is marked by subtle changes, with its single black lines on blue giving way to the characteristic tramlines now seen on this iconic design. Weaved into the fabric of Scotland's history, the Dyce tartan holds a special place in the hearts of those connected to Clan Dyce, whose legacy continues to be celebrated through The House of Edgar's masterful craftsmanship.

name: Dyer [default]
description: The Dyer tartan, a timeless family heritage worn with pride by those sharing the esteemed surname, holds a rich history dating back to the 13th century origins in Dumfries, Scotland. Designed by renowned heraldic expert Donald Suttie Smith in 2001 for James Dyer of Wishaw, Scotland, this tartan serves as a testament to the family's Scottish roots and can be worn by anyone bearing the name. With its distinctive colour palette, the Dyer tartan embodies the tradition and symbolism inherent in Scottish clan systems, where kinship is deeply intertwined with heritage. While restrictions apply, allowing only those of the name to wear it, this tartan remains an enduring symbol of family identity and pride, connecting past generations to their ancestral homeland.

name: Dykes (Sandy) personal
description: The Dykes, of Perthshire tartan embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's storied past, its origins dating back to the 12th century in Strathclyde before spreading to other regions, including the picturesque Perthshire and the Auchterarder area. This distinctive tartan is a masterful blend of influences, drawing upon the iconic Royal Stewart with the addition of dark green hues reminiscent of the old Perthshire design and blue from the Strathclyde tradition. With its complex history and subtle colour variations, this tartan design holds a special place in the hearts of those bearing the surname Dykes or its various spellings, and is now preserved through the meticulous weaving skills of Geoffrey Highland Crafts. However, to ensure its integrity, Sandy Dykes retains sole ownership and control over its production, requiring permission from the individual or organisation seeking to weave or manufacture this tartan, making it a true testament to the power of Scottish heritage and tradition.

name: East Carolina University
description: The East Carolina University Tartan is a rich and vibrant tribute to the storied history of the esteemed institution, proudly representing the university's cherished purple and gold colours. As part of the Corporate category, this prestigious tartan has been carefully designed by Chen, Runying in collaboration with the College of Human Ecology's merchandising major program. The distinctive pattern is woven from the iconic school hues, evoking memories of the early East Carolina Teacher Training School days and the 'Servire' tradition that has come to define the university's ever-growing community. With its unique restrictions ensuring only official permission from the Dean of the College of Human Ecology can bring it to life, this tartan embodies the spirit of East Carolina University, a true emblem of its proud heritage and unwavering dedication to the values of service, tradition, and community.

name: Ebronen [default]
description: The Ebronen tartan, woven with precision by Sven Ebert, is a testament to the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage, even in its Germanic roots. This unique Name tartan was carefully crafted for the Ebronen Family of Muhlhausen, Germany, and is a poignant example of the global connections that have shaped Scotland's tartan tradition. With eight distinctive colours, arranged in a 17-inch sett size, this tartan stands out from the traditional Scottish patterns, reflecting its origins as an imported design. The Ebronen family's personal tartan serves as a tangible link to their German heritage, while its adoption by Kilts & More of Muhlhausen underscores the modern era's ability to blend and celebrate diverse cultural traditions. As such, this intriguing tartan is not only a beautiful expression of Scottish textile artistry but also a powerful symbol of cultural exchange and family identity.

name: Edinburgh Crystal
description: The Edinburgh Crystal tartan is a majestic representation of Scottish heritage in corporate attire, aptly reflecting the city's renowned reputation for luxury and sophistication. With its subtle yet striking pattern, this tartan design was expertly crafted by Sandra Campbell, an employee of the esteemed Edinburgh Crystal company, to symbolise the enduring spirit of Scotland's capital city. As a Corporate tartan, it is perfectly suited for formal wear and business attire, while its beauty also lends itself to making a statement in more casual settings. With no restrictions on usage, this tartan design is free to be worn with pride by those who seek to evoke the glamour and prestige of Edinburgh's crystal industry, embodying the perfect blend of tradition and modern style.

name: Edinburgh Marketing
description: Edinburgh Marketing tartan is a vibrant and modern corporate design inspired by Scotland's rich heritage and cultural significance. Registration notes reveal that the tartan was created in honour of Lord Drummond, the esteemed Lord Provost of Edinburgh, who played a pivotal role in shaping the city's historic New Town district. The colours - navy blue, fiery red, and crisp white - pay homage to the corporate identity of Edinburgh Marketing while evoking the dynamic spirit of Scotland's capital city. Kinloch Anderson Ltd, renowned for their expertise in traditional tartan design, have skillfully woven together these colours to create a striking fabric that not only pays tribute to Lord Drummond but also proudly represents Edinburgh Marketing.

name: Edinburgh University Management School
description: The University of Edinburgh Business School's corporate tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage in the world of business. Designed by Dr Robert Harwood in 2002, this distinctive tartan weaves together the colours of the University's coat of arms and logo, paying homage to Scotland's rich tradition of entrepreneurship and academic excellence. The complex pattern, initially designed to reflect the multifaceted nature of business operations, has been simplified to create a striking yet accessible design that embodies the innovative spirit of the university. As one of only two corporate tartans approved for use by the University of Edinburgh, this iconic pattern is reserved for official wear, making it a coveted symbol of affiliation and distinction among students, staff, and alumni.

name: Edwards of Wales
description: The Edwards tartan is a distinctive Name tartan that proudly wears its Welsh heritage on its sleeve. Designed by Sheila Daniel for Wales Tartan Centres in collaboration with Cambrian Woollen Mill, this vibrant design has captured the hearts of many since its introduction around 1998. With its unique warp and weft thread combinations, and odd-numbered threads, Edwards stands out from other Celtic tartans, evoking a sense of modernity within traditional Scottish weaving. While its historical and genealogical significance is not necessarily tied to territorial identity, the 'of Wales' prefix serves as a testament to its origins and proves the design's connection to the nation's rich textile heritage. Notably, usage of this tartan requires consent from Wales Tartan Centres in Swansea, underscoring the importance of respecting cultural traditions and preserving the integrity of this unique design.

name: Elliot (Clans Originaux)
description: The Elliot tartan, named after its esteemed Clan family, holds a rich history rooted in Scotland's Border region. First recorded in the late 19th century, this unique maroon and blue tartan has been woven by various skilled weavers over the years, including Andrew Elliot of Selkirk, who created an evening version for the Chief in 1993. The Elliots are a prominent family with a long-standing Chiefship, which once belonged to the Redheugh branch but was later transferred to the Stobs near Hawick in Roxburghshire. This tartan's distinctive sett and colour palette have been carefully preserved and reimagined by talented weavers like D.C. Dalgliesh of Selkirk, who wove exquisite silk items in the evening sett. The Elliot tartan remains an important part of Scotland's heritage, symbolising the honour and tradition of the Elliots family, and is now worn with pride by their descendants and those associated with this storied Clan.

name: Ellis of Wales
description: The Ellis tartan is a unique and modern creation born from the heritage of Wales, yet distinctly separate from its traditional Celtic roots. Registered under the category of Name, this vibrant design was carefully crafted by Sheila Daniel, in association with Cambrian Woollen Mill, to represent the growing identity of Wales Tartan Centres. Although it does not claim historical or genealogical significance, the Ellis tartan proudly wears its "of Wales" badge, a nod to its contemporary origins. What sets this tartan apart from others is its innovative construction, featuring odd-numbered threads and striking variations in warp and weft threads, resulting in a visually stunning pattern that defies traditional Celtic norms. As such, it's essential to note the restrictions surrounding its use, requiring consent from Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea prior to weaving. This tartan serves as a testament to the evolving nature of Welsh heritage and tradition, one that proudly asserts its modernity while remaining deeply rooted in the country's rich cultural history.

name: Elmore (Chattan) personal
description: The Elmore tartan is a rare and personal creation, registered as a Name tartan, signifying its unique association with the Elmore family lineage. This distinctive tartan tells the story of Brian Elmore's heritage, born to Kathy and Cecil in Ohio, who brought a piece of Scottish tradition to their American roots. Despite being initially refused due to its close resemblance to other well-established clans like MacGill, Chattan, and MacFarland, this tartan was ultimately accepted and registered as part of the family's honourable legacy. As a Restricted family tartan, it serves as a testament to the family's history and cultural identity, now preserved for future generations to cherish and weave their own stories within its rich, symbolic fabric.

name: Elphinstone [default]
description: The Elphinstone tartan is a proud representation of Scottish heritage, tracing its roots to Montgomery, a Clan/Family tartan with a distinctive twist: the substitution of rich purple stripes for the traditional blue. This deliberate deviation from tradition speaks to the creativity and innovation of those who brought this tartan into being. As documented in the Scottish Tartans Authorities Johnston Collection, Elphinstone is a sample of Montgomery, first recorded in 1986 by Pringles of Inverness. While the original source was claimed to be Vestiarium Scoticum, further research has revealed that this tartan does not exist within the published version of the iconic tome. Nonetheless, the Elphinstone tartan stands as a testament to the ever-evolving nature of Scottish weaving traditions, embracing the past while forging its own unique path forward.

name: Encyclopedia Britannica
description: The Encyclopaedia Britannica tartan is a unique corporate design born from the esteemed pages of Scotland's most iconic publication, the Encyclopaedia Britannica. Created by renowned designer Harry Lindley for Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this tartan pays homage to one of its founding fathers, drawing inspiration from the Farquharson tartan in the process. Accredited by the Scottish Tartans Society, this corporate tartan is designed to be worn with pride by those who value knowledge, tradition, and heritage. With its distinctive colour palette, the Encyclopaedia Britannica tartan embodies the spirit of Scotland's rich cultural history, while serving as a symbol of excellence in the world of publishing. Its registration notes not only attest to its connection to this revered publication, but also underscore its respectability as a corporate tartan, suitable for formal occasions and business attire.

name: Erskine Dress Dance Black
description: The Erskine tartan, with its striking black and white hues, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans. Registered in 1894 by Hugh MacPherson, a renowned Scottish designer, this distinctive sett has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition for generations. Initially based on a dress version of the Vestiarium Scoticum pattern, it is believed to have originated with D.C. Dalgliesh of Selkirk's skilled loom. Now widely accepted as an authentic Erskine tartan, this design not only pays tribute to the storied history of Clan Erskine but also serves as a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy of craftsmanship and cultural pride.

name: Erskine Dress Dance Blue (a)
description: The Erskine, Blue tartan, designed by renowned kiltmaker Hugh Macpherson, is a stunning example of traditional Scottish fashion. Originally created for informal occasions such as dancing, this vibrant dress tartan proudly showcases the distinctive hues of blue that give it its name, a nod to the storied history of Clan Erskine. With its bold colour palette and intricate design, this tartan was once a staple in Edinburgh's kiltmaking scene, evoking the lively spirit of Scotland's cultural heritage. Now registered as a D.C. Dalgliesh weave, the Erskine, Blue tartan continues to delight fashion enthusiasts with its unique blend of tradition and style, making it an honourable addition to any wardrobe.

name: Erskine Dress Purple
description: Erskine Purple is a vibrant and elegant fashion tartan, originally designed for the noble House of Erskine. Weaved with meticulous care by Hugh MacPherson, this distinctive Dance tartan tells the story of a bygone era of Scottish grandeur. The rich purple hues evoke the majesty of Scotland's natural landscape, while the intricate patterns and subtle colour gradations evoke the tradition of traditional Highland dancing. With its unique character and flair, Erskine Purple has become a sought-after choice for fashion enthusiasts seeking to connect with Scotland's storied heritage. As a registered Dance tartan, it is woven by skilled weavers such as David C Dalgliesh of Selkirk, ensuring that each fabric is imbued with the passion and expertise of Scotland's finest textile artisans.

name: Erskine Green
description: Erskine Green is a storied tartan with deep roots in Scottish heritage, designated as a Clan/Family tartan, signifying its association with the noble Erskine family, whose legacy spans centuries of Scottish history. This distinctive tartan was first recorded by the Scottish Tartans Society between 1970 and 1990, providing a glimpse into the traditional weaving practices of the time. The subtle nuances in its design are a testament to the skill of Scotland's master weavers, who painstakingly created each thread and yarn to produce a fabric that not only reflected their family's honour but also served as a symbol of their connection to the land and their ancestors. While the designer remains anonymous, Erskine Green stands as a proud embodiment of Scottish tradition, its rich colours evoking images of rolling hills, heather-covered moors, and the rugged beauty of the Highlands.

name: Erskine Hunting
description: The Erskine Hunting tartan, designated as Military Category by Her Majesty's government, holds a profound place in Scotland's rich military heritage. Registered in 1948, this distinctive sett was granted to the Royal Scots Fusiliers, who wore it with honour, proudly representing their esteemed lineage, the Earls of Mar. The design is steeped in tradition and cultural significance, its origins deeply intertwined with the family history of the aristocratic clan. Although conflicting opinions exist regarding the original sett's parameters, it is evident that this tartan has played a significant role in Scottish military history, evoking a sense of pride and connection to the nation's storied past.

name:
Erskine [default]
[AKA] Erskine Green #2
description: The Erskine tartan is a revered clan pattern steeped in history and tradition, its origins tracing back to the 18th century. First published in the Vestiarium Scoticum by the Sobieski brothers in 1842, this iconic design was later immortalised in Alexander Carmichael's collection of commercial tartans in the late 19th century. As one of the few patterns documented in the VS that can be dated to the 18th century, it provides a unique window into Scotland's rich textile heritage. The Erskine tartan is a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scottish weavers, its distinctive hues evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Highlands. As a clan tartan, it holds significance for the Erskine family and their descendants, who continue to proudly wear this pattern as a symbol of their heritage.

name: Esteba-Quer [default]
description: The Esteba-Quer tartan is a richly woven tribute to the enduring bonds between two storied Scottish clans, one from Scotland and the other from Spain. As a registered Name tartan, it holds great personal significance for its designer, Senora M.L. Quer, who brought together elements of the MacDonald of Clanranald tartan in a unique fusion that celebrates the close ties between families across the centuries. This Spanish-inspired tartan pays homage to the cultural exchange and historical connections that have shaped the lives of those who wear it, weaving together threads of tradition and heritage to create a vibrant, one-of-a-kind design that is both deeply personal and proudly familial.

name: Estes [default]
description: The Estes tartan, registered with the Scottish Tartans Society in 1986, is a striking Name tartan that pays homage to its eponymous designer, Bob Martin. This elegant design features a subtle lavender ground tone, reminiscent of Scotland's national colours, which provides a sophisticated backdrop for the intricate weaving of blue and white stripes, evoking the rolling hills and sparkling lochs of the Scottish countryside. The judicious use of red and green hues adds a pop of vibrancy, echoing the rich cultural heritage of Wales and Ireland, respectively. With its subtle nuances and classic beauty, the Estes tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich textile tradition, and its registration by the esteemed Scottish Tartans Society underscores its legitimacy as an authentic representation of Scottish design.

name: Evans of Wales
description: The Evans of Wales tartan is a vibrant and distinctive name tartan with a rich history that spans across generations. Registered by Sheila Daniel, the talented designer from Cambrian Woollen Mill in Powys, this unique pattern showcases a blend of colour and technique that sets it apart from other Celtic-inspired designs. Initially created for the growing popularity of wearing Cilt in Wales, which dates back to the late 1990s, this tartan has since become an iconic representation of Welsh heritage. Notably, its registration with the Intellectual Property Office comes with a crucial caveat: prior consent must be obtained from Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea, before weaving the design into fabric. As such, the Evans of Wales tartan is a testament to both the enduring power of tradition and the modern commercialisation of Celtic culture.

name: Ewbank [default]
description: The Ewbank tartan is a unique and storied Scottish heritage pattern, bearing the legacy of a distinguished family with roots tracing back to William the Conqueror's era. Named after Capt. Edward E Ewbank, the coordinator who championed its creation among a global community of Ewbanks from diverse backgrounds, this tartan is a testament to the enduring connection between Scottish traditions and those abroad. Inspired by the Vipont tartan, a design created in the 1930s, Keith Lumsden's rendition weaves together elements of the original with modern flair, incorporating colours from the Eubank coat of arms - rich black, golden hue, and fiery red. As a Name tartan, it is open to all spelling variants, including the variant Hughbank, and its presence honours not just the Ewbank family, but also those distant cousins who carry their name across the seas.

name: Exabyte Software
description: Exabyte, a dynamic corporate tartan designed by Keith Lumsden, pays homage to the innovative spirit of America's leading software firm, with its roots firmly planted in Scotland. This modern pattern is inspired by the country's rich textile heritage, yet its sleek and contemporary style makes it perfectly suited for the cutting-edge world of technology. By registering Exabyte as a corporate tartan, the company embodies its values of innovation, progress, and global connectivity. The design, while free from traditional clan affiliations, proudly represents the fusion of Scottish tradition and American ingenuity, reflecting the firm's commitment to pushing boundaries and shaping the digital landscape.

name: James Keith (Personal)
description: The Falconer of Labhdal tartan, named after its esteemed progenitor James K.R. Falconer, is a storied Name tartan born from a legacy of Scottish heritage and tradition. This distinctive design, expertly woven by Drove Weaving of Langholm, pays homage to the family's proud history, with lighter shades rendering the colours in a more subtle yet striking manner. The addition of an extra blue line in the centre of the green adds depth and nuance to this already iconic pattern, evoking the soaring wings of the falcon - a symbol long associated with speed, agility, and loyalty, all qualities embodied by the Falconer clan. As registered through Pride of Lammermuir, Lady Hilary Menzies' meticulous attention to detail ensures that this tartan is an authentic representation of its heritage, ready to be woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition.

name: Falkirk Football Club
description: The Falkirk Football Club tartan is a vibrant corporate tribute to Scotland's proud football heritage, expertly crafted by Strathmore Woollen Company Ltd. This distinctive tartan, registered under the Corporate category, proudly represents the values and traditions of Falkirk Football Club, a beloved institution in Scottish football. The design features a rich navy blue as its primary colour, which provides an impressive backdrop for the subtle black tramlines that add depth and visual interest to the pattern. The Count taken from Strathmore's woven sample ensures consistency across all production methods, reflecting the company's commitment to quality and heritage preservation. This tartan is not only a stylish addition to any corporate collection but also serves as a testament to Falkirk Football Club's rich history and dedicated fan base.

name: Farquharson #3
description: The Farquharson tartan, registered by James M Coutts in 1946, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's esteemed Clan Farquharson, whose ancestry stretches back to the 18th century. This intricately woven design is a testament to the long-standing tradition of tartan-making, with threads bearing witness to the clan's proud history. A sample from the Highland Society of London Collection bears the seal of Farquharson of Finzean, while four fragments, dated to 1774, were showcased at the Highland Exhibition in Inverness in 1930. Its connection to Black Watch and the innovative arrangement of overchecks hints at an even earlier origin, possibly predating 1800. This tartan holds honour within Scottish textile heritage, its presence a reminder of the clan's storied past and their place within Scotland's proud cultural tapestry.

name: Farquharson Dress
description: The Farquharson Dress tartan is a rich and storied design, steeped in the heritage of Scotland's ancient clans. As a registered family tartan, it holds significant importance for those bearing the surname or proud connections to this esteemed sept. With its intricate pattern of blues and greens, reminiscent of Scotland's rolling hills and lochs, this tartan is a testament to the country's timeless beauty and traditions. Though its designer remains unknown, their skillful weaving has captured the essence of Scottish culture, echoing the history and symbolism of this storied clan. As a proud symbol of identity and heritage, the Farquharson Dress tartan will continue to be cherished by those who wear it, serving as a tangible connection to Scotland's enduring legacy.

name: Ferguson Dress
description: The Ferguson Dress tartan, designed by Dalgliesh, D.C., is a timeless and elegant fashion tartan that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's weaving traditions. Originating from the world of high fashion, this distinctive pattern was initially prepared for weaving by D C Dalgliesh Ltd, showcasing the designer's attention to detail and skill. The restrictions in place reflect its status as a commercial design, carefully crafted to meet the demands of the fashion industry. Despite its evolution through two separate registrations - one with the Scottish Tartans Society (#371) featuring an alternative colour variation - the Ferguson Dress tartan remains a cherished representation of Scottish identity and cultural heritage. This iconic pattern has been meticulously revised by Count G. Newnham in 1986, ensuring its enduring presence in the world of fashion and beyond.

name:
Ferguson of Balquhidder [default]
[AKA] Ferguson of Balquhidder
description: The Ferguson of Balquhidder tartan is a revered clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, its origins tracing back to 1831 when James Logan first documented it in his esteemed The Scottish Gael. This distinctive pattern was designed to distinguish the Ferguson family from their kinship ties with the powerful Ferguson of Atholl, a testament to the intricate web of alliances and rivalries that defined Scotland's complex clan landscape. With its unique colour palette and carefully woven threads, this tartan pays homage to the storied history of Clan Ferguson, whose members have worn it for generations as a badge of honour and family pride. As registered by James Logan, this iconic design remains an enduring symbol of Scottish tradition and identity, its significance reinforced by D.C. Stewart's acknowledgement in his historical work.

name: Ferguson [default]
description: The Ferguson of Atholl tartan is an iconic Clan tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Woven with deep respect for its ancestral roots, this distinctive design has been passed down through generations as a symbol of family pride and identity. Registration notes reveal that the tartan's origins date back to the 1830s, initially known simply as 'Ferguson' before being later paired with the name 'of Atholl', which has become synonymous with this storied Clan. Today, the Ferguson of Atholl tartan is still worn by descendants of Malcolm Ferguson of Atholl, a prominent Scottish nobleman who lived in the 18th century, and serves as a powerful reminder of Scotland's rich cultural heritage and the enduring legacy of its families.

name: Fermanagh 1990
description: The Fermanagh tartan, with its distinctively woven threads, tells a story of rich heritage and cultural identity from Northern Ireland's storied county of Fermanagh. Designated as "Other", this unique tartan is a testament to the region's history and craftsmanship, though its origins are attributed to a mysterious tartan rug unearthed in the 1990s. The Fermanagh tartan now holds significance for those tracing their roots or celebrating local pride, evoking a sense of connection to the land and people that have shaped this captivating pattern over time.

name: Fiddes Kelvingrove Artifact
description: The Fiddes tartan is a captivating and enigmatic design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's cultural landscape. As an Artefact classification, it falls under the broader category of Other, signifying its uniqueness and distinction from traditional clan or family tartans. The registration notes reveal that this tartan has been housed in the esteemed Kelvingrove Museum in Glasgow for some time, suggesting a long-standing significance within Scottish society. Although the designer's name is not specified, the tartan's presence in such an iconic institution implies a level of importance and reverence. This intriguing design is no doubt imbued with the stories and traditions of Scotland's past, waiting to be unravelled by those who value the country's rich heritage and textile history.

name: Fiddes Rock and Wheel
description: The Fiddes #3 tartan, registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a stunning example of traditional Highland weaving. This clan tartan, named after its ancestral family connection, boasts a rich history dating back to the early 19th century, when it was first featured in William Wilson's stock list of 1800. Its unique 'rock & wheel' construction, characteristic of soft tartans from that era, adds an air of authenticity to this timeless design. As noted by Telford Dunbar in his seminal work "History of Highland Dress", this tartan was once a staple in the region, and its inclusion in the clan family's heritage is a testament to its enduring significance. With its distinctive colour palette and carefully crafted weave, Fiddes #3 embodies the spirit of Scottish tradition and heritage, inviting wearers to connect with their roots and celebrate the rich cultural legacy of the Highlands.

name: Fiddes [default]
description: The Fiddes tartan, borne by those proud bearers with a heritage rooted in Scotland's rich clan traditions, is a distinctive blend of earthy tones and subtle nuances that reflect its complex history. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds a special significance for families who have worn it for generations, passing down the stories and symbols encoded within its carefully woven threads. According to the registration notes, this tartan was first documented in 1975 by Jamie Scarlett MBE, who identified the threadcount that was originally intended but has since been modified to create a unique variant. Characterised by three purple stripes set against a rich green and blue background, with an absence of a red stripe next to the green pivot, the Fiddes tartan defies the traditional mathematical structures of the Wilson scheme, imbuing it with a sense of historical uniqueness and cultural depth that resonates deeply within Scotland's textile heritage.

name: Fife Flyers
description: The Fife Flyers Corporate Tartan is a vibrant and dynamic design inspired by Scotland's rich sporting heritage. Registered with Kirkwynd Highland House of Kirkcaldy, this distinctive tartan was specifically created to represent the esteemed Fife Flyers Ice Hockey team, the oldest ice hockey team in Britain. Founded in 1938, the team's proud history is woven into every thread of this unique corporate tartan. Designed by Erica Randall, a renowned expert in Scottish textiles, the Fife Flyers Tartan combines bold colours and intricate patterns to evoke the energy and passion of Scotland's hockey community. As a symbol of team spirit and loyalty, this tartan holds great significance for Fife Flyers supporters and is an iconic representation of Scottish sporting tradition.

name: Firefighters' Memorial
description: The Firefighters' Memorial tartan is a powerful tribute to those who have bravely fought fires and risked their lives to protect others, while also remembering those who have fallen in the line of duty. Designed by Kelly Stewart, this corporate tartan features a bold red background that echoes the flames of fire trucks, complemented by black threads in remembrance of the fallen heroes, and an intricate pattern of green and gold threads that pay homage to the Irish community's strong ties with the firefighting occupation. The three red lines woven throughout each square represent the devastating loss of 343 NYFD firefighters on September 11th, 2001, a staggering tragedy that the tartan aims to honour and commemorate. A portion of all sales will be donated to Firefighters' charities, ensuring that this tartan's impact extends beyond its fabric, as a symbol of solidarity and respect for those who serve with courage and selflessness.

name: Fitzgerald Blue
description: The Fitzgerald tartan is a quintessential representation of Scottish heritage, born from the imagination of Robert P. Fitzgerald, a renowned weaver who drew inspiration from the iconic Robertson tartan. This Clan/Family tartan was carefully crafted to pay homage to the esteemed family that bore its name, with JC Thomson noting that the distinctive Blue, Hunting, and Dress settts were meticulously designed by Mr Fitzgerald in Philadelphia. Woven with precision at Strathmore in the UK, this traditional tartan now resides in the esteemed Johnston Collection of the Scottish Tartans Authority, a testament to the enduring legacy of the Fitzgerald family's proud history.

name: Fitzgerald Dress
description: The Fitzgerald Dress tartan is a storied heritage pattern that embodies the rich traditions of the Fitzgerald clan, one of Scotland's most esteemed families. Designated as such by Robert P. Fitzgerald, a renowned Scottish-American designer from Philadelphia, this tartan set was inspired by the iconic Robertson tartan and forms part of what is believed to be the third instalment in the Fitzgerald trilogy, along with the Blue and Hunting sets. Registration notes suggest that these designs were meticulously crafted to reflect the clan's history and prestige, with each colour carefully chosen to represent a specific aspect of their heritage. As such, this tartan holds great significance for those tracing their family connections to the Fitzgeralds, offering a tangible link to Scotland's rich cultural past and a lasting tribute to the enduring legacy of this noble clan.

name: Fitzgerald Hunting
description: The Fitzgerald Hunting tartan is a storied blend of tradition and heritage, born from the Scottish clan system and passed down through generations. Designed by Robert P. Fitzgerald in Philadelphia, drawing inspiration from the iconic Robertson tartan, this set embodies the values of family, loyalty, and courage that define the FitzGerald name. With its distinctive Blue, Hunting, and Dress hues, carefully chosen to evoke a sense of nobility and adventure, this tartan weaves together the threads of Scottish history and culture. Its registration notes attest to its connection to the Johnston Collection in Scottish Tartans Authorities, underscoring the enduring significance of this traditional design within Scotland's rich textile heritage.

name: Fitzgerald Red
description: Fitzgerald Red is a complex and intriguing clan tartan, born from a confluence of creative energies in the late 19th century. Its origins lie with Robert P. Fitzgerald of Philadelphia, an individual who inadvertently found himself at the centre of a confusing tangle of tartans, all bearing the Fitzgerald name. Over time, this distinctive variation emerged, drawing upon traditional Scottish sett and Robertson sett principles, yet diverging into a distinct blue and hunting colour variation, as well as a fanciful dress tartan. As a Clan/Family tartan, Fitzgerald Red is deeply rooted in Scottish heritage and tradition, representing the proud history and cultural identity of those who bear its colours. Its registration notes reflect a fascinating tale of artistic expression and creative experimentation, making it a unique and captivating addition to the rich tapestry of Scotland's tartan traditions.

name: Fitzgibbon [default]
description: The Fitzgibbon tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish clans, born from the threads of family tradition and identity. Designed by Jeffrey Simmons in 2005 under its original name MacSimoin, this tartan has undergone a transformation as it passed into new hands. Initially intended for the Clan MacSimoin Irish society, it was later reimagined and re-recorded as Fitzsimmons before being adopted by Andrew Fitz-Gibbon, who now seeks to share its distinctive weave with all those bearing the name Fitzgibbons, Gibbons, or their variants. This tartan's unique blend of colours and sett is a reflection of the dynamic storytelling that underpins Scottish clan history, where families and traditions are woven into intricate patterns that transcend generations.

name: Fitzpatrick Hunting
description: Fitzpatrick Hunting, a timeless Clan tartan, bears the storied legacy of Scotland's ancient families. Its origins, shrouded in mystery, are tantalisingly unclear, with no definitive link to its esteemed namesake. However, historical hints suggest an intriguing connection to Cameron of Erracht, whose identical sett echoes through this design. The subtle nuances of white and darker hues imbue Fitzpatrick Hunting with a sense of tradition and heritage, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscapes. As a registered Clan tartan, it is woven into the very fabric of Scottish identity, waiting to be worn with honour by those who bear its name, a tangible thread to their family's storied past.

name: Fitzpatrick [default]
description: The Fitzpatrick tartan is a captivating Name tartan with a rich history shrouded in mystery, much like the intricate patterns woven into its very fabric. Dating back to 1992, when Bill Fitzpatrick registered it with the Tartan Educational & Cultural Association, the tartan's origins are steeped in the American West, courtesy of an Oregon-based woolen mill and a sash Jan Crook wove from a sample provided by Fitzpatrick himself. Yet, controversy surrounds this design - was it indeed Irish, or merely mislabeled? Regardless, its striking similarity to the storied Royal Stewart tartan is undeniable, hinting at a deeper connection that remains to be uncovered. Weave of Strathmore Woollen Co. Ltd in Forfar imbues this Name tartan with an authentic Scottish essence, one that continues to captivate enthusiasts and historians alike.

name: Fitzsimmons Hunting
description: The Fitzsimmons tartan, designed by Mark Simmons and Jeffrey Fitzsimmons, is a deeply meaningful and historically significant woven fabric, registered to commemorate the heritage and sacrifices of those bearing the surname Fitzsimmons, an Irish clan name with ties to the country's storied past. This stately tartan, wove by DC Dalgleish of Selkirk, is distinguished by its palette of earthy tones - tan, dark tan, dark green, and olive green - which evoke the rugged beauty of Ireland itself, while the subtle inclusion of black represents those who perished during the Great Famine. By honouring the bravery and resilience of Irish families, this tartan pays tribute to a nation's proud history and those who fought to preserve it, making it an enduring symbol of heritage, loyalty, and remembrance for those who proudly bear the name Fitzsimmons.

name: Fitzsimmons Red
description: Fitzsimmons Red is a richly coloured clan tartan steeped in heritage, born from the distinguished legacy of the Fitzsimmons family. Registered as Scottish Register of Tartans #1201, this tartan's origins date back to Jeffrey Fitzsimmons' meticulous design, which weaves together the threads of tradition and innovation. Characterised by its deep, bold red hue, this tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of those who bear the name Fitzsimmons - a symbol of strength, loyalty, and a sense of honour that transcends generations. As a clan tartan, Fitzsimmons Red holds significant cultural importance, serving as a proud badge of identity for those who claim descent from this esteemed family line, their roots firmly planted in Scotland's rich textile heritage.

name: Flairtex of Darvel Diana Dress
description: The enigmatic Diana tartan, a fashion icon shrouded in mystery, defies singular interpretation due to its proliferation across various colourways. Its origins, claimed by Flairtex of Darvel in Ayrshire, are somewhat disputed, with some attributing its creation to West Coast Woolen Mills and others suggesting Pringles involvement. The tartan's core sett remains a constant, yet its nuances vary, reflecting the diverse artistic visions behind it. Despite the ambiguity surrounding its designer, this intricate design has undoubtedly captured the hearts of many, embodying the timeless allure of Scottish heritage and tradition. Woven with precision, the Diana tartan now resides in the realm of fashion, where its unique charm continues to inspire and influence textile artists and enthusiasts alike.

name: Flairtex of Darvel Diana Hunting
description: The Diana Hunting, Lady tartan is a fashion-inspired design steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition, yet shrouded in mystery due to conflicting claims of its origins. This captivating pattern was allegedly designed by Flairtex, a now-defunct company from Ayrshire, but West Coast Woolen Mill has also laid claim to its creation. The registration notes reveal that multiple variations of the "Diana" tartan exist, with some bearing striking similarities to the original sett claimed by Flairtex. Although this particular version was not produced due to a pre-existing market entry from Pringle's design, it remains an intriguing and potentially unique interpretation of a classic Scottish motif. As a fashion tartan, it is now available for use in clothing and textiles, embracing the cultural significance of Scottish heritage while showcasing the complexities of tartan design's modern era.

name: Fleming Scotland Flanders
description: The Fleming/Frisken/Flanders tartan is a commemorative masterpiece, woven to celebrate Scotland's rich cultural heritage with Polly Wittering, of House of Edgar's Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., as its designer. Registered in 2002, this kilt tartan was specifically created for the Scotland Flanders cultural exchange programme, forging a lasting bond between two nations. The intricate, multi-coloured design not only pays homage to Scotland's military past but also nods to the historical connections between Scotland and Flanders. This commemorative tartan is a testament to the enduring power of tradition and unity, its technical precision a reflection of the skill and craftsmanship that has defined Scottish textiles for centuries.

name:
Fletcher Family
[AKA] Fletcher of Saltoun
[AKA] Fletcher #2
description: Fletcher #2 is a storied tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, worn by all members of the esteemed Fletcher clan regardless of family lineage. Its origins date back to legend, with tales passed down through generations linking it to Glen Orchy, where the Fletchers first raised smoke and boiled their water in a pivotal moment of history. This traditional tartan is preserved within the pages of 'The Tartans of the Clans and Septs of Scotland', a seminal work penned by W & A. K. Johnston, Edinburgh's renowned authority on Scottish textiles. The Lochcarron swatch sample showcases the intricate sett with blue subtly lightened to reveal its distinctive hue, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands and paying tribute to the long-standing legacy of the Fletchers.

name:
Fletcher of Dunans [default]
[AKA] Fletcher of Dunans
description: The Fletcher of Dunans tartan is a storied family heritage, woven from the rich history of the Fletchers, renowned arrow makers in 17th-century Argyll. This Clan tartan, distinguished by its striking red overstripe, tells the tale of a proud and skilled lineage. Its origins lie with Sir George Fletcher, a prominent figure among the Stewarts and Campbells, who played a significant role in the region's artisanal traditions. The Fletchers' expertise was further valued by the MacGregors in Perthshire, cementing their legacy as a testament to the ingenuity of Scotland's highland communities. With its distinctively narrower black tramlines, this tartan design pays homage to the craftsmanship and distinction of the Fletchers, a family whose name remains synonymous with excellence in the world of traditional weaving.

name: Forbes Ancient
description: The Forbes Ancient tartan is an enduring testament to the rich history and heritage of Scotland's clans, with its distinctive pattern bearing witness to the storied past of Clan Forbes. Registered in Lord Lyon's Register of All Arms and Bearings in Scotland on 2nd December 1949, this traditional tartan design has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition for centuries. Its complex weave tells a story of its own, with each thread intricately interwoven to reflect the clan's proud history and motto. The 'Ancient' designation is no mere nod to age, but rather an acknowledgment of the tartan's deep roots, which date back to 1271 when the charter for the Braes of Forbes in Aberdeenshire was granted to Ochonochar, a brave ancestor who claimed the land after defeating a bear. This timeless and storied tartan is now proudly worn by Clan Forbes descendants and enthusiasts alike, a symbol of their honour and heritage that transcends time and generations.

name: Forbes Dress
description: The Forbes Dress tartan is a storied and enduring representation of Scottish heritage, bearing witness to the rich traditions of Clan Forbes, one of Scotland's most esteemed clans. Woven with precision and craftsmanship, this distinctive tartan tells the story of a family bound by history, loyalty, and honour. Registered by Lochcarron Ltd, Galashields, a renowned tartan mill, this fabric pattern is steeped in tradition and authenticity, having been carefully extracted from the finest Scottish wool to create a unique and captivating design that embodies the spirit of Scotland's ancient clans. As a symbol of family pride and identity, the Forbes Dress tartan remains an integral part of Scotland's cultural tapestry, its rich history and significance woven into every fibre of this timeless fabric.

name:
Forbes of Druinnor [default]
[AKA] Forbes of Druinnor
description: The Forbes of Druminnor tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and the enduring legacy of its storied clans. Taken from an old rug belonging to the late Hon Peggy Forbes Semphill, who was the daughter of the esteemed Hon Margaret Forbes-Sempill and owner of the historic Castle Forbes at Druminnor, this tartan holds deep cultural significance. Reconstruction woven in 1968 by Miss Alison Stewart, Director of Research at the Scottish Tartans Society, this design is a remarkable example of Scotland's textile traditions. As an "Other" category tartan, it stands outside the traditional clan affiliations, yet remains deeply rooted in the country's history and identity. The Forbes of Druminnor tartan is now preserved for future generations to appreciate, its intricate patterns and subtle nuances a window into Scotland's storied past.

name:
Forbes [default]
[AKA] Forbes British Army - 74th Regiment
description: The Forbes tartan, a timeless emblem of Scottish heritage, weaves together the threads of history and tradition with elegance and finesse. Registered in 1822 by Wilsons of Bannockburn, this revered clan tartan was once associated with the esteemed Forbes family of Pitsligo, whose ancestors proudly wore it as a badge of honour. While the origins of its design are shrouded in mystery, one thing is certain - this intricate and richly coloured tartan has been cherished for generations, a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's noble clans. With its carefully crafted patterns and nuanced colour palette, the Forbes tartan continues to evoke the proud spirit of Scotland's past, inviting wearers to connect with their heritage and join the tradition of those who have worn it before them.

name: Forbo Nairn Ltd
description: Forbo Nairn, a striking Corporate tartan designed by esteemed Scottish textile house Kinloch Anderson Ltd, pays homage to the rich heritage of Fife's industrial past. Inspired by the iconic Nairn tartan, this specific variation was carefully crafted for Forbo Nairn Ltd, a Swiss-based company with roots in Scotland, founded by Michael Nairn, who pioneered the country's first 'floor cloth' (linoleum) factory in 1847. As a testament to its corporate significance, this tartan is not available for public purchase or use without licence from the Forbo Nairn Ltd, reflecting the company's unique connection to Scottish history and tradition. Through its subtle nuances and thoughtful colour palette, Forbo Nairn embodies both modern industry and timeless Scottish heritage, serving as a distinctive symbol of the company's values and legacy.

name: Forrester Hunting
description: The Forrester/Foster Hunting tartan is a storied legacy woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage. This Clan-specific sett, registered with great honour by the esteemed Davidson/Forrester clan, bears witness to generations of hunting tradition and family unity. First formally recorded in Colin D.I.G.Forrester's seminal book "The Forresters" in 1988, its significance was later validated at Stone Mountain Games in 1994, where a necktie bearing this tartan was showcased as "new Forrester". The official designation of the sett by Stan Forrester, Treasurer to the Clan, in 1996, solidified its place in the annals of tartan history. This traditional hunting tartan is now available for those seeking to connect with their ancestral roots and pay tribute to a rich cultural heritage that has been cherished for centuries.

name: Forrester [default]
description: The Forrester/Foster tartan is a revered and storied clan tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Originally registered with the Lord Lyon and subsequently accepted by the Clan Society as the authentic tartan of Clan Forrester, this complex pattern holds great significance for the descendants of Ian L M Forrester and William N Forrester, who have worn it proudly for generations. Its first green is a distinctive blue-green hue that sets it apart from other tartans, adding to its uniqueness. Although there was some debate over its authorship between Dr D.G Teall and Jamie Scarlett MBE, the tartan's provenance remains rooted in the family's own history, with Clan Forrester notes dating back to 1996. This tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish tradition and the importance of preserving cultural heritage for future generations.

name: Forsyth [default]
description: The Forsyth tartan, registered in 1795, is a rich and storied family heirloom with deep roots in Scottish heritage. Designed by William Forsyth, a talented tailor from Huntly, this distinctive sett was commissioned by the Duchess of Gordon for the 75th Gordon Highlanders regiment in 1794. Now worn by Clan Chief Alistair Forsyth and his descendants, the tartan has undergone a slight evolution over time, with some variations recorded in original Scottish Tartans Authority references - including the substitution of azure for blue in one version. While its accuracy is subject to debate, the Forsyth tartan remains an important symbol of the family's history and legacy, recognised by Lord Lyon as far back as 1978. As a testament to Scotland's enduring textile traditions, this intricate pattern continues to weave its way through generations, proudly worn by those who bear the Forsyth name.

name: Fox Hunting
description: The Fox Hunting tartan is a dynamic and richly textured pattern, born from the creative vision of Jeffrey K MacArthur-Fox of Bolton, Lancashire. Originally designed as a personal tartan, its intended purpose was to unite those who bear the surname Fox or have Fox in their name, evoking a sense of camaraderie and shared heritage among its wearers. This Name tartan, categorised by its association with familial ties, is steeped in tradition and Scottish history, reflecting the country's enduring passion for hunting and the pursuit of the fox. By embracing this distinctive design, one becomes part of a larger narrative that weaves together the past and present, honouring the timeless values of loyalty, kinship, and community that have long been at the heart of British culture.

name: Fox Red
description: This rich and vibrant Red Fox tartan, registered by renowned designer J K MacArthur Fox, pays homage to the esteemed clan Fox, whose heritage is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition. As an asymmetric design, it showcases the unique character of its namesake family, reflecting the individuality of each bearers while still maintaining a sense of unity and kinship. The deliberate light grey line serves as a poignant reminder of the tartan's specific purpose - to honour all individuals bearing the name Fox or incorporating 'Fox' into their surname. This meticulously crafted design not only embodies Scottish heritage but also pays tribute to the enduring legacy of Clan Fox, a testament to the strong bonds of family and identity that this timeless tartan represents.

name: Frame [default]
description: The Frame tartan, designed by Donald B. Frame in 1982, is a striking clan tartan born from a deep fascination with national pride and heritage. This distinctive pattern weaves together elements of the Union Jack, Scotland's iconic St Andrew's Cross, and the American flag, paying tribute to both nations that share Frame's surname.
