The bold red and blue stripes, punctuated by the white of the St Andrew's Cross, create a striking visual effect, while the black and white background stripes lend a sense of contrast and balance. Rooted in clan tradition, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of family legacy and Scottish heritage, its design reflecting Frame's artistic interpretation of a shared history that spans two continents.

name:
Fraser 78th Highlanders
[AKA] Stewart of Atholl #2
description: The Fraser tartan, registered in 1800 by Scotland's esteemed Wilsons of Bannockburn, embodies the storied heritage of Clan Fraser, whose roots run deep in Scottish history. Despite unfounded claims to a century-long association with the 78th Fraser Highlanders, this tartan is a testament to the weavers' skill and craftsmanship that defined generations of Scots. A piece of Wilson's cloth was famously included in the Cockburn Collection, providing tangible proof of its creation between 1810-15. This traditional tartan design, steeped in family pride and clan legacy, has been passed down through the ages, weaving a rich tapestry of Scottish tradition, and a reminder of the intricate relationship between heritage, history, and the skilled artisans who continue to weave these iconic patterns into modern life.

name: Fraser Arisaid; Green
description: The Fraser Arisaid tartan is a vibrant and dynamic clan sett, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered by renowned weaver D C Dalgliesh Ltd of Selkirk, this Modern Dress sett was likely designed for the energetic world of Highland dancing, where its bold and intricate patterns would shine. The Fraser Arisaid's striking colours, carefully selected to evoke the spirit of the Frasers, a Scottish clan known for their bravery and loyalty, create a sense of movement and energy that mirrors the dynamic movements of traditional Highland dance. With its restrictions in place to ensure its authentic preparation by the designer, this tartan remains an important part of Scotland's cultural legacy, offering a unique glimpse into the country's rich weaving heritage.

name: Fraser Arisaid; Red
description: The Fraser Arisaid Red (Dance) tartan is a vibrant and evocative fashion tartan, named after the esteemed Clan Fraser. Its origins are somewhat enigmatic, having initially resurfaced in the Wee Shoppe, a US vendor, before being rediscovered by D.C. Dalgliesh Ltd., who included it in their swatch book of traditional Scottish dance patterns in 2005. As a fashion tartan, this distinctive design is available for incorporation into garments and textiles that celebrate the beauty of Scottish heritage. However, due to its association with Clan Fraser and its origins within the traditional world of Highland dance, this tartan is subject to certain restrictions. Prepared specifically for weaving by D.C. Dalgliesh Ltd., it embodies the rich cultural traditions of Scotland's storied past while offering modern wearers a unique opportunity to connect with the country's fascinating history through fashion.

name: Fraser Arisaid; Wine/Blue
description: Fraser Arisaid #2, a quintessential Fashion tartan, embodies the dynamic spirit of Highland dancing with its vibrant colours and intricate patterns. Weaving together threads of tradition and heritage, this tartan was likely designed for the traditional Scottish dances that have captivated audiences worldwide. Inspired by the majestic landscapes of North Carolina's Highlands, where the Scottish Tartans Society proudly boasts its US Museum, Fraser Arisaid #2 is a testament to the enduring connection between Scotland's rich cultural legacy and the world beyond its borders. With its unique aesthetic, this tartan holds honour among fashion enthusiasts and Highland dancing aficionados alike, evoking the enduring passion for Scottish heritage that has been woven into the very fabric of this iconic design.

name: Fraser Green
description: Fraser Green, a quintessential fashion tartan from renowned designer Pendleton Woollen Mills, embodies the timeless elegance of Scotland's rich textile heritage. This distinctive tartan is categorised as Fashion, evoking a sense of modern sophistication and style. Despite the absence of explicit registration notes, its beauty and allure lie in its understated yet sophisticated colour palette, which whispers tales of the country's lush landscapes and rolling hills. As a fashion tartan, Fraser Green's versatility allows it to complement a wide range of outfits, from formal evening wear to more casual, everyday attire. Its status as a Fashion tartan underscores its ability to transcend traditional boundaries and adapt to contemporary tastes, ensuring this classic design continues to captivate audiences with its enduring beauty and Scottish charm.

name: Fraser Hunting
description: Fraser Hunting #1 is a poignant and storied tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's clan traditions. Originally specified by the Fraser clan themselves, this particular sett has undergone subtle adaptations to reflect the colours of their distinguished regimental ties. Where red once appeared as an alternate white in the original Clan sett (#1424), it now proudly asserts itself in its place, while brown assumes the hue of the former red, imbuing the tartan with a sense of continuity and tradition. The Lovat Scouts and Elgin Company of 2/51, both notable military units, have claimed this tartan as their own, underscoring its significance within the realm of Scottish heritage and family identity.

name: Fraser Hunting Dress
description: The Fraser Hunting Dress is a quintessential example of traditional Scottish tartan heritage, steeped in the rich history and cultural significance of Clan Fraser. As a 'Clan' tartan, it is deeply rooted in the family's history and traditions, with its distinctive pattern and colours forming an integral part of their identity. This specific design was registered by Pringles of Inverness, a renowned tartan designer, who successfully captured the essence of the clan's hunting traditions in his work. With its restricted registration notes classifying it as a 'Dancers' Fancy', this tartan is likely to be used by members of Clan Fraser and other Scottish families with a connection to the Fraser clan, adding an air of authenticity and tradition to their attire.

name: Fraser Isabella
description: The Fraser, Isabella tartan is a poignant and enduring testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage. Weaved from threads of deep blue (the 'Blue' part of its colour sequence), dark green (the 'Green' part), light blue (the 'Light Blue' part), and black, this historic tartan tells the story of Isabella McTavish, a Scottish bride who wore it on her wedding day in 1785. As one of the "Other" category tartans, its origins lie outside the traditional clan affiliations, yet it remains deeply rooted in Scotland's history and tradition. This tartan is not designated to any specific clan but rather serves as a commemoration of Isabella's special occasion, a reminder of love, marriage, and the passing of time through generations. Its intricate patterns and colours evoke a sense of nostalgia and timelessness, connecting us to the past while honouring the memory of this remarkable woman.

name:
Fraser of Altyre [default]
[AKA] Fraser of Altyre
description: The Fraser of Struy tartan, with its rich blues and greens, is a poignant reminder of Scotland's tumultuous past. Ascribed to Captain Thomas Fraser, 7th of Struy, who wore it at Culloden in 1746, this tartan has borne witness to the Jacobite uprising and the bravery of those who fought for their heritage. With its distinctive nine-point pattern, featuring a fine blue line often omitted by careless weavers, this tartan is steeped in tradition and family honour. As a Clan tartan, it holds significance for those bearing the Fraser surname, evoking a sense of pride and connection to their ancestral roots. Its designation as 'Fraser of Struy' makes it an integral part of Scottish clan heritage, a tangible link to the past that continues to inspire and unite members of this distinguished family.

name:
Fraser of Boblainy Hugh
[AKA] Fraser of Boblainy; Hugh
description: The Fraser of Boblainy, Hugh tartan is a proud and storied representation of Clan Fraser's rich heritage. This historic tartan was meticulously reconstructed by Jamie Scarlett MBE from an 1805 fragment measuring just 14ins x 6ins, which provided the foundation for its creation. As part of the Clan Fraser family tradition, this tartan holds great significance as a testament to Hugh Fraser of Boblainy's legacy, who inherited the estate in 1805 following a cousin's passing. The subtle yet distinctive variations in colour and pattern evoke the rugged yet majestic Scottish landscape that has long inspired the Frasers' history and identity. This Lochcarron sample tartan is a valuable tribute to Scotland's textile heritage, and its unique characteristics serve as a poignant reminder of the enduring bond between this distinguished clan and their ancestral lands.

name:
Fraser of Lovat [default]
[AKA] Fraser of Lovat
description: The Fraser of Lovat tartan is an ancient clan tartan steeped in rich history and tradition, bearing the esteemed name of one of Scotland's most illustrious families. As part of the Clan tartan category, it has been woven with great care to evoke the proud heritage of the Frasers, known for their unwavering loyalty and bravery throughout the centuries. According to the registration notes, this iconic design was first illustrated by D.W. Stewart in his seminal work 'Old & Rare Scottish tartans' in 1893, later featured in the prestigious Scarlett Collection of the Scottish Tartans Society. The Fraser of Lovat tartan's significance extends beyond its technical beauty, symbolising a lasting bond with Scotland's storied past and the unshakeable spirit of its namesake clan, who have left an indelible mark on the nation's history.

name: Fraser [default]
description: The Fraser (1842) tartan is an iconic representation of Scottish heritage, steeped in history and tradition. First published in the Vestiarium Scoticum in 1842, this design has become the most popular variant of the Fraser pattern, with its enduring appeal rooted in Lord Lovat's efforts to preserve his family's ancient tartan. The Sobieski Stewarts' contribution to the VS marked a significant milestone, as their unpublished draft shed light on the long-lost original design, which was previously unknown prior to 1745. This tartan is classified under Clan/Family, reflecting its significance in Scottish identity and genealogy. While no restrictions are currently mentioned in the registration notes, its storied past underscores the importance of careful preservation and respect for Scotland's rich cultural legacy.

name: Frater [default]
description: The Frater tartan, named after its esteemed bearers, embodies the rich heritage and tradition of Scottish clan identity. Registered in 1995, this distinctive tartan was crafted with love by House of Edgar's skilled weavers, under the guidance of designer Polly Wittering for the esteemed Frater family. As a Name tartan, it signifies unity and belonging among all who bear its name, allowing them to proudly express their shared ancestry and heritage. With its unique colours and subtle nuances, this tartan design is steeped in history and rooted in Scottish tradition, making it an honour to wear for those of the Frater clan or any individual fortunate enough to be part of this noble lineage.

name: Fulton 1982
description: The Fulton tartan, registered in 1903, is a storied heritage textile with a profound connection to the esteemed name Fulton, synonymous with Scottish clansman George A. Fulton's family legacy. As a Clan tartan, its purpose lies in identifying individuals bearing the Fulton surname, fostering a sense of honour and belonging among those who wear it. Without a rich historical provenance, this tartan instead relies on its symbolic significance, evoking a strong tradition of Scottish identity and heritage. The design itself is characteristic of early 20th-century tartans, with subtle colour variations that reflect the muted hues often found in traditional Clan patterns. As a registered tartan, it serves as a tangible link to Fulton's ancestry, inviting wearers to proudly claim their connection to this storied name.

name: Fulton 1999
description: The Fulton tartan, a Clan/Family registration from 1999, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage. This intricately woven pattern, originating from a long-forgotten ancestral history, has been carefully re-created to honour the descendants of its original bearers. The design's unique character and subtle nuances are a reflection of the rich cultural traditions that once defined the lives of those who wore it. Although the specific originator of this tartan is unknown, its registration as a Clan/Family tartan underscores its significance within Scottish clans and families. Notably, the Fulton tartan bears little resemblance to an earlier 'Fulton' design, highlighting the evolution of tartan traditions over time. With careful attention to historical accuracy, this tartan has been preserved for future generations to wear with pride.

name: Hunter [default]
description: The Galbraith tartan is a rich and storied design steeped in Scottish heritage, its origins rooted in the complex history of the noble family to which it bears name. Originally shared among several clans, including Hunter, Galbraith, Mitchell, and Russell, this tartan has undergone various transformations over the centuries, its pattern evolving from one iteration to another. Notably, it is closely related to the Ferguson of Balquhidder design, distinguished by a distinctive green stripe on blue that has been replaced with white in some versions. This tartan's versatility has been demonstrated through its adoption by prestigious institutions such as the USAir Force Pipe Band, which adopted it and renamed it Mitchell in honour of General Billy Mitchell. With a history spanning over 20th-century developments, the Galbraith tartan remains an enduring testament to Scotland's intricate clan affiliations and cultural traditions.

name: Gallamore [default]
description: The Gallamore tartan is a richly woven tribute to Scottish heritage, registered in recognition of its connection to the esteemed Scottie Gallamore family. Designed by skilled weaver Marjorie Warren, this Clan tartan was originally created for a distinguished lady bearing the name, and as such, it holds great significance for all members of the Gallamore clan who bear it with honour. With Fraser & Kirkbright of Vancouver, Canada, serving as the weaving experts behind its creation, this tartan embodies the timeless traditions of Scottish textiles. Although designed specifically for the Gallamore family, this tartan is now open to wear by anyone carrying the name, serving as a symbol of unity and pride within the clan.

name: Galleries Lafayette Merric Dark Camel
description: The Merrick, Camel tartan is a sophisticated fashion favourite, originating from the renowned Pringles of Inverness designer. This dark, moody weave pays homage to the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands, evoking the dramatic landscapes and rich heritage of the region. As part of the Fashion category, this tartan has been carefully crafted to add a touch of elegance to any garment or accessory. Its origins are shrouded in mystery, but it is believed to have originated from Galleries Lafayette, Paris, where it was later adopted by the Scottish Tartans Society as Merrick Dark Camel. As such, it holds a special place in the annals of Scottish tartan history, and its inclusion in the Johnston Collection serves as a testament to its enduring significance.

name: Gammell 1978
description: The Gammell tartan is a deeply personal and meaningful connection to Scotland's rich heritage, as revealed in its storied history. This clan-style tartan, registered by Dalgliesh, D.C in 1978, was first brought to light through the efforts of Harry Lindley and Stuart Davidson at the Scottish Tartans Society. According to registration notes, this distinctive design was identified as a personal tartan for an individual named Gammell, which shares striking similarities with the Blair tartan. With its unique thread count and colour palette, the Gammell tartan embodies the spirit of Scottish tradition and family legacy, inviting wearers to pay homage to their own heritage and the storied history that has shaped this iconic tartan design.

name: Gammell (Personal)
description: The Gammell tartan, a deeply personal and exclusive design commissioned by the Hill family of Overdale in Forfarshire, holds a poignant significance within Scottish heritage. This unique Name tartan, created for the matriarch Barbara Hill (née Barbara Gammell) by esteemed designers David Thomas and Arthur Mackie of Strathmore Woollen Co, is not available for public use beyond familial ties. With only 20 yards woven initially, its restricted availability serves as a testament to the intimate nature of this design, created specifically for the family's own use and cherished history. The Gammell tartan now resides in the STA Collection, serving as a treasured link to Barbara Hill's lineage and a tribute to the enduring bonds of family tradition.

name: Gary [default]
description: The ancient clan tartan of Gary/Garry is a deeply personal and storied heritage, woven from the very fabric of family tradition. Described by renowned designer Smith Jnr, with input from esteemed Dr Philip D, this distinctive pattern is an honour to bear for those fortunate enough to be part of the Garry clan lineage. With its rich, muted tones evoking the rolling hills and rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands, this tartan design embodies the values of resilience, courage, and community that have defined the Garry family for generations. As a registered clan tartan, it holds significant cultural significance, symbolising the enduring bonds of kinship and loyalty that transcend time and distance.

name: Gates Hunting
description: The Gates, Hunting tartan is a storied and noble design, intricately woven with a rich history dating back to 2004 when it was registered for the esteemed Daniel Gates family. Conceived by renowned designer Dr Philip Smith in 2002, this majestic pattern is steeped in tradition and heritage, evoking the rugged landscapes and timeless spirit of Scotland's great hunting grounds. As a Clan tartan, its significance extends far beyond the gates of one family, allowing members of the Daniel Gates clan to proudly wear their shared ancestry on their sleeves - or rather, on their tartan fabric. With its intricate blues and greens, this tartan design is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's noble clans, weaving together threads of history, heritage, and family pride.

name: Gates [default]
description: The Gates tartan is a proud emblem of Scottish heritage, woven with the essence of family legacy and tradition. Registered in 2002 by renowned Scottish designer Dr Philip D Smith for Daniel Gates, this unique tartan has since become accessible to all members of the Gates name, symbolising unity and shared ancestry. With its distinctive pattern and rich history, the Gates tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scotland's clan system, where family ties are strengthened by the careful selection and transmission of symbolic textiles. As an integral part of Scottish cultural identity, this traditional tartan design continues to evoke feelings of honour and belonging, connecting wearers to their roots and the storied past of the Gates family.

name: Gayre Bodyguard
description: The Gayre Bodyguard tartan is a storied and esteemed Scottish heritage fabric, steeped in tradition and history. Registered as a Clan tartan, this distinctive pattern holds significance for those who trace their roots to the Gayre family or clans associated with it. Originally designed for bodyguards, hence its name, this unique sett was likely woven to signify strength, courage, and loyalty. With five distinct versions recorded - including the Lord Lyon's version, preserved in the Public Register of All Arms and Bearings in Scotland - the Gayre Bodyguard tartan has become an iconic representation of Scottish tradition. Its intricate pattern, though not attributed to a specific designer, is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of the Scottish Highlands, where such tartans were once woven with precision and passion.

name: Gayre Bodyguard #2
description: Gayre Bodyguard #2 is a revered clan tartan steeped in tradition and heritage, its very existence attested to by its restricted application as the ceremonial attire for the bodyguards of the Chiefs. With no designer credited, it is likely that this esteemed tartan was woven at Lochcarron, a renowned Scottish mill renowned for its high-quality tartans. The five variants of Gayre tartan - Hunting, Dress, Bodyguard, Arisaidh, and Lord Lyon's sett - bear testament to the richness and diversity of Scottish clan heritage, with each carrying distinct significance within its own right. This particular version, recorded as Bodyguard #2, holds a special place in history, having been worn by those entrusted with the Chief's personal safety, their loyalty and dedication woven into every subtle pattern and colour combination.

name: Gayre Dress
description: The Gayre Dress tartan is a majestic clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, its intricate pattern evoking the rich traditions of the country's storied past. Recorded in the Public Register of All Arms and Bearings in Scotland on 12th March 1963, this family tartan holds significance for those tracing their ancestry to the Gayre surname or clan. Its precise design and subtle colour palette reflect the craftsmanship of ancient Scottish weavers, who painstakingly wove threads of blue, green, yellow, and black into a rich tapestry that tells the story of community, identity, and legacy. As a testament to its enduring appeal, this tartan continues to be cherished by those connected to the Gayre clan, serving as a powerful symbol of honour, tradition, and Scottish pride.

name: Gayre Dress #2
description: The Stewart, Cairnie tartan is a deeply personal and historic family pattern, originating from a Scottish clan with a rich heritage spanning over six decades. Registered to commemorate Brian John Stewart's connections to his ancestral homeland in North East Scotland, specifically the village of Cairnie, this distinctive tartan embodies the warmth and tradition of Scottish culture. As a Name tartan, it is registered for use by members of the Stewart family and those who hold a special connection to the clan, providing a meaningful way to celebrate their heritage and roots. With its unique character and storied past, the Stewart, Cairnie tartan serves as a testament to the enduring power of Scottish identity and tradition.

name: Gayre Hunting
description: The Gayre Hunting tartan is a storied clan tartan, steeped in tradition and heritage, borne by the descendants of Sir John Campbell, 2nd Earl of Argyll, and his brother, Sir Archibald Campbell, 1st Earl of Ailsa Craig. Registered to the Clan Gayre in 1981 by Captain Robert Campbell of Gayre, this tartan was originally designed for hunting attire, hence its name. With five distinct variations, including a version recorded by Lord Lyon, the Public Register of All Arms and Bearings in Scotland provides a tangible link to the clan's history. As a symbol of family pride and connection to their Scottish roots, the Gayre Hunting tartan is a cherished emblem of the Campbell clan, weaving together threads of nobility, tradition, and rustic heritage, evoking images of rugged Highland landscapes and centuries-old stories of loyalty and bravery.

name: Gayre [default]
description: The Gayre tartan is a storied and distinctive clan pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, originating from the noble House of Gayre. First recorded by Captain of Clan Gayre himself in 1981, this intricate design features five distinct variations: Hunting, Dress, Bodyguard, Arisaidh, and the authoritative Lord Lyon sett, as documented in the Public Register of All Arms and Bearings in Scotland. Each iteration boasts its own unique nuances, reflecting the varied roles and traditions within Clan Gayre's history. The tartan's multifaceted nature is a testament to the clan's rich cultural legacy, spanning hunting expeditions, formal attire, and even bodyguard duties. By wearing or incorporating this tartan into their daily life, individuals can connect with the proud heritage of Clan Gayre, its values, and traditions, evoking a sense of belonging to a storied Scottish family lineage.

name: Geddes [default]
description: The Geddes tartan, a stalwart emblem of Scottish heritage, boasts a rich history dating back to 1840 when it was first registered, with its earliest known iteration featuring a striking MacKintosh variation adorned with a white stripe centred on a crimson ground. This time-honoured design, now synonymous with the Geddes family crest, showcases the traditional Wilson sett, expertly woven into the fabric of Scottish tartan tradition. As part of the Johnston Collection, held by the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan has been carefully preserved for posterity, serving as a poignant reminder of Scotland's storied past and the unyielding bond between families and their ancestral traditions.

name: Gammell [default]
description: The Gemmell tartan is a proud expression of clan heritage, woven from the rich fabric of Scottish tradition. Designed by Peter MacDonald for Thomas Gemmell of Gemmell Tartans, Dumfries, this intricate pattern draws inspiration from the iconic Military Medal sett, superimposed over a single tram-line blue square to create a unique and distinguished design. This tartan is a testament to the bravery and service of Charles Nelson Gemmell, a sergeant in the Argyle & Sutherland Highlanders who fought valiantly in North Africa, Sicily, and mainland Italy during World War II, earning him the esteemed Military Medal. Now available for wear by anyone bearing the name on application to Thomas Gemmell, the Gemmell tartan serves as a symbol of family pride and connection to this distinguished clan legacy, its threads woven from the very heart of Scottish history and tradition.

name: George Heriots School
description: The George Heriots tartan is a vibrant and sophisticated corporate design born from a rich history, carefully crafted by Kinloch Anderson Ltd. Commissioned in 2000 for George Heriots School in Edinburgh, this distinctive tartan was created to reflect the school's honour and prestige. As part of its category, Corporate, it is intended for formal wear and business use, evoking professionalism and elegance. The registration notes reveal a strong connection to Scottish heritage, underscoring the importance of this tartan as an emblem of the school's identity and tradition. With its striking colours and expertly woven fabric, the George Heriots tartan proudly represents the values of excellence and discipline embodied by George Heriots School.

name: Gibson [default]
description: The Gibbs/Gibson tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Benjamin Gibbs, a stalwart member of Scottish society in the late 18th century. This storied clan tartan has been meticulously woven to honour the descendants of this distinguished individual, who bore the name that would become synonymous with tradition and heritage. Registered by renowned designer Dr Philip D Smith Jr, this tartan's origins are rooted in the Buchanan register, a repository of Scotland's most ancient and revered tartans. As such, it holds a special place within the country's rich tapestry of clan history, acknowledging the enduring ties that bind the Gibbs name to its Scottish roots. With its unique thread count adjustment made at the request of Phil Smith in 2003, this tartan design now bears testament to the flexibility and adaptability that has always defined the Scottish way of life.

name: Gift Edge (Edgar) personal; Pride of Glencoe
description: The Pride of Glencoe tartan, lovingly crafted by Claire Donaldson for House of Edgar's esteemed client Gilt Edged Highland Wear, embodies the rugged beauty and unyielding spirit of Scotland's majestic Glencoe valley. This Fashion tartan is a celebration of Scotland's rich heritage, with its striking heather hue - actually a warm, earthy brown in its woven form - evoking the heather-covered moors that stretch as far as the eye can see. The subtle, muted tones are reminiscent of the wild and windswept landscape that has captivated the imagination of Scots for centuries. This tartan is an honour to wear, not just as a statement of Scottish pride, but also as a nod to the region's tumultuous history and the enduring allure of its natural beauty.

name: Gillespie [default]
description: The Gillespie tartan is a quintessential example of Scottish heritage, steeped in tradition and family lineage. Registered as a Clan tartan, it is said to be worn by those bearing the surname Gillespie, whose history and connections to Scotland are rich and storied. Dating back to circa 1860, this tartan has been passed down through generations, its distinctive pattern telling tales of Scottish clan affiliations and ancestral ties. Though the designer's name remains unknown, it is clear that the tartan was inspired by the country's proud history, as evident in its unique colour palette and subtle variations in thread count, echoing the intricate traditions of Scotland's weavers. Wearing this tartan is a badge of honour, connecting wearers to their Scottish roots and heritage.

name: Gillies Blue; Dress Dance
description: The Gillies Dress Blue tartan is a storied family heirloom, steeped in tradition and Scottish heritage. Originally registered as part of the larger Dancers' Fancy motif by renowned weaver D.C. Dalgliesh of Selkirk, it falls under the esteemed category of Clan tartans, reflecting the proud history and identity of the Gillies clan. The intricate design, woven with precision by the skilled hands of Mr Gillies, is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish tartanry, with its rich colours and subtle variations evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Highlands. While this tartan may be most commonly associated with formal wear, its significance extends far beyond the realm of fashion, representing instead a deep connection to family, culture, and tradition that continues to inspire new generations.

name: Gillies Blue; Dress Dance #1
description: Gillies Dress Blue #1, also known as Dance, is a timeless fashion tartan born from the traditional weaves of Scotland's rich heritage. This stunning blue-hued tartan is part of the esteemed Gillies family legacy, renowned for their exquisite designs that have adorned Scottish dress for generations. Specifically, this variation is a variation of the iconic Dancers' Fancy, created by the skilled hands of D.C. Dalgleish of Selkirk in the past. As a fashion tartan, Dance is suited to garments such as kilts, scarves, and dresses, showcasing its versatility and suitability for modern wearers who wish to draw inspiration from Scotland's ancient traditions. With its intricate design, Gillies Dress Blue #1 embodies the elegance and refinement that has come to define the Scottish aesthetic, making it an excellent choice for those seeking to add a touch of cultural sophistication to their attire.

name: Gillies Green; Dress Dance
description: The Gillies Dress Green tartan is a storied and storied clan tartan, steeped in tradition and heritage. Specifically designated as a family tartan, it holds great significance for those bearing the name Gillies. This classic Dancers' Fancy pattern, attributed to the skilled hands of D.C. Dalgliesh of Selkirk, has been worn with pride by generations of Scottish families, evoking memories of ancestral homes and village gatherings. Its subtle yet striking design, characterised by a palette of greens, blues, and yellows, is deeply rooted in Scotland's rich cultural heritage, reflecting the warmth and hospitality of the Scottish people. As a registered tartan, it continues to be an important symbol of clan identity and family honour, proudly worn at formal occasions and special gatherings.

name: Gillies Red; Dress Dance
description: The Gillies Red Dress is a storied tartan rich in heritage, passed down through generations of the esteemed Gillies clan family. Registration notes reveal its connection to D.C. Dalgliesh's celebrated Dancers' Fancy, further solidifying its association with Scotland's revered tradition of tartan weaving. As a Clan tartan, this distinctive design is steeped in history and tradition, symbolising the values and ancestry of its namesake family. Worn with honour by Gillies clansmen and women alike, it serves as a tangible link to their proud heritage, proudly showcasing the craftsmanship and skill that has defined Scottish textiles for centuries.

name:
Gillies [default]
[AKA] Gillis [default]
description: The Gillies #1 tartan is a storied and distinctive Clan tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. This variation of the MacLaren tartan boasts a striking broad black band on alternating blue squares, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. Although its exact origins are shrouded in mystery, it first emerged in the 1940s alongside Gillies #2, sparking curiosity among those familiar with Scottish clans and tartans. The fact that it has endured under various spellings - Gillies, MacLeish, and MacLellan - underscores its enduring significance as a family tartan, weaving its way into the fabric of history and identity. As such, this tartan design serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, honouring those who bear the Gillies name with pride and tradition.

name: Glasgow Academy
description: The Glasgow Academy tartan is a unique and meaningful corporate pattern, born from the merger of two prestigious Glasgow schools: The Westbourne School for girls and the Glasgow Academy. Its creation is a testament to the rich history and cultural heritage of Scotland's iconic institutions. Inspired by the rugged majesty of the Black Watch, this tartan combines elements of the Westbourne uniform's regal purple hue with the Academy's steadfast blue, resulting in a distinctive and stylish design that pays homage to the city's academic and sporting traditions. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, this corporate tartan is woven by Lochcarron from samples held in the Johnston Collection, ensuring its accuracy and authenticity as a symbol of Glasgow's enduring legacy.

name: Glasgow Caledonian University
description: The Glasgow Caledonian University tartan is a vibrant and modern corporate design that embodies the academic spirit of Scotland's largest university. Registered in 1998, this distinctive tartan pattern was created by Keith Lumsden to represent the institution's values and heritage. As a Category Corporate tartan, it is designed for use in business and professional contexts, making it an ideal choice for companies and individuals affiliated with GCU. With its unique colour scheme and subtle texture, this tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich cultural heritage while exuding a sense of innovation and forward-thinking, reflecting the university's commitment to academic excellence and community engagement.

name: Glasgow Celtic Society
description: The Glasgow Celtic Society tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's greatest cities. Originally created for the esteemed Glasgow Celtic Society, this striking asymmetrical sett is rooted in the kilt patterns of the late 19th century outfit on display at the Scottish Tartans Authority. As such, it embodies the proud tradition of Scottish tartanry, evoking memories of ancient clan gatherings and Highland games. With its bold, crimson-red hue and crisp white accents, this tartan is quintessentially Glaswegian, paying homage to the city's storied past while embracing a modern corporate identity. Whether used in formal wear or as part of an organisation's branding, the Glasgow Celtic Society tartan is sure to instil a sense of heritage and pride in all who behold it.

name: Glasgow University
description: The Glasgow, University of tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan woven with pride by Geoffrey Highland Crafts. Designed specifically to represent the esteemed institution, this tartan is an official symbol of the University's livery, as designated by the Scottish Tartans Society. Its significance extends beyond its functional use for university branding and promotional materials, as it embodies the rich cultural heritage and tradition of Scotland's oldest universities. With its unique combination of colours and subtle pattern, this tartan weaves a distinctive narrative of academic excellence, innovation, and community, making it an ideal choice for corporate events, university attire, and any occasion that requires a touch of Glasgow's renowned spirit.

name: Glen Affric;
description: The Unnamed Glen Affric tartan is a remarkably well-preserved fragment of Scottish heritage, unearthed in a peat bog and meticulously reconstructed by the Scottish Tartans Authority to reveal its intricate beauty. Dating back to the 16th century, this enigmatic pattern boasts striking stripes of green and black/brown on a rich red and yellow ground, evoking the wild beauty of Glen Affric's ancient landscape. As one of the earliest recorded tartans from the Scottish Highlands, this design offers a fascinating glimpse into Scotland's rich cultural past, with its origins shrouded in mystery. Protected under UK Design Registration No.6295231, this tartan is now subject to strict controls by the Scottish Tartans Authority, ensuring that its commercial production respects its historical significance and allows for careful preservation of this precious fragment of Scotland's textile heritage.

name: Glen Coe
description: The Glen Coe tartan is an iconic representation of Scotland's rich heritage, hailing from the majestic district of Glen Coe in the Scottish Highlands. This storied tartan has been woven with pride for generations, its intricate patterns evoking the rugged beauty of the surrounding mountains and lochs. Originally registered as a District Tartan, it was designed to represent the people who have called this enchanting region home for centuries. The tartan's subtle yet striking design features pink (coral) lines that subtly replace traditional white lines, lending an air of exclusivity to its ownership. As part of the Dalgety Collection, a testament to Scotland's rich textile history, the Glen Coe tartan is a true reflection of Scottish tradition and culture, awaiting its next wearer to carry on this storied legacy.

name: Glen Moy #2
description: The Glen Moy tartan is a stylish and elegant fashion choice, evoking the rolling hills and rugged beauty of Scotland's countryside. First registered with the Scottish Tartans Society in 1986, this vibrant tartan has been woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage for generations. Dubbed "dress" Moy by some, this tartan design speaks to the country's rich tradition of textile craftsmanship, where every thread tells a story of history and culture. With its unique colour palette and intricate pattern, Glen Moy is perfect for those seeking to add a touch of Scottish flair to their wardrobe, whether for formal occasions or everyday wear, its beauty and character are sure to stand out.

name: Glendronach Whisky Distillery
description: The Glendronach Distillery tartan is a rich and storied Corporate tartan, expertly woven by Lochcarron of Scotland. This distinctive pattern pays homage to the historic distillery situated on the Dronach Burn in the Scottish Highlands, which dates back to 1826. The design's origins are rooted in William Teachers' submission in 1990, yet its inspiration is said to have been drawn from a earlier design created by LOS for Glen Dronach whisky. Characterised by its unique colour palette and subtle texture, this tartan is woven with reverence for the region's rich heritage and tradition of fine whisky production. By wearing or displaying this tartan, one can proudly signal their connection to Scotland's storied past and the revered distilleries that have shaped its cultural identity.

name: Glenfalloch House
description: The Glenfalloch tartan is a striking corporate design that evokes the serenity of New Zealand's Otago Peninsula. Registered by esteemed designer Vilma Ruth Nelson, this unique tartan was inspired by the private residence of Glenfalloch, which was transformed into a public garden for the benefit of the local community and visitors alike. The colours are carefully chosen to reflect the natural beauty of the area, with navy blue representing the dark shadows in the valley's hidden recesses, while shades of green/blue evoke the sea, sky, and lush foliage that surround it. Warm salmon pink and white hues add a pop of vibrancy, reminiscent of wildflowers in season, creating a stunning visual effect that is both elegant and sophisticated. This tartan is a testament to the enduring allure of Scotland's rich heritage, reimagined for modern corporate purposes, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to connect with their cultural roots while projecting a sense of natural beauty and refinement.

name: Glenfinnan [default]
description: The Glenfinnan tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich history and cultural heritage, woven from the threads of its storied past. Registered in 1968, this Clan tartan has been passed down through generations, originating from a scrap discovered in Canada by Ranald S.J.MacDonald, who claimed descent from Captain John MacDonald of Glenaladale, a staunch supporter of Prince Charles's family. The tartan's origins are shrouded in mystery, with an asymmetrical sett attributed to Lt.Col Ian Cameron Taylor's meticulous work at the National Trust's Glenfinnan site. As its name suggests, Glenfinnan is an integral part of Scotland's national identity, evoking memories of the 1915 Jacobite uprising and the brave men who fought for their heritage. Today, this iconic tartan is a proud symbol of family and clan affiliations, worn by those who honour their ancestors' courage and loyalty.

name: Glengarry Highland Games
description: The Glengarry Highland Games tartan is a vibrant and striking corporate design born out of the spirit of Scottish heritage and tradition. Created as a millennium project, this unique tartan brings together the bold red and blue hues of its namesake event with the addition of green, black, and white, evoking the rolling hills and heather-covered moors of the Scottish Highlands. Commissioned by Strathmore Woolen Co. in Forfar, Scotland, and officially registered with the Scottish Tartan Society, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of traditional Scottish weaving. Named after the Glengarry Highland Games, this corporate tartan would be perfect for any organisation seeking to add a touch of Scottish flair to their branding, reflecting its heritage and values in bold and striking design.

name: Glenlivet Whisky Dress
description: The Glenlivet Dress Reproduction tartan is a striking corporate design born from the storied heritage of Scotland's finest whisky distillery, Glenlivet. Registered with Kinloch Anderson Ltd as part of a series commemorating this iconic brand, this tartan embodies the rich tradition and authenticity of Scotland's national beverage. Its subtle colour palette, comprising muted blues and greens, evokes the rustic charm of the Highlands and the timeless allure of fine whisky. As a corporate design, it lends itself perfectly to formal wear and special occasions, while its association with Glenlivet Distillery ensures a deep connection to Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered for use by companies seeking to embody the values of quality, sophistication, and time-honoured craftsmanship that Glenlivet embodies.

name: Glenlivet Whisky
description: The Glenlivet corporate tartan is a masterful blend of tradition and modernity, perfectly capturing the essence of Scotland's finest whisky brand. Registered in 1975 by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this distinctive tartan was specifically designed by Harry Lindley for Glenlivet Distilleries Ltd, Strathspey. As a Corporate tartan, it is intended to be used in business and organisational contexts, yet its timeless beauty and intricate pattern make it equally suitable for formal Highland dress and traditional Scottish attire. With its rich blue-grey colours and subtle sheen, the Glenlivet tartan evokes the majestic landscapes of the Cairngorms and the distillery's proud heritage as a pioneering whisky maker. Whether used in a boardroom or on a Highland garment, this tartan is sure to convey a sense of strength, resilience, and traditional Scottish values that have made Glenlivet one of Scotland's most beloved whisky brands.

name: Glenn [default]
description: The Glenn tartan, named after its proud bearer, the David Glen family, is a timeless and storied Scottish heritage fabric. Registered to be worn by not only the Glen clan but also all its name variations, this tartan holds a unique place in Scottish tradition. Designed by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr, a renowned textile expert with a deep understanding of Celtic design, the Glenn tartan pays tribute to the family's history and heritage. Its distinctive pattern, steeped in the rich cultural traditions of Scotland, is now available for all who share a connection to this esteemed name, allowing them to wear their roots on their sleeve - literally.

name: Glennie Evelyn; Rhythms of
description: The Rhythms of Evelyn is a captivating corporate tartan woven from the threads of innovation and cultural heritage. Designed by the celebrated percussionist Evelyn Glennie, in collaboration with Betty Davies of Scottish Fashions International, this unique stage tartan pays homage to her extraordinary talent and unwavering dedication to music despite profound deafness. As a testament to its significance, The Rhythms of Evelyn was created as a stage tartan, underscoring the importance of the performance on which it will be worn. This striking corporate tartan is now available for businesses to wear with pride, symbolising the fusion of rhythm and professionalism that defines Evelyn Glennie's remarkable career. Its distinctive design not only showcases Scottish heritage but also embodies the spirit of innovation and creative expression that has made Evelyn Glennie a global icon in the world of music.

name: Glennie [default]
description: The Glennie tartan is a deeply personal and evocative family heirloom, steeped in Scottish tradition and heritage. As a Clan tartan, it holds significant cultural importance for those who bear its name, serving as a tangible connection to their ancestral roots and a symbol of their honourable lineage. With its intricate, carefully crafted sett, the Glennie tartan whispers tales of generations past, its threads woven from the very fabric of Scottish history. Though no further details are available, it is clear that this tartan has been imbued with great significance by its designer, D C Dalgliesh Ltd, whose careful preparation ensures that each woven thread honours the family's esteemed heritage. As a treasured family legacy, the Glennie tartan embodies the enduring essence of Scottish clan traditions, proudly worn and cherished by those who call it their own.

name: Glenshee
description: The Glen Shee tartan, a timeless creation by renowned designer Clan Crest Textiles, embodies the quintessential spirit of Scotland's fashion heritage. This stylish pattern is classified under the Fashion category, suiting its modern aesthetic to contemporary tastes. With no restrictions on its use, the Glen Shee tartan invites wearers to proudly showcase their individuality and connection to Scottish tradition. Featured in the esteemed Johnston Collection of the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan's rich heritage is a testament to Scotland's storied past, where craftsmanship and innovation converge in perfect harmony. As one of the many authentic patterns woven into Scotland's cultural tapestry, Glen Shee serves as a poignant reminder of the nation's enduring legacy and the timelessness of its beautiful textiles.

name: Glenturret Distillery
description: This stately Corporate tartan, Glenturret Distillery, is woven with pride, paying homage to Scotland's rich heritage. Named after the oldest distillery in Scotland, dating back to circa 1775, this majestic tartan tells a tale of tradition and legacy. Crafted by esteemed weavers at Lochcarron, it has been carefully recorded in the Scottish Tartans Authority's esteemed Johnston Collection. According to historical records, the design may have been inspired by the renowned Kinloch Anderson, who has played a significant role in preserving Scotland's textile heritage. Worn with honour, this tartan is aptly suited for corporate wear, evoking the spirit of tradition and excellence that defines Scotland's oldest distillery, while also paying tribute to the country's rich weaving history.

name: Gold Brothers
description: The iconic Gold Brothers tartan is a vibrant and modern interpretation of traditional Scottish heritage, born from the vision of the eponymous fashion designers based in Edinburgh and Kirkcaldy. Registration notes reveal that this stunning pattern was first produced in 2005, specifically designed for Highland dress and tourism shops, which are steeped in the rich history and cultural significance of Scotland's tartan tradition. With its bold, gold hues on a deep blue background, the Gold Brothers tartan evokes the warmth and hospitality of the Scottish Highlands, where traditional kilts and ladies' skirts have been worn with pride for generations. Although this design is now restricted to be woven and supplied exclusively by the Gold Brothers themselves, its allure remains undiminished, inviting wearers to embody the spirit of Scottish fashion and flair.

name: Goldstraw [default]
description: The Goldstraw tartan is a highly personal and distinctive family heirloom, woven with intricate precision by the late Donald Suttie Smith in 2002 for Martin Goldstraw of Shropshire, England. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds deep significance for those who bear the name or its variations - Goostrey, Goostry, Goostree, and Gostre. This unique design, which has been carefully documented in Smith's registration notes, is now open to use by individuals with this surname, allowing them to proudly don their heritage on special occasions or simply as a badge of honour. Rich in history and steeped in Scottish tradition, the Goldstraw tartan tells the story of its creator's dedication to preserving family legacy, and its beauty continues to captivate those who are fortunate enough to wear it.

name: Gordon Dress #2
description: The Gordon Dress tartan, named after one of Scotland's most storied clans, is a stunning fashion staple with a rich history. This distinctive tartan was first featured in a 1989 issue of 'Country Home' magazine, highlighting its suitability for dress and formal wear. With F. Schumacher Fabrics as the originator, this tartan design has become synonymous with high-end fashion, evoking the grandeur and heritage of the Gordon family's Scottish legacy. Its registration notes attest to its enduring appeal, while restrictions on its use may be subject to change – a reminder that tradition is not absolute, yet the Gordon Dress remains an iconic testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage, awaiting its next stylish wearer.

name:
Gordon of Abergeldie [default]
[AKA] Gordon of Abergeldie
description: The Gordon of Abergeldie tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and the storied history of the prominent Gordon clan. Registered for the house of Gordon, which has been synonymous with bravery and loyalty since the 15th century, this distinctive tartan was taken from a portrait of Rachael Gordon of Abergeldie, painted in 1723. The intricate design, often mistakenly attributed to 'Abergeldie', is an authentic representation of the Gordon family's identity and legacy. Originally classified as 'Other', this tartan has been passed down through generations, serving as a symbol of honour and tradition for those who bear the Gordon name. Its significance extends beyond mere fashion, embodying the values of courage, loyalty, and duty that have defined the Gordon clan for centuries.

name:
Gordon Old
[AKA] Gordon 1842 variant
[AKA] Gordon of Esselmont
[AKA] Gordon Ancient
description: The Gordon of Esselmont tartan is an iconic Clan tartan steeped in history and tradition, its origins dating back to the 18th century when the 4th Duke of Gordon commissioned Forsyth of Huntly to create kilts for his troops. The story goes that Forsyth produced three distinct designs with varying stripes, but the single yellow stripe was ultimately chosen by the Duke, who then sought input from various Gordon branches on an alternative design. Esslemont, a prominent branch of the Gordon family, chose the three-stripe version, resulting in this distinctive tartan sett that now bears their name. As a registered Clan tartan, the Gordon of Esselmont is not only a testament to the family's rich heritage but also a symbol of their pride and honour in the storied history of Scotland's noble clans.

name:
Gordon (1819)
[AKA] Gordon Old Huntly
[AKA] Gordon Red
description: The Gordon, Red tartan is an iconic example of Scotland's rich clan heritage, its threads woven into the fabric of tradition and history. Designated by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1819 as 'Gordon', it was later popularly referred to as 'Old Huntly' due to its association with the Huntly District. This tartan holds a special place in Scottish culture, representing one of Scotland's most noble clans - the Gordon family. Its modern appellation, 'Red', is a nod to the vibrant colour that has come to symbolise the Gordon clan, while also acknowledging the evolution of tartan design over time. As part of its Clan designation, this tartan is steeped in tradition and history, its intricate pattern telling the story of generations past, its very existence an honourable testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's storied clans.

name: Gordon [default]
description: Gordon #2, also referred to as an incorrect version of the original Gordon (#214), holds a special place in the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage. Designed by renowned Johnston brothers, W. & A.K., this clan tartan was first showcased in their seminal work, "The Scottish clans and their tartans", in 1883. According to historical accounts, two distinct variants of Gordon tartan emerged among branches and cadet families, with three yellow stripes differing from the preferred variant with two yellow lines, which was championed by certain esteemed Gordon clans, such as those at Hallhead and Esslemont. This variation, featuring black guards on the iconic yellow stripe, has been preserved through the years, its earliest known listing dating back to 1798, a testament to the enduring legacy of the Gordon family's storied tradition.

name: Gordonstoun School #1
description: Gordonstoun #2 is a distinctive Corporate tartan, expertly woven to evoke the spirit of modern Scotland's corporate identity. Originally created in 1956 as one of four experimental specimens for Gordonstoun School in Morayshire, this tartan marked an important milestone in the development of Scottish design. By being selected as the final choice (#362) and subsequently registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, Gordonstoun #2 has become a symbol of business excellence and professionalism in Scotland. Its unique blend of colours and subtle texture lends itself to use on corporate clothing, accessories, and other formal garments, ensuring that this tartan design remains firmly rooted in the traditions of Scottish heritage while embracing its modern applications.

name: Gordonstoun School #2
description: The Gordonstoun tartan, designed by Gilbert Duncan Macleod Bullard circa 1956, is a masterpiece of corporate tartanry, its rich heritage woven into every thread. Born from the blending of three storied families - Innes, Gordon, and Cumming - who have owned Gordonstun Estate since the 16th century, this distinctive design embodies the complex tapestry of Scottish clan history. The Hunting Cumming's bold presence is balanced by the pale blue of the Innes and the sunny yellow of the military Gordon, reflecting the intricate relationships between these families over the centuries. This carefully crafted tartan has taken over a year to develop, with multiple attempts at balance woven into its very fabric - a testament to the dedication of its creators. Now produced in two weights by Johnstons of Elgin and originally spun by D.C. Dalgliesh, Gordonstoun is an iconic symbol of Scottish tradition, proudly worn by those who honour their heritage and the storied history of this esteemed estate.

name: Gordonstoun School #3
description: The Gordonstoun #3 tartan is a quintessential example of corporate tartanism, embodying the fusion of tradition and modernity that defined 20th-century Scottish textiles. Originally created as part of an experimental series for Gordonstoun School in Morayshire, this distinctive tartan was one of four contenders vying for favour with the school's governors. Ultimately, it was chosen to represent the esteemed institution, its bold and modern aesthetic reflecting the progressive spirit of its founder, Bill Douglas. Now available for commercial use, this design pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage while evoking a sense of forward-thinking innovation, making it an attractive choice for businesses seeking to forge their own distinctive identity within the country's storied tartan tradition.

name: MacGowan Portrait
description: The Gow Tartan, with its intricate, nuanced colours, evokes the storied heritage of Perthshire's renowned fiddler, Sir Henry Raeburn, who immortalised it in a captivating portrait. Registered as part of the Scottish Tartans Society's registry, this tartan is rooted in Gaelic traditions, meaning 'Smith' - a testament to its association with the blacksmiths of old. A notable entry under the category of 'Other', Gow showcases the diversity and creativity of Scotland's textile heritage. While no specific designer can be attributed to this design, it is likely that it was inspired by Raeburn's portrait, which is now preserved in the Highland Society of London Collection. The Gow Tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the intricate connections between music, craftsmanship, and clan affiliations in Scotland's rich cultural tapestry.

name: Graden [default]
description: The Graden tartan is a unique and storied family heritage from Scotland, proudly borne by its clan and kindred since time immemorial. Designed by renowned tartan expert Jack Dalgety, this distinctive weave showcases a rich blend of blues, reds, and greens, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. The Graden's significance is deeply rooted in its family lineage, with each thread imbued with the history and tradition of its clan. As registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan holds an official place in Scotland's cultural fabric, passed down through generations as a symbol of honour and belonging. By wearing or weaving the Graden tartan, one proudly claims connection to their ancestral roots, embracing the storied heritage that has defined Scottish identity for centuries.

name: Graham Dress
description: The Graham Dress tartan is a revered Clan tartan, richly woven into the fabric of Scotland's cultural heritage. Belonging to the esteemed House of Graham, this majestic pattern has been a proud symbol of Scottish identity for generations. First recorded in the 19th century, the tartan was likely designed by the renowned weavers at Paton, who produced an exquisite range of fabrics from 1830 onwards. Although its origins are shrouded in mystery, it is now firmly established as one of Scotland's most iconic and enduring clan tartans, bearing testament to the country's storied history and tradition.

name:
Graham of Menteith [default]
[AKA] Graham of Menteith
[AKA] Haldane [default]
description: The Graham of Menteith tartan is a proud and storied design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans. First registered in 1819 as 'Cobourg', its origins are shrouded in mystery, with some questioning its antiquity. Nevertheless, this iconic tartan has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition, with references to it appearing in various texts from the early 19th century. Notably, the broad blue stripe is indeed described by Logan as 'smalt', a word evoking the mysterious and majestic quality often associated with Scotland's rugged landscape. As the tartan of the western branch of the Graham family, Menteith, it holds significant cultural value, offering a tangible connection to the history and legacy of this esteemed clan. This timeless design continues to captivate those drawn to Scotland's rich heritage, its very existence a testament to the enduring power of tradition and community.

name:
Graham of Menteith Red
[AKA] Red
[AKA] Graham of Menteith; Red
description: The Graham of Menteith (Red) tartan is a poignant testament to the rich heritage of Clan Menteith, a storied Scottish dynasty with a history spanning centuries. Originally created by Kinloch Anderson Ltd for an American customer, this tartan underwent a deliberate modification when the Scottish Tartans Society reclassified it as "Red Montrose" in 1983, highlighting its distinctive red hues amidst the traditional green. This Clan tartan is an honour to bear by those of Menteith descent or affinity, reflecting the family's proud history and traditions. Its very existence serves as a reminder of the enduring legacy of Scottish clans, woven into the fabric of our collective cultural identity.

name:
Graham of Montrose [default]
[AKA] Graham of Montrose
description: The Graham of Montrose #2 tartan, created by esteemed Scottish weavers at Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1819, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's noble families. Originally referred to as the Abercrombie pattern, this sett has been worn unofficially by the distinguished Graham clan and their kin for generations, its significance woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition. With its striking white stripes, this tartan holds a special place in the annals of Scottish history, having been first published in Smith's book of 1850 and later referenced in esteemed publications such as W and A Smith's 'Authenticated Tartans'. Its enduring presence is a tribute to the enduring legacy of the Graham family, whose name has become synonymous with courage and nobility, much like the tartan itself - a symbol of strength and loyalty that continues to inspire those who wear it.

name: Graham Red
description: The Graham Red tartan is a rich and storied family tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. This clan tartan, named after its original bearer, was registered to Dalgliesh, D C, and has since become an integral part of the family's history and identity. Woven with meticulous attention to detail by D C Dalgliesh Ltd., this tartan features a unique blend of deep reds and subtle greens, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. While not without restrictions, indicating its exclusive heritage for the Graham clan, this tartan remains a proud symbol of family honour and tradition, weaving together generations past, present, and future with its enduring presence in Scottish tartanry.

name: Graham Red; Dress
description: The Graham Red Dress tartan is a vibrant and dynamic fashion design, carefully crafted by renowned Scottish weaver Peter MacDonald, specifically for the art of Highland dancing. Registered as a Fashion tartan, this striking pattern is set to make a statement on the dance floor or in any other setting where its bold colours will be showcased. With its specific purpose being to adorn the attire of dancers, the Graham Red Dress tartan draws inspiration from the rich heritage of Scotland's ancient clans. Its bright red tones evoke the passion and energy of traditional Highland dancing, while its unique blend of dark blues and greens pays homage to the rugged landscapes and rolling hills that have long been synonymous with Scottish culture.

name: Grainger [default]
description: The Grainger tartan, named after its esteemed namesake Paul Grainger, is a majestic Clan tartan steeped in heritage and tradition. Designed in 1968 by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr, an American with a deep appreciation for Scottish culture, the Grainger tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Grainger family. While there may be differing claims about its origins, the tartan's significance remains unchanged - it is an honour bestowed upon all those who bear the name, allowing them to connect with their ancestral roots and proudly showcase their heritage. With restrictions only applicable to those bearing the specific surname, this tartan serves as a symbol of identity and unity for the Grainger family, weaving together a rich tapestry of Scottish tradition and ancestry.

name: Grampian Television
description: The Grampian Television tartan is a quintessential example of modern corporate branding woven into traditional Scottish heritage. Registered as a corporate tartan, it was designed to evoke the distinct identity of its namesake organisation, serving as a visual ambassador for the esteemed broadcaster. Created by renowned designer Bill Johnston, this specific tartan was carefully crafted by Johnstons of Elgin in a scarf form, showcasing the skill and craftsmanship of Scotland's premier textile artisans. With its unique character, the Grampian Television tartan embodies the rich history and tradition of Scottish weaving, now repurposed to symbolise the values and mission of a prominent broadcasting institution. Its registration serves as a testament to the enduring importance of tartan in contemporary branding, seamlessly blending heritage and innovation.

name: Grant 1714
description: The Grant 1714 tartan is a distinctive and storied pattern, born from the threads of Scotland's rich history and heritage. Registered in 2024 by the chief of Clan Grant, this tartan is an evolution of the family's traditional designs, created by combining elements from ancient portraits, including those of Alister Mohr Grant, Champion, and William Cummins, Piper. The result is a striking pattern that pays homage to the clan's legacy, while also reflecting its modern-day significance. With no restrictions on wear due to its adoption as an additional tartan by the chief in April 2024, this design now lends itself to those who wish to connect with their Scottish roots or celebrate the proud heritage of Clan Grant.

name: Grant Hunting (1819)
description: The Grant (1819 #2) tartan, designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1819, holds a fascinating place within Scotland's rich textile heritage. This storied tartan, often mistakenly referred to as 'Grant Hunting', was actually included in the Key Pattern Book simply as 'Grant' - a nod to its enigmatic origins. While speculation suggests it may have been originally intended for military use, there is no concrete evidence to support this theory. As an 'Other' category tartan, Grant defies easy categorisation, adding to its mystique and allure. Its inclusion in the Key Pattern Book demonstrates its significance as a broader representative of Scottish design, reflecting the innovative spirit of Wilsons of Bannockburn - one of Scotland's oldest and most revered tartan houses.

name:
Grant of Achnarrow #3
[AKA] Grant of Achnarrow; #3
description: The Grant of Auchnarrow tartan is a captivating blend of traditional Scottish heritage and mystery, its provenance woven from threads of history and intrigue. This fashion variant of the esteemed Royal Stewart tartan holds a unique place in the country's textile traditions, said to have originated from a plaid donated to the Highland Folk Museum by Miss Peace, a descendant of a Strathspey tacksman who farmed the Auchnarrow estate near Castle Grant. Although likely named in honour of its Scottish roots, rather than being an authentic clan tartan, the Grant of Auchnarrow is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry.

name:
Grant of Edinchat [default]
[AKA] Grant of Edinchat
description: The Edinchat tartan, with its intricate blue and red hues reminiscent of Scotland's majestic landscapes, whispers tales of a storied past. Once owned by a lady Dunbar in the 18th century, who went on to marry a man named MacBain, this plaid is steeped in history and familial ties. The sett bears a striking resemblance to the Grant of Lurg tartan, with the notable difference of a blue line set against a red background instead of the traditional white. This subtle variation adds depth and nuance to the design, underscoring its place within Scotland's rich textile heritage. With no known designer credited, it is clear that this tartan has been passed down through generations, carrying with it the stories and honour of its owners, now woven into the very fabric itself.

name:
Grant of Monymusk [default]
[AKA] Grant of Monymusk
description: The Grant of Monymusk tartan is an authentic and storied weave, steeped in the rich heritage of Scottish clan traditions. Originally compiled by General Sir William Cockburn during his extensive travels, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the 1st Baron Monymusk, the 5th Duke of Lauderdale. Weaved with precision by William Wilson and Sons of Bannockburn, the Grant of Monymusk tartan embodies the proud history of the noble House of Lauderdale, whose roots stretch back centuries. This family tartan, now preserved within the esteemed Cockburn collection at the Mitchell Library in Glasgow, remains an honourable symbol of Scottish identity and a poignant reminder of the nation's complex and storied past.

name:
Grant of Rothiemurchus [default]
[AKA] Grant of Rothiemurchus
description: This intriguing tartan, woven from threads worn by the inhabitants of the 'Grant' estate in Rothiemurchus, is a captivating representation of 18th century Scottish heritage. With its unique colour palette and subtle variations, this plaid embodies the essence of rural life in the Highlands during a time of great cultural significance. As an "Unnamed" tartan, it falls under the "Other" category, setting it apart from more formally designated clan patterns. The origins of its design are shrouded in mystery, with no discernible 'Designer' credited for its creation. Registration notes suggest that the thread count was taken from a genuine 18th century plaid, lending an air of authenticity to this timeless tartan, evoking the rugged beauty and simplicity of Scotland's rural past.

name:
Grant [default]
[AKA] Grant Clan
[AKA] Grant Drummond #2
description: The Grant tartan, registered in 1819, is a rich and storied example of Scotland's iconic woven heritage. Designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, this clan tartan was originally created as 'New Bruce' in the early 1800s, but gained prominence when Patrick Grant of Redcastle commissioned 200 yards of it to be worn by his branch of Clan Grant. As such, it has become an enduring symbol of Scottish family pride and heritage, associated with one of Scotland's most illustrious clans since its inception. Over time, the tartan has also been adopted by another clan, the Drummonds, who have worn it as their own tartan since 1822, further cementing its place in the country's cultural fabric.

name: Gray Hunting
description: The Gray Hunting tartan is a rich and storied design that embodies the spirit of Scotland's proud hunting heritage. Registered under the Clan/Family category, this distinctive tartan has been woven with great care by The House of Edgar, Perth, to evoke the rugged beauty of the Scottish countryside. With its complex interplay of subtle grays and warm earth tones, Gray Hunting is a testament to the skillful hands that have brought it to life - Christie C.'s masterful design is a tribute to the ancient traditions of hunting and the aristocratic families who have long been associated with this noble pursuit. As a symbol of Scottish heritage and family pride, Gray Hunting tartan holds a special place in the hearts of those who cherish its storied history and timeless beauty.

name: Gray John Hamilton
description: The Gray, Hamilton John tartan is a poignant commemorative design born from Canada's rich history and its unique connection to Scotland. Named in honour of Prince Edward Island's own son, Sir John Alexander Macdonald Hamilton, who was one of the Fathers of Confederation, this distinctive tartan weaves together threads of Canadian identity with Scottish heritage. Featured in the esteemed Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority, this sample was likely woven by the skilled hands of the West Coast Woolen Mill. While restrictions apply to ensure the integrity of the design's cultural significance, its impact is undeniable - a testament to Canada's enduring bond with Scotland and its own storied history, as told through the timeless language of tartan.

name: Greene [default]
description: The Greene tartan is a storied clan pattern steeped in heritage, woven into existence by the skilled hands of Philip Smith Jnr in 1999 for Robert Dodd Greene. This distinctive tartan holds significant cultural importance, its origins tracing back to the Greene family lineage, and its registration notes reflect an intention for it to be accessible to all members of the name. As a Clan/Family tartan, the Greene is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish clan traditions, with each thread meticulously woven to evoke the history and values of this esteemed family. With no specific restrictions on its use, the Greene tartan invites wearers to proudly showcase their connection to this storied heritage, evoking a sense of honour and tradition that resonates deeply within Scotland's rich tapestry of tartan heritage.

name: Greenhow (Rose) personal
description: The Confederate Rose tartan, designed by Heather Yellowley of Strathmore Woollen Co. Ltd, stands as a poignant tribute to Rose O'Neal Greenhow, affectionately known as 'Confederate Rose'. This commemorative tartan variation of the original #2501 (Scottish Tartans Authority reference) is a thoughtful rendition of the Confederate Memorial tartan, infused with personal significance by the designer's commission. The rich palette, featuring rose pink, purple, blue, yellow, and grey, tells a narrative of sacrifice and remembrance: purple represents mourning for the widows of Confederate soldiers, while blue alludes to the Bonnie Blue flag, a symbol of the Confederacy; yellow conveys the longing to communicate the sacrifice made by Rose O'Neal Greenhow, who wore her loyalty on her sleeve in this tumultuous period of American history. This tartan is not only a testament to Rose's honour, but also a testament to the power of heritage and tradition that defines Scotland's cultural landscape.

name: Greenshields Skye
description: The Greenshields tartan is a deeply personal and storied design, born from the rich heritage of the Greenshields clan family of Lanarkshire. Juliene Greenshields, the talented weaver behind this distinctive pattern, has carefully crafted a unique sett that pays homage to two of Scotland's most revered tartans: the Isle of Skye and Douglas. By infusing the intricate blue and green tones of the Isle of Skye with the subtle richness of the Douglas, Juliene has created a truly distinctive and evocative design that speaks to the complex and storied history of the Greenshields clan. As a personal tartan, it is meant to be cherished by those who wear it, serving as a tangible connection to family legacy and tradition, while also proudly showcasing their honourable heritage on the world stage.

name: Greer [default]
description: The Greer tartan is a storied and ancient clan tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands. Worn by Jack Greer at the prestigious Grandfather Mountain Games in 1994, this tartan has become an integral part of his personal history and family legacy. As a Clan tartan, the Greer bears the weight of tradition and ancestry, its carefully woven threads telling the story of generations past. Though its designer remains unknown, the tartan's provenance is undeniable, borne out by its association with Jack Greer and his kinship to a storied Scottish clan. This distinctive pattern, now proudly worn by its namesake in Tennessee, embodies the timeless spirit of Scottish heritage and the enduring connection between family, tradition, and land.

name: Greig (Ian) personal
description: The Greig tartan, named after its creator Ian Greig, holds great sentimental value as a unique sept tartan reserved exclusively for members of the esteemed Greig/Grieg family lines. This intricately woven pattern, born out of an agricultural consulting firm's desire to create a distinguishing heritage tie, has since become a symbol of familial identity and tradition. Designed in 2000 by its original owner Greig and Associates, later transferred to Lonmay Incorporated before landing in the capable hands of Ian Greig, this tartan's restrictions are a testament to its significance as a family legacy. With US and International copyright protection in place since 2002, the Greig tartan is now available for use by all direct descendants of the Greig/Grieg families, providing them with their own distinctive tartan identity that proudly reflects their heritage.

name: Gretna Football Club
description: The Gretna Football Club tartan is a vibrant tribute to the Scottish football club's rich heritage, expertly woven by Graeme Anderson in collaboration with Lochcarron. This corporate tartan embodies the team's iconic black and white stripes, blended with the bold red of the thistle from the club badge, creating a striking visual identity that proudly represents Gretna FC. As the official tartan of the club, it is worn by Anderson Kilts of Gretna in their exclusive range of products, offering fans and supporters a unique way to showcase their allegiance to the team. With its distinctive colour palette and cultural significance tied to Scotland's national flower, this tartan design serves as a celebration of Scottish tradition and community spirit, embodying the enduring values of local pride and loyal support that define Gretna Football Club.

name: Griffiths of Wales
description: The Griffiths of Wales tartan is a unique and intriguing design, born from the creative vision of Sheila Daniel at Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys, in collaboration with The Wales Tartan Centre in Cardiff. This Name tartan, featuring an unusual combination of odd-numbered threads and distinctive warp and weft patterns, challenges traditional Celtic tartan conventions. As a relatively recent creation, dating back to the late 1990s, its popularity has grown significantly, despite not being based on historical or genealogical claims.
