The use of 'of Wales' in the design's name serves as a nod to its origins and is intended to identify its source, rather than signify territorial ownership. With strict consent requirements from Swansea's Wales Tartan Centres prior to weaving, this tartan's distinctiveness is carefully preserved, making it a fascinating addition to the world of Scottish heritage textiles.

name:
Gunn [default]
[AKA] #2
description: The Gunn tartan is a testament to the rich history and heritage of the Clan Gunn, whose origins are shrouded in mystery despite its enduring presence on Scottish textiles since at least 1810. Designated as a family tartan, it was first recorded by Robert Cockburn in his collection, which showcases the intricate patterns woven into the fabric of Scotland's clan system. With roots stretching back to the early 19th century, this tartan has been passed down through generations of Clan Gunn members, with its connection to the Lauder and Banniskirk families further solidifying its place within Scottish tradition. Despite its unclear origins, the Gunn tartan remains a cherished symbol of clan identity, honouring the legacy of William Gunn, whose descendants continue to wear it with pride, as recorded in the Register of All Arms and Bearings in Scotland in 1960.

name: Guthrie [default]
description: The Guthrie tartan is a storied textile rich in heritage, originating from the esteemed Dalgety family of Forfar. This clan tartan was designed by Jack Dalgety himself, who created it for Ivan D. Guthrie as a personal motif, only to see it take on a life of its own as an emblem for all members of the Guthrie surname. With roots in the Ingles Buchan region, this tartan is steeped in tradition and has been carefully registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority. The design's significance extends beyond its technical characteristics, representing the honourable legacy of the Guthrie family and their place within Scotland's proud clan heritage.

name: Wynn of Wales
description: The Gwyn of Wales tartan is a distinctive Name tartan born from the heritage of Wales, a region steeped in tradition and history. Designed by Sheila Daniel for Wales Tartan Centres' Cambrian Woollen Mill, this unique tartan is marked by its use of unusual thread numbers and differing warp and weft combinations, setting it apart from other Celtic patterns. Its inclusion in this index underscores the growing popularity of the Cilt in modern times, a development that has been largely driven by Wales Tartan Centres' introduction since 1998. Though not tied to specific historical or genealogical claims, the 'of Wales' designation serves as a testament to its origins and provides context for those tracing their heritage through this vibrant textile pattern.

name: Gwyn [default]
description: The Gwynn tartan is a richly woven tribute to the storied heritage of the Gwynn family, its intricate patterns and colours evoking the rugged beauty of Wales' national tapestry. Designed by Paul Gwynn in 2003, this Clan tartan is a unique blend of tradition and innovation, marrying the timeless elegance of Welsh heritage with the personal nuances of the Gwynn family's history. Recognised as a distinct and authentic family tartan, the Gwynn can be worn by all individuals bearing the name, serving as a potent symbol of kinship and connection to this storied lineage. With its bold, vibrant hues carefully selected from the Welsh national palette, this tartan design proudly embodies the values of tradition, identity, and community that underpin Scottish clan culture.

name: Hackston Green Stripe
description: The Hackston (Green stripe) or Halkerston tartan holds a rich historical significance, its origins dating back to the 18th century. This distinctive pattern is said to have been seen in a portrait of Helenus Hackston, a member of the local Fife gentry, who was depicted soon after the Jacobite rising of 1745. The tartan's design, which features a prominent green stripe, is believed to have been inspired by the colours worn by the clan or family of Hackston, although its exact origins remain unclear. Interestingly, the Scottish Tartans Society notes of 1988 confirm this connection, while a count variation exists, featuring a black line in place of the green stripe. As an "Other" category tartan, the Hackston (Green stripe) is not specifically associated with a particular clan or family, making it a fascinating example of traditional Scottish textiles that have survived despite the passage of time, offering a glimpse into the cultural heritage of Scotland's past.

name:
Haig
[AKA] Gladstone #2
[AKA] Buccleuch Check #2
[AKA] Check 6 Squares
description: The Haig Check, named after Colonel Earl Haig, is a storied tartan with a rich history steeped in Scottish heritage. Designed by Sir Richard W Griffiths, the 4th Battalion King's Own Scottish Borderers' Colonel, in 1908, this unique check pattern was initially used as the pipers' plaid, evoking the rhythmic beats of the pipes at formal gatherings and ceremonies. As its namesake, Colonel Haig's family has carried on the tartan's traditions, imbuing it with their own honour and legacy. Though its origins behind the Gladstone Check and Buccleuch Check connections remain shrouded in mystery, this tartan's significance endures as a testament to Scotland's proud military heritage and the enduring bonds of family and tradition.

name:
Haig & Haig Whisky
[AKA] Haig John
description: The Haig & Haig Whisky tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan, carefully crafted by Johnstons of Elgin to evoke the rich heritage of Scotland's finest whisky. This iconic tartan holds significant status within Scottish heritage, having been meticulously registered by the renowned textile experts at Johnstons of Elgin. A testament to the region's storied past, this tartan design is inspired by the esteemed Haig & Haig Whisky brand, synonymous with fine Scotch malt. As a corporate tartan, it is intended for wear by staff and affiliates of the company, serving as a symbol of pride and connection to Scotland's rich whisky-making traditions. Its origins can be traced back to the late 20th century, as documented in Scottish Tartans Society records, ensuring that this tartan design remains firmly rooted in the history and culture of Scotland.

name: Haliburton Highlands
description: The Highlands of Haliburton tartan is a stunning tribute to the rugged beauty and rich heritage of one of Canada's most iconic regions. Registered as a District tartan, it proudly represents the districts surrounding Minden and Haliburton in Ontario, encompassing the majestic Algonquin Park. Designed by Miss M Patricia Jenkins, a renowned weaver and founder of The Loomcrofters of Gagetown, New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, this intricate design combines a palette of blues, greens, golds, reds, browns, and white to evoke the ever-changing landscape of the Highlands. With blue and green hues evoking the province's majestic waters, autumn foliage in shades of red and gold paying homage to loyalty and tradition, white threads representing the Trillium flower and winter snow, and brown tones symbolising the earth and its furry inhabitants, this tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Canada's natural heritage.

name: Hall [default]
description: The Hall tartan is a richly woven tribute to the heritage of Clan Skene Association members, specifically those bearing the surname Hall. Designed by President Atlas D. Hall himself, with guidance from Scotty Thompson, in 1992, this distinctive tartan was originally created as a means of identification for sept members. The clan's roots run deep through Scottish history, and this tartan is a testament to their proud tradition. Registered in 1994, the design reflects subtle modifications made by Hall himself, bringing it up to date while preserving its timeless essence. As part of the Clan Skene Association, the Hall tartan serves as a visual symbol of family pride and affiliation, carrying on the storied legacy of Scotland's oldest families with quiet dignity.

name: Halliday [default]
description: The Halliday tartan, designed by Matthew Newsome, is a rich and evocative tribute to the Scottish heritage of its namesake family. As a Name tartan, it holds particular significance for those bearing the surname, tracing its roots back to 13th-century Dumfriesshire. This traditional Border shepherd's check tartan, woven with skill by Weaver D.C. Dalgliesh, is deeply rooted in Scotland's rural past, drawing inspiration from the verdant hills of Moffat and Ettrick, where heather blankets the landscape. The subtle balance of greens and purples recalls not only the natural beauty of these regions but also the tumultuous Covenanting wars of the 17th century, when individual Hallidays played a notable part in Scotland's complex history. Now available to anyone with the surname, this tartan serves as a poignant connection to one's ancestry and a celebration of the enduring traditions that bind Scottish families together.

name: Hamilton Hunting
description: Hamilton Green Hunting is a storied tartan woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage, its origins dating back to the mid-20th century as an evolution of the esteemed Clan Hamilton tartan. Specifically designed as a 'Hunting version' of the original clan sett (#477), this variant boasts a striking green palette that subtly deviates from the traditional red hue, imbuing it with a fresh yet still deeply rooted character. This distinctive design, now registered to record its significance and authenticity, continues to hold honour within Scottish tartan tradition, reflecting the family's rich history and enduring legacy in hunting and the great outdoors.

name:
Hamilton of Brandon [default]
[AKA] Hamilton of Brandon
description: The Hamilton of Brandon tartan is a proud and storied example of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, woven from threads of tradition and history. Originating from Dalgliesh, D C, in response to his commission as 'Hamilton of Brandon', this distinctive tartan holds deep significance for the Clan and family it represents. However, its classification as 'Brandon (Manitoba)' by the Scottish Tartans Society has sparked intrigue, leaving one to ponder the connection between the Canadian city and the title once held by a 14th Duke of Brandon in 1711. Despite this anomaly, the tartan remains an authentic representation of the Hamilton family's lineage, its intricate patterns and hues reflecting the craftsmanship and tradition that have defined Scottish weaving for centuries.

name:
Hamilton of Clayton [default]
[AKA] Hamilton of Clayton
description: The Hamilton of Clayton tartan is a quintessential example of Scottish heritage, bearing testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Hamilton. Designed by the esteemed D.C. Dalgliesh Ltd, this distinctive Name tartan has been carefully crafted to reflect the unique character of the Clayton family. A true original, its subtle colour palette and intricate sett ensure that it stands out as a proud representation of Scottish tradition. Although a full sett is not present in the sample, the inclusion of a double white line in every second square adds an air of complexity to the design. Prepared for weaving by Dalgliesh Ltd, this tartan holds significant cultural value, and its registration with the Scottish Tartans Authority further solidifies its connection to Scotland's rich history.

name: Hamilton Red
description: The Hamilton, Red clan tartan is a storied and noble weft through Scotland's rich tapestry, born from the esteemed family of the Dukes of Hamilton. Registered in 1997 by Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan design pays homage to the clan's proud heritage, with its bold red hues echoing the passion and strength that has defined their history for centuries. Originally created for Nervesa Moda (Montana), this modern take on traditional Scottish textile artistry seeks to bring the essence of Scottish culture to a wider audience. While it remains unregistered in full colour due to an initial request for sample, the tantalising glimpse into this tartan's potential is undeniable, inviting all who lay eyes on it to delve deeper into its storied past and connect with the timeless traditions that have shaped Scotland's most iconic families.

name: Hamilton [default]
description: The Hamilton tartan, designed by Sobieski Stewarts of The, is a majestic representation of the heritage and tradition of Clan Hamilton. First recorded in their esteemed Vestiarium Scoticum, published in 1842, this storied design was part of a series created by the renowned Sobieski Stuart brothers. With its unique colour palette and intricate pattern, the Hamilton tartan pays tribute to the proud history of Scotland's noble families. As one of several similar designs by this illustrious clan, it serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Hamilton, whose ancestry stretches back through the centuries, woven into the very fabric of Scottish identity and tradition. This timeless design embodies the honour and prestige associated with its namesake clan, inviting wearers to don the colours of their noble heritage with pride.

name: Hammarby Football Club
description: This striking Corporate tartan, designed by the renowned duo Gillion/Nieminen, pays homage to Hammarby Football Club's rich history and triumphs. Named after Sweden's esteemed football club, which has been a fixture in Stockholm since 1895, this tartan is woven with pride and passion for the city and its beloved team. The registration notes reveal that the design was created by Joacim Nieminen and Patrick McVey Gillion to commemorate Hammarby IF Fotboll's historic Swedish Championship win in 2001, ending a remarkable 104-year wait. As a testament to this momentous occasion, the tartan has become an iconic representation of the club's dedication and perseverance. Prepared for weaving by Strathmore Woollen Company Ltd., this tartan is a fitting tribute to Hammarby Football Club's legacy, showcasing the intricate connection between sport, community, and tradition that underpins Sweden's vibrant football culture.

name:
Hanna of Leith [default]
[AKA] Hanna of Leith
description: The Hanna of Leith tartan is a treasured family heirloom, woven with love and pride by the esteemed kiltmakers A & J Scott in 1960s Aberdeen. Originally designed for the Hannah clan, this vibrant tartan has been passed down through generations, adorning kilts and sashes worn by members of 'Hannah's' of Leith, a revered Edinburgh family. With its bright yellow line adding warmth to a rich, dark blue and green colour palette, this tartan exudes the spirit of Scottish heritage and tradition. The intricate design tells the story of a proud clan history, as well as the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scotland's finest textile artists. Although reserved for family use only, this stunning tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Hannah name, weaving together threads of history, culture, and community that continue to captivate and inspire all who lay eyes on it.

name:
Hanna of Stirlingshire [default]
[AKA] Hanna of Stirlingshire
description: The Hanna of Stirlingshire tartan, named after its esteemed bearer, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans. As one of the most authentic and historically significant designs registered by the Lord Lyon's Tartans Committee in 1984, this tartan holds great honour within Scottish tradition. Documented as Hanna's second count, it showcases the intricate weaving skills of Charles Hanna, who painstakingly preserved the original patterns for future generations to cherish. With its distinctive colours and precise sett pattern, this tartan embodies the proud history of Stirlingshire, a county steeped in the stories of ancient clans and heroic battles. As a cherished part of Scotland's cultural legacy, the Hanna of Stirlingshire tartan will forever be woven into the fabric of the country's identity, connecting its wearers to a noble heritage that transcends time and tradition.

name: Hanna [default]
description: The Hanna (Bible) tartan, a personal and family heirloom of distinction, holds a profound connection to Scottish heritage. This clan tartan, attributed to Charles Hanna's own design, is steeped in tradition and mystery. Said to have originated from the pages of a 19th-century family Bible belonging to a Civil War veteran, the tartan's provenance remains shrouded in uncertainty, with no definitive date for its creation or inclusion within the revered text. Nonetheless, its presence on this biblical manuscript serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish tartanry, transcending time and geographical boundaries. With restrictions in place, this exclusive family tartan is reserved for those who can proudly claim Hanna ancestry, making it a cherished treasure among clan families worldwide.

name: Hannay Blue
description: Hannay Blue, a poignant tribute to the heritage of Clan Hannay, is a family tartan born from the ancestral roots of one remarkable individual, J A Hannah of Balquhidder. Originally crafted as a derivative of the esteemed Clan Hannay tartan, this distinctive blue hue replaces traditional white, imbuing the design with an air of subtle sophistication. Designed by Hannay/Urquhart in 2005, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Hannay's proud history and traditions, its muted tones evoking a sense of quiet dignity and family honour. As a Clan tartan, Hannay Blue holds a special significance for those whose surname carries the badge of this storied lineage, providing an authentic connection to their ancestral heritage and a visual representation of their unbroken ties to the past.

name: Hannay Dress
description: The Hannay Dress tartan, registered in the records as a testament to the Clan Hannay's rich heritage, exudes a vision of feminine elegance with its soft pink hue. Created by renowned weaver Hugh MacPherson, circa 1980, this distinctive tartan is believed to be more closely associated with traditional Scottish dance patterns than official clan dress, sparking debate among enthusiasts about its authentic usage. As a family tartan, the Hannay Dress holds significance for those tracing their roots to this storied clan, and its beauty lies not only in its unique colour palette but also in the stories it may tell of generations past. Despite some uncertainty surrounding its intended use, the Hannay Dress tartan remains an enduring tribute to Scottish tradition and a poignant reminder of the complex history that underpins our most treasured textiles.

name:
Hannay [default]
[AKA] Hanna of Sorbie
description: The Hannay tartan is a richly woven tribute to the proud heritage of Clan Hannay, with its storied history rooted in the South West of Scotland. Registered by Councillor John Hannay in 1984, following the discovery of an ancient kilt belonging to Commander Alex Hannay (1788-1844), this tartan is deeply significant for members of the Clan Hannay Society and those bearing the esteemed surnames of Hannay, Hannah, Hanna, or Hanney. The traditional design features a striking balance of blues, reds, and greens, with Councillor John Hannay's thoughtful addition of a yellow line bringing a vibrant touch to this iconic tartan. Originally recorded in the Lyon Court Books as "the official Clan Hannay tartan," the Hannay has been an integral part of Scottish tradition for centuries, its rich history and cultural significance ensuring that it remains a cherished emblem of clan pride and heritage.

name:
Harden [default]
[AKA] No.001
description: The Harden tartan, designed by esteemed Scottish textile firm Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1819, holds a special place within the realm of Scottish heritage. This Name tartan has been adopted by the Harden family as their own, allowing them to proudly don its distinctive weave on formal and everyday occasions alike. The Harden's story is woven into the very fabric of this tartan, which originated from an original pattern book entry, showcasing Wilsons' masterful craftsmanship and dedication to preserving Scotland's rich textile traditions. As a testament to family history and identity, the Harden tartan serves as a lasting symbol of heritage and belonging for all Hardens, binding past generations together while forging new connections with those who bear its name.

name: Hardie [default]
description: The Hardie tartan is a rich and storied Scottish heritage pattern, bearing testament to the proud legacy of Clan Hardie. Registered in the House of Tartan for Mr P Hardie of Ecclesmachan, West Lothian, this distinctive tartan has been woven into the fabric of family tradition for generations. Named after its creator, Paul Hardie, and associated with the Ecclesmachan branch of the clan, it is a symbol of honour and identity for those bearing the Hardie name. While restrictions on wear have been established by L.L. Bean Inc, ensuring that the tartan is reserved exclusively for members of the Clan Hardie and its variations, its significance extends beyond mere family affiliation, representing a deep-seated connection to Scotland's proud past and the enduring traditions of the Highlands.

name: Harding
description: The Harding tartan is a unique and captivating name tartan, imbued with the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's esteemed clan system. Designed by David Harding, this distinctive tartan brings together traditional Scottish design elements with innovative flair, reflecting the designer's passion for textiles, silverwork, and leathercraft. As part of a broader artistic project, the Harding tartan pays homage to the country's revered tradition of tartanry, incorporating subtle nuances that speak to the individual character of its creator. With no specific clan affiliation, this name tartan is open to interpretation, allowing it to be worn with pride by those who appreciate its distinctive charm and connection to Scotland's storied past.

name: Hargis [default]
description: The Hargis tartan, a rich and storied weave born from the creative vision of Charles "Chuck" E Hargis, is a proud embodiment of Scottish heritage and family identity. As a Clan/Family tartan, the Hargis has been reserved exclusively for use by individuals bearing the name, serving as a symbol of shared ancestry and kinship. Registered in 2002, this distinctive tartan design weaves together a complex interplay of blues, greens, and golds, evoking the rugged landscapes and storied traditions of Scotland's ancient clans. By wearing or using the Hargis tartan, its bearers declare their connection to a shared history and cultural heritage, forging a sense of community and pride that transcends time and geography.

name: Harkness Dress
description: The Harkness Dress tartan is a poignant creation by renowned designer Harvey Harkness Rulien, born from his American roots and infused with a deep understanding of Scotland's rich heritage. This Clan tartan, registered to reflect its family lineage, pays homage to the historical tensions between the Harknesses and the Douglases, whose ancestral lands they once rented. By deliberately diverging from the traditional Nithsdale sett, Rulien has cleverly subverted expectations, imbuing his design with a sense of rebellious independence. The tartan's muted colour palette, characteristic of many Scottish clan patterns, is juxtaposed with an intriguing Hunting sett, adding a layer of nuance to this already complex design. Ultimately, the Harkness Dress tartan serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of its namesake family, forever tied to the storied history of Scotland's clans and their intricate traditions.

name: Harkness Hunting
description: The Harkness Hunting tartan is a storied and evocative pattern, born from the rich heritage of the Harkness clan in Scotland's Highlands. Designed by Harvey Harkness Rulien, an American Scotsman with a deep respect for his ancestral roots, this tartan embodies the tradition of hunting and outdoor pursuits that has long been synonymous with Scottish culture. Characterised by its bold and nuanced colour palette, featuring shades of blue, green, yellow, and red, the Harkness Hunting tartan is a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of traditional tartan weaving. By creating this variation on the iconic Harkness Dress tartan, Rulien has offered a more subdued alternative for those seeking a distinctive yet understated expression of their Scottish heritage. As a Clan tartan, it holds great significance within the Harkness family's history and traditions, providing a tangible connection to their ancestral homeland.

name: Harley Davidson
description: The Harley Davidson tartan is a distinctive corporate design that embodies the iconic spirit of America's most revered motorcycle brand. Registered in 2003, this tartan was conceived by Klaus Hoeller, a creative visionary at Harley-Davidson's Los Angeles studio. Inspired by the rich heritage of the 'hogs', the design seamlessly blends bold colours and subtle textures, evoking the open roads and untamed landscapes that have come to define the American West. Woven by skilled artisans from Fraser & Kirkbright in Vancouver, this tartan is now available for corporate clients looking to project a unique image, one that embodies freedom, adventure, and the unbridled passion of motorcycling culture.

name: Harmer
description: The Harmer tartan is a vibrant and dignified corporate design, carefully crafted for the esteemed Harmer Family Association, a organisation dedicated to tracing the ancestral roots of its members in the UK. This storied tartan holds profound historical significance, its origins rooted in the rich heritage of the British Isles. The subtle nuances of its complex pattern tell the tale of generations past, while its bold colours evoke a sense of pride and tradition. According to Bruce Wayne Harmer's meticulous research, this distinctive design has been passed down through the family lines, now proudly worn by descendants as a symbol of their honourable heritage. As a testament to Scottish weaving traditions, the Harmer tartan embodies the values of loyalty, duty, and connection to one's roots, making it a treasured emblem for those who wear it with distinction.

name:
Harmony Eildon
[AKA] Check
[AKA] Longniddry #2
description: Harmony Eildon, a fashion tartan born from the skilled hands of designer Dalgliesh, D C, weaves together threads of Scottish heritage with modern flair. Originally registered as Longniddry in 1978, its evolution culminated in Harmony Eildon's distinctive blend of blues and greens. This carefully crafted pattern, inspired by the tranquil landscapes of Scotland, embodies the essence of unity and cohesion - a testament to the enduring spirit of the nation. While intended for fashion use, its unique character sets it apart from other designs, requiring special preparation for weaving by Dalgliesh Ltd. The Harmony Eildon tartan stands as a tribute to the rich tapestry of Scotland's past, with a subtle nod to its checkered history, registered under various names, including Harmony Check in 1983, as part of the Scottish Tartans Society's registry.

name: Harmony
description: The Harmony tartan, created by esteemed weaver Dalgliesh, D C, is a stunning Fashion tartan that embodies the very essence of balance and unity. Designed to bring people together in perfect harmony, its palette features soothing Turquoise as the primary GB colour. Characterised by wider stripes with fewer threads, this unique construction gives the tartan a subtle yet striking visual effect. Originally prepared for weaving by Dalgliesh's own firm at Selkirk, Harmony is now ready to be shared with the world, reflecting the beauty of Scottish heritage and the art of traditional weaving. Despite its widespread appeal, some restrictions apply, ensuring that this exquisite design remains true to its origins and cultural significance, a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish tartan-making traditions.

name: Harris (NY)
description: The Harris Personal tartan is a cherished family heirloom, steeped in tradition and heritage, as evident from its origins at the iconic Grandfather Mountain Games in 1997. As a clan tartan, it holds significant importance for families with a connection to the clan of Harris, named after the rugged island that shares its name. Registered by Robert William Harris, this distinctive design is a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of traditional Scottish weaving. The unique pattern, carefully crafted to reflect the cultural heritage of the Harris family, now serves as a symbol of pride for those who bear it. This tartan's rich history and significance are a reminder of Scotland's proud past and its enduring legacy in modern times.

name: Harris (Personal)
description: This Harris (1997) Name tartan is a personal tribute to the Scottish island bearing its name, imbued with a deep sense of heritage and tradition. Designed by Brother Ron William, a member of the Order of the Holy Cross, it draws inspiration from the V.S. MacPherson design, paying homage to the island's claimed ecclesiastical origins. As a registered Name tartan, this design is reserved for individuals or families with Scottish ancestry who wish to wear their heritage on their sleeve. With its unique blend of earthy tones and subtle texture, this tartan evokes the rugged beauty of Harris Island, where Gaelic culture and Christianity intersect in a rich tapestry of history and symbolism.

name: Harrison (Hamilton) personal; Highland Mist
description: Highland Mist, a sophisticated Corporate tartan designed by Claire Donaldson of House of Edgar for Harrisons of Hamilton, embodies the quintessential Scottish spirit with its subtle nuances and rich colours. This distinctive design, carefully crafted to evoke the mystical veil of Scotland's mist-shrouded Highlands, features a striking dark blue-verging-on-black hue that provides a dramatic backdrop for the bold magenta shade reminiscent of a Highland sunset. Originally created for Harrisons' retail outlet and kilt hire operation, Highland Mist is an excellent choice for corporate wear, exuding a sense of timeless elegance and refinement, whilst its unique colour matching challenges serve as a testament to the designer's skill and attention to detail.

name: Harrods Department Store Balnagown
description: The esteemed Balnagowan tartan, crafted by the renowned Kinloch Anderson Ltd, embodies the grandeur and heritage of Scotland's storied past. As a corporate identity for Harrods' exclusive merchandise range, this distinctive tartan is steeped in history and prestige. The design originates from the ancient seat of the Ross family at Balnagowan Castle, a testament to the enduring legacy of the Scottish nobility. With its restrictions in place, ensuring its use solely by the iconic department store, the Balnagowan tartan holds a special significance as a badge of honour for Harrods' discerning customers and connoisseurs of fine quality. As a unique and exclusive creation, this tartan pays tribute to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, its technical craftsmanship a reflection of the country's revered weaving traditions.

name: Harrods Department Store
description: The Harrods tartan is an iconic corporate design born from the renowned British department store's in-house workrooms, with its exact origins shrouded in mystery. Although not formally registered as a traditional Scottish clan tartan, it has been adopted for lining and interior purposes, reflecting the brand's luxurious heritage. This distinctive tartan-like textile design is thought to have been created by the Harrods Workrooms Department, embodying the opulence and sophistication of the iconic London institution. Characterised by its unique blend of reds, blues, and blacks, the Harrods tartan exudes a sense of refined elegance, fitting perfectly into corporate or interior design contexts where high-end style is paramount.

name: Hart (Texas) (Personal)
description: The Hart (Texas) tartan is a deeply personal and meaningful design born from the love of its creator, Linda Clifford, for her husband's family heritage. Specifically designed for the family of Ernest Neve Hart III, originally from St Mary Cray in Kent, England, this tartan tells the story of a transatlantic connection that bridges two worlds. With its unique colour palette and subtle texture, the Hart (Texas) tartan is a testament to the enduring power of tradition and cultural heritage. As a Name tartan, it is worn with pride by those who bear the name, serving as a symbol of family identity and a link to their ancestors' Scottish roots.

name: Hart [default]
description: The Hart of Scotland tartan is a testament to Scottish heritage, born from the esteemed Lochcarron of Scotland mill in 1995. This Clan tartan was registered specifically for Paul Hart's family from Queensferry, a small town on the Firth of Forth, evoking a sense of local pride and tradition. The intricate pattern weaves together shades of blue, green, and yellow, reminiscent of the rolling hills and heather-covered moors that define Scotland's rugged landscape. As a Clan tartan, it is steeped in history and family legacy, its design reflecting the values of loyalty, honour, and heritage that are at the heart of Scottish culture. With its unique character and storied past, the Hart of Scotland tartan continues to be cherished by those who wear it, as a symbol of their connection to this ancient land and its people.

name: Hartman
description: Hartmann Tartan is a deeply personal and storied Scottish textile, steeped in tradition and heritage. This unique Name tartan holds significance for its sole-bearer, Mathias Hartmann, and is thought to have been carefully crafted by renowned tailor Geoffrey Highland Crafts under the supervision of Mathias himself. Characterised by intricate, swirling patterns reminiscent of the rugged Highland landscape, this tartan embodies the resilience and determination of those who wear it, with a deep connection to their Scottish roots. As a Personal tartan, Hartmann Tartan is tailored specifically to its wearer's identity, making it a treasured family heirloom and a symbol of enduring loyalty and heritage.

name: Harvey [default]
description: The Harvey tartan, a timeless and authentic Name tartan, holds a rich place within Scottish heritage. Recognised as such since its recording in 1985, this threadcount was meticulously documented by Jim MacAslan in February 2006, providing invaluable insight into the tartan's history. Originally attributed to D C Dalgliesh and Pendleton Woolen Mills (Oregon), yet named after a sample supplied by Lochcarron, the Harvey tartan embodies the traditional craftsmanship of Scotland's textile industry. Its presence is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish weavers, who have painstakingly preserved and passed down this distinctive design through generations. As a name tartan, it is proudly associated with the families and surnames of those who bear its bearing, an honour bestowed upon individuals and clans alike by virtue of their connection to this storied heritage.

name: Haughdale [default]
description: The Haughdale tartan is a storied design rooted in the history of Clan MacKintosh, one of Scotland's most illustrious clans. As a MacKintosh variation, it has been carefully preserved and refined over time by committee, reflecting the clan's rich cultural heritage. The intricate pattern features a predominantly blue and green colour scheme, with subtle variations in tone that evoke the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. This Clan tartan is steeped in tradition, worn with pride by those who bear the MacKintosh name or are honourably connected to the family. Its origins may be uncertain, but its significance remains undeniable, serving as a poignant reminder of Scotland's complex and fascinating history.

name: Haughfoot
description: The Haughfoot tartan is a proud corporate tribute to the heritage of Freemasonry, woven with meticulous attention to detail by skilled artisans at Lochcarron of Scotland. Designed in honour of the 300th anniversary of the original Haughfoot Masonic Lodge, established in 1702, this distinctive pattern proudly incorporates mid blue, a colour deeply rooted in Masonic tradition. As such, it is steeped in symbolism and significance, reflecting the values of brotherhood and camaraderie that have defined the fraternity for centuries. Woven with a deep respect for Scottish heritage and tradition, the Haughfoot tartan is a fitting tribute to this revered institution, perfect for corporate wear or as a meaningful way to pay homage to one's own Masonic connections.

name: Hawaiian
description: The Hawaiian tartan is a distinctly District-style design, crafted with precision and attention to detail by renowned weaver Douglas Herring in 1997. This unique tartan was born from the intersection of Scottish heritage and Polynesian flair, as embodied by the 'Hawaiian Handweavers Hui.' Characterised by its distinctive colour palette, which blends warm earthy tones with a touch of turquoise, this tartan is steeped in cultural significance - a testament to the growing affinity between Scotland and the Pacific Islands. With no restrictions on use, this beautiful District tartan invites wearers to proudly celebrate their connection to both nations, while embracing the distinctive spirit of Aloha that defines the Hawaiian people.

name: Hawick Common Riding
description: The Hawick Common Riding tartan is a vibrant and symbolic corporate design that embodies the rich heritage of this Scottish town. Conceived to celebrate the ancient customs and traditions of the Common Riding, this tartan weaves together the iconic colours of blue and yellow, echoing the historic Hexham Priory flag captured at the Battle of Hornshole in 1514. A testament to the community's pride and identity, this tartan is a poignant souvenir for Hawick's townspeople, visitors, and exiles alike. As an official corporate design, it offers a unique opportunity for businesses to tap into the town's storied past, while its restricted availability ensures that its authenticity and cultural significance are preserved.

name: Hawick District
description: The Hawick tartan is a richly woven tapestry of Scottish heritage, steeped in history and tradition. Registered as the official district tartan for the town of Hawick in 1996, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the area's storied past, incorporating elements that evoke the bravery of its forebears at Flodden in 1513, where Hawick men gave their lives. The tartan's design seamlessly blends colours from the Pennant of the Priory of Hexham, the iconic Rugby Club and High School of Hawick, as well as the Douglas Clan tartan, which shares a connection to Drumlanrig Tower in the town. With its bold, symbolic elements – including the Red Reed motif representing the Battle of Flodden – this tartan design is both a tribute to Hawick's proud history and a celebration of its enduring spirit.

name: Hawick District #2
description: The Hawick (Trade Sett) tartan is a quintessential example of Scotland's rich textile heritage, evoking the country's storied past as a hub of commerce and industry. This iconic fashion tartan, bearing no specified designer but heavily influenced by the ubiquitous Royal Stewart, has been woven with meticulous care to create a distinctive pattern that exudes the proud traditions of Hawick, a market town in the Scottish Borders. With its subtle yet striking design, this tartan is said to have originated as a Trade Sett, used by merchants and traders to identify their affiliations, thus connecting its wearers to the town's storied history. Today, the Hawick (Trade Sett) tartan is worn with honour, proudly signifying its wearer's connection to this proud Scottish heritage.

name: Hawick Dress
description: The Hawick Dress tartan, a stunning example of Scottish heritage, was commissioned by the Hawick Tartan Company Ltd to create a dress version of the iconic Hawick Tartan. Designated as District 28, this tartan is steeped in tradition and rooted in the rich history of the district it represents. Woven by Wrights of Trowmill Ltd in 1996/1997, the Hawick Dress tartan pays homage to the local artisans who painstakingly crafted this distinctive design. With its unique colour palette and intricate pattern, this tartan is a celebration of Scottish culture and identity, evoking the warmth and history of the Hawick district where it originated. As an authentic representation of District 28, the Hawick Dress tartan holds great significance for those proud to call themselves Hawickshire residents or for anyone fascinated by the rich tapestry of Scotland's cultural heritage.

name: Hawick Rugby Club
description: The Hawick Rugby Club tartan is a vibrant expression of corporate identity, proudly worn by the club's members and supporters alike. Registered to the Corporate category, it embodies the values of teamwork, camaraderie, and community spirit that define the world of rugby. Designed by Ruthven Milne of Piob Mhor (Blairgowrie), this striking tartan is woven with precision and care, drawing inspiration from traditional Scottish colours and motifs. With its bold, modern design, it is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile heritage. The intricate pattern, taken from the Scottish Tartans Authority sample, tells a story of local tradition and cultural pride, making this tartan a distinctive and meaningful representation of Hawick Rugby Club's honour and history.

name: Hay #3
description: The Hay Stewart tartan is a storied name woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage, with its origins dating back to 1938. This distinctive Name tartan was created by Wilsons of Bannockburnn, a renowned firm in the heart of Scotland's tartan country. The design bears a striking resemblance to Victoria Stewart, yet it is distinguished by a bold double red overcheck on the white, imbuing it with a sense of vitality and dynamism. According to historical records, this tartan was probably designed by or for the Sobieski Stuart brothers, adding an air of mystery and connection to Scotland's aristocratic past. Today, the Hay Stewart tartan continues to be celebrated as a testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, inviting wearers to honour their connections to this esteemed Name and to proudly wear its vibrant, intricate patterns on special occasions or simply as a symbol of their enduring love for Scottish tradition.

name: Hay Dress
description: The Hay, White Dress tartan is a timeless example of traditional Scottish textile heritage, woven into the very fabric of the MacGregor-Hastie clan family's history. Dating back to between 1930 and 1950, this sample showcases the intricate craftsmanship that has defined Scotland's tartan weavers for centuries. Originally part of the Scottish Tartans Society's cloth archive, this unmarked but striking design is a testament to the enduring influence of Clan MacGregor-Hastie on Scotland's cultural tapestry. While its exact designer remains unknown, it is clear that this tartan has been lovingly crafted and passed down through generations, embodying the warmth and hospitality that are synonymous with Scottish tradition.

name:
Hay and Leith #2
[AKA] Leith #4
[AKA] Hay of Leith; #2
description: The Hay and Leith tartan is a revered family heritage, its rich history woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition. Originally known as Leith in 1819, this tartan was later adapted to reflect the union of the Hay and Leith families through intermarriage by the mid-1830s. Now commonly referred to simply as Hay, this iconic pattern is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's clan system. Its distinctive design, with its subtle interplay of blues and greens, evokes the mist-shrouded lochs and windswept moors of the Scottish Highlands. As a Clan tartan, the Hay and Leith is steeped in tradition and family pride, worn by descendants of those who first bore it to connect with their heritage and celebrate their shared history.

name: Hay [default]
description: The Hay tartan, a revered Clan family design, weaves its rich heritage into every thread. First documented in 'Vestiarium Scoticum' by the Sobieski Stuart brothers in 1842, this tartan has been woven for centuries, its subtle variations reflecting the intricate traditions of Scotland's noble families. Its unique threadcount, recorded by the Earl of Erroll, Chief of the Hays, in 2002, provides a tangible link to the past, as do the historic references to 'R/12 G8 Y4 G72 R4 G4 R4 G24 R96 G8 R4 K2 R4 W/12'. As one of Scotland's oldest and most storied tartans, the Hay embodies the country's proud history and heritage, a testament to the enduring legacy of its clansmen who wore it with honour. Its complex pattern, passed down through generations, now proudly represents the noble family of Erroll, their tartan woven into the very fabric of Scotland's tradition.

name: Hayes
description: The Hayes fashion tartan, designed by Dorr Woolen Mill, is a striking addition to Scotland's rich textile heritage. Originating from the Johnston Collection, this tartan was originally registered as Hay V.S. #1555, indicating its familial ties. With subtle variations in proportions, the Hayes tartan has become an accepted Clan/Family tartan, symbolising the history and identity of those who bear it. Woven by Lochcarron in 2004/5, this design showcases the artistry and tradition of Scottish weaving. As a fashion tartan, it offers a vibrant and distinctive alternative for wearers looking to make a statement with their heritage, while its acceptance as a Clan/Family tartan affirms its significance within Scotland's rich cultural fabric.

name: Haymarket
description: The Haymarket Dress tartan, crafted with flair by Hugh Macpherson, is a masterful creation inspired by the vibrant spirit of Scotland's capital city, Edinburgh. This Fashion tartan is designed for those who crave the elegance of formal dresswear, yet yearn for the playfulness and charm of traditional Scottish dancing. With its distinctive ground colour scheme subtly tweaked to substitute white for one of the original 'ground' colours, this design perfectly embodies the 'dress' version of clan tartan tradition - a testament to Macpherson's innovative approach to creating visually stunning fabrics that capture the essence of Scotland's rich cultural heritage.

name: Head of the Lakes
description: The Head of The Lakes tartan is a stunning tribute to the natural beauty of Northern Ontario, specifically the majestic Lake Superior, located in Thunder Bay. Registered as a District Tartan, this unique pattern pays homage to the city's rich heritage and its connection to the region's breathtaking landscapes. Designed by Joan Forrester Troniak and Fiona Irwin, this tartan is more than just a colourful textile – it is a celebration of the area's cultural identity and its people. By adopting the Head of The Lakes tartan, Thunder Bay has given a nod to its Northwoods roots, weaving its history and traditions into the very fabric of its community. This carefully crafted design is a testament to the enduring spirit of the region, blending tradition with innovation in a celebration of Canadian heritage.

name: Healy [default]
description: The Healy tartan, shrouded in mystery, whispers tales of its ancestral roots within the storied ranks of Scottish clan heritage. This enigmatic pattern is a curious amalgamation of Clan Cian's original design, with subtle yet significant variations that set it apart from its venerable precursor. The subtle colour shifts - most notably to the incorporation of blue - no doubt echo the sartorial suggestions of esteemed tartan connoisseur Phil Smith, whose seminal work 'Tartan for Me' had piqued the interest of those seeking a distinctive identity. As a Clan/Family tartan, Healy bears the weight of expectation, its wearer duty-bound to uphold the traditions and histories of their forebears.

name: Heart of Midlothian Football Club
description: The Heart of Midlothian Football Club tartan is a vibrant tribute to one of Scotland's most beloved footballing institutions, Edinburgh's Hearts FC. Registered in the corporate category, this tartan pays homage to the club's rich history and heritage, which dates back to 1874 when it was founded by a group of enthusiasts at Tynecastle Stadium. MacArthur & Co.'s Peter designer has masterfully woven the threads of tradition and modernity into this iconic pattern, evoking the passionate spirit of Hearts' devoted supporters. With its bold colours and distinctive sett, this tartan is not only a symbol of corporate identity but also a badge of honour for the club's loyal fans, who proudly wear it to represent their love for the team that has become an integral part of Scotland's sporting fabric.

name: Heart of Scotland #2
description: This enchanting tartan, aptly named Heart of Scotland, is a masterpiece woven by Ruthven Milne of Piob Mhor, Blairgowrie. As a Fashion tartan, it embodies the quintessential spirit of Scottish style and heritage, evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes that define this beautiful country. This unique design boasts an intricate pattern of blues, greens, and yellows, recalling the heather-clad moors and sparkling lochs that dot Scotland's picturesque landscape. With no recorded origins or prior registrations, its existence was only confirmed in September 2002, marking a fascinating discovery that sheds new light on Scotland's rich textile heritage. This tartan is a testament to Milne's skillful craftsmanship and a celebration of Scotland's timeless beauty, awaiting the wearer to bring it to life with pride and distinction.

name: Heart of Scotland
description: The Heart of Scotland tartan, proudly registered in 1999 by Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage. This Fashion tartan is designed for 'Gavin' Kiltmaker, a renowned kilts manufacturer, who has woven it into their hire kilts to celebrate this iconic design. The colour palette, carefully checked against sample and swatch, reflects the rich hues of the Highland landscape - earthy tones of heather and wildflowers, with subtle nuances of gold and blue that evoke the majesty of Scotland's lochs. As a testament to the country's rich cultural identity, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scottish tradition, woven into every carefully crafted stitch.

name: Heart of Strathearn
description: The Heart of Strathearn tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate design that embodies the values of determination and ambition that drive Scotland's young people to succeed. Registred as part of the Scottish Government's Determined to Succeed strategy, this tartan represents the next generation of Scots who are being encouraged to pursue vocational learning, entrepreneurship, and enterprising careers with confidence and self-reliance. Designed by Jennifer Logan, this unique blend of colours pays tribute to the rich heritage of Strathearn, a region steeped in history and tradition. With its bold and modern aesthetic, the Heart of Strathearn tartan is a powerful symbol of Scottish entrepreneurship and a celebration of the country's commitment to empowering the next generation to achieve their goals and realise their ambitions.

name: Heartlands
description: The Heartlands tartan, crafted with meticulous attention to detail by Erica Randall at House of Edgar, is a captivating fusion of traditional Scottish heritage and modern flair. This Fashion tartan was specifically designed for the esteemed MacGregor and MacDuff kilt hire business, drawing inspiration from the timeless Melville sett. The result is a richly textured pattern that evokes the rolling hills and storied landscapes of Scotland's Heartlands region, where tradition and innovation blend seamlessly together. With its distinctive blue and green hues, this tartan is not only a stunning addition to any outfit but also serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile heritage, woven with the skill and passion of the House of Edgar's talented designers.

name: Heather Isle
description: The Heather Isle tartan is a captivating fashion design born from Scotland's lush landscapes, expertly crafted by Lochcarron of Scotland in 2005. This stunning tartan was created to showcase the country's natural beauty and versatility, woven into several high-quality variations for kilt, ladies' skirt, and scarf. The Heather Isle tartan embodies the very essence of Scottish heritage, with its subtle nuances evoking the rolling hills and misty moors of the Highlands. As a fashion design, it has been imbued with the honour of representing a timeless and traditional Scottish aesthetic, perfect for those who seek to wear their passion for Scotland on their sleeve – or in this case, on their tartan-clad attire.

name: Heather MacRae
description: Heather MacRae, a majestic fashion tartan designed by renowned weaver Moffat Weavers, is a testament to Scotland's timeless heritage. This stunning pattern, woven with precision, evokes the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands' heather-clad moors. The Heather MacRae tartan's distinctive characteristics make it a coveted choice for those seeking to embody the essence of Scottish style and tradition. With its intricate design and carefully crafted colours, this tartan is perfect for fashion enthusiasts who want to showcase their love for Scotland's rich cultural heritage. As an officially registered tartan with the Scottish Tartans Authority, Heather MacRae joins a select group of traditional patterns that have been meticulously preserved and passed down through generations, awaiting their next wearer to bring them to life with pride.

name: Hebridean Cairn
description: The Hebridean Cairn tartan, meticulously crafted by renowned designer Kirsty Anderson, embodies the rugged yet elegant spirit of Scotland's iconic island landscapes. This fashion tartan is part of a prestigious collection, marking an honourable debut for a discerning heritage brand. Characterised by deep, dark greys that evoke the mysterious hills and cairns of the Hebridean Isles, this complex pattern is woven with precision to convey the timeless allure of Scotland's wild and majestic interior. With its intricate interplay of muted blues and greens, the Hebridean Cairn tartan presents a fresh yet distinctly Scottish identity, poised to add a touch of understated sophistication to any fashion ensemble that wears it.

name: Hebridean Dress Arisaid Blue
description: Hebridean Arisaid Blue is a stunning fashion tartan that embodies the rugged beauty of Scotland's Hebrides, an archipelago steeped in history and tradition. Named after the Gaelic word for 'rest' or 'haven', this design weaves together a mesmerising blend of blues, greens, and whites to evoke the tranquility of the islands' crystal-clear waters. With its origins shrouded in mystery, this captivating tartan is believed to have been created by the esteemed Dalgliesh D C for fashion enthusiasts seeking to connect with the nation's rich cultural heritage. Though restrictions apply to ensure its authenticity, the end result is a truly unique and evocative design that invites wearers to own a piece of Scotland's timeless beauty.

name: Hebridean Dress Arisaid Red
description: The Hebridean Arisaid Red, also known as Dance, is a vibrant fashion tartan that embodies the essence of Scottish heritage and energy. Created by renowned designer Dalgliesh D C in collaboration with D C Dalgliesh Ltd, this striking design was initially intended for fashion wear. The registration notes remain cryptic, but it is clear that this tartan's purpose is to add a splash of colour and movement to any garment. With restrictions in place, the design must be carefully prepared by D C Dalgliesh Ltd before weaving, ensuring its intricate patterns are preserved for generations to come. This fashion tartan pays homage to the rich cultural traditions of the Hebridean islands, evoking the sense of dynamic movement and joy that comes with traditional Scottish dance.

name: Hebridean Granite
description: Kirsty Anderson's Hebridean Granite tartan is a modern interpretation of Scotland's rugged beauty, echoing the granite landscapes that dominate the islands of the Inner Hebrides. This Fashion tartan is a deliberate choice to add a touch of contemporary glamour to the traditional Scottish textile. As part of House of Edgar's collection, it serves as a bold statement piece, poised to become a wardrobe staple for those who desire a stylish connection to Scotland's rich heritage. The subtle nuances in tone and texture invite exploration, while Anderson's restraint ensures that this tartan remains accessible to all who wish to wear a piece of Scottish flair with honours.

name: Hebridean Heather
description: The Hebridean Heather, designed by esteemed Kirsty Anderson for the fashion world, embodies the rugged charm of Scotland's windswept islands. This striking tartan pattern, characteristic of Scottish Fashion tartans, is woven with a palette of deep blues and greens that evoke the vast, heather-covered moors of the Hebrides. While its dark grey tones may initially appear sombre, it is in fact a rich, muted hue reminiscent of the misty morning skies over Scotland's rugged coastlines. As a fashionable interpretation of traditional Scottish design, this tartan offers a modern take on heritage, perfect for adding a touch of subtle, understated elegance to any outfit.

name: Hebridean North Uist
description: This enigmatic tartan, registered in the Scottish Tartans Authority archives, holds a rich history rooted in the Outer Hebrides' North Uist island. Dated 1814, its origins remain shrouded in mystery, with no designer credited or identified by name. Nonetheless, this unassuming design tells a story of a long-forgotten clan or community that once called the rugged islands home. The tartan's unique pattern, woven from natural dyes, evokes a sense of nostalgia for a bygone era, when traditional weaving techniques were passed down through generations of islanders. As one of the earliest recorded examples from this remote region, Unnamed C19th #1 serves as a tangible link to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, whispering secrets of the past to those who gaze upon its subtle, yet distinctive, beauty.

name: Hebrides #02
description: This enigmatic tartan, designated as Unnamed C18/19th #1, embodies the mystique of Scotland's rich textile heritage. Its origins, shrouded in mystery, are hinted at by the undated specimen held within the National Museum of Scotland's collection. This 'other' category tartan defies categorisation into a specific clan or tradition, instead existing outside the boundaries of traditional Scottish tartans. Its significance lies in its unique place within the narrative of Scottish textiles, a product of the late 18th and early 19th centuries. While no designer is credited with its creation, it remains a testament to the skillful hands of an unknown weaver, whose craftsmanship has been preserved for generations to be admired and worn by those drawn to Scotland's rich cultural traditions.

name: Hebrides #07
description: This historic District tartan, registered in the 18th century, holds a special place in Scotland's rich cultural heritage. Designated as Hebridean #3, it is a testament to the intricate weaving traditions of the islands, where the rugged landscapes and strong clan loyalties have shaped the very fabric of Scottish identity. The tartan's origins are shrouded in mystery, with its designer name lost to time, but its association with Bute Collection in the Scottish National Museum of Scotland serves as a tangible link to the past. As a District tartan, it is an important part of Scotland's tartan heritage, signifying the connections and affiliations that once bound communities together. Its storied history is now preserved, awaiting discovery by those who appreciate the beauty and significance of this enigmatic Hebridean #3.

name: Hebrides #09
description: Hebrides #8 is a captivating tartan design steeped in the rich history and cultural heritage of Scotland's western islands. As part of the esteemed Bute Collection, which resides at Mount Stewart in Rothesay, Firth of Clyde, this subtle yet evocative tartan has been woven with precision to evoke the gentle wildness of the Hebridean landscape. Although not specifically tied to a particular clan or family lineage, its origins in the Bute Collection suggest a connection to the aristocratic history of Scotland's west coast. With no specific designer credited, it is likely that this tartan has evolved organically over time, reflecting the enduring traditions and aesthetic sensibilities of the region.

name: Hebrides #11
description: This enigmatic Unnamed C18th â Hebridean #2 tartan embodies the subtle nuances of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, its provenance shrouded in mystery. Classified under 'Other', it does not belong to a specific clan or family lineage, yet its origins remain tantalisingly obscure. Originally acquired by the esteemed Marquis of Bute, whose extensive collection at Mount Stewart in Rothesay is now a treasured repository of Scottish history, this tartan design whispers tales of 18th-century Hebridean craftsmanship. Despite the unknown designer behind this masterpiece, its intricate patterns evoke a sense of timeless tradition and enduring connection to the rugged beauty of Scotland's western islands, where myths and legends once roamed free.

name: Hebrides Outer
description: The Hebrides, Outer tartan is a timeless and evocative design that embodies the rugged beauty of Scotland's western islands. This Category 'Other' tartan, which defies traditional clan affiliations, was chosen by its designer to celebrate the unique cultural heritage of the Hebridean archipelago. Drawing inspiration from the region's dramatic landscapes and rich history, this tartan weaves together a subtle palette of blues, greens, and yellows, evoking the sea-worn stones, wind-swept moors, and emerald glens that make the Hebrides so breathtakingly beautiful. Without its designer's name specified in the registration notes, it remains an enigmatic testament to the artistry of Scotland's tartan weavers, whose legacy continues to captivate audiences today, inviting wearers to honour their connection to this wild and storied land.

name: Hebrides South Uist #02
description: This enigmatic Unnamed C18th Hebridean #4 tartan is a poignant reminder of the rich tapestry of Scotland's cultural heritage. Registered as a District tartan, it falls under the esteemed category of regional identity, reflecting the distinct traditions and history of the area where it originated. Born from the extensive collection amassed by the Marquis of Bute at Mount Stewart in Rothesay, this tartan is steeped in the stories of the Firth of Clyde's past. Although its designer remains unknown, their craftsmanship and understanding of Hebridean textiles are evident in the intricate pattern, which has been passed down through generations as a testament to the region's enduring legacy.

name: Hebrides [default]
description: The Hebrides tartan, registered with distinction as a District pattern, is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's western coastlines. With its intricate, blue-grey tones evoking the misty mornings and sea-weathered landscapes of the Inner Hebrides, this ancient design whispers tales of a storied history. The West Coast Woolen Mill's creative vision has brought this traditional District pattern to life, paying homage to the rugged beauty and strong sense of community that defines the region. Though its registration notes remain incomplete, it is clear that this tartan holds a special place in the hearts of those who cherish Scotland's wild and windswept beauty.

name: Hebron
description: The Hebron tartan is a fashion-inspired variation on the iconic Black Watch, with its rich heritage firmly rooted in Scotland's storied past. Designed by Aljean of Vancouver, this distinctive pattern features subtle differences that set it apart from the original. Registration notes suggest that it may have been created as early as 1993, making it one of the earliest known variations of the iconic Black Watch design to be registered. The addition of Irene Leys' label hints at a connection to the fashion world, while the overall colour palette and subtle tweaks imply a desire to pay homage to Scotland's rich tartan heritage. As a fashion tartan, Hebron offers a unique blend of modern style and traditional flair, making it an attractive choice for those looking to add a touch of Scottish sophistication to their wardrobe.

name: Hector James Clothing
description: The Hector, James tartan is a modern corporate creation that weaves together the rich heritage of Scottish tradition with sleek, contemporary flair. Registered by the esteemed House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this distinctive tartan was designed by Claire Donaldson specifically for a clothing company bearing its name. The result is a sophisticated, versatile pattern that lends itself perfectly to business attire and corporate wear. While its origins may be rooted in traditional Scottish design, the Hector, James tartan has evolved into a modern statement piece that proudly celebrates British heritage and style.

name: Hector, The Ship
description: The majestic 'Ship Hector, The' tartan is a poignant tribute to the storied history of Scottish emigration to Nova Scotia in 1773. Commissioned by the late Hector Foundation of Pictou, which celebrated the arrival of the ship that brought 189 Scottish settlers to its shores, this commemorative tartan weaves together threads of tradition and heritage. Designed by Janice Gammon, a master weaver of her craft, the intricate patterns evoke the rugged beauty of the North Atlantic coast and the resilience of those brave Scots who braved the unknown to build new lives. This majestic tartan now bears witness to the enduring legacy of the Ship Hector Society, a testament to the power of community and tradition in shaping the identity of this remarkable piece of Canadian history.

name: Heddle [default]
description: The Heddle tartan is a timeless and intimate name tartan, steeped in romantic tradition and Scottish heritage. Designed by Scott Heddle for his own nuptials, it was originally woven by esteemed Lochcarron of Scotland, imbuing the fabric with a sense of history and craftsmanship. Worn at the couple's wedding ceremony in St Magnus Cathedral, Kirkwall, on June 28, 2003, this tartan has since been immortalised as a testament to the enduring power of love and Scottish tradition. With its unique colour palette and traditional weave, the Heddle tartan is a poignant celebration of the union between two people, and an honour to be woven with the finest Scottish yarns, bearing witness to the passing of time and the bond that unites two hearts forever.

name: Heirloom Alba; Blue
description: The Heirloom Blue Alba is a captivating Fashion tartan designed by the renowned Scottish textile mill, Lochcarron of Scotland. This exquisite fabric features a rich, heather-inspired hue with subtle nuances of blue and green, evoking the majestic beauty of Scotland's ancient landscapes. As a Fashion tartan, it is intended for use in clothing and accessories that showcase the wearer's connection to heritage and tradition. The Heirloom Blue Alba holds significant cultural importance, symbolising loyalty and continuity, much like the ancestral ties that bind families together through generations. This carefully crafted design has been registered by the Scottish Tartans Authority, solidifying its place within Scotland's rich tapestry of traditional textiles, awaiting its next wearer to proudly wear it as a badge of honour.

name: Heirloom Dark Alba
description: The Heirloom Dark Alba tartan is a luxurious and sophisticated addition to Scotland's rich textile heritage, inspired by the country's storied past. This exquisite fashion tartan was designed by Lochcarron of Scotland, a renowned Scottish manufacturer of fine textiles, to bring an air of elegance and refinement to garments and accessories. With its intricate weave and subtle colour nuances, Heirloom Dark Alba is a testament to the art of traditional Scottish weaving, evoking the mysterious and romantic landscapes of the Scottish Highlands. As a fashion tartan, it's perfect for dressing up or adding a touch of sophistication to formal wear, while its registration with the Scottish Tartans Authority ensures its authenticity and connection to Scotland's cultural tradition.

name: Heirloom Red Alba
description: Heirloom Red Alba, a timeless fashion tartan designed by Lochcarron of Scotland, is a masterful blend of traditional Scottish heritage and modern style. This stunning pattern, classified as a Fashion tartan, was meticulously crafted to evoke the rich colours and textures of Scotland's ancient weaving traditions. With its distinctive red and blue hues evoking the rolling hills and misty lochs of the Scottish Highlands, Heirloom Red Alba is a true tribute to the country's proud cultural legacy. This beautiful fabric would have been favoured by Scots from all walks of life to add a touch of elegance and sophistication to their everyday attire, and its enduring appeal makes it an excellent choice for fashion enthusiasts seeking to connect with Scotland's rich heritage.

name: Help for Heroes
description: The Help for Heroes tartan is a powerful symbol of camaraderie and national pride, born from the collaboration between esteemed tailors William McGregor and George Neil. Inspired by the colours of the UK Army, Navy, and Airforce, this distinctive design has been created to support the charity of the same name, which provides vital support to injured service personnel and their families. As a corporate tartan, it is worn with honour in business and professional settings, serving as a poignant reminder of the sacrifices made by those who serve our country. With its bold, striking pattern, this tartan design embodies the values of courage, resilience, and community that are at the heart of British military tradition.

name: Henbury
description: The Henbury Corporate tartan is a modern and versatile weave that has been carefully crafted to make a lasting impression on any business or organisation. Asymmetrical in its design, with differing warp and weft patterns, this tartan embodies a sense of dynamic energy and innovation, reflecting the ambitions of those who wear it. Its origins are humble, however, hailing from the Scottish Borders, where the Henbury Ltd. factory, based on High Street in Kinross, first brought this vibrant cotton twill to life. Without a specific designer attributed to its creation, it is clear that the true value of the Henbury lies not in individual creativity, but in its collective significance as a symbol of corporate identity and unity, perfect for organisations seeking to establish a strong brand presence.

name: Henderson Dress
description: The Henderson Dress, also known as Dance, is a timeless fashion tartan steeped in tradition and heritage. Designated as one of Dr Philip D's creations, this intricate pattern was originally intended to adorn the iconic Highland dancing attire of the eponymous clan's members. With its rich colours of blue, green, and yellow, this tartan embodies the vibrant spirit of Scotland's cultural identity, evoking memories of lively ceilidhs and spirited performances on the dance floor. As a Fashion category tartan, it has been adopted by many who seek to embody the country's proud heritage through their sartorial choices, its distinctive design serving as a visual expression of respect for the rich history and tradition that underpins Scottish culture.

name: Henderson Dress #3
description: Henderson Dress #1 is a timeless and storied clan tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. This iconic tartan has been woven with meticulous care since its registration, bearing testament to the skilled hands of Geoffrey Highland Crafts. Dating back to the 18th century, this particular design was approved by the Chief, underscoring its authenticity and cultural significance. As a Clan/Family tartan, Henderson Dress #1 is intricately tied to the history and identity of the Henderson family, with each thread carefully crafted to reflect their unique traditions and values. Its approval by the Chief serves as a badge of honour, acknowledging the tartan's place within Scotland's rich tapestry of woven heritage.

name: Heneghan
description: The Heneghan Name Tartan is a vibrant representation of Scottish heritage, woven with love and tradition by Phil Heneghan and his relatives from San Francisco, Maryland, and Alaska. Commissioned to commemorate the 50th wedding anniversary of John Martin Heneghan and Mary Coyle Heneghan, this tartan embodies the family's Celtic roots and enduring connections across generations and continents. The carefully chosen colours reflect the rich tapestry of Scottish culture, while the intricate design acknowledges the pivotal roles of its designers in strengthening the bonds of the Heneghan clan worldwide. A testament to the power of family tradition and cultural pride, this tartan serves as a lasting tribute to John and Mary's remarkable legacy, forever entwining their heritage with that of their descendants.

name: Henkel
description: The Henkel tartan, designed by renowned textile experts Retl/Bacher, embodies the essence of corporate tradition with its sleek, modern aesthetic. As a Corporate tartan, Henkel is distinguished from other clan and family registrations, denoting its connection to business and professional identities. With no additional information available regarding its origins or historical context, Henkel remains an enigmatic yet sophisticated choice for companies seeking a unique visual representation of their brand. Its reserved colour palette and calculated arrangement of threads evoke a sense of professionalism and discretion, making it an attractive option for organisations seeking to establish a strong, lasting impression. As a testament to the ingenuity of its creators, the Henkel tartan stands as a shining example of contemporary textile design, expertly blending tradition with innovation in the world of corporate branding.

name: Henry WA
description: The Henry, W.A. tartan is a commemorative tribute to Canadian heritage, expertly woven by the renowned West Coast Woolen Mill in Vancouver. This authentic clan tartan, representing one of Canada's Founders, is a testament to the country's rich history and cultural legacy. Registered with Sainthill-Levine & Co., this tartan was born out of a desire to honour the nation's founders and promote national pride. As such, it falls under the Commemorative category, making it a highly distinctive and meaningful addition to any Scottish heritage collection. While restrictions apply, the West Coast Woolen Mill's skillful interpretation ensures that the original intent and traditional essence of this tartan are preserved for generations to come.

name: Hepburn #2
description: Hepburn #2 is a rich and storied tartan, its threads woven with the heritage of a family legacy. As a registered Name tartan, it was intended to be worn by members of the Hepburn clan, but in this case, its origins are shrouded in mystery. Acquired by W.H. Johnston U.S.A, a renowned Tartan collector, Hepburn #2 is now preserved for generations to come. Its subtle nuances and intricate patterns evoke the traditions of Scotland's tartan-making past, where every thread was carefully selected to represent the very essence of its wearer's honour and ancestry. Though the designer's identity remains unknown, this tartan's significance lies not in its creator, but in the stories it holds within its fabric - of family ties, cultural heritage, and the unyielding spirit of Scotland's finest clans.

name: Hepburn [default]
description: The Hepburn tartan, bearing the name of a storied clan family, is steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registred in 1968 by Anderson's of Edinburgh from an existing design for Captain Charles Hepburn, this sett weaves together threads of history and nobility. Associated with Hermitage Castle in Liddesdale, a stronghold once inhabited by the enigmatic James Hepburn, 4th Earl of Bothwell - infamous for his involvement in the tragic fate of Mary, Queen of Scots - the tartan's origins are etched in the annals of Scotland's tumultuous past. This Clan tartan is not merely a design, but a tangible connection to the storied legacy of the Hepburn family, whose intricate story is forever intertwined with the nation's own rich tapestry of tradition and culture.

name: Herbage
description: The Herbage of Laggan tartan, designed by Bob Martin, is a unique and personal creation that tells the story of its namesake's ambitious entrepreneurial spirit. Registered as a Name tartan, it reflects the identity of Sir David Herbage of Laggan, a prominent Scottish businessman who purchased the historic Laggan estates in the early 1980s. This distinctive tartan sample, housed in the Scottish Tartans Authority Johnston Collection, is a testament to Herbage's innovative approach to business and his connection to Scotland's rich heritage. Although the Laggan estates changed hands after Herbage's bankruptcy, this tartan remains an enduring symbol of his legacy and a fascinating footnote in Scotland's textile history.

name: Herd
description: The Herd/Hurd tartan is a name tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, born from the private family tartan application of Councillor R J Herd, an accomplished engineer and member of various esteemed institutions. Recognised by the Scottish Tartans Society in 1978, this distinctive design showcases the interplay of blue and green hues reminiscent of Scotland's rugged landscapes. Woven with affection for both the Herd and Hurd families, it was also specifically created for the wedding celebration of Willard F Hurd and Heather A Petit in 1993, symbolising a union of two families bound by love and tradition. As a testament to its significance, this tartan remains a cherished family heirloom, passed down through generations with pride and honour, its unique character reflecting the enduring legacy of Scottish clans and their rich cultural heritage.

name: Heriot
description: The Heriot tartan is a corporate creation steeped in Scottish heritage, its origins shrouded in mystery despite its recognisable threads. Said to have been unearthed in an ancient pattern book from a lesser-known firm, McBean (or McBain) and Bishop, this tartan's provenance is tantalisingly unclear. Yet, as with many unsung heroes of the Scottish textile world, it remains a testament to the ingenuity and skill of traditional weavers. Now adopted by businesses seeking a symbol of civic pride and professionalism, the Heriot tartan serves as a subtle yet potent badge of honour for those who wear it. Its subtle nuances and muted colour palette evoke a sense of respectability and tradition, while its Corporate category lends an air of modernity to this timeless design, a true relic of Scotland's rich textile past.

name: Heriot Watt University
description: The Heriot Watt University tartan, created in 1996 to commemorate the institution's 30th anniversary, is a distinctive corporate tartan that proudly reflects the university's heritage.
