Designed by Hugh MacPherson, this unique pattern combines traditional Scottish weaving techniques with modern style, making it an excellent addition to any corporate wardrobe or branding initiative. With its roots firmly planted in Scottish tradition, this tartan was carefully crafted from a tie supplied by the Development Officer of the University, ensuring an authentic connection to the institution's history. Now available for use, this tartan's registration notes highlight its significance as a commemorative design, making it a sought-after choice for those seeking to honour Heriot Watt University's legacy and values.

name: Heritage
description: The Heritage tartan is a stalwart emblem of Scottish professionalism, borne from the esteemed partnership between The Kilt Centre in Hamilton and renowned designers Mathieson/Fiddes. Originally created for corporate use, this distinctive design has become synonymous with stability, reliability, and authority, embodying the very essence of Scotland's rich heritage. Woven by skilled artisans at Strathmore Woollen Co. of Forfar and Marton Mills, the Heritage tartan seamlessly blends traditional techniques with modern flair, evoking a sense of time-honoured tradition and unwavering dedication to excellence. As a corporate tartan, it has become an indispensable symbol for organisations seeking to project a strong, dignified image, and its enduring popularity is a testament to the timeless appeal of Scotland's iconic tartans.

name: Heritage of Scotland
description: The Heritage of Scotland tartan is a masterful creation that embodies the very spirit of Scotland's rich cultural heritage. Weaved with precision by the renowned Gold Brothers, this fashion tartan has been carefully crafted to evoke the warmth and tradition of the Scottish nation. With its intricate patterns and subtle colour palette, this tartan is a testament to the skill and craftsmanship of Scottish weavers, who have passed down their techniques through generations. As a 'fashion' tartan, it is designed for modern wearers to proudly showcase their affinity with Scotland's history and culture, while also honouring the traditional textile art form that has been cherished by Scots for centuries. Despite being supplied exclusively by the Gold Brothers, this iconic design remains available to those who wish to pay tribute to the nation's heritage.

name:
Heritage Plaid
[AKA] Hilton Plaid
[AKA] Hilton Champion
description: The Heritage Plaid, a majestic corporate tartan conceived by esteemed designers at Kinloch Anderson Ltd, embodies the spirit of excellence and tradition found in Scotland's storied past. Commissioned specifically for the officials' jacket at the Hilton-sponsored Heritage Classic golf tournament, this distinctive plaid has become synonymous with prestige and sophistication. Originally christened Hilton Champion, the tartan underwent a name change to Heritage Plaid in 2000, reflecting its evolving status as a symbol of heritage and legacy. As a corporate tartan controlled by Hilton, its use is strictly regulated, adding an air of exclusivity to any organisation that chooses to adopt it. With its rich, bold colours and expertly crafted design, the Heritage Plaid proudly asserts itself as a testament to Scotland's enduring heritage and tradition.

name: Heritage Tartan; The
description: The Heritage Tartan is a majestic Corporate tartan design that embodies the spirit of unity and heritage, born from the collaboration between The Lakes Region Heritage Round Table in the USA. This distinctive pattern is part of Scotland's rich textile tradition, as proudly showcased in the esteemed Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority. Its bold colours and intricate weave evoke a sense of history and community, making it an ideal choice for corporate wear and special occasions that celebrate unity and shared values. Designed to honour the region's cultural heritage, this tartan is sure to inspire pride and camaraderie among its wearers, transcending geographical boundaries to connect people across nations through a shared appreciation of Scottish tradition.

name: Herron
description: The Herron of Ulster tartan is a distinctive and personal design, created in 2005 for James Herron of County Tyrone, Northern Ireland by Peter MacDonald. This unique tartan is a colour change on the traditional Ulster Tartan, a testament to its significance as an individual family heritage. As a "Name" tartan, it holds a special place within Scottish clan history, and its personal association with the Herron family makes it a treasured possession for those who bear the name. Although its primary purpose is not for general use, it may be worn by Ulster Herrons with permission, serving as a symbol of pride and connection to their ancestral roots in Northern Ireland. This subtle yet meaningful tartan design weaves together history, culture, and family legacy, reflecting the rich traditions of Scotland's Northern province.

name: Hersbruck (Lossiemouth) personal
description: The Lossiemouth/Hersbruck tartan is a poignant commemorative design that tells the story of 25 years of enduring twinning between these two Scottish coastal towns. Crafted by renowned milliners Johnstons of Elgin, this distinctive tartan features a rich palette of greens, purples, and blues that evoke the rugged beauty of North East Scotland's coastline. By subtly modifying the original registration notes to showcase the sett in a more graphic manner, the designers have created a visually striking design that not only pays tribute to the twinning partnership but also celebrates the local heritage of these two communities. This tartan is a testament to the power of cultural exchange and community spirit, ensuring that the memories of this special twinning relationship will be cherished for generations to come.

name: Heston [default]
description: The Heston tartan, registered by Dr Phil Smith in 1999, is a vibrant and storied design steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Initially conceived as a general tartan for the Heston name, it was later tailored to honour the esteemed Lt Col Robert J Heston - a testament to the strong family ties that bind its wearers. The intricate patterns, featuring two Y pivots replacing the original W, showcase Dr Smith's masterful weaving skills and attention to detail. While the registration notes reveal some subtle adjustments made during production, the tartan remains true to its origins, with dark blue taking on a regal quality reminiscent of Scotland's rich history. This Clan tartan is now a proud emblem for families bearing the Heston name, symbolising loyalty, heritage and the unyielding spirit of Scottish tradition.

name: Hewett
description: This exquisite, unnamed C19th christening dress tartan bears testament to the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage and tradition. Its unique pattern, taken from photographs of a 19th-century christening gown, is eerily reminiscent of the classic Caledonia tartan, a iconic design by Wilsons of Bannockburn that has captivated Scottish hearts for centuries. The origins of this particular tartan are shrouded in mystery, with its possible connection to George Robert Hewett's grandfather, who may have brought it from Scotland in the 1820s or purchased it in the USA at a later date - a tantalising thread in the complex history of this family's tartan. With its subtle variations and subtle nods to the Caledonia design, this tartan is a poignant reminder of the enduring power of Scottish textiles to evoke the past and transcend borders, waiting to be rediscovered by those drawn to the beauty and significance of its unassuming yet captivating pattern.

name: Hibernian Football Club 2004
description: The Hibernian Football Club (2004) tartan is a corporate signature worn by supporters of Edinburgh's beloved football team, showcasing their fierce loyalty and connection to the club's rich heritage. Designated as such, this distinctive tartan pattern has been officially sanctioned for commercial use, allowing it to be proudly displayed on scarves, jackets, and other merchandise by Hibernian FC's fans worldwide. Woven from a traditional Scottish sett, the colours of Lochcarron, the tartan boasts an unmistakable aesthetic that pays homage to Scotland's iconic textile traditions. Although the origins of this specific tartan are shrouded in uncertainty, its registration with McColls in 2004 provides a tangible link to the club's history, and its creation was necessitated by a matching sample provided by Aberdeen FC - adding a layer of intrigue to its provenance.

name: Hibernian Football Club
description: This iconic tartan, registered as Hibernian Football Club, embodies the spirited identity of Scotland's oldest professional football club. Designed by Dalgliesh, D C, for the corporate market, it is a vibrant representation of Celtic pride and heritage. The bold, multicoloured pattern features a rich blend of blues, greens, yellows, and whites, evoking the swirling embers of a Scottish Highland fire. This specially created tartan is prepared by Dalgliesh's own company, ensuring authenticity and precision in its weave. Notable restrictions apply, indicating that it was crafted under the watchful eye of the designer himself, guaranteeing an unmistakably distinctive character that would befit the club's storied legacy.

name: Highfield Dress
description: The Highfield Dress tartan, registered in 1982, is a stunning representation of the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage and tradition. Designed by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr for the esteemed William Paul Highfield family, this particular clan tartan has been woven with precision to reflect the history and prestige associated with its name. As one of three distinctive tartans created specifically for the Highfield family, it is reserved exclusively for use by those bearing the name or any accepted spelling variation. With its unique threadcount multiplied by two, this tartan boasts a rich, complex texture that pays homage to the traditional weaving techniques passed down through generations of Scottish artisans. As a testament to the power of family legacy and cultural identity, the Highfield Dress tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring bonds that unite those who bear its noble name.

name: Highfield Hunting
description: The Highfield Hunting tartan is a rich and evocative clan tartan, woven from threads of heritage and tradition. Designed in 1982 by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr for the esteemed William Paul Highfield family, this tartan holds significant cultural importance as a symbol of family honour and identity. With its distinctive blue, green, yellow, black, and white hues, this tartan design tells a story of a long-standing lineage, where generations have worn their history with pride. This clan tartan is applicable to all variations of the name, making it a versatile choice for those seeking a connection to their family's roots. As one of three tartans created specifically for the Highfield family, this design embodies the values of tradition and heritage that are deeply ingrained in Scottish culture, inviting wearers to draw upon a rich legacy that spans centuries.

name: Highfield [default]
description: Highfield, a stately tartan born from the esteemed William Paul Highfield family's heritage, embodies the traditions of Scottish clan identity. Registered in 1982 by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr, this distinctive pattern is an integral part of the family's history and legacy. Traditionally worn with honour and pride, Highfield tartan has been passed down through generations, weaving a rich narrative of kinship and community. With its carefully crafted colours and intricate design, this tartan pays tribute to the enduring spirit of Scottish clan tradition, serving as a symbol of heritage and belonging for those who bear the name of William Paul Highfield or its variant spellings, such as Highfeld or Hilfild.

name: Highland Cathedral
description: The Highland Cathedral tartan is a stunning example of traditional Scottish weaving, expertly crafted by the House of Edgar to bring a touch of heritage glamour to fashion. As a Fashion tartan, it was designed with style and sophistication in mind, evoking the grandeur of Scotland's majestic cathedrals and the rugged beauty of the Highland landscape. With its intricate, multicoloured pattern, this tartan is sure to add a dash of Scottish flair to any outfit, while paying tribute to the country's rich cultural heritage. As one of the many unique Fashion tartans registered by the Scottish Register of Tartans, the Highland Cathedral tartan serves as a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy in textile design, with its distinctive character and timeless appeal making it a sought-after choice for those looking to celebrate their connection to the nation.

name:
Highland District #2
[AKA] Highland Green
description: Highland Green is a vibrant corporate tartan born out of a unique collaboration between Highland Council and renowned designer Trudi Mann of Wick. Initially commissioned to commemorate the local government's change from Highland Regional Council, two competing designs were merged into one, yielding a striking visual representation that would unite men and women under a shared identity. The result is a bold, verdant pattern that echoes the rugged Scottish landscape, its distinctive hues - Highland Green (#5187) and Highland Blue (#5188) - paying homage to the region's rich heritage. Now used as a symbol of corporate solidarity, this tartan design embodies the values of community and unity, serving as a lasting testament to the enduring spirit of Highland Council and the creative vision of Trudi Mann, who brought these two colours together in perfect harmony.

name:
Highland District
[AKA] Highland Blue
description: The Highland Blue tartan, designed by Trudi Mann of Wick, embodies the enduring spirit of Scotland's storied history. As a corporate tartan, it serves as a symbol of unity and professionalism for businesses seeking to tap into Scotland's rich heritage. Its origins lie in the 2004 commission from Highland Council, where two designs were merged to create this distinctive blue hue - echoing the original Scottish Tartans Authority reference, Highland Green. This deliberate blend of traditions reflects the council's desire to forge a new identity that honours its roots while embracing modernity. Woven with precision and care, the Highland Blue tartan now proudly represents the modern corporate world, paying homage to Scotland's proud cultural legacy through a subtle yet powerful visual statement.

name: Highland Dusk
description: Kirsty Anderson's Highland Dusk tartan is a captivating fusion of traditional Scottish heritage and modern flair, perfectly capturing the essence of the Highlands' breathtaking sunsets. As a fashion tartan, its beauty lies in its versatility, making it an ideal choice for garments that embody the warmth and mystery of Scotland's rugged landscapes. With its distinctive colour palette, comprising rich blues and golden yellows, reminiscent of heather-clad hills at dusk, this tartan is an ode to the land of lochs and legends. As a design registered by Kirsty Anderson of The House of Edgar for ACS Clothing of Glasgow, Highland Dusk embodies the spirit of contemporary Scottish textile art, while remaining deeply rooted in Scotland's rich cultural heritage.

name: Highland Granite
description: The Highland Granite tartan, designed by Lochcarron of Scotland, is a stunning Fashion tartan that embodies the rugged beauty of Scotland's majestic mountains. Inspired by the imposing granite hills and mountains that stretch from Perth to Royal Deeside, this striking tartan weaves together a palette of earthy tones, evoking the sense of adventure and exploration that defines the Scottish Highlands. Originally created for those who wish to wear a kilt without a strong clan connection or prefer a unique design, Highland Granite celebrates individuality while still paying homage to Scotland's rich heritage. With its distinctive colour scheme, this tartan is perfect for anyone looking to tap into the country's timeless spirit and add a touch of authentic Scottish flair to their wardrobe.

name: Highland Hospice
description: The Highland Hospice tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage, as embodied in its vibrant blue and green hues, reminiscent of Scotland's majestic landscapes on a summer's day. This fashion tartan, registered in 1996, was meticulously crafted by Polly Wittering, renowned designer for House of Edgar Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., with Hector Russell handling the registration process. As a Fashion tartan, it is designed to evoke the warmth and generosity of Scottish hospitality, perfect for adding a touch of authentic Scottish flair to any outfit. With no restrictions on its use, this striking design invites wearers to honour Scotland's rich tradition and proudly showcase their love for the country, while supporting a noble cause - as its name so poignantly suggests.

name: Highland Park
description: Highland Park is a distinguished corporate tartan that embodies the sophistication and prestige associated with one of Scotland's finest whisky distilleries. Registered in May 1996 by Lochcarron of Scotland, specifically to reflect the iconic branding of Highland Park Distillery, this intricate design pays homage to the rich heritage of The Orkney Whisky Company. Characterised by a palette of colours inspired by the distillery's logo, this tartan is a testament to the craftsmanship and tradition that defines Scottish textiles. As an official corporate tartan, it is now available for companies seeking to establish a strong connection to Scotland and its esteemed whisky-making heritage, making it an ideal choice for those looking to add a touch of authenticity and prestige to their brand identity.

name: Highland Park High School Pipe Band
description: The Highland Park HS Pipe Band tartan is a vibrant and spirited corporate tartan, born out of the piping traditions of a Texas high school's pipe band. This distinctive design, formerly woven by Peter Anderson of Galashiels, takes inspiration from the iconic MacDonald, Lord of the Isles Hunting tartan, but with a tantalising twist: in place of the traditional green hues, the Highland Park HS Pipe Band tartan boasts a bold blue-green palette, and a striking yellow substitution for the green's characteristic intensity. This adaptation allows it to diverge effortlessly from its Thain Dress counterpart (SRT #4099), which substitutes black for blue. As a corporate tartan, this design embodies the energy and enthusiasm of Scotland's rich piping heritage, expertly distilled into a unique and eye-catching pattern that pays homage to the country's storied traditions while forging its own distinctive path.

name: Highland Pub Company
description: The Highland Pub Company tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan born from the rich heritage of Scotland's iconic pubs. Designed by Polly Wittering for House of Edgar, Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., in collaboration with Scottish & Newcastle Breweries, this vibrant tartan embodies the warm hospitality and lively spirit of the Highlands' legendary watering holes. Category-defining as a corporate tartan, it is set to adorn everything from uniforms to textiles, serving as a badge of honour for those who embody the quintessential pub culture. With its bold colours and traditional sett, the Highland Pub Company tartan pays tribute to Scotland's storied past while exuding a lively, contemporary charm that's sure to raise a glass in celebration of British hospitality.

name: Highland Sky
description: Kirsty Anderson's Highland Sky tartan is a breathtaking fusion of Scotland's elemental beauty, evoking the vast, cloud-studded skies of the Highlands on a clear summer's day. This Fashion tartan was created specifically for ACS Clothing of Glasgow, marking an exciting collaboration between heritage and contemporary style. With its subtle blue ground and delicate, gradated hues of green, yellow, and orange, Highland Sky embodies the warmth and tranquility of Scotland's iconic landscape. Despite the initial misstep in blue ground tone, this tartan remains a vibrant testament to the country's rich textile heritage, inviting wearers to tap into the wild beauty of the Scottish Highlands.

name: Highland Spring 1985
description: The Highland Spring tartan is a distinctive corporate pattern born from Scotland's rich heritage, designed by renowned weaver Peter MacDonald in 1985 for Highland Spring Water Company. This robust and earthy tartan evokes the freshness of the Scottish Highlands, where crystal-clear waters flow through the rugged landscape. As a category, Corporate, it was created to represent a company, rather than an individual clan or family, setting it apart from traditional tartans that typically bore the name and history of their bearers. With its restrictions rooted in its origins as a water company's old corporate tartan, this design has been carefully crafted to evoke the revitalising spirit of Scotland's natural springs, making it an ideal choice for businesses looking to tap into the nation's iconic identity.

name: Highland Spring 1988
description: Highland Spring, registered in 1988, is a corporate tartan designed by Peter MacDonald to represent Highland Spring Water Co., a company whose iconic label features the image of the Scottish thistle. This distinctive tartan is woven with the colours of Scotland's national emblem, paying homage to the country's rich heritage and cultural significance. As a commercial tartan, Highland Spring serves as a symbol of the brand's identity and affiliation with the natural beauty of Scotland. The subtle lightening of green in this sett allows for a clearer visual representation of the pattern, showcasing MacDonald's attention to detail. Interestingly, there appears to be some confusion surrounding the designer's identity, with Michael Peters of London also being credited, potentially due to a familial connection - however, Peter MacDonald's name is officially recorded as the creator of this unique and distinctive tartan design.

name: Highland Spring 1997
description: Highland Spring is a corporate tartan that embodies the revitalising spirit of Scotland's iconic landscapes. Originally created as a secondary design to its predecessor, this modern take on traditional Highland tartans boasts a striking green hue that echoes the majestic Scottish wilderness. By adopting a straightforward colour substitution from the original sett, designers have successfully infused the tartan with a fresh, contemporary feel, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's natural heritage. This Corporate tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish symbolism and tradition, where the essence of the Highlands – from the heather-clad moors to the glinting lochs – is distilled into a vibrant, marketable design that exudes the values of excellence, quality, and heritage.

name: Highland Spring Dress
description: The Highland Spring Dress, designed by Heather Yellowley for Highland Spring of Blackford, is a quintessential corporate tartan that embodies the spirit of Scotland's rich heritage. Registered in 2004, this striking pattern combines the iconic Cross of St Andrew with the warm, earthy tones of Perthshire's rolling hills, paying homage to the Scottish tradition that has been woven into the company's identity since its inception. As a corporate tartan, it is specifically tailored for use on bottle labelling and promotional materials, serving as a potent symbol of Highland Spring's heritage and values. The design's careful balance of bold and muted hues reflects the company's commitment to tradition and innovation, making it a fitting emblem for this Scottish brand.

name: Highland Thistle
description: The Highland Thistle Corporate tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and timeless tradition, expertly woven by Kirsty Anderson, renowned designer for House of Edgar. Registered as a corporate tartan, this distinctive pattern was specifically crafted for Jakes of London's Highlandwear Hire range, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. With its striking thistle motif at its centre, this tartan is deeply rooted in Scottish folklore and cultural significance, symbolising resilience and determination. As a corporate design, it offers a unique identity for businesses looking to connect with Scotland's storied past while maintaining a professional edge, making the Highland Thistle Corporate tartan an ideal choice for companies seeking to honour their heritage while projecting a modern, sophisticated image.

name: Highland Village
description: The Highland Village tartan, #449 in Jamie Scarlett's esteemed collection, is a captivating fashion design inspired by the traditional textiles of Scotland's ancient Highlands. Uniquely, its origins are attributed to James MacKinlay's research, compiled from notes collected by A.W. Geddes, while Fred Ullom, an Ohio-based weaver, brought this rich heritage to life in 1993 with his own interpretation, dubbing it 'Highland Village'. This distinctive tartan is classified under the Fashion category, inviting wearers to embody the spirit of Scotland's rustic beauty. While its origins are unclear, the Highland Village tartan exudes a sense of warm hospitality and community, evoking the vibrant marketplaces and cozy village life that once thrived in the Scottish Highlands.

name: Highlander Company Highland Laddie Kilts
description: The Highlander Highland Laddie tartan is a vibrant and rugged pattern, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's Highlands. Registered as a Fashion tartan, it is intended to evoke the spirit of Scotland's most iconic regions, where bravery, loyalty, and camaraderie are woven into the very fabric of tradition. Designed by W D Aichison, this distinctive tartan is born from a family business rooted in Edinburgh, where the Highland Laddie brand has been synonymous with authenticity and quality since 1997. With restrictions tied to its original branding, this tartan is reserved for those who have walked among its customers, sharing in their passion for all things Highland. By wearing this tartan, you are not only making a statement about your personal style but also paying homage to the timeless values of Scottish heritage and tradition.

name: Highlands Country Club
description: The Highlands Country Club tartan is a quintessential example of corporate design, born out of the vibrant atmosphere of a Golf Championship. Conceived by Martin Jnr and Thomas E., this striking tartan was specifically crafted to adorn the stewards and serve as a prestigious prize jacket for the winner. Its dark green weft provides a sophisticated backdrop for the intricate patterns, subtly evoking the rolling heather and rugged landscapes of Scotland's Highlands. As a corporate design, it embodies the spirit of tradition and excellence that golf embodies, while its modern twist ensures it remains relevant in today's sporting landscape. A testament to the enduring appeal of Scottish heritage, this tartan design is sure to strike a chord with those who appreciate the beauty of the land and the camaraderie of the game.

name: Highlands of Durham
description: The Highlands of Durham tartan is a vibrant celebration of Scottish heritage and Canadian spirit, bearing witness to the enduring legacy of the Highland games movement. Designed by Robbie D. Sprules in 1999, this Corporate tartan was commissioned to commemorate the Millennium, specifically to mark the founding of the Uxbridge Ontario Highland games in 1995. The intricate pattern weaves together shades of emerald green, royal blue, and heathered grey, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands and the warmth of Canadian community. As a testament to the fusion of cultures, this tartan serves as a symbol of unity and celebration, embodying the values of friendship, loyalty, and tradition that define the Highland games tradition.

name: Highlands of Haliburton Dress
description: The Highlands of Haliburton Dress tartan is a majestic representation of Scotland's rich heritage, commemorating its 50th anniversary as a tribute to the original 1963 commission by the Haliburton County Chamber of Commerce. This District Tartan, designed by Luke and Sharon, weaves together a stunning array of colours, each carefully chosen to evoke the natural beauty of the Highlands: the deep green of forest, the cerulean blue of lakes, the snowy white of winter's chill, the golden hues of autumnal splendour, and the warm earth tones of pioneer tradition. With its permission to weave subject to fibre sample authorisation due to a specific shade preference, this tartan invites wearers to tap into the region's storied history and rugged charm, while also respecting the cultural sensitivities that underpin Scotland's cherished tartan heritage.

name: Highlands School North Carolina
description: The Highlands School tartan, a testament to North Carolina's rich Scottish heritage, tells the story of a community's pride and tradition. Designed by Fellow of the Society Bob Martin, this Corporate tartan pays homage to the Highlands in North Carolina, home to the esteemed Scottish Tartans Society Museum Extension. The registration notes highlight the connection to the school colours, blue and gold, which now adorn this distinctive fabric pattern. This carefully crafted design weaves together the cultural significance of Scotland's tartan legacy with the educational institution that proudly wears it, symbolising unity and shared values between two nations separated by distance yet bound by a common heritage.

name: Hill
description: The Hill tartan is a proud representation of the esteemed name found throughout Scotland's rich heritage. Originally derived from the Angus District, this storied tartan weaves together the historical threads of generations past, particularly those based in Lambhill, Merrylee, and others bearing the Hill surname. As per its registration notes, this majestic design incorporates the distinctive blue, silver, and gold hues that adorn the arms of these noble families. By paying homage to the storied past, the Hill tartan not only honours the ancestral homes of those who bear this name but also celebrates the rich cultural tapestry of Scotland's ancient clans, forever linking its wearers to the country's profound heritage.

name: Hilton Check
description: The Hilton Check tartan is a quintessential corporate pattern with a storied history, born from the humble beginnings of Norman Hilton's clothing business. Registered by Lochcarron of Scotland in 1989, this distinctive tartan was originally created for the American arm of the company, Dalgleish. Characterised by its bold, geometric checks and rich colours, the Hilton Check is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage and entrepreneurship. As a corporate tartan, it has become synonymous with professionalism and sophistication, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to make a lasting impression through their branding and attire. Its origins may be rooted in commerce, but this tartan's significance extends far beyond its utilitarian purpose, instead symbolising the ingenuity and innovation that have come to define Scottish industry and tradition.

name: Hinnigan
description: The Hinnigan tartan is a truly personal and unique creation, woven with love by its esteemed designer, Brian Hinnigan, for the occasion of his own wedding celebration. As a Name tartan, it serves as a family heirloom, passed down through generations to signify unity and heritage. This specially commissioned design tells the story of a very special day, one that marked the union of two people bound together by love and commitment. Gardiners of Selkirk, renowned for their exceptional weaving skills, brought this vision to life with precision and care, carefully balancing bold colours and subtle nuances to create a truly distinctive and meaningful tartan that will forever hold a place in Brian's heart and his family's history.

name: Hird
description: The Hird personal tartan, designed by Fiona Hird, holds a deeply personal significance as it commemorates her wedding to Mr Blumsden. This intricate, non-reversing design is a unique blend of three checks, each bearing the names of family members James C.Hird, Kathleen E. Hird and Fiona J.Hird. The exact meaning behind this composition remains unclear, adding to the tartan's mystique. While some variations may differ from the generally accepted sett, this particular design is steeped in tradition and heritage, reflecting the Scottish passion for weaving and heritage that has been passed down through generations. As a Name tartan, it serves as a lasting tribute to Fiona Hird's connection to her family and community, making it all the more precious and meaningful.

name: Hirter Karo
description: Hirter Karo, an evocative corporate tartan inspired by the rich heritage of Austria's Carinthian region, boasts a striking colour palette reminiscent of the rolling Alpine hills and sparkling lakes that dot the landscape. Designed by Thomas Rettl for Braverei Hirt Brewery, this tartan was specifically created to reflect the company's connection to its native land, paying homage to the traditions and craftsmanship that have defined Carinthia for centuries. As a corporate tartan, Hirter Karo is suited to formal occasions, adding a touch of elegance and sophistication to any event or product, while its subtle nuances evoke the warm hospitality and rich cultural heritage of Austria's beautiful region.

name: Hislop #2
description: Hislop/Hyslop Hunting #2, a storied tartan born from the rich heritage of Clan Hislop, is an emblematic representation of tradition and family legacy. This distinctive tartan, falling under the clan category, holds deep cultural significance as a testament to the noble family's illustrious history in Scottish hunting traditions. With its unique blend of earthy tones and subtle nuances, this tartan design echoes the rugged beauty of Scotland's rolling hills and heather-covered moors. As a variation of the original Hislop design (no 2136), it is steeped in tradition and holds its place alongside other revered clan tartans within the Scottish Tartans World Register. Despite its unassuming nature, Hislop/Hyslop Hunting #2 remains an important symbol of family honour and heritage, connecting its bearers to a storied past that spans generations.

name: Hislop Hunting (Personal)
description: Hislop Hunting, a personal tartan designed by renowned textile expert Phil Smith Jr, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's rich hunting heritage. This distinctive Name tartan was created in 1994 for Gordon Hyslop, as requested, and features a striking green/black sett alongside a red sett that had earlier been commissioned. The result is a unique and captivating design that not only pays homage to Scotland's storied past but also showcases the skill and craftsmanship of its weavers. With its bold, earthy tones, Hislop Hunting tartan embodies the spirit of adventure and tradition that has long defined Scottish culture, while its personal classification ensures that it will remain an intimate and meaningful part of Gordon Hyslop's family history.

name: Historic Scotland pre 1998
description: The Historic Scotland tartan is a quintessential representation of corporate identity, steeped in tradition and rich heritage. Originally designed for the custodians at esteemed properties across Scotland, including Edinburgh Castle, this distinctive tartan has been woven with pride by D.C Dalgliesh's weaving firm in Selkirk. Its significance extends far beyond mere functionality, as it embodies the values of a nation proud of its storied past and resilient present. With its specific colour palette and intricate sett pattern, this tartan proudly wears its heritage on its sleeve, evoking images of rugged landscapes, historic landmarks, and the warm hospitality of the Scottish people. Whether worn by staff at Historic Scotland's properties or employed in corporate settings across the UK, this tartan design is a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy and its people's unwavering dedication to preserving their cultural heritage.

name: Historic Scotland
description: The Historic Scotland tartan, registered in 1998, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's rich heritage. As a corporate tartan, it was designed to represent the country's unique cultural identity and is now worn by businesses and organisations around the world who wish to honour its significance. Originally inspired by the first corporate tartan #2122, this modification has been thoughtfully updated by Chief Designer Betty Davies, with the input of Scottish Fashion International of Edinburgh and D.C. Dalgliesh, a renowned weaver. The resulting tartan is a vibrant and symbolic representation of Scotland's storied past, its people, and its traditions - an apt tribute to the nation's historical milestones and a fitting emblem for any organisation seeking to tap into its timeless appeal.

name: Hoban
description: The Hoban tartan, a personal and familial treasure, embodies the rich heritage and traditions of Scotland's most esteemed clans. This intricate design, once crafted with meticulous care by Geoffrey Highland Crafts Ltd of Edinburgh, was specifically produced for the Hoban family, a name steeped in history and honour. As a restricted tartan, its use is reserved exclusively for members of this distinguished lineage, adding to its exclusivity and prestige. With its carefully doubled threadcount, every fibre tells a story of tradition, craftsmanship, and loyalty to one's heritage. This storied tartan, now preserved for generations to come, serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring bond between family, clan, and Scottish legacy.

name: Hoben
description: The Hoben personal tartan is a distinctive and vibrant design created by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr to commemorate the identity of its namesake, JC Hoben, a skilled piper in the Sierra Highlanders Pipe Band. This unique Name tartan holds great cultural significance, as it reflects the individual's heritage and connections to Scotland, despite being set in the United States. The registration notes attest to the tartan's origins as a personal choice, with restrictions in place to ensure its exclusive use by JC Hoben. With its carefully crafted colours and precise pattern, this tartan is not only a testament to the wearer's Scottish roots but also a symbol of their dedication to the piping traditions of the Highlanders Pipe Band.

name: Hobkirk
description: The Hobkirk tartan is a quintessential example of corporate design, born from the vision of Ronnie Hek, a talented weaver from Coldstream. This distinctive tartan holds special significance as it was originally created to represent Hobkirk School in Bonchester Bridge, Roxburghshire, deep within the Scottish Borders. The school's heritage and tradition have been woven into every thread of this corporate tartan, which proudly showcases its connection to the local community. While there are no restrictions on its use, its association with a specific institution lends it an air of authenticity, making it a popular choice for businesses seeking to tap into the rich cultural fabric of Scotland's borders.

name: Hogarth [default]
description: The Hogarth of Firhill tartan is a storied and storied family heirloom, steeped in tradition and heritage. Registered by its esteemed patron, Pirie Hogarth of Firhill, in 1971 within the hallowed halls of the Lyon Court Books, this distinctive tartan pays testament to the Hogarth clan's proud history and connections to the Firhill estate. As a Clan tartan, it is bound to be worn with honour and pride by members of the Hogarth family, serving as a visible emblem of their lineage and ancestry. With its unique and intricate pattern, this tartan design has been preserved for generations, evoking the nostalgia of Scotland's rich cultural heritage and the enduring spirit of its people.

name: Hogmanay Plaid
description: The Hogmany Plaid, designed by Parklands Fabrics, is a commemorative tartan that pays tribute to the dawn of a new millennium. Registered in recognition of the birth of 'A Brand New Year' on 1st January 2000, this striking plaid pattern embodies the spirit of renewal and celebration that characterises Scotland's Hogmanay celebrations. With its vibrant colour palette and distinctive sett, this tartan is an evocative representation of the nation's enduring love affair with tradition and festive cheer. As a commemorative design, the Hogmany Plaid serves as a lasting tribute to a pivotal moment in history, forever etched in the Scottish psyche as a symbol of hope, joy, and the passing of time.

name: Hohenzollern Staff
description: The Hohenzollern Staff tartan is a fascinating relic of Scottish heritage, specifically designed for the esteemed staff at Killochan Castle, a historic residence of the German Hohenzollern family. Created by renowned designers Brian Wilton and Donatus von Hohenzollern, this intricate tartan reflects the unique blend of Scottish tradition and aristocratic European influence that defined the Hohenzollern dynasty. As a registered Clan/Family tartan, it is steeped in significance, symbolising the enduring legacy of a noble family with deep roots in Scottish history. However, due to restrictions placed by its copyright holder, Prinz Donatus von Hohenzollern, this tartan cannot be commercially reproduced or worn without explicit permission, underscoring its exclusive and private nature as a testament to the Hohenzollern family's storied past.

name: Hohenzollern [default]
description: The Hohenzollern tartan is a poignant tribute to the storied German dynasty, which once called Scotland's rugged landscape home at their Scottish stronghold, Killochan Castle. Woven with meticulous care by renowned designers Brian Wilton and Donatus von Hohenzollern, this unique tartan is an integral part of the family's heritage, symbolising a connection between two distinct cultures and lands. As a registered Clan tartan, it holds significant meaning for those who bear the Hohenzollern name, serving as a visual representation of their noble lineage and ancestral roots. Due to strict copyright restrictions, this tartan can only be worn or reproduced with explicit permission from its owner, Prinz Donatus von Hohenzollern, underscoring its sensitive nature and the importance of respecting the family's legacy.

name: Holder (Michael) personal; MacRobart
description: The MacRobart personal tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish tradition, carefully crafted by Michael Owen Holder specifically for his own family's honour. This distinctive Name tartan holds significant cultural value, as it represents the identity and history of the Robarts, who proudly bear this unique thread of their ancestry. As a family design, its purpose is not only to showcase familial ties but also to safeguard the integrity of the tartan, adhering strictly to the restrictions laid out by its creator, Holder. This thoughtful approach ensures that the MacRobart personal tartan remains an integral part of the Robarts' heritage, woven with love and devotion for generations to come.

name: Holder (Michael) personal; MacRobart Dress
description: The MacRobart Dress tartan is a timeless and storied Scottish textile, woven with love and heritage in mind. Designated as a 'Name' tartan, it serves as a proud emblem for Michael Owen Holder's esteemed clan, distinguished by the unique characteristics that reflect their noble lineage. Originally created with the intention of being worn on formal dress occasions, this tartan has been adapted for personal and family use, allowing its wearers to connect with their roots in a more intimate way. Notably registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority (STA) and The Society of Tweed and Wool Worsted Ryals (STWR), the MacRobart Dress tartan embodies the traditional craftsmanship and attention to detail that have come to define Scotland's rich textile heritage. Despite its exclusivity, this tartan is deeply sought after by those seeking to wear their clan pride with dignity and distinction.

name: Holestone
description: The Holestone tartan is a unique and proud expression of corporate heritage, born from the pioneering spirit of Viking Technology Ltd in Glasgow. This distinctive design was created to honour the Holestone Hunt of County Antrim in Ireland, a celebrated Bloodhound pack that first took to the countryside in 1989, reviving the storied title of Holestone Farmers, formed by intrepid farmers in the 1930s. The tartan's significance extends beyond its corporate roots, weaving together a rich tapestry of Irish heritage and tradition. As an important part of Ireland's hunting legacy, the Holestone tartan is a testament to the enduring values of community, camaraderie, and rural pursuits that have defined the country's countryside for generations.

name: Holiday Inn Crown Plaza
description: The Holiday Inn Crown Plaza tartan is a distinctive corporate identity that embodies the modernity and sophistication of a renowned hospitality brand. Designed by Colin Hutcheson of Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this tartan was originally created for the Scandic Crown Hotel, which later became part of the Holiday Inn Crown Plaza chain. The Corporate category highlights its intended use in business settings, where tradition meets innovation. Notably, this tartan is restricted to the exclusive use of Holiday Inn Crown Plaza, underscoring the importance of brand consistency and identity. By drawing upon Scotland's rich heritage of tartan design, Kinloch Anderson Ltd has crafted a unique and lasting visual representation of the company's values and commitment to excellence, weaving together a thread of tradition that extends beyond the hotel's walls into the hearts of its clients and staff alike.

name: Holland Dress
description: The Dutch Dress tartan is a storied District design steeped in Scottish heritage and cultural significance. Registration notes attribute its creation to John Cargill, whose proposal for a simplified colour change resulted in this distinctive sett. The tartan's connection to the Chiefs of Clan Mackay lies in Baron Aeneas Mackay's tenure as Prime Minister of the Netherlands in 1889, marking a notable episode in Scottish-Dutch relations. Its designation as a District tartan underscores its roots within a specific geographic area, in this case, likely originating from Scotland. The simple yet effective colour scheme bears testament to Cargill's ingenuity, marrying elements of both Dutch and Dutch Dress tartans in a way that pays homage to the Clan Mackay's unique history and familial connections.

name: Holman (Michael) personal
description: The Holman tartan, a deeply personal and evocative design, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish tradition. Crafted by Michael Holman, an artist from the Isle of Mull, in collaboration with John Wonnacott, this intricate pattern pays tribute to its creator's family history and legacy. Originally designated as sett no.W3653/33, it was carefully recreated from a Johnsonts of Elgin sample to bring warmth and depth to the design. As a personal tartan, it holds special significance for Michael Holman and his descendants alone, who are bound by a controlled usage agreement that ensures its protection. This distinctive pattern is a poignant reminder of the importance of preserving family traditions and the cultural heritage that shapes our identities.

name:
Holmes [default]
[AKA] Holmes Kennedy #2
description: The Holmes tartan is a family heirloom with a rich history, dating back to the early 19th century when it was first collected by Scottish textile enthusiast William Paton. This distinctive sett is thought to have been part of a larger collection of traditional Scottish patterns, which were later refined and popularised during the Victorian era. With its bold black lines intersecting a rich blue and yellow ground, the Holmes tartan exudes a sense of warmth and tradition, evoking the rugged Highlands and the proud heritage of the families who wear it. As a clan tartan, the Holmes is steeped in history and culture, with its origins tracing back to Inverness, where Margaret McDougal of the Dalgety Archives identified it as a unique and significant example of Scottish textile art. Despite some adjustments for display purposes, this traditional sett remains an important part of Scotland's rich tapestry, embodying the values of family, community, and heritage that are at the heart of tartan tradition.

name: Holyrood Chair
description: The Holyrood Chair tartan is a historic and intriguing textile pattern, evoking the rich heritage of Scotland's storied past. As one of the "Other" category tartans, its origins remain shrouded in mystery, with John MacGregor-Hastie recording its design in his notes. This 19th-century-inspired sett bears a striking resemblance to a traditional Wilson pattern, which was commonly used for chair seat covers. The reference to "chair" is likely a nod to the original purpose of this tartan, rather than a literal connection to a specific piece of furniture. Its close affinity to registration number 5969 lends further insight into its historical context, suggesting a possible link to a larger family of Scottish designs. As such, the Holyrood Chair tartan represents a fascinating glimpse into Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, with its unique characteristics and subtle echoes of tradition waiting to be uncovered by those interested in unraveling the threads of Scotland's storied heritage.

name:
Holyrood Jubilee
[AKA] Heirloom Holyrood Gold
description: The Holyrood Golden Jubilee II tartan is a poignant tribute to the enduring legacy of the British monarchy, particularly the Golden Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II in 2002. Created by renowned Scottish weaver Alistair Buchan of Lochcarron of Scotland, this commemorative tartan was specifically designed to mark this momentous occasion. As part of the UK's rich cultural heritage, this distinctive design is steeped in tradition and symbolism, evoking the majesty of Edinburgh Castle, where the Royal Family traditionally holds its official residence. With a carefully selected palette of colours, Buchan has masterfully woven together a narrative that pays homage to this special event, making this tartan an essential part of Scotland's textile heritage.

name: Home (Vestiarium Scoticum)
description: The Hume Tartan, also known as Home or Vestiarium Scoticum, is a timeless Clan tartan steeped in history and heritage. First recorded by the Scottish registration office for tartans (Vestiarium Scoticum), this traditional pattern has been passed down through generations of the distinguished Home family, whose lineage dates back to ancient times. Though differing in colour from its Grey Douglas counterpart, the Hume Tartan retains the same iconic scheme, evoking a sense of tradition and honour that resonates deeply with Scottish culture. As an integral part of clan heritage, this tartan holds significant symbolic value, connecting families to their ancestral roots and proudly proclaiming their connection to a noble line of Scots.

name: Home (Clans Originaux) (Archived)
description: The Home tartan, registered under the Clans Originaux category, embodies the rich heritage of Scottish clans with its subtle yet striking pattern. Originating from a rare 19th-century swatch book discovered in Paris, this distinctive tartan has been treasured by the Clan Home for generations. Now, held by Pendleton Mills in Portland, Oregon, where it remains an integral part of their collection, the Home tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish tradition and cultural exchange. As a Clan tartan, its significance extends beyond mere fashion, representing the history and identity of the Clan Home community and their connection to the wider world of Scottish heritage.

name: Hood [default]
description: The Hood tartan is a rare and storied pattern, its significance woven deeply into the fabric of Scottish heritage. Registered as "Other", this enigmatic tartan has been a family heirloom for over two centuries, passed down through generations in the United States. According to its registration notes, it was brought to America by Presbyterian Minister Alexander Hood, who emigrated from Scotland in 1759. The tartan has now found its way into the possession of the Tartans Museum in North Carolina, a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish culture. Its origins shrouded in mystery, this tartan is a poignant reminder of the complex history and cultural exchange between Scotland and the New World, and its significance is not only tied to its historical provenance but also to the honour of those who have worn it over the years.

name: Hope-Vere [default]
description: The Hope-Vere/Weir tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish clans, woven with threads of tradition and family pride. Registered in 1906 by William & Alexander K Johston, the esteemed experts on Scotland's clan tartans, this distinct pattern holds honour within the Weir family legacy. Specifically categorised as a Clan tartan, it is steeped in history and significance, reflecting the cultural identity of those who bear its name. The subtle nuances of its design evoke the rugged Scottish landscape, where family ties and traditions have been passed down through generations, evoking feelings of warmth and welcome. As a registered clan tartan, the Hope-Vere/Weir holds a special place in the hearts of Weirs around the world, symbolising a lasting bond to their ancestral heritage.

name: Hopetoun House Preservation Trust
description: The Hopetoun tartan is a prestigious corporate design, its rich heritage woven into the fabric of Scotland's storied history. Originating from the iconic Hopetoun House in West Lothian, this tartan proudly reflects the Marquess of Linlithgow's family colours: gold and blue. Its creation may be attributed to the Scottish Tartans Society, though the exact designer remains unknown. As a corporate tartan, the Hopetoun is licensed for use by companies and organisations seeking to evoke the elegance and sophistication associated with Scotland's noble families. With its storied past and timeless design, this tartan is a fitting choice for those seeking to add a touch of dignity and tradition to their brand or identity. Its significance extends beyond its commercial application, too, as it serves as a tangible link to Scotland's rich cultural heritage and the enduring legacy of Hopetoun House.

name: Hopkins of Wales
description: The Bute Heather, Modern is a captivating fashion tartan that embodies the timeless charm of Scotland's iconic heather moors. Designed by renowned Paisley-based firm Houston Kiltmakers, this vibrant pattern is part of a series of equally striking designs that pay homage to the majestic 'Bute Heather' blooms. By leveraging the versatility of traditional tartan design, the Bute Heather, Modern has been reimagined for modern fashionistas, its clean lines and bold colour palette infusing contemporary style with ancient Scottish heritage. Available for commercial use, this stylish pattern is an excellent choice for those seeking to add a touch of the rugged Scottish Highlands to their designs, and as part of Houston Kiltmakers' enduring legacy in Scottish tartan craftsmanship, it serves as a testament to the enduring appeal of traditional tartan design.

name: Hose
description: The Hose #2 tartan, designed by the renowned Scottish textile firm Wilsons of Bannockburn, is an emblematic example of 19th-century Scottish fashion, steeped in tradition and heritage. This fashion tartan was originally registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, cementing its place within the rich tapestry of Scotland's cultural identity. The subtle yet striking pattern, featuring a symphony of blues, greens, and yellows, is said to evoke the elegance of bygone eras. As a fashion tartan, Hose #2 has been woven into the fabric of Scottish history, adorning kilts, scarves, and other garments worn with pride by those who cherish their heritage. With its understated yet sophisticated charm, this tartan design remains a testament to Scotland's enduring spirit and tradition.

name: Hosey [default]
description: The Hosey tartan is a captivating family crest woven by Robert Boyd, a meticulous designer seeking to celebrate his own heritage and connect with those who share his surname. This clan tartan tells the story of a diasporic family's complex roots, woven from threads of Ireland, Scotland, and England. Red and blue stripes evoke the iconic colours of America, while white and blue represent Scotland, symbolising a sense of national pride and unity. In Ireland, yellow and green are intertwined, signifying a connection to the Emerald Isle. This deliberate juxtaposition of colours reflects the family's experiences of navigating multiple nations and cultures, ultimately seeking a shared identity through their Hosey name. Worn by anyone bearing the name, this tartan serves as a powerful symbol of belonging and heritage, weaving together the disparate threads of Robert Boyd's family lore into a rich tapestry of tradition and pride.

name: House of Bruar
description: The House of Bruar corporate tartan, designed by renowned Scottish textile experts at Johnstons of Elgin, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's esteemed Highland family clans. First used in 1998, but not formally registered until 2001, this distinctive tartan has become an iconic symbol of prestige and sophistication for businesses seeking to connect with the country's storied past. Named after the picturesque town in the Scottish Highlands, which sits at the confluence of the River Bruar and the Black Isle, this tartan design weaves together a palette of earthy tones and muted blues, evoking the rolling hills, rugged landscapes, and warm hospitality that are synonymous with Scotland's rural heartland. As an official corporate tartan, the House of Bruar has been carefully crafted to represent the values of tradition, community, and excellence that define this iconic Scottish family name.

name: Houston #2
description: The Houston tartan is a distinctive and enigmatic pattern, born from the collaborative efforts of John P. Houston of Batesville, Arkansas, and W. James Houston of New Zealand. Originally asymmetric in its design, it has been incorrectly assumed to be symmetrical by the Scottish Tartans Society, resulting in this erroneous yet fascinating rendition. The story behind its creation is one of cultural pride and familial identity, with the two Houstons seeking to register their tartan as a personal symbol of their heritage. Though initially rejected due to TECA's reservations over its qualification as a traditional tartan, the design was ultimately given a temporary designation as 'John Houston' - an outcome that understandably rankled the original designers. name: Hubbard Foundation of Scotland

name: Hudson Bay Company

With its unique blend of blues, reds, and greens, the tartan echoes the rugged beauty of Scotland's wilderness and the adventurous spirit of those who braved its unforgiving landscapes. As a fashion tartan, it is imbued with the values of exploration, resilience, and timeless tradition that have defined Scotland for centuries, making it a revered choice among those who draw inspiration from the country's storied past.

name: Hughes of Wales

This Clan/Family category tartan, designated by its proud bearers, is steeped in tradition and history. With no specific designer credited, the Hughes tartan's timeless design likely predates modern registration, drawing inspiration from the ancient weaving techniques of Scotland's past. The restrictions surrounding this tartan serve as a testament to its significance within the clan's family circle, ensuring that it remains an integral part of their cultural heritage and identity.

name: Hughes Interconnection Int.;
description: The Hughes Interconnection Int. tartan is a rich and meaningful family heritage, woven from the threads of tradition by renowned designer Grace Hughes. This tartan embodies the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage, where tradition meets innovation, and the beauty of a shared history is woven into every intricate pattern.

name: Humphries (Name)
description: The Humphries family tartan is a cherished emblem of Scottish heritage, woven with love and tradition by the esteemed designers Helen and Olive Humphries in 1995. name: Hungerford RFC

name: Hunnisett
description: The Hunnisett/Edinchip tartan is a rare and intimate creation, designated as a "Personal" tartan within the Scottish Tartans Authority's esteemed classification system. name: Hunt (Melanie) personal
description: The Hunt personal tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of family tradition and cultural heritage, woven with love and dedication by weaver Andrew Elliot in his esteemed workshop at Selkirk. name: Hunter 1775
description: The Hunter tartan, registered by the Scottish Tartans Authority in Canada in 2003, is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and tradition. Woven with extraordinary complexity, this hard, superfine tartan features a striking full repeat sett of eight colours, carefully arranged to create a mesmerising pattern. With an astonishing 67 colour changes, this shawl's intricate design tells the story of generations past, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands and the storied history of its clans. The subtle embroidery of 'Donnald 1775' at the shawl's end adds a poignant personal touch, highlighting the intimate connection between family, tradition, and the timeless allure of Scotland's iconic tartans.

name: Hunter Old #2
description: The 'Hunter' fashion tartan, designed by renowned Scottish textile experts at Wilsons of Bannockburn, embodies the rugged charm and timeless appeal of Scotland's great outdoors. As a fashion tartan, 'Hunter' has become an honourable addition to Scotland's rich textile heritage, evoking images of misty glens and heather-clad moors, where tradition meets modern style.

name: Hunter USA

name:
Huntly District

Its association with a diverse coalition of Highland clans, including Brodies, Forbes, Gordons, MacRaes, Munros, and Rosses, lends credence to its antiquity as a District sett. As a tangible connection to the '45 rebellion era, the Huntly tartan embodies the enduring spirit of Scotland's brave warriors, its intricate patterns a poignant reminder of a bygone era when loyalty, duty, and honour were etched into the very fabric of Highland tradition.

name: Huntly District #2
description: Huntly #3 is a classic fashion tartan that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's Highland clans. Associated with the noble House of Huntly, one of Scotland's most historic clans, this fashion tartan has been worn by generations of Scots who proudly wear their heritage on their sleeves. Its timeless elegance and understated charm have made Huntly #3 a favourite among tartan enthusiasts and designers alike, ensuring its continued popularity for years to come.

name: Huntly Gordon Gathering 2000

name: Huntly [default]

With a wealth of variation allowed for related names such as Hutchison, Hughson, MacCutcheon, and others, this tartan invites families and individuals with shared ancestry to wear their heritage with pride, while also celebrating the enduring legacy of Scottish craftsmanship and tradition.

With its intricate weave and storied provenance, Ikelman #6 embodies the proud tradition of Scottish textiles, where the careful blend of heritage and innovation yields a truly distinctive and meaningful design.

name: Impulse
description: Impulse is a vibrant fashion tartan designed by renowned Scottish textile artist Dalgliesh, D C, showcasing a modern and dynamic spirit. Though the name of its creator remains unknown, this tartan stands as a proud embodiment of Scottish tradition, inviting wearers to connect with their own heritage and tap into the deep cultural roots that define this beautiful nation.

name: Incorporation of Weavers (Glasgow)
description: The Incorporation of Weavers (Glasgow) tartan is a rich and storied design, steeped in the proud heritage of Scotland's ancient weaving tradition. Originally commissioned for the Millennium project by Maria Mackellar, this corporate tartan was woven into existence by Lochcarron of Scotland just 13 years later, in 2006. As a symbol of the Weavers' Guild of Glasgow, which dates back to at least 1514 and was formally incorporated in 1528, this tartan proudly represents the long history and charitable mission of this venerable craft. In keeping with its origins as a means of controlling standards in the weaving trade, the Incorporation of Weavers tartan is a testament to the skill and craftsmanship of Scotland's textile heritage. Threadcount from Lochcarron 2007 adds a touch of authenticity to this timeless design, ensuring that it continues to weave its way into the hearts of Scots and corporate entities alike.

name: Independence Universal
description: The 'Independence' tartan, designed by Donald Fraser in 1996, is a stirring symbol of Scotland's unwavering commitment to self-determination. Originally commissioned by New Scots for Independence, this corporate tartan was unveiled at a Scottish National Party (SNP) conference, further solidifying its connection to the country's proud political heritage. With its distinctive blue and green hues evoking the country's rugged landscapes, the 'Independence' tartan embodies Scotland's enduring spirit of autonomy and national identity. This striking design, now available for corporate use, serves as a powerful reminder of Scotland's rich cultural history and its people's unshakeable resolve to forge their own path in the world.

name: Inder
description: The Inder tartan is a vibrant and distinctive corporate tartan, carefully crafted by Brian Ernest for his eponymous family's lavender production business and their beloved visitor attraction on Tasmania's scenic shores. As the largest Lavender maze in the world beckons visitors to wander through its fragrant paths, this tartan embodies the quintessential essence of Australian charm and whimsy. Registration notes reveal that the Inder design serves as an honourable badge for a family with a passion for cultivating beauty and delighting those who seek it – and its unique lavender hue is a testament to the business's Tasmanian roots. Whether worn in corporate attire or proudly displayed at the visitor attraction, this tartan is sure to evoke the relaxed, rural spirit of Australia's southern regions, where creativity and hospitality thrive amidst lush fields of purple.

name:
Indiana State
[AKA] Cardinal
description: The Indiana 'Cardinal' tartan is a vibrant tribute to the state's beloved bird, a majestic creature that has captured the hearts of Hoosiers for generations. Registered by Jan Crook in 1992, this District tartan was carefully crafted to evoke the cardinal's distinctive plumage and rich symbolism. A natural fusion of blues, reds, and golds, reminiscent of the Indiana landscape, The Cardinal celebrates the state's unique heritage while paying homage to a cherished national symbol. Although the Indiana State Legislature ultimately declined to adopt the design in 1993, it remains an enduring testament to Jan Crook's skill as a tartan weaver and her passion for preserving traditional Scottish tartans with a distinctly American twist.

name: Indiana State #2
description: The Indiana tartan, registered with great fanfare for Hoosiers everywhere, is a vibrant celebration of Scottish heritage in the heartland of America. Designed by David McGill, International Tartans Ltd, this stunning district tartan was commissioned to pay tribute to Dr Wallace Allen Shaw, a proud native of Crawfordsville, Indiana, who wanted to share his affection for Scotland with fellow Americans. Recognised by Governor Mitch Daniels himself, this tartan is a testament to the enduring bond between the United States and Scotland, forged through the shared values of community, heritage, and tradition. With restrictions in place requiring the designer's consent, only those with a genuine connection to the State of Indiana or its people may wear this distinctive tartan, ensuring its authenticity and significance are preserved for generations to come.

name:
Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department
[AKA] Indianapolis MPD Emerald Society
description: The Indianapolis MPD Emerald Society tartan is a vibrant and unique corporate tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of Scottish tradition. Designed by Michael Kermon, this striking pattern was commissioned specifically for the Indianapolis Metropolitan Police Department's Emerald Society, an esteemed organisation that embodies the values of courage, loyalty, and service. As an official kilt tartan, this tartan is a testament to the enduring bond between Scotland and the United States, reflecting the strong ties between the two cultures. With its distinctive emerald green tones, evoking the jewel-like colour of Scotland's iconic national treasure, St Andrew's Cross, this tartan embodies the spirit of unity and solidarity that defines the Emerald Society. Its creation is a notable example of modern tartan design, drawing upon traditional techniques to produce a truly distinctive and memorable pattern.

name: Indigo Blue Corporate
description: The Indigo Blue corporate tartan, designed by Michael Quinnen for Indigo Blue Works, embodies the spirit of innovation and style that defines modern Scotland's textile heritage. Originally created to promote the UK-based denim material weaver's products in the Japanese market, this unique tartan is a testament to the versatility and adaptability of Scottish tartans. Its predominantly blue hue, reminiscent of the country's famous indigo-dyed fabrics, is punctuated by subtle nuances that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscapes. As a corporate tartan, it is designed to be worn with pride by businesses and individuals who value tradition, craftsmanship, and a connection to the land - its registration notes highlighting its origins as a specially commissioned design for international markets.

name: Ingenico
description: Ingenico, a distinctive corporate tartan designed by Rodger Moffet for Ingenico UK Ltd, embodies the innovative spirit of Fife's thriving digital hub. Registration notes reveal its origins as a bespoke design for a global EFT leader, reflecting the company's commitment to seamless financial transactions. As a corporate tartan, Ingenico is suited for use by organisations seeking a professional, modern identity. The registration notes highlight Rodger Moffet's collaboration with ScotClans, further underscoring the tartan's connection to Scotland's rich heritage of textile traditions. This vibrant design is now available for companies to proudly represent their values and expertise in the fintech sector, symbolising Ingenico UK Ltd's dedication to excellence and cutting-edge technology.

name: Inglis [default]
description: The Inglis tartan, a timeless example of Scottish heritage, holds a special place in the hearts of those bearing the name. Registration notes reveal a rich history, with the tartan also known as MacIntyre, distinguished by its subtle yet striking variations. Notably, the original design boasts a bold yellow line, setting it apart from its more subdued counterpart. Yet, for some families, an Ancient Inglis version exists, featuring lighter hues that evoke a sense of nostalgia and continuity with tradition. As a Clan tartan, the Inglis is steeped in family pride and identity, symbolising a lasting connection to Scotland's storied past, while its unique design elements ensure that each wearer stands out as a distinct part of this distinguished heritage.

name: Initial City Link
description: The Initial City Link tartan, a distinctive addition to the world of corporate wear, tells the story of modernity and urban connection. As a Category Corporate design, it embodies the values of professionalism and sophistication often associated with business attire. With its unique pattern and colour scheme, this tartan is destined for use in offices, meetings rooms, or any setting where a polished image is paramount. Although the designer's name remains unknown, their creation has undoubtedly contributed to the growing trend of using tartans in corporate environments, where a sense of honour and tradition can be woven into everyday life. Its utilitarian purpose now ensures it will remain a focal point in boardrooms and meeting rooms for years to come, symbolising the enduring appeal of traditional Scottish heritage in contemporary business culture.

name: Innes (Georgina)
description: The Innes Miniature tartan holds a special place in Scottish heritage, originating from a miniature depiction of Georgina Innes at Edingight in Moray. As part of the "Other" category, it defies traditional clan affiliations, instead embodying the spirit of an individual figure who left a lasting impression on the region. Without a designated clan link, this tartan is open to interpretation, allowing wearers to claim it as a personal connection to Scotland's rich history and cultural identity. Its origins at Edingight, a small village in Moray, add depth to its significance, evoking images of rolling hills and picturesque landscapes that shaped the life of Georgina Innes. This miniature tartan serves as a testament to the enduring power of individual stories within Scottish tradition.

name: Innes Dress Dance
description: The Innes Dress tartan is a storied family heirloom, woven from the rich tapestry of Scotland's clan history. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Society, this distinctive pattern tells the tale of the Innes family's proud heritage, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands and the warmth of Gaelic hospitality. Dating back to an era when tartan was more than just a fashion statement, but a symbol of family honour and tradition, this subtle yet striking design is steeped in the history and culture of Scotland's clansmen. As such, it is reserved exclusively for members of the Innes family lineage, serving as a poignant reminder of their ancestral roots and the enduring spirit of Scotland's tartan traditions.

name: Innes Hunting; Lyon count
description: The Innes Hunting tartan is a storied and historic clan tartan, passed down through generations with great honour. Designated as Clan/Family, this tartan holds deep significance for those who bear its threads in their heritage. Woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition, it tells the story of the Innes family's rich history and legacy. Originally recorded by Colin Innes of Tulchan, with the agreement of the Duke of Roxburghe, this threadcount is a testament to the meticulous craftsmanship and attention to detail that has defined Scottish weaving for centuries. Though its exact origins remain shrouded in mystery, with striking similarities to the Innes (Miniature) tartan, this design continues to weave its own narrative, evoking a sense of pride and connection to Scotland's storied past.

name:
Innes of Cowie [default]
[AKA] Innes of Cowie
description: The Innes of Cowie tartan is a rich and storied variation of the traditional Innes clan tartan, with its unique threadcount setting it apart from its predecessors recorded in the Lyon Court Books. This distinctive tartan holds great significance for Sir Thomas Innes of Learney's descendants, as evidenced by his own personal testimony to Scottish Tartans Society officials in 1966. Named after two of their ancestral lands, Raemoir and Cowie, this tartan is an integral part of Scotland's clan heritage, telling the story of a family's history and legacy through its carefully woven threads. As a testament to the enduring power of tradition and family identity, the Innes of Cowie tartan continues to be cherished by those who wear it with pride.

name: Innes of Learney; Hunting
description: Innes of Learney Hunting, a storied name synonymous with Scottish heritage, proudly wears its tartan legacy on its sleeve - or rather, on the fabric of history. This unique Name tartan was once worn by the esteemed Lord Innes of Learney, a past holder of the office of Lord Lyon King of Arms, an honour reserved for Scotland's highest ceremonial and administrative official. According to meticulous records, this tartan was reportedly his personal choice, carefully selected from an intricate combination of reds, browns, and whites, which subtly differ from its original counterparts in SINDEX. With a rich history etched into its fabric, Innes of Learney Hunting serves as a testament to Scotland's enduring love affair with tartanry, transcending generations and cultural traditions to evoke the warmth and pride of this storied Name.

name: Innes Red; Dress
description: The Innes Red, Dress (Dance) tartan is a captivating fusion of bold colour and intricate pattern, evoking the energy and dynamism of traditional Scottish dance. Originally designed for fashion purposes by Dalgliesh, D C in the early 20th century, this tartan's origins as a potential Dancer's Fancy suggest its roots in the lively world of Highland dancing. Characterised by a striking red dominant thread, interspersed with shades of blue and green, this tartan is sure to make a statement on any garment or textile. Notably, its registration comes with a caveat, indicating that it may be more suited to formal dancewear rather than traditional clan attire, underscoring the unique and adaptable nature of this design. As such, the Innes Red, Dress (Dance) tartan remains an exciting and modern interpretation of Scottish heritage, ready to be woven into garments that celebrate movement, tradition, and time-honoured flair.

name: Innes [default]
description: Innes, the enigmatic clan tartan, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's ancient families. This timeless design, recorded by DC Stewart in 'The Setts of the Scottish Tartans' (1950), is a testament to the ingenuity of traditional Scottish weaving. Belonging to the clan family category, Innes weaves a subtle narrative of history and identity, its 12 colours working together in harmony to evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscape. With no restrictions on its wear, this tartan invites wearers to proudly claim their heritage, while its enduring popularity is a tribute to the timeless appeal of Scottish tradition. Despite being the work of an unknown designer, Innes has become synonymous with clan pride and a deep connection to Scotland's storied past.

name: Innis Island
description: Innis, The Island of Innis, is a fashion tartan with deep roots in Scotland's storied heritage. Designed by Aljean of Vancouver, this captivating pattern is claimed to be an authentic representation of Loch Rannoch, a tranquil glen nestled in the Scottish Highlands. Registration notes from 1975 confirm its connection to the loch, lending credibility to its origins as a celebration of Scotland's rugged beauty and rich cultural traditions.
