As a fashion tartan, Innis invites wearers to embody the essence of Scotland's wild landscapes and timeless charm, making it an ideal choice for those seeking a stylish connection to the country's storied past.

name: Inspiration
description: The Inspiration tartan, crafted by Iain Stewart, is a vibrant and poignant creation born from the desire to unite people across cultures and backgrounds in pursuit of peace. This Fashion tartan tells a story of resilience and hope, with its rich red hues evoking the sacrifices made for a better world, while the celestial blue above echoes the majesty of Scotland's skies. The earthy tones of green represent the majestic mountains that cradle this land, serving as a powerful symbol of strength and endurance. Meanwhile, the interlocking black and white threads weave together to celebrate our shared humanity, reflecting the diversity of cultures and faiths that form a rich tapestry of global society. Finally, the bright yellow thread shines like a beacon, illuminating the spark of inspiration that ignites within each individual, a powerful reminder that even in darkness, light can emerge to shape a brighter future.

name: Intergen
description: The Intergen tartan, created by renowned Scottish textile firm Lochcarron of Scotland, is a striking example of corporate branding in traditional tartan form. As a Category Corporate tartan, it was designed to evoke a sense of professionalism and modernity, making it an ideal choice for businesses seeking to establish a strong visual identity. With its bold and vibrant colours, the Intergen tartan is sure to make a lasting impression on any organisation's branding or marketing materials. Not limited by traditional clan or family associations, this tartan is free to be worn and displayed by anyone who wishes to represent their corporate values with pride, its unique design free from restrictions, making it an exciting choice for businesses looking to forge a new path in Scottish heritage-inspired brand identity.

name: International College of Dentists Canadian Section
description: MacLean #2, also known as MacLean of Duart, is a timeless Clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1819, this iconic pattern has been woven with precision and honour to reflect the proud history of the MacLeans of Duart. According to the registration notes, this particular design was first described as featuring a grey central stripe, adding an air of mystery and subtlety to its classic black, blue, green, yellow, red, and black sett. As a Clan tartan, MacLean #2 is not only a symbol of family pride but also a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's storied clans. When worn with honour, this tartan design invites wearer and observer alike to tap into the proud history and traditions of the MacLeans, while its subtle nuances continue to captivate those seeking a deeper connection to their Scottish roots.

name: International Federation of Freight Forwarders Associations
description: The F.I.A.T.A. Congress of 1990 tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of collaboration and unity in Scotland's corporate heritage. Registered as a Corporate tartan, this distinctive weave was specifically designed for business and organisational use, evoking the values of cooperation and shared purpose. Created by renowned designer Ingles Buchan, this tartan bears the scars of its 1994 thread count estimate, with Bill Johnston's keen eye having initially observed the subtle texture of Ingles' craftsmanship. With no restrictions on its use, the F.I.A.T.A. Congress of 1990 tartan is free to be worn with pride by companies and individuals alike, symbolising a commitment to collective achievement and the strong bonds forged through Scottish tradition and ingenuity.

name: International Police Association
description: The International Police Association tartan, expertly woven by Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts, pays homage to the global community of law enforcement officers who come together under its esteemed banner. This corporate tartan was carefully selected to incorporate the iconic colours of the organisation's logo, symbolising unity and solidarity among police forces worldwide. As a registered design, it holds significant cultural and historical value, representing the collaboration between local kiltmakers and the Lothian & Borders branch of the International Police Association. Although its production is controlled by this regional branch, the tartan can be worn by members of the International Police Association globally, serving as a badge of honour and pride for those who serve on behalf of the association.

name: Inverary
description: The Inverary tartan, designated as a District pattern, is a rich tapestry that pays homage to the historic township of Inverary in Ontario's heartland. This unique tartan was carefully crafted to evoke the region's heritage and identity, reflecting the strong Scottish roots that have shaped the area's history. As a District pattern, it is intended for use by residents and organisations connected to the township, fostering a sense of community pride and belonging. Registration notes confirm its design was specifically created to honour the Inverary township, underscoring the importance of preserving and celebrating local traditions through this distinctive tartan.

name:
Inverness District
[AKA] Inverness Earl of Inverness
[AKA] Inverness Princess Elizabeth #3
description: The Inverness, Earl of tartan is a richly woven symbol of Scotland's proud heritage, originating from the 19th century for Augustus Frederick, Duke of Sussex and Earl of Inverness. Created by Wilsons of Bannockburn, this District tartan was meticulously crafted to reflect the territorial designation that gave its name, serving as a powerful emblem of the town and county of Inverness. With its distinctive white stripe, sometimes rendered in sunshine yellow, this tartan pays homage to Scotland's storied past and the region's historical significance. As Logan's seminal work 'The Scottish Gael' demonstrates, this Royal tartan has been immortalised through the ages, a testament to the enduring legacy of the Inverness clan and their connection to the land that bore their noble title.

name:
Inverness Hunting
[AKA] Inverness Duke of York #2
description: The Inverness Hunting tartan, a storied District tartan from Scotland's rich heritage, pays homage to the noble legacy of its namesake, Francis, Duke of York, who held dual titles as Earl of Inverness. This distinctive tartan weaves together elements of Scottish tradition and history, reflecting the county's proud connections to the British royal family. As a District tartan, it is reserved for specific geographic areas, in this case, the region surrounding Inverness, a city steeped in ancient Celtic culture and storied past. The 'Inverness Hunting' name serves as a testament to the area's historical hunting traditions, where brave gentry once roamed the Scottish wilderness. With its intricate blend of earthy tones and rich colours, this tartan design embodies the enduring spirit of Scotland's Highland counties and their storied legacy.

name: Inverness Caledonian Thistle Football Club
description: This distinctive corporate tartan, officially registered in 1996, is a proud symbol of Inverness Caledonian Thistle Football Club's identity. Woven by the skilled hands of Polly Wittering at House of Edgar, Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this vibrant design embodies the values and heritage of Scotland's third-tier football club. As a Category Corporate tartan, it is specifically designed for business and corporate wear, making it an attractive choice for companies or individuals looking to connect with the club's rich history and loyal supporter base. With its unique blend of blues, greens, and yellows, this tartan pays homage to Scotland's natural beauty and the thistle, a national emblem that represents courage and resilience - qualities cherished by the Caledonian Thistle FC community alike.

name: Inverness County Canada
description: The Inverness County (Canada) tartan is a vibrant representation of unity and diversity, born from the imagination of Verna MacMillan, its ingenious designer. This District category tartan serves as a powerful symbol for Inverness County's people, transcending racial and linguistic boundaries to unite all citizens under one shared heritage. The intricate design tells a story of the county's rich history and cultural identity, with each carefully chosen colour holding significance in MacMillan's poetic explanation, now preserved in the Scottish Tartans Authority's archives. Weaved with skill by its creator herself, this tartan embodies the spirit of community and resilience that defines Nova Scotia's Inverness County, inviting wearers to proudly bear a badge of honour that celebrates their shared roots.

name: Investors Group
description: The Investors Group tartan is a distinguished corporate motif, carefully crafted by Kinloch Anderson Ltd to reflect the esteemed reputation of its Canadian client, Investors Group Inc. This striking tartan was specifically designed for the company's attendance at a conference in Scotland in May/June 2005, marking a pivotal moment in their international expansion. As a testament to Scottish heritage and tradition, the Investors Group tartan is a unique blend of colours, meticulously woven to convey the values of personal financial planning and expertise that define the organisation. With its origins rooted in corporate identity, this tartan holds great significance for Investors Group Inc, serving as a lasting symbol of their commitment to excellence and professionalism, while also proudly showcasing Scotland's rich textile traditions.

name: Iona
description: The Iona tartan, designed by the renowned West Coast Woolen Mill, is a captivating fashion-inspired pattern that embodies the spirit of Scotland's western coast. This distinctive tartan features a striking gold warp threading that gives way to a rich green ground colour, subtly revealed through the fabric's weave. With its subtle yet nuanced palette, the Iona tartan evokes the mystical beauty of the island of Iona, a sacred site steeped in Scottish heritage and history. As a fashion tartan, it offers a modern take on traditional craftsmanship, perfect for those seeking to add a touch of effortless elegance to their wardrobe. Despite its stylish appeal, no specific clan or family connections are attributed to this design, leaving its adoption open to all who appreciate the timeless charm of Scottish textiles.

name: Iowa Dress
description: The Iowa Dress tartan is a distinctive District tartan that proudly represents the heritage of Iowans with Scottish and Scots-Irish roots. Registration notes reveal the rich history of Scottish influence in Iowa's founding, which has shaped the state's identity and culture. This tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the pioneers who settled in the region, who brought with them their traditions, values, and textiles. Designed by Mark Osweiler, this tartan is a celebration of Iowans' contributions to various fields, from science and industry to literature and politics, reflecting the state's strong heritage of innovation and progress. With its unique colours and patterns, the Iowa Dress tartan serves as a symbol of unity and pride for the people of Iowa, weaving together their Scottish ancestry with their American identity.

name: Iowa
description: The Iowa tartan is a vibrant tribute to the state's rich Scottish heritage, woven into its very fabric by Mark Osweiler. Designed as a District tartan, this distinctive pattern is steeped in history, reflecting the significant Scottish influence on Iowa's founding and the countless contributions of Iowans with Scottish and Scots-Irish roots in fields such as science, industry, literature, politics, exploration, and conservation. This tartan proudly wears its heritage on its sleeve, symbolising the pioneering spirit and leadership embodied by Iowans who have shaped the state's story. With each intricate thread, the Iowa tartan tells a tale of community, resilience, and tradition, weaving together the threads of Scottish heritage and Midwestern Americana to create a truly unique and meaningful design that honours the state's proud identity.

name: Irish American
description: The Irish American tartan, crafted by Viking Technology Ltd, is a vibrant fusion of heritage and fashion, evoking the spirited blend of Scottish and Irish traditions. Originally part of a set designed in 2003 to commemorate the rich history of Irish counties and national identity, this tartan now bears witness to the intricate web of cultural exchange and artistic collaboration that has defined Ireland's relationship with Scotland for centuries. As one of the esteemed Irish County and National tartans, its distinctive pattern pays homage to the Emerald Isle's storied past while adapting to the evolving tastes of modern fashion. Although restrictions prevent its reproduction without permission from USA Kilts Inc., this stunning tartan remains a testament to the enduring power of intercultural exchange in the world of Scottish textiles.

name: Irish Diaspora
description: The Irish Diaspora tartan is a vibrant, fashion-forward pattern that celebrates the heritage of those with Irish roots, both in Ireland and abroad. Designed by Erica Randall at The House of Edgar in Perth for Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this striking tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Irish diaspora communities worldwide. Characterised by its asymmetrical design, the Irish Diaspora features central stripes that echo the colours of the Republic of Ireland flag, paying homage to the country's rich history and cultural identity. This distinctive pattern is not only a stylish statement but also a heartfelt tribute to the Irish connection, inviting wearers to proudly showcase their ancestry through this unique and meaningful tartan.

name: Irish National
description: The Irish National tartan, created by the renowned fashion house House of Edgar in collaboration with Scottish heritage experts John and Joan Nisbet, embodies the vibrant spirit of Ireland's rich cultural heritage. As a Fashion tartan, it is designed to add a touch of Emerald Isle flair to clothing and accessories, celebrating the country's storied history and mythical landscapes. Though restricted by copyright holder Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this iconic tartan remains available for licencing to those who wish to pay homage to Ireland's proud heritage, ensuring its enduring appeal in Scottish textile traditions. As a nod to the Nisbets' dedication to preserving Celtic knowledge, the Irish National tartan represents a beautiful fusion of innovative design and time-honoured craftsmanship, evoking the warmth and hospitality that has long defined Ireland's welcoming nation.

name: Irn Bru
description: The Irn Bru tartan is a vibrant and iconic corporate design, expertly crafted by Kinloch Anderson Ltd to represent Barr's beloved soft drink. Originally designed as the Barr tartan in 1969, it was later reworked and renamed in 1997 to reflect the brand's distinctive identity. This striking design takes its cue from the Earl of St Andrews tartan, paying homage to Andrew Greig Barr's legacy, who brought the company to life in 1904. The bold orange and blue colours are instantly recognisable as the brand's signature hues, evoking a sense of warmth and energy reminiscent of Scotland's own 'Iron Brew'. With its distinctive character and limited availability, this tartan is now coveted by enthusiasts and corporate clients alike, offering a unique way to showcase Scottish heritage and corporate flair.

name: Ironside
description: The Ironside tartan is a privately registered Name tartan, carefully woven to commemorate the Golden Wedding Anniversary of John T. and Frances A. Ironside, a farming family from Methlick, Aberdeenshire. This richly textured design, named in honour of the couple's enduring love, holds significant cultural value, connecting families across generations to their ancestral roots. The restrictions placed upon this tartan serve as a poignant reminder of its intimate connection to the Ironside family's personal history and heritage, highlighting the importance of preserving traditional patterns for cherished moments and special occasions. Though not officially designated with a clan affiliation, the Ironside tartan remains an authentic representation of Scottish tradition, carefully crafted to be passed down through the generations, preserving a lasting legacy within the Ironside family.

name: Iroquois Falls Centenary
description: The Iroquois Falls Centenary tartan is a poignant commemoration of the community's founding in 2012, woven with deep respect for its natural surroundings. Designed by Marilyn Chircoski, Fran Côté, and Helen Deneault, this tartan pays tribute to the Boreal Forest's majestic trees, the endless skies of Northern Ontario, the snow-kissed winters, and the rich claybelt soil that nourishes the community. The carefully chosen palette reflects the land's essence: two shades of green symbolise the forest's verdant canopy, while two shades of blue evoke the northern sky and numerous lakes that dot the landscape. With its thoughtful design and connection to the community, this tartan serves as a meaningful honour to Iroquois Falls' heritage, accessible only to those who share a personal bond with this unique Canadian town, thus preserving its cultural significance for generations to come.

name: Irvine [default]
description: The Irvine of Drum tartan is a revered clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, its origins dating back to 1858 when Peter MacArthur & Co Ltd of Glasgow created it at the request of Major Irvine, a member of the sept of Forbes. This distinctive tartan combines hues reminiscent of the Forbes family crest with a rich, earthy palette that evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscapes. As an Irvine tartan, it carries the weight of history and tradition, symbolising the identity and honour of those who wear it. With its unique sett and carefully chosen colours, this tartan is a testament to the skill of Scottish weavers and the enduring legacy of the Irvine clan, whose name has been woven into the very fabric of Scotland's cultural heritage.

name:
Irvine of Bonshaw [default]
[AKA] Irvine of Bonshaw
description: The Irving of Bonshaw tartan is a rich and storied weave that proudly wears its heritage on its sleeve, embodying the traditions of the esteemed Clan Irving and their ancestral lands of Bonshaw in the Scottish Borders. Recognised by Captain R.A.S. Irving RN as the official tartan of his clan, this distinctive design has been carefully crafted by the Scottish Tartans Society to preserve the intricate history and legacy of the Irvings and related families. With a deep respect for tradition, this tartan is an honour to wear, signifying family ties, ancestral heritage, and a strong sense of identity that spans generations. Its distinctive colour palette and precise weaving reflect the meticulous attention to detail that has come to define Scottish tartanry, ensuring that this cherished design remains a treasured symbol of clan pride for years to come.

name: Irvine of Bonshaw Tower
description: The Irving of Bonshaw Tower tartan is a distinctive and intimate design, born from the personal taste of its creator, Dr. J. Bruce Irving. This Name tartan holds significance as a variation of the Irvine tartan, #733, reflecting a desire to establish one's own unique identity separate from familial or clan affiliations. With its carefully chosen colour palette, this tartan is intended for personal use only and should not be confused with the Clan tartan 'Irving of Bonshaw' #2609, which bears a different heritage and historical context. As a Personal tartan, the Irving of Bonshaw Tower design allows its wearer to embody their individuality within the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage and tradition, reflecting a deep connection to the land, culture, and history that has inspired so many iconic tartans throughout the years.

name:
Irvine of Glentulchan
[AKA] Irvine of Tulchan
description: The Irving of Glentulchan tartan, designed by Peter MacDonald for John Irvine of Tulchan, is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and family traditions. Originally based on the ancient Irving sett with modifications, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the long-standing association between the Irvine family and their Scottish roots, specifically in the Border area. The addition of a red stripe over the green, inspired by Mrs Irvine's maiden name, Malcolm, adds a touching personal touch to the design. As a Name tartan, it is a symbol of family pride and identity, reflecting the history and culture that has shaped the Irvine family's connection to Scotland. This unique and meaningful tartan serves as a lasting tribute to the enduring bond between Scottish families and their ancestral heritage.

name: Isla Grant
description: The Isla Grant tartan is a vibrant and distinctive name tartan, carefully crafted by Lochcarron of Scotland in 1996 to commemorate the esteemed Scottish singer-songwriter. This unique tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Isla Grant, whose platinum-selling albums have captured the hearts of fans worldwide. Originally designed for her personal use, the tartan now serves as a symbol of her artistic heritage and connection to her Scottish roots. With its bold, rich colours evoking the rugged landscapes and warm spirit of Scotland, this name tartan is a fitting tribute to Isla Grant's remarkable success and enduring influence in the music industry. As a registered name tartan, it holds special significance for fans of Isla Grant, who can now proudly wear their love for her heritage on their sleeve, or rather, on their scarf or tie.

name: Islay
description: The Islay fashion tartan, designed by the esteemed Edinburgh Woollen Mill, embodies the rugged beauty and warmth of the island of Islay, situated off Scotland's west coast. This striking design is categorised as a Fashion tartan, indicating its versatility in being used across a range of clothing items and textiles. With its rich history rooted in traditional Scottish weaving, the Islay tartan showcases the artistry of Scotland's textile heritage. The registration notes reveal that this distinctive pattern has been preserved for posterity by the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, ensuring its enduring legacy for generations to come. This iconic tartan is a testament to the island's unique spirit and cultural identity, making it a staple in any fashion enthusiast's wardrobe or collector's library.

name: Islay Whisky Club
description: The Islay Whisky Club tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan, carefully crafted by Linda van Weenen to reflect the exclusive heritage of its namesake organisation. Designated solely for the members of the Islay Whisky Club, this unique tartan embodies the spirit of camaraderie and conviviality that defines this prestigious group. By incorporating traditional Scottish weaving techniques with modern design sensibilities, Van Weenen has created a visually striking pattern that pays homage to Scotland's rich whisky-making traditions. The tartan's restricted registration ensures that it remains an integral part of the club's identity, while its corporate classification means it can be worn and displayed by members and supporters alike in a manner that proudly honours Islay's storied past and present.

name: Isle of Arran #2
description: The Isle of Arran (Personal) tartan is a distinctive and intimate weave, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's most westerly island. This Name tartan, designed by renowned weavers at Lawson's Kilt Shop, holds great sentimental value as it was originally commissioned for an individual who displayed a swatch at their shop on George IV Bridge in Edinburgh back in 1977. The resulting pattern is a beautiful representation of the island's rugged beauty and unique character, with subtle nuances that evoke the dramatic landscapes and rolling hills that dot its scenic coastline. As a Personal tartan, it remains a cherished family heirloom, passed down through generations, and its distinctive threads serve as a tangible connection to Scotland's storied past.

name: Isle of Arran
description: The Arran, Isle of (Lochcarron) tartan is a timeless and majestic fashion tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's picturesque island of Arran. Woven with precision by Lochcarron of Scotland, this iconic pattern has been cherished for generations as a symbol of Scottish tradition and cultural identity. As a fashion tartan, it evokes images of rugged coastline, heather-covered moors, and crystal-clear lochs - the quintessential Scottish landscape that inspired its creation. With no restrictions on its use, the Arran tartan is free to be worn with pride by anyone who wishes to connect with Scotland's storied past and add a touch of rugged elegance to their wardrobe.

name: Isle of Gigha
description: The Galway County, Crest Range tartan is a striking representation of Ireland's rich heritage, carefully crafted by Viking Technology Limited (now Tartan Web Scotland Ltd) to evoke the spirit of the Emerald Isle. As one of a series of Irish County tartans, this unique pattern pays homage to Galway's distinct identity and cultural traditions. Its distinctive colour palette, comprising blues, greens, and golden hues, is reminiscent of the rugged coastlines and rolling hills that cradle the city of Galway. However, its registration notes reveal a more complex story: due to ownership transfer to USA Kilts Inc in 2012, this tartan's use is now subject to strict permissions, underscoring the importance of respecting Ireland's cultural heritage through responsible reproduction and use.

name: Isle of Harris
description: The Isle of Harris tartan is a vibrant representation of the island's rich heritage, woven by a talented group of young entrepreneurs from Sir E Scott School at Tarbert. Registered as part of the Young Enterprise Scotland Company Programme, this District tartan embodies the spirit of community and innovation that defines the island's 6th year pupils. Beartas, the designer collective behind this distinctive design, drew upon their shared passion for preserving local traditions and promoting the Isle of Harris brand. The Isle of Harris tartan is now a proud symbol of Scottish heritage, reflecting the island's stunning natural beauty, its strong community ties, and the creativity of its young people.

name: Isle of Man Manx #2
description: The Isle of Man tartan is a storied and complex design steeped in the rich heritage of the Celtic island's unique cultural identity. Registered as a District tartan, this distinctive pattern reflects the island's distinctiveness within the UK, its own brand of Scottish tradition. Designed by Richard T Moore, owner of Tynwald Woollen Mills, this tartan was originally intended to be the Manx National tartan but took on a life of its own after a disagreement with Miss McQuaid, leading to an innovative reinterpretation of the original design. This tartan's intricate weave of blues and greens echoes the island's rugged coastline and fertile pastures, while its nuanced tones hint at the subtle nuances of Manx folklore and tradition, creating a fabric that is as much a reflection of its wearer as it is of the island itself.

name:
Isle of Man Manx Centenary
[AKA] Laxey Centenary #2
description: The Manx Centenary tartan is a vibrant celebration of the Isle of Man's rich textile heritage, commemorating the centenary of the St George's Woollen Mill in Laxey village. Commissioned by Robert Wood, this fashion tartan weaves together traditional colours and motifs to pay tribute to the island's historic weaving industry. The predominantly grey flannel represents the original fibre produced at the mill, while subtle accents of blue and green nod to the iconic Manx Laxey tartan, a testament to the island's enduring cultural identity. With its striking palette and meaningful allusions to Manx history, this tartan design serves as a fitting tribute to the Isle of Man's proud textile traditions, inviting wearers to connect with the island's unique heritage and sense of community.

name: Manx Cornaa, Isle of Man (Personal)
description: Manx Cornaa is a unique and evocative tartan design, steeped in the rich cultural heritage of the Isle of Man. Registration notes reveal that its name pays tribute to Dr D.G. Teall's residence on the island, "Cornaa", which adds a personal touch to this distinctive pattern. As a Category Other design, Manx Cornaa does not adhere to the traditional clan or family associations found in other tartans. Instead, it stands as a standalone statement of individuality and connection to the island's unique identity. Dr Teall's inspiration is evident in every thread, weaving together the threads of tradition and personal heritage to create a truly distinctive design that proudly wears its Manx roots on its sleeve.

name: Isle of Man Manx Dress
description: The Manx Dress tartan, a fashion statement steeped in the rich heritage of the Isle of Man, holds a special place in the annals of Scottish textiles. Created by an anonymous designer who was deeply familiar with the island's unique culture, this distinctive pattern has been presented to the Scottish Tartans Society by Dr.D.G.Teall, a former Past President who had a profound affinity for the island's traditions. The Manx Dress tartan is an important representation of the Isle of Man's distinct identity, reflecting its rich history and traditions that have been woven into the fabric of this striking design. Its classification as a fashion tartan speaks to its intended use in modern attire, while Dr Teall's connection to the island lends an added layer of authenticity and cultural significance to this beautiful textile pattern.

name: Isle of Man Manx Ellan Vannin
description: The Manx Ellan Vannin fashion tartan, bearing its distinctive registration notes, tells the story of an island identity woven into fabric. Contrary to its name's supposed connection to the Manx National tartan, Ellan Vannin stands on its own as a unique and captivating design. Its complex interplay of colours - predominantly blue, black, green, yellow, orange, red, and white - creates a visually striking pattern that echoes the rugged beauty of the Isle of Man's landscapes. As a fashion tartan, it is open to interpretation, inviting wearers to embody the spirit of this enchanting island in their personal style. With no specific designer credited, its origins remain a mystery, yet its significance as a vibrant representation of Manx heritage is undeniable.

name: Isle of Man Manx Heritage
description: The Manx Heritage tartan is a poignant tribute to the Isle of Man's rich history and culture, crafted with reverence for the island's unique heritage. As a Corporate tartan, it serves as a unifying symbol for businesses and organisations seeking to connect with the island's proud traditions. Registration notes reveal that this distinctive design was created in 1998 by the Manx Museum, a fitting honouring of the island's storied past. The tartan's existence is deeply rooted in its purpose: to promote and commemorate the island's heritage, making it an essential part of the island's identity fabric.

name: Isle of Man Manx Hunting
description: The Manx Hunting tartan is a stunning fashion design inspired by the rugged beauty of the Isle of Man, situated in the heart of the Irish Sea. Registration notes reveal that this striking pattern was co-created by Kelly/Teall after an agreement between Mr C Ewan Kelly and Dr Gordon Teall, with input from Lochcarron of Galashiels, who first wove it. Characterised by a palette of muted colours evoking the island's landscape - dark grey for the rocky shoreline, grey green for its valleys and hills, clear blue for the sky above, grey blue for the sea around the shores, bright gold for the blooming cushag flowers, and pure white for the mist that lingers over the land. This unique design not only reflects the island's natural heritage but also pays homage to its rich cultural history, making it a treasured addition to any fashion or accessory collection inspired by Scottish heritage.

name:
Isle of Man Manx Laxey; Blue
[AKA] Laxey Manx
description: The Manx Laxey Blue is a vibrant and distinctive fashion tartan, born from the creative vision of Robert Wood, proprietor of St George's Woollen Mill in the picturesque village of Laxey on the Isle of Man. This bold blue tartan is steeped in Manx heritage, reflecting the island's unique cultural identity and rich history. As a fashion category design, it is intended for garments and accessories that pay tribute to this captivating isle, evoking the rugged beauty and warm hospitality of the Manx people. With its restricted registration notes, this tartan is imbued with a sense of tradition and authenticity, ensuring that only true enthusiasts of Manx heritage can wear it with pride, supporting local businesses like St George's Woollen Mill where it was originally woven.

name: Isle of Man Manx Laxey; Dress Green
description: The Manx Laxey Dress Green is a captivating District tartan, meticulously woven to reflect the rich heritage of the Isle of Man's picturesque landscape. Designed by renowned textile expert Dr D.G. Teall in 1981, this unique tartan holds an intriguing air of experimentation, as noted by the Scottish Tartans Society. According to Dr Teall, a Past President of the society, this tartan pays homage to the island's Laxey area, its intricate patterns woven to evoke the natural beauty and distinct character of this Manx district. As a District tartan, it is worn to signify regional identity, and its distinctive colour palette and subtle nuances are a testament to Dr Teall's skill as a weaver and designer, breathing life into the fabric of Manx tradition.

name: Isle of Man Manx Laxey; Red
description: The Manx Laxey (Red) tartan is a vibrant and evocative pattern born from the rugged beauty of the Isle of Man, a self-governing British Crown dependency in the Irish Sea. As a fashion category tartan, it embodies the modern spirit of this Celtic gem, perfect for those who draw inspiration from its rich heritage and unique cultural identity. Inspired by the island's industrial past, particularly the Laxey Wheel, a historic water-powered sawmill, this bold red tartan pays homage to the Isle of Man's remarkable history and industrial prowess. Registration notes reveal the intricate connections between the design and Dr D.G.Teall, a stalwart advocate for Scottish tartans who had a personal connection to the island, lending an air of authenticity to this stunning fabric pattern.

name: Isle of Man Manx National
description: The Manx National Tartan, masterfully woven by Miss Patricia McQuaid, is a vibrant tribute to the natural beauty and heritage of the Isle of Man, an island nation nestled in the Irish Sea. This seven-colour District tartan was commissioned by Lord Sempill, who sought to create a distinctive pattern that would represent his connection to this enchanting island. The Manx National Tartan's colours, painstakingly chosen by McQuaid, evoke the Island's diverse landscapes: the cerulean sky and dark sea meet the emerald hills and valleys, while white cottages, purple heather, and golden gorse add warmth and depth. The tartan also features a striking red hue, reminiscent of fuchsia flowers that bloom on the island's fertile soil. This stunning design not only pays homage to Manx history and culture but also serves as a lasting symbol of community pride for those who bear it, reminding them of their roots in this captivating Celtic isle.

name: Isle of Man Manx [default]
description: The Man, Isle of tartan is a storied District tartan, woven with reverence for its eponymous origins on the rugged Scottish Isle. Designed by Richard T Moore in all its intricate complexity, this traditional tartan pays homage to the island's unique cultural heritage, reflecting the traditions and community that have long called it home. Recognised as a vital part of Scotland's rich tapestry, the Man, Isle of tartan is steeped in history, worn with pride by those who claim connection to its storied past. As an official District tartan, it holds a special place in Scottish tradition, imbued with meaning and significance for those whose families have long cherished this unique design, woven from threads of local identity, community spirit, and the unyielding resilience of island life.

name:
Isle of Mull
[AKA] Mull Millennium #2
description: The Mull Millennium tartan is a stunning commemorative design inspired by the geological wonders of the Isle of Mull, Scotland's westernmost island. Created by esteemed designers Rosalind Jones and Peter MacDonald, this unique tartan weaves together the natural attributes of the island, featuring a striking 'map' of Mull's rich history etched into its distinctive rock colours. Representing the island's diverse landscapes, from Fionnphort to Glen More, the tartan boasts five carefully chosen hues: pink Caledonian Ross granite, grey Moine schist, yellow ring dyke, black Tertiary basalt lava flows, and dark green dolerites and gabbros. This commemorative design not only celebrates Mull's natural beauty but also supports its charitable projects, with proceeds going to support local causes at the Earth Galleries, Natural History Museum, London.

name: Isle of Skye Blue; Dress
description: The Skye Dress Blue, Isle of (Dance) tartan is a captivating Fashion tartan that embodies the rugged beauty of Scotland's iconic Isle of Skye. Designed by renowned weaver Dalgliesh, D.C, this distinctive tartan was originally intended for dance costumes, hence its 'Dance' designation. Its vibrant blue and white hues evoke the majestic landscapes and sparkling lochs of the island, where the gentle lapping of waves against the shore seems to be woven into every thread of the fabric. Notably, however, it has often been confused with the Earl of Skye tartan, a distinction that is now clarified through its Registration Notes, which serve as a testament to the importance of preserving Scotland's rich cultural heritage. With restrictions in place to ensure its exclusive use, this beautiful tartan remains a cherished symbol of the Isle of Skye's enduring spirit and connection to Scottish tradition.

name: Isle of Skye
description: The Skye, Isle of tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's northernmost district, evoking the rugged beauty and timeless charm of the Island of Skye. As a District tartan, it bears the distinction of representing a specific geographic area, in this case, the island itself. This variation of the Stewart clan tartan boasts a distinctive blue and green colour palette, with subtle nuances that reflect the shifting moods of Scotland's iconic sea and sky. The sett, agreed upon by both the original JCT files from 1984 and the Edinburgh Woollen Mill swatches, features a yellow pivot, adding a touch of warmth to this already striking design. This tartan is a proud embodiment of Scottish tradition and identity, woven with the care and expertise of Edinburgh Woollen Mill and steeped in history as a Stewart clan variation, making it a treasured addition to any collection of traditional tartans.

name: J & B Whisky (Original)
description: The J & B Whisky Corporate tartan is an evocative tribute to Scotland's rich whisky heritage, with its distinctive blue and green hues echoing the country's misty Highlands and rugged coastline. Woven by Kynoch of Keith in Scotland for esteemed wine and spirit merchants Justerini & Brooks, this tartan design has become a symbol of sophistication and elegance in corporate settings. As part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's respected Dalgety Collection, this registered tartan pays homage to Scotland's storied history of whisky production, which dates back centuries. While not specifically tied to a particular clan or family heritage, its use as a corporate identity is a nod to the country's proud tradition and cultural flair, making it an attractive choice for companies seeking to connect with Scottish values and history.

name: Jackson [default]
description: This unique tartan, affectionately known as the Jackson family tartan, is a heartwarming tribute to the love shared by Michael Jackson and Brigitte Prager on their special day in 2004. Designed by renowned designer Brian Wilton, this bespoke Name tartan weaves together Scottish heritage with Australian flair, reflecting the union of these two cultures. Inspired by the Scottish Rugby Union tartan, the design incorporates a rich purple hue, symbolising the couple's favourite colour, alongside the iconic blue and white representing Scotland and the gold and green of Australia, respectively. With a subtle nod to the 30th October date, which is woven into the tartan itself, this distinctive pattern celebrates the blended traditions of two nations and serves as a personal testament to the enduring love story of Michael Jackson and Brigitte Prager.

name: Jacobite #2
description: The Jacobite #2 Corporate tartan, with its subtle yet striking design, embodies the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage and tradition. This esteemed fabric, part of a revered collection by Patons of Tillicoultry, is believed to have originated in the 1930s, a time when Scotland's rich cultural identity was being celebrated and shared beyond its borders. As a Corporate tartan, Jacobite #2 is suitable for use by businesses seeking to tap into the timeless appeal of Scottish design, while still conveying a sense of modern professionalism. The sett, though undated, exudes a sense of classic elegance, evoking images of formal events, esteemed gatherings, and the proud traditions of Scotland's storied clans. Its inclusion in this collection serves as a testament to the enduring power of tartan, a symbol that continues to weave its way into the fabric of modern life, connecting past and present with every subtle fibre.

name: Jacobite Dress #2
description: The Jacobite Dress #1 tartan is a stirring example of corporate tartanry, drawing inspiration from the storied history of the Jacobite risings in Scotland. This bold and vibrant design, registered for use in corporate contexts, pays homage to the Old Jacobite tartan (#1603), a classic motif that has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage since the late 20th century. As a dress version of this iconic tartan, it lends itself perfectly to formal wear, evoking the grandeur and pageantry of Scotland's rich past. With its striking pattern and subtle nuances, Jacobite Dress #1 is a fitting choice for businesses looking to tap into the country's proud traditions, while still making a statement that is both modern and memorable.

name: Jacobite Old Sett
description: The Jacobite, Old tartan is a quintessential example of Scotland's rich textile heritage, shrouded in mystery and steeped in history. This distinctive hard tartan pattern, dating back to the 19th century, has been preserved through museum collections, where it remains one of the few remnants of its enigmatic origins. With no known designer credited for this design, it is likely that it was created by an unknown Scottish weaver, their name lost to the annals of time. As a registered "Other" tartan, this pattern defies categorisation into specific clan or family affiliation, instead evoking a sense of nostalgia and connection to Scotland's tumultuous past, when Jacobite risings shook the country. The Jacobite, Old tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's complex history, its symbolism woven into the very fabric of the nation's cultural identity.

name: Jacobite [default]
description: The Jacobite 1850 tartan is a storied and enigmatic pattern with a rich history shrouded in mystery. Its origins date back to the early 18th century, when it was allegedly owned by an unnamed lady who passed down the family tradition to W & A Smith's in 1850. According to the registration notes, this tartan was supposedly worn by Jacobites prior to the '15, but a lack of concrete evidence makes its connection to the Jacobite risings somewhat tenuous. Despite the uncertainty surrounding its provenance, the Jacobite 1850 tartan remains an intriguing and evocative design, evoking the romanticism and nationalism that defined Scotland's tumultuous past. Its category as 'Other' suggests a unique and unaffiliated heritage, distinct from the more formally registered clan tartans, making it a fascinating addition to the world of traditional Scottish textiles.

name: James of Wales
description: The James of Wales tartan is a distinctive and modern name tartan, carefully crafted by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill for Wales Tartan Centres circa 1998. This unique design stands out from traditional Celtic tartans, which typically feature odd-numbered threads, differing warp and weft patterns, and distinct colour schemes. The 'of Wales' suffix acknowledges the origin of the pattern, rather than implying a territorial connection. As a relatively recent creation, its historical and genealogical significance is limited, but its popularity has grown exponentially since its introduction, making it an integral part of modern Welsh cultural heritage. By including this tartan in the index, we honour Sheila Daniel's creative vision, even as we acknowledge that its true worth lies not in its historical pedigree, but in its representation of contemporary Scottish and Welsh identity.

name: James (Personal)
description: This majestic tartan, registered as "James", is a testament to the rich heritage of the Dumfriesshire family, whose personal history is woven into its intricate fabric. Designed by renowned Scottish textile expert Jamie Scarlett MBE, this distinctive tartan was created specifically for the esteemed Dr. Anthony Edward James. With its bold and subtle interplay of colours, "James" embodies the proud tradition of Scottish clan tartans, evoking a sense of honour and heritage that has been passed down through generations. Though restricted to use by the original registrant's family line, this tartan remains a powerful symbol of Scotland's cultural identity, awaiting discovery and reinterpretation by those who value its unique character and historical significance.

name:
Jardine Dress
[AKA] Jardine New
description: The Jardine Dress tartan is a richly woven tapestry of heritage and tradition, passed down through generations of the esteemed Jardine clan. Registered by Strathmore Woollen Company Ltd in 1991, this distinctively vibrant design was approved by the Chief and designated as 'dress', signifying its suitability for formal wear. With its deep red tones evoking the bold spirit of Scottish clansmen past, this tartan exudes a sense of honour and pride that echoes through Scotland's storied history. As part of the Clan/Family category, the Jardine Dress tartan is a tangible connection to the family's heritage, while its restriction-free status allows it to be worn with integrity, unencumbered by ancient restrictions or favouring traditional forms alone. Now preserved in the Scottish Tartans Authority Collection, this tartan design remains an enduring testament to the timeless appeal of Scotland's majestic textile traditions.

name:
Jardine of Castlemilk [default]
[AKA] Jardine of Castlemilk
description: The Jardine tartan is a rich and storied design, steeped in Scottish heritage and tied to the esteemed chiefly house of Applegirth, a baronetcy created in 1672. Originally rejected by its namesake, Colonel Jardine, as a "trade invention", the tartan was reportedly adopted under pressure from his family. This familial legacy is reflected in the intricate patterns and colours, which evoke the rugged beauty of Dumfriesshire's rolling hills and storied history. As one of Scotland's clan tartans, the Jardine design holds a profound place in the nation's cultural fabric, representing the proud tradition and identity of the Jardine family and their historic seat at Castlemilk.

name: Jardine of Castlemilk #2
description: The Provincewide HOG Chapter tartan is a unique and vibrant corporate tartan, born from the traditions of Northern Irish heritage and the thriving community of Harley Davidson enthusiasts. Designed by Tartanweb Ltd, this distinctive pattern is specifically for the members of the Provincewide HOG Chapter, a club that brings together like-minded individuals who share a passion for motorcycles and camaraderie. The tartan's design is rooted in its functional purpose as a visual representation of affiliation and belonging among its wearers, while also paying homage to the rich cultural heritage of Northern Ireland. With restrictions outlined in the registration notes, this exclusive tartan is reserved for members of the Provincewide HOG Chapter, serving as a symbol of honour and solidarity within the club.

name: Jedburgh District Jethart
description: The Jethart tartan is a deeply rooted and meaningful district tartan, born out of a sense of community and heritage. Created in 1996 to commemorate the 50th anniversary of Jedburgh's famous Jethart Calant's Festival, this vibrant tartan pays tribute to the town's rich history and cultural identity. Commissioned by local organisations, the design was conceived by Polly Wittering of House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., and woven by the esteemed Lochcarron of Scotland. As a registered district tartan, Jethart holds significant cultural significance, reflecting the unique traditions and values of Jedburgh's community. Its intricate pattern is a testament to the town's storied past, weaving together threads of history, culture, and local pride.

name: Jedforest District
description: The Jedforest tartan, expertly crafted by esteemed designer Alistair Buchan, is a rich tribute to the storied heritage of Scotland's borders. As part of the esteemed Border District Collection, this majestic design embodies the spirit of the Jedforest region, with its intricate patterns and earthy tones evoking the wild beauty of the Scottish countryside. By registering under the District category, the Jedforest tartan is deeply rooted in its local history and cultural identity, connecting wearers to a long tradition of weaving and storytelling that stretches back centuries. While certain restrictions apply to the use of this design, the Jedforest tartan remains an integral part of Scotland's unique textile heritage, waiting to be woven into the fabric of new stories and experiences.

name: Jefferson
description: This intricate and distinctive tartan, aptly named Jefferson, holds a profound significance in the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage. Registered to commemorate Eric Jefferson of Felton, Pennsylvania, it is a personal and unique creation born from the collaboration between esteemed designers Peter Wilson and Gordon Kirkbright of Great Scot International. As a 'Name' tartan, this design embodies the essence of its namesake, reflecting the individual's character and ancestry. With its distinctive colour palette and carefully crafted sett, the Jefferson tartan pays homage to the American-born Scot who wore it with pride. Its registration serves as a testament to the enduring power of Scottish tradition and the enduring spirit of those who bear their clan or family name on their kilt, sash, or other regalia.

name: Jenkins of Wales
description: The Jenkins of Wales tartan is a distinctive and modern name that has become an integral part of Welsh heritage, albeit one that was initially introduced as a commercial venture by Wales Tartan Centres in the late 20th century. This unique tartan, designed by Sheila Daniel for Cambrian Woollen Mill, sets itself apart from traditional Celtic designs with its use of predominantly odd-numbered threads and distinctive warp and weft patterns. The 'of Wales' suffix, rather than denoting a territorial or historical connection, serves to identify the design's origins and authenticate its authenticity. As such, this tartan is a celebration of Welsh identity, one that has gained widespread popularity since its introduction and now holds an important place in the world of Scottish heritage and tradition.

name: Jeux Canada Games '87
description: The Jeux Canada Games '87 tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate design, woven with the spirit of Canadian unity and sporting excellence. Created by renowned tartan designer Patricia MacMullin (Patsy), this distinctive tartan was specifically commissioned for the 1987 Canada Games, a national multi-sport event that brings together athletes from across the country. Soft handwoven on a Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection sample, this tartan reflects the warmth and camaraderie of Canadian sporting culture. As a corporate design, it is suitable for organisations looking to showcase their connection to Canadian heritage and values. While there are no restrictions on its use, the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection ensures that this tartan is steeped in tradition and authenticity, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to add a touch of Canadian flair to their branding and marketing initiatives.

name: Jewel Look JTB
description: The Jewel Look JTB tartan, designed by the renowned Scottish mill, Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the perfect blend of modernity and tradition in corporate attire. Originally created for the Japan Tourist Board in February 2003, this distinctive tartan has since become a staple of international style. With its sleek, sophisticated colour palette, the Jewel Look JTB is effortlessly chic, yet richly evocative of Scotland's storied heritage. As a Corporate tartan, it's perfectly suited for formal events and business wear, exuding professionalism and poise. Notably, Lochcarron's swatch has played a pivotal role in its development, showcasing the company's dedication to preserving traditional Scottish weaving techniques while innovating for the modern era. This unique blend of heritage and style makes the Jewel Look JTB an outstanding addition to any corporate wardrobe.

name: Jewish
description: The Jewish tartan, designed by Brian Wilton for corporate use, is a vibrant celebration of Scotland's rich cultural heritage with a profound connection to the Jewish faith. Initiated by Rabbi Mendel Jacobs of Glasgow, this iconic tartan embodies the symbolism of the Biblical Tabernacle, Ark of the Covenant, and Kiddush wine, represented by gold, silver, and red threads respectively. The bright blue and white hues of the Israeli flag add a striking contrast to the central motif, reflecting its significance as a unifying emblem for Jews around the world. With seven lines in the central pattern and three in the flag motif, this tartan nods to two revered numbers in the Jewish faith, underscoring its deeper meaning and purpose beyond mere corporate branding.

name: Joe Strummer Commemorative
description: This striking tartan, registered as the Joe Strummer Commemorative, is a poignant tribute to the iconic musician's enduring legacy. Conceived by Kenneth Graham to mark the 60th anniversary of John Graham Mellor - better known as Joe Strummer - the colours are deliberately chosen to evoke the era of audio cassette tapes, paying homage to the humble technology that helped shape Strummer's sound. As a Commemorative tartan, this design holds great significance for fans and fellow musicians alike, serving as a lasting tribute to the influential figure whose music continues to inspire generations. However, its unique character is tempered by restrictions - only with explicit permission from Kenneth Graham and his immediate family can this striking tartan be woven or used.

name: John Paul Jones, US Ship
description: The U.S.S. John Paul Jones #1 tartan is a stirring tribute to the iconic destroyer commissioned in 1993, serving as a symbol of naval heritage and American ingenuity. This Corporate tartan is designed by Bill Johnston, paying homage to the Ship's namesake, the legendary American naval commander John Paul Jones, who led the Continental Navy during the American Revolutionary War. The registration notes reveal that this tartan was likely created as part of design exercises for the USSJPJ, a ship that embodied modern maritime prowess and served with distinction in San Diego's homeport, crewed by 22 officers, 23 chief petty officers, and 295 enlisted personnel. As a Corporate tartan, this design has the potential to be used across various industries and settings, yet its roots remain firmly planted in American naval tradition, evoking the spirit of pioneering sailors who forged the nation's maritime heritage.

name: Johnnie Walker 2003
description: The Johnnie Walker 2003 Corporate tartan, designed by renowned weaver John Gillespie, is a striking fusion of traditional Scottish heritage with international flair. Commissioned for a Spanish promotion/conference, this unique tartan pays homage to the iconic whisky brand while embracing the diversity of modern corporate identity. Characterised by its asymmetrical pattern and distinct colour palette, this tartan stands out from its predecessors, reflecting the dynamic spirit of Johnnie Walker's global reach. As part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's Collection, it serves as a testament to Scotland's rich textile tradition, while also highlighting the innovative role that designers like John Gillespie play in shaping modern tartan designs for contemporary audiences. This captivating corporate tartan is a celebration of cultural exchange and creative collaboration, showcasing the enduring allure of Scotland's iconic woven heritage.

name: Johnnie Walker Whisky
description: The Johnnie Walker (1985) corporate tartan is a symbol of heritage and sophistication, born from the iconic whisky brand's rich history. Registered in 1985 by Mrs Jill Edgeworth on behalf of John Walker & Son Ltd, this distinctive tartan pays homage to Scotland's national drink and its enduring legacy. As a corporate design, it is intended for use by companies seeking to evoke the values of quality, tradition, and refinement associated with the Johnnie Walker brand. With its subtle yet striking colour palette, this tartan design embodies the perfect blend of modernity and nostalgia, evoking images of Scotland's rolling hills and whisky-fuelled gatherings. Its registered status ensures that it remains a unique and authentic representation of the brand, available for use by licence holders to add a touch of prestige and heritage to their corporate identity.

name: Johnson, J.M.
description: The Johnson, J.M. tartan is a poignant commemoration of a trailblazing figure in Canadian history. Registered by West Coast Woolen Mill, this distinctive pattern pays tribute to John Macdonald, one of the Fathers of Confederation, who played a pivotal role in shaping Canada's early years. Born in Liverpool in 1818 and dedicated to public service until his death in Quebec in 1868, Macdonald left an indelible mark on Canadian society. This tartan design, featuring a unique combination of blues and greens, has been carefully recorded by the Scottish Tartans Authority and resides within their esteemed Johnston Collection. As a symbol of remembrance and admiration for this important historical figure, the Johnson, J.M. tartan serves as a testament to Macdonald's enduring legacy in Canadian heritage.

name: Johnstone Dress
description: The Johnston Dress (Dalgleish) is a richly woven tartan steeped in the heritage of Clan Dalgleish, one of Scotland's most storied families. Designated by Dalgliesh, D. C., the creator of this iconic pattern, the Johnston Dress tartan holds great honour within Scottish tradition. The intricate interplay of blues and greens, with its distinctive yellow ochre and subtle earth tones, evokes the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Scottish Borders, where Clan Dalgleish has long held sway. As a registered clan tartan, this design is reserved for wear by members of the Dalgleish family and those who have been granted permission to wear it in favour by the clan's leaders. Prepared specifically for weaving by D C Dalgliesh Ltd., this tartan embodies the craftsmanship and tradition that have defined Scottish textiles for centuries.

name: Johnstone Orange/Black
description: The Johnston Orange/Black tartan is a distinctive corporate motif born from the humble beginnings of Atlas Asbestos Co., a North Wales, PA-based firm founded by members of the Johnston family. Registration notes reveal that this variation of the classic Johnston tartan was specifically created as the company's 'company colours' in the late 1940s, with a deliberate modification to the original ink on printing plates to introduce a deeper, richer orange hue. The result is a vibrant, bold design that exudes industrial heritage and a sense of utilitarian chic, perfectly capturing the essence of corporate identity from a bygone era. Despite its utilitarian roots, this tartan has enduring appeal for those who appreciate the intersection of traditional Scottish craftsmanship and modern commercial design.

name: Johnstone [default]
description: The Johnston/Johnstone tartan is a testament to the storied history of the powerful Border Clan, whose name has become synonymous with bravery and blood feud. First recorded in the 1842 publication of the Vestiarium Scoticum, this tartan was initially borne by the Aberdeenshire Johnstons, whose seat at Caskieben, Blackburn, stands as a poignant reminder of their ancestral heritage. The design's origins are also intertwined with the bitter conflict between Johnston and Maxwell families, which culminated in the infamous burning of Lochwood Tower in 1593. This tartan represents not only the family legacy but also the tumultuous history of Scotland's Border region, where clan rivalries and feuds shaped the very fabric of Scottish tradition. Today, the Johnston/Johnstone tartan is a proud emblem of family honour, worn with reverence by those who seek to connect with their ancestral roots.

name: Johnstons of Elgin
description: The Johnston's of Elgin Bicentennial tartan is a bespoke corporate design that proudly celebrates the esteemed Scottish textile firm's 200th anniversary. Conceived by Johnston's of Elgin, this vibrant and sophisticated pattern pays homage to the company's rich heritage and tradition of craftsmanship. As a Corporate tartan, it is designed for business use, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to establish a strong connection with Scotland's storied past while projecting modern professionalism. The Bicentennial design is rooted in the firm's history and legacy, evoking the warmth and hospitality associated with Scottish culture. With its carefully selected colours and precise sett pattern, this tartan is as much about celebrating tradition as it is about forging a new path forward – a fitting tribute to Johnston's enduring commitment to excellence and quality.

name: Johore District
description: The Johore tartan is a captivating example of Scottish heritage's rich cultural blend, born from the confluence of British and Malay traditions. This District tartan, registered in 1880, tells the fascinating story of a symbolic connection forged between Queen Victoria's visit to Balmoral and the Sultan of Johor during that era. Gordon & Sons' design skillfully weaves together the complexities of history and politics, resulting in a striking pattern that proudly represents the district from which it originates. Note the nuanced distinction between the Malay 'a' and English 'o', reflecting the intriguing cultural exchange that underpins this tartan's creation. Now registered with the Scottish Register of Tartans, the Johore tartan stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of Queen Victoria's diplomatic gesture, evoking a sense of tradition, honour, and connection between two distinct nations.

name: Johore Regiment
description: The Johore Regiment tartan is a distinctive and storied pattern, steeped in military heritage and cultural significance. Registered for the Sultan of Johore's elite regiment, this tartan was woven around 1930 by renowned Scottish designer William Anderson, whose Kinloch Anderson Ltd studio would later become synonymous with quality tartan production. Despite the occasional mis-spelling of "Jahore" as "Johare", this tartan is a testament to the rich history of Johor in Malaysia, and its association with the Johore Regiment's proud tradition. The Johore Regiment tartan holds a special place in military heritage, evoking memories of bravery, loyalty, and discipline - qualities embodied by the Sultan's esteemed regiment. This rare and fascinating tartan is not only a nod to Scottish textile expertise but also a poignant tribute to the enduring legacy of Malaysia's Johor Regiment.

name: Jones (Arctic) personal
description: Rosalind Jones's Arctic tartan is a striking tribute to the polar regions, mirroring its Antarctic counterpart in near identity while boasting subtle geographical nuances. Designated as a District tartan, it was inspired by the conservation efforts of the World Wide Fund for Nature (WWF), symbolising the shared goals and values that unite these twin continents despite their vastly different ecosystems. As a testament to the enduring bond between people and the natural world, this tartan weaves together the threads of protection and preservation, echoing the WWF's mission to safeguard our planet's precious wildlife and habitats. By wearing or using the Arctic tartan, wearers are honouring the conservation ideals that brought it into being, and paying tribute to the polar regions' breathtaking beauty and majesty.

name: Jones #2
description: The Jones Tartan, designed by renowned weaver Peter MacDonald, is a testament to the rich heritage of the name Jones, whose global reach originates from Wales, Scotland, and England. This majestic tartan embodies the dual identity of the Jones family, with its heart sett evoking the red dragon of the Welsh flag, set against a backdrop of pale green representing England's St George's cross and blue, white, and red perimeter signifying Scotland's national identity. The deliberate placement of these elements creates the iconic Scottish saltire, symbolising unity among people with the name Jones scattered across the globe. Originally commissioned by Mrs Ros Jones to raise funds for national and international charities, this distinctive tartan is a poignant reminder of the enduring connection between the Jones family's Welsh roots and their global dispersal, now woven into the fabric of history by Lochcarron's skilled weavers in 2000.

name: Jones Bobby
description: The Bobby Jones tartan, designed by esteemed Scottish weaving house Lochcarron of Scotland in 1997, is a poignant tribute to the iconic golfer who captivated the nation with his remarkable talent and unwavering sporting spirit. This fashion tartan is a personal creation, reflecting the close bond between the designer and the legendary golfer, Bobby Jones. The subtle yet distinctive pattern, woven from rich hues of blue, green, and gold, evokes the rolling hills and emerald landscapes of Scotland's countryside, as well as the country's rich sporting heritage. With no restrictions on its use, this tartan is available for those who wish to pay homage to a sporting legend or simply embody the warmth and hospitality of Scottish culture.

name: Jones Hunting
description: The Jones Hunting tartan is a quintessential example of a traditional hunting pattern, born from the heritage of Wales's esteemed gentry families. As a Name tartan, it holds a special place in the hearts of those who bear the surname Jones, symbolising their connection to this storied lineage. Designed by David R Page, this understated yet elegant tartan embodies the nuances of traditional hunting attire, characteristic of a more subdued version of family or clan tartans. Reflecting its origins as a Welsh tartan, the Jones Hunting pattern is steeped in history and tradition, its muted colours evoking the rugged beauty of the Welsh countryside, where hunting has long been an integral part of the region's cultural fabric.

name: Jones of Wales
description: The Jones of Wales tartan is a distinctive and modern name within the traditional world of Scottish textiles, with its origins firmly rooted in the contemporary heritage of Wales. Registered by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill in Powys, this tartan was specifically designed for Wales Tartan Centres, which has played a significant role in popularising the tradition since its introduction around 1998. This category tartan does not claim historical or genealogical significance, but rather serves as an identifier of its origin and source. Notably, it diverges from traditional Celtic patterns in its construction, featuring almost entirely odd-numbered threads and varying warp and weft dimensions and colours. As such, this design stands out from the more conventional tartans that dominate the cultural landscape, instead reflecting a unique fusion of ancient tradition and modern commercial endeavour.

name: Jong Nederland Born Union
description: The Jong Nederland Born Union dress tartan is a vibrant and striking corporate tartan, expertly crafted by Geoffrey Highland Crafts. This distinctive design was originally created in honour of Mr Hans Knoor, a Dutch national born on 13 December 2000, for whom it holds significant personal significance. With its unique colour palette and technical weave, this tartan embodies the cultural fusion that exists between Scotland and the Netherlands - a testament to the country's rich heritage of trade and collaboration. As a corporate tartan, Jong Nederland Born Union is perfect for businesses seeking to reflect their own unique identity and story, making it an ideal choice for branding and marketing purposes.

name: Jordan Robert Lee; Defiance
description: The Robert Lee Jordan Defiance tartan is a poignant testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage, woven with love and respect for the founder's father. Designed by Matthew A.C. Newsome, this Name tartan tells the story of the esteemed Jordan family name, which emerged as a popular baptismal name in Scotland following the Crusades. The striking red cross on a white field, borne by medieval crusaders, is beautifully rendered in this tartan, paying homage to the noble tradition that inspired its creation. Commissioned by Stephanie Jordan, a proud daughter of Edgewater, Maryland, this personal tartan serves as a tribute to her father's ancestry and a celebration of the rich cultural heritage that connects her family to Scotland's storied past.

name: Joss [default]
description: The Joss tartan is a timeless example of Scottish heritage, born from the clan's tradition and legacy. Registered by renowned designers Scot Milson & Main, this distinctive tartan tells the story of a family's honour and identity. As part of the Clan/Family category, the Joss tartan is steeped in history and meaning, woven into the very fabric of Scotland's past. While specific details about its origins may remain shrouded in mystery, the design itself exudes a sense of warmth and authenticity, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. Those privileged to wear this tartan would be bearing witness to their ancestor's legacy, a tangible connection to the land, culture, and traditions that have shaped Scotland for centuries.

name: Jrgensen [default]
description: The Jrgensen of Taasingee tartan is a deeply personal and symbolic fabric, reflecting the designer's profound love for his ancestral homeland, the Isle of Taasinge. This stunning Clan tartan features light green as its centre motif, evoking the vibrancy of life itself, surrounded by a rich tapestry of autumnal hues that echo the forests and sea that cradle the island. The gentle warmth of these earthy tones is then beautifully framed by a delicate light violet, reminiscent of the breathtaking sunsets that paint the sky above Taasinge. Jens Jrgensenn's thoughtful design choice not only pays homage to his family's heritage but also distills the essence of his beloved Isle into a captivating fabric that proudly represents the Jrgensen clan.

name: Jubilation Commemorative
description: The Jubilation tartan, designed by esteemed John Thompson of Clan Crest Textiles, is a commemorative creation steeped in tradition and pageantry. Originally conceived for the Queen's Jubilee, this vibrant pattern was intended to celebrate a momentous occasion in British history, albeit it remained unadopted by the Scottish community. Despite its lack of adoption, the Jubilation tartan remains a testament to Thompson's skill as a weaver, and its unique colour palette - featuring shades of scarlet, navy blue, and emerald green - captures the essence of jubilant celebrations. As a commemorative tartan, the Jubilation serves as a poignant reminder of the significance of such events in Scottish heritage, inviting wearers to evoke the spirit of grandeur and festivity that defines these special occasions.

name: Jubilee Universal;
description: The Jubilee tartan is a majestic and storied design, its origins shrouded in mystery, yet linked to the silver jubilee celebrations of King George V, an event with strong ties to Hunting Stewart heritage. This stately sett features a rich palette of blues, now replaced by scarlet in some variations, and was originally specified without azure, according to 'Tartan: the Highland Textile'. Associated with the esteemed MacDougal and J MacGregor-Hastie, its influence can be seen in details attributed to these respected figures. As an "Other" category tartan, it defies traditional clan affiliations, instead embracing a broader narrative of tradition and celebration, evoking the enduring spirit of Scotland's rich cultural heritage.

name: Juchter
description: Juchter, a distinctive name tartan, holds a special place in the heart of its creator, Juchter van Bergen Quast, R.A.U., whose name is expertly woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage. This personal tartan, categorised as a 'Name' tartan, was designed to reflect the unique identity and history of its owner, with intricate patterns and subtle variations that tell a story all their own. With Molly Manaugh as one of the recognised weavers, Juchter is an authentic representation of Scottish tartan craftsmanship, steeped in tradition and rooted in the rich cultural heritage of the Highlands. As a personal tartan, it serves as a badge of honour for its wearer, symbolising family lineage, ancestry, and the enduring spirit of Scotland's beloved clans.

name: Junior Chamber International
description: The Junior Chamber International tartan is a vibrant and dynamic Corporate tartan, carefully crafted by Polly Wittering at the House of Edgar to represent the Aberdeen branch of Junior Chamber of Commerce in 1995. This distinctive tartan was designed specifically for the Junior Chamber International Conference, reflecting the organisation's global ambitions and commitment to young professionals. Registration notes from the Scottish Tartans Society reveal that this count is inspired by the Johnston Collection, a renowned repository of traditional Scottish weaves. With its bold colours and modern aesthetic, the Junior Chamber International tartan embodies the spirit of innovation and entrepreneurship embodied by Junior Chamber of Commerce, while also honouring Scotland's rich cultural heritage through its carefully chosen design elements.

name: Junor
description: The Junor tartan is a unique and storied design, born from the rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands. Originally developed by Peter Norman Jones, Lord of Holdingham, as a personal clan tartan for his descendants, this distinctive variation on the classic Inverness pattern tells the tale of its proud bearers' history on the Black Isle. With a black stripe subtly woven into the fabric, this tartan pays homage to the family's storied past and their connections to the land. As a restricted name tartan, its ownership is cherished by its custodians, who hold dear the ancestral ties that bind them to this particular design. This tartan's significance extends beyond mere aesthetics, serving as a poignant reminder of Scotland's complex and fascinating cultural tapestry, woven from threads of history, tradition, and family legacy.

name: Justerini & Brooks
description: The Justerini & Brooks tartan, designed by the esteemed Colin Hutcheson of Johnstons of Elgin, is a rich and timeless corporate tartan that embodies the spirit of Scottish heritage and tradition. Originally created as an expansion of Johnstons' own Bicentennial Tartan, this distinctive design has been carefully crafted to pay homage to Scotland's storied past while also offering a fresh and modern aesthetic for businesses seeking a dignified and professional visual identity. With its bold yet subtle colour palette, the Justerini & Brooks tartan is both sophisticated and approachable, making it an ideal choice for corporate wear and branding initiatives. By choosing this tartan, companies can tap into Scotland's proud history and tradition of excellence while also showcasing their own unique character and values.

name: Justus #2
description: The Justus #2 tartan, created by Christopher Carlisle Justus in 1986, holds a unique place in the realm of Scottish heritage, existing outside the traditional commercial weaving and cultural canon. As part of a small, personal collection of seven tartans designed by Justus, this specific pattern is rendered in the distinct colours K/30 Y6 K6 Y/6, differing from the more widely documented K.100  Y20 K20 Y/20 within Scottish Tartans Society documentation. Designed with historical significance in mind, the Justus #2 tartan stands as an intriguing footnote in the evolution of Scottish textile traditions, showcasing the ingenuity and creativity of its designer amidst the complexities of Scottish clan culture and tartan legacy.

name: Justus Black & Gold
description: The Justus Black & Gold (Angus) is a personal, name tartan created by renowned Scottish weaver Christopher Carlisle Justus in 1986, showcasing his unique blend of heritage and modernity. As one of seven tartans crafted by the designer during his Hendersonville NC residency, this distinctive pattern holds a certain mystique, evoking the rich cultural tapestry of Scotland's clan system. The (Angus) designation adds an air of enigma, leaving the origins and significance of this name unclear, much like the whispered stories of forgotten Highland clans. Despite limited evidence of actual commercial weaving, Justus's innovative spirit and technical skill are evident in every carefully woven thread, inviting the wearer to wear a piece of his artistic heritage with quiet pride.

name: Justus Check
description: This intriguing tartan, dubbed 'Justus Check', is a unique creation of renowned designer Christopher Carlisle Justus, woven in Hendersonville, North Carolina in 1986. As one of seven individual tartans bearing his name, it represents a personal expression of his artistic vision, rather than an officially designated Clan or corporate motif.
