Although its commercial production status remains unknown, the 'Justus Check' tartan embodies the essence of Scottish heritage and tradition, reflecting Justus's skillful blend of technical expertise with artistic flair. A rare example of a privately designed tartan, it offers a fascinating glimpse into the life and work of this talented weaver, whose legacy continues to inspire enthusiasts of traditional textiles.

name: Justus Dress
description: The Justus Dress tartan, a personal creation of Christopher Carlisle Justus, holds a unique place in the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage. As one of seven tartans crafted by the designer in Hendersonville, NC, in 1986, this distinctive pattern is steeped in history and symbolism. The fact that it remains an unweaved design, adopted only by the Justus Family Society, highlights its exclusive significance within the clan community. Despite its limited commercial use, the Justus Dress tartan continues to hold reverence among those who value family lineage and cultural tradition, a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage and the craftsmanship of Christopher Carlisle Justus.

name: Justus Hunting
description: Justus Hunting, a personal tartan of great significance to the Justus family society in North America, is a richly woven tribute to heritage and tradition. Submitted for registration as the family sett, this distinctive pattern has been carefully preserved at 45 threads per inch (tpi) from its original sample, which displayed a subtle 9 tpi variation. As a Name tartan, Justus Hunting holds great honour among those who bear the name, serving as a symbol of familial identity and a connection to Scotland's storied past. Commissioned by Christopher Carlisle, this unique tartan design is steeped in tradition and steeped in history, its intricate weave a testament to the enduring legacy of the Justus clan.

name: Justus International
description: Justus International is a fashion tartan that embodies the modern spirit of Scottish heritage, carefully crafted by Christopher Justus in the early 1980s. Initially spotted at the Grandfather Mountain Games by Bob Martin in 1981 or 1982, this distinctive design has been preserved as part of a personal collection, serving as a testament to the enduring appeal of tartan fashion. Notably registered as a 'personal' tartan, Justus International falls outside the category for formal clan registration, reflecting the designer's intent to create a unique, modern interpretation of traditional tartan motifs. This design is included in Christopher Justus's collection of 'tartans' due to its historical significance and rarity, offering a fascinating glimpse into the evolution of fashion tartans during this period.

name: Justus Yellow & Black
description: The Justus Yellow & Black tartan, registered as a personal name tartan, bears the mark of its creator, Christopher Carlisle Justus, with a thread count estimated by a visual analysis from his photograph. This unique and distinctive tartan design embodies the individuality of its namesake, while also paying homage to Scotland's rich textile heritage. As a Name tartan, it is reserved for those who bear this particular surname, serving as a tangible representation of family identity and cultural legacy. Though not bound by traditional clan affiliations or geographical ties, this tartan holds significance in the story of its owner, a personal and intimate expression of their heritage that can be treasured for generations to come.

name: Justus
description: The Justus tartan is a personal and privately crafted sett, one of seven created by Christopher Carlisle Justus in 1990, and now recorded in the esteemed Johnston Collection of the Scottish Tartans Authority. This distinctive tartan has been submitted for approval as the family sett of the proposed Justus Family Society of North America, awaiting formal recognition. As a personal creation, it is not intended for commercial weaving, but rather exists to commemorate the individual who designed it. Despite its exclusivity, this tartan remains an important historical record of a unique Scottish heritage pattern, one that offers a fascinating glimpse into the traditions and customs of the Justus family, highlighting the enduring significance of Scottish clan identity and the passion of individuals who strive to preserve their ancestral roots through the art of tartan weaving.

name: K9
description: This captivating K9 tartan is a testament to the enduring bond between humans and their loyal canine companions. Inspired by the iconic Doctor Who robot, K9, this unique tartan has been interpreted as a tribute to the loyal friend who stood steadfastly by Tom Baker's Doctor during his tenure from 1977 to 1981. While its origins may be shrouded in mystery, with a possible connection to fashion trends of the period, its significance lies in its representation of friendship and fidelity - values that have been deeply ingrained in Scottish culture for centuries. With no specific designer credited, this tartan is a celebration of the anonymous artisan who brought this design to life, and serves as a reminder of the enduring power of nostalgia and heritage.

name: Kagame
description: The Kagame tartan is a poignant example of the enduring bond between Scottish heritage and international collaboration, as embodied in its unique registration notes. This Name tartan was created by Blair Urquhart of House of Tartan and Jane Hunter of the Hunter Foundation to commemorate the launch of a groundbreaking education and medicine program in Rwanda, under the leadership of President Kagame. The tartan's significance extends beyond its technical characteristics, for it serves as a symbol of cross-cultural exchange and solidarity, honouring the shared values of education and healthcare that unite nations across the globe. As a Personal tartan, the Kagame is also a testament to the enduring legacy of Urquhart and Hunter's design, which has been passed down through generations with pride, representing the personal connection between its owners and this remarkable tale of international partnership.

name: Kalamazoo Caledonians
description: The Kalamazoo Caledonians corporate tartan, designed by Kati Meek in 1996, embodies the spirit of Scottish cultural connection and community. Originally created for the Kalamazoo (Michigan) Caledonians, a Scottish Cultural Club, this tartan represents the harmony between heritage and modernity. As a corporate tartan, it serves as a symbol of unity and affiliation among individuals and organisations connected to the club. The colours carefully selected by Meek reflect the rich tapestry of Scottish tradition, with earthy tones evoking the rolling hills of Scotland's countryside. By embracing this tartan, those who wear or adopt it demonstrate their honourable connection to the Caledonian heritage, while also supporting a cultural movement that celebrates the shared values and history of Scotland and its diaspora communities worldwide.

name: Kalkofen [default]
description: The Kalkofen tartan is a poignant tribute to Alex Langhein's grandfather, Jurgen Robert Kalkofen, a Hamburg native whose fascination with Scottish heritage and clan traditions led him on a lifelong quest for knowledge and connection. Registered as a family tartan, the Kalkofen design bears witness to the late Mr Kalkofen's enduring legacy, open to wear by those who bear his surname. With its rich, earthy tones evoking the rolling hills of Hamburg, this tartan weaves together threads of Germanic heritage and Scottish tradition, a testament to the power of cultural exchange and family ties. As a commemorative design, the Kalkofen tartan serves as a lasting tribute to Mr Kalkofen's memory, inviting wearers to honour their ancestry and connect with a broader sense of clan identity.

name: Kansai 2
description: The Kansai2 tartan is a captivating representation of the vibrant spirit of Japan's western districts, where the city's energy meets the tranquillity of the countryside. As a District tartan, its significance lies in its association with the region's unique cultural identity and geographical distinctiveness. With no designer credited for this design, its creation remains an enigmatic tale, leaving room for interpretation about the vision behind it. Notwithstanding the absence of detailed registration notes, one can't help but be drawn to the Kansai2 tartan's distinctive hues, which evoke a sense of warmth and welcoming hospitality - an apt reflection of Japan's renowned tradition of embracing guests with open arms.

name: Kansai Highland Games
description: The Kansai Highland Games tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate motif that celebrates the spirit of international sporting excellence. Inspired by the annual Highland Games held in Kobe, Japan, this distinctive tartan was designed with the collaboration of Maud Robertson Ramsay Nomiyama, a true champion in her own right, having been awarded an MBE for her services to sports and charity. With its bold and modern colour palette, reminiscent of the bright hues of Japanese autumn leaves, this tartan is poised to add a touch of global flair to any corporate event or product. As a testament to the power of international collaboration and cultural exchange, the Kansai Highland Games tartan is a fitting tribute to the games' founding spirit, while also paying homage to the rich heritage of Scotland's iconic tartan traditions.

name: Kapasi
description: Kapasi, a bespoke tartan born from love and tradition, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage. Created with devotion for a family wedding by Geoffrey, Tailor Highland Crafts, this unique Name tartan weaves together threads of history and personal significance. As a registered design, Kapasi now carries its own distinct identity, free to be cherished by those who bear the name it represents. Its subtle nuances and intricate colour patterns evoke the rich tapestry of Scottish culture, where family ties and community are deeply intertwined. With its creator's skilled touch, Kapasi embodies the time-honoured tradition of tartan-making, now available for families to proudly wear and pass down through generations.

name: Katsushika Scottish Country Dancers
description: The Katsushika tartan is a unique and captivating Corporate design that embodies the spirit of cultural fusion. Created by master weaver Donald Fraser, this distinctive pattern pays homage to Japan's rich heritage through its inspiration from the Katsushika district in Tokyo. As part of a Japanese Scottish Country Dancing Club, this tartan reflects the intriguing blend of traditional Japanese aesthetics with the storied history of Scottish tartans. The registration notes attest to the handcrafted nature of this design, ensuring that every thread and fibre tells a story of cultural exchange and appreciation. By wearing the Katsushika tartan, wearers not only express their professional or corporate allegiance but also celebrate the meeting point of two fascinating worlds: Scotland and Japan.

name: Kaufhaus Des Westes
description: The KaDeWe tartan, a unique fusion of modernity and heritage, embodies the spirit of Berlin's cosmopolitan shopping hub, Kaufhaus Des Westes, whose Glasgow outpost played a pivotal role in its creation. In 1989, a chance discovery at Glasgow Airport - a discarded plastic bag - inspired the design of this striking tartan, which has since been adopted by Corporate wear. As a registered corporate tartan, KaDeWe is available for use by companies and organisations seeking to inject a touch of Berlin's edgy charm into their branding and attire. With its distinctive colour palette and modern aesthetic, this tartan celebrates the cultural exchange that once thrived between Europe's east and west, while paying homage to the city's storied shopping heritage.

name: Kazakhstan Relic;
description: The Kazakhstan Relic tartan is a captivating and enigmatic design, woven from threads that hold the secrets of the ancient Silk Road. Discovered entwined with the remains of mummies in the vast expanses of Central Asia's Kazakhsteppes, this tartan has been meticulously recreated to reflect its fascinating origins. As an "Other" registration, it defies traditional clan affiliations, instead existing outside the boundaries of established Scottish heritage, making it a true relic of a bygone era. Notably, the thread count has been doubled for this graphic, giving the design an otherworldly texture that evokes the mystique of the steppe's shifting sands and the whispers of a long-forgotten past.

name: Keela
description: The Keela tartan, designed by Trudi Mann, is a distinctive corporate tartan born from collaboration between a Scottish designer and an Fife-based enterprise. Drawing inspiration from the iconic St Andrew's tartan, Mann's creation was conceived as a lining for outdoor clothing manufacturers, with Barbour jackets serving as its inaugural application. Although it remains unclear whether this innovative design was ever woven into fabric, its significance lies in its ability to merge traditional Scottish heritage with modern industry. As a corporate tartan, Keela represents the fusion of history and commerce, while its St Andrew's roots reinforce its connection to Scotland's rich cultural tapestry. With Mann's 2006 registration notes providing insight into its design process, the Keela tartan stands as a testament to Scotland's thriving textile heritage and its ability to adapt and evolve for contemporary audiences.

name: Keeper of the Quaich Whisky
description: The Keepers of the Quaich corporate tartan is a rich, storied design woven from threads of tradition and heritage. Registered by Harry Lindley for Kinloch Anderson Ltd on behalf of the United Distillers Group, this distinctive tartan commemorates the company's history and legacy in Scotland's iconic whisky-making industry. The name itself, referencing the traditional Scottish quaich (a shared cup), nods to a time-honoured custom where whisky was enjoyed with camaraderie and respect. While officially controlled by the United Distillers Group, this tartan design has also become an integral part of corporate identity for those who wear it, symbolising a sense of heritage and tradition in their professional pursuits. As registered until 13th October 2008, this tartan remains an enduring testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage and the power of weaving.

name: Keith #2
description: The Keith tartan is a richly woven tribute to Scotland's storied past, originating from the powerful Celtic family who once held the revered office of Great Marischal. Dating back to at least 1838, this iconic sett has been borne by generations of Keiths, an honourable clan deeply rooted in Scottish heritage. Its connections to Lord Falconer, a 19th-century descendant of the Keith line, further underscore its historical authenticity. Designed for those proud to wear their family crest on their sleeve, the Keith tartan is a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy and the traditions that have shaped its people over centuries. As recorded in various pattern books and archives, this distinguished sett remains an essential part of Scottish cultural identity, synonymous with a legacy of strength and honour.

name: Kellogg College University of Oxford
description: The Kellogg College University of Oxford tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan commissioned by Dr Robert Collins in 2013 to commemorate Burns Supper celebrations at the esteemed institution. This unique tartan bears witness to the college's heritage, drawing inspiration from its Coat of Arms and reflecting its close ties with the W K Kellogg Foundation. The subtle blend of gold and dark blues evokes an ear of wheat, symbolising the College's enduring connection to the philanthropic legacy of William Keith Kellogg. As a reserved tartan, it is specifically designated for wear by fellows, students, alumni, and select individuals invited by the President of Kellogg College, underscoring its exclusive significance within the college community.

name: Kelly Dress
description: The Kelly Dress tartan is a striking tribute to the rich heritage of Scottish clans, its Azure ground evoking the tranquil depths of Scotland's lochs. Although its exact origin is shrouded in mystery, with only a swatch from Lochcarron available for reference, it appears to be an adaptation of the esteemed Royal Stewart tartan, a testament to the enduring influence of this iconic clan on Scottish tradition. The sett, though somewhat darker than intended, retains the essence of the original, hinting at possible connections to lesser-known Irish clans from the Scotch Corner region. This enigmatic design stands as a poignant reminder of Scotland's complex and multifaceted history, weaving together threads of heritage and identity that continue to captivate those drawn to its subtle beauty.

name:
Kelly of Sleat Hunting #2
[AKA] Kelly of Sleat; Hunting #2
description: The Kelly of Sleat Hunting tartan is a revered family crest embodying the rich heritage of Clan Donald, a historic Highland clan deeply rooted in Scotland's storied past. Designed by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr with input from Dr Douglas Kelly, Chaplain of the Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, this tartan represents the esteemed Kelly of Sleat Family and their association with Clan Donald. With its unique pattern, this tartan is steeped in tradition, reflecting the family's history and connections to the Highlands. Although a slight adjustment is required for the green colour, the overall design remains true to its roots, showcasing the intricate weave of Scottish heritage and family legacy that has been meticulously preserved.

name:
Kelly of Sleat Red
[AKA] Kelly of Sleat; Red
description: The Kelly of Sleat Red tartan is a revered family heritage from the Isle of Skye, steeped in history and tradition. Registered as a Clan/Family tartan, this distinctive pattern holds deep cultural significance for the descendants of Dr Douglas Kelly, Chaplain to the prestigious Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, which has long been synonymous with Scottish excellence. The design's creation is a testament to Phil Smith Jnr, Dr Philip D, who skilfully wove together centuries-old symbolism and the family's cherished colours, resulting in a tartan that proudly represents the Kelly of Sleat clan, closely tied to Clan Donald's legacy. With its rich history and association with Scottish Highland traditions, this tartan holds a permanent place in the hearts of those who wear it, honouring the family's heritage while paying homage to the enduring spirit of Scotland's iconic Highlands.

name: Kelso
description: The Kelso tartan, born from the skilled hands of Laird Portch, is a fashion staple that weaves together centuries-old tradition with modern style. As a registered Fashion tartan, Kelso embodies the essence of Scottish heritage, its rich hues evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Borders region. The sample in the Johnston Collection serves as a testament to its authenticity, showcasing a classic design that has been carefully crafted to evoke the traditional craftsmanship of Scottish weaving. With no restrictions on its use, the Kelso tartan is free to adorn garments, accessories, or home textiles, allowing wearers to proudly showcase their connection to Scotland's rich cultural fabric.

name: Kelvingrove
description: The Kelvingrove tartan, created by the esteemed West Coast Woolen Mill, is a vibrant and dynamic fashion fabric that embodies the spirit of Scottish heritage. Registered as a fashion tartan, it is intended for use in clothing and textiles where its bold, red-and-blue hues will make a striking statement. Characterised by its distinctive 3-2-1 repeat pattern, the Kelvingrove features a rich palette of blues and golds that evoke the grandeur of Glasgow's iconic Kelvingrove Museum and Art Gallery. While not subject to any specific clan or territorial associations, this tartan design has been crafted to add a touch of Scottish flair to fashion-forward ensembles, allowing wearers to proudly showcase their appreciation for the country's rich textile traditions.

name: Kenmore
description: The Kenmore tartan is a captivating fashion variant that owes its origins to the storied Stewart Bute clan, whose legacy has been etched into Scotland's fabric for centuries. Registered in 2008 by renowned designer Jack Dalgety, this distinctive tartan boasts subtle variations on the traditional Stewart Bute colours, imbuing it with a fresh yet timeless charm. As a fashion tartan, Kenmore is perfect for adding a dash of Scottish flair to outfits, from smart evening wear to country-inspired chic. Its nuanced colour palette and elegant repeat pattern evoke the rolling hills and rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands, making Kenmore an ideal choice for those seeking to connect with the nation's cultural legacy through the universal language of tartan.

name: Kenmore Hunting
description: The Kenmore Hunting tartan is a striking fashion design that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's rugged Highlands. Registered in 1996, this distinctive tartan was created by Polly Wittering for House of Edgar, under commission from Macnaughtons of Pitlochry, a prominent Scottish clan with a long history of hunting and outdoor pursuits. Characterised by its bold, geometric pattern, the Kenmore Hunting tartan is a testament to Scotland's enduring love affair with the great outdoors. Originally designed for a range of gifts, this tartan has since become synonymous with Scottish style and heritage, its unique blend of earthy tones and dynamic motifs evoking the thrill of the hunt and the wild beauty of the Scottish landscape.

name: Kennedy Dress
description: The Kennedy Dress tartan is a vibrant and elegant name tartan, carefully crafted by renowned kiltmaker Hugh Macpherson in 19th-century Edinburgh. Designed for dancing and other informal gatherings, this distinctive pattern was meant to bring joy and pride to those who wore it, reflecting the rich heritage of the Kennedy clan. As a 'dress' tartan, it eschews traditional clan motifs in favour of a striking all-over design, featuring subtle variations in colour that set it apart from its 'ground' counterparts. Although restrictions apply due to Hugh Macpherson's intentions as a kiltmaker, rather than a Clan patron, this beautiful tartan remains a testament to the artistry and tradition of Scottish textile-making, evoking the warmth and hospitality of Scottish culture.

name: Kennedy Irish
description: The Kennedy (Irish) tartan is a fascinating, albeit imperfect, representation of the storied clan heritage of Scotland's north-east coast. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, this unique pattern is often attributed to Irish roots, although its origins are shrouded in mystery, and it appears to be a derivative of the original Scottish Kennedys (#1123). The design's clumsy construction - characteristic of early, unofficial tartan variations - sets it apart from more refined family patterns. Despite its inconsistencies, the Kennedy (Irish) remains an intriguing testament to the rich cultural tapestry of Scotland's clan histories, evoking a sense of pride and connection to the region's complex and storied past.

name: Kennedy [default]
description: Kennedy #3, a stalwart member of the Clan Kennedy tartan family, exudes the proud heritage and storied history of one of Scotland's most noble clans. Woven with the traditional Strathmore Woollen Company techniques, this intricate pattern boasts subtle variations that bring to life the nuances of 19th-century originals. A testament to the enduring legacy of the Scottish Tartans Society, Kennedy #3 is remarkably faithful to its 1880 Clans Originaux counterpart, showcasing the same characteristic blue and green hues that have been woven into the very fabric of Scotland's cultural identity for centuries. As a proud representation of Clan Kennedy, this tartan invites wearers to honour their ancestral heritage and connect with the timeless traditions that have shaped the nation's rich history.

name: Kennison [default]
description: The Kennison tartan, designed by Dalgliesh, D C in all its intricate beauty, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's storied clans. As a Clan/Family tartan, it is steeped in tradition and tied to the history and identity of the esteemed family it represents. According to the registration notes, Kennison may be associated with a traditional dancer's tartan, suggesting a connection to the vibrant world of Scottish ceilidh culture. Interestingly, the same sett is also registered at #5346 under the name Kierson, underscoring the complexities and nuances of Scottish tartan tradition. With its unique characteristics and restrictions, Kennison tartan is not only a testament to Scotland's cultural richness but also a fascinating piece of textile heritage that invites wearers to draw upon their ancestral roots and proudly declare their connection to this storied clan family.

name: Kenspeckle
description: The Kenspeckle tartan is a quintessential corporate design, embodying the dynamism and sophistication of modern Scotland. With its bold, graphic pattern, it lends itself to a wide range of applications, from formal wear to branding initiatives. Created by esteemed designers Wilton/Whitson, this tartan's origins are shrouded in mystery, as no specific details are recorded in its registration notes. Nevertheless, its striking repetition of alternating black and blue stripes, punctuated by distinctive flecks of white, evokes a sense of modernity and visual flair. As a corporate tartan, the Kenspeckle is destined to make a lasting impression on those who wear it or encounter it, serving as a powerful symbol of Scottish heritage and style that transcends traditional clan affiliations.

name: Kentucky State
description: The Kentucky State District tartan is a vibrant representation of the Bluegrass State's rich heritage, woven with precision and passion by renowned designers Rupert Furgerson and Pat Murray-Schweitzer. Adopted as the official statewide tartan in 2000 through a collaborative effort between lawmakers, this distinct design now holds honour among Kentuckians and tartan enthusiasts alike. With its unique colour palette, inspired by the rolling hills, majestic horses, and stunning natural beauty of Kentucky, this tartan is a testament to the state's unique identity. As one of the first district tartans, it serves as a bridge between the traditional and modern world of Scottish textiles, while also proudly representing the Commonwealth's rich history and cultural heritage.

name: Keppoch
description: The Keppoch tartan is a captivating example of Scotland's rich textile heritage, boasting a unique blend of bold and subtle colours. As one of the oldest district tartans in existence, dating back to 1882, it pays homage to the traditional weaving techniques that have been passed down through generations of Scottish weavers. The estimated count from James Cant's hand-painted colour strips suggests that this tartan was created by a skilled artisan, imbuing the design with an air of authenticity and historical significance. With its distinctive pattern, the Keppoch tartan is a testament to Scotland's proud cultural legacy, evoking images of rugged Highland landscapes and the strong sense of community that defines Scottish identity.

name: Kerby, USA (Personal)
description: The Kerby tartan is a poignant and personal tribute to Scottish heritage, woven with love and nostalgia by its esteemed designer, Kenneth W.H.Kerby. Originally created to celebrate the birth of a first son in Tennessee's Cumberland Basin, this unique Name tartan bears the distinctive spelling of "Kerby", a nod to the family's early American settlers who hailed from Berwickshire, Scotland. With its specific restrictions aimed at avoiding confusion with the more commonly spelled surname "Kirby", this tartan design proudly asserts its Scottish roots and family legacy. As a cherished family heirloom, the Kerby tartan embodies the rich cultural traditions of Scotland, carefully preserved for future generations to treasure.

name: Kerby [default]
description: The Kerby/Kirby tartan is a storied heritage pattern, woven from threads of tradition and family legacy. Described by Dalgliesh as a revised interpretation of the esteemed Scottish Tartans Authority reference #2496, this striking design features grey as its principal colour guard, subtly shifting the traditional yellow to red palette, imparting a modern yet distinctive twist. As a Clan tartan, Kerby/Kirby is steeped in significance, likely representing the ancestral heritage and kinship ties of its bearers. Notably, the presence of restrictions indicates that this tartan is reserved for specific families or clans, underscoring the importance of preserving traditional associations and honouring the historical roots of Scottish tartans.

name: Kerr Hunting
description: The Kerr Hunting tartan is a majestic representation of Scottish heritage, rooted in the proud history of Clan Kerr. This distinctive family tartan boasts a rich, dark blue foundation, woven with intricate patterns of reddish-brown and yellow hues, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscape. Originally registered by Lochcarron, this thread count variant showcases a more approachable appearance, making it accessible to those seeking to connect with Scottish tradition without the need for formal tartan etiquette. With its bold colours and enduring symbolism, the Kerr Hunting tartan remains an honouring tribute to the storied past of Clan Kerr, inviting wearers to pay their respects while forging lasting connections with Scotland's rich cultural heritage.

name: Kerr Shepherd's Plaid
description: The Kerr Shepherd's Plaid is a storied and distinctive tartan, carefully crafted for the esteemed Chief of Clan Kerr, the Marquis of Lothian, to make his family's standing in the historic Borders region truly singular. Designed by an unknown yet skilled artisan, this tartan bears the weight of centuries-old tradition and ancestral heritage. As a Clan/Family tartan, it is an honour bestowed upon the noble House of Kerr, one of the most prominent Border families, whose name has been synonymous with bravery, resilience, and the rich cultural tapestry of Scotland's storied past. The Kerr Shepherd's Plaid serves as a poignant reminder of the family's distinguished history, evoking images of rugged Scottish landscapes, proud clan gatherings, and the unwavering loyalty that defines the tartan-wearing heritage of Clan Kerr.

name: Kerr [default]
description: The Kerr tartan is an iconic Scottish clan tartan, steeped in history and tradition. First documented by the Marquis of Lothian, Chief of the Kerrs, in 1588, it has been a cherished part of the family's heritage for centuries. This distinctive tartan was published as early as 1842 in Sobieski Stuart's 'Vestiarium Scoticum', one of the earliest recorded tartans to be shared with the world. The Kerr clan tartan is now proudly worn by members of the Clan Kerr and those who bear its name, serving as a visual representation of their honour and connection to Scotland's storied past. Its enduring significance lies not only in its technical characteristics but also in the rich cultural heritage it embodies, evoking a sense of pride, loyalty, and belonging among those who wear it.

name: Kerry Irish County
description: The Kerry County tartan, registered by House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd, is a vibrant representation of Irish heritage and tradition. As one of a series of Irish District tartans designed by Polly Wittering, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the rich cultural history of County Kerry in southwest Ireland. Originally intended as Fashion tartans, they have gained popularity and recognition as authentic District tartans, reflecting their enduring appeal to those who appreciate Scotland's nuanced clan system. With its unique colour palette and carefully crafted sett, this tartan design embodies the spirit of Irish identity and tradition, its story woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage through the House of Edgar's creative vision.

name: Kidd Rock and Wheel
description: The iconic Kidd tartan, woven by Wilsons of Bannockburn in the late 18th century, is a quintessential representation of Scotland's rich heritage. Originally designed as Clan MacPherson's registered tartan, certified in 1817 by their chief, this storied pattern has become synonymous with the clan's proud history and tradition. As a result of its association with the esteemed MacPherson family, Kidd tartan is now worn with honour, not only by descendants of the clan but also under its non-clan name, Caledonia, making it accessible to those who wish to connect with Scotland's cultural fabric. This timeless design, featured in Wilsons' 1819 Key Pattern Book as No.43, continues to captivate enthusiasts and tartan aficionados alike, evoking a sense of Scottish pride, family heritage, and the enduring legacy of the country's oldest and most revered clans.

name: Kiernan [default]
description: The Kiernan tartan, a Clan/Family registered design, holds a rich and complex history within the realm of Scottish heritage. Traditionally associated with the Clans Originaux publication in 1880, which incorrectly attributed its origins to Ireland, further research has revealed this 'fiction' to be an enduring misconception. The true provenance of the Kiernan tartan remains shrouded in mystery, as the only known copy is housed in the Jack Dalgety collection, and a woven sample exists within the Scotspun folder. Despite these doubts, the Kiernan tartan continues to hold significance for those tracing their ancestry through Scottish clan lines, offering a tangible connection to their heritage and cultural roots. Its existence serves as a poignant reminder of the importance of verifying historical information and respecting the nuances of traditional textile knowledge.

name: Kierson [default]
description: The Kierson tartan, registered with the prestigious Scottish Tartans Authority, is a timeless representation of family heritage and clan tradition. Designed by the esteemed D C Dalgliesh Ltd, this intricate sett has been woven into the fabric of Scotland's rich history for generations to come. Originating from an original reference number (#5336), the Kierson tartan showcases a unique blend of blues, greens, and yellows, evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Scottish countryside. This clan tartan, prepared specifically for weaving by Dalgliesh Ltd, is imbued with the honour of its bearers, serving as a symbol of pride, loyalty, and heritage for those fortunate enough to wear it. Its significance extends far beyond personal adornment, instead representing a deep connection to Scotland's storied past and the families who have woven their history into the very fabric of this iconic tartan.

name: Kilbarchan # 14
description: Kilbarchan Unidentified No. 14 is an enigmatic tartan with a rich history shrouded in mystery, much like its origins remain unknown. As one of the "Other" category tartans, it defies categorisation by clan or family lineage, instead standing as a testament to the artisanal skill of the Kilbarchan weavers. This complex and intricately woven design bears some striking similarities to the MacKenzie Dress tartans, suggesting a possible connection to this storied Highland family, albeit without conclusive evidence. The small woven sample from the Kilbarchan Weaver's Cottage provides tantalising clues about its composition, hinting at a more intricate pattern than initially meets the eye. For those fascinated by Scotland's rich cultural heritage and the time-honoured traditions of tartan-making, Kilbarchan Unidentified No. 14 offers a captivating glimpse into the artistic world of Highland weaving, waiting to be unravelled.

name: Kilbarchan # 2
description: Kilbarchan Unidentified No. 2 is a captivating tartan design that defies straightforward identification, much like its mysterious origins. This enigmatic weave, categorised as 'Other', bears tantalising similarities to the respected Farquharson and MacDuff Dress tartans, leading some to speculate about its potential connection to a traditional wedding tartan. However, the uncertainty surrounding its true identity is palpable, with experts Jamie Scarlett MBE and Blair Urquhart suggesting it may simply be a trial weave, embodying the nuances of experimentation in Scottish textile traditions. This intriguing design serves as a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland, where artistry and tradition are intricately woven together, waiting to be unravelled by those with a keen eye for detail.

name: Kilbarchan # 5
description: Kilbarchan Unidentified No. 5 is a captivating, enigmatic tartan with an air of mystery surrounding its origins. Registered from a plaid at Kilbarchan Weavers' Cottage, this distinctive pattern bears testament to the enduring legacy of traditional Scottish weaving. Suggesting a 19th century design, the sett's intricate complexity hints at a rich history, possibly linked to a long-forgotten clan or family association. As an "Other" category tartan, it exists outside the more conventional clan systems, yet still resonates with the cultural heritage of Scotland's textile traditions. With its unique character and 19th century provenance, Kilbarchan Unidentified No. 5 invites wearers to connect with the region's rich history and weave a thread into the intricate tapestry of Scottish tartans.

name: Kilbarchan # 7
description: Kilbarchan Unidentified No. 7 is a mysterious and captivating tartan, shrouded in intrigue due to its unknown designer. Despite the lack of identification, this unique sett has captured the hearts of many with its distinctive blend of dark green, gold, and blues, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. Originally registered as "Other", it falls outside the traditional clan or name tartans, instead embodying a distinct style that defies categorisation. Notable restrictions highlight the complexity of its design, with the green stripe requiring a subtle reinterpretation to reveal the intricate pattern beneath - a testament to the nuanced artistry involved in traditional Scottish weaving. This enigmatic tartan stands as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich textile heritage and the countless stories waiting to be unravelled within its threads.

name: Kilburnie
description: The Kilburnie tartan, designed by renowned Scottish weavers at Moffat Weavers, is a stunning Fashion tartan that embodies the very essence of Scotland's rich heritage. Registered in the iconic shop of Blairgowrie, Perthshire, this distinctive pattern has been woven with precision and care, paying homage to the region's storied history. As a Fashion tartan, Kilburnie was created for the modern-day enthusiast seeking to inject a touch of Scottish style into their wardrobe. With its unique colour palette and technical characteristics, Kilburnie is a testament to the enduring power of traditional Scottish weaving techniques, expertly reinterpreted by the skilled artisans at Moffat Weavers.

name: Kildare Irish County
description: The Kildare, County tartan is a stunning example of Irish heritage, hailing from the esteemed House of Edgar's Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. designed series of Irish District tartans. Created by renowned textile artist Polly Wittering, this tartan has captured the hearts of many with its rich, symbolic significance. Originally classified as Fashion tartans rather than officially sanctioned District tartans, its popularity has led to speculation that it may eventually be recognised as a genuine District tartan. Characterised by its striking colour palette and intricate pattern, the Kildare, County tartan is a testament to Ireland's rich history and cultural identity. Woven with attention to detail and an understanding of traditional Irish weaving techniques, this tartan design embodies the warmth and hospitality that defines the county it bears its name.

name: Kile
description: The Kile Name tartan is a rare and personal variation, carefully woven to commemorate an individual's heritage. This distinctive sett, registered with Scottish Tartans Society in 1983, was originally designed by Peter MacDonald, although its intended purpose remains unclear. Although never formally woven, this design has been passed down through the Kyle family, with one notable exception: the addition of a red line between two of the white sections, which may have been introduced at a later date. Despite its relatively short history, the Kile Name tartan is an enduring symbol of Scottish tradition and connection to the Clyde Valley, where the Kyle River flows. Its unique character serves as a poignant reminder of the rich cultural heritage that underpins this beloved national fabric.

name: Kilgour [default]
description: The Kilgour (Symmetrical) tartan is an iconic representation of Scottish heritage, borne from the storied history of Clan Kilgour, whose roots stretch back centuries. This symmetrical variation of the original asymmetrical design has been a staple in Scottish tradition for generations, its carefully woven threads evoking a sense of time-honoured pride and identity. With its unique colour palette and precise pattern, this tartan is steeped in tradition and is deeply ingrained in the cultural fabric of Scotland. Its registration as a Clan tartan reflects its significance within the family's lineage, where it continues to play an important role in ceremonies, celebrations, and everyday life.

name: Kilgour (Symmetrical)
description: The Kilgour tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's storied clans, with its rich, dark blues and deep reds evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. Registered in the early 19th century, this traditional family tartan was immortalised by J Claude in his esteemed pattern books 'Clans Originaux' and 'Scotch Tartans', providing a window into the past for those who cherish Scotland's heritage. As a Clan tartan, the Kilgour is worn with pride by members of the Kilgour family, symbolising their honourable lineage and connection to this ancient, storied tradition. The subtle nuances in colour and texture that define this tartan – a true representation of Scotland's proud tartan heritage – make it an exquisite addition to any Scottish legacy or ceremonial occasion.

name: Kilkenny Irish County
description: The Kilkenny, County tartan is a vibrant reflection of Ireland's rich heritage, woven with the intricate traditions of its ancient districts. Designed by Polly Wittering in collaboration with House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this District tartan has captured the hearts of many, despite not being officially sanctioned. The result is a beautifully nuanced design that embodies the spirit of County Kilkenny, where history and culture blend seamlessly with the natural beauty of the Emerald Isle. As one of a series of Irish District tartans, this pattern holds a special place in the realm of Scottish heritage, offering a unique glimpse into Ireland's own distinct tartan traditions, which will undoubtedly be recognised and cherished in time.

name: Killen [default]
description: The Killen tartan is a distinctive Clan/Family design, steeped in tradition and heritage, which was meticulously crafted by Paul Killen for his own wedding celebration in July 2004. This unique tartan, though born from personal love, has been formally registered as a clan tartan, allowing its wearer to bear the name with honour. With its rich, earthy tones of blue, green, and yellow, the Killen tartan evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands, where loyalty, family, and heritage are deeply intertwined. Though designed for one individual, this tartan has been freed from personal favour to be worn by anyone fortunate enough to share the name Killen, embodying the spirit of camaraderie and shared identity that defines Scottish clan culture.

name: Killin [default]
description: The Killin tartan is a deeply personal and ancestral weave, born from the threads of history and tradition. Designed by Robert Killin in collaboration with Lochcarron of Scotland, this clan tartan pays homage to the Campbell and MacNab clans, whose roots run deep into the village of Killin at the west end of Loch Tay. As a family tartan, it has been adopted by members of the Toronto-based Burnett and Struth families, who seek to connect with their Scottish heritage through an annual pilgrimage to the village. Now, after years of spreading from Ottawa to Vancouver and into the USA, this richly woven tartan boasts over 250 wearers worldwide, each one a tangible link to the Killin legacy. This vibrant fabric holds within it the stories, memories, and cultural traditions of generations past, making it more than just a piece of cloth – it is a badge of honour that weaves together family, place, and identity.

name: Kilmarnock Football Club 2005
description: The Kilmarnock Football Club tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate tartan, woven to commemorate the Scottish football club's rich history and dedication to their Ayrshire community. As a Corporate tartan, it holds great significance for the club and its supporters, serving as an emblem of team spirit and pride. Registered in 2005, this distinctive design was created by Lochcarron of Rannoch, a renowned Scottish textile mill, to be worn with honour by members of Kilmarnock Football Club and their fans alike. Featuring a striking blend of blues and greens, reminiscent of the Ayrshire countryside, this tartan is a testament to the club's heritage and its people's strong sense of identity and affiliation. Its design may have been created without a specific designer being attributed, but it embodies the passion and tradition that defines Scotland's beloved football culture.

name: Kilmarnock Football Club Old
description: This iconic tartan design, registered as Kilmarnock Football Club (Old), is a proud emblem of corporate identity for the Scottish club. Dating back to its inception, this distinctive pattern has been woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage, evoking memories of passionate supporters and storied victories. As a Corporate registration, it was carefully crafted by Peter MacArthur & Co. to represent the team's values and traditions. Although the registration notes caution about the reliability of the count, the tartan remains an enduring symbol of Kilmarnock's rich history, its borders and sett meticulously woven together to form a vibrant, dynamic design that echoes the energy of Scottish football culture.

name: Kilmorie
description: The Kilmorie tartan, a rich and storied District tartan, holds a place of pride within Scotland's cultural heritage. Registered in 1882, this distinctive pattern is steeped in tradition and history, its unique colour palette evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. As one of James Cant's meticulously hand-painted colour strips from his manuscript book, we catch a glimpse into the artisanal skill and attention to detail that defined tartan weaving during the 19th century. The Kilmorie design is a testament to the District category, which was traditionally used to denote geographical areas or regions within Scotland. With its distinct count and colour strip pattern, this tartan serves as a tangible link to Scotland's rich past, its threads woven from generations of tradition and heritage.

name: Kilt Centre (Hire) personal; Inverclyde
description: The Inverclyde corporate tartan is a distinctive and modern choice, born from the heritage of Scotland's rich textile traditions. Designed by Kilt Centre, this unique pattern is woven with pride to represent The Kilt Centre's kilt hire business, showcasing their commitment to celebrating Scottish heritage for all occasions. With its characteristic hues of blue, green, and gold, Inverclyde tartan evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's western coastlines, where the River Clyde flows through the heart of Glasgow. This corporate tartan is an honourable reflection of the country's history and craftsmanship, with each carefully woven thread a testament to the skill and tradition that has defined Scottish textiles for centuries.

name: Kilt Centre (Hire) personal; Inverclyde Green
description: Inverclyde Green, the signature tartan of corporate Scotland, is a vibrant and modern creation born from the esteemed Kilt Centre's in-house design team. Specifically crafted for their kilt hire business, this unique tartan reflects the rich heritage of Lochcarron, one of Scotland's most renowned weaving centres. Characterised by its distinctive green hues with subtle undertones, Inverclyde Green embodies the essence of corporate identity and style, while nodding respectfully to Scotland's storied textile past. As a registered corporate tartan, this design is poised to make a statement in modern business attire, effortlessly blending tradition with contemporary flair, making it an excellent choice for companies seeking to establish a strong visual presence that honours their Scottish roots.

name: Kincaid [default]
description: The Kincaid of Kincaid tartan, registered in Lord Lyon's Register of All Arms and Bearings in Scotland, is a rich and storied heritage pattern rooted in Scottish clan tradition. Designed by the renowned textile company Lochcarron of Scotland, this distinctive tartan represents the family name that has become synonymous with proud identity and ancestral legacy. Dating back to 30th March 1960, when it was recorded from the esteemed MacGregor-Hastie Collection, this tartan bears testament to the enduring significance of family ties and clan heritage in Scottish culture. With its complex weave of blues, greens, yellows, and reds, the Kincaid of Kincaid tartan evokes a sense of history and tradition, a tangible connection to Scotland's storied past that continues to inspire pride among those who wear it.

name: Kincardine City Ontario
description: The City of Kincardine tartan is a striking tribute to the picturesque district situated on the shores of Lake Huron in Ontario, Canada. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Society in 1987, this District tartan is a testament to the enduring connection between Scotland and its diaspora communities worldwide. The Strathmore Woollen Company Ltd's design weaves together rich hues and textures, evoking the tranquil beauty of the Kincardine shoreline. As part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, the City of Kincardine tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's global heritage, proudly worn by those who call this Canadian city home or have strong ties to its rich history and culture.

name: Kinfauns Castle Hotel
description: The Kinfauns Castle tartan is a distinctive Corporate tartan, woven with precision to embody the grandeur and heritage of its original commission - the Hong Kong Hilton. Now synonymous with luxury hospitality at Perth's Kinfauns Hotel, Scotland, this tartan tells the story of transatlantic connections and the blending of cultures. Conceived by the esteemed Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this majestic design weaves together subtle nuances of blue, green, yellow, black, brown, red, and purple to evoke the iconic castle that inspired its creation. A testament to Scottish tradition, yet forged in the cosmopolitan spirit of Hong Kong, this tartan stands as a symbol of warmth, hospitality, and refined elegance - fittingly worn by the Kinfauns Hotel's esteemed patrons.

name: King (Austria)
description: The King (Austria) personal tartan is a unique and meaningful design born from the family's heritage in the picturesque region of Vorarlberg in Austria. Designed by Andrew, Emil, and Elmar King, this tartan holds great significance for its intended wearers, who are part of the royal family or have received special permission to don it. The striking red and white stripes that form the heart of the design are said to evoke the family's Austrian residence, while the surrounding yellow and black stripes pay homage to their former Habsburg kingdom connections and their roots in the village of Hoebranz, where they first settled in Austria. As a testament to the rich cultural exchange between Scotland and Ireland, the tartan's base colours - red and blue - represent the two countries that have shaped the King family's history, while the green stripes add a touch of Irish heritage to this striking design, weaving together a narrative of tradition, identity, and loyalty.

name: King (Michael) personal; Bon Accord Aberdeen
description: The Bon Accord tartan, with its rich hues and distinctive sett, proudly represents the historic city of Aberdeen, embodied in the district category. Conceived by renowned designer Michael King of Philip King Ltd, this tartan was born out of a desire to showcase the unique heritage of Scotland's second-largest city. Approved by the City Council, the Bon Accord tartan was unveiled at the prestigious Aberdeen Highland Games in June 1995, paying tribute to the area's rich cultural and sporting traditions. This distinctive design not only celebrates the spirit of the people of Aberdeen but also serves as a lasting symbol of their connection to the land, evoking feelings of community, pride, and Scottish identity.

name: King George IV
description: The King George IV tartan is a poignant example of Scotland's rich heritage, woven into the very fabric of its history. This distinctive tartan was originally created for a banner, measuring 49 inches by 102 inches, to commemorate a significant event - the centenary possession of John Allan's mortification order in 1824. With its intricate design and quarter inch red braid edging, the banner was likely crafted specifically for the Royal visit of King George IV in 1822, underscoring the importance of this tartan as a symbol of Scottish hospitality and tradition. As part of the registration notes, the tartan's origins are linked to the Stirling Incorporation of Weavers, further highlighting its connection to Scotland's proud weaving heritage. This tartan remains an enduring testament to the country's rich cultural past, with its unique characteristics waiting to be woven into new and meaningful contexts.

name: King George (Nash)
description: The King George (Nash) tartan is a fashion icon born out of the glamourous era of 1970s style, with roots in the iconic husband-and-wife duo, Mrs Winnie Nash and Sir Donald Stewart, who wore it to numerous high-profile events, including their wedding celebrations. Woven by esteemed mill Fromm Bros. in 1974, this tartan was later immortalised on fabric when a dress worn by Mrs Nash at a social gathering in the late 1970s caught the eye of textile enthusiasts, leading to its registration. As a fashion tartan, King George (Nash) embodies the whimsical flair and eclecticism that defined the decade, yet remains rooted in traditional Scottish weaving techniques, testifying to the timeless appeal of Scottish heritage and textiles.

name: King George VI; Coronation 1936
description: The Coronation (1936) #2 tartan is a poignant tribute to the regal ceremony that marked the accession of King George VI in 1936. This commemorative tartan was designed to commemorate the historic event, and its creation highlights the enduring significance of the Scottish monarchy. As an alternative count to the original registration #661, this tartan offers a unique perspective on the coronation's symbolism and pageantry. With roots in Coulson Bonner's design and connections to the McGregor Hastie Collection, which holds physical samples of the original designs, the Coronation (1936) #2 tartan serves as a tangible link to Scotland's rich heritage. Its inclusion in this category underscores its role as a celebration of British history, echoing the grandeur and tradition that underpins Scottish culture.

name:
Stewart King George VI
[AKA] Green Stewart
description: The King George VI (Green Stewart) tartan is an intricately woven emblem of Scottish heritage, steeped in tradition and exclusivity. Registered under Royal warrant, this distinctive tartan was specifically created for HM King George VI, with the renowned Wm Anderson, a Royal Warrant Holder, at his request. The tartan's reserved availability reflects its sensitive history, as it was initially used to protect the design from misappropriation by the general public. Today, it is carefully preserved and respected by weavers, primarily in the United Kingdom, in recognition of its exclusive association with the British Royal family. Its occasional appearance on HRH Prince Charles, Prince of Wales's kilt serves as a poignant reminder of the tartan's enduring significance within the royal tradition.

name: Kings Mountain 1780
description: The Kings Mountain 1780 tartan is a poignant tribute to the unsung heroes of the American War for Independence, whose Scottish ancestry played a pivotal role in shaping the course of history. Designed by Leslie Ross Tate, this commemorative tartan commemorates the bravery and sacrifice of frontier settlers from Ulster Scots background who fought on both sides at the Battle of Kings Mountain in 1780. Worn primarily by those with ancestral ties to this pivotal event, the tartan bears testament to a unique chapter in Scottish-American heritage, one that highlights the transatlantic connections between Scotland's fierce history and the birthplace of American independence. As a symbol of kinship and solidarity, the Kings Mountain 1780 tartan proudly wears its historical significance on its sleeve, allowing wearers to connect with their roots while paying homage to a momentous occasion in the Revolutionary War.

name: Kingsbarns Golf Links
description: The Kingsbarns Golf Links corporate tartan is a meticulously crafted design that pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage and the storied history of golfing tradition. Inspired by the Erskine and Earl of St Andrews tartans, this distinctive pattern weaves together elements of Scotland's noble families with the iconic hues of its majestic coastline. The regal blue tones, reminiscent of a clear Scottish sky at dawn, are a fitting tribute to the 'Blue Jackets' uniform worn by the original Kingsbarns Golfing Society in 1793. Yellow sand and red undertones evoke the links course's natural beauty, while subtle nods to the Duke of Fife tartan add depth and complexity to this carefully considered design, which Kinloch Anderson Ltd has brought to life as a testament to Kingbarns' enduring legacy.

name: Kinloch Anderson (personal) #1
description: The Kinloch Anderson tartan is an iconic corporate design that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's esteemed Kinloch Anderson company. This exclusive tartan, controlled by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, pays homage to the Clan Anderson sett first recorded in the 13th century, reflecting six generations of the family's ownership and management. The distinctive three-parallel burgundy lines, with a central line wider than its flanking counterparts, add a touch of classic elegance to this timeless design. Rich in colour, the Kinloch Anderson tartan boasts a striking palette of navy, border brown, two shades of burgundy, black, and antique gold, evoking the enduring traditions of Scotland's storied past. With its sophisticated blend of heritage and modernity, this corporate tartan has become synonymous with excellence and represents the best of Scottish style and tradition.

name: Kinloch Anderson (personal) Check
description: The Dinwiddie Hunting tartan is a storied and dignified design, woven from threads of heritage and history. Registered as a clan name tartan, its presence signifies a deep affinity with William James Dinwiddie's illustrious ancestry. This specific pattern was crafted by Linda Clifford for The Knockomie Collection, drawing upon traditional Scottish weaving techniques to bring forth a rich tapestry of colours. While open to use by all who share the Dinwiddie name, regardless of spelling variation, those seeking to incorporate this tartan into commercial ventures must first establish contact with the copyright holder, Bill Dinwiddie, to ensure respectful and authorised usage. Through its very existence, the Dinwiddie Hunting tartan embodies a sense of pride and belonging, connecting wearers to a noble tradition that stretches back through generations of Scots.

name: Kinloch Anderson (personal) Dress
description: The Kinloch Anderson Old Dress tartan is a distinguished corporate choice, steeped in heritage and tradition, yet adapted for modern purposes. Originally conceived as an "in-house" dress tartan by Kinloch Anderson Ltd in 1997, this timeless design draws inspiration from the iconic Clan Anderson tartan, showcasing its storied roots. Reimagined as 'Kinloch Anderson Old Dress' in 2002, this tartan now stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Anderson clan and their storied history. With its carefully crafted colours and subtle nuances, the Kinloch Anderson Old Dress tartan is an authentic choice for any organisation seeking to connect with Scottish tradition, while also exuding professionalism and sophistication - a fitting tribute to the esteemed Kinloch Anderson Ltd, its controlling authority over this coveted corporate tartan.

name: Kinloch Anderson (personal) Hunting
description: The Kinloch Anderson Hunting Tartan is a striking corporate design, steeped in tradition and rooted in Scotland's rich heritage of hunting and shooting. As part of the esteemed Kinloch Anderson Collection, this exclusive tartan follows in the footsteps of its eponymous precursor, drawing inspiration from the rugged landscape of the Scottish Highlands. Characterised by dark, muted tones of tartan green, blue, burgundy, black, and light beige, this design evokes the mystery and grandeur of the hunt itself. With its restricted control by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this tartan embodies the precision and exclusivity often associated with corporate branding. As a nod to Scotland's storied past, the Kinloch Anderson Hunting Tartan is a testament to the country's enduring love affair with nature and tradition.

name: Kinloch Anderson (personal) Kinloch of Loch Awe
description: Kinloch of Loch Awe, a bespoke Name tartan woven with love for the union of Alan Kinloch and Claire Hardy, stands as a testament to the profound connection between Scotland's rugged landscapes and the families who call them home. Described by renowned designer Kinloch Anderson of Edinburgh, this unique tartan proudly wears its 'of Loch Awe' suffix, signifying a deep affection for the surrounding glen that bore witness to the couple's special day. As an exclusive family tartan, access is restricted to those with a direct bloodline link to Alan Kinloch and Claire Hardy, underscoring the profound personal significance of this heritage fabric. This rare and intimate design embodies the time-honoured tradition of Scottish clan weaves, where each thread tells a story of love, loyalty, and place, forever woven into the very fabric of Scotland's storied past.

name: Kinmount Whisky
description: The Virginia Quadricentennial tartan is a poignant tribute to the enduring legacy of the first European settlers who arrived in America at Jamestown in 1607. Designed by David McGill, International Tartans, this commemorative tartan was specially created to celebrate the quadricentenary anniversary of that historic event. With its carefully chosen colours and intricate patterns, the Virginia Quadricentennial tartan pays homage to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's American diaspora. Originally developed to promote a range of products from Kinmount Scotch Whisky in 2003, this unique tartan has since been granted official recognition by the State of Virginia, bearing testament to its enduring significance as a symbol of state pride and civic honour. With the designer's consent, anyone wishing to wear or use this tartan may do so, making it an exclusive and special choice for those who wish to pay tribute to America's founding fathers and the enduring bond between Scotland and her colonies.

name: Kinnaird #2
description: The Kinnaird tartan, created by Laird Portch in 1984, is a fashion-inspired masterpiece that embodies the spirit of Scottish heritage and tradition. This striking tartan pattern, categorised as a Fashion tartan, was designed to be worn with pride on formal occasions, symbolising elegance and sophistication. While its origins may be rooted in fashion, this tartan holds deep cultural significance, evoking the rich history and traditions of Scotland's clans. The Kinnaird tartan is proudly associated with the Kinnaird family, whose legacy is woven into the very fabric of Scottish identity. With its unique and intricate design, this tartan is a testament to Laird Portch's skill as a textile designer, and its beauty is enhanced by its presence in the renowned Johnston Collection, ensuring its significance will be cherished for generations to come.

name: Kinnaird [default]
description: The Kinnaird tartan is a rich and storied Scottish heritage, woven into existence by Keith Lumsden in celebration of the Kinnaird family legacy. This Clan tartan, designated for the esteemed Kinnaird lineage, holds great honour among Scottish clansmen, serving as a symbol of pride and identity. The design's intricate patterns weave together shades of blue, green, yellow, red, and black, echoing the rugged beauty of Scotland's rolling hills and heather-clad moors. With no restrictions in place, this tartan is open to all who wish to pay tribute to its noble heritage, making it an accessible yet distinctive addition to any collection. As a testament to Scotland's enduring traditions, the Kinnaird tartan stands as a vibrant reminder of the nation's storied past and the timeless bonds of family and clan.

name: Kinnison [default]
description: The Kinnieson tartan is a deeply personal and intimate weaving, registered by J McGregor-Hastie from his esteemed McGregor-Hastie Collection. Originally intended as a family tartan for the Kinnieson clan, its significance lies not only in its clan connections but also in its "do not pass on" notation, suggesting a deep-seated familial bond between the designer and the recipient of this unique tartan. As such, it is a testament to the complex web of Scottish heritage and tradition, where the threads of family history and personal loyalty are intricately woven together. With no reversal permitted, this non-reversing tartan becomes an intimate reflection of its owner's heritage, making it a treasured family heirloom for generations to come.

name: Kinnoull [default]
description: The Kinnoull tartan is a quintessential example of Scottish heritage and tradition, hailing from the esteemed family of MacPhersons of Kinnoull, who proudly bear its distinctive pattern as their own. Registered in 1819 by the skilled designers at Wilsons of Bannockburn, this tartan is part of a series that showcases the company's mastery of traditional Scottish weaving. With its subtle nuances and intricate colourwork, the Kinnoull tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the MacPherson clan, whose name has become synonymous with Scottish bravery and loyalty. This prestigious family tartan holds great honour among those who wear it, serving as a symbol of pride and connection to their ancestral heritage.

name: Kinross District
description: The Kinross tartan, created by renowned textile designers at Brunschwig & Fils, is a captivating fashion tartan with a rich history shrouded in mystery. Originally conceived during a research trip to Britain, the name "Kinross" has been linked to the city of Kinross in Scotland, but its origins remain uncertain - was it a genuine nod to Scottish heritage or a clever marketing ploy? This enigmatic tartan is now associated with interior decorators' drapery fabrics, yet its beauty and charm transcend functional use. With its distinctive sett and subtle colour palette, the Kinross tartan embodies the timeless essence of Scottish tradition, evoking images of rolling hills, crisp lochs, and warm hospitality - a testament to the enduring allure of Scottish culture and craftsmanship.

name: Kinross Family;
description: The Kinross #2 tartan is a deeply rooted and storied heritage pattern, born from the proud history of the Kinross family, whose lineage stretches back through the centuries in Scotland. This distinctive tartan, registered in 1981, holds a special significance for all those bearing the name, serving as a testament to their connection to this ancient Scottish clan. As part of the Clan category, the Kinross #2 tartan is reserved exclusively for members of the Kinross family, allowing them to proudly wear their heritage on their sleeves. With its rich colours and intricate design, this tartan embodies the tradition and culture of Scotland's historic clans, evoking images of rugged landscapes, centuries-old castles, and a deep sense of community and kinship among those who bear it.

name: Kintail Dress
description: The Kintail Dress tartan, designed by the esteemed Jedburgh Woollen Mill, is a quintessential fashion tartan that embodies the essence of Scotland's rich heritage. Registration notes reveal that this distinctive pattern was carefully crafted to evoke the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands, particularly the majestic Kintail mountain range. As a Fashion tartan, it is intended for use in clothing and textiles, allowing wearers to proudly showcase their connection to Scotland's iconic landscape. With its unique colour palette and intricate weaving, this tartan design is sure to make a statement, honouring the country's storied past while adding a touch of modern flair to any garment or accessory.

name: Kintore
description: The Kintore tartan, born from the threads of Scotland's rich heritage in 1988, is a timeless fashion icon that weaves together the country's storied past with modern elegance. Registered at Spean Bridge, Pitlochry, this striking pattern is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish tradition and culture. As a Fashion tartan, Kintore is designed to make a statement on the catwalk or in everyday life, its bold hues and intricate texture evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. With no restrictions placed upon it by the registration notes, the Kintore tartan is free to be interpreted and reimagined by designers and enthusiasts alike, ensuring its continued relevance and appeal for generations to come.

name: Kintyre
description: The Kintyre tartan, expertly woven by the esteemed Edinburgh Woollen Mill, is a stylish and iconic fashion tartan that embodies the rugged beauty of Scotland's southwest coast. Named after the Kintyre Peninsula in Argyll, where the sun-kissed landscapes meet the rolling hills of the Highlands, this vibrant design reflects the region's rich cultural heritage. As a Fashion tartan, the Kintyre is designed to be worn with pride, adding a dash of Scottish flair to any outfit. With its characteristic blues and greens evoking the sea-worn coastline, and subtle touches of red and yellow reminiscent of heather-covered moors, this tartan exudes the warmth and hospitality that Scotland is renowned for. While no longer subject to the strict registration processes of the past, the Kintyre remains a testament to Scotland's enduring textile traditions and the timeless appeal of traditional Scottish design.

name: Kipp
description: The Kipp tartan is a captivating personal design that holds deep significance for its creator, Annette Bair Brown. Registered as a Name tartan, it's a testament to the enduring power of personal heritage in Scottish culture. According to the Society's notes, the name 'Kipp' is thought to be derived from old Scots, potentially translating to 'shoulder' or 'protruding land from a hill', evoking images of rugged hillsides and rolling moors. This tartan design proudly wears its meaning on its sleeve, woven into every subtle hue and texture that reflects the unique story behind its creation. With its roots firmly planted in Scottish tradition, the Kipp tartan is a heartfelt tribute to the land and people that have shaped its maker's identity.

name: Kirk [default]
description: The Kirk tartan is a storied family heirloom, its intricate patterns woven from threads of tradition and heritage. Designed by Dr Philip D Smith, this Clan tartan is a testament to the esteemed Maxwell clan, with subtle nods to its eponymous namesakes, Gilbert and Nancy Kirk. Intended as a unifying thread for families bearing the name Kirk, this tartan design was submitted to the Scottish Tartans Authority in recognition of its significance. Now preserved in the Johnston Collection, the Kirk tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich history and cultural heritage, its deep blue-green hues evoking the misty hills and rugged landscapes that have shaped the country's storied past.

name: Kirk in the Hills Michigan
description: The Kirk in the Hills tartan is a poignant commemorative design that weaves together the rich heritage of Scotland's architectural legacy with the history of a Michigan Presbyterian church. Commissioned by Sharon Fullerton, Grist, to celebrate the 50th anniversary of the foundation of the Kirk in the Hills, this distinctive tartan pays tribute to Melrose Abbey, one of Scotland's most iconic abbeys. The Kirk tartan is specifically associated with the church itself, rather than its surname, serving as a testament to the enduring connection between Scottish tradition and American heritage. With its carefully crafted colours and subtle nuances, this commemorative tartan invites wearers to honour the rich cultural legacy that has brought people together across centuries and continents.

name: Kirk Wynd (St Andrews) personal; Pride of Fife
description: The Al-Fadhli tartan is a unique and captivating Name tartan, carefully woven by Mike King for Meshall Al-Fadhli himself. This distinctive design proudly incorporates the colours of Kuwait's flag - white, green, and red - within its intricate pattern, reflecting Meshall's national heritage. The result is a tartan that not only represents an individual's identity but also pays homage to their country of origin. As a Name tartan, the Al-Fadhli has been meticulously crafted to evoke a sense of family tradition and legacy, with each carefully considered thread telling the story of Meshall's cultural roots. With its subtle yet striking colour palette, this tartan design is sure to hold great significance for anyone who wears it, serving as a tangible connection to Meshall's Kuwaiti heritage and personal history.

name: Kirkton
description: The Kirkton tartan, designed by Laird Portch, is a vibrant and modern fashion tartan that embodies the spirit of Scottish heritage. This striking pattern has been registered in the Johnston Collection, a testament to its enduring appeal and distinctive character. By its classification as a Fashion tartan, Kirkton is part of a long tradition of textile design inspired by Scotland's rich cultural heritage. While no exact thread count is specified, it can be inferred that the original sample features half the number of threads with single white threads woven throughout, adding an extra layer of intricacy to this already engaging design. As such, this tartan holds great favour among fashion enthusiasts and those seeking a unique addition to their wardrobe, while also paying homage to Scotland's storied past through its carefully crafted colour palette and traditional weaving techniques.

name: Kirtle
description: The Kirtle tartan is a timeless fashion favourite, born from the heritage of Scotland's storied textile traditions. Designed by Jedburgh Woollen Mill, this striking fabric pattern draws inspiration from the Stewart sett, a revered part of Scottish tartan lore. As a Fashion tartan, the Kirtle design has been crafted to be versatile and adaptable, making it an ideal choice for clothing and accessories that demand elegance and sophistication. With its carefully considered colour palette and precise sett, this tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, evoking images of traditional Scottish dress worn with pride by generations past. Sampled in the esteemed Johnston Collection, the Kirtle tartan stands as a proud representative of Scottish craftsmanship, awaiting interpretation and celebration by those who appreciate its beauty and significance.

name: Knights Breton
description: The Knights Breton tartan is a majestic fashion design that pays tribute to the storied chivalry of Breton heritage. Registered by renowned designer Richard Duclos, this distinctive tartan is inspired by the rich history of Brittany's 9 counties and its ancient emblem, the Kroaz Du (Black Cross). The colour palette cleverly weaves together symbolic hues, echoing the regions that comprise this historic province in north-western France. By honouring Breton chivalry, the Knights Breton tartan embodies a proud tradition of courage, loyalty, and cultural identity, evoking the rugged beauty and rich heritage of this Celtic region.

name: Knights Templar Dress
description: The Knights Templar Dress tartan is a striking Corporate design that embodies the revered legacy of one of history's most influential military orders. Registered in recognition of its association with the OSMTH - SMOTJ Kinghts Templar, this distinctive tartan pattern pays homage to the chivalrous traditions of the Knights Templar, whose grand Priory once spanned the Holy Lands. Inspired by Gordon Nicolson's design, this tartan is imbued with a sense of nobility and mystique, recalling the ancient rituals and codes of conduct that defined the order's storied history. While its black pivot threadcount may be inconsistent, the tartan's significance endures, a testament to the enduring spirit of the Knights Templar - an esteemed emblem of corporate identity for those who seek to evoke the grandeur and distinction of this storied institution.

name:
Knights Templar Grand Priory
[AKA] Fife & Kinross
description: The Knights Templar - Grand Priory corporate tartan is a majestic blend of rich, earthy tones and subtle symbolism, reflecting the medieval heritage and chivalrous traditions of one of history's most revered military orders. Designated as a corporate tartan, it was created to commemorate the values of leadership, loyalty, and community that define successful business partnerships. Drawing inspiration from the distinctive Red Galloway sett, with its intricate overchecks, this vibrant design embodies the Knights Templar's proud history and noble ethos. Named after one of Scotland's most storied clans, the tartan is steeped in tradition and authenticity, having been registered by Messrs Mackie, Kelly, and Devlin, with technical input from Strathmore Woollen Ltd. Its intricate, woven pattern makes it a striking choice for corporate attire, signifying strength, unity, and an unwavering commitment to excellence.

name: Knights Templar Hunting
description: The Knights Templar Hunting tartan is an iconic corporate design that embodies the esteemed heritage of Scotland's most revered medieval military order, the Knights Templar. Named after their historical association with hunting, this distinguished tartan is reserved for the Magistral Grand Priory of the Holy Lands - a testament to the Order's enduring legacy.
