Designed by renowned Scottish weaver, Gordon Nicolson, this tartan is not only a symbol of corporate identity but also an ode to Scotland's rich history and tradition of chivalry. As an official hunting tartan, it commands respect and reverence, its intricate pattern woven with stories of adventure, bravery, and loyalty. For those privileged to wear this tartan, the Knights Templar Hunting design serves as a badge of honour, connecting them to a storied past that continues to inspire and unite.

name: Knights Templar International
description: The Scottish Knights Templar International tartan, designed by Capt. T.S. Davidson, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's most revered chivalric order. As a Corporate tartan, it serves as a symbol of unity and distinction for companies and organisations that draw inspiration from this storied tradition. The registration notes reveal its rich history, dating back to 1998 when it was ratified by the Grand Conclave of Militi Scotia S.M.O.J in Perth. With its motto OSMTH, "Ordo Supremus Militaris Templi Hierosolymitani" (Order of the Supreme Military Temple of Jerusalem), this tartan design pays homage to the Knights Templar's ancient values of chivalry and martial prowess. Its adoption is reserved exclusively for those who hold a special honour, underscoring its exclusivity and prestige within the world of Scottish heritage and corporate identity.

name:
Knights Templar of Scotland
[AKA] Militi Templi Scotia
description: The Scottish Knights Templar Militi Templi Scotia tartan is a prestigious Corporate design, carefully crafted by Captain T.S. Davidson in 1978. This majestic pattern represents a long-forgotten Order of Chivalry, dedicated to serving God and Scotland. According to the registration notes, the correct name for this tartan is Scottish Knights Templar of Militi Templi Scotia, one of three similar designs created by Davidson, all of which were ratified and approved by the Grand Conclave of the Militi Scotia S.M.O.T.J in Perth in 1998. This unique tartan is steeped in history and tradition, its subtle variations reflecting the 'branches' of the Order that have adopted it over time. As a symbol of Scottish heritage and chivalry, this tartan design holds great significance for those who wear it with honour, paying tribute to the esteemed Order of the Knights Templar that inspired it.

name: Knights Templar St Andrews
description: The Scottish Knights Templar St Andrews tartan is a prestigious corporate tartan that embodies the noble values of chivalry and loyalty, forged in the heartland of Scotland. Designed by Captain T.S. Davidson in 1978, this distinctive pattern is one of three variations created for the Scottish Knights Templar of Militi Scotia, St Andrews Order of Chivalry, which serves God and Scotland. The tartan's subtle differences reflect the varying branches of the order, signifying distinct affiliations with the esteemed organisation. With its rich history and strong roots in Scottish heritage, this tartan is reserved for those who bear honour and distinction, and its distinctive design is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Knights Templar of Scotland, whose motto "Defendendo et Serviendo" (Defending and Serving) continues to inspire loyalty and devotion.

name: Knox #2
description: Knox #2 is a richly woven tapestry of Scottish heritage, borne from the esteemed lineage of Clan Knox. This family tartan, registered in 1999, has been immortalised through various mediums, including its first recorded appearance on a tea towel at Convergence 1998. The design's authenticity was later substantiated by Johnston/Smith's 'Tartans' publication in 1999, cementing its place within the realm of traditional Scottish textiles. Characterised by subtle yet striking interplay between muted earth tones and deeper, richer hues, Knox #2 embodies the very essence of Scotland's storied past. This meticulously crafted tartan not only serves as a symbol of familial honour but also pays homage to the rich cultural traditions that have shaped Scotland's identity over centuries.

name: Komen Rose Plaid
description: The Walk the Walk tartan, designed by Pendleton Woolen Mills, embodies the spirit of determination and charity that has become synonymous with the Edinburgh MoonWalk marathon. Founded in 2005 by Nina Barough CBE, a pioneering campaigner against breast cancer, this corporate tartan reflects the organisation's unwavering dedication to raising funds and awareness for this critical cause. With its bold colour palette, the Walk the Walk tartan is a powerful symbol of endurance and resilience, echoing the 26.2 miles traversed by marathon runners across the globe. Its origins in Nina Barough's personal journey, from wearing a decorated bra during her first New York Marathon in 1996 to founding a charity that has raised over £4 million to date, add depth and meaning to this remarkable tartan, one that honours both the human spirit and the vital work of the Walk the Walk charity.

name: Kormylo
description: The Kormylo tartan is a distinctive Name tartan, woven with precision to commemorate Mr Peter Kormylo's esteemed career as Head Teacher at Loreburne Primary School in Dumfries. Designed by Thomas K Gemmell, a local weaver from Dumfries, this unique tartan was created as a personal tribute to Mr Kormylo, honouring his dedication and years of service before he departed for a new role under the shadow of Stirling Castle. Weaving is credited to D C Dalgliesh of Selkirk, further highlighting the rich heritage of Scotland's tartan-making tradition. This special Name tartan now holds significance not only as a family heirloom but also as a testament to Mr Kormylo's enduring legacy and connection to his community, showcasing the intricate bond between Scottish heritage, personal stories, and traditional craftsmanship.

name: Kozlosky Artifact
description: The Kozlosky tartan is a rare and fascinating example of a personal name tartan, imbued with the history and cultural significance of its owner's life. Designed by Dr D.G. Teall for Joseph Kozlosky, who wore it as a kilt before gifting it to the Scottish Tartans Society, this tartan holds a unique place in Scotland's heritage. Though Mr Kozlosky later requested its return, the society wisely chose to retain the fabric, acknowledging its importance as an integral part of Scotland's cultural identity. The registration notes reveal that the tartan has undergone slight modifications, including the addition of pink hues, which should be rendered even more vibrant. This fireproof cotton fabric is a testament to the resourcefulness and resilience of Scottish weavers, ensuring that this treasured tartan remains a vital part of Scotland's rich heritage for generations to come.

name: KPMG
description: The KPMG tartan is an iconic corporate design, carefully crafted by House of Edgar's in-house designer, Polly Wittering, to reflect the esteemed reputation of the global accounting firm, KPMG. This distinctly tailored pattern is rooted in tradition, drawing inspiration from Scotland's rich heritage and textile history. As a Corporate tartan, it has been registered for use by professional services firms like KPMG, signifying a sense of professionalism and authority. Originally designed to pay tribute to the firm's international presence, this intricate design now holds significance as a visual identifier for businesses that bear its name. Its technical characteristics have been carefully considered to meet the precise specifications required for corporate tartan use, ensuring a cohesive brand image while respecting the traditions of Scottish textile art.

name: Kremlin Zoria
description: The Kremlin Zoria tartan is a striking corporate design that embodies the spirit of international diplomacy and cultural exchange. Created by renowned textile experts at Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan was specifically commissioned for Visit Scotland to commemorate the first Scottish Tattoo held in the historic Kremlin walls of Moscow. As a symbol of goodwill and friendship between nations, the Kremlin Zoria tartan weaves together rich threads of Scottish heritage and international collaboration, its intricate patterns evoking the grandeur of Russia's iconic landmark. This unique design is a testament to the enduring power of tartan as a unifying force, transcending borders and cultures to bring people together in celebration of shared values and traditions.

name: Kungsholmen Snooker
description: The Kungsholmen Snooker tartan is a unique and striking corporate design that brings the thrilling world of snooker to life in a bold and modern way. Created by Anna Czarnecki, this distinctive pattern represents the colours of the iconic snooker balls - red, yellow, green, brown, blue, pink, black, and white - in a harmonious arrangement that exudes energy and dynamism. As specified by the House of Tartan in Comrie, Perthshire, the threadcount is meticulously calculated to reflect the maximum points achievable in a break with just one pink ball, adding an extra layer of depth and meaning to this visually striking design. With its corporate roots, the Kungsholmen Snooker tartan would be perfect for businesses that share a passion for the sport or its rich cultural heritage, making it a unique and memorable choice for everything from bespoke suits to corporate wear.

name: Kyle Blue
description: The Kyle (Blue) tartan is a proud embodiment of Scottish heritage, originating from the Clan Kyle family. Its distinctive dark blue hue, reminiscent of a Highland morning after a gentle drizzle, sets the tone for a rich tapestry of tradition and history. With its specific overcheck in green, as noted by Peter MacDonald, this tartan design pays homage to the authentic colours of the Highlands, evoking images of rugged landscapes and loyal families bound together by blood and kinship. Registered in the 1980s, this tartan was gifted to Phil Smith by Matt Grady of The Wee Shoppe in North Carolina, a nod to the global reach and enduring appeal of Scottish culture. As a Clan tartan, the Kyle (Blue) represents the honourable legacy of its bearers, weaving together past, present, and future with every carefully woven thread.

name: Kyle Green
description: The Kyle (Green) tartan is a quintessential representation of Scottish heritage, evoking the rolling hills and windswept landscapes of the Carrick district in Ayrshire. With its distinctive green hue, this tartan pays homage to the region's rich history and the storied clan that bore its name. According to Peter MacDonald, who has painstakingly preserved the design in its traditional form, the Kyle (Green) is a true testament to Scotland's rich tapestry of culture and tradition. As a Clan tartan, it holds deep significance for families with Scottish roots, serving as a proud symbol of their connection to the land and their ancestors' heritage. With no restrictions on its use, this beautiful tartan invites wearers to channel the rugged beauty and timeless spirit of Scotland's finest districts.

name: Lachine Emblematic
description: The Lachine tartan, named after the historic district in Quebec where it originated, is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Montreal's trading past. This intricate District tartan was carefully crafted by the skilled weavers of the Lachine Guild of Weavers, drawing inspiration from the city's own coat of arms colours. Originally produced for use on traditional Quebecois textiles, including woolen blankets and kilts, this complex asymmetric sett is a classic example of the region's unique weaving traditions. Strategically situated on Lake Saint-Louis, which connected Montreal to the fur trade routes, Lachine's history as a hub of commerce and cultural exchange is woven into every thread of its design, making it a meaningful tribute to the city's proud heritage.

name: Lachine Historic
description: The Lachine Historic tartan, woven by the skilled hands of the Lachine Guild of Weavers, proudly wears its heritage as an emblematic tartan of the Guilde des Tisserandes de Lachine, a testament to the city's rich history as an early fur trading centre in Quebec. This distinctive asymmetric sett utilises traditional 'city colours', evoking the region's cultural significance and its proximity to the island of Montreal on Lake Saint-Louis. Although its origins are shrouded in mystery, the Lachine Historic tartan is undeniably significant, serving as a tribute to this pivotal moment in Quebec's development. As a District tartan, it holds a special place within the world of Scottish heritage, connecting generations to the land and people that inspired its creation.

name: Lady Boys of Bangkok
description: This striking Corporate tartan, lovingly crafted by renowned Scottish weavers Gordon Nicolson Kiltmakers, is an unexpected nod to the vibrant city of Bangkok and its captivating dance troupe, The Lady Boys of Bangkok. Registration notes reveal a fascinating history - in 2009, these talented performers took to the Edinburgh Fringe stage, showcasing their mesmerising routines in kilts adorned with this very tartan. Characterised by bold blues and greens, this tartan's dynamic colour palette is reminiscent of the exotic locales it paid homage to. As a testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage and its ability to seamlessly blend tradition with global inspiration, this unique Corporate tartan serves as a celebration of artistic expression and cross-cultural exchange.

name: Ladybird
description: The Ladybird tartan, a vibrant and charming creation by renowned Scottish textile expert Dawn Robson-Bell for Lochcarron of Scotland, is an enchanting addition to the world of fashion tartans. Inspired by the traditional Carrick design, Ladybird boasts a striking palette of blues, greens, and yellows, carefully balanced to evoke the nostalgic charm of a sun-kissed summer's day in Scotland. Originally registered as a fashion tartan in 1997, this dynamic design is still cherished for its modern twist on classic Scottish heritage, despite requiring colour adjustments to meet precise requirements. As part of Lochcarron's esteemed legacy, Ladybird has taken its place within the Johnston Collection, a testament to the enduring appeal of Scotland's most iconic textiles and the boundless creativity of Scottish designers.

name: Laggen Dress
description: The Laggen Dress tartan is a stylish and timeless fashion design, evoking the rich heritage of Scotland's textile tradition. Registered by Jedburgh Woollen Mill, this captivating pattern holds a place in the Johnston Collection, a treasured repository of Scottish tartans. The Laggen Dress tartan's unique blend of subtle colours and intricate sett creates a visually striking effect, perfect for adding a touch of Scottish flair to any outfit. With its status as a Fashion tartan, the Laggen Dress is designed to make a statement on the catwalk or in everyday wear, while also respecting the cultural significance of this revered textile tradition.

name: Lagrande
description: The Lagrande tartan, designed by renowned fashion designer Highland Queen, is a vibrant and dynamic fabric that embodies the spirit of modern Scotland. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority in 1972, this Fashion category tartan was created to add a touch of glamour to everyday wear. With its distinctive colour palette, which features a range of blues, greens, and yellows, Lagrande evokes the stunning natural landscapes of the Scottish Highlands. Though originally intended for fashion purposes, this tartan also holds significance within the clan system, albeit as a distinct and individual name that doesn't necessarily tie to an established clan heritage.

name: Laidlaw's Highland Drovers
description: Laidlaw's Highland Drovers is a quintessential Corporate tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's rural pastures. Originally designed for Carron Valley Formal Dress, a respected Highland dress hire business based in Central Scotland, this tartan celebrates the traditional attire of the drovers who once roamed these same glens and valleys, herding cattle to market. The subtle, muted colour palette - comprising blues, greens, and browns - evokes the rolling hills and heather-covered moors that cradled the daily lives of these hardy men. While the exact designer remains unknown, the tartan's design is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's rural traditions, making it an ideal choice for businesses and individuals who seek to tap into this storied heritage through their brand identity.

name:
Laing of Archiestown [default]
[AKA] Laing of Archiestown
description: The Laing of Archiestown tartan is a richly woven testament to the enduring heritage of Scotland's clans, with roots dating back to 1767 when John Laing first wove it in his workshop at Archiestown, Morayshire. Now preserved by the Scottish Tartans Society, this intricate design was donated by William Donald Laing of Queensland, Australia in 1996, following its acquisition from Mr Jack Garden's family in 1961. Notably, the dark line within the centre of the red band remains a mystery, with its true hue either blue or black - an enigmatic detail that adds to the tartan's allure. This Clan tartan is a treasured symbol of the Laing family's legacy and connection to their ancestral home, Archiestown, where William's great-great-grandfather once resided in his shop during the 1810 census, underscoring the enduring bond between family history and Scotland's storied past.

name: Laing [default]
description: The Laing tartan is a poignant tribute to the enduring legacy of Clan Laing, whose heritage spans centuries and continents. Weaved with reverence for its ancestors' traditions, this distinctive pattern is rooted in the remarkable story of George Henry Laing, who brought his great-grandfather's sett from Scotland to North Carolina and eventually settled in Texas, where it lay undisturbed beneath a Georgia cemetery until its recovery. This authentic Clan tartan, carefully reconstructed from remnants found on a grave site, now proudly carries the name and legacy of the Laing family, a testament to their unbroken connection with Scottish heritage.

name: Laird
description: The Laird Abdullah tartan is a deeply personal tribute to love and heritage, woven by its creator Eve Louisa, Laird of the family bearing the name. Registered in 2007, this distinctive Name tartan commemorates the union of Asif Abdullah and Eve Louisa Laird on their special day six years prior. The design skillfully blends traditional Scottish colourwork with modern flair, showcasing a thoughtful juxtaposition of contemporary hues against timeless motifs. This unique tartan bears testament to the blending of cultures and traditions that occur when two worlds come together in matrimony, reflecting the enduring spirit of family and community that lies at the heart of Scotland's rich heritage.

name: Lake Ainslie
description: The Lake Ainslie Heritage tartan is a poignant tribute to Cape Breton's rich history, woven from the threads of tradition and resilience. Designed by Verna MacMillan in 1985, this District tartan tells the story of the region's Scottish settlers who bravely navigated the harsh winters and unforgiving landscapes to establish their new home. The subtle nuances of blue, white, gold, red, green, and beige evoke the majestic beauty of Cape Breton's lakes, mountains, beaches, and forests. Each thread is imbued with a sense of pride and strength, recalling the settlers' unwavering faith and perseverance in the face of adversity. As this tartan weaves together the past and present, it honours the heritage of those who came before, while paying testament to the enduring spirit that continues to shape the identity of this special region.

name: Laksaa Manx
description: The Laksaa (Manx) fashion tartan, woven by St. George's Woollen Mills, proudly showcases the rich heritage of the Isle of Man, with its subtle nuances mirroring the island's unique cultural identity. This vibrant yet understated design is deeply rooted in Manx tradition, paying homage to the historic village of Laxey, whose name translates to "Lakes" in the Manx language. As a fashion tartan, Laksaa embodies the essence of the Isle of Man's rich textile history, its colours and patterns expertly woven together to evoke the island's stunning landscapes and strong community spirit. With no restrictions on usage, this stunning tartan invites wearers to celebrate their connection to the Isle of Man and its storied past.

name: Lalage
description: Lalage, a personal tartan created by renowned Scottish weavers at Lochcarron, is a vibrant celebration of its wearer's diverse heritage and passions. This unique Name tartan tells the story of Jane & Dominic Keogh's bespoke request for a tartan that would reflect their beloved pet, Lalage, alongside their love for Scotland and New Zealand. The design skillfully weaves together black and white hues, reminiscent of loyal companionship, with rich purples, pinks, and greens evoking the rugged landscapes of Scotland and the natural beauty of New Zealand. As a personal tartan, Lalage serves as a treasured family heirloom, symbolising the wearer's strong connections to their ancestry, pets, and travels. Its distinctive colour palette makes it an extraordinary addition to any wardrobe, proudly showcasing its individuality and cultural significance within Scottish heritage.

name: Lamont Dress
description: The Lamont Dress tartan is a timeless and elegant fashion choice, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's finest clan families. Registration notes indicate that this vibrant design was inspired by Clan Lamont, evoking the proud history and tradition of the esteemed Highland family. The swatch, gifted to MacIsaac of Nova Scotia, serves as a testament to the tartan's origins, connecting its wearer to a storied legacy. While the designer remains anonymous, their skillful interpretation of traditional Scottish design ensures that this tartan continues to make a statement on the catwalk and in fashion circles. With its roots firmly planted in Scotland's cultural heritage, the Lamont Dress tartan is a stunning choice for those seeking to add a touch of authentic Highland flair to their wardrobe.

name: Lamont Heather
description: The Lamont Heather corporate tartan is a vibrant tribute to Scotland's rugged landscape, evoking the wild beauty of heather-clad moors under which the historic city of Edinburgh lies. Inspired by Lochcarron of Scotland's interpretation of the classic Lamont Sporrans pattern from 1998, this Corporate tartan weaves together rich threads of blue and green hues, recalling the rolling hills and misty lochs that have long fascinated Scottish hearts. With its heritage firmly rooted in the country's storied past, the Lamont Heather tartan offers a modern take on traditional design, one that effortlessly blends heritage with contemporary flair - an apt reflection of Scotland's enduring spirit of innovation and tradition.

name: Lamont [default]
description: The Lamont tartan is a rich and storied legacy of Scotland's clan heritage, meticulously crafted by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1817. Its origins are woven into the fabric of history, having been carefully recorded by W & A Smith in their seminal work 'The Clan and Family Tartans of Scotland' in 1850. The registration notes attest to its authenticity, bearing witness to a specimen sealed in the Highland Society of London Collection by the chief, Lamont of Lamont, on the very same year. This tartan is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition, its intricate pattern reflecting the family's proud history and identity. As a Clan tartan, it holds significant cultural and symbolic value, paying homage to the esteemed House of Lamont, whose name has been etched into Scotland's annals for generations.

name: Lanark
description: The Lanark fashion tartan, designed by Tam-o-Shanter Inn, is a vibrant and modern interpretation of traditional Scottish heritage. Originally registered in California from 1950 to 1965, this Fraser modification has been reclassified as a District tartan, indicating its unique place within the world of Scottish tartans. With roots in the United States, but born out of Scottish tradition, Lanark reflects the cultural exchange and evolution that has shaped the art of tartan-making over time. As a fashion tartan, it is designed to be worn with pride, evoking the history and symbolism of Scotland's rich textile heritage, from its rugged landscapes to its warm and welcoming people. Its distinctive pattern, born of innovation and creativity, joins the ranks of other iconic Scottish tartans, adding a touch of West Coast flair to any outfit.

name: Lanark Highlands District
description: The Lanark Highlands tartan is a striking representation of the district's idyllic rural landscape, woven with eight colours that evoke the rolling hills, dense forests, and sparkling waterways of this majestic township in eastern Canada. As a District tartan, it proudly wears the badge of its heritage as a sparsely populated region of breathtaking beauty, where the tranquility of nature is offset by the warmth of community life. With its population density of less than 5 persons per square kilometre, the Lanark Highlands tartan serves as a testament to the area's unique character and charm, reflecting the intricate balance between wilderness and human settlement that defines this enchanting region. Designed by Susi Reinink, this distinctive tartan is an honour to the people of Lanark Highlands, who cherish their connection to the land and its storied history.

name: Land's End Blue
description: Land's End Blue, a fashion tartan born from the discerning eye of Fiona Hird, is a testament to the enduring allure of Scottish heritage in modern style. Originally commissioned by US mail order house Land's End, this striking blue-and-green pattern was carefully selected as the winning design from the Johnston Collection, a prestigious repository of Scotland's finest tartans. Hired to weave the fabric at Lochcarron, one of Scotland's most renowned mills, Fiona Hird's vision has resulted in a tartan that exudes comfort and sophistication. This fashion tartan is a celebration of Scotland's rich textile traditions, its colours evoking the rugged beauty of the country's coastlines and the tranquil majesty of the lochs. By wearing Land's End Blue, one becomes part of a long-standing tradition of embracing Scottish heritage in modern fashion, a connection to the nation's storied past that is as stylish as it is timeless.

name: Land's End Camel
description: The Land's End Camel tartan is a striking Fashion tartan that boasts a palette of earthy tones, evoking the rugged beauty of the UK's westernmost tip. Designed by Fiona Hird, a renowned British textile expert, this captivating pattern weaves together shades of camel, moss, and heather, creating a timeless design that embodies the quintessential English landscape. Originally created for Land's End - a US mail order house - to appeal to its American customers, this tartan has since become a staple in British fashion, effortlessly blending traditional Scottish heritage with modern style. Its registration notes reveal the designer's vision, while its restrictions remain unchanged, ensuring that this beloved design remains an authentic representation of Scottish textile tradition.

name: Land's End Maroon
description: The Land's End Maroon is a vibrant fashion tartan, carefully crafted to evoke the warmth and energy of Scotland's iconic west coast. Designed by renowned textile artist Fiona Hird, this striking pattern is a celebration of traditional Scottish heritage with a modern twist. Originally registered for use in the USA by Oddy Ladies' Wear for Land's End, a popular mail order house at the time, the tartan's purpose was to add a touch of quintessential British charm to garments and accessories. With its distinctive deep maroon hue and intricate sett, this tartan is perfect for those looking to add a splash of Scottish style to their wardrobe, while also paying tribute to the country's rich cultural heritage.

name: Lang of Sherbrooke
description: The Lang of Sherbrooke tartan is a unique and captivating heritage fabric, woven with deep roots in Scottish tradition yet born in the picturesque Dandenong Ranges of Victoria, Australia. Designed by Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts for the esteemed family of Lang of Sherbrooke Forest, this name tartan proudly showcases the town's history and connection to the Scottish Highlands. With its intricate sett and carefully chosen colours, the Lang of Sherbrooke tartan embodies a blend of British and Australian heritage, reflecting the family's Scottish ancestry while also acknowledging their life in Australia. The subtle nuances of the design, including the earlier use of dull yellow before being reworked into gold in 2007, demonstrate the craftsmanship and attention to detail that has gone into preserving this special family tartan.

name: Lang [default]
description: The Cathro tartan is a timeless and storied Scottish fabric with roots deeply embedded in the region of Strathcathro, Angus. Registered by its renowned designer Robert S Cathro, this tartan has been woven for generations to bear the name of those who proudly claim descent from this esteemed locality. As a Name tartan, it holds a special place among the clan and family affiliations that have defined Scotland's rich heritage. While originally intended for display purposes by individuals with the name, some threads of this fabric now serve as a testament to its enduring appeal, woven with an expanded thread count to preserve the intricate patterns for posterity. With its distinctive colour palette evoking the rolling hills and sparkling waters of Angus, the Cathro tartan is a lasting tribute to a proud tradition that continues to inspire weavers and wearers alike.

name: Langhein
description: Langhein, Alex is a distinctive name tartan with deep roots in Scottish heritage. This unique pattern takes its inspiration from the Black Watch sett, drawing upon traditional tartan design principles to create a bold and striking effect. The Langhein, Alex tartan holds personal significance for its designer, Alex Langhein, who has poured their heart and soul into crafting this one-of-a-kind design. As a Name tartan, it is reserved exclusively for use by those with the surname Langhein, making it an important part of family identity and heritage. With its connection to the storied Black Watch tartans, Langhein, Alex proudly wears its historical significance on its sleeve, evoking the bravery and tradition that have defined Scotland's most iconic regiments.

name: Langston [default]
description: The Langston tartan is a storied family heritage woven into the very fabric of tradition. Registered in 1999 by renowned designer Blair Urquhart of House of Tartan, Perthshire, this distinctive pattern bears the Langston name with pride. Commissioned for Michael W. Langston, Captain USN and his American clan lineage, this tartan is a testament to the enduring bonds of family and loyalty that transcend geographical boundaries. With its rich, earthy tones and subtle nuances, the Langston tartan embodies the history and culture of its namesake clan, paying tribute to generations of brave men who have worn the badge with honour. This beautiful tartan now resides in the hearts of the Langston family and all those who wear it with pride, a tangible connection to their ancestral heritage that will be passed down through the ages.

name: Langtree Corporate
description: The Langtree tartan, created in collaboration between renowned fashion house Selfridge's and esteemed textile manufacturer Pendleton Woolen Mills, embodies the spirit of Scottish heritage with its unique blend of Stewart colours. As a Fashion tartan, it has been designed to add a touch of elegance and sophistication to modern attire, while its origins as a colour variation rooted in Scotland's rich history are undeniable. With one 'l' instead of the traditional 'W', the American spelling nods to Pendleton's Oregon roots, reflecting the global exchange that has shaped Scottish tartan traditions over centuries. This stunning design is now available for those seeking to honour their connection to Scotland or simply to incorporate a piece of heritage into their everyday style, all while wearing the unmistakable mark of Langtree tartan.

name: Lanoir
description: The Lanoir tartan, designed by renowned textile artist Highland Queen, is a dynamic and modern fashion tartan that has captured the hearts of many. Registration notes suggest that this versatile pattern was first showcased in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, with an additional sample woven in 1973. With its distinct colour palette and intricate sett, Lanoir embodies the perfect blend of traditional Scottish heritage and contemporary flair. Originally created by Highland Queen for her sportswear label in Toronto in 1972, this fashion tartan has since become a sought-after choice among designers and enthusiasts alike, whose favour it holds due to its striking visual appeal.

name: Lantern, The
description: The Lantern tartan, created by renowned designer Aljean of Vancouver, is a captivating fusion of light and warmth, evoking the soft glow of traditional Scottish lanterns on a winter's night. This Fashion tartan is part of a growing movement to revive and modernise Scotland's rich textile heritage, breathing new life into timeless designs. As part of the Johnston Collection, the Lantern tartan is recognised as an authentic representation of Scottish craftsmanship, its subtle nuances and colour palette reflecting the nation's deep-rooted cultural traditions. This stunning fabric would be perfect for adding a touch of nostalgia and flair to fashion garments, accessories or home decor, carrying with it the honour of Aljean's artistic vision and the enduring spirit of Scotland's tartan legacy.

name: Laois Irish County
description: The Laois County tartan, designed by Polly Wittering for House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., is a rich and evocative representation of Irish heritage at the heart of Scotland's textile tradition. As one of a series of District tartans, this striking design is intended to evoke the history and identity of Laois County in Ireland, rather than being an officially sanctioned District tartan. The colours – deep blues and greens, with subtle hints of gold and red – blend together to create a complex, nuanced pattern that reflects the county's rich cultural heritage. Originally designed as a collection of trade tartans for Macnaughtons of Pitlochry, this tartan now finds its place alongside other Scottish traditions, its unique character a testament to the enduring power of Scottish textile arts to weave together disparate threads of history and identity.

name: Laporte
description: The Laporte tartan, proudly bearing the mark of fashion designer Highland Queen, is a vibrant and dynamic creation born from the rich tapestry of Scotland's heritage. Registered in 1972, this fashion tartan has been woven into the very fabric of style for over four decades, its bold colour palette and intricate pattern evoking the passion and energy of the Highlands. As part of the Fashion category, Laporte is a testament to the enduring influence of Scottish tradition on modern design, with Highland Queen's skilled hands bringing this iconic tartan to life. A rare example of a fashion tartan still in use today, Laporte remains a popular choice among those seeking to add a touch of Highland flair to their wardrobe, its distinctive design a lasting tribute to Scotland's timeless beauty and craftsmanship.

name: Largs District
description: The Largs tartan, born from Sidney Samuels' vision for a District tartan in 1981, has become an integral part of the town's heritage. Officially adopted to reflect its unique identity, this distinctive weave tells the story of a Scottish district's rich history and cultural roots. Although the original design by Samuels specified specific colour codes, it appears that Marcella Castro's handwoven swatch subtly deviates from these guidelines, introducing an air of nuance and character to the traditional tartan pattern. With its adoption in 1981, the Largs tartan has been woven into the fabric of local tradition, evoking a sense of community pride and belonging among its wearers, whether on formal dresses or everyday attire, as it proudly wears its unique thread.

name: Laronde
description: The Largs Dress tartan, registered by Highland Queen Sportswear in 1972, is a stylish and modern fashion design that embodies the vibrant spirit of Scotland's west coast. This Category Fashion tartan was created to evoke the charm of the picturesque seaside town of Largs, with its rich history and breathtaking coastline. The subtle blend of blues, greens, and yellows, reminiscent of a sea-salted breeze on a summer's day, evokes the classic charm of Scottish sportswear while adding a touch of contemporary flair. With no restrictions in place, this tartan is free to be worn with pride by those who love Scotland's heritage and fashion. As part of the prestigious Johnston Collection, held within the Scottish Tartans Authority, this design not only celebrates the town that bears its name but also pays homage to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile tradition.

name: Las Vegas Fire Fighters
description: The Las Vegas Fire Fighters tartan is a vibrant and bold Corporate tartan, inspired by the bravery and camaraderie of the Las Vegas Fire Department's Honor Guard Band. Registered in the UK, this distinctive design was modified from Ramsay (Dalhousie) to reflect the unique character of the US-based Scottish Weaver's work with the fire department. With its bright, fiery hues evoking the excitement and energy of the city that never sleeps, this tartan is a testament to the spirit of service and loyalty embodied by the fire fighters who wear it. The Corporate category reflects the tartan's utilitarian purpose, designed for use in ceremonial, official, or corporate contexts, where its striking colour scheme and expertly woven design will make a lasting impression.

name: Lasting [default]
description: The Lasting tartan, a masterpiece of intricate design, is shrouded in mystery, its origins unclear, despite being identified as a Clan/Family tartan by Wilsons of Bannockburn, one of Scotland's most esteemed tartan weavers. Dating back to 1819, this complex set features an "extremely fine" weave characteristic of the 'Old Superfine Setts' produced by Wilsons, renowned for their exceptional craftsmanship. While its connection to a specific clan or family is disputed, it is evident that this tartan holds a special place in Scottish heritage and tradition, as noted by historian Telford Dunbar in his 1962 book "A History of Highland Dress". As one of the oldest recorded tartans, Lasting stands as a testament to the ingenuity and skill of Scotland's ancient weavers.

name: Latin [default]
description: The Latin tartan is a fascinating example of Scottish heritage and tradition, woven with meticulous attention to detail by renowned designer Ross-Craven. Registration notes reveal that this unique tartan is based on an 18th-century description of the Cameron men's attire from Lochaber, translated into Latin in 1689. The resulting design follows the classic Cameron sett, yet boasts a distinctive alternative colour palette. This Other tartan holds particular significance as a nod to Scotland's rich cultural history, drawing inspiration from a lesser-known chapter in the country's storied past. With its roots firmly planted in tradition, the Latin tartan serves as a captivating tribute to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage and the skillful weavers who bring these timeless designs to life.

name: Lauder Dress
description: The Lauder Dress tartan is a storied family heritage, its origins rooted in the 19th century Scottish clan tradition. As part of Charles Paton's esteemed collection, this sett has been carefully preserved for generations, with some samples dating back to the early 1830s and subsequent additions during the Victorian era. The Lauder Dress tartan is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's clans, with its intricate pattern weaving together threads of history and family legacy. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds significant emotional value for those tracing their ancestry back to this storied family line. While the designer's name remains unknown, the significance of this tartan lies in its enduring connection to the Lauder family, whose descendants continue to cherish and wear this traditional pattern with pride.

name: Lauder [default]
description: The Lauder tartan is a storied family heirloom, steeped in tradition and heritage. Designed for the Sobieski brothers, with possible input from Sir Thomas Dick Lauder, this Clan tartan is a testament to the intricate bonds between Scottish families. The setts, woven by W & A K Johnston in 1906, reveal a unique identity - No. 87, bearing the distinct characteristics of the Gunn or Lauder sett. This subtle variation hints at the Sobieski brothers' creative flair, adapting the original Gunn tartan to create an enduring family legacy. The Lauder tartan's rich history is woven into the very fabric of its intricate design, reflecting the cultural and social ties that have bound Scottish families together for centuries.

name: Laurel Park
description: The Laurel Park tartan, designed by Marton Mills, is a captivating corporate motif that embodies the prestige and exclusivity associated with the esteemed Laurel Park brand. This distinctive tartan is rooted in its origins as a bespoke design for an independent school in Glasgow, evoking the rich history and tradition of Scotland's educational institutions. Although the registration notes caution that neither the green nor the blue tones are accurate, this only serves to add to the tartan's intriguing narrative, hinting at the complexities and nuances of branding identity. As a corporate design, Laurel Park tartan is poised to evoke feelings of sophistication and refinement, making it an attractive choice for organisations seeking to establish a strong, memorable presence on the global stage.

name: Laurentian University
description: Laurentian University Tartan is a prestigious corporate tartan that proudly represents the esteemed institution in Ontario, Canada. Designated in May 2007, this tartan was woven by renowned Scottish manufacturer Lochcarron of Scotland, drawing inspiration from the classic Ramsay tartan. The vibrant blue and gold colours reflect the school's identity, evoking feelings of tradition and excellence. As the University Pipe Band first wore it during the 2007 convocation ceremonies, marking a significant milestone in the institution's history, this tartan has become an integral part of Laurentian University's heritage, symbolising the values of academic achievement and unity that define its community.

name: Laurie [default]
description: The Laurie tartan is a storied family heirloom, woven with passion and devotion for Kenneth and Iain Laurie, Fife's esteemed clan. This distinctive tartan was originally designed as a personal tartan by Peter MacDonald, a respected Scottish designer, and was intended to be worn by those bearing the name Laurie. With its rich colour palette and subtle variations, the Laurie has become an integral part of Scottish heritage, evoking a sense of pride and identity among those who wear it. Interestingly, this tartan can also be adapted to suit different names, as red is subtly replaced with brown to create the Lawrie tartan, and yellow to produce the Lowry design. First marketed in 2002 by The Laurie Tartan Company of Elgin, this celebrated clan tartan has since become a treasured symbol of Scottish tradition and family honour.

name: Laval District
description: The Laval Tartan de is a striking District tartan that proudly represents the city's rich heritage in Quebec, Canada. Named after its eponymous namesake, this distinctive design was first woven by Les Tisserands de Laval in 1988, paying homage to the area's unique history and cultural influences. The regal purple and dark blue hues evoke the city's official colours, symbolising the wealth and quality of life that have defined Laval since its development as a human settlement. As Guy Menard noted, the addition of white tones serves as a poignant reminder of the city's shared French and British roots, weaving together threads of tradition and identity that are quintessentially Canadian. This tartan design is now an enduring emblem of the region's pride and history, proudly worn by those who share its values and heritage.

name: Laval Dress
description: The Laval Dress tartan is a rich and storied District tartan, steeped in the cultural heritage of Normandy's historic city of Laval. With its unique sett, this tartan was originally intended to evoke the elegance and sophistication of formal attire, fittingly named after a celebrated dress from the region. Registration notes suggest that an attempt was made to translate the English term "Dress" into French, resulting in the distinctive name Tartan de La Ville de Laval - Gala, underscoring its connection to this elegant city. As a District tartan, it is closely tied to the identity of Laval and its surrounding district, making it an important part of Normandy's rich textile heritage.

name: Law
description: The Law of Heather Athol tartan, a personal fashion design created by renowned Scottish textile expert Henry Ballantyne, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage in modern times. Originally commissioned for John Manfield's use in Queensland, Australia, this tartan weaves together the rich cultural threads of the Scottish Highlands and the Australian Outback. The Law of Heather Athol's distinctive pattern, characterised by its intricate interplay of blues and greens, echoes the rugged beauty of Scotland's heather-covered moors while also embracing the sun-kissed landscapes of Australia. As a personal fashion design, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the power of traditional Scottish textiles to transcend geographical boundaries and inspire new connections between cultures.

name: Law Society of Scotland
description: The Law Society of Scotland tartan, crafted with meticulous attention to detail by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, is a quintessential representation of Scottish corporate heritage. Originally designed in line with the colours of the society's shield, this distinctive tartan embodies the values of professionalism and expertise that have long been synonymous with Scotland's esteemed law profession. As a controlled use tartan, its adoption requires formal approval from the Law Society of Scotland, underscoring the importance of tradition and propriety within the world of Scottish law. The intricate design serves as a testament to the rich history and cultural identity of Scotland's legal community, evoking a sense of authority and gravitas that is uniquely befitting of a prestigious organisation like the Law Society of Scotland.

name: Lawers
description: The Lawers Estate Corporate Tartan, designed by Peter MacDonald, is a unique and distinctive fabric that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's most storied estates. Originating from Lawers Estate near Comrie, this tartan was woven with precision by D.C. Dalgliesh Ltd and carefully crafted to reflect its history and surroundings. Characterised by an asymmetric design and striking two-tone black stripes, which serve as a visual anchor for the colours, this tartan exudes a sense of luxury and tradition. As a Corporate Tartan, it is designed for formal wear and business attire, making it an ideal choice for companies and individuals who seek to express their connection to Scotland's esteemed past while maintaining a professional edge. This tartan design not only pays homage to the Lawers Estate but also reflects MacDonald's skill as a designer, seamlessly marrying historical context with modern practicality.

name: Lawlis [default]
description: The Lawlis/Lawless tartan, registered to commemorate a most unorthodox tale, tells the story of Russell Mosher's grandfather, Grandfather Lawlis of West Virginia. Originally acquired from a discount fabric store with no discernible heritage, the tartan was rechristened by its proud owner in honour of his esteemed ancestor. A Lindsay sett pattern, carefully interweaving emerald green and azure hues, this tartan speaks to the whimsical nature of family legacy and the power of tradition. As a Clan/Family tartan, it serves as a testament to the enduring bonds of kinship, even when forged in unexpected circumstances. With its origins rooted in the American heartland, the Lawlis/Lawless tartan proudly wears the mantle of a most singular story, one that celebrates the complexities and nuances of Scottish heritage.

name: Lawrie [default]
description: The Lawrie tartan is a deeply personal and storied fabric, woven with the rich heritage of Fife's esteemed Laurie family. Designed by renowned Scottish weaver Peter MacDonald in 2002, this Clan tartan was originally created for Kenneth and Iain Laurie as a cherished family heirloom, with each wearer able to claim a special connection to their noble lineage. Notably, the subtle substitution of brown for red or yellow thread transforms the tartan into either the distinctive Laurie or Lowry patterns, respectively - a testament to the ingenuity and adaptability of the Laird's legacy. As a symbol of family pride, tradition, and Scottish heritage, the Lawrie tartan continues to be cherished by descendants of the Laurie clan, while also opening its unique charm to anyone bearing the name, inviting all to wear their ancestral history with dignity and honour.

name: Lawsons' Whisky
description: Lawsons' Whisky, expertly crafted by renowned Scottish textile firm Kinloch Anderson Ltd, is a rich and storied corporate tartan born from the legacy of William Lawson's eponymous malt whisky brand. Originally sold primarily in Europe, particularly France, Spain, Portugal, Italy, and Lebanon, this distinctive tartan tells the tale of a whisky that has traversed borders and cultures. Weaving together threads of deep blue (the centre), with subtle gradations to darker indigo and grey-green hues on either side, Lawsons' Whisky embodies the complexity and character of its namesake spirit. This carefully considered palette is woven from the finest yarns, crafted to evoke the sense of warmth and conviviality associated with a well-brewed dram, while also nodding respectfully to Scotland's storied whisky heritage, where tradition meets innovation in perfect harmony.

name: Lawtie
description: The Lawtie tartan is a bespoke creation, woven with love for Roy Lawtie's very special day in October 2005 - his wedding celebration. This unique Name tartan holds deep family significance, its colours carefully chosen to reflect the family coat of arms. Commissioned by Roy Lawtie and designed by Blair Urquhart of The House of Tartan, this tartan is a poignant blend of heritage and personal tradition, creating an unforgettable visual legacy for the happy couple's new life together. As a cherished family heirloom, the Lawtie tartan serves as a tangible connection to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, its intricate patterns and subtle nuances echoing the warmth and history of a bygone era.

name: Leach Hunting
description: The Leach Hunting tartan, designed by Harold S Leach Jnr, is a rich and storied heritage textile with deep roots in Scotland's history. This clan tartan, bearing its proud name since centuries past, has been woven to commemorate the esteemed physicians who have borne the Leach surname through generations. Its significance extends far beyond family lineage, as it can be worn by anyone with the surname Leach, regardless of spelling variation - a testament to the tartan's enduring spirit of inclusivity and tradition. As a wearable connection to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, the Leach Hunting tartan invites wearers to don a piece of history, evoking the legacy of distinguished physicians who have shaped the country's medical landscape for centuries.

name: Leach (Personal)
description: The Leach tartan, named after its esteemed designer Dr Philip D Smith and originally borne by Scottish physicians, is a rich and storied fabric steeped in tradition and heritage. Designed for Carl Leach, this tartan has been woven with care to reflect the varied spellings of the name that have been passed down through generations, a testament to the enduring power of family ties and identity. As a Category Name tartan, it is open to wear by anyone who shares the surname Leach, regardless of its spelling or origin, making it a versatile and inclusive choice for those seeking to connect with their roots. Woven from threads of history and tradition, this tartan stands as a tribute to the timeless legacy of Scottish culture and the enduring spirit of the Leach family name.

name: Leach [default]
description: The Leach tartan, registered in 1995, is a rich and storied clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, its origins dating back centuries to the esteemed profession of physician. Its name serves as a testament to the long-standing tradition of the Leach family, whose members have been respected figures in Scottish society for generations. This tartan can be worn by anyone with the surname Leach, regardless of spelling variation, symbolising unity and inclusivity among those who bear this noble name. Designed by Harold S Leach Jnr, a respected weaver and historian, this tartan is a tribute to the enduring legacy of the Leach family, weaving together threads of tradition, community, and Scottish identity.

name: Leaf Peeper
description: The Leaf Peeper tartan, designed by Kenneth Cormack, is a vibrant and evocative fashion tartan that captures the quintessential spirit of New Hampshire's White Mountains region in autumn. This stunning pattern, named after the enthusiasts who flock to witness the spectacular foliage display, boasts a rich palette inspired by the region's iconic sugar maples, oaks, birches, and elms as they don their finest hues of golden yellow, fiery red, and burnished brown. With subtle nods to the snow-capped summits that punctuate the landscape, this tartan is a testament to the enduring allure of the natural world, inviting wearers to embody the warmth and wonder of autumn in the heart of North America's most scenic mountains.

name: Leask [default]
description: The Leask tartan is a rich and storied fabric, woven with dedication by Scott Brothers of Wilton Mills, Hawick, for the esteemed Madam Leask of Sheringham, Norfolk in 1982. Recorded in Lyon Court Book 44, this Clan tartan holds significance as a cherished family heirloom, passed down through generations to preserve the heritage and identity of the Leask clan. The subtle nuances of its design, now preserved in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Dalgety Collection, evoke the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of Scotland's storied past, paying homage to the country's rich cultural heritage. This tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's tartan tradition, where family ties are woven into the very fabric of history, and the Leask clan's story is forever intertwined with that of their ancestral homeland.

name: Lebrun
description: The Lebrun tartan, designed by the esteemed Highland Queen, is a fashion-forward interpretation of traditional Scottish heritage. Registered in 1972, this modern tartan boasts a striking dark blue (braid) and green (saltire) colour scheme, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's natural landscape. The precise proportions and subtle shading of the design reflect the technical expertise of Highland Queen Sportswear of Toronto, who skillfully wove a sample sett to bring this vibrant tartan to life. Although some details remain shrouded in uncertainty due to limited visibility, the Lebrun remains an iconic fashion tartan that continues to captivate enthusiasts and designers alike with its unique blend of traditional flair and contemporary style.

name: Leckie [default]
description: The Leckie tartan is a storied and intimate family heritage, woven from the threads of history and tradition. Originating with Ross Leckie, a stalwart member of Clan MacDonald, this tartan holds profound significance within the clan's lineage. The original registration notes drew parallels with the Lennox district's #386 tartan, yet a deliberate variation distinguished it - dark red stripes now glimmer as blue, imbuing the fabric with a sense of modernity and contemporary flair. Designed by Peter MacDonald, a master weaver of Scottish heritage, this tartan embodies the blend of old-world nobility and fresh vitality that is quintessentially Scottish. Its existence acknowledges the evolution of tradition while remaining steadfast in its loyalty to the Leckie family's honour and legacy.

name: Lee [default]
description: The Lee tartan, a personal clan tartan of great significance, was registered in 1995 by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr, a renowned Scottish heritage expert. This distinctive design is worn by all members of the Lee family with pride, symbolising their shared ancestry and cultural heritage. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds deep meaning within the community, connecting those who wear it to a rich history and tradition. Notably, Dr Smith has ensured that the tartan remains accessible to all descendants of Phil Smith, registered in 2009, allowing future generations to continue this proud legacy. This intricate pattern, steeped in Scottish heritage, weaves a sense of identity, connection, and belonging, making it an integral part of the Lee family's story.

name: Leeds University
description: The Leeds University (Dance) #1 tartan is a vibrant representation of the University's affinity with traditional Scottish dancing, reflecting the enduring bond between academia and heritage. Originally designed to showcase the capabilities of an automatic loom, Duncan Snowden's creation now proudly embodies the identity of the University of Leeds's Scottish Country Dance Club. Weaving together colours that represent the institution, this tartan has become an integral part of the university's cultural fabric, honouring a rich tradition that transcends generations. With its unique place in the Johnston Collection and restrictions governed by the registration notes, this tartan design serves as a testament to the University's commitment to preserving Scottish heritage while also embracing innovation and self-expression.

name: Leel
description: Leel, a bespoke tartan woven with precision by renowned tailor Geoffrey Highland Crafts, is a deeply personal and meaningful heritage fabric. Originally registered to commemorate the Leel family name, this distinctive tartan has been carefully crafted with love and attention to detail to reflect the identity of its creator, Philip Leel, and his ancestry. As a restricted tartan, its use is limited to the immediate Leel family, making it an exclusive and precious possession that holds immense sentimental value. This beautiful woven fabric not only celebrates Scottish tradition but also serves as a tangible link to the rich history and heritage of Philip Leel's roots, preserving a cherished family legacy for generations to come.

name: Lees-McRae College
description: The Lees-McRae College tartan is a vibrant tribute to the rich heritage of North Carolina's Banner Elk, nestled at the foot of Grandfather Mountain. Designed by Marjorie Warren for the Presbyterian institution, this Corporate tartan masterfully weaves together the colours of the school's identity: green and gold, evoking the natural beauty of the surrounding mountains; blue, paying homage to the sacred saltire of the Presbyterian church; and red and white, respectfully honouring two esteemed individuals - Rev. Edgar Tufts and Elizabeth, a teacher who left an indelible mark on the lives of those at the college. This tartan is more than just a pattern, it's a celebration of community, tradition, and the enduring spirit of education that has shaped Lees-McRae College into the thriving institution it is today.

name: Leiato
description: Leiato of American Samoa is a distinctive Name tartan that pays tribute to the rich cultural heritage of the Pacific Islands, specifically the Polynesian community in American Samoa. Designed by Donald Suttie Smith, a renowned Scottish tartan expert, this unique tartan was commissioned by the Paramount Chief of American Samoa as a way to represent his family's honour and connection to their ancestral homeland. As a Name tartan, it is reserved exclusively for use within the Polynesian community, adding an extra layer of significance to its wearer's identity and sense of belonging. With its striking colour palette and intricate threadwork, Leiato of American Samoa reflects the vibrant traditions and customs of American Samoa, making it a meaningful symbol of cultural pride for those who wear it with honours.

name: Leighton [default]
description: The Leighton tartan, designed by Mrs Wallace Poppe, is a family heirloom of great cultural significance, worn with honour by members of the Dalglish clan for generations. This traditional Clan tartan boasts an intricate thread count of 16, featuring a striking combination of colours including Dark Tan Mauve (DTM), Yellow (Y), Dark Green (DG), and Dark Red (DR). The pivots, located at either end, signify the full counts of the tartan's complex weave. With its rich history and technical precision, this tartan is a testament to the skill and craftsmanship of Scottish weavers, evoking the warmth and heritage of the Dalglish clan and their enduring legacy.

name:
Leinster
[AKA] Leinster Green
description: The Leinster tartan, woven by esteemed Lochcarron of Scotland, pays homage to the storied historical ties between the Scots and the Irish, as embodied in its registration notes. This prestigious District tartan proudly represents the eponymous province of Ireland, specifically Dublin, the nation's capital. The subtle yet nuanced colours, comprising blues and greens that evoke the lush Emerald Isle landscape, are woven with a deep respect for the rich cultural heritage shared between these two nations. By acknowledging this fraternal connection, the Leinster tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's enduring ties to Ireland, both in history and tradition.

name: Leith District
description: The Leith tartan is a proud representation of Scotland's rich maritime heritage, originating from Kinloch Anderson Ltd in 1995 specifically for the Tall Ships event. This storied district tartan is deeply rooted in history, paying homage to Henry Robb, founder of the renowned Leith shipbuilders, and their significant contribution to the claret trade. The red line that traverses the fabric serves as a poignant reminder of Leith's pivotal role in Scotland's industrial past. As the official tartan of the Leith District, this vibrant design has been formally adopted to honour the city's heritage, embodying the values of resilience, innovation, and community spirit that have defined Leith for centuries.

name: Leitrim Irish County
description: The Leitrim District tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich weaving heritage, born from the collaboration between Polly Wittering, a renowned Scottish textile expert at House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Specifically designed for the esteemed Macnaughtons of Pitlochry, this tartan collection represents the quintessential trade patterns of the region. As a District tartan, it has been carefully crafted to reflect the unique history and culture of Leitrim County in Ireland, which shares a deep affinity with Scotland's own tartan traditions. Though not officially sanctioned by the Scottish Tartans Authority, its popularity is undeniable, and it has become an integral part of Irish heritage, echoing the warmth and character of its namesake county.

name: Lemetti (Mike) personal; Italian National
description: The Italian National tartan is a vibrant celebration of the cultural heritage of Scots with Italian roots, designed by Mike Lemetti to commemorate the historic links between Scotland and Italy. This Fashion tartan proudly wears the colours of the Italian flag - green, white, and red - alongside black, gold, and the bold Azzuri blue that evokes the Mediterranean's depths. Inspired by the uniforms of the Civic Militia of Milan and the iconic Praetorian Guard, this unique design not only honours Scotland's own rich history but also celebrates the warmth and beauty of Italian culture. Approved by the Italian Consul in Glasgow, this tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of friendship between two nations, perfect for those who can trace their ancestry back to Tuscany or other parts of Italy, and a striking tribute to the country's rich heritage and passion for football.

name: Lenaghan
description: The Lenaghan tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of the Northern Irish family whose proud history dates back to the 18th century, as immortalised in its intricate weave. Designed by Rev James A Lenaghan in honour of his ancestral kin, this distinctive tartan was originally reserved for descendants of Bernard Lenaghan of Belfast, underscoring the strong sense of family and tradition that underpins Scottish clan culture. As a Name tartan, it holds particular significance, serving as a symbol of identity and connection to a storied lineage, while its unique pattern is a poignant reminder of the enduring legacy of those who came before us.

name: Lendrum Lyon version
description: The Lendrum tartan, worn with pride by those bearing its storied heritage, is a testament to Scotland's rich tapestry of history and tradition. This Clan tartan, registered in 1957, tells the tale of a long-forgotten dynasty that once roamed the rolling hills of Aberdeenshire. Though the connection between the MacFarlane clan, who hailed from Arrochar, is unclear, the Lendrum sett has stood the test of time, its intricate patterns and subtle colour nuances whispering secrets of Scotland's forgotten past. This tartan, now a symbol of family honour, holds within it the whispers of generations gone by, its threads woven with the stories of a people who once called Aberdeenshire home.

name: Lendrum [default]
description: This striking Black & Red tartan, registered as MacFarlane or Lendrum, embodies the fierce spirit of Scottish heritage. As a Fashion category tartan, it is designed to add a touch of dramatic flair to any outfit, evoking the rich history and tradition of Scotland's storied clans. With its distinctive black and red hues, this tartan pays homage to the bold warrior culture that once defined the nation. Rooted in the traditional designs of the Clans Originaux, a rare 19th-century sample book, this tartan boasts an enduring connection to Scotland's past, its beauty now available for modern wearers to adorn themselves with pride, courtesy of its unrecorded but intriguing designer, whose creative vision has left a lasting legacy.

name: Lennie [default]
description: The Lennie tartan is a storied family weft, born from the esteemed Wilsons of Bannockburn's 1819 pattern book No 231. This Clan/Family tartan holds great significance for those bearing the Lennie name, tracing its origins back to a weaving firm founded circa 1770 near Stirling. The tartan's rich history is preserved within the National Museum of Antiquities in Edinburgh and the Scottish Tartans Society archive, where original pattern books and correspondence can be found. Weaving an enduring connection to Scotland's heritage, the Lennie tartan embodies the values and traditions of its patron clan, while also serving as a meaningful tribute for those honouring their family lineage.

name:
Lennox [default]
[AKA] Gartshore [default]
description: The Lennox tartan is an enduring symbol of Scottish heritage, steeped in history and tradition. This distinctive Clan/Family tartan has been woven into the fabric of Scotland's rich tapestry for centuries, bearing witness to the storied connections between families with the surname 'Lennox' and the ancient Clans Stewart and MacFarlane. With roots dating back to the 16th century, this tartan was meticulously recreated by D.W. Stewart from a rare portrait of the Countess of Lennox, now preserved in the Scottish Tartans Society's archives. As a testament to the enduring bond between clan and kin, the Lennox tartan is often worn with honour by those who bear its surname, forging an unbreakable link between past and present, and proudly proclaiming their ancestral heritage.

name: Leonard Hunting
description: The Leonard Hunting tartan, designed by the esteemed Pringles of Inverness, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's clans. Originating from the Johnston Collection, a renowned repository of Scottish tartans, this complex yet harmonious pattern is classified as a Clan/Family tartan, reflecting its historical significance and familial associations. Dating back to the 17th century, Leonard Hunting is believed to have been woven for members of the Hunting family, one of Scotland's oldest and most esteemed clans. With its rich, muted hues evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands, this tartan embodies the tradition and heritage of the Hunter clan, a legacy passed down through generations, woven into the very fabric of Scottish history.

name: Lermontov [default]
description: The Lermontov tartan is a poignant tribute to the Russian noble family's Scottish heritage, woven with deep respect for their country of origin and cultural legacy. Designed by Brian Wilton for the descendants of George Lermont, a 'Scotch Knight' who emigrated to Russia in 1613, this tartan celebrates the enduring connection between Scotland and Russia. The striking blue and white hues evoke St Andrew's patronage and the Saltire flag, while the three black lines paying homage to the Lermontov coat of arms registered in Russia in 1798 add a touch of nobility and tradition. This Clan tartan is not only a testament to the Lermontov family's Scottish roots but also a reflection of their enduring bond with Scotland, a legacy that transcends centuries and borders, much like the poetic spirit of Mikhail Lermontov himself.

name: Les Cercles de Femme
description: Les Cercles de Femme is a striking Corporate tartan design created by renowned textile artist Suzanne Allard-Ouellette, specifically for the organisation of ladies groups in Quebec, making it the oldest such group in North America. Originally named to avoid confusion with another design by the same designer, Les Cercles de Femieres (#2136), this tartan's similarities are a testament to Suzanne's skill as an artist. With its distinctive circular motif and rich colour palette, Les Cercles de Femme embodies the elegance and tradition of Quebec's ladies' groups, while also paying homage to the country's Scottish heritage. As a Corporate tartan, it is intended for use in business and professional settings, offering a sophisticated and refined visual identity that reflects the organisation's values and history.

name: Les Cercles de Fermieres du Quebec
description: Les Cercles de Fermieres du Quebec, or "The Farms of Quebec", is a vibrant and distinctive Corporate tartan born out of celebration and community spirit. Designed by talented textile artist Suzanne Allard-Ouellette, specifically for the 80th anniversary of the Quebec Farmers' Club, this tartan pays tribute to the province's rich agricultural heritage. With its carefully crafted colour palette and precise sett pattern, Les Cercles de Fermieres du Quebec embodies the tradition and pride that defines Quebec's farming community. As a Corporate tartan, it can be adopted by companies and organisations with connections to agriculture or rural industries, serving as a meaningful way to honour the province's pioneering farmers and their contributions to Canadian history.

name: Leslie (J Cant)
description: The Leslie tartan is a storied and ancient Scottish design, steeped in history and tradition. Registration notes reveal its origins as a clan tartan, gifted from one generation to the next, with the latest iteration tracing back to James Cant's hand-painted manuscript book of over 450 colour strips completed prior to 1960. Its classification as a Clan/Family tartan highlights its strong familial significance, worn by members of the noble Leslie clan and other associated families. While no designer is attributed to this tartan, its authenticity lies in its heritage and the stories it tells of Scottish genealogy. The fact that it has been passed down through generations, with notes indicating its presence in a stockbook in Perth, underscores the tartan's enduring connection to Scotland's rich cultural fabric.

name:
Leslie Hunting
[AKA] Leslie Green
[AKA] Leslie Old Colours
[AKA] Leslie Syme
description: The Leslie Hunting tartan is a poignant and storied design, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Worn by the 14th Earl of Rothes, George, who tragically passed away in 1841, this clan tartan has been woven with great care for over two centuries. First documented in the early 19th century, the Leslie Hunting sett was later recorded by notable designers Smibert and W&A Smith, whose works provide a glimpse into the evolution of the pattern. The tartan's history is also intertwined with that of General Sir William Cockburn, who collected and preserved the design between 1810-1820. Now housed in the Mitchell Library, Glasgow, this treasured collection serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Leslie clan, and its intricate colours - a masterful blend of dark blues, greens, and black - continue to evoke the rich traditions of Scotland's noble past.

name:
Leslie [default]
[AKA] Leslie Dress
[AKA] Leslie Red
description: The Leslie Red tartan is an iconic representation of Scottish heritage and family pride, passed down through generations within the noble House of Leslie. This striking pattern, registered under the esteemed Sobieski Stewarts, has been woven into the fabric of Scotland's history for centuries, reflecting the clan's rich traditions and legacy. As described in Vestiarium Scoticum, a seminal tome on Scottish tartans published between 1829-1842 by the Sobieski brothers, the Leslie Red tartan is widely available to weavers and has become synonymous with the family's honour. Its significance extends beyond mere aesthetics, symbolising the unyielding spirit and loyalty that have defined the Leslies for generations, making it a treasured emblem of Scottish clan identity.

name: Letham
description: The Letham tartan, registered in recognition of its significance to James Letham and his family from South Australia, holds a special place in the hearts of those who bear its name. As a personal tartan, it was designed with the intention of honouring the heritage of this South Australian clan, allowing its wearers to connect with their roots and cultural identity. While originally created for James Letham himself, he has kindly granted permission to others bearing the same surname to also wear this distinctive tartan, thereby fostering a sense of community among those who share his family name. With its unique thread pattern woven by D C Dalgliesh, the Letham tartan embodies the rich traditions and histories of Scottish heritage, translated into a vibrant textile that celebrates the enduring spirit of Australian clan culture.

name: Lethbridge City
description: The Lethbridge City Tartan is a vibrant and unique District tartan, carefully crafted by the Lethbridge Handicraft Guild in celebration of the millennium celebrations in 2000. This nine-coloured design, exceeding the traditional maximum, was produced to commemorate the special occasion, showcasing the community's pride and heritage. Featuring a distinctive Lochcarron weave with a warp colour change on the gold 4 to pale yellow 6, this tartan is a testament to the ingenuity of its designer and weavers, Burnett & Struth of Ontario, who undertook the intricate task in December 2001. As an official District tartan, it is a symbol of Lethbridge's rich history and cultural identity, evoking memories of the city's people and traditions, and serving as a proud representation of their connection to this special heritage.

name: Lewis of Wales
description: The Lewis of Wales tartan is a captivating example of modern Celtic textile design, born from the heritage of Wales and the legacy of Sheila Daniel's work at Cambrian Woollen Mill. Registered as a Name tartan, its origins are more contemporary than traditional, emerging in the late 20th century with the establishment of Wales Tartan Centres. Although its historical credibility is not guaranteed, the 'of Wales' designation serves as a testament to its connection to this Welsh region. What sets Lewis of Wales apart from other Celtic patterns lies in its distinctive threading and colouring, featuring an unusual predominance of odd-numbered threads, which adds a unique visual interest to the overall design. This innovative approach reflects the evolving nature of tartan-making, while still respecting the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's west coast.

name: Lexington Fire Department
description: The Lexington Fire Department's Corporate Tartan is a proud symbol of the bravery and dedication of its esteemed firefighters and paramedics. Registered to Maria Polenzani, this distinctive unit tartan was woven specifically for the Kentucky-based fire department to recognise the unique role and sacrifices made by those who serve on the front lines. As a Category Corporate design, it serves as an emblem of unity and solidarity among members of the department, while also making a statement about the proud tradition of serving their community. With its rich colours and technical precision, this tartan is a testament to the skill and craftsmanship that underpins Scotland's iconic textile heritage, now being adopted by modern organisations to represent shared values and mission.

name: Liama, The
description: The Liama, The tartan is a stylish and modern fashion choice, born from the creative vision of Aljean of Vancouver. This contemporary design has been carefully crafted to pay homage to Scotland's rich textile heritage, while also reflecting its wearer's individuality. As a Fashion tartan, it is not associated with any specific clan or family group, but rather embodies the broader cultural spirit of Scottish fashion. Registration notes indicate that a sample of this tartan exists in the esteemed Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority, solidifying its place within Scotland's storied tartan tradition. With its unique colour palette and subtle pattern, The Liama, The is an attractive choice for those seeking to add a touch of traditional Scottish flair to their wardrobe, while also embracing the diversity and creativity of modern fashion.

name: Liberton [default]
description: The Liberton tartan is a distinctive and storied family heirloom, woven with pride and passion by Patrick Liberton, a Dutch native who brought his clan's heritage to life through this very fabric.
