Registration notes reveal that this tartan was specifically designed for the Liberton name, intended to be worn by all members of the family in celebration of their shared ancestry. Woven through The House of Tartan in Comrie, Perthshire, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish clan traditions and the importance of preserving family legacy. With its unique colour palette and carefully arranged threads, the Liberton tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the rich history and cultural heritage that defines this storied name.

name: Lifeboats Royal National Institute
description: The Centre tartan is a quintessential example of Scottish heritage, steeped in tradition and history. Designed for the esteemed Centre family, who have resided in Aberdeenshire since the 1700s, this majestic tartan weaves together the rich cultural fabric of Scotland's north-east region. Originally crafted by DC Dalgliesh of Selkirk, a renowned Scottish weaver, the Centre tartan now bears the mark of Robin Birch and W Center's creative vision. Free to be worn by members of the Centre name, this tartan symbolises family pride, heritage, and identity, its intricate patterns echoing the timeless traditions of Scotland's ancient clans.

name: Limerick Irish County
description: The Limerick County tartan is a richly woven tribute to the heritage of Ireland's districts, exemplifying the complex blend of tradition and innovation in Scotland's textile legacy. Designed by Polly Wittering for Macnaughtons of Pitlochry, this tartan was originally created as a collection of trade tartans, reflecting the region's historical connections with the local community. While not officially sanctioned as a District tartan, its popularity has earned it a place in the hearts of many enthusiasts. As part of the Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority, this sample tartan serves as a testament to the enduring appeal of Ireland's districts, their stories and symbolism forever intertwined with Scotland's own rich cultural heritage.

name: Linden [default]
description: The Linden tartan, designed by James Linden, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's clan and family traditions. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds significant cultural value for those bearing the surname Linden, connecting them to their ancestral roots. This striking design weaves together hues reminiscent of the Saltire and the thistle, Scotland's national symbols, with a unique twist that reflects the associations of the Linden tree - a nod to the iconic lime tree. The subtle nuances of blue and white, evoking the Union Jack, meet the rich tones of purple and green, paying homage to the national flower. This tartan is more than just a colourful pattern; it's a tangible link to Scotland's storied past and the natural world that has long inspired its people - a true testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage.

name: Lindley
description: Unidentified Lindley #4 is a fascinating enigma, a mystery wrapped in threads of history and tradition. This intriguing machine-woven swatch, now housed in the Scottish Tartans Authority's esteemed Lindley Collection, holds secrets of its own identity. As an "Other" category, it defies traditional clan affiliations, instead belonging to a broader spectrum of tartan heritage that may evoke the stories of anonymous Scottish weavers or those whose tartan legacy remains shrouded in mystery. Despite the lack of designer attribution, the swatch's intricate design whispers tales of the past, its technical characteristics a testament to the skilled hands of a long-forgotten artisan. As part of the Lindley Collection, Unidentified Lindley #4 serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich textile legacy, waiting to be unravelled and interpreted by those who seek to uncover the hidden narratives of this captivating tartan design.

name: Lindsay (Blackdown Hills) personal
description: The Blackdown Hills tartan is a striking corporate design, born from Ian Gammon's passion to celebrate the region's natural beauty. Registration notes reveal its creation as a tribute to the Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty (AONB) situated on the Devon/Somerset border, evoking a sense of pride for this unique corner of England. As a Corporate tartan, it is designed to be versatile and dynamic, making it suitable for businesses and organisations looking to add a touch of local character to their branding. With its rich, dark tones, the Blackdown Hills tartan embodies the rugged yet rolling landscape of the region, providing a distinctive visual identity that pays homage to the land's heritage. Sole world distribution rights held by 'Kilts by Lindsay', this exclusive design ensures its significance is not lost in translation, allowing those who wear it to proudly display their connection to this special place.

name: Lindsay Black lines
description: Lindsay #3 is a rich and storied tartan, steeped in the heritage of Scotland's noble clans. Registered as Clan Lindsay in 1856, this distinctive pattern has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish identity for generations. The subtle nuances of its colour palette, comprising blues and greens reminiscent of Scotland's rolling hills and heather-covered moors, evoke a sense of tradition and honour. As part of the Baronage of Angus and Mearns, Lindsay #3 is imbued with the prestige of Scotland's aristocracy, reflecting the proud history and lineage of the Lindsay family. This tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's complex past and the enduring legacy of its noble clans, weaving a sense of connection to the land, culture, and people that have shaped the nation over centuries.

name: Lindsay Dress Dance
description: This enchanting Lindsay Dress #2 tartan is a personal testament to the rich heritage of Scottish clan identity, meticulously woven by a skilled designer, J.R. MacLellan of Edinburgh. As a 'Name' tartan, it holds significant cultural value within the Lindsay family tradition, serving as a badge of honour and familial pride. The subtle nuances in shades of colour, which can vary significantly from one mill to another, reflect the intricate variations found within Scottish tartans. With its distinct character, this personal tartan embodies the timeless spirit of Scotland's weavers, who have carefully preserved their traditions for generations. As a unique example of Lindsay family identity, it stands as a tangible connection to the country's storied past and continues to inspire a sense of community among those who wear it with pride.

name: Lindsay Dress Dance; Green
description: The Lindsay Dress tartan is a quintessential example of traditional Scottish clan weaves, bearing testament to the rich heritage of the Lindsay family. This iconic pattern has been an honourable part of Scottish tradition for centuries, woven into the very fabric of Scotland's history and culture. As a registered Clan tartan, it was designed to identify its bearers as members of the Lindsay clan, a sept of the ancient House of Douglas. With its characteristic blue-green colour scheme, subtle variations in thread tension, and intricate sett patterns, this tartan embodies the essence of Scottish Highland dress, evoking images of brave warriors, noble gentry, and proud family traditions. This timeless design has been cherished by Lindsay clansmen for generations, a symbol of their identity, heritage, and proud connection to Scotland's storied past.

name: Lindsay Dress Dance; Red
description: The Lindsay Dress Red is a storied tartan, steeped in tradition and heritage as a Clan family tartan. Registered in 1896, it was originally designed to be worn by members of the Lindsay clan, whose name is synonymous with bravery and loyalty. The tartan's distinctive red hue, carefully balanced with subtle shades of blue and green, evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. According to its registration notes, weavers D.C. Dalgliesh of Selkirk were entrusted with interpreting the design, which was intended to be worn in the traditional "dress" tartan style - a testament to the enduring importance of family heritage and clan identity. Today, this timeless tartan remains an honourable emblem of Scottish tradition, inviting wearers to proudly represent their Lindsay ancestry and connect with the rich cultural heritage that it embodies.

name:
Lindsay (Smibert)
[AKA] Lindsay Mini
description: Lindsay #2 is a majestic Clan tartan imbued with the rich heritage of Scotland's storied past. Registered by the Tartan Society in 1995, this timeless design is an important link to Lindsay family history, whose ancestral home, Polnumkirk Castle, has stood proudly since the 16th century. According to registration notes from T. Smibert's publication, 'The Clans of the Highlands of Scotland' (1850), Lindsay #2 was one of 55 tartan setts documented by Wilson's of Bannockburn, a testament to Smibert's dedication to preserving Scotland's traditional textiles. As part of the Clan tradition, this tartan is steeped in significance, symbolising the bravery and loyalty of the Lindsay family throughout generations, their legacy woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage.

name: Lindsay [default]
description: The Lindsay tartan is a storied and distinctive clan tartan that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's ancient Borders. Its unique colour scheme, particularly its striking dark blue tone, sets it apart from other tartans in the Stewart family category. Registration notes reveal that the sett bears a resemblance to the Stewart of Athol tartan, with the exception of the black thread, which is rendered as deep blue, a clever variation that showcases the weaver's skill and attention to detail. Named after the Lindsay family, who first appeared in the region in the 12th century, this tartan is steeped in history and tradition, its design reflecting the evolution of Border clan tartans over time.

name: Lions
description: The Lions Club tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of community service and global unity embodied by Lions Clubs International. Designed by Miss M Patricia Jenkins for the esteemed organisation, this corporate tartan weaves together a rich tapestry of symbolism and meaning. The purple and gold hues pay homage to the Lions' colours, while the azure and white reflect the international scope of the organisation, inextricably linked with the United Nations. The black and white threads serve as a poignant reminder of the world's needs and the lions' unwavering efforts to address them. This majestic tartan design not only pays tribute to the Lions Clubs' legacy but also serves as a powerful emblem of unity and cooperation, reflecting the organisation's commitment to fostering a brighter future for all.

name: Lions International
description: The Lions International tartan is a corporate design that embodies the strength and courage associated with one of Scotland's most iconic symbols: the lion. As a registered corporate tartan, it was created to represent unity and solidarity among business professionals and organisations, fostering a sense of identity and shared values. The distinctive eight-petal pattern, characteristic of this tartan, is a modern interpretation of traditional Scottish weaving techniques. While the designer, Bob Martin, has not provided further information about his inspiration or specific design choices, it is clear that Lions International tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage while also embracing global business communities. Its corporate nature sets it apart from more traditional clan tartans, yet its bold and vibrant colours evoke the same sense of pride and tradition found in many Scottish registered patterns.

name: Lions Pride
description: The Lions' Pride tartan, crafted by esteemed weavers at Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the bold spirit and unyielding pride of the British & Irish Lions rugby team. As a Corporate tartan, its purpose is to represent the team's values and heritage, making it a cherished emblem among fans and supporters alike. Designed specifically for the iconic rugby squad, this striking pattern was unveiled in New York during the 2005 Tartan Day celebrations, marking an important moment of Scottish cultural exchange and camaraderie. With its rich history and association with one of Britain's most revered sporting traditions, the Lions' Pride tartan proudly wears its designation as a Corporate design, symbolising unity, courage, and unrelenting passion for the team that bears its name.

name: Lisbon
description: The Lisbon tartan is a vibrant and modern fashion design, carefully crafted by West Coast Woolen Mill to evoke the cosmopolitan charm of Portugal's capital city. As a registered Fashion tartan, it has been acknowledged for its technical excellence and aesthetic appeal, meeting the high standards set by the Scottish Tartans Authority. This dynamic pattern features a palette of blues, greens, and whites that evoke the Atlantic coastline and Lisbon's rich cultural heritage. Without any restrictions, the Lisbon tartan is open to designers, manufacturers, and enthusiasts alike, inviting them to incorporate its unique visual identity into their creations, while proudly paying homage to the city's enduring spirit and tradition.

name: Little Arisaid
description: The Little, Arisaid tartan is a treasured family heirloom, born from the creative vision of Sandy Frediani, a renowned weaver with a deep appreciation for Scottish heritage. This Clan/Family tartan pays homage to the Little clan's rich history and cultural significance, its intricate patterns woven from threads of red, blue, yellow, green, brown, black, and pale blue. The design is rooted in the original 1991 Little tartan, carefully modified by Frediani to create a unique and authentic representation of this esteemed family's legacy. Registration notes indicate that this tartan was designed as a tribute to the clan's ancestry, making it an honourable addition to any family or household seeking to connect with their Scottish roots.

name: Little Dress
description: The Little Dress tartan, created by Sandy Frediani in 2000, embodies the quintessential spirit of Scottish heritage, born from a colour change on the venerable 1991 Little tartan. This District tartan is a testament to the rich tapestry of Scotland's tartan traditions, reimagined with modern flair. By reversing the R and W, Frediani has breathed new life into this classic design, making it accessible to a wider audience while still honouring its historical roots. The subtle colour variation adds depth and nuance to the original pattern, echoing the intricate storytelling that underlies many Scottish tartans. As a District tartan, Little Dress is a symbol of local identity and community pride, inviting wearers to connect with their own heritage and traditions. Its existence serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring legacy of Scottish tartan-making, where tradition meets innovation in perfect harmony.

name:
Little of Morton Rigg
[AKA] Little of Morton; Rigg
description: The Little of Morton Rigg tartan is a distinctive and richly coloured design born from the heritage of Clan Little Society, a family association with Scottish roots. Registered in 1991 by Dr J.C. Little of Morton Rig, this tartan weaves together elements of traditional Border Littles attire, paying homage to the black and white livery colours worn by ancestors of the clan. The addition of red (maroon) from the Wallace tartan adds a bold and storied touch, reflecting the family's connection to William Wallace, a renowned Scottish hero, whose nephew Edward Litill fought alongside him in 1296. As a registered Name tartan, this design is reserved for members of Clan Little Society, or by special permission granted by the designer himself, offering an authentic way for families to express their heritage and sense of belonging to this esteemed clan association.

name: Little of Morton Rigg; Red
description: This captivating tartan design, officially registered as 'Little of Morton Rigg Red', is a deeply personal creation steeped in Scottish heritage. As a designated Name tartan, it was carefully crafted by Crawford Little to commemorate his connection to the esteemed Morton family's ancestral lands at Morton Rigg. The subtle nuances and rich colours of this tartan evoke a sense of history and tradition, echoing the rugged landscapes and storied past of Scotland's rural communities. Though the registration notes remain tantalizingly vague, it is clear that this tartan holds sentimental value for its creator, connecting him to his Scottish roots and honouring the timeless legacy of his forebears.

name: Livingston customer special
description: The Livingston Personal tartan is a richly woven tribute to the storied heritage of Scotland, born from the love of a young bride-to-be named Miss Livingstone. Designed by renowned duo Donald and Fiona Fraser in collaboration with the esteemed Scottish tartan authorities, this distinctive Name tartan was created specifically for her wedding attire. The intricate pattern, imbued with the nuances of the Scottish wool industry's finest threads, embodies the timeless traditions of Scotland's clans and families. As a personal tartan, it remains forever tied to its creator's legacy, making it an exceptionally rare and precious find for those fortunate enough to encounter it.

name: Livingstone [default]
description: The Livingstone #2 tartan is a distinctive and enigmatic design, steeped in Scottish heritage and tied to the storied history of the small Highland clan. Originally borne by the MacDunsleinhe, Mac-an-Leigh, or Maclea families from Lismore and Western Argyll, this tartan bears an intriguing connection to the Stewarts of Appin. Its unique characteristics set it apart from its supposed clansmen, including the MacDonell of Keppoch, with a prominent centre band of green separating two narrow bands that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. According to D.C. Stewart's Setts (1950), this tartan does not appear to align with any specific clan affiliation, yet still holds a profound cultural significance within the realm of Scottish tartans, speaking to the intricate web of family ties and territorial connections that once bound these families together.

name: Livingston Football Club 2001
description: The Livingston Football Club tartan, registered in 2001, embodies the spirited pride of Scotland's footballing heritage. As a Corporate tartan, it has been woven to represent the club's identity and values on and off the pitch. Designed by House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this distinctive pattern pays homage to the club's rich history, having risen through the ranks from its promotion into the Scottish Premier Division that same year. With near Glasgow roots, this tartan design reflects the warmth and camaraderie of Scotland's footballing traditions. As a symbol of loyalty and team spirit, the Livingston Football Club tartan is sure to inspire unity among supporters, proudly showcasing their affiliation with the club's storied past.

name: Livingston Football Club
description: The Livingston Football Club tartan is a vibrant representation of corporate identity, born from the passion and pride of Scotland's footballing community. This distinctive pattern, woven by the esteemed Peter MacArthur & Co., was registered as a corporate tartan, signifying its official association with the club. Though the original registration notes acknowledge some imprecision - particularly in the colour specification, where yellow should be clarified as lime green - this variation remains a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish football and the rich tradition of tartan weaving that underpins it. This dynamic design embodies the energy and camaraderie of Livingston FC, forever linked to the history and heritage of Scotland's beloved national pastime.

name: Livingstone Dress
description: The Livingstone Dress tartan is a poignant tribute to the storied history of the small Highland clan from Lismore and Western Argyll, whose Gaelic name was once rendered in various ways: MacDunsleinhe, Mac-an-Leigh, or Maclea. Tightly woven with a deep sense of connection to the Stewarts of Appin, this tartan design evokes the rugged yet refined heritage of Scotland's west coast. Registration notes attest to its origins, tracing back to W J A Livingstone of Bachuil, while specimens preserved in The Kilt Shop and Cochrane's Store hint at a longer history. This Clan tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Livingstones, whose name was once synonymous with the rugged beauty and proud traditions of Scotland's Highlands.

name: LL Bean Hunting
description: The Bean of Freeport tartan is a unique and distinctive corporate pattern, carefully crafted to commemorate the 75th anniversary of L.L.Bean Inc, the esteemed outdoor sporting specialist based in Freeport, Maine. This specially designed tartan, created by Harry Lindley of Kinloch Anderson Ltd, brings together the colours of the MacBain and MacIntosh clans, symbolising a special connection between these two respected families. The tartan's subtle variations set it apart from other similar patterns, such as Shaw of Tordarroch, with distinct differences in the shade of blue line and black guards on the blue line that distinguish it as an original design. This exclusive corporate tartan celebrates American-Scottish heritage and serves as a testament to the enduring bond between two nations, woven into the very fabric of this distinctive pattern.

name: Llewellyn of Wales
description: The Llewellen of Wales tartan is a captivating Name tartan that proudly embodies the rich heritage of Wales. Registered to commemorate the growing popularity of the Cilt tradition, which has its roots in the late 20th century, this distinctive tartan stands out from its Celtic counterparts with its unusual thread count and colour scheme. Despite not having historical or genealogical significance, the 'of Wales' designation serves as a testament to Sheila Daniel's collaboration with Cambrian Woollen Mill, now sadly closed. This unique design reflects the evolving nature of traditional Welsh attire, where innovation meets cultural revival, and its inclusion in this index acknowledges the significant role Wales Tartan Centres has played in revitalising the Cilt tradition. As such, the Llewellen of Wales tartan remains a notable example of modern tartan-making, one that skillfully weaves together history, heritage, and creative flair.

name: Lloyd #2
description: The Lloyd of Astargus tartan is a poignant tribute to the rich heritage of Scottish ancestry, carefully crafted by Lloyd, James & Katheryne to commemorate its bearers' connection to Scotland. This clan tartan, categorised as Family, proudly represents the Lloyds with Scottish bloodline, their 'Astargus' name derived from Gaelic words meaning 'travelling or making distance', evoking a sense of wanderlust and homecoming. Designed by James Lloyd, born in Ottawa in 1969 to Welsh & Scottish roots, this tartan embodies the values of tradition, identity, and community that are at the heart of Scotland's storied past. As a symbol of family pride and Scottish heritage, the Lloyd of Astargus tartan invites wearers to connect with their ancestors and celebrate the enduring spirit of the Lloyds, no matter where life may take them.

name: Lloyd [default]
description: The Lloyd of Dolobran tartan is a rich and storied tradition, steeped in the history of one of Scotland's most illustrious clans. This personal clan tartan, borne by the MacGregor-Hastie family for generations, boasts a striking non-repeating pattern that showcases the skill and craftsmanship of traditional Scottish weaving. Dating back to an uncertain but likely 1930s or 1940s creation, this asymmetrical design is a testament to the ingenuity and creativity of its original weaver(s). Now preserved in the cloth archive of the Scottish Tartans Society, the Lloyd of Dolobran tartan stands as a proud symbol of family heritage, honouring the legacy of the MacGregors and Hasties who wore it with pride. Its inclusion within the archives is a tribute to the enduring significance of this clan's tradition, one that continues to weave its way through Scottish history and culture.

name: Lloyd of Wales
description: The Lloyd of Wales tartan is a vibrant and distinctive name tartan with a rich cultural heritage, born from the modern tradition of Welsh textile arts. Designed by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys (now closed), this tartan was created in collaboration with Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea, to promote the resurgence of traditional Welsh weaving since the late 1990s. With its unique warp and weft patterns, featuring almost entirely odd-numbered threads, the Lloyd of Wales tartan stands out from other Celtic designs. Originally intended for commercial purposes, its popularity has grown exponentially, with the 'of Wales' descriptor serving as a nod to its origin rather than historical territorial significance. As such, this tartan does not claim genealogical or historical validity but remains an important symbol of modern Welsh cultural identity and textile heritage, earning its place in the UK's rich tapestry of traditional designs.

name: Lobban
description: The Lobban tartan is a deeply personal and enigmatic Scottish heritage design, woven into the very fabric of family legacy and history. As a registered Name tartan, its significance lies in its association with an individual or family bearing the name 'Lobban', whose distinctive patterns and colours are now etched into the annals of tartan tradition. With its unique colour palette carefully selected to ensure accuracy against the original sample, this tartan is a testament to the importance of preserving Scotland's rich cultural heritage. Though its origins remain shrouded in mystery, the Lobban tartan stands as a proud representation of Scottish identity and tradition, passed down through generations with honour and care.

name: Loch Awe
description: The Loch Awe tartan, carefully crafted by renowned designer Jeffrey MacArthur-Fox, embodies the rich heritage and storied history of Scotland's west coast. Specifically designed to reflect the families and geographic area surrounding the majestic Loch Awe, this District tartan weaves a tapestry of meaning that resonates deeply with the region's inhabitants. The base colours of black, green, and blue pay homage to the Black Watch, while the additional colour lines evoke the various Campbell tartans, nodding to the prominent clan's historical significance in the area. Originally created for all who wish to wear it, this tartan invites wearers to connect with their roots and the natural beauty that defines Scotland's most breathtaking landscapes.

name: Loch Carron District
description: Loch Carron, a majestic district tartan, is steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's rugged landscapes and storied past. Woven with precision, its subtle palette evokes the serene beauty of the ancient lochs that crisscross the Highlands. This storied tartan, registered by the Scottish Tartans Society, bears witness to the region's enduring legacy as a haven for history, culture, and natural splendour. While no designer is attributed to this design, it is evident that its subtle nuances have been carefully considered to evoke the essence of District tartan tradition. As such, Loch Carron serves as a testament to Scotland's timeless traditions, inviting wearers to pay homage to the land, its people, and their storied heritage.

name: Loch Fyne
description: The Loch Fyne tartan is a poignant tribute to the rich cultural heritage of the Scottish Highlands, specifically the tranquil region surrounding Loch Fyne on the island of Islay. This District tartan was designed with a singular purpose in mind: to serve as a symbol of community and identity for local youth groups, including the Gaelic Choir and junior pipe band that call the area home. Woven by the skilled hands of the Islay Woollen Mill, this tartan weaves together the threads of tradition and cultural heritage, evoking the rugged beauty and warm camaraderie of life on the island. With its unique characteristics and restricted use to specific local groups, the Loch Fyne tartan embodies the values of community, connection, and a deep affection for the land that inspired it.

name: Loch Garth District
description: Loch Garth tartan is a sumptuous Fashion tartan whose rich, muted hues evoke the tranquility of Scotland's serene landscapes. This distinctive pattern, designated as such by Alec Lumsden of Toronto, a renowned tartan collector, tells the story of a picturesque loch, perhaps reflecting the tranquil beauty of the Scottish Highlands. Characterised by its balanced and harmonious tone palette of blues and greens, Loch Garth tartan is a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy in textile design. With no specific clan or family affiliation linked to this tartan, it remains accessible to anyone who wishes to incorporate elements of Scottish heritage into their fashion choices, making it an excellent choice for those seeking a stylish connection to the country's natural splendour.

name: Loch Laggan District
description: The Loch Laggan tartan is a deeply rooted connection to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, reflecting the history and geography of the Central Highlands. Originally identified as part of the Highland Society of London Collection, its origins remain shrouded in mystery, with some hinting at its existence in the region over centuries past. However, Margaret MacDougall, curator of Inverness Museum, recalled hearing tales from Sir Stewart MacPherson about a tartan worn in this district long ago. This enigmatic tapestry is now an integral part of Scotland's national identity, evoking the majestic landscapes and storied traditions of Badenoch at the head of Glen Spean, where Loch Laggan lies in wait.

name: Loch Leven Dress
description: The Lochleven tartan, with its rich heritage woven into every thread, tells the story of a bygone era where dance and tradition came together in perfect harmony. This iconic Fashion tartan was first registered in 1993, specifically for dancers' kilts, evoking the vibrant spirit of Scotland's rich cultural landscape. Named after the historic Lochleven Castle, this distinctive design is deeply rooted in Scottish heritage, its precise sett woven to evoke the rhythm and movement of traditional dance. With no designer credited, it is said that this tartan's beauty lies not in human creation, but in the timeless traditions of Scotland itself. Today, this captivating design continues to inspire wearers, weaving together a sense of history, pride, and movement, as the very essence of Scottish tradition comes alive through every fibre of its intricate pattern.

name: Loch Leven
description: The Loch Leven tartan is a distinctive District pattern, born from the rich heritage of the Scottish Borders. Designed by Mrs P.J. Thompson, a respected textile artist, this tartan draws inspiration from the natural beauty of its namesake loch, nestled in the heart of Fife. As a variation of the esteemed Aviemore Check and Dogwood patterns, Loch Leven adds a new chapter to the story of Scottish tartans. This traditional design now proudly represents Clan Crest textiles, showcasing Thompson's expertise in crafting unique and meaningful fabrics that honour Scotland's history and culture. The fact that it was showcased in the Johnston Collection, a prestigious archive of Scottish tartans, underscores its significance and relevance within the world of tartan heritage.

name: Loch Lochy
description: The Loch Lochy tartan is an evocative blend of blues and greens, evoking the tranquillity of Scotland's iconic lochs. Designed by Jeffrey MacArthur-Fox, this Fashion tartan was created with the aim of capturing the essence of the Lochaber area, rather than adhering to traditional Clan designs. Its inspiration lies in the natural beauty of the surroundings, where the subtle hues of heather and water lilies blend seamlessly into the landscape. With no specific clan affiliation required, the Loch Lochy tartan is open to anyone who wishes to wear it, making it a unique and accessible way for individuals to connect with Scottish heritage. Its versatility belies its deep roots in local tradition, inviting wearers to draw upon the timeless spirit of Scotland's natural beauty.

name: Loch Lomond #2
description: Loch Lomond #3 is a majestic fashion tartan, inspired by the breathtaking beauty of Scotland's most iconic loch. Named after this storied location, the design embodies the country's rich heritage and natural splendour. As part of the Scottish Tartans Society archive, it has been carefully recorded by renowned Canadian tartan collector, Alex Lumsden. This particular tartan falls under the fashion category, making it a versatile choice for clothing and textile enthusiasts alike. Its registration notes underscore its cultural significance, solidifying its place within Scotland's esteemed tartan legacy. As a testament to the nation's enduring connection with this majestic loch, Loch Lomond #3 is a timeless and evocative design that pays homage to the country's storied past, perfect for those seeking to add a touch of Scottish heritage to their wardrobe.

name: Loch Lomond
description: Loch Lomond #2, a fashion tartan of great beauty and symbolism, originates from Scotland's storied past yet has taken on a distinctly Canadian flair. This iconic sett was originally created by an unknown designer, whose exact identity is lost to time. Characterised by its striking blue-grey hues reminiscent of Scotland's majestic lochs, Loch Lomond #2 features a classic black-and-green pattern that evokes the rugged grandeur of the Scottish Highlands. Despite no clear designer credits, this tartan has been woven with precision and flair, embodying the timeless charm of traditional Scottish heritage. Its registration as a Canadian fashion tartan highlights its enduring appeal across borders, while its striking colours have captured the hearts of many who appreciate the beauty of Scotland's iconic tartans.

name: Loch Lomond Trading Company
description: The Loch Lomond tartan, woven by Gary & Rowena Groves in 1999, is a masterful interpretation of Scotland's majestic landscape. This stunning Fashion tartan draws inspiration from the natural hues of its namesake loch - a deep ecclesiastical purple evoking the reverence of St Kessog, paired with rich red tones reminiscent of the Lennox tartan. The addition of green and aqua undertones brings to mind the glacial waters and surrounding hillsides of this most iconic of Scottish lochs. As a Fashion tartan, it is free to be worn with pride by anyone who values traditional heritage, while also being mindful of its association with the Loch Lomond Trading Company Ltd - an important consideration for those seeking to wear their colours with honour.

name: Loch Ness #2
description: The Loch Ness tartan, a timeless and captivating pattern born from the misty shores of Scotland's most famous loch, is a quintessential fashion choice for those who embody the country's rich heritage. Registered in 1983, this distinctive tartan has been woven into kiltmakers' trade sets for decades, its beauty and symbolism etched deep into Scottish tradition. Characterised by an intricate balance of blues and greens, evoking the mysterious depths of Loch Ness itself, this pattern pays homage to the country's rugged yet enchanting landscapes. As a fashion tartan, it invites wearers to tap into Scotland's storied past, while its versatility ensures it remains a stylish choice for those who appreciate the country's unique cultural identity.

name: Loch Rannoch
description: Loch Rannoch is a captivating fashion tartan that has yet to reveal its origins, leaving its history shrouded in mystery. Registered by an anonymous designer, this striking pattern embodies the essence of Scottish heritage, evoking the rugged beauty of the Highlands' majestic lochs and glens. As part of the Fashion category, Loch Rannoch is a testament to the enduring allure of traditional tartan design, reimagined for modern fashion enthusiasts. Its very existence is a tribute to Scotland's rich cultural legacy, where the boundaries between past and present are woven together in a tapestry of vibrant colours and timeless charm.

name: Loch Tummel District
description: The Loch Tummel tartan is a captivating fashion tartan, its intricate pattern evoking the serene beauty of Scotland's lochs. With a rich history dating back to its registration with the Scottish Tartans Society as a trade sett, this distinctive design has been woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage for centuries. Originally created without an explicit designer attributed, its enduring appeal lies in its timeless charm and ability to evoke the rugged yet refined spirit of Scotland's natural landscapes. As a fashion tartan, Loch Tummel invites wearers to tap into their own sense of Scottish identity and tradition, while its Trade sett classification signifies its origins as a commercial pattern, intended to adorn everyday garments rather than ceremonial attire. This striking tartan design continues to captivate those drawn to the beauty and authenticity of Scotland's rich cultural legacy.

name: Lochaber Cameron
description: The Lochaber Cameron tartan is a timeless and storied weave, born from the skilled hands of John Wilson's descendants at Wilsons of Bannockburn, where tradition meets innovation since 1786. This distinctive Other category tartan is steeped in history, drawing inspiration from the rugged landscape of the Scottish Highlands, specifically the Lake District of Lochaber, which gives it its name. With a rich, muted palette, this tartan is redolent of the wild, windswept moors and heather-clad hills of Scotland's most majestic regions. As registered with the National Museum of Scotland, the Lochaber Cameron tartan holds an honourable place in the annals of Scottish heritage, its legacy a testament to the enduring craftsmanship and attention to detail that has defined Wilsons for generations.

name: Lochaber Scrapbook
description: This enchanting tartan, known as the Lochaber, is an evocative blend of colours reminiscent of Scotland's majestic landscapes. Originating from a scrapbook purchased from Unicorn Books in June 1996, this historic pattern is believed to date back to the late 19th or early 20th century, a period when fashion tartans were gaining popularity. The anonymous designer has skillfully woven together a palette of blues and greens, evoking the misty lochs and rolling hills of Scotland's west coast. Notably, this tartan holds sentimental value, as it was reportedly favoured by the great-great-grandfather of its current owner, adding a touching layer of personal heritage to this timeless pattern.

name: Lochaber [default]
description: The Lochaber tartan, a symbol of Scotland's rich heritage, is a deeply rooted District tartan with an uncertain yet storied past. Dating back to at least 1797, its origins remain shrouded in mystery, but it has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition for generations. As part of Wilsons of Bannockburn's esteemed collection, this tartan was first recorded in their 1819 Key Pattern Book, cementing its place in the annals of Scottish textile history. A testament to the region's storied past, Lochaber tartan exudes a sense of rugged beauty and time-honoured craftsmanship, evoking images of rolling hills and windswept lochs that crisscross Scotland's Highlands. Its intricate design, though shrouded in uncertainty, remains an honour to wear, connecting the wearer to the ancient heritage and cultural identity of this captivating District tartan.

name: Lochcarron (Scotland) personal #2
description: The Lochcarron of Scotland corporate tartan is an embodiment of Scottish heritage and professionalism, evoking the majestic landscapes of the Highlands with its striking blue and green hues. Designed by the renowned Lochcarron of Scotland mill, this distinctive tartan pattern is a testament to the country's rich tradition of weaving and textile craftsmanship. As a corporate tartan, it is ideally suited for formal wear, from business attire to ceremonial events, where its dignified presence commands respect. With no specific details known about its registration history, the Lochcarron of Scotland tartan remains a mysterious and intriguing aspect of Scottish identity, inviting wearers to connect with the country's storied past while making a lasting impression in the present.

name: Lochcarron (Scotland) personal; 1985
description: The Lochcarron tartan is a timeless fashion classic, born from the esteemed Scottish textile company, Lochcarron of Scotland. Registered in 1985 under the Fashion category, this iconic design is an homage to the rich heritage of the Highlands. By copying the original colour palette from a 1985 catalogue, the designers have skillfully preserved the essence of this traditional tartan, evoking memories of mist-shrouded lochs and rugged mountain landscapes. Without restriction, this vibrant pattern invites wearers to make a statement, while still paying homage to the storied history of Scottish fashion. This stylish tartan has become an enduring symbol of sophistication and elegance, perfect for adding a touch of traditional charm to modern attire.

name: Lochcarron (Scotland) personal; Camel
description: The Lochcarron Camel is a timeless and sophisticated fashion tartan that exudes the rich heritage and elegance of Scotland's finest weaving traditions. Registered as a fashion tartan in 1985, this distinctive design has been delighting enthusiasts and designers alike for decades with its classic, elegant colours. Bred from the iconic Lochcarron style, the Camel features a subtle palette of blues, greens, and browns that evoke the rolling hills and majestic lochs of Scotland's rugged landscapes. With no restrictions on use, this stunning tartan invites the wearer to don their heritage with pride, evoking images of traditional Highland dress and modern fashion fusion. Designed by Lochcarron of Scotland, this revered tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile craftsmanship and its enduring appeal in the world of fashion.

name: Lochcarron (Scotland) personal; Dress
description: The Lochcarron Dress tartan is a stalwart of Scottish corporate heritage, bearing the proud crest of the renowned textile house, Lochcarron of Scotland. This timeless tartan, featuring a rich palette of blues, greens, and golds, is woven from a traditional sett that evokes the majestic landscapes of the Scottish Highlands. As a Category Corporate design, it has been carefully crafted to convey a sense of sophistication and professionalism, making it an ideal choice for businesses seeking a strong visual identity. With no specific details available regarding its origins or historical significance within Lochcarron's archives, the tartan remains shrouded in mystery, adding to its allure as a quintessential symbol of Scottish enterprise and tradition.

name: Lochcarron (Scotland) personal; Hunting
description: The Lochcarron Hunting tartan is a quintessential example of corporate tartanry, born from the innovative spirit of Lochcarron of Scotland. This striking pattern, woven with precision and flair, is specifically designed for business attire, evoking the rugged yet refined traditions of Scotland's hunting heritage. As a Corporate tartan, it has been carefully crafted to evoke confidence, authority, and distinction on the office floor, where its noble hues - rich blues, emerald greens, and burnished golds - are sure to make a lasting impression. With no restrictions in place, this tartan is free to be worn with pride by those who aspire to exude style and sophistication, embodying the very essence of Scottish craftsmanship and tradition.

name: Lochnagar
description: The Lochnagar tartan is a quintessential Fashion tartan, woven with meticulous precision to evoke the rugged beauty of the Deeside District's majestic mountains. Designed by renowned Aberdeen Historian and author Fenton Wynnss, this distinctive fabric tells the story of the late Queen Mother's affection for the region, having worn it as a show-stopping skirt during a private picnic in the Aberdeenshire hills. Marled grey threads add a subtle nuance to the design, echoing the soft hues of the Scottish landscape. As a Fashion tartan, the Lochnagar is not tied to any specific clan or heritage group, instead embracing its connection to the natural world and the region's rich history, making it a timeless choice for those seeking to wear their love of Scotland on their sleeve.

name:
Lochranza
[AKA] Isle of Arran Distillery
description: The Lochranza tartan is a corporate colour scheme woven with pride and heritage, born from the collaboration between renowned Scottish textile experts Lochcarron of Scotland and Douglas Davidson for the esteemed Lochranza Distillery Visitor Centre on the Isle of Arran. This unique tartan was specifically designed to create a sense of unity and identity among staff members, featuring a distinctive blend of blue, green, and yellow hues that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's iconic landscapes. Originally crafted into a variety of garments, including waistcoats, trews, kilts, skirts, and ties, this corporate tartan was worn by staff to promote brand awareness and pride, while also being sold in the Visitor Centre as a testament to the distillery's rich heritage.

name: Lochwood Estate Check
description: The Lochwood Estate Check is a District tartan of great historical significance, designed by Bill Johnston for his eponymous estate in Skippak, Pennsylvania. First registered in 1992, this unique tartan was intended to evoke the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands, despite being woven from non-traditional colours. The design's NWB:YKW code indicates a complex palette of five shades, including grey, white, blue, yellow, and black, which was lost when woven by Peter MacDonald in 1993, resulting in this distinctive check pattern. As one of the first district tartans to be registered outside of Scotland, Lochwood Estate Check serves as a fascinating example of cultural exchange and adaptation, bridging the gap between Scottish heritage and American tradition.

name: Lockhart [default]
description: The Lockhart tartan, designed by Angus Lockhart in 1996, holds significant cultural importance as a symbol of the Lowland family's connection to the MacDonalds of Clanranald. This clan tartan, though not strictly a traditional Highland clan tartan, reflects the family's affinity with their Seigneurial counterparts and is woven from the finest Selkirk materials. The intricate sett, featuring a predominantly green and blue palette, has been meticulously registered in the Lyon Court Books and bears the Lord Lyon's approval. As such, this tartan is not only a nod to Lockhart heritage but also an embodiment of the enduring bonds between Scottish families across generations. For those who wear the Lockhart tartan with honour, it serves as a reminder of the rich tapestry of Scotland's clan history and tradition.

name: Locky
description: The Locky tartan is a unique and intriguing name, one that whispers secrets of its origins as a personal symbol. Assumed to be a familial or individual emblem, this tartan's design, though shrouded in mystery, exudes an air of tradition and heritage. Crafted by renowned designer Dalgliesh, D C, with the expertise of D C Dalgliesh Ltd., it is restricted for weaving purposes, implying that its significance lies not only in its aesthetic appeal but also in its connection to a person or family's honour. Like the rugged Scottish landscape that inspired so many tartan designs, Locky embodies the timeless spirit of the Highlands, evoking a sense of nostalgia and pride in those who wear it. Its classification as a Name tartan highlights the significance of personal identity and tradition, underscoring the enduring power of this intricate and storied fabric.

name: Loevenstein Castle; 1
description: The Loevenstein Castle tartan is a captivating tribute to Scotland's rich heritage, woven from the colours and stories of a bygone era. Originally painted on the walls of its eponymous Dutch castle in the 1750s, this intricate design has been meticulously re-constructed and woven by skilled Dutch weavers as a testament to the cultural exchange between Scotland and Europe during the 18th century. The tartan's complex pattern is said to hold nods to Scottish clans and traditions, making it a rare and significant find, referenced in esteemed historical texts such as Neil Grant's work from 1987 (P38). Notably, the black threads may be interpreted as a nod to either navy or dark blue, giving the design a subtle yet nuanced quality. As an 'Other' category tartan, this distinctive design holds a special place within Scottish tartan heritage, embodying the spirit of cultural exchange and artistic collaboration that has defined Scotland's rich textile history.

name: Loevenstein Castle; 2
description: Loevenstein Castle #2 is a unique and enigmatic tartan, its origins shrouded in mystery until its rediscovery at Loevenstein Castle in Holland. Painted on the castle's walls circa 1750, it is believed to have been created by a Scottish officer stationed there with Scottish troops, infusing their heritage into this captivating design. This other category tartan boasts an intriguing narrative, reflecting the cultural exchange and historical ties between Scotland and the Netherlands during the 18th century. Discovered in 1983, the tartan was painstakingly re-constructed and woven by Dutch weavers, with reference to Scottish clans and their tartans, as noted in Neil Grant's seminal work, P38. As a result, Loevenstein Castle #2 is not only a striking textile pattern but also a poignant reminder of Scotland's enduring legacy in the Netherlands, its rich history, and the lasting impact of cultural crossroads on traditional weaving.

name: Loevenstein Castle; 3
description: This distinctive tartan, aptly named Loevenstein Castle #3, holds a rich tapestry of history and cultural significance, woven into its very fabric. Originating from the 18th-century murals adorning the walls of Holland's Loevenstein Castle, this tartan was likely created by a Scottish officer stationed at the castle during that era. The design, now meticulously re-constructed and woven by Dutch weavers in 1983, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage in Europe. With no clear association with a specific Scottish clan, its 'Other' category underscores its unique status as a cultural relic from this period of intermixture between Scotland and the Continent. This captivating tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the complex history that shaped the world we know today, inviting wearers to partake in a fascinating chapter of Scottish tradition.

name: Logan #1
description: The Buchanan, John & Isabella tartan is a poignant commemorative design that pays tribute to the enduring bond between two families, forged in friendship and loyalty. Inspired by a cherished photograph of John and Bella Buchanan, standing proudly together, Graham Alexander Robieson's masterful creation weaves a tapestry of warmth and remembrance. Originally commissioned by Geoffrey Highland Crafts Limited, this universal tartan honours Isabella and John Buchanan, whose family connection transcended generations, much like the strong tradition of Scottish clan ties. As a testament to their friendship, the intricate colours - carefully selected by Robieson - blend in harmony, evoking a sense of unity and honouring the legacy that binds families together through the ages.

name: Logan Dark
description: The Logan - 1819 (Dark) tartan is a timeless and evocative fashion tartan, steeped in the rich history of Scotland's noble clans. This variation on the iconic Logan tartan was designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, a renowned Scottish textile firm, in 1819. As one of two registered variations on the original No 119, this dark-hued interpretation is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Logan clan, whose proud heritage has been woven into the very fabric of Scotland's cultural identity. With its distinctive colour palette and precise sett pattern, this tartan invites wearers to honour their Scottish roots and connect with the storied past of Scotland's clans, while also evoking the elegance and sophistication of traditional Scottish fashion.

name: Logan #5
description: The Logan tartan, registered in 1819 by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is an esteemed emblem of Scottish heritage and tradition. As one of the earliest Fancy Patterns adopted by a clan, it boasts a unique charm that has captivated enthusiasts for centuries. The design's intricate pattern, featuring a subtle blend of blue, green, yellow, red, black, brown, and white hues, reflects the storied history and resilience of Clan Logan. With its roots in 19th-century Scotland, this tartan was once known as Skene, further underscoring its rich ancestry. As an enduring symbol of Scottish family pride, the Logan tartan continues to adorn kilts, scarves, and other textiles with honour, evoking a deep sense of tradition and cultural heritage that resonates across generations.

name: Logan #7
description: The Logan - 1819 (with Yellow) tartan is an iconic fashion pattern that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's Highland clans. Registered with the prestigious Wilsons of Bannockburn in their 1819 Key Pattern Book, this distinctive tartan bears the name and colours of the esteemed clan, Logan. As a Fashion category design, it has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish style, evoking images of rugged landscapes, historic castles, and proud Highland traditions. With its characteristic Yellow tone adding a vibrant touch, this tartan is not only a testament to Scotland's storied past but also a popular choice for fashion connoisseurs seeking a unique and authentic connection to the country's rich cultural heritage.

name: Logan #6
description: The Jedburgh Woollen Mill's Logan (2000) fashion tartan is a vibrant and stylish interpretation of the iconic Clan tartan, carefully crafted to bring the warmth and heritage of Scotland to modern fashion enthusiasts. Born from the threads of tradition and innovation, this striking pattern is now yours to wear with honour, symbolising the proud history of the Logan Clan. As a fashion variant, it's designed to add a pop of Scottish flair to any outfit, perfect for those who want to pay tribute to their heritage or simply inject some tartan charm into their everyday look. With its bold colours and precise weave, this tartan design is a testament to Scotland's rich textile legacy, and Jedburgh Woollen Mill's expertise in preserving the country's time-honoured weaving traditions.

name: Logan Light
description: The Logan - 1819 (Light) tartan, designed by esteemed textile firm Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1819, is a timeless fashion classic steeped in Scottish heritage. Originally registered as one of Wilson's variations on No 119 or Logan, this light-toned tartan is deeply rooted in the traditions of the Scottish Highlands. Woven with care and attention to detail, its subtle colour palette evokes the rugged yet elegant landscapes of the Scottish hills. With its rich history and cultural significance, this tartan is not only a statement piece for fashion enthusiasts but also a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's iconic clan system, where heritage and tradition are woven into every thread.

name: Logan [default]
description: The Logan tartan, registered in 1831, is a stalwart symbol of Scottish heritage, hailing from one of Scotland's most storied clans. This iconic tartan, woven with precision by James Logan himself, has stood the test of time, frequently boasting an unmistakable characteristic: five red lines of equal width that dance across its fabric. Originally designed to represent the Logan family's identity and pride, this tartan now shares a special affinity with the MacLennan clan, demonstrating the deep connections forged between Scotland's clans through shared history and tradition. As a testament to Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, the Logan tartan remains an enduring emblem of Scottish heritage, evoking feelings of pride, loyalty, and kinship among those who wear it.

name: Loganair Uniform Skirt
description: The Loganair tartan is a striking example of Scottish corporate wear, born from the humble beginnings of hostesses at Loganair, a pioneering regional airline in Scotland's Highlands. Initially adopted for their iconic skirts, which were worn by these trailblazing women from 1988 until the uniform was replaced with a more modern design. This tartan, now classified as Corporate, embodies the warmth and hospitality that defined Loganair's service, evoking memories of traditional Scottish heritage and the pioneering spirit of those who wore it. Its significance extends beyond its origins, symbolising the intersection of innovation, community, and national pride in the Scottish aviation industry.

name: Lomond 1983
description: The Lomond tartan, registered in 1983 under the Fashion category, is a vibrant and dynamic design that evokes the majesty of Scotland's finest landscapes. This distinctive pattern, created by West Coast Woolen Mill, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage and textile tradition. Originally featured in the esteemed Johnston Collection, this tartan's sample showcases its bold, interlocking colours - blues and greens reminiscent of glacial lochs and serene mountain ranges. While there are no restrictions on its use beyond the realm of fashion, it remains an authentic representation of Scotland's rich cultural fabric, waiting to be woven into garments that celebrate the nation's beauty and identity.

name: Lomond
description: The Lomond tartan, registered as a fashion tartan by Jedburgh Woollen Mill, embodies the enduring spirit of Scotland's iconic landscapes. Inspired by the majestic Lomond Hills in central Scotland, this richly woven fabric is a testament to the country's profound connection with its natural heritage. As a fashion tartan, it brings together elements of Scottish tradition and modern flair, offering a distinctive choice for those seeking to adorn themselves with the country's storied history. Notably, its registration notes caution against any potential confusion with rival Kile/Kyle tartans, suggesting a deliberate nod towards Scotland's complex tapestry of clan affiliations and regional identities.

name: London 1988
description: The London '88 tartan is a poignant commemorative design, meticulously crafted by Malcolm Campbell to celebrate Edinburgh Woollen Mill's participation in the Lord Mayor's Show in 1988. This distinctive tartan pays tribute to the city's rich history, with its colour scheme mirroring the arms of Christopher Collett, Lord Mayor of London, featuring shades of gold and red reminiscent of the Mayoral chain of office. The incorporation of white overchecks echoes the City of London's arms, creating a striking visual representation of the occasion's significance. With restrictions in place to preserve its original intent, this tartan serves as a lasting tribute to the city's cultural heritage, its design rooted in tradition and nostalgia, evoking memories of a special moment in London's history.

name: London Caledonian
description: The London Caledonian tartan, expertly woven by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage in corporate attire. This striking Corporate tartan features three shades of blue - dark blue, which is reminiscent of Scotland's majestic skies, and two lighter blues that evoke the soft glow of a Highland sunset - creating a captivating visual contrast. Originally registered from Wilsons' notebook notes and supplemented by a sample shown in a weaving book, this tartan design pays homage to the rich cultural traditions of Scotland, where blue was once considered an important colour symbolising loyalty and prestige. Worn with pride by those who value Scottish heritage and tradition, the London Caledonian tartan is a fitting choice for businesses seeking to establish a strong connection with their Scottish roots.

name: London Caledonian Games Association
description: The London Caledonian Games Association tartan is a rich and storied design, woven from threads of tradition and heritage. As a Corporate tartan, it was created to represent the esteemed association's values and identity, symbolising unity and camaraderie among its members. Designed by John Hannay, Vice President of the London Caledonian Games Association in 1933, this tartan pays homage to Scotland's proud sporting traditions and the iconic games held annually at Hampstead Heath. Notably, it appears to share similarities with another well-known design, Wilsons' London Caledonian, suggesting a possible connection between these two prestigious tartans. This intriguing paradox is a testament to the complexity and richness of Scottish textile heritage, where tradition and innovation intersect.

name: London Caledonian Rugby Club
description: The London Caledonian Rugby Club tartan is a vibrant representation of corporate heritage, proudly worn by staff and members of this esteemed organisation. As a registered club tartan, it embodies the history and tradition of the rugby club, its colours paying homage to the rich cultural landscape of Scotland. With its bold design and energetic hues, this tartan celebrates the camaraderie and community that defines the world of rugby, while also serving as an enduring symbol of London's own unique Scottish heritage. By donning this distinctive pattern, individuals are not only representing their affiliation with the club, but also connecting with a broader tradition of Scottish textiles that have been woven into the fabric of British culture for centuries.

name: London Community Gospel Choir
description: The London Community Gospel Choir tartan is a vibrant and uplifting fabric that embodies the spirit of music, community, and faith. Designed by Douglas Gillespie for Geoffrey Highland Crafts of Edinburgh, this corporate tartan tells the story of one of the UK's longest-standing award-winning gospel choirs, the London Community Gospel Choir (LCGC). Founded in 1982 by Revd Bazil Meade and Lawrence Johnson, Delroy Powell, and John Francis, the choir pioneered concert gospel music in Britain. Today, this tartan is woven with pride and control, strictly adhering to the vision of its founder, Rev Bazil Meade. As a symbol of unity and celebration, this corporate tartan is perfect for anyone involved with or inspired by the London Community Gospel Choir's mission to spread love, hope, and gospel music throughout their community.

name: London Fog Black
description: This captivating tartan, aptly titled London Fog Black, embodies the quintessential essence of British style and sophistication. As a fashion tartan, it was created by renowned designer London Fog to add a touch of urban chic to any outfit. The subtle palette, evoking the misty veil of London's iconic fog, features a predominantly dark blue-grey background with strategically placed flecks of navy, black, and grey, carefully arranged in a unique pattern. By adopting this tartan as inspiration, you'll be paying homage to the city's rich heritage and tradition of fashion innovation, while also injecting a modern twist into your wardrobe. With its understated elegance, London Fog Black is sure to delight those with an eye for sophisticated style and a taste for the finer things in life.

name: London House Ltd Diana Princess
description: The Princess Diana tartan is an exquisite Fashion tartan, created by renowned Scottish designer Peter MacDonald in 1997. Inspired by the enduring legacy of the beloved former Princess of Wales, this distinctive tartan pays homage to her royal heritage. Registration notes reveal that the design was initially registered as a work for sale and was subsequently sold to London House (231) Ltd., further solidifying its connection to British fashion traditions. As a Fashion tartan, the Princess Diana is distinguished from other categories by its commercial appeal, making it an ideal choice for designers and manufacturers seeking to incorporate this stylish pattern into their designs. With its elegant colours and intricate weave, this tartan design embodies the timeless elegance of Scottish textiles, making it a treasured addition to any fashion collection.

name: London House Ltd Diana Princess #2
description: The Diana Princess of Wales tartan is an enduring symbol of Scottish heritage and style, born from the visionary hands of renowned designer Peter MacDonald in 1997. This fashion tartan was specifically created to celebrate the life and legacy of the beloved Princess of Wales, a shining figure in British royal history. As a Category Fashion tartan, it was designed for general use, allowing wearers to proudly showcase their admiration for the princess through everyday attire. Notably, this tartan is held in trust by London House (231) Ltd., further underscoring its significance and connection to the royal family's legacy. With its rich colour palette and intricate pattern, this tartan weaves a poignant tribute to Diana's enduring influence on fashion and Scottish culture.

name: London Regiment
description: The London Regiment tartan is a storied and storied fabric, woven from the threads of a rich history that echoes through the heart of England's great capital city. Originally designed by esteemed weavers at Johnstons of Elgin in collaboration with Colin Hutcheson, this distinctive tartan represents the amalgamation of five Territorial Army Regiments - London Scottish, Queen's Regiment, City of London Fusiliers, London Irish Rifles, and Royal Green Jackets - which came together to form the modern-day London Regiment. The tartan serves as a proud badge of honour for those who have served in these iconic units, symbolising their unwavering dedication to duty and service. By its very existence, this tartan design embodies the spirit of camaraderie and resilience that defines the city's storied military heritage.

name: London Scottish Rugby Club
description: The London Scottish Rugby Club tartan is a unique and captivating corporate design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's rugby tradition. Registration notes indicate that it was originally designed by renowned tartan expert Kinloch Anderson for a special project with Art out of Africa, a South African company, but ultimately didn't find favour with its intended recipient. This intriguing history adds to the tartan's appeal, hinting at the complexities and nuances of cultural exchange between Scotland and the continent. With its distinctive pattern, carefully crafted to reflect the values and spirit of London Scottish Rugby Club, this tartan design embodies the perfect blend of tradition and innovation, making it a sought-after choice for those looking to connect with their Scottish roots or champion the sport they love.

name: Londonderry Irish County
description: The Londonderry, County tartan is a rich and evocative District pattern, steeped in the heritage of Northern Ireland's storied past. Designed by Polly Wittering for Macnaughtons of Pitlochry as a collection of trade tartans, this distinctive tartan was originally intended to commemorate the historic district from which it takes its name. As part of the House of Edgar's innovative approach to textile design, these 'unofficial' District tartans have won widespread favour among Scottish enthusiasts and collectors alike, who now eagerly await their formal recognition as authentic representations of Northern Ireland's cultural identity. With its intricate colour palette and nuanced sett structure, this captivating tartan embodies the enduring spirit of Irish tradition and the region's proud history.

name: Longford Irish County
description: The Longford, County tartan is a rich and storied design that reflects the heritage of Ireland's districts. Created by Polly Wittering for Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., specifically for the esteemed Macnaughton family of Pitlochry, this tartan embodies the spirit of commerce and community that defined traditional Irish trade weavings. As one of a series of District tartans not officially sanctioned by the Scottish Tartans Authority, yet widely adopted in their place, Longford, County has proven its authenticity through popular favour. Its intricate pattern, carefully woven to represent the identity of Macnaughton's role as local merchants and traders, now holds a special place in the hearts of those who cherish Ireland's cultural heritage, inviting wearers to honour their ancestral roots with every fibre of this timeless tartan.

name: Longhaugh Primary School
description: The Longhaugh Primary School tartan is a vibrant and meaningful tribute to Scotland's rich heritage, born from the collaborative efforts of 24 talented students in P4/P5 who designed it in 2004. Inspired by the historic Graham of Montrose tartan, which holds significance for Dundee's proud history, this corporate tartan proudly wears its colours on its sleeve - green, blue, and white, with bold reds and purples that pay homage to the city's beloved comic characters, Desperate Dan and Dennis the Menace. The subtle incorporation of black threads nods to the iconic Beano comics, while the narrow bands of purple represent the school's foundation year, 1958, in a beautiful nod to tradition and innovation. By combining the Graham tartan with these unique elements, the Longhaugh Primary School tartan becomes more than just a design - it is a celebration of community spirit, creativity, and the enduring legacy of Scotland's proud past.

name: Longmount
description: The Longmount tartan, born from the skilled hands of West Coast Woolen Mill's designers, is a stylish and modern addition to the world of fashion tartans. Once registered as a corporate tartan, its origins are rooted in the business world, where its unique characteristics were carefully crafted to evoke a sense of professionalism and sophistication. Now reclassified as a fashion tartan, Longmount's beauty lies in its ability to transcend traditional boundaries, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to add a touch of elegance to their wardrobe or personal style. With its subtle tone palette and thoughtful design, this tartan is poised to make a lasting impression on the catwalks and runways of fashion capitals around the world, keeping the rich tradition of Scottish textile heritage firmly in sight.

name:
Longniddry Dress; Eildon Blue
[AKA] Eildon
[AKA] Harmony Eildon #2
description: The Longniddry Blue, a Fashion tartan designed by esteemed weaver Dalgliesh in 1950s Selkirk, exudes the vibrant spirit of Scotland's rich cultural heritage. This intricate Dance pattern is a testament to the traditional craftsmanship and artistic flair of the country's oldest weaving traditions. Originally registered under three distinct names - Longniddry #5486, Eildon #4799, and Harmony Eildon #87 - this tartan has been shrouded in mystery, awaiting resolution from Scottish authorities. As a Fashion design, it was intended to evoke the joy and movement of traditional Highland dancing, with its repeating motifs and subtle colour palette evoking the misty lochs and rugged glens of Scotland's majestic landscape. Prepared for weaving by Dalgliesh Ltd., this tartan is now poised to bring the beauty of Scotland's heritage to modern fashion enthusiasts, awaiting clearance from the Scottish Tartans Authority to unfurl its full splendour.

name: Longniddry Dress; Green
description: Longniddry Green is a vibrant and dynamic Fashion tartan, aptly named after the village in East Lothian that has been a hub for traditional Scottish textile production for centuries. This stunning Dancers' Fancy, as indicated by its registration notes, was designed by Dalgliesh, D C of Selkirk, to showcase the elegance and sophistication of Scottish dancewear. With its intricate, interlocking patterns, Longniddry Green evokes the energy and movement of traditional Scottish Highland dances, such as the Reel and Jig. While available for commercial weaving, this tartan design holds a special place in the hearts of those who value their connection to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, reflecting the country's enduring tradition of excellence in textile craftsmanship.

name: Longniddry Dress; Lavender
description: The Longniddry Lavender Dance tartan is a captivating fashion design inspired by the traditional weaving heritage of Scotland's eastern coast, particularly the historic town of Dunbar, which Longniddry was. First registered in 2004, this unique tartan is a modern interpretation of the original D.C. Dalgleish dancers' tartan, showcased in his swatch book. Characterised by its soothing lavender hues and intricate patterns, the Longniddry Lavender Dance tartan evokes a sense of elegance and sophistication, reminiscent of traditional Scottish kilts worn during formal dances and celebrations. As a fashion category tartan, it is suited for garments such as kilt jackets, trews, or scarves, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to add a touch of heritage-inspired style to their wardrobe.

name: Longniddry Dress; Purple
description: The Longniddry Purple tartan, designed by esteemed weaver Dalgliesh, DC, is a masterful representation of Scotland's rich textile heritage. Specifically categorised as a fashion tartan, its bold and vibrant hues are inspired by the 'dancers fancy' tradition, evoking the dynamic energy of traditional Scottish dance performances. This unique tartan bears a striking resemblance to another notable design, the Eildon tartan, further underscoring its connection to Scotland's storied tartan traditions. Interestingly, the Longniddry Purple tartan is subject to restrictions, with careful consideration given by Dalgliesh, DC, in collaboration with D C Dalgliesh Ltd, ensuring that this beautiful design remains true to its heritage. With its captivating colour palette and proud history, the Longniddry Purple tartan continues to enchant those drawn to Scotland's timeless and iconic textiles.

name: Longniddry Dress; Red
description: This majestic Longniddry Burgundy (Dance) tartan is a masterpiece of Scottish craftsmanship, steeped in tradition and heritage. Registered as "A Dancer's Fancy" by renowned weaver D.C. Dalgliesh of Selkirk, this fashion tartan embodies the lively spirit of Scotland's rich cultural landscape. Originally known for its association with Longniddry Castle, a 15th-century stronghold in West Lothian, the tartan's intricate colour palette and rhythmic sett evoke the elegance of Highland dancing. As a celebrated creation from Dalgliesh's esteemed House of Tartans, this particular design is both a tribute to Scotland's storied past and a celebration of its enduring traditions. Its status as a Fashion tartan underscores its suitability for modern wearers who wish to embody the timeless essence of Scottish heritage.

name: Longniddry Dress; Turquoise
description: The Longniddry Turquoise, or 'Dance', is a vibrant Fashion tartan that embodies the energetic spirit of traditional Scottish dance. Registered in 1924 by renowned Scottish textile designer D C Dalgliesh of Selkirk, this striking pattern was inspired by the lively movements and colours of the dancers' fancy, a popular form of step dancing in Scotland's Highlands. The turquoise dominant hues evoke the icy sparkle of the glens, while the deeper blues and greens recall the rich earthy tones of the Scottish landscape. As a fashionable tartan, the Longniddry Turquoise is perfect for those seeking to add a touch of traditional elegance to their wardrobe or design projects, provided that they comply with the registration restrictions in place to protect Dalgliesh's original work.

name: Longniddry
description: The Longniddry tartan is a striking example of Scottish heritage's enduring influence on fashion, bearing testament to the rich tradition of tartan design. As a non-reversing pattern, it proudly flaunts its distinctive colours against a neutral background, making it an ideal choice for those seeking a bold yet versatile statement piece. With its American fashion classification, this tartan is well-suited to modern ensembles, effortlessly blending traditional flair with contemporary style. Characteristically, the Longniddry's colours work in harmony to evoke a sense of rugged elegance, redolent of Scotland's storied history and the unbridled spirit that once defined its brave Highland warriors.

name: Lootens Jensen
description: Lootens Jensen is a uniquely personal tartan design created by the esteemed Marjorie Warren, renowned for her work in preserving and promoting Scotland's rich textile heritage. This name tartan, designated as such due to its distinctive characteristics and family connections, serves as a testament to the enduring power of Scottish identity and tradition. While the registration notes are currently shrouded in mystery, it is clear that Lootens Jensen holds significant cultural significance for its creator and their community, weaving together threads of heritage, history, and personal narrative in a vibrant tapestry of colour and texture.

name: Lopez
description: The Lopez-Gasparotto tartan is a poignant tribute to Sergeant Melvyn Lopez's heritage and service, carefully crafted by weavers Fraser & Kirkbright. Submitted in his honour, this distinctive Name tartan proudly wears its threadcount doubled signature, a testament to the skill of its creators. Born from a year of military duty in Iraq, where Lopez discovered piping, this tartan is both a symbol of his personal identity and a nod to his Puerto Rican roots through the incorporation of the surname Gasparotto, which holds great meaning for him. Wefting together elements of tradition and modernity, the Lopez-Gasparotto tartan embodies the values of unity and community, allowing wearers to proudly connect with their shared surname heritage.

name: Lord Arran
description: The New Yorker tartan, designed by esteemed Lochcarron of Scotland, is a unique corporate tartan that weaves together heritage and innovation. Originally derived from the historic Earl of Arran tartan, this distinctive design has been reimagined for modern business attire, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to make a statement with their brand identity. As a registered corporate tartan, its use is reserved exclusively for Daidoh Ltd of Tokyo, Japan, underscoring the importance of cultural sensitivity and respect for traditional Scottish heritage. With its bold, contemporary twist on a storied past, the New Yorker tartan embodies the perfect blend of tradition and forward-thinking design, perfectly capturing the dynamic spirit of global business in the 21st century.

name: Lord Glenorchy
