The subtle nuances of this complex design evoke the rugged beauty of the Scottish landscape, while its gentle warmth speaks to the honour and prestige bestowed upon those who wear it. With no restrictions on its use, the Glenorchy, Lord tartan invites those who don it to embody a sense of tradition, nobility, and timeless elegance, reminding all who see it that true Scottish heritage is rooted in the stories of Scotland's storied past.

name: Lord Laird
description: The Lord Laird tartan is a timeless fashion icon, woven with the rich heritage of Scotland's storied past. With no restrictions on use, the Lord Laird tartan invites those who wear it to embody a sense of nobility and tradition, their Scottish heritage woven proudly into every fibre of their being.

name:
Lorne
[AKA] Fifth Royal Scots of Canada

name: Los Angeles

As a District tartan, Los Angeles is specifically woven for those who call the city home or have a strong connection to its diverse communities, making it a unique and meaningful way to represent one's honour and heritage.

name: Los Angeles Police Bagpipe Band

As a symbol of unity and civic pride, this tartan represents the City of Angels' enduring spirit and its deep-rooted connection to Scotland's iconic bagpipe tradition. With restrictions carefully noted in the registration notes, this design is a unique and exclusive representation of Los Angeles' honouring of Scottish heritage, making it an esteemed addition to any corporate attire or personal collection seeking to pay homage to this special bond between two nations.

name: Loton [default]
description: The Loton tartan is a deeply personal and family-orientated design, registered under the Clan/Family category, reflecting its origin within a specific Scottish clan or kinship group. Notable for its specific restrictions, which stipulate that it can only be prepared for weaving by Dalgliesh's own company, the Loton tartan holds a unique place within Scottish textile history. As an authentic clan tartan, it is steeped in significance, not just as a symbol of family pride but also as a tangible link to Scotland's rich cultural past, evoking memories of clan gatherings, heritage celebrations, and timeless traditions that have been passed down through generations.

name: Loudoun's Highlanders
description: The Loudoun's Highlanders tartan is a proud emblem of Scottish heritage, its intricate threads woven into the fabric of military tradition. As a Military category tartan, it was originally designed to signify the allegiance of the Highland regiments, their distinctive patterns a badge of honour for those who served. The registration notes reveal a fascinating story of mistake and correction, as the count was initially misattributed to the Loudoun family, but subsequent research confirmed its true origins. Now recognised as an authentic representation of the Highlanders' tartan, it stands as a testament to the rich cultural legacy of Scotland's storied military past, its design evoking the bravery and resilience of those who wore it into battle.

name: Louisburg
description: The Louisburg tartan, registered by Edith MacIntyre & Jean Kyte, is a poignant tribute to the town's rich history and breathtaking maritime landscape. This District tartan, woven with respect for its Nova Scotian heritage, evokes the rugged beauty of the coastline where the Battle of Louisburgh took place in 1758. The subtle palette of grays and blues echoes the misty mornings by the sea, while the vibrant yellow sunbeams hint at the warmth that lies beneath the surface. The soft white spindrift on the harbour, a nod to the town's tranquil atmosphere, is juxtaposed against the azure sky, creating a sense of dynamic contrast that reflects the intricate relationships between land and sea in this special place. With restrictions in place to protect its cultural significance, the Louisburg tartan stands as a testament to the enduring power of tradition and community in shaping our understanding of Scotland's unique identity.

name: Louise Commemorative;
description: The Lorne, Louise of tartan is a majestic Royal tartan steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Brought to the fore by the marriage of the Marquis of Lorne to Her Royal Highness Princess Louise in 1871, this storied set has been woven into the fabric of Scottish history ever since. Its design, as recorded in Alastair Campbell's seminal work 'Campbell Tartan', is a testament to the intricate craftsmanship of Mr M'Kissock of Girvan, who was personally involved in its creation and received the Marquis's explicit approval. The Lorne tartan takes centre stage alongside its companion, the Louise tartan, which features an alternative black-red stripe, both of which have been lovingly preserved and passed down through generations to become an integral part of Scotland's rich cultural legacy, symbolising honour, heritage, and the timeless traditions of the Scottish Highlands.

name: Louisiana
description: The Louisiana tartan is a vibrant representation of the state's unique cultural heritage, woven with precision by renowned designer Joe McD.Campbell in 2001. Officially designated as the state tartan, it is reserved for those who share an affiliation with the Pelican State - whether born, bred, or drawn to its storied traditions. This striking pattern weaves together a palette of blues, evoking the majesty of the sky and waterways that crisscross Louisiana's landscape, alongside lush greens symbolising the state's rich agricultural lands. Golden hues of magnolias, cotton, rice, and sugar cane add warmth, while dark threads of petroleum and natural resources underscore the state's strong industrial heritage. This tartan is a testament to the complex tapestry of influences that have shaped Louisiana's identity, its very fabric a celebration of the land, people, and culture that make it so distinctively Louisiana.

name: Louth Irish County
description: The Louth, County tartan is a quintessential example of Irish District heritage, bearing witness to the rich cultural traditions of the region's trading communities. Designed by Polly Wittering for Macnaughtons of Pitlochry, this tartan was originally intended as a collection of trade tartans, reflecting the district's economic and social history. Although not officially sanctioned as a traditional District tartan, its popularity has earned it recognition within the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection. This distinctive pattern is now celebrated for its unique character and historical significance, providing a tangible connection to the region's past and its people.

name: Lovat #1
description: This iconic tartan, formally known as Lovat or Fraser #1, is an enduring symbol of Scottish heritage and tradition, with its rich history dating back to the 19th century. Originally included in Wilson's 1819 Key Pattern Book under the name 'Lovat or Fraser', this tartan was likely woven for members of the prestigious MacKintosh clan, one of Scotland's most storied families. As a fashion tartan, it has been worn by generations of Scots with pride, and its distinctive sett continues to evoke images of heather-clad Highlands and rugged lochs. With no designer credited, this tartan is a testament to the timeless appeal of traditional Scottish weaving, where technical skill meets cultural significance in a truly unique and enduring design.

name: Lovat #2
description: This timeless tartan, categorised as the revered Fraser clan design, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's storied history. Weaving together threads of mystery and tradition, the Lovat or Fraser tartan is shrouded in an air of intrigue, its origins veiled by the passage of time. With roots tracing back to the 19th century, this iconic sett is believed to have been woven by Wilson's skilled hands around 1820, a testament to the artisanal skill of Scotland's finest weavers. name: Lowry [default]
description: The Lowry tartan, designed by Peter MacDonald for Kenneth and Iain Laurie, Fife, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish clan traditions. With subtle nuances in colour, the design cleverly adapts to distinguish between its two distinct iterations - one evoking the Laurie and the other the Lowry namesakes. This striking variation highlights the resourcefulness and adaptability of Scottish clan culture, where a single tartan can be moulded to suit individual identities while remaining rooted in family history. Worn by those with the name Laurie or Lowry, this tartan proudly asserts their connection to Fife's storied past, its subtle shifts in hue serving as a poignant reminder of the enduring power of clan identity and tradition.

name: Loyalhanna
description: The Loyalhanna tartan is a poignant tribute to the region that inspired its creation, the Laural Highlands and Ligonier Valley in Western Pennsylvania. Registered in 1997 by Elizabeth Eicher, this District tartan is as much a nod to the natural beauty of the area as it is a testament to the rich heritage of the local community. The autumnal hues of the design - comprising blues, greens, and yellows reminiscent of the region's vibrant foliage - evoke the quintessential charm of the American countryside. By taking its name from a mountain stream, the Loyalhanna tartan serves as a reminder of the special connection between this region and the world beyond its borders.

name: LS Curling
description: The LS Curling tartan, expertly crafted by renowned Scottish weavers at Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the dynamic spirit of corporate Scotland's most esteemed organisations. As a testament to Scottish tradition, the LS Curling tartan is a fitting emblem for companies seeking to demonstrate their commitment to excellence and a deep connection to the country's storied heritage.

name: Luker
description: The Luker tartan is a personal and meaningful creation, imbued with the rich heritage of Scotland's MacDonald clan. Designed by Dusty Luker, a Florida resident who married into the esteemed clan, this tartan weaves together the traditional colours of his adopted family to form a unique and distinctive pattern. As a name tartan, it holds special significance for all individuals bearing the surname Luker, serving as a visual representation of their heritage and connection to the MacDonalds. By incorporating the iconic colours of the MacDonald clan, Dusty has created a tartan that not only pays tribute to his ancestry but also provides a sense of pride and belonging to those who bear the Luker name. This thoughtful design is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish tradition and the lasting impact of family ties on our identity and heritage.

name: Lumsden Hunting

Designed by Peter MacDonald at the request of David Lumsden of Cushnie, this distinctive day tartan was created to provide a bold yet understated option for members of the clan who sought a less radiant alternative to their other tartans. With its rich, earthy tones, the Lumsden Hunting tartan is deeply rooted in Scotland's hunting heritage and evokes the rustic grandeur of the Scottish countryside, where clans once roamed free in search of game. As a family tartan, it holds honour within the clan's family tree, signifying loyalty and tradition. Lumsden of Kintore [default]

name: Lumsden Waistcoat

Lumsden [default]

With its intricate weave and storied history, the Lumsden short tartan remains an enduring emblem of Scotland's rich textile tradition.

name: Lunar
description: The Lunar tartan is a stunning fashion-inspired design created by Pendleton Woolen Mills, evoking the ethereal beauty of Scotland's celestial landscape. name: Lundy
description: The Lundy tartan is a richly woven tribute to the esteemed Dan Lundy family, whose legacy has been immortalised in this distinctive name tartan. Crafted by renowned designer Phil Smith Jnr with Dr Philip D, this intricate pattern draws inspiration from the island of Lundy, a treasured haven in the Bristol Channel, steeped in history and maritime tradition. As a personal tartan, it holds great significance for those connected to the Dan Lundy family, serving as a symbol of honour, heritage, and connection to their roots. With its specific registration with the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan is not only a celebration of individuality but also a proud representation of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, woven from threads of tradition, history, and community.

name:
Lunting Papi

Named after the Old Scots word 'Lunter', meaning 'Walking and smoking a pipe', this tartan was created by Anthony & Jocelyn for fall hiking, evoking images of rugged landscapes and tranquil moments spent in nature. name: Lusk
description: The Lusk tartan is a personal and poignant design, reflecting the rich heritage of its creator, Richard Michael Lusk. As a Name tartan, it holds deep significance within the family, symbolising unity and identity for those who bear the name. This distinctive pattern weaves together blues evoking Scotland's naval traditions, greens representing Ireland's lush landscapes, and reds honouring the family's wartime military service. By registering this design, Richard Michael Lusk has ensured that his family's legacy is forever intertwined with their Scottish heritage, and those who wear this tartan will carry a tangible connection to the past.

name: Lynch (a)
description: The Lynch tartan is a proud representation of the storied heritage of Clan Lynch, one of Scotland's most ancient and noble families. As a family tartan, it holds deep significance for those bearing the Lynch name, serving as a visual link to their ancestors' triumphs and traditions. Though its origins may be steeped in history, this timeless tartan remains an enduring symbol of Scottish pride and heritage, inviting wearers to proudly assert their connection to this storied clan.

Lyon [default]

Weaving a tale of loyalty, courage, and pride, this distinctive design serves as a proud badge for those bearing the Lyon name, their connection to this rich tapestry of tradition an honourable one.

name: Lyon College, Arkansas
description: The Lyon College tartan, designed by Hawkes/Spalding in collaboration with Bob Walker Hawkes and Russ Spalding circa 1990, is a distinctive corporate tartan that embodies the spirit of innovation and entrepreneurship. Originally commissioned for Arkansas College, a US-based institution founded in 1872, this unique tartan was later adopted by Lyon College, its successor entity established in 1994. While distinct from the more widely known 'Tartans' (Johnston/Smith) variant, which bears a similar name, the Lyon College tartan boasts its own characteristic charm. Worn by Willie Muirhead at the Delco Games in 1995, this tartan has become synonymous with the values of professionalism and achievement that define corporate attire. Its adoption by Lyon College serves as a testament to the enduring power of tradition and heritage in shaping modern business identities.

name: Lyons
description: The Lyons tartan is a poignant tribute to Christina Lyons' parents' enduring love, commemorated in a vibrant blend of heritage hues. Designed by Linda Clifford, an American artist with a deep appreciation for Scottish tradition, this Commemorative tartan weaves together the cultural threads of Christina's Irish and Croatian roots. The striking green and red stripes evoke a sense of warmth and camaraderie, while the white accents subtly nod to the modern connections that bind us. Woven by Strathmore Woollen Co., in Forfar, Scotland, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of family honour, beautifully capturing the spirit of Christina's parents' 50-year milestone anniversary celebration. As a symbol of love and legacy, the Lyons tartan remains an evocative reminder of the rich cultural tapestry that makes our heritage so uniquely rich.

name: Lysaght Dress
description: The Lysaght Dress Tartan is a storied and prestigious clan tartan, designed to honour the ancient Mac Giolla Iasachta family, which originated in Clan O'Brien and broke away circa 1122 to form an independent clan. Commissioned by Thomas A. Lysaght, Head of the House of Lysaght, this tartan is a testament to the family's rich heritage, drawing inspiration from their ancestral coat of arms and the Province of Munster. The intricate design features three red stripes on a silver field, symbolising the three lances of the Lysaght arms, alongside three gold stripes on a field of blue, representing the three crowns of the Munster arms. Registered in 1993 by renowned tartan designer Cynthia Balfour-Traill, this tartan is reserved exclusively for the descendants of Mac Giolla Iasachta and variants of the Lysaght surname, serving as a poignant reminder of their distinguished Scottish-Irish roots.

name: Lysaght Hunting
description: The Lysaght Hunting Tartan is a revered Clan/Family tartan, commissioned by Thomas A. Lysaght, Head of the House of Lysaght, to commemorate his illustrious lineage and connection to Clan O'Brien, Ireland's storied High King, Brian Boru. Designed by Cynthia Balfour-Traill, this richly coloured tartan is a testament to the family's distinguished heritage, featuring the metallic hues of Argent (silver) and Or (gold), alongside the deeper tinctures of Gules (red) and Azure (blue). The intricate design is woven with symbolism, reflecting the three lances of the Lysaght arms on a silver field, and three gold stripes on a field of blue, representing the three crowns of the Munster arms. This tartan holds significant cultural importance for the descendants of Mac Giolla Iasachta, particularly those bearing the Lysaght or MacLysaght surname, serving as an honour to their ancestors' history and legacy.

name: MacAlister Dress

description: The Macallan, "The", corporate tartan is a sophisticated and stylish tribute to Scotland's rich heritage. Registered by renowned designers Peter MacArthur and Leah Robertson, this carefully crafted tartan is intended for use in business and professional settings, where its distinctive blue-grey hues and intricate pattern evoke the traditional Scottish weaves that have been passed down through generations. Inspired by the very same sample colours chosen by the Scottish Tartans Authority's Collection, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish tradition, while also catering to the needs of modern businesses seeking to tap into the country's unique cultural identity. With its restrained yet distinctive design, The Macallan tartan offers a subtle yet striking way for companies to express their connection to Scotland and its timeless heritage.

name: MacAlpine [default]
description: The MacAlpine tartan, registered in 1906, is a rich and storied Clan tartan with deep roots in Scottish heritage. Originally designated as Siol Alpine, its name reflects its connection to the royal Clan Alpin, one of the oldest and most revered clans in Scotland's royal lineage. This tartan design is reminiscent of the Hunting Maclean, but distinguished by the unique yellow lines that set it apart. According to the Scottish Tartans Society, other tartans connected with Siol Alpine feature a prominent red thread, underscoring its association with the noble bloodlines of ancient Scotland. With no designer credited and subject to the corrections of the Scottish Tartans Society, this tartan's symmetrical design presents an intriguing puzzle for historians and enthusiasts alike, inviting exploration into the complex world of Scottish clan heritage.

name: MacAn Hose
description: The MacAn of Lurgyvallan (Hose) tartan is a captivating example of a non-clan tartan, born from a fascinating historical anecdote. This enigmatic design was created in honour of Captain Macan of Lurgyvallan, who was gifted with the watercolour portrait by his friend William MacKenzie in 1831. The tartan's connection to this fictional chief is rooted in the presence of three eagle feathers on the subject's headdress, a nod to the MacLean clan of Duart, with whom Captain Macan shares a seemingly tenuous relationship. As an 'Other' category design, the MacAn of Lurgyvallan (Hose) tartan defies traditional clan affiliations, instead embodying the free-spirited nature of its namesake's friendship and the captivating world of 19th-century Scottish art and culture.

name: MacAn [default]
description: The Macan of Lurgyvallan tartan is a captivating and enigmatic weave, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's complex history with Ireland. As one of the "other" categories, it defies traditional clan affiliations, instead forging a unique bond with the ill-fated MacLean of Duart clan. The registration notes reveal a fascinating tale of friendship and artistic exchange, as Captain Macan of Lurgyvallan was gifted a portrait by his friend William MacKenzie in 1831 - an image that has now been auctioned off to collectors worldwide. This tartan is not simply a historical curiosity, but also a poignant reminder of the tumultuous relationships between Scotland and Ireland during the 19th century. Its subtle nuances and muted colour palette evoke a sense of nostalgia and longing, as if capturing the whispers of a bygone era that never quite came to pass.

name: MacArthur 1815
description: The MacArthur Highland Society tartan is a storied and historic weaving that has been shrouded in mystery for centuries, its origins steeped in the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage. First recorded by James MacArthur Moir of Milton, Chief of Clan MacArthur in 2005, this double yellow-lined sett boasts an undeniable air of authenticity, its presence attested to by a portrait from 1860 and allegedly sampled by the Highland Society of London Collection as far back as 1815. The modern single-lined version, taken from Vestiarium Scoticum (1842), is often touted as the definitive MacArthur tartan, but some argue that it is an erroneous interpretation of the true original, which remains, paradoxically, a matter of favour among clan members. Regardless, this tartan has come to symbolise the enduring legacy and traditions of Clan MacArthur, its intricate patterns woven from threads of history and cultural significance, evoking a sense of pride and heritage that resonates deeply within Scotland's storied past.

name:
MacArthur of Milton [default]
[AKA] MacArthur of Milton
description: The MacArthur of Milton Hunting tartan is a rich and storied clan tartan, woven with the heritage of one of Scotland's most esteemed families. Its creation draws upon the storied legacy of Clan Campbell, yet cleverly subverts it to forge an identity all its own. By carefully marrying elements from both tartans, this sett creates a unique visual language that respectfully honours the traditions of both clans, while also forging a distinct path forward. Amended threadcounts were incorporated to ensure the colour palette remained faithful to the original Wilsons' pattern book, crafted in 1830, providing an unimpeachable connection to Scotland's past. As such, this tartan stands as testament to the enduring power of clan identity and the dedication to preserving Scotland's rich cultural heritage.

name:
MacArthur (Personal)

description: The MacArthur tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich tradition of weaving, with its complex pattern reflecting the intricate heritage of one of Scotland's most storied clans. As a Variant of the Clan tartan, it serves as an adaptation of the original family tartan, specifically by relocating the traditional yellow stripe to the black and introducing a bold red stripe. This subtle yet striking alteration imbues the design with a sense of individuality and distinctiveness, fitting for those bearing the MacArthur name. With its carefully crafted threads, this tartan pays homage to Scotland's history and cultural identity, inviting wearers to proudly embody their clan heritage or branch affiliation.

name:
MacArthur [default]

description: The MacArthur tartan is a storied and storied family heirloom, steeped in Scotland's rich heritage. Originally associated with both the MacDonalds and Clan Campbell, this tartan's design echoes the timeless MacDonald sett, while its connections to Campbell of Strachur reflect a more complex web of clan loyalties. As the traditional tartan of the MacArthurs of Skye, it holds deep significance as a testament to their role as hereditary pipers to the MacDonalds. This intricate and beautiful design is a lasting tribute to the ingenuity and artistry of Sobieski Stewarts, The designer behind this authentic Clan tartan. Its unique blend of history, culture, and technical skill makes it a treasured part of Scotland's textile heritage, evoking the proud traditions of Scotland's clans and families for generations to come.

name: MacArthur-Fox Blue
description: The MacArthur-Fox Blue is a cherished personal tartan, carefully woven to reflect the unique heritage of its designer, J K MacArthur-Fox. As a private family tartan, this subtle yet striking pattern holds significant emotional value for those close to the designer, evoking a sense of warmth and identity. With its nuanced balance of blues and earthy tones, this tartan is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition, drawing inspiration from the rich heritage of the MacArthur and Fox families. Although it was created as a personal tartan, with restrictions limiting its use to the designer alone, this design showcases the artistry and passion that goes into crafting bespoke tartans, a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile craftsmanship.

name: MacArthur-Fox Dress
description: The MacArthur-Fox Dress tartan is a storied Scottish heritage textile born from the creative vision of Jeffrey MacArthur-Fox. As a "Name" tartan, it is proudly borne by those with a connection to the MacArthur and Fox families, or who have been granted permission to wear this distinctive pattern through registration. Woven by skilled hands at D C Dalgliesh's workshop in Selkirk, Scotland, this tartan has been carefully crafted to showcase its rich, earthy tones and intricate weave. With permission from Mr MacArthur-Fox himself, individuals can now don the MacArthur-Fox Dress tartan with honour, whether as a formal part of their dress or for more informal gatherings such as ceilidhs or Highland dances. This tartan design embodies the timeless spirit of Scottish tradition and community, its beauty and significance woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage.

name: MacArthur-Fox Green
description: The MacArthur-Fox Green tartan is a poignant tribute to the enduring legacy of Scotland's storied clans. Originally intended for personal use, the MacArthur-Fox Green tartan is now open to anyone seeking to connect with their Scottish heritage or simply to add a touch of tartan tradition to their daily life. Whether worn by clan members, dancers, pipe bands, or social groups, this tartan design serves as a testament to Scotland's rich cultural tapestry and the time-honoured traditions that weave it together.

name: MacArthur-Fox Hunting
description: The MacArthur-Fox Hunting tartan is a timeless and evocative textile that embodies the rich heritage of Scottish tradition. Designed by J K MacArthur-Fox as a universal tartan, its origins are rooted in the fusion of two distinct families' histories - MacArthur and Fox. This distinctive green-based tartan is steeped in tradition, drawing inspiration from the country's rugged landscape and the timeless pursuits of hunting and the great outdoors. While it has since been replaced by the more specific MacArthur-Fox Green tartan, this earlier design remains an important part of Scotland's cultural legacy, offering a glimpse into the lives of two families who have shaped the nation's history and identity.

name: MacArthur-Fox
description: The MacArthur-Fox tartan is a distinctive and personal variant of a well-established Scottish heritage pattern, with its origins shrouded in mystery and intrigue. Credited to the enigmatic J MacArthur-Fox, who allegedly drew inspiration from the classic 'MacArthur' sett, this variation was first showcased in 1989 by Jeffrey MacArthur-Fox. With its unique twist on the traditional design, the MacArthur-Fox tartan has been passed down through generations of a Scottish clan and is now cherished as a symbol of family honour. Notably registered for use by its designer, this tartan's display sett features a halved version of the pattern, allowing it to be showcased in all its glory while still paying homage to its heritage roots. As a testament to Scotland's rich textile history and cultural traditions, the MacArthur-Fox tartan remains an enduring representation of Scottish identity and pride.

name: MacAulay Hunting
description: The MacAulay Hunting tartan is a timeless testament to the rich heritage of Clan MacAulay, one of Scotland's most storied clans. Characterised by its striking pattern of blues and reds, with subtle hints of yellow and green, this tartan embodies the quintessential spirit of Scotland's hunting traditions. As a Clan tartan, it holds great honour among MacAulay families, symbolising their history, identity, and pride. Though modern in creation, the design remains firmly rooted in the country's ancient weaving traditions, evoking images of heather-clad moors and rugged Highland landscapes.

As an authentic clan tartan, it remains an honour to wear, carrying with it the weight of history and family ties, a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's ancient clans.

MacAulay [default]

As the standard clan tartan, it was first published by M'Intyre North in his 1881 Book of the True Highlanders, bearing testament to its significance within the clan's tradition. With a history dating back to at least the late 19th century, this tartan has been woven with pride for generations, its subtle variations and nuances a reflection of the intricate storytelling that lies behind Scottish clan histories. A true gem in the world of Highland textiles, the MacAulay 1880 tartan serves as a powerful symbol of family legacy and cultural identity, a lasting tribute to the history and traditions of Clan MacAulay.

name: MacAvoy [default]
description: The McAvoy tartan, designed by James McAvoy himself, is a deeply personal and storied pattern that carries the weight of history and heritage. Originally inspired by a tartan woven for the Berkshire Highlanders Pipe Band, which they ultimately chose not to adopt, this unique design has been expertly adapted by McAvoy to create a distinctive family tartan. As such, it holds great significance for those claiming descent from the original clan or family group, and is steeped in tradition and cultural relevance. With its complex interplay of blues, greens, and yellows, this tartan embodies the rich history and mystique of Scotland's clans, while also being a testament to McAvoy's skill as a weaver and designer, who has carefully preserved the essence of his heritage for future generations.

name: MacBeams Boy
description: The McBeams Boy corporate tartan, designed by Lochcarron of Scotland, is a dynamic and modern interpretation of traditional Scottish weaving. Originally created for the Beams Co. Ltd., a Tokyo-based company with Scottish heritage, this unique tartan defies traditional asymmetry, instead adopting a more contemporary and balanced design. According to its registration notes, the McBeams Boy tartan was crafted by Lochcarron as part of their corporate services, showcasing the blend of modern business and timeless Scottish tradition. As a Corporate tartan, it is intended for use in formal business settings, yet its innovative colour palette and bold pattern make it suitable for a wide range of applications, from bespoke suits to branded accessories, reflecting the fusion of Scotland's rich cultural heritage with Japan's vibrant corporate landscape.

name: MacBean Dress
description: The MacBean Dress tartan is a poignant testament to the rich heritage of Clan MacBean, carefully woven by renowned designer Scarlett MBE, Jamie, in honour of Hughston McBain's wife Kathleen née Keith. Registration notes reveal that this distinctive design pays homage to the Meta MacBean, with subtle yet significant modifications. The introduction of black guards adds depth and dimensionality, while the replacement of a black line on alternate white bands with red injects a pop of vibrant colour, underscoring the strong connection between Kathleen and her family's legacy. As one of the few clan tartans open to public registration, this design embodies the tradition and history of MacBean, its significance amplified by its association with the 21st Chief himself, Hughston McBain.

name: MacBean Lord Lyon version
description: The McBain, Chief tartan is a storied and ancestral design, recorded in Lord Lyon's Register of All Arms and Bearings in Scotland as the family tartan of Clan McBain. Registered by Hughston McBain of McBain, 21st Chief of Clan McBain, on 8th March 1960, this distinctive tartan set apart from its clan brethren by its subtle two-tone blue hues, replaces traditional black to create a unique and dignified visual identity. As the chief's own personal tartan, it serves as a symbol of family honour and heritage, passed down through generations of Mc Bain chiefs and bearing testament to their storied history and traditions. Its registration in the Lord Lyon's Register attests to its authenticity and significance, ensuring that this noble tartan remains an integral part of Clan McBain's identity for years to come.

name: MacBean, Meta (Personal)
description: The MacBean, Meta tartan is a poignant and intimate tribute to love and legacy, woven from the threads of Scottish heritage. Registered as a personal name tartan by its creator Jamie Scarlett MBE, this unique arisaid setting combines elements of the esteemed Lyon MacBain GWR:RWB clan pattern. First introduced in 1972, when it was specifically designed for Jamie's wedding to his beloved Meta, this tartan tells a story of enduring devotion and commitment. Tragically, Meta's life was cut short in 2000, but her memory lives on through this beautiful, distinctive fabric. The subtle differences between the MacBean dress and its namesake variant serve as a poignant reminder that even the most lovingly crafted traditions can evolve over time. This tartan is a testament to the enduring power of love and tradition, and its private nature only adds to its sense of exclusivity and personal significance.

name:
MacBean of Tomatin [default]
[AKA] MacBean of Tomatin
description: The MacBean of Tomatin tartan embodies the rich heritage of Clan MacBean, its intricate patterns woven into a tapestry of tradition and pride. With roots dating back to 1872, when it was first described from an ancient piece of tartan cloth found in the house of Tomatin, this tartan has evolved over time to become an integral part of Clan MacBean's identity. Recognised as one of the clan's official tartans by their Chief in 2022, its significance extends beyond mere aesthetics, symbolising a long-standing legacy and honourable tradition. The inclusion of a c.1880-1920 specimen in the esteemed Alexander McBean & Sons, Inverness sample book, now housed in the Inverness Museum, serves as a testament to the tartan's enduring presence in Scottish heritage. This authentic tartan design is a tangible connection to the MacBeans of Tomatin's storied past, proudly worn by those who bear the clan's name and legacy.

name: MacBeth #3
description: MacBeth #3 is a distinctive fashion tartan that holds a fascinating place within Scottish heritage, albeit one forged in American tradition. Originally registered for use on men's shirts, its origins are shrouded in mystery, with only an observation of 199 providing a glimpse into its early history. Despite the absence of a designer credited, this tartan design speaks volumes about Scotland's cultural significance and the enduring appeal of traditional tartan. Its inclusion under the fashion category is testament to the versatility and global reach of Scottish textiles, while restrictions on its use for specific garments or purposes serve as a reminder of the delicate balance between tradition and innovation.

name: MacBeth Dress
description: The MacBeth Dress tartan is a storied and historic design, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered by John L Kitt-Hess, President of the Clan MacBeth Society of North America, this tartan holds great significance for the clan that bears its name. As a member of the family category, it was specifically created to reflect the values and identity of the MacBeth clan, with its intricate patterns and subtle colour nuances weaving together to evoke the rich history and culture of Scotland's noble families. While restrictions do apply, limiting its use to those who can demonstrate connection or ancestry to the clan, the MacBeth Dress tartan remains a powerful symbol of Scottish heritage and tradition, inviting wearers to tap into their own roots and celebrate their place within this storied lineage.

name: MacBeth Dress Dance
description: The MacBeth Dress tartan, named after the legendary Thane of Cawdor, is a striking Fashion tartan that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's sartorial traditions. Designed by Dalgliesh, D C, this distinctive pattern has been prepared for weaving by the esteemed D C Dalgliesh Ltd, ensuring its authentic representation on the loom. Notably, despite being a variation on an existing clan tartan, this design boasts its own unique identity, reflecting the intricate tapestry of Scottish history and culture. As a Fashion tartan, it is suited for garments and accessories that make a bold statement, evoking the regal and mystical associations of Scotland's iconic nobility. However, due to restrictions in place, only those with permission from the registering authority may proceed with weaving this tartan, thereby safeguarding its heritage for future generations to appreciate.

name: MacBeth [default]
description: The MacBeth tartan is a richly woven testament to Scotland's storied past, its intricate pattern echoing the bold ambition of the legendary Lord of Dunsinane himself. As one of the most iconic clan tarts, it has been passed down through generations as a symbol of heritage and family ties, evoking the proud traditions of the Highlands. With its striking black background punctuated by alternating reds, blues, and yellows, this tartan is both elegant and unforgiving - much like the complexities of human nature that inspired Shakespeare's timeless masterpiece. Its slight variation, dubbed 'Prince Albert', serves as a poignant reminder that even in the most carefully crafted patterns, nuance can add depth to our understanding of history and tradition.

name: MacBrair #2
description: The McBrayer tartan is a poignant reflection of Scottish heritage, born from a rich history spanning centuries. Originally registered as the MacBrair of Almagill & Netherwood, this distinctive pattern has undergone a transformation, evolving into the esteemed MacBrayer tartan. Notably, May McKerrel's insight suggests that the tartan was initially conceived as a blanket sett, a traditional textile motif characteristic of Scotland's ancient weaving heritage. Its adoption by the MacBrayer clan/family testamentifies the enduring significance of this tartan, symbolising a deep connection to the land, culture and tradition of Scotland.

name: MacBrair Dress
description: The McBrayer Dress tartan is a cherished Clan/Family pattern steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Originating from the esteemed McBrair family, this tartan has been woven into the fabric of their history for generations. With its distinctive sett, this blanket pattern tells the story of a bygone era, evoking memories of warmth, comfort, and kinship. Registered in 2007, the McBrayer Dress tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of this prominent Scottish clan, whose roots run deep through the Highlands. The subtle nuances of its sett, painstakingly documented by Madam May McKerrell's woven sample from Hillhouse in 2007, ensure that this family pattern remains an authentic and poignant connection to Scotland's rich cultural heritage.

name: MacBrair [default]
description: The MacBrair Hunting tartan, with its subtle nuances and earthy tones, embodies the rugged spirit of Scotland's ancient clans. Characterised by its muted blues, greens, and browns, this tartan is said to evoke the natural landscapes of Scotland's Highlands, where hunting was once a vital part of clan life. With no known Irish connections despite the variant spelling, MacBrair Hunting remains an authentic representation of Scottish culture, woven with precision and respect for its storied past.

name: MacBride [default]
description: The MacBride tartan, meticulously crafted by renowned designer Harry Lindley for Kinloch Anderson Ltd in 1992, embodies the rich heritage of one of Scotland's most storied clans. This distinctive pattern, officially registered in 2000, is a testament to the dedication of Captain Stuart C MacBride to preserve his family's legacy. Inspired by the MacDonalds' sept tradition, the tartan weaves together a complex narrative of Scottish history and culture, its subtle nuances hinting at the storied past of this ancient clan. As an official Clan tartan, it is a privilege reserved for those bearing the MacBride surname or in favour with the head of the family to wear and display this respected design. With the Ensigns Armorial's official seal emblazoned on its certificate, the MacBride tartan stands as a poignant tribute to the enduring legacy of Scotland's clans.

name: MacByrd
description: The MacByrd tartan is a unique and enigmatic Scottish heritage pattern, steeped in history and mystery. Discovered in 1984 in the Wee Shoppe in Highlands, North Carolina, it is believed to have originated as a personal or family tartan for an American family called Byrd. With no specific designer credited, this tartan design takes on an air of authenticity, its origins rooted firmly in the cultural exchange and migration that shaped Scotland's rich textile traditions. As a Name tartan, MacByrd holds significance for those with Byrd ancestry, serving as a tangible connection to their Scottish heritage and family legacy. Its distinctive colour palette, while not strictly adhering to traditional Scottish motifs, tells its own story of cultural blending and adaptation, reflecting the complex and fascinating history of Scotland's people and textiles.

name: MacCainsh [default]
description: The MacCainsh tartan is a timeless representation of Scottish heritage, woven with the rich history of Clan Cainsh family tradition. Originating from the esteemed Lumsden Collection, this authentic tartan pattern has been meticulously crafted to evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. As a Clan tartan, it holds great significance for those bearing the MacCainsh name, serving as a symbol of family honour and identity. With its unique colour scheme and distinct sett, this tartan design is steeped in tradition and steeped in the stories of the past. Its registration as a JCT file ensures that its cultural significance is preserved for generations to come, allowing those who wear it to proudly connect with their ancestral roots.

name: MacCall [default]
description: This charming tartan, registered as the MacCall, was carefully crafted to commemorate a special McCall wedding in 2000, a testament to the enduring power of family heritage and tradition. As a Name tartan, it is specifically designed for individuals bearing the name McCall, rather than being an official clan tartan, thus making it accessible to those who proudly bear the name. With its unique sett, this tartan pays homage to Scottish heritage, evoking memories of ancient lochs, heather-clad moors, and the rich cultural history that has been woven into the fabric of the nation. Designed by John C & Margaret MacCall, a masterful blend of colour and texture brings this special tartan to life, a fitting tribute to a McCall family celebration that will be cherished for generations to come.

name: MacCallie [default]
description: The McCallie tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's clans, reflecting the proud history and tradition of the McCallie family. Registered by Viking Technology Ltd in 1955, this distinctive pattern is a true representation of Scottish craftsmanship, woven with precision and attention to detail. With its specific restrictions limiting it solely to use by the McCallie name, this tartan design is a symbol of family honour and legacy, inviting wearers to proudly claim their ancestry. Woven from carefully selected threads, the McCallie tartan embodies the warmth and resilience of Scotland's ancient clans, evoking a sense of belonging and connection to a storied past that continues to inspire and captivate us today.

name:
MacCallum of Berwick [default]
