description: The MacCallum of Berwick tartan is a proud testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans, woven into existence by the storied family of MacCallums who proudly hail from the historic town of Berwick-upon-Tweed. As a registered Clan tartan, this distinctive design holds significant cultural and historical value, passed down through generations as an emblem of Scottish identity and family legacy. With its unique combination of blues, greens, and golds, reminiscent of the rolling hills and windswept moors of the Scottish Borders, this tartan is steeped in tradition and evokes a sense of history and nobility. Its existence is further authenticated by its registration with the Scottish Tartans Society, ensuring that it remains an authentic and enduring representation of Scotland's rich textile heritage.

name: MacCallum [default]
description: The MacCallum tartan is a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich clan heritage, with its complex, dark blue (azure) and black hues evoking the rugged landscapes of Argyllshire. Originally created in an attempt to revive a lost family tradition, this tartan has taken on a life of its own, captivating those who wear it with its unique blend of history and mystery. Registration notes reveal a tale of trial and error, with two competing interpretations - one from the 19th century Tartans Society Register, and another from the more recent recovery of a historic silk sampler - highlighting the challenges faced by families in preserving their cultural legacy. This tartan's story is now part of Scotland's collective heritage, a testament to the enduring power of tradition and community, with its intricate patterns woven into the very fabric of Scottish identity.

name: MacCallum High School, Philadelphia
description: The MacCallum High School tartan is a unique corporate design that proudly represents the Philadelphia institution of the same name. This distinctive tartan was created for use by the school's community, embodying the values and spirit of its students, staff, and alumni. Drawing inspiration from the heritage of Scotland, this tartan weaves together threads from a sample in the prestigious J Rutledge Collection in Belfast and Edinburgh, ensuring an authentic touch to the American setting. As a corporate tartan, its primary purpose is to foster school pride and identity, while also serving as a symbolic connection to the broader cultural traditions that have shaped Scottish history and community.

name: MacCamley [default]
description: The McCamley tartan, registered to its eponymous designer Andrew McCamley, embodies the personal heritage of a distinguished Scotsman. This unique Name tartan holds significant sentimental value, having been woven as a wedding gift - a poignant symbol of love and commitment. The intricate patterns and subtle colour nuances weave together to create a visually striking design that reflects the wearer's individuality. With its origins tied to a cherished life event, the McCamley tartan is not only a testament to Andrew McCamley's skill as a weaver but also a treasured family heirloom, passed down through generations of those dear to him.

name: MacCandlish Green; Arisaid
description: The McCandlish Arisaid Green tartan is a poignant celebration of Scottish heritage and family legacy, carefully woven by Stanton Ward Foster McCandlish in 1992. This clan tartan, lovingly crafted with the guidance of J. Charles "Scotty" Thompson, tells the story of a storied Borders family's history, forged during the tumultuous Jacobite Risings. The striking design features a bold yellow stripe, evoking the pivotal events that split the McCandlish lineage into distinct McCandlish and McCandless branches, while blue hues evoke the vast expanse of the ocean, home to many members of this diasporic community. The tartan's subtle black "tram track" stripes, incrementally widening across its surface, symbolise the global dispersal of the McCandlish name, a testament to the family's enduring spirit and legacy.

name: MacCandlish Grey; Dress
description: The McCandlish Dress Grey tartan is a poignant representation of Scottish heritage, woven with the threads of history and family tradition. Designed by Stanton W F McCandlish in 1992, this Clan tartan pays homage to the Jacobite Risings and the diaspora of the McCandlish and McCandless families across North America and Australia/New Zealand. The subtle nuances of grey tone evoke a sense of gravitas, while the judicious placement of blue, red, and yellow creates a visual narrative that tells the story of a family's journey, bound by their shared Gaelic roots. Notably, this tartan eschews traditional Scottish iconography, opting instead for a contemporary interpretation that celebrates the McCandlish legacy in its own unique way.

name: MacCandlish Red
description: The McCandlish Red tartan is a richly symbolic representation of Scottish heritage, woven by Stanton Ward Foster McCandlish in 1992 with the guidance of J. Charles "Scotty" Thompson FSTS. This family tartan, born from the Black Watch and Gordon traditions, tells the story of the McCandlish clan's storied history, particularly their pivotal role in the Jacobite Risings. The tartan's distinctive yellow stripe, paying homage to the "bright line" events that split the family into two distinct lines, is complemented by red, echoing the earliest known blazon of the McCandlish name. Deep blue undertones evoke the sea that cradled many a McCandlish family member in the Gaelic diaspora, while the increasing width of the black "tram track" stripes represents the tartan's enduring legacy as the family's global footprint continues to grow.

name: MacCandlish Red; Arisaid
description: The McCandlish Arisaid Red, a rich and storied clan tartan, bears witness to the historical journey of the McCandlish family, whose roots stretch back to Scotland's ancient Highlands. Designated by Stanton Ward Foster McCandlish in 1992, with guidance from J. Charles "Scotty" Thompson FSTS, this family tartan weaves together the threads of their ancestral heritage, honouring the Jacobite Risings and the 'bright line' events that shaped their destiny. The tartan's palette is a masterful blend of traditional Scottish hues: deep blues evoke the vast expanse of the sea, which has borne many McCandlishes to distant shores; vibrant yellows symbolise the pivotal moments that cleaved the family into distinct lines; and fiery reds, reminiscent of the earliest blazons, pay tribute to their noble heritage. As the black "tram track" stripes gradually expand, they serve as a testament to the tartan's enduring legacy, tracing the global spread of the McCandlish name with quiet pride.

name: MacCarthy Old
description: The McCarthy, Old tartan is a storied and historic Scottish pattern steeped in Clan tradition, its intricate weaves evoking the rugged heritage of Western Scotland's ancient clans. This family-specific tartan was woven with precision and care, its subtle colour nuances reflecting the nuances of the Gaelic language and the rich cultural legacy of the MacCarthy clan. Registered to the esteemed Lochcarron tartan workshop, this design showcases the dark blue tone specified in the registration notes, a deliberate choice that nods to the tartan's Gaelic roots. With no Sindex records available, it is believed to pre-date the formalisation of modern tartan registration systems, lending an air of authenticity and timelessness to its timeless beauty.

name: MacCarthy [default]
description: The McCarthy Corporate Tartan is a modern interpretation of Scottish heritage, expertly woven into the fabric of corporate identity. Created in collaboration with Sue Stedman Ltd., this distinctive tartan was specifically designed for McCarthy & Stone Limited to reflect their brand values. With its unique thread count taken from a sample of sett size, this livery tartan embodies the company's commitment to excellence and tradition. As part of the Corporate category, it represents a modern take on Scotland's rich textile heritage, where the traditional art of tartan weaving is merged with contemporary design sensibilities. This carefully crafted tartan is not only a symbol of corporate identity but also a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish craftsmanship, honouring the country's storied past while embracing its forward-thinking future.

name: MacCartney (Lady) personal; Day
description: The McCartney Day tartan, designed in honour of Sir Paul McCartney, is a vibrant and iconic fashion tartan created by his late wife, Lady Linda McCartney. Originally intended for use within the McCartney household, this tartan has transcended its domestic origins to become a timeless symbol of style and Scottish heritage. As a Fashion category registration, it's meant to be worn with pride on garments that showcase one's personal taste and flair. With no specific meaning attributed to the initials 'MPL', which are believed to represent the McCartney household name, this tartan remains a celebration of Linda McCartney's enduring legacy as an artist, activist, and devoted wife and mother. This stunning design is now a testament to her lasting influence on fashion and Scottish culture, inviting wearers to pay tribute to her memory while making a statement of their own unique style.

name: MacCartney (Lady) personal; Evening
description: The McCartney Evening/Night tartan is a stunning creation born from the creative vision of Linda McCartney, the iconic musician's wife, in honour of their MPL Household legacy. This fashion tartan, registered for use on garments and furnishings, holds a special place in Scottish heritage as a testament to Linda's enduring spirit and style. Designed after her passing, this tartan serves as a tribute to her memory, evoking the warmth and glamour of evening gatherings and nights spent with loved ones. With its unique, unrecorded initials 'MPL', shrouded in mystery, the McCartney Evening/Night tartan embodies the essence of tradition, innovation, and timeless elegance that define Scottish textile craftsmanship.

name: MacCaskill [default]
description: The MacCaskill tartan, registered in 1951, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's clan system. Named after its creator, Margaret O'MacDougal, and designed for Kenneth MacAskill, a stalwart farmer from Milton of Leys, this distinctive tartan wears its history on its sleeve - literally. As noted by Miss MacDougal herself, the design is a variant of the traditional MacLeod tartan, with an intriguing twist: the colours of the stripes and their guards are reversed, imbuing the fabric with a unique character. This Clan tartan serves as a proud symbol of Scottish family heritage, worn by those bearing the name to honour their roots and connect with generations past.

name: MacCaughan [default]
description: The MacCaughan or MacEachain tartan is a deeply personal and storied design, woven from the threads of Scottish heritage and family tradition. Registered in 1972 by its creator, John A McCaughan, this tartan is a testament to the enduring connections between the MacEachin clan and their esteemed relatives, the Campbells of Cawdor. With its striking similarities to the iconic Campbell of Cawdor tartan, it serves as a poignant reminder of the intricate web of Scottish clans and families that have shaped the country's rich history. As a family tartan, this design is not intended for general wear but rather holds significance for those who bear the MacEachin name, serving as a tangible link to their ancestral heritage and a symbol of their proud identity.

name: MacClafferty [default]
description: The McClafferty tartan is a revered family heritage, woven with tradition and passion by the renowned Scottish designer Peter MacDonald in 2004. Inspired by the esteemed VS MacDonald Lord of the Isles sett, this tartan is specifically registered for all members of the McClafferty surname and its variants, providing a tangible connection to their ancestral roots. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds great significance, symbolising unity, pride, and belonging among those who bear the name. The intricate patterns and subtle colour variations are carefully crafted to evoke the rich history and cultural identity of Scotland's proud clansmen, offering a meaningful way for the McClafferty family to honour their heritage and wear it with distinction.

name:
MacClure Hunting
[AKA] MacClure Green
description: The MacClure Hunting tartan is an iconic representation of the storied heritage of Clan MacClure, woven with precision by DC Dalgliesh to celebrate the family's rich history. This traditional Scottish tartan, registered for the exclusive use of MacClures and their kindred, embodies the values of hunting and camaraderie that have long been synonymous with the clan. Originally designed by Dr Philip D, Smith Jnr, this distinctive sett is not only a proud symbol of identity but also features a subtle variation, 'MacClure Green', woven by Lochcarron of Scotland, which showcases the nuances of Scottish textile tradition. The MacClure Hunting tartan serves as a tangible link to the clan's ancestral roots, evoking images of rugged Highlands landscapes and the steadfast spirit of those who wear it with honour.

name: MacClure [default]
description: The MacClure tartan, a rich and storied heritage fabric, was meticulously designed by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr in 2004 to represent the proud clan family bearing the name. Originally woven by DC Dalgliesh, its creation pays homage to the long-standing tradition of tartan design that has been passed down through generations of skilled weavers. As a Clan tartan, MacClure is a testament to the history and identity of those who bear the name, evoking the values of loyalty, courage, and community that have defined this Scottish clan for centuries. The intricate pattern, woven with precision and care, now serves as a lasting connection to ancestral heritage, honoured by its registration in the tartan register, ensuring that its significance is preserved for generations to come.

name: MacColl Hunting
description: The MacColl Hunting tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's esteemed clans, with its intricate weave carrying on the proud traditions of hunting and outdoor pursuits that have long been synonymous with Scottish culture. As a Clan/Family tartan, this design has been passed down through generations of the MacColl family, its specific roots tracing back to the 1930s-50s, as documented in the esteemed MacGregor-Hastie collection. This storied fabric has likely warmed the hearts and bodies of MacColl kin for decades, evoking memories of brisk Highland air, the thrill of the hunt, and the camaraderie of shared experiences within the clan's favour. Its design, though not attributed to a specific designer, remains an embodiment of Scottish tartanry at its finest – a beautiful fusion of tradition, heritage, and family pride that continues to inspire those who wear it.

name: MacColl Old
description: The MacColl Ancient tartan is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's Clan system, with its intricate and timeless pattern evoking the traditions of yesteryear. Dating back to an unspecified era between 1930 and 1950, this ancient tartan was once a cherished part of the MacGregor-Hastie collection, now held in the cloth archive of the Scottish Tartans Society. As a Clan tartan, it is steeped in history and family honour, with its distinct sett reflecting the storied past of the MacColl clan. Its subtle nuances and muted colours whisper tales of generations past, while its presence serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's enduring cultural identity. This venerable tartan stands as a bridge to the country's storied past, awaiting rediscovery by those who cherish the traditions of Scotland's storied clans.

name: MacComb
description: The McComb tartan, a distinctive Name tartan created by renowned designer Donald Fraser, is steeped in Scottish heritage and personal connection. Registred for Mr McComb to proudly represent himself as club captain of a golf club, this unique tartan incorporates elements of the MacThomas clan, with the addition of over checks in the colours of the golf club, symbolising its significance within his sporting community. As a Name tartan, the McComb is not associated with an ancestral family or clan affiliation, instead embodying Mr McComb's individual identity and status as a respected leader within his chosen sphere. This distinctive design, rooted in Fraser's skillful interpretation of Scottish textile traditions, now holds a special place within the Scottish Tartans Society's register, paying tribute to Mr McComb's lasting legacy in his golf club.

name: MacConnell [default]
description: The MacConnell tartan, expertly woven by Malcolm Stephenson, is a testament to the rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands. This Clan/Family tartan was designed for the McConnel family, who trace their ancestry back to Margaret McConnel of Highland Heritage in the United States. Based on the MacDonald Hunting tartan without the black element, this distinctive design weaves together the storied traditions of the ancient clans, evoking images of rugged highlands and noble lineage. By incorporating elements from the MacDonald Hunting tartan, Stephenson has created a unique and meaningful pattern that pays homage to Scotland's proud history while also providing a distinct family identity for the McConnells. This beautiful tartan is not only a tribute to Scottish heritage but also a symbol of the enduring bonds between tradition and community.

name: MacCord
description: The MacCord tartan is a deeply personal and meaningful blend of tradition and individuality, reflecting the heritage of its creator, Howard McCord. Designed by Jan Crook in 1996, this unique name tartan pays homage to the distinctive surnames that have been woven into the fabric of Scottish society for generations. With its bold, vibrant hues, this tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of family and clan ties that underpin Scotland's rich cultural identity. As an individual tartan, the MacCord design serves as a symbol of personal pride and connection to one's roots, allowing Howard McCord to wear his heritage on his sleeve in a truly distinctive and meaningful way.

name: MacCormick (Personal)
description: The MacCormick tartan is a rich tapestry of tradition, carefully woven by Keith McCormick to honour his family's Hebridean heritage. Registered as a clan name tartan, it holds significant cultural weight for those bearing the same name or spelling variations thereof. This distinctive design, born from the sept of MacLaine of Lochbuie, celebrates the storied history of Scottish clans and their intricate connections. With its unique blend of blue, green, yellow, black, red, and white hues, the MacCormick tartan evokes a sense of authenticity and pride, connecting wearers to their ancestral roots and the storied past of the Highlands. Its restricted availability ensures that only those who bear the McCormick name or its variants may wear this proud emblem of Scottish heritage, underscoring the importance of familial ties and cultural tradition.

name: MacCormick Dress
description: The MacCormick dress tartan, registered with the Scottish Tartans Society in 1985 by Pendleton Woollen Mills, is a fascinating example of the evolution of traditional Scottish design. Named after its supposed origins with Clan MacCormick, this tartan takes creative licence from the Campbell and Lindsay families, sharing similarities with their respective sets, albeit with distinct colour variations. As revealed by Philip D.Smith's notes, it appears that Pendleton's designers drew inspiration from existing Scottish tartans, rather than embarking on a new design from scratch. This clever adaptation reflects the long-standing tradition of tartan makers responding to requests for unique family designs by modifying established patterns. The MacCormick dress tartan thus becomes a testament to the artful blending of heritage and innovation, showcasing the rich tapestry of Scottish history and culture woven into every intricate thread.

name: MacCormick, Festive (Personal)
description: The MacCormick Festive tartan is a joyous and vibrant celebration of Scottish heritage, crafted with love by Keith McCormick. Designated as a Name tartan for those bearing the esteemed surname, this festive tartan is steeped in tradition and honourable lineage. Specifically created to complement its Irish cousin, the MacCormick Dress Tartan (STR #2323), this design embodies the warmth and conviviality of Hebridean Scots culture. Woven with care for solemn and celebratory occasions alike - from Christmas to christenings, weddings, and birthdays - the MacCormick Festive tartan embodies the spirit of community, camaraderie, and merriment that is so quintessentially Scottish. Its distinctive pattern is a proud declaration of family ties and cultural identity, allowing wearers to proudly showcase their heritage on special days and in everyday life.

name: MacCorquodale [default]
description: The MacCorquodale tartan is a rich and storied heritage pattern, steeped in tradition and history. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Society as part of Scotland's clan heritage, this iconic tartan tells the story of the Corquodale family, whose roots run deep in the Highlands. Dating back to the 19th century, when the tartan was originally designed for the MacCorquodale clan, it now serves as a symbol of Scottish identity and cultural pride. Donated to the Society by Kinloch Anderson in 1981, this sample tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's clan system, where intricate patterns like the MacCorquodale reflect the values, traditions, and ancestry of its bearers.

name: MacCorquodale #2
description: MacCorquodale #2, a timeless clan tartan born from the storied heritage of a proud Highland family, weaves its distinctive threads into the very fabric of Scotland's rich history. Originating from an island on Loch Tromlee, near the waters of Loch Awe and Kilchrennan, this tartan holds a deep connection to the Campbell clan, with whom it is intertwined in ancestral ties. The dark, muted tones of the woven sample are almost unrecognisable at times, reflecting the rugged landscape that has shaped the lives of the MacCorquodales for generations. As a testament to their island home and storied lineage, this tartan remains an enduring symbol of family honour and heritage, its intricate pattern a tangible link to the land and traditions that have defined Scotland's Highland clans for centuries.

name: MacCoul [default]
description: The MacCoul tartan is a rich and storied weave that reflects the history and heritage of Scotland's clan families. First recorded in the manuscript of W and A Smith 'Authenticated Tartans of the Clans and Families of Scotland', this traditional tartan was likely created by an unknown designer who drew upon the timeless traditions of Highland weaving. Originating from George Hunter's research into ancient tartans, the MacCoul tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's clan families, whose distinct patterns have been woven into the very fabric of the nation's identity. As a Clan tartan, it holds great honour and significance among those who bear its name, and its inclusion in this esteemed collection serves as a poignant reminder of the cultural heritage that underpins the very essence of Scottish tradition.

name: MacCraig [default]
description: The MacCraig tartan is a storied and authentic clan tartan hailing from the rugged Highlands of Scotland, with its origins tracing back to Lochaber. This traditional sett, bearing the distinctive count of 27 in the fourth position, has a rich history dating back to the tumultuous aftermath of Culloden, when it was said to have been taken to Scandinavia and eventually brought to America. As part of this long-standing family tartan, the MacCraig clan's heritage is woven into its very fabric - a testament to their enduring connection to Scotland's Celtic past and the cultural traditions that defined their community for generations.

name: MacCreary [default]
description: The MacCreary tartan is a family heirloom of great significance, crafted with precision and love by esteemed designer Phil Smith. Registered as a personal clan tartan, it holds a special place in the history of the McCreary family, who commissioned its creation for themselves, Milton and Marion. This intricate design showcases the rich heritage of Scotland's Clan system, where tartans are deeply intertwined with family identity, heritage, and tradition. Characterised by subtle variations in thread weight and weave, the MacCreary tartan embodies the unique story of its bearers, while also paying homage to the timeless traditions of Scottish weaving. This tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the McCreary clan, forever woven into the fabric of their history and identity.

name: MacCrimmon [default]
description: The MacCrimmon from Skye is a storied Name tartan, rich in heritage and history, with its origins rooted in the rugged landscapes of Lewis. Designed by Angus Macleod of Dunvegan, Skye - though unfortunately shrouded in mystery due to an untraceable weaver - this distinctive design has been painstakingly recreated by D.C. Dalgliesh from Selkirk. Originally associated with a knee rug bearing a label from the esteemed Dunvegan estate, the tartan's provenance is reinforced by Dr Hugh Ross MacCrimmon's identification of Angus MacLeod as its designer. A testament to the intricate weaving traditions of Scotland's Hebridean islands, this Name tartan proudly represents the enduring legacy of Scottish clan heritage and cultural identity, inviting wearers to connect with the storied past of the Isles.

name:
MacCulloch #2
[AKA] MacDonald Lord of the Isles #2
description: The MacCullough tartan is a storied and storied heritage thread, woven from the rich tapestry of Scottish clan traditions. Originally designated as MacDonald Lord of the Isles (#873) in 1930s archives, this tartan has undergone a subtle yet significant transformation over time, acquiring its current name. As such, it holds a fascinating dual identity, bearing testament to the complex history of Scottish clans and their shifting allegiances. Its connection to the esteemed MacDonald title lends an air of nobility and prestige to this intricate pattern, while its family origins evoke a sense of warmth and community. With no restrictions on its use, this tartan invites wearers to draw upon Scotland's storied past, infusing modern attire with the timeless essence of Highland heritage.

name: MacCulloch #3 (Personal)
description: The McCulloch, Grant tartan is a poignant tribute to the McCulloch family's rich military heritage, woven into its very fabric. Registered as a Personal Name tartan, it pays lasting honour to those who have served their country over eight centuries, with 807 years of service being a notable milestone marked by the deep green hue. The poppy red commemorates all who fell in the line of duty from 1296 to 2007, while the silver grey represents the many medals won by the family throughout history. This thoughtful blend of colours also acknowledges the significant contributions made by two notable McCullochs: Thomas Hay, who served valiantly in the Royal Navy during World War II, and his wife Christina Mcquid (Veitch), who worked tirelessly in ammunition factories during that same conflict. The McCulloch, Grant tartan serves as a heartfelt tribute to family service, sacrifice, and pride, its intricate weaving a testament to the enduring legacy of this distinguished clan.

name: MacCulloch 1746 Dress
description: The MacCulloch Dress tartan, designed by renowned Scottish weaver Peter MacDonald, is a timeless tribute to the storied heritage of the name MacCulloch. Registered in recognition of its association with the esteemed Mr McCullogh from the USA, this Name tartan embodies the values of tradition and identity that are at the heart of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry. Woven with meticulous attention to detail, the intricate pattern is a masterful blend of earthy tones and subtle contrasts that evoke the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. As the designated tartan for all members of the MacCulloch family and their variants, this stunning design serves as a symbol of honour and pride, proudly embracing its connection to a distinguished lineage and the enduring legacy of Scotland's ancient clan system.

name: MacCulloch [default]
description: The MacCulloch tartan is a stalwart representation of Scottish heritage, bearing witness to the storied legacy of the MacDonald clan. Designed by Peter MacDonald for Donald McCullogh of 'MacCulloch Highlands' in the USA, this tartan was created with the express intention of being worn by members of the name MacCullogh/MacCulloch and its variants. With a rich history rooted in Scottish tradition, the MacCulloch tartan is a testament to the enduring power of clan identity. Its distinctive colour palette, woven from carefully selected threads, evokes the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands, where the MacCullochs have long held a revered place within the country's storied clans. By wearing this tartan, one pays homage not only to their own surname but also to the timeless traditions and history that have shaped Scotland's rich cultural tapestry.

name: MacDevitt [default]
description: The MacDevitt tartan is a quintessential Scottish heritage design, steeped in tradition and family pride. Registered by Pendleton Woolen Mills, this clan tartan holds a special place in the history of Scottish textiles, with its roots tracing back to the iconic Black Watch tartan, albeit with key differences that reflect its unique identity. The adaptation involves substituting green for red, giving the MacDevitt design a distinctive edge and flair. As a family tartan, it is intended to be worn by descendants of the Devitt clan or those who bear honour as their forebears, serving as a symbol of connection to this storied heritage and the rich traditions that underpin it.

name: MacDiarmid [default]
description: The MacDiarmid tartan is a richly storied and deeply rooted heritage tartan, steeped in the history and tradition of Clan Campbell. As a sept of the illustrious clan, this tartan holds significant cultural value, evoking the pride and identity of its bearers. First published by W & A K Johnston in 1906, the MacDiarmid was one of several previously unrecorded tartans introduced by renowned author H Whyte, who sought to preserve Scotland's intricate clan heritage. Now woven by Lochcarron & House of Edgar, this timeless design remains an enduring testament to the Campbell clan's storied past, its very existence a nod to the enduring power of Scottish tradition and family honour.

name: MacDiarmid Dress
description: The MacDiarmid Dress tartan is a timeless and revered heritage pattern steeped in Scottish tradition. As part of the clan system, this tartan represents the esteemed MacDiarmid family, whose history dates back to the 15th century. With roots tracing back to the 1830s, when it was first documented by renowned collector William Paton, this sett has been an integral part of Scottish textile heritage for generations. Characterised by its unique and intricate design, the MacDiarmid Dress tartan is a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scotland's weavers. Although not attributed to a specific designer, its enduring presence in traditional collections underscores its importance as a living link to Scotland's rich cultural past. As a registered clan tartan, it continues to hold significance for the MacDiarmid family and their descendants, symbolising pride, heritage, and tradition.

name: MacDonagh [default]
description: The MacDonagh tartan is a rich and storied heritage weave, steeped in tradition and connection to Scotland's ancient clans. As part of the Clan/Family category, it holds significance for those tracing their roots back to the MacDonalds, one of Scotland's most revered families. This distinctive pattern, featuring a subtle blend of blues and greens, is said to have originated from Peter MacDonald's swatch collection, with influences drawn from Robert Mitchell's 19th-century Pattern Book from Dublin. The weaving mill's location at Brabazon Row, The Liberties, Dublin, adds a fascinating layer of cultural exchange between Scotland and Ireland during this period. While no designer is specified, the tartan's authenticity lies in its connection to Irish traditions, with MacDonald being an alternate spelling for the Scottish surname, highlighting the intricate relationships between Scottish and Irish heritage.

name: MacDonald (Ken) personal; Bute Heather
description: The Bute Heather Ancient tartan is a timeless and evocative fashion tartan, evoking the wild beauty of Scotland's rugged landscapes. This richly woven pattern, created by the renowned Houston Kiltmakers of Paisley, is one of a series produced specifically for their retail and kilt-hire business. Characterised by its distinctive heather hues and subtle gradations, this tartan design embodies the spirit of the Scottish Highlands, where heather blooms in abundance amidst rolling moors and glens. Woven with attention to detail and a deep respect for tradition, the Bute Heather Ancient tartan is perfect for those seeking a authentic and stylish fashion statement that honours Scotland's iconic heritage.

name: MacDonald (Ken) personal; Bute Heather #2
description: The Bute Heather tartan, created by renowned designer Ken MacDonald of Houston Kiltmakers in Paisley, is a captivating tribute to the rugged beauty of Scotland's wild landscapes. Originally designed for MacDonald's retail and kilt hire business, this fashion tartan takes its inspiration from the vibrant heather that blankets the Isle of Bute, a haven for those seeking solace amidst the rolling hills and crystal-clear waters of western Scotland. With its rich, muted tones evoking the misty veil of dawn over the Scottish Highlands, the Bute Heather tartan is an ode to the enduring spirit of Scotland's natural heritage, woven into every thread with meticulous attention to detail that respects both tradition and modernity.

name: MacDonald (Ken) personal; Bute Heather Autumn
description: The Bute Heather Autumn tartan is a quintessential Scottish fashion statement, born from the rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands. Designed by the renowned Houston Kiltmakers of Paisley, this autumnal blend of blues and greens evokes the subtle hues of heather that blanket the rugged landscapes of Argyll and Bute. With "Bute Heather" woven throughout its name, this tartan is part of a series created to evoke the spirit of Scotland's most iconic wildflowers. As a fashion tartan, it's perfect for adding a touch of rustic elegance to any outfit, while its subtle colour palette ensures it won't overpower even the most discerning palate.

name: MacDonald (Ken) personal; Bute Heather Grey
description: The Bute Heather, Grey tartan is a stylish fashion statement inspired by Scotland's rugged beauty. Created by renowned textile artisans at Houston Kiltmakers of Paisley, this distinctive tartan is part of a series designed specifically for commercial use. Characterised by its striking grey hues and geometric pattern, the Bute Heather, Grey tartan pays homage to the heather-dotted moors that blanket the Scottish Highlands. As a fashion tartan, it's perfect for those who want to add a touch of traditional Scottish flair to their wardrobe, while its commercial origins ensure it remains accessible and affordable for the masses. With its unique blend of modernity and heritage, this tartan is sure to turn heads and evoke a sense of pride in Scotland's rich cultural tapestry.

name: MacDonald (Ken) personal; Bute Heather Midnight
description: The Bute Heather, Midnight tartan is a captivating fusion of traditional Scottish heritage and modern fashion sensibilities, expertly crafted by the renowned Houston Kiltmakers of Paisley. As part of a series designed to evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's heather-covered moors, this tartan boasts a distinctive midnight blue tone that evokes the star-filled night sky above the rolling hills of Bute Island. With its unique geometry and subtle colour variations, the Midnight variation offers a sophisticated alternative to its brethren in the "Bute Heather" series, allowing wearers to make a statement with their sartorial choice while still paying homage to the timeless traditions of Scottish textiles.

name: MacDonald (Ken) personal; Glasgow Miles Better
description: Glasgow's Miles Better, a corporate tartan of enduring significance, proudly boasts its connection to Scotland's vibrant cultural heritage. Conceived in collaboration with K MacDonald of Wm Houston Ltd and John Buchan of Waverley Mill, Galashiels, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the iconic Glasgow Garden Festival of the 1980s, which brought a burst of creativity to the city. The tartan's palette, featuring deep red, vibrant yellow, and soothing grey, expertly evokes the official uniforms worn during that pivotal event. Today, as the site is reborn as the Glasgow Science Centre, this tartan design remains a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's rich traditions and the innovative spirit that has always defined its people.

name: MacDonald Dress
description: The MacDonald Dress tartan is a revered example of traditional Scottish heritage, steeped in the proud history of Clan MacDonald. Registered in 1880 under the Clans Originaux category, this timeless design has been woven into the fabric of Scottish identity for generations. Characterised by its distinctive blue and green hues, with subtle variations in sett and weft, the tartan embodies the values of courage, loyalty, and resilience that have defined the MacDonald clan since their origins on the Scottish Highlands. While some historical iterations featured black tramlines on white, today's weavers proudly retain the iconic blue and gold tones, a testament to the enduring legacy of this iconic Scottish family tartan.

name: MacDonald Dress; Irish
description: The MacDonald Dress tartan is a rich and storied example of Clan tartanry, its intricate design reflecting the proud heritage of the MacDonald clan from Scotland's rugged west coast. Registration notes reveal that this specific sett was inspired by Robert Mitchell's Pattern Book, a Dublin publication compiled during his time working in Paisley, Scotland. The unique 'halved count' pattern is particularly noteworthy, with half sets of threads alternating to create an attractive and complex visual effect. Dating back to 1982, when it was meticulously recreated from Mitchell's original designs by Su Grierson of Perthshire, this tartan embodies the enduring spirit of Scottish tradition, weaving together threads of history, culture, and family identity that continue to inspire wearers today.

name: MacDonald Lord of the Isles; Hunting
description: The MacDonald, Lord of the Isles Hunting #2 tartan is a storied heritage weave steeped in the rich history of Scotland's most revered Clan. Woven with precision and tradition, this striking pattern has been worn by royalty and nobility alike, including HRH Prince Charles, who proudly dons the tartan when visiting his Scottish ancestral lands. Its darker, more muted hues of green evoke a sense of solemnity, in contrast to the lighter tones often associated with the Prince's signature colour palette. The tartan also bears testament to its historical significance through its association with the former King Edward VIII, who wore it during his reign as Duke of Windsor. As a Clan tartan, this design is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition and heritage, making it a treasured possession for those who bear the MacDonald name or share their honour with the noble House.

name:
MacDonald of Aird & Valley
[AKA] MacDonald of Aird; & Valley
description: The MacDonald of Glengarry tartan, with its rich, earthy tones, evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. This ancient full-dress tartan, believed to have originated in Lochaber centuries ago, is steeped in history and heritage, its origins carefully documented by MacKay in his seminal work, The Romantic Story of Highland Garb (1924). As a plate included in this esteemed publication, the tartan's authenticity has been verified, solidifying its place as a tangible connection to Scotland's storied past. Once associated with Clan MacDonald, the tartan was later adopted by the Clan MacColl Society in the 1930s and is now commonly known as MacColl, its name bearing testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish clans and families. This tartan design remains an integral part of Scottish heritage, a poignant reminder of tradition, family, and the unyielding spirit of the Highlands.

name:
MacDonald of Ardnamurchan [default]
[AKA] MacDonald of Ardnamurchan
description: The "Homecoming" fashion tartan is a poignant tribute to Scotland's rich heritage, born from the designer's desire to celebrate the 250th anniversary of Scotland's beloved national poet, Robert Burns. At its core lies the iconic Burns family tartan, woven into the fabric as a symbol of enduring legacy. The tartan's distinctive red and moss green stripes represent the ancient bloodlines that have traversed the Scottish landscape for centuries, while the blue with silver surround pays homage to the country's storied maritime past, echoing the symbolism of the Saltire flag. This powerful design serves as a stirring reminder of Scotland's deep-rooted history and its people's unyielding connection to their ancestral homeland, inviting wearers to proudly don the tartan as a badge of honour that bridges cultures and connects them to a nation's timeless spirit.

name:
MacDonald of Boisdale [default]
[AKA] MacDonald Boisdale
[AKA] MacDonald of Boisdale
description: The MacDonald of Boisdale tartan is a quintessential representation of Clan MacDonald's rich heritage, with its storied history dating back to the early 19th century. This distinctive tartan was likely woven by skilled hands in Scotland during the late Georgian era, possibly at Wilsons of Bannockburn, whose sample is now held in the Cockburn Collection. The presence of another sample in the Highland Society of London Collection further reinforces its authenticity, with DC Stewart's 'The Setts of the Scottish Clans' recording it as no.118. This tartan holds great significance for Clan MacDonald, who take their name from the Gaelic 'Mac Domhnaill', meaning 'son of Donald'. With its subtle colour palette and intricate pattern, the MacDonald of Boisdale tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage and the enduring traditions of the country's ancient clans.

name:
MacDonald of Borrodale [default]
[AKA] MacDonald Borrodale Historic
[AKA] MacDonald Lady Borrodale's Gift
[AKA] MacDonald of Borrodale
description: The MacDonald of Borrodale tartan is a revered and historic fabric, imbued with the rich heritage of Scotland's Jacobite legacy. Registred in 1991, this tartan was gifted to Prince Charles Edward Stuart by his hosts, Angus and Catriona MacDonald of Borrodale, during his daring escape from Culloden in 1746. The intricate design weaves a tale of bravery, loyalty, and hospitality, as the Prince and his companions were sheltered and eventually helped to flee to safety. Only fragments of this original sea-soaked tartan cloth have survived, but thanks to the meticulous work of Peter MacDonald, Handloom Weaver, Crieff, and researchers Tom Massey Lynch, a beautifully recreated version has been woven by DC Dalgliesh. Today, the MacDonald of Borrodale tartan is a symbol of the enduring bond between Clan MacDonald and the Scottish Highlands, its technical precision and cultural significance testifying to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scotland's tartan heritage.

name:
MacDonald of Clanranald [default]

description: The MacDonald of Clanranald tartan is an iconic representative of Scottish heritage, woven with deep historical significance and family pride. Originating from the 18th century clan system, this tartan has been passed down through generations, bearing the distinctive signature of two white lines that set it apart from other designs. With its roots firmly planted in Clanranald's history, which was a large estate in Argyll, Scotland, this tartan is closely associated with the MacDonald family's legacy and tradition. Registered by the Lord Lyon Court in 1946, this tartan has been authenticated through various sources, including A and W Smith's 'The Authenticated Tartans of the Clans and Families of Scotland' (1850) and J Grant's work (1886). Today, a certified example can be found in the Highland Society of London collection, serving as a tangible connection to Scotland's rich tartan heritage.

name: MacDonald of Denovan; Personal
description: The Black Country tartan, designed by Philip Tibbetts of Halesowen, is a vibrant representation of the region's rich industrial heritage and distinct cultural identity. As a District tartan, it proudly signifies the people who call the South Staffordshire coal field home - the "Yam Yams" - and their unique traditions. The bold black and dark blue hues evoke the soot-stained landscapes that once characterised the area, while the red and green accents pay homage to the iron smelting industries that drove the region's growth during the Industrial Revolution. With its distinctive pattern, this tartan is a testament to the resilience and creativity of the people who have lived and worked in the Black Country for centuries, and its design serves as a lasting tribute to their history and traditions.

name:
MacDonald of Glenaladale [default]

Originally hailing from the MacDonald clan stronghold at Glenaladale, this tartan's story is one of cultural exchange and resilience, its intricate patterns a testament to the traditions and craftsmanship that defined 18th-century Scotland. With its unique colour palette and carefully woven design, the Glenaladale tartan continues to inspire a sense of pride and connection among those who wear it, their honour tied to the rich history and storied legacy of this iconic Scottish plaid.

As part of 'The Four Seasons' collection, Sakura embodies the vibrant spirit of Spring, evoking the fleeting beauty of cherry blossoms that symbolise new beginnings and renewal. The fabric bears the scars of time, its original cloth fragment, now housed in the West Highland Museum, yielding only fragments of information about its past - that it was spun, woven and dyed by John Rankin, Glencoe, some 200 years ago. With no definitive proof linking it to the MacDonalds beyond their association with the region, this tartan remains a mystery, yet its echoes of Scotland's turbulent past continue to captivate those who behold it.

name:

Though intended for the Prince's own use, it was deemed too vibrant and was eventually passed on to Malcolm Macleod of Macleod, who hid it away before his capture by government forces. The tartan's survival is a testament to the bravery and ingenuity of those involved in its creation, with only a small scrap surviving undamaged. As a result of Stewart's reconstruction efforts, which unfortunately were marred by inaccuracies, this tartan remains an important link to Scotland's complex past, proudly bearing the name of MacDonald of Kingsburgh and the families who have borne it for generations.

Now worn by pilgrims visiting Luss and those married here, this tartan serves as a powerful symbol of heritage and community, its significance woven into the very fabric of Scotland's rich history.

With its complex interplay of blues, greens, and yellows, this tartan design embodies the rugged beauty and majesty of Scotland's Highlands, a testament to the enduring spirit of the MacLeans and their storied heritage.

MacLean of Duart Dress Burgundy

name: MacLean of Kingairloch

The intricate pattern is steeped in Scottish tradition, featuring subtle variations in shade and texture that reflect the nuanced complexities of the clan's relationships with their neighbours. With a rich history spanning centuries, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring bonds within Clan MacLean, while its restricted status serves as a testament to the importance of familial respect and tradition.

name: MacLeay [default]
description: The MacLeay tartan, bearing the proud name of one of Scotland's storied clans, is a timeless testament to the country's rich heritage. Originating from Ingles Buchan, a region steeped in history and tradition, this tartan pattern has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish identity for generations. The clan's legacy, once associated with bravery and loyalty, continues to inspire wearers as they don the MacLeay tartan, symbolising honour and ancestry that runs deep within its threads. With no specified designer credited, it is the tradition of the Scottish Tartans Authority that lends authority to this tartan's authenticity, while threadcounts have been doubled for display purposes - a subtle nod to the craftsmanship and attention to detail that has always defined Scotland's finest textiles.

name:
MacLeish [default]

name: MacLellan #2 (Personal)

With its unique characteristics and personal significance, the MacLellan/McLellan tartan remains a treasured symbol of Scottish tradition and family pride.

name: MacLellan, Dress (Personal)

With its unique pattern, carefully crafted to evoke the essence of Scottish culture, this tartan stands as a testament to the enduring power of family history and personal legacy, reflecting the values of tradition, heritage, and identity that are woven into the very fabric of Scotland's rich tapestry.

name: MacLellan, Hunting (Personal)
description: This distinctive tartan, known as McLellan/McLellan Hunting, holds a special place in the annals of Scottish heritage, borne from the personal tastes of its creator, J R MacLellan of Edinburgh. name: MacLellan [default]
description: The MacLellan tartan is an enduring emblem of Scottish heritage and family tradition, its rich, intricate pattern evoking the storied history of Clan MacLellan, a stalwart Highland clan with deep roots in Scotland's turbulent past. name: MacLeod MacLeod, Bain (Personal)

Created by C.K. & Finlay Mcleod Bain, this unique pattern embodies the traditional Scottish art of tartan weaving, with its carefully selected sett and precise colour palette. With no restrictions on its wear, the McLeod-Bain Personal tartan is a fitting emblem of family identity and pride, allowing its bearers to proudly showcase their clan affiliation through traditional garb and textiles. This beautiful design serves as a tangible link to Scotland's rich heritage, connecting its wearer to a storied past and a sense of belonging to the land and its people.

name:
MacLeod Black & White

description: The MacLeod â 1906 (Black & White) tartan is a poignant and timeless tribute to the storied heritage of Clan MacLeod, a Scottish dynasty steeped in history and tradition. name: MacLeod Dress; Special
description: The MacLeod Special Dress, a unique and captivating dance tartan, holds a special place in Scottish fashion history. As a Fashion category tartan, this design was intended for the creation of special occasion garments, and its intricate patterns are sure to make any wearer feel like royalty. Although certain restrictions apply to ensure the integrity of the design, enthusiasts can still marvel at Dalgliesh's craftsmanship, capturing the essence of Scottish tradition through the beauty and precision of his woven masterpiece.

name: MacLeod German
description: This striking Corporate tartan, known as MacLeod, German, is a unique blend of tradition and international flair, reflecting the German branch of Clan MacLeod's rich heritage. Designed by Mr Uwe Frank, a member of the prestigious Clan MacLeod Gesellschaft Deutschland, this distinctive tartan combines the timeless colours of Clan Macleod with the bold hues of the German national flag: black, red, and gold. As a result, this tartan not only pays homage to its Scottish roots but also proudly celebrates German heritage. The special registration note, sanctioned by the 29th Chief, John MacLeod of MacLeod, confirms the tartan's significance as an honourable representation of Clan Macleod's enduring spirit, making it a treasured symbol for members of the German Clan MacLeod Society and those who aspire to embody its values.

name: MacLeod of Argentina

This vibrant tartan celebrates the country's connection to its expatriate Scots, particularly those from the Argentine branch of the MacLeod Clan Society. Though not officially affiliated with the clan society or the Scottish government, it has been adopted by some groups and wears proudly by pipe bands. The tartan itself is a fascinating blend of Scottish heritage and international flair, reflecting the cultural exchange that has shaped Scotland's relationship with its diaspora communities. While its origins may be disputed, the MacLeod of Argentina tartan remains an intriguing example of how a traditional Scottish pattern can be reinterpreted to tell a new story about Scottish identity and connection to the world beyond its borders.

name:
MacLeod of Assynt [default]

While its cousin tartan, MacLeod of Harris, features black guards to the yellow stripe, this version offers a striking alternative, omitting these darker accents to reveal a more subdued yet no less majestic design. As a testament to Scotland's complex history and cultural diversity, the MacLeod of Assynt tartan is a lasting tribute to a storied family legacy.

name:
MacLeod of California [default]
[AKA] MacLeod of California

Designed by Frank B Cannonito in collaboration with DC Dalgliesh Ltd, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the MacLeods, who have woven their history into the very fabric of Scottish tradition. As approved by the Clan Chief, the MacLeod of California tartan is now a proud symbol of family heritage and cultural identity for those fortunate enough to bear its storied threads.

name:
MacLeod of Gesto [default]

With its distinctive colour palette and precise weft-and-twist construction, this tartan embodies the values of tradition, loyalty, and resilience that have defined the MacLeods for generations. As a testament to the skill and craftsmanship of Tayinloan Lodge, MacLeod of Gesto #1 is an enduring symbol of Scottish heritage and clan identity, inviting wearers to proudly proclaim their honourable ancestry and connection to this storied family.

As a testament to Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, the MacLeod, Green tartan embodies the country's proud tradition of clan identity and heritage, its subtle nuances and rich colours evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands.

MacLeod of Lewis [default]

Named simply 'MacLeod', it has been worn by generations of MacLeods with honour and distinction, evoking a sense of history, loyalty, and connection to the land that has shaped their lives. With its rich blues and greens, subtle reds and yellows, this tartan is a testament to the skill and artistry of traditional Scottish weaving, and its very name conjures images of rugged landscapes, windswept moors, and the unyielding spirit of Scotland's most noble clans.

MacLeod of Raasay [default]

This timeless design, categorised as a Clan/Family tartan, weaves together the rich traditions and legends of the MacLeods, one of Scotland's most esteemed clans. With its intricate patterns and subtle nuances, this tartan evokes the rugged beauty of the Highland landscape, where rugged mountains meet crashing sea. Although the designer remains anonymous, it is clear that their intention was to honour the clan's history and legacy, as reflected in the carefully considered palette and subtle variations of tone that evoke the shifting moods of Scotland's wild and windswept west coast. As a testament to the enduring power of Scottish identity, this tartan continues to captivate hearts and inspire pride among MacLeods and those who cherish their heritage.

MacLeod of Skye [default]

name: MacLeod, Pink (Personal)

While originally created for personal use, its beauty and significance extend far beyond individual ownership, inviting wearers to be part of a centuries-old tradition that celebrates Scottish identity and family ties.

name: MacLeod Snuffbox
description: The MacLeod - 1835 tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage, with its intricate threads woven together to evoke the grandeur of 19th-century Highland aristocracy. Registration notes suggest that this distinctive pattern was inspired by the portrait of John Norman, the 24th chief of Clan MacLeod, painted at Dunvegan Castle on the Isle of Skye in 1835. The tartan's unique characteristics are thought to have been designed for a snuff-box presented during George IV's visit to Edinburgh in 1822, further solidifying its connection to Scotland's storied history. name:
MacLeod, Wedding (Personal)

name: MacLeod Society
description: The MacLeod Society of Scotland tartan is a vibrant and distinctive corporate design, born from the passion of Trudi Mann in 1991 for celebrating the heritage of Clan MacLeod. As a corporate design, it can be proudly worn by members of MacLeod Society or any other organisation that honours Scottish heritage, serving as a symbol of unity and connection to a storied past.

name: MacLeods Highlanders

This bold and rugged tartan, registered as part of the Scottish Tartans Society's collection, is deeply rooted in military tradition, evoking the bravery and discipline of the Highland regiments that proudly wore it into battle. With its distinctive threadcount taken from an original pattern book held by National Museums Scotland, this tartan design embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's armed forces, its colours and sett a testament to the enduring legacy of MacLeod's proud Highlanders, whose name is synonymous with courage and honour in the annals of Scottish history.

The registration notes highlight its origins as a bespoke design for this forward-thinking Dutch organisation, showcasing how Scottish tartan traditions can be adapted and reinterpreted to suit modern contexts, while still honouring the heritage that makes them so enduringly iconic.

name: MacLoughlin
description: The MacLoughlin of Ardmarnoch tartan is a unique and personal creation, borne out of a desire to reflect the individuality and character of its designer's daughters. name: MacManus

With its precise threadcount and elegant colour palette, this tartan is perfect for adding a touch of Celtic flair to any fashion ensemble. Originally registered as part of the UK's National Register of Historic Tartans, the MacManus tartan serves as a lasting connection to Ireland's storied past, while also providing a versatile and stylish choice for modern fashion enthusiasts.

name: MacMaster Canada
description: The MacMaster (Canada) tartan is a unique and meaningful representation of Scottish heritage in North America, celebrating the 200th anniversary of the MacMaster families' arrival in Canada. Designed by Blair Urquhart specifically for David John MacMaster of Beamsville, Ontario, this asymmetric tartan was created to unite the various spellings of the name under one distinctive design. Originating from the Moidart region and later settled in Craignish, Inverness Co, Cape Breton, the MacMaster families' history is deeply rooted in Scotland's west coast. The registration notes highlight a notable instance of two separate entities collaborating to create a shared tartan identity, resulting in a distinctive design that honours the Canadian connection while retaining its Scottish roots.

name: MacMaster, USA #2 (Personal)

As a Name tartan, it holds significant cultural importance, serving as a visual identifier of clan affiliation and family ties, connecting wearers across generations and geographical boundaries.

name: MacMaster USA#1

While it may be used by those who share the surname, its origins lie in Smith Jnr's thoughtful design to encompass various variations of the name, including MacMasters. This tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, where family, clan, and tradition are woven into the very fabric of our history.

With its unique blend of colours, this tartan design pays homage to the storied past of the MacMichael clan, while also serving as a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage and tradition.

name: MacMillan 1946

Despite a century passing since its creation, the MacMillan tartan continues to hold significance, serving as a visual representation of family honour and heritage, its subtle nuances and intricate patterns a testament to the skilled hands of Scotland's finest weavers.

With no designer credited, the tartan's creation remains shrouded in mystery, but its significance as a family heirloom is undeniable, a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan MacMillan and their rich cultural heritage.

name: MacMillan Hunting

A testament to its enduring influence is that the former President of the Clan Macmillan Society, Major Cameron Macmillan, always referred to it as "Baillie Macmillan's tartan", evoking a sense of familial pride and tradition. This Hunting sett was initially adopted by General Sir Gordon MacMillan to distinguish his family from other clan members, yet its popularity soon eclipsed the Ancient sett, cementing its place in Scottish textile history as a symbol of clan identity and heritage.

The subtle variations in thread count and colouration, discernible only to the most discerning eye, attest to the intricate craftsmanship of the weavers who created this masterpiece. As a testament to its enduring significance, the MacMillan Ancient tartan has been passed down through generations, its very name evoking a sense of history, honour, and family ties that are deeply ingrained in Scottish tradition.

The tartan's origins are shrouded in confusion, with some reports claiming its 'duly accredited' status from the State of Maine, while the archives reveal an unclear path. Despite this, the design has been rediscovered and reinterpreted by textile artist Jane Holmes, who wove it into a new fabric in 1988. Today, items featuring this tartan can be found in various outlets, including the Maine Tartan and Tweed Co., reflecting its enduring appeal as a symbol of American identity and connection to Scottish heritage, albeit with a distinction - its official state counterpart, #3068, was adopted by the State of Maine in 2001.

name: Mair [default]
description: The Mair tartan, a personal family emblem, weaves together the rich heritage of Robert George Alexander Mair's ancestry, set against the picturesque backdrop of South Uist, a remote Scottish island. This unique tartan design is rooted in an unnamed sett from the region, reinterpreted by renowned designer Peter MacDonald. The vibrant yellow threads evoke the gold and red hues of the 'Mair' coat of arms, proudly borne by Robert George Alexander Mair Esq., a member of the esteemed Clan Mair family. As a Clan tartan, this design carries weight within Scottish tradition, symbolising the honourable heritage of the Mair surname, which dates back to Alexander Smith Mair's arrival in Australia from Glasgow in 1924. The intricate pattern pays testament to Duine Usail, Robert's father, who had meticulously collected and reimagined the original tartan, said to be his final design before leaving the Tartans Society.

name: Maitland
description: The Maitland Chief, named after the esteemed Clan Maitland, is a majestic and storied tartan that embodies the heritage and tradition of Scotland's finest families. Designed by renowned textile expert Harry Lindley for Kinloch Anderson Ltd in 1953, this iconic sett was first worn by the standard bearers at Queen Elizabeth II's coronation ceremony, marking its grand entrance into Scottish history. Regulated by the Chief of Clan Maitland, use of this tartan is strictly controlled and available exclusively through the chief, underscoring its exclusivity and prestige. With an increased proportion of green and blue threads, this striking design reflects the characteristic colours of the clan's heritage, set against a rich tapestry of tradition and legacy.

name: Makhtoum Regimental
description: The Al-Maktoum Tartan is a storied military pattern steeped in the rich heritage of Dubai's ruling dynasty, the Al Maktoums. Designed by Major Stallard in 1977 for HH Shaikh Rashid Bin Saeed Al-Maktoum, this tartan was initially reserved for the Dubai Pipe Band and has since become an international symbol of pride for the city-state. After a period of decline, its rediscovery in 2002 by the Dundee-based Al Maktoum Institute for Arabic and Islamic Studies marked a new era of recognition, with official use granted to the Al-Maktoum Foundation in 2006. Now woven by the esteemed Strathmore Woollen Company of Forfar, this tartan embodies the legacy of the Al Maktoums and the enduring spirit of Dubai's people, weaving together the threads of tradition, history, and cultural identity.

name: Malcolm 1840
description: The Malcolm tartan (1840), as registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a fascinating example of Scotland's rich textile heritage. Originally created using two distinct shades of red - scarlet and rose - this unique sett reflects the intricate nuances of Scottish weaving traditions from the mid-19th century. Considered to be one of the oldest surviving examples of the Malcolm tartan, it poses an intriguing question about its authenticity, sparking debate among historians and enthusiasts alike. As a Clan tartan, it holds significance for those tracing their ancestry back to the MacDonald clan, who have worn this very fabric with honour and pride for generations. The Malcolm's distinctive colour palette and subtle weave pattern evoke a sense of tradition and heritage, serving as a poignant reminder of Scotland's storied past and the timeless artistry of its weavers.

name: Malcolm Dress
description: The Malcolm Dress tartan is a revered clan tartan steeped in history and tradition, its distinctive asymmetrical sett evoking the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's ancient clans. Registered with Scottish Tartans Authority, this particular version dates back to the 1930s, based on earlier samples collected by J. Cant and the Smith brothers in 1850. The origins of this tartan are further confirmed by D.C. Stewart's Nomindex, which aligns it with a description from a catalogue published by Neilson, Shaw & MacGregor in 1888. Woven by the skilled hands of Peter MacArthur of Hamilton, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Malcolm, a powerful Scottish dynasty whose motto "Fortiter et Liber" translates to 'Strong and Free'. Its status as a family tartan ensures that it remains a cherished part of Scottish heritage, passed down through generations and woven into the very fabric of Scotland's identity.

name: Malcolm Dress Variant
description: Malcolm Dress Tartan is a timeless and storied pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, specifically tied to the esteemed Malcolm clan family. This majestic sett is derived from Wilson's pattern books of 1847, which showcases the intricate connections between family traditions and tartan designs. The dress variant, dating back to the 1890s, likely served as a dignified attire for the clan members' formal occasions. With its rich gold and azure hues reminiscent of the Malcolm family armourial bearings, this tartan exudes an air of nobility and tradition. Though a small discrepancy is noted in the white band, where a blue line appears to be missing, it does little to detract from the overall sense of history and cultural significance that pervades every fibre of this majestic pattern.

name: Malcolm [default]
description: The Malcolm tartan, proudly worn by those bearing the noble surname, is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and tradition of clan identity. This distinctive asymmetrical design, first meticulously recorded in 1850 by W and A Smith's authoritative publication 'The Authenticated Tartans of the Clans and Families of Scotland', has been passed down through generations as an honourable emblem of the Malcolm family crest. Notably, its similarity to the Double Davidson tartan is noted by D.C. Stewart in his Nomindex, highlighting a fascinating connection within the world of Scottish textiles. As such, the Malcolm tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's storied past and the enduring significance of clan identity, evoking a sense of pride and tradition among those fortunate enough to bear this proud tartan.

name: Malmo Sky blue
description: The Malmo Skyblue tartan is a vibrant tribute to the people who call the Swedish city of Malmo home, with roots in the local district's rich heritage. Registered as a District tartan, it embodies the spirit of community that defines Malmo's identity. Designed by the esteemed trio of Goeran Broberg, Patrick McVey Gillion, and Joacim Nieminen, this distinctive pattern seeks to unite everyone connected to the town, from long-time residents to former inhabitants who remain proud of their Malmo roots. The bold colours pay homage to the city's beloved football club, Malmo FF, and its devoted supporters, paying testament to the strong sense of pride and belonging that defines the Swedish district's unique cultural identity.

name: Mandela Commemorative
description: This striking Mandela Commemorative tartan, designed by esteemed Kinloch Anderson Ltd, serves as a poignant tribute to the life and legacy of Nelson Mandela, the former President of South Africa. As a commemorative tartan, it was originally intended for the Scotland/Africa project, with the intention of promoting cross-cultural exchange between the two nations. Although not ultimately adopted, its significance lies in its symbolic representation of unity and reconciliation, reflecting the values of equality and justice that Mandela embodied. With its unique blend of colours and intricate weave, this tartan design embodies the rich heritage and cultural identity of both Scotland and South Africa, serving as a powerful reminder of the enduring impact of Mandela's remarkable life and work on the world stage.

name: Mandela Nelson
description: This poignant Name tartan, named after Nelson Mandela, is a testament to the enduring legacy of South Africa's iconic anti-apartheid leader. Designed by Jane Hunter, the tartan weaves together threads of historical significance and personal meaning, reflecting the profound impact Mandela had on her life and those around her. Presented as a gift from Tom and Marion Hunter of The Hunter Foundation to Graca Machel, Nelson Mandela himself was a recipient of this thoughtful gesture. With its unique blend of symbolism and warmth, this tartan serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of compassion, equality, and human rights - values that Mandela's remarkable life embodied, and which continue to inspire generations today.

name: Manderson #2
description: Manderson #2 is a distinctive Name tartan, carefully crafted by Chris Aitken to evoke the rich heritage of Scotland's clan system. This unique design features a striking colour palette, reminiscent of the country's rugged landscapes and rolling hills. By registering in 1999, Manderson #2 has been officially recognised as a distinct tartan pattern, steeped in tradition and steeped in history. As a Name tartan, it holds significance for families and clans who can trace their ancestry back to its original creator, Chris Aitken's thoughtful blend of blues, greens, and yellows subtly weaves together the stories of Scotland's past. This tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage, where tradition and innovation come together in a vibrant celebration of the country's cultural identity.

name: Manderson
description: The Manderson personal tartan, designed by Chris Aiken in collaboration with Geoffrey Highland Crafts, is a distinctive and meaningful representation of Scottish heritage. As a restricted family tartan, it holds significant cultural importance for the individuals who bear its colours, tracing back to their ancestral roots. Category classified as 'Name', this tartan bears witness to the individual's identity and lineage. Although subject to restrictions, its unique character shines through, showcasing a rich blend of blues and greens reminiscent of Scotland's rolling hills and glen landscapes. According to the registration notes, the Manderson is an alternative count variant from Anderson #2, first documented in 'Tartans' by Johnston and Smith in 1999. This tartan stands as a testament to Scottish tradition, weaving together history, family, and identity into its intricate weave.

name: Manhattan Ethnic
description: The Manhattan Ethnic tartan, designed by esteemed duo J Morgan and Suzanne H Bocanegra, pays homage to the rich cultural heritage of New York's diverse ethnic communities. This Fashion category tartan is deeply rooted in its inspiration from the city's multicultural fabric, with a palette that echoes the skin tones of the various ethnic groups that call Manhattan home. Pink, specifically, represents Caucasian flesh colour, subtly nodding to the city's European-American presence. With this bold and vibrant design, Morgan/Bocanegra has created a tartan that not only celebrates the city's cosmopolitan spirit but also serves as a poignant reminder of its complex and multifaceted identity.

name: Manhattan Financial
description: The Manhattan Financial tartan is a striking fashion-inspired design that embodies the glamour and sophistication of New York's financial district. Registered in 1999, this vibrant pattern is the brainchild of J Morgan and Sizanne H Bocanegra, renowned designers from the Big Apple. Characterised by its distinctive silver-tinsel effect created by a unique white yarn infused with metallic threads, this tartan shimmers like the glittering skyscrapers of Manhattan itself. A testament to the city's enduring legacy, the Manhattan Financial tartan adds a touch of modernity and glamour to any garment or accessory, making it a sought-after choice for fashion-conscious Scots and New Yorkers alike.

name: Manitoba Dress Dance
description: The Manitoba Dress, also known as Dance, is a fashion tartan with a storied past, though its status remains uncertain amidst the complexities of registration. Designed by Dalgliesh, D C, in what was then the Canadian North-West Territories (now Manitoba), this distinctive pattern is said to evoke the rhythmic energy of traditional Highland dances. Although not officially accepted due to unclear provenance and limited documentation, the tartan's design - comprising a striking mix of deep blues and greens, set against a rich gold background - speaks volumes about its cultural significance. Prepared for weaving by Dalgliesh's own company, this garment tartan represents an intriguing chapter in Canada's textile history, one that may yet be vindicated as its status is reevaluated.

name: Manitoba Provincial
description: The Manitoba Province tartan is a vibrant tribute to the history and heritage of Canada's prairies, woven into fabric by Scottish-born designer Hugh Kirkwood Rankine. This District tartan is a testament to the province's rich cultural diversity, with red squares representing the Red River Settlement, green squares symbolising the natural resources that sustain it, and azure blue squares paying homage to Lord Selkirk, the founder of the settlement. The dark green lines woven throughout the tartan nod to Manitoba's multicultural population, reflecting the province's status as a beacon of diversity in Canada. This 'history in cloth' is not only a celebration of the province's past but also a reflection of its people's resilience and spirit, with Rankine's design receiving Royal Assent in 1962, solidifying its place in Canadian tartan heritage.

name: Manitoba Cue Sports
description: The Manitoba Cue Sports tartan is a rich and storied creation, woven with precision by House of Tartan, paying testament to the enduring spirit of Canada's most esteemed organisation. Commissioned by Jay D Janzen, its founder, for the exclusive use of members at formal events, this tartan proudly wears the colours of military service, sacrifice, and national pride. Olive drab evokes a sense of military history and affiliation, while scarlet represents the blood shed by past members in defence of their comrades. Gold thread adds a note of nobility, symbolising the enrichment provided to Canada's people through the organisation's dedication and duty, whilst black nods to the sacrifices made for the greater good. As a Corporate tartan, it is reserved for those who bear the honour of membership within Manitoba Cue Sports, its very presence a testament to the values of loyalty, service, and camaraderie that define this esteemed group.

name: Manitoba Masonic
description: The Manitoba Masonic tartan is a rich and symbolic design created by the Grand Lodge of Manitoba Freemasons for their members, honouring the province's unique heritage and values. This Corporate tartan weaves together a palette of crimson red, blue, white, green, and yellow to represent the Red Ensign of Canada, the infinite prairies, and Manitoba's abundant resources; perfection and truth; purity; immortality; light; and loyalty to the British monarchy. The design's intersection of red and blue creates a regal purple, signifying the union of Freemasons with their concordant bodies, as well as the original peoples and immigrants who settled in Manitoba. This tartan is not only a nod to Scottish tradition but also a testament to the province's history and cultural identity, reserved exclusively for members of the Grand Lodge of Manitoba or those granted permission by this esteemed organisation, ensuring its exclusive use and honourable bearing.

name: Mann (Caithness) personal
description: The Caithness tartan is a rich and evocative District pattern that embodies the rugged beauty and storied heritage of Caithness, a historic county on Scotland's north-east coast. Designed by Trudi Mann of Wick, this distinctive tartan proudly showcases the region's unique colour palette, including the striking blue-grey Caithness flagstone, which has been used in cities around the world to evoke the area's rich history and cultural significance. As a District pattern, the Caithness tartan is deeply rooted in local tradition, its intricate design reflecting the county's complex geology, wild landscapes, and strong sense of community. Through this tartan, Mann pays tribute to the unique character of Caithness, bringing its beauty and distinctiveness to wearers and weavers alike, while also serving as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich textile heritage.

name: Mann [default]
description: The Mann tartan, a timeless and storied design, has been woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage for generations. Registered by Peter MacDonald on behalf of the Lawrie family from Fife, this clan tartan is deeply rooted in tradition and symbolism. The intricate pattern, which features shades of blue and green, is said to evoke the rolling hills and rugged coastlines of Scotland's northeastern coast.
