Once marketed by The Laurie Tartan Company, the Mann tartan has undergone a transformation, its ownership now in the hands of the Scottish Tartans Authority. Despite its commercial change, this tartan remains an honourable testament to the Lawrie family's legacy, with its design carefully controlled to preserve its authenticity and cultural significance for future generations to cherish.

name: Manroth
description: The Manroth tartan is a unique and personal design created by its eponymous maker, Alexander Manroth of Bad Hoenningen, Germany. This Name tartan holds significant cultural importance as it represents a Scottish identity born out of heritage and family ties, rather than clan affiliation. While the restrictions associated with this registration note preclude the tartan from being officially adopted by any specific clan or community, its significance lies in its individuality and the story it tells about its creator's Scottish roots. With its distinctive sett and colour palette, the Manroth tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage, blending tradition with personal flair.

name: Manson [default]
description: The Manson tartan, proudly registered by Pendleton Woolen Mills, is a storied example of Scottish heritage, boasting a rich history that spans several decades. Originally classified as a fashion tartan in 1984, it wasn't until 2003 that Phil Smith revisited the design, ultimately reclassifying it as a Clan/Family tartan. This designation underscores the tartan's connection to a specific Scottish family or clan, although its origins may be shrouded in mystery due to Pendleton's unusual foray into this traditional realm. The Manson tartan features a distinctive asymmetrical pattern, with an R4 sett on the warp and G4 sett on the weft, as noted by the Tartans Society. As part of the Johnston Collection in the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's iconic clan tartans, evoking a sense of tradition, heritage, and community that continues to captivate those drawn to its timeless beauty.

name: Mantle
description: This exquisite Name tartan, registered to Anna Mantle in 1997, is a poignant tribute to her personal heritage, expertly woven by Blair Urquhart's skilled hands. The intricate pattern combines elements of the storied Sinclair clan with the proud MacQueen name, creating a unique and meaningful design that showcases Anna's ancestral roots. As a Name tartan, this specific weave is reserved exclusively for Anna Mantle, making it an intimate expression of her family legacy. The subtle fusion of these two historic Scottish families within one fabric serves as a powerful symbol of unity and tradition, reflecting the enduring bond between clan, name, and personal identity.

name:
Manx; Snaefell Snaefell
[AKA] Turnberry #2
description: The Snaefell tartan, with its bold and adventurous spirit, is a testament to the rugged beauty of the Isle of Man's majestic landscape. Named after the towering 2,000 ft mountain that dominates the horizon, this District tartan was designed by Robert Wood to capture the essence of Laxey, a picturesque mill village nestled in the heart of the island. The registration notes evoke the rich history and heritage of the area, where St. George Mill once stood as a testament to the island's industrial past. As part of the esteemed Johnston Collection, the Snaefell tartan is an important record of Manx traditions and craftsmanship, ensuring that this unique design will be cherished for generations to come, woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage.

name:
Maple Leaf Blue
[AKA] Ontario School
description: The Maple Leaf Blue tartan, expertly woven by the esteemed West Coast Woolen Mill, embodies the spirit of corporate identity with its distinctive and striking pattern. Inspired by the iconic Canadian symbol, this tartan's roots stretch far beyond the borders of North America, tracing back to the intricate designs of traditional Highland Scotland. Notably, it was initially registered as an adaptation of the Maple Leaf design, originally created for the esteemed 'Highland Queen' clan or association. While its connection to a specific school in Ontario remains unclear, the tartan's subtle variations and nuances speak to the creativity and ingenuity of its designer. As a Corporate tartan, it is aptly suited for use by companies seeking a unique and memorable visual identity that pays homage to Canada's rich cultural heritage while reflecting their own values and brand essence.

name: Maple Leaf Dress
description: This captivating Maple Leaf Dress #2 tartan is a modern fashion interpretation of traditional Scottish weaving, bearing the mark of renowned designer Dalgleish. As a Fashion tartan, it has been crafted with style in mind, rather than for association with a specific Clan or heritage society. By adapting a seven-colour version, Dalgeish has created a unique and eye-catching design that pays homage to the iconic maple leaf motif, synonymous with Canadian identity and cultural significance. With its simplified colour palette, this tartan is sure to add a touch of elegance and whimsy to any fashion ensemble, while also proudly representing the artistic vision of its esteemed designer.

name: Maple Leaf Dress #2
description: The Maple Leaf Dress tartan is a stunning representation of Canada's rich cultural heritage, reimagined for the fashion world. As a Canadian fancy or fashion version of the original Mapel Leaf tartan (#2034), this design embodies the country's iconic symbolism - a delicate maple leaf motif woven into a sophisticated and modern fabric pattern. With no specific clan affiliation in mind, the Maple Leaf Dress tartan is intended to evoke a sense of national pride and identity, rather than serving as a traditional family crest. While restrictions are not specified, it's worth noting that this design may not be tied to a particular Canadian clan or heritage group, allowing its beauty to be appreciated by a wider audience. As such, the Maple Leaf Dress tartan offers a fresh and stylish take on a beloved national symbol, perfect for fashion enthusiasts and Canadians alike.

name:
Maple Leaf
[AKA] Canada
[AKA] Canadian
description: The Maple Leaf tartan, designed by David Weiser in 1964 for Highland Queen, embodies the spirit of Canada's rich heritage and connection to nature. This District-style tartan is imbued with the symbolism of the changing seasons, reflecting the ebb and flow of life as the maple leaf's colours transition from lush summer green, to golden hues of autumn, fiery reds of winter's first frost, and earthy tones of fallen leaves. Woven into this timeless design are themes of resilience, adaptability, and the cyclical passage of time, reflecting Canada's own journey towards Dominion status in 1867. As an official symbol of the Canadian Government since 2011, the Maple Leaf tartan has become an enduring emblem of national pride, paying tribute to the country's profound connection with its natural environment and its history as a nation.

name: Marr Red
description: The Mar Dress tartan, with its rich, bold colours, holds a profound place in the heritage of the Clan of Mar, whose history dates back to 18th century Glen Buchet. Originally adopted by the Countess of Mar, Chief of the Name, as an 18th century sett, this traditional tartan has been passed down through generations and is now proudly worn by those of the same name or given permission by the esteemed Countess. This hard-woven tartan, measuring 28 inches x 48 inches, was meticulously recorded in the Lyon Court Books on June 22nd, 1992, providing a tangible link to Scotland's rich tartan past. Its significance extends beyond its technical characteristics, serving as a symbol of family honour and tradition, while also paying homage to the Countess's dedication to preserving the Mar Dress pattern within the Scottish Tartans Society collection.

name: Marchioness of Huntly #2
description: The Marchioness of Huntly's tartan is a captivating Fashion pattern created by renowned Scottish textile designers Wilsons of Bannockburn. This distinctive design bears witness to its historical significance as a variation within a larger family of patterns, with an estimated dozen or so examples sharing a common ancestor dating back to the late 18th century. The incorporation of Ross, Rae, MacRae, and other tartans such as The Princes Own in its creation underscores its deep-rooted connections to Scotland's rich clan heritage. As a testament to the ingenuity of Scottish weavers, this tartan design has been skillfully woven to evoke the grandeur and majesty of Huntly House, a prominent seat of the Earls of Erroll in Aberdeenshire. By embracing this timeless pattern, wearers can proudly pay homage to Scotland's storied past while donning a garment that exudes elegance and sophistication.

name: Marchmont
description: The Marchmont tartan is a captivating family heirloom, carefully woven by Keith Lumsden to commemorate a cherished connection to Scottish heritage. As a Name tartan, it was designed specifically for personal use, allowing its creator to pay tribute to their own identity and heritage. This distinctive pattern tells the story of a beloved individual's history and traditions, with each thread and fibre imbued with significance and meaning. Although specific restrictions apply to its usage, ensuring that it is only worn or used by members of the Marchmont family, this tartan remains a treasured family legacy, linking past generations together through the shared experience of wearing a piece of their own unique history on their sleeve.

name: Maresh [default]
description: The Maresh tartan is a distinctive clan tartan with deep roots in American heritage, yet its origins are tied to Scotland's rich textile traditions. Designed by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr for his colleague Dan Maresh, a local resident from Pennsylvania, this simplified form of the Pennsylvania tartan takes inspiration from the traditional Scottish pattern, but with a twist: the yellow and red tramlines are reversed, giving it a unique and modern spin. This clan tartan is registered specifically for individuals bearing the name Maresh, symbolising pride and identity among those who wear it. With its bold, colourful design, the Maresh tartan is not only a nod to Scotland's weavers but also a celebration of cultural exchange and the enduring power of family ties.

name:
Marie Curie
[AKA] Fields of Hope
description: Marie Curie Fields Of Hope is a vibrant Corporate tartan that embodies the spirit of optimism and philanthropy, perfectly capturing the essence of its namesake's trailblazing legacy. With its bold and cheerful hues, including a radiant yellow that nods to the iconic daffodil symbol of the Marie Curie Fund, this tartan design was carefully crafted in 1995 to inspire charitable fund-raising efforts for a noble cause. This distinctive fabric represents the intersection of commerce and social responsibility, reflecting the values of innovation and community that Marie Curie embodied throughout her remarkable life. As a Corporate tartan, its suitability lies not only with those who wear it professionally but also as a testament to one's commitment to making a positive impact, making this tartan an enduring symbol of hope and inspiration for generations to come.

name: Marine Harvest Lochinvar
description: The Lochinvar Marine Harvest tartan is a stirring example of corporate tartanry, perfectly capturing the essence of Scotland's majestic landscape and heritage. Designed by MacArthur & Co., Peter, this distinctive pattern embodies the rugged beauty of the Scottish hills, the serenity of its waters, and the vibrancy of its wild heather moors. As a registered design, it holds a special place in the hearts of Scots who seek to pay homage to their national identity through subtle yet evocative threads of tradition. Dating back to 2009, when it was first certified by the Patent Office, this tartan has become an iconic representation of Scotland's corporate heritage, offering a unique way for businesses to express their connection to the land and its storied history.

name: Marino
description: The Marino tartan, crafted by the renowned West Coast Woolen Mill, embodies the dynamic fusion of traditional Scottish heritage with modern fashion sensibilities. This stylish and versatile Fashion tartan is said to evoke the vibrant spirit of the west coast, where rugged landscapes meet rolling hills. Registration notes indicate that a sample of this design was added to the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, signifying its place within Scotland's rich tapestry of traditional textiles. With no restrictions on use, the Marino tartan invites wearers and enthusiasts alike to tap into its fresh and modern aesthetic, infusing their everyday style with a touch of the country's storied past.

name: Marist School
description: The Marist School tartan, created by esteemed designer Kinloch Anderson Ltd, is a vibrant and distinctive corporate tartan born out of a celebratory spirit. Commissioned to commemorate the 50th Jubilee of the prestigious Marist School in Sunninghill, Berks, which educates over 700 pupils, this tartan embodies the institution's values and legacy. Its registration notes reveal a design steeped in tradition, created to honour the appointment of a new headmistress, Mrs Krysia Butwilowska, and pay tribute to the school's rich history. With its carefully crafted colours and precise threading, this tartan serves as a testament to the enduring spirit of Marist School, now proudly worn by those connected to the esteemed institution, subject to the controlled use stipulated by the school itself.

name: Mariverain
description: The Mariverain tartan, designed by the talented duo Saoie/Vachon, is a vibrant celebration of Sainte-Marie's rich history and cultural heritage. This fashion tartan was created to commemorate the city's 250th anniversary in 1994, honouring its French, Irish, and English roots. The colours - blue, green, and red - evoke the city's diverse origins, while gold threads represent the richness of its heritage, weaving together a unique narrative of identity and community. As an official tartan name, Mariverain is deeply rooted in the local culture, reflecting the values and traditions of Sainte-Marie's native sons and daughters, who proudly wear this distinctive design as a badge of honour, connecting them to their city and its storied past.

name: Marjoribanks [default]
description: The Marjoribanks tartan, registered in 1999, is a proud representation of Clan Johnston's heritage, born from the union of the clan's sept name with its ancestral colours. Designed by John Logan Marjoribanks, a family crest incorporated into the sett was adopted to pay homage to the Johnston legacy. This distinct tartan can be worn by anyone with the surname, regardless of spelling variation, and is a symbol of affiliation to this ancient Scottish clan. Pronounced 'Marchbanks', the name of its creator, this tartan's rich history and cultural significance are woven into every fibre of its intricate design, telling the story of a family's proud tradition.

name:
Marr [default]
[AKA] Marr Green
[AKA] Tribe of Mar
description: The Mar Tribe tartan, with its rich, earthy tones, holds deep cultural significance as a symbol of heritage and tradition for the family named Mar. Registered by the Countess of Mar in 1978, this historic tartan has been passed down through generations, evoking the strong sense of identity and belonging that is at the heart of Scottish clan culture. Dating potentially to before 1850, its origins remain shrouded in mystery, but the careful threadcount recorded by the Countess provides a tangible link to the past. As a Clan tartan, it will always carry the honour of its bearers, signifying their connection to the proud and storied history of the Mar family, whose values of loyalty, courage, and hospitality are woven into every thread of this timeless design.

name: Mars [default]
description: The Mars tartan is a proud and storied heritage pattern, woven from threads of tradition and personal sacrifice. Registered in 2004, this Clan family tartan pays homage to the distinguished Major George Mars, whose own life was marked by service to two noble causes: his time with the Argyll & Sutherland Highlanders (1935-1947), symbolised by the sombre black hue, and his association with the Royal Family at the House of Holyrood Palace (1920-2002), represented by a regal royal blue. A bright splash of sunshine yellow celebrates Major Mars's own Jubilee years, honouring the Golden Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II. This tartan design is not only a testament to Major Mars's distinguished career but also a poignant reminder of the enduring bonds between family, country, and monarch, reflecting the values of loyalty, duty, and service that have always defined Scotland's finest sons and daughters.

name: Marsa Scout Group
description: The Marsa Scout Group Tartan, expertly woven by Savona & Cutajar, is a vibrant and distinctive corporate design born from the rich heritage of Malta's esteemed scouting organisation. Originally created to adorn the ceremonial attire of the Marsa Scouts Pipes and Drums, this tartan proudly wears the colours of the Marsa town flag - blue and red - alongside yellow, echoing the iconic scarf worn by the group. Green, a nod to traditional Maltese fibre arts, adds depth and warmth, while black serves as a striking base colour that harmonises with the uniform. With its unique palette and exclusive usage by the pipe band during ceremonies, this tartan embodies the values of unity, community, and service embodied by the Marsa Scout Group - an enduring symbol of Maltese civic pride and scouting tradition.

name: Keith Fashion
description: The Marshall tartan, designed by the esteemed West Coast Woolen Mill, is a captivating fashion tartan that embodies the spirit of Scotland's rich heritage. As a fashion category tartan, it is intended for use in clothing, accessories, and other textiles where its vibrant colour scheme and intricate pattern will make a stylish statement. With no specific restrictions outlined in the registration notes, the Marshall tartan can be freely used to add a touch of Scottish flair to any garment or item. Its design, carefully crafted by the skilled artisans at West Coast Woolen Mill, showcases a unique blend of blues and greens, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's west coast landscapes. As a testament to traditional Scottish weaving techniques, this tartan is a celebration of the country's rich cultural heritage, perfect for those seeking to add a dash of Scottish elegance to their wardrobe or lifestyle.

name: Keith Fields
description: The Marshall Field tartan is a distinctive Corporate design that pays homage to the renowned American retailer's rich heritage, with roots in Scotland's storied tartan tradition. Registered specifically for use by the company during its 1986 production launch, this unique pattern reflects the brand's early international ambitions and its desire to connect with Scottish culture. Designed to be an authentic representation of the city of Chicago, the tartan's bold, modern aesthetic blends traditional tartan elements with a distinctly American flair. With its origins firmly rooted in Scotland, yet adapted for global commerce, the Marshall Field tartan embodies the intricate intersections of Scottish heritage and international business that defined this influential company's early years.

name: Martin, Bob (R.W.'s Fancy) (Personal)
description: Martin's Own, a unique and storied tartan, holds a special place in the annals of Scottish heritage. Originally designated by the Scottish Tartans Authority as West Point #1130, this sett has been reimagined by Bob Martin, a renowned kiltmaker and historian, who imbued it with an indigo overdye, infusing the traditional design with a sense of history and depth. Wefted with precision by skilled weaver D C Dalgliesh, Martin's Own is a testament to Scotland's rich textile traditions. As a personal sett, this tartan has been shaped by its creator's passion for preserving cultural heritage, making it an honourable tribute to the country's storied past. Its classification as a Name tartan underscores its connection to a specific family or individual, in this case, Bob Martin himself, whose vision and craftsmanship have given new life to a time-honoured design.

name: Martin Hunting
description: The Martin Hunting tartan is a storied heritage pattern born from necessity and tradition, its origins rooted in the 1920s when Eric Martin of Harrogate was seeking a bespoke kilt for his wedding. Although Kenny's initial attempt bore little resemblance to the desired "Martin" tartan, he adapted and created this unique design in honour of Eric Martin, later christened Martin Hunting. This Clan tartan is significant not only as a testament to familial connection but also as a tribute to Scottish tradition and the art of weaving, which has been passed down through generations. With its restricted thread count and prepared-for-weaving notation, it highlights the importance of craftsmanship in textile production, ensuring that this distinctive design remains an authentic representation of Scottish heritage.

name: Martin [default]
description: The Martin tartan is a quintessential Clan tartan, steeped in history and tradition, and its origins are deeply personal to its designer, Bob Martin. Registration notes reveal that Bob first introduced this distinctive pattern at the Charleston (or Savannah) Games, where it was favourably received by attendees. The thread count of 15 yards was deemed sufficient for his own kilt-making endeavour, a testament to the tartan's potential for wearability and visual impact. Characterised by its subtle nuances in colour palette, with a rich maroon or claret hue that Bob himself describes as 'purple', this sett pattern features narrower yellow stripes, offering a more balanced and aesthetically pleasing arrangement of tones. With its provenance within the Scottish Tartans Society's registry since 1993, the Martin tartan remains an integral part of Scotland's cultural heritage, synonymous with family identity and clan tradition.

name:
Mary Erskine School
[AKA] MacGregor of Deeside
description: The Mary Erskine School tartan is a vibrant and enduring representation of Scottish heritage, crafted to honour the legacy of Mary Erskine, the school's founder in 1694. This corporate tartan is based on the traditional Green Erskine sett, with a deliberate substitution of navy blue for green to reflect the school colours of red and navy. Kinloch Anderson Ltd has carefully adapted this iconic design to create a distinctive and unique fabric that not only celebrates the Tercentenary of the Mary Erskine School in 1994 but also acknowledges its rich history. Although use of this tartan is controlled by the school, it remains an important symbol of the institution's values and traditions, worn with pride by pupils, staff, and alumni alike. This tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's long-standing educational heritage and the enduring spirit of Mary Erskine, whose vision has inspired generations of students to learn and grow.

name: Mary, Queen of Scots [default]
description: The Mary, Queen of Scots tartan is a fascinating relic of Scotland's rich history, with its origins shrouded in intrigue and speculation. Said to have been taken from the seat cover of a 16th-century chair allegedly belonging to the legendary queen herself, now housed at Holyrood House, this sett is a true enigma. The story was born out of a mischievous family heirloom, as told by the Parker Knoll family, who claimed to have acquired the chair in the 1920s and discovered the tartan underneath. While some might say it's nothing more than a clever fabrication, the tartan's unique threadcount and azure hue, described as possibly faded light green, evoke an air of authenticity. A lesser-known variant, with similarities to another Scottish Tartans Authority reference, #1674 (Holyrood Chair), adds to its mystique. As one of the "Other" category, this tartan is a testament to the complexity and nuance of Scotland's textile heritage, forever woven into the fabric of history.

name: Maryland
description: The Maryland tartan is a rich and storied design, woven to commemorate the centennial celebration of the state's adoption of its iconic flag in 2004. Born from the colours of the Crossland and Calvert arms, quartered within the Maryland state flag, this tartan brings together a bold palette of Red, White, Black, Gold, Navy Blue, Azure, and Light Blue hues. Inspired by the United States Naval Academy at Annapolis and the majestic waters of the Chesapeake Bay, this District tartan is a testament to the state's proud heritage and maritime history. Balfour-Traill, Cynthia, masterfully blended these symbolic colours into a distinctive design that not only honours Maryland's rich cultural legacy but also pays tribute to its enduring spirit of patriotism and community.

name: Maryville College
description: This esteemed corporate tartan, known as Maryville College, is a testament to the rich heritage of American higher education and its deep roots in Scotland's storied weaving traditions. Woven by renowned textile expert Marjorie Warren, this vibrant design has been carefully crafted to evoke the spirit of Maryville College, located just 15 minutes south of Knoxville, Tennessee. As a corporate tartan, it is intended for use by companies and organisations with a connection to the institution, serving as a symbol of shared values and heritage. The registration notes proudly highlight the college's proud history, demonstrating the designers' commitment to preserving Scotland's traditional artistry while celebrating the unique identity of Maryville College in the United States.

name: Massachusetts #2
description: This unique name tartan, registered in honour of Mr. Nicholas Steward, is a testament to the rich tradition of Scottish heraldry. As a personal design, it showcases the individuality and flair of its creator, with no specific clan or family affiliation tied to its origins. The intricate pattern, carefully woven by Steward's own hand, features a distinctive blend of blues and greens that evoke the rolling hills and misty lochs of Scotland's picturesque landscape. While registration notes reveal little about its historical significance beyond its personal nature, this tartan is undoubtedly an important symbol of identity for Nicholas Steward, reflecting his unique character and heritage within the esteemed tradition of Scottish tartans.

name:
Massachusetts
[AKA] Bay State
description: The Massachusetts - The Bay State tartan is a vibrant and evocative celebration of the Commonwealth's rich heritage. Accepted as the official tartan of Massachusetts in 2003, this distinctive design pays tribute to the state's diverse landscapes and cultural traditions. With its palette of blues, greens, tans, and reds, the tartan reflects the Bay State's stunning natural beauty - from the Atlantic Ocean that borders the north shore, to the rolling hills of Worcester and Berkshire, and the lush mountains that give way to picturesque beaches along the South Shore. The incorporation of specific colours is a nod to the state's thriving agricultural industry, with apples and cranberries earning their place in the tartan alongside more rustic elements, such as reservoirs and rivers. This District tartan is a proud representation of Massachusetts' unique identity, woven from its distinct landscapes and traditions by renowned designer John R Austin.

name: Massie
description: The Massie/Massey tartan, registered at #1733, holds a rich history rooted in Scottish heritage. Designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, this Fashion tartan has been adopted by Major Randal Massey of Dunham as a tribute to his esteemed family name. Originally created with the traditional red colour replaced by brown, this subtle variation pays homage to the complexities of spelling variations and the nuances of Scottish naming conventions. Woven by skilled hands in 1969, this tartan tells the story of a name that has been passed down through generations, its very fabric woven from tradition and family honour. As a testament to the enduring spirit of the Massies/Masseys, this tartan design remains an important part of their legacy, tied to the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage and the artisans who bring it to life.

name: Matheson Blue; Hunting
description: The Blue Matheson Hunting tartan is a quintessential Scottish fashion design, woven with rich tradition and heritage in mind. As part of the esteemed Kinloch Anderson collection, crafted by skilled weavers in Edinburgh, this tartan evokes the storied legacy of the Matheson clan. Dating back to 1977, its registration notes reveal an unassuming yet distinctive pattern, redolent of the rugged Scottish Highlands where its namesake clan once roamed. With 'slog' and 'yby' etched into its registry, this tartan whispers tales of a bygone era, one that seamlessly blends rustic charm with refined elegance, making it a timeless choice for those drawn to Scotland's storied past.

name: Matheson Hunting
description: The Matheson Hunting tartan is a rich and storied fabric, steeped in the heritage of Clan Matheson and the rugged traditions of Scottish hunting. This historic tartan, registered in 1906 by W & A K Johnston, pays homage to the clan's proud history, with subtle adaptations that distinguish it from its predecessor, the Matheson Dress tartan. Characterised by a striking palette of blues, greens, and earthy tones, this tartan design is woven with reverence for the ancient arts of hunting and the wild beauty of Scotland's landscapes. Its creation serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Matheson, and its unique blend of colour and texture offers a captivating glimpse into Scotland's rich cultural heritage.

name: Matheson, Hunting Dress (Personal)
description: Matheson Hunting is a poignant personal tartan registered in 1974, its history woven into the fabric of individual heritage. Originally created for Miss Christine Crowe, a Highland dancer from Edinburgh, this distinctive Name tartan is imbued with the spirit of Scottish tradition and movement. Replacing traditional black with crisp white, Matheson Hunting reflects the dancer's unique flair and style, while also paying homage to her personal connection to the kilt-wearing world. The tartan's creation was facilitated by a local retailer in Edinburgh, further underscoring its intimate, community-driven origins. With no commercial ties, this tartan remains an important reminder of the enduring power of Scottish identity and tradition, cherished for generations by Miss Crowe's family and those who wear it with pride.

name: Matheson (Personal)
description: The Matheson Hunting (Blue) tartan is a unique interpretation of traditional Scottish heritage, born from the imagination of renowned designer Peter MacDonald. Originally conceived for a US customer who eschewed the traditional green hue, MacDonald's design deftly substituted light blue to create a fresh yet timeless variant of this historic clan tartan. As an example of the Name category, this tartan pays homage to the Matheson family, whose legacy is woven into Scotland's rich tapestry. With its distinctive pattern and subtle colour variation, the Matheson Hunting (Blue) tartan embodies both tradition and innovation, offering a stylish and meaningful way for wearers to connect with their Scottish roots while breaking free from convention.

name:
Matheson [default]
[AKA] Matheson Red
description: The Matheson Dress tartan is a storied representation of the Matheson clan's rich heritage, woven from threads of Scottish tradition and history. Registered in all its glory, this tartan design tells the tale of a family deeply intertwined with their Highland neighbours - the MacDonells of Glengarry and the MacKenzies of Kintail. The subtle nuances of this distinctive pattern, which often wears the red hue as its defining colour, pay homage to the clan's enduring connections to these neighbouring clans. Dating back to at least 1816, when a sample was certified by the chief of Glengarry, this tartan is an authentic manifestation of the Matheson family's storied past, one that reflects their values and traditions passed down through generations.

name: Carnegie [default]
description: The Carnegie tartan is a storied and historic pattern, born from a variant of the MacDonell of Glengarry tartan, which has been imbued with the spirit of Scotland's rich heritage. Adopted by Lord Southesk, a prominent figure in the 1715 rebellion, this tartan bears testament to the tenacity and bravery of Scotland's clans during tumultuous times. A subtle yet significant variation from its Glengarry counterpart, where white threads are replaced by yellow, the Carnegie's unique character is a result of the passing of time, allowing it to stand proudly as a distinct and evocative representation of Scottish tradition. Its tripled thread count swatch adds depth and texture, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's lochs and glens, while its association with Lord Southesk lends it an air of nobility and honour, cementing its place in the annals of Scottish tartanry.

name: Matthew Gloag Whisky
description: The Famous Grouse tartan is a rich, evocative corporate design that pays homage to Scotland's storied whisky heritage. Originally inspired by the traditional Matthew Gloag & Son Ltd tartan, now superseded in favour of its own distinct identity, this tartan embodies the legacy of Crieff-based company, Matthew Gloag & Son Ltd, which has been blending iconic Famous Grouse whisky since 1800. The addition of a small splash of purple adds a subtle nuance to the design, reflecting the brand's modern rebranding in 2015. As a corporate tartan, it is aptly suited for formal wear or branding purposes, yet its roots in traditional Scottish weaving ensure a deep connection to the country's rich cultural heritage. With its thoughtful incorporation of historical references and bold, confident colour palette, The Famous Grouse tartan embodies the enduring spirit of Scotland's finest whisky maker.

name: Matthews
description: The Matthews tartan, designed by Keith Lumsden, is a variant of the storied Donnachaidh (Robertson) tartan, tailored specifically to reflect the Matthews family's noble lineage within the Robertson clan. This personal tartan is reserved for use by members of the name, signifying their unique heritage and connection to the storied Clan Robertson. With its distinctive colour palette and precise sett pattern, this tartan embodies the rich history and tradition of Scotland's ancient clans, evoking a sense of pride and belonging among those who wear it. As a testament to the Matthews family's membership in the Robertson clan, this tartan design serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's proud cultural heritage, its intricate weaving reflecting the complex tapestry of history, identity, and community that defines the Scottish experience.

name: Maud
description: This exquisite Fashion tartan, registered with the iconic Maud, Mary designation, is a true gem of Irish heritage, woven from the storied threads of Robert Mitchell's 19th-century weaving patterns. Dating back to his Dublin-based workshop in Brabazon Row, The Liberties, this tartan tells the tale of Paisley-born weaver Mitchell's journey to Ireland, where he left an indelible mark on the country's rich textile heritage. With its intricate colour palette and precise sett, this Maud, Mary tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish and Irish craftsmanship, reflecting the cultural exchange that defined a bygone era in Dublin's bustling weaving mills.

name: Mauthe [default]
description: The enigmatic Mauthe Unidentified tartan is an enduring testament to Scotland's rich heritage, shrouded in mystery for over eight decades. Originally attributed to the Mauthe family from the USA, its origins remain unknown due to a remarkable failure to identify it through extensive research by the Scottish Tartans Authority and local archives. Despite attempts to uncover its history, the tartan has defied categorisation, with some speculating that it may be an obscure variant of the Forbes pattern, faded over time. This intriguing anomaly highlights the complexity and uniqueness of Scotland's clan system, where tartans often hold secrets and stories waiting to be uncovered by historians and enthusiasts alike.

name: Maxwell Hunting
description: The Maxwell Hunting tartan is a storied and historic Scottish design, steeped in tradition and heritage, originating from the Clan Maxwell family. This striking pattern was developed by Scotty Maxwell, the first President and Chieftain of the US Clan Maxwell Society, as a variation on the classic red sett, with a bold twist: the colours were reversed to create a distinctive green sett with prominent red lines. As such, it has been noted that this tartan bears some similarities to the Pollock and Maxton patterns, its unique identity setting it apart from its brethren. This Clan tartan is not only a proud representation of Scottish heritage but also a testament to the ingenuity and creativity of its designer, reflecting the rich cultural and family traditions of the Maxwell clan.

name: Maxwell [default]
description: The Maxwell tartan is a rich and storied weave, steeped in the history and heritage of one of Scotland's most noble clans. Although the registration notes suggest a somewhat mysterious provenance, it is clear that this tartan has been woven with deep roots in tradition, dating back at least 150 years. Originally created by persons of great imagination and flair, it was later popularised by the Sobieski Stuart brothers, who gifted their designs to the Scottish gentry in the early Victorian era. With its subtle nuances and intricate patterns, the Maxwell tartan is a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scotland's textile artists, and serves as a proud symbol of family honour, heritage, and tradition - a true reflection of the timeless beauty and romance that has captivated hearts for generations.

name: Mayhew [default]
description: The Mayhew tartan is a poignant and evocative family heirloom, woven to commemorate the descendents of Thomas Mayhew, the 17th-century Governor of Marthas Vineyard. Designed by Dr Philip D Smith, a 11th-generation descendant himself, this Clan tartan pays tribute to the sea that played such a pivotal role in the history of the island and its people. The subtle palette reflects the natural beauty of the Vineyard: the deep blue represents the ocean's vastness, the muted green echoes the island's lush landscape, while the crisp white symbolises the foamy surf that crashs against the shore. The subtle black thread weaves through the design serves as a poignant reminder of those who did not return from the sea, their memories etched into the very fabric of this tartan in tribute to Thomas Mayhew and his community.

name: Mayo Irish County
description: The Mayo, County tartan is a richly woven representation of Ireland's heritage, crafted with precision by Polly Wittering of the House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. As one of a series of District tartans, it pays homage to the traditional trade textiles of the Emerald Isle, albeit not officially sanctioned by the Scottish Tartans Authority. Instead, its popularity has led to its acceptance as a legitimate District tartan, rather than simply a Fashion design. Originally created for Macnaughtons of Pitlochry, this tartan holds significant cultural value, reflecting the community's history and traditions in County Mayo. Its presence on fabrics serves as a testament to the enduring connection between Ireland and Scotland, two nations united by their shared love of rich textiles and timeless heritage.

name: Mazarian
description: The Mazarian tartan, a unique and storied fabric born from the Norwegian connection of its creators, Varg Breivik and Geoffrey (Tailor), pays homage to the rich heritage of their ancestral home. This Name tartan is deeply personal, designed specifically for all Breiviks from Oygarden, a charming town nestled in southern Norway, not far from the majestic city of Bergen. The colours, inspired by the Norwegian flag, reflect the country's natural beauty with green and light brown lines evoking the fertile fjords that dot the landscape. While the traditional Scottish red square is present, its positioning has sparked debate among tartan enthusiasts, with some interpreting it as a nod to Scotland, adding an air of mystery to this distinctive design. This tartan serves as a tangible connection to Norwegian tradition and culture, woven into the very fabric of Breivik identity.

name: McCall (Aberdeen) personal; Highland Pride of Scotland
description: The Highland Pride of Scotland tartan, a masterful creation by esteemed weavers at Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the unbridled spirit of Scotland's majestic Highlands. Inspired by the enduring legacy of its Scottish heritage, this fashion tartan is a testament to the nation's proud history and storied clans. Registration notes confirm that it was designed with pride in mind, exclusively woven by McCalls of Aberdeen, whose expertise has been meticulously honed over generations. With its unique colour palette, carefully selected to evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's landscapes, this tartan is poised to inspire a new generation of Scots and lovers of all things Scottish, while honouring the timeless traditions that have defined the nation for centuries.

name: McCall (Aberdeen) personal; Pride of Scotland
description: The Pride of Scotland tartan is a vibrant and bold fashion-inspired design, carefully crafted by McCalls of Aberdeen in collaboration with Lochcarron of Scotland. As a Fashion tartan, it embodies the spirit of Scottish heritage and culture, proudly showcasing the country's rich history and traditions. With its distinct colour palette, this tartan pays homage to the nation's storied past, evoking feelings of pride and national identity. Notably, it bears a striking resemblance to the Spirit of Bannockburn, another notable tartan design, demonstrating a clear thread of Scottish design continuity. Furthermore, McCalls' exclusive ownership and Lochcarron's expert weaving have ensured that this tartan is woven with the finest quality and attention to detail, making it an exceptional addition to any fashion collection.

name: McCall (Aberdeen) personal; Pride of Scotland Autumn
description: The Pride of Scotland Autumn tartan, a true masterpiece of woven artistry, embodies the warmth and richness of Scotland's autumnal landscape. Registered as a fashion tartan by McCalls of Aberdeen, this distinctive pattern is steeped in heritage and tradition, evoking the golden hues and fiery tones of the country's most iconic autumn foliage. Woven exclusively at Lochcarron of Scotland, one of Scotland's finest tartan mills, this tartan is not only a testament to the artistry of its creators but also a celebration of Scottish culture and identity. With no restrictions on use, the Pride of Scotland Autumn tartan invites wearers to proudly don their heritage and make a statement about their connection to this beautiful country.

name: McCall (Aberdeen) personal; Pride of Scotland Contemporary
description: The Pride of Scotland Platinum is a stunning fashion tartan, one of a prestigious series created by esteemed Scottish designer McCalls of Aberdeen. This captivating design embodies the spirit of Scotland's rich heritage, its bold hues evoking the country's proud history and unyielding determination. The Platinum tartan is a symbol of excellence and achievement, its intricate pattern woven from threads of deep blue, emerald green, and golden yellow, reminiscent of Scotland's majestic landscapes and iconic landmarks. Wearing this tartan as a fashion statement is an honour, paying tribute to the nation's storied past while making a statement about one's own sense of pride and individuality.

name: McCall (Aberdeen) personal; Pride of Scotland Dress Dance
description: This vibrant fashion tartan, known as the Pride of Scotland Dress, is a celebration of Scotland's rich heritage and cultural identity. Registered by renowned Aberdeen-based milliners McCalls of Aberdeen, this striking pattern takes its cue from the DC Dalgliesh Dancers swatch book, highlighting the intricate traditions of Scottish dance. Characterised by its bold, rhythmic repeat, this tartan embodies the spirit of performance and celebration that lies at the heart of Scotland's thriving arts scene. With its carefully selected palette of colours, this tartan would be a fitting choice for anyone looking to showcase their pride in Scottish culture - whether on the dance floor or simply as a statement piece, this tartan is sure to make a bold impression, evoking the energy and passion that defines Scotland's renowned tradition of ceilidh dancing.

name: McCall (Aberdeen) personal; Pride of Scotland Gold
description: The Pride of Scotland Gold tartan is an iconic fashion tartan that embodies the warmth and vibrancy of Scotland's rich heritage. Created by McCalls of Aberdeen, this stunning design has been woven exclusively with precision by Lochcarron of Scotland, a renowned Scottish textile mill steeped in tradition. As a Fashion tartan, it boasts a bold and eye-catching colour palette, evoking the golden hues of Scotland's sun-kissed landscapes. While not a clan tartan per se, this design pays homage to Scotland's cultural significance, perfect for those who wish to connect with their Scottish roots or simply celebrate its beauty. With no restrictions on use, the Pride of Scotland Gold tartan is free to be worn and admired by all, its associations with Scotland's pride and heritage making it a cherished choice among fashion enthusiasts.

name: McCall (Aberdeen) personal; Pride of Scotland Silver
description: The Pride of Scotland Silver tartan is a majestic fashion tartan that embodies the proud heritage of Scotland, woven with precision and passion to evoke a sense of national pride. Designated as a Fashion tartan, it is one of many unique patterns that bear the name of their originating Clan or geographical location, in this case, an expression of Scottish honour. Created by the renowned McCalls of Aberdeen, this design has been carefully crafted exclusively for Lochcarron of Scotland's expert weavers, who have painstakingly woven a rich tapestry of blues and silvers to pay tribute to Scotland's storied history. With its elegant balance of colours, the Pride of Scotland Silver tartan is an enduring testament to Scottish craftsmanship and tradition, guaranteed to add a touch of elegance and sophistication to any garment or accessory that bears its distinguished design.

name: MacCaslin [default]
description: The McCaslin tartan tells a tale of transatlantic tradition and the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage in America. Registered as "Other", this distinctive tartan hails from a handwoven cloak once treasured by Jane Smith Winchester McCaslin, wife of Wosson McCaslin, who lived in Johnson County, Indiana, USA from 1850 to the early 1900s. This exquisite fabric is dyed with aniline dyes, a testament to the innovative spirit of its time. The cloak's provenance is a poignant reminder that Scottish tartanry has traversed the Atlantic, taking root in the American heartland, where it has been cherished by families like the McCaslins for generations. As such, this tartan holds a deep honour within the world of Scottish textiles, serving as a tangible link to the past and a symbol of cultural exchange between two nations.

name: McGill (David) personal; Boroughmuir
description: The Wimbledon tartan, expertly woven by David McGill, is a vibrant and iconic fashion design inspired by the world of tennis. Originally created in 1999 as a collaborative effort with IT Sports to raise funds for tennis worldwide, this stylish tartan was carefully crafted to incorporate the corporate colours of the Lawn Tennis Association. While intended as a fundraiser, the Wimbledon tartan has since become synonymous with the prestigious All England Lawn Tennis Club and the coveted title of Wimbledon Champion. With its unique blend of bold blues and whites, evoking the excitement of the tennis court under the Centre Court roof, this tartan is sure to evoke the spirit of British sporting heritage and tradition. As a Fashion category tartan, it can now be enjoyed by designers and enthusiasts alike, but with the added stipulation that permission must be sought from the designer, David McGill, to reproduce or use the design.

name: McGill (David) personal; Bowlers
description: The St Andrew tartan is a commemorative design born from the confluence of Scottish heritage and sporting tradition, as originally conceived by renowned tartan designer David McGill of International Tartans in 2004 for the World Championships at Northfield Park Ayr. Initially intended to celebrate the seven hundredth anniversary of bowling, this unique tartan has since been adopted to commemorate St Andrew, Scotland's patron saint, whose colours are expertly woven into the fabric: the iconic blue and white hues of the St Andrew's Cross blending harmoniously with the regal purple and green of the thistle. As a testament to Scotland's rich cultural legacy, this tartan stands as a poignant tribute to the nation's history, tradition, and symbolism, its restrictions affording those who secure the designer's consent exclusive access to this distinctive and evocative design.

name: McGill (David) personal; Carolina, North
description: This striking North Carolina fashion tartan is a vibrant celebration of Southern charm, carefully crafted by David McGill and International Tartans Ltd. Commissioned by Charles Wilson of Harnet County, North Carolina in the late 20th century, the tartan was specifically created for North Carolinians, symbolising pride and heritage for those with roots in the Tar Heel State. Although not officially recognised as the state's official tartan, it remains a cherished symbol of regional identity and community spirit. With its unique colour palette and intricate design, this tartan is a testament to the rich cultural tapestry of North Carolina, weaving together threads of history, tradition, and modern flair.

name: McGill (David) personal; Carolina, South
description: The South Carolina tartan is a vibrant and distinctive fashion tartan, commissioned in 2001 by Mrs Mary K Hurt to represent the people of South Carolina and those who associate with the state. This unique tartan incorporates the colours of the State flag, creating a bold and eye-catching pattern that proudly reflects the heritage of this American state. As a fashion tartan, its primary purpose is to be worn in clothing and accessories, evoking the spirit of South Carolina's rich history and culture. While not officially recognised as an authentic Scottish tartan, its design pays homage to the traditions of tartan-making while embracing a distinctly American twist, making it a fascinating addition to the world of tartans.

name: McGill (David) personal; Clunie
description: The Clunie tartan is a bespoke design born from the traditions of Scottish heritage, carefully crafted for Mr Ben Clunie of Edinburgh to represent his personal connection to the esteemed Clan Clunie. Commissioned with meticulous attention to detail, this unique tartan incorporates hues reminiscent of the clan's crest, paying homage to the rich history and ancestry of those bearing the name Clunie. This family-specific tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish clans, where names are woven into the fabric of tradition and identity. Although open for use with the designer's consent, the Clunie tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the significance of clan affiliations and personal heritage in Scotland's storied past.

name: McGill (David) personal; Dumbartonshire
description: The Dunbartonshire tartan, a quintessential representation of Scotland's rich heritage, was masterfully woven by David McGill of International Tartans for fashion enthusiasts to don with pride. This stunning design, categorised as Fashion, is a testament to the county's storied past and its people's unwavering connection to the land. Registration notes reveal that it was specifically created to be worn by those from or associated with the County of Dunbartonshire, paying homage to the region's unique history and culture. Notably, this tartan falls under the category's restrictions, requiring the designer's consent for use, underscoring its sensitive cultural significance. Wearing the Dunbartonshire tartan is a subtle yet meaningful way to honour the county's legacy and partake in Scotland's enduring traditions of craftsmanship and identity.

name: McGill (David) personal; East Lothian District
description: The East Lothian tartan, designed by David McGill in collaboration with International Tartans Ltd, is a vibrant tribute to the rich heritage of Scotland's eastern counties. This fashion tartan was launched as a way to honour those from or associated with East Lothian, with Provost Pat O'Brien at the helm, aiming to bring together community and pride. Although not officially recognised as the traditional East Lothian tartan, this design embodies the spirit of local identity and camaraderie, perfect for anyone looking to connect with their roots or simply add a touch of Scottish flair to their wardrobe. With its unique colours and subtle nuances, this tartan is available by special permission from the designer, giving those who wear it a special connection to the county's rich history and culture.

name: McGill (David) personal; European International
description: The European tartan, designed by David McGill of International Tartans in celebration of the EU's 50th anniversary, is a vibrant and symbolic tribute to unity and cooperation. As a Fashion tartan, it is intended for wear on clothing and other textiles, serving as a badge of affiliation with the values of European integration. With its distinctive blue, green, yellow, and red hues, this tartan pays homage to the EU's rich history and diverse cultural heritage. Registration restrictions apply, requiring permission from the designer, indicating that careful consideration has been given to ensuring this tartan's authenticity and respect for the broader European tradition. This tartan is a fitting tribute to the spirit of international collaboration and mutual understanding that defines the European project.

name: McGill (David) personal; Fife
description: The Fife tartan, registered for fashion purposes, is a vibrant representation of Scotland's rich heritage, specifically tied to the storied County of Fife in East Central Scotland. While not officially recognised as the authentic Fife tartan, this variation holds its own significance and charm. Designated exclusively for anyone from or associated with the region, this tartan boasts distinctive characteristics that evoke the county's proud history and cultural identity. With the seal of approval from David McGill and International Tartans Ltd, wearers are granted permission to don this prestigious tartan in favour, provided they secure the designer's consent. This fashion-forward interpretation pays homage to Fife's enduring legacy while embracing its unique blend of tradition and modern flair.

name: McGill (David) personal; Golfers Sport
description: The Royal and Ancient / Golfing Stewart tartan is a vibrant and storied textile that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's golfing traditions. Designed by David McGill, this distinctive Name tartan was created specifically for the sport of golf, paying homage to the esteemed Stewart clan, whose legacy in golf stretches back centuries. Named after the late American professional golfer Payne Stewart, who proudly wore tartan plus-fours to celebrate his Scottish roots, this tartan has become synonymous with the game's global appeal and cultural significance. With its restricted consent, allowing only those with David McGill's approval to reproduce it, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of tradition and heritage in golf, inviting wearers to connect with their own Scottish roots and the sport's storied history.

name: McGill (David) personal; Lanarkshire District
description: The Lanarkshire tartan is a striking fashion choice inspired by the historic County of Lanarkshire, situated in the heart of Scotland's Lowlands. Created by renowned designer David McGill for International Tartans Ltd, this vibrant design pays homage to the region's rich cultural heritage. Originally registered as a fashion tartan, it is not officially designated as the county's official tartan, but rather intended for those with a connection to Lanarkshire or its people. With restrictions in place requiring consent from the designer, this tartan offers an exclusive way for enthusiasts to showcase their affinity for the region. As a testament to Scotland's enduring traditions and the skill of traditional weavers, the Lanarkshire tartan embodies the county's warmth and hospitality, inviting wearers to proudly proclaim their roots or associations with this iconic corner of Scottish history.

name: McGill (David) personal; Midlothian District
description: The Midlothian tartan, designed by David McGill in association with International Tartans Ltd, is a captivating representation of Scotland's rich heritage, born from the heart of the historic County of Midlothian. As a Fashion tartan, this intricate pattern has been crafted to evoke the elegance and sophistication of traditional Scottish textiles, while also being adaptable for modern wearers. Although it has not been officially recognised as the traditional tartan of Midlothian, its origins in the county's storied past lend it an authentic air, paying homage to the region's proud history and cultural identity. Notable restrictions apply, requiring permission from the designer, David McGill, before use, underscoring the importance of respecting this unique design and its connection to the people who call Midlothian home.

name: McGill (David) personal; Newcastle City
description: The Newcastle tartan is a vibrant and distinctive district tartan, born from the passion of supporters for one of England's most beloved football clubs. Designed in the colours of the team - black, white, and red - by renowned tartanist David McGill of International Tartans Ltd, this fabric celebrates the rich heritage of Newcastle and its people. Recognised as an authentic representation of the district by Councillor Diane Parkham, Lord Mayor of Newcastle, the tartan is a badge of honour for anyone from or associated with this iconic city. Due to copyright restrictions, permission must be obtained from David McGill of International Tartans before use, ensuring that this unique and meaningful design remains true to its roots and the spirit of the Toon Army.

name: McGill (David) personal; Norwegian Centenary
description: The Norwegian Centennial tartan is a poignant tribute to the nation's storied history, commissioned by Mr Arne Silvertsin, the Norwegian Consul General, to commemorate the centenary of Norway's establishment in 1905. This District tartan, registered in honour of Norwegians worldwide and those with a connection to the country, is a rich tapestry woven from deep reds and blues, evoking the rugged Scandinavian landscape and the nation's proud heritage. Designed by David McGill of International Tartans, this distinctive tartan holds significance for those who proudly claim Norwegian ancestry or have a special affinity for the land of fjords and midnight sun. With restrictions in place, allowing only those with the designer's consent to wear it, this tartan is a treasured symbol of identity and tradition, steeped in the rich cultural heritage of Norway.

name: McGill (David) personal; Renfrewshire District
description: The Renfrewshire tartan, named after the historic county in West Central Scotland, is a distinctive fashion tartan that pays homage to the region's rich heritage. Designed by David McGill and registered by International Tartans Ltd, this iconic pattern has been reserved for those with the designer's consent, reflecting its exclusive nature. Though not officially recognised as the Renfrewshire tartan, it remains an authentic representation of the county's identity and traditions. Woven with precision, this tartan features a rich blend of blues and greens that evoke the rolling hills and rugged coastline of western Scotland, evoking feelings of nostalgia and connection to the land and its people. Its significance extends beyond mere aesthetics, serving as a symbol of regional pride and affinity for those from or associated with Renfrewshire.

name: McGill (David) personal; Rosslyn Chapel
description: The Rosslyn Chapel tartan is a breathtaking tribute to Scotland's rich heritage, commissioned by the esteemed Rosslyn Chapel Trust in collaboration with renowned designer David McGill of International Tartans. As a corporate tartan, it has been created for business and organisational use, yet its significance extends far beyond its functional purpose. Inspired by the intricate stone carvings and mysterious symbolism of the iconic chapel itself, this tartan design weaves together a rich tapestry of Scottish tradition and mystique. Originally registered in honour of Mr Stuart Beattie, Chief Executive of the Rosslyn Chapel Trust, the tartan is now available for use with the designer's consent, offering those who wear it a connection to this revered piece of Scotland's cultural fabric.

name: McGill (David) personal; West Lothian
description: The West Lothian tartan is a storied fabric born from the rich heritage of Scotland's 'Book Town' – Linlithgow, now known as part of West Lothian. This fashion tartan, woven with precision by renowned designer David McGill and International Tartans Ltd, pays homage to the county's proud history. Though not officially sanctioned as the West Lothian tartan, its registration notes proudly declare it for use by anyone from or associated with this historic region. Worn with honour, this tartan represents a strong connection to the land and its storied past – perfect for those who wear their heritage on their sleeve. With restrictions in place, only those with the designer's consent may don this iconic design, underscoring the importance of preserving cultural traditions and respecting the community's legacy.

name: McMain
description: The Meanwood McMain tartan is a unique and meaningful blend of heritage and personal affection, born from a heartwarming gesture by Maxine Scott, House of Tartan's esteemed designer. Commissioned as a gift for Dr McMain, a long-standing member of the Leeds-based Meanwood Group Practice, this tartan represents the special bond between colleagues and community. The personal significance of its creation is palpable, reflecting the dedication and camaraderie that defined 16 years of service in Leeds, ultimately marking a new chapter in Australia. As a Name tartan, the Meanwood McMain is an expression of individuality, imbued with the values of trust, loyalty, and friendship that have been passed down through generations, weaving a rich tapestry of Scottish heritage and contemporary connection.

name: Me to You
description: The Me to You tartan is a vibrant and endearing design that evokes the warmth and affectionate spirit of Scotland's beloved teddy bears. This Corporate tartan was specifically created for a iconic children's brand, showcasing its practicality and appeal to businesses seeking distinctive branding. The Me to You tartan's unique pattern, though not attributed to a traditional Scottish clan or heritage, is deeply rooted in British culture, reflecting the country's rich tradition of textile craftsmanship. In registration notes, it is noted that this tartan was designed for clothing marketed under the 'Me to You' brand by Carte Blanche Greetings Ltd of Chichester, West Sussex, highlighting its status as a modern, commercially inspired tartan.

name: Meath Irish County
description: The Meath, County tartan is a rich and storied District tartan, expertly woven by Polly Wittering for House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Originally designed for the esteemed Macnaughton family of Pitlochry, this tartan collection embodies the traditions of Irish trade and heritage. While not officially sanctioned as a District tartan at the time of registration, its popularity has since proven its legitimacy, paving the way for its potential recognition within the Scottish Tartans Authority's formal classification. As part of the Johnston Collection, the Meath, County tartan now takes its rightful place among Ireland's esteemed textiles, evoking the history and craftsmanship that underpin these iconic patterns.

name: Meeting Professionals
description: The Meeting Professionals International (MPI) Corporate Tartan, registered to Kinloch Anderson Ltd, proudly represents the global community of meeting professionals at its core. Originally designed for the 2004 conference held in Edinburgh, this unique corporate tartan was brought together by Historic Scotland and MPI to promote unity among industry leaders. As the world's largest association of meeting professionals, MPI's identity is woven into the very fabric of this distinctive design, reflecting its international reach and Texas-based roots. However, with control over its use comes a responsibility for those who wear or display it, ensuring its dignified representation in accordance with the MPI's guidelines. This striking tartan embodies the intersection of Scottish heritage and modern corporate identity, making it an iconic symbol for the meeting professionals who wear it with pride.

name:
Mehrtens #2
[AKA] Clifton's fancy
description: This unique and exclusive Mehrtens variant tartan is a true reflection of Scottish heritage and tradition. Designed by renowned Matthew Newsome in collaboration with Clifton Mehrtens, the tartan holds significant personal importance, having been created as a variation from the original Mehrtens tartan due to an error in thread count during its initial production run by D.C. Dalgliesh. This distinctive design was preferred by Mehrtens himself, and thus became the fabric for his personal kilt. As a 'Name' category tartan, this unique variant bears the Mehrtens family name, allowing wearers to proudly showcase their heritage and affiliation with this distinguished clan. The registration notes highlight the intricacies of its creation, underscoring the skill and attention to detail that goes into crafting each tartan.

name: Mehrtens
description: The Mehrtens personal tartan is a poignant tribute to the American heritage of Clifton Mehrtens, whose ancestors hail from Hanover, Germany. Designed by Matthew Newsome, a renowned expert in traditional Scottish weaving, this unique tartan weaves together the rich history and cultural traditions of its namesake's homeland with his connection to the United States during the American Civil War. The registration notes reveal that 13 out of 14 Mehrtens found in the US Census at the time fought for the Confederacy, underscoring the significance of this tartan as a symbol of family legacy and loyalty. With its distinctive colours, which evoke the Hanover Arms, German flag, and Confederate States of America, the Mehrtens personal tartan is a powerful representation of cultural heritage and tradition, honouring both the Mehrtens' ancestral roots and their commitment to their country's history.

name: Melange
description: Melange, a fashion tartan born from the innovative spirit of Highland Queen, embodies the dynamic fusion of traditional Scottish heritage with modern flair. Registered in 1972 by Highland Queen Sportswear of Toronto, Melange exemplifies the intersection of culture and fashion, its very name 'melange' evoking the French concept of blending disparate elements to create something new and striking. This stylish tartan is a testament to the enduring influence of Scottish heritage on global fashion, its sporty-chic aesthetic making it a versatile choice for those seeking to add a touch of Scottish flair to their wardrobe.

name: Melieres #2
description: The Melieres, Michel tartan is a captivating Name tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of Scottish tradition. Designed by French-born Michele Melieres in 1966, this distinctive tartan was woven for his wedding celebration at Dunblane Cathedral, symbolising a union that bridged cultures and countries. A unique blend of influences, the tartan's intricate patterns reflect Melieres' time spent in Scotland, where he assisted the Tartan Information Centre during his stay. The two setts registered under reference #1168 and #1171 form an integral part of this distinctive Name tartan, which has become a cherished emblem of family identity and heritage for those who wear it, carrying with it the story of a lasting love and connection to Scotland's timeless traditions.

name: Melieres
description: The Melieres, Carolyn tartan is a personal design created by Michel Melières, a renowned Scottish textile artist, in honour of his ancestral home in the Scottish Borders. This Name tartan holds significant cultural value, representing a family's connection to their heritage. The distinctive eight-needle pattern weaves together a palette of deep blues and emerald greens, echoing the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of Scotland's rural past. While this tartan may not be registered for commercial use due to its personal nature (restricted by registration notes), it serves as a poignant reminder of the importance of preserving family traditions and cultural identity. As a testament to Melières' skillful craftsmanship, the Melieres, Carolyn tartan embodies the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage and tradition, inviting wearers to connect with their roots and celebrate their unique place within the country's rich tapestry.

name: Melrose of Alabama
description: The Melrose of Alabama tartan is a unique fusion of Scottish heritage and American flair, borne out of an intriguing collaboration between the esteemed House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., and Polly Wittering, its talented designer. Registered as a Corporate tartan, this vibrant pattern was specifically created for a trade association from Alabama, USA, reflecting the melting pot of cultures that have shaped America's identity. With its bold and striking colours, this tartan embodies the spirit of innovation and unity, blending the timeless traditions of Scottish weaving with the entrepreneurial zeal of the American South. As a symbol of cross-cultural exchange and commercial endeavour, the Melrose of Alabama tartan proudly wears its heritage on its sleeve, telling a story of international collaboration and shared values.

name: Melrose
description: The Melrose tartan is a storied District pattern, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's historic towns and villages. Registered by esteemed weavers at Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan holds great honour and significance as it has been specially commissioned for promotional purposes and as a gift to Her Majesty the Queen during her spring visit to Melrose in 2002, a fitting tribute to mark the Queen's Jubilee Celebrations in Scotland. Supported by local community councils and traders' associations, this District tartan is deeply rooted in the traditions of the town, evoking the rolling hills and picturesque charm that has captivated visitors for centuries. Its creation serves as a testament to the enduring spirit of Melrose, weaving together past, present, and future in a vibrant celebration of Scottish identity.

name:
Melville #2 depr
[AKA] #2
description: The Melville tartan, registered by Lochcarron of Scotland, is a quintessential representation of Scottish heritage and tradition. This distinctive Clan/Family tartan features two black lines woven into its majestic blue fabric, creating an unmistakable visual identity that echoes the rich history of the Melville family. With roots dating back to 1824, this ancient sett has been meticulously recorded in various archives, including the Scottish Tartans Society's collection and the esteemed Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority. While differing references may note varying shades of blue, the essence of this tartan remains unchanged - a testament to its enduring significance as an emblem of family pride and Scottish legacy.

name: Melville [default]
description: The Melville tartan, registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn, holds a revered place within Scotland's rich heritage of clan tartans. This storied sett, also known as Oliphant and Melville, has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition since 1824, when it was first mentioned in a letter to the historian John MacPherson. Now, preserved in esteemed collections such as the Moy Hall collection and the Scott Adie (London) collection, this tartan bears testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's clans and families. With its distinctive single black line on the blue, this set is an authentic representation of the traditional tartans that have been woven into the very heart of Scottish identity, reflecting the intricate history and cultural significance of the Melville clan.

name: Menez Du
description: Menez Du, named after the rugged mountain range in the heart of Brittany, embodies the unyielding spirit of the region's storied history. This District tartan, designed by Richard Duclos of La Maison du Kilt, Paris, is a testament to the bravery and resilience of those who have called Menez Du home. With its unique, complex pattern reflecting the unforgiving yet breathtaking beauty of Brittany's terrain, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the region's rich cultural heritage. Its very existence honours the district's storied past, where mountainous landscapes and fierce traditions once proved an imposing barrier to outsiders. As such, Menez Du holds a special place in the hearts of those who cherish their Breton roots, offering a tangible link to the land, its people, and their enduring legacy.

name: Mens Bigi
description: The Lochcarron of Scotland's "Mens Bigi" corporate tartan is a stylish and professional choice for business attire, embodying the very spirit of Scottish enterprise and enterprise. This distinctive design, registered in the company's stable of iconic patterns, boasts a rich, dark blue ground, punctuated by intricate blocks of red, green, yellow, black, white, and grey. With its bold, graphic appearance, "Mens Bigi" is perfectly suited to corporate wear, exuding confidence and authority without ever feeling too formal or stuffy. As a registered tartan, it carries the weight of tradition and heritage, its very existence a testament to Scotland's rich weaving history, while its modern application speaks to the enduring appeal of Scottish design in the contemporary business world.

name: Mensah
description: The Mensah tartan, registered as a Clan/Family tartan, is a rich and intricate pattern steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Its origins are shrouded in mystery, with no known designer credited for its creation, but it is believed to have been first woven by D C Dalgliesh of Selkirk in the corporate context. This enigmatic tartan tells the story of a family's history and legacy, its complex interplay of colours evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish landscape. With its precise weaving and symmetrical design, the Mensah tartan exudes honour and tradition, a testament to the enduring power of Scotland's clan system and the bonds that unite families across generations. Its subtle nuances hint at a storied past, inviting wearers to connect with their ancestral heritage and wear their family's history on their sleeve.

name: Menteith District
description: The Menteith tartan is a stunning example of Scotland's rich textile heritage, woven from the very fabric of its history and culture. Registered as a District Tartan, it bears the name of the historic district situated in the upper reaches of the River Forth, where the rugged landscape meets the gentle flow of the water. This unique design, rescued from obscurity by Graeme Menteith in 1941, boasts distinct proportions and a subtle twist on traditional sett patterns, its azure overcheck replaced by a crisp white stripe. The tartan's connection to the Graham of Menthonett sett recorded by Logan in 1831 is evident, yet it proudly stands apart with its own identity, evoking the proud spirit of Scotland's ancient clans and their storied pasts.

name: Menzies Brown & White
description: The Menzies Brown & White tartan, a fashion favourite among those who value traditional yet stylish flair, boasts a rich heritage rooted in Scotland's storied past. This elegant design, with its distinctive brown and white hues, is a testament to the country's enduring cultural identity. As a fashion tartan, it has been adopted by many for its versatility and adaptability, making it an excellent choice for clothing, accessories, or home textiles that embody a sense of classic British charm. Although the designer behind this iconic pattern remains unknown, its presence in esteemed collections such as those from Scott Bros & Co Hawick and Patons, alongside its inclusion in the Scottish Tartans Society archive, speaks to its enduring significance within Scottish tradition, making it a cherished choice for those seeking to connect with their heritage through timeless style.

name:
Menzies Dress; Black & Red
[AKA] Menzies Hunting #2
description: The Menzies Hunting tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's esteemed clan families. Woven with a deep respect for tradition, this timeless sett has been passed down through generations, its distinctive red and black hues evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. Originally recorded by D.W. Stewart in his seminal work 'Old and Rare Scottish Tartans' in 1893, this tartan's authenticity is undeniable, having undergone official registration from the esteemed W & A K Johnston in 1906. As a Clan tartan, it holds significant honour within Scottish families, such as Menzies, who have proudly worn their ancestral heritage on their sleeves – or rather, on their kilt and other traditional attire.

name: Menzies Dress Dance; Black & White
description: The Menzies tartan, registered in 1938, is a poignant family legacy steeped in Scottish heritage. Originally created to commemorate a Clan and then adopted as a mourning tartan by its bearers, this intricate design speaks volumes about the emotional depth of Scottish tradition. Woven with meticulous care, the subtle nuances of this tartan reveal the rich cultural heritage of the Menzies clan, whose history is inextricably linked to the Highlands. Although no designer's name is recorded, the expert craftsmanship and attention to detail evident in its design suggest a deep understanding of traditional Scottish weaving techniques. Today, the Menzies tartan remains an important part of Clan tradition, serving as a lasting tribute to the family's enduring legacy and connection to Scotland's storied past.

name: Menzies Dress; Black
