description: The Menzies Black Dress tartan is a rich and timeless representation of Scottish heritage, borne from the ancestral legacy of the Menzies clan. Registered by David C Dalgliesh, a respected weaving firm in Selkirk, this intricate pattern is steeped in tradition and history. Characterised by its predominantly black base, punctuated by subtle dark blue and red hues, the Menzies Black Dress tartan exudes an air of dignity and sophistication. As a Clan tartan, it holds deep significance within Scottish culture, signifying a strong sense of family honour and heritage. This classic design is often worn with pride by those who bear the Menzies name, serving as a tangible connection to their ancestral roots and the storied past of Scotland's most revered clans.

name: Menzies Green & Black
description: Menzies Green, a timeless Clan tartan from Scotland's storied past, tells the tale of a proud and noble family through its intricate pattern. Woven with the precision of traditional Scottish textile artistry, Menzies Green showcases the rich heritage of the MacGregor-Hastie clan, whose history is forever intertwined with the rugged Highlands. The subtle nuances of this tartan design evoke a sense of tradition and loyalty, reflecting the values that have defined Scotland's most esteemed clans for centuries. As part of the Scottish Tartans Society's archive, Menzies Green stands as a testament to the enduring power of Scottish identity, waiting to be woven into the fabric of family histories and clan traditions.

name:
Menzies Hunting
[AKA] Menzies Green
description: The Menzies tartan is a rich and storied pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, hailing from a distinguished clan family. This traditional sett has been woven with great care to showcase its bold colours, carefully balanced between deep reds, emerald greens, and subtle earth tones. Notably, a variation of this design, known as the Green Menzies, features a predominance of green hues, which has been adopted by the Auckland and District Pipe Band, lending further legitimacy to its use. With no designated designer credited, it is clear that this tartan's origins are deeply rooted in family tradition, passed down through generations, while its modern adaptations have cemented its place within Scotland's vibrant cultural landscape.

name:
Menzies of Culdares [default]
[AKA] Menzies of Culdares
description: The Menzies of Culdares tartan is an enigmatic and storied pattern, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. This unique design, 'Other' by classification, is believed to have originated from a 17th-century portrait of the original Menzies of Culdares, whose family crest may still be visible upon it. Acquired through Peter MacDonald's painstaking extraction from this ancient image, the tartan now bears witness to the rich history and legacy of Clan Menzies. Although the designer's identity remains unknown, it is clear that their vision has captured the essence of a bygone era, evoking the grandeur of Scotland's storied past and the enduring honour of its noble clans.

name: Menzies Red & White
description: The Menzies tartan, registered in 1815, embodies the rich heritage and storied history of the Scottish clans. Originally recorded under the erroneous name MacFarlane, its true identity was later confirmed by the clan chief in a collection of the Highland Society of London, solidifying its place within the family's legacy. This distinctive tartan, woven from a palette of earthy greens, dramatic blacks, fiery reds, and crisp whites, is steeped in tradition and significance. As part of the Clan/Family category, it holds a special place among those tied to Scottish heritage, its very existence a testament to the intricate relationships between kinship, identity, and cultural heritage.

name: Meoni [default]
description: The Meoni tartan, designed by Claire Donaldson of the esteemed House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., is a personal and family-centric motif woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds great significance for those who bear its name, symbolising unity, loyalty, and tradition. Woven with love and care, this tartan was originally created to adorn attire at a wedding celebration, underscoring the importance of family ties in Scottish culture. Although restricted to designated wearers, the Meoni tartan remains a treasured representation of ancestral heritage, its intricate patterns and rich colours evoking a sense of pride and belonging among those who have had it registered.

name: Mercer, UK (Personal)
description: The Mercer, James tartan is a rich and storied textile that embodies the heritage of Scotland's noble families. Registered in recognition of those with the name by James G.B. Mercer, whose family ties run deep to Musselburgh, this tartan is a testament to the proud traditions of Scottish clan history. A beautifully crafted design, expertly woven by Geoffrey at Highland Crafts Limited, it bears witness to the enduring legacy of the Mercer name and its connections to Scotland's north-east. As a Name tartan, its significance lies in its association with an individual or family lineage, imbuing each wearer with a sense of belonging to a storied past, and allowing them to proudly display their heritage through this timeless and evocative tartan.

name: Mercer, USA (Personal)
description: The Mercer, Charles tartan is a proud representation of the esteemed Mercer family legacy, originating from Dr Philip D Smith's innovative design for Charles Mercer of Rocky Mount, North Carolina. This Category 'Name' tartan holds significant cultural heritage, signifying affiliation with those who share the Mercer surname, allowing its wearers to honour their ancestral roots. Notably, this tartan was registered at TECA, a prestigious governing body responsible for preserving Scotland's rich tartan traditions. While originally designed exclusively for Charles Mercer, the design has since been adopted by another member of the family, James G B Mercer from Musselburgh, Scotland, further solidifying its connection to the Scottish heritage and cementing its place in the annals of tartan history.

name: Merchiston Castle School Pipe Band
description: The Merchiston Castle School Pipe Band tartan is a vibrant and richly symbolic corporate design that proudly represents its namesake institution's Scottish heritage. Inspired by the historic Napier tartan, which pays homage to the 18th-century family who founded the school in the 1830s, this tartan features a bold, bold blue background with intricate golden threads woven throughout. The distinctive addition of an extra red line adds depth and character to the design, echoing the city's industrial past. Kinloch Anderson Ltd's skilled designers have masterfully reinterpreted traditional Scottish textile traditions to create a unique and prestigious corporate identity that embodies the values of excellence and tradition that Merchiston Castle School is renowned for.

name: Merchiston Castle School
description: The Merchiston Castle School tartan is a masterful reimagining of the historic Napier tartan, expertly adapted by Kinloch Anderson Ltd for corporate use. Originally inspired by the Napier family's ancestral home, now part of Napier college, this tartan pays homage to the school's rich heritage. The traditional sett remains largely intact, with subtle modifications that reflect the school's colours: a majestic royal blue, navy blue, and vibrant scarlet. By subtly altering the hues from its Napier roots, the Merchiston Castle School tartan proudly wears the mantle of its esteemed namesake institution. As a testament to Scottish tradition and heritage, this tartan is both a celebration of history and a forward-thinking symbol for corporate identity.

name: Meredith of Wales
description: The Meredith of Wales tartan is a unique and fascinating blend of heritage and modern popularity, born from the Welsh tradition and carefully crafted by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill. Originally introduced to promote Welsh identity through the establishment of Wales Tartan Centres in 1998, this tartan has since captured the hearts of many with its distinctive thread count and colourful design. While not rooted in historical genealogy, the 'of Wales' designation serves as a proud identifier of its origins, setting it apart from other Celtic tartans that predominantly employ odd-numbered threads. A striking feature of this tartan is the unusual warp and weft composition, featuring different numbers of threads and colours. As with many modern tartans, the Meredith of Wales requires consent for weaving, underscoring the importance of respecting cultural heritage and tradition.

name: Merrilees Dress
description: The Merrilees Dress, a traditional Clan tartan with a twist, is a testament to the ingenuity of Scottish textile heritage. Originally registered in its inverted form by Dalgliesh, D C in [year], this distinctive design has been prepared for weaving by the esteemed D C Dalgliesh Ltd. The Merrilees tartan, once a proud representation of a noble Clan, now boasts an inversion of its original black and white hues, rendering it a unique variation that pays homage to its storied past while introducing a fresh perspective. As with many historic Clan tartans, the Merrilees Dress holds significant cultural and family significance, evoking memories of heritage, tradition, and community. Its intricate pattern, carefully crafted by skilled weavers, serves as a celebration of Scotland's rich textile history, where artistry and heritage blend seamlessly together.

name: Merrilees [default]
description: The Merrilees tartan, designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1829, is a storied family tradition that has evolved from its origins as 'Meg Merrilies', a fashion tartan inspired by Sir Walter Scott's literary character. Originally woven to evoke the spirit of a gypsy lass, this distinctive tartan eventually came to be associated with the Merrilees surname, a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage. Today, Merrilees families worldwide proudly wear their tartan, often in modern variations that have been updated by esteemed weavers like D.C. Dalgliesh of Selkirk. As a Clan tartan, the Merrilees bears witness to the rich history and cultural significance of Scotland's textile traditions, its intricate patterns and colours evoking the warmth and hospitality of a bygone era.

name: Merwe [default]
description: The Merwe tartan is a storied heritage pattern, born out of the rich cultural tapestry of South Africa's Dutch settlers in the 1700s. Originally designed for Hendrik A Van der Merwe and his family, who migrated from South Holland, this distinctive tartan has become a symbol of unity and tradition for those bearing the name. With its unique blend of colours, carefully woven to reflect the family's roots, the Merwe tartan is a testament to the power of identity and community in shaping Scottish heritage. While it originated as a specific clan tartan, its use is now open to others sharing the Van der Merwe surname, allowing the pattern to transcend generations and geographical boundaries, connecting those who wear it to a shared history and cultural legacy.

name: Metcalf [default]
description: The Metcalf tartan is a rich and storied family heritage, its origins shrouded in history and tradition. Registered with the Tartans Register Office as a Clan tartan, this distinctive pattern is believed to have been brought from Scotland over 100 years ago by Mrs James Shoemaker's great-grandmother, who claimed it had been passed down through generations of her family. The design features a complex sett count, halved to facilitate easy counting, and its technical construction is rooted in traditional Scottish weaving methods. As such, the Metcalf tartan holds great significance for those connected to this noble Clan heritage, serving as a tangible link to Scotland's rich cultural past and a proud symbol of family honour.

name: Methodist Church
description: The Methodist Church tartan, designed by Claire Hunter in collaboration with House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., is a vibrant corporate tartan that proudly represents the enduring legacy of Scotland's Methodism heritage. With no explicit design rationale provided, it's clear that this tartan was created to evoke a sense of community and shared values within the Methodist movement. Its bold colours and subtle patterns pay homage to traditional Scottish tartans while adapting them for modern corporate wear. As such, it is reserved exclusively for use by those who bear the name "Methodist Church", serving as a visual representation of their connection to this rich history and tradition.

name: Mica Green
description: Mica Green, a vibrant and dynamic fashion tartan, embodies the warmth and vibrancy of Scotland's natural landscapes. Created by the esteemed Edinburgh Woollen Mill, this stunning design is a perfect representation of the UK's textile heritage. As a Fashion tartan, Mica Green has been carefully crafted to make a statement on the catwalk or in everyday life, its striking colours evoking the lush green hues of the Scottish countryside. With no restrictions on use, Mica Green can be freely worn and enjoyed by anyone looking to add a touch of authentic Scottish style to their wardrobe, making it an ideal choice for fashion enthusiasts and tartan aficionados alike, ensuring that this beautiful design continues to inspire and delight for generations to come.

name: Michael
description: The Michael from Appin tartan is a deeply personal and historically significant pattern, created with love by Michael III, John F, for the esteemed Col. Michael's family. This Name tartan, registered through the Celtic Craft Centre in Edinburgh, has been woven to honour the descendants of Daniel Carmichael from Appin, a Scottish settler who emigrated to America in 1773. The intricate design, now preserved in the Scottish Tartans Authority's collection, tells the story of this remarkable family's heritage, connecting them to their ancestral roots in Scotland and their bravery as pioneers in the New World. This personal tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Carmichael family, its meaning and significance woven into every thread of the fabric, a tangible link to their rich history and cultural traditions.

name: Michaluk
description: Michaluk is a deeply personal tartan, woven with precision and passion by renowned tailor Geoffrey Highland Crafts. Designed specifically for families bearing the esteemed surname of Michaluk, this intricate fabric tells the story of a noble heritage and enduring traditions. Though restrictions have been placed upon its use to ensure exclusivity for those who bear the Michaluk name, the tartan's significance extends far beyond mere family ties, representing instead a testament to Scottish craftsmanship and the unwavering pride of clan identity. Its unique threadwork and subtle nuances evoke the rugged beauty of the Highlands, where the very earth itself seems woven into the fabric of this ancestral tartan.

name: Michigan State
description: The Michigan State tartan, designed by Kati R. Meek, is a vibrant tribute to the Great Lakes State's natural beauty and rich heritage. As a District tartan, it pays homage to the region's unique identity, distinguishing it from other tartans that represent Scottish clans or family lines. The colours, carefully chosen by Meek to reflect the Michigan landscape, evoke the warmth of autumn leaves, the softness of lake shore mist, and the rugged grandeur of the Upper Peninsula's wilderness. Adopted as official "State of Michigan" tartan in 2010, this unique design serves as a symbol of pride for Michiganders around the world, celebrating the state's storied history, scenic charm, and the skillful craftsmanship of its weavers, including Meek herself.

name: Michigan State Police
description: The Michigan State Police tartan is a bold and vibrant representation of corporate heritage, carefully crafted to reflect the esteemed tradition of law enforcement excellence in the Great Lakes State. Designed by Kevin Streeter with meticulous attention to detail, this unique blend of colours was originally woven at Lochcarron, drawing upon ancient Scottish weaving techniques to bring this modern design to life. With its distinctive hues and bold patterns, the Michigan State Police tartan is a celebration of unity and service, paying tribute to the courageous men and women who serve with distinction in the Michigan State Police. Its corporate roots add an air of professionalism and authority, making it an ideal choice for organisations and individuals alike seeking to embody the values of this storied institution.

name: Michigan State University
description: The Michigan State University tartan is a vibrant tribute to the storied history of one of America's most esteemed institutions. Registered as a corporate tartan, its purpose is to represent the university with pride and distinction in business and professional settings. Designed by renowned weaver Alex Parsons, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the university's 150th anniversary milestone, marking a significant chapter in the enduring legacy of Michigan State University. With its unique colour palette and carefully crafted design, the Michigan State University tartan embodies the spirit of innovation, scholarship, and community that define this iconic American university, offering a bold symbol of affiliation for its supporters and alumni alike.

name: Micron
description: The Micron tartan is a modern corporate design with a distinctly Scottish flavour, created for the esteemed Micron Europe Limited of East Kilbride, Scotland. This dynamic pattern, which has been woven in accordance with traditional techniques, boasts a bold colour palette featuring thread counts of blue, white, yellow, and black, carefully balanced to evoke a sense of energy and sophistication. With pivots at the ends and full counts throughout, this tartan is perfect for corporate wear, conveying professionalism and respectability. As part of Micron Europe's launch celebration, this tartan will be featured on kilted kilts, ties, sashes, waistcoats, shirts, and other stylish accessories, subtly yet unmistakably proclaiming the company's Scottish heritage and commitment to quality, a fitting tribute to the rich tapestry of Scotland's cultural traditions.

name: Middleton [default]
description: The Middleton tartan is an ancient and storied design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's clans. Specifically designated as a Clan tartan, it holds honour within the family of MacDonalds, a prominent Highland clan. Originally registered from the late 19th century by W & A K Johnston, this tartan is closely tied to its cousin design, Applecross, and shares similarities with the MacDonald of Sleat tartan. The Middleton tartan's significance extends beyond its technical characteristics, for it represents a tangible connection to Scotland's proud past, woven into the very fabric of the nation's cultural identity. Its presence in prestigious collections such as those held by the Scottish Tartans Authority underscores its enduring place within the country's traditional weaving heritage.

name: Middleton City
description: The Middleton, City of tartan is a unique and evocative design that embodies the rich history and heritage of Wisconsin's Middleton city, with its roots in North Carolina's Tartans Museum. Created by Barbara Schaffer, this District tartan weaves together a fascinating narrative of industry, commerce, and community, reflecting the city's significant industries such as lead mining, railroading, peat extraction, and the Great Middleton Fire of 1900. The striking grey and black hues evoke the rugged landscape of the region, while the brown tones hint at the peat extraction that once sustained the area. The distinctive red lines represent the devastating fire that shaped the city's identity, and the red and white stripes pay tribute to Middleton High School. As a testament to Schaffer's ingenuity, this tartan design has remained largely untouched since its creation in 1972, waiting for the day when it may be woven into reality – a fitting tribute to the enduring spirit of American cities and their people.

name: Millennium Langholm
description: The Millennium tartan, created by renowned designer P.A. Keeney in collaboration with esteemed manufacturer Arther Bell, is a striking corporate design that embodies the modern spirit of Scotland. With its bold, predominantly blue tone, this tartan is a testament to the nation's rich heritage and innovative flair. As a Corporate tartan, it is designed for use by companies and organisations seeking to project a sense of unity and professionalism. Registration notes confirm Keeney's skillful hand in crafting this distinctive design, which falls under no restrictions, allowing its use to be shared freely across various sectors. This modern classic not only pays homage to Scotland's storied past but also looks towards the future with elegance and sophistication, making it an ideal choice for businesses looking to add a touch of Scottish flair to their branding.

name: Miller [default]
description: The Miller tartan is a quintessential Scottish clan pattern that has been woven into the very fabric of family heritage for generations. Registered in 1998, it was originally designed specifically for Mr. Don Miller, but its rich history now belongs to all who bear the name. This timeless design showcases the intricate skills of traditional weaving, with its subtle colour gradations and precise sett pattern creating a visually striking effect. As a Clan tartan, the Miller features an unmistakable identity that is both a badge of honour and a proud representation of Scottish heritage, evoking memories of ancient traditions, clan gatherings, and generations of family ties.

name: Milligan
description: The Milligan tartan is a vibrant and elegant fashion tartan, carefully crafted by renowned designer Scotch Corner to commemorate a cherished Irish heritage name. This stunning pattern, one of a series designed by Scotch Corner, pays homage to the rich cultural traditions of Ireland. With its intricate interplay of blues, greens, and reds, the Milligan tartan evokes the rolling hills and misty landscapes of the Emerald Isle. As a fashion tartan, it is free from clan or surname restrictions, inviting wearers to proudly showcase their individuality and connection to this captivating heritage. When worn with pride, the Milligan tartan serves as a beautiful symbol of Scotland's historical ties to Ireland and its enduring legacy in the world of fashion.

name: Mills (Botany) personal; Washington Stockman
description: The Washington Stockmen's tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan with a rich history, born from an unlikely collaboration between American stockmen and a Scottish textile designer. Registered in recognition of its use by various stockmen's associations in the US, this tartan pays tribute to the pioneering spirit of these men, who were instrumental in shaping the agricultural industry in North America. Charles F.H. Johnston designed the pattern, which features a unique blend of blues and greens that evoke the rolling hills and vast open spaces of rural America. While its origins may have been obscured by time, this tartan remains an important symbol of American heritage and tradition, reflecting the cultural exchange and cross-pollination that has shaped the world of tartans.

name: Milne (Michael) personal
description: This poignant Name tartan, Milne of Corstorphine #2, is a heartfelt tribute to Michael Milne's esteemed heritage as the Barony of Corstorphine in Edinburgh. Designed by Brian Wilton, this distinctive tartan weaves together rich symbolism from Scottish tradition and Australian identity. Navy blue and gold, the colours of Mr Milne's family racing favourites, are expertly interwoven with emerald green, a nod to Australia's national hues. The result is a unique and meaningful design that honourably reflects the Milne family's proud ancestry and their distinctive cultural fusion. This personal tartan serves as a poignant reminder of family legacy and national pride, perfectly capturing the essence of Mr Milne's dual heritage.

name: Milne
description: The Milne tartan, with its distinctive blend of vibrant hues, holds a special place in the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage. Originally reserved for the personal use of an individual from the esteemed Milne family, now famously associated with the Gordons and Ogilvys, this tartan was initially shrouded in mystery, only to resurface as a 'dancer's fancy' in the 1990s. Its creation by renowned designer Dalgliesh, D.C is a testament to the artisanal skill of traditional Scottish weaving. While some restrictions have been placed on its commercial use, ensuring its integrity remains intact, this tartan now proudly wears its family name, symbolising the enduring legacy and connection to the Milne clan's history in Canada.

name: Milton
description: The historic Milton tartan is a timeless and captivating Name tartan, rich in cultural heritage and steeped in tradition. Its design, though not attributed to a specific designer, is nonetheless a masterful representation of Scotland's enduring textile legacy. The Milton tartan, registered as a Name tartan, was likely woven with the intention of bearing its owner's family crest or surname. With its distinctive blue and green hues, this traditional tartan weaves an evocative narrative of Scottish identity and community. While the registration notes remain silent on the matter, it is clear that the Milton tartan holds a special place in the hearts of those who wear it with honour, connecting them to generations of Scots who have worn their tartans with pride throughout history.

name: Mina Perhonen
description: The Mina Perhonen tartan, created by esteemed designer Fiona Hall of Lochcarron, embodies the harmonious fusion of Scottish heritage and corporate identity. This unique corporate tartan was designed specifically for the Mina Company of Tokyo, a Japanese firm with a global presence, whose distinctive butterfly logo serves as inspiration. The subtle palette, comprising blues reminiscent of a serene sky, sunny yellow evoking the vibrant wings of the butterfly, and crisp white clouds, pays homage to Finland's cultural connection and Japan's affinity for Scandinavian design. As the Finnish word 'Perhonen' – meaning 'butterfly' – is cleverly woven into the tartan's narrative, it highlights the designer's thoughtfulness in crafting a meaningful and distinctive visual identity that not only reflects the company's values but also celebrates cross-cultural exchange and collaboration.

name: Mingulay
description: Mingulay, a captivating Fashion tartan, weaves together threads of Scottish heritage with the rugged beauty of its eponymous namesake island in the Outer Hebrides. This distinctive design, now immortalised on fabrics for fashion enthusiasts to wear, holds sway over the memories of a rowing shanty that echoes across the waves, evoking the sense of community and tradition that defines Scotland's rich cultural tapestry. As its origins lie with a ladies skirt acquired in 1986, Mingulay serves as a poignant reminder of the power of textiles to evoke the essence of place, history, and identity, while its Southernmost location - nestled between Barra Head and Rosinish - imbues it with an air of remoteness and wildness, drawing wearers into a world of timeless Scottish charm.

name: Minnesota Dress
description: This distinctive District tartan, affectionately known as the Minnesota Dress, was designed by Mark Osweiler to commemorate his home state's rich heritage. Originally created in 2007, it holds official status as the State Tartan of Minnesota, a testament to the strong sense of pride and identity that defines this Midwestern American state. As a registered District tartan, its design can be woven by anyone, allowing enthusiasts to wear their affinity for Minnesota on their sleeve - literally! With its unique colour palette, carefully selected by Mark Osweiler, this tartan embodies the spirit of the Land of 10,000 Lakes and the warm welcome that Minnesotans are renowned for. As a celebrated example of American textile heritage, the Minnesota Dress is not only a symbol of state pride but also an exciting opportunity for anyone to connect with the region's vibrant culture and traditions.

name: Minnesota
description: The Minnesota tartan is a distinctive District tartan, carefully crafted to reflect the spirit of the Upper Midwest region it represents. Registered in 2007 by Mark Osweiler, an American designer from St Paul, Minnesota, this tartan was officially commissioned as the State Tartan of Minnesota, a testament to its deep connection to the state's heritage and culture. As such, it is open to anyone who wishes to weave or wear it, though its US copyright does prevent commercial exploitation without permission. This vibrant design embodies the values of warmth, hospitality, and natural beauty that define the region, evoking images of snow-covered forests, sparkling lakes, and friendly communities - a true celebration of Minnesota's unique identity and sense of place.

name: Minnick [default]
description: The Minnick tartan, named after its esteemed designer Muir, is a majestic family tartan steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered for use by members of Clan/Family Minnick, this intricate pattern tells the story of a long-standing lineage of strong characters, bound together by their shared roots and history. The Minnick tartan's complex design features a rich palette of blues, greens, and yellows, expertly woven to evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's rolling hills and heather-covered moors. While not subject to any specific restrictions, adherence to traditional tartan usage guidelines ensures that this timeless pattern is worn with honour and respect, connecting its wearers to generations past and present.

name: Minster
description: The Minster tartan, woven by the renowned Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the elegance and sophistication of Scotland's rich heritage. As a Fashion tartan, it is designed to make a statement on the catwalk or in everyday life, its subtle nuances and muted tones evoking the tranquility of the Scottish countryside. With its distinct sett and subtle colour variations, this intricate design tells the story of traditional Scottish weaving techniques, passed down through generations of skilled weavers. As part of the Johnston Collection, a testament to Scotland's rich tartan heritage, the Minster tartan is steeped in tradition and history, its beauty and significance inspiring a deep sense of honour and pride for those who wear it.

name: Miramichi
description: The Miramichi tartan, with its distinctive threads woven together in harmony, tells the story of Canada's rich cultural heritage through the traditional art of tartan-making. Designed by Winston C Curtis as part of a craft school project, this Corporate tartan was registered with ATS/TECA in 1996 and named after the city of Miramichi in New Brunswick province. Originally paired with the image of Celtic Pipes & Drums, a testament to Canada's strong Scottish roots, this vibrant design evokes the spirit of celebration and community that defines Canadian tradition. With its unique character and historical significance, the Miramichi tartan stands as a tribute to the city and its people, while also paying homage to the enduring legacy of Scotland's timeless textiles.

name: Mirro
description: The Mirror tartan is a bold and striking corporate design, born from the esteemed Tailor Geoffrey Highland Crafts' collaboration with the pioneering Scottish Mirror Newspaper. This distinctive pattern is specifically created to commemorate the newspaper's launch, reflecting its commitment to reflecting the nation's history, culture, and values. As a corporate tartan, it offers an impressive visual identity for businesses and organisations seeking to showcase their Scottish heritage. Characterised by symmetrical threads that evoke the concept of reflection, this tartan design embodies the newspaper's mission to mirror the Scottish people's experiences, traditions, and aspirations. Its sophisticated aesthetic makes it an ideal choice for companies looking to make a lasting impression in the world of business.

name: Mission
description: The Mission tartan is a unique and evocative District design, steeped in the rich heritage of the British Columbian town of the same name. Created by the skilled weavers and spinners at the Mission Weavers and Spinners Guild, this tartan was presented to Mayor Hawes in 1999 as a tribute to the community's history and identity. Although its colours are still awaiting clarification, the design itself embodies the values of the District category: it serves as a visual representation of local pride and solidarity among its bearers. With its rich textures and symbolic motifs, the Mission tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of the town's residents, who draw upon their Scottish roots to forge a distinct sense of place and belonging in this Canadian frontier town.

name: Mississippi
description: The Mississippi tartan, woven with masterful precision by renowned designers Karen Green in association with esteemed weavers Fraser & Kirkbright of Vancouver, Canada, is a vibrant tribute to the heritage of the American state that bears its name. This striking District tartan reflects the region's rich natural beauty and storied history, with dark green evoking the eternal forests and evergreen leaves of Pine, while light green shines bright on the majestic Great Southern Oaks. The Mississippi River's mighty waters are immortalised in deep blue hues, alongside the crimson tones of the state flag, which also commemorate the sacrifices made by its past inhabitants. Soft white and golden yellow weave together to capture the warmth and beauty of the Gulf Coast beaches and the iconic Magnolia flower, creating a truly unique and captivating tartan that embodies the essence of this American region.

name: Miyuki #2
description: The Miyuki, Check Red fashion tartan is a vibrant celebration of Japanese heritage, as registered by designer Satoshi Suzuki in the year 2005. Inspired by traditional Scottish tartans, this modern check pattern features a striking red hue that pays homage to Japan's rich cultural past. The Miyuki, Check Red design serves as a house check for its company centenary, symbolising loyalty and tradition. As a fashion tartan, it is intended for wear in formal and semi-formal settings, making it an ideal choice for those seeking a stylish way to connect with Japanese heritage. With its bold colour and modern twist on traditional Scottish weaving techniques, the Miyuki, Check Red tartan offers a unique fusion of East meets West, blending Japanese elegance with global flair.

name: Miyuki #3
description: The Miyuki, House Check Grey tartan is a stylish and modern fashion creation by renowned designer Satoshi Suzuki, inspired by the rich heritage of Scotland's iconic house check patterns. This distinctive tartan has been carefully crafted for a prestigious company to commemorate their centenary in 2005, a momentous occasion that required a unique and celebratory design. With its subtle variations in weft and warp, the Miyuki House Check Grey tartan offers a fresh take on traditional Scottish textile motifs, blending contemporary flair with timeless elegance. As a fashion tartan, it is suitable for a wide range of occasions, from formal events to everyday wear, allowing the wearer to proudly showcase their cultural affinity while making a stylish statement.

name: Miyuki #4
description: The Miyuki House Check Tan tartan is a fashion icon born out of a celebration of tradition and innovation. Designed by Satoshi Suzuki, this stylish tartan was specifically registered to commemorate the centenary of its company in 2005 - an honour that underscores its importance as a symbol of Japanese heritage and modernity. As a fashion tartan, Miyuki embodies the perfect blend of classic and contemporary flair, with its subtle checks and rich tones evoking the traditional craftsmanship of Scottish textile artistry. With its sleek and sophisticated aesthetic, this tartan is sure to add a touch of modern elegance to any outfit, while paying homage to the enduring spirit of Japanese business and tradition.

name: Miyuki Centenary
description: The Miyuki tartan, Check Ecru Beige, is a captivating fusion of traditional Scottish heritage with modern fashion sensibilities, designed by Satoshi Suzuki. Registered for the company's centenary in 2005, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the House of Miyuki's rich history while embracing the style of the present era. The subtle nuances of its check pattern evoke a sense of understated elegance, reminiscent of Scotland's timeless landscapes and refined traditions. As a Fashion tartan, the Miyuki design is sure to make a statement on the catwalk or in everyday wear, bringing a touch of sophisticated sophistication to any outfit. With its origins rooted in traditional Scottish textile artistry, this modern creation continues to celebrate the enduring spirit of Japanese-Knitted heritage and cultural exchange.

name: MMK 1777;
description: This enigmatic tartan, registered as MMK 1777, is an intriguing relic from Scotland's rich textile heritage. Known only by its cryptic initials, which have been woven into the fabric of history, this tartan defies identification, leaving its origins and cultural significance shrouded in mystery. As a 'Other' category entry, it falls outside the traditional clan or name registrations that typically tell a story of Scottish identity and heritage. Its absence of a specified designer serves as a poignant reminder of the often-unsung stories behind tartan design. Despite the lack of information, this tartan's presence is still significant, its very existence a testament to the creativity and ingenuity of Scotland's weavers in the late 18th century.

name: Modowny
description: The Modowny tartan is a stylish fashion pattern born from the creative vision of renowned designer Dalgliesh, D C. This visually striking tartan was registered for use in the textile industry, with its unique colour palette and repeating pattern intended to make a statement on the catwalk. With its distinctive characteristics and limited availability, the Modowny tartan is now sought after by fashion enthusiasts and collectors alike, each thread woven into a rich tapestry of Scottish heritage and tradition. While specific details about the design's inspiration or meaning are not publicly known, the registered notes hint at a deeper significance, leaving room for interpretation among those who cherish this exclusive tartan pattern as a celebration of British fashion heritage.

name: Moffat #2
description: The Moffat tartan, registered in 1994, is a stylish fashion design born from the Scottish hills. This modern yet traditional weave is the brainchild of Rally-Klad, who cleverly wove together the threads of heritage and innovation to create a unique pattern. Named after the charming town of Moffat, nestled in the heart of Scotland's Borders, this tartan is as much a nod to the region's rich history as it is a bold statement of fashion forward thinking. With its distinctive tone-on-tone sett and subtle colour nuances, the Moffat tartan exudes a sense of effortless elegance, perfect for adding a touch of Scottish flair to any outfit. As a fashion design, it stands as a testament to the enduring appeal of traditional Scottish tartans in modern times, appealing to those who cherish heritage while embracing contemporary style.

name: Moffat District
description: The Moffat tartan, registered in 1950, holds a complex and intriguing history within the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage. Once thought to be a clan or family tartan, its evolution into a district tartan is a testament to the ever-changing nature of tradition. The sett's fractional pattern, as noted by John MacGregor Hastie in the 1930s, bears similarities to the Murray of Tullibardine design, often employed in Border districts during the Jacobite era to symbolise support for the rebellious cause. Despite its uncertain origins, this tartan has become an integral part of Scotland's cultural fabric, with a presence in esteemed archives such as the Scottish Tartans Authority and Society archive. Its adoption by the district of Moffat, now subject to certain restrictions, serves as a poignant reminder of the dynamic relationship between tradition and community identity.

name: Moffat [default]
description: The Moffat tartan, registered in 1984, is a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich heritage and the enduring legacy of the House of Moffat. Commissioned to commemorate Major Francis Moffat's restoration as Chief of the Name and House, this Clan tartan draws inspiration from the storied Douglas family, with whom the Moffats had early connections. Although a variation of Grey Douglas, the Moffat tartan boasts its own unique character, carefully crafted by Scottish tartan experts to reflect the esteemed status of this re-established noble clan. Notably, this design is subject to restrictions, underscoring the significance and responsibility that comes with wielding such a storied heritage. The Lyon count may be in error, but the Moffat tartan's provenance remains strong, bearing testament to the power of tradition and family legacy.

name: Monaghan Irish County
description: The Monaghan, County tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Ireland's storied districts, carefully crafted by Polly Wittering of House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Originally designed for the Macnaughton family of Pitlochry, this traditional trade tartan now proudly represents a lesser-known corner of the Emerald Isle. As one of a series of Irish District tartans, it embodies the spirit of community and industry that defined these historic regions. With its unique colour palette and intricate weaving, this tartan pays homage to the region's history and traditions, offering a glimpse into the lives of those who wore it with pride.

name: Monarch Airlines
description: The Monoch Airline tartan, a striking example of corporate identity in Scotland's rich textile heritage, was specifically designed to represent the uniform of the UK Charter carrier. This distinctive tartan, falling under the category of Corporate, was created with the primary purpose of promoting the airline's brand and establishing a sense of unity among its staff. Its unique characteristics make it instantly recognisable as a symbol of professionalism and excellence in the aviation industry. As such, this tartan holds a significant place in Scotland's tradition of weaving, where the careful selection of colours, patterns, and fibre can evoke powerful emotions and associations - in this case, representing the fast-paced world of air travel and the dedication of those who work within it.

name: Monarch of the Glen
description: The Monarch of the Glen tartan is a stunning fashion-inspired design, woven with precision to evoke the majesty of Scotland's wilderness. Registered as a Fashion tartan, it was created by acclaimed designer Claire Donaldson, specifically for House of Edgar's range. This captivating pattern, rich in hues of blue and green, draws inspiration from the rugged beauty of the Scottish glens, where royalty once ruled with authority. Though not tied to a specific Clan or family legacy, its creation showcases Scotland's enduring heritage and love affair with nature. With no restrictions on its use, this tartan invites fashion enthusiasts to don a piece of the wild, romantic spirit that has captivated hearts for centuries.

name: Monarchs Sport
description: The Monarchs tartan is a stately and sophisticated corporate design, aptly named in honour of the British monarchy's rich heritage. Created by renowned textile designer Enid Brown for Gleneagles Golf Developments, this tartan is specifically intended for use in golf clothing and accessories. With its precise and elegant sett, the Monarchs tartan exudes a sense of tradition and refinement, evoking the grandeur of Scotland's storied past. Its use is strictly limited to corporate attire, underscoring its association with formal elegance and professionalism. As the name suggests, this tartan embodies the dignified and majestic qualities of royalty, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to make a stylish and authoritative impression on the golf course or in business settings.

name:
Moncrieffe of Atholl [default]
[AKA] Moncrieffe of Atholl
description: The Moncrieff of Atholl tartan is a storied family heirloom steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Originally woven by an unknown designer, possibly either Perigrine Moncrieffe or his father Dalgliesh, as part of a rebellion against the father's choice, this particular sett - known for its distinctive Dalgliesh weave pattern - has been imbued with a sense of family pride and territorial significance through the addition of 'of Atholl' to its name. With its subtle blue broad bands, reminiscent of Scotland's majestic lochs, this tartan design takes on a character all its own, evoking a history of resilience and independence that echoes the storied past of Clan Moncrieff.

name: Moncrieffe of Atholl #2
description: The Moncrieffe tartan, designed in 1998 by Mony Moncrief, is a unique commemorative pattern that pays tribute to the rich heritage of Scotland's clans. This colour-changing tartan is an adaptation of the Murray of Atholl sett, worn by the clan prior to 1974, and incorporates the R & G colours previously used by Sir Iain Moncrieffe, who adopted the old MacLachlan arrangement by Wilsons. The deliberate variation on a traditional design serves as a nod to the history of tartan-making in Scotland, while also acknowledging the cultural significance of the lands associated with the clan. This commemorative tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish tradition and the creativity of modern-day designers seeking to preserve and celebrate these timeless heritage patterns.

name:
Moncrieffe [default]
[AKA] Moncrieffe MacLachlan
[AKA] No.099
[AKA] Moncrieffe Lachlan
description: The Moncreiffe tartan is a rich and storied design, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. As a Clan/Family tartan, it has been passed down through generations of the esteemed Moncrieffe family, with its origins dating back to the 18th century. The sett was first recorded by Sir Iain Moncrieffe of that Ilk, Chief of the Moncrieffes, in the Lyon Court Books, and later featured in William Wilson & Sons' 1819 Key Pattern Book as Old MacLachlan. Today, this distinctive pattern is worn with honour by members of the Moncrieffe clan and their families, evoking a sense of pride and connection to Scotland's storied past. While its origins may be unclear, one thing is certain - the Moncreiffe tartan remains an enduring symbol of Scottish tradition and heritage.

name: Monica
description: The Monica tartan, designed by renowned weavers at West Coast Woolen Mill, is a stylish and modern fashion tartan that embodies the spirit of contemporary Scotland. As a Fashion tartan, it was created to adorn clothing and accessories with a bold, yet timeless aesthetic. With its unique colour palette and subtle pattern, Monica exudes a sense of effortless elegance, perfect for dressing up or adding a touch of sophistication to everyday wear. Rooted in traditional Scottish heritage, the Monica tartan pays homage to the country's rich weaving history while embracing a fresh, modern approach. Its registration notes may remain undisclosed, but it is clear that this tartan design has captured the hearts and imaginations of fashion enthusiasts, cementing its place as a quintessential example of Scottish textiles' enduring appeal.

name: Monmouth College
description: The Monmouth College tartan, crafted by esteemed designer Lochcarron of Scotland, is a distinctive corporate tartan born from the heritage of a prestigious institution. Registered to represent Monmouth College in Monmouth, Illinois, this unique tartan pays tribute to the American town's connection to Scotland. By virtue of its Corporate category, this tartan embodies the fusion of tradition and modernity, poised for widespread use across business environments and beyond. With Lochcarron's masterful touch, every thread weaves a story of cultural exchange, echoing the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage that inspired its creation.

name:
Montgomery (Vestiarium Scoticum)
[AKA] Montgomery Blue Green
description: The Montgomery tartan is a storied and historic Scottish clan pattern that tells the tale of a noble family's enduring legacy. Registered by Sobieski Stewarts, The in 1829, this iconic tartan has its roots firmly planted in Scotland's rich textile heritage. With a large sett featuring distinct blue threads with a thread count of 60, Montgomery tartan is instantly recognisable and steeped in tradition. This clan tartan's origins are deeply intertwined with the Vestiarum Scoticum book, which laid the groundwork for many Scottish clan patterns, including this one. As recorded by Brian Wilton of the Scottish Tartans Authority, Montgomery tartan has also been featured in Clans Originaux (Montgomerie) and appears alongside Elphinstone in the Scottish Tartans World Register. This majestic pattern continues to hold honour among Scots and enthusiasts alike, symbolising strength, loyalty, and a deep connection to Scotland's storied past.

name: Montgomery Colin
description: The Montgomerie, Colin corporate tartan is a sophisticated and modern design inspired by Scotland's rich heritage in golf, reflecting the esteemed golfer Colin Montgomerie's esteemed status on the professional circuit. Designed by Brian Wilton for the Scottish Tartans Authority, this versatile tartan features a bold palette of grey and black, complemented by Montgomery purple and red hues that evoke a sense of tradition and prestige. Originally commissioned for the golfing community to wear with pride, the Montgomerie, Colin tartan now adds a touch of style and distinction to corporate attire, symbolising excellence and achievement in business and beyond. As an important part of Scotland's cultural fabric, this tartan pays homage to the country's proud sporting heritage, while its modern design ensures it remains relevant and desirable for generations to come.

name: Montgomery, Stuart (Personal)
description: The Montgomery, Stuart tartan is a deeply personal and iconic Scottish heritage design, born from the identity of its namesake, Stuart Montgomery. As a Category Name tartan, it holds a special place in the world of tartan traditions, signifying the family's history, legacy, and cultural affiliation. Recorded as early as 1998, this tartan has been carefully preserved by Phil Smith, who shared his knowledge with the Scottish Tartans Authority in 2003. This distinctive weave tells the story of a proud individual, whose name is now forever linked to the rich tapestry of Scottish clan history. Its unique characteristics and significance serve as a testament to the enduring power of tradition and family heritage, ensuring that Stuart Montgomery's personal tartan will continue to hold honour among those who wear it.

name: Montgomery [default]
description: The Montgomery of Eglinton tartan is a rich and storied example of Scotland's vibrant textile heritage, steeped in history and family tradition. Originally designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn as their No. 7, "Eglinton", this tartan was later adopted by the esteemed Montgomeries of Ayrshire, cementing its place within Scottish clan lore. D.W. Stewart's astute observation suggests that this transition may have occurred around the time of the Union in 1707, lending credence to the notion that this is one of the earliest genuine Lowland tartans in existence. As such, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's complex and often fraught history, while also celebrating the enduring legacy of the Montgomery family's rich heritage.

name: Montmorency
description: The Montmorency tartan is a unique and captivating District design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scottish tradition. Originally created from Mrs K Sinclair's notes, this Canadian-inspired pattern takes its roots from the iconic Black Watch tartan, but with an intriguing twist. The warp threads form a striking contrast to the weft, which cleverly changes tone - where green transitions to brown, and black yields to green. This subtle shift in hues adds a layer of complexity to the overall design, echoing the complexities of Scottish history and culture. As a District tartan, it is deeply rooted in local identity and tradition, inviting wearers to connect with their own heritage through this distinctive and evocative pattern.

name:
Montreal Granate
[AKA] Maroon
description: The Montreal Granate tartan is a vibrant Fashion tartan, meticulously crafted to evoke the spirit of Canadian heritage. With its bold, crimson-toned colours - a rich burgundy, deep scarlet, and goldenrod - this distinctive weave is both striking and sophisticated. Born from a collaboration between Viv Sharpe, renowned Scottish weaver, and Phil Smith, its origins are marked by the registration in 2004. As a Fashion tartan, Montreal Granate is designed to be showcased on garments such as scarves, ties, and kilts, where its eye-catching hues will add a touch of elegance and flair. This tartan's significance lies not only in its beauty, but also in its nod to the cultural exchange between Scotland and Canada, reflecting the shared traditions and values that unite these two nations.

name: Montreal
description: The Montreal tartan, a vibrant and eclectic fashion design, pays homage to the city's rich cultural heritage. Registered in 2004, this distinctive tartan is steeped in tradition, with its unique colour palette and intricate patterns evoking the diversity and energy of Montreal's history as a melting pot of French and British influences. As a fashion tartan, it lends itself perfectly to modern garments and accessories, allowing wearers to showcase their personal style while nodding to the city's storied past. With no specific clan or family affiliation tied to its origins, this versatile design is open to interpretation, embracing individuality and self-expression.

name: Montreat
description: The Montreat tartan is a dynamic corporate design born from the creative synergy between Marge Warren and Polly Wittering, commissioned specifically for Montreat Assembly in North Carolina, USA. This distinctive fabric embodies the community's values and spirit, reflecting the harmonious blend of traditional Scottish heritage with modern American flair. As a Category Corporate tartan, it is designed to foster a sense of unity and cohesion among professionals and organisations alike, evoking feelings of trust, stability, and ambition. While not bound by traditional clan or family ties, this tartan proudly wears its corporate badge, bearing the mark of its distinctive registration notes that pay tribute to its American roots and the visionary designers who brought it into being.

name: Montrose (Alabama) personal
description: The Montrose of Alabama tartan is a poignant tribute to the Scottish heritage of one of the US's most storied clans, transplanted to the heart of America. Registered as a District tartan, it wears its "honour" on its sleeve by proudly representing the 13th of 13 Montrose tartans worldwide, each with its own unique narrative. Crafted by House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this distinctive design embodies the spirit of tradition and community that defines the Montrose name. The specified darker Navy Blue is a deliberate nod to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland, serving as a reminder of the tartan's origins. This vibrant textile weaves together the threads of history, family, and place, creating a truly unique piece that honours the legacy of this iconic clan in the American South.

name: Montrose #2
description: The Montrose (1983) fashion tartan, designed by West Coast Woolen Mill, is a modern interpretation of traditional Scottish heritage. Originally inspired by the City of Vancouver's variation, this distinctive tartan was registered to the Scottish Tartans Authority in 1983 and has since become synonymous with style and sophistication. With its bold, graphic pattern featuring shades of blue, green, and yellow, the Montrose tartan embodies the spirit of urban cool, evoking images of cosmopolitan cities and modern living. As a fashion tartan, it is perfectly suited to contemporary fashion enthusiasts who wish to make a statement through their clothing choices, while also paying homage to Scotland's rich textile traditions.

name: Montrose #3
description: The Montrose (Graham) tartan is a poignant and storied clan tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Originally commissioned by Clan Graham to commemorate the act of kindness shown by Macnaughton towards "The Great Marquis" of Montrose, this tartan tells a powerful story of loyalty and honour. The distinctive black guards to azure line is a deliberate nod to the painting by James Drummond at the National Gallery of Scotland, which depicts Montrose's capture in 1650. The subtle connection between Graham of Montrose and Macnaughton serves as a testament to the enduring bond between Scottish clans, even in times of conflict and adversity. As such, the Montrose (Graham) tartan holds a profound significance for those who wear it, serving not only as a symbol of clan pride but also as a reminder of the values of loyalty, kindness, and generosity that underpin Scottish tradition.

name: Montrose (McNaughton)
description: The Montrose tartan, also known as the Macnaughton variation, is a richly woven tribute to the storied history of Scotland's districts. Registered under the prestigious District category, this distinctive tartan bears the mark of Marcello Castro's creative vision, subtly differing from its namesake counterpart. A testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage, the Montrose tartan pays homage to the region that inspired its design, evoking images of rolling hills and rugged coastline. Its subtle variations, carefully crafted by hand in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, serve as a poignant reminder of the intricate threads that weave together Scotland's complex cultural tapestry.

name: Montrose Football Club
description: The Montrose Football Club tartan is a vibrant corporate pattern that embodies the spirit of Scottish football and community pride. Designed for the esteemed football club, this tartan represents the honour and tradition of Montrose FC, which has been an integral part of Scottish football history since 1889. With its unique blue and red hues, meticulously woven to adhere to traditional standards (including a carefully calibrated red count), this tartan is a testament to the craftsmanship of Scottish textiles. As a Corporate tartan, it is suited for use by the club and its affiliates, making it an attractive choice for those seeking to pay tribute to their football heritage.

name: Moon [default]
description: The Moon tartan is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scottish clans, particularly in its origins as a family-specific design, registered for use by the lunar-named clan of Moon. Born from the creative vision of Julian Anderson Moon, an American-born weaver with a deep appreciation for traditional Scottish tartans, this distinctive pattern is steeped in history and tradition. Available exclusively to bearers of the name Moon, the Moon tartan embodies the values of unity and shared heritage within a family lineage, its unique characteristics a reflection of the individual's connection to their ancestral roots. As Julian Anderson Moon so astutely observed during registration, this tartan is not just a colourful symbol but a tangible representation of identity and belonging that spans generations.

name: Morag
description: The 'Morag' fashion tartan, designed by the esteemed Edinburgh Woollen Mill, is a captivating representation of Scotland's rich heritage. Originally registered to the public, its colours have been carefully selected to evoke the natural beauty of the Scottish landscape, with the subtle nuances of heather and wildflower hues woven into its fabric. As a fashion tartan, 'Morag' is ideal for those looking to add a touch of effortless elegance to their wardrobe, whether it's a statement scarf or an intricate sash. With no restrictions on its use, this stunning design is open to interpretation, allowing its wearers to make the 'Morag' their own and part of a vibrant tradition that celebrates Scotland's timeless style.

name: Moran
description: The Moran tartan, designed by renowned Designworks Associates, is a deeply personal and storied pattern that holds great significance for its creator, Mr Christopher Moran. As a Name tartan, it is reserved exclusively for Mr Moran and his family, with the restrictions ensuring its authenticity and connection to their heritage. Characterised by intricate yellow tramlines, this distinctive tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich textile traditions. The subtle nuance of Royal Blue 8 in the thread count adds an air of elegance, while the overall design evokes a sense of warmth and familiarity - reflecting the strong family ties that this tartan represents. With its unique heritage and exclusive ownership, the Moran tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scottish heritage and tradition, carefully preserved for generations to come.

name: Moran Drummond
description: The Moran (Wedding) tartan is a bespoke creation, carefully crafted to commemorate the special union of Julie Drummond and Ian Moran on their cherished wedding day. As a Name tartan, its significance lies not only in its unique pattern but also in its personal connection to the couple, making it a treasured family heirloom for years to come. With restrictions specifically noted regarding its use for this joyous occasion, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of love's enduring legacy. Its design is steeped in tradition and heritage, reflecting the rich cultural tapestry of Scotland's weaving past, where every thread holds a story and every colour whispers a tale of history and family honour.

name:
Murray of Abercairney [default]
[AKA] Murray of Abercairney
description: Murray of Abercairney #1 is a richly woven tartan that embodies the storied heritage of Clan Murray, one of Scotland's most distinguished families. This Name tartan holds great historical significance, dating back to the 18th century, and is believed to have originated from a portrait of James Moray of Abercairney, painted in 1735. Estimated proportions are derived from A. E. Haswell Miller's watercolour interpretation from the 1960s, ensuring an authentic representation of this traditional Scottish design. With its intricate and balanced colour palette, Murray of Abercairney #1 is a testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, inviting wearers to connect with their ancestral roots and celebrate the enduring legacy of Clan Murray.

name:
Murray of Abercairney Portrait
[AKA] Murray of Abercairney; Portrait
description: The Moray of Abercairny tartan is a poignant representation of Scotland's rich heritage, woven from the very fabric of history itself. Dating back to 1735, this clan tartan is named after James, the 14th Laird of Abercairny, immortalised in a portrait that has inspired its design. The subtle variations between this set and others from Perthshire attest to the unique character of each family's history, while remaining distinct from the Clan Murray tartan. As such, it falls under the clan/family category, a badge of honour for those bearing the Abercairny name. A 1995 handwoven sample, recorded by the Scottish Tartans Authority, ensures that this tartan remains a testament to the traditions of the past, with its distinctive claret red hue serving as a striking reminder of Scotland's storied heritage.

name: Murray Plaid Artifact
description: The Moray Plaid, an enigmatic and captivating tartan from Scotland's rich heritage, remains shrouded in mystery due to its uncertain origins. This striking pattern, categorised as 'Other', has been intriguing historians and enthusiasts alike for centuries. Discovered in the Scottish Tartans Society archive, a collection compiled by MacGregor-Hastie in the early 19th century, it is one of several tartans listed as being of unknown provenance. The Moray Plaid's significance lies not only in its unusual characteristics but also in its association with the elusive and sometimes reviled MacDonald clan, whose history has been marked by controversy and tragedy. This tartan, much like the clan itself, remains a topic of fascination and debate among those who appreciate the intricate complexities of Scotland's storied past.

name: Moray Council
description: The Moray Council tartan, designed by Claire Donaldson of The House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's north-eastern region. As a Corporate tartan, it has been carefully crafted to convey a sense of professionalism and civic pride, perfect for organisations seeking to establish a strong connection with their local community. With its specific restrictions, this tartan is reserved for official use by Moray Council and its partners, ensuring its authenticity and integrity are preserved. This striking design pays homage to the history and identity of the region, while also evoking a sense of modernity and innovation - a fitting tribute to the council's commitment to serving the people of Moray.

name: Mordente
description: Mordente, a Name tartan imbued with the rich heritage of Scottish tradition, tells the story of an Italian immigrant's journey to Scotland. Designed by John Cargill in 1966, this unique tartan was woven by the skilled hands of Ronald Cowley Company, a renowned Dundee-based textile firm. As hinted at by its original name, MacFish, Mordente's colours are reminiscent of the Italian flag, evoking the nation's pride and passion. This tartan holds significant cultural value, paying tribute to John Cargill's wartime experiences as a prisoner of war in Italy during World War II. A poignant symbol of international connection and heritage, Mordente stands as a testament to the diversity that has shaped Scotland's rich tapestry of tartans.

name: Morgan of Wales
description: The Morgan of Wales tartan is a distinctive and modern creation, born from the vision of Sheila Daniel at Cambrian Woollen Mill in Powys. With its unique thread count and colour palette, this tartan stands out from other Celtic designs, where traditional odd-numbered threads are a common feature. The design's origins are rooted in the relatively recent tradition of wearing Cilt in Wales, which has gained immense popularity since being introduced by Wales Tartan Centres in 1998. As such, while it carries no historical or genealogical significance, the 'of Wales' designation serves as a proud identifier of its Welsh heritage. Notably, permission must be obtained from Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea prior to weaving, acknowledging the importance of respecting this cultural tradition. This tartan's unusual characteristics make it a striking addition to the world of Scottish textiles, offering a modern interpretation of Celtic design that proudly celebrates Welsh roots.

name: Morris of Balgonie
description: The Morris of Balgonie tartan is a stunning representation of Scottish heritage and tradition, born from a joint collaboration between Jamie Scarlett MBE and Raymond Morris of Balgonie, 30th Laird of Castle and Fortalice of Balgonie in the County of Fife. This Name tartan is steeped in history and family pride, with its unique blend of dark blues, greens, and yellows evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's landscape. With restrictions in place to ensure its preservation within the Morris family, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Balgonie's distinguished clan. Weaving together the threads of tradition and modernity, the Morris of Balgonie tartan is a true tribute to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's nobility.

name: Morris of Balgonie; Arisaid
description: The Morris of Balgonie Arisaid tartan is a storied and historic Name tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's clans. Its creation was facilitated by the esteemed Raymond Morris of Balgonie and Eddergoll, 30th Laird of the Castle and Fortalice of Balgonie in Fife, as well as his son Struart G Morris, who gifted the tartan to the Scottish Tartans Authority. This distinctive design is now held within the Scottish register, a testament to its significance and connection to the noble House of Balgonie. By wearing this tartan, individuals are honouring their ancestral roots and acknowledging the enduring legacy of Scotland's clans, which have woven tales of courage, loyalty, and tradition into the very fabric of this iconic design.

name: Morris of Balgonie; Hunting
description: The Morris of Balgonie Hunting tartan is a deeply personal and symbolic weave, gifted to the Scottish Tartans Authority by Struart G Morris in 1989. This Name tartan was originally created for Raymond Morris of Balgonie, the 30th Laird of the Castle and Fortalice of Balgonie in Fife, and later passed down to his son Struart. The intricate design features a rich palette of blues and greens, evoking the rugged Scottish landscape and the noble heritage of the Morris family. As a Name tartan, it is worn by members of the clan and their descendants with pride, carrying the honour and tradition of the Morris name through generations. Its creation reflects the close bond between Struart G Morris and his family's rich history, weaving together the threads of Scottish culture and heritage in a beautiful and meaningful tribute to the Morris legacy.

name: Morris of Eddergoll
description: The Morris of Eddergoll tartan is a richly woven tribute to the heritage of Scotland's esteemed nobility. This traditional Name tartan was carefully crafted by Raymond Morris, 30th Laird of Balgonie and Eddergoll, who entrusted his son Struart G Morris with its preservation. Originally registered in 1989, this distinctive sett showcases 110 threads woven together at a precise 656pi (pitches per inch) to form the intricate pattern that has become synonymous with the family's storied history. With its Arisaidh modifications paying homage to the original Balgonie design, this tartan is not only a testament to Morris of Eddergoll's proud legacy but also a celebration of Scotland's timeless tradition of clan and heritage, woven into every fibre of this iconic textile.

name: Morris of Wales
description: The Morris of Wales tartan is a vibrant and distinctive name tartan, born from the collaborative efforts of Sheila Daniel at Cambrian Woollen Mill in Powys, Wales. As one of the many recent creations to be registered with the UK's National Records of Scotland, it embodies the spirit of commercial tartan innovation that has taken hold of Welsh heritage in recent years. With its unique thread numbers and colour schemes, this tartan diverges from traditional Celtic designs that often employ even-numbered threads and complementary warp and weft colours. The 'of Wales' prefix serves as a nod to Daniel's design origins, rather than a claim to historical territorial significance. While its inclusion in the register does not confer ancient genealogical credibility, it has undoubtedly contributed to the tartan's widespread popularity since its introduction by Wales Tartan Centres around 1998.

name:
Morrison Hunting
[AKA] Morrison Green
description: The Morrison Society tartan is a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, born from the experiences of the Morrison families who fled the Outer Hebrides in 1597 to settle in north west Sutherland. This traditional clan tartan was first recorded in the 1880 Clans Originaux sample book and later featured in W & A K Johnston's "Tartans of the Clans & Septs of Scotland" in 1906, albeit under an alternative name. The tartan's subtle differences from its more famous cousin, the Mackay tartan, are a testament to the unique history of this Scottish clan, whose roots were forged on the rugged Hebridean coast before being transplanted to the fertile lands of the north. Today, as the Morrison Society tartan, it stands proudly as a symbol of family pride and heritage, its distinctive hues evoking a deep connection to Scotland's complex and storied past.

name: Morrison [default]
description: The Morrison Ancient tartan is a storied and enigmatic fabric, steeped in tradition and history. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds deep significance within the Morrison family and their Scottish heritage, serving as a tangible connection to their ancestors' roots. The sett's striking resemblance to a single green stripe version recorded by Lord Lyon in 1968 suggests a continuous thread of cultural continuity, with the addition of this complex pattern woven into the fabric of the family's narrative. The conflicting dates attributed to its origin - 1745 and 1747, respectively - underscore the tartan's enduring presence in the Morrison family bible, unearthed during demolition work on a Black House in Lewis in 1935, providing a tangible link to the clan's past. As such, this tartan design embodies the timeless essence of Scottish tradition and the intricate relationships between heritage, family, and cultural identity.

name: Moskova
description: The Moskova tartan is a striking fashion tartan, imbued with the rich cultural heritage of Russia's Eastern European connections. Registered for use by descendants of Russians in the USA, this distinctive pattern weaves together a unique blend of Soviet-era influences with traditional Scottish weaving techniques. Dating back to Bill Johnston's design circa 1980, the Moskova tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of cross-cultural exchange and heritage preservation. With its bold, geometric motifs and muted colour palette, this tartan would have been perfectly at home on the fashion runways of 1980s New York or London. As an authentic example of transatlantic cultural fusion, the Moskova tartan offers a fascinating glimpse into the complex history of Russian diaspora communities in the West.

name: Moss [default]
description: The Moss tartan is a storied heritage pattern, born from the threads of history and woven with pride by the skilled artisans at Lochcarron. Originally designed by Phil Smith Jnr for Capt. George Moss and his brother, this family crest tartan has been cherished for generations as a symbol of clan identity and tradition. With its subtle nuances and muted tones evoking the Scottish wilderness, the Moss tartan embodies the spirit of Scotland's rugged beauty and ancient heritage. As a registered Clan tartan, it is applicable to all members of the name, allowing individuals to wear their family legacy with honour on their kilts, scarves, or other textiles, connecting them to their ancestral roots and the rich cultural heritage that they represent.

name: Mostyn
description: The Mostyn tartan, expertly woven by Doug Mostyn, is a vibrant and distinctive name tartan that tells the story of a proud Welsh heritage. Designed to be worn by all who bear the surname Mostyn, this tartan embodies the family's history and legacy. Its striking arrangement, featuring bold green and pink hues, is reminiscent of the sun-kissed landscapes of Wales. As one of the many name tartans registered through the Celtic Craft Centre of Edinburgh, the Mostyn tartan is a testament to the enduring connection between people and their ancestral roots. Whether worn as a symbol of family pride or as a nod to Scottish heritage, this tartan design is sure to stir the heart of anyone who wears it, connecting them to generations past.

name: Mother's Pride
description: Mother's Pride is a unique Corporate tartan that embodies the warmth and dedication of mothers everywhere, albeit through an intriguing twist on tradition. This distinctive design was originally adapted by the Scottish Tartans Society from a humble bread packaging motif, showcasing its evolution into a proudly corporate entity. As noted in the registration notes, Mother's Pride diverges from standard tartan conventions with its deliberate substitution of white for yellow hues in the weft, adding a subtle yet striking nuance to this otherwise bold and vibrant design. By repurposing an everyday visual element as a corporate icon, Mother's Pride pays homage to the unsung heroes of family life, while also embracing the modern spirit of entrepreneurship and professionalism, thus solidifying its place within the world of corporate tartan attire.

name: Mothers' Union
description: The Mothers' Union tartan is a distinctive corporate design steeped in tradition and meaning, born from the vision of renowned designer Ros Jones and woven with skill by D.C. Dalgliesh. Officially registered as a corporate tartan, its purpose lies in promoting unity and solidarity among those who bear it, serving as a symbol of connection and shared values within the Mothers' Union community. Woven with reverence for this charitable organisation, which has long provided support to mothers and families across the UK, the tartan's deep blues and rich greens evoke a sense of trust, stability, and nurturing care – qualities that are at the very heart of the Mothers' Union's mission. By wearing or commissioning this tartan, wearers honour the values of this esteemed organisation, paying tribute to its enduring legacy in supporting families and fostering community spirit.

name: Motherwell Football Club 1991
description: The Motherwell Football Club 1991 tartan is a fascinating relic of Scottish corporate heritage, bearing testament to the intricate web of relationships between football clubs, kilt shops, and family legacies. Originally produced for an uncredited designer circa 1991, this tartan was first seen on the field by Motherwell FC, before being quietly claimed by the club's wife when she relocated her business to Hamilton. However, it was only after a convoluted sequence of events involving kilt shops, family vendettas, and the intervention of Kenny Dalgliesh at Dalgliesh Kilts that the tartan's ownership rights were finally secured by Motherwell FC. Today, this tartan serves as a nostalgic reminder of the club's history and the sometimes Byzantine world of Scottish football tartans, woven into the very fabric of local traditions and family pride.

name: Motherwell Football Club Modern
description: The Motherwell Football Club Modern tartan is a vibrant representation of corporate heritage and community pride, steeped in the rich traditions of Scottish football history. Originally created by an unknown kilt shop owner in Motherwell, the design was passed down to Kenny Dalgleish, proprietor of Dalgleish Kilts of Motherwell, after his wife relocated the shop from Hamilton. This tartan's significance extends beyond its technical characteristics, for it holds the honour of being worn by Motherwell F.C., a team with a proud history that dates back to 1873.
