The Modern design may lack specific restrictions, but its connection to Dalgleish Kilts ensures that it remains faithful to traditional Scottish weaving methods. As a Corporate tartan, it is used to promote the values and identity of Motherwell F.C. among its supporters, embodying the town's fierce loyalty and passion for the beautiful game.

name: Mount Isla
description: The Mount Isla tartan, designed by renowned Scottish textile artist Dalgliesh in 1900, embodies the rugged yet refined charm of Scotland's majestic landscapes. As a fashion tartan, it was intended to be worn with pride by those who sought to make a statement about their heritage and personal style. The intricate design features a predominantly blue and green colour scheme, evoking the rolling hills and sparkling lochs that dot the Scottish countryside. According to registration notes, this tartan was carefully prepared for weaving by Dalgliesh Ltd in Selkirk, highlighting its connection to Scotland's rich textile traditions. Notably, restrictions have been placed on the tartan's use, underscoring the importance of respecting cultural heritage and tradition when wearing such an esteemed design.

name: Mountain Rescue Association
description: The Mountain Rescue Association Honor Guard tartan is a striking representation of bravery, resilience, and camaraderie, born from the partnership between esteemed designers Tim Kovacs, Dave Moore, and Neal Jeffers and Dr Phil Smith. As the exclusive corporate tartan of the Mountain Rescue Association, this 14oz weave embodies the Alpine environment's majesty and the boundless sky that supports it, featuring a striking blue and white colour scheme. Weaved by skilled artisans at Fraser & Kirkbright, this tartan is a symbol of honour and service to the association, reserved for its members only, with all proceeds supporting the noble work of Mountain Rescue. Worn with pride by those who have dedicated their lives to saving others in perilous mountain environments, this tartan weaves together tradition, heritage, and the unyielding spirit of those who wear it.

name: Mounth, The
description: The Mounth, The tartan is a stunning corporate design that pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage, specifically the Kincardine & Deeside region. Created by renowned designer Jamie Scarlett MBE, in collaboration with the National Trust for Scotland, this tartan celebrates the beauty of the Scottish landscape and the history of its people. With a unique blend of earthy tones and subtle nuances, The Mounth, The tartan is perfect for those seeking to incorporate a touch of Scottish tradition into their corporate branding. As part of the prestigious Scottish Tartans Authority Scarlett Collection, this design is steeped in authenticity and craftsmanship, ensuring that it will remain an enduring symbol of Scotland's cultural identity for generations to come.

name: Mowat (Clans Originaux)
description: The Mowat tartan, registered as part of the Clans Originaux collection, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish clans. Originating from France in 1880 with J. Claude Fres Et Cie, this family tartan has undergone subtle alterations since its inception, most notably the omission of a broad black band at the centre of the green sett. This striking variation not only sets it apart from the original #258 reference but also showcases the influence of French design on early Scottish textile traditions. Characterised by its predominantly green ground with black and yellow threads, the Mowat tartan pays homage to the storied history of the Mowat clan, whose name has become synonymous with bravery, loyalty, and a proud sense of Scottish identity.

name: Mowat Sir Oliver
description: This majestic Sir Oliver Mowat tartan, commemorating the life and legacy of the 3rd Premier of Ontario and one of Canada's Fathers of Confederation, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage in North America. Registered by the West Coast Woolen Mill, this distinctive tartan pays homage to Sir Oliver Mowat's remarkable contributions to Canadian history, while also honouring his Scottish roots. As part of the Johnston Collection, a treasure trove of Scotland's finest tartans, this commemorative design is steeped in tradition and significance. With its unique pattern and restricted colours, as per the Scottish Tartans Authority's guidelines, this tartan is not only a tribute to Sir Oliver Mowat's remarkable life but also a poignant reminder of Canada's rich cultural heritage.

name: Mowat [default]
description: The Mowat tartan is an esteemed Clan tartan, proudly worn by the descendants of Sir Sanday, 2nd Baronet of Ardno, a prominent Scottish aristocrat in the 17th century. Its rich heritage is rooted in the intricate designs and subtle colour nuances described in 'The Scottish Tartans' by W Johnston & A K Johnston. This setting, woven by esteemed manufacturers House of Edgar and Lochcarron, has been meticulously replicated to evoke the traditional craftsmanship of Scotland's tartan weavers. As a Clan tartan, the Mowat features strict guidelines for its use, ensuring that only those with direct connections to the Mowat family may wear it with honour. Its unique characteristics have cemented its place in Scottish tradition, serving as a symbol of ancestral pride and heritage.

name: Mowbray
description: The Mowbray tartan is a unique and personal designation, registered as part of Scotland's rich heritage of traditional weaving. Designed in 1984 by renowned Scottish designer Peter MacDonald for an American gentleman named Mr Mowbray, this tartan holds significant cultural value, reflecting the individual's family ties to the storied clans of Scotland. As a Name tartan, it is reserved exclusively for those bearing the surname Mowbray, making it a treasured connection to their Scottish roots. The intricate pattern, though not officially affiliated with any specific clan, serves as a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish identity and tradition. This distinctive tartan embodies both personal heritage and familial legacy, evoking the warmth and pride that comes from tracing one's ancestry back to Scotland's storied past.

name: Muir [default]
description: The Muir/Moore tartan is an intricate and distinctive clan tartan, boasting the classic blue-black-green base colours characteristic of Scotland's rich textile heritage. What sets it apart, however, are its three narrow red stripes, which appear twice on the green square, creating a bold and striking visual effect reminiscent of the rugged Scottish landscape. This unique motif echoes that of the Cochrane tartan, underscoring the Muir tartan's connection to a specific family history. The origins of this tartan design are rooted in tradition, with documented records dating back to John Ross's 'Land of the Scottish Gael' published in 1930 and samples preserved in the Scottish Tartans Society's archive and the Dalgety Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority. As an example of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, the Muir/Moore tartan remains a potent symbol of clan identity and pride.

name: Muirhead Hunting
description: The Muirhead tartan, a timeless emblem of Scottish heritage, has been intricately woven for generations to represent the esteemed Muirhead clan family. This traditional sett, registered with the Tartans Museum in Franklin, boasts a rich colour palette of earthy tones and subtle nuances that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. Comprising dark browns, light browns, blues, greens, and a hint of yellow, this carefully crafted pattern is steeped in tradition and history, passed down through the ages to symbolise unity, loyalty, and pride among those who wear it with honour. Although there appears to be a slight variation between this original sett and that displayed on the Clan Muirhead website, the authenticity of its provenance remains unassailable, connecting wearers to a rich cultural legacy that continues to inspire and unite members of this distinguished clan family.

name: Muirhead [default]
description: The Muirhead tartan is a revered Clan tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Originating from the worn kilt outfit donated to the Scottish Tartans Museum by Frances Swanson in 2003, this authentic sett was carefully recreated from threadcounts obtained from Matt Newsome of the Tartans Museum in Franklin, North Carolina, with input from Phil Smith. This Clan tartan holds significance for its connection to the Muirhead family, although the original sett's authenticity has been subject to some variation over time - a modern adaptation of an unfaded colour version by D.C. Dalgliesh of Selkirk, inadvertently introducing an extra green block and omitting a blue section, which seems to have become accepted as the accepted clan tartan. Its rich history and association with this storied Clan make the Muirhead tartan a treasured part of Scotland's cultural fabric, reflecting the traditions and values of its namesake family for generations.

name: Mulcahy [default]
description: The Mulcahy tartan, intricately woven with precision and devotion, holds a rich heritage within its intricate patterns. Designed by Paul Mulcahy specifically for the esteemed Mulcahy family and their descendants, this clan tartan embodies the traditions and history of a storied name. Woven with pride and honour, the design is freely available to anyone bearing the name, allowing its beauty to be shared far and wide. As a testament to Scottish heritage and tradition, the Mulcahy tartan represents unity, identity, and connection to one's roots – a symbol that transcends generations, family ties, and geographical boundaries.

name: Mulholland [default]
description: The Mulholland tartan is a deeply personal and meaningful family heirloom, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. As Mowat #2 with distinctive modifications, this unique tartan tells the story of a long-standing clan or family legacy. Designed by renowned weaver Dalgliesh, D C, this complex design features a rich blend of blues and greens, punctuated by striking black-and-yellow accents that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's highlands. Though restricted for weaving, the Mulholland tartan holds great historical significance, warranting further investigation into its origins and provenance. This intricate pattern is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish family traditions and the timeless appeal of traditional textiles.

name:
Mull District
[AKA] Glenlyon
[AKA] No.053
description: The Mull tartan, designed by esteemed textile artisans at Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a quintessential example of Scotland's rich heritage in District Tartans. Originally named 'Mull', its distinctively broad black stripes set it apart from other traditional designs, evoking the rugged beauty of the Isle of Mull, a haven for wildlife and picturesque landscapes off the west coast of Scotland. As a District Tartan, this pattern is rooted in the region's history and cultural identity, reflecting the unique characteristics of the area that inspired its creation. While specific details about its origins are unclear, the Mull tartan remains an authentic representation of Scottish tradition, inviting wearers to honour their connection to the land, its people, and the storied past that has shaped this timeless textile.

name: Mull Rugby Club
description: The Mull Rugby Club (Old) tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish sporting traditions and community spirit. Registered under the Corporate category, this distinctive pattern was designed by Peter MacDonald at the behest of Mrs Ros Jones, Aros, Mull, for the esteemed Mull Rugby Club. With its unique weave and subtle colour variations, this tartan evokes the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands and the camaraderie of rugby clubs across the nation. As a Corporate registration, it is reserved exclusively for use by the Mull Rugby Club and its affiliates, making it an important symbol of club identity and shared history. This historic design embodies the values of community, teamwork, and tradition that are at the heart of Scottish sporting culture.

name: Mundigl [default]
description: Mundigl, the tartan designed by Alexander Mundigl as a family tartan, is a unique and personal connection to heritage for those bearing the name. Inspired by the iconic Scottish clan tartans, this distinctive design echoes the grand tradition of the Campbell family, with whom it was favourably compared. Yet, unlike traditional clans, Mundigl's tartan has been intentionally crafted to be worn by anyone who shares its name, rather than solely by descendants of a specific line. This flexibility makes it an accessible symbol of family pride for individuals worldwide. With its carefully considered colour palette and historical context, the Mundigl tartan stands as a testament to the enduring appeal of Scottish heritage and tradition, now available to all who bear the name.

name: Mungall
description: The Mungall tartan is a poignant tribute to William de Mungall, a Scottish warrior who played a pivotal role in the Battle of Falkirk, resulting in his tragic demise. Designed by Thomas Gordon Mungall as a personal tribute, this Name tartan proudly bears witness to the history and heritage of those bearing the name. Featuring a rich blend of earthy tones and subtle nuances, the blue hue is slightly darker than expected, imbuing the design with a sense of depth and authenticity. As a registered Name tartan, it holds honour among Scottish clans, allowing anyone of the Mungall lineage to proudly wear it as a badge of family pride.

name: Munro Black & Red
description: The Munro Black and Red tartan is an ancient Scottish heritage pattern steeped in history and tradition, borne from the Vestiarium Scoticum's 1842 repository of long-forgotten tartans. As a Clan tartan, it holds significant cultural value for those descended from the legendary Munro family of Assynt, renowned for their bravery and seafaring prowess. This distinctive black and red design has been carefully woven to reflect the values of strength and resilience associated with its clan patrons. The registration notes reveal that this tartan was previously unknown, adding a sense of mystique to its rediscovery, which has since become a cherished symbol of Scottish identity for those who wear it with honour. Sobieski Stewarts' thoughtful design embodies the rich tapestry of Scotland's past, inviting wearers to connect with their roots and celebrate their heritage in style.

name:
Munro [default]
[AKA] Munro Old
description: The Munro tartan, registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn in the early 1800s, holds a storied place in Scotland's rich heritage. Originally designed as "Lochiel Tartan" for the Cameron family, it was later adopted by the Munros, a prominent Highland clan. Its inclusion in James Logan's The Scottish Gael in 1831 solidified its association with the Munro family, though the exact reason for the name change remains unclear. Despite this, the tartan's distinctive sett has remained steadfastly associated with the Munro heritage, making it an enduring symbol of Scottish tradition and clan identity. This historic design continues to be cherished by the Munro family and their supporters, its intricate pattern a testament to the skillful weaving that has been passed down through generations.

name: Munster
description: The Lochcarron of Scotland's Munster tartan is a rich and storied heritage cloth, born from the early historical and cultural ties between the Scots and the Irish. Registration notes confirm its classification as an Irish district tartan, specifically representing the southwest counties of Ireland, including Cork, Limerick, and Waterford. This intricate design embodies the distinct character of Munster's people, woven with precision to reflect their unique traditions. Woven in a deep, rich palette, this tartan is deliberately distinguished from its lighter-toned counterpart, ensuring a sense of authenticity and tradition. Produced by renowned Scottish mill Lochcarron of Scotland in 1997, the Munster tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring bonds between these two Celtic nations.

name: Murdoch, Nicholsby (Personal)
description: The Murdoch (Geoffrey) tartan is a rich and storied fabric with deep historical roots, originating from the esteemed House of Murdoch. This iconic Name tartan was specifically commissioned for a discerning customer, but its beauty and significance have since been shared with the world. Designated by Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts, this tartan showcases the intricate balance of blue and green hues that evoke the rugged Scottish Highlands. While originally created as a bespoke piece, the Murdoch (Geoffrey) tartan can now be worn proudly by those who bear the name, symbolising heritage and tradition. Note: Due to its exclusive creation process through Geoffrey Highland Crafts, orders must be placed directly with him to ensure authenticity and adherence to original specifications.

name: Murray Hose
description: The majestic Murray, Lord George (Hose) tartan is a richly woven tribute to Scotland's storied past. This distinctive pattern, born from an estimate of the hose in a portrait of the 18th-century Jacobite hero at Blair Castle, embodies the complexity and depth of Scottish heritage. As one of "other" designs, it defies easy categorisation, instead existing as a unique thread in the intricate tapestry of Scotland's tartan legacy. Its creation by renowned designer Peter MacDonald was no doubt inspired by the storied history of Lord George Murray, a brave and loyal figure who embodied the spirit of Scottish independence. Despite its noble origins, this tartan remains freely available for those drawn to its distinctive character, inviting wearers to honour their own connection to Scotland's proud tradition of weaving and craftsmanship.

name:
Murray of Atholl [default]
[AKA] Murray of Mansfield
[AKA] Murray of Atholl
description: The Murray of Atholl tartan is a rich and storied fabric, steeped in the history and tradition of the Scottish Highlands. Originally known as 'Atholl' when first registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1819, its association with the noble Clan Murray was formalised later through an undated specimen in the Highland Society of London's collection between 1816-22, simply labelled as 'Murray'. This subtle distinction highlights the evolution of tartan identities and the complexities of Scottish clan history. As a family tartan, the Murray of Atholl fabric is imbued with a deep sense of heritage and pride, its distinctive blue and green hues evoking the rolling hills and heather-covered moors of Scotland's storied past. Today, this timeless design continues to hold significance for those bearing the Murray name, serving as a poignant reminder of their family's noble roots and enduring connection to the Highlands.

name:
Murray of Atholl Dress
[AKA] Murray of Atholl; Dress
description: The Murray of Atholl Dress tartan is a storied heritage fabric, its origins rooted in the esteemed clan traditions of Scotland's ancient families. Registered in 1880 within the Clans Originaux, this iconic pattern has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish identity for generations. The Murray Dress is deeply entwined with the history of Clan Murray, one of Scotland's most revered and noble families, whose ancestral lands stretch across the majestic Atholl Highlands. Its intricate design, carefully crafted by unknown hands at the time of its registration, now serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of this illustrious clan.

name:
Murray of Elibank [default]
[AKA] Murray of Elibank
description: The Murray of Elibank tartan is a quintessential example of Scottish heritage, woven from the rich traditions of Clan Murray. This family tartan, designated for the esteemed clan, has been passed down through generations of Murrays, its intricate pattern reflecting the storied history and connection to their ancestral lands at Elibank Castle. Dating back to the 1930s and 1940s, this tartan design showcases a unique blend of colours that evoke the rolling hills, lochs, and woodlands of Scotland's rugged landscape. Though the identity of its designer is lost to time, the Murray of Elibank tartan remains a treasured symbol of family pride and cultural heritage, its very existence a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Murray.

name:
Murray of Ochtertyre [default]
[AKA] Murray of Ochtertyre
description: The Murray of Ochtertyre tartan is a quintessential example of Scotland's rich clan heritage, its dark blues and reds evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. This family tartan, as indicated by its category, holds deep significance for those bearing the name Murray, with roots tracing back to the 18th century portrait of Helen Murray of Ochtertyre, whose dress inspired the design. The subtle variations in tone and texture, evident upon closer inspection, showcase a masterful weaving technique that has been passed down through generations. With its restricted registration notes underscoring its historical authenticity, this tartan stands as a testament to Scotland's enduring cultural traditions, its intricate patterns and colours woven into an enduring fabric of family pride and heritage.

name:
Murray [default]
[AKA] Murray Hunting
description: The Murray 1816 #2 tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Clan Murray, one of Scotland's most storied families. This ancient sett, first documented in the early 19th century by Logan in his seminal work 'Scottish Gael', has been woven with meticulous attention to detail, evoking the proud traditions of the Highland clan system. Characterised by its distinctive red and green hues, punctuated by two majestic blue pivots, this tartan design is a poignant representation of Scottish heritage at its finest. As one of the two Murray sets included in the prestigious Highland Society of London's collection, it has been carefully preserved for generations to admire, wear with honour, and connect with the storied history of Clan Murray.

name: Murray, Lord George;
description: The Murray, Lord George (Plaid) tartan is a storied and distinctive pattern woven into the very fabric of Scotland's rich heritage. This beautifully rendered plaid, registered to commemorate the likeness of Lord George Murray at Blair Castle, pays homage to the illustrious 18th-century Scottish leader whose portrait inspired its creation. As a 'Other' tartan, it falls outside the traditional clan system, instead embodying the spirit of the nobility and gentry who proudly wore their own unique designs. With no specific restrictions on its use, this captivating tartan invites wearers to claim their place within Scotland's history, evoking the grandeur and tradition of a bygone era.

name: Murray Mungo
description: The Murray, Lord Mungo tartan is a rich and storied fabric, steeped in Scotland's noble heritage. This distinctive pattern, designated as an "Other" category, has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition for centuries. Originating from a 1670 painting of Lord Mungo Murray by renowned artist Michael Wright, now housed in the National Gallery, Edinburgh, the tartan is also immortalised in other versions of this portrait and a study by esteemed weaver Alasdair MacLeod of Edinburgh in 1994. As such, it holds great significance for those tracing their clan history or with a connection to the esteemed Murray family. With no formal restrictions on its use, the Murray, Lord Mungo tartan remains an exquisite example of Scottish heritage and tradition, inviting wearers to proudly embody the honourable legacy of this distinguished clan.

name: Murtaugh, Hunting (Personal)
description: The Murtaugh Hunting tartan is a vibrant and storied fabric, borne from the Gaelic heritage of its namesake, O'Muircheartaigh, meaning 'navigator'. Registered in recognition of all individuals with the name Murtaugh or its variants, this tartan is an honour to those who bear it. Inspired by Stephen M Murtaugh's ancestral roots in County Mayo, which later influenced his move to Pittsburgh USA, this design serves as a poignant link to Scotland's rich history and tradition. By adapting Don Smith's original Scottish Tartans Authority reference, #4022, the Murtaugh Hunting tartan has been reimagined with colour changes that reflect its modern significance. Whether worn by those of the name or simply drawn to its bold hues, this tartan embodies the spirit of community and connection that defines Scottish heritage.

name: Murtaugh [default]
description: The Murtaugh tartan is a richly woven tribute to the storied heritage of the Scottish clan and family bearing its name, with roots dating back to ancient Gaelic. Translated as "navigator", the tartan's origins reflect the navigational prowess of Stephen M Murtaugh, an ancestor who emigrated from County Mayo in the mid 19th century. This distinguished tartan, designed by Donald Suttie Smith and woven by D.C. Dalgliesh, can now be worn by all individuals bearing the name or its variant spellings, a fitting nod to the widespread presence of the Murtaugh family across the United States. As a Clan tartan, it holds particular significance, signifying honourable descent from a noble lineage and embodying the traditions of Scottish heritage and family identity.

name: Muskoka Canada
description: The Muskoka tartan is a breathtaking representation of the natural beauty of Southeastern Ontario, Canada, born from the collaboration between M Wattson and J Kirkvaag of the Copper Lantern in Huntsville. As part of the District category, this tartan embodies the essence of Muskoka's unique landscapes, which were carefully woven together by the designers to evoke the region's distinct seasons. The rich colour palette reflects the area's stunning foliage, with deep reds reminiscent of autumnal hues, emerald greens evoking springtime forests, and golden yellows capturing the filtered rays of summer sunshine. Amber tones also nod to the region's woodland heritage, while white and gold hues convey the purity of Muskoka's snowfall and the warm glow of its maple trees. A true testament to Canadian craftsmanship, the Muskoka tartan is a beautiful tribute to the region's natural splendour, as recorded in D.C. Stewart's Nomindex and showcased in the esteemed collections of the Scottish Tartans Authority.

name: Musselburgh District
description: The Musselburgh tartan, registered in 1956, embodies the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's historic district town. Designed for the town's prestigious "Riding of the Marches" celebrations, this striking pattern weaves together the iconic colours of Musselburgh - azure and white - with those of the local Fisherrow fishermen, blue and yellow, and the Crusaders Riding Club, red. This District tartan is a testament to the community spirit and pride that has driven the town's traditions for centuries. The registration notes reveal a design born from collaboration between the Scottish Co-operative Wholesale Society textile designers in Glasgow, reflecting the strong social bonds at the heart of Musselburgh's identity. Today, this vibrant tartan is preserved and celebrated by enthusiasts, paying homage to a bygone era when community events like the Riding of the Marches brought townspeople together in joyous celebration.

name: MX-5 Owners' Club
description: The MX-5 Owners' Club tartan is a unique blend of corporate flair and automotive heritage, showcasing the enduring passion of car enthusiasts in Scotland. Designated as a Corporate tartan, it was created by Geoffrey Highland Crafts to pay tribute to the iconic Mazda MX-5 roadster, an affectionately cherished vehicle among its devoted followers. This distinctive tartan features a striking combination of blues, reds, and greens, evoking the vibrant spirit of Scottish culture and the open roads that brought people together through their shared love of motorcycling. As a registered Corporate tartan, it is available for use by the Mazda MX-5 Owners' Club and other affiliated organisations, providing a visible symbol of camaraderie and shared values among its members.

name: Myron
description: The Myron tartan is a fashion-inspired design with a rich history dating back to the 19th century. Originally numbered #29, this distinctive pattern was once considered an unknown sample, discovered in 1985 amongst the renowned Paton Collection at the Scottish Tartans Society archive. However, further research revealed that it was actually Kennedy tartan with its characteristic yellow and magenta colours transposed, lending it a unique character of its own. As part of the Paton Collection, which was compiled around the 1830s, Myron is steeped in tradition and heritage, evoking the rich cultural fabric of Scotland's textiles past. Its classification as a fashion tartan signifies that it is intended for use in modern fashion designs, allowing enthusiasts to incorporate this historic pattern into their own creations and continue its legacy.

name: Nairn #2
description: The Nairn tartan, registered with the renowned Edinburgh Woollen Mill, is a modern interpretation of traditional Scottish heritage, expertly woven for fashion enthusiasts. This vibrant and sophisticated design pays homage to Scotland's rich cultural legacy, with its distinctive colours and patterns evoking the beauty of the country's natural landscapes. As a Fashion tartan, it's perfect for adding a touch of Scottish flair to any outfit, from statement coats to scarves and accessories. With its association with the esteemed Edinburgh Woollen Mill, this tartan is not only a stylish choice but also a testament to the enduring appeal of Scotland's iconic textiles.

name: Nairn [default]
description: The Nairn tartan is a timeless and evocative design that has been woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage since the 1930s. Registration notes reveal that it originated in the esteemed Andersons of Edinburgh, now Kinloch Anderson, collection, for the distinguished Spencer-Nairn family of Inverness. This Name tartan holds significant cultural significance, symbolising a connection to a storied clan line and its rich history. Its origins in the 1930s provide a fascinating glimpse into the past, showcasing the intricate processes involved in traditional Scottish weaving. While woven in darker shades than those used for illustration, the subtle nuances of this tartan remain true to its ancestral roots, inviting wearers to Honour their heritage with every fibre.

name: Nance #2
description: The Nance (2002) fashion tartan, expertly woven by West Coast Woolen Mills of Vancouver, is a stunning representation of modern Scottish flair. Registered under the Fashion category, this vibrant tartan celebrates the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's west coast, where the Pacific Ocean meets rugged landscape. Inspired by the beauty of its native region, the Nance tartan features an intricate blend of blues and greens, evoking the ocean's depths and the misty hillsides. With no restrictions on use, this dynamic design is perfect for fashion enthusiasts and those looking to add a touch of West Coast charm to their wardrobe or home decor. This modern interpretation of Scottish tradition is a testament to the enduring appeal of tartan as a symbol of cultural identity and style.

name: Nance [default]
description: The Nance tartan, registered in 1998, is a proud representation of Scottish heritage, woven with love and legacy by Dr Phil Smith for the esteemed Nance family. As a Name tartan, its purpose is to identify and connect individuals who share a common surname, fostering a sense of unity and belonging among those bearing the name. This intricate design, carefully crafted to reflect the family's history and traditions, can now be worn with honour by all members of the Nance clan, symbolising their shared roots in Scotland's rich cultural tapestry.

name: Napier Rose
description: The Napier Rose fashion tartan is a vibrant and elegant creation, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Once the proud tartan of Clan Napier, its origins date back to the clan's rich history, with the blue hue now replaced by the striking pink tone that gives this fabric its unique character. As part of the Fashion category, this tartan is designed to be showcased through clothing, accessories, or textiles, allowing modern wearers to pay homage to Scotland's storied past while making a stylish statement. With no specific restrictions on use, enthusiasts are free to incorporate the Napier Rose tartan into their fashion choices, adding a touch of Scottish flair and history to everything from scarves to coats.

name: Napier [default]
description: The Napier tartan is a proud emblem of Scottish heritage, hailing from the esteemed clan of the same name. Originally registered in 1880, this historic tartan has been preserved through various publications, including Clans Originaux and W & AK Johnston's 'Tartans of the Clans & Septs of Scotland' (1906). Characterised by its striking red and blue hues, punctuated by subtle yellow and green tones, this tartan design is steeped in tradition. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds significant cultural value for those bearing the Napier name, serving as a visual representation of their ancestry and heritage. While not associated with any specific sept or branch of the clan, the Napier tartan remains an enduring symbol of Scottish identity and history.

name: Nashotah House
description: The Nashotah House tartan is a commemorative tribute woven with reverence for the esteemed Nashotah House Theological Seminary in Wisconsin. Designed by Rev John B Pahls in 1907, this distinctive tartan was created to mark the anniversary of the seminary's founding. As a token of respect and gratitude, the Reverend's thoughtful design weaves together traditional elements with a modern sense of purpose, reflecting the enduring legacy of Nashotah House as a hub of theological learning and spiritual growth. The tartan's intricate pattern and rich colours evoke a deep connection to Scottish heritage, while its association with this unique American institution serves as a powerful reminder of the global reach and significance of Christian faith.

name: National Ballet of Canada
description: The National Ballet of Canada's corporate tartan is a masterpiece of modern Scottish weaving, proudly wearing its UK heritage on its sleeve. Designed by the renowned West Coast Woolen Mill, this distinctive tartan was originally created for the National Ballet of Scotland, highlighting the close ties between two nations. As a Corporate category design, it embodies a sense of national pride and sophistication, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to connect with Canadian audiences while celebrating their shared love of traditional textiles. With its bold, modern colour palette and intricate weave, this tartan is not only a stunning addition to any corporate wardrobe but also serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring bonds between Scotland and Canada.

name: National Fallen Firefighters Foundation
description: The Firefighters Corporate Tartan is a vibrant tribute to the brave men and women who put their lives on the line to protect others. Designed by Linda Clifford in collaboration with Heather Yellowley, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the selfless courage and dedication of firefighters worldwide. The colours - a bold combination of blues, golds, and reds - evoke the fiery passion and resilience that defines these heroic individuals. As a Corporate tartan, it's intended for use by companies and organisations that share values of bravery, teamwork, and community service, making it an ideal choice for businesses seeking to honour their commitment to public safety. By supporting this tartan, you'll not only be showing your appreciation for the fire service, but also contributing to the vital work of the National Fallen Firefighters Foundation, whose mission is to support the families and loved ones of fallen firefighters.

name: National Galleries of Scotland
description: The National Galleries of Scotland tartan is a stirring representation of corporate identity, born from the collaboration between Dr Timothy Clifford, Director of the Museum, and inspired by the storied Black Watch or Government tartan. This distinctive weave combines rich claret hues with bold blue and green tones, evoking the three galleries that comprise this hallowed institution: the National Gallery, the National Museum of Scotland, and the Scottish National Gallery of Modern Art. The colour palette is rooted in William Playfair's original scheme for the National Gallery, lending a sense of continuity and heritage to the design. As a Corporate tartan, this weave is designed to proudly represent the National Galleries of Scotland, its subtle nuances a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish tradition and cultural excellence.

name:
National Millennium
[AKA] McLennium
description: The National Millennium tartan, designed by renowned Lochcarron of Scotland, is a poignant tribute to Scotland's rich heritage, commemorating a momentous occasion in the country's history - the year 2000. As an official Commemorative tartan, it pays homage to significant events and milestones that took place during this pivotal period. The tartan's design bears striking resemblance to the 1934 National tartan, which, although never gaining widespread favour, still holds a special place in Scotland's textile history. Interestingly, Lochcarron of Scotland has recorded an alternative threadcount for this specific tartan, reflecting its unique characteristics. With its subtle nuances and thoughtful reinterpretation of existing patterns, the National Millennium tartan serves as a meaningful symbol of unity and celebration, evoking the spirit of community and shared experience that defines Scottish culture.

name: National Trust
description: The National Trust tartan is a bold and modern corporate design, born from a partnership between Tweedmill, Clwyd and the esteemed heritage organisation. This striking pattern, reserved for use by members of the National Trust team, serves as a symbol of unity and shared purpose among those dedicated to preserving England's rich cultural landscape. With its innovative blend of earthy tones and subtle nuances, this tartan embodies the trust's values of conservation, education, and community engagement. Despite its utilitarian origins, the National Trust tartan holds a certain aesthetic appeal, its modernity subtly nodding to Scotland's rich weaving heritage while forging a distinctive identity for those who wear it with pride.

name: National Trust for Scotland
description: The National Trust for Scotland tartan is a prestigious corporate design that pays homage to the storied heritage of Scotland's national treasure, the National Trust. Created by Colin Hutcheson of renowned weaving house Johnstons of Elgin, this tartan is based on the historic Stewart Old, a favourite of the Queen Mother, an esteemed patron of the trust. As such, it embodies the values of tradition, conservation, and community that underpin the trust's mission to protect Scotland's natural beauty and cultural heritage. With its roots firmly planted in Scottish history and culture, this tartan is woven with pride by Johnstons of Elgin, who have sold it by the metre for the benefit of the National Trust. By wearing or using this tartan, one not only supports a worthy cause but also takes part in a long-standing tradition that celebrates Scotland's rich heritage.

name: National Wedding
description: The National Wedding tartan is a breathtakingly beautiful fashion tartan designed to celebrate the joyous occasion of marriage, as embodied by MacKenzie Menswear, the esteemed Scottish textile heritage brand from Glasgow. This stunning tartan has been registered under the Fashion category, suggesting its intended use is for formal and celebratory attire, such as wedding wear or special occasion garments. Its significance lies not only in its visually striking pattern but also in its symbolic representation of unity, commitment, and love - all core elements of the wedding experience. With its meticulously woven threads, the National Wedding tartan evokes a sense of tradition, heritage, and Scottish culture, perfectly capturing the essence of Scotland's rich textile history and the country's deep-seated traditions surrounding marriage and celebration.

name: National, The
description: The Boat of Garten tartan is a vibrant and distinctive pattern born from the community spirit of north-east Scotland's charming district town. Weaved with pride by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this tartan was created in honour of the residents and visitors alike who call the area home, fostering a sense of belonging and connection to the land. As a District tartan, it embodies the unique character and heritage of Boat of Garten, paying tribute to its natural beauty, rich history, and warm welcome to all who arrive. The registration notes highlight the community's pride in their roots, reflecting the town's commitment to preserving traditional values and celebrating its status as a haven for those seeking a tranquil retreat from urban life.

name: Naysmith Personal
description: The Naysmith tartan, designed by William A Naysmith, is a unique and personal weaving that pays homage to the family heritage of its creator. Based on the classic Gunn tartan, this distinctive design has been tailored to reflect the individual style and character of William A Naysmith, who was a renowned textile designer and Governor of the Edinburgh College of Art. The Naysmith tartan is a Name tartan, indicating that it represents a specific family or clan, in this case, controlled by the designer's own family legacy. Although restrictions are in place to limit its use to those with a legitimate connection to William S Naysmith and his esteemed lineage, the Naysmith tartan remains a cherished symbol of Scottish heritage and tradition, reflecting the enduring spirit of a remarkable individual who wove together art, design, and family history into a truly distinctive tapestry.

name: Nazarian
description: The Nazarian tartan, designed by Varg Breivik, is a unique and meaningful tribute to the Norwegian heritage of those who claim descent from the esteemed Breivik family in Ã¸ygarden, Norway. This distinctive Name tartan features an asymmetric pattern that pays homage to the country's natural beauty, with green and brown stripes evoking the deep, fertile fjords that dot Norway's landscape. Symbolically, the north-east offset alignment reflects the clan's geographical roots north-east of Scotland's heartland, highlighting the intricate cultural connections between these two nations. Written permission from Varg Breivik must be obtained before wearing this tartan, underscoring its importance as a family heirloom and testament to the rich tapestry of Norwegian tradition, expertly woven by Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts Limited.

name: Nebraska University
description: The University of Nebraska Alumni Association's tartan is a vibrant representation of corporate unity, woven with pride to symbolise the enduring bond between alumni and their institution. Designed by Strikke Designs in Hastings, Nebraska, and expertly crafted by Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan is an honour to its namesake university. The colours - a bold blend of scarlet red, navy blue, and ivory, inspired by the University's own hues - come together to form a distinctive pattern that reflects the Alumni Association's commitment to fostering a sense of community and shared identity among its members. As a Category Corporate tartan, it is designated for use in corporate settings, yet its rich heritage and nostalgic value also make it an appealing choice for those looking to connect with their Nebraska roots.

name: Nery [default]
description: The Nery tartan, named after its creator Dalgliesh, DC, is a timeless and elegant choice for those seeking to connect with Scottish heritage. Registration as a Named Tartan signifies its official recognition by The Queen's Official Dressmaker and the Scottish Register of Tartans, underscoring its significance in Scottish culture. Originally intended to be worn as part of formal attire, this tartan has been specially prepared for weaving by Dalgliesh, DC Ltd, ensuring it adheres to traditional standards. Notably, an alternative threadcount recorded by The Tartan Education and Cultural Association (TECA) replaces the black overcheck with white, offering a subtle yet distinctive variation on this classic design. Its inclusion among registered tartans reflects its enduring appeal as a symbol of Scottish identity and tradition.

name: Nevada State
description: The Limerick County, Crest Range tartan is a distinctive District tartan that celebrates the heritage of Ireland's storied past. Woven by Viking Technology Limited (now Tartan Web Scotland Ltd) in 2005, this vibrant pattern pays homage to the region's rich history and natural beauty. Originally created as part of a set of Irish County tartans, it has since become an iconic representation of Limerick's proud identity. While its distinctive design is steeped in tradition, ownership of the tartan was later transferred to USA Kilts Inc in 2012, introducing certain restrictions on reproduction without explicit consent. Despite these limitations, this District tartan remains a cherished symbol of Irish heritage and cultural affinity, inviting wearers to connect with the county's storied history and rugged landscapes that inspired its creation.

name: Nevis Dress
description: The Nevis Dress, a fashion tartan designed by Jedburgh Woollen Mill, embodies the essence of Scottish heritage in its sleek and modern aesthetic. This dynamic pattern, registered as a fashion tartan, was conceived to add a touch of traditional flair to contemporary fashion. By embracing the rich cultural traditions of Scotland, the Nevis Dress celebrates the nation's stunning landscapes and rugged beauty, particularly the majestic Nevis mountain range in the Scottish Highlands. With its unique blend of vibrant colours and intricate design, this tartan is sure to make a statement on the catwalk or at any formal occasion, serving as a stylish tribute to Scotland's timeless traditions.

name: New Brunswick #2
description: The New Brunswick tartan, registered by PIK Mills of Toronto, is a unique District tartan that pays homage to the Canadian province's rich history and cultural heritage. Designed as a tribute to the region, this distinctive tartan features an asymmetrical pattern with non-repeating warp and weft stripes, creating a striking visual identity. As part of Canada's distinct tartan family, the New Brunswick tartan holds significance not only for its geographical roots but also for its representation of the country's diverse communities and traditions. Notably, this design shares similarities with its counterpart, the CIDD 28101 version (STR #5702), highlighting the importance of preserving and celebrating these regional variations within Canada's vibrant tapestry of tartans.

name: New Brunswick
description: The New Brunswick tartan is a stunning representation of the province's rich history and natural heritage. Registered in honour of King George III, who held royal connections to the House of Brunswick, this distinctive District tartan pays tribute to the Atlantic seaboard region's thriving industries and loyal settlers. Dominated by a vibrant forest green for the lumbering industry, meadow green for agriculture, and blue for its vast waterways, the design is expertly woven with gold threads to symbolise the province's promise of prosperity. The bold red blocks proudly signify the devotion of early loyalist settlers and the New Brunswick Regiment, while a subtle brown band may evoke the 'beaver' – a nod to Lord Beaverbrook, a press baron who commissioned this very tartan. This unique design is a testament to the intricate weave of Scottish heritage and Canadian identity, evoking the rugged beauty and resilient spirit of New Brunswick's people.

name: New Club Centenary
description: The New Club Centenary tartan is a distinctive commemorative pattern woven with great reverence for Scotland's rich heritage. Registered in 2001, this specially designed tartan honours the centenary year of the esteemed New Golf Club St Andrews, a venerable institution that has been a hub of Scottish golfing tradition for over a century. With its unique set of threads and colours, carefully selected by the club's designers to reflect its storied history, this tartan is reserved exclusively for the members of the New Golf Club St Andrews, serving as a badge of honour and pride for those fortunate enough to be part of this distinguished community.

name: New Hampshire
description: The New Hampshire tartan is a vibrant celebration of the Granite State's rich heritage, woven by the esteemed Lochcarron of Scotland. Designed by Ralf L Hartwell Jr to commemorate the 20th anniversary of the New Hampshire Highland Games in 1994, this district tartan was adopted through Governor's proclamation, underscoring its official recognition. The colours - purple representing the state bird and flower (the purple finch and lilac), green evoking the lush forests, black nodding to the granite mountains, white symbolising the snow, and red honouring the State's heroes - come together in a striking pattern that embodies New Hampshire's unique blend of natural beauty and proud history. As a testament to the state's strong Celtic roots, this tartan design is not only a stunning tribute to its namesake but also a lasting legacy of Scotland's iconic weaving traditions.

name: New Loudoun
description: New Loudoun is a striking fashion tartan, its subtle yet distinctive colour palette evoking the elegance of Scotland's storied past. As a Fashion tartan, New Loudoun has been woven to capture the imagination of those who appreciate the art of traditional Scottish textile design. With no known designer credited with its creation, this tartan remains an enigma, shrouded in mystery and waiting to be interpreted by those who wear it. Its registration notes remain tantalisingly brief, leaving much to the imagination - and to those who proudly don the New Loudoun tartan, undoubtedly a badge of honour that connects them to Scotland's rich heritage.

name: New Mexico Land of Enchantment
description: This vibrant Fashion tartan, "New Mexico: Land of Enchantment", weaves together a rich tapestry of symbolism and cultural heritage. Commissioned by Kathy Lare, Chair of the St Andrews Society of New Mexico, in June 1997, this distinctive design has captured the essence of the state's unique spirit. As a Fashion tartan, it is intended for everyday wear, rather than formal or traditional contexts, allowing its bold colours and striking patterns to take centre stage. With restrictions in place, including its non-formal adoption by the New Mexico State Legislature, this tartan design has firmly established itself as an authentic representation of the Land of Enchantment's identity. Designed by House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., it is a testament to the enduring power of traditional Scottish tartans in modern times, while also celebrating the distinct heritage and traditions of New Mexico.

name: New Mexico State of
description: The New Mexico State of Tartan is a poignant representation of the state's rich cultural heritage, woven from the threads of its diverse populations. Designated as the official state tartan in 2003, this distinctive pattern pays tribute to the area's Scottish, Welsh, Irish, Manx, Spanish, and Native American ancestry, as well as its unique natural landscapes. Comprising a palette of four colours - blue for the sky, green for the forests, red for the native cultures, and gold for the desert minerals - this tartan tells the story of the state's people and place, woven by Ralph Stevenson in 1995 with input from a cross-section of New Mexico citizens. A symbol of unity and pride, the New Mexico State of Tartan holds a special significance as a public domain tartan, now on permanent display at the New Mexico State Library, and serves as a testament to the state's complex history and cultural identity.

name: New Millennium
description: The New Millennium tartan is a vibrant and modern fashion tartan designed by renowned tailor, Geoffrey Highland Crafts, to commemorate the dawn of a new era in Scottish heritage. Registered for market, this striking pattern is a celebration of innovation and progress within the traditional world of tartanry. Characterised by its bold, geometric motifs and a predominantly blue colour scheme, the New Millennium tartan embodies the dynamic energy of the 21st century, while still paying homage to Scotland's rich cultural roots. As a fashion tartan, it is perfect for those who wish to make a statement with their clothing or textiles, injecting a touch of modernity and sophistication into traditional Scottish attire.

name: New Providence Presbyterian Church
description: The New Providence Presbyterian Church tartan is a stately corporate tartan celebrating the rich heritage of one of America's oldest Christian congregations. Inspired by the traditional Graham plaid, this distinctive design was carefully crafted by renowned designers Alden Dalzell, Carrie Eaton and Marilew Rudisill for the esteemed New Providence Presbyterian Church in Maryville, Tennessee, founded in 1786. Dedicated on Heritage Sunday in 2000, the tartan has since become a proud symbol of community spirit and tradition. As a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's national art form, this corporate tartan proudly wears its Graham plaid heritage on its sleeve, weaving together the threads of history, faith and civic pride to create a truly unique and meaningful fabric for those who wear it with honour.

name: New South Wales Scottish Rifles
description: The New South Wales Scottish Rifles tartan is a testament to the rich history of Scottish military heritage in Australia, specifically in the late 19th century. Registered in recognition of its distinctive characteristics, which bear a striking resemblance to the iconic Black Watch tartan, this military tartan was worn by the esteemed New South Wales Scottish Rifles regiment from 1885 to 1911. The design's subtle variations and nuances reflect the unique cultural identity of the regiment, forged through their experiences in Australia's rugged terrain. This tartan is a poignant reminder of the strong Scottish roots that shaped Australia's early military history, and its enduring significance is a tribute to the bravery and camaraderie of those who wore it with pride.

name: New South Wales Waratah
description: The New South Wales Waratah tartan is a vibrant and distinctive fashion design, born from the rich cultural heritage of Australia's oldest colony. Designed by the Scottish Lair of Queanbeyan in New South Wales, this striking tartan pays homage to the iconic waratah flower, which holds significant symbolic value as the emblem for the region. Exclusively woven by Strathmore Woollen Company in Forfar, Scotland, this tartan is a testament to the enduring ties between Australia and its Scottish roots. As a fashion design, the New South Wales Waratah tartan is not only a celebration of Australian identity but also a vibrant representation of the cultural exchange that has shaped the country's history. With its unique colour palette and technical specifications carefully guarded by Strathmore Woollen Company, this tartan is an exclusive favourite among those who wear their Scottish heritage with pride.

name: New South Wales
description: The New South Wales tartan is a proud representation of the district's rich heritage, woven with symbolism and meaning by renowned designer Betty Johnston. As the official State tartan, launched in 2000 at Glen Innes, it serves as a celebration of New South Wales' unique identity. The tartan's colours, carefully chosen by Johnston, pay homage to the state's notable symbols: the red Waratah flower and the St George cross from the Coat of Arms, alongside golden hues representing the lion and stars, as well as the wattle national flower. This District tartan is a testament to the community spirit that inspired its creation, with funds raised for important causes such as the Cerebral Palsy Association and Motor Neurone Association of Australia.

name:
New York City
[AKA] Tunes of Glory
description: The Lochcarron of Scotland's 'New York City' tartan is a poignant tribute to the city's rich cultural heritage, woven with deep respect for its history and resilience. Originally named 'Tunes of Glory', this District tartan was designed by Alistair Buchan specifically for Tartan Day in 2002, commemorating the majestic Pipe and Drum parade that took place on the streets of Manhattan. The tartan's colours tell a story of their own: vibrant green evoking Central Park's serenity, blue representing the city's lifeblood rivers, while two black stripes pay homage to the twin towers lost on 9/11. This unique design not only honours New York City's identity but also serves as a powerful symbol of solidarity and remembrance. As the name 'New York City' attests, this tartan has become an integral part of the city's fabric, woven into the hearts of its people by Lochcarron of Scotland.

name: New York Fire Dept. Pipe Band
description: The New York Fire Department Pipe Band tartan is a vibrant and dynamic Corporate tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of Scottish tradition. Designed by renowned tartan specialists Grainger & Campbell, this distinctive tartan was created specifically for the esteemed New York Fire Department Pipe Band, paying homage to their unwavering dedication to serving their community with bravery and precision. Drawing inspiration from classic Hunting Rose (STR#3548) and Nisbet Dress Rose (STR#3141), this tartan features a striking azure line replacing the traditional red of the rose, setting it apart as a unique interpretation of Scottish tartan design. As an official Corporate tartan, its use is restricted to the New York Fire Department Pipe Band, ensuring its distinctive identity and heritage are preserved for generations to come, while still allowing the tartan's inspiring spirit to be worn by those who share its values of courage and honour.

name: New York State Police Pipe Band
description: The New York State Police Pipe Band tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan that pays homage to the storied tradition of Scottish piping in the American state. Designed by CW4/TPR Thomas J Morley, Jr DFC, NYSP Ret in 1993, this tartan was originally created for the New York State Police Pipe Band, and its unique sett has since been adopted by the New York State Troopers. With a bold and vibrant colour palette, this tartan is deeply rooted in the heritage of Scottish piping, which has played a significant role in American law enforcement tradition. The corporate category reflects the tartan's adoption for use in official contexts, such as uniforms and ceremonies, while its restricted registration notes highlight the collaborative process between Morley Jnr and the New York State Troopers to refine the design.

name: New York State Troopers
description: The New York State Troopers corporate tartan, designed in 1997 by Morley Jnr, Thomas J for CW4/TPR Thomas J Morley Jr DFC, NYSP Ret, is a distinctive and proud representation of the state's law enforcement heritage. This amended version of the original New York State Police Pipe Band tartan (STR#3122) was carefully crafted to reflect the values and traditions of the New York State Troopers, with Ann Stewart of Ann Stewart Kiltmakers playing a key role in bringing the design to life. Today, this tartan is woven by Lochcarron of Scotland and features prominently on kilts worn by members of the force, serving as a symbol of honour and pride for those who serve the state.

name: New Zealand #2
description: The New Zealand Fashion Tartan is a vibrant and modern design that embodies the spirit of adventure and cultural heritage of Aotearoa's indigenous people. Registration notes indicate that Blair Urquhart, a renowned Scottish tartan designer, drew inspiration from Clint McInnes' original design for Timely Marketing Promotions in Christchurch, New Zealand. This unique fusion of traditional and contemporary elements has resulted in a striking pattern that weaves together reds, blues, greens, and yellows reminiscent of the country's stunning landscapes and rich cultural traditions. As a Fashion Tartan, this design is perfect for adding a pop of personality to clothing and accessories, while its restrictions acknowledging the exclusive ownership by CJ & PJ McInnes ensure the integrity of New Zealand's distinctive tartanic identity is preserved.

name: New Zealand
description: The New Zealand Fashion Tartan, designed by the Piping and Dancing Association of New Zealand, embodies the vibrant spirit of Aotearoa's indigenous culture and its Pacific connections. Registered in 2003, this distinctive tartan was unveiled at a significant ceremony held in Wellington, marking a milestone in promoting the art of piping and dancing in the country. The design, launched with great fanfare by Frank MacKinnon and Helen Clark, celebrates New Zealand's unique heritage as a nation of settlers, Māori people, and Pacific Islanders. As a Fashion Tartan, its purpose is to add a touch of Kiwi flair to clothing and accessories, while also paying tribute to the country's rich cultural diversity. With its carefully crafted threads, this tartan weaves together the history, traditions, and values that define modern New Zealand, making it an honourable addition to the world of tartans.

name: Newfoundland
description: The Newfoundland tartan is a storied and distinctive District tartan, born from the creative vision of Samuel B Wilansky, a St John's entrepreneur with a passion for heritage textiles. Woven in 1973, this intricate pattern was meticulously recorded by the Minister of Provincial Affairs in the Lyon Court Books, verifying its authenticity as one of Newfoundland's cherished traditions. As a District tartan, it holds particular significance within the province, symbolising the unique cultural identity of St John's and its people. This rich, earthy design tells the story of a city's history and heritage, evoking the rugged beauty of the surrounding landscape and the warmth of its communities. Now preserved for generations to come, the Newfoundland tartan remains an enduring testament to the province's history and traditions.

name:
Newlands [default]
[AKA] Walker Newlands
description: The Newlands of Lauriston tartan is a rich and storied heritage design, steeped in history and tradition. Originally commissioned by Willy Newlands of Lauriston, Baron of Miltonhaven, for members of his esteemed family, it was later made freely available to the clan, perpetuating the legacy of this ancient Scottish dynasty. Named 'Falconers' Tartan', it is a testament to an ancestor's distinguished service as a Royal Falconer at the Court of King James IV, showcasing the intricate connection between loyalty, duty, and the nobility of the Scottish aristocracy. With its unique blend of historical significance and familial connection, this tartan design proudly embodies the honourable traditions of the Newlands family, restricted to those who bear the name with pride - including members of the Worshipful Company of Basketmakers.

name: Newman [default]
description: The Newman tartan, designed by Peter MacDonald, is a storied Name tartan rich in Scottish heritage, its subtle variations and intricate pattern evoking the rustic beauty of the Scottish Highlands. With its distinctive white line separating the black and green hues, this tartan stands out as a testament to the traditional weaving techniques that have defined Scotland's textile history for centuries. Originally registered under STR#3128, known as Newlands, the Newman tartan has been adapted with a slight modification - the addition of a white stripe between its iconic black and green tones. Now accessible to anyone bearing the name, this tartan serves as a poignant connection to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's clans and families, inviting wearers to draw upon their ancestral roots and proudly proclaim their identity through the timeless language of tartan.

name: Newmill
description: The Newmill tartan is a striking corporate motif born from the rich heritage of Johnstons of Elgin, Scotland's oldest weaver of fine textiles. Designed in 1997 by John Gillespie specifically for the refurbishment of the Newmill Mill Shop, this tartan pays homage to the mill's iconic 'house colours'. As a testament to the company's enduring legacy, the Newmill tartan is now synonymous with corporate excellence and heritage-driven style. Its roots firmly planted in Scottish tradition, this tartan design serves as a celebration of Scotland's textile history and the iconic Johnstons of Elgin brand, evoking feelings of warmth, professionalism, and cultural pride.

name: Newsome (Matthew) personal; Franklin Museum
description: The Fermanagh County, Crest Range tartan is a richly woven representation of the heritage of Northern Ireland's largest county, Fermanagh. Registration notes indicate its classification as a District tartan, signifying its association with a particular geographic area or community. Commissioned by Viking Technology Limited in 2005, this tartan now resides within the ownership of USA Kilts Inc, reflecting the complex history of tartan design and cultural exchange that has shaped Ireland's fabric traditions. As one of a set of Irish County and National tartans, it embodies the symbolism and storytelling inherent to these iconic patterns, weaving together threads of local identity and national pride. With its specific restrictions in place, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the importance of respecting intellectual property rights while preserving the integrity of Scotland's age-old textile heritage.

name: Newton Primary School
description: The Newton Primary School tartan is a vibrant representation of corporate identity, woven with pride by the pupils who designed it. This unique fabric reflects the school's colours and heritage, born from the creative talents of Laura Aitken, Katherine Garner, and Abigail Worthington, members of P6 and P7 classes. As a Corporate tartan, its purpose is to represent the school's corporate identity, perfect for use in school attire, branding materials, or as a symbol of community pride. Note that due to copyright restrictions, this tartan is owned by Newton Primary School, Dunblane, ensuring its exclusive rights and honouring the school's ownership. Woven by Elliots, the intricate design showcases the collaborative spirit of the pupils who brought their vision to life, creating a lasting legacy for the school and its community.

name: NHS National Health Service
description: The NHS Grampian tartan is a distinctive corporate pattern born from a collaboration between Michael King, founder of Philip King Ltd in Aberdeen, and the esteemed National Health Service (NHS) Grampian. This striking design was woven by DC Dalgliesh, imbuing it with precision and craftsmanship. The NHS Grampian tartan serves as a badge of honour for its patrons, representing a deep connection to the region's rich heritage and tradition. As a corporate tartan, it has become synonymous with excellence in healthcare delivery across the north-east of Scotland, proudly bearing witness to the region's esteemed institutions and values.

name: Niagara Falls
description: The Niagara Falls tartan, designed by the esteemed Highland Queen, is a stunning interpretation of Canadian heritage in fashion form. This captivating pattern draws inspiration from the majestic waterfalls that straddle the border between Ontario and New York, evoking the natural beauty of North America's most famous wonder. As a variation of the 'Maple Leaf' tartan (STR#2824), this design pays homage to Canada's rich history and cultural identity. Woven with precision and flair, the Niagara Falls tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish textile traditions, reimagined for modern fashion enthusiasts who appreciate the beauty of nature and the strength of national pride.

name: Niagara Region
description: The majestic Niagara Region tartan is a testament to the region's rich heritage, woven from the very fabric of its storied past. Inspired by the majestic natural wonders of Ontario and New York, this stunning tartan brings together a palette of colours that reflect the unique character of the area. Dark blue hues evoke the serene lakes of Ontario and Erie, while light blue tones capture the essence of the Niagara River and the Welland Canal. The misty veil of white represents the Falls themselves, an iconic symbol of the region's power and beauty. Green threads signify the fertile agriculture and lush parks that dot the landscape, a reminder of the area's natural bounty. Lastly, bold red accents pay tribute to the military history that has played such a significant role in shaping the region's identity. Woven by the skilled hands of Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan is an honour to the people and places that have inspired it, and is sure to hold a special place in the hearts of those who wear it.

name: Nibley
description: The Nibley tartan is a distinctive Name tartan that pays homage to its creator's personal heritage. Registered by Lochcarron of Scotland, this unique weave tells the story of the Nibley family reunion in California, where it was first showcased. Recognising the similarities between this tartan and the historic Ruthven tartan, permission from the Earl of Gowrie was required, acknowledging a familial connection that may or may not exist. As such, the Nibley is a testament to the enduring power of tradition and family ties, even across continents and centuries. Its distinctive design serves as a celebration of Scottish heritage and the rich history of the Nibley clan, ensuring its place in the world of tartan traditions for generations to come.

name: Nickel Lodge Centennial
description: The Nickel Lodge Centennial tartan is a richly woven tribute to Canadian heritage, steeped in tradition and brotherhood. Registered in 1991 by Brother F Gordon MacLeod, who was the Grand Master of Masonic Lodge #427 at the time, this corporate tartan proudly celebrates the centenary of one of Ontario's oldest Masonic lodges. The distinctive pattern, with its muted tones and intricate sett, embodies the values of brotherhood, loyalty, and community that have guided masonic traditions for centuries. As a corporate tartan, it is now available to businesses and organisations seeking to embody these timeless principles in their brand identity, providing a lasting connection to this storied institution and the enduring spirit of its members.

name: Nicol (Rabbie Burns) personal
description: The Rabbie Burns Corporate Tartan is a vibrant tribute to Scotland's most celebrated bard, Robert Burns. Designed by Claire Donaldson for House of Edgar, this bold tartan was created to commemorate the poet's enduring legacy and intended for use in dress hire for Robert Nicol's Perth-based business. As a corporate tartan, it lends itself perfectly to formal wear and dignified attire, evoking the grandeur and tradition of Scotland's cultural heritage. With its rich, symbolic colours and intricate pattern, this tartan is sure to add a touch of Burnsian flair to any occasion, from high-society events to business gatherings, while proudly showcasing Scottish identity and heritage.

name: Nicolsby (Geoffrey) personal; Twenty First Century
description: The Twenty First Century tartan is a vibrant and futuristic textile, perfectly capturing the essence of a new era. Designed by Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts, this fashion tartan is inspired by the colours of war, peace, unity, and technological advancements. The bold palette features Red for remembrance, White for serenity, Blue to represent international cooperation, Deep blue evoking the vast oceans that shape our world, Green symbolising the land's ecological balance, and Silver (grey) nodding to the rapid pace of innovation. Originally intended as "The Third Millennium", this tartan was rebranded due to trademark issues, a testament to its significance in heralding a fresh chapter in human history. As a fashion tartan, Twenty First Century embodies the dynamism and optimism of our modern age, inviting wearers to don a symbol of forward-thinking style that proudly proclaims "we're moving into the future".

name:
MacNicol Red
[AKA] Nicolson Red
description: The Nicolson tartan, also known as McIan, is a rich and complex weave that embodies the storied heritage of Scotland's Clan Nicholsons. While its origins are shrouded in mystery, with one of its earliest recorded appearances bearing an uncanny resemblance to a drawing by Ian Nicholson of Scorrybreac, Chief of the MacNicols, the tartan has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition for generations. Recognised as a distinct clan identity only in 1980, the Nicholsons' tartan boasts a unique sett that nods to its history and cultural significance. The tartan's design is also mirrored by an earlier variation, recorded in the Oban Times in 1929, which highlights the evolution of this iconic pattern over time. As a testament to Scotland's enduring textile heritage, the Nicolson tartan remains a powerful symbol of family pride and clan identity, weaving together threads of history, tradition, and community.

name:
MacNicol #2
[AKA] Nicolson #2
description: The Nicolson (Lochcarron) tartan is a poignant representation of Scotland's rich heritage, born from the storied history of Clan Nicolson. This family tartan, though designed without an attributed creator, is steeped in tradition and rooted in the earliest documented evidence of its kind, dating back to 1845-7. The distinctive four by four red squares within a predominantly blue and yellow hue evoke a sense of timelessness and authenticity, drawing inspiration from earlier interpretations, including that famously illustrated in 'The Highlander'. Notably close to the STR #3139 variant, which also features these same red squares in connection with the MacLeods, this tartan design serves as a testament to Scotland's complex textile history. With its subtle nuances and deep roots, the Nicolson (Lochcarron) tartan stands as a proud symbol of Clan Nicolson's enduring legacy, weaving together generations past.

name: Nike Golf Dark
description: The Nike Golf Dark tartan is a distinctive corporate pattern woven by Lochcarron of Scotland, born from a deep connection between the heritage of golf and the global sportswear brand Nike. This unique tartan was designed to pay homage to the rich cultural traditions of golf, while also reflecting Nike's values of innovation and performance. As a registered corporate tartan, it is reserved exclusively for customers of Nike Golf, signifying a special affinity with the brand that transcends individual affiliation. Through its distinctive colour palette and carefully crafted design, the Nike Golf Dark tartan embodies the fusion of tradition and technology, capturing the essence of the game's enduring heritage.

name: Nike Golf Light
description: The Nike Golf Light tartan is a distinguished corporate colourway woven by Lochcarron of Scotland, designed to pay tribute to the rich heritage of golf in Scotland. Registered as part of the Corporate category, this unique tartan holds significant cultural resonance, symbolising respect for the game's storied past while reflecting its modern vitality. As a customer exclusive, Nike Golf Light is reserved for those who favour the brand's golfing attire, underscoring the company's commitment to authenticity and tradition. With Lochcarron of Scotland at the helm, this tartan design showcases the finest Scottish textiles, expertly crafted to connect Nike's innovative spirit with the timeless traditions of Scotland's national game, evoking a sense of honour and distinction for those who bear the Nike Golf Light tartan.

name: Nisbet Rose
description: The Nisbet Dress Rose Dance tartan, designed by renowned textile expert DC Dalgliesh, is a stunning example of Scottish fashion heritage at its finest. Originally created as a dance tartan, this elegant pattern was carefully prepared for weaving by Dalgliesh Ltd to ensure its intricate threads were preserved in their precise original form. As part of the fashion category, the Nisbet Dress Rose Dance embodies the artistic and cultural traditions that have defined Scottish textiles for centuries. While restrictions apply due to its origins as a dance tartan, this beautiful design remains an integral part of Scotland's rich tapestry of tartan heritage, evoking the country's storied history of craftsmanship and tradition.

name: Nisbet [default]
description: The Nisbet tartan is a timeless and storied design, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Its origins are shrouded in mystery, having been featured in the Vestiarium Scoticum as MacIntosh, a name seemingly unrelated to its bearers. However, further research reveals that this tartan has been associated with the Nisbet family, who have claimed connections to the ancient barony of Nisbet in Berwickshire dating back to 1160. The tartan's unique sett is reminiscent of another distinctive design, the Dunbar tartan, albeit with a reversed colour palette. This intriguing coincidence only adds to the Nisbet's mystique, making it an enigmatic yet fascinating addition to Scotland's rich tapestry of tartans.

name: Nithsdale District
description: The Nithsdale tartan is a storied District tartan, intricately woven from threads of heritage and tradition, bearing testament to the rich tapestry of Scotland's history. Registered in 1895 by Galt/Hannay, this timeless design draws its inspiration from the Nithsdale district, an area renowned for its rugged beauty and deep cultural roots. Although there are restrictions on its use, as it was originally reserved for members of the MacDonald clan, the Nithsdale tartan remains a coveted choice among those seeking to connect with their Scottish heritage. Its distinctive threadcount, taken from an original MacGregor Hastie sample, ensures that every fibre is imbued with authenticity and tradition, evoking the very essence of Scotland's storied past.

name:
Nobiliary Fraternity
[AKA] No.217
description: The Nobiliary Fraternity tartan is a corporate tribute to the esteemed membership of Scotland's most exclusive gentlemen's society, as registered with The Tartans Authority. Originating from the renowned house of William Wilson and Sons, number 217, this tartan has been adopted by the Nia Naisc (meaning "our friendship" in Gaelic), highlighting the bond between its wearers. By donning this distinctive pattern, individuals demonstrate their affiliation to this prestigious organisation, which values brotherhood, camaraderie, and a shared heritage of Scottish tradition. As a symbol of unity and shared identity, the Nobiliary Fraternity tartan proudly asserts its place within the rich tapestry of Scotland's social history, inviting wearers to participate in an ancient fraternity that transcends mere corporate affiliation.

name: Nooten-Boom (A) personal
