description: Nooten-Boom is a unique and vibrant Name tartan, expertly crafted by renowned designer Donald Suttie Smith for Mr A Nooten-Boom II. Born from a deep connection with Scottish heritage, this distinctive tartan tells the story of its wearer's ancestry through a palette of five different shades of yellow, carefully chosen to evoke the warmth and richness of gold. With no restrictions on its use, Nooten-Boom invites anyone to wear its beauty with pride, while its origins serve as a powerful testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish clans and tradition. As a personal tartan, it holds deep significance for its namesake and their family's history, a true reflection of the rich cultural heritage that has inspired generations of Scottish weavers and wearers.

name: Norham and Ladykirk District
description: The Norham and Ladykirk tartan is a vibrant and meaningful corporate design, woven from the threads of local heritage and community spirit. This unique tartan was created by the pupils of the Norham & Ladykirk primary school in the Scottish Borders, who drew inspiration from the natural surroundings that surround their classrooms - including the River Tweed, the iconic grey stones of a bridge, and the majestic green hill at Ladykirk. The design's colours reflect these connections, with blue symbolising the River Tweed, red paying homage to the pupils' school jumpers, and black and white evoking the keys of an accordion. Under the guidance of designer Ronnie Hek, who has ties to the school through his son, the children's creative vision came together in a stunning pattern that now proudly represents the community that inspired it. Launched at the school in 2001, this tartan is a testament to the power of collaboration and creativity, bringing people and place together in a beautiful and lasting way.

name: Normandy
description: The Normandy tartan is a vibrant Fashion tartan inspired by the historic ties between Scotland and the French region of Normandy. Registered by Philippe Leroux, this striking design pays homage to the distinctive colours of the Normandy flag, featuring bold reds and sunny yellows alongside classic black and white hues evoking the ancient North Men's colours. As a testament to the strong bonds between these two storied nations, the Normandy tartan is an ode to cultural exchange and heritage, weaving together threads of tradition and innovation in a rich tapestry of colour and meaning.

name: Norris Hunting
description: The Norris Hunting tartan, registered by Corrine-Ann Barnes, is a heritage-inspired design that embodies the rugged spirit of Scotland's great outdoors. description: This majestic Nova Scotia Dress #2 tartan exudes the rugged charm of Scotland's most storied province, evoking the windswept coastlines and rich history of the Maritimes. As a fashion tartan, it is perfectly suited for garments that make a statement, from luxurious kilts to intricately woven scarves. Originally identified in the Scottish Tartans Society documentation records as an unidentified tartan dating back to 1983, this sett was later confirmed by its almost identical thread pattern on the official Nova Scotia government website. The subtle variations in thread differences aside, the G/6 W58 G6 B6 G6 B12 G26 Y6 R/4 count holds fast, a testament to the enduring craftsmanship and cultural heritage of Scottish textile traditions.

name: Nova Scotia Dress #2
description: The Nova Scotia Dress is a storied tartan, rooted in the rich heritage of its namesake region. As a District tartan, it represents a specific geographic area within Scotland, imbuing it with a sense of place and history. This distinctive design, while not attributed to a particular designer, showcases the skillful craftsmanship of Scottish weavers, who have carefully interwoven its characteristic stripes to evoke the rugged beauty of the province. With its restrictions governed by the Scottish Tartans Society archive, the Nova Scotia Dress is steeped in tradition, serving as a testament to the region's cultural significance and the enduring legacy of Scotland's tartan heritage.

name: Nova Scotia
description: The Nova Scotia Province tartan, designed by Mrs Douglas Murray in 1953, is a testament to the rich heritage of Canada's Atlantic province. This District tartan was born from a trade display on sheep rearing at the Halifax Weavers' Guild, where the president aimed to avoid favouring any particular group. The result was a design that perfectly captured the essence of Nova Scotia - a symphony of blues and greens reminiscent of the province's majestic coastlines and forests; the warmth of golden light evoking the Royal Charter and the lion rampant on the Province's crest; and the subtle touch of red, echoing the colours of the sea and sky. Recorded in the Lord Lyon Book, this Provincial tartan holds a special place in Canadian history, its design reflecting the province's unique blend of natural beauty and cultural significance.

name: Nova Scotia Pik Mills #1
description: The Nova Scotia tartan, proudly registered with the Scottish Tartans Society archive, is a storied design born from the rugged landscape and rich heritage of one of Scotland's most celebrated districts. As a District tartan, it represents the collective identity and history of the region's clans, their traditions and values woven into every subtle nuance of its intricate pattern. With its distinctive blue and green hues evoking the Atlantic coastline and rolling hills, this tartan is an enduring tribute to the province's pioneering spirit and Celtic heritage, worn with honour by those who call Nova Scotia home or are drawn to its timeless beauty.

name: Nova Scotia Pik Mills #2
description: Nova Scotia #2 is a quintessential District tartan, reflecting the rich heritage of its Canadian namesake. Designed for the Pike Mills of Toronto, this distinctive tartan weaves together elements of Scottish tradition with the history of Nova Scotia's textile industry. The subtle yet striking pattern, designated as Nova Scotia #2, bears testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scottish settlers who brought their weaving expertise to North America. With its carefully considered colour palette and precise construction, this tartan is a poignant tribute to the cultural exchange and resilience that shaped the province's identity.

name: Nowell [default]
description: The Nowell/Noel tartan, designed by the esteemed Dalgliesh, is a quintessential representation of Scottish heritage and family legacy. Originally registered as a Clan/Family tartan, it embodies the rich history and traditions of the Nowell/Noel clan, whose roots are steeped in Scottish ancestry. This carefully crafted tartan, prepared for weaving by D C Dalgliesh Ltd, is a testament to the meticulous attention to detail and expertise of its designer. With no additional details provided in the registration notes, the beauty of this tartan lies in its enigmatic nature, allowing it to be woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition without the need for further embellishment. As a family heirloom, the Nowell/Noel tartan is sure to evoke feelings of pride and connection to one's ancestral heritage, its intricate design a tangible link to Scotland's storied past.

name: Nunavut
description: The Nunavut tartan is a majestic representation of the Inuit heritage and Canadian identity, woven into existence to commemorate the founding of the Territory of Nunavut in 1999. Organised by Burnetts & Struth of Canada (Lochcarron), this District tartan proudly wears its Inuktitut roots on its sleeve, with the word "Nunavut" meaning 'our land' in the language spoken by the indigenous people of the region. The tartan's significance extends beyond its design, symbolising the connection between the Inuit community and their vast, untouched territory, which spans one-fifth of Canada's landmass. This striking tartan is a testament to Canadian history and cultural diversity, paying homage to the resilience and adaptability of the people who call Nunavut home.

name: Nutwood
description: The Nutwood tartan is a captivating representation of rural charm, born from its humble origins in the fictional district of Nutwood, made famous by the beloved children's character Rupert Bear. Designed by Gordon Cavell, this classic tartan embodies the traditional Scottish heritage that has come to define the nation's textiles. The intricate design is rooted in the town's history and culture, evoking the rolling countryside and rustic charm that Nutwood represents. As a District tartan, it holds a special significance for those with family ties or connections to the area, while its timeless appeal makes it a popular choice for fashion and corporate wear alike. With its restrictions carefully noted by Cavell in his registration notes, this tartan remains an integral part of Scotland's rich textile heritage, cherished by fans of Rupert Bear and enthusiasts of traditional tartans alike.

name: O'Boyle [default]
description: The O'Boyle tartan is a proud representation of Irish heritage, bearing the name of a storied clan family with roots dating back to the Emerald Isle's rich history. This timeless pattern, designated as Clan/Family, weaves together a unique blend of blue, green, and yellow hues in a distinctive Dalgliesh weave. With no discernible designer credited for this traditional design, its origins are attributed to the ancient artistry of Scottish weaving techniques, which were refined over centuries to create this striking motif. As a registered tartan, it is protected by law, acknowledging the honour bestowed upon those who bear the O'Boyle name and their enduring connection to the land, culture, and traditions that have shaped Ireland's storied past.

name: O'Brien #2
description: The O'Brien (Scotch Corner) tartan is a vibrant fashion design steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's ancient traditions. As one of a series of Irish name tartans created by esteemed designer Scotch Corner, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the history and culture of the Irish people. With its unique blend of colours and intricate stitchwork, the O'Brien tartan is a stunning representation of Scottish flair and craftsmanship, reflecting the artistic vision of its English creator. While not subject to the traditional clan associations of some other tartans, the O'Brien design still holds significant cultural value, evoking the warmth and hospitality of Irish heritage. Its registration as a fashion tartan ensures that this beautiful pattern will continue to inspire and delight those who wear it, forging a lasting bond between Scotland's rich traditions and the contemporary world.

name: O'Connor #2
description: The O'Connor tartan is a storied and historic design that proudly represents the esteemed O'Connor clan from Ireland's Emerald Isle. Designed by Jerry O'Connor himself, this tartan is steeped in tradition and heritage, its subtle nuances and rich colours evoking the rugged beauty of the Irish landscape. According to the registration notes, this tartan holds no restrictions, allowing it to be worn with pride by O'Connors around the world, or anyone drawn to the warmth and identity of this ancient clan's legacy. With its intricate patterns and symbolic motifs woven into every thread, the O'Connor tartan serves as a testament to the enduring spirit of Irish history and culture, connecting wearers across generations to their rich heritage.

name: O'Connor Dress
description: The O'Connor Dress tartan is a masterful creation from renowned designer Scotch Corner, expertly weaving together traditional Scottish heritage with innovative flair to produce a truly distinctive fashion statement. Registration notes reveal that this tartan forms part of a series of Irish name tartans designed by the talented Scotsman, underscoring the rich cultural exchange between Scotland and Ireland. This particular design embodies the values of tradition and excellence, making it an honourable addition to any fashion collection. With restrictions in place, this tartan is now open for use by anyone seeking to pay tribute to Irish heritage through their wardrobe choices. As a testament to Scotland's enduring connection with its Celtic cousins, the O'Connor Dress tartan remains an evocative and striking choice that showcases the very best of Scottish textile tradition.

name: O'Connor Royal Na Connaught
description: The Royal Na Connaught tartan is a majestic representation of traditional Scottish heritage, hailing from the District category, which signifies its historical connection to a specific geographic region. This striking design, woven with precision by House of Edgar under the creative guidance of Jerry O'Connor, pays homage to the rich cultural legacy of Ireland's Connacht province. Named 'Royal na Connaught' in recognition of its noble origins, this tartan embodies the honour and prestige associated with the region's aristocratic traditions. With its distinctive colour palette and expertly woven threads, the Royal Na Connaught tartan is a true tribute to the craftsmanship and storytelling that have defined Scottish textiles for centuries.

name: O'Donoghue
description: The O'Donoghue tartan is a vibrant and stylish Fashion tartan, created by renowned designer Scotch Corner of Gateshead, England. As one of a series of Irish name tartans, it pays homage to the rich heritage of Ireland's distinct surnames and families. This intricate and dynamic design tells the story of the O'Donoghue clan, whose history and traditions are deeply woven into the fabric of Irish culture. The O'Donoghue tartan is not associated with a specific Scottish Clan, but rather holds cultural significance as an Irish name tartan, reflecting its origins in the Emerald Isle. With Scotch Corner's skilled touch, this Fashion tartan brings a modern twist to traditional tartan design, while still honouring the rich history and traditions of Ireland's storied past.

name: O'Donohue [default]
description: The O'Donohue tartan is a quintessential example of Scottish clan heritage, woven with meticulous attention to tradition and precision. Designed by Dr Philip D Smith for Hugh O'Donohue, this distinctive pattern has been meticulously registered for use by all variations of the name, allowing families to proudly wear their ancestral legacy on their sleeves. With its carefully crafted colours and intricate sett, the O'Donohue tartan embodies the rich history and cultural significance of Scottish clan tartans, which have played a vital role in preserving family traditions and identities for centuries. This beautiful pattern is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage, evoking a sense of pride and connection to one's roots that has captivated families for generations.

name: O'Farrell [default]
description: The O'Farrell tartan, a storied family heritage woven into its very fabric, holds a rich tapestry of history within its intricate patterns. This Clan tartan, registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, is believed to have originated from the Clans Originaux publication in 1880, although its true Irish roots remain shrouded in mystery. Now held by Pendleton Mills in Portland, Oregon, this enigmatic design has been meticulously preserved and passed down through generations of Scottish families. According to historical records, the O'Farrell tartan was featured alongside other Clan and family tartans in the now-discredited Clans Originaux publication, leaving behind a tantalising question mark over its Irish origins. With its unique weft and pattern, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage and tradition, waiting to be woven into the story of those who proudly wear it.

name: O'Keefe [default]
description: The O'Keefe tartan, woven by the esteemed Pendleton Woollen Mills, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish clansmen and their enduring legacy. This majestic tartan, registered as part of the Clan/Family category, evokes the proud traditions of the O'Keefe family, whose roots stretch back through the generations. With its distinctive red, blue, green, and yellow hues, this striking design is steeped in the timeless beauty of Scottish textile tradition. As a registered tartan, it holds a permanent place within Scotland's tartanscape, ensuring that the O'Keefe family's history and identity are preserved for generations to come. Its existence serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring power of clan loyalty and the unbreakable bonds that unite families across time and space.

name: O'Long
description: This distinctive O'Long tartan is a deeply personal expression of identity, crafted by Tartanweb with unique flair. Registration notes reveal that it was created for Patrick J Long and his family, marking an important moment in their heritage. A Name tartan, as its category suggests, this design holds no specific historical or clan significance, yet still exudes a sense of pride and belonging. The subtle colour palette and intricate pattern weave together to form a distinctive and meaningful fabric that represents the individual's honour and tradition. With its roots firmly planted in personal history, the O'Long tartan serves as a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage and the importance of preserving one's own family legacy.

name: O'Mahony
description: This commemorative tartan, The O'Mahony, is a vibrant celebration of Irish heritage, cleverly woven by Brian Wilton. Inspired by the traditional Brabazon Row from Dublin's Liberties, this unique design incorporates the colours of the Irish tricolour (white, green and red) alongside those of County Kerry (gold, green, blue and red), paying homage to Pierce O'Mahony's Bulgarian heritage. The addition of a grey counterpoint is a thoughtful nod to the Irish wolfhound breed, which was prized by the 19th-century breeder. Woven with meticulous attention to detail, this tartan is a testament to the rich cultural tapestry of Ireland, and its commemorative status makes it an especially meaningful tribute to Pierce O'Mahony's legacy.

name: O'Meehan [default]
description: The O'Meehan tartan is a proud and storied tradition steeped in Irish heritage, hailing from the esteemed clan family of the same name. Originally designated for the principal clans of West Breifne or Leitrim, this iconic tartan was worn by the distinguished Mossie Meehans as a badge of honour, signifying their noble lineage and connection to the powerful O'Rourkes. As Marshals and Coarbs of St Molaise, the O'Meehans played a significant role in the rich history of West Breifne, and this tartan serves as a testament to their bravery, loyalty and devotion to their heritage. Designed by Frank Meehan, the O'Meehan tartan is a vibrant and meaningful representation of Irish tradition, its intricate patterns and colours evoking the rugged beauty of the Emerald Isle's landscapes and the unyielding spirit of its people.

name: O'Monaghan
description: The O'Monaghan tartan, a personal creation by Jamie Scarlett MBE, is a unique and storied pattern steeped in Irish heritage. Registered as a Name tartan, it is closely tied to its namesake family, who claim a connection to The O'Monaghan. This distinctive design features mustard yellow squares against a rich backdrop of darker hues, evoking the majestic landscape of Lochcarron, where one of the original pieces originates. While Jamie Scarlett MBE's own standard 18ins x 12ins square boasts buff squares, the larger piece from Lochcarron adds a striking contrast to this variation. As a Name tartan, its significance lies in its association with an individual family's history and identity, making it a meaningful and personal choice for those seeking to connect with their heritage.

name: O'Neill Australia
description: The O'Neill (Australia) tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage, woven into the very fabric of Australia's indigenous clans. This unique design, registered as an O'Brian tartan, was later identified as O'Neill, carrying with it the storied history and traditions of the esteemed Irish clan. Although differing slightly from its more widely recognised counterpart, this Australian interpretation retains the essence of its namesake, boasting a palette of earthy tones with white accents that evoke the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. Rooted in the family traditions of O'Neill, this tartan weaves together the past and present, reflecting the cultural exchange and adaptation that has shaped the Australian clan's identity over time.

name: O'Neill Cliffford
description: The O'Neill tartan, carefully crafted by Linda Clifford for Timothy Powers O'Neill's wedding in 2000, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's most iconic clan family. This distinctive tartan weaves together traditional Irish hues of saffron, green, and crimson, echoing the O'Neill crest's prominent use of red. Originally commissioned to mark a very special occasion, this tartan is now reserved exclusively for those bearing the esteemed surname O'Neill, making it an honourable symbol of family identity. Its construction is reminiscent of earlier examples in STR #3248 and #3251, further underscoring its roots in Scottish tradition. Woven by Strathmore Woollen Co Limited, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's clans, where heritage and family ties are deeply intertwined.

name: O'Neill Red (Dalgliesh)
description: The O'Neill, Red corporate tartan is a bold and storied variation on a classic Irish heritage pattern. Originally created for the Co. Tyrone Pipe Band in 1985, this distinctive design has been worn with honour by the band since its conception, evoking the rich history of Ulster's most famous clan, the O'Neills. The tartan's design is rooted in traditional Scottish tartans, but its unique twist - characterised by a notable absence of black and two broader blue guards - sets it apart as a distinctively modern creation. Now worn with pride by corporate teams around the world, this vibrant red tartan remains a testament to the enduring legacy of Irish culture and tradition.

name: O'Neill Pipe Band 1983
description: The O'Neill Pipe Band 1983 tartan embodies the spirit of Scottish heritage and cultural connection, proudly representing the Co. Tyrone Pipe Band from Forest Hills, New York, at the Delco Games in 1983. This Corporate tartan was designed by Bill Johnston, a master weaver who skillfully blended colours to evoke the rich traditions of Ulster's O'Neill clan legacy. Originally intended for pipers and their bands, this distinctive design now finds its place in corporate collections, allowing individuals to pay homage to the region's storied past while embracing modern professionalism. Notably, it bears similarities to the iconic O'Neill Red, distinguished by an additional green line on the red and two additional blue lines on the green, creating a unique visual identity that pays tribute to the rich tapestry of Scottish culture.

name: O'Neill Pipe Band 1999
description: This striking Corporate tartan, designated as O'Neill Pipe Band 1999/ Oliver dress, pays tribute to the esteemed O'Neill Pipe Band, whose rich heritage spans centuries. Designed to evoke the spirit of Scottish piping tradition, this complex and intricate pattern is a testament to the skill and craftsmanship of the band's pipers. As depicted in 'Tartans' by Johnston/Smith (1999), which attributes its origins to the J.C. Thompson Collection, this tartan is a poignant reminder of Scotland's storied past, its pipes and drums having played a pivotal role in shaping the country's cultural identity for generations. With no designer credited, it is clear that this tartan has been carefully preserved and passed down through the ages, awaiting its new wearer to wear with pride, symbolising excellence, tradition, and the enduring legacy of Scotland's pipers.

name: O'Reilly
description: The O'Reilly tartan, a captivating creation of Scottish heritage, was meticulously woven by English designer Scotch Corner in Gateshead, England. This stunning fashion tartan is part of a series of Irish name tartans, carefully crafted to honour the rich cultural legacy of Ireland's storied past. In its intricate design, the O'Reilly tartan tells the tale of a proud clan and their enduring connection to the Emerald Isle, with each carefully selected thread count woven into a unique narrative. While restrictions exist regarding its use due to its Irish heritage, this tartan remains an integral part of Scotland's rich tapestry, waiting to be woven into the fabric of fashion history.

name: O'Rourke #2
description: The O'Rourke tartan is a striking Fashion tartan, born from the skilled hands of English designer Scotch Corner. This vibrant design is one of a series created to celebrate the rich heritage of Irish names, reflecting the country's complex history and cultural identity. With its unique colour palette and intricate threadwork, the O'Rourke tartan pays homage to the storied surname that bears its name, evoking the emerald landscapes and Celtic traditions of Ireland. Although originating from England, this tartan has a distinct Scottish flair, thanks to the country's long-standing influence on the textile arts. With no restrictions on its use, the O'Rourke tartan is free to be woven into garments, accessories, or other items that celebrate its beauty and significance, allowing wearers to proudly express their connection to Irish heritage.

name: O'Shaughnessy Memorial
description: The O'Shaughnessy Memorial tartan, designed by Jim Rawson in tribute to his dear friend Thomas A O'Shaughnessy, is a poignant corporate tartan steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's piping tradition. Based on the Royal-Stewart tartan, this unique design pays homage to Thomas's enduring legacy as a master piper and instructor, whose impact continues to inspire a thriving pipe band community. With its subtle variations and thoughtful colour palette, the O'Shaughnessy Memorial tartan is a fitting tribute to a life devoted to sharing the beauty of piping with others. As such, it serves as a powerful symbol of remembrance and celebration of Thomas's remarkable achievements, while also honouring the enduring spirit of camaraderie that binds the Long Island Bagpipe Company and its esteemed Pipe Band to their heritage.

name: O'Shaughnessy
description: The O'Shaughnessy tartan is a vibrant and captivating fashion-inspired design that pays homage to the rich heritage of Ireland's storied clans. One of a series of Irish name tartans crafted by renowned designer Scotch Corner of Gateshead, England, this distinctive pattern holds special significance for those tracing their ancestry back to the Emerald Isle. With its bold colour palette and intricate threadwork, the O'Shaughnessy tartan evokes the spirit of Ireland's proud history and cultural traditions. As a fashion design, it lends itself perfectly to creating statement pieces that showcase individuality and style, while also serving as a poignant connection to one's heritage for those who proudly wear their O'Shaughnessy tartan with honour.

name: O'Sheehan
description: The O'Sheehan tartan, nestled within the Scotspun folder of unidentified provenance, bears testament to the enduring legacy of Irish heritage in Scotland's rich textile tradition. As one of seven 'Irish' tartans, it joins a storied fraternity of clans and families who, despite centuries of separation from their ancestral lands, maintained the sacred bond with their cultural roots. The O'Sheehan design, though labelled as an 'unimaginative adaptation' of the Royal Stewart, stands as a poignant example of the symbiotic relationship between Scottish and Irish traditions. This tartan's existence serves as a poignant reminder of the historical overlap between these two nations, whose shared experiences in diaspora forged a lasting connection through the timeless language of pattern and colour.

name: O'Sullivan [default]
description: The O'Sullivan tartan is a storied and iconic design steeped in Irish heritage and tradition. As the most numerous name in Ireland, its creation tells the story of a people and their place within Scotland's rich cultural tapestry. Registered with a fascinating provenance, this tartan was originally displayed at the Scottish Tartans Society Museum in Edinburgh, and later accurately recounted by Phil Smith. The O'Sullivan design features 11 distinct sett stripes, each carefully woven to evoke the warmth and authenticity of the Irish diaspora experience. As a Clan/Family tartan, it serves as a proud emblem for those bearing the name, their roots forever linked to Scotland's unique cultural landscape.

name: O'Sullivan McCragh
description: O'Sullivan McCragg, a name tartan born from the threads of Irish heritage, is a testament to the rich cultural legacy of Scotland's Celtic cousins. Designed by Chris Aitken in 1994 for Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts Ltd., this distinctive pattern takes its inspiration from the esteemed O'Sullivan and McCragh families, renowned for their history and bravery in Ireland. With restrictions tied to surname registration notes, the tartan's creation embodies the intricate connections between Irish identity and Scottish heritage. As a name tartan, it holds significance for those bearing the O'Sullivan or McCragh names, serving as a tangible link to their ancestral roots and familial traditions.

name: O'Sullivan-Beare [default]
description: The O'Sullivan-Beare tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Clan O'Sullivan, a storied family from southern Ireland whose ancestral lands stretch along the picturesque peninsula of Beare. This iconic tartan was designed by renowned expert Dr Philip D Smith for Rev Cyril O'Sullivan, a devoted priest who shared a passion for traditional Irish music, particularly the soulful Uillean pipes. The result is a vibrant and intricate design that reflects the proud history of the House of Beare, whose approval lends weight to its authenticity. With each carefully woven thread, this tartan pays tribute to the region's unique cultural heritage and the family's enduring legacy, weaving together a tapestry of tradition and identity that continues to captivate those who wear it today.

name: O2
description: The O2 Corporate tartan, woven with precision by renowned designer Brian Wilton, pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage as it commemorates the launch of communications company 02's Scottish operations in Glasgow. This distinctive tartan was specifically created for the esteemed occasion, reflecting the blend of innovation and tradition that defines modern Scotland. As a corporate tartan, O2 is designed to be worn with pride by employees and associates of the company, fostering unity and identity within their organisation. However, its significance extends beyond the boardroom, as it proudly represents Glasgow's vibrant culture and Scotland's enduring legacy of creativity and entrepreneurial spirit.

name: Oakhall
description: The Oakhall tartan is a storied and exclusive corporate tartan, carefully crafted by Heather Yellowley on behalf of Crawfords Celtic House to commemorate the esteemed Oakhall School Pipe Band of Florida. Originally designed for the band's pipers, this vibrant tartan is steeped in tradition and heritage, drawing inspiration from the rich colours of burgundy and gold that signify the Pipe Band's colours. As a corporate tartan, it holds a special place in the hearts of those connected to the school, serving as a badge of honour for pupils and former pupils alike. Worn with pride by those privileged enough to have been part of this esteemed institution, the Oakhall tartan embodies the spirit of camaraderie and achievement that defines Scotland's iconic pipe bands, while also celebrating the enduring legacy of the Oakhall School Pipe Band of Florida.

name: Oakwood
description: The Oakwood tartan is a striking fashion tartan, its subtle blend of earthy tones evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's ancient woodlands. Without a designer to credit, its origins remain shrouded in mystery, but one thing is certain: this tartan was carefully crafted with style and sophistication in mind, destined for the catwalks and high-street runways that showcase the very best of British fashion. With no specific clan or family association to claim it, the Oakwood tartan remains a proudly independent creation, free to make its mark on the world of fashion. Its registration notes may remain tantalisingly vague, but one thing is clear: this tartan design embodies the timeless spirit of Scottish heritage and tradition, with all the elegance and charm that comes from being a true product of British textiles.

name: Oban
description: The Oban tartan, named after Scotland's picturesque coastal town on the west coast, belies its lack of authentic heritage with its vibrant hues and traditional sett. Designed by West Coast Woolen Mill, this fashion tartan is a prime example of commercial tartans originating from North America, borrowing inspiration from Scottish traditions without any direct connection to the country or its clans. Yet, despite this dubious provenance, Oban remains a striking design that embodies the timeless spirit of Scottish heritage, with its distinctive 3-2-1 pattern of blues and greens evoking the rugged beauty of the Highlands. A staple in North American fashion for generations, Oban has become synonymous with the quintessential Scottish look, albeit one that is far removed from its actual roots.

name: Ochiltree [default]
description: The O'Connor/Ochiltree tartan is a timeless representation of Scottish heritage, woven with deep historical roots and a sense of family pride. This category-specific tartan was registered by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr in honour of the esteemed clan that bore the name, the Stewarts of Ochiltree. Originating from an ancient Stewart motif (as referenced in the original Scottish Tartans Society records), this tartan design has been carefully crafted to evoke a sense of tradition and unity among those bearing the name. Its creation is a testament to the rich tapestry of Scotland's clan history, where the past and present converge through the threads of family legacy and cultural identity.

name: Ochterlony [default]
description: The Ochterlonie tartan, named after its storied family heritage, is a testament to Scotland's rich clan traditions. Registered as a Clan/Family tartan, it was designed by renowned weaver Dalgliesh, D C, who painstakingly wove the intricate pattern with precision and attention to detail. This distinctive design holds significance for the Ochterlonie family, whose history and legacy are woven into its very fabric. However, to respect the family's connection to this tartan, it is prepared specifically by Dalgliesh, D C Ltd for weaving, ensuring that only authentic reproductions of this revered clan pattern can be worn or used with honour. As a symbol of Scottish heritage and tradition, the Ochterlonie tartan embodies the timeless values and history of its namesake family.

name: Offaly Irish County
description: The Ofally County tartan, designed by Polly Wittering for House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., is a stunning representation of Irish heritage, nestled firmly within the boundaries of traditional District tartans. As one of a series crafted by Wittering, this design has proven to be a crowd-pleaser, bridging the gap between authentic and popular patterns. Although not officially sanctioned by The Tartan Registry, its widespread adoption has all but cemented its place as a legitimate District tartan, forging a unique connection with those who bear it. With its intricate texture and rich colour palette, the Ofally County tartan embodies the warmth and character of rural Ireland, evoking memories of lush landscapes and community spirit.

name: Ogilvie (Logan)
description: This intricate and complex Ogilvie - 1831 tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans, born from the meticulous work of James Logan in his seminal publication, 'The Scottish Gael', 1831. As a member of the Clan Ogilvie, this tartan design embodies the family's esteemed history and traditions, woven with precision and care by Wilsons of Bannockburn in the early 19th century. The subtle nuances and variations inherent to its complex pattern serve as a poignant reminder of the potential for misinterpretation, highlighted by Logan himself, underscoring the importance of preserving traditional knowledge through careful transcription. This tartan stands as a proud representation of Scottish clan identity, its intricate patterns telling a story of tradition, family, and heritage that continues to captivate those who wear it with honour and pride.

name: Ogilvie #3
description: Ogilvy #2, a storied clan tartan with a rich history, is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Ogilvie family. Designed by Caird of Dundee, one of Scotland's most esteemed tartan manufacturers, this complex and intricate pattern was first registered in 1964. Its threadcount, derived from a bespoke kilt crafted for John G Ogilvy in 1945, provides a tangible connection to the past, while its adaptation into a new kilt in 2002 ensures the design remains relevant to modern wearers. As a Clan tartan, Ogilvy #2 carries significant honour and pride among those bearing the Ogilvie name, and its careful creation and registration by Caird of Dundee reflect the importance placed on preserving Scotland's unique textile heritage.

name: Ogilvie Black & White
description: The Ogilvie (Black and White) tartan is an iconic fashion pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, its distinctive black and white stripes evoking the rugged beauty of the Highlands. This timeless design, which falls under the category of Fashion, has been a staple in the world of Highland dress for generations, its simplicity belied by a rich cultural significance that speaks to the enduring legacy of Scotland's tartan traditions. As part of the MacGregor-Hastie collection and registered with the Scottish Tartans Society archive, this trade sett tartan is a testament to the country's rich textile history, and its design has been prized by fashion enthusiasts and Highland heritage aficionados alike for its elegance and versatility.

name: Ogilvie Hunting
description: The Ogilvie of Inverarity tartan, also designated as Ochterlonie, holds a storied place within Scotland's rich tapestry of heritage. This distinctive Clan tartan has been woven with pride by members of the esteemed Ogilvie family for generations, its origins dating back to the 19th century. With its unique characteristics carefully documented in the Lauder Transcript and Vestiarium Scoticum, this tartan design is an integral part of Scotland's historical and cultural fabric. As a Clan tartan, it is reserved exclusively for those bearing the Ogilvie surname or their direct descendants, signifying a deep-rooted connection to the family's Scottish roots. Stuarts Sobieski, The, has skillfully captured the essence of this iconic design in his registration, ensuring its preservation for future generations to cherish and wear with honour.

name:
Ogilvie of Airlie [default]
[AKA] Ogilvie of Airlie
description: Ogilvie #2 is a timeless and storied Clan tartan, woven with meticulous care to preserve a fragment of Scotland's rich textile heritage. This distinctive pattern, officially registered by The Scottish Tartans Authority, holds great significance for the Ogilvie family and their descendants. Transferred from an early 20th century sample in the esteemed Paton collection, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of traditional Scottish weaving. Although its designer remains anonymous, the intricate details and nuanced colour palette evoke the intricate patterns and rich history of Scotland's cultural fabric. As a Clan tartan, Ogilvie #2 serves as a cherished family heirloom, symbolising pride, heritage, and connection to the land that shaped its creation, now worn with honour by those who bear the Ogilvie name.

name:
Ogilvie of Inverarity (Vestiarium Scoticum)
[AKA] Ogilvie of Inverarity; (Vestiarium Scoticum)
description: The Ogilvie of Inverarity tartan, registered as VS #2, is a storied family crest woven from threads of tradition and heritage. Originating in the 19th century with the name "Ogilvie" emerging from an earlier publication of the Vestiarium Scoticum in 1828, this tartan's evolution over time reflects the growth and identity of the Ogilvie clan. While its earliest recorded version predates its later naming as "Ogilvie of Inverarity" in a 1893 publication, it is the latter designation that has become synonymous with the tartan's enduring significance. As part of the Clan/Family category, this tartan design holds a special place within Scottish heritage, woven into the fabric of family history and tradition, with no restrictions currently noted, allowing its wearers to proudly represent their ancestral roots.

name:
Ogilvie of Inverarity (Wilson)
[AKA] Ogilvie of Inverarity; (Wilson)
description: The Ogilvie of Inverarity (Wilsons') / Ochterlonie tartan is a rich and storied heritage pattern, steeped in history and tradition. Registered as part of the Clan/Family category, it holds significant meaning for those tracing their roots to this noble Scottish family. Designed by the esteemed Wilsons of Bannockburn, this distinctive sett is distinguished by its striking red and blue hues, punctuated by two black lines on each side, creating a dynamic and elegant visual effect. Notably, this tartan has undergone documentation through various sources, including James Cant's manuscript book and Jack Dalgety's pencil markings in the Mary Hall collection, suggesting a long history of ownership and use. With its provenance deeply rooted in Scottish heritage, the Ogilvie of Inverarity / Ochterlonie tartan remains a cherished symbol of family identity and tradition.

name:
Ogilvie of Strathallan [default]
[AKA] Ogilvie of Strathallan
description: Ogilvie #7, an ancient and storied clan tartan, has been woven into the very fabric of Scotland's rich heritage for centuries. First registered in a sample at Kilbarchan weaver's cottage circa 1900, this tartan is also famously known as Drummond of Strathallan, bearing testament to its enduring significance within the noble family. As a Clan tartan, Ogilvie #7 holds dear honour among Scottish families, signifying a proud heritage and ancestral ties that stretch back generations. Its distinctive pattern, carefully crafted by skilled weavers over the years, is both a nod to tradition and a celebration of the past, its subtle variations reflecting the intricate history and stories behind this revered tartan.

name: Ogilvie [default]
description: Ogilvie #3 is a richly woven tartan with a storied history, steeped in Scottish tradition and family heritage. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds significant importance for those bearing the Ogilvy surname or connected through marriage to the clan's esteemed families. According to D.W. Stewart's 'Old & Rare Scottish Tartans', this count dates back to 1812, although it is indeed a partial section of a more complex design, and not older than Stewart's work itself. Interestingly, Stewart noted that elements from this tartan appeared in the Drummond of Strathallan clan, leading some to speculate about a possible familial connection or even an intriguing portent - perhaps hinting at a long-forgotten union between the Ogilvies and Drummonds that took place as early as 1812.

name: Ohio
description: The Ohio tartan is a proud representation of the state's rich heritage, born from the collaboration between Mary Jayne McMichael Fischbach and the Scottish Tartan Society in 1983. Inspired by the colours of Ohio's flag and state seal, this distinctive tartan pays tribute to the state's admission to the Union in 1803, with stripes of red and blue reflecting the date - two widths for 18 and one width for three, respectively. The design was adopted by the Ohio Scottish Games Board of Trustees in 1984, solidifying its place in Scottish heritage. This striking tartan is a testament to the enduring connection between Scotland and the United States, celebrating the cultural exchange that has shaped both nations.

name: Oilmens
description: The Oilmens corporate tartan is a distinctive and enduring design born from the Scottish golfing tradition. Originally commissioned for the 33rd Oilmens' Golf Tournament, this striking pattern was later renamed 'Barkwell' in recognition of its creator, Don Barkwell. The Corporate category testament to its versatility as a suitable choice for businesses looking to forge a strong, lasting impression. Notably restricted by the registration notes, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of its heritage, originating from a specific golf tournament with a rich history. As such, the Oilmens/Barkwell tartan embodies the values of Scottish tradition and sporting excellence, inviting its wearers to join the ranks of those who value community, camaraderie, and fair play.

name: Oklahoma
description: The Oklahoma tartan is a quintessential example of a District tartan, originating from the heartland of America's southernmost state. Registered in 1999 with Jerrel R. Murray as its designer, this unique weave pays homage to the rich heritage of Scottish clans that have shaped the region. Woven by the House of Edgar, the Oklahoma tartan incorporates vibrant colours, evoking the vast prairies and wildflower fields that blanket the state's landscape. Its distinctive graphic pattern is said to match a printout from the same esteemed house, underscoring its status as a celebrated example of Scottish textile artistry in America. As a registered District tartan, the Oklahoma has been formally recognised by the Scottish Tartans authority, solidifying its place within the pantheon of traditional Scottish weaves that reflect the history and cultural identity of its wearers.

name:
Oliphant [default]
[AKA] #2
description: The Oliphant tartan is a storied and complex clan tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registration notes reveal its murky origins, with some sources dating back to the 18th century, yet uncertainty surrounding the identity of Clan Chief during the Highland Society of London's early registration process. Claimed by Lord Lyon in 2004, this tartan now proudly represents the Oliphant clan family, potentially worn by supporters of the chief as a badge of honour. The setts are recorded in both the Vestiarium Scoticum No. 54 and W & A K Johnston's collection from 1906, with some historical accounts linking it to a union with Clan Melville, 'Oliphant and Melville'. This intricate and historically significant tartan design now holds significance for those bearing the Oliphant name, symbolising a deep-rooted connection to Scottish tradition.

name: Oliver Hunting
description: The Oliver Hunting tartan, designed by John Cargill in 1973 for the Oliver Society, weaves a rich tapestry of Scottish heritage and tradition. Based on an ancient cottage weaver's formula known as 'Tweedside', dating from around 1820, this Clan tartan is steeped in history and evokes the rolling hills and rustic charm of the Northumberland-Tweed Valley region. A sett that has been documented in the notebooks of Wilson's of Bannockburn, a renowned Tweed-based mill, adds to the authenticity of this design. With its distinctive blue and green hues reminiscent of Scotland's rugged landscape, the Oliver Hunting tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile traditions, carefully preserved and passed down through generations by the Oliver Society and its members.

name: Oliver Pink; Dress
description: The Oliver Dress Pink tartan, designed by John Cargill in 1973, holds a special place within Scottish heritage as a Clan/Family tartan, reflecting the legacy of the Cargill clan's rich history. The distinctive blue and green hues evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands, while the subtle introduction of pink adds a touch of warmth and elegance, reminiscent of traditional Scottish textiles passed down through generations. According to the Scottish Tartans Authority's Dalgety Collection, the original design featured a missing pink line between its primary colours, but through careful re-creation, this has been meticulously reinstated in woven samples, ensuring the authenticity of this tartan's heritage. As a testament to Scotland's enduring cultural traditions, the Oliver Dress Pink tartan remains an essential part of Scottish identity, reflecting both the clan's ancestry and the country's timeless beauty.

name: Oliver [default]
description: The Oliver Dress Red tartan, designed by John Cargill for the Oliver Society in 1973, is a testament to Scotland's rich weaving heritage. Originally based on the circa 1820 Tweedside formula, this intricate pattern was revived through the connection with Wilson's of Bannockburn notebooks and its subsequent interpretation by Lochcarron weavers. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds significant cultural value for those bearing the Oliver name, evoking the traditions of Scottish cottager weavers from over two centuries ago. The registration notes highlight the tartan's authenticity, linking it to a specific historical era and place, underscoring its importance as a symbol of family identity and heritage. This timeless design continues to be worn with pride by members of the Oliver Society, ensuring the enduring legacy of Scottish tartan-making.

name: Olympic Games
description: The Olympic tartan is a symbol of unity, excellence, and international competition, born from the fusion of sport and tradition at the 1976 Montreal Olympics. This corporate tartan, designed with the iconic five interconnected rings, was originally intended to celebrate global sporting achievement, bringing together nations in a shared spirit of endeavour. With its bold red squares bearing the distinctive ring motif, this tartan represents the coming together of athletes from around the world, their individual colours merged into a powerful symbol of international cooperation and fair play. Its creation, as noted in NOMINDEX by D.C. Stewart, serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Olympics, where tradition meets innovation to inspire greatness on the world stage.

name: Olympicana
description: The Olympicana tartan is a commemorative masterpiece, designed by renowned West Coast Woolen Mill in celebration of Canada's historic hosting of the 1976 Montreal Olympics. This unique and striking pattern proudly bears the iconic Olympic logo, skillfully integrated into a traditional Quebec tartan. Registration notes reveal that this deliberate mashup was an innovative effort to incorporate the Olympic symbol into a distinctly Canadian textile tradition. As a testament to Canadian heritage and sporting excellence, the Olympicana tartan remains an honourable tribute to Montreal's remarkable achievement in hosting the Games. Its non-reversing design ensures an unbroken visual connection to the original motif, serving as a lasting reminder of the event's significance.

name: Oman Regiment; 2nd Pipe Sqn.
description: The Omani Regiment 2nd Pipe Sqn. tartan is a poignant tribute to the military heritage of Oman, with its roots firmly planted in British tradition. Woven by the skilled hands of Lochcarron's expert weavers, this distinctive tartan is registered under the strict guidelines set forth by the Scottish Register of Tartans, signifying its unique cultural significance and connection to the Omani Regiment's storied history as a 2nd Pipe Squadron unit. As a military tartan, it embodies the bravery, sacrifice, and esprit de corps of those who have served in Oman's armed forces. The unassuming yet unmistakable design pays testament to the enduring bond between Oman and the United Kingdom, reflecting the shared values of loyalty, duty, and honour that underpin this special relationship.

name: Oman Royal Army
description: The Royal Army of Oman tartan is a distinguished military pattern, registered by Arthur Mackie of Strathmore Woollen Co., Forfar, to commemorate the Omani Army Pipe Band's inaugural performance at the 2003 Edinburgh Military Tattoo. This unique tartan holds significance not only in its connection to the Omani military heritage but also as an expression of international cooperation and cultural exchange. The design embodies the values of pride, unity, and tradition that are synonymous with Scottish tartans, whilst reflecting the distinct history and identity of Oman. As a registered military tartan, it is subject to the guidelines of the Scottish Tartans Authority, ensuring its authenticity and adherence to traditional standards.

name: Oman Sultanate of
description: The Oman Sultanate of Oliver dress tartan is a distinctive military tartan imbued with deep historical significance, its very fabric woven into the rich tapestry of Scotland's military heritage. Registered as a Pipe Band regimental tartan, this tartan holds pride of place in the Air Force Juniors and is also worn by the renowned Scottish pipes band tradition. Its origins rooted in the Middle East, where Oman was once an independent Sultanate, this tartan reflects the cultural exchange and influences that have shaped Scotland's military traditions over the centuries. As a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage, the Oman Sultanate of Oliver dress tartan is a powerful symbol of excellence, discipline, and tradition.

name: One Account
description: One Account, a corporate tartan designed by Virgin One, embodies the spirit of efficiency and professionalism, perfectly capturing the essence of a business entity that prides itself on streamlined operations. This modern, sleek design is rooted in the advertisement agency's original concept, distilled into a vibrant yet utilitarian motif. The restrictions imposed by the registration notes highlight its corporate roots, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to establish a strong brand identity through their visual presentation. As a testament to the power of branding, One Account tartan exudes modernity and precision, evoking the notion of seamless transactions and streamlined services – values that Virgin One's corporate identity aims to uphold.

name: Ontario Centennial
description: The Ontario Centennial tartan is a unique and captivating fashion tartan, designed by Pik Mills, specifically for the centennial celebrations in 1967. This intricately woven design boasts an exceptionally complex sett pattern, resulting from different warp and weft threads, which distinguishes it from other tartans. Notably, this non-reversing tartan showcases a distinct character that remains unchanged when viewed from either side. According to the Scottish Tartans Society's Count from Scottish Tartans Series 3 No. 2, this tartan was part of an exclusive presentation commemorating the Ontario centennial year. As a fashion tartan, it is likely intended for use in clothing and accessories, such as scarves or kilts, by those who wish to wear a piece of Canadian heritage with pride, while also paying tribute to the country's rich history and tradition.

name: Ontario Northern
description: The Ontario, Northern tartan is a striking District tartan that weaves together the rich heritage of Canada's northern territories. Registered in honour of its creator, Teall/Smith, this unique pattern was born from the colours of the land itself: N, for the local rocks that yielded precious nickel and iron; W, for the snow-capped peaks that stretch across the frozen tundra; Y, for the auroral glow of local gold; G, for the forests and fields that cover vast expanses of wilderness; B, for the crystal-clear lakes and rivers that flow through the heart of this unforgiving yet beautiful landscape; and R, for the indigenous peoples who have called these lands home for millennia. Donated to The Scottish Tartans Society archive by Canadian tartan collector Alex Lumsden in 1967, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the north, where rugged beauty and rich history converge in a vibrant tapestry of colour and tradition.

name: Ontario Provincial
description: The Ontario, Ensign of tartan is a striking representation of Canada's rich history and heritage, specifically its connection to the province of Ontario. Registered in 1965 by Rotex Ltd, this District Tartan was inspired by the Provincial Coat of Arms granted by Queen Victoria in 1868, a symbol that signified Ontario for nearly a century. The tartan's distinctive design features a bold combination of colours: yellow, green, red, black, and brown, each chosen to represent significant elements of the provincial emblem - the three maple leaves, the Cross of St George, the bear, and the moose and deer that adorn the shield. This intricate weave not only pays homage to Ontario's historical roots but also celebrates its natural beauty and iconic wildlife, making it a fitting tribute to this Canadian province.

name: Open Championship 1998
description: The Open Championship (1998) tartan, a Corporate creation by esteemed designer Claire Donaldson of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd's House of Edgar, embodies the quintessential spirit of Scotland's most revered golf tournament. Registered in 2002, this unique and vibrant design is an embodiment of the British Open's enduring legacy, with its rich blues and whites evoking the majestic links courses that host the world-famous championship. As a corporate tartan, it has become synonymous with excellence, sophistication, and sporting heritage, making it an ideal choice for businesses and individuals alike seeking to tap into the tournament's prestigious reputation.

name: Open Championship 2000
description: The Open Championship (2000) tartan is a dynamic corporate design born from a unique collaboration between the Royal and Ancient Golf Club of St Andrews and Mizuno, Japan's renowned sports equipment brand. Created to promote The Open Championship in 2000, this tartan embodies the prestige and tradition of Scotland's most iconic golf tournament. Its distinctive sett, comprising blues, whites, and yellows, pays homage to the game's rich heritage while injecting a modern, sporty flair. As an officially registered corporate tartan, it is now available for use by companies looking to tap into the prestige and exclusivity associated with one of golf's most revered events. A testament to the enduring power of Scottish culture and tradition, this tartan is sure to make a lasting impression on any organisation seeking to connect with the world of golf.

name: Orban-Prentice
description: The Orban-Prentice tartan is a rare and intimate personal tartan, carefully crafted by renowned Scottish weaver Peter MacDonald for his esteemed clients. As a 'Name' tartan, it was specifically created to commemorate the heritage of its bearers, reflecting their family lineage and connection to the clan system that has shaped Scotland's rich history and culture. With no publicly recorded details about its origins or inspiration, this tartan remains an enigmatic testament to the individuality and character of those who proudly wear it, each thread woven with the subtle nuances of a bygone era. Its existence serves as a poignant reminder of the intricate web of family histories, traditions, and loyalties that have been passed down through generations, forever tied to the timeless spirit of Scotland's tartan heritage.

name: Order of the Holy Sepulchre of Jerusalem
description: The Order of the Holy Sepulchre tartan is a poignant and symbolic corporate tartan, rooted in the rich history of Scotland's knightly orders during the Crusades. This distinctive design is said to be based on the iconic Wilsons Priests or Clergy tartan, yet with its own unique twist, evoking the golden hues of Jerusalem and the crimson colour of the cresses worn by Crusaders. The addition of black threads pays homage to the Canons Regular at the Holy Sepulchre, lending a sense of reverence and devotion to the fabric. Designer Ronald Stuart Kinsey has masterfully woven together these threads, resulting in a tartan that exudes a sense of honour, tradition, and spiritual values. With its approval from the Lieutenant of the Order in Scotland, this tartan is sure to be cherished by those who appreciate the enduring legacy of chivalry and brotherhood embodied by this storied knightly order.

name: Oregon State
description: The Oregon State Tartan, designed by Robert Harding in 1999, is a majestic representation of the state's unique landscape and heritage. As an official symbol of the State, this District tartan embodies the diverse colours and textures of Oregon's natural beauty. The blue tone evokes the ocean's waves, while gold nods to the agricultural regions that thrive across the state. Earthy tones of green and taupe evoke the forests and high desert landscapes, respectively, balancing these with fiery crimson hues reminiscent of volcanic pasts. Finally, azure and black bring to life the streams, creeks, wetlands, and snow-capped mountains that define Oregon's dramatic topography. This stunning tartan was adopted by the 72nd Legislative Assembly in 2003 and officially enrolled as the state's tartan in 2017, cementing its place in Oregonian history and cultural identity.

name: Oregon State University
description: The Oregon State University tartan is a vibrant corporate design born from a spirited competition run by the College of Health and Human Sciences, encouraging students to showcase their weaving prowess on a real-world challenge. The resulting tartan, carefully crafted by Krisja Lorenson, now proudly represents the university's spirit among licensed vendors who have secured permission to produce it. This distinctive tartan holds a special place in the hearts of OSU alumni, students, faculty, and fans, who collectively voted online to select the winning design from three finalists. With its unique character, the Oregon State University tartan embodies the institution's values and heritage, making it an ideal choice for those with a connection to the university or looking to pay tribute to its esteemed reputation.

name: Oriel District
description: The Oriel #1 tartan is a proud representation of the historic 'Oriel' region of Ireland, now part of modern South Ulster. Designed by renowned Scottish historian and weaver, Dr Philip D Smith, in 1992, this tartan is deeply rooted in the cultural heritage of the Emerald Isle. As a District tartan, it is an authentic expression of local identity and tradition, acknowledging the region's rich history and distinct character. With its carefully crafted pattern, Oriel #1 pays homage to the unique blend of Scottish and Irish influences that have shaped this storied corner of Ireland. This tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring connections between Scotland and Ireland, while also celebrating the region's unique identity and cultural heritage, now safely preserved for future generations through its registration with the Scottish Tartans Authority.

name: Orion Nebula
description: The Orion Nebula tartan, designed by Pierre Arpin, is a breathtakingly beautiful fashion tartan that embodies the wonder of the night sky. This stunning pattern, inspired by the mesmerising spectacle of the Messier 42 nebula, transports wearers to the celestial realm with its rich, jewel-toned colours. The dominant purple hue evokes the majestic sweep of the nebula's purple-blue wisps, while subtle shades of green, red, and blue bring to life the intricate dance of hydrogen atoms and star-forming gas. As a fashion tartan, this design is perfect for those who appreciate the drama and beauty of astronomy, and its registration as a fashion tartan means it can be worn with pride in modern attire, from scarves to kilts. Its amateur astronomer origins add an extra layer of meaning, connecting wearers to the shared passion and sense of wonder that unites enthusiasts across the globe.

name: Orkney
description: The Orkney tartan, meticulously crafted by Scottish designer Ronnie Hek of Coldstream, pays homage to the unique heritage of these northern islands. Despite its lack of historical precedent in the region, this fashion tartan showcases a rich blend of blues, greens, and yellows that evoke the rugged beauty of Orkney's landscapes. Created with no formal tradition or official recognition, it is inherently modern and avant-garde. As such, it embodies the spirit of innovation and creativity often associated with fashion tartans. With its distinctive colour palette and bold design, the Orkney tartan offers a refreshing alternative to more traditional Scottish patterns, perfectly capturing the sense of adventure and exploration that defines these windswept islands.

name: Orlando City Dress
description: The Orlando Dress, City of tartan is a vibrant and unique tribute to the city's heritage, designed by Eva Brecheen in collaboration with local organisations. As one of four Orlando-inspired tartans, this distinctive sett features a striking ground colour, set against a backdrop of intricate pattern weaving. Originally created for the dress worn by Eva Brecheen herself, this tartan is now worn by those who bear honour and connection to the City of Orlando, while also paying tribute to its esteemed institutions - the fire department in bold red hues, and the police in majestic blue tones. This District tartan embodies the spirit of community and civic pride that defines Orlando's identity, as an integral part of the city's rich tapestry.

name: Orlando City
description: The All as One tartan, designed by pupils at St Stephen's Primary School in Glasgow, embodies the spirit of unity and diversity that defines its school community. With its carefully chosen palette inspired by the flags of 35 nations, this corporate tartan weaves together a vibrant tapestry of colours that reflect the rich cultural heritage of its young designers. The harmony of these hues, symbolising the students' ability to work together in perfect balance, regardless of their backgrounds or beliefs, is both heartening and humbling. As a testament to the power of inclusivity and diversity, this tartan design is a powerful reminder that even in our differences lies the strength of collective endeavour, making it an inspiring addition to any corporate collection.

name: Orlando Fire Department
description: The Leitrim County, Crest Range tartan is a stirring tribute to the rich heritage of rural Ireland, its subtle nuances echoing the rugged beauty of the Emerald Isle's verdant landscapes. As one of a set designed by Viking Technology Limited in 2005 as part of a series celebrating Irish counties and national identity, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the rolling hills and timeless traditions of Leitrim. Yet, its story is also one of complex ownership - having originally been created for USA Kilts Inc, which acquired it in December 2012, restricting its wider reproduction without their explicit consent. Despite these stipulations, the Leitrim County, Crest Range tartan remains an evocative testament to Ireland's storied textile traditions and the enduring legacy of its storied districts.

name: Orlando Police Department
description: The Orlando Police Department tartan is a vibrant representation of civic pride and community spirit, proudly bearing the badge of a storied institution in the heart of Florida. Designed by the late Eva Brecheen, one of four bespoke Orlando tartans she created for the city or its organisations, this Corporate tartan is a masterful blend of tradition and innovation. While the fundamental sett remains consistent across all four tartans, Brecheen's genius lies in her subtle yet deliberate variations on the ground colour, cleverly reflecting the unique character of each entity: green for the City of Orlando, white for dress wear, red for the fire department, and blue for the police service. This thoughtful nod to diversity and distinction has secured its place as a cherished emblem of Orlando's identity, symbolising honour, duty, and devotion to public service.

name: Orvis Sports Company
description: The Orvis Sports Company tartan is a vibrant and enduring corporate fashion pattern, woven with the rich heritage of Scottish textiles and the storied legacy of the iconic American sporting brand. Registered as a Corporate Fashion tartan for the Orvis Sporting Co in Manchester, Vermont, this distinctive design pays tribute to the company's commitment to excellence in outdoor apparel and equipment. With its unique blend of colours and subtle sett, this tartan is not only a statement piece for fans of the brand, but also a testament to the enduring tradition of Scottish weaving and the timeless appeal of traditional tartans. Its corporate roots notwithstanding, the Orvis Sports Company tartan embodies the adventurous spirit of the great outdoors, evoking images of rugged landscapes, crisp wilderness, and the joy of discovery that has defined the Orvis name for generations.

name: Otago District
description: The Otago tartan, designed by Vilma Ruth Nelson, holds a rich history as a tribute to the pioneering settlers who first arrived in New Zealand's South Island in the late 19th century. Originally commissioned by the Otago District Council, this distinctive district tartan weaves together elements of Scottish heritage with the region's own unique cultural identity. The fabric tells the story of early Crofters and Shepherds from Scotland, who were among the first to stake a claim on the land that would eventually become Otago. As other nationalities joined them in their quest for fortune, the tartan became a symbol of the diverse community that flourished in the Goldfields region. Today, this remarkable tartan is licensed by The Suit Surgeons Ltd, New Zealand, and its beauty continues to evoke a sense of pride and connection to the land's storied past.

name: Ottawa City
description: The Ottawa tartan, designed by Mrs Jean Docton (corrected to D.C. Stewart in some sources), is an unusual and striking example of a District tartan, born out of a unique commission by the Centennial Committee of the City of Ottawa in 1966. This symmetrical sett, comprising two distinct blocks - one featuring navy and gold hues on alternating stripes, the other with azure and white - tells the story of Canada's capital city. The registration notes reveal that Docton was an award-winning textile designer and weaver who brought this distinctive design to life, which was subsequently adopted as the Official Tartan of Ottawa by order of the Council in 1966. Although it is no longer commercially produced, the Ottawa tartan remains a testament to the enduring spirit of Canadian heritage and tradition, its bold colours evoking the country's rich history and cultural diversity.

name: Over Mountain District
description: The Over Mountain tartan is a poignant commemoration of the courageous Scots who braved the unforgiving terrain of the South Appalachian Mountains to establish new lives. Designed by Katie A Boyd, this distinctive tartan tells the story of the region's rich history, specifically the exploits of the 'Over Mountain' men who outwitted the British forces in 1780 during the War of Independence. In recognition of their bravery, this tartan marks an important milestone in the heritage of the Scots who settled in the area, forever etched in the annals of American history. By adopting this commemorative tartan, wearers pay tribute to a pivotal moment in the region's past, connecting with the land, its people, and the unwavering spirit that defined their ancestors' struggles and triumphs.

name: Owen of Wales
description: The Owen of Wales tartan is a distinctly modern creation, born out of a recent phenomenon in Welsh heritage wear. Originally designed by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys, to be woven specifically for Wales Tartan Centres, this name tartan has become increasingly popular since its introduction around 1998. While not rooted in traditional Welsh history or genealogy, the 'of Wales' designation serves as a nod to its origins and a badge of honour for those who wear it. Characterised by its unusual thread count and warp/weft pattern, this tartan sets itself apart from other Celtic designs, reflecting the innovative spirit of modern Welsh textile traditions. As with many contemporary tartans, the Owen of Wales is not without controversy, and its inclusion in this index acknowledges its commercial origins rather than any historical or ancestral significance. Nonetheless, it remains a vibrant representation of Welsh cultural identity and a testament to the enduring power of traditional craftsmanship.

name: Oxford Dress
description: The Oxford University Dress is a distinctive corporate tartan, skillfully woven with a rich tradition in mind. Originally registered as sister to the historic #2652 Scottish tartan, this modern creation pays homage to Scotland's storied heritage while embracing its global appeal. Designed by Albion Highland for Oxford Ltd, this tartan was likely crafted with the esteemed University of Oxford at its core, reflecting the institution's values and academic excellence. Its corporate status makes it a fitting choice for businesses seeking to associate themselves with the university's prestige, while its modern design ensures a timeless appeal that transcends traditional Scottish attire.

name: Oxford University
description: The Oxford University tartan is a striking Corporate design, meticulously woven to evoke the academic excellence and prestige of one of the world's most revered institutions. Created by Albion Highland for Oxford Ltd, this tartan was formally registered with the Scottish Tartans Society, solidifying its place in the rich tapestry of British heritage. Characterised by its distinctive colour palette, including midnight blue, emerald green, and crimson red, this tartan is a fitting tribute to the university's enduring legacy. As a Corporate design, it is designed for formal occasions and corporate wear, allowing individuals associated with Oxford University to proudly wear their affiliation on their sleeves – or rather, their kilt. This tartan's significance extends beyond its functional use, however, as it serves as a powerful symbol of tradition, excellence, and the pursuit of knowledge that defines this iconic institution.

name: Pacific
description: The Pacific tartan, designed by visionary weaver Aljean of Vancouver, embodies the spirit of modernity within Scotland's rich cultural heritage. As a fashion tartan, it has been crafted to add a touch of contemporary flair to any ensemble, yet its very existence is a testament to the enduring connection between Scottish tradition and global creativity. Originally registered in the Johnston Collection, this sample showcases the colours - a deliberate departure from Aljean's original vision - serve as a reminder that even the most carefully considered designs can benefit from refinement. The Pacific tartan's inclusion within the Fashion category highlights its suitability for modern fashionistas seeking to incorporate subtle nods to Scotland's storied past into their wardrobe, while the designer's intentions underscore the ongoing evolution of Scottish textiles in the 21st century.

name: Paget [default]
description: The Paget tartan is a storied family heirloom, born from the threads of Scottish heritage and tradition. Designated as a Clan/Family tartan, this distinctive pattern holds special significance for those bearing the Paget name, weaving a connection to their ancestors and roots in Scotland's rich cultural tapestry. Weaving its way back to MacKay, DCS #137, the Paget tartan boasts an intricate design that showcases Mr Paget's skill as a weaver, with suggestions from esteemed Scottish textile expert Peter MacDonald bringing this classic pattern to life. Although woven by another skilled hand, Peter MacDonald's contribution serves as a testament to the enduring power of Scotland's traditional weaving traditions. Today, the Paget tartan remains an honourable part of Scottish heritage, its storied past and technical precision ensuring it will continue to inspire generations to come.

name:
Paisley District
[AKA] Cathcart of Paisley
[AKA] Sempill of Paisley
description: The Paisley tartan, created by Alan C. Drennan in 1952, is a quintessential District tartan steeped in Scottish heritage. Originally designed to win first prize at the prestigious Kelso Highland Show, it has since become synonymous with the historic town of Paisley and its eponymous inhabitants. As a family tartan, it is treasured by those bearing the name, evoking a sense of pride and connection to their ancestral roots. This iconic design showcases Drennan's skill as a weaver, its subtle variations in tone and texture hinting at the rich history and traditions that lie behind it. Despite being exhibited under different sett names, including 'Drennan' by D.C. Dalgliesh, the Paisley tartan remains an enduring symbol of Scottish craftsmanship and the timeless appeal of traditional tartan design.

name: Palatine Union
description: The Palatine Union tartan, a bespoke creation by renowned designer Traepischke Graves, holds a deeply personal significance as it was specially designed for the union of Trapper Graves and Steve Lalor's wedding celebration in Seattle. Drawing inspiration from its namesake, an old Scottish name with roots in the region, this unique tartan pays homage to the couple's heritage while also reflecting their Seattle-based connection. As a Name tartan, it is a distinctive and exclusive pattern, reserved for individuals who wish to personalise their own tartan identity. Though not affiliated with any particular clan or family legacy, its significance lies in its creation as a bespoke tribute to love and partnership, weaving together the threads of two people's lives into a beautiful, one-of-a-kind fabric.

name: Palm Beach Gardens Police
description: The Palm Beach Gardens Police tartan is a distinctive corporate design born from the vibrant colours of South Florida, as embodied by its namesake city. Registered in 1994 with the Tartan Educational & Cultural Association, this tartan's creation was spearheaded by Jan Crook, expertly weaving together a palette that echoes the subtropical warmth and optimism of Palm Beach Gardens. With its unique thread count specified at registration, this tartan is an authentic representation of a modern corporate identity, one that pays homage to the cultural heritage of its eponymous city while also serving as a versatile tool for businesses looking to forge their own distinct identity.

name: Palmer Arnold
description: The Palmer, Arnold tartan is a vibrant and iconic corporate design born from a most unlikely union: the legendary golfer Arnold Palmer and William Smith of Rubicon Footwear. First registered as a proprietary tartan for use on Palmer's products, this distinct design embodies the enduring spirit of America's greatest golfer. With a palette of bold colours - red, yellow, white, green, and black - inspired by the iconic Arnold Palmer logo, the Palmer, Arnold tartan is an authentic celebration of American sporting heritage. Its corporate origins notwithstanding, this tartan exudes warmth and enthusiasm, evoking memories of sunny golf courses and championship victories.
