As a testament to its enduring appeal, the Palmer, Arnold tartan has become synonymous with Palmer's brand, cementing its place in the pantheon of Scottish textile tradition.

name: Palmer Edward
description: The Palmer, Edward tartan is a poignant commemorative design steeped in Canadian history and Scottish heritage. Registered in 1889, this tartan tells the story of Edward Palmer, a prominent figure who opposed the Confederation of Canada, serving as the premier of Prince Edward Island during a pivotal time in the country's formation. Weaving his name into the fabric of history, this tartan bears testament to the intricate relationships between Scotland and its Canadian colonies. Commissioned by West Coast Woollen Mill, the design is thought to have originated from the renowned 'Fathers of the Confederation', a group whose namesake tartans evoke the rich cultural legacy of Scottish settlers in North America. Now preserved within the Johnston Collection, this tartan serves as a lasting tribute to Palmer's enduring legacy and the complex tapestry of history that binds Canada and Scotland together.

name: Palmer General W.J.
description: The Palmer, General W.J. corporate tartan is a tribute to the legacy of William Jackson Palmer, the visionary founder of Colorado Springs, Colorado, whose enduring impact on the city's history still resonates today. Designed by Rev. John B. Pahls in 1995, this distinctive tartan was specifically created for the Colorado Springs High School/Palmer High School Alumni Association, solidifying its connection to the community that Palmer helped shape. With its unique characteristics, carefully crafted by Mr Pahls to evoke a sense of civic pride and tradition, the Palmer tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the city's rich heritage, weaving together threads of local identity and Scottish textile tradition in a symbol of lasting honour.

name: Papi (Anthony) personal; Uitwaaien Papi
description: The Uitwaaien Papi tartan is a vibrant and eclectic Name tartan, expertly woven by Anthony & Jocelyn to reflect the rich cultural heritage of its creators. Named after the Dutch phrase "uitwaaien", meaning "to air out", this tartan design celebrates the blending of diverse influences from Italy, Scotland, France, and Canada, resulting in a truly unique and captivating pattern. The colours - a testament to the family's love of nature - evoke the rugged beauty of Cape Breton's hills and shores, where the wearers' ancestors once walked and breathed in the fresh air. As a Name tartan, it is reserved for those with this specific tartan heritage, serving as a lasting connection to their Scottish roots and the stories that have been woven into its very fabric.

name: Papua New Guinea
description: The Papua New Guinea tartan is a vibrant and symbolic corporate design, born from a request to esteemed members of Papua New Guinea for their Pipes & Drums ensemble. Woven by skilled hands at Selkirk, this distinctive pattern draws inspiration from the country's national flag, proudly incorporating its colours into a unique and striking tartan. Recognised as a Corporate tartan, it has been carefully crafted for use in formal events and ceremonies, reflecting the nation's rich heritage and cultural identity. Conceived by John Hocknull J.P., this tartan is not only a testament to his skill as a designer but also a nod to the country's history and its people's deep connection to their traditions.

name: Park [default]
description: The Park tartan is a proud emblem of Scottish heritage, born from the desire of its namesake, William D. Park, to create a distinctive identity for himself and his family. Registered as a clan tartan, this traditional weaving embodies the values and history of those bearing the name Park, allowing wearers to honour their ancestry through their attire. Keith Lumsden's expert design brings together threads of rich blue, crimson, and gold, evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of Scotland's Highland countryside. However, it is worth noting that this tartan holds a subtle restriction: its wearing is reserved for those with a genuine familial connection to William D. Park, ensuring the authenticity and dignity of this revered clan symbol.

name: Park Estate
description: The Park Estate tartan, a masterpiece crafted by Lochcarron of Scotland, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish tradition. This District tartan, reserved exclusively for Mr John Foster's esteemed estate, embodies the grandeur and history of its namesake. Designed with meticulous care, this tartan weaves together a palette of deep blues and greens, evoking the rolling hills and serene lochs that surround Park Estate. With restrictions in place to ensure its exclusive use on Mr Foster's lands, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the intricate connections between Scottish culture, family legacy, and the natural beauty of the Highlands. By its very creation, the Park Estate tartan honours the timeless traditions of Scotland's tartan heritage.

name: Parker Dress; USA
description: The Parker Dress tartan is a unique blend of Scottish heritage and personal flair, reflecting the blending of traditional tartan-making with contemporary creativity. Originally designed by David J. Parket, this clan tartan holds special significance for individuals bearing the surname Parker, yet its versatility allows it to be worn by anyone of that name. The palette takes inspiration from the American flag's bold colours, complemented by a touch of gold from David's high school days, symbolising the fusion of American roots with Scottish tradition. With no restrictions on wear, this tartan invites those who bear the Parker name to proudly don its distinctive pattern, evoking a sense of connection to their heritage while also embracing individuality and modern style.

name: Parker USA
description: The Parker tartan, named after its designer David J. Parker, is a unique blend of heritage and personal flair, reflecting the blending of Scottish tradition with American pride. This Clan/Family tartan may be worn by anyone bearing the name, yet it holds a deep personal significance for its creator, who wove together iconic colours from the American flag - rich reds, whites, and blues - with a touch of gold, symbolising his own high school years. Born out of a desire to connect with his roots while also celebrating his adopted homeland, this tartan embodies the spirit of cultural exchange and identity that defines modern Scotland's global community.

name: Parkhead District
description: The Parkhead tartan is a striking example of Scottish heritage and tradition, born from the creative vision of Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts. As a District tartan, it holds significant cultural importance, paying homage to the historic districts of Glasgow, where its design takes inspiration from the Celtic Football Club's iconic colours. According to the registration notes, this 'Universal' tartan bears an uncanny resemblance to that of Scotland's beloved football club, whose stadium proudly sits in the heart of Parkhead. This nod to local identity not only pays tribute to the community but also serves as a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish sporting culture. With its rich history and cultural significance, the Parkhead tartan is a true representation of Glasgow's proud heritage, weaving together tradition, community, and football fever in perfect harmony.

name: Parkin (Daniel) personal
description: The Parkin tartan is a poignant fusion of two cultures, carefully woven together by its designers, Daniel and Kirsty Parkin. This unique Name tartan, registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, tells the story of a union between Scotland's rich heritage and Yorkshire's storied past. The subtle blend of purple for Scotland, white to evoke the white rose of Yorkshire, and blue, paying homage to the St Andrew's cross and the sea, which holds significance for both nations, creates a compelling visual narrative. As a personal tartan, it is a celebration of love, blending the colours of two countries in a meaningful way, symbolising the coming together of two hearts and cultures. This beautiful tartan, now held in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Collection, serves as a testament to the enduring power of heritage and tradition.

name: Parma
description: The Parma tartan, designed by the esteemed West Coast Woolen Mill, is a stylish and timeless fashion choice that embodies the essence of Scottish heritage. As a fashion tartan, it has been carefully crafted to make a statement on the catwalk or in everyday life, its vibrant colours and intricate patterns evoking the sophistication of Italy's rich cultural history. The Parma tartan's distinctive design, featuring subtle shades of blue, green, and yellow, is deeply rooted in the traditional Scottish weaving techniques that have been perfected over centuries. With no restrictions on use, this stunning tartan can be worn with pride by anyone looking to add a touch of glamour and tradition to their wardrobe, while also paying homage to the rich cultural exchange between Scotland and Italy.

name: Parr
description: The Parr tartan, proudly registered by West Coast Woolen Mill, is an enduring representation of Scottish heritage and family legacy. Originally designated as a Clan tartan, its rich history and cultural significance are woven into every thread. While it may be viewed in both a fashion and clan context, the Parr's true essence lies in its familial connections, passed down through generations. Recognised by the Tartans Society, this tartan is a poignant reminder of Scotland's storied past, with subtle variations evident in its sett pattern. Produced at West Coast Woolen Mills in Canada, the Parr remains an authentic and time-honoured design, carefully crafted to showcase the intricate weave of Scottish tradition.

name: Partick Thistle Football Club
description: The Partick Thistle Football Club tartan is a vibrant and energetic design, woven in the iconic Lochcarron style, which has been a staple of Scottish textiles for generations. Registered in 2002, this Corporate tartan was commissioned by Newline Products of Kirkintilloch, a company with a strong connection to the local community. The thistle motif, which is often associated with Scotland's patron saint, Saint Andrew, takes centre stage in this striking design, paying homage to the city of Glasgow's beloved football club. While the designer's identity remains anonymous, it is clear that this tartan was created to represent a sense of civic pride and loyalty, reflecting the club's values of community, passion, and dedication. Today, the Partick Thistle Football Club tartan continues to fly the flag for Glasgow's favourite team, adding a touch of Scottish heritage and tradition to corporate attire and accessories.

name: Pasteur [default]
description: The Pasteur tartan, designed by Marie-Claude Fortier, is a deeply personal and storied weave, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's textile tradition. This unique pattern, born from a 19th-century portrait of Louis Pasteur's mother, tells a fascinating tale of family legacy and artistic inspiration. The shawl or cloak depicted in the painting, rendered in soft pastels, has been carefully transcribed by Fortier into a modern tartan design that respectfully captures its essence. As an "Other" category, this tartan is not affiliated with a specific clan or historical lineage, yet it remains a poignant tribute to the enduring power of family stories and cultural legacy. With restrictions carefully noted in the registration notes, this tartan is now available for those seeking a meaningful connection to France's celebrated scientist, Louis Pasteur.

name: Paterson (John) personal; Pearl o' the Tay
description: The Kilkenny County, Crest Range tartan is a majestic representation of the rich heritage of Ireland's easternmost county. Registered as a District tartan by Viking Technology Limited (now Tartan Web Scotland Ltd) in 2005, it is one of a series inspired by the country's diverse counties and national motifs. This distinctive design pays homage to Kilkenny's proud history, with its characteristic colours evoking the rolling green landscapes and sturdy stone architecture that define the region. Although ownership has been transferred to USA Kilts Inc since 2012, the tartan remains an integral part of Irish cultural tradition, available for use by those who wish to honour the county's legacy - but please note that reproduction without explicit consent is strictly prohibited.

name: Paterson #2
description: The Paterson (Dalgleish Version) tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's storied clans, specifically the Dalgleish family, whose heritage is woven into every thread of this majestic design. Designed by D.C. Dalgliesh Ltd., a renowned authority on Scottish tartans, this variation pays homage to the original Dalgleish tartan, showcasing the subtle nuances that have made it an iconic emblem of Scottish identity. As a Clan tartan, the Paterson is steeped in tradition and history, carrying the family's honour and legacy forward through generations. Although subject to restrictions for weaving by D.C. Dalgliesh Ltd., this tartan remains a cherished expression of Scottish heritage, one that evokes the rugged beauty of the Highlands and the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's ancient clans.

name: Paterson [default]
description: The Paterson Clan Tartan is a deeply personal and historic weave, steeped in tradition and heritage. Designed in 1993 by Lowell W Patterson, an American who was drawn to his Scottish roots, this tartan represents the connection between the clan and its individual bearer. With its unique colour palette and carefully balanced composition, the Paterson Clan Tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of the Scottish clans. Its creation, while not directly linked to a specific Scottish family or landholding, reflects the pride and sense of identity that defines the clan system. As a personal tartan, it can be worn by those who feel a connection to their heritage, serving as a symbol of honour and loyalty to one's ancestral roots.

name: Paton
description: The Paton tartan, born from the creative genius of Haggart of Aberfeldy, tells the story of an Aberdeenshire family's rich heritage. This distinctive Name tartan is steeped in history, with roots dating back to the 1930s and a likely connection to the late Mr John Robertson. Discovered in 1993 at P and J Haggart, weavers in Aberfeldy, it was probably woven again in 1952, bringing it into our present day. Characterised by a subtle blend of blue, green, yellow, black, brown, and red, this tartan bears an uncanny resemblance to the Ancient Gordon, previously known as the Gordon of Abergeldy, adding depth to its narrative. With its unique sett and muted colour palette, the Paton tartan is a poignant tribute to the family who commissioned it, their story now woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition.

name: Patterson Blue
description: Paterson Blue, a timeless Name tartan, holds a profound place in Scottish heritage, reflecting the deep roots of its bearers within the community. Registration notes indicate that this distinctive tartan was created as a second tartan for the family of John Patterson, a kin to those who had already been registered with the iconic Red Patterson tartan. The assumption of a shared designer implies a harmonious blending of artistic vision and clan tradition, underscoring the importance of familial heritage in Scottish textiles. Paterson Blue's unique character, rooted in the history and culture of its namesake family, makes it an honourable testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish clansmen who have worn their tartan with pride for generations.

name: Patterson Red
description: The Patterson, John tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans. Specifically designated as a family tartan, it is a symbol of pride and identity for those bearing the name, evoking a strong sense of belonging to a storied lineage. With its distinctive muted colour palette, this tartan design tells the story of a Scottish legacy that spans generations. Unfettered by geographical boundaries, it has transcended national borders to become an integral part of modern attire and home decor, worn with honour by those who bear the name in the United States, where it was formally registered in 1993. As a tangible link to Scotland's storied past, this tartan design embodies the enduring spirit of Scottish culture and tradition.

name: Paxton #2
description: The Paxton tartan is a deeply personal and romantic design, woven with love and legacy by the esteemed brothers Geoffrey and Richard Paxton. This exclusive name tartan was carefully crafted for the 2002 wedding celebration of its creators, where it first took centre stage amidst joyous festivities in Aberdeen. As such, the Paxton tartan holds an honourable place in Scottish heritage, symbolising the union of two families bound together by love and tradition. Its unique threads weave a narrative of family, commitment, and community, making it a cherished possession for those fortunate enough to wear its distinctive pattern, evoking feelings of warmth, nostalgia, and timeless devotion.

name: Payne of Wallins Creek
description: The Payne of Wallins Creek tartan, personally registered by Luther Payne, embodies the quintessential Scottish spirit of heritage and community. Originally intended as "Payne of Wallins Creek to Edinburgh", this tartan was ultimately accepted for registration with a nod to its American roots, reflecting the blend of cultures that shape our shared identity. Black threads represent the unyielding strength of one's family lineage, while purple denotes compassion and understanding - essential qualities in any heritage tapestry. White and gold hues signify truth, justice, and prosperity, echoing Scotland's storied history of values such as fairness, equality, and economic flourishing. This unique tartan design serves as a testament to the enduring bonds between Scotland and its fellow nations, weaving together threads of tradition, community, and shared human experience.

name: Payne [default]
description: The Payne tartan is a storied and storied heritage pattern, borne from the esteemed clan family synonymous with strength and courage. Designated by renowned weaver Robin Birch for all individuals bearing the name Payne, this distinctive tartan is steeped in tradition and symbolism. Originally crafted by Connell Reid Kiltmakers of Blairgowrie, this tartan has been carefully woven to commemorate the Payne lineage, evoking a sense of pride and connection to Scottish heritage. Although it is no longer kept in stock, enthusiasts can still commission D.C. Dalgliesh of Selkirk to specially weave their own version of this cherished pattern, ensuring its continued relevance and celebration for generations to come, as an enduring testament to the Payne family's unwavering dedication to their ancestral legacy.

name: Peachy Keen
description: The PeachyKeen tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate design, carefully crafted by Frank Noel Gordon to embody the ethos of a holistic sports/fitness brand from Scotland's Fife coast. Originally registered as a company tartan for the Kirkcaldy-based firm, PeachyKeen, this distinctive pattern has been created to reflect the brand's colours and values, while also paying homage to Scotland's rich textile heritage. Characterised by its unique and modern colour palette, PeachyKeen is an exciting addition to the world of corporate tartans, demonstrating the innovative spirit and commitment to wellness that defines the PeachyKeen brand. As a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish tartanry, this design is sure to inspire a sense of pride and connection among those who wear it, while also serving as a powerful symbol of brand identity for companies seeking to tap into Scotland's cultural heritage.

name: Peacock Samantha
description: The Peacock tartan, registered by Samantha Peacock as part of her BSc honours degree in clothing design and manufacture, is a vibrant and eye-catching design that embodies the spirit of its namesake bird. This Clan/Family tartan, which can be worn by anyone with the name, boasts a stunning combination of blues, greens, and golds that evoke the majestic plumage of the peacock. While the exact shades used are subject to interpretation, the LA thread count ensures a rich and intricate texture that adds depth and visual interest to any garment. With restrictions in place requiring permission from the designer for commercial use, this tartan is a treasured family heirloom that holds significant cultural significance, connecting its wearers to their heritage and legacy.

name: Peacock (Personal)
description: The Peacock tartan is a richly woven tapestry of Scottish heritage, born from the marriage of five distinct tartans held dear by the Peacock family. This bespoke Name tartan, created at their request, pays homage to the family's connection to Maxwell, Maclean, Ferguson, MacBeth, and Pailsey District - all celebrated through intricate patterns and colours that evoke a deep sense of tradition and history. Inspired by the ancestral roots of the Peacocks in Scotland, particularly during their time in the Pailsey District until the late 1800s, this tartan design masterfully weaves together threads of Scottish heritage to create a unique and lasting family legacy. Expertly crafted by Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan is now preserved in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Collection, serving as a testament to the enduring power of family tradition and cultural identity.

name: Pearson [default]
description: The Pearson tartan is a deeply rooted emblem of Northumbrian heritage, its origins dating back to 1951 when it was discovered in Cumbria, England. Donated to the Scottish Tartans Society by A.H. Pearson of Egremont, this historic tartan was once a treasured family heirloom, passed down through generations of the Pearson clan. Characterised by a predominantly bluish grey ground, the Pearson tartan showcases a rich and muted palette that evokes the rugged beauty of the Cumbrian moors. Its classification as a Clan/Family tartan underscores its significance to Scottish history and tradition, serving as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Pearson family's ancestral homeland.

name: Peebles Royal Burgh
description: The Peebles Beltane Centenary tartan is a vibrant and meaningful District tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Designed by the esteemed Royal Burgh of Peebles Callants Club, this tartan was created to commemorate a pivotal event - the celebration of 100 years of the Peebles Beltane Committee, an ancient Celtic festival that marks the renewal of community spirit with the relighting of fires from a central flame on May day. This District tartan is a testament to the rich history and cultural significance of the Royal Burgh of Peebles, where this cherished tradition originated. With its distinctive colours and carefully crafted pattern, the Peebles Beltane Centenary tartan pays homage to the past while celebrating the present, serving as a poignant symbol of community, renewal, and the unbreakable bonds between people.

name: Peeper #2
description: The Peeper tartan, named after its creator Matthew A.C. Newsome, is a distinctive name tartan with roots in New Orleans' rich cultural heritage. Originating from Quinn Peeper's bespoke design, this tartan has been registered for use by all individuals bearing the surname Peeper, symbolising family and clan ties that transcend geographical boundaries. With its unique colour palette and intricate pattern, the Peeper check embodies the city's unique blend of Scottish and American influences, reflecting the complexities of identity and heritage in a melting pot culture. As a symbol of lineage and shared ancestry, this tartan design serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring legacy of Scottish tradition in North America, waiting to be woven into the fabric of family histories and stories.

name: Peeper
description: The Peeper tartan is a unique and intriguing design born from the creative vision of Matthew A.C. Newsome, carefully crafted to represent the name Quinn Peeper, an individual with roots in New Orleans, Louisiana. As a Name tartan, it is designated for use by those bearing the surname Peeper, signifying a sense of heritage and tradition that transcends geographical boundaries. With its distinctive pattern, this tartan embodies the cultural significance of its namesake, while also alluding to the city of New Orleans, which has played a significant role in shaping Quinn Peeper's identity. Although it was initially designed as a standalone tartan, Newsome went on to create an additional 'Peeper Check' variation, further highlighting the complexity and nuance of this distinctive design, which now serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Peeper name.

name: Pendleton (Oregon) personal; Dress
description: This iconic Corporate Tartan, designed by Annette Hoeffel in collaboration with Pendleton Woolen Mills, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's renowned textile industry. Registration notes reveal its origins from Pendleton Mills, established in 1863, a company synonymous with quality woollens and traditional tartans. The 'Pendleton Dress' Tartan is virtually identical to an original Scottish Tartans Authority reference (#2467), with a subtle distinction between the tan line on the traditional design replaced by a vibrant yellow line for this unique corporate variation. This distinctive pattern not only pays homage to Scotland's tartan tradition but also serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of Pendleton Mills, whose family business has consistently delivered exceptional woollens and timeless tartans that have captivated hearts and industries alike for generations.

name: Pendleton (Oregon) personal; Hunting
description: Pendleton Hunting is a sophisticated corporate tartan designed by renowned textile artist Annette Hoeffel for Pendleton Mills, a esteemed family business established in 1863. This striking tartan was originally registered with the Scottish Tartans Society, but its near-identical duplicate at #2468 suggests an error on the society's part. Despite this, the Pendleton Hunting tartan has become an iconic representation of quality and heritage, synonymous with the prestigious manufacturer that has been weaving traditional patterns since the 19th century. With a subtle, muted palette featuring a light fawn-coloured tan over check, this corporate tartan is perfect for those who wish to add a touch of understated elegance to their business attire or corporate identity, while paying homage to America's rich Scottish heritage.

name: Penman, Grey (Personal)
description: The Penman Grey, designed by Russell Penman of St Fillans, is a Personal tartan born from the joyous occasions of its creator's life. Commissioned for his graduation and wedding, this subtle yet striking design pays homage to Kyle, a family name that has been intricately woven into the fabric of the Penman clan's history. While bearing resemblance to another American Personal tartan, the Penman Grey remains distinctly unique in its own right, bearing testament to the innovative spirit of its designer. By registering as a Name tartan, the Penman Grey is reserved for individuals who wish to carry this special heritage on their own personal garments, providing an opportunity for them to honour their family's legacy while forging their own identity within the tradition of Scottish tartanism.

name: Penman [default]
description: The Penman tartan is a rich and storied heritage pattern, steeped in tradition and tied to the esteemed Penman clan family. Designed by William W.C., the Penman tartan is a testament to the intricate weaving traditions of Scotland's Highlands. This Clan tartan was carefully registered by the Scottish Tartans Authority, ensuring its authenticity and legitimacy, and features a distinctive sett that showcases the artful doubling of thread count to reveal its beauty. With its complex weave and subtle colour palette, the Penman tartan is a fitting tribute to the history and culture of Scotland's clan system, evoking the proud heritage of those who bear this name.

name: Pennsylvania
description: The Pennsylvania tartan, designed by Bill Johnston, holds a significant place in the annals of Scottish heritage, reflecting the state's rich history and cultural ties to the United Kingdom. This District tartan was inspired by the Black Watch regiment, which played a pivotal role at the Battle of Bushy Run in 1763, securing western Pennsylvania and the Ohio Country for British interests. As the allegedly State Tartan, it is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's tartan traditions in North America. While awaiting official recognition from the state, this tartan design remains an important symbol of the historical connections between Scotland and its American counterpart, evoking the storied past of Scottish settlers who helped shape the region's identity.

name: Perratt
description: The Perratt tartan, registered under the name category, holds a special place in the hearts of those who bear it, as it is a personal connection to one's heritage. This unique pattern, crafted by Geoffrey Highland Crafts, is a testament to the rich tapestry of Scottish tradition, woven from threads of history and identity. The restrictions surrounding this tartan serve as a poignant reminder of the responsibility that comes with carrying such a significant piece of family legacy. Assumed to be Personal in its registration, it is likely that the Perratt tartan has been passed down through generations, telling a story of love, loyalty, and tradition. Its significance extends beyond mere aesthetics, representing a deep sense of honour and belonging to those who wear it.

name: Perry Arisaid
description: Perry Arisaid is a deeply personal tartan, borne of the distinct heritage and traditions of the Perry family clan. This unique pattern, carefully crafted by the renowned designer Ross Henderson of Stirling in 1982, is an authentic recreation of the original Perry tartan, registered at #1212 with the Scottish Tartans Authority. With its distinctive blue-grey hues and intricate weave, this tartan pays homage to the rich history and cultural significance of Scotland's clan system, where family heritage and identity are woven into the very fabric of tradition. As a personal tartan, Perry Arisaid holds profound emotional value for those who bear it, serving as a tangible connection to their ancestral roots and a symbol of enduring family honour.

name: Perry Dress
description: The Perry Dress tartan, registered by Dr J.R. Perry of Alberta with the Scottish Tartans Society in 1986, is a bespoke Clan tartan steeped in family heritage and tradition. Originally designed by Ross Henderson for Stirling, its distinctive maroon hue sets it apart from traditional reds, imbuing the fabric with a unique warmth and character reminiscent of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry. This intimate family tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish clans, woven into the very fabric of Dr Perry's personal history and passed down through generations. As registered by the esteemed Scottish Tartans Society, this tartan holds significant cultural value, serving as a tangible link to the country's storied past and the proud traditions that continue to shape its identity today.

name: Perry Hunting
description: The Perry Hunting (Green) tartan, a personal family legacy woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage, tells the tale of a storied clan's history and traditions. Registration notes reveal that this distinct pattern was inspired by Dr J.R. Perry, an Alberta-based historian, who drew upon the original Perry tartan registered in 1982 by Ross Henderson of Stirling. The Society approved its registration in 1986, solidifying its place within Scotland's rich tapestry of clan traditions. Characterised by a blend of earthy tones and natural hues, this tartan design embodies the values of pioneering spirit, heritage, and kinship that have long been synonymous with Scottish culture.

name: Perry [default]
description: This enigmatic tartan, registered under the designation 'Unidentified #2', shrouds itself in mystery, its origins veiled by the passage of time. Yet, as recorded in the Wilson of Bannockburn letter, dated 1810, it is clear that this intricate pattern held significance for some Scottish family or individual, warranting formal registration. Without a specified designer, its creation remains an unsolved enigma, leaving room for speculation about the person or clan behind this captivating design. Nonetheless, as part of Scotland's rich tapestry, 'Unidentified #2' stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of traditional tartan weaving, with its unique character and subtle nuances evoking the timeless heritage of the Scottish Highlands.

name: Perry Golf
description: The Perry Golf tartan, woven by renowned Scottish textile experts Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the spirit of luxury travel and exclusivity. Registered for corporate use, this distinctive tartan was specifically designed to reflect the high-end clientele of PerryGolf, a distinguished Scottish travel company that caters to discerning golf enthusiasts. With its unique colour palette and intricate weave, this tartan is suited for luxurious furnishings, uniforms, and other corporate attire, instantly conveying an air of sophistication and refinement. As a testament to Scotland's rich heritage in textile craftsmanship, the Perry Golf tartan pays homage to the country's storied traditions while serving as a modern symbol of excellence and prestige in the world of hospitality and tourism.

name: Perth #2
description: Perthshire or Drummond of Perth is a richly storied tartan, steeped in history and tradition. As a District tartan, it holds a special significance for the region of Perthshire, from which its name is derived. Its intricate pattern is said to be connected to the legendary Stewart of Fingask, allegedly left behind by Prince Charles Edward Stuart at his Scottish stronghold, Fingask, in 1746. The tartan's unique combination of red and blue hues evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands, while its subtle variations pay homage to the storied past of the local clans. With no restrictions on use, this timeless design is open for anyone to wear with honour, serving as a poignant reminder of Scotland's cultural heritage and its enduring spirit.

name: Perthshire Tourist Board
description: The Perthshire Tourist Board tartan is a vibrant celebration of Scotland's rich heritage, born out of a partnership between Brian Wilton, Executive Member of Perthshire Tourist Board, and renowned designer Peter MacDonald. Registered as a District tartan, its purpose is deeply rooted in the tourism industry, reflecting the warm hospitality and natural beauty that defines this beloved region. As a testament to its enduring popularity, the tartan has become an integral part of tourist workers' attire and visitor's souvenirs alike. Now immortalised in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, the Perthshire Tourist Board tartan embodies the spirit of Scotland's welcoming heartlands, where tradition meets innovation and local culture is proudly showcased to visitors from around the world.

name: Peter Pan
description: The Lochcarron of Scotland 'Peter Pan' corporate tartan is a timeless and iconic design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scottish tradition. Originally created to support the esteemed Great Ormond Street Hospital for Sick Children, this tartan holds a special place in the hearts of those who wear it, as it pays homage to J.M. Barrie's beloved character, Peter Pan. The story behind its creation is as poignant as it is fascinating, with Barrie donating his rights to the hospital and securing their future through his will. Today, the royalties from this tartan continue to support the hospital's life-saving work, making every wearer a part of a special legacy. With its unique blend of colours and intricate weave, the 'Peter Pan' tartan is a symbol of hope, courage, and charity, evoking the values of Scottish culture and the enduring spirit of Peter Pan himself.

name: Peters Chief
description: The Peter of Lee Chief tartan, designed by Harry Lindley, is a richly evocative testament to Scotland's intricate heritage of clan identity and tradition. Originating from a 1996 Lochcarron swatch labelled 'Peter Chief', it tells the story of Leslie Peters, Baron of Lee, who elevated his family's tartan status through an innovative revision that reasserted yellow as a central stripe on a lighter blue ground. This subtle transformation, born from a desire to distinguish the chief's personal sett from that of lesser individuals, resulted in a tartan that not only reflects the evolving nuances of Scottish clan tradition but also celebrates the regal dignity of the Baron of Lee. As part of the esteemed Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority, this unique design serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's storied history and the intricate cultural currents that continue to shape its textiles today.

name:
Peter of Lee (Personal)
[AKA] Peters [default]
description: The Peter of Lee tartan is a dignified and historic design steeped in Scottish heritage, accredited by the prestigious Scottish Tartans Society in 1988. Created for E Leslie Peter, Baron of Lee, this tartan bears testament to its namesake's noble lineage. As a Category Name tartan, it is specifically designated for use by individuals bearing the name Peter, and its unique pattern is an integral part of their family legacy. With its distinctive colour palette and carefully woven threads, the Peter of Lee tartan evokes a sense of tradition and honour, recalling a bygone era of Scottish aristocracy and distinguished titles. Designed by Harry Lindley for Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this tartan remains an important part of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, a tangible connection to the country's storied past.

name: Phillips of Wales
description: The Phillips of Wales tartan is a modern creation born out of the growing popularity of traditional Welsh attire, thanks in part to the pioneering efforts of Wales Tartan Centres since 1998. Designed by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, now sadly closed, this unique tartan stands out from its Celtic counterparts with an unconventional thread count and warp-weft composition. While often associated with clan heritage, the 'of Wales' descriptor is purely a nod to its origins, rather than indicative of historical or genealogical significance. As such, its inclusion in this register serves more as a testament to its widespread adoption and cultural relevance, rather than any claimed territorial or ancestral ties. Nonetheless, this striking tartan design continues to captivate those drawn to the rich heritage of Welsh textile traditions, inviting wearers to proudly don its distinctive pattern and celebrate their connection to this storied region.

name: Phillips [default]
description: The Phillips tartan is a storied heritage fabric steeped in family tradition and clan history, woven with pride by its designers Maxine Scott of House of Tartan and Rachael Phillips. Registered for the Phillips family worldwide, this distinctive tartan is deeply rooted in Scottish culture, evoking a sense of unity and identity among those who bear the name. Its origins lie within the esteemed Clan/Family register, where it has been meticulously crafted to reflect the unique characteristics and values of its namesake. Available exclusively for families bearing the Phillips surname, this exquisite tartan pattern is a treasured symbol of heritage and kinship, proudly worn by generations to come.

name: Phinn
description: Phinn, Antony Thomson's eponymous tartan, is a subtle yet striking Name tartan that embodies the quiet elegance of personal heritage. Registered in 2005 for a bespoke silk stole, Thomson's design has since been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition, with its re-registeration in 2007 for a heavyweight wool kilt testament to its enduring appeal. This understated yet distinctive tartan is a celebration of individuality and cultural identity, reflecting the quiet strength and resilience that defines the Scottish spirit. As a Name tartan, Phinn holds significant personal significance, symbolising the unique heritage and history of its wearer, while its technical precision and attention to detail demonstrate Thomson's mastery of traditional weaving techniques.

name: Phoenix Police Honor Guard
description: The Phoenix Police Honor Guard tartan is a majestic, corporate design created by Sean Connell, paying tribute to the prestigious unit's esteemed role within the Phoenix Police Department. Commissioned specifically for ceremonial and official purposes, this striking tartan embodies the department's unwavering dedication to service, honour, and tradition. As a registered Corporate tartan, it holds significance in formal settings such as ceremonies, graduations, and public events, where the unit's precision and pageantry are showcased. Notably, the PPHG reserves the right to approve or deny authorisation for its use, underscoring the importance of this tartan in representing the department with dignity and pride. By embracing this unique design, Connell has masterfully woven together elements of Scottish heritage and municipal tradition, resulting in a tartan that exudes strength, resilience, and unity – embodying the very essence of the Phoenix Police Honor Guard's noble mission.

name: Pictou County
description: Kirsty Anderson's enchanting 'Pictou County' fashion tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's northeast, where the rugged landscape meets the warmth of Highland hospitality. Inspired by the picturesque Pictou County in Nova Scotia, Canada, this distinctive tartan weaves together a narrative of local pride and tradition. Registration notes reveal that Kirsty Anderson, renowned for her fashion designs, was commissioned to create this pattern by Whigmaleeries of Pictou, evoking a sense of community and connection to the land. With its unique colour palette and carefully crafted sett, 'Pictou County' tartan is an ode to the region's storied history and the people who call it home, inviting wearers to don a symbol of their own cultural heritage with pride.

name: Pienaar
description: The Pienaar tartan is a deeply personal and intimate design, carefully crafted by its creator, Rob Pienaar. As a Name tartan, it holds great significance for the designer and his immediate family alone, who are permitted to wear and weave this unique pattern in their honour. This bespoke tartan is not open to public sale or wider use, serving as a private badge of identity and heritage for those privy to its existence. With no detailed background information available on the design's inspiration or origins, it remains a tantalising enigma, a testament to the enduring power of personal tradition and family legacy in Scottish textile culture.

name: Pierce [default]
description: The Pierce tartan is a vibrant and storied heritage pattern, woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition. Designed by renowned designer Dr. Philip D, in collaboration with Dr. Albert Pierce, this distinctive tartan has been registered to represent not only the esteemed surname Pierce, but also its variants Pearce and Pearse. With roots dating back to February 2000, this carefully crafted design is an honour to bear for those who proudly claim descent from this distinguished clan. While it may favour a range of family lines across Scotland, the Pierce tartan remains deeply rooted in Scottish heritage and tradition, evoking a sense of pride and connection to the land and its people that has been passed down through generations.

name: Pike
description: The Pike tartan is a deeply personal and distinctive name tartan, created by renowned designer Theo Pike to commemorate his family's heritage. This unique and striking pattern features a darker, richly textured background, punctuated by bold and vibrant hues that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's highlands. As a registered name tartan, it holds significance not only for the individual who bears the name, but also for their clan or sept affiliation. With its carefully considered colour palette and thoughtful design, the Pike tartan is a testament to the enduring power of tradition and identity in Scottish culture. Its creator, Theo Pike, has carefully crafted this tartan to reflect the values and history of his family's name, ensuring that it will remain a treasured symbol of heritage for generations to come.

name: Pilette (Kinnear) personal
description: The Kinnear, Barony of (Personal) tartan is a storied and intimate design woven from the rich heritage of Scotland's Fife region. Commissioned by Michael Jean George Pilette, Baron Kinnear, and crafted by Blair Urquhart, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the local lordship that once held sway over Wormit. Featuring an understated yet distinctive combination of colours inspired by the Duke of Fife and incorporating overcheck elements from the Kinnear Arms, this tartan is a symbol of family honour and lineage. As such, it falls under the category of 'Name' tartans, indicating its association with a specific noble house or personal identity. Although restricted to those bearing the Kinnear arms, this tartan remains an essential part of Scotland's cultural tapestry, preserving the history and traditions of the region for future generations.

name: Pinehurst Resort
description: The Pinehurst Resort tartan is a bespoke corporate design that weaves together the rich heritage of North Carolina's finest resort with Scotland's timeless tradition of tartan weaving. Reconstructed by renowned designer Phil Smith, Jnr, in collaboration with the esteemed Gleneagles Hotel equivalent on the east coast, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the Pinehurst Resort's storied history. Inspired by a meagre yet fascinating fragment retrieved from an old postcard in the mid 1990s, this tartan now proudly represents the corporate identity of its namesake, symbolising the enduring spirit of hospitality and luxury that defines Pinehurst Resort. With its unique provenance and meticulously crafted design, this tartan serves as a testament to the power of tradition and innovation in creating a distinctive visual heritage for generations to come.

name: Pinewoods Jubilee
description: The Pinewoods Jubilee tartan is a vibrant celebration of heritage and community spirit, born from Joel LaMarre's innovative design. This Corporate tartan was created to commemorate the 50th Anniversary of the Royal Scottish Country Dance Society session at Pinewoods Camp in Plymouth, Massachusetts, USA - a milestone marking the enduring bond between Scotland's traditional folk culture and American friends. The resulting pattern is a masterful blend of colour and craftsmanship, evoking the rustic charm of New England's Pinewoods while respectfully nodding to Scotland's iconic tartan traditions. This unique corporate design is now available for businesses seeking to tap into the rich cultural significance of Scottish heritage, making it an ideal choice for companies looking to showcase their values and connection to the global community that celebrates the joy of country dancing.

name: Pinney's of Scotland
description: Pinney's of Scotland is a vibrant and distinctive corporate tartan designed by Keith Lumsden in 1996, born from the collaboration between the Scottish Tartan Society and Pinney's company to promote their Smoked Salmon brand. This striking pattern, now available for corporate adoption, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's iconic industry, while also reflecting its modern commercial appeal. By embracing this tartan design, companies can honour the country's rich fishing traditions and proudly display a unique Scottish identity. With its bold colours and dynamic weave, Pinney's of Scotland is an evocative representation of Scotland's maritime past, making it an attractive choice for businesses looking to establish a strong Scottish flavour in their brand.

name: Pitcairn Heritage
description: Pitcairn Heritage is a stunning corporate tartan that pays homage to the rich history of the Pitcairn family, whose heritage spans centuries. With its unique blend of blues, greens, and yellows, this tartan evokes the rolling hills and rugged coastlines of Scotland's majestic landscape. Recognised as a clan tartan from 2004, it is steeped in tradition and signifies a deep connection to the Pitcairn family's Scottish roots. Although its exact specifications are still being verified, the Scottish Tartans Society has confirmed that the design features an intricate palette of azures, greens, and yellows, expertly woven by Diene P. Duncan, the tartan's original designer. As a corporate tartan, Pitcairn Heritage offers a versatile and sophisticated alternative for businesses looking to connect with their heritage, while also serving as a proud symbol of family identity and tradition.

name: Pitcairn Hunting
description: The Pitcairn Heritage Hunting tartan is a rich and storied corporate pattern, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's wilderness through its distinctive red and blue hues. Originally registered as part of the Pitcarin Heritage collection (#2199), this hunting-inspired design has been adapted for modern commercial use by Diene P. Duncan. Weaving itself into the fabric of business attire, this tartan seeks to honour the rich heritage of Scotland's hunting traditions, while also paying homage to the trust that once bore its name - the Pitcairn Heritage Trust, although now largely defunct (August 2005). With its bold, graphic pattern, the Pitcairn Heritage Hunting tartan is sure to make a statement on the corporate landscape, proudly carrying the spirit of Scotland's wild and storied past.

name: Plaid Wine
description: The Plaid Wine tartan, expertly crafted by West Coast Woolen Mill, is a stunning addition to the fashion world, boasting a rich, vibrant hue reminiscent of a warm summer evening in Scotland. This dynamic pattern, categorised as Fashion tartan, is designed to make a statement and add a touch of effortless elegance to any outfit. Although not reversible, the Plaid Wine's non-reversing design ensures that its unique beauty remains consistent, with no need to flip or rotate the fabric to appreciate its full splendour. A testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage, this tartan is a celebration of the country's iconic patterns and colours, which have been carefully preserved and presented by the Scottish Tartans Authority's esteemed Johnston Collection.

name: Platt [default]
description: The Platt tartan is a testament to the rich tapestry of Scotland's heritage, its origins steeped in history as part of the Provost Macbean Collection, one of the country's most revered repositories of traditional tartans. As a Clan/Family tartan, the Platt has been woven with pride by Scottish weavers for generations, its intricate patterns and subtle colour nuances reflecting the enduring bond between community and tradition. With no specific designer credited, it is evident that this tartan has evolved through oral traditions, passed down through the generations before being formally registered. Its modern colours, as discerned from the Scottish Tartans Society's notes, bring a sense of continuity with the past, while slight variations in colour strip highlight the nuanced artistry of weavers like James Cant, whose work continues to inform our understanding of Scotland's iconic tartan heritage.

name: Plowman (Steven) personal
description: The Plowman tartan, with its rustic charm and rich history, embodies the spirit of rural England's agricultural heritage. This symmetrical adaptation, born from an earlier asymmetrical South Uist design circa 1730, is a poignant testament to the evolution of traditional Scottish textiles in Hampshire. As a Name tartan, it holds significance for Stephen J F Plowman's family and, by extension, anyone privileged enough to bear his name, underscoring the importance of personal connection and heritage. With its complex interplay of colours, carefully woven into a harmonious whole, this tartan design speaks to the hardy folk who tilled the land and worked the earth with their hands - a fitting tribute to the humble ploughman's craft.

name: Plummer [default]
description: The Plummer tartan, a personal clan tartan with deep-rooted heritage, holds a special place within Scottish tradition. This unique design was first registered by David C. Dalgliesh, showcasing the intricate characteristics of the tartan. Over time, it has been woven and worn with pride by families across generations, including notable individual Marjorie Warren, who painstakingly handwove a scarf in this very tartan. As a clan tartan, the Plummer design is steeped in history and cultural significance, symbolising the connection to one's ancestral roots. With its distinctive pattern, evoking the rugged landscapes of Scotland, this tartan serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of family heritage and tradition.

name: Plymouth Armada 400
description: The Plymouth Armada tartan is a stirring tribute to Scotland's rich maritime heritage, specifically commemorating the 400th anniversary of the triumphant defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588. This striking tartan was designed by Malcolm Campbell of Edinburgh Woollen Mill to pay homage to this pivotal moment in Scottish history. As a Commemorative tartan, it serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's proud naval traditions and its long-standing connection with the British Empire. The restrictions associated with this tartan reflect its sensitive subject matter: while not strictly prohibited, its use should be undertaken with respect for the Armada's storied past, ensuring that the tartan is worn honourably to evoke the bravery and seafaring prowess of Scotland's sailors through the centuries.

name: Police College Tulliallan
description: The Police College Tulliallan tartan is a distinctive Corporate design born from the esteemed Tulliallan Police College, nestled in the heart of Fife, Scotland. Registration notes attribute its creation to Frank Noel Gordon, an accomplished Scottish textile expert. This tartan's significance lies not only in its origins as a badge for the college but also as a symbol of professionalism and dedication within the UK policing force. By adopting this specific tartan, organisations can evoke a sense of tradition, respect, and authority, while paying homage to Scotland's rich heritage of tartan craftsmanship. With no restrictions on use, the Police College Tulliallan tartan is now available for those seeking to convey their affiliation with the esteemed institution, as well as for any organisation looking to instil professionalism and discipline into their corporate identity.

name: Polish
description: The Polish tartan, designed by David McGill for International Tartans, holds a profound cultural significance as a symbol of identity and heritage for people worldwide who trace their ancestry to Poland or hold a deep affinity for the nation. As a District tartan, its origins are rooted in traditional Scottish textile design, yet it has been carefully adapted to represent the rich history and folklore of Poland. Approved by Consul-General Alexander Dietkow, this distinctive tartan is reserved exclusively for permission from the designer, David McGill, underscoring its importance as a cherished emblem. Weaving this tartan requires careful consideration, as it serves as a poignant reminder of the complex connections between Scotland and Poland, forging a lasting bond between nations and communities.

name: Pollock [default]
description: The Pollock tartan, named after its eponymous clan and family connections, is a revered and storied textile rich in Scottish heritage. This traditional Clan tartan, registered by Dalgliesh, D.C., is deeply rooted in history, drawing inspiration from the Vestiarium Scoticum of 1842 and incorporating elements of the Maxwell sett, where white supplants the traditional green. The design's origins are closely tied to the Pollocks, a Scottish Lowlands family serving as feudal dependants of the Maxwells, with J.C. Thomson's skilled hand contributing significantly to its evolution. As such, this tartan stands as a testament to Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, weaving together threads of history, clan loyalty and tradition.

name: Pope of Wales
description: The Pope of Wales tartan is a unique and modern design that pays homage to Welsh heritage, though its historical roots are relatively recent. Registered as a Name tartan, it was conceived by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill in Powys, a now-defunct textile mill that played a significant role in popularising the tradition of wearing Clils (Cilt) in Wales since the late 1990s. Notably distinct from traditional Celtic tartans, which predominantly feature odd-numbered threads and unconventional warp and weft combinations, this design showcases an innovative approach to tartan weaving. As with many contemporary designs, its inclusion in this index does not guarantee historical or genealogical authenticity, but rather serves as a testament to the enduring appeal of Welsh identity. Obtaining consent from Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea, prior to weaving, underscores the importance of respecting cultural heritage and acknowledging the commercial origins of this design.

name: Popular Fancy
description: The Popular tartan is an enduring testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, with its origins shrouded in mystery and intrigue. Despite being classified as an 'Other' category, this distinctive tartan has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition for generations, evoking memories of community and kinship among those bearing it. Its connection to the MacDougall clan is well-documented, yet the involvement of other prominent Scottish weavers, such as Wilsons of Bannockburn, adds to its mystique. Now registered with the Scottish Tartans Society, this tartan's provenance is slowly unraveling, revealing a complex tapestry of history and symbolism that speaks volumes about Scotland's storied past.

name: Porcelanosa
description: The Porcelanosa tartan, commissioned by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, is a striking example of modern corporate design, carefully crafted to reflect the sleek sophistication of one of Spain's leading ceramic tile manufacturers. Registered specifically for the opening of their Glasgow showroom, this tartan was created to showcase the company's international presence and commitment to style. With its unique colour palette, inspired by the earthy tones of terracotta and the luminosity of glazed ceramics, the Porcelanosa tartan is a testament to the fusion of traditional Scottish weaving techniques with contemporary flair. While restricted to corporate use, this tartan has already become synonymous with luxury and refinement, making it an attractive choice for businesses seeking to make a statement in Scotland's design capital.

name: Porcupine
description: The Porcupine tartan, designed by Kathleen Sinclair, is a fascinating example of modern Scottish fashion heritage. This striking pattern, while its origins remain unclear, has captured the imagination of those drawn to its unique aesthetic. As a Fashion tartan, it does not bear the traditional associations with Clan or territorial ties that often accompany other tartans. Instead, its existence is largely tied to the realm of style and individuality, suggesting a connection to the broader cultural landscape of 20th-century Scotland. Despite the lack of documentation on its specific inspiration, the Porcupine tartan remains a captivating addition to the rich tapestry of Scottish textile traditions, inviting wearers to draw upon the country's storied history and timeless beauty in their sartorial choices.

name: Porcupine, City of
description: This richly woven District tartan, affectionately known as Northern Ontario or the City of Porcupine, proudly embodies the rugged beauty and pioneering spirit of one of Canada's most iconic regions. Registration notes reveal its origins in the 19th century, designed to commemorate the area's distinctive geographical features and thriving mining community. The name "Porcupine" is a testament to the region's unique landscape, with the porcupine rock formation being a prominent geological feature. This tartan's association with Northern Ontario serves as a poignant reminder of Canada's rich history and cultural heritage, reflecting the resilience and adaptability of its people who have called this vast and unforgiving terrain home for generations.

name: Port Authority of NY & NJ
description: The Port Authority of NY & NJ tartan is a vibrant and modern corporate design that pays homage to the iconic institutions of New York City's Hudson River waterfront. Registration notes reveal that this distinctive pattern was created by Clair Hunter, a talented Scottish-born weaver, specifically for The Pipers Cove - a Highland dress shop in Kearney, New Jersey, which catered to local pipe bands. The tartan's significance extends beyond its corporate origins, as it now serves as a symbol of the rich cultural heritage of Scottish-American communities across the region. Its design is deeply rooted in traditional Scottish weaving techniques, yet its utilitarian purpose as a corporate identity fabric sets it apart from more ceremonial tartans, making it a unique and fascinating addition to Scotland's storied textile tradition.

name: Port Moresby City Pipes & Drums
description: Port Moresby City Pipes & Drums is a vibrant corporate tartan that pays homage to the rich cultural heritage of Papua New Guinea, its capital city Port Moresby. Designed by John Hocknull J.P., this unique tartan is inspired by the national flag's colours and wove with accuracy using the same sett as Mo. 7235, one of the country's traditional patterns. The transposed colours add a distinctive twist to the original design, reflecting the blending of cultures that defines Papua New Guinean identity. As a corporate tartan, it is perfect for organisations, clubs, or individuals seeking to connect with this fascinating Pacific nation and celebrate its spirit. By embracing this remarkable tartan, its wearers will honour the city's history, culture, and resilience, while proudly showcasing their connection to the beautiful island of Papua New Guinea.

name: Porteous [default]
description: The Porteous tartan is a revered clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition, designed specifically for the esteemed Porteous family association by Captain Stuart Davidson, founder of the Scottish Tartans Society. This distinctive tartan pattern is woven with pride by those who wear it as an honour to their ancestral roots. Registered in recognition of its cultural significance, the Porteous tartan holds a special place within the world of Scottish textiles, symbolising the values and history of the Porteous clan. Captains Stuart Davidson's and Barry Porteous' collaboration resulted in a uniquely crafted tartan that reflects the family's distinguished heritage, now available for wear by those who wish to pay tribute to their surname's rich tradition.

name: Portmeirion District
description: The Portmeirion tartan is an iconic corporate design, carefully crafted for the esteemed Portmeirion Group PLC, a renowned English pottery company based in Stoke on Trent. With its unique characteristics, this sett has become synonymous with the brand's heritage and craftsmanship. Originally created by halving a traditional pattern, the resulting design showcases a distinctive blend of colours and textures that reflect the company's rich history. As a corporate tartan, it is intended to evoke the sense of tradition, quality, and excellence that Portmeirion embodies in its products. The absence of designer credit is a testament to the set's enduring appeal, as its beauty lies not in individual creativity but in its connection to a storied company with a legacy that spans generations.

name: Portrait, The
description: Portrait, The is a fashion tartan designed by Aljean of Vancouver, its beauty rooted in the rich heritage of Scottish textiles. This vibrant design takes inspiration from the tradition of heraldic portraiture, evoking the likenesses of noble families adorning ancient coats of arms. With shades slightly at odds with those documented in Scotland's esteemed Johnston Collection, Portrait, The remains a bold and modern interpretation of Scotland's iconic tartan heritage, perfect for fashion enthusiasts seeking to add a dash of Scottish flair to their wardrobe.

name: Portree Blue; Dance
description: Portree Blue, a dynamic Fashion tartan, was designed by Strathmore Woollen Company Ltd with the intention of capturing the energetic spirit of dance in the picturesque town of Portree on the Isle of Skye. This vibrant design features an intricate pattern of blues and greens that evoke the movement of the dancers' footsteps and the rhythmic sounds of the traditional Scottish ceilidh music. Registration notes indicate its origins as 'Strathmore Dancers' Team', a nod to the iconic Strathmore Dancers, a renowned dance troupe known for their energetic performances at Portree's Highland Games. With this tartan, the wearer is invited to embody the lively and carefree essence of Scottish dance culture, connecting them with generations of dancers who have proudly worn the tartan in celebration of tradition and community.

name: Portree Check
description: The Portree Check tartan, registered with District category, bears testament to the rich heritage of the Isle of Skye, where its namesake village is situated. Dr D.G. Teall's design pays homage to the rugged landscape and strong traditions of the region. While its exact origins are unclear, this tartan appears remarkably similar to the iconic Portree tartan used on Pringles chips, suggesting a possible influence from commercial production rather than traditional Scottish weaving practices. Nonetheless, Strathmore Woollens' association with the design lends credibility to its authenticity as a genuine District tartan, reflecting the island's unique cultural identity and reinforcing the importance of preserving Scotland's distinctive textiles for future generations.

name: Portree District
description: The Portree tartan is a captivating representation of Scottish heritage, hailing from the idyllic district of Portree on the Isle of Skye. Originally designed with its unique character in mind, it's possible to categorise this tartan as either a District or Fashion pattern, given its distinctive personality. The creation of Pringles of Inverness is a fascinating footnote to its history, but what truly sets the Portree apart is its enduring connection to the region. A visit to the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection serves as a tangible link to its past, while the mention of 1986 in NOMINDEX suggests a wider cultural significance that continues to be felt today.

name: Potts
description: The Potts tartan is a timeless and storied design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's north-eastern borders. Named after its creators, the Potts family, whose ancestry dates back to the 11th century, this tartan weaves together threads from their own history with those of allied clans, Elliott, Home, and McKnight. With azure and gold at its core, reminiscent of sun-kissed Scottish hillsides, this tartan's subtle nuances are a testament to the intricate tapestry of family ties and cultural exchange that has shaped Scotland's most iconic patterns. As a Name tartan, it holds particular significance for blood relatives of the Potts clan, who can proudly wear their family crest with permission from Stephen, Neill, Connor, or David Potts. This treasured design is a poignant reminder of Scotland's enduring legacy of tradition and kinship.

name: Poulain League
description: The Poulain League tartan, designed by Keith Lumsden in 1994, is a captivating corporate tartan with strong Celtic roots, forged through a unique cultural exchange between Scotland and Brittany, France. Originally intended for a Celtic group from Brittany, this distinctive tartan is now used in corporate settings to convey a sense of unity and shared heritage among members. The design's intricate patterns evoke the rich history of both Scottish and Breton cultures, reflecting a symbiotic blend of traditions that transcend geographical boundaries. By adopting the Poulain League tartan, companies can tap into this cultural significance, fostering a strong sense of identity and community among their employees.

name: Howells of Wales
description: The Howell of Wales tartan is a modern yet deeply rooted design that pays homage to the rich heritage of Wales. Created by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys, this distinctive tartan was specifically commissioned for Wales Tartan Centres in 1998, marking its introduction as a growing force in Welsh cultural revival. Characterised by unusual thread numbers and warp/weft variations, this Celtic pattern stands out from traditional designs, yet still embodies the timeless spirit of Scotland's ancient textile traditions. The "of Wales" designation serves as a badge of origin, acknowledging the design's connection to Wales' unique history and culture. Notably, the tartan's registration notes caution that its use does not confer historical or genealogical credibility, underscoring the importance of respecting Wales' cultural boundaries. Today, this vibrant tartan has become an integral part of modern Welsh identity, with enthusiasts proudly donning it as a symbol of national pride and heritage.

name: Presbyterian Synod of Living Waters
description: This Corporate tartan, registered in 1993 by Sally T Gay, is a striking representation of American Presbyterian heritage, specifically that of the Presbyterian Synod of Living Waters. Its distinctive pattern, woven with meticulous attention to detail, evokes the rich traditions of Scottish weaving while paying homage to the Synod's Christian values and mission. As a Corporate tartan, this design has been created for use in business and professional settings, where its unique visual identity can help promote unity and affiliation among organisations connected to the Presbyterian Church of the United States of America (PCUSA). With its origins rooted in 19th-century American Presbyterian tradition, this tartan remains an important symbol of community, faith, and shared values among those who bear it.

name: Presley of Lonmay
description: The Presley of Lonmay tartan is a vibrant and eclectic fashion tartan, woven with a deep sense of Scottish heritage and connection to the iconic music legend, Elvis Presley. Registered in 2003 by Michael King of Philip King Ltd, this distinctive tartan was created as a tribute to the 18th century ancestors of the King of Rock 'n' Roll, who were discovered to hail from the small village of Lonmay in north Aberdeenshire. As a fashion tartan, the Presley of Lonmay boasts a rich and varied colour palette, with deep blues and greens evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscapes. With its unique blend of historical and cultural significance, this stylish tartan is sure to make a statement on anyone who wears it, proudly proclaiming their connection to this fascinating piece of Scottish heritage and music legend.

name: Presley of Memphis
description: Presley of Memphis, a vibrant fashion tartan, pays homage to the enduring legacy of Elvis Presley. Inspired by the iconic 'America' sett, originally presented to US First Lady Betty Ford in 1976, this adaptation weaves together a rich narrative of American music and Scottish heritage. Brian Wilton and Rob Kingsley's design subtly incorporates Elvis's favourite colour pink and gold threads, evoking the legendary musician's numerous Gold Discs. The tartan's colours also nod to Elvis's birthdate, with narrow white threads representing August 16th, and his death month, December 8th. With its distinctive US flag hues and thoughtful incorporation of pink and gold, Presley of Memphis is a unique tribute to the King of Rock 'n' Roll, perfect for fashion enthusiasts and fans alike.

name: Press & Journal
description: The Press & Journal tartan is a vibrant and modern corporate motif, expertly woven by Carol Howie in celebration of the Highland Year of Culture. This distinctive pattern reflects the heritage of Scotland's iconic newspaper, the Press & Journal, which has been a stalwart of the nation's media landscape for over a century. By incorporating the company's core colours into this tartan design, Howie masterfully distils the essence of the Press & Journal's identity and shares it with those who bear the pattern. The Corporate category ensures that this tartan is not only worn with pride by its designers but also serves as a powerful symbol of professionalism and civic pride, connecting wearers to the rich history and traditions of Scotland.

name:
Prestoungrange [default]
[AKA] Prestoungrange Dolphinstoun
[AKA] Prestoungrange Wills
description: Prestoungrange, a dignified Clan tartan born from the Scottish heritage of one Baron's legacy, tells the story of family ties and historical influence. Designed by Keith Lumsden for Gordon Wills, Baron of Prestoungrange, in 1999, this intricate pattern weaves together elements of Kerr, Morrison, and Grant tartans, honouring the ancestral connections that defined the barony. Initially reserved for those bearing the name Wills, it was later adopted as a District tartan by the Prestoungrange Barons Court in 2004, recognizing the traditional lands and families bound to this noble title. With its rich, complex design, Prestoungrange embodies the values of Scottish tradition and clan identity, inviting wearers to proudly claim their heritage and connection to this storied barony.

name: Rice of Wales
description: The Rice of Wales tartan is a distinctive name tartan born from the growing popularity of wearing the Cilt in modern Wales, a tradition introduced by Wales Tartan Centres in 1998. Designed by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys, this unique tartan stands out from traditional Celtic patterns due to its unusual thread counts and colour schemes, featuring almost exclusively odd-numbered threads. The 'of Wales' prefix is a nod to the design's origins, rather than a claim to historical or genealogical significance, and as such, its inclusion in this index serves primarily to acknowledge its modern creation. With the consent of Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea, prior to weaving, the Rice of Wales tartan is a testament to the evolving nature of Scottish heritage, embracing contemporary design while respecting the country's rich textile traditions.

name: Pride of Wales
description: Pride is a vibrant fashion tartan designed by Sheila Daniel for Wales Tartan Centres, reflecting the growing popularity of the Cilt tradition in modern Wales. Originating from the Welsh language, the 'C' spelling pays homage to the country's unique heritage. This distinctive tartan stands out from other Celtic designs due to its unconventional thread count and colour palette. While it may not hold traditional historical or genealogical significance, Pride proudly wears its "of Wales" badge, signifying its connection to this vibrant nation. The designer's innovative approach has made this tartan a modern favourite among those embracing Welsh culture, making it an excellent choice for anyone looking to showcase their national pride through fashion.

name: Pride of New Zealand
description: The Pride of New Zealand tartan is a vibrant tribute to the country's rich cultural heritage, woven from the threads of its diverse population and majestic landscapes. Designed by Ivan Coward, a renowned bespoke tailor, in collaboration with John Clark of Alliance Textiles, this District tartan tells the story of Aotearoa's unique blend of multicultural identity, sporting prowess, and natural beauty. The palette of black, grey, and white - reminiscent of the iconic 'All Blacks' rugby team, the country's multifaceted society, and the snow-capped peaks that dot its mountains - pays homage to New Zealand's distinct spirit. With a license held by The Suit Surgeons Ltd for distribution, this tartan is a symbol of national pride, ready to be worn with honour by Kiwis from all walks of life.

name: Pride of Norway
description: The Pride of Norway tartan is a stylish and modern fashion design inspired by the rugged beauty of Norway's natural landscapes. Registered in 1998, this tartan was created by Norwegian-born designer Rolf Winther-Larsen of Scottish Products Ltd to evoke the nation's proud heritage and cultural identity. With its bold, vibrant colours, reminiscent of the midnight sun and Northern Lights, this fashion tartan is a testament to Norway's unbridled spirit and pioneering history. The design is a Lochcarron swatch, indicating its connection to the renowned Scottish textile company known for producing high-quality wool tartans. By wearing the Pride of Norway, one honours the country's rich traditions and cultural values, while also making a bold fashion statement that showcases their personality and individuality.

name: Pride of the Clyde
description: The 'Pride of the Clyde' tartan is a vibrant fashion choice that embodies the spirit of Scotland's iconic River Clyde, which has long been the lifeblood of Glasgow and its people. This dynamic tartan, registered as a fashion design, is woven with bold colours and intricate patterns, evoking the city's rich history and cultural heritage. Although the identity of its creator remains unknown, the 'Pride of the Clyde' tartan stands as a testament to Scotland's enduring tradition of textile artistry and craftsmanship. Its registration notes remain shrouded in mystery, but this striking design is sure to make a lasting impression on those who wear it, proudly proclaiming their affiliation with Glasgow and its people.

name: Pride of Yorkland
description: The Pride of Yorkland tartan is a vibrant and elegant fashion tartan, designed by the renowned Scottish textile company Lochcarron of Scotland. This striking design is steeped in tradition and heritage, its bold colours and intricate patterns evoking the rich history of the City of York. As a fashion tartan, it is perfect for adding a touch of sophistication to any outfit, from formal evening wear to smart business attire. With no restrictions on its use, the Pride of Yorkland tartan can be proudly worn by anyone who wishes to embrace their inner Scot and showcase their connection to this storied city. This beautifully crafted tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage and a fitting tribute to the proud spirit of the people of York.

name: Prince Charles Edward Stuart; #2
description: This exquisite tartan, officially registered as 'Prince Charles Edward (Edinburgh)', holds a rich historical significance tied to the 18th-century Highland leader Bonnie Prince Charlie.
