The intricate patterns woven together represent fragments from a plaid worn by the prince during his brief sojourn in Edinburgh in 1745. According to legend, he presented this cherished garment to Susanna, Countess of Eglinton, who then shared its portions amongst her seven daughters, leading to their eventual distortion into altered forms - one even being transformed into slippers. This captivating tartan has been meticulously reconstructed and is now part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's esteemed collection, paying homage to the enduring legacy of Prince Charles Edward and the storied heritage of Scotland's tartaned traditions.

name:
Prince Charles Edward Stuart; #3
[AKA] Earl of Moray
description: The Stewart, Prince Charles Edward tartan embodies the storied legacy of Scotland's noble clans, with its roots firmly planted in history. Originally part of the Royal Stewart sett, this variant features a striking reduction in the iconic red square, a nod to Wilsons of Bannockburn's influence on the design. This Other category tartan has been woven for generations, first appearing in print in their 1819 Key Pattern Book, and later adopted as the regimental tartan of the 72nd Duke of Albany's Own. While its origins are shrouded in mystery, it is known to have been worn by Prince Charles Edward himself, as attested to by W & A Smith's 1850 publication 'The Clan and Family Tartans of Scotland'. With a design richly steeped in tradition, this tartan remains an enduring symbol of Scottish heritage and pride.

name: Prince Charles Edward Stuart; #5
description: This enigmatic tartan is steeped in history, its origins tracing back to a fragment of a plaid discovered at Blair Castle, a stately residence in Perthshire, Scotland. The mysterious design, attributed to being worn by none other than Prince Charles Edward, the infamous Jacobite leader, holds great significance for those fascinated by the complexities of Scottish heritage. As an "Unnamed C18th" tartan, it falls into the "Other" category, defying traditional clan affiliations and instead belonging to a broader category that encompasses various historical and cultural remnants. With no specified designer credited, its creation remains a mystery, while the restrictions surrounding its use serve as a reminder of the importance of preserving Scotland's rich textile history.

name: Prince Charles Edward Stuart; #6
description: This exquisite tartan, known only by its historical provenance, is a remarkable relic from the early 19th century, linked to none other than the legendary Prince Charles Edward Stuart, also known as Bonnie Prince Charlie. As one of several coats said to have belonged to him, now preserved in the National Museum of Scotland's collection, this tartan holds immense cultural significance, representing a pivotal moment in Scottish history. Without an attributed designer, its origins remain a mystery, yet its intricate design and rich heritage are unmistakable. A testament to the craftsmanship of yesteryear, this tartan is a poignant reminder of the storied past, woven with threads of tradition and rebellion.

name: Prince Charles Edward Stuart; #7
description: This enigmatic tartan, unnamed in its youth but later immortalised as a relic of 18th-century Scottish heritage, holds a captivating tale within its intricate threads. Originally worn by Prince Charles Edward in 1745, its origins were all but lost to the annals of time - that is, until it underwent significant alterations in the mid-19th century, likely for feminine wear. The reversibility of the closure and distinctive collar, crafted from Wilsons' No.169, offer a tangible link to the esteemed textile house, whose patterns have woven their way into Scotland's fabric for centuries. As a testament to the enduring legacy of this tartan, it remains a poignant reminder of the nation's rich cultural history, its shades and quality evoking the grandeur of a bygone era, and its story waiting to be unravelled by those with a keen eye for tradition.

name: Prince Charles Edward Stuart; #8
description: The Pr Ch Ed (1970) Stewart tartan, registered by Pendleton Woolen Mills, embodies the majesty and tradition of Scotland's royal heritage. Inspired by the iconic Prince Charles Edward, the 1745 Jacobite leader who led the final rebellion against the British monarchy, this tartan is a masterful blend of colours that evoke the grandeur of the Scottish Highlands. The broad red stripe, which dominates the design, gives way to a rich tapestry of blues, greens, and yellows, weaving together in a complex yet harmonious pattern. This Fashion tartan, often referred to by those familiar with the Royal Stewart, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's storied past and its continued influence on modern fashion.

name: Prince Charles Edward Stuart
description: This enigmatic tartan, designated as Unnamed C18th - Prince Charles Edward #2, holds a rich historical significance, having been worn by the legendary Bonnie Prince Charlie during his time at Blair Castle in Perthshire. Woven with reverence for his hosts, the tartan's presence is steeped in tradition and camaraderie, reflecting the Prince's honourable custom of donning the plaid to pay tribute to those who took him under their wing during his travels. As a testament to Scotland's storied past, this tartan remains a poignant reminder of the country's proud heritage, while its category as "Other" underscores the complexity and diversity of Scotland's rich tapestry of clan associations and traditions.

name: Prince David;
description: The Prince David tartan is a majestic Royal tartan, steeped in tradition and heritage, its intricate patterns evoking the grandeur of Scottish nobility. Designed with great flair for a young royal's personal use, this tartan holds a poignant story: James Mackinlay suggests that it was created as a tribute to the pet name 'David', which the Duke of Windsor bore when he was a boy. With its unique sett and subtle nuances, the Prince David tartan embodies the refinement and elegance of Scotland's storied royal family, its beauty and history waiting to be unravelled by those with an eye for tradition and heritage.

name: Prince Edward Island Dress
description: The Prince Edward Island Dress Tartan, designed by the esteemed West Coast Woolen Mill, is a testament to the rich heritage of Prince Edward Island in Canada's Maritime provinces. As a District Tartan, it holds a special place within the island's cultural identity, symbolising a strong sense of community and locality. Though its registration status is uncertain, the tartan's presence in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection suggests a connection to traditional Scottish weaving practices. This distinct design, though not officially recognised as the island's dress tartan, still holds great significance for Prince Edward Islanders, reflecting their unique blend of Scottish and Canadian influences.

name: Prince Edward Island Provincial
description: The Prince Edward Island tartan is a vibrant representation of the island's rich history and cultural heritage, born from a district of Scotland with strong ties to its Canadian namesake. Originally part of Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island was named in honour of Queen Victoria's father, Prince Edward, Duke of Kent, who played a significant role in shaping the region's history. The tartan's colours - red for the island's fertile soil, green for its lush fields and trees, and yellow and brown evoking the warmth of autumn, with white representing the sea's foam or summer snow - pay testament to the island's unique blend of Scottish and Maritime influences. Designed by Mrs Jean Reid in 1960 as part of a national tartan design competition, this District tartan proudly reflects the island's proud heritage and its people's enduring connection to Scotland, where it all began.

name: Prince George;
description: The Prince George tartan is a poignant tribute to the life and legacy of the Duke of Kent, who tragically lost his life in the Second World War. This royal tartan, registered by The Scottish Tartans Society Archive, holds immense historical significance as it was designed in commemoration of the duke's untimely passing. As a member of the British royal family, the Prince George tartan embodies tradition and heritage, evoking memories of Scotland's rich cultural history and its revered monarchs. With no designer credited, this tartan serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Duke of Kent, whose memory continues to be cherished by the Scottish Tartans Society Archive, preserving his story for generations to come.

name: Prince George's Police Pipe Band
description: The Prince George's Police Pipe Band tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate pattern, born from the union of British heritage and American pride. Designed by renowned expert J.C. 'Scotty' Thompson in 1988, this tartan was originally created to enhance the public image of the police department in Prince George, Maryland. As such, it falls squarely within the Corporate category, reflecting its utilitarian purpose as a symbol of civic unity. The tartan's significance extends beyond its corporate roots, however, as it represents the blending of Scottish traditions with American culture. A testament to Scotty's extensive knowledge and passion for tartan design, this pattern is steeped in history and tradition, making it a unique addition to any collection.

name: Prince of Denmark Historic
description: The Prince of Denmark tartan is a striking Corporate design that tells the story of a bygone era's industrial heritage, as embodied in its unique registration notes. Created by skilled weaver Ian Phillip, this distinctive tartan was originally designed to match the colours of the iconic cigarette packaging for the Prince of Denmark brand. As a testament to Scotland's rich textile past, the tartan's subtle warp and weft counts set it apart from other Corporate designs, adding a layer of authenticity to its modern applications. With its bold, vibrant hues, this tartan is sure to make a lasting impression in corporate environments, honouring Scotland's proud tradition of innovative textiles while connecting businesses to their heritage.

name: Prince of Orange #2
description: The Prince of Orange #2 tartan is a fascinating District pattern steeped in Scottish heritage and rich history. Its distinctive black guards on blue background evokes the dramatic contrasts of Scotland's rugged landscapes, while its origins lie shrouded in mystery - with notes suggesting that the blue or black may be incorrect. This intriguing design has been credited to Pic Mills, Toronto, though some researchers remain uncertain about the firm's true identity. Regardless, this tartan is a testament to the ingenuity and tradition of Scottish weaving, where bold, striking patterns have long served as symbols of clan affiliation and regional identity.

name: Prince of Orange
description: The Prince of Orange tartan is a storied and intricate District tartan, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's military past. This distinctive design takes its inspiration from the Mackay family, renowned for their bravery during the 17th Century's Jacobite risings, particularly in their allegiance to the Dutch and Swedish Crowns. The tartan's complex pattern weaves together a tapestry of tradition and loyalty, evoking the exploits of General Mackay and his Regiment, who fought valiantly for foreign monarchs amidst Scotland's own turbulent history. As a testament to this fascinating chapter in Scottish military history, the Prince of Orange tartan remains a poignant reminder of the country's complex relationships with its European neighbours.

name: Prince of Wales Check
description: The Prince of Wales Check, aptly named after the iconic Welsh royal title, is a timeless tartan design steeped in tradition and heritage. As a District tartan, it was created to commemorate a specific geographic region, in this case, Wales. This distinctive check pattern, with its bold stripes of blue and green, red and yellow, evokes the rugged beauty of the Welsh countryside. With no restrictions on use, the Prince of Wales Check is free to be worn with pride by anyone who wishes to connect with the rich history and culture of Wales. Designed by Woolly Mill, this tartan has become an enduring symbol of Welsh identity and a cherished part of Scotland's rich textile heritage.

name: Prince of Wales
description: The Prince of Wales tartan is an iconic fashion tartan with a rich history rooted in Scottish heritage. Designed by Lochcarron of Scotland, this striking pattern was originally created to evoke the grandeur of the British monarchy, specifically the Royal Family's association with the Duchy of Rothesay. Although intended as a variant of the Duke of Rothesay hunting tartan (#1533), an error led to the omission of a distinctive white line, resulting in the creation of this unique and enduring design. Today, the Prince of Wales tartan is a highly sought-after fashion choice, worn by those who appreciate its association with royal tradition and Scotland's rich cultural fabric. Its origins as an unintended variant have given way to widespread recognition and admiration, cementing its place in the annals of Scottish textiles.

name: Prince's Own;
description: The MacRae, The Prince's Own tartan is a storied and storied heritage pattern steeped in tradition and family history. Registered to the Highland Society of London in 1816-22, this variant was submitted by the chief himself, bearing the mark of its authenticity. According to legend, it was donned by none other than Prince Charles Edward, who wore it during his time in MacRae country during the Jacobite rising of '45, earning it the nickname "The Prince's Own". This tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of the MacRae clan and their proud heritage, woven from threads of history, loyalty, and Scottish tradition.

name: Princess Beatrice; Dress Dance
description: The Princess Beatrice Dress tartan is a striking fashion tartan that evokes the elegance and sophistication of Scotland's rich heritage. Designed by renowned kiltmaker and designer, Hugh MacPherson, this vibrant pattern pays homage to the historical Princess Beatrice tartan, with subtle variations to distinguish it from its original counterpart. According to the registration notes, this modern interpretation features three reversals of green/black, setting it apart from the historic #1206 reference. By drawing upon Scotland's storied past, while adapting it for contemporary fashion, MacPherson has created a unique and captivating tartan that is sure to make a statement on the dance floor or beyond. This stunning design not only celebrates Scottish tradition but also showcases the skill and craftsmanship of Edinburgh-based kiltmaker Hugh MacPherson.

name: Princess Beatrice; Hunting
description: This exquisite Princess Beatrice Hunting tartan is a masterful blend of traditional Scottish craftsmanship with modern style, perfectly captured under the Fashion category. The MacKinlay strip's subtle nuances speak to its origins in the 1930s, when it was carefully designed and woven by an uncredited craftsman. This storied tartan pays tribute to Princess Beatrice, the elegant daughter of Queen Victoria, whose life and legacy are woven into its very fabric. As a testament to British heritage and tradition, this tartan evokes images of refined elegance and understated sophistication, inviting wearers to pay homage to a bygone era of regal refinement while making a statement that is quintessentially Scottish in style and essence.

name: Princess Beatrice; Hunting #2
description: The Princess Beatrice Hunting tartan is a storied and storied family heirloom, originating from Clan/Family registration records. This intricate and elegant tartan design pays homage to the heritage of its namesake, Princess Beatrice, a member of the British royal family known for her philanthropic endeavours and dedication to her community. The traditional hunting colours of blue and green are juxtaposed with darker blues and greens, creating a rich and sophisticated palette that evokes the wild beauty of Scotland's countryside. While it is currently unclear which thread count constitutes the 'authentic' Beatrice Hunting tartan, this alternative version remains a testament to the enduring legacy of its namesake, inviting wearers to connect with their own Scottish heritage and join the proud tradition of this illustrious clan.

name: Princess Beatrice;
description: The Princess Beatrice Dress tartan is a sumptuous fashion design that embodies the elegance and refinement of late 19th-century Scottish heritage. Originally believed to have been created for the wedding of Queen Victoria's youngest daughter, Princess Beatrice, in 1885, it was not until the 1930s that this exquisite sett first appeared in records. However, a 2003 study revealed that a woven sample of the tartan had actually been included in a Parisian publication, Clans Originaux, as early as 1880 - five years before the anticipated wedding date. This tartan is now a treasured fragment of Scotland's rich cultural history, its beauty and craftsmanship a testament to the skill of traditional Scottish weavers. As a Fashion tartan, it remains an important part of our shared heritage, offering a glimpse into the past through its intricate patterns and colours.

name: Princess Elizabeth; #2
description: The Princess Elizabeth #2 tartan is a revered Royal tartan, designed to commemorate the reign of Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II. Registered in 1954 by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this majestic pattern is steeped in tradition and heritage, reflecting the esteemed status of its namesake monarch. As a Royal tartan, it is reserved for use by members of the British royal family and other dignitaries, carrying weighty history and prestige. Its registration notes proudly note the year Queen Elizabeth II succeeded to the throne, crowned in 1953, rendering this tartan an enduring symbol of the British monarchy's enduring legacy.

name: Princess Elizabeth;
description: The Princess Elizabeth tartan is a majestic Royal tartan steeped in British heritage, worn with honour by members of the House of York and, later, the House of Windsor. Registered as part of the Coulson Bonner collection, this esteemed tartan was popularised during the reign of her father George VI, who would later become King after his older brother Edward VIII abdicated. This stunning pattern has been preserved in the Scottish Tartans Society archive, serving as a poignant reminder of the rich history and tradition that underpins British monarchical regalia. With its intricate design, evocative of Scotland's storied past, this tartan is an enduring symbol of national identity and a testament to the enduring legacy of the British monarchy.

name: Princess Louise
description: The Princess Louise fashion tartan is a stunning representation of Scottish heritage, with its intricate woven pattern evoking the grandeur of royal tradition. Named after the daughter of Queen Victoria, who was born in Edinburgh Castle, this tartan's history is deeply rooted in the cultural significance of Scottish aristocracy. Originally registered for general wear, the Princess Louise tartan is now predominantly used in fashion, symbolising elegance and refinement. Notably, the Dalgleish version boasts a distinctive wider black-edged green band on its blue background, adding an extra layer of visual interest to this already striking design. With no specific designer credited, it is clear that the true creators behind this tartan are the skilled weavers who have preserved and passed down this legacy through generations.

name: Princess Margaret Rose;
description: The Princess Margaret Rose tartan is a majestic and storied heritage design, steeped in royal tradition and history. Woven with reverence for the British monarchy, this tartan holds significance as a registered Royal Tartan, designated to commemorate the late Princess Margaret Rose, sister of Queen Elizabeth II. Its distinctive red and green colour reversal pattern pays homage to the MacGregor clan, yet its unique blend evokes a distinct identity all its own. With its origins dated back to the 1930s, this tartan has been meticulously preserved in the Paton Collection, serving as a poignant testament to the enduring legacy of the British royal family's rich heritage.

name: Princess Marina
description: Princess Marina #2 is a quintessentially fashion-forward tartan, born from the world of high-end style and sophistication. This vibrant, blue-based design - characteristic of the British fashion scene - has been woven with precision to evoke the glamour of royal heritage. The subtle interplay of blues, greens, and golds in this sophisticated pattern is reminiscent of a bygone era, when royalty reigned supreme. Although its designer remains anonymous, it's clear that Princess Marina #2 was created with the fastidious attention to detail that underpins the finest fashion tartans. With no restrictions on its use for non-clan or corporate wear, this captivating design is perfectly suited to add a touch of high-end glamour to any outfit, making it a coveted choice among fashionistas and tartan enthusiasts alike.

name: Princess Mary
description: The Princess Mary #2 tartan is a storied and exclusive design rooted in Scottish heritage, steeped in tradition and prestige. Originally commissioned by members of the Royal Family in the early 1930s, it was created as an alternative to the esteemed Hunting Stewart tartan, showcasing its unique character and honours its connection to the British monarchy. Since its inception, this tartan has been closely tied to the esteemed House of Windsor, with many notable royals donning the distinctive green and blue hues in various settings. As a Royal tartan, it carries significant cultural weight and is only available for use by those granted special permission from the relevant authorities, underscoring its exclusivity and status within Scotland's rich textile tradition.

name: Pringle [default]
description: The Pringle #2 tartan is a highly personal and exclusive creation, designed and woven by renowned Scottish textile expert Kenny Dalgliesh of Selkirk in 1998 as a one-off for an individual with the surname Pringle. This unique Name tartan holds significant cultural and historical value, reflecting the artisan's skillful interpretation of Scotland's rich tartan heritage. While the specific intentions behind its creation are deeply personal to the Pringle family, this tartan is imbued with the same technical precision and traditional craftsmanship that has defined Scottish weaving for centuries. Notably, Dalgliesh's company has carefully prepared the design for weaving, ensuring its intricate patterns meet rigorous standards of quality and authenticity. Due to its bespoke nature and limited availability, the Pringle #2 tartan is a rare opportunity for those interested in exploring Scotland's storied tartan legacy.

name: Pringle, James
description: The Pringle, James tartan is a captivating fashion statement born from the esteemed Pringles of Inverness mill, with roots in Moffat, Scotland. As a fashion tartan, its primary purpose is to adorn garments and accessories that embody modern style and sophistication. The unique design features distinct warp and weft patterns, setting it apart from traditional Scottish clan tartans. First registered in 1996, this tartan pays homage to the rich heritage of Scotland's textile industry, while also embracing contemporary flair. Named after its creator, Pringles of Inverness, this tartan is an excellent choice for those seeking a fashion-forward yet deeply rooted in tradition. Its story serves as a testament to the enduring appeal of Scottish craftsmanship and design.

name: Printing Industries of America
description: The Printing Industries of America tartan is a distinctive corporate pattern born from the creative collaboration between renowned designers Robert Hall and Phil Smith. Originally registered in 2003, this bold and vibrant tartan was designed to celebrate the heritage and excellence of the printing industry. As an officially sanctioned corporate tartan, it holds significance for organisations within the sector, proudly showcasing their affiliation with a rich history of innovation and craftsmanship. The intricate design, a testament to the skills of its creators, is steeped in traditional Scottish weaving techniques, reflecting the enduring spirit of British heritage that has shaped this iconic industry. With its unique colour palette and distinctive pattern, the Printing Industries of America tartan serves as a powerful symbol of professionalism and excellence, endearing itself to those who wear it with honour and pride.

name: Richards [default]
description: The Pritchard tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's esteemed clans, specifically its Stewart variants. Designed by Mabel Pritchard of Dunkeld, Perthshire in 1923, this distinctive tartan holds great honour among Scottish families. As a registered clan tartan, it is steeped in tradition and steeped in history, bearing the legacy of one of Scotland's most storied clans. The Pritchard tartan's subtle nuances and intricate patterns reflect the craftsmanship of its weaver, Mabel Pritchard, who painstakingly brought this design to life in 1923. With restrictions indicating it is a Stewart variation, the Pritchard tartan remains an authentic representation of Scotland's complex and storied clan history, evoking a sense of pride and connection to one of Britain's most iconic and enduring families.

name: Rosser of Wales
description: The Rosser of Wales tartan is a vibrant and distinctive Name tartan, born from the creative vision of Sheila Daniel, with assistance from Daniel himself, for Wales Tartan Centres circa 1998. This modern design has become a beloved representation of Welsh heritage, though its origins lie in recent tradition rather than ancient history or genealogical ties. The unusual thread count and colour palette set it apart from more traditional Celtic tartans, earning it recognition within the world of contemporary tartan design. Woven with careful attention to detail, the Rosser of Wales tartan now holds a special place in the hearts of those who wear it, serving as a proud symbol of Welsh identity and culture. However, it's essential to acknowledge that its status as an officially registered Name tartan does not confer historical or territorial significance upon it, and its 'of Wales' designation serves primarily as a testament to its design origins.

name: Protheroe of Wales
description: The Protheroe of Wales tartan is a unique and striking name, reflecting the Welsh heritage from which it originates. As a Name tartan, its primary purpose is to identify its connection to the Protheroe family, rather than being tied to a specific clan or territory. Designed by Sheila Daniel for Wales Tartan Centres in collaboration with Cambrian Woollen Mill, this tartan design has become a popular representation of Welsh tradition since its introduction around 1998. However, it's worth noting that, as with many modern tartans, the Protheroe of Wales does not hold historical or genealogical significance, and its use should be seen as a way to acknowledge its cultural roots rather than claim any direct connection. The distinctive characteristics of this tartan - including its unusual thread numbers and colour variations - set it apart from other Celtic designs, making it a fascinating addition to the world of traditional Scottish textiles.

name: PSD Operation Iraqi Freedom
description: The PSD: Operation Iraqi Freedom tartan is a poignant and evocative tribute to the service of Private Military Contractors who served as Personal Security Detail during Operation Iraqi Freedom. Commissioned by 'The Baghdad 12' in January 2006, this asymmetric tartan was designed by Matthew Newsome to commemorate the bravery and sacrifice of those who risked their lives to protect others in a foreign land. The deliberate choice of colours - brown and tan for the desert landscape, green for a hopeful future, red for the blood shed, and black for fallen comrades - serves as a powerful reminder of the sacrifices made by those who wore this tartan. Authorised to be worn by PSD members, direct support staff, and immediate family, this tartan is a badge of honour that pays tribute to a specific chapter in modern military history, its significance woven deeply into the fabric of Scottish heritage through the esteemed traditions of tartan design.

name: Puffin
description: The Puffin tartan, created by the esteemed Lochcarron of Scotland in 1997, is a vibrant and stylish addition to the world of fashion tartans. Inspired by the iconic birds that nest on the rugged Scottish coastlines, this distinctive design embodies the country's rich heritage and cultural identity. As a fashion tartan, it was intended for use in clothing and accessories, allowing wearers to showcase their affection for Scotland's picturesque landscapes and charismatic wildlife. Although not open to public registration due to its commercial origins, the Puffin tartan remains an intriguing glimpse into the intersection of art and commerce, reflecting the innovative spirit that has always defined Scottish textiles.

name: Punky Princess
description: The Punky Princess tartan is a vibrant and modern corporate design that embodies the spirit of youthful rebellion with a touch of regal sophistication. Created by Accessories 4 Technology Ltd specifically for their 'Punky Princess' brand, this tartan utilises a bold palette of pink, black, and silvery-grey hues to evoke a sense of confidence and empowerment. As a licensed design, its use is restricted to UK-produced products woven exclusively by the renowned Lochcarron of Scotland, ensuring that each fabric meets the highest standards of quality and craftsmanship. By embracing this tartan's edgy charm, brands can tap into the enduring appeal of Scottish heritage and tradition, while also communicating their commitment to creativity and individuality.

name: Purdy (Illinois) personal; Black #2
description: With its subtle yet distinctive colour palette, Wilsons' No.95 is a quintessential corporate tartan that exudes professionalism and timelessness. As part of the esteemed Corporate category, this modern take on traditional Scottish weaving is designed to evoke respect and authority in equal measure. Registered by a renowned weaving firm founded in 1770 near Stirling, Wilsons' No.95 is deeply rooted in Scotland's rich textile heritage. The tartan's design, although not attributed to a specific designer, is still steeped in tradition, reflecting the intricate weaves and subtle nuances of its ancestral predecessors. With its restricted availability due to its origins in pattern books stored at the National Museum of Antiquities, Edinburgh, and archives held by the Scottish Tartan Society, Wilsons' No.95 offers a unique opportunity for those seeking to tap into Scotland's storied past while still meeting modern standards.

name: Purple Watch
description: The Armagh County, Crest Range tartan is a richly woven tapestry of heritage, reflecting the proud history and identity of Ireland's ancient county of Armagh. Designated as a District tartan, it proudly represents the local community, steeped in tradition and tied to the region's storied past. Crafted by Viking Technology Ltd in 2005, this distinctive tartan was part of an esteemed set of Irish County and Irish National designs, showcasing the nation's vibrant cultural tapestry. With ownership now vested with USA Kilts Inc, this tartan serves as a testament to Armagh's enduring heritage, while its restrictive reproduction rights safeguard its integrity and exclusive status as an authentic representation of the county's crest range.

name: Quabboos Sultan of; Air Force
description: The Sultan of Qaboo's Air Force tartan is a proud declaration of military heritage, born from the expertise of Lochcarron of Scotland. This distinctive tartan is designated as a Military category, signifying its origins in the esteemed ranks of the Royal Air Force (RAF). The design itself is steeped in tradition and symbolic significance, reflecting the values of bravery, loyalty, and dedication embodied by the RAF's storied history. Although limited information exists regarding potential connections to other tartans, such as a pipe band variant boasting red hues, the Sultan of Qaboo's Air Force tartan stands resolutely on its own merits, imbued with the very essence of British military tradition.

name: Quaboos Regimental Pipers Plaid
description: The Quaboos Pipers Plaid, designed by renowned tartan house Granger & Campbell for His Majesty Sultan HM Qaboos Bin-Said, stands as a testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage and its enduring connections with the Middle East. This striking Military tartan was specifically commissioned for the Sultanate of Oman, a country situated on the Arabian peninsula, and is now associated with the personal band or that of Sultan Quaboos University. The intricate design weaves together shades of blue, green, and yellow, evoking the majesty of the Omani desert landscape and the grandeur of the sultan's court. As a symbol of respect and admiration for Oman's leadership, this tartan holds great significance in Scottish heritage, serving as a poignant reminder of the country's long-standing diplomatic ties with the region.

name: Quadra
description: The Quadra tartan, designed by the renowned West Coast Woolen Mill, is a stylish addition to any fashion collection. This vibrant and modern tartan was registered in 1966 under the classification of Fashion (category), indicating its suitability for garments and textiles intended for everyday wear. With no specific restrictions noted in its registration, the Quadra tartan can be freely used in fashion designs, allowing creatives to bring its unique blend of warmth and energy to their projects. Born from the expertise of West Coast Woolen Mill, this tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage of textiles and tradition, evoking the dynamic spirit of the west coast's rugged landscape.

name: Quebec Centennial
description: The Quebec Centennial tartan is a commemorative design steeped in Canadian heritage, paying tribute to the province's enduring spirit and resilience. Registered by renowned designer Pik Mills of Toronto, this distinctive tartan honours a pivotal moment in Canada's history - the 100th anniversary celebration of the Province of Quebec's entry into confederation. With its unique blend of red, blue, yellow, green, black, and white sett threads, this tartan embodies the rich cultural tapestry of Quebec's distinctiveness within the Canadian fabric. While not specifically tied to a particular clan or family, it remains an important symbol of national pride and unity, serving as a lasting testament to the province's storied past and its enduring place in Canada's shared heritage.

name: Quebec Centennial Dress
description: The Praetorian Green, a modern fashion tartan born from the innovative spirit of Graham Alexander Robieson, embodies the dynamism of Scotland's rich heritage. This distinctive design, once known as 'Predator Green', has been reimagined with a fresh perspective, its nuances now reflecting the timeless beauty of Scotland's natural landscapes. As a Fashion tartan, it was intended for the modern wearers who seek to celebrate their Scottish roots with style and panache. Its technical characteristics are well-suited for garments that require a versatile and eye-catching presence, be they kilts, scarves or dress shirts. Registration notes reveal its humble beginnings at Highland Crafts Limited, under the skilled hand of Geoffrey, highlighting the artisanal traditions that continue to shape Scotland's iconic textiles.

name: Quebec Provincial
description: The Quebec Plaid du is a striking Corporate tartan design born from the rich history and cultural heritage of Canada's largest province. Created in 1965 by Rotex Limited, a clothing manufacturer, this tartan pays homage to the Scottish immigrants who settled in Quebec over 400 years ago, leaving an indelible mark on the region's identity. Inspired by the three horizontal divisions of the provincial shield, the Plaid du Quebec features a bold and distinctive pattern that reflects the province's unique blend of French and British influences. With its deep blue, green, and red hues evoking the St Lawrence River and the surrounding landscape, this tartan design is a fitting tribute to the enduring legacy of Scotland in Quebec, even if it has never been officially adopted by the Canadian government. As a testament to the province's Scottish roots, the annual Tartan Day on April 6th is a celebration that may soon gain greater recognition – for now, the Plaid du Quebec stands as a proud and enduring symbol of this fascinating cultural heritage.

name: Queen Alexandra
description: The Queen Alexandra fashion tartan, designed by the renowned Scott Brothers of Hawick, is a timeless and elegant choice for those who wish to honour Scotland's rich heritage. Named after the wife of King Edward VII and queen consort from 1910 until her death in 1924, this tartan design embodies the sophistication and refinement that defines the Victorian era. With its intricate balance of blues, greens, and reds, Queen Alexandra's colours evoke a sense of dignity and poise, making it an excellent choice for formal occasions or as a statement piece in one's wardrobe. Although originally collected by James Mckinlay, this tartan has been officially registered by the Scottish Tartans Society, allowing wearers to proudly display their connection to Scotland's vibrant cultural heritage.

name: Queen Mary RMS
description: This stately corporate tartan, known as Queen Mary RMS, is a testament to the enduring legacy of a bygone era's maritime grandeur. Designed with the preservation of a historic Royal Mail Ship at its centre - RMS Queen Mary itself - now proudly moored in Long Beach, California, this distinctive tartan is an invitation to join in the celebration of Scottish heritage and tradition. With no clan or family association, yet still deeply rooted in the country's rich history, this corporate tartan serves as a symbol of cultural exchange and community, honouring the ship that has brought Scottish festivals and games to life for countless visitors over the years, its presence serving as a subtle yet striking nod to the enduring spirit of Scotland.

name: Queen of Scots
description: The Queen of Scots tartan is a majestic commemorative design, painstakingly crafted by renowned designer David McGill to commemorate the re-creation of Scotland's Parliament and the resumption of its storied monarchical title after nearly three centuries of absence. This rich and intricate tartan is steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition, its carefully considered colours and pattern evoking a sense of history and prestige. By paying homage to this pivotal moment in Scotland's story, McGill has created a tartan that not only honours the nation's past but also looks towards a brighter future. Although permission must be sought from the designer before use, this unique tartan is sure to command respect for its cultural significance and timeless beauty.

name: Queen of the South Football Club
description: The Queen of the South Football Club tartan is a vibrant and dynamic representation of Scottish football heritage, born from the passion and dedication of its namesake club's supporters. Registered as a corporate tartan, this distinctive weave embodies the unity and pride of the Queen of the South Football Club community, with Ronnie Hek's creative vision bringing the team's history to life through bold colours and intricate patterns. By embracing this tartan design, individuals and organisations can proudly demonstrate their connection to Scotland's beloved football culture, while respecting the club's exclusive ownership rights – a testament to the enduring legacy of Queen of the South Football Club.

name: Queen Victoria; Royal
description: This captivating Victorian-inspired tartan, registered as Victoria (Variant) #1, embodies the elegance and sophistication of a bygone era. As a fashion tartan, it was designed to make a statement, with its intricate, repetitive pattern evoking the opulence of the British Empire's golden age. Created in the late 19th century, this variant was a nod to Queen Victoria's enduring legacy, reflecting the cultural values of the time. With its subtle nuances and rich colours, this tartan is an excellent example of the art of traditional weaving, where every thread and fibre tells a story of Scotland's rich heritage and tradition.

name: Queen Victoria;
description: The Victoria tartan, designed by renowned Scottish textile firm Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1838, is a sumptuous fashion tartan that evokes the elegance of a bygone era. Specifically created to complement their adjacent Albert tartan, this iconic design showcases a subtle balance of rich blues and vibrant greens, reminiscent of Scotland's majestic landscapes. As one of several fashionable tartans popular during the Victorian era, Victoria tartan was woven with precision, reflecting the craftsmanship and skill of Scottish weavers. While not part of a traditional clan or territorial heritage, Victoria tartan is still deeply rooted in Scottish tradition, embodying the nation's love for intricate design and timeless style. Its association with Wilsons of Bannockburn adds to its historical significance, solidifying its place as an enduring symbol of Scottish fashion heritage.

name: Queens University of Ontario
description: The Queens University Kingston Ontario tartan is a unique and meaningful corporate tartan, designed by Judge John Matheson to represent the esteemed institution in Ontario. Specifically created for Queens University, this tartan weaves together six rich colours, each meticulously chosen to signify one of the university's academic hoods: Medicine (blue), Arts & Science (red), Applied Science (gold), Nursing Science (white), Commerce & MBA (green), and Theology (purple). This deliberate colour palette serves as a powerful symbol of the institution's commitment to excellence in six distinct fields, reflecting its dedication to fostering well-rounded individuals who embody academic rigour. With restrictions on marketing usage, this tartan is reserved for official university communications and merchandise, ensuring its integrity and authentic connection to the institution's proud heritage.

name: Queensferry District
description: The All Breeds Dairy Goats Corporate Tartan, designed by F & M Lawson at Crofter's Weaving Mill, is a vibrant and distinctive pattern steeped in tradition and Scottish heritage. Originally conceived for a prestigious award at the Gunnedah Show in New South Wales, this tartan has now been adapted for use at similar state shows across Australia, symbolising excellence in the world of dairy goats. Characterised by its unique mixed thread design, where brown and white threads alternate to create a striking effect, this tartan embodies the ingenuity and craftsmanship that underpins Scotland's rich textile heritage. As a corporate tartan, it offers businesses and organisations the opportunity to showcase their connection to this unique aspect of Australian agricultural culture, making it an attractive choice for those seeking to make a statement with their branding and uniforms.

name: Queensland District
description: The Queensland tartan is a stunning representation of the State's unique landscape and natural beauty, meticulously woven by Jack Allen in 2001. As a District tartan, it holds significant cultural heritage for the people of Queensland, reflecting the region's diverse geography and climate. The tartan's seven core colours expertly capture the essence of the state: wispy white clouds, cerulean skies, royal blue hues evoking the Coral Sea and tropical beaches, golden sun-kissed sands, lush green forests, delicate lilac blooms, and the majestic crimson tones of the Cooktown Orchid. With its thoughtful colour palette, this tartan design serves as a testament to Queensland's natural splendour and the rich heritage of its people.

name: Quinn (Wedding) personal
description: The Quinn Personal Tartan is a unique and meaningful design, born from the union of love between Elaine Mackay and Edward Quinn at their wedding celebration in Anta Scotland Ltd. As a Name tartan, it holds a special place in the hearts of those bearing the Quinn name, signifying family heritage and legacy. Designed by Annie Stewart, a talented weaver with a deep understanding of Scottish tradition, this tartan is steeped in history and cultural significance. The restrictions surrounding its registration serve as a testament to its exclusivity, making it an even more cherished possession for those who bear the Quinn name. As a tribute to Elaine and Edward's love story, the Quinn Personal Tartan serves as a lasting reminder of the enduring power of family ties and tradition in Scotland's rich tapestry.

name: Raeside [default]
description: The Raeside tartan is a rich and storied weave, born from the convergence of two esteemed Scottish clans: Douglas and Raeside. Registered in 2005 by its designer Archie Raeside, this family tartan tells the tale of a remarkable union forged between Charlotte Douglas and William Raeside, who married in Glasgow in 1909. The light green guard lines that punctuate this tartan serve as a poignant reminder of the bloodline that once connected Scotland to Ireland, symbolising the enduring bond between two families bound together by love, legacy, and heritage. As a Clan/Family tartan, the Raeside is open to wear by all who bear its name, serving as a proud badge of family identity and a testament to the shared history and traditions that unite those with this noble surname.

name: Rafferty
description: The Rafferty tartan is a vibrant and sophisticated Fashion tartan, intricately woven to evoke the spirit of Scotland's rich heritage. Created by renowned designer Scotch Corner of Gateshead, England, this tartan draws inspiration from the Emerald Isle, reflecting the strong Irish connections in its creation. One of a series designed by Scotch Corner, the Rafferty tartan is steeped in tradition and honour, featuring a striking colour palette that pays tribute to Scotland's intricate clan system. While open to fashion interpretation, the registration notes caution against misusing this tartan, ensuring its prestige and status are upheld. As a Fashion tartan, the Rafferty design embodies the perfect blend of elegance and cultural significance, making it an coveted choice for those who value Scottish heritage and tradition.

name: Rainbow Canada
description: The Rainbow tartan, a vibrant fashion staple created by Vancouver-based designer Aljean, embodies the spirit of diversity and inclusivity that defines modern Scotland. As a Fashion tartan, its primary purpose is to make a statement on the runway or in everyday life, rather than being tied to a specific clan or heritage tradition. Unlike other tartans that draw upon ancient Scottish history, the Rainbow tartan's colours - red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and indigo - are carefully arranged to evoke a sense of hope and celebration, rather than connection to a particular clan or family lineage. Registration notes caution against confusion with Ronnie Hek's 1999/2000 design, making it a unique addition to the world of Scottish textiles, one that continues to inspire and influence fashion designers around the globe.

name: Rainbow Fort Worth
description: The Rainbow Tartan, as registered by Barbara Hayes, is a vibrant and eclectic design that defies the traditional boundaries of Scottish heritage. As a District tartan, it is believed to have originated in Fort Worth, Texas, giving it an intriguing transatlantic flavour. This bold and colourful fabric has its roots in the rich cultural tapestry of North America's Texan heartland, where diversity and innovation reign supreme. While its exact provenance remains uncertain, the Rainbow Tartan's unique character undoubtedly honours the traditions of Scottish weaving, reimagining them through a distinctly American lens. Despite its unorthodox origins, this tartan remains a testament to the enduring power of textiles in shaping identity and community – a testament that transcends borders and geography, speaking to the universal language of colour, pattern, and heritage.

name: Raith Rovers Football Club
description: The Raith Rovers Football Club tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate colour scheme, born from the team's success on the pitch. Designed by renowned duo Norma Scollin and D.C.Dalgleish, this tartan was created in recognition of Raith Rovers' foray into European competition in 1995, culminating in an historic match against Bayern Munich. The tartan holds significant cultural weight, symbolising the team's triumph over adversity and its growing presence on the continent. With restrictions noted by the Scottish Tartans Society regarding its use and interpretation, this tartan serves as a proud emblem of Raith Rovers' heritage, representing the passion and dedication of its loyal supporters.

name: Rajput
description: The Rajput tartan is a storied and historic Military pattern, hailing from the ancient State of Rajisthan in north-western India, where the fiercely warrior-caste Rajputs once ruled with pride. Discovered by renowned researcher Colin Hutcheson during his 2003 expedition, this distinctive design has been meticulously woven into the fabric of military tradition, reflecting the valor and martial prowess of its namesake people. As a registered Military tartan, the Rajput pattern is steeped in heritage and authenticity, bearing testament to the rich cultural tapestry of India's regal past. With no specific designer credited for this unique design, it stands as a tribute to the anonymous artisans who painstakingly wove these threads into a symbol of strength and loyalty, now cherished by members of the armed forces and history enthusiasts alike.

name: Ralston UK
description: The Ralston tartan is a distinctive and storied design that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's name tartans. Registered in the UK, this iconic pattern reflects the coat of arms and the unique cultural connections between the Scots-Irish communities of Tyrone, Donegal, and Renfrewshire. Created by the talented designers Robin Elliot and Alison Ralston, the Ralston tartan is a celebration of Scottish identity and tradition. Woven with careful attention to detail, this complex pattern weaves together a rich tapestry of symbolism, from the subtle nuances of colour to the intricate balance of threads. As a name tartan, it holds great significance for families and clans alike, offering a tangible connection to their heritage and ancestry.

name: Ralston US
description: The Ralston tartan is a family-designed heritage pattern, carefully crafted by Michael T Ralstin to celebrate the 60th birthday of Michael R. Ralstin of Scioto County, Ohio, and to provide an enduring visual representation of the name Ralston in all its variations. This Clan tartan is a testament to Scottish tradition, with its distinctive colours meticulously chosen to evoke the warm, earthy tones reminiscent of Scotland's rugged landscapes. As close as possible to those found in the Scottish Tartans Authority's collection, this tartan design holds significant cultural and familial value, serving as a meaningful symbol of connection to the Ralston heritage and a tribute to the occasion that sparked its creation - a milestone birthday that marked an enduring legacy within the family.

name: Ramsay Angus & Mearns
description: The Ramsay Tartan, registered under the Baronage of Angus & Mearns, is a proud embodiment of Scottish heritage and family tradition. Woven with precision and passion, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the esteemed Clan Ramsay, whose history dates back centuries. As the chief of the clan since 1999, James Ramsay, the 17th Earl of Dalhousie, has ensured that the tartan remains an integral part of his family's legacy. With its unique characteristics and subtle variations, this tartan is not only a testament to the Ramsay name but also a symbol of Scottish culture and identity. Its registration notes reveal the intricate details of its design, including the subtle additions of Jack Dalgety in pencil, hinting at the complex history and relationships within the clan.

name: Ramsay Blue
description: Ramsay Blue Hunting is a storied clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, with its origins dating back to the early 20th century. Registered under the Scottish Tartans Society, this distinctive tartan bears testament to the ingenuity of Harry Lindley's designs for Kinloch Anderson Limited, where he cleverly adapted blue dyes to replace traditional red, giving rise to a now-recognised Hunting tartan. As a Lowland clan tartan, its muted blues evoke the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of Scotland's south-western regions, where the MacGregor-Hastie family has historically resided. With permission from the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan is also proudly worn by The Pilgrim Bandits charity, symbolising unity and community spirit. This richly woven fabric not only celebrates a clan's heritage but also serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's long history of textile innovation and cultural expression.

name: Ramsay Green
description: The Dunedin Chapter tartan, expertly woven by Lochcarron of Scotland, pays tribute to the enduring spirit of Scotland's corporate heritage. As part of the Corporate category, this vibrant design embodies the fusion of tradition and modernity, reflecting the innovative flair of Harley-Davidson's Dunfermline branch. Born from the creative partnership between Harley-Davidson and Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan is steeped in history, having originated as a collaboration with Dalbeath Tartan #2197. Now, the Dunedin Chapter tartan stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of Eastern Western Motor Group's acquisition in 2003, marking a new chapter in Scottish textile traditions. This distinctive design serves as a symbol of affiliation for Harley-Davidson's esteemed partner, exuding a sense of style and heritage that reverberates throughout Scotland's rich cultural landscape.

name: Ramsay Orange
description: The Ramsay Orange Fashion Tartan, expertly crafted by Edinburgh Woollen Mill, is a vibrant and enduring representation of Scottish heritage. Originally identified as a trade tartan with particulars provided by Donald Brown through Angela Nisbett MST, this distinctive pattern has been adopted for fashion purposes. The tartan's reddish tan hue provides a warm and engaging base tone, punctuated by carefully chosen orange stripes that evoke the spirit of the Scottish Highlands. As a Fashion Tartan, its usage is open to designers and manufacturers looking to incorporate traditional Scottish motifs into their designs, allowing the timeless appeal of this colourway to be experienced in modern contexts.

name:
Ramsay Red
[AKA] Ramsay of Dalhousie
description: The Ramsay Red tartan, registered in the Vestiarium Scoticum, is a poignant representation of Scotland's rich clan heritage, hailing from the esteemed Lothian district. Named after the influential Ramsay family, whose crest dates back to 1633 when Sir William Ramsay was created Earl of Dalhousie, this tartan embodies the storied history and traditions of the Chiefs of Ramsay. The subtle nuances in its design – two light red lines woven against a deeper crimson hue – reflect the family's proud legacy, while its registration as a clan tartan underscores its strong connection to Scottish culture and identity. With the tartan expertly crafted by Sobieski Stewarts, it serves as a testament to the enduring spirit of the Ramsay clan, whose ancestry is woven into the very fabric of Scotland's history and heritage.

name: Rangers Football Club 1989
description: The Rangers Football Club tartan, designed by Messrs John MacGregor's Tartan Sportswear company in 1989, is an iconic corporate tartan that embodies the spirit of Glasgow's beloved football club. This unique design was created specifically for the Scottish giants, featuring a distinctive colour palette and subtle texture that evokes the passion and pride of the Rangers' loyal fanbase. Originally launched at a high-profile match featuring Ally McCoist in full Highland Dress, this tartan has since become synonymous with the club's identity. Although the original company behind the design is no longer in operation, its legacy lives on through Geoffry (Tailor) Highland Crafts Ltd's registration under the Design Act in 1994, ensuring that the Rangers Football Club tartan remains a cherished part of Scottish heritage and tradition.

name: Rangers Football Club Dress
description: The Rangers Football Club Dress Tartan is a storied corporate tartan that pays tribute to Scotland's most iconic football club. Registered in 1994 by Chris Aitken, this distinctive tartan was originally woven for the club's merchandise by both Lightweight Ingles Buchan and Heavyweight Lochcarron, two renowned Scottish weaving establishments. With its specific colour palette and precise sett, this tartan has become synonymous with the club's identity, reflecting the passion and pride of its devoted fans. Although Aitken no longer holds the licence to weave or retail Rangers tartan merchandise, his creation remains an enduring symbol of the club's heritage, proudly worn by supporters around the world.

name: Rankin (Dalgliesh) #2
description: The Rankin (Dalgleish) #2 tartan is a storied family tartan steeped in tradition and heritage, bearing testament to the rich history of the Dalgleish clan. Woven with precision and attention to detail, this distinctive pattern features a striking combination of blues, reds, and greens, accented by bold black tramlines that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscapes. Originally developed as part of the Dalgleish family register, this tartan has undergone subtle modifications over time, incorporating an additional black guard on what was once a clear blue band, giving it a unique character that sets it apart from its predecessor. With its intricate design and storied past, the Rankin (Dalgleish) #2 tartan remains a cherished symbol of family identity and heritage for those who proudly bear the Dalgleish name.

name: Rankin (Dalgliesh) (SRT Version)
description: The Rankin (Dalgleish) tartan is a revered heritage pattern, steeped in tradition and rooted in Scotland's rich clan history. This distinctive design originates from the esteemed Dalgleish family, whose name is synonymous with bravery and loyalty. The registered tartan features a striking black guard on white, a subtle yet powerful motif that pays homage to the family's unyielding spirit. As part of the Clan/Family category, this tartan holds significant cultural value, evoking memories of Scottish heritage and the proud traditions of the Dalgleish clan. While not associated with a specific individual designer, the design itself is a testament to the artistry and craftsmanship of Scotland's textile pioneers, whose legacy continues to inspire and captivate enthusiasts of traditional tartans today.

name: Rankin #1
description: Rankin #2 is a storied Clan tartan imbued with the rich heritage of Scotland's esteemed Rankin family. This intricately woven design, passed down through generations, was carefully documented by Reverend Millar in 1952, who obtained it from Ewen Rankin, the last recorded source of the sett. Although the original manufacturer remains a mystery, its significance lies in its connection to the Rankins and their Scottish roots. As a Clan tartan, Rankin #2 is often worn with pride by members of the family and their affiliates, symbolising a deep-seated honour and loyalty to the family's traditions. Its complex patterns and subtle colour nuances evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscapes, where this tartan once played an integral role in the daily lives of its wearers.

name: Rankin (Dalgliesh)
description: The Rankine tartan is a poignant representation of Scottish heritage, hailing from the esteemed MacGregor-Hastie family collection. This Clan tartan, categorised as a familial emblem, holds deep roots in the country's rich history and tradition. Woven with meticulous attention to detail, the intricate design showcases the craftsmanship of Scotland's renowned weavers. Registered by the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan is now part of the national heritage, allowing families to proudly display their clan affiliation. The use of Lochcarron yarn in the swatch adds a subtle texture, underscoring the authenticity of this ancient pattern. First woven in 2000, the Rankine tartan remains an enduring testament to Scotland's cultural legacy, waiting to be treasured by those who bear its noble name.

name: Ranking
description: The Ormiston tartan is a bespoke family heirloom, woven with love and tradition for the esteemed Ormiston clan from Aberdeen. Registered in 2008, this unique Name tartan was specifically created to commemorate the graduation of Andrew Ormiston, the family's son, marking an important milestone in his life. Paying homage to their ancestral heritage, the design is rooted in the classic Roxburgh tartan, a nod to their rich family history. As a Personal tartan, its use is reserved exclusively for the Ormiston family, ensuring that this treasured fabric remains a cherished family tradition, passed down through generations, and forever tied to the family's deep roots in Scotland.

name: Rannoch Red
description: The Rannoch Red fashion tartan, designed by the esteemed Pringles of Inverness, is a vibrant and striking pattern that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's Highlands. Originating in the Johnston Collection, this tartan sample is steeped in history and cultural significance, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish landscape. As a fashion tartan, Rannoch Red is perfect for adding a pop of colour to clothing, accessories, or textiles, while also paying homage to the nation's iconic tartan traditions. With its bold, crimson hues and subtle variations in tone, this tartan design is sure to make a statement and leave a lasting impression, much like the storied past it pays tribute to.

name: Rathmore
description: Rathmore, a fashion tartan born from the threads of tradition, takes its inspiration from a storied kilted skirt once belonging to Frau Fretloeh in West Germany. Registered with Pitlochry Woollen Mill in 1987, Rathmore's intricate design weaves together the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage, reflecting the cultural exchange that has long defined Scotland's relationship with Europe. As a fashion tartan, Rathmore offers a vibrant alternative to traditional clan patterns, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to add a touch of modern style to their kilt or sash. With its origins rooted in Frau Fretloeh's unique and historic garment, Rathmore pays homage to the complexities of Scottish identity while embracing the fashion-forward spirit of the 20th century.

name:
Rattray of Lude [default]
[AKA] Rattray of Lude
description: The Rattray of Lude tartan is an ancient and storied clan pattern, steeped in history and tradition. Originally discovered in the Romanes & Paterson pattern book of circa 1830, this tartan shares striking similarities with its counterpart, MacInroy, yet boasts subtle variations that set it apart as a distinct family heritage. As part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's accredited collections, Rattray of Lude is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's clans and families, who have woven their unique stories into the fabric of tartan tradition for centuries. Its intricate design, while identical in essence to its Romanes & Paterson counterpart, carries an air of authenticity born from generations of use and reverence within the Rattray family, underscoring the rich cultural significance of this esteemed clan tartan.

name: Rattray [default]
description: The Rattray tartan is a revered Clan tartan, bearing witness to the rich history and heritage of the Murrays of Atholl family, who claim descent from Adam de Rattrieff in the 13th century. Originating at their ancient seat at Craighall, Blairgowrie in Perthshire, this traditional tartan weaves together a deep connection with Scottish tradition. Notably recorded in the Lord Lyon Book and granted recognition by the Scottish Tartans Society, the Rattray tartan is not merely a fashion statement, but an honourable representation of family lineage and cultural identity. Its subtle colour palette, thread count halved to reveal the sett, evokes a sense of understated elegance, fitting for a sept that follows in the footsteps of a noble Clan heritage.

name: Raymond of Doune
description: The Raymond of Doune corporate tartan is a rich, darkly woven tribute to Scotland's storied heritage, its very fabric steeped in tradition and pageantry. Registered for use by a Northern Ireland-based pipe band in 1997, this iconic pattern was specifically commissioned by Lochcarron of Scotland for the 'Raymond of Doune' store - a nod to one of Scotland's most historic and scenic locations. With its sombre hues and intricate textures, this tartan design echoes the country's rich cultural history, recalling images of regal ceremonies, traditional ceilidhs, and the proud tradition of pipe bands that have served as cornerstones of Scottish community life for centuries.

name: Rea [default]
description: The Rea tartan, designed by esteemed weaver Dr Philip D Smith in 1973, is a rich and timeless tribute to Robert Rea of Paoli, Pennsylvania, who proudly bore the surname. This Clan tartan, registered for the name rather than a specific family line, invites wearers to honour their connection to this storied heritage. With its subtle yet vibrant hues, the Rea tartan pays homage to Scotland's revered tradition of tartanry, where clan affiliations were once deeply tied to geographical and familial roots. While originally created for Robert Rea, the design's open registration allows it to be worn by all who bear the name, fostering a sense of community and shared identity among those bound by this enduring legacy.

name: Reagan, (Personal)
description: The Reagan tartan is a personal design born out of heritage and history, created by renowned Dr Philip D Smith in 1962 for Tom Reagan, a distinguished alumnus of the University of Nevada-Reno. Though it remained hidden until 2005, its discovery shed new light on this lesser-known variant of the Reagan tartan, previously registered as #6427. Originally conceived to represent the entire name of Reagan, this specific tartan now stands as a testament to the intricate relationships between Scottish heritage and personal legacy. As part of the Name category, it serves as an important link to Tom Reagan's family history, allowing him to connect with his roots in a unique and meaningful way.

name: Reagan [default]
description: The Reagan tartan is a deeply personal and proud expression of Irish heritage, crafted by Debra J. for the O'Reagan clan to wear with honour. This intricate weave tells the story of a storied family legacy, drawing inspiration from the Clan's esteemed first chief and their ancestral homeland. Crimson threads evoke the regal livery colours of days gone by, while gold accents pay tribute to traditional armorial achievements that have shaped the family's history. The oceanic blues, reminiscent of the waves that surround Ireland, represent the clan's connection to this emerald isle, while lush green hues symbolise a rich and verdant heritage. By wearing the Reagan tartan, one embodies not only their own family ties but also the storied traditions of the O'Reagan clan, proudly proclaiming their Irish roots to the world.

name:
Red Bull
[AKA] Tarbh Deargh
description: The Tarbh Deargh tartan, aptly named Red Bull, embodies the energetic and revitalising spirit of Scotland's most iconic beverage brand. As a Corporate tartan, it is designed to evoke the dynamism and drive of the global company that bears its name. The intricate pattern weaves together a rich tapestry of blues and greens, punctuated by flashes of bold reds, evoking the drink's stimulating properties. Registration notes reveal that Red Bull aims to energise both body and mind, and this tartan seems to capture that essence perfectly - invigorating, refreshing, and ideal for occasions when action is required.

name: Red Chapeau
description: The Red Chapeau Corporate Tartan, designed by St Croix Weaving, embodies the spirit of professional excellence and prestige in Scotland's rich corporate heritage. This distinctive tartan pattern, woven at 60 threads per inch (EPI) with a thread count that exudes sophistication, is reserved for the most esteemed businesses and organisations. Its careful composition, featuring a bold red dominant theme punctuated by subtle secondary colours, creates a striking visual identity that commands respect and authority. Rooted in Scotland's centuries-old tradition of weaving and textile design, the Red Chapeau Tartan is a testament to the country's enduring legacy of innovation and excellence, expertly crafted to make a lasting impression on those who wear it.

name: Red Deer, City
description: The Red Deer City of tartan is a vibrant and storied design that weaves together threads of history and community, thanks to its origins in a poignant commemoration of the 50th anniversary of the Red Deer Highland Games in an Alberta township. Conceived by Joyce Munawych, this District tartan was born from the district's desire to celebrate its unique heritage and cultural identity. Now set to take on a life of its own, it will forever be tied to the town's spirit and tradition, its distinctive pattern echoing the strength and resilience of the local community. This rich and nuanced design embodies the very essence of District tartan – a testament to the enduring power of local history and the indelible mark left by the Highland Games on the lives of those who call it home.

name: Red Hatters United
description: The Red Hatters United tartan is a vibrant, unifying fabric woven with purpose by Mrs Debra Benteau for the Canadian Chapter, Sisters Unlimited, of the Red Hat Society. Inspired by Jenny Joseph's iconic poem "Warning", which urges women to defy convention and wear purple, this tartan reimagines that bold statement in red and purple hues. As a corporate tartan, it embodies the organisation's values of sisterhood and camaraderie among thousands of like-minded individuals around the world. Woven with the intention of creating a distinctive symbol of unity, The Red Hatters United tartan proudly celebrates the collective spirit of women supporting one another, its red and purple colours evoking warmth, creativity, and confidence – a testament to the enduring power of female friendship and community.

name: Red Rum
description: The Red Rum tartan is a poignant tribute to one of British racing's most iconic figures, commemorating the extraordinary achievements of the beloved Thoroughbred horse Red Rum. Registered by Edinburgh Woollen Mill, this Commemorative tartan pays homage to Red Rum's remarkable three-time Grand National Steeplechase win, as well as his second-place finishes in subsequent years. The distinctive design features a striking red colour scheme, echoing the racing colours of maroon and gold, with a nod to the lush green grass of the turf. This timeless tartan serves as a lasting honour to Red Rum's enduring legacy, a testament to his unwavering dedication and skill, which has captivated generations of racing enthusiasts.

name: Red Watch
description: The Red Watch tartan is a striking Fashion design that tells the story of a storied piece of luggage with a rich history. Registered in 1969, this tartan was once known to be associated with 'Queen's Rifles', a name allegedly bestowed upon it by an American manufacturer. Although its origins are somewhat murky, it is now recognised as being woven in Japan for Clemco PDTS., a Baltimore-based company. This distinctive pattern has found new life in the fashion world, evoking the nostalgia of classic luggage and the adventurous spirit of those who once carried their treasured belongings with pride. With no specific connection to a Clan or family heritage, the Red Watch tartan stands on its own as a testament to the enduring legacy of a bygone era, waiting to be woven into the stories of modern fashion enthusiasts.

name: Red White Blue Watch Dress
description: The Red, White, Blue Watch (Dance) tartan, designed by Bill Johnston, is a striking Fashion tartan that embodies the spirit of tradition and movement. This unique variation on the Black Watch sett, originally associated with the Campbell clan, has been adapted to produce a distinctive 'dancer's' tartan for American wearers. Characterised by its bold colour palette of blue, red, white, and green, this tartan tells the story of heritage and cultural exchange. As a Fashion tartan, it is meant to be worn with pride, evoking images of traditional Highland dress and modern-day flair. Although restricted from being worn in formal or traditional settings due to its special association with Clan Campbell's dress, it remains an honourable tribute to Scottish heritage, perfectly suited for those seeking to make a statement through their fashion choices.

name: Redland
description: The Redland tartan is a distinctive and smart design specifically created for the girls' High School for Girls in Bristol, commissioned by Lewis Department Store as their school uniform supplier. This corporate tartan was woven with precision by Marton Mills and Otley Weavers, showcasing its unique characteristics with distinct warp and weft patterns. Originally intended to add a touch of elegance and sophistication to the school's kilted uniform, the Redland tartan has become an integral part of British heritage, celebrating the rich tradition of Scottish textiles while reflecting the modern needs of a forward-thinking educational institution.

name: Redwood
description: The Redwood Dress tartan is a vibrant, fashion-forward creation that embodies the timeless spirit of Scotland's rich textile heritage. As a registered fashion tartan, it has been carefully crafted to complement a range of garments and accessories, from statement dresses to tailored coats. Designed by the skilled weavers at West Coast Woolen Mill, this stunning tartan draws inspiration from the majestic redwood forests that blanket the Scottish countryside. With its bold, saturated colours - rich reds, deep greens, and weathered blues - the Redwood Dress tartan is a fitting tribute to the country's natural beauty and cultural traditions. As part of the Johnston Collection, this tartan is a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy in the world of textiles, where tradition meets innovation and style.

name: Redwoods
description: The majestic Redwoods tartan is a stunning fashion-inspired design, born from the visionary imagination of Aljean of Vancouver. This captivating pattern weaves together shades of deep, rich reds, burnished golds, and subtle earthy tones to evoke the grandeur of ancient forests. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority's esteemed Johnston Collection, Redwoods stands as a testament to the enduring appeal of Scotland's iconic tartan heritage. While not tied to a specific clan or family lineage, this fashion tartan embodies the same rich cultural traditions that have shaped the country for centuries, inviting wearers to don its vibrant colours with pride and sense of Scottish history and identity.

name: Reese
description: The Reese tartan is a unique and personal expression of Scottish heritage, bearing testament to the enduring legacy of its namesake family. Registered as a "Name" tartan, it is reserved exclusively for use by the descendants of Nick Reese, the talented American designer who created this distinctive pattern through Celtic Craft Centre, San Francisco & Edinburgh. Organised with meticulous attention to detail, the Reese tartan weaves together a rich tapestry of Scottish tradition and history, its intricate design echoing the timeless values of family honour and continuity. With its creation predicated on the strong bonds of kinship and belonging, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring importance of personal heritage and cultural identity.

name: Reflections of the Sea
description: Reflections of the Sea is a captivating fashion tartan, inspired by the ever-changing moods of the ocean. Designed by Aljean of Vancouver, this unique pattern weaves together shades of deep blue, rich navy, and weathered grey, evoking the misty Scottish coastlines where sea meets sky. As a Fashion tartan, it is intended to add a touch of maritime elegance to any garment or accessory, while also paying homage to Scotland's rich heritage of nautical tradition. Registration notes confirm that this tartan is part of the Johnston Collection, highlighting its connection to Scotland's storied past and the country's ongoing passion for its iconic textiles.

name: Regalia
description: The Regalia tartan, designed by the renowned Edinburgh Woollen Mill, is a majestic fashion tartan steeped in tradition and heritage. Woven with reverence for Scotland's storied past, this striking pattern is rooted in the Johnston Collection, a treasure trove of Scotland's finest tartans. As a Fashion tartan, Regalia embodies the elegance and sophistication that has come to define Scottish textile design. With its intricate weave and bold colours, it is a testament to the country's rich cultural heritage, evoking images of grandeur and ceremonial splendour. Originally reserved for formal occasions, this tartan now invites wearers to make a statement with their fashion choices, embracing Scotland's timeless traditions while forging a new path forward in style and distinction.

name: Regan [default]
description: The Regan tartan, meticulously designed by Donald Suttie Smith in 2002, holds profound significance for those bearing the name, as well as its newly formed clan family association. Originally created for Father Thomas Regan of Abergavenny, Wales, this distinctive tartan is now reserved exclusively for members of the Regan Clan/Family Association, including individuals with the surname O'Regan and O'Riagain. By virtue of its restricted nature, the Regan tartan serves as a powerful symbol of heritage and identity, connecting its wearers to a rich cultural tradition spanning centuries. Woven with care and attention to detail, this tartan design is not only a testament to Scottish textile ingenuity but also a proud declaration of familial ties and ancestral roots.

name: Regent
description: The Regent tartan, created by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a quintessential example of 20th-century fashion tartanry, its origins shrouded in controversy. Originally derived from the Grant Hunting (#311) by removing its black lines and re-interpretating them as a deep blue hue, it shares identical sett with MacLaren (#342).
