While Wilsons' actions may have raised eyebrows among purists, this fusion of colours has resulted in a stylish, modern tartan that evokes the glamour of Scotland's royal heritage. As a fashion tartan, Regent is designed to be a versatile and eye-catching choice for garments, accessories, or even wallcoverings - its bold, sophisticated colour palette making it an ideal addition to any wardrobe or design scheme.

name: Rei Okamoto
description: This exquisite tartan, designated as 'Rei Okamoto', is a deeply personal creation born out of a desire for uniqueness and exclusivity. Registered to commemorate a special gift from Hiroko Nakada to Rei Okamoto, its very existence serves as a testament to the enduring bond between these two individuals. As a name tartan, this distinctive pattern has been woven with love and dedication, its colours carefully selected to evoke the essence of their relationship. Its unique character is a poignant reminder that, in the world of tartan, each design tells a story - a narrative woven from threads of love, honour, and tradition, destined to remain an intimate secret shared between two souls.

name: Reid 1939
description: The Reid tartan, registered in 1939, is an enigmatic and intriguing example of a lesser-known Scottish heritage design. Originally identified as the 'Family tartan for Reid' by an American visitor, Alma Barker Johnson, its origins are shrouded in mystery, sparking speculation about its pre-1939 existence or potential connection to Sir John Reid. The tartan's significance lies not only in its historical provenance but also in the fact that it was brought back to the United States and incorporated into family clothing, highlighting the strong cultural ties between Scotland and its diaspora communities. With an estimated thread count of approximately 35 threads per inch, this tartan holds a unique place within the world of Scottish textiles, serving as a tangible link to the country's rich heritage and tradition of weaving.

name: Reid (Mill City)
description: The Reid (Mill City) tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Dr John W 'Jack' Reid and his family, whose commitment to serving the Mill City area and surrounding Santiam Canyon in Oregon was marked by dedication to medicine. This poignant name tartan weaves together a rich tapestry of colours, evoking the medical profession's crimson reds and whites, as well as the vibrant shades of green that echo the lush forests of the Cascade mountains, while blues reminiscent of the tranquil Santiam River provide a soothing counterpoint. Registered in honour of Dr Reid and his family, this tartan proudly wears its heart on its sleeve, celebrating their unwavering service to the community and the lasting impact it has had on generations to come.

name: Reid Green
description: The Reid, Green tartan is a testament to the rich heritage and traditions of Clan Reid, whose members have proudly worn this distinctive design for generations. Registered in 1991 by Philip D. Smith for William M. Reid, Jr., this variation on the classic Robertson tartan was created as an inclusive alternative, allowing all bearers of the name to claim kinship with the esteemed clan. With its subtle nuances and historical depth, the Reid, Green tartan is a vibrant representation of Scottish culture, reflecting the values of community, loyalty, and heritage that have long defined Clan Reid's identity. As a proud member of this family tartan tradition, the Reid, Green tartan invites wearers to connect with their roots and honour their ancestors, while also celebrating the enduring legacy of Scotland's most storied clans.

name: Reid of Straloch
description: The Reid of Straloch tartan, designed by J. Wallace Reid in the 1980s, is a personal family tartan imbued with deep Scottish heritage. As a Name tartan, it is reserved for use within specific families, in this case, those bearing the surname Reid. This unique design was registered to signify its significance and distinction from other tartans, reflecting the individuality of the Reid family's history and tradition. With an intriguing variation between entries #2066 and #4079, both referencing the Scottish Tartans Authority, it is clear that this tartan has been carefully considered and executed with attention to detail. The Reid of Straloch tartan serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Reid family, whose roots stretch back through generations, bound by threads of tradition, culture, and family ties.

name: Reid Taylor House Check
description: The Reid and Taylor tartan is a striking corporate design that embodies the essence of modern Scottish heritage, launched with great fanfare in 1984 to coincide with the Scottish launch of Tokyo's iconic fashion show. As a registered Corporate tartan, it has been selected for its versatility and adaptability, making it an ideal choice for businesses and organisations seeking to establish a strong connection to Scotland. This distinctive House Check pattern, with its bold colours and intricate design, is said to have captured the attention of Her Royal Highness, the Duke of Edinburgh, at the prestigious Edinburgh fashion show in Parliament Hall. Today, this tartan continues to symbolise excellence and professionalism, inviting wearers to draw upon the rich traditions of Scotland's textile heritage.

name: Remony Red
description: The Remony (Red) tartan, designed by renowned textile expert Polly Wittering, is a vibrant and modern fashion tartan that embodies the warm spirit of Scotland's Highlands. This bold and eye-catching design, registered under House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., was created with the intention of being showcased on a range of gift products, set to be sold by this esteemed retailer. With its distinctive red hues and subtle texture variations, the Remony (Red) tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage while evoking a sense of modernity and style. As a fashion tartan, it is perfectly suited for anyone looking to add a touch of Scottish flair to their wardrobe or home decor, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to honour the country's iconic tartan traditions.

name: Renfrew 2
description: The Renfrew #2 tartan is a timeless fashion classic, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's storied clan families. As a variation of the esteemed Stewart tartan, it wears the honour of the Scottish royal dynasty on its sleeve, evoking the grandeur and pageantry of centuries past. Registered under the Fashion category, this tartan design was carefully crafted by the skilled weavers at West Coast Woolen Mill to bring a touch of traditional elegance to modern fashion. With no restrictions on its use, the Renfrew #2 tartan invites wearers to don a piece of Scotland's storied history, making it an ideal choice for anyone seeking to add a dash of Highland flair to their wardrobe or accessories.

name: Renfrew
description: The Renfrew tartan is a stylish and enduring fashion favourite, with its rich hues and subtle pattern evoking the warmth and heritage of Scotland's west coast. Registration notes reveal that it was first woven in the Tam-o-Shanter collection, likely inspired by the distinctive headdresses worn by Scottish Highlanders during the 18th-century military campaign that bore this name. As a fashion tartan, Renfrew has been reproduced by renowned designers such as West Coast Woolen Mill, whose #4334-#10800 variant is also recorded in a prestigious book collection. Free from restrictions on its use, the Renfrew tartan can be worn with pride by anyone looking to connect with Scottish heritage and add a touch of authentic style to their wardrobe, whether for formal or casual occasions alike.

name: Rennie
description: The Rennie tartan is a deeply personal and storied design, originating in Fife during the early 1980s for its namesake, Robin Rennie. As a Name tartan, it is closely tied to the MacDonald family's heritage, specifically the sept of MacDonell of Keppoch, from which Rennies, Rainys, and Rainnies are derived. The tartan's design was influenced by an old Wilsons' sample of Gunn, reflecting the rich weaving traditions that have long defined Scotland's clan system. Weavers were challenged to adapt and innovate, resulting in unique patterns like this one. With its distinctive balance of colours and subtle nuances, the Rennie tartan embodies the complexities and histories of Scotland's intricate tapestry, offering a tangible connection to the country's proud heritage for those who wear it with honour.

name: Renton [default]
description: The Renton tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's ancestral Berwick tartan, expertly reimagined by Blair Urquhart for this family's personal crest. As an asymmetric design, it cleverly subverts traditional symmetrical patterns, reflecting the natural world and the changing hues of autumn that evoke the Renton family's roots in the region. Muted tones in antique colour palettes pay homage to the subtle nuances of the Scottish landscape, imbuing the tartan with a sense of tradition and history. This bespoke Name tartan is more than just a design - it serves as a proud declaration of family identity, woven from the threads of heritage and ancestral connection that define Scotland's storied past.

name: Renwick [default]
description: The Renwick tartan is a poignant and storied woven heritage, steeped in the rich traditions of Scotland's clan history. As one of the few tartans not specifically associated with a particular Scottish clan or family, it bears an uncanny resemblance to the revered Clergy tartan, differing only subtly in colour palette. Its origins shrouded in mystery, with details gleaned from a specimen in the Catto Collection, this tartan is believed to have been inspired by the country's complex religious past. Commemorating James Renwick, the last Scottish man executed for his convictions in 1688, this tartan serves as a powerful tribute to those who fought for their principles and faith. With restrictions in place to preserve its historical integrity, the Renwick tartan remains an evocative testament to Scotland's complex heritage, waiting to be woven into the fabric of its history once more.

name: Rhode Island State
description: The Rhode Island State tartan is a vibrant and distinctively American interpretation of traditional Scottish weaving, created specifically for the Ocean State by Claire Donaldson of House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. As an officially designated state tartan, it serves as a proud symbol of Rhode Island's heritage and identity, reflecting the state's rich history and cultural traditions. Designated as the district tartan, its unique patterns and colours are carefully chosen to evoke the spirit of the region, rather than representing a specific clan or family association. Recognised by the St Andrew's Society, this distinctive tartan is now an integral part of Rhode Island's fabric, with distribution controlled by the Society to ensure its authenticity and integrity is maintained.

name: Rees of Wales
description: The Rhys of Wales tartan is a distinctive and modern design, born from the cultural resurgence of Welsh heritage in recent years. Registration notes reveal that, although not rooted in centuries-old genealogical or territorial significance, the 'of Wales' suffix serves as a nod to its origins. This tartan's unusual composition, featuring odd-numbered threads and varied warp and weft patterns, sets it apart from traditional Celtic designs. Crafted by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, now sadly closed, Rhys of Wales reflects the growing commercial appeal of the Cilt in Wales since its introduction by Wales Tartan Centres around 1998. As such, it holds a special place in the realm of contemporary tartan design, one that pays homage to Welsh tradition while embracing innovation and commercial endeavour.

name: Richards of Wales
description: The Richard of Wales tartan is a distinctive name tartan, woven with great flair by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys, for Wales Tartan Centres in 1998. This vibrant pattern pays tribute to the rich heritage of Wales, albeit one that is more commercially popular than historically rooted. The use of "of Wales" in its title serves as a nod to its origins, rather than indicating territorial significance. Notably, this tartan deviates from traditional Celtic patterns, incorporating odd-numbered threads and unusual warp and weft combinations, setting it apart from other Celtic designs. As with many modern tartans, its inclusion in this index does not confer historical or genealogical credibility, yet its popularity endures, a testament to the enduring appeal of Welsh cultural heritage.

name: Richecourt
description: The Richecourt, Baron of tartan is a rare and esteemed family register tartan, carefully crafted for Gary Martin Beaver's distinction as a noble titleholder. Registered in honour of his multifaceted titles, which spanned both secular and ceremonial realms, this intricate tartan weaves together a rich tapestry of heritage and tradition. As the creation of renowned designer Gordon Nicolson, it embodies the technical expertise and artistic flair that define traditional Scottish textiles. With its unique characteristics specified in the registration notes, this tartan serves as a tangible representation of Lord Beaver's illustrious status, bearing witness to the enduring legacy of his noble lineage.

name: Richmond (Alan) personal; Richmond de Ellel
description: The Richmond de Ellel tartan, a rare and intimate family heirloom, tells the story of a cherished legacy passed down through generations. Registered in a private capacity for the sole use of the Richmond de Ellel family, this personal tartan design holds a profound significance within its exclusive circle. Its muted colour palette, reminiscent of the timeless Burberry check, belies a rich history and cultural heritage that is uniquely tied to this Scottish clan's identity. As an unregistered tartan, it falls outside the formal frameworks of traditional tartan guilds, yet its exclusivity only serves to underscore its importance within the family's own tradition and honour. Woven with love and devotion by Alan Richmond, the designer himself, this tartan is a poignant reminder of the enduring bonds that tie families together through their shared heritage and history.

name: Richmond
description: The Stewart, Royal Blue tartan is a storied and revered heritage pattern, steeped in the rich history of Scotland's most noble clan. As a registered member of the Scottish Tartans Society, this iconic tartan holds great honour within the world of Scottish heritage, tracing its roots back to the esteemed House of Stewart, whose descendants have long been synonymous with Scottish royalty. Characterised by its distinctive blue tone and carefully woven patterns, this tartan is a symbol of tradition, family pride, and a deep connection to Scotland's storied past. With no designer credited, it is likely that this traditional pattern has been passed down through generations, awaiting discovery by those seeking to weave their own unique thread into the fabric of Scottish history.

name: Riddoch (archive)
description: The Riddoch tartan, designed by Tony Murray for Albert "Bert" Riddoch of Bearsden, Glasgow, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's clan system. Originally created as a personal tartan for Bert, it was later adopted by anyone bearing the name, reflecting the strong connections between family ties and tribal identity. This distinctive design is based on Campbell of Breadalbane, a nod to the historical significance of the Campbell clan in Scottish history. As a private investigator involved in high-profile covert operations, Bert Riddoch's association with this tartan serves as a symbol of his esteemed profession and dedication to justice, while also honouring his family heritage that has been woven into the very fabric of Scotland's traditions.

name: Rikaco (Japan) personal; Classic
description: The Rikaco Classic tartan is a sophisticated and modern interpretation of traditional Scottish weaving, carefully crafted by renowned textile experts at Lochcarron of Scotland. Registered specifically for use by Japan's esteemed fashion house, Dinos Inc, this iconic tartan embodies the country's unique cultural fusion with Western style. The Fashion category classification reflects its intended application in high-end fashion design, where bold statements and striking visuals reign supreme. Notably, a licence agreement grants exclusive rights to weave the Rikaco Classic to Lochcarron of Scotland, ensuring that only authentic reproductions of this tartan are produced. As an ambassador for Scottish heritage in the world of fashion, the Rikaco Classic tartan pays homage to the country's rich weaving traditions while embracing its cosmopolitan spirit, blending timeless elegance with cutting-edge flair.

name: Rikaco (Japan) personal; Morning Dew 1
description: The Rikaco Morning Dew tartan, designed by renowned Scottish weavers at Lochcarron of Scotland, is a vibrant and captivating fashion tartan that embodies the spirit of cultural exchange and fusion. Originally registered for a Japanese company, this distinctive tartan is a testament to the global connections and influences that have shaped Scotland's rich textile heritage. With its unique colour palette and precise sett pattern, Rikaco Morning Dew adds a modern and international flair to traditional Scottish tartanwear. This fashion tartan is perfect for those looking to make a statement with their sartorial choice, while also paying homage to the country of origin that inspired its creation.

name: Rikaco (Japan) personal; Morning Dew 2
description: This exquisite Fashion tartan, designated as Rikaco Morning Dew #2, is a masterful creation by renowned Scottish weavers at Lochcarron of Scotland. This captivating design was originally presented under the name Rikaco Morning Dew, with its colour palette somewhat compromised in the registration notes. Despite this, the subtle nuances of the colours shine through, evoking the misty dawns of Scotland's rugged landscapes. As a Fashion tartan, it is ideal for adding a touch of traditional Scottish style to clothing and accessories, paying homage to the country's rich heritage and textile traditions. With its unique character and Lochcarron's expertise, Rikaco Morning Dew #2 promises to bring a hint of the Highlands to any outfit, while respecting the ancient art of tartan weaving.

name: Ritch
description: The Ritch tartan, registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1819, is an enduring testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage. Originally intended for silk weaving, which seems unlikely given its sturdy construction, this 'Old Superfine Tartan Sett' has withstood the test of time. Named after the remarkable quantity of fine fabric it was made from, the exact origin of the name 'Ritch' remains a mystery, but its significance in Highland dress is undeniable. Featured in William Wilson's stock list as early as 1800, this tartan has been worn and cherished by generations of Scots for its timeless beauty and traditional craftsmanship.

name: Ritchie [default]
description: The Ritchie tartan, a storied family crest from Scotland's rich clan heritage, holds a deep significance within Scottish tradition. Registered under Clan/Family category, this distinctive pattern is steeped in history and cultural importance. Commissioned by Dalgliesh, D.C, a renowned expert in traditional tartan design, the Ritchie tartan has undergone meticulous preparation for weaving, ensuring its authenticity. Despite not featuring any specific details within the registration notes, it is understood that this tartan holds a special place in the family's lineage, woven into the very fabric of Scottish identity and tradition. As an official tartan, the Ritchie will forever be tied to its family's honour and legacy, proudly carrying on the rich tapestry of Scotland's storied past.

name: Rob Roy (Film)
description: Rob Roy, the iconic corporate tartan, is an inspired interpretation of Scotland's rich heritage, born from the cinematic world of the legendary Highland warrior, Rob Roy MacGregor. Designed by Gordon Covell at The Islay Woollen Mill, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the film of the same name, which brought the 19th-century hero to life on the big screen. Woven with precision and flair, Rob Roy corporate tartan embodies the spirit of Scottish tradition and cultural identity, its subtle nuances and rich textures evoking the rugged beauty of the Highlands. Perfect for those who embody the values of courage, loyalty, and resilience, this tartan is a fitting choice for individuals, companies, or organisations seeking to celebrate their Scottish heritage with style and authenticity.

name: Robb Red
description: The Bhatti tartan is a stirring example of Scottish heritage, woven from threads of tradition and family history. Registered in 2006, this Name tartan was created by Dr Nadeem T to commemorate his own wedding celebration, held in the heart of Glasgow's Pollokshields district. As a second-generation Scot with a proud military lineage - his father and grandfather having served in the British Army - Dr Bhatti sought to honour his ancestors' service through this vibrant design. The tartan now carries the Bhatti name as its licence, open to anyone bearing the surname to proudly wear. This richly woven fabric not only celebrates Scottish tradition but also serves as a testament to the enduring bonds of family and heritage that connect us all.

name: Robb
description: The Robb tartan is a personal design born from the esteemed Martin Robb of Carroglen, Comrie, Perthshire, and crafted by renowned weaver Peter MacDonald. This subtle yet distinctive tartan holds significance for those bearing the name Robb, serving as a symbol of heritage and identity. As a registered Name tartan, it can be worn by anyone with the surname Robb, yet its association with Martin Robb is deeply personal. A nod to Scotland's rich clan history, this tartan weaves together ancient traditions with modern significance, providing a unique means of self-expression for those who bear the name. Those sporting this tartan would do well to consider bearing the designer's wish, and extend a courtesy to its original creator by advising any Martin Robb they may know that their namesake has been represented in such fine fashion.

name: Robberstad
description: The Robberstad tartan is a unique and captivating Name tartan, woven with love and passion by Strathmore Woollen Co. of Forfar, Scotland. Designated as the exclusive heritage tartan of its namesake family, it holds deep significance for those bearing the name Robberstad, hailing from Norway's Rogoland and Bomlo, or connected through blood ties to Scottish and English families through the female line. Originally created by John W. Robberstad and his wife, both accomplished pipers, this tartan tells a story of cultural heritage and family legacy. With its distinct colours and precise sett, it can be worn with pride by anyone with the surname Robberstad, serving as a symbol of identity, history, and tradition that connects the wearer to their roots.

name: Robbins [default]
description: The Robbins tartan, with its bold and striking colours, is an iconic fashion design born from the renowned Pendleton Woollen Mills. Although originally intended as a Clan/Family tartan by the Scottish Tartans Society, it is widely regarded as a fashionable choice, reflecting the American company's signature style. The tartan's origins are rooted in a single thread weave of a wool shirt, which was painstakingly counted to create this unique pattern. While its classification may be subject to debate, one thing is certain - Robbins has captured the hearts of many with its dynamic interplay of blues and greens, evoking the wild landscapes and rich heritage of Scotland.

name: Robert Gordon University
description: The Robert Gordon University tartan, created by Michael King of Philip King Kiltmakers in 1997, is a distinctive corporate tartan born from the rich heritage of Scotland's industrial past. Originally commissioned to represent Robert Gordon University, this carefully crafted pattern weaves together elements of Scottish tradition with modern flair, evoking the dynamic spirit of innovation and learning that defines the institution. With its unique colour palette and precision-cut threads, this tartan serves as a proud emblem of university life, connecting past and present through its connection to the historic Edinburgh Woollen Mill in Langholm, where it was first worn as a scarf many years earlier.

name: Robert Wiseman Dairies
description: The Wiseman, Robert corporate tartan is a celebration of Scottish heritage and community spirit, woven into its intricate pattern. Designed by Geoffrey Highland Crafts in honour of Robert Wiseman's Golden Jubilee, this distinctive tartan bears testament to the company's significant contribution to Scotland's dairy industry. As a Category Corporate design, it reflects the values of professionalism, hard work, and tradition that define business excellence in Scotland. The registration notes pay tribute to the man behind the name, acknowledging his enduring impact on the country's rural communities. This tartan serves as a proud symbol of corporate identity, proudly representing Robert Wiseman's legacy and heritage, while paying homage to the rich cultural tapestry of Scotland.

name: Roberts of Wales
description: The Roberts of Wales tartan is a vibrant and distinctive Name tartan that embodies the rich cultural heritage of the Welsh nation. Designed by Sheila Daniel for Wales Tartan Centres, this modern tartan celebrates the region's unique identity, though its historical significance is somewhat more recent in development. With an unusual warp and weft structure featuring odd-numbered threads and varied colour schemes, it deviates from traditional Celtic tartans. The use of 'of Wales' in the tartan name serves as a nod to its creation by Cambrian Woollen Mill, now closed, and highlights the collaboration between Sheila Daniel and the centre. To ensure authenticity, a consent is required from Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea prior to weaving, underscoring the importance of respecting Welsh tradition.

name: Robertson 1819
description: The Robertson tartan is a storied and prestigious Scottish heritage pattern, originating from one of Scotland's most renowned clans, Clan Robertsons. Designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, a respected Scottish family of weavers, this tartan has been woven with pride since the early 19th century, when it first appeared in their influential Key Pattern Book of 1819. With its rich history dating back to at least 1800, the Robertson tartan is steeped in tradition and honour, reflecting the clan's values and legacy. As a Clan/Family registration, this tartan holds significant cultural significance for those bearing the name Robertsons or seeking connection with their ancestral heritage, allowing them to wear a tangible symbol of their family's history and identity.

name: Robertson Dress
description: The enigmatic Robertson Dress #1, designed by esteemed D.C. Dalgliesh in its prime, is a true marvel of Scottish tartanry. Originally intended as 'Dancers' Fancy', this captivating design has captured the hearts of many, yet remains shrouded in mystery among mainstream weavers, who have opted to neglect its production. This Fashion category tartan tells a tale of elegance and refinement, evoking the grandeur of Scotland's storied past. The intricate pattern, woven with precision by Dalgliesh's skilled hands, is said to embody the spirit of traditional Scottish dancing - a fusion of movement, music, and community that continues to enthrall audiences to this day. As a rare and exclusive creation, the Robertson Dress #1 holds a special place in the annals of tartan heritage, waiting to be rediscovered by those with a passion for Scotland's rich textile traditions.

name: Robertson Dress #2
description: The Robertson Dress #2 is a fashion tartan steeped in traditional Scottish heritage, its elegant colours and intricate pattern evoking the sophistication of Scotland's rich cultural history. Designed by renowned textile artist Dalgliesh, D C, this tartan was originally intended as a 'Dancers' Fancy', suggesting its origins in the ornate designs used to adorn kilts worn by Highland dancers. Its classification as a Fashion tartan ensures that it can be used for a wide range of stylish garments, from formal evening wear to more casual attire, allowing the wearer to add a touch of traditional Scottish flair to their wardrobe.

name: Robertson Hunting
description: Robertson Hunting #1 is an intricate and storied tartan set, steeped in the rich history of Scotland's clan culture. Originally used by the Loyal Clan Donnachie Volunteers raised in 1803, its provenance lies with the Robertsons of the North, a family dynasty that has woven their own unique identity into this ancient design. A testament to the traditions of Scottish heritage, this tartan is said to date back to pre-referenced times, making it one of the oldest and most enigmatic patterns in the Register of Tartans. The set's association with the Robertsons of Kindeace adds a layer of complexity to its narrative, yet ultimately underscores its significance as an enduring symbol of family and loyalty.

name: Robertson Hunting #2
description: Robertson Hunting #2, designed by W & A. K. Johnston in 1906, is a timeless testament to Scotland's rich hunting heritage. Originally introduced as part of H. Whyte's 'The Tartans of the Clans and Septs of Scotland' publication, this tartan variant was inadvertently created due to a printing error. Despite this, it has become an enduring representation of the Robertson clan, whose history is steeped in tradition and bravery. Weaving this tartan today is a nod to Scotland's storied past, with its distinctive colours evoking images of rugged Highland landscapes and storied battles. Though it exists in a 'dress' rather than the traditional 'hunting' version, Robertson Hunting #2 remains an honourable symbol of family heritage, bearing witness to the enduring legacy of the Robertson clan.

name:
Robertson of Struan [default]
[AKA] Robertson of Struan
description: The Robertson (Struan) tartan is a timeless and storied pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, registered to the esteemed Clan MacKenzie - one of Scotland's most noble and ancient clans. This distinctive tartan, woven with precision and care, holds a place of honour within the macKenzie family's tradition, symbolising their enduring connection to the Highlands. With its unique blend of blues, reds, and greens, the Robertson (Struan) tartan evokes the rugged beauty and rich cultural heritage of Scotland's majestic mountains and lochs. Its origins, though shrouded in mystery, date back to a 20th-century sample stored within the Highland Society of London's archives, adding a layer of authenticity to this revered clan tartan.

name:
Robertson White line
[AKA] Robertson New
description: The Robertson (White line) tartan, a stalwart symbol of Scottish heritage, tells the story of a proud clan lineage through its intricate weave. This distinctive variation, created by Wilsons in 19th-century Bannockburn, marks a subtle yet significant deviation from the traditional Robertson tartan. Characterised by its white lines on a dark blue background, this tartan was first seen at a grand occasion in 1822, when the Chief of the clan wore a bespoke suit adorned with Wilsons' unique tartan to the Levee of George IV. As a testament to the enduring power of tradition and family identity, the Robertson (White line) tartan remains an honourable emblem of Scottish history, weaving together threads of cultural significance and personal legacy.

name: Robieson (Graham) personal
description: The Robieson, Graham Alexander tartan is a distinctive and intimate design, carefully crafted by its creator to reflect his own unique heritage and identity. As a personal name tartan, it holds great significance for Graham A Robieson himself, serving as a tangible representation of his family history and Scottish roots. Although the registration notes specify that this tartan may only be used in the personal favour of the designer, it remains an important part of Scotland's rich textile tradition, woven with love and attention by Geoffrey Highland Crafts Limited. This tartan embodies the warmth and depth of Scottish heritage, its subtle nuances and earthy tones evoking a sense of tradition and continuity that connects us to the country's storied past.

name: Robieson #2
description: Meet Robieson Kith & Kin, a vibrant and uniquely personal tartan designed with love for those closest to Graham A Robieson. This Name tartan, registered specifically for his friends and family, is a nod to the iconic packaging of Scotland's beloved Irn-Bru soda. The colours, carefully selected by Graham himself, evoke a sense of warmth and camaraderie, much like the bonds shared among kin. As a testament to Scottish heritage and tradition, this tartan is woven with pride by Geoffrey Highland Crafts Limited. With its bold and playful spirit, Robieson Kith & Kin is the perfect choice for those seeking a distinctive and meaningful way to connect with their loved ones, whether through family gatherings or social events – an honourable tribute to Graham's heritage and the joy of shared company.

name: Robieson
description: The Robieson tartan is a distinctive and meaningful name tartan, created to honour the Robieson surname and its connections. Designed by Graham Alexander Robieson, this tartan is a variation of the Robertson Red sett, paying homage to the origins of the nickname "Robieson" as a diminutive form of Robert Stewart. Woven with pride by Geoffrey Highland Crafts Limited, this tartan is open to use by anyone with a name connection or familial ties to the Robieson surname, making it a cherished emblem of Scottish heritage and tradition for those who bear the name.

name:
Robin Hood
[AKA] MacGregor Rob Roy; Hunting
description: This vibrant Fashion tartan, designated as Robin Hood/Wilsons' No.224/Rob Roy Hunting, is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and the enduring legacy of its most famous heroes. Weaving back in 1994 for Haggerts of Aberfeldy as 'Rob Roy hunting', this tartan design draws inspiration from the bold spirit of the legendary outlaw Robin Hood, whilst also paying homage to the storied Scottish hero Rob Roy MacGregor. Crafted by Wilsons of Bannockburn, a renowned textile firm established in 1770 near Stirling, this tartan's complex colour palette and precise sett are a masterclass in traditional weaving. While its design was created for fashion purposes, it proudly wears the badge of Scottish tradition, its historical significance and cultural resonance underscoring the enduring appeal of Scotland's most beloved symbols of courage and defiance.

name: Robinson, Barbara Ann (Personal)
description: The Robinson, Barbara Ann tartan is a deeply personal and intimate design, woven with love and devotion to commemorate its creator's mother, Barbara Ann Robinson. As a registered Name tartan, it holds a special place in Scottish heritage, signifying family identity and tradition. Designed by Graham Alexander Robieson for his mother's enduring legacy, this unique tartan is reserved exclusively for Barbara Ann Robinson and her immediate family members only, due to the restrictions placed upon its registration. Woven with skill and care by Geoffrey of Edinburgh, the tartan's intricate pattern tells a story of family history, cultural tradition, and personal devotion, imbuing its wearers with a sense of pride, connection to their roots, and love for one another.

name: Robinson Dress
description: The Robinson Dress tartan is a storied family heritage woven into its very fabric, originating from the esteemed Pendleton Woolen Mills in Oregon, USA. This ancient clan tartan, dating back to Irish and Scottish roots, boasts a rich maroon hue reminiscent of the royal or Styrian purple, imbuing it with an air of grandeur and solemnity. While the historical authenticity of its origins remains uncertain, its enduring adoption by the Robinson family is a testament to the power of tradition and community. Today, this tartan holds significance on special family occasions, evoking memories of ancestors past and the strong cultural bonds that unite them.

name: Robinson Dress #2
description: The Swiss Red #2 tartan is a vibrant and distinctive District pattern, woven with great precision to pay tribute to a most unexpected yet welcome guest in Scotland's rich cultural tapestry: Switzerland. Registered to commemorate the Swiss Consulate General, this tartan design embodies the warm hospitality and camaraderie that has long been a hallmark of Scottish tradition. With its bold, crimson hues and intricate threadwork, the Swiss Red #2 tartan is a testament to the enduring power of international friendship and collaboration. Created by Geoffrey at Tailor Highland Crafts Limited, this unique District pattern is poised to become a cherished symbol of Scotland's special affinity with Switzerland, as well as a vibrant expression of Scottish heritage in its own right.

name: Rocca (Bundanoon) personal
description: The Bundanoon tartan is a vibrant tribute to the charming town in the Southern Highlands of New South Wales, Australia, where Scottish heritage meets Australian culture. Designed by Betty Johnston, with input from estate agent Peter Rocca, this District tartan weaves together the region's unique identity, featuring a green background representing the town's 'deep green valleys', complemented by the bright hues of yellow wattle and red Waratah, an emblem of the Wingecarribee shire. The parallel lines evoke the railway track that runs through Bundanoon, a nod to the town's rich history. The tartan also incorporates blue for the Australian sky and white for the misty mornings that signal a new day in this idyllic town. Originally introduced at the 2000 Brigadoon - Bundanoon Highland Games, this design is now an official representation of Bundanoon's spirit, with its registration notes underscoring the tartan's connection to the annual gathering that attracts over 20,000 visitors and supports local charities and community groups.

name: Roderick Dhu
description: The Roderick Dhu tartan is a District tartan, one of the six categories of recognised Scottish tartans, designated to specific geographical regions or clans. This distinctive tartan's origins are tied to a 1967 necktie purchased in Ottawa, with information from Alex Lumsden of Toronto providing insight into its history. The threads that now weave together in intricate patterns evoke a sense of place and heritage, reflecting the enduring legacy of Scotland's textile traditions. With no specific designer credited for this traditional tartan, it stands as a testament to the rich cultural tapestry of Scotland, shaped by generations of skilled weavers and dyers who have preserved its heritage through the careful handling of each thread.

name: Roeger (Rocky) personal; American Heritage
description: The American Heritage tartan, designed by William C (Rocky) Roeger III of USA Kilts, is a poignant tribute to the nation's heritage and its people. Inspired by the iconic colours of the American flag - red, white, and blue - this fashion tartan proudly wears these hues, symbolising freedom, courage, and patriotism. The addition of black to the palette serves as a sombre reminder of the sacrifices made by those who have defended the country's values and way of life. This privately designed tartan is open to all, regardless of Celtic ancestry, offering an opportunity for anyone to wear their American heritage with pride. As a testament to the enduring spirit of the nation, the American Heritage tartan embodies the very essence of American tradition and identity.

name: Roeger (Rocky) personal; Dropkick Murphys
description: The Dropkick Murphys corporate tartan is a vibrant and energetic design born from the spirit of Irish-American Punk Rock, carefully crafted by Roeger III, William C for the eponymous Boston band in 2004. Commissioned specifically to represent the band's unique identity, this tartan draws inspiration from the rich heritage of Scottish culture, specifically the Wallace Hunting tartan, which Scruffy, their bagpiper, proudly wears on stage. The bold colours and distinctive pattern are a testament to the band's Irish-American roots and their unapologetic punk rock attitude, making this tartan an authentic expression of their honour and tradition. As a corporate design, it is intended for use by companies that want to associate themselves with the energetic and rebellious spirit of the Dropkick Murphys, but its authenticity is contingent upon obtaining explicit written consent from the copyright holders, Rocky Roeger and Josh Wallace, ensuring the integrity and cultural sensitivity of this iconic tartan.

name: Roeger (Rocky) personal; German American
description: The German American tartan, designed by William C Roeger III of USA Kilts, is a unique fusion of Scottish heritage with modern flair, celebrating the rich cultural heritage of German Americans. This fashion tartan was specifically created to pay tribute to the significant contributions of German immigrants to American history, and as such, it proudly wears its colours on its sleeve - literally. The vibrant red and white stripes, reminiscent of the American flag, are complemented by black and red chevrons, echoing the German national colours, creating a striking visual representation of unity and shared heritage. While not affiliated with any specific clan or family group, this tartan is open to anyone who wishes to wear it in honour of their own German-American roots, making it a powerful symbol of cultural pride and identity.

name: Roeger (Rocky) personal; German Heritage
description: The "German Heritage" tartan, designed by William C. Roeger III, is a vibrant and meaningful fashion tartan that pays homage to those with German roots. This unique tartan was created as a way for individuals to proudly showcase their heritage, regardless of clan affiliation or nationality, making it an ideal choice for anyone looking to add a touch of German culture to their wardrobe. The colours, inspired by the German flag, evoke the spirit of unity and tradition that is at the heart of German identity. As a private fashion tartan, this design allows its wearer to express their individuality while still celebrating their shared heritage, making it a special choice for anyone looking to make a statement about their cultural roots.

name: Roeger (Rocky) personal; Irish Heritage
description: The Irish Heritage tartan, designed by William C Roeger III with USA Kilts, is a vibrant expression of solidarity and pride for those with Irish roots. This fashion tartan is not bound by clan affiliations or nationalities, allowing its wearers to proudly don the colours of their heritage. The bold green represents the Emerald Isle's lush landscapes, symbolising the warmth and hospitality that Ireland embodies. Conversely, the deep black hues pay homage to the struggles and strife that Ireland has endured, while the crisp white signifies a brighter future for the country and its people. As a private fashion tartan, it is accessible to all who wish to embody Irish heritage, making it a unique opportunity to connect with one's roots and celebrate the nation's enduring spirit.

name: Rollings
description: The Dewi Sant tartan, registered in recognition of its distinctive character, is a testament to the rich heritage of Welsh identity. Named after St David, the patron saint of Wales, this tartan embodies the country's proud history and cultural traditions. Designed by the skilled weavers at Cambrian Woollen Mill Llanwrtyd Wells, Dewi Sant has been carefully crafted to reflect the unique nuances of Welsh textiles. As a Category Name, this tartan is meant to evoke the spirit of national identity, worn with honour to signify pride in Welsh heritage. While no restrictions apply to its use, it remains an important part of Wales' cultural legacy, weaving together generations of tradition and storytelling.

name: Rollo [default]
description: The Rollo tartan is a deeply rooted and storied Scottish heritage, its existence validated by its registration on the Lyon Court Book in 1984. Originating from an asymmetric sett pattern, this Clan/Family tartan has been woven to commemorate Lord Rollo, whose life was marked by a philanthropic society formed in the mid-1970s, in his honour. D.C. Dalgliesh's contribution to this tradition is notable, as he wove the tartan in 1976, utilising Old Colours exclusively. A testament to Scotland's rich textile history and cultural significance, Rollo tartan is woven from a specific count of dark blue, dark blue with mid-blue, or light blue threads, although it was intended to be depicted in azure hues on its original registration notes. Its existence serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring legacy of Lord Rollo and the dedication of those who continue to preserve Scotland's storied tartans.

name: Romantic Scotland Madonna
description: The Romantic Scotland tartan, designed by John Gillespie of renowned Scottish textile firm, Johnstons of Elgin, is a commemorative tribute to the iconic American singer-songwriter Madonna's historic wedding to Guy Ritchie at Dornoch Cathedral and Skibo Castle in 2001. This unique tartan weaves together a vibrant palette of colours, including blue reminiscent of her early album 'True Blue', yellow evoking the vibrant energy of her 'Blonde Ambition' tour, pearl white inspired by the classic 'Like A Virgin', and rich purple to represent Scotland's iconic heather. Incorporating elements from various Scottish and American tartans, this design nods to the couple's global connections while proudly celebrating their Scottish heritage. Originally designated as the Madonna tartan, it now bears the commemorative title of Romantic Scotland, serving as a cherished reminder of the special occasion that brought together two international powerhouses in a union of love and style.

name: Rome City
description: The City of Rome Pipe Band tartan is a vibrant celebration of Italian heritage, woven with precision by weaver Batley of Huddersfield. This District tartan was specifically designed for the City of Rome Pipe Band, formed in 2000 to showcase the unique blend of Scottish and Italian traditions. The distinctive black and navy blue background pay homage to the colours of the Italian national football team, while shades of yellow, orange, and maroon reflect the gold of the Vatican and the iconic hues of Rome's Eternal City. This tartan is a testament to the growing popularity of pipe bands in Italy, with the City of Rome Pipe Band being one of the first to be formed on Italian soil. With its rich symbolism and cultural significance, this tartan is not only a fitting tribute to Rome but also an honour to the UK's centuries-old piping tradition.

name: Romsdal Norway
description: The Romsdal tartan is a testament to the rich history of Scottish heritage in Norway's western fjords. Registered as a District tartan, it tells the story of Captain Sinclair's ill-fated campaign with the Swedish army in 1612, where he was tragically killed by a silver bullet. The distinctive red hue could be interpreted as a deep, earthy brown, echoing the rugged landscapes of Romsdal and its unique tartan tradition. As one of only a few tartans originating from this region, Romsdal pays homage to the brave Scots who settled in Norway after their defeat at Kringen, leaving behind lasting place names such as Skottlia and Skotte. This striking design is not only steeped in historical significance but also proudly represents the cultural identity of its Norwegian birthplace, serving as a poignant reminder of the enduring bonds between Scotland and her Nordic kin.

name: Romsdal Tresfjord
description: Romsdal Tresfjord, a quintessential Norwegian tartan design, bears testament to the rich cultural heritage of the region from which it originates. As a District tartan, it is deeply rooted in its geographical roots, reflecting the unique character of Romsdalen, a picturesque district in western Norway. This carefully crafted pattern features a subtle interplay of earthy tones and crisp blues, evoking the rugged beauty of the surrounding fjords and mountains. Originally intended as a design for a man's waistcoat, the tartan's precise colouration - with subtle variations in shade and hue - is said to have been documented by Aud Aslaksen, curator at Romsdalsmuseet in Molde. Although the designer's name remains unknown, their meticulous attention to detail has resulted in a timeless design that not only honours its cultural roots but also pays tribute to the rich traditions of Norwegian textile heritage.

name: Roscommon Irish County
description: The Roscommon, County tartan is a richly woven representation of Ireland's storied heritage, carefully crafted by Polly Wittering of the House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Originally designed for Macnaughtons of Pitlochry as a collection of trade tartans, this District tartan has been adopted by locals and enthusiasts alike to evoke a sense of place and community. One of a series of Irish District tartans, though not officially sanctioned, the Roscommon, County pattern has proven remarkably popular, earning its place alongside other authentic District tartans in the Scottish Tartans Authority's esteemed Johnston Collection. As a testament to the enduring power of traditional tartan-making, this design continues to honour the history and culture of Ireland's west coast, where Macnaughtons have traded for generations, their legacy woven into every carefully selected thread.

name: Rose Dress
description: The Rose White Dress tartan is a storied and historic Clan tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. This timeless pattern, woven from threads of deep red and striking green, evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's rolling hills and majestic mountains. Originating from the esteemed MacGregor-Hastie sample, this tartan has been passed down through generations as a symbol of family pride and allegiance to Clan Rose. Originally presented as Dancer's tartan by renowned weaver D.C. Dalgliesh, the subtle variation in green hue serves as a poignant reminder of the intricate nuances that distinguish one interpretation from another. As an accepted member of Scotland's rich tapestry of clan tartans, this Rose White Dress tartan continues to hold significant cultural and historical value, weaving together threads of tradition, family legacy, and enduring Scottish identity.

name: Rose Hunting
description: The Rose Hunting tartan is a timeless and evocative heritage pattern, steeped in Scottish tradition and history. First recorded in James Logan's seminal work 'The Scottish Gael' in 1831, this distinctive tartan has been woven into the very fabric of Scotland's clan culture for generations. With its intricate blend of blues, greens, and reds, this beautiful pattern is a testament to the country's rich textile heritage. As a Clan/Family registered design, the Rose Hunting tartan holds significance for those with Scottish roots, serving as a tangible link to their ancestral heritage. While the designer's identity remains unknown, it is clear that their work has left an enduring legacy, now cherished by families around the world who wear this majestic pattern with pride.

name:
Rose of Kilravock [default]
[AKA] Rose of Kilravock
description: The Rose of Kilravock tartan is a captivating family tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. This beautiful, carefully crafted design was created by renowned weaver Jack Dalgety of Forfar to commemorate a personal association, as hinted at by the registration notes, which suggest a strong connection to a long-forgotten history. With its subtle palette of muted greens, rich browns, and delicate pinks, this tartan evokes the beauty of Scotland's rolling hills and rural landscapes. As a family tartan, it is reserved for those with a direct lineage to the original designers' clan or family, making it a treasured possession passed down through generations. Despite its storied past, the Rose of Kilravock tartan remains a relatively rare find, making it all the more special for those fortunate enough to come across it in their own family's heritage.

name:
Rose [default]
[AKA] Rose Dress #2
[AKA] Rose Red
description: The Rose tartan, named after the esteemed Clan Rose family, embodies the rich heritage and tradition of Scotland's clan system. This storied tartan, registered in 1946, is believed to have originated from a letter to Wilsons circa 1822, as the clan tartan system was still developing at the time. The intricate design, with its subtle variations in mid blue and scarlet hues, has been passed down through generations, tied to the historic Kilravock Castle, which has been the seat of the Rose family for over five centuries. This 'dress' tartan, as noted by D.C. Stewart, was likely intended for formal wear, while a variant version, referred to as a 'hunting' pattern, emerged in the 19th century. Today, the Rose tartan holds significant cultural and historical value, its beauty and significance a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy of clan tradition and family heritage.

name: Rosevear [default]
description: The Rosevear tartan is a beautiful and evocative name, woven into existence by the Cornish family of Rosevear in 1990 to commemorate a significant gathering. This intricately designed Name tartan was created with love and care by Constance and Donald Rosevear, and their collaborative efforts were even joined by that of Donald Rawe, lending his expertise to this unique piece of Scottish heritage. Woven by the esteemed House of Edgar, the Rosevear tartan now holds a special place in the hearts of those bearing its family name, serving as a lasting testament to tradition, history, and community. This stunning tartan is a proud representation of Cornish identity and a cherished family legacy, forever woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage.

name: Rosie
description: The Rosie tartan is a deeply personal creation, woven from the very fabric of Scottish heritage by its namesake, Grant Lawson. This distinctive Name tartan is a poignant blend of Caithness and Grant Htg, reflecting the intertwining threads of family history and cultural identity. The subtle nuances of this traditional tartan, carefully reinterpreted by Lawson, serve as a testament to the enduring bond between community and kinship. Worn with pride, the Rosie tartan proudly asserts its wearer's honour and connection to their ancestral roots. As an individualised tartan, it invites others to share in the tradition, while also respecting the designer's wish for prior notification before use, underscoring the importance of preserving family heritage and unique identity.

name: Ross (Wilsons)
description: The Ross (Wilsons') tartan is a poignant tribute to the storied heritage of the Clan Ross, whose history stretches back centuries. Originating in the 18th century, this iconic tartan was formally registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn and has since become an integral part of Scottish clan tradition. With its rich, muted colours evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of Scotland's north-east, this tartan is a testament to the bravery and resilience of the Ross family. According to Peter MacDonald's Key Pattern Book, the Ross (Wilsons') shares a common ancestry with other influential tartans such as Rae, MacRae, and Marchioness of Huntly's, further solidifying its place in Scottish heritage. This esteemed design is an honour to wear, signifying not only family pride but also a deep connection to Scotland's storied past.

name: Ross Arisaid
description: The Ross Arisaid tartan is a storied and evocative design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's Clans. This Clan-specific tartan, registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, holds particular significance for its connection to the historical Dunbeath Castle in Caithness, which has been the seat of the Earls of Ross since the 14th century. The subtle variations in tone and texture, evident in this intricate sett, evoke a sense of tradition and continuity, recalling generations of Scottish families who have worn these distinctive plaids with pride. While its origins are unclear, it is believed to have evolved from an earlier pattern linked to Lochan, a body of water mentioned in the works of J C Thomson. This tartan's unique identity, though not attributed to a specific designer, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's woven heritage, where each thread tells a story of history, family, and community.

name: Ross David
description: The Ross, David tartan is a poignant commemorative design, woven with meticulous attention to detail by Chris MacLeod, curator of the Weaver's Cottage, Kilbarchan. This unique plaid tells the story of David Ross's historic 2005 walk from Robroyston to London, paying tribute to William Wallace and those who have fought for their convictions. The tartan's palette is rich with symbolism: grey threads represent steel and determination, while green echoes hope for the future, mirroring the age of David Ross's child. Rust hues nod to the Bore Well at Elderslie, a local landmark that holds significance for the weaver's family, whose ancestors once used it. The subtle inclusion of elder threads adds a personal touch, representing the birthplace of the designer herself. This thought-provoking tartan is more than just a decorative motif - it's a powerful expression of remembrance and dedication to those who have given their all for a noble cause.

name: Ross Hunting
description: Ross Hunting #3 is a storied tartan woven from the very fabric of Scottish heritage, its intricate patterns evoking the rugged beauty of the Highlands. This Clan tartan, registered in 1906 by W & A K Johnston, tells the tale of a long-standing family legacy, with its unique sett born from the ancestral threacount of Ross clan. The design's smaller sett, as originally registered, would have been a subtle yet meaningful nod to tradition; however, this larger, Loccarron-inspired version adds a touch of grandeur, fitting for a family who has left their mark on Scottish history. As with many Clan tartans, Ross Hunting #3 is steeped in significance and honour, its presence a testament to the enduring spirit of the Ross clan and their enduring connection to the land they once called home.

name: Ross Old
description: The Ross, Old tartan is a deeply rooted and storied family heirloom, its origins dating back to the early 19th century when it was first woven by skilled Scottish artisans. This traditional clan tartan, still registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, tells the story of the Ross dynasty's history and heritage. Woven from rich, dark blues, deep greens, and subtle golds, this intricate pattern evokes a sense of tradition and timelessness, its design echoing the rugged landscapes and storied clans of Scotland's Highland past. With no designer credited for its creation, it is likely that this tartan was passed down through generations of Rosses, each adding their own unique thread to its rich tapestry, before being formally recorded with the Scottish Tartans Authority.

name: Ross Wedding; Dress
description: The Ross Wedding Dress tartan is a poignant fragment of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, evoking the tumultuous period of Jacobite risings in 18th-century Angus. Originally part of a wedding dress worn by Miss Middleton at her 1766 nuptials to George Ross, this tartan bears an uncanny resemblance to Jacobite tartan, reflecting the complexities and tensions of that era. Due to proscription laws, which banned the wearing of specific tartans associated with the Jacobite cause, the Ross family likely chose a muted alternative, such as this fragment. As such, the Ross Wedding Dress tartan serves as a captivating testament to Scotland's complex history, where traditional dress was often intertwined with politics and identity, leaving an indelible mark on the country's cultural landscape.

name:
Ross [default]
[AKA] Ross Red
description: Ross #6, a time-honoured clan tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, has been woven with precision for generations to come. Originally registered by the MacGregor-Hastie family, this distinctive pattern is synonymous with the storied history of the Clan Ross, one of Scotland's most illustrious clans. Characterised by its bold, muted colours and varied thread counts, which may have been deliberately halved for display purposes, this tartan design showcases a unique blend of traditional craftsmanship and subtle nuance. While its exact designer remains anonymous, the significance of Ross #6 lies in its representation of the clan's rich cultural legacy, which continues to inspire pride and connection among those who wear it today.

name: Rossi
description: The Rossi tartan is a deeply personal creation, woven from threads of family heritage and tradition. Designed by David and Kerry Rossi, this Name tartan is a unique expression of their identity and connection to their family's history. Closely based on the iconic Malcolm tartan, the Rossi design pays homage to the ancestral roots that have shaped their lives. Registered through The Celtic Craft Centre in Edinburgh, this tartan serves as a tangible representation of the Rossi family's honour and legacy, passed down through generations with pride. By embracing their Scottish heritage, the Rossi family has created a tartan that not only reflects their individuality but also strengthens their bond to their ancestral home.

name: Rosslyn Da Vinci
description: The Roslin Roseline Da Vinci tartan is a mesmerising corporate design that weaves together the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage and artistic tradition, inspired by Dan Brown's bestselling novel The Da Vinci Code. Created by Brian Wilton, this distinctive tartan commemorates the iconic Rosslyn Chapel, founded by Sir William St. Clair in 1446, and draws upon its mystical and cultural significance. With an asymmetrical design that incorporates the Golden Section ratio, this unique tartan pays homage to Scotland's national flag, featuring blue and white reminiscent of the Saltire, alongside purple heather, red representing Mary Magdalene's hair, and green evoking the chapel's 100 ancient stone gargoyles. This captivating design not only celebrates Scotland's connection to the film but also distills its history, symbolism, and artistic flair into a bold and memorable corporate tartan.

name: Rotary International
description: The Rotary International tartan is a striking corporate design born from the union between tradition and innovation. Registered in 1996 under the Scottish Tartans Authority, this distinctive tartan was formally launched at the Rotary World Convention in Glasgow, Scotland, in 1997. Created with the support of the Tartans Society, Keith Lumsden, and later attributed to Geoffrey Nicholsby as a Tailor, it embodies the values of global community and unity embodied by the Rotary International organisation. As such, this tartan is a significant representation of corporate identity for those involved with the international service club. Its use is subject to some restrictions, with colours needing to be checked against its registered notes in the Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority.

name: Rothesay #2
description: The Rothesay tartan, with its distinctive and storied threads, is a testament to the rich tapestry of Scotland's heritage. As a District tartan, it holds a special place in the country's cultural fabric, evoking the history and traditions of the region from which it originates. Designed by A.C. Lumsden, a renowned collector and advocate for Scottish tartans, this distinctive design was brought to life with meticulous attention to detail and a deep respect for the traditional weaving techniques that have defined Scotland's textile heritage for centuries. With its registration notes recorded in the Scottish Tartans Society archive, the Rothesay tartan is a tangible connection to Scotland's past, one that continues to captivate those who cherish its unique beauty and significance.

name: Rothesay Hunting
description: The Rothesay #2 tartan embodies the storied heritage of Scotland's districts, its rich hues and intricate weave a testament to the country's proud tradition of textile craftsmanship. Registration notes indicate that this District tartan was introduced in 1906 by H. Whyte and others, featuring alongside other clan tartans in W & A. K. Johnston's seminal publication, 'The Tartans of the Clans and Septs of Scotland'. This edition marked a significant milestone in the codification of Scottish tartans, providing a shared visual language for clans and families to express their identity and honour their heritage. As one of the first 'Dress' and 'Hunting' versions of clan tartans to be registered, Rothesay #2 is an important example of Scotland's complex and multifaceted cultural fabric, its intricate design reflecting the country's rich history and tradition.

name: Rothesay Red
description: The Rothesay Royal tartan, named after the historic Royal Burgh of the same name on the Isle of Bute, holds a rich and storied history within Scotland's fabric. Designed by Sobieski Stuarts, The, in collaboration with the Scottish Tartans Authority, this majestic tartan was previously classified as Royal and worn by none other than King Edward VII as a child. Dating back to c.1840-50, the original kilt belonging to the Sobieski Stuarts, now housed at the National Museum, provided the foundation for this magnificent design. With its distinctive colour palette and intricate sett pattern, Rothesay has become an iconic representation of Scottish heritage, not only as a Royal tartan but also as a testament to the strong connections between the Stuart dynasty and the Isle of Bute.

name: Round Table of Britain and Ireland
description: The Round Table tartan, registered in 1997 by House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., embodies the spirit of corporate unity and innovation. Inspired by the esteemed Round Table of Britain and Ireland, this distinctive tartan was designed with a purpose: to represent excellence, harmony, and progress. For the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, Polly Wittering's creative vision brings together the traditional colours in a unique twist, substituting darker shades for red, green, and blue. As a Corporate tartan, it is suited for businesses seeking to establish their identity through distinctive branding, while its origins in British heritage ensure a strong connection to Scotland's rich cultural fabric.

name: Rowan
description: This majestic Rowan tartan is a personal legacy, steeped in heritage and symbolism, as designed by renowned textile expert Philip D. Smith for Robert Rowan in 1990. As a Name tartan, it holds special significance within Scottish clan traditions, yet its exclusivity lies in its unique status as a privately commissioned design. The subtle nuances of this tartan weave together threads of history and personality, reflecting the individual character of its creator, Robert Rowan. With its roots firmly planted in Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, the Rowan tartan embodies the country's timeless spirit and timelessness, inviting wearers to embody their own personal connection to the land and its storied past.

name: Rowardennan
description: The Rowardennan tartan, designed by Clan Crest Textiles, is a sumptuous fashion tartan inspired by the majestic landscapes of Scotland's Loch Lomond region. This stunning pattern draws upon the traditional Aviemore/Dogwood tartans, with subtle variations that evoke the wild beauty of the surrounding mountains and forests. According to its registration notes, the Rowardennan tartan is a variation of these classic patterns, carefully crafted by Scotty Thompson in collaboration with the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection. As a fashion tartan, it is designed to be worn with pride, evoking the timeless spirit of Scotland's heritage and tradition. Its rich colour palette and intricate design make it an ideal choice for those seeking to add a touch of Scottish flair to their wardrobe, while also honouring the rich cultural traditions that have shaped this beautiful country.

name: Roxburgh Green
description: The Roxburgh tartan, registered by the Scottish Tartans Society in 1952, is a rich and storied example of Scotland's timeless weaving heritage. Originating from Dr Phil Smith Jr's 1949 sample labelled 'Roxburgh', this District tartan is steeped in history and tradition. The design, with its distinctive blue and green hues evoking the rolling hills and misty lochs of the Scottish Borders, holds strong connections to the region's proud past. As a District tartan, Roxburgh represents a specific geographic area within Scotland, and its registration serves as a testament to the preservation of this unique cultural identity. With no designer credited for the original creation, it is the anonymous expertise of Dr Smith Jr that has ensured the enduring legacy of this beautiful tartan, woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage.

name:
Roxburgh Red
[AKA] Haig [default]
[AKA] Riddell [default]
[AKA] Rutherford of Roxburgh
description: The Roxburgh Red tartan is an enduring emblem of Scottish heritage, its roots tracing back to pre-1850 when it was recorded by M Castro, a renowned handloom weaver. This District tartan, once thought to be an obscure relic from the past, has been rediscovered and reinterpreted for modern wearers. With its distinctive red hue at its centre, this tartan is inextricably linked to the historic Roxburgh district in the Scottish Borders, a region steeped in tradition and rich cultural history. Now commercially woven for the first time in over a century and a half, the Roxburgh Red tartan pays homage to a bygone era of traditional craftsmanship and community identity. This ancient design is an honour to its original makers and weavers, serving as a vibrant symbol of Scotland's enduring textile heritage.

name:
Royal & Ancient
[AKA] St Andrews Royal & Ancient
description: This majestic Corporate tartan, "Royal and Ancient, The", is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and its deep-rooted connections with golfing traditions. Designed by esteemed weavers at Kinloch Anderson Ltd in honour of the prestigious Royal and Ancient Golf Club, St Andrews, this distinctive pattern holds significant cultural value as a symbol of the Club's rich history and philanthropic endeavours. As a corporate tartan, it is specifically intended to raise funds for the restoration of the Club's iconic buildings, underscoring the importance of preserving Scotland's most storied golfing landmarks. Accredited by the Scottish Tartans Society in 1993, this revered design has been carefully crafted to evoke the traditions and values that have defined the game of golf in Scotland for centuries.

name: Royal Agricultural Winter Fair
description: The Royal Agricultural Winter Fair tartan is a commemorative masterpiece that weaves together the rich heritage of Canada's equestrian tradition with its royal connections. Designed by Russell Macleod, N and J, in collaboration with Strathmore, this distinctive tartan was created to celebrate the 75th anniversary of the esteemed fair. The colour symbolism behind this design is as fascinating as it is meaningful, with red and yellow (representing gold) paying tribute to the Royal Family's enduring presence at the event, while also nodding to Canada's bountiful harvest and winter seasons. The incorporation of W for winter and G and R for equestrian connections adds depth and nuance to this commemorative tartan, which serves as a testament to the fair's long history and its enduring connection to the country's equine culture.

name: Royal Army Physical Training Corps Association (Scotland)
description: The Royal Army Physical Training Corps Association (Scotland) tartan is a proud tribute to the esteemed Military unit, granted Royal status in 2011 on its milestone 150th anniversary. Designed by Jonathan Brown, this tartan was created as an informal dress option for serving and ex-serving members, honouring the Corps' colours while allowing for personal expression. The Strathmore Woollen Co Ltd has carefully established restrictions on its use to ensure its authenticity and integrity. This richly textured design weaves together the traditions of Scottish heritage and military camaraderie, echoing the values of discipline, perseverance, and physical excellence that define the Army Physical Training Corps Association (Scotland). As a testament to the enduring legacy of this iconic unit, this tartan serves as a poignant symbol of unity and pride among its members.

name: Royal Ashburn Golf Club
description: The Royal Ashburn Golf Club tartan embodies the rich heritage and traditions of Scotland's oldest golfing clubs, translated into a vibrant Canadian landscape. Registration notes reveal that this corporate tartan is inspired by the history of the hamlet of Ashburn, Ontario, where the Royal Ashburn Golf Club was founded in 1961 as Thunderbird Golf Club. The colours of red, yellow, green, and black are carefully woven to represent Canada's maple leaf spirit (red), the dawn of a new day (yellow), the manicured beauty of golf courses (green) and the majestic presence of trees and rough terrain (black). Masterfully crafted by Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan design serves as a testament to the enduring power of tradition, community, and a love for the game of golf.

name: Royal Australian Air Force #1
description: The Correctional Service Canada tartan is a distinctive and formal corporate tartan, carefully designed to reflect the values and history of one of Canada's most respected institutions. Originally created for use by the Correctional Service Canada pipebands, this tartan has become an integral part of the organisation's identity. Its unique pattern, developed in collaboration with the renowned tartan designer D.C. Dalgliesh Limited, pays homage to the country's rich Scottish heritage while also conveying a sense of discipline and professionalism. As a corporate livery tartan, it is now proudly worn by the Correctional Service Canada as a symbol of their commitment to justice, rehabilitation, and community service. The tartan's restricted use ensures that its unique character remains an integral part of this iconic organisation's tradition.

name: Royal Australian Air Force #2
description: The Spotsylvania County, Sheriff's Office tartan is a distinct corporate tartan that pays homage to the rich heritage of Virginia's history. Registered in 2005, this bespoke design was created by Geoffrey of Tailor Highland Crafts Limited to represent the official uniform for the Sheriff's Office of Spotsylvania County. This striking tartan features a unique blend of colours, carefully selected to reflect the county's storied past and its connections to British heritage. As a corporate tartan, it is specifically designed for use in formal wear, livery, and other business contexts, allowing individuals to proudly showcase their affiliation with this esteemed organisation while drawing inspiration from Scotland's timeless tradition of tartan design.

name: Royal Australian Air Force #3
description: This captivating Corporate Tartan, "Roseline", bears witness to the fascinating intersection of art and literature. Registered under its original name, "Da Vinci Rosslyn Rose", in 2003, this distinctive pattern was created by renowned designer Keith Campbell to promote Dan Brown's bestselling novel, The Da Vinci Code. Named after Leonardo da Vinci and the mysterious Rosslyn Chapel, this tartan weaves together threads of artistic heritage and intellectual curiosity, reflecting the global fascination with the codes and secrets hidden within medieval architecture. With its unique blend of colours, "Roseline" now carries a broader significance, appealing to corporate clients seeking a distinctive identity that echoes the innovative spirit of the Renaissance era.

name: Royal Australian Air Force #4
description: The Pengelly, The Cornish tartan is a richly woven tribute to the heritage of Cornwall, a region steeped in history and tradition. Designed by Peter R. Morton-Nance at Gwethnoc Tartan Co Ltd, this name tartan is inspired by the many families who bear the name Pengelly, whose connection to the land dates back centuries before the Norman conquest. The silver lion rampant, a symbol of armigerous families in Cornwall, shines brightly in the light grey hue that represents its metallic sheen, echoing the geometric patterns found in the Cornish National Tartan, #1567. Initially created for a family wedding, this tartan has been reimagined to honour all Cornish families bearing the name Pengelly, serving as a poignant reminder of their ancestral ties and cultural identity.

name: Royal Australian Air Force #5
description: The Crofters tartan, designed by F & M Lawson in 1903, is a poignant tribute to the Scottish heritage of the New South Wales district where it originated. Originally created as a universal tartan for the Crofters Tartan Weaving Mill, this distinctive pattern was intended to commemorate the establishment of the mill and pay homage to the local community that inspired its creation. As a District tartan, the Crofters is an integral part of New South Wales' cultural fabric, symbolising the region's history and traditions. However, due to restrictions imposed by the designer, this beautiful tartan can only be used under licence from F & M Lawson of Crofters Weaving Mill, ensuring its authenticity and integrity are preserved for future generations to enjoy.

name: Royal British Legion
description: The Royal British Legion tartan is a poignant tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of the United Kingdom's armed forces, with its powerful colour palette reflecting the diverse contributions of the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Merchant Navy to the nation's protection. Designed by MacDonald/Sharpe in 1997, this Corporate tartan is a masterful blend of symbolic colours, including the dignified black overcheck that honours the countless individuals who made the ultimate sacrifice in service to their country. The intricate sett weaves together these powerful motifs, evoking the rich history and tradition of British military heritage, while also serving as a symbol of pride and remembrance for the Royal British Legion and its members.

name: Royal Canadian Air Force
description: The Royal Canadian Air Force tartan, registered by G/C Elmer Fullerton in 1942, is a poignant tribute to Canada's military heritage. This distinctive military tartan was inspired by the Anderson tartan and the RCAF colours, reflecting the nation's shared history with Scotland. Woven from approximately 16 yards of yarn, the tartan was initially used as a sample before being approved by the Air Council of RCAF in May 1942. The tartan's significance extends beyond its technical characteristics, symbolising the bravery and camaraderie of Canada's aviators during wartime.
