The fact that it was submitted to Lord Lyon, King of Arms in Edinburgh, further underscores its connection to Scotland's rich tartan heritage. Today, this military tartan serves as a proud reminder of Canada's role in the Second World War and its enduring bonds with Scottish tradition.

name: Royal Canadian Mounted Police
description: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police tartan is a storied corporate design born from the meticulous craft of Violet Holmes, B.C., Canada's esteemed weaver. Initially designed to represent the iconic police force, this distinctive tartan now serves as an enduring symbol of Canadian heritage and tradition. Registration notes reveal that the original sample was presented to Princess Anne by the RCMP during a visit to New Brunswick in 1998, solidifying its status as the official regimental tartan. Characterised by a bold red and blue palette, this complex design requires six weft colours, setting it apart from other corporate tartans. Although minor adjustments were made to the original count, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police tartan remains an honourable tribute to the RCMP's unwavering dedication to service and protection.

name: Royal College of General Practitioners
description: The Meiklejohn tartan, with its richly woven threads, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage. As a personally registered Name tartan, it holds a special place in the hearts of those who bear the name John, whose family history has been intertwined with this distinctive pattern for generations. Designed by Geoffrey, a skilled tailor at Highland Crafts Limited, this tartan is steeped in tradition and restraint, reflecting the values of a family proud to carry their ancestral legacy forward. While its registration notes note that it is subject to certain restrictions due to its family association, the Meiklejohn tartan remains a cherished symbol of kinship and cultural identity, woven from threads of history, community, and the unwavering bonds of family ties.

name: Royal College of Midwives
description: The Royal College of Midwives tartan is a majestic, corporate design steeped in tradition and heritage, bearing testament to the esteemed institution's rich history. Crafted by renowned designer Brian Wilton for the Scottish Tartans Authority, this unique blend of colours tells a story of midwifery's dualities - represented by the black and white hues of night and day. Blue, traditionally associated with the nursing profession, is paired with grey, a nod to the College's secondary corporate colour, evoking stability and trust. The gold thread weaves together the ancient crown motif from the College's coat of arms, signifying its Royal patronage under Queen Victoria, whose legacy this tartan celebrates. As a tribute to the Star of Bethlehem, symbolising birth, this sophisticated tartan embodies the very essence of midwifery - a balance of contrasting elements coming together in harmony, reflecting the College's enduring commitment to supporting the lives of women and their families.

name: Royal College of Physicians Edinburgh
description: The Royal College of Physicians of Edinburgh tartan is a distinguished Corporate tartan, carefully crafted to represent the esteemed institution it was designed for - the Royal College of Physicians, founded in 1681 as a hub for postgraduate medical students. Woven by renowned Scottish weaver Donald Fraser Weavers and originally produced by Lochcarron in May 1997, this tartan is woven from silk and proudly displayed in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection. The Royal College of Physicians of Edinburgh tartan serves as a symbol of tradition and heritage, embodying the values of learning, excellence, and innovation that have defined the institution for centuries. Its corporate significance extends beyond its medical roots, representing the academic and cultural institutions that have shaped Scotland's rich tapestry.

name: Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh
description: The Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh, The is a majestic corporate tartan born from Scotland's rich medical heritage, woven with honour and precision by Kinloch Anderson Ltd. Dating back to 1506, this esteemed institution was founded by Royal Charter under the reign of James IV, solidifying its place as one of Scotland's most prestigious healthcare organisations. As a symbol of excellence in surgical practice, this tartan embodies the College's proud tradition and commitment to advancing medical knowledge and innovation. With its unique design, this corporate tartan is reserved exclusively for the Royal College of Surgeons of Edinburgh, serving as a fitting emblem of its esteemed status and dedication to the advancement of surgery worldwide.

name: Royal Columbian of Canada
description: The Royal Columbian tartan is a vibrant and stylish fashion tartan, showcasing the rich heritage of Scotland's textile traditions. Designed by the renowned West Coast Woolen Mill, this tartan was originally registered as Aljean in 1968, with its distinctive colours forming a non-reversing pattern. A testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish design, Royal Columbian features a striking combination of blues and greens reminiscent of Scotland's majestic landscapes, evoking the grandeur of the country's natural beauty. Its association with Miss Kathleen Sinclair, a pioneering figure in the world of Scottish textiles, adds further depth to its significance, underscoring the importance of traditional weaving techniques and community heritage. With its unique character and flair, Royal Columbian tartan is perfect for those who appreciate the classic charm and sophistication of Scotland's finest fashion tartans.

name: Royal Delight
description: Royal Delight, a fashion tartan designed by Aljean of Vancouver, embodies the essence of opulence and luxury, echoing the rich heritage of Scotland's royal families. This stunning pattern, registered as a Fashion tartan, is carefully crafted to make a statement on the catwalk or in everyday wear. With its intricate, muted colours - blues, greens, and golds reminiscent of Scotland's majestic landscapes - Royal Delight pays homage to the country's storied past while exuding modern sophistication. As an officially registered design, this tartan ensures a lasting connection to Scottish tradition, while its fashion-forward application makes it accessible to those seeking to add a touch of regal flair to their wardrobe.

name: Royal Highland Show
description: The Royal Highland corporate tartan is a majestic blend of traditional Scottish heritage and modern style, designed by esteemed firm Kinloch Anderson Ltd. Originally derived from the iconic Black Watch tartan, this distinctive pattern incorporates rich earthy tones to represent the agricultural interests of The Royal Highland Society of Scotland. This carefully curated design subtly pays homage to Wilson's Wellington sett, with an additional black line introduced to enhance its unique character. As a controlled use tartan, it is subject to the governance of the esteemed organisation, ensuring its integrity and authenticity are maintained, while also allowing for its adoption by corporate entities seeking to evoke the proud history and tradition of Scotland's rural heritage.

name: Royal Marines Condor (a)
description: The Royal Marines Condor tartan, designed by renowned weaver Jack Dalgety in 1994 for Lt.Col. Wilsey of Royal Marines' Condor Depot, is a striking tribute to Scotland's rich heritage. Category classified as Military, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the country where its origins lie, taking inspiration from the Angus (#1179) tartan - a testament to the county's historical significance in the Scottish landscape. By altering the overcheck, Dalgety cleverly adapted the traditional design to create a unique and meaningful variation, paying respect to the region that is home to Condor Depot. This tartan's very existence serves as a nod to Scotland's proud military history, solidifying its place within the fabric of British tradition and heritage.

name: Royal Pharmaceutical Society
description: The Royal Pharmaceutical Society tartan is a poignant commemoration of the esteemed institution's 150th anniversary, woven with meticulous care by Kinloch Anderson Ltd. This Commemorative tartan was specifically designed to honour the legacy of the Royal Pharmaceutical Society of Great Britain, a prestigious organisation that has played a vital role in shaping the pharmaceutical industry for over five decades. The tartan's rich colours and intricate patterns evoke the tradition and heritage of Scottish craftsmanship, while its creation served as a fitting tribute to the society's significant milestone. Now preserved in the Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan serves as a lasting testament to the organisation's enduring impact on the world of pharmacy, reminding us of the importance of preserving Scotland's rich cultural and historical legacy.

name: Royal Scottish Agricultural Benefits Institution
description: This distinctive Corporate tartan, inspired by the renowned Buchleuch pattern, pays tribute to the enduring legacy of the Royal Scottish Agricultural Benevolent Institution (RSABI). Registered in 1996 by Colin Hutcheson, a master weaver at Johnstons of Elgin, this unique design reflects the charity's commitment to supporting those who have dedicated their lives to working in the agricultural industry. With its roots firmly planted in Scottish heritage, the RSABI tartan embodies the values of kindness, generosity, and community that define the organisation's mission to provide financial assistance to those in need. The deliberate blend of traditional and modern elements serves as a testament to the enduring spirit of Scotland's rural communities, while also marking an important milestone in the charity's centenary celebrations in 1997.

name: Royal Scottish Assurance
description: The Royal Scottish Assurance tartan is a distinctive corporate pattern that pays tribute to the legacy of the iconic insurance company, launched in Scotland in 1990. Woven with precision by the esteemed Scottish Tartans Society, this tartan's unique sett reflects its commercial heritage, evoking the values of trust and stability that underpin financial security. As a corporate tartan, it is designed for use in formal wear, business attire, and official events, making it an ideal choice for individuals associated with the insurance sector or those seeking to add a touch of Scottish elegance to their professional identity. Its registration notes proudly affirm its connection to this milestone event, providing a tangible link to Scotland's rich history and tradition of enterprise and innovation.

name: Royal Scottish Corporation
description: The Royal Scottish Corporation tartan, designed by Lochcarron of Scotland in 2005, is a poignant tribute to a historic institution that has been supporting Scots abroad for centuries. Originally woven with a mission to assist those in need, regardless of background or circumstances, the tartan embodies the charity's enduring spirit of compassion and generosity. As one of the oldest Scottish charities still operating today, the Royal Scottish Corporation's legacy is rooted in its royal charter of 1665 and its continued commitment to providing aid to those from Scotland who have fallen on hard times. This corporate tartan not only signifies a connection to this noble heritage but also serves as a badge of honour for those who wear it, proudly carrying the values of kindness, empathy, and community that define this remarkable Scottish tradition.

name:
Royal Scottish Country Dance Society
[AKA] RSCDS
description: The Royal Scottish Country Dance Society tartan is a vibrant and iconic corporate tartan, born from the creative vision of Kirsty Anderson, in collaboration with David Norman-Harris. This distinctive design holds significant cultural value, representing the esteemed organisation responsible for promoting traditional Scottish social dancing across the globe. As an official corporate tartan, it was designed to showcase the society's heritage and traditions, highlighting the rich tapestry of Scottish history and identity. With restrictions in place, ensuring that Macnaughton Group remains the sole distributor, this tartan serves as a proud symbol of unity and community, embodying the infectious energy and joy associated with country dancing in Scotland.

name: Royal Scottish Pipe Band Association
description: This Corporate Tartan, designed by Geoffrey (Tailor) Highland Crafts, is a proud representation of the Royal Scottish Pipe Band Association's emblem, carefully woven into a vibrant fabric that embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's piping tradition. Adopted from a competition held to celebrate the association's winning design, this tartan is steeped in history and cultural significance, evoking the pomp and ceremony of traditional Scottish bagpipe performances. With its distinctive colour scheme, inspired by the organisation's logo, this tartan has become an enduring symbol of excellence and achievement within the pipe band community, proudly worn by those who share a passion for this storied tradition.

name:
Royal Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children Heather
[AKA] RSPCC
description: The Heather Tartan, registered by Jan Crook, holds a profound significance in corporate Scotland, reflecting the values and mission of the Royal Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Children (now rebranded as Children 1st). Created at the Society's request, this distinctive tartan design embodies the organisation's commitment to protecting children's welfare. The colours - Dark Pink Mix, Light Pink Mix, Kingfisher, and Emerald - are inspired by the Society's badge and letterhead, paying homage to its rich heritage. Inspired by Tom Lockie of Edinburgh Woollen Mills, who is credited as either the source or designer of this tartan, it serves as a testament to Scottish textile tradition, expertly woven with purpose and meaning. This corporate tartan not only pays tribute to an esteemed institution but also symbolises the enduring bond between Scotland's rich cultural heritage and its philanthropic spirit.

name: Royal Warrant Holders
description: The Royal Warrant Holders tartan is a distinguished corporate tartan, proudly worn by those who have been honoured with a royal warrant for their excellence in manufacturing or providing goods/services to members of British royalty. Designed by esteemed weaver Douglas Kinloch Anderson, who served as President of the Royal Warrant Holder's Association at the time, this distinctive tartan was originally featured on table linen and was specifically created to represent the association's values and prestige. While it may be worn in various contexts, its origins and connotations remain deeply rooted in the world of British business and tradition. Note that, in accordance with its designations as a corporate tartan, restrictions apply regarding its use, ensuring its exclusivity for members of this prestigious group.

name: Royal Yacht Britannia
description: The Royal Yacht Britannia corporate tartan, designed by renowned Scottish textile experts at Kinloch Anderson Ltd, pays homage to the iconic British vessel that has become an enduring symbol of national pride. Originally created for the Royal Yacht Britannia Charitable Trust, this tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich maritime heritage and the trust's commitment to preserving the yacht as a treasured visitor attraction in Edinburgh's Leith district. With its distinct colours and carefully considered pattern, this tartan proudly celebrates British history and tradition, while also acknowledging its charitable roots. As with all corporate tartans, it is available for use by approved organisations only, ensuring that its distinctive design is reserved for those who share the trust's passion for preserving the Royal Yacht Britannia's legacy.

name: Rui
description: The Rui tartan, a personal and storied weave, bears testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage. Worn by pipers, drummers, and Highland warriors for generations, the specific art of tartan weaving was once reserved for the skilled hands of trained weavers. Yet, Sarah Deming's bold decision to create her own unique tartan, Rui, underscores the democratizing power of tradition. Registered in 1996, this kilt pattern is not bound by clan affiliation or corporate sponsorship, but rather serves as a symbol of individuality and honour within the Scottish piping community. Its origins, woven into the very fabric of Sarah's personal experience, serve as a poignant reminder of the rich cultural heritage that defines Scotland's national identity.

name: Hunter #2
description: The Finnish tartan is a vibrant and distinctive District tartan, carefully crafted to evoke the spirit of the land and its people. Registered in recognition of the global Finnish community, this tartan is reserved for those who bear a connection to Finland, whether by heritage or affinity. Designed with flair by David McGill of International Tartans, the Finnish tartan features a unique combination of blues, greens, and yellows that recall the country's majestic lakes and forests. As with all District tartans, there are restrictions on its use, requiring permission from the designer to ensure authenticity and avoid misappropriation. Approved by Honorary Consul Michael Walker, the Finnish tartan is a testament to the enduring appeal of Finland's unique cultural identity, and those who wear it do so in honour of their heritage or affection for this Nordic nation.

name: Russian Scottish
description: The Russo-Scottish tartan is a poignant tribute to the cultural heritage shared by Russia and Scotland, brought to life through the masterful weaving of Brian Wilton. Commissioned by the Russian Consul General in Edinburgh as a gift to the Russian people, this district tartan seamlessly blends elements from two iconic families - the Barclays and Lermontovs. The red on green hues echo the Barclays' tartan, while the white on blue pays homage to the cross of St Andrew, revered by both nations. The gold and three white lines, reminiscent of Lermontov's tartan, add a touch of elegance, as do the Russian flag's red, white, and blue, and the State Arms of Russia's gold and black. This stunning tartan weaves together the threads of history, forging a lasting bond between two nations through their shared heritage - a testament to the enduring spirit of friendship between Scotland and Russia.

name: Rust
description: The Rust tartan is a personal and storied design, born from the imagination of Gordon Rust, a stalwart of Scottish heritage residing in the exotic lands of Salalah, Oman. This Name tartan was woven with great care for the esteemed Rust family, its subtle nuances and rich tones evoking a sense of warmth and familiarity. Although initially crafted with royal blue hues, which have since been adapted to azure blue by Peter MacDonald's skilled hands, this tartan remains an endearing testament to Scottish tradition and cultural affinity. As a registered design with the Scottish Tartans Society, the Rust tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring bond between Scotland and its diaspora communities worldwide, its presence a cherished honouring of family legacy and historical connection.

name: Rutherford [default]
description: The Rutherford tartan, bearing the proud crest of Clan Rutherford, tells the storied tale of a Scottish heritage intertwined with American roots. Designed by esteemed Phil Smith for Keith Rutherford of Davison, Michigan, USA, this traditional Home tartan has been woven to honour a name that transcends borders. With its subtle variations and rich colours, the Rutherford tartan embodies the legacy of a family's enduring spirit and dedication to tradition. Permitted for wear by all spellings of the name, this tartan proudly wears its associations with Scottish roots, paying testament to the timeless connection between Scotland's Highlands and the diaspora that has nurtured it across the ages.

name: Ruthven [default]
description: The Ruthven tartan is a rich and storied fabric, steeped in the heritage of Scotland's ancient clans. Originally designated for the Earls of Gowrie, its origins date back to the 16th century, when the Ruthven family was distinguished as members of the aristocracy. The tartan's design, named only with the publication of the Vestiarium Scoticum in 1842, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's forgotten nobility. Handwoven by skilled artisans, this intricate fabric weaves together threads of history and tradition, its colours evoking the rugged landscape and storied past of the Scottish Highlands. As part of the Clan tartan category, it holds significance for those proud to bear the Ruthven name or legacy, a symbol of their noble heritage that continues to weave its way through generations.

name: Rutledge [default]
description: The Rutledge tartan is a rich and storied heritage pattern, born from the late 20th century in Glasgow's renowned tartan mills. Designed by Donald Suttie Smith, a master weaver with a deep understanding of Scotland's tribal traditions, this Clan tartan was specifically created for Richard Armstrong Rutledge, an American of Scottish descent. With its unique blend of earthy tones and subtle nuances, the Rutledge tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of the Scots, whose clan affiliations have shaped the very fabric of their identity. Now available to anyone bearing the name in its various forms, this tartan serves as a proud symbol of heritage and cultural connection, allowing wearers to pay homage to their roots while forging their own path forward.

name: Ruxton Dress
description: The Ruxton Dress tartan is a quintessential example of traditional Scottish heritage, woven with the rich history and traditions of Clan Ruxton. Registered as a family tartan, it holds significant cultural importance for those bearing the name or affiliated with the clan. Designed by Paul Ruxton, a skilled weaver and member of the clan, this tartan pattern is steeped in tradition and symbolism, evoking images of Scotland's rugged landscapes and proud heritage. With its carefully balanced sett and subtle colour nuances, the Ruxton Dress tartan exudes a sense of timeless elegance, while also acknowledging the enduring legacy of Clan Ruxton. Its significance extends beyond mere fashion, representing a tangible connection to the past and a deep-seated family pride.

name: Ruxton Hunting
description: The Ruxton Hunting tartan is a storied heritage pattern, steeped in tradition and reverence for generations to come. Originally presented online alongside three other designs by renowned weaver Paul Ruxton, this tartan was later adopted as the quintessential hunting tartan by Ian Ruxton, son of the original designer. As such, it holds great significance for those with the surname Ruxton, serving as a proud symbol of familial heritage and connection to the land. With its rich, earthy tones evoking the wilds of Scotland's hunting grounds, this tartan is deeply rooted in the country's ancient traditions of hunting and the pursuit of game. As such, it can be worn by anyone with the name Ruxton as a badge of honour, connecting them to a proud history that stretches back through generations.

name: Ruxton [default]
description: The Ruxton tartan is a proud declaration of heritage for those bearing this esteemed name, hailing from the historic Clan family tradition. Designed by Paul Ruxton, a weaver of Scottish pride, this distinctive tartan has been championed by members worldwide, earning its place as one of four competing designs presented online. The Ruxton thread count is carefully specified in the Scottish Tartans Society's records, showcasing the intricacies of traditional weaving techniques. With its unique pattern and rich history, this tartan now resides with D C Dalgliesh's skilled loom, weaving a lasting tribute to the Ruxton name, forever linked to the country of Scotland's timeless heritage.

name: Ryder Cup 2006
description: The Ryder Cup 2006 tartan is a unique corporate design, woven to commemorate a pivotal moment in golfing history. Registered by Brian Wilton of the Scottish Tartans Authority for the PGA Wentworth, this striking pattern pays homage to the storied rivalry between American and British players, as conceived by Samuel Ryder in 1926. The tartan's distinct colour palette, featuring dark green fairways and light green greens, is inspired by the esteemed Mitchell tartan. By incorporating elements of Scotland's rich golfing heritage, Wilton has created a distinctive and lasting tribute to the sport that has captivated the hearts of enthusiasts around the world, for generations to come.

name: S.C.O.T.S. USA
description: The S.C.O.T.S tartan, a specially commissioned corporate design by esteemed Scottish textile company Kinloch Anderson Ltd, is a distinctive blend of colours that embodies the spirit of British heritage and expert guidance. Originally designed for American travel agents trained to sell Scottish holidays as 'Special Counsellors of Travel to Scotland', this tartan's purpose was rooted in fostering cultural exchange between nations. As an official corporate tartan, its use is strictly reserved for SCOTS counsellors, adding a touch of exclusivity and professionalism to their work. The S.C.O.T.S design proudly wears its origins on its sleeve, paying homage to Scotland's storied history as a hub for international tourism, while also celebrating the nation's reputation for warm hospitality and expert guidance.

name: SA Club Private
description: The Private SA Club tartan is a vibrant and sophisticated corporate design, expertly crafted by renowned Scottish weaver, Lochcarron of Scotland, in 2004. Inspired by the colours of a private South African club, this unique tartan embodies the elegance and refinement of international business, with its distinctive red, blue, and white hues. As a Corporate tartan, it is designed for use on formal wear, tie bars, and other corporate regalia, allowing companies to showcase their global connections and prestigious affiliations. With its registration notes dated June 2005, this tartan has become an integral part of the fabric of South African business culture, symbolising excellence and prestige in a highly competitive industry.

name: Sabema
description: The Sabema tartan, a stylish and modern fashion favourite, boasts a rich, dark colour palette with subtle hints of earthy tones. As a partially registered sett, its full potential remains a mystery, as it is currently only fully defined in brushed wool sample form. Despite this, the available information suggests that Sabema was created to make a bold statement on the catwalk. Originally designed for the fashion category, this tartan's intricate patterns and bolder hues evoke the dynamic spirit of modern Scottish style. With its unique blend of dark blues, greens, and blacks, Sabema is sure to turn heads, its fashion-forward design making it perfect for those seeking a contemporary twist on traditional tartan heritage.

name: Sabrettes
description: The Sabrettes tartan is a vibrant and distinctive corporate tartan, expertly woven by Nina Walsh for Sabres of Paradise Ltd's record label subsidiary, Sabrettes. With its bold colours and unique pattern, this tartan was originally designed to evoke the energetic and edgy vibe of the music scene, first appearing on vinyl and CD house bags before being showcased in a limited range of bespoke clothing. As an integral part of British music heritage, the Sabrettes tartan is a testament to the innovative spirit of its creators, while also underscoring the importance of respecting intellectual property rights - prospective wearers are advised to seek permission from the copyright holders and sole manufacturers, Mr Andrew Weatherall and Miss Nina Walsh, before using or reproducing this unique design.

name: Sachie Hara
description: Sachie Hara's Scottish Check, designed by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, is a unique and captivating tartan that embodies the spirit of cultural fusion and creative expression. This Name tartan is a distinctive representation of Sachie Hara's Japanese heritage and her introduction to Scotland, reflecting her connection with the nation through its iconic tartans, such as Douglas. The design cleverly weaves together elements of these two rich traditions, incorporating subtle checks reminiscent of the traditional Scottish fabric with bold stripes evoking the Japanese flag's vibrant colours. With a combination of historical significance, cultural nuance, and innovative flair, Sachie Hara's Scottish Check is a fascinating example of modern tartan design that proudly celebrates both its Japanese roots and its adoption in Scotland.

name: Sackett [default]
description: The Sackett tartan, designed by Matthew Newsome with roots in Gary Sackett's English heritage, embodies the traditions of rural England. This distinctive Clan tartan is rooted in the history of Bolingbrook & Jones, renowned Norwich-based weavers, who wove a foundation pattern upon which this design was created. Characterised by a palette of muted greens and browns evoking the family's agricultural past, the bold contrasts of black and silver - reminiscent of the Sackett Arms - add depth and sophistication to the overall design. As a Family tartan, it is steeped in heritage and storytelling, with each thread weaving a narrative of its own. A testament to the enduring power of tradition and cultural identity, this tartan stands proudly as a reflection of Gary Sackett's proud English roots.

name: Sacramento City Fire Department
description: The Sacramento City Fire Department's corporate tartan is a stirring tribute to the bravery and camaraderie of its Pipes & Drums, which was established in 2004. Designed by Fergus Johnson, the distinctive tartan features a vibrant palette that evokes the spirit of firefighting, with blues and reds reminiscent of flame-kissed embers. As a Corporate tartan, this design is intended for use by members of the Fire Department, providing an unmistakable symbol of pride and unity among its ranks. While not bound by strict heritage or clan ties, the tartan's origins in the department's Pipes & Drums tradition imbue it with a sense of civic purpose, reflecting the essential role that firefighters play in safeguarding their community.

name: Safeway
description: The Safeway tartan, a corporate stalwart with a rich history, boasts a striking McKinley sett pattern, first utilised by the Argyll Group before being rechristened in December 1997 under its current name. As one of Kinloch Anderson Ltd's esteemed designs, this tartan is imbued with the spirit of tradition and heritage that underpins Scotland's storied textile legacy. Originally intended for use by a prestigious group, Safeway has transcended its origins to become a versatile and enduring symbol of corporate identity, gracing everything from uniforms to merchandise with its distinctive hues. Despite being born out of formal affiliation, this tartan remains an integral part of Scottish cultural heritage, its adaptability serving as testament to the country's enduring capacity for innovation and tradition in harmony.

name: Saffron Colour Special
description: The Special Saffron tartan is a storied District pattern, originating from Ireland, with its rich history woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage. This captivating design, once part of the esteemed Paton Collection in Scotland's Tartans archive, has now been returned to its rightful home at Alloa, where it remains an integral part of the Paton firm's legacy. Characterised by a predominantly golden hue with subtle undertones of crimson and ochre, Special Saffron is a testament to Ireland's rich cultural heritage. As a District pattern, this tartan is deeply rooted in Irish tradition, evoking images of rolling emerald landscapes and storied history. While the designer's name remains unknown, their creative vision has left an indelible mark on the world of tartanry, leaving Special Saffron to be cherished by those who appreciate the beauty and significance of this ancient textile art form.

name: Sail Chalmadale
description: The Sail Chalmadale tartan is a captivating fashion design, woven with a deep sense of Scottish heritage and tradition. Named after its namesake, the village of Chalmadale in Perthshire, this tartan evokes the rolling hills and rugged coastlines of Scotland's storied past. Registered as a Fashion tartan, it is designed to make a stylish statement on clothing, accessories, or textiles. Although no specific details are known from the registration notes, one can assume that this tartan was carefully crafted by David A. Cumming with attention to traditional weaving techniques and an understanding of the cultural significance of its namesake village. As a fashion tartan, Sail Chalmadale offers a unique opportunity to incorporate a touch of Scotland's rich history into modern attire, making it a fascinating addition to any fashion collection or enthusiast's wardrobe.

name:
Salem Scottish Dancers
[AKA] Wee Bluett
description: The Salem Scottish Dancers Tartan is a vibrant and energetic fashion tartan born out of the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's finest dance troupe. Described by its designers at House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this dynamic pattern pays tribute to the tradition of Scottish dancing, which has been an integral part of community gatherings for centuries. With roots tracing back to 1974 and influenced by Sally Dee, a renowned kiltmaker from Massachusetts, USA, this tartan is a unique blend of classic Scottish design with a distinctly American twist. Although designed as a fashion tartan, its connection to the esteemed Salem (MA) Scottish Dancers adds an air of honour and authenticity, underscoring the importance of preserving Scotland's rich cultural legacy for future generations.

name: Salich-Plaja
description: The Salich-Plaja tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Salichs-Plaja family, woven with meticulous attention to detail by Barcelona-based designer Eduard Salichs. Registered as a personal tartan, this distinctive pattern holds great significance for the family and their successors, symbolising their unique heritage and tradition. As a "Name" category tartan, it is imbued with deeper cultural meaning, reflecting the intricate history and identity of the clan behind it. Despite being designed primarily for personal use, this tartan design has transcended its original intention, offering a tangible connection to Scottish heritage and the rich traditions that underpin it. With its distinctive sett and carefully considered colour palette, the Salich-Plaja tartan is a poignant reminder of the intricate tapestry of family history and tradition that binds people across generations.

name: Salt Lake County
description: The Salt Lake County tartan, designed by Richard David Barnes, is a distinctive District tartan that proudly represents the heritage of a Utah county founded in 1850. Its registration on 18th September 1996 marked an important milestone in preserving the cultural identity of its namesake community. The rich, earthy tones woven by D C Dalgliesh of Selkirk evoke the natural beauty of the American West, while the tartan's complex pattern pays homage to Scotland's ancient weaving traditions. As a District tartan, Salt Lake County is part of an exclusive group of patterns that are uniquely tied to specific geographic areas or communities, underscoring the importance of preserving local histories and cultural connections.

name: Salt Lake Scots
description: The Salt Lake Scots tartan is a stunning example of traditional Scottish weaving, born from the fertile land of the Salt Lake District in Cumbria. Registered as a district tartan, it proudly represents the local heritage and community, paying homage to the region's rich history and cultural identity. Designed by Claire Donaldson, the House of Edgar's talented weaver, this vibrant tartan features a unique blend of blues and greens, evoking the misty lochs and rolling hills of the Scottish countryside. With its distinctive pattern, the Salt Lake Scots tartan is not only a testament to the region's beauty but also an honour to the people who call it home.

name: Saltcoats District
description: The Saltcoats tartan is a vibrant tribute to the coastal charm of Scotland's Ayrshire region, born from the pages of registration notes penned by Ronnie Hek. As a District tartan, it represents the unique heritage of the town of Saltcoats, where the rugged Atlantic coastline meets picturesque promenades and warm community spirit. The design's varied hues evoke the shifting tones of sea and sand, while its intricate patterns nod to the traditional weaving techniques that have been passed down through generations of Scottish textile artisans. With its roots firmly planted in local history, the Saltcoats tartan is a celebration of the town's identity and a testament to the enduring power of place and tradition, woven into every fibre of this distinctive and captivating pattern.

name: Saltire
description: The Saltire, a tartan design steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland, was created by renowned fashion expert Claire Donaldson for House of Edgar's Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. This striking pattern is not only a masterpiece of textile artistry but also a nod to the nation's beloved flag, with its pleated form reproducing the iconic Saltire motif. As a Fashion tartan, it is designed to add a touch of Scotland's signature flair to garments such as kilts, scarves, and accessories, while its association with the country's national symbol ensures a strong sense of cultural pride and identity. With its registration notes highlighting Donaldson's innovative design, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage and tradition in modern fashion.

name: Salvation Army Dress
description: The Salvation Army Dress tartan, designed by Jack Dalgety in 1983, is a poignant Corporate tartan that celebrates the centenary of the Perth Citadel Corps. At its core, the bold red hue represents the sacrificial blood of Christ, while the blue and yellow tones evoke the Heavenly Father and the Holy Spirit's presence at Pentecost, respectively. This richly symbolic design, initially intended to commemorate a significant milestone in the Army's history, has become an enduring representation of the organisation's values and mission. A testament to Dalgety's skill as a tartan designer, the Salvation Army Dress tartan is now woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage, its meaning and significance woven into the very essence of corporate identity.

name: Salvation Army Hunting
description: The Salvation Army Hunting tartan, designed by renowned textile artist Jack Dalgety in 1983, is a distinctive corporate pattern born out of reverence for the Perth Citadel Corps' centenary celebration. Initially inspired by Captain H Cooper's work on the Official Salvation Army Tartan, this variation replaces the traditional red hue with a vibrant green, striking a unique chord in the colour palette. Weaving together historical significance and modern purpose, the Hunting tartan has become an iconic representation of corporate identity for The Salvation Army, embodying the organisation's enduring values and heritage. By marrying traditional Scottish craftsmanship with contemporary design sensibilities, Dalgety has created a tartan that not only pays tribute to the Corps' rich history but also serves as a powerful symbol of community and collective endeavour, perfectly encapsulating the spirit of service and solidarity that defines The Salvation Army.

name: Samios (Rosemary) personal; Isle of Skye
description: The Isle of Skye tartan, registered by Mrs Rosemary Nicolson Samios in 1992, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scotland's majestic Highlands. This District tartan, born from a worldwide competition won by Angus MacLeod, weaves together the island's signature hues - soft blues and greens that evoke the misty veil often shrouding Skye's rugged landscape. The subtle variations in shade, particularly the thin strip of light grey not white, pay homage to the subtle nuances found within Scotland's most dramatic natural setting. As a symbol of Skye's unique heritage and identity, this tartan holds significant cultural value for those with Scottish roots or affinity, reminding us of the island's enduring presence in our collective memory. Lochcarron's appointment as exclusive supplier of fabrics and woven accessories ensures the authentic production and preservation of this revered tartan, a true reflection of Scotland's rich textile heritage.

name: Samios (Rosemary) personal; Loch Ness #2
description: Loch Ness #2, a fashion tartan designed by Donald John MacKay, embodies the mystique and beauty of Scotland's most famous loch. Exclusively handwoven under licence in Harris Tweed by Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan is steeped in tradition and heritage, showcasing the islanders' skillful weaving techniques. Although initially created for Mrs Rosemary Samios, it has gained acceptance as a district tartan for the area, reflecting the unique cultural identity of the region. Its adoption by the Broomhedge pipe band in Ireland highlights its versatility, bridging the divide between Scotland and the Emerald Isle. This intricate design weaves together the rich history of Harris Tweed with modern flair, making it an enchanting addition to any fashion ensemble that pays tribute to the rugged charm of Loch Ness itself.

name: Samye
description: The Samye corporate tartan embodies the harmonious fusion of Tibetan and Scottish heritage, reflecting the profound spiritual connection between these two rich cultures. Designed by Dr Akong Tulku Rinpoche, guardian of Tibetan tradition, in 1967, this majestic tartan celebrates the unity of Earth, Air, Fire, Water, and Space - the five elements in perfect balance. Inspired by the original Samye monastery in Tibet, now named after this Scottish centre, the design weaves together a vibrant tapestry of Scottish heritage with the wisdom and mysticism of Tibetan Buddhism. The result is a stunning representation of harmony and balance, reflecting Akong Rinpoche's guiding philosophy: "when the elements are in perfect balance, there is perfect harmony." This iconic tartan serves as a powerful symbol of cultural exchange, mutual respect, and spiritual understanding between two nations, now proudly worn by Scottish organisations seeking to embody these shared values.

name: Samye Sangha
description: The Samye Sangha tartan is a poignant tribute to the Tibetan Buddhist monks and nuns who call South West Scotland home. Designed by Abbot Lama Yeshe Losal Rinpoche, originally from Tibet, this simple yet dignified red check tartan was created with great affection for the Scottish community that has welcomed the Samye Ling Centre and Monastery into its fold. As a corporate tartan, it is worn by those who share the Sangha's commitment to Tibetan Buddhist practice, symbolising unity and appreciation for Scotland's rich cultural heritage. The design is both a reflection of the Abbot's gratitude towards his adopted homeland and a celebration of the blending of traditions that defines this unique Scottish institution.

name: Sandberg of Greenock
description: The Sandberg of Greenock tartan is a unique and family-centric design, borne from the personal heritage of Harry Sandberg of Greenock, Baron of Greenock and holder of the Scottish arms associated with this name. As a Name tartan, it holds special significance for its original creator and his loved ones, serving as a meaningful way to connect with their ancestral roots. The restrictions on its use ensure that the family's personal connection to this tartan remains intact, allowing them to weave it in accordance with the designer's intended light and bright colours when worn as a dress tartan, while its dark tones come alive for hunting occasions. This bespoke tartan is a testament to the rich history and tradition of Scottish heraldry, its very existence woven from the threads of family pride and loyalty.

name: Sandberg [default]
description: The Sandberg tartan, a storied textile bearing the proud name of its designer, Baron Harry Sandberg of Greenock, is a quintessential representation of Scottish heritage and tradition. This Clan tartan, registered in recognition of its association with the noble surname, is worn by descendants and those honouring the name with distinction. Woven from the rich hues of earthy tones, this intricate pattern evokes the rolling hills and rugged coastlines of Scotland's western Highlands. Its technical design, meticulously crafted to adhere to traditional tartan principles, belies a deeper significance - a symbol of family legacy and identity, woven into the very fabric of Scottish culture and tradition.

name: Sandelin
description: The Sandelin tartan is a deeply personal and treasured family heirloom, designated as a Name tartan, signifying its association with the Martin Sandelin clan heritage. This distinctive woven pattern has been reserved for use by members of the Sandelin family alone, lending it an air of exclusivity and significance. As a private tartan, it is not open to broader adoption or commercial utilisation, underscoring its exclusive nature. Its creation and transmission have likely been imbued with generations of storytelling, tradition, and affection, reflecting the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage that this family's history has woven.

name: Sanix Blue
description: The Sanix Modern tartan is a vibrant fusion of traditional Scottish heritage and modern flair, crafted by the renowned House of Edgar for the discerning fashion-conscious individual. Originally designed for clothing items with a Japanese client, its name may lead one to assume a muted tone, but in reality, this striking design boasts a bold, dynamic palette that effortlessly blends into contemporary style. As a Fashion tartan, it is free from clan or family associations, making it an accessible choice for anyone seeking to add a pop of modern sophistication to their wardrobe. With its innovative twist on traditional Scottish weaving, the Sanix Modern tartan is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland and its ability to evolve and thrive in the modern era.

name: Sanix Green
description: The Sanix Muted tartan, designed by Claire Donaldson for House of Edgar in association with Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., is a unique fashion-inspired creation that pays homage to traditional Scottish heritage. This distinguished tartan falls under the category of Fashion, suggesting its intended use is for garments and accessories that showcase individual style rather than a familial or clan affiliation. Notably, this design does not stem from an existing registered tartan, such as Sanix Modern, but rather represents a distinct alternative with its 'muted' colour palette. By embracing this innovative interpretation of traditional tartan, the Sanix Muted adds a modern twist to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, making it an attractive choice for those seeking a fashionable yet authentic connection to Scottish roots.

name: Sarafilovic
description: The Sarafilovic tartan, registered for corporate use, is a vibrant and distinctive pattern born from the creative vision of House of Edgar's designers. This unique tartan pays homage to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland, where tradition meets modernity. With its carefully crafted colours and precise sett, this design evokes the warmth and energy of the country's storied history. As a corporate tartan, it is designed for businesses looking to make a bold statement while honouring their Scottish roots. Notably, restrictions apply due to copyright held by Mr André Sarafilovic, ensuring that this distinctive pattern remains an exclusive representation of his design legacy. For Robert Nicol, the registration notes serve as a testament to the enduring power of tartan in symbolising identity and community, a thread woven deep into Scotland's fabric.

name: Sarasota Dunfermline
description: The Sarasota - Dunfermline tartan is a poignant commemorative design that weaves together the rich heritage of Scotland with the warm, sun-kissed spirit of its transatlantic twin town, Sarasota, Florida. Registered in honour of Robert Nicol of Dunfermline, this distinctive tartan celebrates the twinning of these two beloved communities, forging a lasting bond between the Highlands and the Sunshine State. Created by House of Edgar's Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish identity and its ability to bridge cultural divides, inviting wearers to share in the stories and traditions of both Dunfermline and Sarasota.

name: Sarna District
description: The Sarna town tartan is a quintessential example of Scottish heritage, evoking the rich history and culture of a specific district in the Highlands. Registered under the district category, this distinctive tartan represents the unique character of its associated locality. With its specific palette of blues and greens, reminiscent of Scotland's rolling hills and lochs, the Sarna town tartan is a testament to the country's enduring tradition of weaving. While the designer remains unknown, their skillful interpretation of local hues has created a timeless design that would have been worn with honour by locals and clan members alike, serving as a symbol of community pride and identity.

name: Sarna State
description: The Sarna District tartan is a fascinating example of Scotland's rich weaving heritage, with its unique blend of colours and count echoing the country's complex history. Originally gifted to the Scottish Tartans Society by Gudrun Joyce of Comrie, Perthshire, Sweden/Scotland, this tartan is steeped in tradition and cultural significance, its very existence testament to the intricate relationships between Scotland and its Nordic neighbours. As a 'State' tartan, it reflects the country's broader identity and allegiance, while also referencing its smaller district counterpart, Sarna (town), highlighting the intricate nuances of Scottish territorial affiliations. With its distinctive warp and weft count featuring odd numbers, this tartan is a true reflection of Scotland's storied textile past, waiting to be woven into the fabric of our collective heritage.

name: Saskatchewan
description: The Saskatchewan tartan, designed by Mrs F.L. Bastedo in 1961, embodies the natural beauty and rich heritage of Canada's prairie province. As one of the few district tartans to be registered, it represents a unique blend of regional identity and cultural significance. Inspired by the diverse landscapes of the region, from lush forests to rolling farmland, this tartan weaves together a tapestry of earthy tones and subtle nuances, evoking the tranquility of Saskatchewan's 100,000 plus lakes, rivers, and marshes. With its origins rooted in the Cree Indian language, the name Kisiskatchwani Sipi, meaning 'swift-flowing river', is a testament to the tartan's deep connection to the province's indigenous heritage. As a tribute to the land and its people, this tartan design serves as a poignant reminder of Saskatchewan's distinct identity within the fabric of Canadian history and tradition.

name: Satchidananda
description: The Satchidananda tartan, designed by Giovanna McCall, holds profound significance as a personal tribute to Reverend Sri Swami Satchiananda, founder of Integral Yoga International. Handwoven with meticulous care at 22 threads per inch (tpi), this unique set of 5.5 inches features an intricate pattern that reflects the spiritual and philosophical principles embodied by its namesake. As a Name tartan, it serves as a personal identifier for those who bear the Satchidananda name, connecting them to their heritage and the revered figure who inspired its creation. This exquisite tartan not only pays homage to Reverend Sri Swami Satchiananda's remarkable life and legacy but also represents a commitment to his teachings of love, self-awareness, and spiritual growth.

name: Satisfashion Argyll
description: The Satisfashion Argyll tartan is a captivating blend of colours and tradition, specifically designed for a Belgian clothing company seeking to bridge the cultural divide between their European roots and their affinity with Scotland's rich heritage. Named after the esteemed County of Argyll in western Scotland, this Corporate tartan proudly wears its Scottish credentials on its sleeve. Created by renowned designer Tommy Gemmell, Satisfashion Argyll weaves together a harmonious palette of blues, greens, and yellows that evokes the rolling hills and sparkling lochs of the Scottish countryside. As a celebration of cultural exchange and appreciation, this tartan serves as a powerful symbol of mutual respect and admiration between two nations, its subtle nuances and warm tones inviting wearers to forge strong connections with Scotland's storied past.

name: Saul
description: This unique Name tartan, Saul, is a personal tribute to Gavin Saul of Northumberland, England, created by the esteemed Donald Suttie Smith in 2002. As a registered Name tartan, its primary purpose is to represent an individual's heritage and identity. The subtle variations in tone, achieved through the lighter blues, cleverly depict the sett, showcasing the intricate balance of traditional tartan design. This distinctive tartan holds significant cultural value, not only as a means of self-expression but also as a nod to Gavin Saul's personal history and ancestral roots. Notably, certain restrictions apply, underscoring the importance of responsible usage and respect for the tartan's intended owner. The expertise of Donald Suttie Smith is evident in this carefully crafted design, which serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich heritage and tradition.

name: Savoy
description: The Savoy tartan, a vibrant and modern fashion choice inspired by the West Coast Woolen Mill's skilled artisans, is a testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage. Designed for the fashion category, this distinctive tartan has been carefully crafted to evoke the spirit of innovation and flair that defines 21st-century Scottish design. Recognised by the Scottish Tartans Authority, the Savoy tartan holds a special place in the country's tartan canon, and its registration in the Johnston Collection serves as a testament to its enduring appeal. While there are no specific restrictions on the use of this tartan, it is fitting that it should be admired for its originality and style, reflecting the best of Scotland's modern textile tradition.

name: Sawyer [default]
description: The Sawyer tartan is a deeply rooted clan tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition, originating from the esteemed Sawyer family. Registered in 1994 by renowned designer Dr Philip D Smith, this distinctive design has been woven into the fabric of Scottish identity for generations. As a member of this respected family, the Sawyer tartan holds great honour and is often worn with pride to signify affiliation and connection to its proud bearers. This beautiful tartan pattern, carefully crafted to reflect the unique characteristics of its namesake clan, is now a cherished part of Scotland's rich tapestry, passed down through families for years to come.

name: Scandinavian
description: The Scandinavian tartan, registered in recognition of its proud heritage by Finn Stavnsbo, is a testament to the cultural ties that bind the Scottish diaspora to their Nordic roots. Designed for Scandinavians of Scottish descent, many of whom can trace their ancestry back to legendary commanders like Munro and Mackay, who fought alongside King Christian of Denmark & Norway and King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden & Finland in the 17th century, this tartan weaves a narrative of shared history and tradition. The distinctive sett, featuring alternating squares of blue and white reminiscent of the modern flags of Denmark and Sweden, is punctuated by black and green threads that pay homage to the countries' respective emblems - a poignant reminder of the dark sorrows of war and the verdant battlefields of centuries past. This tartan's very existence serves as a badge of honour for those who wear it, proudly proclaiming their heritage in a rich tapestry of Scottish-Nordic identity.

name: Schiehallion
description: The Schiehallion tartan is a majestic corporate design that embodies the grandeur and heritage of Scotland's storied past. Registered by House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this distinctive pattern pays tribute to Robert Nicol's vision for the iconic kilt hire shops that bear his name. Named after the majestic Schiehallion mountain, a revered landmark in the Scottish Highlands, this tartan is steeped in tradition and craftsmanship. With its rich blues and golds evoking the heather-clad moors, it is an inspired choice for corporate clients seeking to tap into Scotland's timeless appeal. By drawing inspiration from the natural beauty of Scotland, the Schiehallion tartan serves as a powerful symbol of heritage and sophistication, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to establish a strong connection with Scottish culture.

name: Schneidersohne
description: The Schneidersohne Centenary tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage and corporate tradition, as designed by Maxine Scott for Inveresk PLC in 2002. This Corporate tartan was woven with great intention, bringing together the colours of two esteemed organisations: Inveresk's own hues and those of Schneiders Papier, a paper manufacturing company celebrating its centenary at the time. The result is a unique and distinctive pattern that embodies the values of innovation, quality, and community spirit, evoking the rich history of Scotland's industrial past. By proudly showcasing this tartan, Inveresk PLC honoured the 100-year milestone of Schneiders Papier, solidifying their partnership with a lasting tribute to Scottish tradition and corporate identity.

name: Schranz-Gritte
description: The Antrim County, Crest Range tartan is a rich and storied design rooted in the heritage of Northern Ireland's most iconic county, Antrim. As one of a set of Irish County tartans, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the region's complex history and cultural identity. Originally created by Viking Technology Limited (now Tartan Web Scotland Ltd) in 2005, the tartan was carefully crafted to reflect the unique character of the area, drawing inspiration from the natural beauty of the surrounding landscape. Its ownership has since been acquired by USA Kilts Inc, a development that reflects the evolving nature of Scottish heritage and cultural exchange. While this tartan's design is now subject to certain restrictions, it remains an important and evocative representation of Antrim County's proud history and traditions.

name: Scolpaig Fragment Artifact;
description: This enigmatic Unidentified (Scolpaig) tartan is a fragmentary fragment of a larger whole, its origins shrouded in mystery as it originates from Scolpaig, North Uist on the rugged west coast of Scotland's Outer Hebrides. Category 'Other' suggests that this tartan does not directly relate to a specific clan or family, yet its presence still holds significance within the broader tapestry of Scottish heritage. Although its designer remains unknown, the Scottish Tartans Society's collection lends weight to its authenticity. As such, this tantalising piece of tartan is all the more captivating - a tangible connection to the wild, windswept landscapes and the communities that have called North Uist home for centuries, waiting to be unravelled by those willing to delve deeper into Scotland's rich textile past.

name: Scotch House (London); Raibert Check
description: The Raibert Check, a stylish and timeless fashion tartan, embodies the quintessential spirit of Scottish heritage. Registered by the esteemed Scotch House in London, this vibrant check pattern is steeped in tradition and elegance, evoking images of the British capital's rich cultural tapestry. As a fashion design, the Raibert Check exudes sophistication and versatility, making it an ideal choice for a wide range of garments, from statement coats to elegant accessories. With its bold colour palette, this tartan is sure to add a dash of glamour to any outfit, while its enduring popularity is a testament to the timeless appeal of Scottish textile traditions.

name: Scotch House 2000 Antique
description: The Scotch House 2000 Antique tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage, carefully crafted by Kinloch Anderson Ltd as part of The Scotch House's exquisite millennium collection. This fashion tartan is a unique addition to Scotland's iconic woven traditions, bearing the esteemed mark of The Scotch House - a renowned Scottish brand synonymous with excellence in textile design. Registering one of three tartans created specifically for this collection, the Scotch House 2000 Antique is steeped in history and cultural significance, its intricate patterns evoking the nostalgia of a bygone era. With restrictions ensuring its exclusive association with The Scotch House, this stunning tartan is a true celebration of Scotland's artisanal heritage, expertly woven to pay homage to a legacy that continues to influence fashion and textiles to this day.

name: Scotch House 2000 Original
description: The Scotch House 2000 Dress tartan is a vibrant and modern interpretation of traditional Scottish heritage, born from the renowned Kinloch Anderson Ltd's creative vision. As one of three tartans designed specifically for The Scotch House millennium collection, this stylish fabric is steeped in history and cultural significance. With its unique combination of colours and subtle texture, this fashion tartan embodies the spirit of Scotland's rich textiles tradition, effortlessly blending modern flair with timeless heritage values. However, it's worth noting that due to its exclusive association with The Scotch House, this tartan is subject to certain restrictions, ensuring its authenticity and exclusivity are preserved for discerning wearers who appreciate the finer nuances of Scottish design.

name: Scotch House Callum
description: The Scotch House tartan, designed by the esteemed house, is a fashion tartan that embodies the warmth and hospitality synonymous with Scotland's rich heritage. With its roots firmly planted in tradition, this iconic pattern features a distinctive sett, almost identical to the genuine Scotch House Fashion at #1315, albeit with subtly different hues that set it apart from its authentic counterpart. Whether worn as a statement piece or woven into the very fabric of Scottish identity, the Scotch House tartan is a testament to the country's enduring legacy, its beauty and character distilled into every intricate thread and subtle colour variation.

name: Scotch House Corporate
description: The Scotch House 2000 Original tartan, expertly crafted by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, is a vibrant interpretation of traditional Scottish heritage, reimagined for the modern era. As one of a trio created specifically for The Scotch House's millennium collection, this tartan embodies the spirit of renewal and celebration that defined the dawn of a new century. With its unique colour palette and intricate sett, this fashionable tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich textile tradition, carefully balancing traditional motifs with contemporary flair. Though it was designed exclusively for The Scotch House, its enduring appeal makes it a desirable choice for anyone seeking to honour the country's cultural heritage and add a touch of Scottish sophistication to their wardrobe.

name: Scotch House Dorcas
description: The Dorcas tartan, registered in the Scottish Tartans Authority's collection, is a fashion-inspired design steeped in heritage and tradition. Named after its original patron, Aljean, this vibrant and striking tartan was created by West Coast Woolen Mill with a focus on bold colours and precise weaving. As part of the Fashion category, Dorcas showcases the versatility and creativity of Scottish tartans beyond traditional clan affiliations. Its origins in the late 1970s and early 1980s reflect the era's influence on Scottish fashion, with the distinctive weft and warp slogs hinting at a more experimental approach to tartan design. With its registration notes referencing both its historical significance and technical details, the Dorcas tartan serves as a testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage, while also demonstrating the enduring appeal of this iconic pattern in modern fashion.

name: Scotch House Dorcas #2
description: The Dorcas tartan, designed by John Bain for Scotch House of London in 1980, embodies the essence of modern Scottish fashion with its unique blend of traditional geometry and innovative colour palette. As part of a pair of identical geometric designs differing only in hue, the Dorcas tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich textile heritage while pushing the boundaries of contemporary style. Its similarities to Menzies and Vestiarium Scoticum No. 196 reflect a deep understanding of Scottish traditional weaving, yet its distinct colours – carefully chosen by Bain – inject a touch of sophistication and modernity. With its registration notes tracing its creation as one of a pair for Scotch House's client, the Dorcas tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish design to captivate global audiences and inspire new generations of fashion enthusiasts.

name: Scotch House House Tartan
description: The Scotch House corporate tartan is an iconic representation of Scottish heritage and professionalism, born from the renowned brand's own distinctive weave. As its own registered design, this tartan embodies the values of tradition, quality, and authority that have come to define Scotch House. Originating as a bespoke creation for the company, it has since been adopted by those in favour of embracing the timeless charm of Scotland's textile traditions. With its subtle, nuanced colour palette and deliberate sett pattern, this tartan exudes a sense of understated sophistication, perfectly capturing the essence of corporate identity while remaining deeply rooted in Scottish history and culture.

name: Scotch Mist
description: The Scotch Mist tartan, designed by John Stevens, is a quintessential corporate design that embodies the spirit of British heritage and tradition. This stylish and versatile weave was originally created for hire and sales at Davison Menswear, a prominent Edinburgh-based retailer, in the 1980s. Commissioned by Batley Mills in Leeds, a renowned textile manufacturer, the Scotch Mist tartan is a 'random design', meaning it doesn't adhere to traditional clan or family ties, making it an accessible and distinctive choice for corporate clients seeking a unique brand identity. Characterised by its soothing blend of blues, greens, and subtle neutral tones, this tartan evokes the misty, mystical atmosphere of Scotland's rugged landscapes, inviting businesses to tap into the country's rich cultural heritage and establish themselves as authentic British brands.

name: Scotch Whisky Heritage Centre #2
description: The Trotter Name Tartan, carefully crafted by renowned Scottish designer Alasdair Macleod, holds a special place in the hearts of those who bear its noble bearing. This unique tartan was specifically designed for Wayne Trotter of Victoria, Australia, as part of his personal regalia, signifying his honour and heritage. As a Name Tartan, it is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition, passing down family lineage and identity through generations. The intricate weaving of Geoffrey (Tailor) Ltd in Edinburgh adds a touch of authenticity to this treasured fabric, imbuing the wearer with a sense of pride and connection to their ancestral roots. With its rich history and cultural significance, the Trotter Name Tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage, evoking feelings of warmth, tradition, and community among those who wear it.

name: Scotch Whisky Heritage Centre
description: The Scotch Whisky Heritage Centre tartan is a dynamic and evocative corporate design born from the expertise of renowned weaver Harry Lindley of Kinloch Anderson Ltd in Edinburgh. Asymmetric in its composition, this unique tartan is specifically tailored for the esteemed Scottish Whisky Heritage Centre, proudly situated on the Royal Mile of Scotland's capital city. A testament to Scotland's rich whisky-making heritage, this tartan design embodies the warmth and hospitality that defines the nation's love affair with whisky. While its corporate usage is restricted to the Scotch Whisky Heritage Centre, the inspiration behind it can be shared by all who appreciate Scotland's storied past and the cultural significance of this iconic symbol, forever woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition.

name: Scotia Hunting
description: The Scotia tartan, registered by the Edinburgh Woollen Mill, embodies the timeless spirit of Scotland's majestic landscapes and rich heritage. As a fashion tartan, it is woven to evoke the country's rugged beauty and storied history, making it an ideal choice for those who cherish Scottish tradition. The subtle, muted tones evoking the heather-covered moors and the gentle lapping of Highland seas evoke a sense of grandeur and mystique. With its roots firmly planted in Scotland's cultural identity, this tartan is deeply rooted in the country's history, echoing the tales of brave warriors who once roamed the Highlands under the banner of Scotia, as immortalised in the legend of Jack Dalgety.

name: Scotia
description: The Scotia tartan is an iconic fashion tartan steeped in Scottish heritage, first conceived by James Allan of East Kilbride in 1850. Originally intended to represent Scotland's rich history and culture, the tartan was later reimagined and revised by David Easton of Eastons of Galashiels in 1968, with its sett subsequently checked and verified by renowned textile expert Jack Dalgety in 1979. Today, this celebrated design is synonymous with Scottish identity, worn by fashion enthusiasts around the world as a symbol of national pride and tradition. As a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy, the Scotia tartan embodies the country's storied past, its timeless beauty woven into the very fabric of British heritage.

name: Scotland 1782
description: The Scotland 1782 tartan is an iconic Fashion tartan steeped in rich Scottish heritage, woven by renowned designers MacDonald, Todd & Isabel for the House of Edgar. Registration notes reveal its origins as a bespoke commission from R & I MacDonald, Kiltmakers of West Calder, West Lothian, Scotland, underscoring the tartan's deep connection to traditional craftsmanship and local expertise. This storied fabric is deeply rooted in the country's history, evoking the late 18th century period when tartan was an integral part of Scottish military regalia and Highland dress. The subtle variations in the tartan's reds and blues evoke a sense of refinement and elegance, perfect for formal occasions or as a stylish statement piece.

name: Scotland 2000
description: The Scotland 2000 tartan is a poignant commemorative design created in honour of Scotland's millennium celebrations in the year 2000, conceived by esteemed textile artist Arthur Mackie of Strathmore Woollen Co., Forfar. This richly woven tartan represents a celebratory yet nostalgic tribute to Scotland's heritage and cultural identity, symbolising the country's enduring spirit and resilience. With its carefully crafted colours and precise sett pattern, this tartan pays homage to the nation's complex history and storied past, while embracing the promise of a brighter future. Its registration notes proudly declaring it a 'millennium tartan' serve as a testament to Mackie's innovative approach to textile design, one that blends tradition with modernity to create a truly unique and meaningful tribute to Scotland's enduring legacy.

name: Scotland
description: The Robieson QAHS tartan is a poignant commemoration of the formative years of Graham Alexander Robieson, whose love for his alma mater, Queen Anne High School in Dunfermline, has been woven into fabric. This carefully crafted tartan, designed with meticulous attention to detail by its creator, proudly wears the colours of the school on its sleeve - a testament to the enduring bond between place, people, and tradition. As a Commemorative tartan, it serves as a lasting tribute to Graham's time at QAHS, where he shares memories of his brother and father, who also spent years within its walls. This unique tartan is a celebration of Scottish heritage and the significance of education in shaping lives, with the registration notes serving as a fitting reminder of the people and places that inspired its creation.

name: Scotland Forever
description: "Scotland Forever" is a vibrant and stirring fashion tartan that embodies the indomitable spirit of Scotland's proud military heritage. Designed by Chris Mcleod, this iconic pattern is a testament to the bravery and camaraderie of Scotland's finest regiments, most notably the Scots Greys who famously rallied with this very war cry at the Battle of Waterloo in 1815. A joint endeavour between Alex Scott & Co of Aberdeen and Lochcarron of Scotland, 'Scotland Forever!' tartan is a celebrated symbol of Scottish tradition and heritage, worn by those who honour their country's proud history and unyielding pride. With its bold colours and distinctive pattern, this tartan is sure to evoke the grandeur and bravery of Scotland's storied past, making it a timeless choice for those who wear it.

name: Scotland the Brave Dress Dance
description: Scotland the Brave Dress is a vibrant and iconic fashion tartan, inspired by the stirring words of Cliff Hanley's song of the same name. This popular design, originally created by Scott & David Millsom of Millsom & Main in Aberdeen, now bears the mark of esteemed designer Dalgliesh, D C. The registration notes reveal that traditional Scottish colours were carefully chosen to represent the nation's rich heritage: navy blue and white evoke the iconic Saltire flag, while green and purple pay homage to Scotland's beloved national emblem, the Thistle. This tartan design is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scotland, its people, and their rich cultural traditions - an honourable tribute that continues to captivate audiences around the world.

name: Scotland the Brave
description: Scotland the Brave, a fashion tartan born from the stirring words of Cliff Hanley's iconic song, embodies the proud spirit of Scotland's heritage. This distinctive tartan is a masterful blend of traditional colours, drawing upon the country's rich symbolism to create a bold and eye-catching pattern. The registration notes reveal that navy blue and white hues were carefully chosen to evoke the revered Saltire flag, while green and purple tones were selected to pay tribute to the national thistle emblem. As a fashion tartan, Scotland the Brave is sure to make a statement, exuding a sense of bravery and national pride. Its origins rooted in music and tradition, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's storied past and its enduring cultural significance.

name: Scotland Undiscovered
description: The Undiscovered Scotland corporate tartan is a striking representation of Scotland's untamed beauty, carefully woven to reflect the nation's connection to its stunning landscapes and maritime heritage. This distinctive design combines a rich palette of greens, evoking the country's lush forests, rolling hills, and heather-covered moors, with a deep blue that echoes the sea's unifying presence throughout Scotland and its islands. As a corporate tartan, it embodies the values of innovation, exploration, and community that define Undiscovered Scotland, while paying homage to the country's enduring spirit of discovery and adventure. By incorporating these elements, this tartan design serves as a powerful symbol of Scottish identity and a testament to the nation's rich cultural heritage.

name: Scotland United Colours
description: The United Colours of Scotland tartan is a vibrant and modern corporate design, woven by Marton Mills for Nicholsons Highland Supplies, a reputable kilt hire business based in Ingatestone, Essex. This bold and eclectic pattern, created by Mike Nicholson, embodies the spirit of unity and shared heritage that defines Scotland's rich cultural identity. With its striking combination of colours, this tartan is perfect for any organisation or individual seeking to evoke the warm and welcoming atmosphere of Scotland's national pride. As a corporate design, it lends itself beautifully to branding and visual identity, while its roots in traditional Scottish weaving ensure a deep connection to the country's proud heritage. By wearing or displaying this tartan, one can proudly showcase their affiliation with Nicholsons Highland Supplies and their commitment to celebrating Scotland's unique culture.

name: Scotland's Lionheart
description: Scotland's Lionheart is a stirring fashion tartan, inspired by the bold spirit of Scotland's legendary Lionheart, King Alexander III. Registered for fashion use, this vibrant design embodies the country's rich heritage and sense of pride. Crafted with precision by The House of Edgar, this tartan weaves its way through history, evoking the tales of brave warriors and noble monarchs. Originally designed by Claire Hunter at The Kilt Centre of Hamilton, Scotland's Lionheart has been meticulously woven to showcase the technical mastery of the Scottish tartan tradition. As a Fashion registration, it is limited to being used exclusively with House of Edgar, ensuring its unique authenticity shines through in every finished garment or textile creation.

name: Scotland's National Dress
description: This iconic tartan, registered as Scotland's National Dress, is an enduring symbol of Scottish heritage and national pride. Designed by renowned weaver Dalgliesh in 1898, it was officially adopted as the national dress for Scotland in recognition of its unique cultural significance. Characterised by a subtle variation in thread count and bold black guards on white, this tartan proudly wears its distinctive markings like a badge of honour. As one of the most recognisable tartans in existence, it has been woven into the fabric of Scottish identity, featuring prominently at ceremonial events and national gatherings. Its status as a District tartan underscores its historical significance and connection to Scotland's rich regional heritage, making it a treasured icon of Scotland's cultural legacy.

name: Scotland's National
description: Scotland's National tartan, designed by Michael King in collaboration with Philip King Kiltmakers, is a majestic representation of Scotland's rich heritage. As a Fashion tartan, it has been adopted by many as a symbol of national pride, perfect for those looking to embody the country's spirit. Originally a modification of the iconic Black Watch / Campbell tartan, this revised design boasts subtle yet striking differences that set it apart.
