Woven with precision by Lochcarron and launched on St Andrew's Day 1993, Scotland's National tartan is steeped in tradition, its roots tracing back to the country's esteemed kilt-making history. With its intricate patterns and storied past, this tartan is a testament to Scotland's timeless beauty and cultural significance.

name: Scotland's Own
description: Scotland's Own, a majestic tartan designed by Elizabeth Ballantyne Designs, embodies the spirit of inclusivity and national pride. This fashion tartan, categorised as such, was created to be worn by anyone who feels no ancestral connection to a traditional clan or family tartan. As a universal tartan, it serves as a celebration of Scottish heritage for all, regardless of familial ties. With its distinctive sett and rich colours, Scotland's Own pays homage to the country's storied past while inviting wearers to identify with the broader cultural narrative of Scotland itself. By embracing this tartan, individuals can proudly express their affinity for Scotland, free from any specific clan affiliation.

name: Scotland's People
description: Scotland's People is a vibrant and captivating fashion tartan, woven with the rich heritage of Scotland's past at its core. Designed by renowned textile experts at Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this tartan pays tribute to the Sutherland family legacy, as Trevor Yerbury's grandmother was from this esteemed clan. With its distinctive colour palette inspired by the rugged landscapes of Sutherland, this tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scotland's people. Originally produced for a poignant photographic exhibition showcasing the nation's identity, Scotland's People has been carefully woven to evoke the warmth and hospitality that define Scottish culture. Its inclusion in the Scottish Tartans Authority's collection serves as a permanent testament to its significance, ensuring that this timeless design continues to captivate audiences for generations to come.

name: Scotsman
description: The Scotsman tartan is a storied and iconic Corporate design born from the esteemed Kinloch Anderson Ltd. Created specifically for The Scotsman, Scotland's national newspaper, this tartan pays homage to the publication's founders, MacIntosh and MacLaren, by drawing inspiration from their signature setts. By marrying the corporate colours with these historic weaves, the design embodies the spirit of Scotland's proud journalism tradition. Though subject to certain restrictions, this tartan is now available for those who wish to honour The Scotsman's legacy in their own work or endeavours. This distinctive Corporate tartan serves as a testament to the enduring connection between Scottish heritage and modern industry, its bold colours and rich textures echoing the country's storied past while embracing the present.

name: Scott Autumn
description: The Scott Autumn tartan, designed by esteemed textile artist Artmark, is a stunning addition to the world of fashion tartans. With its rich, autumnal hues, this vibrant pattern evokes the warmth and coziness of Scotland's changing seasons. As a fashion tartan, it has been carefully crafted to add a touch of elegance and sophistication to clothing and accessories, perfect for making a statement on the catwalk or on a special occasion. With no restrictions in place, the Scott Autumn tartan is free to be worn with pride, its beauty and heritage open to interpretation by those who wear it. As a celebration of Scottish style and tradition, this tartan design embodies the spirit of autumn, inviting wearers to experience the country's unique cultural legacy through the timeless art of woven textiles.

name: Scott Black & White
description: The Scott Black and White tartan is a quintessential representation of Scottish heritage, boasting a rich history as a Clan tartan dating back to the 19th century. Originally part of the Morgan collection held by the Scottish Tartans Society, this timeless design features alternating stripes of dark and light hues that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's moorlands and glens. As a Clan tartan, it is steeped in tradition and signifies loyalty to the MacDonald clan, one of Scotland's most storied families. The Scott Black and White tartan has been woven with precision for generations, its unique character reflecting the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scottish weavers. With no restrictions on its use, this iconic design remains a proud symbol of Scottish identity and heritage, perfectly capturing the essence of the country's ancient traditions and timeless beauty.

name: Scott (Sir Walter) Personal
description: The Scott B&W - 1850 tartan is a rich and evocative heritage pattern, steeped in the romantic legacy of Scotland's most iconic author, Sir Walter Scott. Registration notes reveal that this distinctive design was allegedly created by Scott himself in 1822, for his own private use as a Lowland shepherd's plaid. Although the authenticity of these claims is disputed, one thing is certain: this tartan has captured the hearts and imaginations of those who cherish Scottish heritage and tradition. A member of the Clan Scott family or indeed any individual seeking to honour their ancestral roots, would do well to respect the restrictions placed on this tartan's use, ensuring its enduring significance is preserved for future generations. Worn with pride by those who bear its name, the Scott B&W - 1850 tartan remains a poignant testament to the power of Scottish identity and tradition.

name: Scott (Sir Walter) Abbreviated
description: The Stewart, Black #1 tartan is a storied name in the rich tapestry of Scotland's heritage, evoking the proud legacy of the Dukes of Albany who once held sway over the Scottish throne. As a registered Name tartan, it has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition, its intricate pattern and deep blues a testament to the country's unyielding passion for its own unique identity. Originally submitted by Mrs Ella Cook from Aberdeen in 1976, this particular specimen now resides in the prestigious archives of the Scottish Tartan Society, a fitting resting place for a tartan that has been imbued with the honour and history of one of Scotland's most illustrious clans.

name: Scott Brown Hunting
description: The Scott Hunting tartan is a storied and revered clan pattern, its rich heritage woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition. First glimpsed in the pages of W & A.K. Johnson's 1906 publication, this timeless tartan has been passed down through generations as a symbol of pride and identity for those bearing the Scott name. Weaved to perfection by the skilled artisans at Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan design embodies the very essence of Scottish heritage: strength, loyalty, and unyielding spirit. As a registered clan tartan, it holds a special place in the hearts of those who wear it with honour, serving as a poignant reminder of their ancestral roots and connection to the land that shaped their family's story.

name: Scott Dress
description: The Scott Dress tartan is a rich and storied family heirloom, its origins deeply rooted in Scotland's clan traditions. This distinctive pattern, categorised as a Clan/Family tartan, takes inspiration from the 'Red' Scott, first recorded in the 17th-century Vestiarium Scoticum. According to registration notes, it is part of the esteemed Scarlett Collection, showcasing the finest examples of Scottish tartans. As such, this tartan design holds great honour among Scotland's clans and families, its subtle nuances and intricate colourwork a testament to the country's rich textile heritage. The Scott Dress tartan may not be specifically designed by a named individual, but its significance is undeniable, serving as a tangible connection to Scotland's storied past and the families who have worn it for generations.

name:
Scott Green
[AKA] Scott Hunting
description: The Scott (Green) tartan, a proud emblem of Clan Scott heritage, weaves together ancient traditions and familial ties. Originating from the MacKinlay strip in the Marcus K Milne Collection, Aberdeen, this tartan has been passed down through generations as an honourable symbol of Scottish clan identity. Known affectionately as Green Scott, its rich green hues evoke the rolling hills and verdant landscapes of Scotland's borders region, particularly around Selkirk, where the 9th Duke of Buccleuch resides. With restrictions governing its use to maintain the integrity of the tartan's heritage, this design remains an important part of Clan Scott's history and legacy, held dear by those who wear it with pride as a testament to their family's storied past.

name: Scott Hunting #2
description: The Scott Hunting special tartan is a poignant tribute to the rich heritage of Clan MacKenzie, one of Scotland's most storied families. Traditionally woven for generations, this distinctive tartan was once an integral part of the clan's identity, worn by its members with pride and honour. The specific pattern, featuring shades of blue, green, yellow, black, and red, is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition, reflecting the country's rolling hills, sparkling lochs, and rugged landscapes. With no designer credited, it is believed to have been passed down through oral tradition before being formally registered with the Scottish Tartans Society. Though its origins are shrouded in mystery, this tartan remains a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan MacKenzie, a symbol of family ties that continue to weave themselves into Scotland's rich tapestry of heritage.

name:
Scott [default]
[AKA] Scott Red
description: The historic Scott tartan is a timeless symbol of Scottish heritage, with roots dating back to the early 19th century. This renowned clan tartan has been woven into the very fabric of Scotland's history, bearing testament to the storied legacy of the Stewarts and their illustrious ancestors. Although Sir Walter Scott famously rejected an association with this particular tartan in 1829, his rejection has only served to cement its place in popular consciousness. Interestingly, some researchers have suggested that the design may owe a debt to the traditional Clan Gregor tartan of 1819, adding a layer of complexity to its origins. As one of the most sought-after tartans of modern times, the Scott is an enduring tribute to the country's rich cultural legacy, evoking images of rugged Highland landscapes and the proud traditions of Scotland's storied clans.

name: Scott (Sir Walter) #2
description: Sir Walter Scott's Bi Centenary Tartan, also known as Scott #2, is a fashion tartan steeped in Scottish heritage and literary history. Designed by renowned weaver Gardiners in 1971 to commemorate the birth of Scotland's beloved national poet, Walter Scott, this iconic tartan weaves together Ingles Buchan sample strips to evoke the rolling hills and rugged landscapes that inspired Scott's timeless works. As a Fashion tartan, it was created for modern wearers to pay homage to this cultural touchstone, while also referencing the traditional Scottish Tartans Authority reference number #57, which shares its origins with another iconic tartan design. Now cherished by fashion enthusiasts and fans of Scottish literature alike, Sir Walter Scott's Bi Centenary Tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage and tradition.

name: Scott Green (Sir Walter)
description: The majestic Scott Green (Sir Walter) tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans, woven from the very fabric of its storied past. This timeless family tartan, registered by Sir Walter Scott himself, holds a special place in the annals of Scottish tradition. With its intricate patterns and earthy tones, reminiscent of the rolling hills and heather-covered moors that cradle the Scottish Highlands, this tartan is an ode to the land, the people, and the storied history that has shaped the country's identity. As part of the esteemed J.Telfer Dunbar Collection in the Scottish Tartans Society Archive, the Scott Green tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the artistic legacy of Sir Walter Scott, Scotland's beloved national bard and literary icon.

name: Scott (Sir Walter)
description: The Scott, Sir Walter fashion tartan, designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a timeless and iconic Scottish heritage pattern that evokes the spirit of 19th-century Scotland. Named after Sir Walter Scott, the renowned author of historical novels set in Scotland, this tartan was originally registered as part of Wilsons' esteemed Pattern Book No.4 in 1840. The colour palette features a rich, muted blend of blues and greens, with subtle hints of earthy tones, carefully balanced to reflect the poet's love affair with the Scottish landscape. Notably, there appears to be some historical confusion surrounding this tartan's registration, with an identical design mistakenly attributed to the Campbell clan. Thankfully, clarification has been achieved, ensuring that this beautiful pattern is now celebrated in its rightful context as a testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage and the enduring legacy of Sir Walter Scott.

name: Scottish Airports
description: The Kinloch Anderson Ltd's "Scottish Airports" tartan is a fitting tribute to Scotland's aviation heritage, designed specifically for corporate use by airports across the country. This distinctive tartan, registered with The Scottish Tartans Society, pays homage to Percy Pilcher, an early aviation pioneer who drew inspiration from his Gunn family connections. The design cleverly weaves together the classic Gunn sett with a bold purple line, symbolising the thistle, Scotland's national emblem, and representing the country's rich history and cultural identity. As a corporate tartan, this unique pattern is meant to evoke pride and professionalism in Scottish Airports, while also honouring Pilcher's legacy as a trailblazer in aviation. With its carefully chosen colour palette inspired by the British Airports Authority, this tartan design is sure to become an iconic symbol of Scotland's aviation sector.

name: Scottish Ambulance Service
description: The Scottish Ambulance Service tartan, designed by renowned textile experts at Lochcarron of Scotland, pays tribute to the bravery and selflessness of Scotland's dedicated paramedics. As a Corporate tartan, it was originally intended for use in official uniforms and equipment, symbolising the unity and professionalism of the Scottish Ambulance Service. Registered in 1996, this distinctive tartan was first woven in January 1997 and is now proudly showcased in the esteemed Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority. With its bold and striking pattern, this tartan embodies the values of courage, compassion, and community that define the ambulance service's vital work, ensuring a lasting legacy for generations to come.

name: Scottish American Athletic Association
description: This corporate tartan, designed by Nathan MacDonald, proudly bears the badge of the Scottish American Athletic Association, a nod to the rich heritage of Scottish sportsmanship and community spirit. With its distinctive woven sample, this tartan is steeped in tradition and represents the values of unity, friendship, and athletic excellence that have defined the association since its inception. As a Category Corporate tartan, it has been carefully crafted for corporate wear, evoking a sense of professionalism and civic pride. Its very existence serves as a testament to the enduring ties between Scotland and the United States, where the love of sports brings people together across borders.

name: Scottish Borders; Borderland
description: The Scottish Borderland tartan, designed by renowned textile artist Alistair Buchan, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's storied borders, where history and culture converge. As a Fashion tartan, it is perfect for those who wish to celebrate their affinity with the land and its people without an ancestral claim. With its distinctive sett and subtle colour palette, this tartan pays homage to the rugged beauty of the Scottish Borders, where the gentle rolling hills meet the dramatic scenery of the Cheviot Hills. Registration notes indicate a connection to Lochcarron of Scotland, lending weight to its authenticity as part of the country's revered tartan legacy.

name: Scottish Borders;
description: The Border Sett, registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a testament to the rich tapestry of Scotland's historical heritage. This striking tartan, categorised as "Other", pays homage to the intricate weaving traditions of the 18th century, its threads painstakingly extracted from the border of an authentic antique blanket. By acknowledging the distinction between the Border Sett and District tartans, the designers have ensured that this unique pattern is woven into the fabric of history, rather than being associated with a specific geographical region. As part of the Telfer Dunbar Collection, this tartan joins the esteemed ranks of Scotland's most celebrated designs, its intricate patterns evoking the storied past of the Scottish Borders and the artisans who once called it home.

name: Scottish Borders Health Board
description: The Borders Health Board tartan is a distinctive corporate design, born from the creative vision of renowned designer Harry Lindley in the 1990s. With its unique sett and colour palette, this tartan pays homage to Lindley's illustrious career as the Royal Family's go-to expert for all Highland dress requirements, having advised them on their sartorial needs for many years prior to his retirement from Kinloch Anderson. As a corporate design, the Borders Health Board tartan is imbued with the values of professionalism and community, reflecting its origins in the public sector that serves the Borders region of Scotland. The tartan's significance extends beyond its functional use, however, as it also serves as a symbol of regional identity and pride, celebrating the rich cultural heritage of the Borders and its people.

name: Scottish Borders Tourist Board
description: This striking Corporate tartan, designed by renowned Scottish textile experts at Lochcarron of Scotland, proudly showcases the rich heritage of the Scottish Borders region. The carefully selected colours, featuring a distinctive midnight blue, reflect the dramatic landscapes and atmospheric skies characteristic of the area. As part of the Corporate category, this tartan is ideal for use in business and professional settings, conveying the unique character of the Scottish Borders whilst maintaining a level of sophistication. Registered to fairly accurate specifications, with only one notable tweak - a darker, more intense blue than originally specified - this tartan remains true to its original design intent. As such, it embodies the perfect blend of traditional craftsmanship and modern corporate style, making it an excellent choice for any organisation seeking to tap into the timeless appeal of Scottish heritage.

name: Scottish Borders Union Cattle Show
description: The Border Union Cattle Show tartan is a vibrant and distinctive corporate design born from the rich heritage of Scotland's Borders region. Woven with a deep respect for tradition, this tartan tells the story of the 1994 event, which brought together the community to celebrate all things cattle-related. With its bold, contrasting colours reminiscent of the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Scottish Borders, this tartan is a testament to the area's proud history as a hub for agriculture and trade. As a corporate design, it has become a symbol of hospitality and welcome, evoking the warm and generous spirit of the Border Union Cattle Show. Its association with James Cockburn, Galashiels' renowned butcher, adds an air of authenticity to this tartan, making it a unique and special addition to any organisation or individual looking to make a statement about their Scottish roots.

name:
Scottish Canals
[AKA] Highland Canals
description: The Scottish Canals tartan is a captivating representation of Scotland's rich industrial heritage, perfectly encapsulating the country's pioneering spirit and romanticised past. As a Corporate tartan, it has been adopted by various organisations seeking to evoke the nation's sense of innovative enterprise and community pride. Designed by Claire Donaldson for House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this distinctive pattern takes its cue from the majestic Caledonian Canal, one of Scotland's most iconic waterways, which played a vital role in shaping the country's industrial history. Originally known as Highland Canals, the tartan underwent subtle revisions before being renamed Scottish Canals, reflecting its evolution over time and cementing its place in the nation's textile heritage.

name: Scottish Chieftain
description: The Scottish Chieftain corporate tartan embodies the proud heritage of Scotland's storied past, expertly woven to evoke the grandeur of the country's historic clans. This versatile and modern design, registered for use in promotional settings, draws its inspiration from the rich traditions of Scotland's chieftains, whose bravery and leadership have left an indelible mark on the nation's history. With its striking, symmetrical pattern, this tartan is perfectly suited for corporate branding, adding a touch of Scottish flair to any business or organisation seeking to connect with its roots. Whether used as a badge of honour or a symbol of identity, the Scottish Chieftain tartan promises to convey strength, resilience, and a deep sense of national pride, making it an ideal choice for those looking to make a lasting impression.

name: Scottish Claymores
description: The Scottish Claymores corporate tartan is an emblematic weave of heritage and modernity, born from the bold spirit of Scotland's American Football Team. Designed by esteemed textile masters at Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this vibrant tartan pays homage to the team's rich colours, taken directly from their logo. Originally created for the 1996 'World Bowl' hosted at Murrayfield, Edinburgh, the Scottish Claymores tartan has become a symbol of unity and pride among fans and players alike. While its origins are specifically tied to corporate use, this striking design is steeped in tradition and history, reflecting Scotland's proud sporting heritage. Not open for public purchase, this exclusive tartan remains an honour reserved for those in favour with the team's governing body, a testament to its enduring significance in the world of Scottish American Football.

name: Scottish Crofting Foundation
description: The Scottish Crofting Foundation tartan is a vibrant representation of Scotland's rich heritage and its people's unwavering commitment to preserving traditional ways of life. As a corporate tartan, it embodies the values of a dedicated organisation, established by crofters themselves, which tirelessly advocates for policies that benefit rural communities and the environment. The intricate design weaves together threads of Scottish tradition with a sense of forward-thinking social responsibility, reflecting the SCF's mission to make a lasting impact on issues affecting agricultural and environmental welfare. With its bold colours and distinctive pattern, this tartan not only pays homage to Scotland's rural roots but also serves as a symbol of collective endeavour and community-driven activism.

name: Scottish Cultural Society
description: The Scottish Cultural Society tartan is a vibrant representation of corporate tradition, born out of a charitable endeavour with roots in Illinois, USA. In 1977, Judie MacRae and Jean Givler designed this distinctive pattern to commemorate a charity founded by members with Scottish heritage or interests. The resulting tartan is an innovative blend of colours that reflect the rich cultural legacy of Scotland, imbued with a sense of community and shared purpose. As a corporate tartan, it's worn with pride by organisations and individuals who draw strength from their Scottish roots, fostering a connection to the land, its people, and its traditions.

name: Scottish Express International
description: The Scottish Express International tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate design, expertly crafted by the renowned MacArthur & Co. team under the guidance of Peter MacArthur. Registered to commemorate the 25th anniversary of an international delivery company, this tartan embodies the spirit of modern Scotland's global connections. Characterised by its distinctive red and blue tones, interwoven with subtle golden threads, Scottish Express International is a testament to the country's rich heritage and ability to adapt to an ever-changing world. With its sleek, contemporary aesthetic, this tartan is poised to make a lasting impression on any corporate entity seeking to forge strong links with Scotland's storied past, while embracing the dynamism of international commerce.

name: Scottish Flair (Canberra) personal
description: The Canberra, City of tartan is a vibrant Fashion tartan that celebrates the nation's capital with pride. Registered in 2004, this striking pattern takes its inspiration from the iconic Australian flag and features a dark blue field representing the Canberra flag, punctuated by gold and white stars evoking the city's connection to the Commonwealth. Medium blue undertones pay homage to the Canberra Bluebell, a nod to the city's natural beauty. Designed by Peter Burrows and Stewart Smith with technical support from Strathmore Woollen Company, this tartan is steeped in Australian heritage and tradition. Originally used by the Canberra City Pipes and Drums, it has become synonymous with the city's rich cultural identity, making it a cherished symbol of Canberra's history and civic pride.

name: Scottish Foundation VA Highlands
description: The Scottish Foundation VA Highlands tartan, designed by Jean Oxley, Elberta Raisbeck, Anne Sampson, and Charlene Dixon Hutcheson, is a captivating corporate tartan that celebrates the rich cultural heritage of Virginia's Scottish settlers. Inspired by the strength and resilience of the Blue Ridge Mountains, this distinctive pattern pays tribute to the area's Scottish ancestors who, in the 18th century, brought their traditions and values to the New World. The registration notes highlight the tartan's significance as an educational tool, educating those about the preservation of cultural aspects of the original Scottish and Scots-Irish settlers. Available for use by members of the Scottish Foundation of the Virginia Highlands, this tartan also holds appeal for others who appreciate its unique blend of traditional Scottish craftsmanship and American roots.

name: Scottish Funereal Association
description: The Scottish Funereal Association tartan is a striking yet sombre corporate pattern, carefully crafted by the esteemed designers at Lochcarron of Scotland in 1996. As a Category Corporate design, it was created for use in business settings, evoking professionalism and respect. Despite its association with funerals, this tartan is not intended to be morbid or mournful, but rather serves as a dignified tribute to the deceased. With its subtle nuances of blue and green hues, reminiscent of Scotland's misty hills and heather-covered moors, this tartan embodies the nation's stoic resilience in the face of loss. The registration notes provide insight into its technical characteristics, but it is the cultural significance that truly sets this design apart - a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich heritage and tradition.

name:
Scottish Gas
[AKA] William Murdoch
description: The Scottish Gas tartan, created by Robert Williamson Hill in 1985 with the assistance of his daughter Lesley, is a distinctive corporate tartan that pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage. Based on the iconic Black Watch sett, this tartan was initially inspired by William Murdoch, one of the pioneers of gas lighting, and later adopted by Scottish Gas for its staff and pipe band. Characterised by colours derived from the company's flame logo, this tartan reflects the fusion of tradition and innovation that defines Scotland's history. As a corporate tartan, it is designed to represent Scottish Gas's values and identity, yet the subtle nuances of its sett and colour palette remain rooted in Scotland's storied textile traditions. While permission from Scottish Gas is required to access threadcount details, this tartan serves as a powerful emblem of the company's connection to its Scottish roots.

name: Scottish Heather
description: The Scottish Heather tartan, with its soft and subtle nuances, embodies the rugged yet elegant spirit of Scotland's rolling hills and heather-covered moors. Registration notes reveal that this fashion tartan was meticulously designed by ER for Houston Kiltmakers of Paisley, drawing inspiration from the natural beauty of the country's iconic heather blooms. A staple in any traditional Scottish wardrobe, this tartan is also synonymous with a sense of style and sophistication, making it a popular choice for designers like House of Edgar to feature in their collections. With its restrictions largely focused on formal occasions, the Scottish Heather tartan remains an enduring tribute to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, evoking images of crisp Highland air, rustic landscapes, and timeless tradition.

name:
Scottish Heritage USA
[AKA] SHUSA
description: The Scottish Heritage USA (SHUSA) tartan is a vibrant corporate design that embodies the spirit of innovation and tradition that defines modern Scotland. Registered by Philip D Smith, a renowned Scottish textile expert, in 2000, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the country's rich heritage while embracing its cosmopolitan appeal. With roots firmly planted in the Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority, SHUSA tartan draws inspiration from the country's storied past, yet maintains a contemporary edge that makes it instantly versatile for corporate wear and branding. By wearing this tartan, individuals not only pay tribute to Scotland's timeless traditions but also signal their commitment to a shared sense of honour, heritage, and civic pride – making SHUSA a fitting choice for those who wish to celebrate their Scottish roots while forging their own path forward.

name: Scottish Highlander
description: The Scottish Highlander Dress tartan is a vibrant and striking fabric, born from the rich heritage of Scotland's Highlanders. Designed by House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this fashion tartan combines the traditional Grampian tartan with bold additions of Maroon and Lavender, evoking the majestic beauty of the Scottish wild heather and thistles. Its origins lie in a collaboration between Gavin Kiltmakers & Dress Hire of Fraserburgh and the House of Edgar, with the aim of creating a unique and eye-catching kilt hire range. This tartan is a testament to Scotland's enduring cultural identity, reflecting the country's deep-rooted traditions and values. With its restrictions in place, allowing only authorized kiltmakers to manufacture garments bearing this distinctive design, it remains a coveted choice for those seeking to connect with the history and symbolism of Scotland's proud Highland heritage.

name: Scottish Hockey Union
description: The Scottish Hockey Union tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate design that embodies the spirit of Scotland's national pastime, while also reflecting its rich cultural heritage. Registered by Lochcarron of Scotland, this distinctive pattern was created to represent the values and traditions of Scotland's hockey community. As a corporate tartan, it is intended for wear by individuals associated with the sport, from players to officials, as well as organisations such as clubs and leagues. While the registration notes highlight some technical considerations, the tartan itself remains an enduring symbol of Scottish identity and sporting excellence, woven from the very fabric of the nation's rich cultural tapestry.

name: Scottish Institute of Sport
description: This distinctive Corporate Tartan, designed by David McGill, embodies the spirit of Scotland's thriving sporting sector, reflecting the Institute of Sport's commitment to excellence in high-performance sports. Established in 1998, the Scottish Institute of Sport has become a cornerstone of Scotland's sporting heritage, and this tartan is a proud symbol of its legacy. Although specific details about the rationale behind its design are not recorded, it is clear that McGill's creation is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition, blending bold colours to evoke a sense of energy, competition, and community. As a Corporate Tartan, it is intended for use by organisations and individuals associated with the Institute of Sport, providing a visual identity that is both authentic and professional. The subtle variations in sett showcased on McGill's website add depth and nuance to this striking design, ensuring that the Scottish Institute of Sport tartan remains a powerful representation of Scotland's sporting prowess.

name: Scottish Islamic
description: The Scottish Islamic Tartan is a groundbreaking corporate design that beautifully weaves together Scotland's rich heritage with the spiritual traditions of Islam, symbolising unity and inclusivity for the modern era. Registered by DC Dalgliesh Ltd, this unique tartan is the result of a collaborative effort between esteemed Islamic scholars and Scottish academic Dr Azeem Ibrahim, who drew upon the expertise of Shaikh Humza Yousaf, Imam Zaid Shakir, Dr Umar Abd-Allah, and Shaikh Amer Jamil to create a striking pattern that reflects the five pillars of Islam and the six articles of faith. The tartan's colour palette - with the Scottish flag blue, Islamic green, and gold representing the six articles of faith - serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's historical connections to the Muslim world, while the black square at its centre nods respectfully to the revered Holy Kabah in Mecca. By bringing together two ancient traditions, this tartan design embodies the values of mutual respect and understanding that are at the heart of Scotland's Islamic heritage.

name: Scottish Lion
description: The Euphoria tartan, designed by Graham Robieson of Dunfermline, is a vibrant and uplifting fashion tartan that embodies the concept of joy and relief. With its colours inspired by the iconic packaging of Barr's Diet Irn-Bru, this unique tartan captures the essence of happiness in a bottle, evoking feelings of euphoria. As a universal design, Euphoria is meant to be inclusive, transcending clan or family affiliations, instead embracing a broader sense of personality and style. With no specific clan or heritage tied to its origins, Euphoria is perfect for those seeking a fashion statement that's both bold and joyful, free from the traditional restrictions of Scottish tartan registration.

name: Scottish Monuments
description: The Racing Stewart (Stealth) tartan, designed by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, is a striking corporate motif inspired by the storied heritage of Sir Jackie Stewart's racing legacy. Initially created for Paul Stewart, son of the World Champion racing driver, as a bespoke tartan for his family's Scottish Motor Racing company, "Stewart Grand Prix". This contemporary take on the classic Racing Stewart tartan (STR #3940) boasts darker colours, evoking the intense competition and adrenaline-fueled spirit of motor racing. The corporate category designation reflects its intended use, while the restrictions clause underscores the intimate connection with Sir Jackie's family line. A testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage and tradition, this tartan is a unique expression of Paul Stewart's connection to his illustrious father's achievements in motorsport, now imbued with personal significance for his own esteemed legacy.

name:
Scottish Motor Trade Association
[AKA] SMTA
description: This striking corporate tartan, designed by Fiona J H Blunsdon, pays homage to Scotland's rich motor trade heritage through its creation for the Scottish Motor Trade Association established in 1903. As a testament to the nation's industrial prowess, this distinctive tartan reflects the industry's contributions to the country's economic growth and reputation. The registration notes clarify that, although differing from the Society of Scottish Tartans' threadcount, the design correctly captures the first pivot as dark blue (G/12) rather than its initially recorded hue. This tartan, now recognised by both societies, serves as a lasting symbol of unity and tradition within Scotland's esteemed motor trade sector, where innovation and progress have long been valued alongside heritage and culture.

name: Scottish National Dress
description: The Scottish National Dress tartan is a storied fabric that embodies the very essence of Scotland's rich cultural heritage. Inspired by the original 1934 'Scottish National' design, Scott Millsom's 1994 iteration pays homage to the country's proud tradition of textile craftsmanship. This Fashion category tartan was registered as a patented design in 1994 and has since become an iconic representation of Scottish national identity. Woven with reverence for the nation's history and heritage, the Scottish National Dress tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's iconic tartans, with its subtle nods to the original design, carefully reimagined by Millsom to evoke the very spirit of the Scottish nation.

name: Scottish National
description: The Scottish National tartan, created by Michael King, is a stylish and timeless fashion choice that embodies the spirit of Scotland's national identity. Originally designed for the Scottish National Party, this tartan has been separated from its political affiliation and now stands on its own as a vibrant representation of Scottish heritage. With its unique sett proportions reminiscent of the 1934 Scottish Woollen Manufacturers Association's National Tartan, this design pays homage to the country's rich textile history while also being distinctly modern. Recorded by the esteemed Scottish Tartans Society in 1994, the Scottish National tartan is a testament to Scotland's enduring cultural significance, making it an ideal choice for those seeking a fashion statement that proudly wears its national colours on its sleeve.

name: Scottish Netball 1987
description: The Scottish Netball Association tartan, registered in 1987, is a vibrant corporate design that pays homage to Scotland's rich sporting heritage. Woven with purpose by Clan Weaving Mill in Hamilton, under the guidance of renowned designer Peter MacArthur, this unique tartan was specifically created for the World Netball Championship held in Glasgow that year. Its colours - predominantly blue and red with touches of white - evoke a sense of energetic dynamism, while its striped pattern recalls traditional Scottish textiles. Originally worn by Scotland's netball team on their international tour of Australia, this tartan now proudly represents the country's sporting endeavour and corporate identity, forever linked to the iconic Glasgow event that brought the world's best netball teams together.

name: Scottish North American Business Council #2
description: The Scottish North American Business Council tartan is a symbol of unity and affiliation between Scotland's rich heritage and the business community of North America, reflecting the growing ties between these two nations. Designed by renowned textile expert Lochcarron of Scotland, this corporate tartan was carefully crafted for the Scottish North American Business Council, a organisation dedicated to fostering economic growth and cultural exchange between its members. The registration notes reveal that this unique design is a culmination of two concepts, showcasing Lochcarron's skill in blending traditional Scottish tartanry with innovative flair. As a Corporate tartan, it holds great significance for businesses and individuals seeking to pay homage to their Scottish roots while embracing the modern world, and its distinctive pattern tells a story of heritage, community, and progress.

name: Scottish Nuclear
description: The Scottish Nuclear tartan is a striking corporate design that pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage while reflecting its unique energy sector credentials. Registered by Adrian Wilson, Director of Marton Mills, Yorkshire for staff at Torness and Hunterston Power Stations, this tartan represents the fusion of traditional Scottish symbolism with modern industrial values. As a Corporate tartan, it is intended for use in work environments, fostering a sense of pride and identity among those who wear it. The registration notes reveal that this design was born from the collaboration between Adrian Wilson and his team, reflecting the importance of staff and their families at these pioneering power stations. This tartan embodies the blend of innovation and tradition that defines Scotland's nuclear industry, its vibrant colours and intricate patterns evoking a sense of strength, resilience, and national pride.

name: Scottish Odyssey
description: The Scottish Odyssey tartan, expertly woven by Lochcarron of Scotland, is a vibrant tribute to the enchanting experiences waiting to be discovered in Scotland's breathtaking landscapes. This commemorative tartan celebrates the country's most stunning contrasts, from rugged mountains to serene lochs, and evokes a sense of adventure and wonder that lingers long after the journey has ended. As one of Lochcarron's Commemorative tartans, it was registered to mark a significant event or milestone, perhaps a historic anniversary, a remarkable achievement, or a cherished memory. With its bold colours and intricate patterns, this tartan invites wearers to reconnect with Scotland's rich heritage and the sense of pride that comes from honouring a special occasion or moment in time.

name: Scottish Parliament Commemorative
description: The Scottish Parliament tartan, designed by Ronnie Hek in 1998, is a vibrant and symbolic fashion tartan that pays tribute to Scotland's resurgence as an independent nation. As an unofficial yet officially sanctioned design, it embodies the country's renewed sense of pride and identity. Sanctioned by the Scottish Tartans Society, this tartan was created to commemorate the Referendum result and serve as a Parliamentary livery, marking the re-establishment of a Scottish Parliament in 1998. Weaving together elements of tradition and modernity, the Scottish Parliament tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and its people's enduring connection to their nation. With Registration No: 0602797 under the 1988 Design Act, this tartan design adds a touch of colour and significance to any garment or textile, serving as a badge of honour for those who cherish Scottish culture and identity.

name: Scottish Piping Society of London
description: The German tartan, designed by renowned weaver David McGill, is a vibrant and distinctive pattern steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered specifically for German people worldwide and those who associate themselves with Germany, this tartan design embodies a sense of national pride and identity. As a District tartan, it is closely tied to the cultural and historical ties between Scotland and Germany, reflecting the shared values and customs that have developed over centuries. With its unique colour palette and subtle texture, the German tartan is a bold statement of connection to one's roots, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to honour their heritage or express their love of German culture through traditional Scottish tartan.

name: Scottish Power
description: The Scottish Power tartan is a modern, dynamic design that embodies the energy and vitality of Scotland's largest energy company. Created by Kinloch Anderson Ltd for corporate use, this tartan was specifically developed to reflect Scottish Power's brand identity and colours. With its bold, rich hues, this tartan is steeped in traditional Scottish heritage yet distinctly contemporary in its approach. As a Category Corporate design, it is intended for business and professional use, conveying professionalism and authority. However, due to the company's strict ownership of the design, permission must be sought from Scottish Power Corporate Communications before use. Nevertheless, this tartan remains an intriguing representation of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, evoking the country's proud industrial heritage and its enduring spirit of innovation.

name: Scottish Pride
description: The Scottish Pride tartan is a vibrant and dynamic fashion tartan, born from the desire to embody the unwavering spirit of Scotland's heritage. This commercially available design, though not officially registered with The Tartans Authority (previously known as The Scottish Register of Tartans), has been unearthed on the online platform www.tartanstore.net, a testament to the enduring passion for Scottish textiles. Characterised by its striking colour palette and precise threadcount, this tartan is believed to feature 8 threads per inch, with a predominantly blue and green scheme that echoes Scotland's natural landscapes. Though its origins remain a mystery, the Scottish Pride tartan is undoubtedly an authentic representation of Scotland's rich cultural legacy, waiting to be worn with pride by those who cherish the country's history and traditions.

name: Scottish Prison Service
description: The Scottish Prison Service tartan is a unique and significant corporate colourway, proudly representing a vital part of Scotland's correctional system. Registered in 2005, this distinctive tartan was woven by Ingles Buchan, an esteemed Scottish weaver, for the Scottish Prison Service to signify its identity and professionalism within the nation's justice sector. As a corporate tartan, it is designed to promote unity and cohesion among staff working in prisons across Scotland, while also paying homage to the country's rich heritage of weaving and textile tradition. By wearing this distinctive tartan, members of the Scottish Prison Service demonstrate their honour and commitment to their role, connecting them with a long history of service and dedication that spans centuries.

name: Scottish Pup
description: This charming Fashion tartan, aptly named Scottish Pup, is a heartwarming tribute to Paul and Susie's beloved canine companion, Hannah. Designed with an outdoorsy flair inspired by her Washington State surroundings, the tartan weaves together a palette of natural hues that reflect the region's distinctive character. Earthy browns evoke the sturdy tree trunks and pine cones that dot the landscape, while vibrant greens pay homage to the state's nickname, the Evergreen State. Blues represent the ocean, lakes, and streams that flow through the territory, interspersed with sunny yellows that nod to Washington's iconic state bird, the Goldfinch. This endearing tartan is not just a fashion statement, but a celebration of the special bond between humans and their furry friends – an honour bestowed upon those who understand and appreciate this unique connection.

name: Scottish Qualifications Authority
description: The Scottish Qualifications Authority tartan is a distinctive and sophisticated corporate design, born from the partnership between House of Edgar's Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. and the talented weaver Polly Wittering. This unique tartan was registered to reflect the organisation's commitment to academic excellence and professional development, serving as a symbol of the nation's rich educational heritage. As a Corporate tartan, it is designed for use in business settings, such as formal wear, stationery, or branding, and its formal tone makes it suitable for a wide range of formal occasions. The subtle nuances of this tartan are deeply rooted in Scotland's cultural traditions, drawing upon the country's storied history of scholarship and intellectual pursuits, and is sure to add a touch of dignity and authority to any corporate event or gathering.

name:
Scottish Scouts 1922
[AKA] Grey Watch Dress
description: The Scottish Scouts tartan, registered in 1922, is a storied corporate design born from the Scout Association of Scotland's desire to provide a uniform tartan for its members. Created by Chief Commissioner Lord Glentanar, this distinctive pattern weaves together three shades of grey, reminiscent of the Black Watch, to evoke the spirit of scouting's rich heritage. Originally intended as a utilitarian solution for Scouts without their own tartan or requiring a uniform, it has since become a symbol of camaraderie and shared values within the Scout community. Though not widely adopted during its initial release, a variation with white instead of light grey gained popularity in the 1989 'Dress Grey Watch' iteration, demonstrating the enduring appeal of this tartan to those who wear it with honour.

name: Scottish Scouts
description: The Scottish Scouts #2 tartan is a vibrant and symbolic corporate tartan, created to honour the generosity of a benefactor who gifted an estate to the scouts. Based on the MacLaren tartan, it features a distinctive red overcheck that represents the Rover Scouts, with finer, more subdued lines denoting the younger Scout and Senior Scout divisions. The warm yellow thread adds a touch of youthful energy, representing the Wolf Cubs. This tartan was designed by A.G. Porteus or J. Porteus of Alva, and its creation pays tribute to the significant contribution made by this benefactor to the scouting movement. As a corporate tartan, it is suitable for use by organisations that value community service and youth development, while still proudly bearing the heritage and spirit of Scotland's beloved scouts.

name: Scottish Tartan Society
description: The Scottish Tartan Society is a distinctive Corporate tartan, showcasing a vibrant blend of blues and greens that evoke the rolling hills and sparkling lochs of Scotland's majestic landscapes. Registered by renowned designer D.C. Dalgliesh, this tartan is steeped in tradition and heritage, reflecting the country's rich cultural fabric. As a corporate identity, it offers a bold and eye-catching way to represent Scottish values and pride. However, its creation is subject to specific restrictions, with the original pattern prepared exclusively for weaving by D.C. Dalgliesh Ltd. This nod to the designer's expertise highlights the importance of authenticity in tartan design. With its striking colour palette and historical significance, the Scottish Tartan Society is an ideal choice for businesses seeking to tap into Scotland's enduring cultural legacy.

name: Scottish Thistle
description: The Scottish Thistle corporate tartan, designed by renowned textile artist Kirsty Anderson, embodies the resilient spirit of Scotland's national emblem, the thistle. This vibrant and distinctive tartan is specifically registered for David Divine's DA Formal Wear brand, symbolising his commitment to authenticity and heritage. As a Corporate tartan, it boasts a wider appeal, making it suitable for a range of business and formal occasions. With its bold colours and precise sett, this tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich cultural heritage while exuding modern style and sophistication. Its unique design tells the story of Kirsty Anderson's skillful craftsmanship and attention to detail, ensuring that DA Formal Wear customers make a statement with every event.

name: Scottish Tourist Board 1981
description: The Scottish Tourist Board tartan, designed by Peter MacDonald in 1981, is a vibrant and iconic corporate design that proudly showcases Scotland's rich heritage. Based on the revered Black Watch, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the storied tradition of the Scottish regiments, whose bold and rugged spirit has long been synonymous with the country's proud history. With restrictions in place to ensure its respectful use, this tartan is reserved for official and approved corporate wear, ensuring that the image of Scotland remains a cherished asset, rather than a generic marketing tool. As a registered design, it is now an integral part of Scottish cultural identity, proudly displayed on everything from uniforms to branding materials, serving as a potent symbol of national pride and hospitality, inviting visitors from around the world to experience the warmth and beauty of Scotland.

name: Scottish Tourist Board 1990
description: The Scottish Tourist Board (1990) tartan, created by esteemed designers at Kinloch Anderson Ltd, embodies the vibrant spirit of Scotland's iconic tourism industry. As a corporate tartan, it was designed to proudly represent the country's hospitality sector, reflecting the warmth and welcome that tourists associate with visiting Scotland. Characterised by its bold colour scheme featuring navy, white, and blue hues reminiscent of Scotland's majestic landscapes and waters, this tartan is a testament to the nation's enduring appeal. Despite being restricted for commercial use, this tartan remains an attractive option for businesses seeking to tap into Scotland's rich cultural heritage and showcase their connection to the country.

name: Scottish Watch
description: The Scottish Watch tartan is a striking corporate design born from the vision of Lt Col W.M., Ritchie, former occupant of Glenborrowdale Castle, with the aim of promoting Scottish culture to a wider audience. This distinctive tartan was specifically created for those without an established connection to a Clan or Scottish Society, offering a unique opportunity for individuals and businesses to embody their pride in Scotland's heritage. With its bold colour palette and carefully considered sett, the Scottish Watch tartan evokes the steadfastness and timelessness of Scotland's watchful eyes on its rich cultural legacy, while also providing a modern and versatile visual identity that can be worn with honour by those who wear it.

name: Scotts Valley
description: The Scotts Valley corporate tartan is a sophisticated and modern interpretation of traditional Scottish heritage, expertly woven to reflect the values of innovation and progress in the workplace. Designed by Dalgliesh, D C, a renowned textile expert, this tartan pattern was specifically created for corporate wear, evoking a sense of professionalism and authority. With its striking combination of blues and greens, the Scotts Valley tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich cultural traditions while embracing the forward-thinking ethos of modern business. Notably, its registration notes reveal that careful consideration has been given to the design's technical specifications, prepared with precision by Dalgliesh Ltd for weaving into fabric that exudes excellence and distinction.

name: Scout Mapping Service #1
description: The Scout Mapping Service tartan, a unique Corporate motif, pays homage to the pioneering spirit of scouting organisations in Scotland. Approved by the Scottish Tartans Society on 18th April 1979, this distinctive pattern reflects the values of exploration, navigation, and adventure embodied by scouting groups. Characterised by its bold, graphic design, the tartan's blue and green hues evoke the great outdoors, with subtle checks and stripes evoking maps and compasses. As a Corporate tartan, it is intended for use in business and institutional settings, where its adventurous flair can inspire a sense of teamwork and expeditionary spirit. While not associated with a specific Clan or family heritage, this tartan design embodies the values of exploration and camaraderie that have come to define scouting organisations across Scotland.

name: Scout Mapping Service #2
description: The Scout Mapping Service #2 tartan is a stalwart symbol of corporate heritage, steeped in tradition and history. As one of twoMapping Service designs registered by the Scottish Tartans Society, this tartan pays homage to the pioneering spirit of mapping and exploration that defined Scotland's rich cultural landscape. Originally inspired by the Maclaren tartan, with its distinctive sett modified to include an additional red line slicing through the blue and green hues, this corporate tartan has been carefully crafted to evoke a sense of adventure and navigation. With two shades of green used inwards and outwards of the red line on the blue field, the subtle interplay between these colours creates a visually striking design that is as functional as it is evocative of Scotland's storied past, serving as a proud emblem for any organisation or individual drawn to its bold and distinctive character.

name: Scozia
description: The Scozia tartan, created in collaboration with Lochcarron of Scotland, is a unique and distinctive fashion tartan that pays homage to Italy's vibrant colours and Scotland's proud heritage. As its name suggests, this tartan claims to be the world's first designed specifically for Scots Italians, cleverly fusing the azure blue of Italian national flags with the navy blue of Scotland's iconic rugby shirt. Exclusive to Anderson Kilts of Dumfries, Scozia is a testament to the intersection of cultures and traditions. Its blend of bold colours evokes the passion and flair of Italy's sporting teams, while its roots in Scottish heritage ensure it remains an authentic representation of Highland craftsmanship, inviting wearers to proudly celebrate their mixed heritage.

name:
Scrimgeour of Glassary [default]
[AKA] Scrimgeour of Glassary
description: Heritage #2 is a commemorative tartan designed by renowned textile experts F & M Lawson at Crofter's Weaving Mill, specifically created to mark the bicentenary celebrations in Australia in 1988. This unique tartan embodies the rich cultural heritage and shared history of Scotland and its former colonies, showcasing a vibrant blend of colours that pay homage to the nation's enduring legacy. As a Commemorative tartan, Heritage #2 holds significant sentimental value for those who have ancestral ties to Scotland or Australia, serving as a poignant reminder of the country's connection to the past. While restrictions may apply to its use in certain contexts, this majestic tartan is an integral part of Australia's cultural identity, honouring the shared heritage of two nations and their enduring bond.

name:
Scrymgeour [default]
[AKA] Scrymgeour Scrimgeour
description: The Scrymgeour tartan is a majestic representation of the proud heritage of its eponymous clan family. Registration notes reveal that this distinctive pattern was first created in 1971 by renowned Scottish tartan designer, Trudi Mann, under the expert guidance of esteemed authority on Scottish tartans, D.C. Stewart. As an Hereditary Standard Bearer, the Scrymgeour tartan is steeped in tradition and carries significant historical weight, its design reflecting the storied history of its bearers. With this clan tartan, families can proudly showcase their lineage and connection to Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, while Mann's masterful weave breathes new life into the intricate traditions of Scottish heritage.

name: Seaforth Estate Check
description: The Seaforth Estate Check tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's District tartans, born from the traditions of the country's storied past. Registration notes reveal little about its origins, but a swatch in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection hints at its significance. As a District tartan, it is deeply rooted in the history and identity of a specific geographic region, in this case, the Seaforth Estate. The subtle check pattern imbues the design with a sense of rustic charm, evoking images of rolling hills and windswept coastlines. Major Peter G. Stone's creation is a tribute to the timeless beauty of Scotland's natural landscape and its people, who have woven their stories into the fabric of this unique tartan.

name: Seaside
description: The Seaside tartan, registered by West Coast Woolen Mill as a fashion design, embodies the carefree spirit of Scotland's rugged coastline. This striking pattern, now immortalised in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Dalgety Collection, is a testament to the nation's rich textile heritage. Characterised by its predominantly blue and green hues, reminiscent of a misty dawn or a gentle sea breeze, the Seaside tartan exudes a sense of relaxed elegance. Originally designed for fashion purposes, it would be perfect for creating statement pieces such as scarves, coats, or dresses that evoke the beauty and tranquillity of Scotland's scenic shores. By embracing this unique design, you can add a touch of Scottish flair to your wardrobe while celebrating the country's enduring love affair with the sea.

name: Seattle District
description: The Seattle tartan, designed by Mrs Tomoko Edwards, is a vibrant tribute to the Emerald City's natural beauty. As a District tartan, it reflects the unique character of its geographical area, with each colour carefully chosen to evoke the region's distinct charm. The palette is reminiscent of a misty morning in the Pacific Northwest: emerald green for the city itself, Aegean blue evoking the waters that surround it, primrose pink - although some threads may substitute red - capturing the wild rhododendrons that thrive in the area, snowy white symbolising the majestic mountain ranges, and golden yellow representing the warmth of summer sunshine. This distinctive tartan design not only pays homage to Seattle's natural splendour but also serves as a testament to the ingenuity of its creator, Mrs Edwards.

name: Sekai Fushigi Hakken
description: Sekai Fushigi Hakken, meaning "The Discovery of the World's Mysteries" in Japanese, is a captivating Corporate tartan designed by renowned weaver D.C. Dalgliesh in 2001. Commissioned specifically for the television programme 'Discovery of the World's Mysteries', this unique tartan was created to illustrate the intricate weaving process, bringing together traditional Scottish craftsmanship with modern storytelling. As a testament to Japan's cultural exchange with Scotland, Sekai Fushigi Hakken seamlessly blends Japanese aesthetics with the rich heritage of tartan design, reflecting the country's fascination with global mysteries and the discovery of new ideas. Although its primary purpose was educational, this intriguing tartan has taken on a life of its own, showcasing the versatility and creative potential of corporate tartans in modern business attire.

name: Selby
description: The Selby tartan is a storied Name tartan born from the rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands, specifically the Southern Estates of the Duke of Sutherland. Inspired by the timeless elegance of the Sutherland Old tartan and the soft light green hues of the Hunting Ross, this distinctive design tells the story of Dr Selby's childhood fascination with these iconic tartans. As a child, the designer was graciously permitted to walk on the estates and wear the Sutherland Old tartan by none other than the Duchess herself, an honour that would later inform his creation of the Selby tartan. This Name tartan is now freely available for anyone to wear, allowing its wearers to connect with a piece of Scotland's storied past while embracing their own unique identity.

name: Seletar Elliot
description: The Seletar tartan is a striking corporate motif born from the branding of Seletar Shipping (Scotland) Ltd, a company deeply rooted in Scotland's maritime heritage. Weaved by the skilled hands of House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this tartan tells the story of a proud and storied legacy. Its utilitarian origins shine through in its functional use as curtains, carpets, uniforms, and gifts, underscoring the design's role in representing the company's honourable values and commitment to tradition. With its carefully considered palette of colours inspired by the Seletar Shipping logo, this tartan embodies a sense of British enterprise and sophistication, a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish industry and entrepreneurship.

name:
Selkirk #2
[AKA] No.217
description: The Milne dress green tartan is a rich and storied heritage pattern, woven with pride by Marton Mills from Otley, West Yorkshire. Belonging to the esteemed Clan Milne, this traditional tartan has been passed down through generations, its distinctive green hue evoking the rolling hills and lush landscapes of Scotland's picturesque countryside. As a family tartan, the Milne dress green holds deep significance for those who bear the Milne name, serving as a tangible connection to their ancestral heritage. With no restrictions on use, this beautiful tartan is free to be worn with honour by anyone fortunate enough to carry it, adding a touch of Scotland's storied past to their daily life.

name: Selkirk District
description: The majestic Selkirk tartan embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's storied towns, evoking the proud history of Selkirk itself. Registered by renowned designer Andrew Elliot in 1996, this District tartan is deeply rooted in the local tradition, featuring seven colours that pay homage to the town's distinct character. As part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's esteemed Johnston Collection, the sample has been carefully preserved for posterity, serving as a tangible connection to Selkirk's storied past. With its intricate weave and symbolic colour palette, this tartan design not only celebrates the town's identity but also pays tribute to the skilled weavers who have passed down their expertise through generations.

name: Selkirk High School
description: The Selkirk High School tartan is a vibrant and spirited creation that embodies the proud heritage of Scotland's esteemed educational institution. Originally designed by Lochcarron of Scotland in collaboration with the pupils themselves, this Corporate tartan weaves together the rich colours of the school tie to create a unique and distinctive pattern. As an official corporate tartan, it holds significance for organisations and individuals connected to Selkirk High School, serving as a badge of honour that celebrates the school's values and traditions. With its origins rooted in Scottish tradition and history, this tartan design is not only a tribute to the school's legacy but also a testament to the enduring spirit of young minds shaped within its walls.

name: Seller #2
description: The Seller tartan, a personal family legacy rooted in the storied connections of Mr D Sillers to the Isle of Arran and the esteemed Clan Stewart, is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage. This distinctive clan tartan, registered with the Scottish Tartans Society, is steeped in tradition and history, its bold colours evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. The design, crafted by Mr D Sillers himself, draws upon the island's natural landscapes and the Clan Stewart's storied past, reflecting a deep sense of family honour and cultural pride. As such, this tartan is reserved for the Siller clan and their immediate descendants, serving as a poignant reminder of the enduring bond between Scotland's clans and their ancestral lands.

name: Seller Dress
description: The Seller tartan, a family heirloom of unparalleled significance, is steeped in the rich history and heritage of the Isle of Arran and the esteemed Clan Stewart. This reproduction dress tartan, registered in 1978, is a faithful recreation of the original Siller's connection to the island, as well as the Clan Stewart's heritage from 1978. Crafted with meticulous attention to detail by D.C Dalgliesh, a respected weaving firm in Selkirk, this tartan celebrates the strong bonds between generations and the ancestral ties that weave together the fabric of Scottish clan life. As a testament to the enduring traditions of Scottish family and heritage, the Seller tartan invites wearers to don the mantle of their forebears, embracing the timeless stories and symbols etched into its intricate threads.

name: Seller Dress #2
description: The Seller Dress tartan, as registered in 1897 by esteemed designer Dalgliesh, D C, weaves together the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's storied past with the enduring allure of fashion. Inspired by the Sillers connection to the Isle of Arran and the proud legacy of Clan Stewart, this intricate design tells a tale of tradition and belonging. The tartan's creation is deeply rooted in Scottish heritage, evoking images of heather-covered moors and windswept coastlines, while its application in fashion represents a modern interpretation of timeless elegance. Notable restrictions, including preparation for weaving by the designer's own company, ensure that this unique design remains true to its origins, preserving the artistic integrity of Dalgliesh's vision for generations to come.

name: Seller [default]
description: The Sellers/Sillars tartan, designed by Mr D Sillers, embodies the rich heritage of Scotland's clans and family ties. This traditional tartan weaves together the storied connections between the Sillars clan and the Isle of Arran, with its associations to the Clan Stewart. With its specific registration notes hinting at a deep rooted history, this tartan is not only a testament to Scotland's cultural identity but also a tangible link to the past. As a Category Clan/Family tartan, it proudly wears its heritage on its sleeve, paying homage to the Sillars family's ancestry and their place within the broader Scottish clan landscape.

name: Sempill [default]
description: The Sempill tartan is a rich and storied woven fabric, steeped in Scottish heritage and clan history. Registered as part of the Clan/Family category, this distinctive sett is a testament to the enduring legacy of Lord Sempill, Chief of the Sempills, who meticulously recorded its threadcount in the Lyon Court Books. The similarity between this tartan and that of the Forbes clan is no coincidence, reflecting the historical connections and interweaving traditions of these two clans. This intricate design is a celebration of Scottish tradition and the enduring honour of the Sempill name, woven with precision and care to evoke the proud history and cultural significance of the region.

name: Semple [default]
description: The Semple tartan is a proud embodiment of Scottish heritage and identity, woven with meticulous care by Iain Semple himself. As a family tartan, it holds dear significance for those of the name Semple, serving as a symbol of kinship and belonging. Originally designed in collaboration with Clan Chief Lord Semple, this intricate design pays homage to the rich history and traditions of the Sempill clan, whose roots stretch back through generations. With its striking colours and distinctive pattern, the Semple tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish culture, passed down through the ages from one family to the next. While it bears some resemblance to another tartan design, the Semple is unmistakably its own unique expression, imbued with the love and legacy of its creator and the Sempill clan's proud heritage.

name: Serenade
description: The Serenade tartan, designed by Aljean of Vancouver, is a captivating fashion choice that embodies the timeless elegance of Scottish heritage. This stunning tartan is categorised as a Fashion tartan, suggesting its versatility and suitability for a wide range of garments and accessories. Its distinctive pattern, registered in Scotland's esteemed Johnston Collection, evokes the soothing melodies and poetic rhythms of a night serenade. As a fashion tartan, Serenade is free from restrictions, allowing it to be freely woven into a variety of clothing items, from scarves to kilts. With its sophisticated colour palette and intricate design, this tartan is sure to add a touch of Scottish sophistication to any outfit, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to incorporate the beauty and tradition of Scottish textiles into their everyday style.

name: Service
description: The Service of Drymen tartan is a personal, Name category design steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. This unique and complex pattern has been meticulously crafted from existing sources, including the MacKinlay strip from the Anderson Collection in Edinburgh. First checked by the Scottish Register Office in May 2002, its authenticity was further verified by two esteemed experts, M.O.McD and D McGregor-Hastie, adding credibility to its provenance. As a Name tartan, the Service of Drymen has been designated for use by individuals, serving as a tangible connection to their personal history and heritage. With its distinctive character and rich cultural significance, this tartan design is sure to be cherished by those who bear it, their honour tied to the traditions and stories that underpin Scotland's unique fabric.

name: Seton Hunting
description: The Seton Hunting tartan is a storied and ancient Scottish design, steeped in tradition and heritage. With its roots firmly rooted in the Vestiarium Scoticum, this iconic pattern has been woven with precision and care for generations. The subtle nuances and intricate details reveal a rich history, evoking the rugged landscapes and hunting traditions of Scotland's noble families. Dating back to the early 20th century, this tartan was allegedly first recorded by James Cant, a respected authority on Scottish tartans in the 1930s. Although its exact origins are shrouded in mystery, its association with the Johnston Collection and the Tartans Society lends weight to its authenticity. With no restrictions placed upon it, the Seton Hunting tartan remains an integral part of Scotland's cultural fabric, proudly worn by families and clans to celebrate their heritage and affinity for this timeless, hunting-inspired design.

name: Seton [default]
description: The Seton tartan, registered under the Scottish Tartans Society, holds a rich history within Scotland's clan heritage. Described as Innes No 102, this tartan was associated with the Seton family, whose early connections with the House of Gordon are well-documented. The design, named after its esteemed patrons, is now a symbol of family and clan pride, reflecting the intricate relationships between Scottish clans throughout the centuries. Sobieski Stewarts, The, played a significant role in preserving this tartan's legacy through their VS Plate No.55, which sheds light on the Seton family's historical significance within Scotland's noble lineage. With its distinctive pattern and storied past, the Seton tartan remains an important part of Scottish heritage, evoking a sense of honour and tradition that continues to captivate those drawn to its timeless beauty.

name: Setting Sun
description: Ben Dubh, meaning 'The Black Mount' in Gaelic, is a timeless fashion tartan that embodies the rugged beauty of Scotland's wilderness. Originally woven by Marton Mills, its registration notes reveal a masterful blend of two shades of black, expertly combined through traditional weaving techniques to create a striking visual effect. While the exact hues may be somewhat subjective, the essence of this tartan remains firmly rooted in Scottish heritage and tradition. As a fashion design, Ben Dubh exudes sophistication and elegance, its dark tones evoking the dramatic landscapes of the Scottish Highlands. This sophisticated tartan is sure to make a statement, perfect for those who appreciate the nuances of traditional Scottish textiles and desire a timeless piece that honours the country's rich cultural legacy.

name: Sey [default]
description: The Sey tartan is a unique and personal design created by Allen Victor Sey, reflecting his distinctive heritage and style. This Name tartan is categorised as a personal signature pattern, signifying its exclusive connection to the individual who wears it. With intricate guardlines adding a touch of vibrancy, the Sey tartan draws inspiration from the traditional Brodie Hunting tartan, yet uniquely incorporates orange hues into the classic red pivot on the blue, paying homage to this Scottish icon while showcasing the wearer's individual flair. As such, the Sey tartan serves as a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland, with its subtle nuances and distinctive colour palette evoking a sense of pride and connection to the country's storied past.

name: SFA Scottish Football Association
description: The Scottish Football Association tartan is an iconic corporate design, synonymous with the nation's beloved national team. Originally woven by Lochcarron in 2003, specifically for the SFA, this distinctive tartan has become a symbol of Scottish football pride. The subtle, muted tones and carefully balanced colours evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's landscapes and the fierce passion of its supporters. With no specific designer credited, it is clear that the creation of this tartan was a collaborative effort to represent the SFA in all official capacities. As such, its use must adhere to registration notes stipulating that threadcount be reliable, but fortunately, the colours have proven consistent, making it an enduring and authentic representation of Scotland's national team.

name: Shanahan
description: The Shanahan corporate tartan, expertly woven by renowned Scottish textile mill Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the spirit of Canadian enterprise with its unique blend of blues and greens. As a specially commissioned design for Burnetts & Struth of Ontario, this distinctive tartan is deeply rooted in the country's heritage, yet its modern flair makes it an attractive choice for corporate identities. With no restrictions on usage, this versatile tartan invites businesses to proudly display their Scottish connections while projecting a fresh, contemporary image. By incorporating elements of Lochcarron's expert craftsmanship and traditional Scottish design, Shanahan strikes a perfect balance between nostalgia and innovation, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to forge strong ties with the nation that inspired its creation.

name: Shandon
description: The Shandon tartan is a deeply personal and storied family heirloom, registered under the name of its esteemed designer, Sir Niall Horan Bt, The Lord Shandon. This restricted tartan is specifically associated with those who claim descent from the Barony of Shandon in Ireland, a region steeped in rich history and tradition. As such, ownership of this tartan comes with honourable responsibility to preserve its heritage and cultural significance. Notably, the design falls under Category Name, signifying its status as a family legacy rather than a clan affiliation or fashion statement. With restrictions in place, the Shandon tartan is a highly sought-after possession for those who can prove their connection to this ancient lineage, making it a treasured family treasure that continues to weave together generations of identity and tradition.

name: Shapiro
description: The Shapiro tartan is a unique and personal creation, borne out of a whimsical desire for family identity. Designed by renowned textile expert Dalgliesh, D C, this tartan was originally commissioned for a Jewish family named 'Shapiro' who playfully added the "Mac" suffix to their name, a nod to their heritage and cultural traditions. Although initially intended as a joke, the tartan ultimately took on a life of its own, with colours altered to match a cherished photograph from 2007 by Phil Smith. As a Category Name, this tartan is imbued with the honour and dignity associated with family names, while its restrictions reflect Dalgliesh's commitment to quality control and preparation for weaving by his own esteemed company, D C Dalgliesh Ltd.
