This distinctive design proudly wears its cultural significance on its sleeve, weaving together threads of identity, heritage, and tradition into a rich tapestry of Scottish tartan excellence.

name: Shaughnessy
description: The Shaughnessy tartan, a fashion staple born from the innovative designs of Scotch Corner in Gateshead, England, pays homage to the rich heritage of Irish name tartans. As one of a series created by this esteemed designer, the Shaughnessy tartan weaves together the threads of Scottish and Irish traditions. Its distinctive pattern, characteristic of the fashion category, offers a modern take on traditional tartan design. Originally inspired by the Gaelic world of Ireland, this tartan's cultural significance lies in its representation of the shared history and identity of Scotland and Ireland through the fusion of their iconic plaid patterns. By wearing the Shaughnessy tartan, one not only makes a statement about their personal style but also connects themselves to the timeless traditions of both nations.

name: Shaw of Carolina
description: The Shaw of Carolina tartan, designed by Mary, Marghret & Irvine, is a poignant tribute to the historical alliance between the Shaw and Irvine clans in North and South Carolina during the early 19th century. This Name tartan, woven with great care from traditional sett elements, pays homage to a fragment of a historic tartan blanket worn by Mary Irvine for her husband John Shaw around 1800. The subtle variations in tone and texture evoke a sense of heritage and tradition, while also acknowledging the clan's enduring legacy in the Americas. With its roots firmly grounded in Scottish history and its connection to American families, this tartan design serves as a powerful symbol of cultural continuity and family honour.

name:
Shaw of Tordarroch [default]
[AKA] Shaw Red
[AKA] Shaw of Tordarroch
description: The Shaw of Tordarroch Red tartan, registered by David C Stewart in 1971 for Major C.J. Shaw of Tordarroch MBE, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish clan heritage. Originally designed as a replacement for an erroneous sett from the late 19th century, this tartan honours the memory of Captain Farquhar Shaw, a Black Watch mutineer who made headlines in his time. The Stewart's careful recreation of the traditional colours and patterns pays homage to the past while respecting the wishes of the Black Watch's Colonel, allowing for continued use by the Clan as a nod to their esteemed ancestor. This historic tartan now resides in the respected collections of the Scottish Tartans Authority and the Johnston Collection, ensuring its significance is preserved for future generations to appreciate and wear with pride.

name:
Shaw of Tordarroch Hunting
[AKA] Shaw of Tordarroch; Hunting
description: The Shaw of Tordarroch Green, also known as 'Green Shaw of Tordarroch', is a storied clan tartan born from the legacy of Major C.J. Shaw of Tordarroch MBE. Registered in 1971, this distinctive Hunting pattern was designed by D.C. Stewart in 1969 to replace an erroneous sett previously used by the Shaw family. By permission of the Colonel of the Black Watch, a small part of this original set will remain in use as a poignant tribute to Cpl Farquhar Shaw, the Black Watch mutineer. This tartan is deeply rooted in Scottish heritage and tradition, its rich green hues evoking the rolling hills and heather-covered moors of the Highlands. With a storied history woven into its very fabric, the Shaw of Tordarroch Green is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Shaw clan and their connection to Scotland's proud tartan heritage.

name: Shaw Women's; Dress
description: This exquisite tartan, known as Shaw Dress, holds profound cultural significance as an arisaidh setting of the esteemed Red Shaw of Tordarroch, woven with love for Miss Rebecca Shaw, daughter of the Chief. Designed by renowned designer James Scarlett MBE, this family heirloom was created to be worn as a majestic shawl, measuring approximately 108 inches in length and 27 inches in width. As a clan tartan, the Shaw Dress is deeply rooted in Scottish heritage, evoking memories of warmth, comfort, and pride among those who wear it. The registration notes attest to its personal significance, underscoring the enduring bond between Miss Rebecca Shaw and her father, Chief of Clan Tordarroch. This intricate weaving not only pays tribute to their ancestral ties but also celebrates the artistry and craftsmanship that has defined Scottish tartan-making for centuries.

name: Shaw [default]
description: The Shaw tartan is a richly woven testament to Scotland's complex history and tradition. Originally created by McIan in 1845 for Farquhar Shaw, a member of the Black Watch who was wrongly executed for mutiny in 1743, this clan tartan holds significant cultural weight. The distinctive red line that distinguishes the philabeg from the belted plaid is said to have originated from an error in the graphic illustration of the Black Watch's 'regimental' tartan. Today, the Shaw tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's turbulent past and its continued relevance in modern times. As a registered clan tartan with the Scottish Tartans Society, it remains an honourable part of Scotland's heritage, available for use by those seeking to connect with their ancestral roots or celebrate their Scottish affiliation.

name: Shawl West Virginia
description: This majestic Gothenburg tartan, designed by the Baron of Prestoungrange for the esteemed institutions still bearing the 'Gothenburg Principles', holds great cultural significance as a testament to Scotland's enduring ties with the storied Swedish city of Goteborg. Registration notes reveal that this unique design was created in honour of Lord Mayor Jorgen Linder's historic visit to Scotland, meticulously capturing the colours and proportions of the City's noble Coat of Arms. As a District tartan, it pays tribute to the geographic and historical connection between these two great nations, weaving a rich tapestry of Scottish heritage and Nordic tradition that is both visually striking and steeped in meaning.

name: Sheard (Roy) personal; Devon District
description: The Devon Companion tartan, designed by renowned weaver Roy Sheard in 1984, is a vibrant reflection of Devon's rich heritage, echoing the success of its Cornish counterparts. This fashion tartan was woven at Coldharbour Mill in Uffculme, Devon, paying homage to the region's unique identity. Originally registered for general use, the Devon Companion tartan now has limited worldwide distribution rights, held by Kilts by Lindsay, a Scottish company. With its distinctive colour palette and meticulously crafted texture, this tartan embodies the warmth and hospitality of the southwest England's iconic county, inviting wearers to don a slice of local history with every step.

name: Sheard (Roy) personal; Devon Green
description: The Devon tartan is a distinctive District sett, born from the pioneering spirit of Coldharbour Mill in the early 1980s. Its origins are rooted in the Cornish St Piran sett, with which it shares a striking aesthetic. This beautiful, subtle pattern weaves together a narrative of regional identity and cultural heritage. Roy Sheard's design is a testament to the enduring allure of Devon's landscape and people, evoking the tranquil beauty of the region's countryside and its rich history. With its Accreditation Certificate proudly presented in 1991, the Devon tartan has become an iconic representation of District tartans, cherished by those who honour their Cornish roots and proud heritage.

name: Shearer [default]
description: The Brown Ellis tartan is a deeply personal and exclusive design, registered under the category of 'Name' to signify its unique association with its individual owner, D C Dalgliesh. Created by renowned designer Dalgliesh in 1928, this tartan is steeped in tradition and heritage, yet remains a private and intimate affair. According to its registration notes, Brown Ellis was designed specifically for personal use, distinguishing it from the clan or corporate tartans that often bear names with strong historical connections. Unfortunately, any attempts to reproduce or commercially exploit the Brown Ellis tartan are restricted by its preparation and registration with Dalgliesh Ltd, ensuring this special design remains a cherished family secret, tied to the life and legacy of D C Dalgliesh himself.

name: Sheffield City
description: The Hopkins tartan is a unique and modern name in Wales' rich textile heritage, dating back to the late 20th century. Originally designed by Sheila Daniel for Wales Tartan Centres in collaboration with Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys, this distinctive tartan has become an iconic symbol of Welsh identity and culture. Despite being a relatively recent creation, it has gained immense popularity since its introduction around 1998, reflecting the growing interest in Welsh heritage among enthusiasts worldwide. As one of the few Celtic tartans to deviate from traditional odd-numbered thread patterns, the Hopkins features innovative warp and weft combinations that set it apart from other historic designs. While it does not carry historical or genealogical significance, its association with Wales Tartan Centres has firmly rooted it in Welsh tradition, making it a treasured part of modern-day cultural expression.

name: Sheffield High School
description: The Missouri tartan is a vibrant and dynamic fashion tartan, woven with precision and flair to evoke the spirit of the American Midwest. Created by renowned designer David McGill in collaboration with International Tartans Ltd, this captivating design celebrates the rich heritage of Missouri, its storied history, and its people. Commissioned specifically for Barbara Allan Gard of Lamar, Missouri, and designed with the consent of Jim Anderson, a stalwart supporter of traditional tartanry, this tartan is an unqualified testament to the enduring allure of Scottish textiles in contemporary fashion. With its bold colours and expertly balanced pattern, the Missouri tartan is poised to add a touch of American charm to any outfit, while remaining deeply respectful of Scotland's storied tartan tradition.

name: Shenzhen
description: The Shenzhen tartan embodies the fusion of Scottish heritage and modern corporate identity. Registered by Lochcarron of Scotland as a corporate tartan, it was conceived by Peter Gerlam in collaboration with Rangers Football Club for a Chinese team, marking a significant milestone in the development of international sports partnerships. This unique blend of traditional Scottish craftsmanship and cutting-edge branding has resulted in a striking design that combines bright orange hues with the iconic club badges, a testament to the power of sport and commerce. As a symbol of the three-year twin club agreement, the Shenzhen tartan now also finds itself woven into the fabric of everyday life through ties, sold in support of this innovative partnership.

name: Shieldhall
description: The McCulloch Military Colours tartan is a poignant commemoration of family heritage, honouring the military service of the McCulloch clan since 1296. Designed specifically for Grant McCulloch's family to celebrate their connection with the Armed Services, this distinctive tartan weaves together a complex narrative of history and sacrifice. The subtle nuances of poppy red, bottle and moss green, slate and electric blue, battleship grey, and silver grey evoke a sense of reverence and respect, each colour carefully chosen to represent a specific chapter in the family's military past, from centuries of loyal service to more recent conflicts in World War 2, the Falkland Islands, and Desert Storm. Controlled use of this tartan is reserved for Grant McCulloch alone, ensuring its significance is preserved as a cherished family heirloom, symbolising a deep-rooted tradition of duty, loyalty, and service.

name: Shotts & Dykehead Pipe Band
description: The House of Edgar Shotts & Dykehead tartan is a unique Corporate design, born out of a historic partnership between the esteemed Scottish brand, House of Edgar, and the Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., its parent company. Commissioned in 2003 for their first-ever commercial sponsorship deal with the renowned Shotts & Dykehead Pipe band, this tartan pays homage to the band's traditional heritage, albeit with a distinctive twist. The original MacLean of Duart tartan, worn by the pipe band, serves as the foundation, yet with deliberate variations, the H of E has subtly reimagined the design by replacing the warp's Grey28 band with blue in the weft, yielding a fresh and modern interpretation that still resonates deeply with Scotland's rich cultural heritage. As a result, this tartan now proudly bears the House of Edgar's mark, signifying its role as a cherished corporate identity within Scottish tradition.

name: Shrek
description: This vibrant Fashion tartan, aptly named 'Shrek', is an undeniably modern take on traditional Scottish weaving, courtesy of esteemed designer Lochcarron of Scotland. Although the registration notes remain tantalisingly vague, one thing is certain: this bold and eye-catching design is sure to turn heads with its eclectic mix of blues, greens, and yellows, reminiscent of a misty Highland glen on a drizzly day. As a Fashion tartan, 'Shrek' is destined for the catwalks and fashion magazines, bringing a dash of Scottish flair to the world of high fashion. Though its exact inspiration may remain a mystery, one thing is clear: this tartan is an integral part of Scotland's rich textile heritage, weaving together tradition and innovation in a vibrant celebration of colour and creativity.

name: Sikh
description: The Sikh tartan, designed by esteemed Kinloch Anderson Ltd, is a poignant commemoration of the rich cultural heritage shared between Scotland and the Sikh community. Originally commissioned to celebrate the 50th anniversary of Mr AJ Singh's family arrival in Scotland and the 300th anniversary of the founding of the Sikh religion, this unique tartan weaves together threads of Scottish tradition with the vibrant colours of Sikh identity. As a Commemorative tartan, it is reserved exclusively for members of the Sikh faith to wear, paying tribute to the enduring bonds between two nations. Its significance extends beyond a simple textile, instead symbolising the historical ties and mutual respect that unite Scotland and the Sikh diaspora, with Mr AJ Singh's family proudly carrying on this legacy.

name: Sildesalaten
description: The Sildesalaten tartan is a poignant commemoration of Norway's brief union with Sweden, which came to an end in 1905. Designed by Åge Jonny Jorgensen, this distinctive tartan weaves together the rich heritage of both nations, drawing inspiration from the iconic Norwegian flag, "Sildesalaten", or "Herring Salad". The flag, featuring a blue Scandinavian cross on a red background, was proudly displayed during the union and has now been immortalised in tartan form. This Commemorative tartan is a testament to Norway's complex history with its Nordic neighbour, and serves as a lasting tribute to the country's unique cultural identity.

name: Sillars [default]
description: The Sillars tartan is a storied and historic clan weft, steeped in tradition and heritage, with its origins shrouded in mystery. As an assumed Stewart variation, it stands as a testament to the storied history of Scotland's noble families, whose intricate patterns and colours tell tales of battle, loyalty, and family ties. This particular tartan design has been passed down through generations, its unique blend of earthy tones and rich textures evoking the rugged landscapes and proud heritage of the Scottish Highlands. With its origins rooted in the Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority, the Sillars tartan is a tangible link to Scotland's complex past, weaving together threads of clan identity, family tradition, and cultural legacy that continue to captivate and inspire to this day.

name: Sillitoe
description: The Sillitoe tartan is a unique and fascinating design, born from the functional needs of law enforcement rather than traditional Scottish heritage. As a corporate tartan, it was created to symbolise unity and solidarity among police forces worldwide. Its distinctive blue and white chequered pattern, originally worn as a hatband by Highland soldiers, has evolved into a widely recognised emblem of authority and service. While Sir Percy Sillitoe, the eponymous designer, played a key role in popularising this design, its roots lie in ancient Scottish heraldry. This tartan's significance extends beyond its corporate context, however, representing a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich history and the enduring bond between tradition and modernity.

name: Silver
description: The Silver tartan, registered by its esteemed designer Hulbert Silver of Vancouver, Canada, is a name tartan of singular distinction, born from a desire to complement his newly acquired Coat of Arms. This striking design, part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's Collection, showcases an intricate balance of blues and silvers, evoking the frosty gleam of a Canadian winter morning. As a name tartan, its purpose is twofold: not only does it proudly represent the individual to whom it belongs, but also serves as a visual manifestation of family heritage and clan identity. With its unique colour palette and carefully crafted pattern, the Silver tartan is a testament to the ingenuity and creativity of its designer, Hulbert Silver, and his deep affection for Scottish tradition and heritage.

name: Silver Mist
description: The Silver Mist corporate tartan, designed by Kirsty Anderson, embodies the ethereal beauty of Scotland's rugged coastlines. Inspired by the soft, grey mist that shrouds the shores, this sophisticated design is steeped in the country's rich heritage and natural splendour. Originally created for MacGregor & MacDuff Ltd's Mist Range, Silver Mist has been specifically crafted for corporate clients seeking a unique and prestigious tartan to represent their organisation. Notably, its production is restricted to Macnaughton Holdings Ltd, ensuring exclusivity and authenticity. With its understated elegance and subtle character, the Silver Mist tartan is an apt choice for companies looking to forge a strong connection with Scotland's storied past while projecting a professional image.

name: Silver Thistle
description: The Silver Thistle fashion tartan, designed by Claire Donaldson for House of Edgar's Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., embodies the essence of Scottish heritage with its striking, modern aesthetic. This distinctive pattern pays homage to Scotland's iconic wild thistle, a symbol of resilience and strength that has been woven into the nation's fabric for centuries. As a fashion tartan, it is perfectly suited to adding a touch of elegance and sophistication to any outfit, making it an excellent choice for those who want to incorporate traditional Scottish design into their everyday style. With its limited restrictions, the Silver Thistle tartan invites wearers to embrace their individuality while still paying tribute to Scotland's rich cultural heritage.

name: Silvicola
description: In celebration of Japan's historic ties with the UK, renowned designer David McGill has created 'Chouchou', a vibrant Fashion tartan inspired by the beauty of summer. This exclusive design, one of four in 'The Four Seasons' collection, pays tribute to Thomas Blake Glover's arrival in Nagasaki in 1859 and marks a significant milestone in the two nations' relationship. Named after the Japanese word for butterfly, 'Chouchou' embodies the carefree essence of summer. According to registration notes, this tartan represents the warmth and joy that comes with longer days, symbolising the perfect fusion of Scottish heritage and Japanese culture. As one of a set of four tartans in the series, 'Chouchou' is steeped in history and tradition, yet its striking colour palette ensures it remains distinctly modern and eye-catching. A true masterpiece of fashion tartan design, 'Chouchou' requires the designer's consent for use, underscoring its exclusive nature and connection to this remarkable cultural exchange.

name: Simple Technology
description: The Simple Technology tartan, designed by Keith Lumsden, is a modern corporate pattern that pays tribute to the cutting-edge technology of East Kilbride's American counterpart, Simple Technology Corporation. Launched at the grand opening of their new plant, this tartan reflects the fusion of innovation and heritage, symbolising the bridge between Scotland and Silicon Valley. With its bold, graphic design, the Simple Technology tartan embodies the spirit of forward-thinking and progress, evoking images of sleek circuit boards and futuristic manufacturing processes. As a corporate tartan, it is suited for use by companies that value modernity and technological advancement, yet still maintain a strong connection to their Scottish roots.

name: Sin-Cos
description: The Sin-Cos tartan is a vibrant Corporate tartan designed by James Leonard, born out of a tribute to two remarkable women: Mrs Ramsay, whose Red Ramsay tartan inspired its base colour, and Lindsay Cameron Nomiyama Kawai, whose yellow stripe adds warmth and depth to the design. Named after The Sin-Cos Group, a Scottish company that has had a profound impact on promoting Highland culture in Japan since 1982, this tartan represents the group's dedication to supporting highland traditions through the Kansai Highland Games and the Ramsay Pipeband. The Sin-Cos tartan is more than just a design - it symbolises the connection between Scotland and Japan, as well as the enduring spirit of community and cultural exchange that has blossomed from this unlikely friendship. Its rich green base, punctuated by yellow and blue stripes, evokes the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of Scotland, while also celebrating the unique blend of Scottish heritage and Japanese innovation that has come to define The Sin-Cos Group's mission.

name: Sinclair Dress (Dance)
description: The Sinclair Dress, also known as Dancers' Fancy, is a timeless and majestic tartan that embodies the heritage and tradition of the noble House of Sinclair. As a Clan/Family tartan, it bears witness to the enduring legacy of this ancient Scottish dynasty. With its distinctive blue, green, yellow, black, and white stripes, this tartan design tells the story of a family's history and cultural identity. Although the designer remains unknown, their creative vision is evident in the nuanced balance of colours, which subtly evoke the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Scottish Borders, where the Sinclairs once held sway. While some may view its subtle variations as a departure from traditional patterns, this tartan's authenticity lies in its adherence to the Sinclair family's storied past, as recorded by D.C.Dalgliesh Ltd, Selkirk in 1998, cementing its place within Scotland's rich tapestry of tradition and heritage.

name: Sinclair, Green (Personal)
description: The Sinclair Green tartan is a unique and storied variation designed by R.M. Sinclair, carefully crafted to reflect his personal heritage and flair. As a 'Name' tartan, it holds significant cultural weight as a distinctive identifier for the Sinclair family name. This distinctive pattern weaves together a rich tapestry of Scottish tradition, drawing inspiration from the country's timeless heritage. While this tartan is imbued with historical significance, its use is restricted to personal or familial purposes only, ensuring that its connection to the Sinclair legacy remains cherished and intimate. By wearing or working with the Sinclair Green tartan, one becomes part of a privileged circle of those honoured with this family name, connecting them to centuries of history and tradition.

name: Sinclair Hunting
description: The Sinclair Hunting tartan is a storied and majestic variant of the traditional hunting pattern, born from the proud heritage of Clan Sinclair. As a clan tartan, its purpose is to identify members of the Sinclair family with their ancestral lineage, evoking a sense of honour and tradition. Although it deviates from the original design through misweaving, this unique variation was first showcased in the 1884 edition of the Clansman magazine, a testament to the enduring passion for Scottish heritage. This tartan's significance lies not only in its clan connections but also as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich textile history and the traditions that have been woven into the very fabric of its culture.

name: Sinclair Lyon Count
description: The Sinclair tartan is an iconic and storied design that embodies the proud heritage of Scotland's most noble clan, the Sinclairs. Registered in the Lyon Court Books, a treasured repository of Scottish tartan history, this tartan has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition for centuries. Created with a threadcount recorded by the Earl of Caithness, Chief of the Sinclairs, on 29 June 1951, this distinctive pattern is steeped in family history and cultural significance. As one of Scotland's most enduring clan tartans, the Sinclair design continues to hold honour among Scottish families and clans, evoking a sense of loyalty, pride, and connection to a rich heritage that spans generations. Its exact origin remains shrouded in mystery, attributed only to the unknown designer whose name has been lost to time, yet its significance remains unmistakable – a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's most noble clan.

name:
Sinclair [default]
[AKA] Sinclair Red
description: This esteemed Sinclair tartan, registered under its "Logan" variation, embodies the rich heritage and noble lineage of one of Scotland's most storied clans. With roots dating back to the 18th century, this intricate pattern tells the story of Alexander, 13th Earl of Caithness, whose portrait served as the foundation for the threadcount used in its design. First featured in Logan's influential 'The Scottish Gael' publication from 1830, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Sinclair clan, which has played a significant role in Scotland's history and tradition. As an "Other" classification, the Sinclair tartan stands apart from those tied to specific clans or families, instead representing the broader cultural and historical significance of Scottish heritage, making it a treasured symbol of national identity and pride.

name: Sinclair-Brown
description: The Sinclair-Brown tartan is a storied family heirloom, carefully registered in 1991 for personal use by Mr Nicholas Sinclair-Brown from London. This distinctive Name tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's clans and families, where tradition and identity are deeply intertwined. As such, it is not open to commercial reproduction, ensuring its exclusive connection to the Sinclair-Brown family's history and legacy. The intricate patterns woven into this tartan speak volumes about the enduring significance of Scottish clan culture, with its bold colours and carefully balanced design reflecting a deep respect for tradition and heritage. This privately registered tartan remains a cherished family treasure, preserving the Sinclair-Brown name in perpetuity.

name: Singh [default]
description: The Singh tartan, registered to Lochcarron of Scotland in 1999, is a unique and meaningful design born from the rich heritage of the Singh family. Commissioned by Mr Sirdar Iqbal Singh of Lesmahagow, south of Glasgow, this tartan weaves together symbolic colours that pay tribute to his Indian roots. The distinctive blue ground shade represents a cherished colour reserved for the Singh family, while the yellow motif signifies peace and harmony. In recognition of Mrs Singh's Swiss heritage, red and white threads are woven in, alongside green, which symbolises the landholdings of her late grandfather, 'Grandfather' Singh. This tartan is not only an honourable legacy to Mr Singh, but also a testament to his connection to Scotland, as it can be worn by any Asians with Scottish ties, serving as a powerful emblem of cultural exchange and unity.

name: Sir Billi
description: The Sir Billi tartan is a dynamic corporate design that embodies the spirit of creativity and excellence that defines the partnership between esteemed names in Scottish entertainment and animation. Named after its protagonist, Sir Billi the Vet, a star-studded animated short feature film, this tartan weaves together a rich tapestry of heritage and innovation. Designed by Sascha Hartmann, this distinctive pattern is rooted in Glasgow's thriving animation industry and has been carefully crafted to reflect the high-profile collaboration between Sir Sean Connery, Alan Cumming, Patrick Doyle, and other acclaimed talent. As an officially registered Corporate tartan, it is a symbol of pride for those associated with Billi Productions Ltd, while also paying tribute to Scotland's storied history of animation and cinematic excellence.

name: Skene [default]
description: The Skene tartan is a complex and intriguing pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, worn by the late Skene of Skene, a Lowland family with Highland connections. Registered in 1850, this clan tartan is one of several attributed to the Smiths, who noted its antiquity but also expressed doubts about its authenticity. A unique feature of the Skene tartan lies in its blue line separating two distinct reds on a broad green background, characteristic of many Lowland patterns. However, the woven sample from the Scottish Tartans Authority's Dalgety Collection poses a challenge, as the dark blue and dark green hues can be difficult to distinguish from one another. As such, this tartan design remains an enigmatic representation of Scotland's rich clan history, its subtle nuances waiting to be unravelled by those with a keen eye for tradition and heritage.

name: Skibo
description: The Skibo tartan, a masterful creation by Hunters of Brora, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish craftsmanship. Originating exclusively for Skibo Limited, this Corporate tartan was woven with precision and flair to adorn The Carnegie Club at Skibo Castle. Its intricate blues and subtle earthy tones evoke the grandeur of Scotland's iconic estates, while its association with the esteemed Skibo Castle lends an air of exclusivity and sophistication. Notably, permission to weave this design is strictly granted by Skibo Limited, underscoring the tartan's bespoke nature and highlighting the importance of preserving its unique cultural significance. This stunning tartan design serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's storied past, expertly woven for the esteemed Skibo Limited.

name: Skinner [default]
description: The Skinner tartan is a poignant tribute to Scottish heritage, born from the threads of family legacy and tradition. Named in honour of its creator's grandfather, John Skinner, who was emigrating to the USA with his father in 1880, this distinctive Name tartan holds a deep significance for those bearing the name. Though it bears a striking resemblance to the iconic Wallace tartan, permission was obtained from the esteemed Chief to record it as the 'Skinner', ensuring its authenticity and cultural relevance. This carefully preserved pattern, worn by John Skinner himself in 1941, has been lovingly passed down through generations, including his grandson John H Beach, who sought to preserve its identity. Today, the Skinner tartan remains a cherished emblem of family pride, awaiting permission from the Chief to be worn with honour, and is eagerly embraced by those fortunate enough to carry the name.

name: Skye
description: The Skye tartan, a stylish and modern fashion choice born from the storied heritage of Scotland's northernmost isle, evokes the windswept beauty of the Hebrides. As a fashion tartan, it is part of the esteemed tradition of textiles that have adorned the nation's people for centuries. The design, inspired by the Stewarts' own variation on the Dalgliesh pattern, bears the mark of Edinburgh Woollen Mill's renowned expertise in weaving and colourwork. With its distinctive sett and subtle colour palette, this tartan is not only a tribute to Scotland's rich cultural heritage but also a testament to the country's enduring appeal as a fashion destination. As such, it remains a popular choice among those seeking to add a touch of Scottish style and sophistication to their wardrobe.

name: Slanj Dress
description: The Slanj Dress tartan is a stylish and modern fashion favourite, steeped in traditional Scottish heritage. With its unique and eye-catching colour palette, this tartan was designed to make a statement on the catwalk. As a fashion tartan, it falls under the category of formal wear, making it perfect for dressing up or adding a touch of sophistication to any outfit. Registration notes indicate that the tartan's wider widths may vary by just a couple of threads, suggesting a more relaxed and casual approach to its design. With its rich history and subtle nuances, this tartan is sure to add a dash of Scottish flair to any fashion ensemble, honouring the country's iconic textile traditions while embracing contemporary style.

name: Slanj
description: The Slanj tartan is a distinctive corporate design born from the esteemed Highland Dress outfitters Slanj Scotland, with its roots firmly planted in Glasgow's West George Street. This bold and modern tartan was created to reflect the company's heritage and values, and its registration notes reveal a deep connection to traditional Scottish textiles. Characterised by a lighter blue tone that serves as a subtle counterpoint to deeper hues, this sett-based design showcases Lochcarron swatches in their original form, lending an air of authenticity to the overall aesthetic. As a corporate tartan, Slanj embodies professionalism and sophistication, making it an excellent choice for businesses seeking to establish a strong Scottish identity whilst maintaining a contemporary edge.

name: Slessor
description: This intimate Name tartan, registered by renowned designer Brian Wilton, tells the story of love and heritage through its subtle yet distinctive colours. Born from a wedding present gifted to Kirsteen Slessor's parents in 1977, this tartan is a nostalgic reminder of the happy couple's special day. The simple yet meaningful design features two biscuit-coloured lines - representing Kirsteen's siblings - intertwined with three blue lines, symbolising the bridesmaids who supported her on that unforgettable day. As a Name tartan, it holds significance not only for the Slessor family but also as a testament to the blending of traditions from Scotland and Ireland, reflected in the light biscuit threadcount (1977) and green threadcount (22), signifying the wedding date and blessing date respectively. This delicate yet enduring design is now preserved and shared with honour, allowing future generations to appreciate its significance within Scottish heritage.

name: Sligo Irish County
description: The Sligo, County tartan is a quintessential representation of Irish heritage, reflecting the rich cultural traditions of the Emerald Isle's west coast. Designated as a District tartan by the House of Edgar's Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this distinctive pattern has been meticulously crafted by Polly Wittering to capture the essence of Sligo's unique character. While not officially sanctioned as a traditional District tartan, its popularity endears it to those who cherish authentic Irish connections. A fitting addition to any collection of tartans with historical significance, the Sligo, County tartan embodies the warmth and hospitality of the region, inviting wearers to pay homage to the county's storied past.

name: SmartWool
description: The SmartWool tartan is a vibrant, modern design born from the fusion of Scottish heritage and corporate flair. Registration notes reveal its origins as a bespoke creation for the Smartwool Corporation of Steamboat Springs, Colorado, marking it as an authentic example of American-Scottish cultural exchange. Johnstons of Elgin, renowned tartan weavers, skillfully brought this design to life on scarves for corporate use. As a Corporate tartan, its purpose is to evoke professionalism and sophistication while proudly sporting the Smartwool brand. Note that restrictions on usage mean it can only be used with SmartWool products, underscoring the company's commitment to its own identity. This tartan is an intriguing blend of tradition and innovation, reflecting the dynamic relationship between Scottish textiles and international corporations.

name: Smeaton Hunting
description: The Port Moresby City Pipes and Drums tartan is a vibrant and stirring corporate design, steeped in the rich cultural heritage of Papua New Guinea. Inspired by the iconic colours of the country's national flag, this distinctive tartan pays tribute to the traditions of Bagpipe playing in PNG, as championed by the Papua New Guinea Pipes and Drums Association Inc. Designed by John Clelland Hocknull, this tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of community and cultural identity that defines this Pacific nation. With its bold colour palette and traditional weaving techniques, this tartan is an honouring tribute to the musicians, drummers, and communities who have preserved the ancient art of Bagpipe playing in PNG, while also offering a unique corporate branding opportunity for those seeking to tap into the rich cultural heritage of this fascinating country.

name: Smeaton (Personal)
description: Smeaton 1997 is a timeless Name tartan, carefully crafted by Alfred & Andrew Smeaton to commemorate a momentous occasion - a wedding summertime celebration in 1997. The intricate pattern weaves a tale of love, tradition, and heritage, paying homage to the rich tapestry of Scottish culture. As a registered tartan, it embodies the values of exclusivity, with its unique design reserved for the select few who can wear it with honour, signifying a special bond between wearer and this enduring symbol of Scottish identity. With its origins rooted in a joyous celebration, Smeaton 1997 reminds us that tartans are more than just patterns - they hold within them the stories and emotions of our past, waiting to be woven into the fabric of our present.

name: Smeaton Wedding; #1
description: The Papua New Guinea Pipes and Drums tartan is a vibrant and evocative corporate design, expertly crafted by John Clelland Hocknull. Inspired by the traditions of Bagpipe playing in Papua New Guinea, this distinctive tartan tells the story of a nation's rich cultural heritage. The colours, drawn from the country's National flag, are carefully woven to evoke the warmth and spirit of the Pacific Islands. As a corporate design, it is perfectly suited for organisations that seek to connect with the values of tradition, community, and performance that underpin Papua New Guinean culture. With its bold stripes and subtle nuances, this tartan is sure to make a lasting impression, honouring the traditions of the Pipes and Drums Association Inc. while also celebrating the country's unique identity on a global stage.

name: Smith of Pennylands
description: The Smith of Pennylands tartan, registered in 1972 by renowned weaver Hary Lindley of Kinloch Anderson, Edinburgh, is a testament to the enduring heritage of Scottish tradition. As a Name tartan, it was created to represent the distinguished family of Smiths from Pennylands, a location steeped in history and clan affiliation. This intricately woven design, steeped in the rich cultural traditions of Scotland, was originally designed for the Smiths' Highland dress requirements and has since become an iconic representation of Scottish identity. With its storied connection to Kinloch Anderson, one of Edinburgh's oldest and most respected tartan mills, this tartan holds a special place in the hearts of those who cherish Scottish heritage, and is often worn with pride by those seeking to honour their ancestral roots.

name: Smith, Sir William (Personal)
description: The Sir William Smith Corporate Tartan is a poignant and enigmatic design, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Originally created as the personal tartan of its eponymous founder, Sir William Smith, a renowned Laird of Strathblane and armourer to the Barony of Mugdock, this corporate tartan has been imbued with over 400 years of family history and legacy. Inspired by the Hunting Gow tartan, it now bears witness to the enduring spirit of the Smith clan, whose ancestors were distinguished members of Scottish society. With its mysterious variations from the original, the Sir William Smith Corporate Tartan is a testament to the evolution of tradition and the power of heritage to transcend time. Its widespread availability has ensured that this tartan remains a symbol of honour, identity, and connection to Scotland's rich cultural fabric for generations to come.

name:
Smith [default]
[AKA] MacGowan Hunting
description: The Smith tartan holds a rich heritage, its origins deeply rooted in Scotland's proud tradition of weaving and armoury. As a Name tartan, it is a testament to the enduring legacy of Gow Hunting, whose Gaelic name "Gow" translates to metal worker or armourer, signifying a long line of skilled craftsmen. The subtle modifications to this historic pattern, with the dark blue stripe replaced by the azure hue, serve as a poignant reminder of its evolution over time. While it is unclear who specifically designed this tartan, its significance remains undiminished, evoking the spirit of Scottish craftsmanship and the storied history of those who wielded metal and fought for their country's honour.

name: Smithers [default]
description: The Smithers tartan, a proud emblem of Canadian heritage, tells the story of a family bound by history and tradition. Designed by Alfred Arnold Smither, this Clan/Family tartan was registered to signify connection to the name, welcoming anyone who shares its surname to wear it as a badge of honour. Characterised by subtle variations in blue tone, which appear as 'lightened' blues in the sett, this tartan is not only visually striking but also steeped in the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's tartan legacy. As a testament to the enduring bond between family and tradition, the Smithers tartan stands as a reminder of the countless generations who have woven their stories into its intricate patterns, now available for those with the name to wear with pride.

name: Smithsonian
description: The Smithsonian tartan is a unique and vibrant corporate design born from a momentous occasion - Alistair Buchan's creation to support Scotland's participation in the prestigious Smithsonian Institute's For Life Festival in Washington DC, USA. This distinctive tartan has been registered specifically for corporate wear, symbolising the enduring bond between Scotland and the global community of the Smithsonian Institution. As such, it is an esteemed addition to any business or organisation seeking to make a statement about their Scottish heritage and values. With its rich colours and intricate weave, the Smithsonian tartan embodies the warmth and hospitality that define Scottish culture, while also representing innovation and international collaboration - a fitting tribute to Scotland's enduring spirit of global engagement.

name: Snodgrass [default]
description: The Snodgrass tartan, designed by Captain T.S. Davidson, is a rich and storied pattern steeped in the heritage of Scotland's esteemed clans. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Society in 1978, this family tartan was specifically created for the Snodgrass Clan Association, paying homage to the clan's ancestral roots. Drawing inspiration from the Cunningham tartan, the Snodgrass design incorporates deep blues, evoking the traditional Highland 'Blue Bonnet', as well as earthy greens and golden hues, reminiscent of the clan's coat of arms. The result is a complex yet harmonious blend that beautifully represents the Scottish tradition of tartanry, honouring the rich history and cultural significance of the Snodgrass Clan, whilst also serving as a proud symbol of family heritage and identity.

name: Snoozzzeee
description: The Snoozzzeee tartan is a delightful example of corporate Scottish heritage, specifically designed for pet bedding accessories. Created by Paul Foden at Pupster House, Winsford Trading Estate, in Cheshire, England, this vibrant tartan is registered by Lochcarron of Scotland and showcases a playful, whimsical character that's sure to delight dog owners everywhere. As a corporate tartan, it was crafted with the intention of bringing a touch of Scottish flair to pet accessories, making it a unique and distinctive choice for businesses looking to establish their brand identity on a national stage. With its bright colours and cheerful tone, Snoozzzeee tartan embodies the warmth and hospitality that Scotland is renowned for, making it the paw-fect choice for any business looking to add a bit of Scottish charm to their products.

name: Snowbird
description: The Snowbird tartan, woven in the rich traditions of Lochcarron of Scotland, is a symbol of Canadian military heritage and pride. Registered for 431 (Air Demonstration) Squadron "The Snowbirds" of the Royal Canadian Air Force, Moose Jaw, Saskatchewan, this distinctive tartan was created to commemorate the squadron's airborne display team. Woven in 2005, it is a testament to the enduring legacy of Canada's military traditions. The Snowbird tartan's technical characteristics reflect its origins as a formal tartan for an elite military unit, with a balanced and harmonious colour palette that echoes the icy blue skies and crisp white snowflakes of the Canadian wilderness. This tartan design embodies the courage, skill, and discipline of Canada's Air Force, and is a treasured emblem of national pride.

name: Sobieski-Stewart [default]
description: The Sobieski-Stewart tartan is a richly woven tribute to the historic ties between Poland and Scotland, born from the legacy of the Sobieski Stewart brothers who played a pivotal role in shaping the Scottish tartan industry. Designed by Bernard O'Hagan, this Clan tartan is a vibrant celebration of the Polish national flag's red and white hues, combined with the majestic black and silver of the Royal Sobieski eagle. Woven with pride, this tartan is intended to inspire a sense of heritage and connection among the Polish community in Scotland and their families back home, while also serving as a symbol of Scottish-Polish camaraderie. As a testament to the enduring spirit of collaboration between these two nations, the Sobieski-Stewart tartan embodies the principles of cultural exchange and mutual respect that have defined the historic relationship between Poland and Scotland for centuries.

name:
Society of Santa Fe
[AKA] Scottish Heritage Preservation
description: The Scottish Heritage Preservation tartan is a symbol of unity and celebration of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, designed by esteemed Dr Philip D Smith Jr for Peter Campbell, President of the Scottish Heritage Preservation Society in 2000. As a Corporate tartan, it embodies the values of tradition, history, and community that underpin Scotland's iconic heritage, with its unique patterns and colours evoking the rolling hills, rugged landscapes, and storied past of this beloved nation. This distinctive design has been carefully crafted to promote the Society's mission, ensuring that every thread honours the legacy of Scottish craftsmanship and the people who have shaped it over centuries. With its roots firmly planted in the Johnston Collection, a treasured archive of Scotland's tartan heritage, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of tradition and community spirit.

name: Solberg-Wormald
description: The Solberg-Wormald tartan, a personal creation woven with love and precision by D C Dalgliesh of Selkirk, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish weaving tradition. As a Name tartan, it serves as a family identifier, proudly bearing the Wormald clan name. With its distinctive and complex pattern, this tartan tells the story of two Scottish families united in their love for their ancestral homeland. The unique characteristics of this design, carefully crafted by Dalgliesh, reflect the skill and craftsmanship of traditional Scottish weaving, ensuring that the Solberg-Wormald tartan will be treasured for generations to come. Its significance extends beyond mere fashion, representing a deep connection to Scotland's history, culture, and community.

name: Somerset District
description: The Somerset tartan is a vibrant representation of the rich heritage of this West Country district, woven with meticulous care by renowned designer Roy Sheard. Registered as part of the esteemed District Tartans category, this distinctive pattern reflects the local history and identity of Somerset, situated in the heart of England's south-west. Its origins rooted in the Coldharbour Trust, a testament to the region's strong community spirit. With its unique colour palette and traditional sett, the Somerset tartan embodies the warmth and hospitality that defines the county's proud tradition of craftsmanship and storytelling. A true celebration of local pride and cultural heritage, this tartan is an honour to wear or display, evoking memories of rolling hills, picturesque villages, and a rich history that continues to shape the identity of this beloved district.

name: Somerville [default]
description: The Somerville tartan is a stunning example of traditional Scottish heritage, woven into existence to honour one of Scotland's most esteemed clans. This modern family tartan, as described by its early collectors in the 1930s, was painstakingly recreated from samples provided by respected weavers such as J Johnston of Edinburgh and Lochcarron. According to Nomindex, dating back to 1980, this particular tartan is believed to be derived from the MacDougall family crest. As a Clan tartan, Somerville holds significant cultural significance, reflecting the rich history and traditions of its namesake clan. Its intricate pattern, woven with precision and care, embodies the values and legacy of the MacDougalls, whose heritage continues to captivate those who cherish Scotland's rich tapestry.

name: Sons of Scotland
description: The Sons of Scotland tartan is a striking corporate motif that embodies the camaraderie and heritage of fraternal organisations formed in Scotland. Registered in 1880, this distinctive weave celebrates the country's rich cultural tapestry, paying homage to its storied history, literature, traditions, customs, and amusements. Originally designed for the SOS association, this tartan was woven from Lochcarron wool, a nod to the traditional Scottish weaving heritage. Characterised by a specific balance of greens, including Geen that's noticeably lighter than usual, the Sons of Scotland design has become an enduring symbol of solidarity and shared identity among its members. While not attributed to a specific designer, this tartan remains an important part of Scottish heritage, serving as a visual representation of the values and principles that have guided these organisations for generations.

name: Sonsub
description: The Sonsub tartan is a striking corporate colour scheme designed to reflect the heritage and prestige of Sonsub Ltd, a respected company based in Bridge of Don, Aberdeen. Created by talented textile designer Maxine Scott for House of Tartan, this distinctive tartan is specifically tailored to evoke the region's rich history and cultural identity. With its unique blend of deep blues and vibrant yellows, the Sonsub tartan embodies the energy and dynamism of Scotland's industrial heartland. Its corporate credentials ensure that it can be confidently used by businesses seeking a bold and sophisticated visual identity that pays homage to their Aberdeen roots.

name: Sorbie [default]
description: The Sorbie tartan, designed by renowned textile artist Colin Hutcheson in the late 19th century, is a testament to the rich heritage and tradition of the Sorbie family. This Clan tartan, registered for Miss Muriel Sorbie herself, has been woven to embody the family's values and history, and its subtle nuances are a reflection of the intricate cultural tapestry of Scotland. As an authentic clan tartan, it can be worn by all members of the name with pride, symbolising unity and kinship. The design itself is a masterful blend of earthy tones and rich blues, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands and the warmth of family tradition. With its heritage firmly rooted in the Sorbie's own story, this tartan remains an enduring emblem of Scottish identity and a celebration of the unique bond that unites those who bear the name.

name: Soroptimist International
description: The Offaly County, Crest Range tartan is a richly evocative representation of Irish heritage, carefully crafted by Viking Technology Limited (now Tartan Web Scotland Ltd) to reflect the distinct traditions of Offaly's storied history. This District tartan, registered in 2005, was one of a set of Irish County and National designs intended to proudly showcase the unique characteristics of each region. As an official tartan, it holds great significance for those from Offaly or with a connection to this western Irish county, serving as a symbol of local honour and identity. However, due to ownership transfer in 2012, reproduction of this tartan requires the express written consent of USA Kilts Inc., highlighting the complexities of modern tartan ownership and the importance of respecting intellectual property rights while preserving the integrity of these precious designs.

name: Soutar [default]
description: The Soutar/Souter tartan is a rich and storied heritage fabric, woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition. Believed to have been created for Ronald Henry Soutar and Robin Scott Soutar, this intricate design is now available to anyone bearing the surname Soutar or Souter, serving as a lasting tribute to their family legacy. The subtle variations in tone and texture evoke the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands, where generations of Soutars have left an indelible mark on history. With its estimated thread count noted for display purposes only, this tartan invites wearers to don a piece of their family's honour, connecting them to a storied past that whispers tales of courage, loyalty and community.

name: South Australia District
description: The South Australia tartan is a vibrant and modern fashion tartan, evoking the vast open spaces and rugged beauty of the Australian Outback. Designed by renowned textile expert Betty Johnston of 'House of Tartan' in Canberra, this bold and striking pattern was created to capture the essence of the region's unique landscape and cultural heritage. As a Fashion tartan, it is free from restrictions that might apply to other categories, such as Clan or Corporate tartans, allowing it to be worn with pride by those who appreciate the distinctive style and symbolism of Australian fashion. With its striking colour palette and modern design, the South Australia tartan is perfect for anyone looking to add a touch of Aussie flair to their wardrobe, while paying homage to the country's rich history and stunning natural beauty.

name: South Australia Pipes & Drums
description: This vibrant corporate tartan, aptly named South Australian Pipes & Drums, is an honour to its eponymous namesake, celebrating the state's rich cultural heritage through its bold colours. Weaved with precision by Elliot Fine Fabric of Selkirk, this distinctive tartan holds a special place in history as it was worn by the South Australian Pipes & Drums band during their memorable performance at the Edinburgh Tattoo in 2003. As a registered corporate tartan, it is now available for use in business and organisational contexts, allowing companies to tap into the proud tradition of Scottish piping and drumming that has captivated audiences across the globe.

name: South Lanarkshire
description: The South Lanarkshire tartan is a quintessential representation of the district's rich heritage, bearing testament to its proud history and cultural identity. This storied design, born from the vision of late Donald Suttie Smith, was specifically commissioned by the South Lanarkshire Council, making it an authentic and exclusive emblem of the region. With its unique characteristics, this tartan has been woven into the fabric of local tradition, with the tale of its creation being as fascinating as its origins. Originally sold to the Provost, who then saw a kilt made for a pipe band, before eventually being split between Don Smith's estate and a musical ensemble, this tartan embodies the vibrant spirit of South Lanarkshire, where its intricate pattern weaves together past and present, honouring the land that has given it life.

name: Southdown Grey
description: The Southdown Grey tartan, created by Jedburgh Woollen Mill, is a stunning addition to the world of fashion, embodying the timeless spirit of Scotland's rich heritage. This beautiful tartan design falls under the category of Fashion, indicating its versatility and suitability for a wide range of clothing items. The subtle nuances of this unique pattern are carefully woven, evoking the rolling hills and moors that dominate the South Downs in southern Scotland. As part of the Johnston Collection, housed by the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan is a proud representation of Scotland's cultural legacy, showcasing the intricate traditions of tartan design that have been passed down through generations. With its sophisticated colour palette and enduring appeal, the Southdown Grey tartan is sure to make a lasting impression on those who wear it.

name: Southdown
description: The Southdown tartan is a vibrant and stylish fashion creation with no discernible connection to Scotland's rich heritage. Notably registered by Miss A Nisbitt in Forsyth's of Edinburgh, this tartan defies tradition as it falls under the category of Fashion, eschewing any ties to Clan or family affiliations. Its design, now available for commercial use, is a testament to the enduring appeal of tartan patterns in modern fashion. With its bold colours and distinctive weave, Southdown is sure to add a touch of sophistication to any outfit, yet its lack of Scottish provenance ensures it remains an intriguing anomaly in the world of tartans.

name: Southwell Australian
description: The Southwell tartan, a personal design by renowned Australian weaver Betty Johnston, holds a special place in the hearts of its original creators - an Australian family with strong ties to the wool industry. With no discernible design rationale, it is a testament to the intuitive storytelling that often underlies Scottish heritage patterns. The subtle nuances of Johnston's skillful weaving are evident in this name tartan, which features an intricate balance of 78 green threads per 12-inch repeat, carefully offset by white and possibly cream, to create a sense of depth and warmth. While specific meanings behind the design may be lost to history, its existence serves as a poignant reminder of the personal stories woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition, awaiting discovery by those who wear it with pride.

name: Southwick [default]
description: The Southwick tartan is a rich tapestry of heritage, woven from the threads of a storied Scottish clan. Registered to the Southwick family crest, this distinctive design pays homage to an ancient Galloway family name with deep roots in southwest Scotland. Tim Southwick's masterful creation serves as a symbol of honour and tradition for those who bear the name Southwick, connecting them to their ancestral homeland and the tartan's storied past. With its subtle nuances and deliberate colours, this tartan design evokes the rugged beauty of the Scottish wilderness and the warm, welcoming spirit of the Southwick family, whose history stretches back through generations, forged in the heartland of Scotland.

name: Souza Nery
description: The Souza Nery tartan is a unique and personal expression of heritage, carefully crafted by the Scottish Tartans Society for a Brazilian-based family. Designed with love and respect for one's roots, this tartan reflects the cultural blend of its creators, weaving together threads of Scottish tradition with the warmth and vitality of Brazilian life. Though it may be worn as a statement piece or treasured in domestic settings, the Souza Nery is not available for general commercial use due to its private nature, reserved instead for those closest to its designer's heart. This rare and intimate tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring power of family, community, and cultural identity.

name: SPA Association
description: The SPA Association tartan, designed by Fiona Hall of Lochcarron, is a rich and vibrant corporate tartan, woven with pride for one of Scotland's most esteemed organisations - the Scottish Passenger Agents Association. To commemorate their 75th dinner, Hall created this distinctive pattern, which now serves as a symbol of unity and celebration among members and supporters alike. As a Category Corporate tartan, it is designed to be easily identifiable with the organisation, yet remains versatile enough for use in various contexts, from formal events to everyday wear. With its bold colours and intricate design, this tartan pays tribute to Scotland's rich heritage and tradition of textiles, while also honouring a dedicated group of professionals who have contributed to the country's tourism industry for generations.

name: Spar UK
description: Spar (UK) Ltd's corporate tartan is a testament to the enduring appeal of traditional Scottish textiles, expertly woven by Keith Lumsden. This distinctive design was crafted specifically for the grocery chain's 1997 conference in Scotland, a nod to the country's rich cultural heritage and its long history of textile innovation. Launched at Blair Castle in Perthshire on 6th May 1997, this tartan is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition, evoking images of rustic landscapes and warm hospitality. As a corporate tartan, it serves as a symbol of unity and identity for the Spar brand, while also paying homage to Scotland's timeless beauty and craftsmanship.

name: Spencer
description: The Spencer tartan, a fashion icon born from the West Coast Woolen Mill's innovative spirit, pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage while embracing modern style. As a Stewart modification, this distinctive tartan takes its cue from Lady Diana's personal favourite, reflecting the timeless elegance and refinement of the British Royal Family. Registered in 1990, the Spencer design has been carefully crafted to evoke the very essence of Scottish tradition, with its subtle nuances and intricate patterns evoking memories of Highland landscapes and ancestral homes. With its bold yet understated charm, this tartan has become a wardrobe staple for those seeking to honour their Scottish roots or simply to add a touch of sophistication to their fashion sense, while adhering to the strict guidelines set by the Scottish Tartans Authority, ensuring that this iconic design remains true to its heritage.

name: Spens [default]
description: The Spens/Spence tartan is a mysterious and intriguing clan tartan, shrouded in history and intrigue. Registered as part of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, this distinctive design has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition. Dating back to an 19th century kilt formerly owned by the esteemed John Telfer Dunbar, the Spens/Spence tartan was identified with the name Spens, though no definitive proof exists. This enigmatic tartan remains a testament to Scotland's rich clan history and the often complex threads that weave families together. With its unique characteristics and storied past, the Spens/Spence tartan is a poignant reminder of the country's proud heritage and the lasting legacy of those who wear it with honour.

name: Spice Apple
description: The Spice Apple tartan is a vibrant, fashion-forward design created by Clinton Mills, evoking the warmth and energy of autumnal harvests in Scotland. This table top fabric tartan features a striking combination of blues, reds, and greens, reminiscent of ripening apples and the spices that flavour traditional Scottish cuisine. As a fashion tartan, it is free to be used without restriction, allowing wearers to express their individuality and add a touch of Scottish flair to any outfit. With its unique colour palette and rhythmic thread pattern, the Spice Apple tartan embodies the spirit of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, inviting those who wear it to embody the warmth, vitality, and hospitality that define the country's people.

name: Spirit of 1994
description: This vibrant Fashion tartan, designed by Mike Oettle, embodies the spirit of 1994, a momentous year in South African history when democracy was finally achieved. The colours inspired by the country's flag are deliberately chosen to evoke the ideals of freedom and equality enshrined in the Constitution, which came into effect on that day. By adopting this tartan, wearers can proudly associate themselves with South Africa and its people, while also celebrating a pivotal moment in the nation's journey towards unity and self-determination. With its bold and uplifting colour scheme, the Spirit of 1994 tartan is a fitting tribute to the values of justice, equality, and human rights that have long been at the heart of South African society, inspiring wearers to embody these same principles with pride.

name: Spirit of Alba
description: The Spirit of Alba tartan, a vibrant and captivating creation from House of Edgar's esteemed Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., embodies the very essence of Scotland's rich heritage. This fashion tartan is named after the Latin term for Scotland, Alba, evoking the country's ancient history and cultural identity. Originally designed by Claire Donaldson with Robert Nicol of Perth & Dunfermline as its intended wearer, this tartan's restrictions reflect its intended use for kilt fabric, a nod to the traditional Scottish dress that has long been an integral part of Highland life. The Spirit of Alba tartan is sure to add a touch of Scottish flair to any outfit, its modern design seamlessly blending with the country's storied past, making it an excellent choice for those seeking to honour Scotland's rich heritage.

name: Spirit of Bannockburn
description: The Spirit of Bannockburn tartan, expertly woven by Lochcarron of Scotland, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scotland's most pivotal moment in history. This fashion tartan, once known as 'Scotland the Brave', pays homage to the bravery and resilience of the Scottish people at the Battle of Bannockburn in 1314. By rebranding it as the Spirit of Bannockburn, Lochcarron of Scotland has breathed new life into this iconic design, evoking the sense of pride and national identity that defines Scottish heritage. With its bold and striking colours, this tartan is sure to make a statement, perfect for those who wear their Scottish roots with honour. Its registration notes mark it as a true representation of Scottish textile tradition, making it an ideal choice for anyone looking to weave their own connection to Scotland into the fabric of their wardrobe.

name: Spirit of Dunkeld
description: The Spirit of Dunkeld tartan is a stunning fashion-inspired design, born from the collaboration between esteemed designers Robert Mitchell and Scott Davie. This breathtaking tartan is an ode to the majestic town of Dunkeld in Perthshire, Scotland, evoking the spirit of adventure and heritage that defines this picturesque region. Woven with love by Lochcarron of Scotland, a renowned Scottish mill, this fabric embodies the rich cultural traditions of Scotland's west coast. Notable for its restrictions, the Spirit of Dunkeld tartan is exclusively permitted for use in fashion contexts, ensuring its beauty remains preserved for generations to come. By wearing or using this magnificent tartan, you are not only making a stylish statement but also paying homage to the enduring legacy of Scotland's ancient heritage.

name: Spirit of Fife
description: The Spirit of Fife tartan, commissioned by Fife Radio, is a vibrant corporate tartan born from the rich heritage of Scotland's historic county of Fife. Designed by Claire Donaldson for House of Edgar, in collaboration with Robert Mathieson of The Kilt Centre, this distinctive design was created to reflect the unique spirit and character of the region. With its distinct warp and weft patterns, the Spirit of Fife tartan is a testament to Scotland's enduring textile traditions. While colour accuracy may vary due to the limitations of photographic representation, it remains a striking example of the county's rich cultural identity, with each thread woven from threads of local history and community pride. This specially designed tartan serves as a symbol of regional identity and unity, its corporate roots ensuring its use is both widespread and deeply rooted in Scottish heritage.

name: Spirit of Morningside
description: The Spirit of Morningside tartan is a vibrant tribute to the esteemed 'Morningside' district in Edinburgh, Scotland's elegant heartland. Designed by John Stevens for Davison Menswear, this Fashion tartan embodies the area's rich social heritage and architectural grandeur. The subtle blue threads evoke the majestic River Forth, its Firth stretching across the design, while the green and heather tones nod to the picturesque Pentland Hills, which rise majestically beyond the district's fine streets and avenues. With its sophisticated balance of colour and texture, this tartan is a testament to Edinburgh's status as a city of refinement and culture, inviting wearers to embody the spirit of its storied Morningside community.

name:
Spirit of Queensland
[AKA] Capricornica
description: The Capricornica tartan, designed by Doug Manger of All Things Scottish, is a vibrant and distinctive fashion tartan, woven with pride for those associated with Queensland, Australia. Originally registered as Spirit of Queensland in 1995, the name was later changed due to a naming dispute with a different registrant, reflecting the region's unique cultural identity. This tartan's origins in the kilt hire industry demonstrate its practical application, yet it has also become a statement of local pride and affiliation for those connected to the Sunshine State. With maroon as its signature colour, evoking the official Queensland rugby football team, known affectionately as the 'Maroons', this tartan design embodies the spirit of Queensland's warm-hearted community and rich heritage, now proudly worn by all who call it home.

name:
Spirit of Scotland
[AKA] Fyvie Castle
description: The Spirit of Scotland tartan is a stately corporate design, woven with pride by esteemed mills Lochcarron and Strathmore, in close collaboration with the renowned designer Michael King of Philip King Tailoring Ltd, Aberdeen. As part of the National Trust for Scotland's extensive collection, this tartan was carefully selected to adorn Fyvie Castle in Aberdeenshire, showcasing the rich heritage and traditions of Scottish history. Its dignified colours - a palette of deep blues, greens, and golds - evoke the rugged beauty and warm hospitality that are synonymous with the land of lochs and mountains. As a corporate tartan, it is designed to foster unity and camaraderie among business associates and partners, embodying the timeless values of Scottish culture and craftsmanship.

name: Spirit of Solway
description: The Solway Spirit tartan, designed by esteemed textile artist Douglas Anderson, embodies the rugged yet enchanting beauty of the lowland hills in Dumfries and Galloway. As an exclusive district tartan for this region, it proudly wears its purple and green hues, reminiscent of heather-dusted moors and sun-kissed hillsides. This distinctive design, now a staple of regional identity, pays homage to the natural splendour of the Solway Firth and the surrounding landscape that has inspired countless generations of locals. With its bold yet nuanced colour palette, the Solway Spirit tartan serves as a vibrant representation of community spirit and cultural heritage, inviting wearers to proudly showcase their connection to this storied region.

name: Spirit of Ulster
description: The Spirit of Ulster tartan is a vibrant and dynamic fashion design, born from the creative vision of Helen Marshall at Marton Mills, and registered in celebration of the enduring spirit of the region it represents - Northern Ireland's storied province of Ulster. This bold and striking tartan is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of its namesake, drawing upon the intricate traditions of Scottish textile craftsmanship to evoke the rugged beauty of the Irish landscape. As part of Marton Mills' kilthire range, this design holds significant honour within the world of traditional Scottish textiles, offering a unique blend of colour and character that is sure to favour those who choose to wear it - a symbol of bold individuality and celebration of Ulster's enduring identity.

name: Spirit of Wales
description: The Spirit of Wales tartan is a vibrant and evocative fashion design that embodies the proud heritage of Wales. Registered to be used exclusively by Dyfed Menswear, a Welsh-based retailer, this tartan's purpose is deeply rooted in promoting Welsh culture and identity. Category classified as Fashion, it is likely to adorn garments such as kilts, scarves, or accessories, allowing wearers to showcase their connection to the land of song and poetry. Designed by Claire Donaldson, a talented weaver with expertise at The House of Edgar, this tartan's technical characteristics are woven into its very fabric - literally. Its unique pattern is a testament to Welsh craftsmanship and tradition, serving as a visual representation of national pride and heritage.

name: Spirit of West Lothian
description: The Spirit of West Lothian tartan embodies the rich heritage and proud traditions of Scotland's West Lothian district. Designed by Kirsty Anderson for the House of Edgar, this corporate tartan weaves together a tapestry of colours that honour the region's history and natural beauty. The palette is a deliberate blend of the council's corporate colours, with green and coral shades evoking the majestic Bathgate Hills and the shale oil bings of the past. A soothing blue represents the shimmering Linlithgow Loch, while black pays tribute to Westlothiana, the world's oldest reptile fossil, which has strong connections to Marjory, daughter of King Robert The Bruce. This captivating tartan design is a testament to the district's storied past and its aspirations for the future, making it an ideal choice for corporate attire that proudly reflects the unique identity of West Lothian.

name: Spotsylvania County Sheriff's Office
description: The Spotsylvania County Sheriff's Office tartan is a distinctive corporate design born from the rich heritage of rural America, with its roots firmly planted in the heart of Spotsylvania, Virginia. This unique tartan has been registered specifically for the Spotsylvania County Sheriff's office, reflecting the county's proud history and tradition of law enforcement service. As a corporate tartan, it is intended to evoke a sense of professionalism, duty, and community, making it an ideal symbol for the office and its constituents. With no designer credited, the tartan's design remains an anonymous tribute to the dedication and public service that defines the Sheriff's office, inviting wearers to proudly embody the values of their local authority.

name: Spring Morning
description: The Spring Morning tartan, designed by the esteemed Aljean of Vancouver, is a vibrant and uplifting fashion tartan that embodies the warmth and beauty of Scotland's springtime landscapes. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority in October 1973, this unique and captivating pattern is perfectly suited to add a dash of colour and personality to any fashion outfit. As a fashion tartan, Spring Morning has no clan affiliation, but its playful and lively character makes it an excellent choice for adding a touch of whimsy to any ensemble, from springtime clothing to accessories. With its carefully crafted design reflecting the subtle hues of dawn breaking over Scotland's rolling hills, this tartan is sure to bring a smile to your face and a spring in your step.

name: Sprouston
description: The Sprouston tartan is a corporate design steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's Borders region, where tradition and community come together in perfect harmony. Registered specifically for Sprouston Primary School in Roxburghshire, this distinctive pattern pays tribute to the town's history and its name, which is rooted in Old English as 'tun' - a farmstead or settlement. The Sprouston tartan is a celebration of local identity and pride, with Ronnie Hek's design expertly woven into being by skilled weavers. As a Corporate tartan, it lends itself to company uniforms, branding, and other business applications, allowing organisations to tap into the unique cultural significance of this Border town, while also showcasing their commitment to preserving Scotland's rich textile heritage.

name: Squash Scottish Open
description: The Icelandic tartan, designed by renowned expert David McGill of International Tartans, is a vibrant representation of the Nordic country's rich heritage. As a District tartan, it pays homage to the communities that have strong ties to Iceland, both in terms of geographical location and cultural affinity. This distinctive design features a palette of blues and greens reminiscent of the rugged Icelandic landscape, punctuated by subtle nuances of red and gold, evoking the warmth and resilience of its people. As a tartan with restrictions, it is reserved exclusively for those who can obtain the designer's consent, making it all the more exclusive and coveted among those seeking to connect with their Icelandic roots or honour the country's unique cultural identity.

name: Sri Lanka
description: The Sri Lankan Scottish Tartan, designed by Brian Wilton, is a poignant tribute to the devastating effects of the 2004 tsunami disaster on the coastal towns and settlements of Sri Lanka. This District tartan was woven not only as a gesture of solidarity with the affected communities but also as a testament to the enduring friendship between Scotland and Sri Lanka, forged over centuries of cultural and economic ties. With its striking design, the Sri Lankan Scottish Tartan serves as a powerful symbol of hope and resilience in the face of adversity, honouring the memories of those lost and celebrating the rebirth of communities strengthened by international aid and support. This distinctive tartan now holds great significance for both countries, reminding us of the enduring bonds between nations and the power of textile heritage to bring people together.

name: SRU Scottish Rugby Union
description: The Scottish Rugby Union tartan is a vibrant and energetic corporate design, commissioned by Chris Aitken of Geoffrey Tailor (Highland) Crafts to commemorate Scotland's rich rugby heritage.
