First woven in the distinctive Johnston Collection, a sample is now held at the authority for future reference, reflecting its enduring significance within Scottish tartan tradition. Originally produced by D C Dalgliesh before being claimed as the work of Geoffrey Tailor himself, this tartan embodies the values and passion of Scotland's national rugby team, evoking images of muddy pitches, triumphant victories, and a proud nation united behind the huddle. As an official corporate design, it now adds its own colours to the rich tapestry of Scottish tartans, celebrating both tradition and modernity in equal measure.

name:
St Andrew Society American
[AKA] US Bicentennial
description: The American St Andrews Societies tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate tartan, designed to pay tribute to the rich history and heritage of Scottish culture in North America. Originally conceived to commemorate the American Bi-Centennial in 1976, this striking tartan was later adopted by the American St Andrews Societies, an organisation dedicated to promoting the interests of Scottish society abroad. Initiated by J C Thompson, with modifications by Jamie Scarlett MBE, this tartan reflects a unique blend of traditional and modern elements, featuring a bold and colourful sett that showcases full threads. By halving the threadcount to reveal the full sett, the designer has created a visually striking effect, highlighting the strong cultural connections between Scotland and its American kinship. This corporate tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage and the vibrant community of St Andrews Societies in America.

name: St Andrew Society Illinois
description: The Illinois St. Andrews Society tartan is a vibrant and symbolic corporate tartan that tells the story of Scotland's enduring connection to the American state of Illinois. Designed by Francis Gillan in 1990, this unique tartan was created to mark the 150th anniversary of the Illinois St. Andrews Society, a philanthropic body founded by Scots in 1854. The colours - blue, red, and green - pay homage to the State of Illinois flag, the Chicago sports teams, and the iconic St Andrew's flag, weaving together a rich tapestry of cultural heritage and community spirit. Today, this tartan holds great significance as the official tartan of the State of Illinois, proudly worn by the Illinois Saint Andrew Society and its members, serving as a tangible link to Scotland's past and a symbol of shared values between two nations.

name: St Andrew Society of Java; Dress
description: The Java Saint Andrew Society Dress tartan is a vibrant and sophisticated corporate design, expertly crafted by Erica Randall of House of Edgar on behalf of the prestigious St Andrew's Society of Jakarta. This striking pattern, woven with a rich blend of blues and greens, pays homage to Scotland's iconic symbol, St Andrew's Cross, while also drawing inspiration from the exotic flavours of Java. As a corporate tartan, it is perfectly suited for formal wear, business attire, and other professional settings, evoking the sense of honour, tradition, and cultural heritage that defines Scottish identity. With its unique blend of Eastern and Western influences, this tartan design embodies the spirit of cultural exchange and exchange, reflecting the global connections forged by Scotland's rich history of exploration and trading.

name: St Andrew Society of Java; Hunting
description: The Java Saint Andrew Society Hunting tartan is a vibrant and dynamic corporate tartan that proudly bears the heritage of Scottish tradition in the heart of Southeast Asia. Designed by House of Edgar, Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., for the St Andrews Society in Jakarta, this distinctive pattern is deeply rooted in Scottish history, reflecting the values of camaraderie and community embodied by the Society. Originally created as a dress tartan for their Highland Games events in Indonesia, this tartan showcases the bold and adventurous spirit of the Scottish people, while also paying homage to the cultural exchange between Scotland and the wider world. With its unique blend of colours and subtle variations on traditional motifs, the Java Saint Andrew Society Hunting tartan serves as a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage in modern corporate contexts.

name: St Andrew Society
description: The St. Andrew Society tartan is a corporate motif that embodies the values of unity, pride, and heritage. Registered as a corporate tartan, it holds no specific connection to a Scottish clan or family legacy, instead representing a broader sense of identity and affiliation for individuals and organisations. Its threadcount originates from renowned Scottish weaving mill, Lochcarron, which lends an air of authenticity to this design. Despite its unclear provenance, the St. Andrew Society tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, with the iconic cross of St. Andrew at its centre, symbolising the country's patron saint and national emblem. This versatile tartan is perfect for corporate wear, adding a touch of Scottish flair to business attire and fostering a sense of honour among its wearers.

name: St Andrew's College
description: St Andrew's College Tartan, woven with precision and passion by Heather Yellowley and Brian Wilton, is a testament to Scottish heritage and corporate tradition. This stylish Corporate tartan was specifically designed for St Andrew's College, evoking the rich history and academic excellence of Scotland's finest educational institutions. Its distinctive pattern, comprising blues, greens, and yellows, echoes the country's picturesque landscapes and cultural treasures. As an officially registered design, this tartan is steeped in tradition and authority, making it a sought-after choice for companies and organisations seeking to establish their Scottish roots. With its unique blend of colour and character, St Andrew's College Tartan embodies the values of learning, achievement, and community that are at the heart of Scotland's esteemed academic heritage.

name: St Andrew's Presbyterian Church Quebec
description: The St Andrew Quebec City tartan is a striking corporate design born from the rich history of Scotland's military legacy and the enduring spirit of community. Commissioned by David Stafford, a renowned designer in his own right, this distinctive pattern pays tribute to the 78th Fraser Highlanders' remarkable victory on the Plains of Abraham in 1759, an event that would forever shape the nation's connection with Canada. The tartan's design is deeply rooted in Scottish heritage, its colour palette and sett reflecting a strong sense of tradition and honour. With its unique categorisation as a corporate tartan, this pattern is now available for use by businesses and organisations across the globe, serving as a powerful symbol of national identity and cultural connection to the storied history of Scotland's military past.

name: St Andrews Bay Hotel
description: The St Andrews Bay tartan, registered by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, embodies the spirit of Scotland's iconic east coast. This corporate tartan, specifically designed for the prestigious St Andrews Bay Hotel, combines rich blues and greens to evoke the tranquil atmosphere of the Fife coastline. The intricate design showcases a harmonious balance of 8 colours, carefully selected to reflect the subtle hues of the Scottish sea and sky. As a registered corporate tartan, this pattern is permitted for use by the hotel and its affiliates, adding a touch of formal elegance to their branding and uniform attire. Rooted in Scotland's rich heritage, the St Andrews Bay tartan pays homage to the country's timeless traditions while exuding modern sophistication, making it an attractive choice for those seeking to evoke the essence of Scottish hospitality.

name: St Andrews Golf Links
description: The St Andrews Links tartan is a timeless and distinctive corporate tartan, carefully crafted by Polly Wittering at the House of Edgar in 1997. This iconic design has been entrusted to represent one of Scotland's most revered institutions: the St Andrews Links Trust, established in 1974 to preserve this historic golfing estate. As a testament to Scottish heritage and tradition, the tartan features a subtle balance of blues, greens, and yellows, evoking the rolling fairways and windswept dunes of the famous Old Course at St Andrews. Now recorded by the Scottish Tartans Society, this livery tartan is an enduring symbol of excellence and prestige, its corporate appeal making it an ideal choice for merchandise and branding, while remaining a fitting tribute to Scotland's rich golfing heritage.

name: St Andrews Grand
description: The St. Andrews Grand corporate tartan is a vibrant and dynamic design that embodies the spirit of Scotland's storied heritage. Registered as part of the UK Tartans Register, this tartan was created by Geoffrey Highland Crafts, a renowned tailor from Edinburgh. While its purpose remains unclear, it is understood to pay tribute to Scotland's iconic St. Andrews golf links, which have hosted numerous prestigious tournaments over the years. The colours in question - blues, greens, and yellows - are said to evoke the rolling dunes, sparkling lochs, and majestic coastlines that make up the dramatic Scottish landscape. As a corporate tartan, it is designed for companies seeking to tap into Scotland's rich cultural identity and sporting traditions, offering a unique and distinctive branding opportunity that will resonate with Scottish heritage enthusiasts and beyond.

name: St Andrews International Golf Club
description: The Feddinch Club tartan is a distinctive corporate design, born from the esteemed connections of St Andrews in Scotland's Fife region. Formerly associated with the St Andrews International Golf Club Limited, this tartan now proudly represents The Feddinch Club, St Andrews Ltd. Rooted in tradition and sporting heritage, theFeddinch Club tartan embodies the spirit of excellence and camaraderie found at some of Scotland's most iconic golf courses. Characterised by its subtle yet striking colours, this tartan is poised to make a stylish statement in corporate attire, symbolising a sense of honour and tradition that aligns with the values of its affiliated club.

name:
St Andrews Links
[AKA] Greenways Marketing
description: The Greenways Marketing Intl tartan is a quintessential example of corporate branding in Scotland's rich textile heritage. Originally designed for Mr Mervyn Campbell, founder of Greenways Marketing, a Glasgow-based company with a passion for golf, this striking tartan was intended to promote the sport at prestigious St Andrews Links. Although the venture ultimately went into liquidation, the tartan has endured as a testament to the enduring appeal of Scotland's iconic national game. Characterised by its bold, vibrant green hues and subtle textures, this commercial tartan embodies the dynamic energy of modern corporate Scotland, with a subtle nod to the country's storied golfing traditions.

name: St Andrews Ltd
description: The St. Andrews tartan is a revered District pattern, steeped in tradition and rich in Scottish heritage. Designed by renowned weaver Robin Elliot for St Andrews Ltd, this intricate design reflects the town's proud history and cultural identity. As one of the few officially registered District tartans, it holds a special place in the hearts of those connected to the Royal Burgh of St Andrews Community Council, which has formally recognised its authenticity since 2003. This storied pattern is now an integral part of Scotland's textile legacy, its distinctive hues and sett reflecting the town's enduring spirit and the proud traditions of its people.

name: St Andrews Management School
description: The St. Andrews Management School tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's oldest university, with its sophisticated palette echoing the noble heraldry of the institution. Designated as a Corporate tartan by the Scottish Register of Tartans, this distinctive pattern draws inspiration from the University's Arms, which embody the values of Communication, Persuasiveness and Courage - 'Aien Apieteyein' (Be the Best) being its motto. Crafted with precision by Dr David Wishart, this tartan is a celebration of the institution's rich heritage and academic excellence. Woven with attention to detail, the St. Andrews Management School tartan embodies the spirit of Scottish tradition and intellectual pursuit, making it an impressive addition to any corporate or professional uniform.

name: St Andrews New Golf Club
description: This majestic tartan design, aptly named after Scotland's renowned St Andrews New Golf Club, embodies the proud heritage and traditions of Scottish golfing culture. Created by esteemed designer Sheila Falconer for Glen Falconer, this Corporate tartan is a unique tribute to the centenary celebration of the historic club. The subtle yet striking colour palette, featuring lighter tones of purple, earth, and green, expertly balances visual appeal with discreet sett visibility - ensuring that members of the club can proudly wear their affiliation. With its restricted designation as official attire for Members of the Club, this tartan design serves as a symbol of exclusive membership, honouring the club's rich history and tradition while embracing modern fashion sensibilities.

name: St Andrews Old Course
description: The St Andrews Old Course Hotel, Golf Course and Spa tartan is a vibrant celebration of Scotland's rich sporting heritage, carefully crafted by Kinloch Anderson Ltd to commemorate the opening of the new Craigtoun Golf Course at St Andrews. As a corporate tartan, its purpose is to represent the hotel, golf resort, and spa, while also paying homage to one of Scotland's most iconic courses. This meticulously designed tartan weaves together a unique blend of traditional colours, carefully chosen to reflect the natural surroundings and rich history of St Andrews. With restrictions in place to safeguard the integrity of this special design, it is reserved exclusively for official use by the St Andrews Old Course Hotel, Golf Resort and Spa, ensuring its authenticity and prestige are preserved for generations to come.

name: St Andrews Queens University
description: This Corporate tartan, known as St. Andrews (Queens University), holds a rich connection to Scotland's storied heritage. Adopted by the esteemed institutions of Queen's University in St Andrews and others, its inspiration stems from the Bannockbane series, a renowned fashion tartan collection of the 1970s. The sett's subtle nuances evoke a sense of tradition and respect for this Scottish town's revered status as the home of Scotland's oldest university. This Corporate tartan serves as a symbol of unity and identity for its respective organisations, embodying the values of academic excellence, innovation, and community spirit that define Queen's University and its affiliates.

name:
St Andrews University
[AKA] International
description: The University of St Andrews tartan is a quintessential example of corporate heritage, evoking the academic traditions and iconic landmarks of Scotland's oldest university. Designed by esteemed tartan house Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this vibrant and enduring pattern has been woven with the intention of promoting the university's brand globally. As the sole registered tartan for the University of St Andrews, its distinctive colours and sett are carefully guarded to maintain the university's unique identity. Formed from the legacy of North East Enterprise Trust in 1997, the tartan has since become an integral part of the university's visual identity, symbolising excellence, tradition, and Scottish heritage.

name: Earl of St. Andrews
description: The St. Andrews, Earl of tartan is a quintessential Scottish heritage pattern with a rich history dating back to 1930, when Arthur Bottomley, a director of Peter MacArthur Ltd, created it specifically for Prince George, the Duke of Kent, who bore the title Earl of St. Andrews. This prestigious District tartan has undergone a remarkable transformation from its early days as a Restricted Royal tartan, initially reserved for the British royal family, to becoming a beloved symbol of the St Andrews and surrounding areas. Its gradual adoption by Marks & Spenser's in the 1970s cemented its status as a cherished regional tartan, worn with pride by locals and enthusiasts alike. With its storied past and deep connections to Scottish tradition, the St. Andrews, Earl of tartan is an evocative and meaningful design that proudly embodies the heritage and identity of this historic district.

name: St Christopher
description: The St. Christopher tartan, designed by renowned Scottish textile company Lochcarron of Scotland, proudly wears its corporate colours with distinction. Created in collaboration with the owner of Japan's beloved St. Christopher Tea Shop, Mr Mitsuno, this unique tartan brings a touch of global flair to traditional Scottish heritage. Inspired by the shop's distinctive branding, the dark green and biscuit hues evoke memories of sturdy carrier bags and warm hospitality, respectively. This versatile tartan is destined for sports garments, home furnishings, and accessories, as well as tea cosies, ensuring it remains firmly rooted in the heart of Japan's corporate identity. Although some shade adjustments were made to achieve optimal colour accuracy, this St. Christopher tartan remains an intriguing blend of traditional Scottish craftsmanship and international flair, honouring the cultural traditions that unite both nations.

name: St Clement of Rome School
description: The St. Clement of Rome School Corporate Tartan is a dynamic and sophisticated design born from the world of business, yet deeply rooted in Scotland's rich heritage. Originally woven in plain weave with an asymmetrical motif, its threads have been expertly reworked to create a striking graphic pattern, with the threadcount doubled to enhance its visual impact. This tartan represents the fusion of tradition and modernity, making it an ideal choice for corporate entities seeking to establish a strong brand identity. As a Corporate Tartan, it is designed to convey professionalism, elegance, and a sense of innovation - perfect for companies that value style and substance alike. Its understated yet distinctive design makes it a versatile choice for uniforms, promotional materials, and other branded applications, allowing businesses to wear their values with pride.

name: St Columba #2
description: The St. Columba Corporate Tartan, designed by Peter MacDonald, commemorates the 1400th anniversary of the legendary saint's passing at St. Columba's Church on the Isle of Mull. Originally registered with seven colours, including two shades of green, this tartan has been simplified to produce a more practical version, but retains its rich heritage significance. The choice of corporate tartan for this design speaks to the enduring spirit of community and connection to Scotland's natural beauty that St. Columba embodied as an 6th-century missionary. In production, the two-green variant #2383 still nods to the original's lush tones, echoing the church's reverence for its patron saint while being suitable for a wide range of corporate applications, from merchandise to uniform wear, and reinforcing the connection between this tartan's wearer and the storied history of Scotland's western isles.

name: St Columba
description: This poignant District tartan, known as St. Columba, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage and community. Designed by renowned weaver Peter MacDonald in 1990, the tartan pays tribute to the revered saint who brought Christianity to Scotland over a thousand years ago. Based on the natural hues of Iona, the colours blend harmoniously to evoke the island's rugged beauty. Initially created to raise funds for the restoration of St. Columba's Church in Groline on Mull, this distinctively green tartan now holds significance as a symbol of unity and charity. Its limited palette and striking design ensure that every thread tells a story, connecting past and present through the shared values of community and tradition that are at the heart of Scotland's rich cultural fabric.

name: St David's Brithwe Dewi Sant
description: The Brithwe Dewi Sant tartan, originating from Wales, is a vibrant fashion pattern steeped in Celtic heritage, albeit with a relatively recent commercial introduction dating back to the late 1990s through Wales Tartan Centres in Swansea. Designed by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, this unique tartan deviates from traditional Celtic designs, featuring odd-numbered threads and an unusual warp and weft combination. Notably, its inclusion in this index underscores the fact that the association with "of Wales" is a marketing device rather than a historical or genealogical affiliation. Despite this, the Brithwe Dewi Sant tartan has gained immense popularity worldwide, embodying the spirit of Welsh craftsmanship and textile tradition. A testament to the enduring appeal of Celtic designs, this fashion tartan proudly wears its 'Welsh' badge, reflecting the ingenuity and creativity of Sheila Daniel's design.

name: St Denis & Cranley School
description: The St. Dennis & Cranley School tartan is a vibrant and distinctive corporate tartan that embodies the spirit of innovation and education that defined Edinburgh's esteemed school, now merged with Cranley School. Registered in 1995, this tartan was specifically designed by renowned Scottish textile expert Lochcarron of Scotland to commemorate the amalgamation of these two prestigious institutions. Utilising their colours from the original school design, the tartan pays homage to the rich history and tradition of Scottish education while also embracing a forward-thinking approach, reflecting the progressive ethos of its namesake schools. With its unique colour palette, carefully crafted by Lochcarron for this special occasion, this tartan now stands as a symbol of unity and celebration, proudly representing the legacy of St. Dennis & Cranley School in the world of corporate tartans.

name: St Eloi
description: The St. Eloi corporate tartan is a unique and intriguing design, steeped in history and cultural significance. Originally registered as Le tartan de St. Eloi des Ouvriers, French for 'St. Eloi workers' tartan', it was introduced to showcase the working-class heritage of France. This distinctive tartan holds a special place in the nation's history, its origins tracing back to the 19th century when French workers wore the bold and vibrant design as a symbol of solidarity and pride. With a thread count tripled for display purposes, the St. Eloi tartan has been carefully adapted from its original form, ensuring that its intricate patterns and rich colours remain true to the traditions it represents. Designed by Viv Sharp in 2006, this corporate tartan is now worn with honour by companies and organisations seeking to connect with their French heritage or promote a sense of community and shared values.

name: St Francis Xavier University
description: This distinctive Corporate Tartan, bearing the name St. Francis Xavier University, is a vibrant representation of Canadian heritage and academic excellence. Registered in 1996 by John Andrea of Canada, this tartan proudly embodies the values and traditions of one of Nova Scotia's most esteemed institutions of higher learning. Originally observed on the internet with subtle variations that may have been mistaken for black, it has since undergone refinement to accurately reflect its true colour palette, a deep navy blue replacing the darker hue. As a Corporate Tartan, this design is suited for use in business and official contexts, yet its origins and associations remain firmly rooted in the rich cultural tapestry of Canada's academic community, making it a meaningful and authentic choice for those who value tradition and heritage.

name: St George's School Birmingham
description: The St George's School tartan is a distinctive corporate pattern born from the esteemed halls of education in Edgbaston, Birmingham. Designed by Christine Woolmer-Tyler, this tartan was created to commemorate the Church of England School, which has been a cornerstone of British education since its inception. As a corporate tartan, it is worn with pride by alumni and staff alike, evoking memories of academic excellence and tradition. With its unique colour palette and subtle texture, this tartan is a celebration of the school's rich heritage and values, reflecting the important role it plays in shaping future generations of leaders and thinkers. Its creation serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of Christine Woolmer-Tyler's design, which continues to inspire loyalty and pride among those associated with St George's School.

name: St George's School Edinburgh
description: The St George's School tartan is a distinctive corporate pattern woven with pride by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, commissioned specifically to adorn the prestigious institution's new Great Hall and Dining Room in Edinburgh. This vibrant and elegant design was originally created to reflect the school's history and tradition, bringing together the rich heritage of Scotland's textile legacy. As a Category Corporate tartan, it is specifically licensed for use by St George's School, Edinburgh, ensuring that only authentic and approved samples are used by the institution. Despite its corporate status, this tartan design still holds deep significance as a representation of Scottish tradition, evoking images of ancient lochs, rugged mountains, and warm hospitality - an enduring testament to the country's rich cultural fabric.

name: St Giles Cathedral
description: The Kenya tartan is a vibrant and symbolic fabric, born from the spirit of friendship and humanitarian endeavour between Scotland and Kenya. Commissioned by Mr Eric Melvin of Edinburgh as part of International Tartans' 'tartans for Africa' series, this District tartan weaves together the colours of the Scottish and Kenyan flags to forge a unique identity that transcends borders. Designed by David McGill, a renowned expert in the field, Kenya is more than just a tartan - it's a testament to the power of cultural exchange and cooperation. With its approved status by the Kenyan High Commissioner to the UK, this tartan carries the honour of promoting unity between nations and supporting worthy humanitarian causes. Its restricted ownership underscores the significance of this design, reserved only for those who have secured the designer's consent - a reminder that true tartan heritage is not just about aesthetics, but also about purpose and responsibility.

name: St Giles Check
description: The St. Giles Check, a quintessential fashion tartan, is an understated yet striking woven masterpiece that embodies the timeless spirit of Scottish heritage. This distinctive design, with its characteristic diagonal checks, was carefully crafted to evoke the revered patron saint of Edinburgh, Saint Giles. As a fashion tartan, it has been carefully considered and registered by The Scottish Tartans Society, ensuring its authenticity and adherence to traditional weaving methods. With no specific designer credited, this tartan's origins remain somewhat enigmatic, adding to its mystique. Its classification as a Fashion tartan suggests that it is designed to be worn with flair and style, perfect for those seeking a subtle nod to Scotland's rich cultural heritage without being bound by the formalities of clan affiliations or traditional formal wear.

name: St John's
description: The St John's corporate tartan, designed by Robert W Norcross in 1909, is a storied fabric steeped in tradition and heritage. Originally woven in cotton for the vestments of his local church in Clarksburg, Massachusetts, this distinctive tartan has since been adopted by corporate wearers seeking to evoke the spirit of community and unity that lies at the heart of Scottish culture. As a Category Corporate tartan, it is worn to signify affiliation with various businesses and organisations, but its true significance extends far beyond its practical application. The St John's tartan represents a nod to the rich history of American-Scottish diaspora, as well as a testament to the enduring power of traditional craftsmanship. Its subtle nuances and earthy tones evoke the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Scottish Highlands, transporting wearers to a world of timeless tradition and honourable heritage.

name: St Johnstone Football Club
description: This prestigious corporate tartan, designed by House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., proudly represents one of Scotland's most beloved football clubs, St. Johnstone Football Club. Originally discovered in a kiltmaker's shop in Perth in 1996, this tartan is steeped in local heritage and tradition, paying homage to the city's iconic Saints team. As a corporate tartan, it embodies the values and excellence of the club, making it an ideal choice for businesses and individuals alike seeking to connect with Scotland's rich sporting culture. While there may be newer versions on the horizon, this classic design remains a testament to the enduring legacy of St Johnstone FC, its colours and patterns woven into the fabric of Scottish identity and tradition.

name: St Joseph de Sorel #2
description: Saint Joseph de Sorel #2 is a captivating District tartan that embodies the rich heritage of French Canadian history. Conceived by the skilled hands of Louise Pontbriand, this distinctive design commemorates the 125th anniversary of the founding of Saint Joseph de Sorel in 1875. Characterised by its asymmetrical composition, the tartan celebrates the cultural identity of this historic district, paying homage to the traditions and values of its French-Canadian community. With a subtle nod to the region's rich past, this tartan is an authentic representation of the District category, proudly showcasing the unique blend of Scottish and Canadian influences that define this remarkable piece of heritage.

name: St Joseph de Sorel
description: Saint Joseph de Sorel, a commemorative tartan rich in history and heritage, was meticulously woven by Madame Louise Pontbriand to mark the 125th anniversary of the founding of the historic town in Quebec, Canada. This distinctive tartan tells the story of a pivotal moment in Canadian history, its intricate patterns and colours echoing the region's Celtic roots. As part of the commemorative category, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Saint Joseph de Sorel, a name synonymous with the province's rich cultural identity. With no restrictions on wear or use, this tartan invites wearers to connect with their Canadian heritage and proudly celebrate the region's unique blend of French and British influences that have shaped its people and traditions over the centuries.

name: St Kilda
description: The St Kilda tartan is a poignant and evocative representation of Scotland's rich heritage, its authenticity rooted in the island's rugged beauty and storied past. As a District tartan, it was originally worn by the islanders who called the remote archipelago home, their identity woven into every subtle nuance of the fabric. Reconstructed from a fragment found in the Royal Museum of Antiquities, late of Queen Street, Edinburgh, and later verified through a sample at Glasgow City Museum, this tartan holds great significance for those tracing their ancestry to St Kilda's unique cultural landscape. While no creator is credited with its design, Dr Phil Smith's meticulous recreation speaks volumes about the island's history and the traditions that lie within it - an enduring testament to Scotland's intricate tapestry of heritage.

name: St Lawrence #2
description: St. Lawrence #2 is a timeless fashion tartan, its beauty rooted in tradition and heritage. As a trade sett, it has been carefully crafted to evoke the rich cultural fabric of Scotland, with its distinctive colour palette and precise weaving technique. Designed for those who value understated elegance, this tartan's subtle tones and intricate texture make it an excellent choice for garments that demand sophistication and refinement. With no specific clan or family affiliation associated with this design, St. Lawrence #2 is perfect for individuals seeking a versatile fashion option that still honours the country's storied past. As part of the Scottish Tartans Society archive, its provenance is secure, ensuring that this classic tartan continues to weave its way into the hearts and wardrobes of those who appreciate the beauty of Scotland's enduring heritage.

name: St Lawrence
description: The St. Lawrence tartan, a District tartan still awaiting its official designation, holds a rich history within Scotland's intricate tapestry of heritage. Originally conceived as a Fashion tartan, this distinctive pattern has evolved over time, with some ambiguity surrounding the precise blue count - a detail that may yet contribute to its coveted District status. Despite these uncertainties, the St. Lawrence tartan is now proudly part of the Scottish Tartans Society collection, having been donated by Mr A Yule in 1963. As an integral part of Scotland's cultural legacy, this tartan represents the enduring tradition of weaving and the storytelling that comes with it, awaiting the official recognition that will cement its place within the country's cherished tartan heritage.

name: St Leonards
description: The St. Leonards tartan is a distinctive corporate design born from the traditional Scottish weaving heritage, with its creation rooted in the esteemed history of St. Leonards School, St. Andrews, Scotland. Commissioned by renowned weavers Bellars/Strathmore, this tartan was specifically woven to represent the school's identity, serving as an integral part of the students' uniform. A testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish craftsmanship, the St. Leonards tartan embodies the nation's rich cultural heritage and tradition. By embracing its unique characteristics, the corporate design caters to the school's values and heritage, fostering a sense of belonging among its members. The very essence of this tartan lies in its connection to Scotland's storied past, where it continues to weave its way into the fabric of its wearer's identity.

name: St Margaret's School Edinburgh
description: This unique Corporate tartan, designed by Geoffrey Highland Crafts, pays tribute to Edinburgh's esteemed St Margaret's School for Girls, founded by the visionary James and Annie Buchanan in 1890. As an asymmetrical design, it showcases a distinctive blend of traditional Scottish textiles with a touch of modernity. The registration notes reveal the intricate connection between this tartan and the Buchanan family, whose legacy continues to inspire the school's students and staff to this day. This tartan is not only a celebration of Scotland's rich heritage but also a symbol of feminine empowerment and education, reflecting the values that St Margaret's School holds dear. Its distinctive character and subtle nuances make it a striking addition to any corporate wardrobe or branding, proudly declaring its association with this historic and prestigious institution.

name: St Mary's Help of Christians
description: The St. Mary's Help of Christians School tartan is a distinctive Corporate design, created for an esteemed institution that values tradition and heritage. Originating from the warp only, this unique tartan was carefully crafted by Barbara Sue Brodie of Aikens, South Carolina, in collaboration with Agnes Boncek, whose expertise added depth to its construction. Notably, the weft lacks a traditional red line, setting it apart from other corporate tartans. This omission is a deliberate choice, rather than a restriction, and allows the design to maintain a sense of distinctiveness while still being grounded in its heritage roots. With its origins tied to a school that honours the patron saint of Christians everywhere, this tartan embodies the values of education, tradition, and community that are at the heart of Scottish culture.

name: St Mirren Football Club
description: This vibrant corporate tartan is a proud representation of Scotland's passionate football culture, born from the iconic St Mirren Football Club. Designed by House of Edgar in collaboration with Macnaughton Holdings Ltd, this distinctive pattern was carefully crafted to reflect the club's rich heritage and dedication to the beautiful game. As a Corporate category design, it's perfect for businesses that share the club's values and spirit, making it an ideal choice for merchandise, branding, or corporate wear. With its bold colours and dynamic texture, this tartan embodies the energy and pride of Scottish football fans, paying homage to a beloved institution with over 125 years of history.

name: St Patrick
description: The St. Patrick tartan is a vibrant and iconic fashion tartan with deep roots in American heritage, yet woven into the rich tapestry of Scottish tradition. Commissioned for the American St Patrick's Pipe Band, this distinctive design was not actually created by Lochcarron, but rather woven by them on numerous occasions. Originally identified as an unregistered design, its origins are now attributed to the USA, where it is believed to have originated. The St. Patrick tartan's story was unearthed in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Dalgety Collection and further verified through a Lochcarron sample. This tartan now holds significance not only for its association with American pipe bands but also as a testament to the dynamic exchange of ideas between Scotland and its North American counterparts, reflecting the enduring spirit of cultural collaboration and cross-pollination that has long defined Scottish heritage.

name: St Patrick's Krewe
description: The St Patrick's Krewe tartan is a vibrant, modern design born from the spirit of camaraderie and celebration among friends. Created by Mark Sullivan for the corporate category, this unique tartan reflects the diverse heritage of its members, weaving together threads from Ireland, Wales, Scotland, the USA, and even sunny Florida. Its colours - green, white and blue, red, and gold - evoke a sense of national pride and unity, while also paying homage to the group's eclectic roots. Named after the Gasparilla Pirate Invasion in Tampa, this tartan is deeply rooted in the traditions of St Patrick's Krewe, an inclusive community that welcomes friends from all backgrounds. The fact that only members of St Patrick's Krewe may wear or use this tartan serves as a testament to its exclusivity and significance, making it a true badge of honour for those who are part of this special group.

name: St Piran
description: The St. Piran Dress tartan, registered in April 2006, is a vibrant and evocative District tartan that pays homage to Cornwall's rich heritage. Designed by Donald Rawe, this distinctive pattern was originally created as a dress version of the #1618 tartan, with its roots firmly planted in traditional Cornish textile design. With restrictions now held by Peter Morton-Nance of Gwethnoc Tartan Company, this tartan is steeped in history and cultural significance, weaving together threads of Cornish identity and artistic expression. Woven with precision by Marton Mills, the St. Piran Dress tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile tradition, its unique colours and intricate design reflecting the beauty and diversity of Cornwall's natural landscapes.

name: Staffa [default]
description: The enigmatic Staffa tartan, shrouded in mystery as its designer remains unknown, invites us to unravel the secrets of Scotland's rich tapestry. This striking silk pattern is rooted in the heritage of Clan MacDonald, specifically the MacDonald of Staffa, whose tartans have long been revered for their beauty and historical significance. The registration notes reveal a tantalising connection between this design and the MacDonalds' own tartan traditions, suggesting that it may have originated as a variation or adaptation within the clan's broader family of designs. With its unique character and silken sheen, Staffa tartan evokes the rugged grandeur of Scotland's island landscapes, from the windswept hills of Mull to the mystical isle of Staffa itself, where the sound of the waves crashing against the shore has left an indelible mark on this captivating textile.

name: Staghorn
description: Bell's Whisky tartan is a distinctive corporate design that embodies the spirit of Scotland's iconic whisky heritage. Registered for Bell's Whisky, one of South Africa's leading spirits brands, this tartan reflects the brand's rich history and tradition. Designed by Will Carter of Staghorn, a company with a passion for Scottish heritage, the tartan combines traditional weaving techniques with modern flair. Originally woven at Lochcarron of Scotland, using a thread count taken from a sample provided by STA (Scottish Tartans Authority), this tartan pays homage to the country's rich textile history. Its corporate design makes it an ideal choice for companies looking to tap into Scotland's iconic whisky culture and add a touch of heritage to their branding.

name: Stakis Hotels
description: The Stakis Hotels tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan, carefully crafted to reflect the hospitality and warmth of the Stakis group of hotels. Registered in recognition of its use by hotel and shop staff, this tartan design embodies the brand's values of comfort, elegance, and quality. Specifically designed for corporate wear, it is an ideal choice for staff across various establishments, from luxurious resorts to retail shops. With its unique colour palette and subtle texture, this tartan weaves a sense of cohesion and identity among employees, serving as a tangible representation of the Stakis Hotels brand in everyday life.

name: Star Is Born
description: The Star Is Born tartan, designed by the talented Aljean of Vancouver, is a stunning Fashion tartan that embodies the magic of the night sky. Its striking black, blue, and gold hues evoke the twinkling stars that have captivated Scottish imagination for centuries. As a Fashion tartan, it was created to be worn as outerwear or accessories, such as scarves, hats, or bags, making it perfect for adding a touch of celestial glamour to any outfit. With its sample registered in the esteemed Johnston Collection, this tartan is part of the revered Scottish Tartans Authority's heritage, acknowledging its place within Scotland's rich cultural tapestry.

name: Starr [default]
description: The Starr tartan is a timeless and captivating blend of blue, green, and yellow hues, evoking the celestial beauty of the night sky. Registered as a Name tartan, this distinctive pattern is reserved exclusively for individuals bearing the surname Starr, making it a cherished family heirloom and symbol of heritage for those who bear it. Weaved by skilled artisans at Lochcarron of Scotland, each thread has been carefully crafted to create a rich tapestry that reflects the Scottish tradition of tartanry. With its distinctive colour palette and subtle texture, the Starr tartan is a powerful emblem of identity and belonging, connecting wearers to their Scottish roots and the enduring legacy of John Starr's design vision.

name: Staves
description: The Staves tartan, intricately woven by renowned Scottish designer Mrs Janice Staves Buchanan, is a deeply personal and poignant creation, imbued with the love and legacy of her immediate family. As a Name tartan, its purpose is to identify and celebrate the heritage of the Staves clan - in this case, a singular identity, rather than a widespread kinship network. Registered by Dr Philip D Smith Jnr, this tartan's significance lies not only in its technical complexity but also in its emotional resonance, bearing witness to Mrs Buchanan's devotion to preserving her family's history and traditions for future generations. Though initially designed solely for personal use, the Staves tartan holds a profound allure, inviting wearers to pay homage to their own roots and those they cherish most.

name: Ste-Anne-de-Portneuf
description: The Ste-Anne-de-Portneuf tartan is a unique blend of heritage and geography, woven from the threads of Quebec's rich history and cultural diversity. Registered as a District Tartan, it reflects the blending of traditions that defined this picturesque village on the St Lawrence River. Established by English and Scottish industrialists in 1902, the community's early residents drew inspiration from their ancestral roots, incorporating elements of both cultures into the distinctive pattern. Weaved from cotton by Leclerc, this tartan celebrates the resilience and adaptability of the French Canadian workforce that joined these pioneers, creating a distinctive textile identity that proudly honours Ste-Anne-de-Portneuf's distinct history.

name: Steel
description: This personal Steel tartan, registered for the esteemed Steel family of Lockerbie, is a masterful rendition of a traditional Scottish fabric. Crafted by Anthony Steel himself, it pays homage to his own heritage while diverging from the iconic King George VI tartan, STR #1985. This distinctive design, imbued with the essence of Scottish tradition, was carefully created to reflect the family's unique identity and history. As a 'Name' tartan, its significance lies in its ability to proudly identify its bearers as part of a distinct clan or sept. With its rich symbolism and intricate weaving, this Steel tartan is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage, where family legacy and cultural tradition are woven into every fibre of the fabric.

name: Steiff
description: The Steiff tartan is a striking corporate motif born from Ronnie Hek's collaboration with the esteemed Steiff, renowned purveyors of exquisite teddy bears since 1880. Specifically designed for Teddy Bears' clothing, this distinctive tartan is steeped in tradition and heritage, evoking the golden age of plush toy manufacturing. Its creation was a bespoke endeavour by Hek, who drew inspiration from the iconic Steiff 'button in the ear' design, imbuing it with a rich and vibrant colour palette that would complement the soft toys perfectly. With no clan affiliations to claim, this tartan is distinctly corporate in nature, perfect for brands seeking to evoke a sense of nostalgia and whimsy in their branding or marketing materials, while also showcasing its unique connection to a beloved cultural institution.

name: Stenhousemuir Football Club
description: This distinctive Corporate tartan, woven with precision by renowned designer Dalgliesh, D C, pays tribute to the proud heritage of Stenhousemuir Football Club, a beloved institution based in Stirling. The carefully registered pattern reflects the club's rich history and local roots, its blues, greens, and yellows evoking the rolling hills and sparkling lochs that surround this Scottish town. As a Corporate tartan, it is intended for use by businesses and individuals who wish to associate themselves with the values of camaraderie, teamwork, and community spirit embodied by Stenhousemuir FC. Note that, in keeping with the club's tradition, this tartan has been prepared specifically for weaving by Dalgliesh's own company, D C Dalgliesh Ltd, ensuring its quality and authenticity.

name: Stephens Dress
description: The Stephens Dress tartan, registered to the esteemed Scottish heritage of the MacDonald clan's patronage, embodies the rich tradition of personal tartans. Designed by Peter MavDonald for Mr G R Stephens, a gentleman bearing Scottish armorial bearings, this unique tartan was created as one of two personal designs (7029 and 7030) for the sole use of the name Stephens. Worn by all members of the Stephens family, this tartan is steeped in the history and identity of its namesake, reflecting the honour and distinction bestowed upon Mr Stephens through his Scottish roots. With its intricate weave and subtle nuances, the Stephens Dress tartan stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish clan culture and tradition, connecting its wearers to a storied heritage that transcends generations.

name: Stephens
description: The Stephens tartan, a personal design created by renowned Scottish weaver Peter MacDonald, is steeped in heritage and tradition. Originally commissioned for Mr G R Stephens of London, who proudly holds Scottish Armorial Bearings, this distinctive name tartan is an honour to wear. As one of only two personal tartans registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, the Stephens pattern stands out from more established clan or family associations, reflecting its unique connection to a specific individual and his storied history. With its distinct sett and subtle colour palette, this tartan embodies the timeless spirit of Scottish heritage, while also paying tribute to Mr Stephens' personal legacy.

name: Stevens
description: The Stevens tartan is a deeply personal and meaningful design, registered specifically for Mark Stevens and his family. As a Name tartan, it holds significance as a unique identifier for the Stevens clan, allowing them to proudly express their heritage through fabric, fashion, and tradition. This distinctive weave features a rich palette of blues, greens, and reds, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's landscape and the warmth of family ties. With its creation, Mark Stevens has been able to pass down his own unique connection to the country that has shaped his identity, while also providing a lasting legacy for generations to come.

name: Stevenson Hunting
description: Stephenson Hunting #2 is a rich, earthy tartan meticulously woven by G.W. Stephenson in 1981 as an honourable tribute to his own surname and those who bear it. This Clan/Hunting tartan serves as a proud badge of family heritage, its complex thread patterns evoking the storied traditions of Scotland's noble hunting grounds. Although not officially sanctioned by the Chief or head of the Family, Stephenson Hunting #2 remains an integral part of the 'a' Stephenson Htg tradition, reflecting the craftsmanship and history of Scotland's renowned tartan weavers. Its design may be distinct from other Hunting tartans, but it embodies the same spirit of authenticity and respect for heritage that underpins all genuine Scottish clan tartans.

name: Stevenson Old
description: This esteemed Stevenson tartan, designed by Miss Elizabeth Littlejohn, holds profound significance as a personal family heritage, bearing witness to the unyielding bond between Charles Stevenson of Glasgow and his American-born descendants. Commissioned in 1980, the tartan was woven with the intention of honouring Charles's memory, who had emigrated to America in 1861, leaving behind a legacy that would be celebrated across generations. While it may not be the officially recognised 'Stevenson' tartan by the Scottish Tartans Society, its unique characteristics and intricate design make it a treasured family heirloom, quadrupling in count with the society's 1981 registration notes, a testament to its enduring popularity among Stevenson clan members and kindred spirits alike.

name: Stevenson [default]
description: The Stephenson tartan, registered in 1975, is a testament to Scotland's rich clan heritage, born from an ancient un-named sett discovered by Jack Dalgety of Forfar and R.C. Stephenson of Dundee. This family tartan was originally mis-spelled as Stevenson, but fortunately, corrected to reflect the true identity of its designers and their ancestors. The colours, closely matching those in the Scottish Tartans Authority Dalgety Collection, evoke a sense of tradition and authenticity, weaving together threads of history and cultural significance. Woven by House of Edgar, this tartan is steeped in Scottish heritage and would be proudly worn by those connected to the Clan Stephenson lineage, carrying forward a legacy that spans centuries and has been meticulously preserved for future generations to honour.

name: Stewart #2
description: This vibrant fashion tartan, registered in 1994, has become an iconic representation of modern American style. With its distinctive colour palette and intricate weave, it was designed to make a statement on the catwalks of New York Fashion Week. As a 'Princess Mary' modification, this tartan pays homage to the influence of Australian fashion royalty, Princess Mary of Teck, who has long been associated with British and Scottish heritage. While its origins may be shrouded in mystery, as it was created without a specified designer, its impact on the fashion world is undeniable. This tartan's popularity endures as a testament to the power of global style and the enduring appeal of traditional Scottish design, woven into the fabric of modern fashion.

name: Stewart Artifact
description: Stewart #1, one of Scotland's most storied and enduring tartans, has been woven with honour and tradition in its intricate threads. This ancient design, categorised as 'Other' - a designation often reserved for lesser-known, yet no less significant, clan associations - is steeped in history and heritage. Though the identity of its creator remains lost to time, this tartan bears the weight of the storied House of Stewart, whose noble lineage once spanned the length and breadth of Scotland. In its subtle variations of blues and greens, Stewart #1 whispers tales of Scotland's storied past, evoking memories of Highland lochs, heather-clad moors, and the proud clans who called this land home.

name: Stewart Black
description: The Stewart (Black) tartan is a proud emblem of Scottish heritage, bearing witness to the storied history of the noble House of Stewart, whose allegiance to the British Crown was tested by the tumultuous Jacobite rebellions. With its sombre black background, intricately woven in shades of blue and green, this tartan design embodies the resilience and courage of Scotland's clan system. Registered with W & K.A. Johnston's esteemed publication, The Tartans of the Clans and Septs of Scotland, in 1906, it is a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Stewart, whose members have worn their ancestral tartan with honour since the 16th century. As a revered symbol of Scottish identity and tradition, the Stewart (Black) tartan continues to inspire pride among those who bear its name, reminding them of their storied past and their place within the rich tapestry of Scotland's cultural heritage.

name: Stewart Blue #2
description: The Stewart, Blue #2 tartan is a stunning fashion tartan that embodies the proud heritage of Scotland's Royal House. Designed by Laird Portch, this iconic pattern draws inspiration from the esteemed Royal Stewart tartan, with subtle nuances to create a unique and captivating design. By substituting light Scottish blue for the traditional red ground and white over-checking, Portch masterfully breathes new life into this classic tartan, making it a fitting choice for anyone seeking to honour their connection to Scotland's storied history. As noted in the registration notes, the weft variation does pose a slight challenge, but this only serves to underscore the attention to detail and dedication to authenticity that defines Portch's design. Whether worn as a statement piece or woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition, the Stewart, Blue #2 tartan is an unforgettable expression of Scotland's enduring legacy.

name: Stewart Camel
description: The Stewart Camel, also known as Lochcarron, is a timeless fashion tartan that embodies the rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands. This majestic design, woven by the renowned Lochcarron of Scotland, is steeped in history and tradition, bearing the iconic name of the Clan Stewart, one of Scotland's most illustrious families. As a Fashion tartan, it is free from any restrictions, allowing its wearer to proudly display this striking pattern. With its distinctive colours and intricate weave, the Stewart Camel tartan evokes the rugged beauty of the Scottish glens and lochs, exuding a sense of sophistication and elegance that is quintessentially British. As a testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, this tartan design is sure to make a statement, inspiring a sense of pride and connection to the country's storied past.

name:
Stewart Cromarty Mss
[AKA] Broun of Castlehaven
description: Not Specified #3, a tantalising and enigmatic tartan, weaves a rich narrative of Scottish heritage and mystique. As part of the 'Other' category, its origins remain shrouded in mystery, yet rooted in the uncertain pages of the Cromarty Manuscript. This treasured plaid, once owned by Mme. Rolland de Maubeuge and her great-grandfather Thomas Brown, born in 1786 at Castlehaven, whispers secrets of a bygone era. The actual count divided by two for display may obscure the full story, but the essence of this tartan remains intact, bearing testament to the complex and often fragmented history of Scotland's textile traditions. With its uncertain provenance, Not Specified #3 becomes a captivating enigma, inviting interpretation and imagination, as we delve into the fascinating world of Scottish tartans.

name: Stewart Dress
description: Dress tartans feature more white than traditional tartan designs. The Stewart Dress tartan is a variant of the popular Stewart Royal design.

name: Stewart Dress; Blue Lines
description: The Stewart Dress #2 tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's noble families, specifically the illustrious House of Stuart. This distinctive sett, registered in the past, was taken from a dress in the esteemed collection of the Royal Scottish Museum, Edinburgh, underscoring its historical significance and connection to the country's storied clans. With its unique combination of colours - blue, green, yellow, black, brown, and grey - this tartan embodies the complex tapestry of Scotland's past, where the boundaries between royalty, heritage, and tradition blur. As a 'Other' category, this tartan defies traditional clan affiliations, instead reflecting the broader cultural legacy that underpins Scottish identity, a living testament to the enduring power of this ancient woven art form.

name: Stewart Fragment
description: This enigmatic Unnamed C18th #1 tartan weaves a rich tapestry of Scottish heritage, its origins shrouded in mystery but imbued with historical significance. Registered from a fragment attributed to Clan Stewart, albeit without conclusive proof, the tartan's connection to this esteemed clan is tempered by the intriguing 'Forbes Bequest' moniker, whose provenance remains unknown. Its discovery has led to its adoption by the prestigious Royal Celtic Society as their official tartan in 2022, testament to its enduring appeal and importance within Scottish cultural circles. With its unassuming yet distinctive appearance, this tartan holds a quiet dignity, evoking the nuanced complexities of Scotland's storied past while awaiting further exploration into its mysterious provenance.

name: King George VI
description: The Stewart, Green fashion tartan is a timeless and elegant choice, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. As part of the broader Stewart clan legacy, this tartan represents the proud history of the Dukes of Albany, who were known for their unwavering dedication to Scotland's nobility. The distinctive green hue, which dominates this classic pattern, symbolises the country's lush landscapes and rolling hills. With its subtle balance of darker blues and lighter tans, the Stewart, Green tartan evokes a sense of sophistication and refinement, making it an ideal choice for those seeking a stylish yet understated expression of Scottish flair. This iconic fashion tartan has been woven with skill and precision to ensure its enduring beauty and versatility.

name: Stewart Mourning Originaux
description: The Stewart, Mourning tartan, a poignant representation of Scottish heritage, bears the name of one of Scotland's most illustrious clans. Registration notes suggest its origins lie with the Clans Originaux pattern book produced in Paris in 1880 by J. Claude Fres Et Cie, highlighting the intricate connections between Scottish tradition and international influences. This clan tartan is a testament to the storied history of the Stewarts, whose legacy has been woven into the fabric of Scotland's cultural identity. While the exact characteristics of this particular design remain somewhat enigmatic due to limited information on its original composition, its significance as a tangible link to the Stewart family and their enduring place in Scottish heritage is undeniable.

name: Stewart Mourning Originaux #2
description: The Stewart, Mourning #3 tartan is a poignant tribute to the storied Clan Stewart, whose rich history spans centuries of Scottish nobility. This sombre yet dignified pattern, registered for the family's use, bears testament to the clan's affinity for mourning attire in the 18th century. Originally designed as a trade version without the exact date known, it is believed to be one of several iterations created by a skilled weaver, though the identity remains lost to history. Within its complex interplay of blues and greys, subtle greens evoke the mist-shrouded Highlands, while deeper hues suggest the gravitas of ancestral legacy. As a poignant representation of Scottish heritage, this tartan design continues to honour the Stewart family's storied past, its very existence a testament to the enduring power of tradition and the indelible mark of clan identity.

name:
Stewart of Appin #2
[AKA] Stewart of Appin; #2
description: The Stewart of Appin #2 tartan is a timeless and storied design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans. As part of the esteemed Stewart clan legacy, this tartan holds significant honour among Scottish families, its distinctive pattern woven with precision and tradition. Designed with a deep understanding of the clan's history and values, the Stewart of Appin #2 tartan features a unique blend of colours that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. With its specific registration notes hinting at an earlier Trade error, this tartan is a poignant reminder of the complexities of tartan heritage, offering a glimpse into the intricate tapestry of Scottish history and tradition.

name: Stewart of Appin Dress
description: The Stewart of Appin Hunting Dress tartan is a storied and prestigious design, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered in 1891 by D.C Dalgliesh, a respected weaving firm in Selkirk, this tartan holds deep significance for the Clan Stewart family, who hail from the Appin region in Argyllshire. The Hunting Dress category denotes its origins as a specific type of tartan worn by members of the clan during hunting and other outdoor pursuits, showcasing their status and connection to the land. With restrictions only governing its use within the Stewart of Appin lineage, this tartan remains an honour to wear for those carrying the family name, evoking a sense of history, loyalty, and pride in Scotland's rich cultural tapestry.

name: Stewart of Appin Dress #2
description: The Stewart of Appin Dress is a quintessential example of Scottish heritage, with roots in the 18th-century fashion of the British Highlands. This majestic tartan was originally manufactured by Peter MacArthur Ltd, but became synonymous with the esteemed House of Stewart through the trade. As a Fashion category tartan, it evokes the elegance and refinement of a bygone era, perfect for formal occasions or as a statement piece in modern attire. With its distinctive sett and precise colouration, this tartan design is steeped in tradition and history, paying tribute to the proud legacy of Clan Stewart and the Appin region, which has been an integral part of Scotland's cultural identity for centuries.

name:
Stewart of Appin Hunting
[AKA] Stewart of Appin; Hunting
description: The Stewart of Appin Hunting tartan is a storied Clan sett, steeped in tradition and heritage, with a rich history spanning centuries. Woven with an intricate blend of greens, blues, and browns, this distinctive pattern pays homage to the hunting traditions of the Stewarts, who have long been synonymous with Scotland's rugged landscape. The subtle nuances of the colours, particularly the range of blues that evoke Balmoral and med blue, underscore the evolution of the design over time, as attested by correspondence in the Stewart files at the Scottish Tartan Society. With its 'Brown' band between the green and azure, this tartan embodies a sense of proportion and balance reminiscent of 19th-century designs, with some speculating that the original brown may have been black, as noted in an early record from The Highland Textile (No.417). As a Clan sett, it holds significance for families claiming descent from the Stewarts, and its registration with the Scottish Tartan Society serves as a testament to its enduring place within Scotland's textile heritage.

name:
Stewart of Ardshiel [default]
[AKA] Stewart of Ardshiel
description: The Stewart of Ardshiel tartan, expertly woven by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a poignant embodiment of Scotland's rich clan heritage. Registered in 1816-22, this ancient tartan tells the story of the Stewart family's history and traditions, with subtle variations from its cousin, the Stewart of Appin. Notably, the red and blue hues are reversed in this design, setting it apart as a unique testament to the clan's distinct identity. As one of the earliest recorded tartans, it has been preserved by the Highland Society of London, offering a glimpse into Scotland's storied past. This timeless design remains a powerful symbol of Scottish tradition, steeped in history and cultural significance, its intricate patterns evoking the country's resilient spirit and enduring legacy.

name:
Stewart of Atholl [default]
[AKA] Stewart of Atholl
description: The Stewart of Atholl tartan, designed by Sobieski Stuarts, holds a revered place in Scottish heritage, its storied past woven into the very fabric of the sett. Originally prepared for the Vestiarium Scoticum, this clan tartan was subsequently published by D.W. Stewart in his 1893 book 'Old and Rare Scottish Tartans', cementing its association with the fabled relic from the 45th Jacobite Rising. While distinct from its Lindsay counterpart, the Stewart of Atholl features a subtle yet striking variation, as the dark blue hue through red is rendered in a deep, mysterious black, imbuing the tartan with an air of mystique and historical authenticity. As one of Scotland's oldest and most enduring clan tartans, this design not only pays tribute to the storied history of the Stuarts but also serves as a testament to the rich cultural traditions that have shaped the nation over centuries.

name:
Stewart of Fingask [default]
[AKA] Stewart of Fingask
description: The Stewart of Fingask #1 tartan is a poignant testament to Scotland's rich heritage, woven from threads of history and family legacy. As one of the few surviving patterns from the Jacobite era, it holds a profound significance, said to have once belonged to Prince Charles Edward himself, who left his cloak behind at Fingask Castle after his stay in 1745. This tartan is almost identical to its more famous counterpart, the Drummond of Perth, but its provenance and sentimental value are undeniably distinct. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds deep meaning for those bearing the Stewart name, tracing their ancestry back to this storied fabric of tradition and honour.

name:
Stewart of Galloway [default]
[AKA] Stewart of Galloway
description: The Stewart of Galloway (Wilsons') tartan is a rich and storied weave, steeped in history and tradition. Originating from the esteemed Wilsons family, who proudly bore the name of Clan Stewart's seat at Galloway, this tartan is a testament to the heritage of the ancient Borders region. Dating back to 1830, when a specimen was recorded at the Smith Institute in Stirling, this design has remained largely unchanged, with its distinctive setts and colours evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Galloway countryside. As a registered Clan tartan, it holds honour among fellow families and clans, and is reserved for those who bear the name Stewart or have a legitimate claim to the title. With its authentic provenance and deep-rooted history, this tartan is an invaluable part of Scotland's cultural tapestry, inviting wearers to proudly represent their ancestral ties and connection to the storied history of Clan Stewart.

name:
Stewart of Galloway (VS)
[AKA] Stewart of Galloway; #2
description: The Stewart of Galloway tartan, with its rich, muted hues evoking the rugged Scottish landscape, holds a profound honour within Scotland's clan heritage. Designed by the Sobieski Stewarts, The, this timeless sett was originally part of a collection of drawings not published in J D Scarlett's esteemed 'Tartan', instead awaiting its momentous publication in the Vestiarium Scoticum. This weavers' version, bearing reference number #410, is a testament to the enduring tradition of Scottish textile craftsmanship, passed down through generations of skilled artisans. As a Clan tartan, it proudly bears the name of one of Scotland's most storied families, and its restricted publication serves as a poignant reminder of the importance of preserving these cherished designs for future generations.

name:
Stewart of Killiecrankie [default]
[AKA] Stewart of Urrard
[AKA] Stewart of Killiecrankie
description: This distinctive Corporate Scottish Jewish Community tartan is a poignant tribute to the rich heritage of Scotland's Jewish community, woven into the very fabric of its history. Designed to support the vital charities KKL-JNF and Jewish Care Scotland, this unique tartan represents a symbol of unity and solidarity amongst those who share a common faith. As a first-ever tartan to be created with a specific Jewish connection, it holds great significance as a landmark in the world of Scottish textiles. The Corporate category ensures that this tartan is widely recognised and available for use by any organisation seeking to express its commitment to this important cause, while the restrictions ensure that the tartan's charitable purpose remains protected. This remarkable design proudly wears its meaning on its sleeve, embodying the spirit of community and giving back that defines Scotland's Jewish heritage.

name:
Stewart of Rothesay [default]
[AKA] Duke of Rothesay #2
[AKA] Stewart of Rothesay
description: The Stewart of Rothesay #1 tartan is a revered clan tartan, bearing the proud heritage of Scotland's royal dynasty, the Stewarts. This distinctive pattern, registered to date back to 1829, has its roots in Charles Sobieski's (also known as Allen) drawings for Vestiarium Scoticum, a seminal work on Scottish tartans. Initially named 'Duke of Rothesay' - an honour bestowed upon the heir apparent to the British throne - this tartan is steeped in tradition and history. As part of the Clan Stewart family tartans, it serves as a symbol of identity and heritage for those bearing the name, connecting them to their noble past. The tartan's subtle variations in tone and colour evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands, while its intricate design pays tribute to the country's rich cultural legacy.

name: Stewart Old
description: The Stewart, Old tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's storied clans, with its rich heritage woven into its very fabric. Registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1819, this iconic pattern has been passed down through generations, its distinctive design evoking the proud traditions of Clan Stewart. Originally designated as the 'Clan Stewart' due to its ancient provenance, dating back to 1745 when Stewarts of Appin and Grandtully were clans in every sense, this tartan is a tangible link to Scotland's complex and fascinating history. The intricate weaving of this tartan tells the story of loyalty, family, and community, reflecting the values that have defined Scotland's people for centuries. Its registration notes not only attest to its antiquity but also underscore its significance as a symbol of Scottish identity, proudly worn by those who bear the Stewart name.

name: Stewart Pink
description: This striking fashion tartan, named after Mary Stewart, Queen of Scots, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's most iconic monarch. Designed by Kelly Stewart of USA Kilts, this regal tartan pays homage to Mary's storied past, drawing inspiration from the Prince Charles Edward Stewart tartan and evoking the romance of Holyrood Palace. The pinkish-hued background, a nod to the Queen's fondness for roses, adds a touch of elegance and sophistication, while the intricate pattern weaves together a rich tapestry of Scottish heritage and tradition. Although limited by copyright restrictions, this stunning tartan is available exclusively through USA Kilts, offering fashion enthusiasts a unique opportunity to own a piece of Scotland's history.

name:
Stewart Royal
[AKA] Royal Stewart
description:
Stewart Royal gained its name from its association with the Royal House of Stewart. 

Although originally unable to be worn without royal assent, the Stewart Royal tartan has become widely known and used - it is a common decoration on Scottish shortbread tins, and became associated with the punk rock movement of the late 1970s.

name: Stewart Royal (Black & White & Grey)
description: The Stewart, Black (1880 Fashion) tartan is an enduring symbol of elegance and sophistication, born from a chance encounter between French fashion and Scottish heritage. This iconic tartan was first brought to prominence in 1880 by J. Claude Fres Et Cie, a Parisian fashion supplier, who included it in the esteemed Clans Originaux' collection. Characterised by its striking black background with subtle blue-green stripes, this tartan is quintessentially Scottish yet unmistakably European - a testament to the cultural exchange that once flourished along the Silk Road of Scotland's storied past. With no restrictions on use, the Stewart, Black (1880 Fashion) tartan invites wearers to channel their inner aristocrat or fashion connoisseur, as its timeless design continues to adorn coats, scarves, and accessories with a hint of 19th-century flair.

name: Stewart Royal (Black & White)
description: The Stewart, Black & White tartan is an iconic and enduring emblem of Scottish heritage, borne by one of the most influential families in Scottish history - Clan Stewart. Registered by William and Alexander K. Johnston in 1906, this traditional clan tartan has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition for centuries. Characterised by its bold black and white hues, alternating rows that evoke the stark contrasts of Scotland's rugged landscapes, the Stewart tartan exudes a sense of solidity, strength, and nobility - fitting for a family whose members have played such an important role in shaping Scotland's destiny. As a registered clan tartan, it holds significant cultural value, symbolising the identity and ancestry of those who bear the Stewart name, and its inclusion in the historic registration notes serves as a testament to its enduring place within Scottish heritage.

name: Stewart Royal (Vestiarium Scoticum)
description: The Stewart Royal tartan is a storied and majestic design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's noble clans. Originating from the esteemed House of Stewart, this tartan has been woven with pride for centuries, its intricate pattern telling the tale of Mary Queen of Scots' complex French connections. The subtle spelling variation, adopted by the Sobieski Stewarts in their 19th-century publication, Vestiarium Scoticum, adds a layer of depth to the traditional Stewart sett, reflecting the nuanced cultural exchanges that shaped Scotland's history. This family tartan, proudly worn by those who bear the Stewart name, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's most iconic royal dynasty, its threads woven from the very fabric of the country's storied past.

name: Stewart Royal #3
description: The Royal Stewart tartan is an enduring symbol of Scotland's rich heritage, its storied history woven into the very fabric of the intricate pattern. Registered with Wilsons of Bannockburn in the early 19th century, this majestic tartan was once a fashionable favourite among Scots, its popularity rivaling that of the finest Highland clans. While the exact inspiration behind its creation remains shrouded in mystery, its association with Bonnie Prince Charlie's loyal followers is a tantalising myth. Rather, it was the grandeur of George IV and Queen Victoria's adoption of the tartan that cemented its place within the British royal family. Initially featuring interchangeably used Blues, this timeless pattern has undergone countless adaptations over the years, with restrictions imposed only by King George V in an attempt to restrict its use - a testament to the tartan's enduring appeal as a symbol of Scottish tradition and heritage.

name: Stewarton
description: The Stewarton tartan, crafted by renowned textile designer Dawn Robson-Bell at Lochcarron of Scotland, is a modern fashion design inspired by the rolling hills of Somerset. This vibrant and elegant pattern has become synonymous with Scottish heritage, yet its origins lie in the picturesque countryside of southwest England. Registered in 1997, Stewarton tartan is one of several fashion designs created for The Check Trading Co. Japan, highlighting the enduring appeal of traditional Scottish textiles to a wider audience. With restrictions in place to maintain the integrity of this iconic pattern, Stewarton has become an coveted choice for fashion designers and enthusiasts alike, evoking images of lush green fields, rustic charm, and timeless Scottish tradition.

name: Stinson [default]
description: The Stinson tartan is a striking family crest woven with great significance, born from the reversal of the esteemed Stevenson design. Created by Robbie Stinson, an American weaver with a passion for Scottish heritage, in collaboration with J. Dalgety Ltd and Forar, this unique tartan tells the story of its namesake clan's rich history. As a colour reversal, the Stinson tartan presents a fascinating opportunity to reinterpret the original design, yielding a fresh yet deeply rooted visual identity. Rooted in Scottish tradition, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of family heritage and the art of traditional weaving, where every thread tells a story of its own.

name:
Stirling and Bannockburn
[AKA] Bannerman [default]
description: The Stirling and Bannockburn tartan is a poignant tribute to the rich heritage of Scotland's historic districts. Originally created in 1847 by Wilsons of Bannockburn, this traditional District tartan has strong connections to the local community, having been worn by the officers and boys educated at the Caledonian Society's establishments. Now recognised as the official tartan for the Stirling and Bannockburn area, it continues to weave a sense of pride and identity among its wearers. Weaved with precision by Strathmore Woollens & House of Edgar, this vibrant design reflects the enduring legacy of Scotland's storied past, from the Battle of Bannockburn to the historic district of Stirling itself.

name: Stirling and Bannockburn Dress
