description: The Stirling & Bannockburn Dress is a richly woven tartan that tells the storied tale of Scotland's mighty past. As a District tartan, it is deeply rooted in the cultural heritage of the Scottish Highlands, evoking the very essence of the region's history and identity. This vibrant design, woven by the esteemed MacArthur & Co., D of Glasgow, takes its inspiration from two pivotal moments in Scotland's chronicles: Stirling Castle and the Battle of Bannockburn. The intricate pattern is a testament to the bravery and resilience of the Scottish people, their clans and communities bound together by thread and tradition. As such, this tartan holds great significance for those proud of their Highland ancestry, serving as a symbol of heritage, unity, and national pride.

name: Stirling Millennium
description: The Stirling Millennium tartan, with its distinctive palette of blues, greens, and yellows, is a celebration of corporate identity in Scotland's rich heritage. Designed by Annie Stewart for Anta Scotland, this tartan was originally created as a promotional cloth to commemorate the year 2000 - the millennium year marked by Stirling Council. The colours, chosen to evoke the naturally occurring blooms of the local flora, reflect the area's unique natural beauty and are a testament to the ingenuity of Annie Stewart, a skilled weaver and textile artist. As a Corporate tartan, this design is now available for use in business settings, allowing companies to connect with their Scottish roots while projecting a bold and modern image.

name: Stirling [default]
description: The Stirling tartan is a majestic and storied design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's most esteemed Clan Society. First woven by renowned designer Tony Murray in 1998/1999 for the Stirling Clan Society, this distinctive tartan was chosen through an online poll conducted by Michael Jex, with the majority of respondents favouring its striking appearance. Now preserved and woven by Lochcarron, this tartan proudly embodies the values and traditions of the Stirling family, whose honour and legacy are forever linked to this iconic textile. As a testament to Scotland's ancient weaving traditions, the Stirling tartan is a beautiful representation of the country's complex history and cultural identity, woven with precision and care to be treasured by generations to come.

name: Stirling University
description: Stirling University #2, a corporate tartan born from the esteemed halls of learning at Stirling University, embodies the spirit of innovation and academic excellence that defines Scotland's revered institutions. Designed by the Scottish Tartans Society, this distinctive tartan is reserved for the university's official wear, proudly worn by students, staff, and alumni alike as a badge of honour. With its unique blend of colours, carefully crafted to reflect the university's values and heritage, Stirling University #2 pays tribute to the rich cultural tapestry that underpins Scotland's education system. As a symbol of affiliation with this esteemed institution, this tartan design stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of knowledge, creativity, and achievement that defines Stirling University.

name: Storrie [default]
description: The Brethwe Powys tartan, a stunning creation from the skilled hands of Cambrian Woollen Mill, embodies the rich cultural heritage of Wales. As one of a series of Welsh tartans commissioned in the early 2000s, this fashion tartan is steeped in tradition and history, yet refreshingly modern in its design. The Brethwe Powys pattern is a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of the Cumbrian Woollen Mill, which drew inspiration from the region's own textile traditions to create something uniquely Welsh. By wearing this tartan, one not only pays homage to the beauty and diversity of Wales but also supports the preservation of traditional skills and cultural heritage. As a fashion tartan, Brethwe Powys is designed to be worn with pride, adding a touch of Celtic flair to any outfit or occasion.

name: Stott
description: Mark Stott's eponymous tartan, registered to commemorate his personal connection to the distinctive Cross of St Piran, is a poignant celebration of Cornwall's rich heritage. This Name tartan proudly displays the white cross that has been an enduring symbol of Cornish identity since the 5th century, woven into the fabric of family history and tradition. By incorporating this iconic emblem, Mark Stott's design pays homage to his own Cornish roots and those of his surname, forging a lasting bond between the wearer's personal honour and the storied past of the region. As a testament to the enduring power of tartan, Stott's Personal is a beautiful expression of family legacy, weaving together past, present, and identity in a rich tapestry of tradition and culture.

name: Strachan (register)
description: The Strachan tartan, bearing the family crest of this storied clan, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage. Designed by Tony Murray in 1987, this timeless pattern was originally woven for the personal use of its namesake, but has since been adopted as a symbol of identity and tradition for all members of the Strachan name. Woven on the finest Lochcarron tweed, with its characteristic weathered tones evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands, this tartan exudes warmth and authenticity. As one of the many clan tartans of Scotland, it proudly wears its heritage on its sleeve, a tangible connection to the history and culture that has defined this proud family for generations.

name: Strakan
description: The Strakan tartan, expertly crafted by renowned Scottish textile manufacturer Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the perfect blend of modernity and heritage, making it an ideal choice for corporate and professional wear. As a Corporate tartan, Strakan is designed to evoke a sense of sophistication and authority, while its distinctive colour palette subtly nods to Scotland's rich cultural heritage. Originally commissioned by Strakan Ltd of Galashiels, this tartan was carefully created to represent the company's values and identity, reflecting the very best of Scottish tradition in modern design. With no restrictions on use, Strakan is now free for any organisation or individual to wear with pride, its unique pattern a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish excellence and enterprise.

name: Strang [default]
description: The Strang tartan is a unique and historic family pattern, carefully designed by Dr Philip D Smith for the esteemed Richard Strang family of Edinburgh. This 'double white stripe MacGregor' tartan is distinguished by its intricate count, pivots, and sett, which reflects the traditional skills of Scottish weavers. The design is rooted in the rich heritage of the Clan Strang, with a storied history that dates back to the 17th century. With its distinctive blue and green hues, this tartan embodies the timeless spirit of Scotland's highland traditions, evoking images of rugged landscapes and proud clansmen. As a personal family tartan, it holds great significance for those who bear the Strang name, serving as a tangible connection to their ancestral roots and cultural identity.

name:
Strange of Balcaskie [default]
[AKA] Strange of Balcaskie
description: The Strange of Balcaskie tartan is a captivating Name tartan, carefully crafted by D.C. Dalgliesh of Selkirk in 1996. This distinctive design pays homage to its namesake's heritage, with a rich blend of greens and blues that evoke the rugged Scottish landscape. The subtle nuances in tone, particularly the lightened green and blue sett, imbue the tartan with a sense of elegance and sophistication. As a registered Name tartan, it is reserved for use by members of the Strange family, ensuring its preservation as a vital part of their history and identity. With its technical precision, reflecting Kenny Dalgliesh's expert weaving skills, this tartan embodies the intricate traditions and storytelling inherent in Scottish textiles.

name: Strategic Staffing Solutions
description: The S3 Corporate Tartan is a distinctive and modern Scottish fabric, born from the vision of Ronnie Hek, its ingenious designer. Originally created for Strategic Staffing Solutions, an IT recruitment company founded in 1990, this vibrant tartan has become synonymous with professionalism and innovation. As a Category Corporate design, it's carefully crafted to reflect the values of business and industry, making it an ideal choice for companies seeking to project a bold and modern image. With its unique pattern and limited registration, the S3 Tartan is a testament to the fusion of traditional Scottish heritage and forward-thinking corporate identity, perfectly capturing the essence of a company that has been shaping the IT recruitment landscape for over three decades.

name: Stratford (Ontario), City of
description: Stratford (Ontario), City of, a vibrant district tartan born from the heritage of Canada's oldest city, has been woven into existence by Jonathan Brown. This District tartan is a testament to the City's rich history, which dates back to its founding by Tiger Dunlop in 1817. Inspired by the Coat of Arms registered by the City in 1991, the Stratford tartan proudly showcases the colours that reflect the city's natural beauty and symbolism - serene Lake Victoria blue, lush parks and gardens green, snowy swans white, majestic red and golden crown. As a nod to the University of Waterloo digital media campus, this tartan design embodies the city's modern spirit while honouring its heritage, available for wear in Canada only due to restrictions. Strathmore Woollen Co Ltd, Forfar, has woven this stunning tartan with precision, bringing the City of Stratford to life through threads of tradition and innovation.

name: Strath Hallidale
description: The Strath Hallidale (Sutherland) tartan is a timeless representation of the rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands, specifically within the district of Sutherland. Registered to preserve the cultural legacy of this beautiful region, this distinctive tartan design features a striking palette of blues and greens, evoking the rolling hills and sparkling lochs that cradle the strathland in question. As a District tartan, it serves as an honourable emblem for those with a connection to this storied area, symbolising a deep affection for the land and its history. Designed by Claire Donaldson of House of Edgar, this authentic design is now protected under law, ensuring that the Strath Hallidale (Sutherland) tartan will continue to hold a cherished place in the hearts of those who cherish Scottish tradition and heritage.

name: Strathblane
description: The Strathblane tartan is a stylish and timeless fashion choice, its origins rooted in the nostalgia of Scotland's rich heritage. This distinctive pattern, categorised as a fashion tartan, has been woven with care to evoke the tranquility of the Scottish countryside. With its trade sett provenance, dating back to 1984 at Gretan Green, this tartan is steeped in tradition and authenticity. While its designer remains anonymous, it is clear that this tartan was designed to bring a touch of elegance and sophistication to modern fashion. Seen on clothing sold at the A74 Motorway Service Station's gift shop, Strathblane has become synonymous with Scottish style, available for those who wish to favour this classic and enduring design in their wardrobe.

name: Strathclyde
description: The Strathclyde tartan, an official designation of the Scottish administrative region, is a modern yet timeless design created by Laird Portch. This District tartan, registered in 1975, proudly showcases the heritage of Strathclyde's rich history and cultural identity. According to its registration notes, this thread count was meticulously verified by the Strathclyde Region, ensuring its authenticity and accuracy. As a symbol of the region's pride and tradition, the Strathclyde tartan is steeped in Scottish heritage, reflecting the area's unique blend of architectural styles, geographical features, and natural beauty that have shaped its identity over centuries. Today, this iconic tartan continues to be an integral part of Scotland's fabric, worn with honour by those who claim a connection to this storied region.

name: Strathclyde University
description: The Strathclyde, University of tartan is a prestigious Corporate design that proudly represents the esteemed University of Strathclyde in Glasgow. Created by renowned designer Dalgliesh, D.C, in collaboration with the University's founders, this tartan honourably pays tribute to Professor John Anderson, the institution's founder, drawing inspiration from the City of Glasgow's traditional tartans. The striking design features a distinctive colour palette that echoes the university's crest colours of red, blue, and gold, complemented by the rich tones of the Anderson Tartan, adding depth and complexity to this corporate pattern. While originally prepared for weaving, restrictions now exist, highlighting its significance as an exclusive representation of the University's heritage. This tartan serves as a testament to Strathclyde's rich history, dating back to 1796, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to showcase their connection to Scotland's iconic institution.

name: Strathdee
description: The Strathdee tartan is a heartwarming tribute to Scottish heritage, born from a desire to create a family legacy for Ron Strathdee's mother's 90th birthday celebration. Commissioned specifically to commemorate her wishes, this Name tartan weaves together the rich hues of the "strath" - the lush green valleys that dot Scotland's scenic landscape - with the soothing blues of the River Dee, which flows gently through the heart of Aberdeenshire. As a personal and bespoke design, the Strathdee tartan proudly bears its creator's family name, serving as a cherished testament to the power of tradition and the importance of preserving cultural heritage for future generations.

name: Strathearn [default]
description: The Strathearn tartan, registered by Wilsons of Bannockburn in 1820, is a rich tapestry of heritage and tradition woven into its very fabric. As the adopted tartan of the Comrie Pipe Band, it proudly carries on a legacy that spans generations, evoking images of bagpipe bands marching through Scotland's picturesque landscapes. With its origins rooted in the 19th century, this distinctive District tartan was famously worn by H.R.H. Edward, Duke of Kent, also known as the Father of Queen Victoria, who sent a sample to Wilsons with the intention of 'dressing' his regiment. Today, the Strathearn tartan remains an integral part of Scottish heritage, its intricate sett pattern a testament to the country's rich history and cultural significance, worn by pipers and clansmen alike in honour of their ancestors and the traditions that bind them together.

name:
Strathgaela
[AKA] Order of the Tartan
description: Strathgaela is a corporate tartan woven with rich symbolism, reflecting the heritage of those who bear it. This distinctive design, born from a committee of Scots descendants in the Chattahoochee Valley area of Georgia, USA, draws inspiration from the American landscape and their ancestral roots. Earthy tones of terra cotta and green evoke the pine forests and rugged terrain of this region, while crimson represents the blood shed by Scotland's brave sons and daughters throughout the centuries. The subtle inclusion of purple thistle, a nod to Scotland's national emblem, adds a poignant touch. This tartan is a testament to the enduring connection between Scots abroad and their Scottish heritage, its design reflecting the blending of cultures that has shaped the identity of this community.

name: Strathisla
description: Strathisla, a majestic District tartan, pays homage to the serene beauty of the Angus glen in Scotland's picturesque countryside. Conceived by the skilled hands of David Cowley and Arther MacKie, founders of the Strathmore Woollen Company, this timeless design embodies the rich heritage of their native region. The subtle interplay of blues, greens, and golds evokes the rolling hills, sparkling streams, and lush vegetation that define the glen's natural splendour. As a District tartan, Strathisla is closely associated with the district of Angus, where it was originally designed to reflect the local colours and character. This storied tartan continues to evoke the values of tradition, community, and pride that are deeply ingrained in Scottish culture.

name: Strathspey #2
description: The Strathspey tartan is a timeless fashion classic, born from the creative vision of Mrs P.J. Thompson in 1976. This iconic Scottish pattern was registered by Clan Crest Textiles Ltd and has since become synonymous with elegance and sophistication. Named after the picturesque valleys of the north-east Highlands, where traditional music and dance continue to thrive, Strathspey embodies the spirit of Scotland's rich cultural heritage. Its intricate design, carefully woven from a palette of blues, greens, and golds, evokes the rolling hills and sparkling streams of the Scottish countryside. As a fashion tartan, Strathspey is perfect for adding a touch of Scottish flair to any outfit, while its enduring popularity ensures that it remains a timeless choice for those seeking to make a statement with their sartorial style.

name: Strathspey Check
description: The Institute of Directors (Scotland) tartan is a prestigious corporate design that embodies the values of professional excellence and integrity, woven into its fabric since its inception in 1903 by Arthur Adinsell CA. This distinctive tartan, registered to the kinship of Kinloch Anderson Limited, was specifically created for the esteemed organisation, The Institute of Directors (Scotland). Its significance extends beyond mere aesthetics, representing the honour and distinction of its wearer within the corporate world. As a symbol of professional standing, this tartan is reserved exclusively for the use of the Institute of Directors (Scotland) to signify their authority and expertise. With its rich heritage and technical precision, this tartan continues to uphold the values of its founders, inspiring a sense of pride and identity among those who wear it.

name: Strathyre #2
description: Strathyre Dress (Dance) #2 is a captivating fashion tartan that embodies the spirit of traditional Scottish dance. Designed by renowned weaver Dalgliesh, D C, in 1996, this Stewart Modern tartan was originally intended for ballgowns and other formal attire, but its versatility has made it a popular choice for fashion enthusiasts alike. Registration notes suggest an alternative name, 'Dancers' Fancy', highlighting the tartan's connection to the energetic world of Highland dancing. The design is steeped in Scottish heritage, reflecting the rich history and cultural traditions of the Stewart clan. Due to restrictions on commercial use, prepared by Dalgliesh Ltd, this tartan remains a rare find for those seeking to incorporate authentic Scottish style into their wardrobe or textile projects.

name: Stuart of Bute [default]
description: The Stuart of Bute tartan, a family heirloom woven with meticulous attention to detail, tells the storied tale of the noble Stuarts of Bute, Clan Chiefs for centuries. Originally recorded in the Sobieski Stewarts' 'Vestiarium Scoticum' (1842), this timeless design has undergone subtle revisions, including a 2013 reinterpretation by Bute Fabrics, to produce a contemporary yet authentic rendition. As the registered tartan of the current Clan Chief and owner of Bute Fabrics, Lord Bute, it holds significant cultural weight for those with Stuart of Bute heritage. The intricate sett, featuring a classic blue-green ground with subtle red tones, pays homage to the clan's rich history, with its evolution mirroring the passing of time and the influence of modern design sensibilities. This tartan serves as a testament to Scotland's storied textile traditions and the enduring legacy of the Stuart family's proud heritage.

name: Stuart-Houghton
description: The Stuart-Houghton tartan is a uniquely crafted, Name category design created by renowned designer Chevalier Andrew Stuart-Houghton KHT. As a personal family tartan, it holds great significance for its owner, representing a cherished legacy and heritage. This distinctive tartan has been meticulously woven with care, boasting a rich, intricate pattern that showcases the designer's skillful hand. Its registration notes reflect its intimate connection to Chevalier Stuart-Houghton's own family history, making it all the more special and exclusive. Notably, this is a personal tartan, protected by copyright restrictions, which emphasize the importance of respecting the owner's wishes regarding reproduction or commercial use. As such, the Stuart-Houghton tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the value placed on traditional Scottish heritage and the significance of preserving family legacies through carefully crafted textiles.

name: Sturrock [default]
description: The Sturrock (Blue/Black) tartan is a testament to the rich history and heritage of the Sturrock family, whose legacy is woven into the very fabric of Scotland's cultural tapestry. This Clan tartan, which has been meticulously registered by the Scottish Tartans Society, is a subtle yet significant variation on the original pattern. The introduction of blue, replacing part of the black stripe, may seem like a minor tweak, but it belies a fascinating story of colour evolution and the passage of time. It is likely that this darker hue was initially mistaken for black, highlighting the nuances of human perception and the power of tradition to shape our understanding of heritage. With its unique character and storied history, the Sturrock (Blue/Black) tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's complex past and the enduring importance of family ties.

name: Styrian
description: The Styrian tartan, woven by the renowned Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the rich heritage of Austrian cultural fusion with Scottish tradition. Registration notes reveal its origins in Austria, with parallels drawn to a prehistoric Carinthian tartan, making it a unique and intriguing addition to the world of fashion tartans. With its distinct marled hues of light and dark grey, this design defies graphic representation, adding to its enigmatic allure. A product of collaboration between Lochcarron's skilled weavers and Austrian heritage, the Styrian tartan exemplifies the blending of historical traditions that has come to define Scotland's vibrant textile legacy. As a fashion tartan, it offers a distinctive and sophisticated choice for those seeking to honour their cultural roots or simply to make a bold statement.

name: Suevia Heidelburg Corps
description: The Corps Suevia Heidelburg tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan born out of the rich heritage of Heidelberg University's student fraternity, Corps Suevia zu Heidelburg. Designed by Chevalier Andrew Stuart-Houghton, this unique tartan was created to honour the traditions and values of its members, who have been associated with the esteemed institution since 1816. As a corporate tartan, it is intended for use exclusively by members of the Corps, fostering a sense of community and esprit de corps amongst its wearers. With its bold, rich colours evoking the university's Germanic roots, this tartan design embodies the spirit of academic excellence and camaraderie that defines the Corps Suevia Heidelburg.

name: Suffolk County NY Police
description: This distinctive Corporate tartan, designed by renowned dyers Macpherson/Dalgliesh, pays tribute to the rich heritage of Suffolk County Police in the State of New York. Created by Hugh Macpherson of Edinburgh and Dixon 'Dick' Dalgliesh and his son Kenny of D C Dalgliesh Ltd., this unique tartan was specifically commissioned for the county's police force, symbolising unity and solidarity among its members. As a Corporate tartan, it is intended for use in a variety of contexts, from formal wear to corporate attire, making it an ideal choice for organisations seeking to demonstrate their connection to the community they serve. Notable restrictions apply, with the design prepared for weaving by D C Dalgliesh Ltd., ensuring that only authentic reproductions are created and upheld the original creators' meticulous attention to detail in capturing the essence of Suffolk County Police's heritage.

name: Sullivan
description: The Sullivan tartan is a striking fashion tartan, one of a celebrated series of Irish name tartans expertly crafted by renowned designer, Scotch Corner of Gateshead, England. This bold, modern design draws inspiration from the rich heritage of Irish culture, with its distinctive threading patterns weaving together to evoke a sense of traditional Scottish roots and Celtic flair. As a fashion tartan, it is perfect for adding a pop of personality to clothing, textiles, or accessories, while its association with the surname Sullivan lends it an air of history and authenticity, connecting wearers to their Irish ancestry. With no restrictions on use, this vibrant design invites wearers to proudly showcase their individuality while embracing the timeless beauty of Celtic tradition.

name: Superfast Ferries
description: Nihon, meaning "Japan" in Japanese, is a fashion tartan designed by David McGill of International Tartans, paying homage to the historic ties between Scotland and Japan. This stunning tartan was originally commissioned by Mr Eric Melvin of Edinburgh as part of "The Four Seasons" collection, celebrating the 150th anniversary of the first treaty between Japan and the UK in 1858 and the arrival of Thomas Blake Glover, a Scottish Samurai, in Nagasaki in 1859. The Nihon tartan serves as a symbol of this pivotal moment in history, where Eastern and Western cultures intersected, paving the way for the enduring friendship between Scotland and Japan. With its unique colour palette and technical accuracy, this fashion tartan embodies the spirit of cultural exchange and tradition, making it an honour to wear and celebrate this special bond between two nations.

name: Susan G Komen 6
description: The Susan G Komen 06 tartan is a vibrant and poignant fashion design inspired by the pioneering spirit of breast cancer awareness and research. Registered with Pendleton Woolen Mills, this distinctive tartan holds a special place in the hearts of those who wear it, as a symbol of solidarity and support for a vital cause. Originally created to raise funds and promote education about breast cancer, this tartan's significance extends beyond its functional purpose as a fashion statement, serving instead as a powerful honouring of the memories of those affected by the disease. By wearing the Susan G Komen 06 tartan, individuals demonstrate their commitment to supporting vital research and initiatives that bring hope and healing to those touched by breast cancer.

name: Susan G Komen 7
description: The "Weaving for Life" tartan, designed by renowned American textile house Pendleton Woolen Mills, embodies the timeless spirit of Scottish heritage in the world of fashion. This striking pattern, registered under Pendleton's esteemed brand, is rooted in the tradition of weaving and storytelling that has been at the heart of Scottish culture for centuries. Its vibrant colour palette and intricate design make it a statement piece, perfect for those who embody the values of creativity, resilience, and community that define the Weaving for Life philosophy. As a fashion tartan, this design is open to interpretation and personal expression, inviting wearers to weave their own narrative into the rich tapestry of Scottish tradition, while also reflecting Pendleton's enduring commitment to heritage-driven innovation and artistic excellence.

name: Sutherland, de Albergaria (Personal)
description: The Sutherland de Albergaria tartan is a captivating blend of heritage and heritage, woven from the rich tapestry of Scottish and Portuguese traditions. Designed by Stephen de Albergaria, this personal tartan is deeply rooted in the family's history and cultural affiliations, bearing testament to their strong connections with Scotland and Portugal. As a Name tartan, it holds a special significance, serving as a visual representation of the family's identity and legacy. With its unique combination of colours, carefully chosen by the designer, this tartan embodies the essence of a long-forgotten era when family ties transcended borders and cultures merged. The Sutherland de Albergaria tartan is a tangible link to the past, woven with pride and devotion by Stephen de Albergaria, and now cherished as a treasured family heirloom, symbolising the enduring spirit of its namesake clan.

name: Sutherland Dress
description: The Sutherland Dress tartan is a timeless and elegant Fashion tartan, evoking the sophistication of 1930s London's esteemed department stores. Originating from the MacGregor Hastie Collection, this classic pattern was featured in iconic retail giant John Lewis on Oxford Street during the 1930s era. The Sutherland Dress tartan's subtle palette of blues and greens recalls the rolling hills and rugged coastlines of northern Scotland, paying homage to the region's rich heritage. As a Fashion tartan, it is designed for wearability and versatility, making it an excellent choice for those seeking a stylish and versatile addition to their wardrobe. Despite its origins, this tartan remains unfettered by specific clan or family associations, instead embracing a broader appeal that celebrates the beauty of Scottish textiles in a timeless and sophisticated manner.

name: Sutherland Dress #2
description: The Sutherland Dress tartan, expertly crafted by renowned Scottish weaver Hugh MacPherson, is a majestic fashion tribute to the region's rich heritage. Originally registered as a dance tartan, this stunning design was specifically created for dancers in the 19th century, evoking the elegance and poise of traditional Highland movement. The Sutherland Dress tartan weaves together a vibrant palette of blues and greens, reminiscent of the rugged coastline and heather-clad moors that define the region's breathtaking beauty. With its intricate patterns and subtle colour nuances, this tartan embodies the timeless charm of Scottish tradition, inviting wearers to channel their inner Highland aristocrat with effortless sophistication.

name: Sutherland Dress; Royal Blue
description: The Sutherland Dress Royal tartan, named after the storied Scottish clan of Sutherland, exudes elegance and refinement, making it an ideal choice for fashion enthusiasts. Originally registered by Tartantown Ltd in this context, it was mistakenly identified as a variation of the authentic Sutherland Dress (Dance) from Scotland, which features two green lines on the white. The erroneous addition of a single green line gives this tartan a distinctive yet questionable touch of 'royal' flair. Despite the lack of clear justification for its naming, the Sutherland Dress Royal tartan remains an intriguing example of the complex and sometimes misinterpreted history of Scottish textiles. Its origins in Vancouver's Tartantown Ltd serve as a testament to the global reach and adaptability of traditional Scottish tartans, inviting wearers to draw upon their cultural heritage with style and panache.

name: Sutherland Hunting
description: Sutherland #3 is a rich and storied tartan, steeped in the proud heritage of Scotland's far north. As one of 'Other' tartans, it defies categorisation by clan or family affiliation, instead embracing its independent spirit and unique character. Originating from the Fort William museum in Argyll, this tartan is deeply rooted in local tradition, its subtle nuances evoking the rugged beauty of the Highlands. With a designer's name unknown to us, we can only assume that it was crafted by an unassuming expert, drawn upon the timeless wisdom and craftsmanship of generations past. Despite lacking the formal recognition afforded to clan tartans, Sutherland #3 remains a testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage, its very existence a celebration of community and shared identity, woven into the fabric of Scottish history.

name:
Sutherland of Duffus [default]
[AKA] Sutherland Lord Duffus Plaid
[AKA] Sutherland of Duffus
description: The Sutherland of Duffus tartan is a timeless and storied Scottish heritage design, steeped in tradition and pride. Originally woven for the esteemed Sutherland family, this distinctive tartan tells the story of a clan with a rich history dating back to the 12th century. The intricate pattern, comprising a subtle blend of blues, greens, and golds, is a testament to the craftsmanship of Scotland's renowned textile artisans. This Clan tartan, registered in recognition of its cultural significance, holds honourable place within the Sutherland family's traditions, reflecting their noble heritage and proud identity.

name: Sutherland Old
description: The Sutherland tartan is a majestic representation of Scottish heritage, richly woven with tradition and history. This Clan tartan, registered by Sobieski Stewarts, The, embodies the proud legacy of the Earls of Sutherland, with its distinctive sett reminiscent of the iconic Black Watch. Although the Society's notes hint at a more complex origins story, the recorded accounts from Gordon Earl's 18th-century directive and Smibert's 1850 observations lend weight to this tartan's authenticity. Featuring bold red and white lines superimposed over a traditional base colour palette, this tartan is a testament to the enduring influence of Scotland's clan system on its fabric and culture. Woven with reverence for the past, the Sutherland tartan proudly asserts its place within Scotland's storied tapestry.

name: Sutherland District
description: The majestic Sutherland #2 tartan embodies the rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands, evoking the rugged beauty and proud traditions of the Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders. As a District tartan, it represents a specific geographic region within Scotland, in this case, the storied lands of Sutherland. Typically woven in lighter shades, with azure instead of the darker blue of its cousin, the Black Watch, this tartan is distinguished by its distinctive subtle green tones, accentuated when kilted to showcase the Argyll and Sutherland Highlanders' iconic uniform. With a long history tied to the distinguished regiment that bears its name, the Sutherland #2 tartan remains an enduring symbol of Scottish identity, woven from threads of tradition, honour, and the unyielding spirit of the Highlands.

name: Suzugamine
description: The Suzugamine tartan, created by the esteemed Lochcarron of Scotland, embodies the spirit of modern professionalism with its sleek and sophisticated design. As a corporate tartan, it was carefully crafted to convey a sense of stability, reliability, and forward-thinking progress - all hallmarks of the contemporary business world. This distinctive pattern is not associated with any specific Scottish clan or family legacy, but rather serves as a versatile tool for companies seeking to establish their own unique identity. With no restrictions on its use, the Suzugamine tartan is free to be woven into fabric, used in branding, and emblazoned on corporate paraphernalia, allowing its wearer to proudly project a sense of modernity and innovation that honours Scotland's rich heritage while embracing the dynamism of the 21st century.

name: Svanholm
description: The Svanholm tartan is a unique and fascinating heritage fabric, created by renowned Scottish heraldic expert Donald Suttie Smith in honour of Lars Svanholm from Gavle in Sweden's Gastrikland region. This distinctive Name tartan is deeply rooted in Scandinavian culture and draws inspiration from the vibrant wild pansy flower, featuring its characteristic yellow and white hues alongside two rich shades of purple reminiscent of the Styvmorsviol pansy. Though a personal creation by Smith, the Svanholm tartan has been carefully crafted to evoke the history and traditions of the region, reflecting a blend of Scottish heritage and Swedish influence that is as captivating as it is meaningful.

name: Svanstrmm
description: The Swanstrom tartan is a distinctive Name tartan, carefully woven to reflect the identity and heritage of its bearers. Created by Justin Swanstrom, Laura Ferre-Middleton, and Jeanne Swanstrom, this unique design tells the story of a personal connection to Scottish tradition. As an officially registered Name tartan, it holds significance for those who have been gifted or chosen this tartan as part of their family's history, clan affiliation, or cultural roots. The intricate patterns and hues evoke a sense of strength and resilience, echoing the symbolism often associated with the swan - a bird renowned for its majesty and adaptability in Scotland's rich heritage.

name: Swallow Hotels
description: The Swallow Hotels tartan is a modern corporate design born from the rich heritage of Scotland's iconic Highlands, woven into the fabric of the country's thriving tourism industry. Created by renowned designer Kenneth MacAulay, this distinctive tartan is specifically tailored for staff uniforms and furnishings at Highland Hotels, reflecting the company's commitment to embodying the warmth and hospitality that defines Scottish culture. By marrying traditional weaving techniques with a contemporary colour palette, MacAulay has successfully brought together a unique visual identity that honours the region's storied past while embracing the forward-thinking spirit of its esteemed client, Swallow Hotels.

name: Swan [default]
description: The Swan tartan is a captivating Clan/Family tartan that embodies the elegance and mystery of Scotland's rich heritage. This storied design, though lacking a definitive origin story, is believed to be an Erskine colour variation, hinting at its esteemed lineage. The subtle nuances in shade and texture suggest a deep connection to one of Scotland's oldest families, where tradition and honour are deeply intertwined. With its understated beauty, the Swan tartan invites contemplation of Scotland's storied past, particularly that of the noble Erskine clan. Although the Affleck slides' true significance remains shrouded in mystery, their association with this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the intricate tapestry of Scottish history and tradition, waiting to be unravelled by those who dare to explore its hidden threads.

name: Swankie
description: Swankie tartan is a personal, family-honed design, steeped in the rich heritage of Scotland's fishing communities. Inspired by the MacIntosh clan, Gillian Kirkwood, of House of Edgar, created this distinctive pattern for the wedding of John Bruce Swankie and Janice, a union between two esteemed Arbroath families whose names are synonymous with the town's thriving fishing industry. This tartan proudly bears the honourable name 'Swankie', a testament to its origins as a bespoke family legacy, rather than a corporate or clan affiliation. Registration notes confirm that copyright remains with House of Edgar, ensuring this unique design is cherished by its original creators and their descendants for generations to come.

name: Swedish
description: Swedish #2 is a vibrant and unique district tartan that embodies the spirit of cross-cultural exchange and affinity. Designed by renowned weaver Peter McDonald, this distinctive tartan was created specifically for a member of Perth Royal Scottish Country Dance Society who wished to gift it to a Swedish friend as a token of their special bond. Not the sole representative of Scotland's Swedish heritage, but rather an emblem of friendship and connection between nations, Swedish #2 is a testament to the rich tapestry of relationships that transcend borders. This tartan's story is one of cultural exchange and camaraderie, making it a poignant reminder of the enduring power of tradition and community.

name: Swiss National
description: The Swiss National tartan is a vibrant fashion design that celebrates the country's rich heritage, carefully woven by Gemma Teviotdale of the House of Edgar in collaboration with Donald McPhee of Kilts & More. This striking pattern proudly wears its colours on its sleeve, featuring bold red and white stripes reminiscent of the Swiss flag, alongside serene blue tones evoking Switzerland's breathtaking lakes. As a fashion tartan, it is reserved for those who wish to honour their connection to this picturesque nation, and its registration notes confirm that it was specifically created to be worn by Swiss Nationals on their national day - 1st August. Despite being woven exclusively through the House of Edgar, restrictions apply, but for those seeking to showcase their affinity with Switzerland, this tartan offers a unique opportunity to do so in style.

name: Swiss Red
description: The Swiss Red tartan, registered under Geoffrey Highland Crafts, is a stunning fashion-inspired design that weaves together the rich heritage of Scotland with the vibrancy of international flair. This striking pattern, registered to evoke the style of the Edinburgh Old Town Weaving Company's online graphic, boasts a distinctive red base colour that evokes warmth and energy, punctuated by subtle darker and lighter shades that add depth and nuance. With its fashion-forward profile, this tartan is perfect for those seeking to make a bold statement with their tartan attire. A fitting tribute to Scotland's enduring cultural identity, the Swiss Red tartan offers a unique fusion of traditional craftsmanship and modern style, perfectly capturing the essence of Scottish heritage in a fresh and exciting way.

name: Sydney Nova Scotia #2
description: The Sydney (Nova Scotia) #2 tartan is a richly woven tribute to the industrial heritage of Nova Scotia's City of Sydney, where Mrs Rod McMullin's innovative design was born. As a District tartan, it proudly represents the city's history and identity, reflecting the dominant presence of Sepco Steel Works, the mainstay employer in this former textile town. The unique colour palette, featuring predominantly blue and red hues with touches of green, is a masterful blend of function and aesthetics, echoing the industry's legacy while also paying homage to the city's natural surroundings. Through its careful balance of colours and intricate patterns, the Sydney (Nova Scotia) #2 tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the city's industrial past and its people's connection to the land that nurtured it, making it a treasured emblem of Nova Scotian heritage.

name: Sydney Nova Scotia
description: This Commemorative tartan, designed by Mrs R MacMullan, pays tribute to Sydney, Nova Scotia's pivotal industry - the Speco Steel Plant, which played a crucial role in shaping the city's economy. The subtle palette of grey, red-orange, and black reflects the plant's significance in manufacturing steel for railway lines, while the off-white hue nods to the limestone used in its production. Originally presented with blue as the primary colour, it has since been modified to reflect the industry's true colours. As a commemorative tartan, this design serves as a poignant reminder of Sydney's industrial heritage and the enduring legacy of its steel plant, now a testament to the city's rich history and cultural identity.

name: Syme [default]
description: The Syme tartan is a timeless and intricate pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, its rich history woven into the very fabric of tradition. Registered as a Clan tartan, it proudly represents one of Scotland's storied families, evoking a sense of pride and connection to the nation's past. Characterised by its distinctive blue and black checks set against green lines, punctuated by white and red stripes, this complex yet elegant design is reminiscent of 19th-century Glasgow International Exhibitions. While the designer remains anonymous, the tartan's significance lies in its association with James Cant's manuscript, which dates it back to 1882, a testament to the enduring power of Scottish tradition.

name: Symington [default]
description: The Symington tartan is a rich tapestry woven from the threads of Scotland's storied history, bearing witness to the legacy of Thomas Dickson, a loyal servant of Lord Douglas who earned the lands of Symington through his valour. This Clan tartan, designed by Paul Symington, is a masterful blend of traditional colours, drawing inspiration from the Douglas family's own coat of arms and incorporating distinctive overchecks of red, white, and gold. With its roots firmly planted in Lanarkshire's rich heritage, this tartan can be proudly worn by all who bear the name and spelling variations associated with Symington. Though weaving restrictions have been imposed to ensure the authentic expression of this design, the essence of the Symington tartan remains unchanged, a testament to the enduring spirit of Scotland's noble clans and families.

name: Tache, Sir Etienne Paschal #2
description: The Tache, Sir Etienne Paschal #2 tartan is a poignant commemorative design, steeped in the rich history and tradition of Scotland's most revered clans. Registered by the Scottish Tartans Society, this version boasts a distinctive green hue, replacing the dark blue of its original counterpart, giving it a fresh yet reverent tone. With no designer credited, it is likely that the Sainthill-Levine firm, either as weavers or retailers, played a role in its creation and dissemination, ensuring its authenticity and cultural significance. This tartan holds honour within Scotland's clan heritage, serving as a testament to the enduring legacy of Sir Etienne Paschal, whose name and legacy are woven into the very fabric of this stunning design, forever binding it to the country's storied past.

name: Tache, Sir Etienne Paschal
description: The Sir Etienne Paschal Tache tartan, designed by renowned mill West Coast Woolen Mill, is a poignant commemoration of the life and legacy of Sir Etienne Paschal, one of Canada's earliest Fathers of Confederation. Registering in 1795-1865, this tartan celebrates Paschal's remarkable achievements as a soldier, politician, and member of the royal retinue, including his role as aide-de-camp to Queen Victoria. With its complex, historic pattern, this tartan is a testament to Paschal's unwavering dedication to his country and monarchy. As part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, this sample serves as a lasting tribute to Paschal's enduring influence on Canadian history, inviting wearers to pay their respects to a trailblazing figure who helped shape the nation's identity.

name: Tait Wedding
description: The Tait #2 tartan is a rich and storied heritage design, rooted in the traditions of Scotland's esteemed clan families. Registered for the exclusive wear by all members of the name, this distinctive pattern holds great sentimental value to the Tait family, dating back to 1982 when Dr Phil Smith designed it for the wedding of Edward Tait. Drawing inspiration from the Edinburgh district tartan, this Clan tartan is a testament to the family's strong Scottish heritage and ancestral connections to the city of Scotland's capital. With its carefully crafted colours and intricate patterns, the Tait #2 tartan embodies the enduring spirit of Scottish tradition, inviting wearers to proudly honour their family lineage and cultural roots.

name: Tait [default]
description: Tait #1, a revered Clan tartan, holds significant cultural heritage for those bearing its storied threads. Created by esteemed weaver Dalgliesh, D.C., this distinctive pattern was meticulously prepared for weaving by his own hands in 2001. The tartan's roots stretch back further, having been initially recorded by Phil Smith from a Dalgliesh swatch in the early 2000s. While no additional historical context is available, Tait #1 undoubtedly represents an important chapter in the family history of those privileged to wear it, serving as a tangible connection to Scotland's rich clan traditions and ancestral heritage. Its very existence underscores the enduring power of tartan, weaving families together through generations while symbolising unyielding loyalty and kinship.

name: Takashimaya Dm Rose
description: This captivating fashion tartan, designated as Takashimaya DM Rose, embodies the essence of modern style with its understated yet sophisticated charm. As a Fashion category tartan, it is likely to be featured in high-end clothing and accessories, adding a touch of elegance to any outfit. Despite the lack of information regarding its designer, one can sense the influence of Japanese design sensibilities, which may have inspired this unique colour palette. The subtle nuances of this tartan's hues evoke the beauty of the cherry blossom season, evoking feelings of serenity and refinement. Its classification as a Fashion tartan means that it is designed to be versatile and chic, suitable for everyday wear, formal events, or simply adding a pop of personality to an ensemble.

name: Takla Makan (Red)
description: Takla Makan (Red) is a striking, six-colour tartan that has traversed centuries and continents to find its way onto our needles. Registration notes reveal that this ancient design originates from the 6th century BC in Qizilchoqa, near Hami in China, where it was worn by nomadic tribes on ceremonial garments. The Takla Makan pattern is a poignant reminder of the rich cultural exchange between East and West, with threads of Chinese silk woven into the fabric of Scottish heritage. This 'Other' category tartan defies traditional clan affiliations, instead embracing its status as an enigmatic relic from a bygone era, much like Elizabeth Barber's groundbreaking discovery in her book 'The Mummies of Urumchi'. Noteably, some thread count issues are present in this tartan, suggesting careful handling is required to preserve the integrity of this extraordinary textile.

name: Takla Makan #2
description: The Takla Makan #2 tartan is an enigmatic and captivating design, born from the ancient burial site of Qizilchoqa near Hami in China. This Other tartan is a testament to the Silk Road's rich cultural heritage, with its unique patterns reflecting the blending of Chinese and Central Asian influences. As noted by Elizabeth Barber in her book 'The Mummies of Urumchi', this tartan was discovered on a mummy, highlighting its significance as an authentic piece of ancient textile history. Its origins date back to the 1st millennium BC, during the time of the Han Dynasty. With no specified designer credited, this tartan stands as a tribute to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of long-lost cultures, inviting wearers to connect with the rich traditions of the Silk Road.

name: Talisman
description: The Talisman tartan, a fashion masterpiece designed by Strathmore Woollen Company Ltd, is a captivating blend of rich heritage and modern style. Inspired by an old trade sett from Strathmore Woollens in 1981, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the region's rich textile history while forging its own path. With its similarities to the iconic Royal Stewart tartan, Talisman is sure to turn heads with its unique charm. Registration notes suggest a strong connection to Scottish cultural tradition, evoking images of the rugged Highlands and the storied past of Scotland's weavers. Perfect for fashion enthusiasts and those looking to add a touch of authenticity to their wardrobe, the Talisman tartan offers a stylish way to honour the country's heritage.

name: Talladale
description: The Talladale tartan is a striking fashion variation of the esteemed Black Watch 'b' pattern, crafted by the skilled designers at West Coast Woolen Mill. This stunning design is rooted in Scotland's rich heritage and is deeply connected to the storied history of the Black Watch Regiment. As a registered fashion tartan, it holds significant cultural significance, evoking the proud traditions of Scottish military heritage. With its distinctive black-on-blue tones, reminiscent of the rugged Highlands landscape, Talladale exudes a sense of timeless elegance and sophistication, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to add a touch of Scottish flair to their wardrobe.

name: Tam O'Shanter Inn (Glendale)
description: The Ballater tartan is a stylish and elegant fashion tartan that has captured the hearts of many. Registered in 1963, this distinctive sett was discovered by DC Stewart at Tam O'Shanter Inn, Glendale, CA, where it had been carefully preserved for generations. As a fashion tartan, the Ballater design exudes sophistication and refinement, making it perfect for adding a touch of Scottish heritage to any outfit. With no specific clan affiliation, this tartan's beauty lies in its versatility, allowing wearers to don it with pride as a tribute to Scotland's rich cultural heritage. The sett's origins, though unattributed to a particular family or community, are still steeped in tradition and nostalgia, evoking memories of rural Scottish landscapes and the warmth of Scottish hospitality.

name:
Tara
[AKA] Murphy #2
[AKA] O'Keefe #2
description: The Murphy/Tara tartan is a richly woven thread in the intricate tapestry of Scottish heritage, its origins shrouded in mystery until recently unearthed. Once believed to be a variant of MacLean of Duart, this District tartan is now understood to have been recorded under the name 'Murphy' in an 1880 publication, only later to be renamed 'Tara'. While its exact provenance may remain unclear, its significance as a distinct and unique tartan design is undeniable. With its carefully balanced colour palette, influenced by both Scottish and Irish traditions, the Murphy/Tara tartan embodies the complexities of cultural identity and the enduring legacy of Scotland's ancient clans. Its registration notes serve as a testament to the meticulous record-keeping of tartan enthusiasts, ensuring that this distinctive pattern remains alive for generations to come.

name: Tartan Army Kirkcaldy
description: The Kirkcaldy Tartan Army, designed by esteemed weaver Kirsty Anderson, embodies the spirit of unity and civic pride. This corporate tartan was registered to represent the municipality of Kirkcaldy in Fife, Scotland, symbolising the town's rich heritage and community values. With its bold, modern colour palette and distinctive sett, this tartan pays tribute to the city's industrial past and its people's unwavering commitment to their honourable institution – the Royal Burgh of Kirkcaldy. As a corporate tartan, it is perfect for use in business attire, merchandise, or as a symbol of civic pride, allowing individuals and organisations to proudly showcase their connection to this charming Scottish town.

name:
Tartan Army
[AKA] Direach mars Spors
description: The Tartan Army, named after Scotland's revered sporting fans, embodies the country's passion for football with pride. Created by Keith Lumsden, this corporate tartan has become an iconic symbol of Scottish sport supporters' unity, originating from a modified Royal Stewart pattern infused with the rich heritage of the Black Watch. First unveiled at the 1998 World Cup, where Scotland made a memorable appearance, the Tartan Army's significance extends beyond its association with football, representing the nation's collective honour and centre-stage performances on the world stage. Today, this distinctive tartan is worn by supporters worldwide, reflecting Scotland's unbridled enthusiasm for the beautiful game and their loyal dedication to the Scottish national team.

name: Tartan Army Whisky
description: Tartan Army Whisky is a bold and dynamic corporate tartan, born from the desire to evoke the spirit of Scotland's national pride and its iconic whisky industry. Designed by Protègé International, this striking pattern is specifically crafted for use in marketing materials and branding for Tartan Army, a renowned Scotch whisky. This limited-edition tartan showcases a rich, dark blue (or "black") colour scheme, punctuated by bold, golden yellow stripes that evoke the warmth of a fine dram. The overall effect is one of confidence, sophistication, and Celtic flair - perfect for a brand seeking to establish itself as a force to be reckoned with in the world of whisky. By tapping into Scotland's rich heritage, Tartan Army Whisky embodies the values of tradition, quality, and passion that are at the heart of this iconic national symbol.

name: Tartan de Longueuil
description: The Tartan de Longueuil, woven with precision on a traditional 36-inch Leclerc Fanny loom, pays homage to the rich heritage of Quebec's City of Longueuil. Designed by Marie-France Bolduc Quirion and Marthe Roy, members of the Cercle de Fermieres de Longueuil, this District tartan commemorates the city's 350th anniversary and draws inspiration from its coat of arms and surrounding municipalities' symbols. The subtle palette, featuring blue, yellow, green, and black, reflects the tranquility of life by the River Lawrence, the richness of local farmlands, the municipality's determination for international recognition, and the wealth of its storied history. As a testament to the district's unique identity, this tartan is an important part of Longueuil's cultural fabric, weaving together tradition, community, and local pride.

name: Tartan Tangerine
description: The vibrant Tartan Tangerine is a dynamic corporate tartan, carefully crafted by renowned designer Donald Suttie to represent the IT company Tartan Tangerine Ltd based in Derby, England. This energetic and youthful design, registered in 2002, is a bold statement of innovation and forward-thinking, reflecting the company's commitment to embracing cutting-edge technology. With its distinctive tangerine hues and intricate weaving pattern, this tartan is set to stand out in the corporate world, symbolising energy, creativity, and progress. Notable restrictions apply to ensure its use as part of the company's logo and trademark, but for those who secure the right to wear it, Tartan Tangerine promises to add a splash of modernity and flair to any outfit or branding.

name: Tartan TV
description: Incorporating the vibrancy of Scotland's rich heritage, the House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd.- designed Tartan TV is a distinctive Corporate tartan, expertly woven to reflect the growing presence of Scottish media on global screens. Originally registered to promote the launch of the Aberdeen-based 'Tartan TV' production company, which specialised in producing magazine programmes for international audiences, this bold and modern tartan takes its cue from the country's storied past while embracing the dynamism of the digital age. With its unique colour palette and carefully crafted pattern, Tartan TV embodies the vision and innovative spirit of Scotland's thriving media sector, inviting wearers to showcase their connection to this rapidly expanding industry.

name: Tasmania State
description: The Tasmanian tartan is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Australia's southernmost state, woven from the very fabric of Scotland itself. Designed by Isabella Lamont Shorrock, a Scottish-born weaver with a deep connection to Tasmania, this District tartan tells the story of the region's unique landscapes and native flora. The subtle palette of blues, greens, and yellows evokes the mist-shrouded highlands, the rust-red soils, and the majestic blue gum trees that dot the Tasmanian wilderness. Recognised as the official state tartan in 1999, this distinctive design is a celebration of Tasmania's Scottish roots and its enduring connection to the land it now calls home, forever woven into the very essence of its identity.

name: Tau-Taurini
description: The Tau-Taurini tartan is a poignant tribute to the ancestral heritage of its wearer, specifically those bearing the surname Taurini. This unique name tartan, registered by Don Bricker, tells the story of his Celtic roots, tracing back to the ancient region of Taurini in north-west Italy, now part of Piedmont Canton. The 12th marker on his DNA indicates a connection to this Keltic country, and thus, the tartan has been reserved for those who can claim this noble ancestry. This intricate design weaves together a rich tapestry of symbolism, incorporating shades of blue, gold, red, white, brown, green, purple, and white, evoking the landscapes, flags, and traditions of Bricker's ancestors' former homes in Italy, Switzerland, Alsace, and Germany. As a badge of honour, the Tau-Taurini tartan proudly asserts its bearer's connection to this storied heritage, making it a treasured symbol of family identity and cultural heritage for those fortunate enough to claim their place within this noble tradition.

name: Taylor Dress
description: The Taylor Dress tartan is a vibrant, fashion-forward design steeped in tradition and heritage. Originating from the 'Arisaidh' designed by Col. Cameron Taylor for his wife circa 1965, this dress tartan has been registered with the Scottish Tartans Society as one of Hugh MacPherson's creations, intended for informal occasions such as dancing. Characterised by its distinctive colour changes and conventional pattern, this tartan is a quintessential example of Scotland's rich textile heritage. While some variations may exist, including a pink-tinged rendition by Dalgliesh in 1983, the core essence of the Taylor Dress remains an evocative blend of traditional Scottish craftsmanship and modern flair, embodying the spirit of Scotland's sartorial traditions.

name: Taylor [default]
description: The Taylor tartan, with its distinctive double black lines, tells a rich story of heritage and tradition. Designed by the esteemed duo Miss Margaret MacDougall and Lt.Col I.B. Cameron Taylor in 1955, this Clan/Family tartan is steeped in history and symbolism. The twin black outlines are said to evoke the Black Tailor, a legendary figure who embodied the artisanal skill of traditional Scottish weaving. The tartan's connection to the Cameron clan, particularly that of Lochiel, adds depth to its significance, with some interpretation suggesting a possible link to the 17th-century warrior Taillear dubh na Tuaighe, or Black Taylor of the Axe. This remarkable design has been recognised by the Cameron of Lochiel and is now a treasured part of Scotland's cultural heritage, its beauty and craftsmanship continuing to inspire generations.

name: Tayside Police
description: The Tayside Police tartan is a distinct and meaningful corporate tartan, bearing the badge of authority and tradition worn by members of the force and the esteemed Tayside Police Pipe Band. Registered in 2003, this bold and striking design was created by serving officers Grant Edward, Lindsay Ellis, and Pipe Major Terry Reid, who poured their dedication and passion into its creation. The tartan's significance extends beyond its corporate use, serving as a tangible link to the rich heritage of Scotland's law enforcement community. Weaving master Marton Mills brought this vision to life, imbuing the design with technical precision and authenticity. Now proudly worn by those in favour of the Tayside Police, this tartan remains an honourable symbol of service, unity, and tradition.

name: Teall [default]
description: The Teallach tartan is a deeply personal and meaningful design, registered as a Clan tartan in honour of its creator's family heritage. Born from the vision of Dr Gordon Teall, a renowned expert in Scottish tartans, this distinctive pattern reflects the rich cultural traditions of Scotland's Highlands. With a subtle blend of blues, greens, and yellows, evoking the rugged landscapes and heather-covered moors that cradle many Scottish clans, the Teallach tartan pays tribute to Dr Teall's ancestral roots. As a Clan tartan, it is reserved for members of the Teall family and those who have been honoured by its registration, serving as a symbol of identity, heritage, and tradition.

name: Teirney
description: The Teirney tartan is a stunning example of Scottish heritage woven into fashion, originating from a series of Irish name tartans expertly crafted by Scotch Corner, an accomplished textile designer from Gateshead, England. As part of this esteemed collection, the Teirney tartan holds significant cultural value, paying homage to the rich traditions of Ireland's ancient naming practices. While not restricted for clan affiliation, this fashion tartan is instead designed to evoke a sense of elegance and sophistication, perfect for dressing up or adding a touch of Irish charm to any outfit. With its unique characteristics and historical context, the Teirney tartan serves as a beautiful testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile traditions in modern fashion.

name: Templar GP USA
description: The Templar Grand Priory USA tartan is a unique and storied design, born from the vision of esteemed tartan designer Douglass Talley, specifically for the noble Order of Templars in the United States. This corporate tartan holds profound historical significance, as it pays homage to the ancient chivalric order that once safeguarded Christendom's sacred places during the Crusades. As an exclusive designation, the Templar Grand Priory USA tartan serves as a badge of honour for its wearers, symbolising their lineage and connection to this storied brotherhood. With restrictions in place to ensure its use is reserved only for members of the Order in the USA, this tartan represents a cherished thread in the rich tapestry of American chivalry, weaving together the traditions of centuries past with the modern-day pursuit of virtue and service.

name: Tenmaya Check
description: The Tenmaya Check is a captivating Fashion tartan, born in Scotland's rich weaving heritage and destined for international appeal. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority in 1996, this vibrant design was originally commissioned by Tenmaya Department Store Ltd in Japan to promote British textiles. Designed by Lochcarron of Scotland, its unique character was brought to life by skilled weaver Archie Snmall from Selkirk. The tartan's distinctive check pattern is a testament to the skill and craftsmanship of Scotland's textile artisans, while its origins in Japan reflect the dynamic cultural exchange that has long shaped the country's design heritage. With its bold colour palette and striking texture, the Tenmaya Check is a truly modern Scottish tartan, poised to make a lasting impression on fashion enthusiasts worldwide.

name: Tennant #2 (Personal)
description: The Tennent from Strathaven tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Tennent clan, woven with reverence for their heritage and history. Authenticated by Geoffrey Highland Crafts as a Name tartan, it embodies the proud traditions of the Avondale region, where its colours evoke the land's rich symbolism: red, representing the bloodline of the Tennents; green, honouring the fertile pastures that sustained them; blue, paying tribute to the Avon's life-giving waters; and white, invoking the heather's promise of good fortune. This tartan was specially authorised by Mr Mungo Jamie Tennent in memory of his father, William Prentice Tennent, and all those who have come before him, ensuring its continued relevance and respect for generations to come, as a poignant reminder of Scotland's storied past.

name: Tennant Yules
description: The Tennant tartan is a richly woven family heritage, passed down through generations of the esteemed Lord Glenconner's lineage, who descended from John Tennant of Blairston in 1635. This distinctive sett originated from The Scotch House in Knightsbridge, where it was first spotted, and is believed to have been adopted by a branch of the Tennants due to its resemblance to MacDuff, although some notes suggest an alternative reason for its adoption, possibly stemming from similarities with the MacDuff Hunting tartan. Interestingly, this design also has roots in Brora, where a kilt material was woven around 1953, featuring a different sett altogether. Notably, the original threadcount is doubled here, and as such, no restrictions are stated on its use by members of the Tennant family or those with a legitimate connection to the clan.

name: Tennant [default]
description: The Tennant #2 tartan is a proud representation of Scotland's rich clan heritage, with its origins rooted in the esteemed family of Lord Glenconner. This distinctive tartan was designed by Captain James Tennant, who sought to establish a unique identity for his own name and that of his lineage. By referencing the MacGregor-Hastie collection, it becomes clear that this design is an integral part of Scotland's cultural tapestry, woven with threads of history and tradition. As a Clan tartan, the Tennant #2 holds honour at its core, signifying the values and loyalty embodied by Captain Tennant himself, who boldly declared his intention to create a distinctive tartan for his family. The subtle lightening of blue in the sett adds nuance to this already striking design, inviting wearers to pay homage to Scotland's storied past while embracing their own heritage with pride.

name: Tennessee State
description: This esteemed District tartan, officially designated as the state tartan of Tennessee on April 7, 1999, pays homage to the Volunteer State's rich heritage and scenic beauty. Crafted with precision, the vibrant colours of Green (representing Agriculture), Blue (symbolising the majestic Smoky Mountains), Purple (honouring the Iris, Tennessee's state flower), Red (commemorating the sacrifices of veterans and pioneering settlers), and White ( embodying the state's three grand divisions), this tartan embodies the very essence of Tennessee's history and identity. Inspired by the Heart of Tennessee Scottish Celebration's initiative, this stunning design not only reflects the state's proud heritage but also serves as a lasting tribute to its people and landscapes, forever woven into the fabric of the Volunteer State's traditions.

name: Tennessee Volunteer
description: The Tennessee Volunteer tartan is a vibrant and distinctive corporate tartan born from a collaborative effort between University of Tennessee students and alumni, who came together to create a unique and iconic fabric to represent their esteemed institution. With its bold colour palette and modern design, this tartan embodies the spirit of collegiate tradition and community pride. Unveiled at the prestigious European Splendor gala in 2013, following a nationwide vote among students and alumni, the Tennessee Volunteer tartan has become a symbol of UT's entrepreneurial flair and innovative spirit, proudly worn by those who favour its bold and eclectic charm.

name: Tennessee
description: The Tennessee tartan is a vibrant and distinctive district tartan that celebrates the rich heritage of the region in which it originated. Originally created for the Scottish Celebration by the Heart of Tennessee, this tartan was specifically designed to represent the state's history, culture, and natural beauty. As one of only 13 official state tartans in Scotland, the Tennessee tartan holds a unique place within the world of traditional textiles. Its bold and colourful design is sure to evoke the spirit of the American South, with its deep reds, blues, and greens evoking the rolling hills and lush landscapes that crisscross the state. This tartan is an honour to Scotland's tartan tradition, serving as a celebration of cross-cultural exchange and a testament to the enduring power of heritage and identity.

name: Terre D'Ecosse #2
description: Terre De'Ecosse, meaning "Land of Scotland" in French, is a corporate tartan designed by renowned Scottish textile expert, Lochcarron of Scotland. This distinctive tartan was specifically created to evoke the country's rich heritage and rugged landscape, transporting those who wear it to the rolling hills and heather-covered moors that cradle the nation's history and culture. With its unique weave of 12 dyes on 16 yarns, this corporate tartan is a celebration of Scottish tradition and values, perfect for organisations seeking to project a sense of heritage and national pride. While there are no restrictions associated with this registration, which was granted in March 2000, Terre De'Ecosse remains an excellent choice for any company looking to establish its roots in Scottish business and community.

name: Terre D'Ecosse
description: Terre D'Ecosse, a majestic fashion tartan, embodies the rugged beauty of Scotland's unspoiled landscapes. Registered with Lochcarron, one of Scotland's oldest and most prestigious weavers, this tartan is a testament to the country's rich textile heritage. The Terre D'Ecosse pattern, featuring a predominantly green and brown colour scheme, evokes the rolling hills and heather-covered moors that stretch as far as the eye can see. As a fashion tartan, it lends itself perfectly to creating stylish and sophisticated garments, from tweed jackets to kilts, perfect for making a statement at formal events or adding a touch of Scottish flair to everyday wear. With its roots firmly planted in Scotland's natural beauty, Terre D'Ecosse is a timeless and versatile design that embodies the country's enduring spirit of tradition and innovation.

name: Terry [default]
description: The Terry tartan is a storied clan motif, woven with deep roots in Scottish heritage, despite its American origins. Designed by Thomas Terry, an Illinois native who proudly claims his tartan as a family legacy, this tartan was formally registered with the Scottish Tartans Society in 1993, marking it as an officially sanctioned part of Scotland's rich tapestry of tradition. As such, the Terry tartan is a symbol of clan identity and familial honour, open to all who bear the surname Terry, allowing them to proudly wear their heritage on their sleeve. With its distinctive colour palette and intricate weave, this tartan embodies the warmth and resilience of Scottish culture, inviting wearers to connect with their ancestors and forge a lasting bond with their heritage.

name: Teviotdale District
description: The historic Teviotdale tartan, designed by renowned weaver Alistair Buchan, is a poignant reflection of the rugged beauty of Scotland's Scottish Borders. This District tartan, registered in 2001, pays tribute to the picturesque valley of the River Teviot, whose gentle waters flow through the region. The subtle palette, reminiscent of a misty dawn, features soft blues and greens that evoke the tranquillity of this idyllic landscape. According to Buchan's own notation, the colours have been carefully chosen to represent the shifting hues of the valley's riverside – lightened blues to mirror the serene tones of the surrounding hills. As one of Scotland's oldest District tartans, Teviotdale proudly embodies the rich cultural heritage and timeless traditions of this storied region, inviting wearers to connect with their ancestral roots through the traditional art of tartan weaving.

name: Texcraft Clothing Millennium 2000
description: The Millennium Tartan, designed by Texcraft, is a striking Fashion tartan born from the excitement of a new millennium. This innovative design was created to commemorate the year 2000 with a bold and modern line-up of upholstery and clothing items, featuring a distinctive white background woven with intricate silver thread. The complex sett, comprising two unique colours - Balmoral Blue and Light Green, both assumed non-repeating - adds depth and visual interest to this futuristic tartan. As a Restricted design under the Design Act, its creation is marked by a trademark notice, acknowledging its distinctiveness in the world of Scottish textiles. With its edgy charm and celebration of tradition, the Millennium Tartan embodies the spirit of modernity and heritage, making it a unique addition to any collection.

name: Thain [default]
description: The Thain Dress #1 tartan is a storied and evocative variation of MacDonald, Lord of the Isles Hunting, with roots stretching back to the early 20th century. Originally designed for members of the Thain family, its subtle nuances set it apart from its Highland Park High School Pipe Band counterpart, distinguished by the substitution of blue for black hues. This Name tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich clan heritage and tradition, where intricate patterns and subtle colour variations held great significance among families and communities. While the exact date of creation is unclear, Tony Murray's suggestion that it was worn circa 1930-1940 adds an air of authenticity to this dignified and timeless design, one that continues to honour the legacy of the Thain family and the broader MacDonald clan tradition.

name: The Glen
description: The Spirit of the Glen tartan is a vibrant corporate design, carefully crafted by Fiona Hall to evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's most iconic landscapes. This distinctive pattern is specifically registered for Gavin Kiltmakers of Fraserburgh, a respected kilt-making and hire business, allowing them to proudly represent their heritage through their bespoke kilts. The use of Lochcarron swatch materials lends an air of authenticity, tying this modern design firmly to Scotland's rich textile traditions. With its bold colour palette and unique sett, the Spirit of the Glen tartan is a fitting tribute to the country's timeless spirit, making it an excellent choice for businesses seeking to connect with Scottish heritage through their branding and identity.

name:
Think Pink
[AKA] Imperial Cancer Fund
description: The Think Pink tartan, registered under its International Colour Foundation (ICF) designation, embodies the spirit of corporate philanthropy and Scottish heritage. Created specifically for the Imperial Cancer Research Fund by renowned designers at Lochcarron of Scotland, this distinctive tartan pattern was designed to bring attention and support to a vital cause. As a Category Corporate tartan, it represents a unique blend of tradition and modernity, symbolising the connection between Scotland's rich textile heritage and the contemporary world of corporate branding. While subject only to general guidelines for use in the public eye, this tartan's significance lies in its association with a worthy charitable cause, serving as a powerful reminder of the enduring influence of Scottish design on global fashion and textiles.

name: Thirkill #2
description: The Thirkill (Dalgliesh) tartan is a storied clan pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority and worn by members of the Dalgliesh family and its allies. Designed in 2002 by Don Smith of Heraldic Graphics, Glasgow, this distinctive tartan was originally intended for a Black Watch officer of the same name, but its beauty and significance have transcended its origins to make it accessible to anyone bearing the surname Thirkill. With its rich, earthy tones and intricate sett, this tartan evokes the rugged grandeur of Scotland's glens and mountains, and its registration notes attest to the enduring legacy of Scottish clans and their traditions. As a testament to the skillful weaving of Dr Phil Smith's count in 2004, this tartan design remains an integral part of Scottish heritage, worn with pride by those who bear the Thirkill name and its associated history.

name: Thirkill [default]
