description: The Thirkill tartan is a distinctive Name tartan, registered for the distinguished family of Thirkill, a name steeped in Scottish heritage. Designed by renowned Heraldic Graphics of Glasgow, this vibrant pattern was originally intended for a Black Watch officer bearing the surname, but its beauty and significance extend far beyond familial ties. Worn by anyone bearing the name Thirkill, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the clan's history and tradition. Although contact with the original designer, Don Smith, has been lost to time, the Thirkill tartan remains a cherished symbol of Scottish identity, its bold colours and intricate design evoking the rugged beauty and proud heritage of Scotland's Celtic past.

name: Thistle Dubh
description: Thistle Dubh, a fashion tartan with a story as prickly as its namesake, is a testament to the whimsical side of Scottish heritage. Named after an anecdote from its designer, Geoffrey Highland Crafts, this vibrant design was born when someone exclaimed, "This'll do!" – a phrase that became synonymous with the Thistle Dubh motif. As a fashion tartan, Thistle Dubh embodies the laid-back charm of Scotland's fashion scene, perfect for those who want to inject a touch of Scottish flair into their wardrobe. With its unique tone-on-tone colouring and subtle texture, this tartan is sure to add a dash of personality to any outfit. Originally created by Geoffrey Highland Crafts for his kilthire business, Thistle Dubh has become a beloved staple in the world of fashion tartans, evoking a sense of relaxed sophistication that's quintessentially Scottish.

name: Thistle Stop LLC
description: The Thistle Stop LLC Corporate Tartan, designed by Cynthia Balfour-Traill, embodies the spirit of modern entrepreneurial endeavour with its bold, vibrant hues reminiscent of Scotland's rich heritage. Woven for Thistle Stop Shop, a Maryland-based retailer catering to fans of Scottish and Celtic culture, this tartan is as much about tradition as it is about innovation. A registered corporate tartan, it serves as a symbol of unity and identity for the company, while its unique design ensures that the brand stands out on store shelves. By drawing inspiration from Scotland's iconic thistle flower, this tartan pays homage to the country's cultural significance while embracing the forward-thinking ethos of its American clients - a testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage in the modern world.

name: Thomson, Jean Marc (Personal)
description: The Thomas, Jean Marc tartan is a unique and intriguing personal tartan, woven with a deep sense of heritage and history. This distinctive design, reserved for the exclusive use of its owner, Jean Marc Thomas, showcases a richly layered palette of blues, reds, and yellows that evoke the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of Scotland's majestic countryside. As a Name tartan, it holds great significance, symbolising family legacy and identity, while the lack of designer information adds to the mystery surrounding this design. Despite the absence of detailed registration notes, it is clear that this tartan has been carefully crafted with precision and attention to detail, reflecting the artisanal traditions that have defined Scottish weaving for centuries. Its limited availability only serves to increase its allure, making it a treasured possession for Jean Marc Thomas, and potentially one day, for his own family to inherit.

name: Thomas of Wales
description: The Thomas of Wales tartan is a relatively modern creation, born out of the growing commercial popularity of Welsh tartan wear since its introduction by Wales Tartan Centres in the late 1990s. Designed by Sheila Daniel for Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys, this unique tartan design stands out from traditional Celtic patterns due to its unconventional threading and colour palette. With its distinctive warp and weft characteristics, the Thomas of Wales tartan is an intriguing addition to the world of Scottish textiles. While it may not be rooted in centuries-old heritage or genealogical significance, its inclusion in this register serves as a testament to the enduring appeal of Welsh culture and tradition. By obtaining consent from Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea, prior to weaving, owners of this tartan are acknowledging its commercial origins while embracing its current popularity.

name: Thomson Black
description: The Burberry Black tartan is an iconic fashion staple that embodies the timeless elegance of British heritage. Originally designed for Burberry's esteemed fashion houses in 1986, this tartan has become synonymous with classic British sophistication. Its dark, muted tones evoke a sense of understated refinement, perfect for adding a touch of quintessential English style to any outfit. Notably, its subtle nuances may actually appear as deep navy upon closer inspection, lending an air of mystery and nuance to its design. As a fashion tartan, Burberry Black is carefully crafted to add a dash of luxury and sophistication to coats, scarves, and other garments, while remaining true to the traditional values of this revered British textile heritage.

name: Thomson Black #2
description: Thompson Black is a striking fashion tartan, meticulously crafted by the renowned Pringles of Inverness to make a bold statement on any garment. This dynamic pattern holds its own in the world of Scottish textiles, bearing testament to the ingenuity of its designer. As a registered fashion tartan, Thompson Black has secured its place within the esteemed Johnston Collection, a showcase of Scotland's rich tartan heritage. The design's origins and intentions are deeply rooted in traditional Scottish weaving techniques, demonstrating an honourable connection to the nation's rich cultural tapestry. By embracing this bold and modern interpretation, Pringles of Inverness has ensured that Thompson Black will remain a cherished part of Scotland's vibrant textile traditions for generations to come.

name:
Thomson Blue
[AKA] Thomson Thompson Dress
[AKA] MacTavish Lord Thomson of Fleet
[AKA] MacTavish Dress
description: The Thomson Dress Blue tartan is a storied family heritage, woven with precision by renowned designers John Bain and Alfred Bottomley at MacArthurs of Hamilton in the early 20th century. Created specifically for Lord Thomson of Fleet, this dignified tartan was recorded in the Lyon Court Books on 15 October 1965, cementing its place within Scotland's rich tapestry of clan traditions. As a Clan/ Family tartan, the Thomson Dress Blue is an honourable representation of family identity and ancestry, tied to the esteemed Lord Thomson and his lineage. Its significance extends beyond personal connection, too, representing the enduring legacy of Scottish clans and their rich cultural heritage.

name: Thomson Camel
description: Thomson Camel is a unique fashion tartan designed by J.C. 'Scotty' Thompson in what is believed to be the 1970s or early 1980s, with some sources suggesting an alternative designer, Laird Portch. This distinctive tartan has garnered attention for its subtle variations on traditional themes, including its distinct placement of red stripes and narrower white stripes that feature a central white line between them, effectively distinguishing it from the iconic Burberry tartan. With its characteristics thought to have been influenced by Scottish heritage and textile traditions, Thomson Camel is an intriguing addition to the world of fashion tartans, embodying the spirit of innovation and creative interpretation that defines modern tartan design.

name: Thomson Camel #2
description: The Thomson Camel tartan, woven at Jedburgh Woollen Mill, exudes the quintessential spirit of Scottish fashion with its rich, nuanced hues. As a Fashion tartan, it is undoubtedly inspired by the iconic Burberry Check, although, like a tantalising variant, it subtly diverges from its counterpart in its colour palette. The camel-toned red, carefully sandwiched between black-guarded broad white stripes, pays homage to Scotland's proud heritage while distinguishing itself through its unique texture and visual flair. This tartan's origins, spanning some 30 years, have instilled a sense of tradition and continuity, though controversy over its similarity to Burberry has led to occasional disputes with the luxury brand. Nevertheless, Thomson Camel remains an authentic and captivating representation of Scottish craftsmanship, awaiting those who would wear their heritage with pride.

name: Thomson Camel #3
description: The Burberry Counterfeit #4 tartan is a quintessential example of corporate style, evoking the iconic British brand's rich heritage in luxury textiles. Originally registered in 1957, this distinctive design was created for Burberry's esteemed equestrian clients, reflecting their love affair with fine fabrics and precision craftsmanship. As a Corporate tartan, it has since been adopted by fashion enthusiasts and professionals alike, who value its classic charm and timeless appeal. With no restrictions on use, the Burberry Counterfeit #4 tartan can be worn with pride to signify affiliation with this esteemed brand, paying homage to a legacy of excellence in British manufacturing and equestrian tradition.

name: Thomson Dance
description: This vibrant Fashion tartan, registered as Thompson (Dance), is an evocative embodiment of the exuberant spirit of traditional Scottish dance. Dubbed 'dancers' fancy', this interpretation of Lord Thompson's original tartan adds a whimsical touch, perfect for those who revel in the rhythmic beauty of Highland reels and jigsteps. As a registered Fashion tartan, it is intended to be used as a vibrant accentuate fabric in clothing and accessories, allowing wearers to embody the dynamic energy of Scotland's rich dance heritage. With its unique blend of colours and subtle nuances, this tartan design pays homage to the traditions that have shaped Scotland's identity for centuries, making it an ideal choice for anyone seeking to add a touch of Scottish flair to their wardrobe.

name: Thomson Dress; Grey
description: The Thompson Grey Dress, created by Pringles of Inverness, is a captivating fashion tartan that embodies the timeless spirit of Scottish heritage. Initially registered as a grey version of the iconic Camel Thompson, its provenance lies in the storied archives of the Scottish Tartans Society, where it's showcased alongside notable examples in the Johnston Collection and Dalgety Collection. Though the original Thomson Grey, featuring a distinctive yellow line through the black band, remains an enigmatic variant, this design has become a staple in the industry, woven with precision by skilled artisans. This versatile fabric pattern is now commonly referred to as Thompson Grey, its subtle nuances and earthy tones evoking the sombre grandeur of Scotland's ancient weavings, where tradition meets modern elegance.

name: Thomson Grey
description: The George family tartan is a cherished and highly personal design, created to commemorate the rich Celtic heritage of Michael Roderick George from Wales. Commissioned by his son Jason Duglere George, this distinctive Name tartan weaves together the symbolism of its colours to evoke the land of their ancestors. The deep blues and greens represent the lush forests and majestic lochs that crisscross Wales and Scotland, while crimson threads signify the enduring spirit of the Celtic people who have long called these lands home. The inclusion of white threads adds a touch of purity and timelessness, honouring the ancient connection between the natural world and the Celtic heritage. As a Restricted tartan, this design is reserved for family use only, ensuring its significance and cultural relevance are preserved for generations to come, under the guidance of the George family's tailor, Geoffrey Highland Crafts Limited.

name: Thomson Grey #2
description: The Thompson, Grey tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's clans and families, woven with precision and tradition by the skilled hands of Jack Dalgety. Registered as Clan/Family, this timeless design holds honour within Scottish tartanry circles, evoking the noble lineage of the Thompsons, whose history dates back centuries. Despite its association with another name, Logan Air, this tartan is unequivocally Grey Thompson, a distinction highlighted by the Dalgety Collection's expertly preserved sample. While there may be some confusion over its origins, one thing remains clear: this tartan is an integral part of Scottish cultural heritage, proudly representing the Thompson family and their enduring legacy.

name: Thomson Hunting
description: The Thomson tartan, a personal clan tartan designed by the esteemed John Bain & Alfred Bottomley for newspaper magnate Lord Thomson of Fleet, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage and tradition. Originally recorded in the prestigious Lord Lyon Book 23 on 7th December 1971, this tartan has undergone a transformation, with its name being adopted by many members of the Thomson family regardless of spelling variation. Despite its origins as a personal design, the Thomson tartan now shares a common sett with the historic MacTavish Hunting, leaving some questions unanswered about its original design intentions. Nevertheless, its association with Lord Thomson's patronage and its inclusion in the Scottish Tartans Authority Johnston Collection underscores the significance of this tartan in Scottish textile history.

name: Thomson Hunting #2
description: The Burberry Hunting tartan is an iconic corporate design steeped in tradition and heritage, born from the renowned British fashion house's roots in equestrian style. With its bold, structured weave, this tartan embodies the classic blend of British sophistication and adventurous spirit, perfectly capturing the essence of hunting traditions that have been a cornerstone of British culture for centuries. Originally registered as a corporate tartan, it has since become synonymous with Burberry's timeless approach to luxury and elegance, evoking images of fine tweed, crisp linings, and refined country attire. With no specific design details provided in its registration notes, the Burberry Hunting tartan remains an enigmatic yet instantly recognisable symbol of British heritage and refinement.

name: Thomson, J.C.'s Fancy (Personal)
description: J.C. 'Scotty' Thompson's 'Thompson's Fancy', also known as MacTavish, hunting, is a distinctive Name tartan imbued with the story of its creator's ingenuity and passion for traditional Scottish heritage. Commissioned by J.C. Thompson, an American of Scottish descent, in the early 20th century, this unique tartan was designed to honour his clan roots while breaking free from conventional colour schemes. The result is a striking combination of red stripes on a rich brown background, punctuated by a vibrant blue border - a bold move that reflects Thompson's creative spirit and dedication to preserving Scottish traditions. As the Tartan Society notes, this tartan was intended for personal use only, making it an intimate and exclusive representation of its owner's heritage.

name: Thomson Navy
description: The Burberry Blue tartan, registered under Peter MacDonald's design in 1991, is a stalwart of corporate identity, evoking the storied heritage of one of Britain's most iconic brands. This blue-hued variant of an earlier design, as seen in Scotch House, Edinburgh in 1985, pays homage to the rich traditions of Scottish weaving while imbuing it with a modern, professional edge, fitting for corporate attire. As a Corporate tartan, Burberry Blue is designed to be worn by individuals and organisations looking to convey a sense of prestige and respectability, its subtle nuances and muted tones lending themselves perfectly to formal occasions or everyday business attire. With MacDonald's masterful touch, this tartan design has come to embody the enduring spirit of British tradition and style.

name: Thompson Variant
description: The Thompson Variant tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish clans, weaving together threads of history and tradition into a vibrant fabric. Designed by John Hannay in all likelihood, this distinctive tartan has been carefully preserved within the Hannay Collection, evoking the stories of a family with roots dating back generations. As a Clan/Family tartan, it bears the weight of ancestral legacy, its specific design reflecting the unique characteristics and values of the Thompson clan. While no further details are available, the tartan's existence speaks to the enduring power of Scottish tradition and the importance of preserving cultural heritage for future generations, making it a treasured and integral part of Scotland's rich tapestry.

name: Thorburn USA
description: The Thorburn tartan, registered in 1992, holds a special place in the hearts of those bearing the esteemed surname. Designed with the intention of being worn by all who share the same heritage, this unique tartan is a testament to the enduring bond between family and identity. Dr Philip D Smith Jnr's creation pays homage to the rich Scottish heritage, with its intricate pattern woven from threads of deep blue, green, yellow, black, red, white, and blue, evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Highlands. As a Name tartan, it is reserved for those who bear the name Thorburn, serving as a visual representation of their connection to this storied clan lineage, which stretches back through generations of proud Scottish families.

name: Thorburn [default]
description: Thorburn (Lochcarron) is a time-honoured clan tartan steeped in rich heritage and tradition, woven into the very fabric of Scotland's storied past. Originating from the Thorburn family of Lochcarron, this distinctive design has been passed down through generations, its intricate patterns and subtle nuances evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. Notably, it bears a striking resemblance to another Thorburn tartan (#6615), painstakingly recreated by renowned designer Dr Phil Smith in 1992, as recorded by the Scottish Tartans Authority. This deliberate nod to tradition underscores the importance of preserving Scotland's cultural legacy, while also acknowledging the evolution and revitalisation of traditional designs that continue to captivate and inspire new generations of tartan enthusiasts.

name: Tiger
description: The Tiger tartan, designed by Mangaroca International SA, embodies the bold spirit of Scotland's fashion heritage. As a Fashion category design, it is a modern take on traditional tartan, blending vibrant colours to create a dynamic pattern that evokes the wild beauty of the Scottish wilderness. The unique registration notes reveal that this design was created specifically for a Scottish product by an independent Swiss company, Mangaroca International SA, producing premium spirits and soft drinks. Notably, restrictions apply, indicating that this tartan is exclusively licensed to Mangaroca International SA. Nevertheless, its cultural significance remains rooted in Scotland's rich textile tradition, where the Tiger's striking design pays homage to the country's fearless heritage, making it a fitting representation of Scottish fashion excellence.

name: Tilley, Sir Samuel Leonard
description: The Tilley, Sir Samuel Leonard tartan is a poignant tribute to a pioneering figure in Canadian history. Registered as a Commemorative tartan, this distinctive design honours Sir Samuel Leonard Tilley, one of the key architects of Confederation who played a pivotal role in shaping Canada's early years. The West Coast Woolen Mill's expert weaving brings to life the rich heritage of Scotland and Canada, blending traditional techniques with modern sensibilities. While restrictions apply due to its commemorative nature, this tartan remains an evocative celebration of Sir Samuel Leonard Tilley's remarkable contributions to the country's development. As part of the Johnston Collection in the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan is a treasured testament to Canada's rich cultural roots and its enduring connection to Scotland's timeless traditions.

name: Timely Marketing (Auckland)
description: The Auckland tartan, registered under the esteemed House of Tartan, embodies the spirit of a bygone era, evoking the grandeur and history of Scotland's districts. Designed by Blair Urquhart for Clinton McInnes, a prominent New Zealander with Scottish heritage, this tartan pays tribute to the country's roots while embracing its unique cultural identity. As a District tartan, Auckland is steeped in tradition, reflecting the strong community bonds and family ties that defined Scotland's rural past. With restrictions in place regarding colour usage and proportion, the Auckland tartan remains a treasured representation of Scottish heritage, proudly worn by those who honour their ancestral connections to New Zealand's rich cultural tapestry.

name: Timespan
description: The Timespan tartan is a unique and distinctive corporate design that embodies the rich heritage of the north-east of Scotland. Registration notes reveal that it was created by MacKay of Strathnaver, commissioned specifically for the 'Timespan Heritage Centre' at Helmsdale, Sutherland, opening in 1989. This centre celebrates the region's history and culture, making the tartan a fitting symbol of its legacy. Characterised by subtle shades of blue and green, this modern corporate design weaves together traditional elements to create a cohesive visual identity that honours the past while embracing the future. With its roots firmly planted in Scottish heritage, the Timespan tartan is a testament to the enduring power of tradition and community, making it an ideal choice for organisations seeking to connect with their local roots.

name: Tindal [default]
description: The Tindal tartan is a timeless and dignified Scottish heritage textile, steeped in tradition and honour. Registered in recognition of those who bear the surname Tindal, this distinctive tartan design is a symbol of pride and identity for its wearers. Described as "A dark blue or black ground with two thin stripes of red, white, and pale blue", it evokes the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands and the rich history of clan affiliation. With its origins rooted in the Name category, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish family heritage. A fitting tribute to those who wear the Tindal tartan, it embodies the values of tradition, loyalty, and community that are at the very heart of Scottish culture.

name: Tipperary Irish County
description: The Tipperary, County tartan is a vibrant representation of Irish heritage, expertly woven by Polly Wittering of the House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. As one of a series of District tartans, this design defies official sanction yet has quickly gained popularity among those seeking to connect with their ancestral roots. Originally crafted for the esteemed Macnaughtons of Pitlochry as trade tartans, this unique pattern now boasts a rich history that transcends its utilitarian origins. By embracing the Tipperary, County tartan, one honours not only a storied Scottish heritage but also pays tribute to the region's own distinct cultural identity, as if the very fabric of Ireland itself has been intricately woven into its threads.

name: Tiree Grey
description: The Tiree Grey, a fashion tartan by design, holds a special place in the heart of Scottish heritage, despite its unclear origins. This subtle yet striking pattern bears a resemblance to Burberry checks, albeit with distinct differences, leaving room for interpretation about its true inspiration. As a fashion category tartan, it's designed to add a touch of sophistication and elegance to clothing and accessories, evoking the laid-back charm of Scotland's west coast islands. Its understated beauty makes it an attractive choice for those seeking a unique and stylish twist on classic tartan designs, while its relative anonymity has allowed it to carve out its own identity within the world of Scottish textiles, free from the strong ties of clan or geographical affiliation.

name: Tiree
description: The Tiree tartan, a vibrant and striking fashion tartan created by the renowned Edinburgh Woollen Mill, is deeply rooted in Scotland's rich textile heritage. As a Category Fashion tartan, it embodies the glamour and sophistication of modern Scottish style. With its distinctive colour palette and precise weave pattern, this tartan design has captured the imagination of many, serving as a powerful symbol of Scottish flair and individuality. Its registration with the Scottish Tartans Authority, a testament to its authenticity, is further endorsement of its status as a genuine representation of Scotland's ancient traditions. When worn or displayed, the Tiree tartan proudly wears the honour of Scotland on its sleeve, connecting wearers to a centuries-old legacy of craftsmanship and cultural identity.

name: Titanic
description: The Titanic tartan is a poignant commemoration of one of history's most tragic maritime disasters, meticulously woven into existence by an unknown designer. Registered in 1999, this distinctive tartan draws inspiration from the SS Titanic's ill-fated maiden voyage, with its intricate patterns reportedly reconstructed from a fragment and photograph of a deck chair found on board the ship that sank in 1912. As a Commemorative tartan, the Titanic is steeped in reverence for the lives lost, evoking the sombre tones of sea-weathered leather and worn, weathered fabric that echoes the ageless legacy of this maritime catastrophe.

name: Todd (Tom) personal; Tantallon
description: The Tantallon Golf Club tartan is a vibrant and sophisticated corporate tartan that embodies the rich heritage and tradition of Scotland's oldest golfing club, founded in 1853. Designed by renowned weaver Tommy Todd, this distinctive tartan showcases a palette of black, blue, red, green, yellow and white hues, evoking the dramatic landscapes of the North Berwick West Links and the Firth of Forth. As an exclusive use tartan, reserved for club members only, it serves as a proud badge of membership, connecting wearers to a storied history and a sense of camaraderie that spans generations. By specifying Bespoke Tartans as the sole permitted weaver, the Tantallon Golf Club tartan ensures an authentic and bespoke finish, befitting its esteemed status within the world of corporate tartans.

name: Todd (Tom) personal; Tribal
description: Tribal #2, a stunning corporate tartan by renowned designer Cynthia Balfour-Traill, evokes the rich heritage of Scotland's ancient traditions while embracing modernity. Originally created in 2003 for Tom Todd's wedding, this majestic design has since been adopted for corporate use, exuding sophistication and professionalism. Woven from the finest Lochcarron yarns, Tribal #2 embodies the untamed spirit of the Scottish wilderness, with its distinctive sett and colour palette evoking the rugged beauty of the country's most iconic landscapes. As a testament to its enduring appeal, this tartan has been entrusted with corporate applications, promising to add an air of prestige and distinction to any business or organisation that chooses to wear it.

name: Todd [default]
description: The Todd tartan, bearing the proud name of Gregory V Todd, is a striking variation of Tweedside Green Hunting, imbued with a sense of family heritage and tradition. With its distinctive red hue replacing the black pivot, this tartan embodies the spirit of Scotland's rugged Borders, where fox hunting once reigned supreme. Named in Border dialect after the cunning creature that was its namesake, the Todd is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish clans and their rich textile traditions. As a registered family tartan, it holds significant cultural value for those bearing the name, allowing them to wear their heritage with pride. Woven by skilled hands at D.C. Dalgliesh's loom in Selkirk, the Todd tartan is now proudly part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, a tangible connection to Scotland's storied past.

name: Tokharion
description: This captivating Tokharion tartan is an exquisite fusion of ancient traditions, born from the inspiration of Ronnie Hek's travels to the Mongolian desert. Dating back to 700-1200BC, its origins are rooted in the textiles discovered on the mummies of Urumchi, where intricate woven designs once adorned the bodies of ancient warriors and nomads. By marrying this heritage with his artistic vision, Hek has created a truly unique Fashion tartan that not only pays homage to Scotland's rich weaving history but also bridges cultures and time zones, paying tribute to the silk roads that once connected the East and West. Its subtle blend of dark blues and reds, reminiscent of the vast expanse of the Mongolian steppes, invites wearers to embody the adventurous spirit of exploration and discovery.

name: Tokyo Bluebells Dance
description: Tokyo Bluebells, a vibrant Fashion tartan, brings a unique fusion of Scottish heritage to the global stage. Weaved by the accomplished designers Donald & Fiona Fraser, this stunning design was formally registered in October 2002. Originally commissioned by a Scottish Country Dance club based in Tokyo, Japan, the tartan pays homage to the rich cultural exchange between Scotland and its international partners. The Bluebells' gentle hues evoke the beauty of Edinburgh's Botanic Gardens, while subtle undertones hint at the rugged Scottish hillsides. This fashion-forward tartan now holds pride as a symbol of modern Scottish craftsmanship, connecting communities across cultures through its elegant and distinctive pattern.

name: Tomass [default]
description: The Tomass tartan is a deeply personal and ancestral motif, registered by Antony Albert Tomass in 1995 for his family's heritage. Weaved by the skilled hands of Lochcarron of Scotland, this Clan tartan proudly bears the name of its originator, evoking a sense of history and tradition that spans generations. With no known restrictions, the Tomass tartan is free to be worn with honour, allowing Tomass descendants to proudly display their family ties through their textiles. This subtle yet meaningful design is an important part of Scotland's rich tartan heritage, serving as a tangible connection to the land, culture, and people from whom it was born.

name: Tombow 21st School Memorial
description: This dignified Corporate Tartan, registered by Lochcarron of Scotland as Tombow 21st School Memorial, embodies the values and spirit of its namesake school memorial. Its carefully chosen colours - green for the earth's well-being, blue for tranquility and peace, royal blue representing the sky and youth, red symbolising love, and white denoting truth and solidarity - weave together to convey a sense of unity and purpose. As a Corporate tartan, it is intended to inspire loyalty and pride among those who wear it, whether in formal or informal settings, while also serving as a poignant reminder of the importance of education and remembrance. This tasteful design pays tribute to the enduring legacy of schools like the one it commemorates, and its subtle yet striking pattern makes it an ideal choice for corporate attire, events, and charitable initiatives that align with its values.

name: Tommy
description: The Tommy tartan is a vibrant corporate tartan designed by Tommy Hilfiger, a renowned American fashion house. This iconic tartan was created for business wear and leisure occasions alike, embodying the essence of modern American style. With its bold colour palette, comprising a striking mix of reds, blues, and greens, the Tommy tartan is deeply rooted in traditional Scottish heritage yet distinctly American in its execution. As part of Hilfiger's corporate identity, this tartan has become synonymous with the brand's high-energy, all-American aesthetic. Originally designed for men's sportswear, it has since been adapted for a wide range of applications, from business attire to fashion statements, making it an instantly recognisable symbol of contemporary American style and a testament to the enduring power of traditional Scottish tartans in modern fashion.

name:
Tooth
[AKA] Breacan Buan No Teuch
description: This unique Tooth tartan, registered under Jamie Scarlett MBE's design, is a personal creation intended to bear its name proudly. A Name tartan is one that has been created specifically for an individual or family, making this particular example a distinctive and meaningful representation of its owner. The subtle nuances of this tartan's colour palette - with muted greens, rich blues, and earthy tones - evoke the natural beauty of Scotland's rugged landscape, while the intricate texture and weave speak to the skill and tradition of Scottish weaving. As part of the Dalgety Collection, a cherished repository of Scotland's most iconic and historically significant tartans, this Tooth design serves as a tangible connection to its creator's heritage and personal legacy.

name: Toronto Blue Jays
description: The Toronto Blue Jays tartan is a vibrant, corporate-inspired design born from the union of Scottish heritage and North American sports culture. Designed by renowned Scottish mill Lochcarron of Scotland, this distinctive tartan was created with honour in mind for Pat Snair, a Dunedin (Florida) local doctor who brought his community together to celebrate their connection to Canada's beloved baseball team. With its unique blend of blues, whites, and greens, the Toronto Blue Jays tartan is a symbol of Canadian identity and a nod to the city's transatlantic ties with Scotland. Its corporate classification speaks to its enduring popularity as a fashion statement and branding tool, worn by fans around the world and proudly displayed on team merchandise.

name: Toronto Fire Services
description: The Toronto Fire Services tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan designed by renowned Scottish mill, Lochcarron of Scotland, in 2000. This bold and dramatic design was specifically created to commemorate the esteemed Toronto Fire Services, evoking a sense of strength, courage, and community spirit that defines this vital public service. Characterised by its striking black-blue hue, reminiscent of smoke and flames, amidst subtle nuances of gold and red, this tartan embodies the bravery and resilience of those who serve with distinction. As an official corporate tartan, it is available for use by registered corporations and organisations associated with the Toronto Fire Services, proudly showcasing their connection to a city's rich heritage and tradition of public service excellence.

name: Toshach [default]
description: The Toshach tartan is a storied and evocative design, steeped in Scotland's rich cultural heritage. As an early Celtic title bestowed upon minor territorial chiefs, its origins are deeply rooted in the country's medieval history. The sett, taken from a rug once cherished by generations of a family with alleged connections to Sir Walter Scott's librarian, has been carefully preserved and registered as a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's tartan traditions. As a Clan/Family tartan, it holds significance for those bearing the name or title Toshach, serving as a visual representation of their heritage and ancestry. With its rich colours and subtle variations, this tartan design embodies the intricate complexity and depth of Scotland's tartan tradition, inviting wearers to proudly connect with their ancestral roots.

name: Total Oil Company
description: The Total tartan, designed by esteemed weaver Andrew Elliot for the Total Oil Company, embodies the sleek, modern spirit of corporate Scotland. Registered as part of the company's bespoke identity, this tartan pattern is deeply rooted in the tradition of Scottish textile heritage, yet its utilitarian purpose belies a distinctive aesthetic that resonates with the global oil and gas industry. By employing Total's signature colours, Elliot has crafted a visual identity that not only reflects the company's values but also pays homage to the rich cultural fabric of Scotland. As a corporate tartan, it serves as a potent symbol of unity and professionalism, making it an indispensable part of Total Oil Marine plc's visual identity.

name: Tough
description: The Tough tartan, born from the vision of Peter MacDonald in 1997, holds deep roots in Scottish heritage and tradition. This unique Name tartan was specifically designed for Kenneth Tough's family, hailing from Aberdeenshire, where their history is woven into the fabric of the Tribe of Mar tartan. The designer cleverly merged this foundation with a bold accent of grey, evoking the family's connection to salmon farming, a nod to their Scottish marine heritage. While it may be worn privately, the Tough tartan whispers tales of the rugged Highlands and the sea-kissed coastlines that have shaped its story. With restrictions in place, this intimate design is cherished by the Tough family alone, yet its significance echoes through generations, binding its wearers to the rich tapestry of Scottish clan history.

name: Toyokawa Check
description: The Toyokawa Check is a unique corporate tartan, carefully crafted by Lochcarron of Scotland for a most remarkable purpose: to represent the students and staff of the Toyokawa Kindergarten and Elementary schools in Aichi, Japan. Born from a special request to celebrate the cultural exchange between Scotland and Japan, this distinctive design weaves together elements of both nations' rich heritage. The registration notes reveal that it is specifically intended for use by the pupils and educators of these esteemed institutions, serving as a symbol of unity, respect, and friendship between two distant lands. With its bold checks and carefully chosen colours, the Toyokawa Check tartan embodies the spirit of international cooperation and cultural understanding, proudly bearing the mark of Lochcarron's renowned craftsmanship.

name: Trades House
description: The Trades House tartan is a richly woven emblem of corporate heritage, born from the vision of Lochcarron of Scotland in 1997 for Gordon M Wyllie of Biggart Baille Solicitors. Commissioned specifically for one of Glasgow's most esteemed institutions, the Trades House - incorporated in 1605 and steeped in history, this tartan weaves together threads of tradition and innovation. Reserved exclusively for the members of the Trades House of Glasgow, this corporate tartan embodies a sense of pride and identity among its wearers. As a Registered Design, its rights have been formally gifted to the institution, ensuring that this distinctive pattern will continue to signify loyalty and affiliation with one of Scotland's most revered cultural institutions.

name: Trafalgar
description: The Trafalgar tartan is a stylish and sophisticated fashion tartan, designed to make a lasting impression on any wearer. Named after one of the most iconic naval battles in British history, the Trafalgar tartan embodies the spirit of bravery and patriotism that defines Scotland's rich heritage. Created for use in Canadian trade or fancy tartan (Toronto, to be precise), this design was envisioned by A.C. Lumsden, a renowned expert in the field. With its distinctive blue-and-red hues, the Trafalgar tartan is sure to add a touch of dashing elegance to any outfit, evoking memories of Nelson's triumphant victory at sea and the enduring legacy of British naval power.

name: Traill [default]
description: The Louth County, Crest Range tartan is a testament to Ireland's rich heritage and the intricate traditions of its counties. Registered as one of a set of Irish County and National tartans in 2005 by Viking Technology Limited (now Tartan Web Scotland Ltd), this vibrant design embodies the essence of County Louth. As a District tartan, it holds a special place within Irish tartan heritage, reflecting the county's unique identity and cultural traditions. Yet, due to its restrictions imposed by USA Kilts Inc, which now owns the rights to this tartan, its widespread reproduction is limited, ensuring its significance remains tied to those who have been granted permission to wear or reproduce it. This intriguing paradox highlights the complex web of ownership and cultural exchange that underlies Ireland's storied tartan tradition.

name: Traynor [default]
description: The Traynor tartan is a proud emblem of Scottish heritage, woven with the rich history and traditions of one of Scotland's most storied clans. Registered to acknowledge its origins as a personal design for Dr Elizabeth Traynor by esteemed designer Dr Phil Smith, this tartan embodies the timeless spirit of family and unity that defines Clan Traynor. With no restrictions on wear, the Traynor tartan is an inclusive symbol of identity that can be worn by all who bear the name, transcending generations and geographical boundaries to represent a shared heritage and cultural roots. As a testament to its enduring significance, this iconic tartan design continues to inspire pride and loyalty among members of Clan Traynor, serving as a poignant reminder of their ancestral connections to Scotland's storied past.

name: Trevison
description: The Trevison tartan is a bold and striking fashion design that embodies the spirit of innovation and flair, courtesy of its creator Marco Trevison. Originally inspired by the iconic colours of the Italian flag - green and white - this unique tartan has been expertly woven to incorporate these hues in a distinctive pattern. As a Fashion tartan, it is designed to make a bold statement on any garment, from a jacket to a scarf, and its modern twist on traditional Scottish heritage makes it an exciting addition to any fashion-forward wardrobe. Notably, this design does not adhere to the traditional clan or family associations found in many other tartans, instead opting for its own distinct identity as a fashion statement, free from any restrictions or family ties.

name: Triad Highland Games
description: The Triad Highland Games Proposed tartan is a vibrant and dynamic creation inspired by the annual Highland Games events held in Greensboro, North Carolina, USA. Designed by Harry Blair, this corporate tartan is specifically commissioned for Triad Highland Games, Inc., an organisation that celebrates Scottish heritage and culture. The registration notes reveal the tartan's purpose: to promote unity and camaraderie among participants, spectators, and enthusiasts of the Games. With its bold colour palette and traditional Scottish design elements, this tartan embodies the spirit of Scottish tradition and community, paying homage to the rich history of Highland Games while embracing a modern corporate identity.

name: Tricor
description: The Tricor tartan, created by Alistair Buchan, is a striking Corporate design that pays homage to Scotland's rich heritage while embracing international flair. Inspired by the Bermuda tartan, this distinctive pattern has been adapted for use by Canadian car dealerships across Scotland, reflecting the country's strong cultural ties with Canada. By registering this tartan under Scottish law, Tricor becomes an official symbol of identity and tradition, embodying the values of enterprise and cooperation that define corporate Scotland. While its origins lie in a unique collaboration between Lochcarron of Scotland and Canadian car dealerships, the Tricor tartan has become a testament to the enduring power of Scottish textiles to bring people together across borders.

name: Trillard
description: The Trillard tartan, registered by Geoffrey Highland Crafts, is a deeply personal and intricate motif woven with honour and faithfulness in mind. As a restricted clan tartan for the family of Tom Trillard, it bears witness to the proud heritage of those who bear the Trillard name, with its roots firmly planted in France but tied to the rich cultural tapestry of Scotland. The subtle nuances of this tartan are said to evoke "Onair agus Dilseachd", a Gaelic motto that conveys unwavering commitment and loyalty - sentiments deeply ingrained in the Scottish tradition. Its careful balance of earthy tones, rich blues, and vibrant greens creates a complex yet harmonious whole, evoking the intricate patterns and stories woven into Scotland's own tartan legacy.

name: Trinity Presbyterian Church
description: This dignified corporate tartan, designed by esteemed weaver Mary Jo Pribble, pays tribute to the rich heritage of Trinity Presbyterian Church in Hendersonville, North Carolina. Inspired by the iconic Clergy tartan, which originated among Scotland's ministerial class, Pribble has carefully adapted its timeless motifs to create a distinctive and respectful tribute to the American Presbyterian tradition. As a corporate tartan, this design is intended for formal wear and ceremonial occasions, evoking the values of faith, community, and leadership that underpin the church's mission. The registration notes serve as a poignant reminder of the tartan's origins in Scottish tradition, while its adoption by a US institution underscores the enduring power of cultural exchange and mutual respect between nations.

name: Trost
description: The Trost tartan, aptly named after its corporate inspiration, is a unique blend of tradition and innovation. Originally created as a birthday present for a senior staff member at Trost GmbH in Stuttgart-Wangen, this striking tartan was designed by Robin Elliot with input from the company itself, reflecting their distinct identity. The colours, particularly the red, have been carefully calibrated to evoke a subtle warmth, infused with a hint of orange to give it an edge. This thoughtfully crafted tartan is a testament to the intersection of Scottish heritage and modern corporate style, celebrating the rich cultural exchange between Scotland and Germany. By registering this unique design through the Scottish Tartans Authority, Trost GmbH has secured its place in the proud tradition of tartan-making, forever linking their company's values with that of Scotland's esteemed textile art.

name: Tulloch Homes
description: The Tulloch Homes tartan, created by the renowned designer Claire Donaldson of the House of Edgar, is a quintessential corporate motif that embodies the spirit of excellence and sophistication. As a registered Corporate tartan, it has been carefully crafted to evoke a sense of professionalism and prestige, making it an ideal choice for businesses seeking to establish a strong brand identity. Designed specifically for Tulloch Homes, this tartan draws upon Scottish heritage and tradition, paying homage to the rich history and culture of the country. With its unique colour palette and precise weaving, the Tulloch Homes tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile craftsmanship, now reimagined for the modern corporate world.

name: Tulsa District
description: The Tulsa, City of tartan is a unique District tartan with a rich history, reflecting the cultural heritage of Oklahoma's vibrant city. Designed by Richard Crawford, Chinnubbie McIntosh, and Bea Notley, in collaboration with the Mayor of Tulsa, Robert J. La Fortune, this tartan was officially registered as the only District tartan outside the British Commonwealth. The colours, chosen to represent Tulsa's distinctive features, pay homage to its Native American heritage, serene lakes, verdant Green Country, and the state's significant petroleum industry. As a symbol of civic pride, the Tulsa tartan serves as a testament to the city's Scottish roots and its status as a melting pot of cultures.

name: Tupper, Sir Charles
description: Sir Charles Tupper's commemorative tartan, crafted by the esteemed West Coast Woolen Mill, is a poignant tribute to the life and legacy of Canada's first Prime Minister. This distinctive tartan, registered in recognition of Tupper's distinguished service as Premier of Nova Scotia and Prime Minister of Canada, pays homage to his remarkable achievements as one of the Fathers of Confederation. Its significance extends beyond mere commemoration, as it serves as a lasting symbol of Canadian unity and identity, woven from the very fabric of history. As part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, this tartan design not only honours Tupper's memory but also provides a tangible connection to his remarkable story, which spans Edinburgh's academic halls to Canada's parliamentary chambers.

name: Turcan Connell
description: The Turcan Connell corporate tartan is a masterful blend of tradition and innovation, reflecting the heritage and values of one of Scotland's most esteemed law firms. Designated as an asymmetrical tartan, it cleverly balances earthy tones - rich greens and browns evoking wealth, land, and family law - with bold accents in deep red, symbolising the unyielding connection to the bloodline that drives the firm's success. Meanwhile, light grey blue threads weave a subtle narrative of modernity and technological savvy, acknowledging the evolving nature of the profession. With its distinctive colour palette and expert craftsmanship, this tartan embodies the perfect blend of heritage and forward thinking, serving as a proud emblem for the Turcan Connell family and their commitment to excellence in law.

name: Turnberry MacArthur
description: The Turnberry (MacArthur) tartan is a captivating fashion tartan that weaves together the rich heritage of Scotland's clan system with the subtleties of traditional colourwork. Designated as a Fashion tartan, it embodies the elegance of Scottish textiles, evoking the iconic Black Watch 'B' in its variation on a darker palette. The coincidence in its registration notes with Baillie Dress and Snaefell, both produced by esteemed mills, highlights the convergence of artisanal techniques across the British Isles. While not attributed to a specific designer, the tartan's evolution is testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's weaving traditions. As an altered colour variation in the Scottish Tartans Authority's collection, Turnberry (MacArthur) stands as a vibrant representation of Scotland's cultural heritage, its subtle nuances reflecting the artful manipulation of traditional hues and patterns that have defined Scottish tartan-making for centuries.

name: Turnberry
description: The Turnberry tartan, a proud representative of Scotland's rich textile heritage, tells a story of history and tradition. Originally originating from Aviemore/Dogwood Thompson, this district tartan has undergone a transformation through Clan Crest Textiles' interpretation. The intricate pattern, featuring a palette of earthy tones, is reminiscent of the rugged Scottish landscape. With its roots firmly planted in Scottish tartan tradition, Turnberry is a testament to the country's rich cultural heritage and the skilled weavers who have brought it to life over the centuries. Although its origins are well-documented, an error in the registration notes has resulted in a discrepancy that requires further investigation. Nonetheless, this stalwart tartan remains a source of pride for those who cherish Scotland's traditional textiles and the enduring legacy of Clan Crest Textiles' innovative design.

name: Turnbull Dress
description: The Turnbull Dress tartan, registered by Bob Martin, holds a special place within Scottish heritage, having been woven to represent a family or clan identity. Notably, its unique characteristic lies in its absence of white, a departure from traditional dress tartans that typically incorporate the colour in their designs. This deliberate choice adds to the tartan's distinctiveness and reflects the preferences of its creator, whose name is shrouded in mystery, leaving room for interpretation about his intentions. The Turnbull Dress shares geometric similarities with the Douglas of Roxburgh tartan, a nod to the influence of William H.Johnston & Philip D.Smith jr's work, "Tartans", which documented various clan weaves. This tartan's rich history and distinctive colour palette evoke a sense of tradition and cultural significance, its dark green hues almost indistinguishable from black, as noted in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Dalgety Collection.

name: Turnbull Hunting
description: The Turnbull Hunting tartan, designed by Mr Turnbull himself in 1983, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's storied clans. This Clan tartan, #2, seamlessly blends elements from two iconic Scottish families: Douglas and Bruce. The sett's distinctive combination of yellow lines on a dark blue-green background, offset by black stripes, pays homage to the Turnbulls' ancestral connections. According to Mr Turnbull and verified by the renowned tartan authority Alistair Buchan of Lochcarron, this specific variation was introduced with a subtle modification in 1983: the removal of maroon to present a more subdued effect. The result is a striking and elegant design that adds depth and nuance to Scottish heritage, its dark blues and greens evoking the rugged landscapes and storied histories of Scotland's most revered clans.

name: Turnbull of Thornton
description: The Turnbull of Thornton tartan is a richly woven tribute to the heritage of its namesake, Brian Turnbull, a stalwart son of York, whose family's legacy would soon be marked by the dawn of a new millennium. Designed with meticulous care by Peter MacDonald in 1996, this Name tartan pays homage to the Turnbull clan's esteemed history, as signified by the distinctive blue and red hues that evoke the grandeur of Yorkshire's rolling hills. The intricate pattern, steeped in tradition, is now proudly worn by Brian himself, Thornton Manor its ancestral seat, as a testament to the enduring bonds between family, land, and Scotland's storied past.

name: Turner
description: The Turner personal tartan is a unique and intriguing example of traditional Scottish weaving, bearing witness to the rich heritage of individual expression within the tartan world. As a Name tartan, it is a registered design that represents a family or clan connection, albeit in this case, its origins are shrouded in mystery due to the absence of a specified designer. The swatch, created by D.C. Dalgliesh in 2001, suggests that the tartan may have been designed for personal use, adding an air of intimacy and personal significance to its creation. Despite the lack of historical context, this tartan design remains a testament to Scotland's enduring tradition of artisanal weaving and the importance placed on clan and family heritage, where tartans serve as tangible links to one's ancestry and cultural identity.

name: Tweedmouth Community Middle School
description: The Tweedmouth Middle School corporate tartan, designed by Ronnie Hek of Coldstream, is a vibrant tribute to the rich heritage of the English-Scottish border region. Named after its namesake school, situated near the picturesque River Tweed, this distinctive tartan weaves together the traditions of local communities with the commercial and professional ambitions of a modern corporate identity. By embracing the colour palette and fabric woven into the very essence of the Scottish Borders, Hek has created a unique and eye-catching design that proudly represents Tweedbank Community Middle School's values and aspirations. As a testament to its roots in Coldstream and Tweedmouth, this tartan is sure to evoke feelings of warmth, nostalgia, and regional pride among those who wear it.

name: Tweedside Hunting
description: The Tweedside Hunting tartan, with its rich hues and intricate pattern, evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's countryside. This District tartan, woven by skilled hands at William Wilson & Sons' Bannockburn workshop, is a testament to the country's proud heritage of hunting and outdoor pursuits. Although its origins are shrouded in mystery, with no recorded presence in 19th-century collections, it is believed to have emerged as a 20th-century creation, reflecting the changing tastes and traditions of Scotland's rural communities. Woven by DC Dalgliesh in 1968, this tartan design has become an important part of Scottish cultural identity, cherished for its connection to the land, the lochs, and the thrill of the hunt – a true celebration of Scotland's wild beauty and rich tradition.

name: Tweedside Red
description: Tweedside Red is a captivating District tartan that evokes the rugged beauty of the Scottish Borders. Originally conceived as a fashion tartan by Wilsons of Bannockburn, its distinctive red hue and subtle colour palette reflect the region's rich history and tradition. The registration notes reveal that this tartan was inspired by a fine silk specimen from 1840, which has since become an integral part of the Scottish Tartans Society's heritage. As one of the many tartans to have been designated as District, Tweedside Red carries a deeper significance, symbolising the local connection to the River Tweed and its surroundings. Today, this tartan continues to be worn with pride by those who hold it dear, serving as a tangible link to Scotland's storied past and cultural identity.

name: Tweedsmuir
description: This captivating Fashion Tartan, known to its designer as the Tweedsmuir Dress, holds within it the rich heritage of Scotland's noble Lindsay clan. Named after the Lindsay family's ancestral seat in Angus, this distinctive sett is a masterful blend of traditional and modern elements, showcasing DC Dalgliesh's skill as a weaver and designer. Originally designated as the Lindsay Tartan, the Tweedsmuir Dress was later renamed to reflect its unique characteristics, highlighting the complexity and nuance that define this particular tartan. With its restrictions in place to ensure its authentic production, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of Scottish tradition, waiting to be woven into the fabric of fashion history by skilled artisans inspired by Dalgliesh's masterful design.

name: Twempy
description: The Twempy tartan, born from the ingenious mind of Ronnie Hek, embodies the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's Borders. As a Fashion tartan, it is designed to evoke the stylish flair of modern Highland dress, while its unique seven-colour pattern nods to the region's complex history. Notably, 'Twempy' itself is an informal term for someone from Tweedmouth in Northumbria, a town straddling the English-Scottish border near Coldstream - Hek's own base in the Scottish Borders. This tartan weaves together a blend of tradition and local flair, honouring the nuances of Scotland's intricate relationships with its southern neighbours. A testament to Hek's design skill, Twempy now takes its rightful place among the many iconic patterns that define modern Scottish style.

name: Tyndrum District
description: The Tyndrum tartan is a poignant tribute to the quaint village of northwest Perthshire, situated between Glasgow and Fort William on the historic rail line. Designed by Mairi MacIntyres in 1983, this District tartan tells the story of a close-knit community, with subtle variations in tone and texture evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. With its muted browns and gentle shading, the Tyndrum tartan invites contemplation of the village's rich heritage, from traditional industries to its picturesque surroundings. Though no detailed history accompanies the registration notes, it is clear that this tartan holds a special place in the hearts of those who know its origins, and its subtle nuances serve as a testament to the enduring spirit of the Tyndrum community.

name: Tyneside District
description: The Tyneside Scottish (Blue) tartan is a poignant testament to the region's rich military heritage, specifically associated with the ill-fated Tyneside Scottish Regiment, which played a significant role in World War I. Although the regiment was disbanded following the war, its tartan has endured as a district pattern, evoking the industrial and maritime history of the Tyneside coast. Originally designed during WW1 by an unknown craftsman, this variation of the Black Watch tartan is distinguished by subtle nuances - sometimes manifesting in deep blue hues, other times darkening to rich brown tones or even deep purple undertones. Thread count verified by A.G. Murray, a renowned tartan historian from Stirling, ensures that each fabric thread adheres to traditional Scottish weaving standards, while the tartan's multifaceted character reflects the shifting sands of history and the enduring legacy of the Tyneside Scottish Regiment.

name: Tyneside Scottish Green
description: The Tyneside Scottish Green is a poignant tribute to the region's rich heritage, born from a distinctive colour variation of the iconic Black Watch tartan. Registered in 1914 specifically for the Tyneside Scottish Regiment, now proudly regarded as a district tartan, this unique design tells the story of a community bound by duty and loyalty during World War I. With its subtle colour nuances, this tartan embodies the spirit of the North East of England's industrial heartland, where coal mining and shipbuilding forged a proud identity. As an official District Tartan, it holds a special place in the hearts of those with Tyneside roots, serving as a lasting testament to the region's honourable history and tradition.

name: Tyneside Scottish Khaki
description: The Tyneside Scottish Khaki tartan is a unique and intriguing variation of the traditional Black Watch, born out of the utilitarian needs of World War I for the Tyneside Scottish Regiment. As a district tartan, its origins lie in the practicalities of military life, rather than a specific clan or family heritage. Characterised by an unusual palette that oscillates between dark neutrals such as black, dark brown and khaki, this tartan defies convention with occasional splashes of blue, purple and green. Its nickname, 'Sandbag tartan', is a testament to its utilitarian origins, and its evolution from a functional military design to a distinctive district tartan reflects the complex history of the Tyneside Scottish Regiment's legacy.

name: Tyrconnell Whiskey
description: The Tyrconnell tartan, a personal creation by skilled tailor Geoffrey Highland Crafts, holds deep significance for those bearing the name Tyrconnell. This subtle, yet striking design is based on the MacIntyre Hunting, a historical clan pattern, suggesting a strong connection to Scottish heritage and tradition. A Name tartan like Tyrconnell is reserved exclusively for families with this specific surname, making it a cherished and unique identifier of familial affinity. With its rich, muted tones evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Scottish countryside, the Tyrconnell tartan serves as a poignant reminder of ancestral roots and cultural heritage. Its personal significance extends far beyond mere aesthetics, representing a tangible link to history and community for those fortunate enough to bear this storied name.

name: Tyrone Irish County
description: The Tyrone, County tartan is a captivating representation of Ireland's rich heritage, expertly woven by Polly Wittering on behalf of House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. Originally created as a series of unofficial Irish District tartans, this particular design has proven remarkably popular among enthusiasts and collectors alike. Its classification as a District tartan rather than a Fashion tartan is a testament to its authenticity, acknowledging its origins as a collection of trade tartans for the esteemed Macnaughton family of Pitlochry. As part of the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's enduring connections with Ireland, while also paying tribute to the country's own vibrant textile heritage.

name: UEFA Glasgow
description: The UEFA (Glasgow) tartan, created by esteemed Scottish textile firm Lochcarron of Scotland, is a vibrant corporate design that embodies the spirit of Glasgow's rich heritage and passion for football. As a registered tartan, it holds great honour among those who wear it, signifying their affiliation with the city's esteemed UEFA Club. The threadcount may be an estimate, but the intricate pattern evokes a sense of tradition and craftsmanship that is quintessentially Scottish. Originally designed to adorn scarves, this tartan has the potential to bring warmth and pride to corporate wearers, while also serving as a subtle yet meaningful nod to Glasgow's storied football history.

name: Ulster Peat
description: The Ulster Tartan is an enchanting relic from Northern Ireland's rich cultural heritage, unearthed in a bog burial near Dungiven, County Londonderry, dating back to the mid-17th century. Its origins are shrouded in mystery, but expert interpretation by Audrey Henshall at the National Museum of Antiquities in Edinburgh, revealed that this ancient fabric had been remarkably preserved by the peat soil. The resulting tartan is a testament to the craftsmanship of a bygone era, characteristic of the traditional weaving techniques employed during the 1640-50 period. As one of the oldest known tartans outside of Scotland, its significance extends beyond mere aesthetics, holding dear sway in Northern Ireland's identity and cultural fabric; it is an honouring tribute to the region's complex history and the people who wore these threads with pride.

name: Ulster Red
description: The Ulster (Red Reconstruction) tartan is a poignant tribute to the rich heritage of Northern Ireland's troubled past, distilled from fragments unearthed in a bog near Dungiven, County Londonderry, in 1956. This District tartan, not formally registered by a specific designer, is an evocative interpretation of what the original garments might have looked like, rather than a direct reproduction. The bold red hues and subtle colour nuances evoke the rugged beauty of Ulster's natural landscape, while also paying homage to the complex history and cultural identity of this storied region. As a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's weaving traditions, this tartan design serves as a powerful reminder of the importance of preserving historical heritage and respecting the stories that lie beneath its surface.

name:
UNC Greensboro
[AKA] University of North Carolina at Greensboro
description: The University of North Carolina at Greensboro tartan is a vibrant and distinctive corporate design, woven with pride to represent the institution's rich heritage and academic excellence. Registered under the auspices of Dr Philip D Smith Jnr, this tartan was specifically created for the use of the university alone, solidifying its connection to the esteemed institution's history and traditions. As a Corporate tartan, it is tailored to be worn with honour by members of staff, alumni, and students who wish to pay tribute to their association with the University, while the restrictions in place ensure that this unique design remains an integral part of Greensboro's identity. This tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of North Carolina's premier research university, and its presence on the wearer's garments serves as a badge of honour, signifying affiliation with a prestigious academic community.

name: Union Memorial Tartan
description: The Union Memorial Tartan is a poignant tribute to Britain's military heritage, specifically designed to commemorate the fallen soldiers who have defended the nation in times of war. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority in 1996, this representational tartan features a striking palette of colours, evoking the bravery and sacrifice of various branches of service: light blue for infantrymen, red for artillery units, yellow for cavalry set against a backdrop of Union blue and red, and white and blue echoes of the American flag. Dr. Philip Smith's 1995 design is a masterpiece of tartan craftsmanship, its technical precision and nuanced colour choices paying homage to the rich history and traditions of British military regiments. As a military tartan, the Union Memorial Tartan holds significant cultural importance, serving as a lasting tribute to those who have served their country with valour and distinction.

name: United Distillers Warp
description: The United Distillers tartan, conceived by James Welstead, embodies the spirit of corporate identity in Scotland. As a Corporate tartan, it was designed to represent a brand's heritage and values, rather than a specific family or geographical territory. The distinctive pattern, characterised by its unique thread count and subtle colour nuances, is intended to evoke the rich history and tradition of Scottish distillation. Although the registration notes reveal that the colours may not accurately reflect those originally specified, the tartan's design remains rooted in Welstead's vision of blending different warp and weft threads to create a striking visual effect. As part of the Johnston Collection at the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan serves as a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy of innovation and craftsmanship, where tradition meets modernity in a truly distinctive and captivating way.

name: United Scots American
description: The United Scots American tartan is a vibrant and timeless fashion tartan, embodying the spirit of heritage and tradition that Scotland embodies. Registered as a fashion tartan by renowned designer Trudie Ainsworth of The House of Edgar, this distinctive weave pays homage to the rich cultural exchange between Scotland and America. Its unique combination of colours, carefully chosen to evoke the bold and adventurous nature of the Scottish diaspora, is set against a backdrop of tradition and heritage that continues to inspire wearers around the world. With no restrictions on its use, this tartan invites individuals to proudly celebrate their American-Scottish roots, or simply to add a touch of authentic flair to any outfit.

name: United Services Planning Association
description: The United Services Planning Association tartan is a striking representation of unity and service, born from the innovative design of Dawn Robson-Bell at Lochcarron of Scotland in 1992 or 1993. This distinguished military tartan, registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, weaves together four distinct colours: navy blue for the Navy, red for the Marines, green for the Army, and light blue for the Air Force and United Services Planning Association. Its distinctive pattern pays homage to the bravery and dedication of those who serve in these esteemed branches, while also acknowledging the independent spirit of the United Services Planning Association. This tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich tradition of textile craftsmanship and its enduring connection to the country's military heritage.

name: Universal Scientific Industrial
description: The Universal Scientific Industrial tartan is a modern corporate colourway designed to represent innovation and global reach, born from the pioneering spirit of Universal Scientific Industrial Co., Ltd's (USI) humble beginnings in Irvine, Scotland in 1999. This distinctive tartan has been registered for its association with USI's ambitious expansion into the Digital Media Solutions industry, symbolising the company's strategic partnerships with leading Global Brands across multiple sectors. With a palette of modern blues and greys, reflecting the cutting-edge technology at the heart of USI's product offerings, this corporate tartan embodies the fusion of style, sophistication, and forward-thinking that defines the company's values, making it an ideal choice for businesses seeking to establish their mark in the global market.

name:
University of Kentucky
[AKA] Gaines Center for the Humanities
description: This corporate tartan, designed by Sally T. Guy, pays homage to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland, albeit with a modern twist. Although initially rejected by the Scottish Tartans Authority due to its perceived similarity to MacLeod Hunting, it was subsequently accepted by Bill Johnson's Tartans Educational and Cultural Association, giving it a new lease on life. As such, this tartan has become a unique addition to the world of corporate wear, bearing witness to the evolution of design and tradition. With its distinct colour palette and subtle nuances, it is sure to make a statement in any setting, while also acknowledging the proud history of Scottish textiles that have come before it.

name: University of Trinity College
description: The University of Trinity College tartan is a rich and storied design, woven from the threads of Canadian heritage and Scottish tradition. Registered as a corporate tartan, it serves as a symbolic representation of the institution's values and history, reflecting both the official colours of Trinity College and its sister foundation, St Hilda's College. Created by esteemed designer Bruce Barnett-Cowan, this unique tartan tells the story of Bishop John Strachan's journey from Aberdeen to Upper Canada, where he founded the University of King's College in 1827. The colours chosen evoke a sense of heritage and continuity, linking the college's early beginnings to its enduring legacy as one of Canada's most prestigious institutions.

name: University Plaid
description: The University Plaid is a vibrant and dynamic fashion tartan, boasting a rich history steeped in the academic tradition of Scotland's esteemed institutions. Registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, this distinctive plaid was first spotted at a local catalogue from 'Country Curtains' at the Red Lion Inn, Stockbridge, MA, by Shirley Smith in January 1995. The registration notes reveal that this tartan was discovered in the Johnston Collection, further solidifying its connection to Scotland's rich textile heritage. Named after its discoverer, Dr Philip D (Smith Jnr), who brought it to our attention, the University Plaid is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish fashion and tradition. With no restrictions on its use, this tartan invites wearers to draw inspiration from the country's storied past and proudly showcase their connection to Scotland's academic heritage.

name: Unnamed C18/19th; Antigonish (A, border)
description: This enigmatic Antigonish tartan, unnamed due to its origins shrouded in mystery, offers a fascinating glimpse into Scotland's rich textile heritage. With its distinctive offset pieces of cloth joined at the pivot edge, this unique construction reveals the ingenuity of its creator, likely a weaver or textile artisan from the 18th century. The intricate pattern, comprising two full repeats and an elaborate border sett, is a testament to the skill and craftsmanship of traditional Scottish weaving. As one of the oldest and most intriguing tartans in existence, this piece has been documented by Peter MacDonald in 1997, with estimates suggesting it was woven between 1750 and 1885. Its presence at the Tartan Authority reference #6162 provides a tangible connection to Scotland's cultural past, while online resources offer further insight into its history and significance within the Antigonish region of Nova Scotia.

name: Unnamed C18/19th; Antigonish (A, main)
description: This enigmatic tartan, designated as an "Unnamed C18/19th - Antigonish" (A), is a rare and fascinating relic from Scotland's rich weaving heritage. Weaving in 1750-1885, this piece was meticulously crafted with single full repeat sett, approximately 13 inches wide, interspersed with an elaborate border sett that adorns all four edges of the finished fabric. Its origins are shrouded in mystery, but the unique offset pieces, measuring 26.5 inches wide and 134.5 inches long, with a distinctive 5-inch fringe, hint at its possible Nova Scotian connections. Considered by many to be an example of pre-colonial Scottish tartanry, this Antigonish design is now preserved as part of the Tartans Authority's collection, awaiting further research and discovery to unravel the secrets hidden within its intricate patterns.

name: Unnamed C18th; Hebridean (B)
description: This captivating unregistered tartan, dated to the late 18th century, boasts a striking multicolour check pattern, reminiscent of the intricate weaving traditions of Scotland's Highlands. Although its origins remain uncertain, it is speculated to have been worn by a bride in 1730, lending an air of romantic mystique to this design. The tartan's fine silk threads weave together in a beautifully complex interplay of colour and texture, evoking the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's clans and families. Its status as 'Other' highlights the tartan's intriguing status outside the traditional clan affiliations, allowing it to transcend familial boundaries and connect with those drawn to its timeless beauty and historical significance, regardless of their ancestral roots.

name: Unnamed C18th; S.Uist
description: This enigmatic Unnamed C18th - S.Uist tartan is a fascinating relic from Scotland's rich cultural heritage, its origins shrouded in mystery until recently rediscovered by the Scottish Tartans Society. Originally designated as Hebridean, it has been formally authenticated and dated to circa 1730, placing it firmly within the 18th-century period of Scotland's tartan history. Worn by a notable wearer, Bob Martin, in 1994, this tartan now resides in the esteemed Telfer Dunbar collection, further solidifying its significance as an important piece of Scottish heritage. The S.Uist designation signifies its origins within the Hebridean islands, underscoring the profound impact of these island communities on Scotland's textile traditions. With its complex, intricate weave and mysterious provenance, this tartan design is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's rich cultural past.

name:
Unnamed C19th; (Plaid)'
[AKA] Graham of Menteith Plaid
description: This 19th century plaid, categorised as 'Other', holds a wealth of historical significance, its origins dating back to the tumultuous period following the Battle of Culloden in 1746. Once believed to be handwoven, further analysis by Peter MacDonald revealed that it was actually machine woven, a nod to the technological advancements of the era. Characteristic of this tartan is its striking resemblance to the Graham of Menteith, with an added distinctive black line on the purple ground colour. This unique variation, though not officially registered, remains an intriguing testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scottish textile makers during a pivotal time in the country's history. Its classification as 'Other' acknowledges that it does not conform to the traditional clan tartans, instead falling into a broader category that encompasses lesser-known patterns.

name: Unnamed C19th; Miss Peffer's Plaid
description: Not specified is an intriguing title for this enigmatic tartan, one that hints at a rich history shrouded in mystery. As a Category "Other" design, its purpose may be open to interpretation, though it remains deeply rooted in Scotland's heritage. Lacking a designer byline, we can only assume that this tartan has been woven with the traditional expertise of Scottish artisans, passed down through generations. The fact that no restrictions are mentioned suggests that it is free from any clan or family ties, existing instead as a standalone entity within the world of tartans. Despite its ambiguity, Not specified #4 holds a quiet significance, inviting us to ponder the stories and traditions that may have inspired its creation, and the secrets it keeps hidden beneath its intricate patterns.

name: Unnamed C19th; Wilsons'
