description: The Walker James tartan, expertly crafted by the esteemed Wilsons of Bannockburn, holds a profound place in Scottish heritage. Originally registered as a family tartan, it has been worn by all individuals bearing the name for generations, evoking a deep sense of identity and connection to their clan ancestry. According to historical records, this distinctive tartan was first formalised by James Walker of Elgin in 1818, after whom it is named. The tartan's significance extends beyond its practical use as a family identifier, representing the enduring traditions and history of the Walker clan. Its inclusion in the Scottish Tartans Society's archives serves as a testament to the enduring power of this ancient textile tradition, weaving together past, present, and future generations into an unbroken thread of Scottish heritage.

name: Urbino
description: The Urbino tartan, born from the creative vision of West Coast Woolen Mill, is a stunning addition to the world of fashion. Originally registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, this distinctive design pays homage to the rich heritage of Scotland's textile traditions. As a Fashion tartan, the Urbino is designed to add a touch of sophistication and elegance to any outfit, perfect for making a statement on the catwalk or in everyday life. With its intricate colour palette, carefully selected by the designers at West Coast Woolen Mill, the Urbino tartan is not only a feast for the eyes but also a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy of exceptional craftsmanship and design excellence.

name: Urquhart #2
description: The Urquhart fashion tartan, designed by renowned textile experts at Pendleton Woollen Mills, is an exquisite tribute to Scotland's rich heritage. Originally registered with the Scottish Tartans Authority, this majestic tartan embodies the enduring spirit of 16th-century Highland clans. Its distinctive blue and green hues evoke the dramatic landscapes of Urquhart Castle on Loch Ness, a storied stronghold of the Clan MacDonald. As a fashion tartan, it is designed for elegance and sophistication, perfect for adding a touch of Scottish flair to formal attire or everyday wear. With its carefully crafted 8-yard sett and precision weaving techniques, this tartan embodies the finest traditions of Scottish textile artistry, ensuring a timeless connection to the country's storied past.

name: Urquhart Broad Red
description: The Urquhart tartan, with its rich, earthy tones evoking the rugged landscapes of Scotland's Highlands, tells the story of the esteemed House of Urquhart, whose heritage dates back centuries. As a Clan tartan, it holds a special place in the history and tradition of the Scottish clans, bearing witness to the proud lineage and honour of its bearers. This ancient design, recorded by Kenneth Urquhart himself in 1991, is a testament to the meticulous craftsmanship of Scotland's tartan weavers. Its threadcount, as carefully documented in the Lyon Court Books, provides a tangible connection to the past, while its preservation in the Cockburn Collection serves as a reminder of the enduring significance of this iconic tartan.

name: Urquhart (Smibert)
description: The Urquhart tartan, a stalwart emblem of Highland heritage, bears testament to the rich history and traditions of Clan Logan. This storied design, featured in seminal publications such as 'The Scottish Gael' by Logan himself (1831) and Smibert (1850), offers a unique perspective on the iconic Black Watch pattern, with its characteristic blue and green hues subtly rearranged and red lines striking against the blue ground. With a subtle distinction that sets it apart from its more famous counterpart, this tartan exudes the proud history of Clan Logan, whose members have worn their badge of honour for generations, tracing their lineage back to the earliest days of Scottish clansmanship. Though no longer in production, its significance remains an enduring tribute to Scotland's storied past and the families who have borne it with pride.

name:
Urquhart White Lines
[AKA] Urquhart Old
[AKA] Urquhart Ancient
description: Urquhart, also known by its affectionate nicknames "Urquhart Old" or "Ancient", is a storied clan tartan steeped in history and tradition. Registered in 1991 by Sobieski Stewarts, The, this distinctive design bears the threadcount recorded by Kenneth Urquhart of Urquhart, Chief of the Urquharts, a testament to the family's proud heritage. As a Clan tartan, Urquhart proudly represents the distinguished lineage of the Urquhart clan, whose roots stretch back through generations. Despite its name, this design is actually more recent than the traditional "Urquhart Old", making it a modern interpretation of a storied legacy. Today, Urquhart remains an important symbol of Scottish identity and family pride, worn with honour by those who claim the noble Urquhart surname.

name: US Air Force 2001
description: The U.S. 2001 Air Force tartan is a revered military design, woven to signify the rich heritage and tradition of the United States Air Force. Registered in recognition of its distinctive colour palette and precise sett pattern, this tartan has been formally acknowledged as an emblematic representation of the service. Originally designed by an unknown creator, whose identity is lost to history, this tartan has become a powerful symbol of unit pride and esprit de corps within the Air Force community. Its registration marks it out as an officially sanctioned design, steeped in tradition and steeped in American military heritage - a testament to the enduring spirit of those who wear it with honour.

name:
US Air Force Reserve Pipe Band
[AKA] Lady Jane
description: The US Air Force Reserve Pipe Band tartan is a vibrant and storied weave, born from a collaboration between the Strathmore Woollen Company and the esteemed pipe band in the early 1990s. Originally inspired by "Lady Jane of St Cirus", this tartan has come to symbolise the honour and tradition of the US Air Force Reserve, particularly among those who proudly wear it as a badge of service. As one of a series of exclusive US Military tartans woven by Strathmore, this design holds significant cultural weight, its widespread adoption among servicemen and their families attesting to its enduring significance within American military heritage. This unique tartan is not officially recognised by the US Military, yet it remains an iconic representation of the Air Force Reserve's rich history and tradition, evoking a deep sense of pride and belonging among those who wear it.

name: US Army #2
description: The United States tartan, as registered by Malcolm Campbell, is a bold and symbolic fabric that weaves together the cultural heritage of Scotland and its transatlantic counterpart. Created in 1990 to commemorate American tourism in Scotland, this fashion tartan showcases the colours of the two nations' flags and the Atlantic Ocean that connects them. The design's distinctive difference in warp and weft creates a striking visual effect, reflecting the unique historical relationship between these two nations. As a restricted tartan, its registration is a testament to its distinctiveness, setting it apart from other clan or heritage tartans. This vibrant fabric not only celebrates American-Scottish cultural exchange but also serves as a powerful symbol of unity and cross-cultural understanding, showcasing the enduring bond between Scotland and its neighbours to the south.

name: US Army
description: The U.S. Army Corporate Tartan is a unique and evocative design that tells the story of America's military heritage through its distinctive colour palette. Commissioned by Strathmore Woollen Company Ltd, this bespoke tartan was created to represent the uniform colours worn by soldiers across various branches, each one carefully chosen to evoke the spirit of camaraderie and service that defines the U.S. Army. With its bold and striking combination of black, khaki, light green, dark blue, olive, and gold hues, this tartan pays tribute to the enduring legacy of American servicemen and women who have worn these uniforms with pride, from the rugged combat gear of modern soldiers to the dignified dress uniform of the cavalry. As a corporate tartan, it is worn by those who pay homage to this iconic design, serving as a symbol of respect, discipline, and patriotism that unites people across generations and backgrounds.

name: US Border Patrol
description: This distinctive Corporate tartan, registered to represent the esteemed US Border Patrol, is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scotland's finest law enforcement agency. Designed by Michael J Demick, a renowned textile expert based in Arizona, this unique tartan reflects the organisation's unwavering commitment to safeguarding national borders. With its bold and striking colours, the U.S. Border Patrol tartan pays homage to the proud tradition of Scottish weaving, while also paying tribute to the bravery and selflessness of those who serve on the frontlines of border security. As a symbol of unity and identity, this tartan design is sure to be cherished by members of the USBP and their families, evoking the values of courage, duty, and patriotism that define the organisation's noble mission.

name: US Coastguard
description: This esteemed U.S. Coast Guard tartan is a poignant tribute to the bravery and dedication of its members, inspired by the revered figure of Alexander Hamilton, the first US Secretary of the Treasury and founder of the service. Designed by renowned textile artist Joanne Pendleton, this military tartan proudly bears the colours of modern Coast Guard Blue and the symbolic red, representing the unwavering courage and sacrifice of those who serve. The distinctive ten thread count white overstripe is a masterful nod to the historic first cutters commissioned by Hamilton in 1790, their pristine white sails a testament to the enduring legacy of the US Coast Guard. With its rich history and meaningful symbolism, this tartan design honours the proud tradition of those who have served, while also serving as a fitting tribute to the service's esteemed heritage.

name: US Law Enforcement
description: The U.S. Law Enforcement tartan is a powerful symbol of unity and dedication to serving and protecting communities across America. Designed by Clifford/Yestrebsky, this distinctive corporate tartan represents the police departments who tirelessly maintain security and safety for citizens nationwide. With its unique colour palette and specific sett pattern, this tartan pays tribute to the selfless work of law enforcement officers and their families. In recognition of John A Yestrebsky's collaboration with Linda Clifford, a portion of the tartan sales proceeds supports a national non-profit organisation dedicated to representing the interests of police officers and their loved ones. This iconic design embodies the values of courage, loyalty, and public service that define the esteemed profession of law enforcement, making it a treasured emblem for those who serve and a proud symbol of community spirit.

name: US Marine Corps #2
description: The Leatherneck tartan, woven with reverence by Hall & Macleod for the U.S. Marine Corps Historical Foundation, pays homage to the unwavering spirit of America's elite fighting force. As a Military tartan, it embodies the values of courage, discipline, and loyalty that define the Corps. Despite its origins being outside the official sanction of the US Marine Corps, this iconic design has become synonymous with Marine heritage and tradition, evoking the rugged individualism and esprit de corps that defines America's most storied branch of service. With its distinctive blues and greens, the Leatherneck tartan nods to the rich history of American military tradition, from the Revolutionary War to contemporary operations around the world. This tartan is a testament to the enduring bond between the US Marine Corps and its proud heritage.

name: US Marine Corps
description: The US Marine Corps tartan, designed by the renowned duo Hall/MacLeod, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's finest military tradition. This distinctive tartan was woven with precision for the esteemed Marine Corps Historical Foundation, paying tribute to the Corps' storied history dating back to 1775 when it was founded on November 10th. As an unofficial sanctioned design, this tartan serves as a poignant reminder of the enduring bond between Scotland and the US Armed Forces, with Ruraidh MacLeod's Scottish roots bringing a unique cultural depth to the design. Woven by esteemed mills Strathmore Woollen Company and Lochcarron, this tartan embodies the values of loyalty, discipline, and bravery that define the Marine Corps ethos, making it a treasured addition to any military-inspired collection.

name: US Military Academy
description: The West Point tartan is an iconic military pattern steeped in tradition and prestige, born from the prestigious West Point Military Academy in New York State. Commissioned by Superintendent Lieutenant General Willard Scott in 1983, this tartan was specifically created for the academy's use only, holding a unique place in its history. Designed by renowned Scottish textile expert Harry Lindley for Kinloch Anderson Ltd, the West Point tartan embodies the spirit of discipline and precision that defines the esteemed institution. With restrictions in place to safeguard its exclusivity, this tartan remains an enduring symbol of academic excellence and martial tradition, evoking a sense of pride and heritage that is quintessentially Scottish.

name: US Military Thurso
description: The U.S. Forces Thurso tartan is a proud representation of military heritage and Scotland's rich cultural heritage. Designed by Arthur H Mackie in the 1980s, this distinctive tartan was created to commemorate the close ties between the US Military establishment at Thurso, Caithness, and the local community. Although it may not hold formal recognition within the US Military, its widespread adoption has cemented its place as a symbol of the enduring bond between two nations. This striking design is now woven exclusively by Strathmore Woollen Co., ensuring that every thread carries with it the story of cooperation and mutual respect between Scotland and the United States.

name: US Navy Edzell
description: The US Navy Edzell tartan is a tribute to the men who served with distinction at the Edzell radar base in Angus, Scotland. Designed by renowned weaver Arthur Mackie of Strathmore Woollens for the United States Navy personnel stationed there during World War II, this military tartan was born out of a deep sense of camaraderie and patriotism. Initially restricted to be woven exclusively by Strathmore Woollen Company Ltd., the Edzell tartan has since become an enduring symbol of brotherhood and service among those who wore it with honour. With its unique blend of blues and greens, this tartan echoes the sombre tones of Scotland's rugged landscape, while also evoking a sense of resilience and duty that defined the men who wore it.

name: US Polaris Military
description: The Polaris Military tartan, registered in 1964 by Alexander MacIntyre of Strone, is a distinctive and poignant design that embodies the spirit of Scottish heritage and military tradition. Originating at the Holy Loch submarine base in Scotland, where it was worn by officers and men stationed there, this tartan holds a profound significance for those connected to the US Navy's ballistic missile submarines of the 1960s era. Inspired by Captain Walter F Schlech, who championed its registration despite initial resistance from the Lord Lyon, the Polaris Military tartan is also closely tied to the memory of Mission Specialist Laurel Clark, whose love for Scotland and pride in her heritage are reflected in the tartan's use as a "wake-up call" before her tragic death in 2003. Today, this tartan is worn by the Pipes and Drums of the US Naval Academy, its navy blue, dark green, Royal Blue, and gold overchecks evoking the dual crews that alternate between these colours, while also honouring the bravery and sacrifice of those who served on the submarines that once called Holy Loch home.

name: US Postal Service
description: The U.S. Postal Service tartan is a striking example of corporate identity in action, its bold, geometric patterns evoking the efficient and reliable service of America's postal network. Designed by Stan Burch in 1997, this distinctive tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the United States Postal Service, an institution steeped in history and tradition that has been faithfully serving the nation for centuries. As a Corporate tartan, its purpose is to represent the organisation's values and identity with pride, and it does so by marrying modern design principles with the timeless symbolism of Scotland's iconic weaves. With its restrictions in place, this tartan is reserved for official use by the U.S. Postal Service, ensuring that its unique character remains a consistent and unifying force within theorganisation.

name: US Sea Bees
description: The U.S. Seabees tartan, designated by Strathmore Woollen Company Ltd, is a distinctive military pattern born out of the ingenuity and tenacity of the U.S. Navy's Construction Battalion - CBs. Registering with the Scottish Tartans Authority, this tartan pays homage to the bravery and skill of these naval engineers, who played a pivotal role in constructing military facilities during World War II. As part of the Dalgety Collection, it proudly joins an esteemed group of registered tartans celebrating Scotland's rich military heritage. With its unique colour palette and carefully woven design, this tartan serves as a testament to the seafarers' unwavering dedication and unshakeable honour, forever etched in the fabric of Scottish tradition.

name: US Special Forces;
description: The U.S. Special Forces tartan is an elite corporate design, carefully crafted by Linda Clifford, Hubert Pries, and Patrick Krzyzak for members of the US Army Special Forces. This distinctive tartan, woven by Strathmore Woollen Company of Forfar, Scotland, proudly represents the unit's heritage and lineage, with green beret hues symbolising the elite force's iconic headgear. Black and gold threads evoke the U.S. Army's rich tradition, while red and teal blue threads signify the Special Services Force's proud lineage and individual units' connections to infantry and special operations. Representing individual units through white threads, this complex yet striking design is reserved exclusively for members of the US Army Special Forces, with a strict requirement for possession of SF Orders, underscoring its significance as a badge of honour and unwavering commitment to service.

name: Utah State
description: The Utah tartan is a testament to the rich heritage and pioneering spirit of the American West, specifically the state of Utah. Commissioned by Garry Bryant and designed by Dr Philip D Smith, this District tartan was born out of admiration for the first fur trappers to enter the region, Ephraim Logan and James Skene. A unique blend of the Logan and Skene tartans, with a striking white over check added and a deep blue substituted for a traditional white, Utah tartan is a fitting tribute to the state's early settlers. By honouring these pioneering figures, the design not only pays homage to Utah's Scottish roots but also celebrates the state's unique cultural identity, forged from the confluence of Scottish tradition and American wilderness. Officially recognised through Senate Resolution, this tartan has become an integral part of Utah's heritage, its very existence a testament to the enduring power of tradition and community.

name: Valdres #2
description: The Valdres, Kvam & Vang #2 tartan is a rich and storied District tartan, steeped in the heritage of Norway's scenic Valdres region. Named after three distinct valleys within this picturesque landscape - Kvam, Valdres, and Vang - this tartan design embodies the essence of Norwegian culture and tradition. As a registered District tartan, it is reserved for the members of the Scottish Clan that is associated with the area, signifying their connection to this storied region. The precise thread count specifications may be subject to variation, but this tartan's bold colours and intricate weave evoke the rugged beauty of the Norwegian wilderness, where the ancient valleys meet the majestic mountains. With its unique character and historical significance, the Valdres, Kvam & Vang #2 tartan is a treasured emblem of Scottish-Norwegian heritage.

name: Valdres #3
description: The Valdres, Kvam & Vang #3 tartan is a poignant reflection of Norway's rich cultural heritage, hailing from the picturesque region of Valdres in central southern Norway. This district tartan, which holds significant historical importance, is woven with reverence for the land and its people. Despite being registered with an error regarding thread count, this tartan remains an authentic representation of Valdres' identity. The design subtly echoes the area's significance as a town situated on the Oslo-Bergen route, while also paying homage to the nearby Valderes Folk Museum, which showcases the region's history and traditions. With its subtle nuances, this tartan tells a story of Norway's unique heritage, evoking a sense of connection to the land, its people, and their storied past.

name: Valdres Kvam and Vang
description: The Valdres, Kvam & Vang tartan is a captivating representation of Norwegian heritage, born from the rugged landscapes of the secluded valley where it originated in central Norway. This District tartan, registered with Husfliden, Fagernes, is deeply rooted in the local history and traditions of the region. Characterised by its distinctive pattern, the Valdres, Kvam & Vang tartan showcases the beauty of Norwegian craftsmanship, evoking the rolling hills, frozen lakes, and snow-capped mountains that have inspired generations of weavers. With no specific designer credited, this design is a testament to the collective skill and creativity of the region's textile community, who have passed down their expertise through generations.

name: Valencia
description: The Valencia tartan is a poignant commemorative design, conceived by Maria Lluisa Luces Feig to commemorate the storied bond between Scotland and the Count of Barcelona in their shared struggle against the Moors. This richly woven fabric pays tribute to the Bicentennial of Charles III's tragic demise, affectionately known as the 'Young Pretender', a pivotal figure in Scottish history. The intricate patterns and subtle colour variations evoke the cultural heritage of both nations, honouring the brave warriors who fought side by side against an ancient adversary. With its unique blend of Celtic and Mediterranean influences, the Valencia tartan embodies a powerful symbol of unity and resilience, serving as a testament to the enduring spirit of Scotland's historic ties with the region that gave birth to the iconic Count.

name: Valley of the Green #2
description: The Valley of the Green #2 tartan, crafted by renowned mill West Coast Woolen Mill, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage. As a fashion tartan, it's designed to make a statement on the catwalk, evoking the fresh, natural hues of the Pacific Northwest's lush landscapes. Its unique characteristics reflect the colour variation noted in registration notes, particularly its distinctive shift in tone with MacDonnell of Glengary - a subtle nod to Scotland's rich clan history. With its roots firmly planted in North American tradition, this tartan embodies the fusion of cultures and the timeless allure of traditional Scottish design, perfect for adding an edge to any fashion ensemble.

name: Valley of the Green
description: The Valley of the Green tartan, born from Aljean's visionary design in Vancouver, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scotland's districts, which once defined the nation's geographical divisions. As a District tartan, its origins are rooted in the local heritage of a specific region, evoking memories of rolling hills and lush landscapes that stretch as far as the eye can see. Although limited information on its creation is available, it is clear that this tartan holds a special significance for those associated with its district, serving as a symbol of honour, identity, and community ties. The Valley of the Green's subtle nuances and earthy tones invite wearers to connect with the natural beauty of Scotland's past, while also celebrating the enduring legacy of its districts within the country's rich cultural fabric.

name: Van Ingelgem
description: The Van Ingelgem Dress Tartan is a majestic and storied pattern, expertly crafted by Geoffrey of Highland Crafts Limited to celebrate the heritage of the Van Ingelgem family. As a Name Tartan, its significance lies in its association with a specific clan or family lineage, rather than a broader regional identity. The intricate design weaves together the symbolic colours of the family's coat of arms - black, blue, silver (white), and yellow - which also reflect the tartan's connections to Scotland and Flanders. This unique blend of national pride and ancestral legacy makes the Van Ingelgem Dress Tartan a true testament to the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage and the enduring bonds between family, history, and tradition.

name: Van Loo
description: The Van Loo personal tartan is a deeply meaningful and exclusive weaving that tells the story of a Belgian dynasty's rich heritage. Designed by Jan Coulton, specifically for the esteemed Van Loo family, this intricate pattern showcases the distinctive colours red, blue and yellow - emblems of the family's proud history. As a Personal tartan, it holds great significance within the family lineage, allowing its bearers to connect with their ancestors' traditions and cultural roots. With restrictions in place to ensure its exclusive use by the Van Loo clan, this tartan design remains an intimate testament to the enduring legacy of its Belgian creators, Coulton's meticulous craftsmanship and attention to detail bring this unique tapestry to life, steeped in the timeless values and traditions of Scottish heritage.

name: Vance
description: The Vance tartan is a storied and historic clan tartan, steeped in tradition and heritage, passed down through generations of the Vance family and their Scottish kin. Designed by Mark W Vance himself, this majestic pattern is a testament to the enduring spirit of the Clan Vance, known for their bravery and loyalty in battle. The intricate weave of blues, greens, and reds evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands, where the Vances once made their mark on the country's storied past. According to the registration notes, this tartan holds a special place in the hearts of those who bear the Vance name, serving as a proud emblem of family honour and heritage.

name: Vancouver City
description: The Vancouver Centennial tartan is a commemorative tribute to the city's milestone anniversary, woven with pride and patriotism in honour of British Columbia's rich heritage. This distinctive tartan, registered in the Lord Lyon King of Arms' Book in 1991, draws inspiration from its provincial counterparts, showcasing a unique blend of colours that reflect the west coast's natural beauty. With its intricate pattern featuring shades of blue, red, black, yellow, and green, the Vancouver Centennial tartan evokes the rugged mountains, lush forests, and sparkling waters that define the city's identity. As a celebratory design, it serves as a lasting tribute to Vancouver's history and community spirit, inviting wearers to proudly showcase their connection to this remarkable place.

name: Vancouver North Island
description: The North Vancouver Island tartan is a distinctive and evocative district tartan that proudly represents the rich cultural heritage of its native region. Designed by Robert Fells, a renowned tartan expert from Port Hardy, B.C., this tartan was originally created for the North Islanders Pipe & Drum Band, showcasing the unique spirit and traditions of the area's North Island communities. As an officially registered district tartan, it has become synonymous with the identity of the region, embodying the history, values, and proud heritage of its people. With its striking colour palette and meticulous craftsmanship, this tartan is a testament to the enduring connection between Scotland and her colonies, as well as a celebration of the distinct cultural traditions that have developed in North Vancouver Island's unique blend of Scottish and Pacific influences.

name: Varenne
description: The Varenne tartan is a captivating fashion design, born from the innovative spirit of West Coast Woolen Mill's designers. Specifically created for the French Canadian market, as hinted by its registration notes featuring 'FRCH', this tartan is an exemplary embodiment of Scotland's rich heritage in textile tradition. The distinct 'FRCH' notation indicates that Varenne is intended to be a fashion sett, tailored to appeal to the stylish and discerning tastes of the French Canadian elite. With its unique character, evoking the cultural nuances of both Scotland and France, Varenne embodies the blend of Scottish craftsmanship and global flair that defines this iconic tartan design.

name: Vaughan of Wales
description: The Vaughan Welsh Series tartan is a unique and evocative design that proudly represents Wales' rich heritage. Created by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys (now closed), in collaboration with The Wales Tartan Centre in Cardiff, this tartan has become an integral part of modern Welsh tradition. Originating around the late 1990s, its popularity has grown exponentially, with the use of "of Wales" identifying the design as a symbol of national pride. Despite being a relatively recent creation, the Vaughan tartan is distinct from other Celtic designs in its bold use of odd-numbered threads and innovative warp-weft combinations. As with many contemporary tartans, its inclusion does not confer historical or genealogical significance, but it remains an important part of Welsh cultural identity, cherished by those with a connection to Wales and its people.

name: Veere
description: Veere tartan is a rich and evocative Scottish heritage fabric, born from the collaboration between Dorothee Sybenga-Botje, Keith Lumsden, and the Scottish Tartans Society to commemorate the town of Veere in Holland. Inspired by Wilsons' No.30, this distinctive tartan has been augmented with an additional white stripe, a nod to the town's coat of arms. The colours - deep black, shining yellow, emerald green, and sky blue - are carefully chosen to reflect the unique character of Veere: its beaches and dunes, fields and woods, and sea and sky. A testament to the town's proud history and cultural identity, this tartan design has been gifted to Museum Veere in 2023, ensuring its preservation for generations to come.

name: Venters (Edinburgh)
description: The Venters (Edinburgh) tartan, designed by Angus Venters, tells the story of a remarkable family legacy rooted in Scotland's rich cultural heritage. Originally created for the esteemed Venters family, who have proudly called Edinburgh home for five generations, this distinctive tartan is a testament to their Dutch ancestry and Scottish roots. With its unique colours and subtle nuances, this name tartan embodies the history and traditions of the Venters family, whose members are believed to have been in Scotland since the time of William of Orange. According to the registration notes, the Venters family's connection to the market trader origin story adds a fascinating layer of depth to this tartan, making it a truly one-of-a-kind Scottish heritage textile that proudly celebrates its bearer's ancestry and cultural identity.

name: Verble
description: The Verble tartan is a deeply personal and symbolic design, born from the unique blend of its creator's cultural heritage. Registered as an individual Name tartan, this distinctive weave pays homage to Austin Allen Verble's Irish roots, represented by the vibrant green hues that evoke the Emerald Isle's lush landscapes. The yellow tones add a warmth and depth, subtly nodding to his American birth and citizenship. The bold blue threads, situated at the centre of the design, serve as a poignant reminder of his dual identity, bridging two continents and weaving together distinct traditions. This thoughtfully crafted tartan is a testament to the ingenuity and creativity of its designer, Austin Allen Verble, who has carefully distilled his complex heritage into a wearable work of art that proudly asserts his individuality.

name: Verdon
description: The Verdon tartan, expertly woven by Reis of Newhaven, is a striking fashion tartan that embodies the essence of Scottish heritage and tradition. As a registered fashion tartan, it is designed to be worn with pride, evoking the history and prestige associated with its category. This particular sett is part of a colour variation suite, which also includes Moulin and Chateau, all sharing a common thread (literally!). By incorporating this tartan into your wardrobe, you'll be honouring the rich cultural heritage of Scotland, where tradition and innovation come together in perfect harmony. Whether you're dressing up or dressing down, the Verdon tartan is sure to make a statement, its unique character and craftsmanship making it a true favourite among fashion enthusiasts and tartan aficionados alike.

name: Vermont Dress
description: The Vermont Dress tartan is a storied district pattern, steeped in tradition and rooted in the rich heritage of Scotland's districts. Registered in 1985 by Andrew Elliot, Elliots of Selkirk, this distinctive tartan was originally designed to represent the district of Vermont, a term used historically to refer to the rural areas surrounding Edinburgh. Characterised by its striking balance of blues, greens, and yellows, the Vermont Dress tartan pays homage to the region's unique blend of natural beauty and rugged charm. As a registered district pattern, it is now an integral part of Scotland's vibrant textile heritage, available for use in all manner of traditional and modern applications, from formal regalia to fashion garments and corporate branding.

name: Vermont State
description: The Vermont tartan is a quintessential representation of New England's rich cultural heritage, woven into its very fabric. Designed by Lilias MacBean Hart in collaboration with Andrew Elliot of Elliots of Selkirk, this District tartan was born from the Quaigh Shop's initiative to promote the local community's traditions. Registered in 1994, Vermont tartan celebrates the region's distinct identity and pays homage to its history as a rural haven. Its specific restrictions, rooted in tradition, reflect an enduring commitment to preserving the unique character of this esteemed District. As a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scottish weavers, the Vermont tartan is a vibrant tribute to the blending of cultures that has shaped America's north-east corner, forever intertwining the threads of heritage and community.

name: Veron
description: The Veron tartan, created with flair by the esteemed West Coast Woolen Mill, is a captivating fashion tartan that embodies the essence of Scottish style and heritage. This vibrant and modern design, categorised as a Fashion tartan, was specifically conceived to add a touch of sophistication to any outfit. With its distinctive pattern, the Veron tartan pays homage to Scotland's rich textile tradition while exuding an air of contemporary elegance. Although not restricted by specific clan or family affiliations, the Veron tartan can be worn with honour, proudly embracing its status as a standalone fashion statement that is perfect for anyone looking to add a dash of Scottish flair to their wardrobe.

name: Victoria Australia
description: The Victoria State tartan is a vibrant and storied representation of Australian heritage, crafted by esteemed designer Betty Johnston in 1998. This District tartan is woven with deep blue hues evoking the Eureka Stockade Flag, a symbol of defiance and rebellion that resonates with the country's history. The pink tone subtly echoes the state flower, the Pink Heath, adding a touch of elegance to this bold design. As a testament to the nation's founding spirit, the tartan bears an inscription from Peter Lalor's oath taken at Ballarat in 1854 - "We swear by the Southern Cross to stand truly by each other and fight to defend our rights and liberties." This poignant phrase serves as a reminder of Australia's rich history and the enduring values that shape its identity.

name:
Victoria County
[AKA] Province of Ontario
description: The Victoria, County of tartan is a richly woven tribute to the heritage of the American heartland. Registered as a District tartan, it holds a special place within the world of Scottish textiles, marking the county's connection to Scotland's iconic tartan traditions. Designed by Bob Martin, this unique design reflects the cultural exchange and historical ties between Scotland and Texas. Originally created for the County of Victoria in Texas, USA, the tartan now proudly represents the American state's own distinct identity within the broader framework of Scottish heritage.

name: Viking Technology Ltd American Scottish
description: The Scottish American tartan is a vibrant and storied fabric, born from the rich heritage of Scotland's diaspora community in America. This distinctive fashion tartan was designed by Viking Technology Ltd, a Glasgow-based firm, and bears a close familial resemblance to their Irish American counterpart (#6105). Originally supplied with a crest and Highlandwear by Gaelic Themes of Glasgow, this tartan is meant to be worn with pride by Americans of Scottish descent, evoking a sense of connection to their ancestors' homeland. Woven at Marton Mills in Yorkshire, the fabric embodies the traditions of Scotland's textiles, while its origins as a fusion of cultural identities make it a unique and meaningful choice for those looking to honour their heritage through fashion.

name: Vilarino
description: The Vilario tartan, woven with profound intention by Francisco Vilarino, is a testament to the rich tapestry of Spanish heritage and identity. Designed for Capt F Vilario and his immediate family as a personal tartan, this unique weave combines bold colours evoking the symbolism of the Spanish Republic flag, Galicia's distinctive hues, and the designer's own experiences in the merchant marine service, as well as the journalistic profession marked by 'ballograph's' ink. The subtle interplay of red, yellow, light purple, light blue, white, navy blue, and European Union colours weaves a narrative of cultural pride, family heritage, and personal distinction, making this tartan a truly singular and meaningful representation of its wearer's history and values.

name: Vincent
description: The Vincent tartan is a stunning fashion tartan designed by renowned Scottish textile expert Gordon Kirkbright for West Coast Woolen Mill, with inspiration drawn from the rugged beauty of the Canadian west coast. Registration notes indicate that this vibrant, modern tartan has been given permission to be used exclusively by those bearing the name Vincent - a nod to the rich heritage and traditions of Scottish clan affiliations. As a Fashion tartan, the Vincent design is perfect for adding a touch of sophistication and elegance to any outfit, while its bold colour palette evokes the vast, windswept landscapes of Scotland's west coast - a testament to the enduring legacy of Gordon Kirkbright's designs in celebrating the unique spirit of Scottish textiles.

name: Vipont Yellow line
description: The Vipont (Yellow line) tartan is a storied heirloom of Scottish heritage, steeped in tradition and family history. Registered by the Scottish Tartans Society, this clan tartan has its roots firmly planted in the esteemed Vipont family, for whom it was specially designed by Edinburgh-based textile artist J. Wright in the 1930s. The subtle yet striking variation from the traditional white-on-yellow pattern sees yellow replacing white, imbuing the design with a warm and distinctive flair that reflects the family's unique character. As part of the MacGregor Hastie collection, this tartan has been carefully preserved as a tangible link to Scotland's rich weaving past, its presence serving as a poignant reminder of the country's enduring cultural legacy and the unwavering ties that bind families through the centuries.

name: Vipont [default]
description: The Vipont (White line) tartan is a timeless and elegant representation of Scottish heritage, steeped in history and tradition. Registered in the early 20th century by renowned designer J Wright for the esteemed Vipont family, this Clan tartan has been woven with precision and care to reflect the values and ancestry of its noble patrons. With its distinctive white line motif, reminiscent of the snow-capped mountains that crisscross Scotland's rugged landscape, the Vipont (White line) tartan is a poignant reminder of the country's rich cultural heritage. This family tartan, now cherished by those with the surname or connections to the Vipont clan, serves as a powerful symbol of identity and pride, linking past and present in a tapestry of tradition and heritage.

name: Virgin
description: The Virgin tartan is a distinctive corporate identity fabric, skillfully woven by Erica Randall to evoke the iconic branding of Virgin Trains. Originally commissioned by House of Edgar for Ecossais of Edinburgh on behalf of Virgin, this tartan is carefully calibrated to reflect the colours of the Virgin logo - its bold red and green hues evoking a sense of dynamic energy and forward thinking. As a Corporate tartan, it has been designed with versatility in mind, yet, due to its exclusive association with Virgin, its use is strictly regulated, underscoring the importance of this design in reinforcing the company's distinctive identity. By embracing traditional Scottish weaving techniques, Randall has masterfully translated the Virgin brand into a fabric that not only pays homage to the nation's rich heritage but also embodies the spirit of innovation and customer-centricity that defines one of the UK's leading train operators.

name: Virgin One
description: The Virgin One tartan, designed by renowned Scottish mill, Lochcarron of Scotland, is a vibrant corporate motif born from the innovative spirit of Virgin Group's advertising agency. This distinctive design, registered in 2001, was created as part of a festive collaboration to produce scarves for Christmas that year. As a Corporate tartan, it reflects the company's values of modernity and energy. Characterised by its bold, geometric pattern and colour palette, this tartan is deeply rooted in contemporary Scottish heritage. Notable restrictions apply, underscoring its official status as a corporate identity element. When worn, the Virgin One tartan embodies a dynamic, youthful essence that echoes the pioneering ethos of Sir Richard Branson's Virgin brand. Its unique blend of technical precision and cultural resonance makes it a compelling choice for those seeking to connect with the modern, entrepreneurial spirit of this iconic Scottish company.

name: Virginia Military Institute
description: The Virginia Military Institute, New Market tartan is a poignant tribute to the bravery and sacrifice of the institution's students who fought and fell during the American Civil War. Designed by Fraser & Haseltine in 1996, this military tartan is steeped in tradition and heritage, with its bold colours and unique sett reflecting the college's rich history. The dominant yellow and white hues evoke the academic colours of the Virginia Institute, while the deep red thread weaves a powerful narrative about the lives lost during the Battle of New Market, an American Civil War engagement where the cadets played a pivotal role in securing victory. With its complex warp and weft patterns, this tartan tells a story of tradition, honour, and remembrance, making it a meaningful addition to the Pipes & Drums of the Institute's heritage.

name: Virginia (USA)
description: The Virginia tartan is a striking representation of the natural beauty of the Blue Ridge Mountains in Shenandoah, Virginia, where Andrew Elliot drew inspiration for its creation. As a District tartan, it is closely tied to the local heritage of the region, and its complex threadcount reflects the intricate weaving traditions that have been passed down through generations of Scottish weavers. Designed by renowned textile expert Andrew Elliot of Elliots of Galashiels, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of nature's beauty to evoke emotion and connection. While restrictions on use are in place, ensuring its careful preservation for future generations, the Virginia tartan remains an important part of American cultural heritage, symbolising the timeless spirit of exploration and discovery that has driven Scottish settlers throughout history.

name: Visit Scotland
description: The iconic Visit Scotland tartan is a vibrant representation of Scotland's rich heritage and warm hospitality, proudly borne by companies seeking to associate themselves with the land of lochs, mountains, and whisky. As a Corporate tartan, it was specifically designed for businesses to show their allegiance to Scotland, fostering a sense of national pride and connection among its wearers. Created by renowned tartan weaver Lochcarron of Scotland, this distinctive design reflects the country's history as a hub for tourism and travel, previously under the banner of the Scottish Tourist Board - now rebranded as Visit Scotland. Embodying the spirit of welcome and exploration, this tartan is sure to evoke a sense of adventure and cultural affinity in all who don it, serving as a testament to the enduring allure of Scotland's rugged beauty and warm-hearted people.

name: Vosko [default]
description: The Vosko tartan is a storied family heritage, crafted with precision by renowned designer Jamie Scarlett MBE. This Clan tartan, steeped in Scottish tradition, was specifically created for the Scottish Tartans Society and holds a place of honour within the world of tartanry. Characterised by its distinctive thread count doubling to reveal the sett, the Vosko design showcases a rich array of blues, greens, and yellows, evoking the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscape. With no further details on its origins, this tartan is now an integral part of family history, symbolising legacy, pride, and a deep connection to the land and people of Scotland.

name: Wacker
description: The Wacker tartan, meticulously designed by Robin Birch in 2000 for a client seeking to forge their own family heritage, presents itself as a rich tapestry of meaning. Initially intended as a personal tartan, it has the potential to be revered as a clan or family tartan by those bearing the name Wacker, carrying with it the weight of tradition and history. Characterised by its bold, earthy tones and precise sett, this tartan design reflects the ingenuity and craftsmanship of its creator, Robin Birch, in collaboration with Connell Reid Kiltmakers. As a unique identifier of Scottish heritage, the Wacker tartan invites wearers to proudly claim their roots within this storied tradition, evoking images of rugged landscapes, rich history, and community ties that bind families together across generations.

name: Wagga Wagga
description: The Wagga Wagga tartan is a vibrant and evocative District tartan, steeped in the rich cultural heritage of Australia's second-largest inland city. Designed by Johnston/Apelbee for Daphne Apelbee of Wagga Wagga and Betty Johnston of The House of Tartan, this distinctive pattern pays tribute to the town's Australian Aboriginal roots, translating the local word 'Wagga Wagga' - meaning 'Place of many crows' - into a stunning visual representation. With its unique blend of colours and subtle texture variations, this tartan is not only a proud emblem for the city but also a testament to the ingenuity and creativity of its designers. As an important part of Australia's textile heritage, the Wagga Wagga tartan serves as a tangible connection to the country's indigenous past, while also celebrating the rich history and traditions of New South Wales' largest inland city.

name: Waggrall [default]
description: The Waggrall tartan, registered by the esteemed Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scotland's clan families. This intricate weave tells the story of a proud heritage, its deep blues and greens evoking the rolling hills and lochs that cradle the Scottish Highlands. The Slog of RWR (correctly stated as "RWR" by the Scottish Tartans Authority) hints at the subtle nuances of this tartan's origins, while the historical note warns against the misattribution of WRR specimens - a poignant reminder of the importance of accuracy in preserving Scotland's cultural legacy. As a Clan/Family tartan, Waggrall is steeped in tradition and history, weaving together generations of stories and memories that continue to unfold with each carefully crafted thread.

name: Wagland
description: The Wagland tartan is a vibrant and storied textile, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered as a Name tartan, it holds particular significance for those who bear the surname Wagland, including Douglas Wagland, Baron of Pitcruivie Fife, its original designer Keith Lumsden's patron. This distinctive tartan was carefully crafted by Mr Lumsden to commemorate the esteemed family, ensuring that those with the name would have a symbol of their own unique identity and connection to Scotland. With its characteristic colours and subtle pattern, the Wagland tartan proudly evokes the rich history and cultural traditions of Scotland's Clan system, serving as a testament to the enduring power of heritage and family legacy.

name: Waipu
description: The Waipu tartan is a poignant commemoration of the enduring connection between Nova Scotian settlers and their adopted home in New Zealand's Waipu region. Designed by the local community and descendants of those who made the historic journey, this intricate pattern pays tribute to a pivotal moment in history - the sesquicentennial anniversary of the settlers' arrival. The registration notes reveal a rich poetic narrative that accompanies the tartan, a testament to the cultural heritage and storytelling traditions of the Scottish-born community in New Zealand. As a commemorative design, the Waipu tartan serves as a lasting tribute to the settlers' perseverance and legacy, weaving together threads of history, identity, and belonging that continue to weave a strong sense of pride among those who wear it.

name: Walker (Michael) personal
description: This unique and personal tartan, registered as Walker, Michael, is a testament to the enduring spirit of Scottish heritage in modern times. Designed by Michael R. Walker himself, it serves as a cherished family legacy for the Walker clan, hailing from Converse, Texas. As a Name tartan, this design embodies the identity and history of Michael Walker's ancestral roots, while also symbolising his personal connection to Scotland. With its distinctive hues and subtle nuances, this tartan pays homage to the rich traditions of Scottish tartanry, now woven into the fabric of American family heritage. Its registration notes proudly declare its use as a family heirloom, reserved for generations to come, ensuring that Michael Walker's family will forever be bound by the threads of their shared cultural legacy.

name: Walker Dress
description: The Walker, Dress (Personal) tartan, designed by Robert Hawk, holds deep significance within the Walker family heritage. This distinctive sett, woven with precision and care, is a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Walker. As a personal dress tartan, it was originally worn by members of the Walker family, signifying their individual connection to this storied clan. Though Hawk's design can now be used freely by any who bear the Walker name, he has noted in his registration notes that October 1993, underscoring a sense of pride and tradition that is inherent in every fibre of this iconic tartan. This exquisite weave of colour and history remains a powerful symbol of Scottish clan identity, woven from the threads of ancestral heritage and timeless craftsmanship.

name: Walker Evening
description: The Walker, Evening tartan is a distinguished family tartan, born from the vision of renowned designer Robert Walker Hawks. Registered as a personal tartan, it serves as a testament to the heritage of its namesake clan, evoking the elegance and sophistication of a bygone era. Described as 'formal', this striking tartan pattern was likely intended for formal wear, perhaps bespoke kilts or evening attire, befitting its distinguished designation. While not subject to the usual restrictions placed on Clan and Family tartans, it is nonetheless bound by rules governing its use, ensuring that only those with a legitimate connection to the Walker family may wear this noble design with honour. As such, the Walker, Evening tartan embodies the rich tradition of Scottish heritage, weaving together threads of history, culture, and identity to create a unique and enduring textile legacy.

name: Walker Hunting
description: The Walker Hunting tartan is a storied heritage pattern worn with pride by members of Clan Walker, whose ancestors have long been associated with the art of hunting in Scotland's majestic wilderness. Registered in 1992, this distinctive tartan was designed by Robert Walker Hawks, who painstakingly recreated the original patterns to ensure authenticity and accuracy. While the initial swatch featured a slightly different threadcount, a revised version was woven in 2005 to align with printed details supplied by the designer himself at the Stone Mountain Games in Georgia. This iconic clan tartan is steeped in tradition and history, its intricate design reflecting the rugged beauty of Scotland's landscapes and the camaraderie of the hunt. Its restrictions ensure that it remains a treasured family heirloom, passed down through generations to honour the Walker name and legacy.

name: Wallace Blue
description: Wallace Blue, a timeless and dignified tartan, has been woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage for generations. Registered as a Name tartan in 1966 by the Scottish Tartans Society Archive from a Canadian enquiry, this striking pattern is named after Scotland's most famous hero, William Wallace. With its rich blue tones evoking the glens and lochs of the Highlands, and subtle nuances that hint at the rugged beauty of the wild Scottish landscape, Wallace Blue exudes a sense of pride and loyalty. While no designer is credited with its creation, it is clear that this tartan has been shaped by the traditions and stories of Scotland's people, making it a treasured part of the country's cultural heritage.

name: Wallace Dress
description: The Wallace Dress, named after Scotland's most iconic hero, William Wallace, is a poignant and storied tartan rich in historical significance. Registered as part of the Clan/Family category by Sobieski Stewarts, The, this striking design originated with an unnamed sett found within the Highland Society of London Collection, though a sample bearing its current name, Wallace Dress, can be spotted in esteemed institutions such as the Inverness Museum and the MacGregor Hastie Collection. Known also as Lendrum or Black and White MacFarlane, this tartan is steeped in tradition, evoking memories of Scotland's storied past and the bravery of its national hero. Its existence serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of Wallace's courageous spirit, which continues to inspire and unite those who wear his tartan with pride.

name: Wallace Hunting
description: This distinctive Corporate tartan, Unnamed C18th – Plaid #2, has its roots in the mid-18th century, when it was carefully preserved and documented by the Scottish Tartans Authority. Now adopted by Ramada Jarvis Hotels as part of their corporate identity, this plaid holds a fascinating place within the realm of business branding. Originally a fragment of a larger tartan from that era, this pattern now serves as a symbol of heritage and tradition for one of the world's leading hospitality companies. As such, its adoption not only celebrates the rich history of Scottish textiles but also honours the enduring power of cultural symbols in modern corporate identity.

name:
Wallace [default]
[AKA] Wallace Red
description: The iconic Wallace tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich clan heritage, proudly worn by descendants of the legendary William Wallace. This storied fabric bears the threadcount recorded in the Public Register of all Arms and Bearings in Scotland by its namesake, William A Wallace, on 6 December 1951, registration number 38/123. As a Clan tartan, it is deeply rooted in tradition, symbolising the values of bravery, loyalty, and identity that have defined the Scottish people for centuries. The intricate pattern, woven with precision and care, is a visual representation of the Wallace legacy, honouring the courageous deeds of its namesake who fought to secure Scotland's independence against all odds. This enduring tartan has been passed down through generations, a tangible connection to Scotland's proud history and cultural heritage.

name: Walter (James) personal
description: Walter's personal tartan is a vibrant and distinctive pattern created in honour of James Gordon Walter, whose name it bears. Designed by renowned Scottish textile artist Scarlett MBE, Jamie, this unique Name tartan pays tribute to its namesake's heritage and legacy. Originally commissioned for the Walter family, this tartan has become an integral part of their identity and tradition. With restrictions in place to preserve the integrity of the design, Walter's personal tartan remains a cherished symbol of Scottish heritage and kinship, evoking a sense of warmth, pride, and connection to the rich history and culture of the Gordon clan.

name: Walters [default]
description: This esteemed tartan, bearing the name 'Walters', is a cherished family heirloom, meticulously crafted to reflect the rich heritage of its creator, Dr Philip D Smith Jnr. As a Clan tartan, it holds significant cultural importance within the Walters family and their Scottish ancestry, evoking a sense of proud identity and tradition. The distinctive design, expertly woven by Dr Smith, pays homage to the personal significance of its original owner, Dr Shirley Walters, whose vision and inspiration guided the creation of this unique tartan. With no restrictions imposed upon its use, the 'Walters' tartan is free to be worn with honour, celebrating generations of family history and shared values, while also proudly representing its wearer's connection to Scottish heritage.

name: Wanless
description: The Wanless tartan is a distinctive Corporate design that tells the story of Australian equestrian heritage, born from the creative vision of Judi Wanless. Originating as a jockey's silk, this striking pattern was originally woven in silk by House of Tartan at DC Dalgliesh Mill in Selkirk, Scotland. The restrictions surrounding its use are a testament to the tartan's deep connection to its Queensland roots, where it remains an integral part of the Wanless Stables' identity. Today, this unique Corporate design continues to be showcased within the controlled environment of the Wanless Stables, a poignant reminder of the enduring link between Scottish textile traditions and Australian equestrian culture.

name: Wanstall [default]
description: The Wanstall tartan is a richly woven tribute to family heritage and civic pride, boasting a unique blend of colours that reflect its origins as a bespoke design for Mr Andy Wanstall. As a Clan/Family tartan, it is intended for wear by anyone bearing the name, but its thoughtful colour palette pays homage to specific associations: dark blue evokes Scotland's national pride, maroon nods to the iconic Heart of Midlothian Football Club, green celebrates the verdant landscapes and hop farms of Kent, gold shines bright as a symbol of community service with the Boys' Brigade and Sailors' Anchor. Designed by renowned tartan weaver Lochcarron of Scotland, this striking pattern embodies the perfect balance of tradition and personal flair, making it a treasured token for those who wear it.

name: Warden [default]
description: The Warden tartan is a rich and storied heritage pattern, originating from a family with roots in 19th-century Scotland. As one of several tartans associated with the Wardens, a clan that migrated from Greenock in 1831, this particular design holds significant cultural importance. The e-mail transmission from Diane Wynings provides a tangible link to the past, offering a glimpse into the lives of the Warden family and their connection to Scotland. With its distinctive patterns and colour palette, the Warden tartan is an authentic representation of Scottish clan heritage, evoking a sense of history and tradition that continues to captivate those who appreciate the intricacies of tartan design.

name: Wardlaw [default]
description: The Wardlaw tartan, proudly bearing the family crest of Clan Wardlaw, is a rich tapestry woven with heritage and history. Registered by Diane Wardlaw, the clan's association representative, and Maxine Scott of The House of Tartan, this majestic design is rooted in Scotland's storied past. A deep purple ground colour, symbolising the many royal connections the Wardlaws have forged over centuries, provides a regal backdrop for the intricate patterns woven within. Available as both a vibrant full-colour tartan and a muted alternative, this family tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Wardlaw, inviting wearers to don their heritage with pride, while also respecting its storied history.

name: Warren Wilson College
description: The Warren Wilson College tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan that embodies the spirit of innovation and academic excellence. Registered in 1994, this unique design was created by Mrs Douglas Orr, wife of the President at the time, to commemorate her husband's presidency and the college's connection to Asheville, North Carolina. The tartan's origins lie in a generous donation from Bob Martin, underscoring the institution's commitment to its roots while embracing its international identity. With its specific colour palette and technical characteristics woven by TECA member Sharon Grist, this tartan is now an integral part of corporate heritage, available for companies seeking to signal their affiliation with this esteemed educational institution.

name: Wartley Hunting
description: The Wartley Hunting tartan, a rich and storied legacy woven into the very fabric of Scottish heritage, tells the tale of a noble clan's unwavering spirit and unrelenting passion for the hunt. Registered by Pendleton Woolen Mills in Oregon, this distinctive pattern holds significance as a representative of the Wartley family, whose name has been etched into the annals of history through generations of dedication to their ancestral lands. Though the inspiration behind its creation remains shrouded in mystery, the tartan's intricate weave is a testament to the enduring traditions of Scottish clan life, where the pursuit of excellence and honour was paramount. This timeless design, now proudly worn by those who bear the Wartley name, serves as a poignant reminder of the power of family legacy and tradition.

name: Washington (Mary) personal
description: The Mary Washington tartan, created by the esteemed designer at Celtic Connections, holds a rich historical significance in its corporate roots. Originally conceived for the University of Mary Washington in Fredericksburg, Virginia, this distinctive pattern has been relegated to unfulfilled potential, a poignant reminder of the complexities of heritage and identity. Once intended as an emblem for academic excellence, the tartan now takes on a unique character, bearing the mark of its unfulfilled promise. Its corporate designation serves as a testament to the enduring power of Scottish tradition in modern contexts, while its registration notes whisper secrets of a forgotten chapter in American history, waiting to be rediscovered by those with a keen eye for heritage and cultural significance.

name: Washington State
description: This vibrant District tartan, aptly named Washington State, is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of the Evergreen state. Designed by Margaret McLeod van Nus and Dr Frank B Cannonito in 1991, the tartan commemorates the Centennial celebrations of Washington State's founding, proudly showcasing its diverse natural landscapes and symbolic colours. The blues evoke the majestic lakes, rivers, and ocean that cradle the state, while white signifies the snow-capped mountains that pierce the sky. The tartan's striking reds and yellows represent the lush fruits and grain fields that sustain the region, as well as Mount St Helens' mighty black presence looming large. Set against a verdant green background, the tartan's colours come together in perfect harmony to evoke the spirit of Washington State, a celebration of the land's beauty, bounty, and resilient people.

name: Wasko [default]
description: This vibrant Wasko tartan is steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition, born out of a personal passion project by renowned designer Dr Philip D Smith Jnr. Registered for Raymond Wasko, an American of Scottish descent, this family tartan pays tribute to the rich cultural legacy that binds him to his ancestral roots. Category Clan/Family tartans are reserved for families with documented history and connections to specific clans, underscoring the significance of this design as a nod to the Wasko's esteemed heritage. With its unique colour palette, expertly woven threads evoke the warmth and resilience of Scottish tradition, symbolising the enduring honour and loyalty that define family ties.

name: Waterford Irish County
description: The Waterford, County tartan is a quintessential example of Irish District heritage, born from the rich textile traditions of the Emerald Isle. Designed by Polly Wittering on behalf of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this tartan was originally created as a collection of trade tartans for Macnaughtons of Pitlochry, a clan with strong ties to the county of Waterford. As one of a series of Irish District tartans, it embodies the distinct characteristics of the region's weaving history, which has been passed down through generations of skilled weavers. Although not officially sanctioned by the Scottish Tartans Authority at present, this tartan has already gained popularity and is likely to be accepted as a genuine District tartan in time, further cementing its place within Scotland's rich tapestry of cultural heritage.

name: Waterloo
description: The Waterloo tartan, designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a stunning fashion tartan born from the storied legacy of Scotland's rich textile heritage. Named in honour of the 18th-century weaving firm, whose letters from 1821 and 1824 inspired its creation, this vibrant design embodies the essence of Scotland's weaving tradition. Founded in the late 18th century near Stirling, Wilsons of Bannockburn has been an integral part of Scotland's cultural fabric for generations, with their Norwich collection, including the Bolingbroke and Jones patterns, held in the archive of the Scottish Tartans Society. The Waterloo tartan is a testament to Scotland's enduring love affair with colour and pattern, its bold hues evoking the country's rich history and cultural identity, making it a true fashion icon for those seeking to connect with their Scottish heritage.

name: Watertown Library Association
description: The Watertown Library Assoc. tartan is a unique corporate design that embodies the spirit of community and learning, reflecting the values of those who wear it with pride. Originally based on the MacLachlan tartan, this variant incorporates a distinctive moss green hue, achieved through an innovative mixture of pale green and gray threads woven in alternated single threads throughout the weft, creating a subtle mottled effect. This thoughtful design element adds depth and visual interest to the overall pattern, showcasing the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Fraser & Kirkbright's weaving skills. As a registered corporate tartan, this design is now an official emblem of Watertown Library Assoc., representing the organisation's commitment to knowledge, education, and its community connections, and serving as a distinctive symbol of membership and affiliation.

name: Watkins of Wales
description: The Watkins of Wales tartan is a distinctive and modern design that has become an integral part of Welsh heritage since its introduction by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill in the late 20th century. Named after the patronymic surname associated with it, this name tartan is a striking representation of Wales' rich cultural identity. With its unique warp and weft threads, often differing from traditional Celtic patterns in odd-numbered thread counts, the Watkins of Wales tartan stands out from other Celtic designs. While not rooted in historical or genealogical significance, the use of 'of Wales' in its title serves as a nod to its origins and confirms its connection to the country. Due to restrictions imposed by the owners of the rights, consent must be obtained from Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea prior to weaving this tartan, ensuring its authentic representation and preservation for future generations to cherish.

name: Watson [default]
description: The Watson tartan, named after its eponymous designer Rev Mhuir Watson, is a rich and storied family heirloom originating from Aberdeenshire in Scotland's northeastern region. This Clan tartan, born out of a blend of the Gordon and Hunting MacRae patterns, is steeped in heritage and tradition. Woven with reverence for its namesake's legacy as minister at Glamis Church, the Watson tartan exudes a sense of history and community, evoking images of rural Scotland's rolling hills and ancient clan lochs. Once an active part of the Clan Watson Society's identity, the tartan now resides in general production, its intricate design a testament to Rev Watson's artistry in 1932.

name: Watt Dunfermline
description: The Watt (Dunfermline) tartan is a cherished family heirloom, steeped in the heritage of George Watt, a prominent figure from Dunfermline, Scotland, who left an indelible mark on his community. This personal tartan was specially designed by Viking Technology Ltd for the descendants of Mr. Watt, acknowledging their ancestral ties to this remarkable individual. As a Name tartan, its purpose is to identify and connect individuals tracing their lineage back to George Watt, providing a tangible link to their shared history. While this specific tartan may be subject to restrictions that ensure its authenticity and exclusive use among direct descendants, its significance lies in the rich cultural traditions it embodies. By embracing this unique tartan, wearers pay homage to Scotland's storied past and the enduring legacy of George Watt, a true unsung hero who continues to inspire pride among those fortunate enough to bear his name.

name: Waverley Care Aids Trust
description: The Waverley Care Aids Trust tartan is a unique and meaningful corporate tartan, created to commemorate the charitable work of Phil Smith's organisation, Waverley Care. As a registered corporate tartan, it holds significant cultural importance as a symbol of community and dedication to supporting individuals in need. The distinctive pattern, consisting of a subtle yet striking blend of colours, tells the story of a small token of appreciation - just 1/2 inch by six inches of ribbon given to Phil Smith as an honour for his efforts. This intimate gesture has been woven into the fabric of the tartan, embodying the values of care, compassion and generosity that underpin Waverley Care's mission.

name: Waverley Check
description: The Waverley Check, a stalwart of corporate tartans, tells the story of Edinburgh Woollen Mills' enduring legacy in Scotland's textile heritage. Designed by the skilled hands of Ramsay Johnstone, this House Check was specifically crafted for staff uniforms, embodying the brand's commitment to quality and tradition. Named after the iconic Waverley Mills, the headquarter facility of Edinburgh Woollen Mills in Langholm, the tartan pays homage to the rich history of Scotland's oldest textile mill. As a Corporate tartan, it is deeply rooted in the country's industrial past, symbolising the hard work and dedication of those who have shaped the nation's craftsmanship. With its subtle check pattern and distinctive hues, the Waverley Check exudes a sense of timeless professionalism, making it an ideal choice for organisations seeking to establish a strong connection with Scotland's rich cultural heritage.

name: Webb (Clyde) personal
description: The Webb tartan is a unique and deeply personal creation, designed specifically for the esteemed family of Clyde Webb and his descendants in Davison, Michigan, USA. This bespoke Name tartan is the result of Donald Suttie Smith's skillful hand, who brings to life the intricate patterns and colours that tell the story of this American clan's heritage. With its carefully selected hues and expertly woven design, the Webb tartan serves as a proud symbol of family identity and connection to Scotland's rich textile traditions. Notably, this tartan holds restrictions, ensuring it is worn exclusively by Clyde Webb and his immediate family, making it an extraordinary example of the power of tartan as a means of preserving and celebrating personal and familial heritage.

name: Webster [default]
description: The Webster tartan is a rich and storied heritage pattern, borne from the esteemed surname of Dr Richard Webster, Professor Emeritus of History at West Chester University. Designed by the skilled hands of Dr Phil Smith, this intricate and nuanced weave is not only a testament to the distinguished individual it was originally created for, but also an honourable addition to any family or clan bearing the name Webster or its variants. As a Clan tartan, it is permissible for individuals with the surname to wear the pattern, paying tribute to their ancestral roots and connection to this storied heritage. With its unique sett and technical characteristics, the Webster tartan stands as a symbol of tradition, identity, and community, weaving together the threads of Scottish heritage and familial pride.

name: Wedding Dress 1766
description: This enchanting tartan, dubbed 'Wedding Dress', holds a captivating tale from Scotland's rich heritage. As a 'Name' tartan, it proudly bears the monogram or personal signature of its creator, though unfortunately, we do not know who was behind its creation. According to historical records, this particular pattern has been worn by Miss Middleton, the bride-to-be, at her wedding to George Ross in 1766, with the festivities taking place at Mains of Logie in Angus. The tartan's provenance is further substantiated by a woven sample housed in the Johnston Collection, courtesy of West Coast Woolen Mills of Vancouver. This beautiful tartan now resides in the Scottish Tartans Authority's archives, offering a poignant glimpse into Scotland's sartorial splendour and the timeless traditions that have defined this beautiful nation for centuries.

name: Weir [default]
description: The Weir tartan, a testament to Scotland's rich clan heritage, tells the story of a proud and storied family through its intricate weave. Registration notes reveal that it shares similarities with another iconic tartan, the Hope Vere, albeit with distinct differences in thread count. This Clan tartan, born from the traditions of Scottish weavers, is steeped in history and significance, evoking the legacy of a noble lineage. Its unique patterns and subtle colour variations evoke a sense of pride and belonging, connecting wearers to their ancestral roots. With its designation as a registered clan tartan, the Weir stands as a living embodiment of Scotland's cultural identity, woven from the threads of its storied past.

name: Weir Minerals
description: The Weir Minerals tartan is a corporate identity woven into being to reflect the pioneering spirit and global reach of one of the world's leading mining companies, Weir Group. Registered with its Division Head Office in Wisconsin, USA, this distinctive tartan tells the story of a business that has built a reputation for excellence across five divisions, employing over 8,000 people worldwide. Characterised by its bold, industrial colours and precise grid pattern, the Weir Minerals tartan is a testament to the company's innovative approach to pumping, valves, hydrocyclones, and mill lining systems, serving the mining and mineral processing industries. This corporate tartan serves as a visual representation of an honourable tradition of excellence, craftsmanship, and dedication to its people and communities worldwide, making it a meaningful symbol of Weir Group's values and legacy.

name: Weisfeld [default]
description: The Weisfeld tartan, expertly crafted by Duncan Mathers of Highland Dress Hire, is a storied symbol of Scottish heritage for the Weisfeld clan family. Registered in recognition of its association with the esteemed Glasgow businessman Gerald Weisfield, who founded the influential 'What Everyone Wants' chain of stores, this tartan weaves together rich tradition and contemporary significance. Its origins are deeply rooted in Scottish clan culture, where family ties were woven into the very fabric of community. As a result, the Weisfeld tartan is reserved for those bearing the surname Weisfeld, with the designer's consent required to use the pattern. With its distinctive colour palette and subtle texture, this tartan embodies the honourable legacy of Gerald Weisfield's entrepreneurial spirit, inviting wearers to proudly pay tribute to their heritage and the enduring values of Scottish tradition.

name:
Wellington (Wilson 122)
[AKA] No.122
description: The Wellington tartan, affectionately known as Wilsons' No.122, is a striking fashion tartan with roots deeply entwined in Scotland's rich heritage. Registered in 1997, this vibrant design was once worn by soldiers and civilians alike during the Napoleonic Wars, symbolising the triumph of British forces at Waterloo under the leadership of the Duke of Wellington. Founded in 1770 near Stirling, Wilsons of Bannockburn, a renowned weaving firm, played a pivotal role in supplying tartans to regiments, leaving behind an enduring legacy. By distilling the essence of the original Old Gallowater tartan (#1025) into a condensed sett size, this Fashion category design has been preserved for modern wearers, allowing them to tap into the spirit of Scotland's military history and celebrate the Duke's historic victory.

name: Wellington
description: The Wellington tartan is a commemorative masterpiece, designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, to commemorate the legendary Duke of Wellington's victory at Waterloo in 1815.
