This iconic tartan holds significant cultural weight, as it was originally created for use on military uniforms worn by British soldiers during that pivotal battle. Now, this storied design is available to wear with pride, evoking the grandeur and heroism of a bygone era. The registration notes reveal the tartan's roots in the old firm's pattern books, now safely preserved at the National Museum of Antiquities, Edinburgh, and in the Scottish Tartans Society archive. A fitting tribute to British history, the Wellington tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Duke Wellington's remarkable military prowess, allowing wearers to honourably pay their respects to this iconic figure through the time-honoured tradition of tartan design.

name: Wellmont Foundation
description: This striking corporate tartan, known as the Wellmont Golf Tournament, is a testament to the enduring spirit of community and philanthropy in the heart of Tennessee's countryside. Designed by Marjorie Warren in 1997 specifically for the Wellmont Medical Foundation of Bristol, this vibrant tartan was created to support fundraising efforts and bring together like-minded individuals who share a passion for golf and giving back. The unique pattern, now registered with The Scottish Tartans Authority, not only pays homage to the rich history of golf in Scotland but also celebrates the values of the Wellmont Medical Foundation, which has contributed significantly to healthcare in the region. As a symbol of corporate identity, this tartan embodies the perfect blend of tradition and modernity, evoking the fairways and greens of a well-golfed course while conveying a sense of honour and commitment to a noble cause.

name: Wells (Greg) personal; Red
description: The Wells Red, Greg tartan is a unique personal creation, woven with love and inspired by the rich heritage of the Scottish Register of Tartans. Designed by the tartan's namesake, Greg Wells, in collaboration with skilled weaver Molly Manaugh, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the Maryland State tartan (Scottish Register reference #2847), a nod to the designer's American roots. As a personal tartan, the Wells Red, Greg is reserved exclusively for Greg Wells' use, making it an intimate and meaningful connection to his heritage and identity. This remarkable tartan embodies the intersection of tradition and innovation, blending Scottish craftsmanship with contemporary flair, resulting in a truly one-of-a-kind design that celebrates its wearer's individuality and cultural affinity.

name: Welsh Assembly
description: The Welsh Assembly tartan, designed by Ronnie Hek, is a commemorative tribute to the creation of Wales's devolved government. This distinctive pattern, borne from the Scottish Parliament's own tradition, bears testament to the shared heritage between Scotland and Wales. While produced "on spec" without official approval, its significance lies in its cultural resonance with both nations. The tartan's origins evoke a sense of unity and cooperation among Celtic peoples, reflecting the historical bond between Scotland and Wales. Its commemorative nature serves as a poignant reminder of this pivotal moment in Welsh history, inviting wearers to honour their nation's unique identity and contribution to the UK's rich tapestry.

name: Welsh Costume
description: The esteemed Welsh Costume tartan, designed by the illustrious Sir Michael Leighton, is a distinctive name tartan that holds a special place in the hearts of those who claim descent to Welsh ancestry. This beautifully woven fabric pattern is deeply rooted in Welsh heritage and tradition, its unique combination of blues, greens, and yellows evoking the rugged beauty of the Cambrian mountains and the rolling hills of mid-Wales. As a personal tartan, it is reserved for individuals who have a direct connection to Wales, providing a meaningful way to express their honour and cultural affiliation. With no further information available on its design or origins, the Welsh Costume tartan remains an enigmatic yet captivating representation of Scotland's rich textile heritage, waiting to be cherished by those who bear its name.

name: Welsh National #2
description: Welsh National #2 is a distinctive District tartan born from the rich heritage of Wales, woven with love by Wallace Laird in 1993. This captivating design is a testament to the country's storied past, featuring a striking palette of black, donkey brown, mustard, and pink hues that evoke the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Welsh countryside. As designated as District tartan, Welsh National #2 holds an honourable place within the world of traditional Scottish textiles, signifying its connection to a specific geographic region and cultural identity. The use of this tartan is restricted by registration notes, ensuring its authenticity and exclusivity, making it a treasured symbol of Welsh heritage for those fortunate enough to wear it with pride.

name: Welsh National
description: The Welsh National tartan is a storied tribute to the nation's rich heritage, born from the vision of a Cardiff-based society in 1967. This distinctive District tartan pays homage to Wales' enduring Celtic roots and its historical connections with other nations. Inspired by the 18th-century Lord of the Isles tartan, the Welsh National features a bold red dragon motif against a vibrant green and white background, evoking the country's iconic flag. According to Don Richards, the design's creator, this tartan aims to celebrate the unique cultural bonds between Wales and its Celtic counterparts, reflecting a desire for unity and shared heritage among these nations. With its striking colours and storied provenance, the Welsh National tartan serves as a powerful symbol of Welsh identity and pride.

name: Wemyss [default]
description: The Wemyss tartan is a rich and storied heritage cloth, steeped in the history and mystery of Scotland's ancient clans. Meaning "cave" in Gaelic, this distinctive pattern is believed to have originated from the mysterious caves beneath MacDuff castle, a fitting inspiration for a family tartan that has been woven with pride by generations. As one of the foundation patterns of William Hume's Vestiarium Scoticum, a seminal work on Scottish clan tartans published between 1829-42, the Wemyss tartan is deeply rooted in Scotland's tradition of textile craftsmanship. First recorded in this influential book, this beautiful and intricate design has been woven with precision and care by skilled weavers, its subtle variations reflecting the unique characteristics of each hand-woven sample.

name: West Highland Way
description: The West Highland Way tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich heritage and the storied routes that traverse its rugged landscape. Designed by Brian Wilton, this corporate tartan honourably represents the region through which one of Scotland's most iconic long-distance footpaths winds its way - the West Highland Way. The registration notes reveal a deliberate nod to the traditional clan territories through which the path passes, reflecting the intricate tapestry of history and cultural identity that defines these Highlands' communities. As a corporate tartan, it is intended for use by companies looking to tap into Scotland's distinctive character and evoke the sense of adventure and natural beauty that defines this magnificent land.

name: West Lothian Woolen Mill
description: The West Lothian Woolen Mill tartan is a quintessential corporate design, born from the industrial heritage of Scotland's textile industry. Registered as a corporate tartan, it is likely designed for use by businesses with connections to the region or the Hudson Bay Company, which had a significant presence in West Lothian. The muted colour palette, featuring orange (or red) and blues, evokes the rustic charm of 19th-century Scotland's woollen mills, where skilled weavers crafted traditional tartans. With its roots in Hudson Bay's retailing of a similar tartan, it is possible that this design was inspired by both Scottish and North American influences. Dr William E Johnston, who kindly contributed to the registration notes, ensured that this distinctive tartan would honour the history of West Lothian's woollen mills.

name: West of Scotland Water Authority Loch Katrine District
description: The Loch Katrine tartan, a Corporate design created by Ronnie Hek, pays homage to one of Scotland's most majestic lochs while embracing its versatility in a professional setting. Originally commissioned by West of Scotland Water Authority, this stunning pattern was intended as a District Tartan, reflecting the local heritage and identity of Coldstream, where it was designed. Although formal recognition by the local authority remains uncertain, the tartan has since been adopted for corporate purposes, allowing its rich blues and greens to bring a touch of Scottish sophistication to any occasion. By embracing this unique design, organisations can draw upon Scotland's storied history and natural beauty, while also making a bold statement about their values and connection to the nation.

name: West Virginia Old Shawl;
description: The West Virginia Old Shawl tartan is a captivating fragment of American-Scottish heritage, recorded in 1994 from a lady's handspun shawl believed to date back to circa 1820. This unique tartan was discovered in the DAR collection at Barboursville, West Virginia, USA, and its provenance is steeped in history. Originally described as asymmetrical, it may have been created as an one-off fabric design rather than a traditional clan tartan. Despite this, the intricate patterns and colours evoke a sense of tradition and heritage, reflecting the cultural exchange between Scotland and America during the 19th century. The double-counting of the sett for clarity serves as a testament to its status as a historic document, preserving a piece of the past for future generations to appreciate.

name: Westenra
description: The Westenra of Christchurch tartan is a commemorative tribute to New Zealand soprano Hayley Westenra's iconic visit to Scotland in 2006, expertly woven by Andrew Fenning. This distinctive tartan is reserved for fashion wear and accessories, symbolising the honour bestowed upon Hayley Westenra, a celebrated opera singer whose name has become synonymous with Scottish cultural heritage. As a commemorative design, it serves as a permanent reminder of her special connection to Scotland, where her remarkable talent was warmly received by the nation. With its unique colour palette and subtle nuances, this tartan is a fitting testament to Hayley Westenra's enduring legacy, one that continues to favour those who wear it with pride.

name: Westgaard
description: The Westgaard of Kileatheringco tartan is a deeply personal and exclusive design, created by Thomas Paul Westgaard of Kileatheringco, Greenfield, Wisconsin, in 1993. As a Name tartan, it holds significant importance for members of the 'family' that has claimed this particular set. This distinctive pattern, featuring a unique sett, was woven exclusively to date, with only one sample preserved in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection. With its distinct character and family ties, the Westgaard of Kileatheringco tartan embodies the rich heritage and tradition of Scottish clans, weaving together threads of history, identity, and cultural pride.

name: Westmeath Irish County
description: The Westmeath tartan, crafted by Polly Wittering on behalf of Macnaughton Holdings Ltd's House of Edgar, embodies the rich heritage of Ireland's Districts. As one of a series designed to capture the nuances of regional identity, this tartan weaves a tale of local pride and tradition. Originally intended as Fashion tartans rather than officially sanctioned District designs, its enduring popularity has paved the way for potential future recognition. The Westmeath tartan's distinct pattern, featuring an intricate balance of blue and green hues, pays homage to the county's unique cultural landscape, reflecting the blending of Celtic traditions with historical influences that have shaped Ireland's storied past.

name: Westminster College
description: The Westminster College tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish heritage, expertly woven into the fabric of corporate identity. Designed for a prestigious educational institution in the heart of London, this distinctive tartan is a reflection of the institution's esteemed history and tradition. As a Corporate tartan, it has been carefully crafted to be both professional and iconic, making it an ideal choice for branding and marketing materials. With no designer credited, its origins are shrouded in mystery, adding to its mystique. Nonetheless, this tartan is steeped in Scottish roots, bearing witness to the intricate craftsmanship of traditional weaving techniques. Thread count verification is paramount, as per registration notes, ensuring that every thread is meticulously counted and carefully placed to create a fabric worthy of the institution's name.

name: Weston
description: The Weston tartan is a unique and intimate personal design, crafted specifically for the union of David and Karen Weston on their special day in 2002. As a Name tartan, it reflects the individuality and heritage of its creators, with no specific clan affiliation or historical roots to draw upon. Rather, this subtle yet distinctive pattern is an expression of the couple's shared identity and love story. With its carefully chosen colours and precise weaving, the Weston tartan whispers tales of a private celebration, woven into the very fabric of tradition that underpins Scottish heritage. As such, it serves as a testament to the enduring power of family, friendship, and love, forever entwined in this bespoke tartan's elegant and understated beauty.

name: Westwood
description: The Westwood tartan is a fashion-forward interpretation of traditional Scottish weaving, born from the pages of 'Scottish Banner' in July 1999. As registered under its category as Fashion, this tartan embodies the modern spirit of style and sophistication, marrying timeless elegance with contemporary flair. With no specific designer credited, it's clear that this design has been shaped by a collective understanding of Scottish heritage and tradition. The Westwood tartan boasts a rich, muted colour palette, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish hills and glens, while its precise sett and subtle variation in tone convey a sense of refinement and poise. As a Fashion tartan, it's perfectly suited for adding a touch of authenticity to modern attire, from statement accessories to fashion-forward garments that celebrate Scotland's rich cultural legacy.

name: Wexford Irish County
description: The Wexford, County tartan is a richly woven tribute to the Emerald Isle's storied past, born from the creative vision of Polly Wittering, a talented weaver at House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd. As one of a series of Irish District tartans, this distinctive design takes its cue from the region's proud heritage and cultural identity. Though not formally sanctioned by the governing authorities, its popularity speaks to its authenticity, and it is likely that time will confirm its status as a genuine District tartan. With its intricate patterns and subtle colour variations, this tartan evokes the rolling green hills, rugged coastlines, and warm hospitality of Wexford County, inviting wearers to connect with the land, its people, and the enduring spirit of Irish tradition.

name: Wheadon [default]
description: The Wheadon tartan is a testament to the rich cultural heritage of Scottish clan traditions, born from a union of love and family ties in the United States. Originally created by Dave Wheadon and Mike Kowalski for a wedding celebration, this tartan has transcended its origins to become a symbol of the Wheadon name and its various spellings across generations. Registration notes confirm its suitability as a family tartan, allowing it to be worn with pride by those bearing the name, while also acknowledging its unique roots in a global celebration. With an estimated thread count for display purposes only, this tartan's technical specifications serve as a reminder of its storied past, woven from the fabric of love and connection that unite families across the centuries.

name: Whisky
description: The Whisky Corporate Tartan is a richly woven tribute to Scotland's finest export, evoking the sights and scents of the nation's storied whisky heritage. Designed by Edgar van de Crommert, this distinctive pattern celebrates the artisanal craftsmanship that goes into crafting the country's iconic drams. Registration notes reveal the intricate details behind the design, with yellow fields representing barley, black squares symbolising peat and coal, small brown squares for yeast, darker blue squares representing Scottish water, and white lines denoting glass bottles. The result is a vibrant tapestry that weaves together the very essence of Scotland's whisky-making traditions, making it an ideal choice for corporate entities seeking to tap into the country's storied heritage and connect with its people.

name: White Stripes
description: The White Stripes Hunting tartan is a quintessential corporate motif, its clean lines and simplicity rendering it instantly recognisable as a dependable choice for businesses seeking to convey a sense of tradition and reliability. This distinctive tartan was designed by Wilson/Kirkbright, a renowned duo in the world of Scottish textile art, who carefully crafted this specific design to evoke the spirit of hunting, a time-honoured pursuit steeped in Scottish heritage. With its striking white stripes set against a deep blue background, this tartan exudes an air of dignity and professionalism, making it an ideal choice for corporate wear, stationery, or branding initiatives seeking to establish a strong connection with Scottish roots and tradition.

name: White Thistle
description: The Joker, The tartan is a bold and iconic fashion design inspired by the unforgettable character of Jack Nicholson's portrayal of the Clown Prince of Crime in the 1989 Batman film. Created from meticulous re-creation of film stills by renowned designer Andy Garringer, this tartan is an homage to the iconic attire worn by Nicholson in his chilling performance. As a Fashion tartan, The Joker, The is perfect for those who dare to stand out with its vibrant and unpredictable colour scheme. Registration notes confirm that no other individual or company may reproduce this design without permission, underscoring the significance of this unique creation within the world of tartan heritage.

name: Whitley
description: The Whitley tartan, a personal creation with no discernible roots or provenance, stands as a testament to the ephemeral nature of Scottish heritage. Registered in its current form, it is categorised as a Name tartan, suggesting an individual association rather than a familial connection. Notably, this design bears little originality, with Phil Smith's comment of it being an unimaginative copy from the Vestiarium Scoticum echoing the sentiments of many in the tartan community. Despite its questionable provenance, the Whitley tartan remains a notable addition to the ever-evolving tapestry of Scottish textile traditions, offering a glimpse into the often-blurred lines between tradition and innovation.

name: Whitson [default]
description: The Whitson tartan is a deeply rooted family heirloom, registered under the prestigious designation of Clan tartans. Designed by Peter MacDonald, a renowned weaver of Scottish heritage, this distinctive pattern holds profound cultural significance for those bearing the name. The registration notes, UK Design No 514358, attest to its unique character, ensuring that this tartan remains an integral part of family tradition and identity. Weaving together threads of history and community, the Whitson tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich tapestry, with each intricate design element echoing stories of loyalty, pride, and ancestral connection.

name: Whitworth Artifact
description: The Whitworth tartan is a storied and mysterious textile, shrouded in the rich heritage of Scotland's weavers. Originally loaned to the Scottish Tartans Society by Antony Whitworth in the early 1980s, this unique tartan holds secrets within its intricate pattern. While the exact origins and meaning behind the design remain unknown, it is clear that the Whitworth has a special place in the hearts of those who cherish Scotland's traditional craftsmanship. As a 'Other' category, this tartan defies easy categorisation, existing outside the traditional boundaries of clan or family associations. Instead, its significance lies in its connection to Antony Whitworth and his enduring legacy as a guardian of Scotland's textile traditions. Its very existence serves as a testament to the power of storytelling and the preservation of cultural heritage.

name: Whitworth [default]
description: The Whitworth tartan, registered in 2003, is a proud representation of a Scottish clan heritage, woven from threads of tradition and history. Given to Phil D Smith at the prestigious Stone Mountain Games by Larry Whitworth himself, this tartan embodies the values of family and community that have defined the Whitworth lineage for generations. As a Clan/Family tartan, the Whitworth is reserved exclusively for those with a direct connection to the clan's ancestry, serving as a symbol of honour and identity for its wearers. With no further details available on its origins or design intent, the Whitworth remains an enigmatic yet captivating testament to the enduring power of Scottish heritage and tradition.

name: Wicklow Irish County
description: The Wicklow, County tartan is a testament to the rich heritage of Ireland's Emerald Isle, its subtle yet striking hues evoking the rolling hills and misty landscapes of County Wicklow. As one of a series designed by Polly Wittering for House of Edgar - Macnaughton Holdings Ltd., this tartan is classified as an Irish District tartan, reflecting its roots in the traditional weaving traditions of Ireland's districts rather than fashion trends. Although not formally sanctioned by the Scottish Tartans Authority, these 'unofficial' designs have won widespread favour among enthusiasts and collectors alike, who appreciate their authenticity and cultural significance. The Wicklow, County tartan is a poignant reminder of the country's complex history and its enduring connection to the land and people that inspired it, making it a treasured addition to any Scottish heritage collection.

name: Wicks
description: The Wicks tartan, created by renowned designer Christopher Wicks, embodies the rich heritage of Aberdeen, a city synonymous with granite strength and natural beauty. This bespoke Name tartan was carefully woven to commemorate the union of Christopher Wicks and Nichola Rundle in 2014, marking a significant milestone in their lives. description: Wilsons' No.194 is a quintessential Scottish fashion tartan, born from the meticulous craftsmanship of Wilsons of Bannockburn, a renowned weaving firm established in 1770 near Stirling. As documented in the National Museum of Antiquities' Pattern Book collection, this particular design boasts a striking yet balanced combination of blues, greens, yellows, and reds, showcasing the skillful artistry of Scottish weavers. With its inclusion in Wilsons' No.194, this tartan embodies the honour and prestige associated with Scotland's iconic textile tradition, evoking images of kilts, scarves, and other traditional garments worn with pride by Scots around the world, their favour reflected in the very fabric itself.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.195
description: In the realm of Scottish heritage, Wilsons' No.195 stands as a testament to the enduring legacy of fashion tartans. Today, Wilsons' No.195 continues to captivate enthusiasts of Scottish textiles, its intricate sett design and carefully calibrated colours showcasing the artisans' skill in crafting unique and beautiful patterns that reflect the nation's rich heritage.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.196
description: Wilsons' No.196, a fashion tartan designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish textiles. As a fashion tartan, Wilsons' No.196 is perfect for adding a touch of Scottish elegance to clothing and accessories. Its distinctive pattern, though subject to the same cautionary note as its predecessor about Sindex's use of orange in similar designs, offers a fresh and dynamic take on traditional tartan motifs, fitting perfectly into the storied tradition of Scotland's most iconic textile art forms.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.197
description: Wilsons' No.197, a majestic fashion tartan crafted by esteemed weavers at Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a testament to Scotland's rich textile heritage. Registered in the early 20th century, this striking pattern features a predominantly blue and green palette, with subtle variations in tone that evoke the rolling hills and heather-covered moors of the Scottish countryside. With its distinctive sett and carefully considered colour choices, Wilsons' No.197 is a masterpiece of traditional Scottish weaving, reflecting the skill and craftsmanship of generations of weavers at Wilsons of Bannockburn, founded in 1770 near Stirling. As a fashion tartan, it would add a touch of elegance and sophistication to any outfit, while its origins in the National Museum of Antiquities' Pattern books and the Scottish Tartans Society's archives serve as a poignant reminder of Scotland's enduring cultural legacy.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.198
description: Wilson's No.198 is a classic fashion tartan, woven with timeless elegance by the esteemed Wilsons of Bannockburn. This distinctive design, registered in recognition of its cultural significance, was created to pay tribute to the heritage of Scotland's iconic clans and families. Characterised by a striking balance of rich blues and greens, evoking the rolling hills and misty lochs that cradle the Highlands, this tartan boasts subtle nuances that invite the wearer to claim their place within Scotland's storied traditions. While traditionally associated with the fashion world, Wilsons' No.198 also nods to its clan roots, reflecting a deep respect for the past while embracing contemporary style.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.199
description: Weaving together the threads of Scottish heritage, Wilsons' No.199 is a captivating fashion tartan that embodies the style and sophistication of Scotland's rich cultural landscape. Registration notes reveal that, although not a traditional clan sett, this distinctive design has been carefully crafted to evoke the traditions of the nation. The subtle nuances in colour, with its green subtly lightened here to distinguish it from other sets, add depth and character to this versatile tartan. As a fashion tartan, Wilsons' No.199 is poised to adorn everything from classic kilts to modern garments, making a statement about the wearer's connection to Scottish heritage without being bound by traditional clan affiliations. A testament to the innovative spirit of its creators, Wilsons of Bannockburn have designed a tartan that will undoubtedly leave a lasting impression on those who wear it.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.200
description: Wilson's No.200, a fashion tartan designed by the esteemed Wilsons of Bannockburn, is a masterful creation that embodies the timeless spirit of Scottish heritage. With its rich, muted tones, this iconic pattern tells the story of tradition and community, evoking images of Highland landscapes and centuries-old clan gatherings. The subtle variations in colour, most notably the lightened green sett, add depth and nuance to the design, rendering it both striking and understated. As a fashion tartan, Wilson's No.200 is ideal for those who desire to connect with Scotland's storied past while making a stylish statement. Whether worn proudly by individuals or featured in luxury textiles, this tartan's enduring appeal lies in its ability to transcend generations and cultures, serving as a poignant reminder of the nation's unwavering tradition and sense of honour.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.201
description: The captivating Wilsons' No.201 tartan is a stunning example of Scottish fashion heritage, born from the renowned weaving house of Wilsons of Bannockburn. This beautiful design, classified as Fashion tartan, pays homage to the rich cultural traditions of Scotland's textile arts. As designated by its registration notes, the subtle variations in tone are deliberately highlighted, with the green hues softly muted to reveal a deeper sense of depth and character. With its unique pattern and timeless appeal, Wilsons' No.201 is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish tartanry, evoking images of the rolling hills, rugged landscapes, and warm hospitality that define this remarkable country's identity.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.202
description: Wilson's No.202 is a timeless fashion tartan, carefully crafted by the esteemed firm of Wilsons of Bannockburn to add a touch of Scottish heritage to modern attire. This dynamic design features a bold, rich blue-and-green palette, evoking the rolling hills and glens of Scotland's countryside. The registration notes highlight a deliberate choice to lighten the green hue in this illustration, allowing the intricate sett pattern to take centre stage. As a fashion tartan, Wilson's No.202 is designed to make a statement, its unique blend of colours and textures sure to add a dash of Scottish flair to any outfit. Its classification as a fashion tartan signifies that it was created with style and elegance in mind, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to incorporate the finest aspects of Scottish tradition into their wardrobe.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.203
description: Wilson's No.203 is a captivating fashion tartan that embodies the essence of traditional Scottish heritage, yet exudes modern flair. Designed by Wilsons of Bannockburn, this distinctive pattern is rooted in the 24-reed sett, featuring an intricate cheek design that adds a touch of whimsy to its classic charm. The muted tones, particularly the green, are subtly varied throughout the tartan to evoke a sense of movement and energy. As a fashion tartan, Wilson's No.203 has been carefully crafted to appeal to those seeking a statement-making scarf, shawl, or other accessories that showcase their individual style. Its registration notes, which include guidance on sett width and gang spacing, serve as a testament to the attention to detail that underpins this design, ensuring that every aspect of the tartan comes together in perfect harmony.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.204
description: Wilson's No.204, a fashion tartan design by renowned Scottish house Wilsons of Bannockburn, embodies the spirit of 18th-century Scottish elegance with its distinctive yet refined appearance. This stylish pattern, registered for commercial use, boasts a subtle sheen that hints at its rich history and heritage. Characterised by a muted tone palette, the tartan features a green that has been deliberately lightened to reveal the underlying sett, lending an air of authenticity to its traditional design. As a fashion tartan, Wilson's No.204 is destined for high-profile catwalks and red-carpet events, where its classic charm and sophisticated flair will undoubtedly turn heads. This esteemed pattern is a testament to Scotland's rich weaving traditions, with its intricate design evoking the country's storied past and enduring cultural heritage.

name: Wilson's Collection; No.205
description: Wilson's No.205 is a timeless fashion tartan that exudes the classic elegance of Scotland's rich heritage. Designed by the esteemed Wilsons of Bannockburn, a renowned weaving firm founded in 1770 near Stirling, this distinctive tartan has been delighting generations with its subtle yet striking nuances. The registration notes hint at a storied past, as the original pattern books are now housed within the National Museum of Antiquities, Edinburgh, and copies can be found preserved within the Scottish Tartans Society archive. As a fashion tartan, Wilson's No.205 is perfect for those who appreciate tradition blended with modern style, evoking images of Scotland's picturesque landscapes and the warmth of its people.

name: Wilton (Matthew) personal; Wilton of Toronto
description: The Wilton (Toronto) tartan is a bespoke blend of Scottish heritage and personal affection, meticulously woven by Peter MacDonald with input from the esteemed Brian Wilton of the Scottish Tartans Authority. As a gift to his son Matthew on their wedding day in 2002, this unique tartan commemorates the union between Matthew and his wife Susan in Winnipeg. Category-defined as 'Name' tartan, the Wilton (Toronto) proudly wears its personal significance, honouring the love story of a family bound by Scottish tradition and cultural roots. With no restrictions placed upon it, the tartan is free to be worn with pride, symbolising the timeless connection between Scotland's rich heritage and the modern-day families who call it home.

name: Wishart (David) personal; Holland
description: The Holland Tartan, designed by Dr David Wishart of Edinburgh, is a vibrant fashion design that pays homage to Dutch heritage, combining the colours of the national flag with the symbolic hues of the House of Orange. Regarded as a Fashion design due to the absence of approval from a relevant Dutch organisation, this tartan has taken on a life of its own, blending Scottish weaving traditions with international flair. As a 'District' tartan, it could have been celebrated within the Netherlands itself, but instead, its unique fusion of red, white, and blue hues has made it a sought-after choice for fashion enthusiasts around the world. Weavers at Lochcarron of Scotland bring this bold design to life, infusing the traditional tartan-making craft with international passion and style.

name: Wishart Dress
description: The Wishart Dress tartan is a rich tapestry of heritage, woven from the threads of history and tradition. Registration notes reveal that this clan tartan was born from the union of two storied families: the noble Wisharts of Pittarrow and Logie Wishart, whose name "Guiscard" originates from Norman-French, meaning 'cunning'. The design cleverly fuses elements of the Wallace and Douglas tartans, a testament to the 16th Century marriage between Sir John Wishart and Jean, daughter of William Douglas, 9th Earl of Angus. As such, this tartan embodies the intricate web of alliances and cultural exchange that have shaped Scotland's storied past, creating a unique and authentic expression of Scottish heritage that continues to captivate those who wear it with honour.

name: Wishart Hunting (Archived)
description: The Wishart Hunting tartan is a richly woven tapestry of Scottish heritage, crafted by Dr. David Wishart to commemorate his family's storied history. Originating in the 12th century as a Lowland clan, the Wisharts' origins remain shrouded in mystery, but their name, Guiscard, Wiscard, Wishart, speaks volumes about their cunning and resilience. Through strategic alliances, such as the marriage of Sir John Wishart to Jean, daughter of William Douglas, 9th Earl of Angus, the family's tartan has been forever entwined with that of the revered Clan Douglas. This innovative sett, created in 1990, skillfully blends the bold spirit of Clan Wallace with the noble bearing of the Douglases, resulting in a unique and captivating design that proudly embodies the Wishart clan's distinct honour and legacy.

name: Wojtek Memorial Trust
description: The Wojtek Memorial Trust Tartan, designed by Kinloch Anderson Ltd, is a poignant tribute to the unbreakable bond between Scotland and Poland. This corporate tartan commemorates the extraordinary story of Wojtek, a Syrian brown bear cub adopted by Polish soldiers during World War II, who found refuge in Springwood Park, Kelso, owned by the Duke of Roxburgh. As an interpretation of the traditional Roxburgh tartan, the Wojtek Memorial Trust Tartan skillfully weaves together vibrant red and white colours, evoking the Polish flag and representing the unique relationship between Scotland and Poland. The design also incorporates trews-inspired greens from the Leslie tartan, symbolising the Scottish Borders' rolling countryside, alongside a sandy over-check, reminiscent of the Middle East's arid landscapes and Wojtek's soft fur. This tartan is more than just a design - it's a testament to the power of friendship and camaraderie between nations, and its careful balance of colours pays tribute to the enduring spirit of those who wore it: the brave Polish soldiers and their beloved bear companion.

name: Wolfe [default]
description: The Wolfe tartan is an iconic representation of Scottish heritage, woven with precision by renowned clan specialists at Kinloch Anderson Ltd. As a registered family tartan, it holds a profound significance for those bearing the name, serving as a symbol of pride and connection to their ancestral roots. The subtle balance of blues and greens in this distinctive pattern creates a striking visual identity that embodies the values of strength, resilience, and loyalty synonymous with the Wolfe clan legacy. With its rich history and timeless appeal, the Wolfe tartan remains an enduring emblem of Scottish tradition, meticulously preserved for generations to come.

name: Wood Wood, Ian (Personal)
description: This stately Corporate tartan, aptly named "Wood", is a testament to the rich heritage of Scottish industry and innovation. Designed by Michael King for Sir Ian Wood's 60th birthday in 2003, the pattern pays tribute to the illustrious career of the renowned businessman and energy leader. As the chairman and chief executive of The Wood Group, one of the world's leading oil firms, Sir Ian Wood's legacy is deeply rooted in Aberdeen's thriving energy sector. This tartan design serves as a lasting honour, reflecting the city's proud industrial heritage and Sir Ian Wood's significant contributions to its success. Its Corporate classification underscores its utilitarian purpose, making it an ideal choice for companies and organisations wishing to connect with Scotland's vibrant business community and celebrate their own history of excellence.

name: Wood [default]
description: The Wood tartan, registered in 2007, is a storied heritage pattern steeped in history and cultural significance. Originally initiated by Leslie N Wood, with Keith Lumsden as its designer, this Clan/Family tartan pays homage to the Woods' ancestral roots in the Angus district and their historical connections to the Duke of Fife's territories. The distinctive design blends the rich colours of these adjacent tartans, reflecting the intricate tapestry of Scottish clan affiliations and territorial influences that have shaped the nation's identity. Adopted by the Clan Wood Society and sanctioned by the Chief of Clan Wood, this tartan is a testament to the enduring power of tradition and community, weaving together the past, present, and future of the Wood family legacy.

name: Wotherspoon [default]
description: The Wotherspoon tartan is a storied and historic design rooted in the Lowlands of Scotland, with recorded origins dating back to the early 14th century. This sett is part of the esteemed MacGregor-Hastie collection, meticulously curated by the Scottish Tartans Society, and was originally produced for Septs and Families of Scottish lineage between 1930 and 1950. Its design tells the story of a distinguished clan, likely one of lesser stature than some of Scotland's more prominent families, but still with a rich heritage. The presence of the Rev. John Witherspoon, an influential figure in American history as the President of Princeton University from 1768, underscores the tartan's enduring connection to Scottish-American roots. This timeless and evocative design is now preserved for posterity, serving as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry and its enduring legacy among those of Scottish descent.

name: Wren [default]
description: The Wren tartan is a poignant tribute to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, borne from the esteemed Clan Smith family. Designed by Dr Philip D, a renowned textile expert, this intricate pattern weaves together a tale of Scottish tradition and heritage. As a Clan/Family tartan, it is steeped in history and association with one particular sept (sub-clan) or branch of the larger clan. The Wren's striking hues evoke the symbolism of its namesake bird - small yet fierce - reflecting the family's own values of resilience and determination. While no further details are recorded in the registration notes, it is understood that this tartan holds a special significance for those bearing the Smith surname, serving as a tangible link to their ancestral roots and cultural identity.

name: X Marks the Scot
description: The "X Marks the Scot" tartan is a modern corporate design created by renowned weaver Matt Newsome, drawing inspiration from Scotland's rich heritage. This striking pattern was chosen for an online kilt-wearer's forum, reflecting the growing global interest in Scottish culture and tradition. Characterised by its bold, navy blue background and prominent white line denoting the St Andrew's Cross of the Scottish Saltire, this tartan pays homage to Scotland's iconic national symbol. With its unique blend of modernity and historical reference, the "X Marks the Scot" tartan is a fitting tribute to the country that has captured the hearts of people around the world.

name: Yorkshire Cricket Club
description: The Hodgkinson tartan, designed by Amanda Hodgkinson, holds a unique place in British textile heritage. Originally submitted to Yorkshire County Cricket Club with the intention of becoming an official club tartan, it was ultimately not endorsed, resulting in its distinction as a standalone corporate tartan. This distinctive design now bears its creator's name and is valued for its distinctiveness within the world of corporate wear, evoking a sense of professionalism and identity that is both modern and rooted in British tradition. With its technical characteristics carefully crafted to meet the demands of corporate attire, the Hodgkinson tartan stands as a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of textile designers, while also celebrating the rich history and cultural significance of Scottish heritage.

name: Young Christina
description: This enchanting blanket tartan, CY, holds a treasure trove of Scottish heritage within its intricate weave. Discovered in a 1966 purchase from the Scottish Tartans Society, it is believed to have originated in the early 18th century, with threads tracing back to Christina Young's wedding blanket in 1726. Weaved by Christina herself in Peterhead, this joined plaid tartan exemplifies the ancient art of traditional weaving, a true testament to the skill and craftsmanship of the past. Often described as an arisaid, it is now the foundation for the modern Young tartan, created in 1992 to commemorate Christina's legacy. This captivating tartan design serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's rich cultural heritage and the enduring tradition of family and community that it represents.

name: Young [default]
description: The Young tartan is a cherished family heritage, born from the innovative spirit of Derek Young, who painstakingly crafted this striking design in 1992 at his Benderloch workshop near Oban. This Clan tartan proudly wears the distinctive arisaidh plaid motif of Christina Young's blanket, registered as STR #4799 in 1726, and transformed it into a modern masterpiece by overlaying it on a blue background, punctuated by traditional West Coast greens and blues reminiscent of the rugged Scottish coastlines. The original tartan's purple-yellow-orange box check is preserved, adding a rich layer of depth to this family-registered design. While its kilt version would typically feature woven colours at twice the width shown here, this particular variant offers a unique glimpse into the designer's creative vision, imbuing the Young tartan with a sense of history and tradition that will undoubtedly endure for generations to come.

name: Yule [default]
description: The Yule tartan is a storied and historic pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, born from the traditions of families hailing from Aberdeenshire, Lanarkshire, and East Lothian. Registered with distinction by renowned designer Scarlett MBE, Jamie, this tartan has been carefully woven to reflect the unique identity and history of its namesake clans. Not connected to Clan Buchanan, as per registration notes, the Yule tartan proudly stands as a testament to the distinctiveness of these families' cultural heritage. This timeless and intricate design is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition, evoking a sense of warmth, conviviality, and celebration - fittingly, given its association with the festive season of Yule, where community and merriment reign supreme.

name: MacLachlan Hunting
description: The MacLachlan Hunting tartan, a storied family tradition woven into the fabric of Scotland's rich heritage, holds a mystique all its own. With its distinctive hues of blue and green, evoking the rolling hills and rugged landscapes of the Scottish wilderness, this tartan is said to have been inspired by generations of MacLachlan clan members who cherished the thrill of the hunt. While its origins remain shrouded in mystery, it is widely regarded as a Fashion pattern, adopted by those seeking to pay homage to Scotland's storied past while forging their own unique identity. With no formal restrictions on its use, this tartan invites wearers to tap into their ancestral roots and connect with the unbridled spirit of Scotland's rugged landscape.

name: Strathtay
description: The Strathtay tartan is a testament to the timeless beauty of Scotland's most majestic waterway, the River Tay. This District tartan, born from the fertile imagination of designer Jonathan Brown, is woven with a deep reverence for the valley's dramatic autumn hues - olive greens and fiery reds that paint the wooded banks in vivid contrast against the silver blue and lush green of the river itself as it flows swiftly to the estuary. With its restrictions ensuring its exclusive use by Strathmore Woollen Co Ltd, this tartan embodies the essence of a Scotland cherished for centuries, where tradition and heritage blend seamlessly with the ever-changing colours of nature. As a poignant reminder of the River Tay's storied past, the Strathtay tartan stands as a proud symbol of Scotland's rich cultural tapestry, its significance woven into the very fabric of this majestic land.

name: Strathtummel
description: The Strathtummel tartan is a breathtaking tribute to the majestic beauty of Scotland's Perthshire countryside, where the River Tummel meanders through valleys of serenity and rugged mountainscapes. Registered by renowned designer Jonathan Brown, this District tartan is steeped in the heritage of the Scottish Highlands, with its colours evoking the subtle nuances of summer: the rich purple of heather-dusted moors, the cerulean blue of towering mountain ranges, and the emerald green of lush ferns that thrive in the valley's foothills. Yet, amidst these vibrant hues, a distinctive white stripe shimmers like the snowfields that blanket the mountains during the winter months - a poignant reminder of the cyclical rhythms of nature that have shaped this timeless landscape for centuries. As a District tartan, Strathtummel is uniquely tied to its native territory, with strict weaving restrictions in place to ensure its integrity and authenticity are preserved through the centuries by Strathmore Woollen Co Ltd, a testament to the enduring power of Scotland's tartan legacy.

name: Harry of Wales
description: The Harry of Wales tartan is a unique and modern design born from the cultural heritage of Wales, created by Sheila Daniel of Cambrian Woollen Mill, Powys. While its historical roots are uncertain, this name tartan has gained significant popularity since its introduction in the late 1990s through the efforts of Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea. This distinctive weave stands out from other Celtic patterns, featuring an unusual combination of odd-numbered threads and innovative warp and weft sequences. The 'of Wales' suffix serves as a nod to its origins, rather than a claim of territorial significance, underscoring the design's modernisation of traditional tartan-making techniques. Due to restrictions in place, permission must be obtained from Wales Tartan Centres prior to weaving, ensuring the integrity and authenticity of this captivating Welsh-inspired tartan.

name: Wild Geese
description: The Wild Geese tartan is a poignant commemoration of the Irish mercenaries who sought refuge in France during periods of sectarian persecution, their fate a testament to the enduring power of heritage and tradition. This striking design, featuring a harmonious blend of green, white, gold, red, white, blue, and black hues, pays tribute to the sacrifices made by those who defied convention to forge new lives abroad. Crafted by Tartan Web Scotland Ltd (formerly Viking Technology Limited) in 2005 as part of a set dedicated to Irish County and National tartans, this commemorative tartan serves as a powerful reminder of the complex history of the Emerald Isle's diaspora. Note that ownership has been transferred to USA Kilts Inc, underscoring the importance of respecting intellectual property rights while preserving the rich cultural heritage represented by this unique design.

name: Scottish Heritage
description: The Scottish Heritage tartan is a vibrant representation of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, commissioned by The Sporran Shop in Perth as part of their esteemed tradition of honouring the country's storied past. As a corporate tartan, its purpose is to evoke pride and identity among businesses and organisations that value their Scottish roots, yet also appeals to those who appreciate the timeless beauty of traditional tartans. With no specified designer credited, the design itself remains a testament to the skillful hands of Janet and Hamish Eagleton, who carefully crafted this distinctive pattern for The Sporran Shop's Jan 1996 registration. Rooted in Scotland's long history of weaving and craftsmanship, the Scottish Heritage tartan embodies the country's enduring spirit, blending bold colour combinations with subtle nuances that speak to a rich cultural legacy, inviting wearers to proudly express their connection to this storied land.

name: Confederate Memorial
description: This poignant tartan, known as the Confederate Memorial, is a powerful tribute to the history of the American Civil War. Designed by Dr Philip D Smith in 1995, it commemorates the Confederate States of America and their military heritage, with grey serving as a nod to the nation's troubled past. The striking design features light blue fields representing infantry, flanked by red for artillery and yellow for cavalry - a deliberate choice to evoke the iconic proportions of the Confederate flag. Restricted to specific categories due to its sensitive historical connotations, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the American Civil War in Scottish culture.

name: Lewis Red
description: The Lewis Red fashion tartan, registered as one of a series by esteemed designer Kirsty Anderson, embodies the vibrant spirit of Scotland's dance traditions. Designed specifically for the House of Edgar's in-house collection, this dynamic pattern is part of a bespoke range of dancer's tartans that pay homage to the rich heritage of Scottish clan culture. The Lewis Red tartan's distinctive red and blue hues evoke the fiery passion and energy of traditional Scottish dancing, where intricate steps and rhythmic movements weave together to create an unforgettable spectacle. As a fashion tartan, it offers a bold and striking alternative for those looking to incorporate a touch of Scottish flair into their wardrobe, while its connection to Kirsty Anderson's celebrated designs ensures a level of craftsmanship and attention to detail that is quintessentially Scottish.

name: Highland Heather
description: The Highland Heather tartan, created by renowned designer Yvonne Macrae, is an exquisite fusion of traditional Scottish heritage and modern flair, perfectly encapsulated in its vibrant and subtle colour palette. Originally designed for Macrae's couture dressmaking work, which draws inspiration from the breathtaking landscapes of the Scottish Highlands, this tartan weaves together a rich tapestry of symbolic significance. As a fashion tartan, Highland Heather embodies the elegance and refinement of Scottish tradition, while Yvonne Macrae's exclusive ownership restrictions ensure its authenticity and artistic integrity are preserved for generations to come. Prepared for weaving by the esteemed Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish textile craftsmanship, forever entwined with the natural beauty and mystique of the Highlands.

name: Henderson [default]
description: The Henderson/MacKendrick tartan is a proud representation of Scottish heritage, tracing its roots back to the 19th century. Originally known as MacEanruig, which translates to "son of Eanruig", this Clan tartan was first documented in Vestiarium Scoticum in 1842, predating its modern counterpart by nearly four decades. Its similarity to the Davidson tartan highlights the shared history and traditions of Scotland's noble families. Registration notes from the Scottish Tartans Society confirm that both Henderson/MacKendrick and Davidson were recorded in 1906 by W. & A.K.Johnston, further solidifying their connection. This tartan design is a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan MacKendrick, whose storied past is woven into the very fabric of Scottish culture and tradition.

name: Stewart Blue (Dress)
description: The Stewart Dress Blue tartan is a deeply rooted and storied pattern, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registration notes reveal that it was taken from an original dress housed in the Royal Scots Museum, Edinburgh, lending testament to its historical authenticity. As a Clan tartan, this design embodies the rich history of House Stewart, one of Scotland's most esteemed royal families, who have played a significant role in shaping the country's destiny. The Dress Blue shade, with its distinctive dark blue tone, is a nod to the dignified and refined qualities associated with the Stewarts, while the intricate pattern itself is a masterful blend of threads, reflecting the skill and craftsmanship of Scotland's weavers. Designed by the renowned tartan house Kinloch Anderson Ltd, this tartan design continues to hold significance for those seeking to connect with their Scottish heritage or pay homage to the noble House Stewart.

name: Chisholm Colonial
description: The Chisholm Colonial tartan is a rich and storied fabric that tells the tale of Scottish heritage and transatlantic endeavour. Designed by Kat Moore, a twelfth-generation descendant of the esteemed American-Scots line of Chisholms, this majestic tartan embodies the symbolism of her ancestors' pioneering spirit. The palette of blues evokes the vast oceans that once separated their families from Scotland, while the earthy tones represent the fertile lands they colonised. The incorporation of the fern - a nod to the family's clan emblem - weaves in a thread of connection to Scotland's ancient traditions. Each shade is imbued with meaning: the blood red that binds all Chisholms worldwide by birth and heritage, paying homage to their shared ancestry. This storied tartan serves as a testament to the enduring legacy of the Chisholm family name, woven into every thread with love, tradition, and a deep reverence for their Scottish roots.

name: Fife Ethylene Plant
description: The Fife Ethylene Plant tartan is a vibrant representation of innovation and industrial heritage, showcasing the 30-year anniversary celebration with precision and colour. Created by renowned designer John Barclay, this corporate tartan was born out of the plant's seafront location, where blue hues evoke the ocean's bounty that fuels its operations. The surrounding green landscape, comprising grass and trees, provides a striking contrast to the steelwork and steam represented by white, while yellow accents nod to the essential equipment that drives the facility forward. As a testament to Scotland's rich industrial past, this tartan pays homage to Fife's pioneering spirit, marrying functional precision with traditional craftsmanship, making it an ideal choice for corporate institutions looking to reflect their heritage and values.

name: Hamworthy Association
description: The Hamworthy Association tartan is a vibrant and distinctive corporate pattern born from the creative vision of Stuart Wallace, paying homage to an exclusive group of colleagues and former associates with Scottish roots. This carefully crafted tartan reflects the rich heritage and camaraderie that binds its wearers together, evoking the warmth and solidarity of a long-standing honourable association. Registered specifically for the sole use by the Hamworthy Association, this tartan's unique design is a testament to the enduring power of shared identity and community spirit, its technical precision and colourwork a celebration of Scottish tradition and cultural pride.

name: Hickory
description: The Hickory tartan is a captivating fashion statement inspired by the storied city of Nashville, Tennessee, where its designer, Andrew Dauphinee, found solace in the region's majestic old-growth hickory trees. This distinctive tartan weaves together the cultural heritage of America with the rich history of Scotland, echoing the strong and resilient qualities embodied by Andrew Jackson, "Old Hickory", a figure revered for his unyielding spirit. With its unique colour palette and carefully crafted pattern, this tartan pays homage to Nashville's natural beauty and historical significance, while also reflecting Dauphinee's vision for fashion that is both bold and authentic. Due to the exclusivity of this design, only those who have established a connection with the designer will be able to don or adorn the Hickory tartan, making it an exclusive and coveted choice for those seeking to make a lasting impression with their sartorial choices.

name: Holy Loch
description: The Holy Loch tartan is a vibrant testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's rich cultural heritage, with its distinctive pattern weaving together threads of local history and personal connection. Designed by Carmen Munoz and Elizabeth Melendez, whose families had long ties to the towns surrounding the iconic loch - Ardentinney, Strone, Kilmun, and Dunoon - this fashion tartan is a poignant tribute to their shared roots. As a registered design, Holy Loch holds a unique place in the world of tartanry, with its very existence contingent upon the designers' consent. This coveted fabric bears witness to the power of family, place, and community in shaping our identities and traditions, making it an instantly compelling addition to any fashion collection or Scottish heritage enthusiast's wardrobe.

name: International College of Dentists (Canadian Section) Dress
description: The International College of Dentists (Canadian Section) Dress tartan is a prestigious corporate design, woven to honour the esteemed Fellowship of the organisation established in 1927. Designed by Carol A L Martin, this unique tartan reflects the international humanitarian spirit of the ICD, featuring its signature colours - green and gold - alongside a distinctive houndstooth pattern comprising 15 lines, symbolising the College's 15 sections. Worn with pride at convocations, this tartan is reserved for wear by Fellows, their spouses and families, as well as distinguished visiting dignitaries, and can only be reproduced with Carol Martin's explicit permission. As a testament to Canada's place in the ICD's history, this tartan holds significant cultural value, marking the first Canadian Section to receive its own distinctive design, while also underscoring the organisation's commitment to promoting dentistry worldwide through its numerous humanitarian projects.

name: MacKenzie Dress #2
description: The MacKenzie Dress #2 tartan is a storied heritage pattern steeped in Scottish tradition, born from the MacGregor-Hastie collection, a treasure trove of tartans preserved by the Scottish Tartans Society. This Clan tartan, woven with precision and passion, was likely created to commemorate the esteemed MacKenzie family, whose proud history stretches back centuries. Dating between 1930 and 1950, this tartan sample hints at the golden age of traditional weaving in Scotland, where artisans carefully crafted these intricate patterns to tell stories of clan affiliations, ancestral lines, and enduring loyalty. As one of the many unmarked samples from this revered collection, the MacKenzie Dress #2 tartan remains a testament to the ingenuity and craftsmanship of Scotland's finest weavers, waiting to be rediscovered by those seeking to unravel the rich tapestry of Scottish heritage.

name: Matheson Hunting (Highland Society of London)
description: The Matheson Hunting tartan is a storied example of traditional Scottish weaving, born from the esteemed Highland Society of London collection. This intricate clan tartan has been passed down through generations of the noble Matheson family, whose heritage is deeply rooted in Scotland's rich history and culture. As recorded in D C Stewart's NOMINDEX, this tartan was originally registered as part of the Highland Society's collection, a testament to its significance within Scottish society. The Matheson Hunting tartan embodies the values of courage, loyalty, and tradition that have long been synonymous with the Matheson name. Its unique pattern weaves together threads of heritage and identity, reflecting the enduring legacy of this distinguished clan in Scotland's storied past.

name: Norwegian Night
description: The Norwegian Night tartan is an ethereal and captivating Fashion tartan, inspired by the breathtaking beauty of the Aurora Borealis that dances across the Norwegian sky on clear nights. Designed by the renowned Kvam & McSprea duo using the Scotweb online tartan designer, this stunning pattern embodies the magic of Norway's natural heritage. According to its registration notes, the tartan was created specifically for those associated with Norway, evoking a sense of national pride and connection to the country's rich cultural history. The subtle colour palette, ranging from soft blues and greens to fiery oranges and pinks, conjures images of shimmering curtains of light in the night sky, inviting wearers to experience a touch of Nordic mystique.

name: Scottish Wildcat
description: The Scottish Wildcat tartan is a vibrant and striking fashion pattern, carefully designed by Glen Allardyce to pay tribute to Scotland's majestic native feline heritage. This distinctive tartan, registered under the category of Fashion, features an intricate arrangement of blues and greens reminiscent of the wildcat's natural habitat, evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish wilderness. As a symbol of conservation efforts, the sale of this tartan is dedicated to supporting Wildcat Haven's initiatives to protect and preserve the critically endangered species. With its unique characteristics restricted by Wildcat Haven, the Scottish Wildcat tartan serves as a powerful reminder of Scotland's rich cultural heritage and the importance of safeguarding its natural treasures for future generations.

name: Sound of Mull
description: The Sound of Mull tartan is a sumptuous fabric creation, born from the meticulous hands of Scottish designer Sheila Grant, whose inspiration was drawn from the sonic landscapes of her native Hebridean island, Mull. This exclusive fashion tartan is woven with colours that hold deep significance to the designer, evoking the rugged beauty and mystical essence of this enigmatic isle. A registered creation, available for the sole use of its creator and Gordon Grant Ltd, this stunning tartan embodies the very essence of Scottish heritage and tradition - a testament to the enduring power of Scottish design and the artistic vision of Sheila Grant.

name: Wallace High School
description: The Wallace High School tartan is a stirring celebration of Scottish heritage and community spirit, rooted in the very heart of the country near Stirling. Designed to reflect the school's rich history and connection to the iconic Wallace Monument, this corporate tartan combines deep purple hues reminiscent of the school tie with subtle undertones of silver and dark grey, evoking the enduring traditions of Scotland's past. The deliberate incorporation of two distinct tones of purple, echoing previous eras of the school uniform, pays homage to the institution's evolution while maintaining a sense of continuity with its storied heritage. As such, this tartan serves not only as a symbol of corporate identity but also as a poignant testament to the enduring power of Scottish tradition and community pride.

name: WestJet
description: The WestJet tartan is a unique corporate design born from a partnership between WestJet Airlines and renowned Scottish weavers, Robertson, Lindsay & D C Dalgliesh. Specifically commissioned to commemorate WestJet's inaugural flight service from Halifax, Nova Scotia to Glasgow, Scotland, this tartan pattern proudly represents the company's identity and values. As a Corporate tartan, its purpose is to signify the WestJet family at work, whether in the airline's offices or on-the-go employees, while also paying homage to Canada's East Coast roots and Scotland's rich heritage. Although restricted to official use by WestJet and its employees, this vibrant tartan design has become an integral part of the company's branding, allowing select family members to purchase items bearing the distinctive pattern.

name: Rainbow
description: The Rainbow tartan, a vibrant and colourful fashion choice, embodies the free-spirited nature of Scottish heritage without any direct ties to its geographical origins. As a District Check, this tartan's complex pattern and irregular sett suggest a deep connection to Scotland's rich textile tradition. The rainbow hues - red, blue, yellow, green, white, orange, and black - evoke the country's breathtaking natural beauty, from the rugged Highlands to the rolling glens. While its design is unencumbered by clan affiliations or geographical associations, the Rainbow tartan remains a testament to Scotland's enduring legacy of innovation and creativity in the world of textiles.

name: Madoc of Wales
description: The Madoc of Wales tartan is a vibrant and unique design that proudly wears its heritage on its sleeve. Registered as a Name tartan, this distinctive pattern is deeply rooted in Welsh tradition, albeit with a relatively recent genesis. As Sheila Daniel's creation for Wales Tartan Centres, Cambrian Woollen Mill, it embodies the modernising spirit of contemporary tartanry. Notable for its departure from traditional Celtic patterns, Madoc of Wales features an uncommon warp and weft composition, setting it apart from its peers. To ensure respect for Welsh heritage, consent must be obtained from Wales Tartan Centres, Swansea prior to weaving. With 'of Wales' proudly emblazoned on the design, this tartan serves as a testament to the power of cultural preservation and innovation, bridging the past with the present in a beautiful display of traditional flair and modern sensibility.

name: Rogers Family (Kilkeel) (Personal)
description: The Rogers Family (Kilkeel) tartan is a storied and deeply personal design, rooted in the rich heritage of James Rogers' family, who hail from Kilkeel, Northern Ireland. Commissioned by Mr Rogers himself, this name tartan is steeped in tradition and history, drawing inspiration from the iconic Black Watch sett. The palette of dark blues and light blues evokes a sense of maritime journeying, symbolising the countless miles of sea that have connected family members to their various homes across England, Ireland, Scotland, and Australia. This intricate pattern serves as a poignant testament to the long-standing service and dedication to crown and country by Rogers family members, while also paying homage to the sweeping landscapes and atmospheric skies of Northern Ireland's rugged coast.

name: Harbison 2015
description: Designed by Arthur R Harbison as a family tartan using colours of significance to the family. This tartan may be worn by anyone with the Harbison surname.

name: Maver Dress
description: The Maver Dress tartan is a stunning, unique Name tartan created by John Maver, showcasing an intricately woven blend of colours that exude a sense of boldness and sophistication. Registered as a dress version of its eponymous predecessor (SRT Ref #10329), this tartan is perfect for those seeking to make a statement with their fashion choices. With its distinctive pattern, the Maver Dress tartan pays homage to Scottish heritage and tradition, evoking the rugged beauty of the Highlands while exuding modern flair. As a Name tartan, it holds significance within the family or clan that has chosen to register it, serving as a proud emblem of identity and connection to Scottish roots.

name:
MacLulich [default]
[AKA] Stewart Blue
description: The Stewart, Blue #1 fashion tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich cultural heritage, its design bearing a striking resemblance to the iconic MacBeth tartan, albeit with a bold twist. By retaining the traditional blue-black-blue-green pattern, but replacing the yellow bars with vibrant red ones, this tartan pays homage to the storied past of the Stewarts, one of Scotland's most revered royal clans. As a fashion choice, it exudes a sense of nobility and grandeur, evoking the grandeur of Scotland's Highland regalia. With its restricted colour palette, this tartan is designed for those who desire a stylish and symbolic connection to their Scottish heritage, free from the complexities of complex clan affiliations, making it an ideal choice for those seeking to favour a more general representation of Scotland's rich tradition.

name: Pride of LGBT
description: The Pride of LGBT tartan is a vibrant and powerful tribute to the modern LGBTQ+ movement, born from the heart of 1969's New York City protests. This fashion tartan, designed by Brian Wilton, draws inspiration from the iconic bright colours used during that pivotal moment in history, which have become synonymous with the community's courage and resilience. The registration notes reveal a rich cultural heritage at play, as this specific tartan pays homage to a global movement that has continued to thrive and evolve over the decades. A testament to the enduring spirit of pride and identity, the Pride of LGBT tartan is a bold statement that celebrates diversity and individuality, and its exclusive licence ensures that it remains a cherished symbol of LGBTQ+ solidarity, available only with the permission of its copyright holders.

name: Northumberland Check
description: The Northumberland tartan is an enduring emblem of Scotland's rich heritage, with its storied past stretching back to Roman times. Once worn by humble shepherds tending their flocks along the Border, this distinctive check pattern has been inextricably linked with the Percy family, Dukes of Northumberland, who have adorned their pipers with it for generations. The tartan's connection to this esteemed aristocratic lineage is a testament to its enduring significance, and its adoption as the official dress of the piper has cemented its place in Scotland's cultural identity. Originally woven from undyed sheep's fleece, the Northumberland tartan was later enhanced with vegetable dyes, giving rise to the natural shades of greens and browns that are synonymous with this iconic design today. With a history dating back over 1,700 years, this tartan is more than just a pattern - it is a poignant reminder of Scotland's ancient traditions and the enduring legacy of its noble past.

name: Strachan Hunting
description: Strachan Hunting is a time-honoured tartan, proudly worn by Clan Strachan's descendants as a symbol of heritage and kinship. Registered for use in 2008, this distinctive hunting tartan was created to commemorate the family's rich tradition of fox hunting and shooting. The design, expertly crafted by Jim Strachan and Rob Strachan alongside Dennis Strawhun, features a classic repeating pattern of blues and greens, evoking the rolling Scottish hills and heather-clad moors where Clan Strachan's ancestral lands are found. With its approval from Commander Rob Strachan, this tartan is now recognised as an official emblem of Clan Strachan, proudly worn at family gatherings, formal events, and other celebrations of Scottish heritage.

name: MacLeod Red
description: The MacLeod Red tartan is a deeply rooted and historically significant textile, woven from the threads of Scotland's rich clan heritage. This striking pattern, designed in honour of Norman MacLeod, 22nd Chief of the clan, boasts a vibrant red hue with subtle variations in tone that evoke the rugged Scottish landscape. The sett was originally painted by Allan Ramsay in 1747 and later embellished with a yellow stripe by Ruairidh MacLeod to accentuate family connections. Adopted as an official tartan at a clan Parliament in 1982, this tartan represents the proud legacy of the MacLeod clan, whose name is synonymous with bravery, loyalty, and Scottish tradition. Wearing or displaying the MacLeod Red tartan is not only a testament to one's heritage but also a celebration of the clan's enduring values and history.

name: Douglas WCMM
description: The Douglas tartan, registered as WCWM, is a storied fashion tartan born from the traditions of Scotland's rich heritage. Woven by the skilled artisans at West Coast Woolen Mill, this timeless design is steeped in history and culture, its intricate patterns evoking the rugged beauty of the Scottish Highlands. As a fashion tartan, the Douglas is perfect for adding a touch of Scotland's signature style to any outfit, from casual wear to formal attire. With no specific details known about its origins or inspiration, this tartan remains a testament to the enduring power of traditional Scottish design, ready to be worn with pride by anyone who embodies the spirit of the Highlands.

name: Connolly Dress
description: The Connolly Dress tartan is a rich and storied pattern, steeped in the heritage of one of Ireland's most esteemed clans. Registration notes reveal that this distinctive tartan was specifically designed to bear the name of Professor Joseph F. Connolly II, an American scholar who chose to re-establish his family's roots in Ireland, thus cementing his connection to the Emerald Isle. As a Clan/Family tartan, its significance extends beyond mere fashion, speaking instead to a sense of ancestry and tradition that runs deep within the Irish diaspora. While no designer is credited with creating this tartan, it is clear that its origins are rooted in a desire to preserve and promote the Connolly name, making it a treasured emblem of family pride and cultural heritage.

name: Rutherford, Simon Travis Alan
description: A personal family tartan featuring the following colours: white and blue as a tribute to bratach na h-Alba, dark red which represents fortitude and yellow which represents constancy and faith with which family lineage has endured and prospered.

name: Rutherford, Simon Travis Alan Hunting
description: A hunting version of the Rutherford, Simon Travis Alan (Personal) family tartan.

name: MacFadyan (MacGregor Hastie)
description: The MacFadyan tartan, borne by the storied MacGregor Hastie clan, is a testament to Scotland's rich tapestry of heritage and tradition. This distinctive family tartan, rooted in Scottish history, is remarkably similar to its sibling sett, the MacBean, lending credence to the notion that these two clans have long been intertwined. While not specifically designed by a renowned weaver, this threadcount has been carefully preserved within the Scottish Tartans Society's esteemed MacGregor Hastie Collection. As an unmarked sample, it provides a glimpse into the subtle nuances of tartan design, with each thread meticulously woven to evoke the enduring spirit of the MacFadyan clan and their storied legacy.

name: Abel (2015)
description: The Abel tartan, registered in 2015, is a name tartan that holds deep significance for families bearing the esteemed surname. Designed by Dannie Abel, a weaver of discerning taste, this vibrant and intricate pattern pays homage to the colours associated with the family's heritage. By virtue of its registration, the Abel tartan may be worn by all individuals with the surname Abel, serving as a powerful symbol of pride, identity, and connection to their ancestral roots. This unique tapestry of blues, greens, and yellows is more than just a fabric motif – it is a visual representation of family legacy, woven into the very fabric of Scottish tradition.

name: Raeburn [default]
description: The Raeburn tartan is a richly woven testament to Scotland's storied past, its origins shrouded in mystery but its cultural significance undeniable. First appearing on trade lists in the 1930s, this distinctive pattern bears a familial resemblance to the MacLeod tartan of the 19th century, albeit with narrower yellow bands and no central red stripe. Bearing the name of the ancient lands of Rayburn in Ayrshire, this tartan is deeply rooted in Scottish heritage, evoking memories of centuries past when the region was settled by brave clansmen like Sir Henry Raeburn, a notable figure from the 18th century. Registered by the Scottish Tartans Society and housed in esteemed collections such as the Dalgety Collection and Johnston Collection, the Raeburn tartan serves as a poignant reminder of Scotland's complex history and its enduring legacy in the world of traditional textiles.

name: Wallace Dress; Blue
description: This enchanting Wallace Blue Dress dance tartan is a modern interpretation of Scotland's rich heritage, crafted by renowned designer Dalgliesh, D C. Originally inspired by the timeless Wallace Blue STR #4483, this unique variation flips the traditional colours on their head, with green and white replacing the blue in the iconic pattern. A staple for any fashion-conscious tartan enthusiast, the Wallace Blue Dress dance tartan embodies the spirit of Scottish tradition and history, perfect for adding a touch of Highland flair to any outfit. With its bold and striking design, this tartan is sure to make a statement, but please note that it falls under restrictions and must be prepared for weaving by DC Dalgliesh Ltd., ensuring the integrity of this cherished heritage design.

name: Auld Alliance
description: The Auld Alliance tartan, lovingly crafted by David McGill, pays tribute to the enduring bond between Scotland and France, forged through nearly five centuries of shared history and cultural exchange.
