Commissioned by Mme Olga Poivre d'Arvor, Director of the French Institute in Scotland, this commemorative tartan marks a milestone in the 40th anniversary celebration of the Institute. The Auld Alliance, which spanned from 1295 to 1903, granted dual citizenship to citizens of both nations, fostering a deep sense of mutual respect and understanding between two countries that share a rich heritage in art, literature, and philosophy. This stunning tartan, reserved for those with the designer's consent, is a poignant reminder of the long-standing honour and friendship between Scotland and France, now cherished by a new generation of enthusiasts who continue to weave the threads of this storied alliance into their lives.

name: SotoBerg, Cedessa & Shelby (Personal)
description: The SotoBerg, Cedessa & Shelby tartan is a vibrant testament to love and unity, woven from the threads of two families' unique histories and personal preferences. As a Name tartan, it bears the surname of its designer, Berg, Cedessa, who meticulously crafted this distinctive design to commemorate the joining of two families, bridging separate backgrounds and forging a new union. The palette reflects the couple's individual favourites, as well as their wedding colours, creating a rich tapestry that celebrates their commitment to each other. This personal tartan is a poignant reminder of the power of love and tradition, its very existence a celebration of the couple's decision to weave together their lives, creating something entirely new and beautiful from the fabric of their shared heritage.

name: Chubbs, L & S
description: A personal tartan for L & S Chubbs and their family. The Chubbs family came from England, via the Jersey Islands, and settled in Labrador, Canada in the 19th century. The colours were chosen to represent the Chubbs family history.

name: Grand Lodge of Canada
description: The Grand Lodge of Canada tartan is a bespoke corporate design, expertly crafted by Masonic Themes of Glasgow to commemorate the esteemed organisation's 150th Anniversary celebration in Hamilton. This unique and prestigious tartan has been specifically created for the Grand Lodge of Canada, with its distinctive pattern and colours woven together to pay tribute to this venerable institution. As an exclusive creation, it is only available for purchase from the Lodge itself, highlighting the close connection between the design's creator, Derek McNulty, and the fraternal organisation that commissioned it. This tartan embodies the values of camaraderie and heritage that are at the heart of Masonic tradition, making it a treasured symbol of affiliation and loyalty among members of the Grand Lodge of Canada.

name: Gammon, W & Family (Personal)
description: The Gammon, W & Family tartan is a unique and meaningful textile pattern steeped in Scottish heritage, specifically designed for families centred around the esteemed Gammon clan. This personal tartan, registered under Ashley Gammon's creative vision, embodies the values of military and public service that are deeply ingrained within the family's history. The design's distinct blue and grey hues pay homage to these revered traditions, evoking a sense of pride and honour among those who bear this tartan. Woven into its intricate pattern is a rich tapestry of Scottish tradition and identity, reflecting the enduring legacy of the Gammon name and its proud bearing by families across generations.

name: Holyrood
description: The Holyrood tartan is a prestigious Commemorative design, crafted by renowned weaver Alistair Buchan to pay tribute to Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II on the occasion of her Silver Jubilee in 1977. This majestic tartan is deeply rooted in Scottish tradition and heritage, reflecting the country's rich history and royal heritage. Named after the iconic Holyrood Palace in Edinburgh, which serves as the Queen's official residence in Scotland, this tartan is steeped in symbolism and significance. The registration notes reveal a strong connection to Buckingham Palace, highlighting the unique bond between the Scottish monarchy and its English counterpart. With its rich colours and distinctive sett, the Holyrood tartan proudly embodies the enduring spirit of Scottish tradition and its enduring ties with the British royal family.

name: MacGirr
description: Designed as a tartan for those of the name of McGirr. According to MacLysaght 'The Surnames of Ireland' (1985) MacGirr is an old County Armagh name which is also found in Co. Tyrone.

name: Murdoch [default]
description: The Murdoch (Dalgliesh) tartan is a storied emblem of the esteemed Dalgliesh clan, whose rich heritage dates back to Scotland's turbulent past. Registered by D.C. Dalgliesh Ltd in all likelihood as part of a larger clan identity, this distinctive tartan pattern holds great significance for families and descendants tracing their ancestry to this respected sept. The Murdoch (Dalgliesh) design, though shrouded in mystery regarding its origins, boasts a unique blend of blues, reds, and yellows that evoke the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highland landscapes. Prepared specifically for weaving by Dalgliesh Ltd, this tartan invites wearers to proudly don their clan heritage on formal occasions, such as weddings or ceremonial events. Though restrictions exist regarding its use, the Murdoch (Dalgliesh) remains a treasured symbol of Scottish tradition and family honour, worthy of respect and reverence.

name: Otago Peninsula
description: The Otago Peninsula tartan is a vibrant and evocative tribute to the natural beauty of New Zealand's southern shores. Designed by renowned textile artist Vilma Ruth Nelson, this District tartan was created in honour of the Otago Peninsula Trust, which safeguards the historic house and gardens of Dunedin open to the public. The colours chosen by Nelson evoke the region's stunning wildlife, with salmon pink representing the iconic salmon that thrive in the peninsula's waters, alongside kingfisher blue, a nod to the majestic bird that calls this place home. This unique tartan not only celebrates the Otago Peninsula's rich heritage but also serves as a testament to the enduring spirit of conservation and preservation that defines its people.

name: Murray of Polmaise [default]
description: The Murray of Polmaise tartan is a storied family heirloom, steeped in the rich heritage of the Scottish Highlands. This Clan tartan, inspired by its variation from the revered Tullibardine sett, holds great sentimental value for Lord James Stewart Murray, 9th Duke of Atholl, who gifted it to his troop of Boy Scouts as a symbol of community and tradition. Weaving together threads of history and loyalty, this tartan design has been intricately crafted by skilled manufacturers in Stirling, paying homage to the esteemed Murray family lineage. Its significance extends beyond the realm of fashion, representing a sense of honour, duty, and belonging that is deeply rooted in Scottish culture.

name: Royal Naval Association
description: The Royal Naval Association tartan is a poignant tribute to the British naval tradition, weaving together threads of Scottish heritage with the rich history of Her Majesty's Fleet Air Arm. Designed by esteemed weavers Macnaughtons of Perth and Granville Cooper as the official tartan for this esteemed organisation, it was specifically crafted to commemorate Queen Elizabeth II's Golden Jubilee and her long-standing patronage towards the Royal Naval Association. As a military category tartan, its purpose is rooted in tradition and camaraderie among naval personnel, while its incorporation of Fleet Air Arm colours pays homage to the bravery and sacrifice of those who serve on the nation's seas. This distinctive tartan design serves as a symbol of honour, pride, and service, carrying the legacy of Her Majesty's naval heritage forward with reverence and respect.

name: South African Air Force
description: The South African Air Force tartan is a poignant tribute to the country's rich military heritage, woven with precision and pride by Jenny Edmondson at the renowned Lochcarron of Scotland mill. This distinctive tartan, registered in the Scottish Tartans Authority's Johnston Collection, was carefully designed to reflect the bravery and camaraderie that defines the South African Air Force. As a military category, this tartan is steeped in tradition and honour, its bold colours and intricate patterns evoking the values of loyalty and service that have defined the air force for generations. With its unique design, the South African Air Force tartan serves as a lasting reminder of the country's proud military history, worn with favour by those who wear it, and an enduring symbol of national pride.

name: Lochcarron Ruby
description: Lochcarron Ruby, a fashion tartan of unparalleled elegance, embodies the timeless spirit of Scotland's rich heritage. Inspired by the ancient traditions of tartan-weaving, this captivating design masterfully blends modern hues with subtle nods to the country's iconic Saltire flag. A symphony of vibrant colours, from deep crimson reds reminiscent of Scotland's rugged landscapes to rich jewel tones that evoke the warmth of a Highland winter's night, Lochcarron Ruby is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scottish tartanry. Exclusive in its appeal, this fashion tartan is reserved for the discerning few who can wear their heritage with honours, making it a treasured possession for those privileged enough to own it.

name: Red Red Rose
description: The Red Red Rose tartan is a vibrant celebration of the intersection of Chinese New Year and Burns Night, two festivals that converge on January 25th. Designed by Lochcarron of Scotland in 2020, this fashion tartan weaves together the rich cultural heritage of both Scotland and China, with the iconic Burns Check red colourway now presented in a bold new hue, symbolic of joy and happiness in Chinese culture. This restricted tartan is not only a testament to Scotland's long-standing connections with the Asian community, but also marks a unique moment in history when two nations' most treasured festivals coalesce. With its intricate patterns and colours evoking the warmth and camaraderie of these special occasions, the Red Red Rose tartan invites wearers to join in the celebration of both Chinese New Year and Burns Night, as it looks forward to being woven again in 2096.

name: Lochcarron Graphite
description: Lochcarron Graphite, a fashion tartan born from the rich industrial heritage of Scotland, is a testament to the country's unyielding spirit of innovation. This striking design, featuring a palette of grey tones punctuated by vibrant reds, pays homage to the steel-making and ship-building industries that once defined the nation's economy. According to its registration notes, the tartan's creator, Lochcarron of Scotland, drew inspiration from the rugged landscape and industrial legacy of Scotland's heavy sectors, distilling the essence of these traditions into a timeless and sophisticated fabric. Wearing Lochcarron Graphite is not just a statement of personal style, but an expression of respect for Scotland's proud industrial heritage and its people who have shaped the country's history and identity.

name: Steps to Hope
description: Steps to Hope is a powerful corporate tartan, designed by Lochcarron of Scotland with the intention of supporting a charitable cause close to its heart. Dedicated to Edinburgh-based charity Steps to Hope, which cares for the homeless and those struggling with addiction, this unique tartan embodies the organisation's mission to help individuals turn their lives around and find hope. By being used exclusively by Lochcarron of Scotland and its customers, this distinctive tartan pays homage to the charity's vital work, and serves as a symbol of commitment to helping others in need. Its registration notes serve as a poignant reminder of the charitable purpose behind its creation, making it a truly meaningful and significant addition to any corporate wardrobe.

name: Hame
description: The Hame tartan is a stylish and evocative fashion design inspired by the breathtaking landscapes of Scotland, reflecting the very heart of the nation's heritage. Based on the traditional Lochcarron sett, this distinctive pattern features a palette of muted hues reminiscent of heather and gorse-drenched braes, sky-blue lochs, and sea-kissed coastlines. As an exclusive creation by Lochcarron of Scotland, this tartan is steeped in tradition, yet effortlessly modern in its appeal - a testament to the enduring power of Scottish textiles to evoke feelings of warmth, belonging, and timelessness. Its intended use for Lochcarron customers underscores the close bond between the designer, the heritage brand, and the rich cultural fabric that underpins the tartan's creation.

name:
O'Buckley Hunting
[AKA] O'Buckley, C
description: A tartan for C O’Buckley using colours intended to represent Ireland.

name: MacCandlish Green; Hunting
description: The McCandlish Hunting Green tartan is a rich and storied family tartan, steeped in Scottish heritage and tradition. Registered in 1992 by Stanton Ward Foster McCandlish and his esteemed advisor J. Charles 'Scotty' Thompson, this distinctive design weaves together the complex history of the McCandlish clan, with influences from both the Black Watch and Gordon tartans. The tartan's bold colours, including a vibrant yellow stripe representing the pivotal Jacobite Risings that split the family into distinct lines, evoke the passion and resilience of the McCandlish ancestors. The deep blue tones, reminiscent of the vast oceanic expanse where many McCandlises settled as Gaelic diaspora, serve as a poignant reminder of their global dispersal. With its unique blend of colour and symbolism, the McCandlish Hunting Green tartan embodies the enduring legacy of this storied family, whose roots in Scotland's Borders region continue to flourish worldwide.

name: Ross Hunting Dress
description: The Ross Hunting Dress tartan is a quintessential example of Scottish fashion heritage, born from the fancies of Dalgliesh's dancers in the 19th century. Designed by Hugh MacPherson, this iconic tartan was originally recorded in J & S Lawson's Edinburgh swatch book, providing a glimpse into the evolution of traditional Scottish weaving. The subtle variations between different thread counts add to its unique character, reflecting the skillful craftsmanship of Scotland's textile artisans. This Fashion tartan is a testament to Scotland's rich history and cultural tradition, embodying the country's love affair with hunting and outdoor pursuits. Its association with the Ross clan adds an air of nobility and heritage, making it a coveted choice for those seeking to connect with Scotland's storied past.

name: Veitch H & Family
description: The colours chosen for this tartan are intended to represent the history of the Veitch surname which was first recorded in Berwickshire when Randolph Veitch witnessed a charter by Henry de Graham c.1200; red and grey represent the Aberdeenshire granite of Darwyk House, first built by the Veitch family; green represents the Dawyck arboretum and botanical gardens; blue represents the River Tweed and the Scrape burn which runs through the gardens; yellow and white represent the yellow Winter Aconites and white Snowdrops which carpet the banks of the Scarpe burn in springtime.

name: Lindsay-McGee, C & V - Wedding (Personal)
description: The Lindsay-McGee Wedding tartan is a unique and personal creation, woven to commemorate the special day of Victoria Lindsay and Calum McGee's union. This exclusive name tartan is the result of collaboration between the bride and groom, with designers Victoria Lindsay and Calum McGee bringing their individual flair to create a truly bespoke design. As a category "Name" tartan, this design signifies that it is specifically associated with the individuals who commissioned it, making it a deeply personal and meaningful part of Scottish heritage. However, due to copyright restrictions, this tartan is not open for commercial use, ensuring its significance remains closely tied to the happy couple's special day. This exclusive tartan design is now an integral part of the Lindsay-McGee family's legacy, preserving their love story through the rich tradition of tartan weaving.

name: Culross
description: The Culross tartan is a captivating tribute to the historic and picturesque royal burgh in West Fife, Scotland. Designed by Taffled Threads, this district tartan has been inspired by the village's rich heritage and folklore, with blues and greens evoking its stunning estuary location on the Firth of Forth. Orange, red, brown, and black shades, reminiscent of the village's unique architectural features, including Culross Palace, add depth and character to the design. Restricted exclusively for use through Lindsey Marchant at the Greengate Gallery Culross, this tartan is a testament to the village's enduring legacy as a place of pilgrimage and trade. Prepared for weaving by Claire Hunter, Taffled Threads has carefully woven together these inspirational elements to reflect the unique Scottish heritage of Culross, making it an authentic and meaningful addition to any collection.

name: Boyter, D
description: A personal tartan for David Boyter to celebrate his Scottish heritage.

name: Riddoch [default]
description: Designed by Tony Murray for an Albert (Bert) Riddoch of Bearsden, Glasgow, as a personal tartan. It was then changed to use by anyone of the name. Bert Riddoch (2002) is a private investigator involved in covert drugs investigations and 'highly thought of by the police'. Tartan based on Campbell of Breadalbane.

name: MacInnes Dress
description: The MacInnes Dress tartan is a quintessential example of Clan tartanry, woven with pride by the esteemed weavers at D.C. Dalgliesh's renowned firm in Selkirk. This timeless design has been formally registered under the Tartans Act 1994 and is a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan MacInnes. The complex interplay of blue, green, red, yellow, black, and brown hues creates a rich tapestry that echoes the rugged beauty of Scotland's Highlands. Originally intended for formal wear, such as kilted dresses, this tartan holds great cultural significance among descendants of Clan MacInnes, who continue to cherish its heritage. As a family tartan, it remains an honourable part of Scottish tradition and identity.

name:
MacPherson Hunting
[AKA] MacPherson Badenoch
description: The MacPherson Hunting tartan is a revered heritage design, steeped in history and tradition. Originally recorded by the Smiths in 1850, this distinctive pattern is said to have been worn by the clan in two forms: as a white-ground tartan or a grey-ground hunting tartan. The latter, in particular, holds significance as it was purportedly first introduced by the clan's family members, with one such example preserved in the ancient shawl of a MacPherson grandmother, passed down through generations and even stored within Cluny Castle. This testament to the tartan's enduring importance not only highlights its cultural relevance but also underscores its connection to the clan's rich heritage and tradition.

name: Miami Dade Fire Rescue
description: The Miami Dade Fire Rescue tartan, designed by Thomas Quinn, is a distinctive corporate tartan worn with pride by members and retired personnel of this esteemed fire service organisation based in Miami-Dade County, Florida. This vibrant and meaningful tartan commemorates the history and bravery of MDFR's 2,300 uniformed personnel, who provide comprehensive emergency services to the community. The subtle yet striking colour palette reflects the unity of theorganisation - with grey representing the iconic uniform, lime green symbolising the apparatus that rushes to the scene, blue honouring the dedication to Emergency Medical Services, and red embodying the ferocity of fire itself. Gold accents nod to the heroism of firefighters and black serves as a poignant tribute to those who have given their lives in service. As a wearable badge of honour for its members, this tartan proudly embodies the values and tradition of MDFR, paying testament to the courage and selflessness that define this esteemed organisation.

name: Jordan Fabbro & Family (Personal)
description: This tartan was designed as a family tartan to be worn by Jordan Fabbro and his family.

name: Castle on the Hill
description: The Castle on the Hill tartan is a fashion-inspired design that embodies the mystique and romance of Scotland's storied castles. Designed by Andrew Dauphinee, this intricate weave weaves together elements of medieval grandeur and rugged landscape, evoking the dramatic silhouettes of Scottish hill forts and the imposing solidity of stone strongholds. With its rich, muted colours and subtle texture, this tartan invites wearers to embody the proud heritage and history that defines Scotland's architectural icons. Though restricted to being worn by Andrew Dauphinee, his family, friends, and with his explicit permission, this unique tartan represents a rare opportunity for those in favour of Scottish tradition and flair to own a piece of authentic, designer-crafted heritage.

name: McAndrew, B (Personal)
description: This timeless tartan, registered as the McAndrew, B (Personal), holds a deeply personal significance for its namesake and his esteemed family lineage. As a Name tartan, it is a unique and distinctive identifier, set apart from the more general Clan or Corporate registrations. Designed by Benedict McAndrew himself, this tartan weaves together a rich tapestry of heritage and tradition, paying homage to Ben's family's history and values. With its carefully crafted patterns and colours, this tartan serves as a visual representation of Ben's identity and connection to his roots, making it a treasured family heirloom for generations to come.

name: Culloden 1746
description: Count from the original Culloden coat discovered (and later examined) by Peter MacDonald on display at the Kelvingrove Museum, Glasgow July 07.

name: Redpath, The Ronald
description: The Ronald Redpath tartan is a proud tribute to Scottish heritage, carefully woven by Alan Redpath to honour his father's legacy. As a Name tartan, it bears its family name with distinction, evoking a sense of tradition and continuity. The registration notes reveal that this unique design was inspired by the life and service of Ronald Redpath, a former BAOR artillery officer born in Cowdenbeath, Fife, whose dedication to country and community has been a constant source of inspiration for his son, Alan. This tartan embodies the values of Scottish identity, family pride, and the unwavering commitment to serving one's country, making it a truly special and meaningful addition to the world of tartan design.

name: Highland Titles
description: The Highland Titles tartan is a rich and vibrant celebration of Scotland's breathtaking landscapes, woven into a distinctive corporate identity for a pioneering conservation company. Designed by Peter Bevis, this tartan has been carefully crafted to reflect the values of the Highland Titles, a unique venture that allows individuals to purchase small plots of land in the Scottish Highlands. With its bold, earthy tones and intricate patterns, the Highland Titles tartan evokes the rugged beauty of Scotland's wilderness, while also paying homage to the country's rich cultural heritage. As a corporate tartan, it is designed to be worn with pride by the company's employees, ambassadors, and supporters, serving as a tangible connection to the land, the environment, and the sense of community that underpins this innovative initiative.

name: Freemasons Universal
description: This was commissioned by the Grand Lodge, Free & Accepted Masons of Utah for the use of all Masons worldwide. Designed by Anne Carroll Gilmour of Park City, Utah the colours relate to the various 'Masonic organisations and appendant bodies.'

name: Guilder (2018)
description: The Guilder tartan, registered in 2018, is a proud declaration of heritage and family identity. Created by renowned designer Fiona Whitson for the esteemed Guilder family, this intricate tartan was carefully crafted to reflect their unique colours and traditions. As a Name tartan, it serves as a testament to the family's history and legacy, allowing its wearers to showcase their connection to their ancestral roots. With restrictions in place, ensuring the design is woven with Scotweb's approval, this tartan is a treasured asset for those who bear the Guilder name, providing an authentic means of self-expression and cultural continuity. By embracing this unique tartan, the Guilder family continues to honour their ancestors' legacy, while also forging a lasting bond with their Scottish heritage.

name: Great Orchestra of Christmas Charity
description: Designed to honour the thousands of volunteers from all over the world, united in the long-term mission of The Great Orchestra of Christmas Charity in the field of health protection. Colour: red symbolises the heart in the Foundation's logo; grey represents the hard work and involvement of volunteers; yellow represents the joy of helping. White and red were included colours of the flag of Poland and white and blue were chosen to represent the involvement and support of the people of Scotland.

name: Lochcarron Platinum Jubilee
description: The fourth commemorative tartan in the Holyrood series from Lochcarron of Scotland, this was designed in recognition of the Platinum Jubilee of Queen Elizabeth II. The original sett of the Holyrood, as designed in 1977 by Mr Alistair Buchan, has been recoloured to include purple and platinum in celebration of the reign of Queen Elizabeth II through several Jubilee years.

name: Stovell (2015)
description: The Stovell tartan, registered in 2015, is a poignant tribute to the esteemed Stovell family, crafted with love and respect by Stephen McLean in honour of William Stovell's remarkable 90th birthday celebration. This Name tartan is specifically designed for those who share the Stovell surname, serving as a badge of pride and connection to their heritage. Wearing this tartan is not just about fashion, but about being part of a shared legacy and tradition that transcends generations. With its unique sett and carefully chosen colours, the Stovell tartan embodies the values of family, loyalty, and community that are at the heart of Scottish culture. By donning this tartan, those who bear the Stovell name are able to proudly express their roots and connection to Scotland's rich history and traditions.

name: Dickson (Personal)
description: The Dickson tartan is a richly woven tapestry of Scottish heritage, born from the family's ancestral roots in the 1st colours of Ross, Anderson, Wallace, and Forbes. This personal clan name tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of Scotland's storied past, where the threads of history and tradition are intricately intertwined. As a Name tartan, the Dickson design is deeply rooted in its family's unique identity, evoking a sense of pride and connection to those who bear its name. The subtle nuances of this traditional tartan speak volumes about the intricate tapestry of Scottish clan histories, where threads of loyalty, honour, and tradition are forever woven together.

name: von Goble, Brant
description: A personal tartan for Brant von Goble and his family. The colours black, red, and orange are intended to represent the Goble family’s appreciation of autumn and the celebrations of the season. Purple is intended to symbolise the beauty of the sky at twilight.

name: Hodgert, Connor & Family
description: A tartan for Connor Hodgert and his family. The tartan was created to connect the whole family, started by Betty Jean McMillan (1923-2010) who had 3 sons with Robert H Hodgert (1912-1965). The design is intended to represent an emphasis on hard work, new beginnings, the raising of animals, and family bonds.

name: Menzies Hunting (variant 1570)
description: The Round Table Sweden tartan is a distinctive corporate tartan, carefully crafted by Egbert Harmse at Cargokilts to represent the exclusive heritage of Round Table Sweden. Its rich falu-red base, reminiscent of Swedish wooden cottages and barns, sets the tone for this vibrant design, which also incorporates blue and yellow hues evoking the traditional colours of the organisation. According to its registration notes, the tartan's significance lies in its connection to the annual Central Tablers' Meeting held in Stirling, Scotland, where it was first unveiled. With restrictions in place, limiting its use to current or former members of Round Table Sweden, this tartan is a powerful symbol of unity and affiliation among those who bear it. When worn with pride, it pays homage to the organisation's Swedish roots and traditions, while also representing a sense of global connection and shared values among its members.

name: Bizzell, Thomas Dress (Personal)
description: The Thomas Bizzell, Thomas Dress tartan is a bespoke design born from the personal taste of its creator, Thomas Bizzell. Registered as a "Name" tartan, it embodies his unique style and heritage, set apart from other clan or corporate designs. This distinctive pattern holds sentimental value for its maker, intended exclusively for Thomas's own use, thereby making it an intimate reflection of his individuality. Although restricted to his sole use, the Bizzell tartan remains a testament to the art of traditional Scottish weaving, a tradition steeped in history and cultural significance, where every thread tells a story of identity, heritage, and family legacy.

name: McFarland-Collins
description: The McFarland-Collins tartan is a proud celebration of Scottish heritage, woven into the very fabric of family tradition. Designed by Sebastian Collins to commemorate his own Scottish roots and those of his wife, who bears the esteemed surname McFarland, this distinctive tartan tells a story of love, loyalty, and legacy. As a Category Name tartan, it has been granted to anyone bearing the surname Collins, giving rise to a global community bound together by this shared connection to Scotland's rich cultural heritage. With its unique character, carefully crafted using the latest tartan design software, this tartan is more than just a colourful pattern - it's a badge of honour, a symbol of family pride and a testament to the enduring power of tradition and legacy.

name: Jamaican National
description: The Jamaican National tartan is a vibrant tribute to the island's rich heritage, born from the enduring legacy of Scotland's influence on Jamaica's history. Registered by the West India Committee, this District tartan commemorates Jamaica's 50th anniversary of independence and honours the significant Scottish presence that shaped the country from the 17th to the 19th centuries. The tartan's colours, carefully chosen to match the iconic hues of the Jamaican National Flag, pay homage to the nation's strong identity as a multicultural society with Scottish roots. As a symbol of unity and national pride, this distinctive tartan design proudly represents Jamaica's unique history and heritage, celebrating its distinct blend of Scottish, African, and Caribbean traditions.

name: McClure, Niall & Family (Personal)
description: This captivating Name tartan, designed by Niall McClure himself, tells the poignant story of his family's history and heritage. Commissioned as a tribute to his three deceased brothers, Ian, William, and Robert, whose memory lives on through their children, including Niall. The tartan's carefully selected colours pay homage to Glasgow, the city where the brothers grew up, with lush green hues that evoke a sense of warmth and community. The blue and white stripes nod to Whitehill Former Pupils Football Club, where all three brothers were dedicated players, instilling a spirit of camaraderie and shared passion. Lastly, the subtle pink undertone nods to the family's diverse cultural roots, blending their Scottish heritage with Pakistani influences in a beautiful display of unity and tradition. This unique tartan is more than just a design – it is a tribute to the enduring legacy of Niall McClure's brothers and the rich tapestry of his family's story.

name: Connacht Green (Dalgliesh)
description:
Previously (Dalgliesh K1) but we made the decision to merge the K1/K7 spec as they weirdly used slightly different shades, which is just asking for trouble.  Not actually present on the SRT

Original source as per the description from design #920:

Phil Smith obtained in Perthshire from a swatch dated 1994 shown to him by Keith Lumsden of the Scottish Tartans Society. Provenance such as this is extremely questionable and of little value. However www.uniq-orn.com shows this as Connaught Green.

name: Connacht
description: The Connacht tartan, registered with the Scottish Tartans Society, proudly embodies the rich heritage of the west coast of Ireland, long considered part of the Emerald Isle's western province. This iconic District tartan pays homage to the region's storied history and cultural identity, evoking a sense of rugged beauty and Celtic tradition. Woven from threads of deep blue, striking green, and warm gold, the Connacht tartan tells a tale of the land's ancient connections with Scotland, yet remains unmistakably Irish in its essence. With no designer credited, it is assumed that this tartan was created by local hands, infusing the fabric with the authentic spirit of the region, now an integral part of Ireland's rich textile heritage.

name: Ballarat
description: The Ballarat tartan is a poignant tribute to the rich history and heritage of Australia's gold rush era, set against the stunning backdrop of Victoria's Ballarat district. Designed specifically for an exhibition showcasing Scotland's connection to Australian identity, this unique tartan weaves together the colours of basalt, blue, and white to evoke the rugged landscape and symbols of national pride that have shaped the nation's story. The incorporation of yellow, reminiscent of the gold that once flowed through Ballarat's streets, adds a sense of vibrancy and optimism to the design. Endorsed by the Mayor of Ballarat, this tartan celebrates the city's proud history and its enduring connection to Scotland, while also serving as a powerful symbol of Australian identity and democracy, as embodied by the iconic Eureka flag.

name: Fogarty (Tipperary)
description: The Fogarty (Tipperary) tartan is a richly symbolic textile that embodies the proud heritage of the Fogarty Clan and County Tipperary in Ireland. Designed by USA Kilts, this Name tartan is reserved for descendants of O'Fogartaigh, officials of Thurles township, and individuals with ancestry to the Barony of Eliogarty, as well as those who can trace their lineage back to the ancient Celtic kingdoms. The tartan's palette, featuring blue and gold, green, brown, red, white, and black, weaves together the threads of history, myth, and family tradition. These colours pay homage to the Tara tartan, representing the connection between the Fogarty Clan and County Tipperary, as well as the fertile landscape of Elyogarty, symbolised by the wheat sheaf on the family crest. With its intricate patterns and symbolic resonance, this tartan is a testament to the enduring legacy of the Fogartys, their bravery in battle, and their hopes for glory, all woven into a majestic and meaningful fabric.

name: Copper Haze
description: The Copper Haze tartan, designed by renowned textile expert Marton Mills, embodies the fleeting beauty of an autumnal landscape, distilled into a sumptuous weave of rich golds, fiery reds, and earthy tones. This Fashion tartan is a vibrant expression of Scottish heritage, where the passage of time is woven into every thread. The subtle nuances of organic brown and green evoke the fading light of a harvest season, while the deep golds and crimson hues recall the warmth and vitality of Scotland's natural surroundings. With its unique colour palette, this tartan whispers secrets of the Highlands' rugged beauty, inviting wearers to embody the spirit of an era defined by nature's cycle of growth and decay.

name:
Hope-Vere #2
[AKA] Weir #2
description: The family tartan of Hope-vere/Weir as shown in Clan Originaux and chosen as the official tartan of the Clan Hope of Craighall Society.

name: Lumsden Green
description: Lumsden Green, a storied clan tartan imbued with the heritage of the noble Lumsdens of Scotland, has its roots firmly planted in the 15th century. Chief Gillem Lumsden's meticulous threadcount records, preserved in the esteemed Lyon Court Books, provide a tangible link to this tartan's history. While it shares similarities with the more well-known Lumsden Hunting tartan, Lumsden Green is a distinct variation that proudly asserts its family identity. This distinctive design has been woven into the fabric of Scottish tradition, its very existence a testament to the enduring legacy of Clan Lumsden and their storied history.

name: Heartfelt Welcome
description: The Heartfelt Welcome tartan is a vibrant and uplifting design, carefully crafted by David Reid to evoke the warmth and hospitality of Scotland's breathtaking landscapes. Inspired by the rolling hills, serene lochs, and wildflower-strewn heather moors, this fashion tartan features a striking palette of greens and blues that represent unity and harmony. The golden brown and lilac hues add a touch of whimsy and elegance, reminiscent of the Scottish hillside's fiery summer days. As part of an event identity for the Jehovah's Witnesses Special International Convention in Glasgow, this tartan was specifically designed to create a welcoming atmosphere for international attendees, symbolising the organisation's commitment to inclusivity and community. Notably, the design is reserved exclusively for members of the Jehovah's Witnesses faith, making it a distinctive and meaningful representation of their heritage.
